english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants during the hot dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nɛkɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high because extreme heat prevents proper pollination. Providing steady moisture and mulching around the base keeps the root zone cool and helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ejaakɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli daa. Shishitoo lɛ haa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Yam leaves produce the food that grows the tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines so the leaves can spread out and catch maximum sunlight, leading to much larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ woɔ niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara babaoo baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over when the fruit bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and tall stems, making them top-heavy when carrying fruit. Supporting the main stem with strong bamboo props prevents wind from pushing the plant over before harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni kɛlɛ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛji ewo yibii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni wa fi tso lɛ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ akatswa tso lɛ shi dani akpa.

english: Why are the roots of my cassava rotting inside the soil before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil for too long without draining away. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow off, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the sap and spreading plant viruses. Spraying neem oil solution helps control these pests and protects the leaves.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tso lɛ mli helai lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing large outer leaves but failing to form a hard round ball in the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ baai wuji shi enyɛɛɛ efee bɔɔlu ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head when soil temperatures are too warm or when they receive irregular watering. Consistent moisture and cool soil encourage the center leaves to wrap tightly into a head.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ awo cabbage yitso kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ awo nɔ nu yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ baaha baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ kɛ bulb lɛ abɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are some of my pineapple plants flowering early while others in the same farm take months longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple tsei lɛ ekomɛi fɔɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo fe nakai lɛ?

english: Pineapples flower based on plant size and weather stresses like unexpected dry spells or cool nights. Using proper spacing and uniform planting material ensures the crop flowers and ripens evenly.
ga: Pineapple fɔfɔi damɔ tso lɛ dalɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ nɔ, tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ loo gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ. Kɛ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kɛ dumɔ nibii ni yaa nɔ daa tsu nii lɛ, ehaa fɔfɔi kɛ amɛshweremɔ feɔ ekome.

english: Why does polishing my harvested rice make it lose its health benefits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa sɛɛnamɔi ni eyɔɔ kɛha hewalɛnamɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ?

english: Polishing rubs off the outer brown skin (bran) of the grain, which holds most of the vital vitamins, minerals, and fiber, leaving behind mostly starch.
ga: Skrubimɔ shwieɔ ŋmãa lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ni ji blɔfo (bran) lɛ nɔ, ni vitamini, mineral, kɛ fiber ni he hiaa lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɔɔ mli. ni eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli babaoo ni eshwɛɔ

english: Why is imported white rice in our Ghanaian markets usually much whiter than the rice I mill locally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa yɛŋ ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba yɛ wɔ Ghana jarayelihe lɛ yɛŋ fe ŋmãa ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Foreign factories use high-powered machines to strip away all the outer natural coatings of the grain to give it a very bright look, while local basic mills often leave some healthy bran intact.
ga: Nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ maŋsɛɛ lɛ kɛ tsɔnei ni he wa waa tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ koni amɛfee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛkpɛɔ waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, maŋ lɛ mli shishijee ŋtayaai lɛ shĩɔ ŋmãa ni mli wa ko yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Does putting my harvested grains through a polishing machine reduce their food value?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ midumɔwui ni akpa lɛ wo tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii amli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni mli wa lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, heavy machine polishing scrapes away the seed's outer coat where key nutrients like iron and B-vitamins live, leaving mainly plain carbohydrates.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɔnei ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwu lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ dade kɛ B vitamini lɛ yɔɔ lɛ, ni eshiɔ carbohydrates ni yɔɔ mlɛo babaoo.

english: Is bright white polished rice healthier for my family than slightly brown local rice?
ga: Ani ŋmãa yɛŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ fioo kɛha miweku lɛ fe maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa ni mli tse?

english: No, bright white rice has had its nutrients stripped away. Local rice that keeps some of its outer brown layer retains natural fiber and vitamins that are much better for your family's health.
ga: Dabi, ŋmãa yɛŋ ni mli tse lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ efite. Kuu lɛ mli ŋmãa ni hiɛɔ kponɔgbɛ fã ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ eko lɛ hiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli fiber kɛ vitamini ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa kɛha oweku lɛ hewalɛnamɔ.

english: What actually happens to the goodness inside my rice when the milling machine cleans it?
ga: Mɛni baa kpakpa ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ tsuu he?

english: The machine uses friction to remove the grain's outer layer to make it look smooth and clean, but that removed outer layer is where almost all the seed's essential nourishment is stored.
ga: Shishitoo lɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛjieɔ ŋmaa lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ koni eha efee tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe tse. Shi kponɔgbɛ fã ni ajieɔ lɛ ji he ni akɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ babaoo toɔ.

english: Why do foreign countries polish their rice so heavily before sending it to Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋsɛɛ maji shwieɔ ŋmãa nɔ waa dani amɛkɛmajeɔ Ghana lɛ?

english: Removing the outer oil-rich bran layer stops the rice from going bad quickly, allowing it to stay fresh during long ship voyages, even though it reduces the nutrient content.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmãa ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ fɔ lɛ, ehaaa ŋmãa lɛ afite oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni omɔ lɛ hiɔ shi ehee yɛ lɛlɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa shi moŋ.

english: Which specific part of the rice grain has the most nutrients before processing?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ fã ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli fe fɛɛ dani atsuɔ he nii?

english: The tiny germ inside the seed and the thin outer brown skin (the bran) hold almost all the vitamins, fiber, and minerals before any processing takes them off.
ga: Muawai bibii ni yɔɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ kɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibioo (bran) lɛ toɔ vitamini, fiber, kɛ minerals lɛ ateŋ babaoo dani nɔ ko ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ajie amɛ.

english: Why does my local unpolished rice fill people up faster than imported polished rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa ni atsɔko nɔ lɛ haa mɛi eyiɔ obɔ oya fe ŋmãa ni atsɔ nɔ ajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ?

english: Unpolished rice still has its natural fiber and bran intact, which digestion takes longer to break down, keeping you feeling full longer than stripped imported rice.
ga: Omɔ ni ajieee lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli tsɔji kɛ bran fɛɛ lolo. ni baahe be babaoo dani efite lɛ Haa onuɔ he akɛ oye nii be babaoo fe ŋmãa ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ.

english: How can I explain to buyers that my slightly dark local rice is better than shiny foreign rice?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ mli akɛ mimaŋ ŋmãa ni mli edɔ fioo lɛ hi fe maŋsɛɛ ŋmãa ni kpɛɔ lɛ?

english: You can tell buyers that the darker color means the rice has not lost its natural nutrients in heavy machines, while shiny white rice has lost its vital vitamins to look clean.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ akɛ, su ni tsuɔ waa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, tsɔnei ni tsii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ efiteee niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa yɛŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ laajeɔ vitamini ni he hiaa ni haa efeɔ nɔ ni he tse.

english: Can I get a machine that cleans my rice without destroying the healthy parts?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahe tsɔne ko ni tsuɔ ŋmãa he nii ni efiteee fãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, adjusting milling machines to lightly dehusk the grain without full polishing removes the hard outer hull while preserving the nutrient-rich brown layer.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ atsake tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmeii fioo komɛi ni ekɛshwieee nɔ fɛɛ nɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and remain small when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɔ shi bibioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When maize plants are planted too close together, their roots fight for the same water and nutrients in the soil, and their leaves block sunlight from one another. Giving each plant proper spacing allows them to get enough sunlight and food to stay green and produce large ears.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ toi wuji aba.

english: What happens if I plant my yam seeds too deep inside the soil mound?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu sweet potato dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ?

english: If you plant yam seeds too deep, the young shoot struggles to break through the heavy soil to reach the sunlight. This wastes the energy stored in the seed tuber, resulting in weak growth or the seed rotting before it can sprout.
ga: Kɛji odu o-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbote shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli koni amɛná hulu la. Nakai feemɔ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ dumɔwu lɛ yitso lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ loo dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Leaving some tall shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa creates a cool canopy that protects the young seedlings from heat stress and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. releasing tall trees Shade loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he lɛ baa. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants falling off during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry spells to save water and keep their roots alive underground. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh new leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛha amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni eda bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is my maize harvest getting smaller every year even though I plant on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ miiba shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Maize uses up specific nutrients from the soil every season. Planting maize continuously in the same place drains those nutrients and allows maize-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating your crop with beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsuɔ nii daa be. Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ hoɔ. ni ehaa ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Groundnuts belong to a family of crops that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This nitrogen acts as natural fertilizer, which feeds the nearby maize plants and improves overall leaf growth and crop yield.
ga: Peanuts ji tsei akuu ko ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii ni ehaa baa lɛ fɛɛ daa kɛ tsei lɛ ayibii lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread a virus while feeding on the leaves, or by extreme heat stress. Keeping the field free of weeds and managing insect pests early prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa lɛ He ni jwɛi akafee yɛ shia lɛ mli kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do the stems of my cowpea plants turn soft and rot at the ground level after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess rain causes water to collect around the roots and lower stem of cowpeas. When soil stays soaked for too long, roots cannot breathe, allowing fungal rot diseases in the wet soil to attack and destroy the stem base.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu buaa ehe naa yɛ cowpea shishifãi kɛ shishigbɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ atutua tso lɛ shishi ni efite.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience sudden temperature changes, water shortages, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to focus only on growing leaves instead of holding onto its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tsake trukaa. nu ni faaa Aloo be mli ni nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ pɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookpɛtɛ fɔfɔi ahe lɛ

english: Why do weeds grow and spread much faster than my crops right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to quickly absorb water and nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early gives your young crops a fair chance to feed and grow without being choked out.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otsei bibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛye niyenii ni amɛdara ni nɔ ko nɔ ko etsĩii amɛnaa.

english: Officer, I want to start farming in a dry area with tough soil, can pineapple plants survive there?
ga: Official Miisumɔ ni mabɔi ŋmɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni shikpɔŋ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ani anana tsei baanyɛ ahi jɛmɛ?

english: Yes, pineapples are very tough crops that can endure hardship. Their leaves are naturally designed to trap moisture and withstand hot weather and poor soil conditions better than many other food crops.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, pineapple ji tso ko ni wa waa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ naagbai anaa. Afee baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ mli fe niyenii tsei krokomɛi.

english: What makes the pineapple plant able to survive when there is no rain for a very long time?
ga: Mɛni haa anana tsei hiɔ shi ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be kakadaŋŋ nɛkɛ?

english: Pineapples store water inside their thick leaves and restrict water loss during hot dry spells. This natural drought tolerance allows the crop to endure long periods of dry weather without dying.
ga: Pineapple kɛ nu toɔ ebaa ni mli tse lɛ mli ni ehaa nu ni fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baa shi. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli hɔmɔ he tsuishitoo nɛɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛɔ amɛdamɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni amɛgbooo.

english: How long does it usually take for a pineapple crop to grow and produce fruit after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni ewoɔ yibii beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Pineapples require time and patience. Depending on the variety and management, it takes about two to three years for a pineapple crop to grow fully and give a good yield.
ga: Pineapple heɔ be kɛ tsuishitoo. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ kɛ bɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ ahaa lɛ nɔ. Eheɔ aaafee afii enyɔ loo etɛ dani ŋmei lɛ shɛɔ ŋmei ni ewoɔ ŋmãa kpakpa.

english: Why do pineapples take so much longer to mature compared to crops like maize or vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pineapple heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai ahe lɛ?

english: Pineapples are long-term perennial crops. They spend many months building strong roots and leaf structures before developing a single quality fruit, unlike fast-growing seasonal crops.
ga: Pineapple ji tso ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Amɛheɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛnáa shishifãi kɛ baai ni mli wa dani amɛnáa yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Esoro lɛ yɛ be mli tsei ni daa oya lɛ ahe.

english: If I plant a field of pineapples today, can I harvest from those same plants for more than one year?
ga: Kɛji ŋmɛnɛ midu pineapple yɛ ŋmɔ mli Ani manyɛ makpa tso kome nɔ nɔ ni fe afi kome?

english: Yes, after harvesting the main fruit, pineapples grow side shoots (suckers) that can produce a second or third harvest from the same plant over several years if well managed.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni akpa aduawai titri lɛ sɛɛ. Pineapple woɔ sɛɛ ŋmeii (ŋmeii) ni baanyɛ ajie ŋmaa ni ji enyɔ loo etɛ kɛjɛ tso kome mli yɛ afii babaoo mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Since pineapples endure hard conditions, does that mean I can just plant them and leave them without care?
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, pineapple nyɛɔ edamɔɔ shihilɛi ni mli wawai anaa. Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ manyɛ madu ni mashi lɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko akwɛɛɛ nɔ?

english: No, even though pineapples endure hardship, successful farming requires strict discipline. Without regular weeding, pest control, and proper feeding, your plants will produce small or unmarketable fruits.
ga: Dabi, eyɛ mli akɛ pineapple toɔ etsui shi yɛ naagbai amli moŋ. Shi okwaayeli ni yeɔ omanye lɛ biɔ tsɔsemɔ ni mli wa. Kɛji akɛ jwɛi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ lɛ bɛ kɛ niyenii ni sa Otso lɛ baawo yibii bibii loo ni anyɛɛɛ ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: What kind of daily care or discipline is needed to make sure my pineapple farm succeeds?
ga: Daa gbi kwɛmɔ loo tsɔsemɔ he miihia koni mi-anana ŋmɔ lɛ aye omanye.

english: Discipline on a pineapple farm means maintaining proper plant spacing, keeping weeds under control, protecting the fruit from pests, and allowing the plants enough time to mature naturally.
ga: Tsɔsemɔ ni yɔɔ pineapple ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akwɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛ ni sa nɔ. jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ Abuɔ aduawai ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni ahaa tsei lɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Is it better for me to start with a small piece of land or go straight into farming hundreds of acres of pineapples?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko baaje shishi? Aloo oya tɛ̃ɛ ni oyadu ŋmeii ni dalɛ ji acre ohai abɔ lɛ?

english: It is always safer to start on a small plot of land first. This allows you to master the required management practices and costs before scaling up to large farm sizes.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe be fɛɛ be akɛ oooje shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni ole bɔ ni akwɛɔ nibii anɔ ahaa kɛ shika ni he hiaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani oyashɛɔ ŋmɔ agbo ko mli.

english: Why do some pineapples on the market grow very big while others remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ dara waa ni ekomɛi hu dara lolo lɛ?

english: Fruit size depends on good field discipline, soil fertility, and proper plant care. Plants that receive balanced nutrients and clean field conditions have the strength to grow large fruits.
ga: Bɔ ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ da ha lɛ damɔ tsɔsemɔ kpakpa nɔ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsei akwɛmɔ ni sa Tsei ni naa niyenii ni ja kɛ shihilɛi ni mli tse ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaadu aduawai wuji.

english: Officer, how much land do I need if I want to build a large commercial pineapple farm?
ga: Official Kɛji oosumɔ ni oma jarayeli ŋmɔ agbo ko ni ji pineapple Shikpɔŋ enyiɛ he hiaa?

english: Commercial operations can span anywhere from tens to hundreds of acres, but success on a large scale requires significant investment, workforce discipline, and continuous farm management.
ga: Jarayeli nitsumɔi baanyɛ ashɛ he fɛɛ he kɛjɛ acre nyɔŋmai kɛyashi ohai abɔ nɔ. Shi omanyeyeli yɛ gbɛ ni da nɔ lɛ biɔ ni akɛ shika babaoo awo mli. Nitsulɔi atsɔsemɔ kɛ ŋmɔ nɔkwɛmɔ ni yaa nɔ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nutrients, especially nitrogen, or that the soil has too much water drowning the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted poultry manure helps them regain their deep green color and grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ o-corn tsei lɛ amli. titri lɛ nitrogen Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloi aŋmɔŋ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow much better when I mix dried animal manure into the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with essential nutrients that plants need to grow strong roots and healthy leaves. It also improves the soil structure, helping it hold onto water longer during dry days.
ga: Manure haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni shishifãi ni wa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cassava and maize together on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting cassava and maize together allows you to maximize your land and rain. Maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, while cassava grows slower and stays in the ground longer, giving you two harvests from one field.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fee ekome lɛ, ehaa onáa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛ nugbɔ babaoo. Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ daa blɛoo ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii shii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my yam mounds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When yam mounds are too close, the vines fight each other for sunlight and the roots compete for nutrients in the soil. Giving them proper space ensures each plant gets enough food and light to develop large tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii akuu ko bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Wein tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ koni ekɛwo tsɔnei wuji amli.

english: What causes holes to appear in my cabbage leaves and how do I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni haa buji jeɔ kpo yɛ kaabe baa nɔ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ aaatsɔ atsĩ naa?

english: Holes are caused by caterpillars and insects feeding on the leaves. You can protect your crop by checking plants regularly to pick off pests by hand, spraying neem seed extract, or applying recommended crop protection products early.
ga: Buji kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ baa ji nɔ ni kɛ bu baa. Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ otsei lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ daa koni okɛ onine ajie tsɛŋemɔ helai. Shwɛmɔ neem dumɔwu mli nu loo okɛ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe lɛ atsu nii mra

english: Why do weeds harm my pepper crop so much if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ awui waa kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your pepper plants for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing weeds early ensures your pepper plants get all the resources they need to produce abundant fruit.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ pepper tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha o-pepper tso lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil becomes too dry, or if there are no insects around to pollinate them. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing shade during extreme heat helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii bɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees dry up and shed during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season, young cocoa trees lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can draw water from the dry soil. To survive, the trees shed their leaves to conserve water until the rains return.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. koni amɛhi shi Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai koni amɛkɛbu nu he kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why should I buy certified hybrid maize seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ŋmãa ni ahere kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred to resist diseases, handle climate stress better, and produce higher yields. Seeds saved from a previous hybrid harvest lose these special characteristics and will result in lower crop yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai. Kpee kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he haomɔ naa jogbaŋŋ. ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsutsu hybrid ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baafite sui nɛɛ. ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aba shi

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are fully mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ edara ni esa akɛ mafo?

english: Groundnuts are ready for harvest when the leaves begin to turn yellow and dry up, and when you open a few pods and see that the inner lining of the shell has turned dark brown or black.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Ni kɛ́ ogbele ŋmeii fioo komɛi ni ona akɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmeii loo ediŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops stop producing fruits when the rains stop for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ yibii kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Crops need constant water to move nutrients from the soil up into their stems and fruits. Without enough water, the plant gets stressed and drops its flowers or stops forming fruits to save its own life.
ga: Nu ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ he miihia tsei koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛyibii lɛ anɔ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa efɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi loo ekpaa yibiiwoo koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: What does irrigation mean, and how can it help my crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni nu shwiemɔ tsɔɔ? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Irrigation simply means bringing water to your crops manually, with pipes, or pumps instead of waiting for rain. It allows your crops to keep growing and bearing fruit even when there is no rainfall.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ onibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ okɛ onine baahã onibii lɛ nu kɛtsɔ hose loo pɔmpi nɔ, moŋ fe ni ooomɛ nugbɔ, ni eye ebua onibii lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: How can I know if my crops are wilting because of too little rain or because of a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo tsɔ loo hela hewɔ?

english: Water-stressed crops usually curl their leaves during the hottest part of the day and perk back up at night or in the early morning. Plants affected by disease will stay wilted or yellow regardless of the time of day.
ga: Tsei ni nu efo amɛmli lɛ fɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni ebaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ baaya nɔ agbi loo amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ekɔɔɔ gbi lɛ mli be he.

english: How can I keep the soil around my crops damp when the sun is very hot and the rains delay?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso waa ni nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ?

english: You can cover the bare soil around your crops with dry grass, leaves, or crop leaves—a practice called mulching. This acts like a blanket that shades the soil, stopping the hot sun from evaporating the water.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ sũ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko awo ehe. Akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmɔshi nibii duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsĩɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni shwieɔ shi.

english: Which crops can I plant that will still give me a good yield even if the rains are small?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ madu ni baawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lolo kɛji nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ po?

english: Crops like cassava, millet, sorghum, and cowpeas have deep root systems or low water needs. They are hardier and can survive dry spells much better than sensitive crops like maize or vegetables.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo nu ni he ehiaaa tsɔ. Amɛhe wa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni waaa tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai.

english: If my crops produce flowers during a dry period, will those flowers still turn into good fruits?
ga: Kɛji mitso lɛ wo fɔfɔi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Ani nakai fɔfɔi lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi lolo?

english: Hot, dry weather usually causes flowers to dry up and fall off before turning into fruits. If water does not reach the crop during flowering, the plant cannot support fruit growth and the yield will fail.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ aduawai. Kɛji nu shɛɛɛ tso lɛ he yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ aye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ ni nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni sɛɛ efooo.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a dry stretch. If seeds sprout after one rain and then face days of hot weather without water, the young seedlings will dry up and die before establishing roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ nyiɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome sɛɛ No lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ kpe Dumɔwui bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛfee shishifãi.

english: If I carry water in buckets to my small plot, is it better to water a little bit every day or give a heavy watering twice a week?
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni okɛ nu awo baagi mli kɛya shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Nu fioo daa gbi. Aloo nu ni oooha shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli lɛ hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Watering deeply a few times a week is better because it forces roots to grow deeper into the soil where water lasts longer. Light daily watering keeps roots near the surface where they burn quickly in the sun.
ga: Nu ni mli kwɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli shii 2-3 yɛ otsi mli lɛ hi fe no. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ adara kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni nu baanyɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa shishifãi lɛ fioo daa gbi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ, he ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How can I collect rainwater during the wet season so I have water for my farm when the dry season begins?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabua nugbɔ nu naa yɛ nugbɔ be mli koni maná nu kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ beni nugbɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: You can dig small farm ponds lined with plastic sheets, or collect rain from roof gutters into barrels. Storing this water lets you hand-water valuable crops when the rain stops unexpectedly.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nubu bibioo ko. Yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni akɛ plastic tsɔji ehà nɔ Aloo bua nugbɔ ni jɛɔ tsũ yiteŋ nubui amli lɛ naa kɛwoɔ baagi mli. Nu nɛɛ ni ooobua naa lɛ baaha bo diɛŋtsɛ okɛ nu awo onibii ni jara wa lɛ amli kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa.

english: Can I apply chemical fertilizer to my crops when the soil is completely dry and there is no rain coming?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa ni nugbɔ enɛko?

english: No, putting fertilizer on dry soil can burn and destroy your crop's roots. Fertilizer needs water to dissolve into the soil so the plant can drink it safely without getting damaged.
ga: Dabi, shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni tsei lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ shweshweeshwe ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee.

english: Why is it better to measure the distance between my maize seeds instead of just planting them randomly like we used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu gbɛ ni kã mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ he moŋ fe ni madu amɛ trukaa kɛkɛ? Etamɔ tsutsu lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ ehi fe no.

english: When crops are spaced properly, each plant gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water to grow strong. Planting seeds too close together forces them to fight for resources, resulting in thin stalks and smaller yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ Tso fɛɛ tso baaná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha shweremɔ kpakpa Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛwuu kɛha nibii ni he hiaa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do extension officers tell me not to burn the bush when clearing my land for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛkashã kooi kɛ́ amɛmiikpa ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Burning destroys beneficial nutrients and helpful organisms in the soil while drying it out. Leaving cleared organic matter to decompose naturally adds nutrients back into the dirt and helps hold moisture for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli gĩɔ. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni ajie lɛ mli lɛ fite yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker and produce less when I plant maize on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or beans restores nitrogen to the soil and keeps it fertile.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmãa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is missing the food that my crops need to grow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Unhealthy soil shows through your crops. If plants grow very slowly, have pale yellow leaves instead of deep green ones, or produce small fruits, the soil is likely lacking key nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ baajie ehe kpo yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ daa blɛoo waa Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ. loo ewoɔ aduawai bibii Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from an agricultural store instead of using seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase yɛ okwaayeli shwapo ko mli moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred to resist local diseases, tolerate drought better, and produce higher yields, whereas seeds saved from past harvests lose their strength and quality over generations.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Hɔmɔ he tsuishitoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛ amɛhe kpakpa kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Giving them steady moisture and sufficient nutrients helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni mli edɔ daa kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wither and die so quickly under intense sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have delicate, shallow roots that cannot reach deeper water in the soil. Without shade crops or a layer of mulch to cover the soil, the intense heat dries out the roots and scorches the leaves.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ nu he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ bɛ lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha shishifãi lɛ agbi ni ebaashã baai lɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce small yields even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm; their aggressive roots steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops before your plants have a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Eshishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ baaju nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ onibii amli dani otsei lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Curling yellow leaves on cassava are a sign of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings prevents this disease from destroying your yield.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle yucca he lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ odu ŋmeii ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela nɛɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my harvested maize get damaged by insects so quickly after I store it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii fiteɔ mi-ŋma ni mikpaa lɛ oya beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils multiply quickly when grain is stored before it is completely dry or when kept in unsealed spaces. Drying your maize properly until it is hard and storing it in airtight bags keeps insects out.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii babaoo yaa hiɛ oya kɛ́ akɛ ŋmaa to dani egbi kwraa loo kɛ́ akɛto he ko ni atsĩko naa. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ewa ni okɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akabote mli.

english: Why do oil palm fruits stick so tightly together on the bunch when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oil palm yibii lɛ kpɛtɛɔ amɛhe waa yɛ kui amli kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Oil palm fruits grow packed tightly in a bunch to share nutrients and protect each other while maturing. Boiling the harvested bunch or allowing it to ferment for a day or two helps loosen the fruits naturally from the central stalk.
ga: Mu tso yibii lɛ feɔ kui ni mli wa koni amɛja niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛbu amɛhe he kɛji amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ shã loo oha amɛfee gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ ajie amɛhe kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What is the difference between the soft outer flesh of the palm nut and the hard shell inside?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ kɛ emli ŋmei ni wa lɛ teŋ?

english: The soft outer orange flesh produces traditional red palm oil used for cooking, while the hard inner nut contains a kernel seed that yields palm kernel oil, which is used for soaps and cosmetics.
ga: Loo ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ haa anáa blema tsofa tsuru ni akɛhooɔ nii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ mli ni wa lɛ mli ŋmei ni haa ŋmei ŋmei fɔ, ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ samlai kɛ tsofai ni akɛsaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my harvested palm nuts spoil quickly if I leave them inside my house before boiling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shĩa mli dani mikɛshã lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested palm nuts contain high moisture and natural sugars. If kept in warm, unventilated spaces, fungi and bacteria quickly break down the fruit, causing rot and increasing oil acidity.
ga: Palm ŋmeii ni akpa ehee lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ sugar ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Fungi kɛ bacteria fiteɔ aduawai lɛ oya. Enɛ haa fɔ lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa acid lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How can I easily tell when my palm nut bunch is ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-palm tsei lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A bunch is ripe when the outer fruits turn a deep reddish-orange color and at least five to ten fruits fall off naturally onto the ground under the tree.
ga: No mli lɛ, tso yibii lɛ asɛɛgbɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ. Ni kɛ hoo lɛ, aduawai enumɔ kɛyashi nyɔŋma baagbee shikpɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What causes the flesh of the palm nut to turn oily as it grows?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei tso lɛ loo lɛ feɔ fɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: As the palm fruit matures, the plant converts sunlight, water, and soil nutrients into natural vegetable fats, storing them in the outer fruit wall to nourish the developing seed.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ yibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Tsei lɛ tsakeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei amli fɔji ni ji adebɔɔ mli fɔji. ni akɛtoɔ tso yibii lɛ kponɔgbɛ gbogbo lɛ mli koni ekɛha dumɔwui ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does it take such a long time for a fresh palm nut seed to sprout when I plant it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani ŋmei dumɔwui heei kwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ lɛ?

english: The inner palm nut has a thick, hard shell that prevents water and air from reaching the seed quickly. This protective layer must slowly break down under moisture and heat before the sprout can push through.
ga: Tso lɛ mligbɛ fã lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe oya. Esa akɛ ajie nɛkɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he nɛɛ fiofio. Efiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo kɛ latsaa shishi dani dumɔwui baanyɛ abote mli.

english: Why do young oil palm seedlings need shade when I first put them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni oil palm dumɔwui lɛ he hiaa ni amɛná hulutsoo be mli ni adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Young palm seedlings have tender leaves and small root systems that cannot pull enough water from the soil to survive harsh, direct sunlight, so shade protects them from drying out.
ga: Palm dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ ajie nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛdamɔ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, hulutsoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ he koni ekagbi.

english: Why are some of my palm trees producing very small fruit bunches compared to my neighbor's trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ yibii bibii kwraa kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋbii tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Fruit bunch size depends on soil nutrients, consistent rainfall, and proper tree spacing. Trees growing in poor soil or planted too close together compete for food and produce smaller bunches.
ga: Yibii akuu lɛ dalɛ damɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa kɛ tsei ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa Tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ loo ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baatswa niyenii he akaŋ ni amɛbaawo jwɛi bibii.

english: Why do birds and small animals keep attacking my ripening palm nuts on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi kɛ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛtutuaa ŋmei yibii ni ekwɛ̃ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The bright red color and high fat content of ripe palm nuts make them a major food source for wildlife. Clearing brush around your trees and harvesting promptly reduces animal damage.
ga: Su tsuru ni mli tse kɛ fɔ ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli lɛ haa amɛfeɔ niyenii titri ni koo mli kooloi yeɔ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishi ni akpa amɛ lɛ, ebaaha kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ aba shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to trim off old, dry leaves from around my oil palm fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ baai ni egbɔ ni egbi kɛjɛ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning old leaves opens up the tree canopy, allowing more sunlight and air flow around the fruit bunches, which prevents fruit rot and makes harvesting much easier.
ga: Tso lɛ baai momoi ni afolɔ mli lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɔleɔ he fɛɛ he. Yibii akui babaoo Enɛ haaa yibii lɛ afite ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How do I know if the seeds I am buying at the market are good quality?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Good quality seeds are usually certified by government agricultural offices and come with official tags. These certified seeds are tested to ensure they sprout easily, grow uniform crops, and are free from pests and diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, maŋ nɔyeli okwaayeli nitsumɔhe lɛ haa dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he odaseyeli ni amɛhiɛɔ nɔyeli lɛ kadimɔ nii. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli nɛɛ mli koni ana akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ oya. Dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ daa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai bɛ mli

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of just using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ pɛ baatsu nii?

english: Seeds saved from past harvests lose their strength over time and can carry diseases to the next season. Certified seeds are specially produced to give high yields, fight off diseases, and grow uniformly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai aya be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo, amɛwu amɛshi helai ni amɛdara daa.

english: What is a foundation seed and why do extension officers keep talking about it?
ga: Mɛni ji Shishitoo Dumɔwu? Ni mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nitsumɔ nɔ lɛ yaa nɔ amɛwieɔ he lɛ?

english: Foundation seed is the super-pure, high-quality starting material produced under strict expert supervision. It is the original seed used to produce the certified seeds that farmers plant in their fields.
ga: Dumɔwui shishitoo ji shishijee nɔ ko ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni he tse waa. Afee yɛ ŋaalɔi akwɛmɔ ni mli wa shishi. Eji shishijee dumɔwu ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛfee dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni okwaafoi duɔ yɛ amɛŋmɔji amli lɛ.

english: Are certified plant cuttings or cassava suckers really better than the ones my neighbor gives me for free?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛfoɔ tso loo tsɔne ni akɛjieɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ hi fe ŋmei ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛha mi yaka lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, because cuttings from a neighbor's farm might carry hidden viruses or insects. Certified planting materials are inspected and proven to be clean, healthy, and capable of producing a bigger harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ekolɛ ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii yɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ kɛjɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli. Akwɛ nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni awo he odase lɛ amli ni ana akɛ amɛhe tse, amɛyɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it important to clear and break up the soil deeply before I sow my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni mli kwɔ dani adu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Proper land preparation loosens hard dirt so young crop roots can spread easily, helps the soil hold moisture, and removes weeds that would otherwise steal food and water from your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bɔni afee ni tso bibioo lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni ojie jwɛi ni baanyɛ aju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ onibii amli lɛ.

english: How can bad soil preparation cause my crops to fail early?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni asaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite oya?

english: If the land is not prepared well, seeds get trapped in hard soil or air pockets, making it difficult for them to sprout. Unprepared land also leaves weed roots behind, which quickly overpower young seedlings.
ga: Kɛji asaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa loo kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui amli, ni no haa ewaa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛakwɛ̃. Shikpɔŋ ni asaaa he lɛ hu shĩɔ jwɛi shishifãi yɛ sɛɛ. ni yeɔ dumɔwui bibii anɔ kunim oya.

english: How do I know my field is fully ready for me to start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ eshɛ he kɛha dumɔ?

english: Your field is ready when the soil is free from big weeds and trash, broken down into fine crumbly soil, and moist enough so that planted seeds can absorb water without drowning.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ efee klalo beni jwɛi kɛ jwɛi wuji bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Egbɛ eshwa ni etsɔ sũ kpakpa. ni edɔ bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni dumɔwui ni adu lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu ni ekɛ nu akafo mli.

english: If I buy good seeds, does that mean I don't need to worry much about field maintenance?
ga: Kɛ mihe dumɔwui kpakpai Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ ehe ehiaaa ni mahao babaoo yɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ he?

english: Good seeds are only the first step to a high yield. Even the best seeds need well-prepared soil, correct planting distance, regular weeding, and adequate water to grow to their full potential.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai ji klɛŋklɛŋ gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ po he miihia shikpɔŋ ni asaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ. dumɔ he ni ja Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ daa. kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha eda kɛyashɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ

english: Why do some plants on my farm grow big and strong while others right next to them stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa ni amɛhe wa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmasɛi lɛ hiɔ shi bibii lɛ?

english: Uneven growth happens when seeds are of mixed quality, soil preparation is uneven across the farm, or some plants have to compete harder against weeds and hard soil patches.
ga: Dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee baa kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ji nɔ ni futuɔ amɛhe. Shikpɔŋ nɔ saamɔ yeee egbɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Aloo esa akɛ tsei komɛi kɛ jwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa abɔ akaŋ babaoo.

english: How does starting with quality planting material affect how early my crops mature?
ga: Te nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ shishijee baaná mitsei lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: High-quality, certified seeds grow faster and more predictably because they are free from seed-borne diseases, allowing the crop to establish quickly and reach harvest time without unnecessary delays.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni ana he odaseyeli lɛ daa oya ni anyɛɔ atsɔɔ nɔ ni baaba. Ejaakɛ helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli kɛbaa lɛ bɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛshɛɔ kpamɔɔ be lɛ he ni sɛɛ efooo ni he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my young maize plants turn yellow and dry up after I burn the bush to clear my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi beni mishã jwɛi lɛ koni mikɛjie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Burning bush off your field destroys organic matter and beneficial soil organisms, leaving the soil dry and starved of essential nutrients like nitrogen which young maize needs to stay green and grow.
ga: Tsoi bibii ni ashãa yɛ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ kponɔ lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbɛ́ɔ ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni he hiaa ŋmãa bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crops right after I clear a new plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ beni mijie saatso hee ko nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit hidden in the soil for a long time. Clearing the bush opens up direct sunlight and rain access, which triggers those wild seeds to germinate much faster than domestic crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe teeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Tsoi bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ nugbɔ aba tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya kwraa fe tsei ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I wait for the soil to get soaked by a few heavy rains after clearing before I sow my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fioo beni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Early light rains only wet the very top layer of dirt. If you plant too early, the subsoil stays dry, causing the new seed roots to dry out and die under the afternoon sun.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo leebi lɛ baaha muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni egbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui heei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane hulu lɛ shishi.

english: If I plant my cassava stems very close together on my cleared farm, will I get a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni ajie mli lɛ mli lɛ Ani maná yibii babaoo?

english: Planting too close makes crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which leads to weak stems and small, thin tubers instead of a large yield.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yitsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I clear away all the tall trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight. Tall shade trees act like natural umbrellas that keep the ground moist and cool while the young cocoa grows.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo, ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa edɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and curl downwards during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miiho ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl down in peak heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, which helps the plant conserve water until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛbuɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Extreme hot temperatures sterilize flower pollen and stress the plant, forcing it to drop its flowers to conserve energy and save itself from dying of thirst.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ gbeɔ pollen ni ehaa tso lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhere amɛhe kɛjɛ kumai he.

english: Why does cutting off the small side branches of my pepper plants make the peppers grow larger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ agbo?

english: Pruning off extra side shoots stops the plant from wasting energy on extra leaves and redirects all its nutrients directly into growing bigger, healthier peppers.
ga: Kɛtsɔ sɛɛ ŋmeii ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ efiteee hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. ni okɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ lɛ aya ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yams when I plant yam on the exact same soil two years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii enyɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam plants suck out specific nutrients from the soil. Planting yam continuously on the same spot exhausts those specific nutrients and causes soil-borne pests to build up.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ shwieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oya nɔ adu ŋmeii yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite. ni ehaa ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do insects attack the young green leaves on my crops more than the older leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ fe baai ni eda lɛ?

english: Young leaves and fresh shoots are soft, tender, and full of water and sugar, making them much easier and more nutritious for insects to eat than tough, old leaves.
ga: Baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii heei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni nu kɛ sugar eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa eyeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kooloi, ni eyɛ niyenii babaoo fe baai ni egbɔ ni wa.

english: Should I sow my pepper seeds directly into the main farm or start them in a nursery bed first?
ga: Ani esa akɛ matsɔɔ akɛ adu pepper dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli loo adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: It is best to start pepper seeds in a small, protected nursery bed. Young pepper seedlings are very delicate, so nurturing them in a nursery allows you to shade and water them carefully until they are strong enough to survive being transplanted to the main field.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooobɔi pepper dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko ni abuɔ he lɛ mli. Pepper dumɔwui bibii lɛ waaa kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ hulutsoo kɛ nu woɔ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu amɛ awo ŋmɔ titri lɛ mli.

english: Do vegetable crops like peppers and onions need full sunlight all day to give a good harvest?
ga: Aduawai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ Ani hulu muu fɛɛ he miihia amɛ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: Yes, peppers and onions need at least six to eight hours of direct sunlight every day to manufacture their food and grow healthy bulbs and fruits. If you plant them under big tree shade, they will grow tall and weak without producing much food.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ hoo lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai enumɔ kɛyashi kpaanyɔ he miihia ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii daa gbi koni amɛná niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ atɛo yɛ tso agbo ko hɔɔ shishi lɛ, ebaada ni egbɔjɔ ni ewooo niyenii babaoo.

english: Can I plant onions and pepper together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting onions alongside peppers is a great traditional practice. Onions have a strong natural smell that repels many harmful insects that usually attack pepper plants, helping to protect your peppers without buying expensive sprays.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ ji kusum nifeemɔ kpakpa. Sabala yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa ni shwieɔ kooloi bibii babaoo ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni bei pii lɛ amɛtutuaa pepper tsei lɛ. Ye obua ni abu ŋmeii ahe ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ ni jara wa.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing on pepper plants is usually a sign that tiny insects like aphids or mites are sucking the juice from the leaves, or that the plant lacks nutrients. Sprinkling clean wood ash on the leaves or using a mild soap-and-water spray can help clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii miimu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. aloo etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai Okɛ tso sũ ni he tse afɔ baai lɛ anɔ loo okɛ samla kɛ nu ni mli ejɔ atsu nii. Ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before any fruits grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani yibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers usually drop off when the plant is stressed by hot weather, dry soil, or too much fertilizer. Making sure your plants get consistent water during dry heat helps the flowers stay on and turn into healthy peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ hao tso lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ koni otsei lɛ ana nu daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my onion bulbs staying tiny instead of growing big and round?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onions lɛ ji bibii yɛ agbo kɛ kokroo najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Onion bulbs stay small if the soil is squeezed too hard for the bulbs to expand, or if the seeds were planted too deep. Onions need loose, soft soil and light covering so the bulbs can easily swell near the soil surface.
ga: Sabala baahi shi bibioo kɛji akɛ atswa shikpɔŋ lɛ waa tsɔ bɔni afee ni sabala lɛ agbɛ ashwã. aloo kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ he miihia Onion koni bulbs lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mlɛo yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable crops in the morning or in the evening?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo aduawai tsei anɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ?

english: It is best to water your vegetables early in the morning. Morning watering gives the roots water to survive the hot sun during the day, whereas evening watering leaves the plants wet overnight, which can attract crop diseases.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha aduawai anɔ nu leebi. Nu ni afɔɔ amɛnɔ leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa nu koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni oooha tso lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ baaha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ nyɔɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ. ni baanyɛ agbala tsei ahe helai

english: How do weeds hurt my pepper and onion plants if I leave them in the soil?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye mi-pepper kɛ onion tsei lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors—they steal the light, water, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds early gives your vegetables full room and food to grow fast and yield more harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ—amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha o-vegetables lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii babaoo ni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know when my onions are fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-onions lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Onions are ready to harvest when their green leaves turn yellow, go soft at the neck, and fall over naturally on the ground. Once half of the leaves fall over, stop watering and harvest them a few days later.
ga: Sabolai efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai eŋɔli lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ, efee blɛoo yɛ etsitsi nɔ, ni egbee shikpɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji baai lɛ fã egbee shi lɛ Kpa nu ni oooha lɛ ni okpa gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: How can I store my harvested onions at home so they do not rot quickly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ato shĩa koni ekafite oya?

english: To keep onions fresh for a long time, dry them in a cool, shady, airy spot for a week until their outer skin turns dry and papery. After drying, keep them in woven baskets or mesh bags where air can freely pass around them.
ga: Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ Ha egbi yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli otsi kome kɛyashi be mli ni kponɔgbɛ lɛ baagbi ni efee tamɔ wolo. Kɛji amɛgbi lɛ, Okɛ amɛ awo tsɛnsi ni akpɛ́ loo mesh kotoku mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This makes the plants weak and small, leading to lower yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni efeɔ bibioo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: What is the benefit of spreading dry bush leaves around the base of my plants?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ jwɛi baai ni egbi ni mikɛshwãa mitsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ he?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry leaves, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation during hot days, and stops weeds from growing easily.
ga: Mulching around Okɛ baai ni egboi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ aha onibii ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ mlɛo

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key plant nutrient. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen-based fertilizer helps the plant turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ mli niyenii titri ko bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I grow maize on the exact same land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing maize in the same spot continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up. Switching to crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ atsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii anɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady. The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell, which can dry out and kill newly germinated seeds in the hot soil.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ, ni baanyɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get enough regular water. Consistent watering during hot periods helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai lɛ ahiɔ shi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking plant juices. Spraying the leaves with neem water or a recommended pesticide kills the pests so healthy foliage can sprout.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem nu loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ koni baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are ready to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakumɔ?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the lower leaves dry up and drop off. You can also gently clear away topsoil near the base to check if the tubers are large enough.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ Ojie ŋwɛi sũ ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ hu fiofio koni okwɛ kɛji bulbs lɛ dara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my stored seed yams starting to sprout before the rainy season arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Seed yams naturally wake up after a few months of rest, especially if stored in warm, dark areas. Keeping seed yams in a cool, well-ventilated barn helps delay sprouting until planting time.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ baate shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni akɛjɔɔ amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ. Titri lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni duŋ ewo. Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ to ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛkwɛ̃mɔ asɛɛ afo kɛyashi be ni esa akɛ adu lɛ baashɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food for leaf growth, or that the soil is waterlogged and drowning the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa lɛ. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho.

english: Why do my maize stalks fall over easily whenever strong winds blow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over when their root systems are shallow, which often happens if seeds are planted too shallowly, if the crops are crowded together, or if soil isn't mounded around the base of the stems.
ga: Abɛi baagbee baai lɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Kɛji tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo loo kɛji akɛ sũ lɛ ebɔleko tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why is my cassava plant growing very tall with big leaves, but only producing small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko pɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich manure, cassava plants use all their energy to grow top leaves and stems instead of storing food in the roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do some of my planted seed yams take a very long time to sprout even after the rains have started?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural resting period called dormancy after harvest, and they will not sprout until this internal resting clock finishes, regardless of rain or soil moisture.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Ni amɛdaraŋ kɛyashi nɛkɛ mligbɛ hejɔɔmɔ ŋmɛlɛtswaa nɛɛ baagbe naa. Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ lɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off before any green tomatoes form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when daytime temperatures get too hot or when the plants do not get a regular supply of water, causing the plant stress.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa nu daa Ekɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a virus carried into the plant by insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi kɛyaa tsei amli lɛ anɔ

english: Why do my cabbage seedlings look weak and wilted right after I move them from the seedbed to the farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Moving young plants damages their tiny feeding roots, causing temporary transplant shock. Transplanting late in the evening and watering immediately helps them recover quickly.
ga: Tsei bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi bibii ni yeɔ nii lɛ, ni ekɛ be kukuoo mli shoofeemɔ baa. Kɛ́ adu amɛ gbɛkɛ ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhe waaa oya.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct hot sunlight; they need shade crops like plantains to protect their delicate leaves and keep the ground cool during their first years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe jɔɔ tamɔ plantains koni amɛbu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli.

english: Why does my plantain stalk take more than a year to produce fruit while my neighbor's plantain fruits much faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ heɔ nɔ ni fe afi dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ plantain lɛ woɔ yibii oya kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantains grow and fruit much faster when excess suckers are cut away so that the main mother plant gets all the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients.
ga: Plantains baakwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii oya kwraa kɛji akɛ afo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tso titri lɛ aná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my land make the maize I plant next season grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpea roots form tiny nodules that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant after them.
ga: Cowpea shishifãi feɔ kui bibii. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when there is too much rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: When the soil becomes flooded with water, air cannot reach the plant's roots. This prevents the maize from absorbing key nutrients like nitrogen, causing the leaves to lose their green color.
ga: Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ ji koni ŋmãa lɛ akaŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni no aha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli.

english: Cassava plants naturally shed their leaves during dry periods to reduce water loss. Dropping leaves helps the plant save moisture and protect the underground roots until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Baai ni egbee shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to produce fruit if I plant them during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛji midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains require steady soil moisture to build strong root systems. Planting them in dry conditions causes severe stress, which slows early growth and delays fruiting.
ga: Plantains he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni ekɛ shishifãi ni mli wa aba. He ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa. Enɛ haa edalɛ baa shi ni ehaa yibiiwoo sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil is rich enough to grow healthy vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Good soil is typically dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds water well without staying flooded, and shows signs of life such as earthworms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ onine mli, ehiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ, ehiɛɛɛ nu, ni eyɛ wala he okadii tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help my soil and crops?
ga: Te tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds nearby crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa niyenii.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually triggered by heat stress, irregular watering, or viruses spread by tiny insects like whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ he haomɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ be ni sa mli loo helai ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from high heat, lack of water, or when there are too few pollinating insects like bees to fertilize the blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kɛ́ ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa tsɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster in my field than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe tsei ni mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ du lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants naturally adapted to survive harsh local soil and weather conditions, allowing them to absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji maŋ tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need shade crops like plantains planted beside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under harsh, direct sunlight. Plantains provide vital shade and humidity while the cocoa plants establish their roots.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa waa. Beni kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi miida lɛ

english: Why do certified seed varieties grow better than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
