ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected and bred by researchers to resist common diseases, survive drought better, and produce higher, more uniform yields than traditional saved seeds.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi ehala dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni amɛkwɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii ni fa ni yaa nɔ daa fe blema dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under intense sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects young cocoa from heat stress and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he haomɔ he lɛ baa. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crop roots with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry vegetation—known as mulching—acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the ground cool under hot sunshine, stops water from evaporating quickly, and prevents weeds from sprouting around your plants.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ tsei ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ otsei lɛ ahe.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to stay green and turn sunlight into food. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help the maize recover its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛtsake hulu la lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and produce smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil food. When weeds grow close to your crops, they steal essential nutrients away, leaving your main plants hungry and undersized.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ Amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei titrii lɛ ni amɛbaafee bibii.

english: It is best to wait until the soil gets thoroughly soaked by two or three steady rains rather than sowing after the very first light rain, ensuring the seeds have enough deep moisture to sprout and survive.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Mohu ɔ, du ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ nɛ nɛ ɔ se konɛ dumi ɔmɛ nɛ ná nu nɛ mi kuɔ bɔ nɛ sa konɛ a nyɛ nɛ a wa nɛ a hi si.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to crowd each other and fight for light and root space, resulting in thin stems and poor yields. Proper spacing gives each plant room to feed and improves airflow to prevent leaf diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ekome ni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná la kɛ shishifãi ahe he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa anyɛɔ ayeɔ niyenii yɛ tso lɛ mli tsu fɛɛ tsu mli, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ koni akaye tsei lɛ ahe helai.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines to climb up tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makudɔ sweet potato tso ko kɛya tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to capture direct sunlight through their leaves, which allows the plant to produce enough energy to grow large tubers underground while keeping leaves safe from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baa lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when plants suffer from extreme heat or dry soil, which prevents proper pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants from extreme sun helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi. ni tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ tsei ahebuu kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground when heavy rains soak the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: When soil stays flooded for too long, water drives away air in the ground, suffocating the roots and creating ideal conditions for rot-causing fungal diseases to attack the tubers before harvest.
ga: Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baa lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ dani akpa.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the undersides of the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by whiteflies. Clearing surrounding weeds and controlling tiny pests stops leaf curl from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Enɛ baaha baai lɛ abɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbɛɛɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so quickly after I pick them from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikpa amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continue to breathe and produce a natural ripening gas called ethylene even after harvest. If they are kept in tightly sealed bags or under heat, this gas builds up and causes them to soften, ripen too fast, and rot quickly.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ emuɔ ni ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni haa mɔ shwereɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ po. Kɛ akɛto kotoku ko ni atsĩ naa mli loo akɛwo la mli Gas nɛɛ buaa amɛhe naa ni ehaa amɛfeɔ blɛoo. Amɛshwereɔ oya tsɔ ni amɛgboɔ oya.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cassava so the tubers don't spoil in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, typically around 9 to 12 months. Leaving tubers in the ground too long after maturity makes them tough, woody, and susceptible to rot during heavy rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12. Kɛ́ ashi bulbs yɛ shikpɔŋ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee nɔ ni wa, ni amɛbaafee tsei, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to build green leaves. It can also mean the roots are drowned in waterlogged soil and cannot breathe to absorb nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni aná baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ afu shishifãi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. ni enyɛɛɛ emu koni ekɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii

english: Why do my pepper plants droop during the hot afternoon sun even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane latsaa mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Hot sun makes plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can suck it up from the soil. The plant droops on purpose to reduce its exposure to heat and save water, usually recovering when evening comes.
ga: Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛha hulutsoo aba shi ni amɛbu nu he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehaa ehe feɔ shoo kɛ́ gbɛkɛ shɛ

english: Why do my plantain leaves get scorched and turn brown at the edges during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves are very large and lose water quickly under direct hot sun and dry winds. When soil moisture drops, the leaf edges dry out and burn because the roots cannot supply water fast enough.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ dara waa ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shishi. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ba shi lɛ Baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aha nu oya bɔ ni sa.

english: Extreme heat, drought, or too much nitrogen fertilizer causes stress to the plant. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for survival rather than spending energy growing seeds and fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu dumɔwui kɛ aduawai

english: Why are my yam vines remaining short and weak even after I applied fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa beni mikɛ amɛ wo mli po lɛ?

english: If the soil underneath is too hard, compacted, or waterlogged, the roots cannot spread to drink water and absorb the fertilizer you provided. Yam roots need soft, loose soil to grow deep and feed the vine.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã koni amɛnu nu ni amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛhaa lɛ lɛ. Sweet potato shishifãi taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛye amɛbua wain tso lɛ.

english: Will planting my maize seeds very close together give me a bigger harvest from my field?
ga: Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛduɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ baaha maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: No, planting too close forces crops to compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin stalks and empty or small corn cobs, while proper spacing yields fewer but healthier, larger ears.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ abɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmãa bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli loo bibii baa. Yɛ be mli ni sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa baaha toi lɛ akafee agbo shi ehi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I grow cassava on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the specific soil nutrients that plant loves and allows pests and diseases targeting that crop to multiply in the soil, leading to smaller harvests each season.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ edaa lɛ baaha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tso lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ pɛ ajɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei anɔ lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nikpamɔ fioo pɛ baaba yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my food crops when the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to harsh conditions, so their roots are designed to absorb rain and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops, allowing them to overpower your planted seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, afee amɛshishifãi lɛ koni amɛŋɔ nugbɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii oya fe tsei ni amɛduɔ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛyeɔ dumɔwui ni oduɔ lɛ anɔ kunim.

english: Can I plant my oil palm nuts anywhere on my land, or does it prefer a specific type of soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu mu tsei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he fɛɛ he? Aloo esumɔɔ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko?

english: While oil palm trees are tough and can grow in many different places, they yield much more fruit when planted in deep, fertile soil that drains well and holds moisture easily.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ mu tsei lɛ wa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hei srɔtoi babaoo moŋ, shi amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli mlɛo lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land will make my palm trees thrive before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ baaha mi-palm tso lɛ aya hiɛ dani mabɔi dumɔ?

english: Land with rich dark topsoil, good water retention without flooding, and strong wild vegetation is usually a great spot for growing oil palms.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ. Eyɛ nu ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni nu afua bɛ mli. Ni bei pii lɛ, koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ji hei ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mu tsei akwɛmɔ.

english: If oil palms grow easily in my region, does that mean every plot of land will give me the same harvest?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mu tso lɛ dumɔ waaa yɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ baawo yibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, crop performance varies across different parts of the same town. Spots with deeper soil and better moisture will produce significantly higher yields than poorer patches of land.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ baasoro lɛ yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ anaa. of the same city Hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe hei ni shihilɛi lɛ ehiii kwraa lɛ.

english: Why are the palm trees on my neighbor's farm producing bigger fruit bunches than mine even though we planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii wuji fe mi nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔfee ekome kɛdu amɛ moŋ?

english: Different patches of soil contain different amounts of nutrients and water. Land that naturally favors palm trees provides the extra nourishment needed to produce larger fruit bunches.
ga: Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ esumɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ krokomɛi ni he hiaa koni aná aduawai akui wuji.

english: Why do some palm nuts sprout quickly while others take a long time to grow in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tɛŋ tsei komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Sprouting speed depends on the soil warmth, moisture level, and seed quality. Soil that stays consistently moist and well-aerated encourages seeds to germinate faster.
ga: Bɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ damɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu yɔɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: Will a palm tree planted in a shaded area grow as well as one planted in open land?
ga: Ani tɛŋ tso ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shade mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ tamɔ nɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, oil palms need full sunlight to generate energy for making leaves and heavy fruit bunches. Planting them in heavy shade will slow down their growth and reduce yield.
ga: Dabi, hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia mu tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛfee amɛbaai kɛ amɛyibii ni tsii lɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ fioo ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Is it better to plant palm nuts directly into the farm or raise them in a nursery first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaakwɛ tsei yɛ ŋmɔji amli tɛ̃ɛ loo aaatsɔse amɛ yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhei klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Raising palm nuts in a nursery allows you to protect young sprouts from pests and harsh weather, ensuring you only transfer the strongest seedlings to your main farm.
ga: Beans ni ooodu yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii ahe. Enɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ yaa oŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to space out palm trees when planting instead of putting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ esa akɛ wɔkɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ato he kroko kɛ́ wɔmiidu amɛ moŋ fe ni wɔkɛ amɛ baabɔ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures that each mature palm tree gets enough sunlight, air, and room for its roots to gather water and plant food without competing with neighboring trees.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tsei ni eda lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ shishifãi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbua nu naa ni ekɛduɔ niyenii ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ.

english: If my farm land is not the best for palm trees, what can I do to help them grow better?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ esaaa kɛha ŋmei tsei hu? Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni maye mabua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: You can improve poorer soil by adding organic manure, clearing weeds that steal nutrients, and placing dry leaves around the base of the trees to trap soil moisture.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ni okɛ baai ni egbi abɔle tso lɛ shishi koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Do oil palm trees need land right next to a stream to produce well, or can they survive on normal rainfall?
ga: Mu tsei he miihia shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ faa ko koni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ. Aloo ebaanyɛ ehi shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mli?

english: Oil palms can thrive on normal rainfall as long as the soil holds moisture well during dry periods, though land with a reliable water table nearby helps them produce heavily year-round.
ga: Mu tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mli. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu jɛɛhe ni bɛŋkɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ moŋ, shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow early in the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize plant is starving for nutrients, especially nitrogen, or the soil is too waterlogged. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the leaves stay green so the plant can produce large, healthy corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmãa ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing lots of tall green leaves but producing very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaŋŋ agboi babaoo shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or foliage growth isn't managed, the cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves instead of expanding its edible roots. Cassava needs potassium-rich soil and balanced feeding to push its energy downward into thick tubers.
ga: Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Kasava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ. Mohu ɔ, e haa sisifãhi nɛ a yeɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni potassium eyi mli obɔ kɛ niyenii ni ja he miihia cassava koni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ aba shi ni etsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off the trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from water stress, extreme heat, poor soil nutrients, or lack of pollination by small insects like midges. Planting temporary shade trees and maintaining soil moisture keeps the flowers healthy enough to form cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji nu he haomɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui. Aloo kooloi bibii tamɔ midges lɛ bɛ pollination. Tsei ni aduɔ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: This rot is caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, which often happens when soil moisture goes up and down unpredictably. Watering your plants regularly helps the roots absorb calcium steadily from the soil to protect the fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake yɛ gbɛi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ koni ebu aduawai lɛ ahe.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes allows every leaf to catch sunlight and air, which feeds the underground tuber and makes it grow larger.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ haa baa fɛɛ baa nine shɛɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ. ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii ni ehaa baai lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or beans makes my soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas have beneficial bacteria in their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When the crop is harvested, that natural fertilizer remains in the soil to feed the next plant you put there.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas yɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller and weaker when I plant seeds close together instead of spacing them out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe moŋ fe ni mikɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots fight underground for water and plant food, while their leaves shade each other from the sun. Proper spacing gives every plant its own room to feed and grow to full size.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ tsei aniyenii. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa tsu ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni edaa kɛyashɛɔ elɛɛmɔ he.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the underside of leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents leaf damage so the plant can produce good peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni akafite baa lɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmeii kpakpai.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches of fruit high off the ground. Planting suckers deep enough into the soil and supporting fruiting stems with wooden props prevents the heavy trees from uprooting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni aduawai babaoo hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ashishifãi kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni akɛ tsei fiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tsei ni tsii lɛ anaa koni amɛkajie amɛ.

english: Why does my lowland rice need standing water in the field during its early growth stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ aná nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ shishijee dalɛ beaŋ lɛ?

english: Shallow standing water smothers weeds that compete with rice for sunlight and soil nutrients, while keeping the soil consistently moist so young rice roots can easily soak up plant food.
ga: Nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni yɔɔ dioo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ he akaŋ lɛ kɛyaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmãa shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ tsei niyenii oya.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and weak roots that dry out easily. Planting them under fast-growing shade plants like plantains protects them from harsh sunlight and keeps the soil moist until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my old cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-kookoo tso momo lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches so sunlight and air can reach all parts of the tree. This prevents wet rot diseases like black pod from building up and helps the tree put its energy into producing bigger pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ashɛ tso lɛ hei fɛɛ. Koni helai ni fiteɔ tamɔ ŋmeii diji akabua amɛhe naa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which maize plants need to stay green and grow fast. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: What is causing small worms to eat holes in the middle of my maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm that hide inside the growing center of the plant. Checking your field early and spraying neem leaf extracts or recommended treatments helps protect your maize.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ dalɛ he lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofai krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu o-ŋmã lɛ he.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because the soil becomes waterlogged. Planting your cassava on top of raised earth mounds or ridges allows extra water to flow away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Yam leaves need to reach up high to catch maximum sunlight so they can feed the tuber growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot wet ground, which prevents leaf diseases and produces bigger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni awo sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la ashɛ enɔ bɔ ni aaanyɛ bɔni afee ni eha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai akabote hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ foliar hela naa ni ehaa sweet potatoes wuji baa.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baadu tsina loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it into the dirt. When planted near maize, they feed the soil naturally while giving you an extra food harvest from the same plot.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa Ebaaha niyenii kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaaha oná niyenii krokomɛi hu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small even when I plant on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be naa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and plant food directly from the soil that your crops need to grow. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehe hiaa ni otsei lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛ koni otsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heavy heat stress, sudden lack of water, or poor nutrients in the soil. Consistent watering and keeping the soil cool with mulch helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni faaa trukaa loo niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why must I wait for the major rains to settle well before putting seeds into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Dry or warm soil after just one light rain can scorch seeds or cause them to sprout and dry up quickly. Waiting for reliable, deep soil moisture gives seeds enough water to germinate and grow strong roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Be kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ ashã loo eha amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi oya. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni mli kwɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni eye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: What is 2-month rice, and can it really mature that fast on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmãa ni eye nyɔji 2 ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eda oya nakai yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: 2-month or early-maturing rice varieties are specially bred crops that complete their growth cycle in about 60 to 70 days. They are ideal for areas with short rain seasons because they yield quickly before dry weather sets in.
ga: Omɔ henɔi ni yeɔ nyɔji enyɔ loo ni shwereɔ mra lɛ ji ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛi ni amɛdalɛ be lɛ gbeɔ naa yɛ aaafee gbii 60 kɛyashi 70 mli. Amɛhi jogbaŋŋ kɛha hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli ejaakɛ amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya dani kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ.

english: Why do many farmers in my area wait until September to harvest their crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ mɛɔ kɛyashiɔ September dani amɛkpaa amɛnibii lɛ?

english: September usually marks the tail end of the main rainy season. Harvesting then allows crops to reach full maturity with sufficient rain while giving farmers clear, drier days to dry their harvest safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, September ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ naagbee. Nikpamɔ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa okwaafoi lɛ naa gbii babaoo ni hulu tsoɔ waa, ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi koni amɛgbi amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Can I plant a new crop immediately after harvesting my field in September?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ September mli lɛ?

english: Yes, you can plant immediately after a September harvest if you choose fast-growing varieties like short-duration rice or cowpeas that can use the remaining soil moisture from the late rains.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu amɛ yɛ September ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛji ohala ŋmeii srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa ni yeɔ be kuku loo tsina ŋmãa lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni eshwɛ ni jɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why are some farmers afraid to harvest their crops earlier in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi sheɔ gbeyei akɛ amɛbaakpa amɛnibii lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Farmers often fear harvesting too early because damp weather can cause harvested grains to rot or mold quickly before they can be properly dried and sold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi sheɔ nikpamɔ mra tsɔ gbeyei. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ agbo oya loo amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ dani agbi amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Is it possible for me to get two rice harvests from the same field in one year?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ makpa ŋmãa shii enyɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ afi kome mli?

english: Yes, by planting quick-maturing varieties (like 2-month agro-rice) right after your first harvest, you can complete two full crop cycles within a single rainy season.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni daa oya (tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ nyɔji 2) ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ ni yeɔ emuu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome mli.

english: How do short-season crops help me handle irregular rainfall patterns?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni matsu nugbɔshiimɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ he nii?

english: Short-season crops need less total rainfall over time. Because they grow so fast, they escape late-season droughts that usually destroy late-maturing traditional crops.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ biɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kwraa yɛ be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraa oya waa. No hewɔ lɛ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ ni bei pii lɛ efiteɔ blema ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: What happens if I panic and harvest my crops before they fully mature?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mihe fee mi yaa ni mikpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ hu?

english: Harvesting prematurely leaves you with smaller, lighter grains that carry high moisture. This reduces your overall yield weight and makes the crop spoil faster in storage.
ga: Kɛ́ okpa mra lɛ, ebaaha oná dumɔwui bibii ni mli tseee ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ tsiimɔ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Should I plant quick-maturing seeds even if none of my neighbors are doing it?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra kɛji mikutsoŋbii lɛ efeee nakai po?

english: Yes, being the first to adopt fast-maturing seeds can yield good results, but keep an eye out for birds and pests, as early-maturing crops in a single field can attract hungry wildlife if surrounding farms aren't ready yet.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko ji mɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni kɛ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ ba lɛ, ebaanyɛ ewo yibii kpakpai. Shi kwɛmɔ okpoi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baanyɛ agbala koo mli kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ kɛji ŋmɔji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ efeko klalo.

english: Does my soil still have enough strength to nourish a new crop right after a harvest?
ga: Ani mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa lolo bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei anɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The soil retains moisture, but nutrients are often depleted by the crop you just harvested. Adding organic compost or the right fertilizer before your second planting ensures the new crop grows strong.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni okpa amrɔ nɛɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he dani adu nɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ, ebaawo ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: What type of crops should I put in the ground if the dry season is coming soon?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ miibɛŋkɛ?

english: You should plant short-duration crops—such as quick-maturing rice, vegetables, or early beans—that complete their life cycle in 60 days or fewer before the rains completely stop.
ga: Esa akɛ odu nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ omɔ, aduawai, loo ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Egbeɔ ewala shihilɛ naa yɛ gbii 60 loo nɔ ni shɛɛɛ nakai mli dani nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ kwraa.

english: Why do my crops still get ruined by pests even after I spray chemicals on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ nɔ moŋ?

english: Chemicals work best when pests or sicknesses are just starting or actively feeding. If you wait until the damage is already severe or spray after the problem has passed, the chemicals cannot reverse the crop destruction.
ga: Tsofai tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ kooloi loo helai miije shishi kɛkɛ loo amɛmiiye nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji omɛ kɛyashi nɔ ni efite lɛ mli wa momo loo okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ beni naagba lɛ eho lɛ, Chemicals nyɛŋ aku sɛɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do fall armyworms suddenly appear in huge numbers on my farm overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ asraafoi amli ŋmeii babaoo je kpo trukaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔɔŋ kome mli lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm moths lay hundreds of eggs under leaves in a single night. Once they hatch in warm weather, the tiny caterpillars feed rapidly, making it seem like an overnight invasion.
ga: Moth ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ baai ashishi yɛ gbɛkɛ kome mli. Kɛ́ amɛfɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ nii oya. Ehaa efeɔ tamɔ shwane kome mli tutuamɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the field has too much standing water, which prevents crop roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ. Enɛ haaa tso shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when plants suffer from drought, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil moist and shaded helps save the blossoms.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei kpɛɔ hɔmɔ naa loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to apply chemical fertilizer when the farm soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo mli lɛ? Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli egbi kwraa, no hewɔ lɛ ehiii kɛha mi?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve into a form roots can drink. Putting fertilizer on dry ground can burn and kill the plant roots, wasting your investment.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ nɔ ko ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei shishifãi. ni kɛ shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fitemɔ baa

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and provide large leaf canopy umbrellas that shade cocoa plants and keep the soil moist during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛhaa baai agbo ko ni haa kookoo tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater collects and stays around them for too long without draining. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges lets excess water flow away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu bua amɛhe naa ni ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ efooo Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow so much faster than my main crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that adapt quickly to consume rainwater and soil food before your crops can. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get the food they need to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ ni etsake amɛhe oya koni amɛye nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aye. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do the seeds I save from my harvested maize yield less corn when I replant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-ŋmãa yibiiwoo lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo kɛji mikɛdu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Modern hybrid seeds are bred for maximum harvest only in their first planting. Saving and replanting those seeds breaks their special vigor, resulting in smaller cobs and weaker plants.
ga: Akwɛɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ koni akɛkpa nii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛto ni adu ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ yɔɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why should I cut off extra leaves and branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai kɛ niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing extra side branches and leaves forces the plant to send its water and food energy into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of wasting energy on excess leaves.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ kɛ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni daraa lɛ ahe nii moŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: How do I know if my land has the right soil for growing healthy cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛha kookoo tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛmɔ?

english: Good cocoa soil is deep, soft, rich in organic matter (dark soil), and drains water well so that roots do not rot during heavy rains while still holding enough moisture during dry spells.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo (shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ), ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli, yɛ be mli ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and burn when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or bananas planted nearby to protect them until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo banana ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: When planted too close, cocoa trees compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to tall, weak trees that yield fewer pods and allow diseases to spread easily.
ga: Kɛ adu Cocoa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ, ni ehaa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo.

english: How many years can a cocoa tree keep producing good yield before it gets too old?
ga: Afii enyiɛ cacao tso baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai dani egbɔ tsɔ?

english: With good maintenance, soil care, and pruning, a cocoa tree can produce abundant cocoa pods for 25 to 30 years or more, making it a reliable long-term investment for a farm family.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Cacao tsei baanyɛ awo cocoa ŋmeii babaoo afii 25 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Enɛ haa efeɔ shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛhaa ŋmɔ mli wekui.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off the water sprouts and extra branches on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafo cacao tso lɛ kɛ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning extra branches and water sprouts (chupons) allows air and sunlight to move freely through the tree canopy, which reduces fungal diseases and ensures tree energy goes into forming pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mli dumɔwui ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ nu mli dumɔwui (chupon) ni fata he lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi, ni ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ feɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: How does clearing weeds regularly around my cocoa trees help them grow better?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Te cacao tsei ni akwɛɔ amɛ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal vital soil nutrients, water, and space from your cocoa trees. Clearing them ensures your cocoa tree gets full access to plant food and moisture.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ he ko ni yɔɔ o-cocoa tsei lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha o-cacao tsei lɛ aná tsei niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa.

english: Why do so many of the small flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii bibii Tsei babaoo ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce many more flowers than they can support. Many flowers drop because they were not pollinated by tiny insects (midges), or because the tree is saving energy during dry or low-nutrient periods.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ kooloi bibii (teŋgbɛ nibii) kɛ amɛhe wooo mli loo ejaakɛ tsei lɛ toɔ hewalɛ he yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa lɛ.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and rot during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain and high humidity cause a fungal disease called Black Pod to spread. The fungus thrives in wet, dark conditions, especially on trees with dense foliage that lack proper sunlight.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Fungus lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ duŋ mli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ tsei ni baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni hulu la ni sa bɛ amɛhe lɛ anɔ.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees during the dry Harmattan season, and how do they survive it?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli ni te amɛbaafee tɛŋŋ amɛhi shi?

english: During Harmattan, cocoa trees naturally drop some of their leaves to reduce water loss. They conserve energy and rest until the rains return, though proper watering or mulching helps them survive severe dry spells.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ekomɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua amɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa bei amli moŋ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa tree is lacking proper food or nutrients in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii loo niyenii ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Nutrient-deficient trees show clear signs such as pale green or yellowing leaves, slow growth, small or deformed pods, and premature pod dropping.
ga: Tsei ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa lɛ baajie okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛdaraa blɛoo, kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ni efite. ni ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya

english: Why do some of my mango trees produce lots of fruit while others right next to them produce almost nothing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni mango tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ? Ani aduawai ko kwraa bɛ?

english: Fruit trees can vary in yield due to differences in age, tree health, pollination success, or soil nutrient levels. Applying compost or manure around the base and pruning shaded inner branches helps encourage steady fruit production across all your trees.
ga: Tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ baanyɛ afee srɔtoi yɛ afii ni amɛye lɛ hewɔ. tso hewalɛnamɔ Pollination omanyeyeli loo niyenii mli hewalɛ srɔtoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle he lɛ atsu nii Niji ni yɔɔ mligbɛ ni yɔɔ shade lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ baaye abua otso lɛ ni ewo yibii pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers during periods of severe afternoon heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil moist by mulching with dry grass helps keep root temperatures steady so flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ amli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi daa bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee aduawai.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce hundreds of tiny flowers, but only a few turn into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi bibii ohai abɔ, shi amɛteŋ fioo pɛ tsɔɔ cacao ŋmɔji ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support into full pods. Tiny beneficial insects called midges must pollinate the flowers, and keeping damp leaf litter under the trees creates a good habitat for midges to do their job.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli. ŋmeii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ Esa akɛ nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii. Ni baai ni mli efɔ ni akɛtoɔ tsei ashishi lɛ haa amɛnáa shihilɛhe kpakpa kɛha amɛnitsumɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my citrus trees drop a lot of small young fruits shortly after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii babaoo beni efɔ fɔfɔi sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Citrus trees naturally shed young fruits if they do not have enough water or nutrients to grow them all to maturity. Watering the trees during dry spells right after flowering helps prevent excessive fruit drop.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ baawo yibii bibii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdara kɛyashɛ shweremɔ he. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ akagbee shi fe nine.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize crop turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Applying manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer near the roots helps green up the leaves and boosts crop development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ebaaha tsei lɛ adara.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing tall and thin instead of bushy, with very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni efeɔ mlɛo yɛ bushy najiaŋ ni eyɛ pepper fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants grow tall and weak when they are overcrowded or shaded because they are stretching to find sunlight. Planting them with proper spacing in open, sunny areas encourages bushy growth and higher pepper yields.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛji amɛyi obɔ kɛ hulu loo amɛyɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ esa akɛ amɛkpã amɛhe kɛya hulu lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni akɛ gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ he ko ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ baawo jwɛi shweremɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up and droop in the hot afternoon even when the soil is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Plantains have huge leaves that lose water rapidly in intense sunlight, so they curl slightly to protect themselves from heat stress. As long as the soil has moisture, they usually bounce back once temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai wuji ni kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ, nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, efoɔ ehe fioo koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu sumɔɔ ni ekɛ ehe aku sɛɛ aba kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants give me small, weak cobs when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei woɔ ŋmãa bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the roots compete aggressively for water, soil food, and light. Spacing seeds out properly gives every plant enough resources to grow large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ la he akaŋ. Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: How do I know if my cassava tubers are ready underground when the stem and leaves look full and green?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaaya shikpɔŋ shishi? Beni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kɛ baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ eŋɔli?

english: Very leafy cassava stems do not always mean large tubers underneath, as high soil nitrogen causes leaf growth instead of root development. Checking the variety's recommended maturity time (usually 9 to 12 months) and carefully digging up one test plant is the best way to inspect tuber size.
ga: Kasava tso ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ eyɛ tuber agbo ko yɛ shishigbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Be ni atsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ shwereɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ (bei pii lɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12) kɛ tsei ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ lɛ ni akwɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ bulb lɛ dalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger on my land than the actual crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to steal food and water from the soil far quicker than farm crops. Clearing weeds early in the season gives your main crop a head start to capture the sunlight and nutrients it needs.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni atsake amɛ koni amɛye niyenii kɛ nu ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he akaŋ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ haa onibii titri lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ mlimɔ mli.

english: How can I keep my farm soil wet during the hot dry season so I do not have to carry heavy water buckets every day?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli? Bɔni afee ni ehe akahi ni okɛ tsɔne ni tsiimɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ awo ohe daa gbi.

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dry grass, leaves, or palm fronds (called mulching) acts like a blanket. It blocks direct sunlight from drying out the dirt, keeping the soil cool and moist for much longer so you spend less time and energy watering.
ga: Ni akɛhaa he ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ he Nibii ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmei baai ni egbi duɔ. (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni ehaaa muji akagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ be kɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ shwieɔ nu nɔ.

english: Why does planting my crops in straight rows make my work less tiring than scattering seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haaa mɔ he ajɔ lɛ fe dumɔwui ni agbɛɔ ashwãa he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: When crops are in straight lines, it creates clear pathways. This allows you to quickly clear weeds using a hoe without worrying about accidentally cutting down your crops, saving you hours of exhausting hand work.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ, ebaaha gbɛ ni mli ka shi faŋŋ Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ ŋmei jieɔ jwɛi oya ni ohaooo akɛ obaafo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ oshara mli. Enɛ haaa okɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo atsu nii kɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with big green leaves, but produce very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji Shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen (often from using the wrong fertilizer), the plant puts all its energy into making leafy branches up top instead of sending energy down to build big tubers in the soil.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ (Bei pii lɛ, ejɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli) Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ niji kɛ baai ni yaa ŋwɛi. Mohu ɔ, a haa he wami kɛ baa si konɛ e pee bulb nguahi ngɛ zugba a mi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before the peppers can even grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ ada lɛ?

english: When the plant is stressed by very hot afternoons or dry soil, it gets weak and drops its flowers to save its own life, because producing fruit takes extra energy that it cannot spare.
ga: Kɛji tsei miihao kɛjɛ shwane ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔii baashwie shi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, aduawai afeemɔ biɔ hewalɛ kroko ni anyɛɛɛ akɛto he.

english: Why do my maize crops get smaller harvests when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close fight with each other underground for soil food and water. Because no single plant gets enough nutrients, all of them end up growing small, weak cobs.
ga: Tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baawu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛkɛ lɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ daa ni etsɔ ŋmei bibioo ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my soil grow weaker crops if I plant maize on the exact same plot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ baa shi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Maize eats up the exact same nutrients from the dirt every season. If you do not rotate with crops like peanuts or beans, which put food back into the soil, the ground gets exhausted and cannot support healthy growth.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeee. ni kɛ niyenii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛɛɛ eye ebua shweremɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and burn when I clear away all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Big trees act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool air it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi Tsei wuji tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale and yellow after heavy, continuous rain flooding the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ eha ŋmɔji lɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Excess rain washes away important plant food (nutrients) deep into the ground where roots cannot reach, and waterlogged soil stops roots from breathing, causing the leaves to turn yellow from starvation.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ hoɔ tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa (nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ) lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Ni sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ mumɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ hewɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in the afternoon heat even when the ground feels slightly wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo moŋ lɛ?

english: In intense midday heat, water evaporates out of the tomato leaves faster than the roots can drink it from the dirt. The plant temporarily droops to protect itself, but usually recovers when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Nu ni jɛɔ tomato baai amli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei baagbee shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he. Shi bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ, amɛhe jɔɔ amɛ.

english: Why do weeds sprout up and grow so much faster than my crops right after I clear my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are already sleeping deep in the soil from previous seasons. The moment you clear the land and expose the dirt to sunlight, those wild seeds wake up and grow rapidly before your crop seeds can even catch up.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui miiwɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛjɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. Kɛji ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo hulu la mli pɛ kɛkɛ, Nakai koo mli dumɔwui lɛ baate shi ni amɛdara oya dani odumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when they are exposed to full direct sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and small root systems that cannot handle intense heat. They need shade crops like plantains or tree canopies to block direct sunlight, keep the soil cool, and prevent the leaves from drying out while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ koni amɛtsi hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, ni amɛtsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why are small worms eating the center whorl leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋ lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which prefer the sweet, tender leaves growing at the stem's core. Detecting them early allows you to use appropriate biological or chemical controls before they destroy the growing tip of the maize.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ baai ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. mra mli ni anaa Enɛ baaha okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni sa atsu nii dani okpãtã ŋmãa lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my green maize plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, a crucial nutrient for leaf growth. The plant starves its older leaves to feed newer top growth, signaling that your soil needs compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Tso lɛ baagbe baai ni egbɔ lɛ hɔmɔ koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my crops with dry cassava leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo he ni ebɔle he lɛ mli lɛ? Nibii ni akɛ ŋmei baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ewo mli?

english: Covering soil with organic material (mulching) acts like a blanket that keeps soil cool, stops moisture from evaporating quickly in the heat, suppresses weed growth, and eventually decays to fertilize your land.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli (mulch) ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni yɛ naagbee lɛ efiteɔ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize in the exact same plot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores soil nitrogen and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, will I get a larger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too closely actually reduces your total yield because crops must compete for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water. Proper spacing gives each crop enough room and light to grow big, healthy fruit or tubers.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ baa shi. Akɛni esa akɛ tsei atswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, hulu la, kɛ nu mli hewɔ lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa gbɛ kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ aduawai loo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops right after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with deep roots that adapt quickly to local conditions and pull moisture and nutrients instantly. They compete directly with cultivated crops, which is why early weeding is critical after heavy rains.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe oya kɛyaa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shihilɛi amli. ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ baa amrɔ nɔŋŋ Amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛduɔ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off without making any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers often drop off due to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. When the plant gets stressed, it sheds its flowers to conserve energy for basic survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ kɛji tsei lɛ miihao Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛto hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully grown underground without digging all of them up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni okɛ amɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava plants signal maturity—usually between 9 to 12 months depending on the variety—when the lower foliage turns yellow and falls off, and small cracks appear on the soil surface near the stem base as expanding roots push the earth upward.
ga: Cassava tsei kɛ dalɛ he okadii tsuɔ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ, ni enɛ damɔ tso lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi ni ŋmeii bibii komɛi ba Amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi be mli ni shishifãi ni eda lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why is it better to apply water directly to the soil around the plant instead of pouring it over the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ nu baatsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni akɛaafɔse baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Plant roots swallow nutrients and water from the soil, not through leaves. Wetting leaf surfaces frequently creates warm, moist environments that encourage fungal leaf diseases and rot, while root watering ensures the plant stays hydrated safely.
ga: Tse shishifãi lɛ heɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, shi jeee baai lɛ. Baai ni efɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔɔ, ni mli ejɔ baa. Enɛ woɔ fungal leaf hela kɛ fitemɔ he hewalɛ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly into tubes when the sun gets very hot at midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense to conserve water. By rolling up, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to direct sunlight and wind, which slows down water loss during the dry hours of the day.
ga: Abɛi baai ni abɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni haaa nu akafite. kɛtsɔ Tsei ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fioo yɛ gbi lɛ mli be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop almost all their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fite yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during Harmattan to save moisture and stay alive. The plant enters a resting state while the roots remain healthy underground, and it will quickly grow fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan beaŋ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhi wala mli. Tso lɛ boteɔ shihilɛ ni mli wa mli yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Ni baai heei lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without growing into any fruits when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when extreme heat stresses the plant, preventing proper pollination. When temperature or moisture levels swing too drastically, the plant sheds its flowers to preserve its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ha tsei lɛ miihao. Tsi pollination naa jogbaŋŋ Kɛji hulutsoo loo hulutsoo be lɛ tsake waa tsɔ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhi shi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily burn under strong direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide living shade umbrellas that keep the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni kookoo bibii lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of just spreading across the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves toward the sun, allowing them to capture light better and make more food for growing big tubers underground. It also keeps leaves off damp soil, reducing fungal diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛmɔɔ la jogbaŋŋ. ni afee niyenii babaoo kɛha bulb agboi ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Etsiɔ baai hu anaa koni amɛkaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ aba shi

english: Why should I cut away extra young shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Jiemɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Multiple shoots (suckers) fight with the main tree for soil nutrients, water, and light. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant gets enough food to yield a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi (shishifãi) ​​babaoo kɛ tso titri lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu, kɛ la mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow in a V-shape while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means the soil is low in nitrogen. The plant starves from below, moving stored nitrogen from older bottom leaves up to feed the new growth and forming corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Hɔmɔ baaye tso lɛ kɛjɛ shishi. Ejieɔ nitrogen ni ato lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii ni efee ŋmãa toi.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my farm make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that work with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decay, they release this free natural fertilizer into the soil.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ fite lɛ, amɛjieɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it bad to apply fertilizer when my farm soil is completely dry or during heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli beni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbi kwraa loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Applying chemical fertilizer to dry soil can burn plant roots because there is no water to dissolve it safely. Conversely, heavy rain washes away the fertilizer into gutters before the crop's roots can absorb it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ejaakɛ nu bɛ ni baaha amɛshwie shi shweshweeshwe. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii awo nubu mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling upward and looking wrinkled and tiny at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛji bibii yɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on young leaves, or by a plant virus carried by whiteflies that damages normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. ni fiteɔ dalɛ ni sa lɛ

english: Why are my crops dying or turning yellow when I plant on land near old galamsey sites?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboiɔ loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ Old Galamsey lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Illegal mining (galamsey) leaves behind dangerous heavy metals and chemicals in the soil. These toxic substances damage crop roots, preventing them from taking up the water and nutrients the plants need to stay green and healthy.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ (galamsey) lɛ haa dade ni tsii kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ tsofai fɔji nɛɛ fiteɔ tsei shishifãi. Enɛ haaa amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Is it safe for my family to eat vegetables grown on land where people used to dig for gold?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ miweku lɛ baaye aduawai ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni be ko ni eho lɛ atsaa shika tsuru yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: It can be risky. Plants can absorb heavy metals from polluted mining soil into their leaves, stems, and fruits. Eating these crops over time can cause health problems, so polluted soil needs testing or treatment before growing food crops.
ga: Ebaanyɛ efee oshara. Tsei baanyɛ ajie dade ni tsii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli kɛya amɛbaai, amɛshishifãi, kɛ amɛyibii amli. Kɛ́ aye nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai aba. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ aka shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ akwɛ loo atsu he nii dani adu niyenii.

english: Can I wash away bad chemicals and metals left in my farmland soil by flooding it with clean water?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafo tsofai kɛ dade gbohii ni eshwɛ yɛ mi okwaayeli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni mli tse ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, heavy metals stick tightly to soil particles and do not easily wash away with water. Removing them requires special soil treatments, organic matter, or planting specific non-food crops that draw out toxins over several seasons.
ga: Dabi, dade ni tsii lɛ kpɛtɛɔ sũ mli nibii bibii ahe waa. ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ nu afɔ he mlɛo Amɛjiemɔ biɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii krɛdɛɛi, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, loo tsei ni jeee niyenii ni jieɔ tsofai fɔji kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ bei babaoo mli lɛ adumɔ.

english: If my soil has chemicals from illegal mining, will putting extra fertilizer make my crops grow normally?
ga: Kɛji tsofai ni jɛɔ shika tsuru ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ mli yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ani ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaha mitsei lɛ adara bɔ ni sa?

english: Fertilizer gives plants food, but it cannot destroy or remove heavy metals. While fertilizer might help the plant grow a bit, the crop will still absorb the poisonous chemicals from the ground.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii. Shi enyɛŋ efite loo ejie dade ni tsii. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye abua tsei lɛ fioo moŋ, shi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baajie tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo.

english: How do heavy metals in the ground actually stop my maize from producing good ears?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni dade ni tsii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ atsĩ ŋmãa naa koni ekawo toi kpakpai?

english: Heavy metals act like poison to the plant's internal veins. Even if the plant gets sunlight and rain, the damaged internal channels cannot transport food up to form healthy maize ears.
ga: Dade ni tsii tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofai fɔji yɛ tsei amli fãji lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ nine shɛɔ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɔ po Shi emli gbɛi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ ekɛ niyenii aya koni ekɛfee ŋmãa toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has been damaged by mining chemicals before I clear the land for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofai ni jɛɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔ mli lɛ efite shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Dani abaajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Look out for warning signs like oily film floating on water puddles, hard grayish crusts on top of the soil, patches where weeds refuse to grow, or unusual chemical smells coming from the dirt.
ga: Taomɔ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii, tamɔ sini ko ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ mu ni hoɔ yɛ nu ŋshɔi lɛ anɔ. Tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa yɛ shikpɔŋ He ni jwɛi kpooɔ akɛ amɛakwɛ̃ loo tsofai ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni jɛɔ muji mli

english: Why are the roots of my cassava rotting and failing to spread in my farm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite ni amɛgbɛɛɛ amɛshwãaa yɛ tsɛnsi sũ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil contains high levels of chemicals or heavy metals, the toxic ground burns delicate young root tips as soon as they try to push through the dirt, causing them to turn black and rot instead of growing big.
ga: Be mli ni tsofai loo dade ni tsii babaoo yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. He ni poison yɔɔ lɛ baashã shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ pɛ kɛji amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa etsɔɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ agbo.

english: Why do crops grow differently on land in the savannah region compared to forest areas in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ savannah kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ akɛto koo mli shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ he lɛ?
