english: Savannah soils have different mineral compositions, higher heat exposure, and less natural shade. Plants in the savannah need soil rich in organic matter to hold water and nutrients around their roots.
ga: Savannah shikpɔji lɛ yɛ sũ mli nibii srɔtoi. Eyɛ dɔlɛ ni nɔ kwɔ ni ebɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo babaoo. Savannah tsei lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli eyi mli obɔ lɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni ebɔle amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ amli.

english: Can I use water from a nearby river that was used for gold washing to water my vegetable garden?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ faa ni bɛŋkɛ ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shika tsuru he lɛ mli lɛ awo mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu?

english: No, water from galamsey sites is often filled with heavy metals and chemicals. Watering your vegetables with it will transfer those poisons straight into the plants and poison your farm soil.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ, dade ni tsii kɛ tsofai eyiɔ galamsey nu lɛ mli obɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ aduawai amli lɛ kɛ nakai tsofai fɔji lɛ yaa tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. ni okɛ poison awo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Are there any crops I can safely grow on soil that has heavy metal chemicals in it?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ madu shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dade tsofai ni tsii yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: It is safest to grow non-food crops like bamboo, cotton, or timber trees on contaminated land. These plants can grow without putting heavy metals into human food sources.
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nibii ni jeee niyenii tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, loo tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ewo muji nɔ? Tsei nɛɛ baanyɛ adara ni akɛ dade ni tsii fataaa adesai aniyenii he.

english: How can I tell when my plantains are mature enough to be cut?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-plantains lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafolɔ?

english: Plantains are mature when the sharp, flat edges on the individual fruits become rounded and plump. You do not need to wait for them to turn yellow on the plant; harvesting them while green and full ensures they stay firm for sale.
ga: Plantains lɛ eda kɛji akɛ aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehe ehiaaa ni omɛ ni tsei lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Nikpamɔ be mli ni jwɛi lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo lɛ haa jarayeli yaa nɔ daa.

english: How do I keep my plantains fresh and green after cutting them so they don't spoil on the way to market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-plantains lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni mifo amɛ sɛɛ? Bɔni afee ni ekafite yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Keep harvested plantain bunches in a cool, shaded area away from direct sunlight and cover them with broad leaves. Avoid bruising or dropping the bunches during handling, as injuries make the fruit ripen and rot quickly.
ga: Kɛ plantain tsei ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni shade yɔɔ. He ni hulu la shɛɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni baai ni mli kwɔ ehà nɔ Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ loo shigbeemɔ he beni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, pilamɔ lɛ baaha aduawai lɛ akwɔ ni amɛgboi oya.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over when the fruit bunch gets big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches, especially in high winds. You can protect them by propping up the main stem with a strong bamboo pole or wooden fork braced against the stem.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii lɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. Obaanyɛ obu amɛhe kɛtsɔ ŋmei tso ni wa loo tso ni akɛfee ŋmei ni fiɔ ŋmei titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the plantain bunches from my farm very small compared to other farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains ni jɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ faaa kwraa kɛ akɛto ŋmɔji krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Small bunches usually happen when the soil lacks organic matter or nutrients like potassium, or when too many shoots are growing from one root. Removing extra shoots and applying poultry manure around the base helps the plant grow larger bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo niyenii, tamɔ potassium, loo kɛji ŋmeii babaoo jɛ shishifã kome mli kwɛ̃. Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni akɛ kooloi ashishifãi woɔ he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni etsɔ jwɛi agbo.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up quickly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have large leaves that lose water very fast in hot weather. Laying dry weeds, crop leaves, or straw around the base of the plant creates a blanket that traps soil moisture and protects the roots from heat.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai agboi ni nu fiteɔ oya waa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, tsei ahe baai, loo jwɛi wo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he.

english: How do I choose the right plantain shoots to plant for a strong farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni sa kɛha dumɔ koni miŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Look for 'sword suckers'—young shoots that have narrow, blade-like leaves and a broad stem base at the soil level. Avoid shoots with wide, broad leaves because they tend to grow into weak plants with poor yields.
ga: Taomɔ ‘sword shoots’, ni ji tsei bibii ni baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ ŋmei kɛ shishigbɛ ni da yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ ahe ejaakɛ amɛfɔɔ dalɛ ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni wooo yibii fioo.

english: Space your plantain suckers about 3 meters (10 feet) apart in straight rows. Planting them too close together causes them to shade each other and compete for water, resulting in thin stems and small fruits.
ga: Okɛ plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ato he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 (naji 10) yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛhe naa ni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu he. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ aduawai bibii baa.

english: Why do I see black spots on my plantain leaves that make the whole leaf wither and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii diji yɛ plantain baai anɔ ni haa baai lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: This is a common fungal leaf disease spread by moisture and wind. Cut off and burn damaged leaves away from the farm to stop the fungus from spreading to healthy plants.
ga: Enɛ ji fungal leaf hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kpãa ni oshã baai ni efite kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ koni ŋmei lɛ akagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: What causes the roots of my young plantain plants to rot and turn soft underground?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi plantains bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miifite ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: This is usually caused by tiny worms called nematodes or stem borers living in the soil. Cleaning and trimming the outer skin of suckers before planting, or dipping them briefly in hot water, kills these pests before they enter your soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Tsumɔ ni ofolɔ tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ dani odu loo okɛwo nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli fioo. Ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Can I plant crops like maize or vegetables in the same field with my young plantains?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi-plantains bibii lɛ?

english: Yes, during the first year while the plantains are small, intercropping with fast-growing crops like maize, pepper, or beans is beneficial. It suppresses weeds and provides food while the plantains grow to form a canopy.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli be mli ni plantains lɛ ji bibii Nibii ni akɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa hu duɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa ni ehaa niyenii yɛ be mli ni plantains lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmei.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Planting shade trees or plantains nearby protects them until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which the plant needs to stay green and healthy. Adding manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps fix this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why does planting beans on my farm make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmeii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the bean plants are harvested, that extra nitrogen stays in the soil and feeds the next crop naturally.
ga: Beans kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Beni akpaa ŋmeii tsei lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Cassava roots rot when trapped in standing water because wet, heavy soil blocks air from reaching the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni tsii lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during strong winds when they start carrying fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli kɛ́ ebɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that struggle to hold up the heavy weight of full bunches. Supporting the stem with a strong wooden fork or bamboo pole prevents them from tipping over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi jwɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ muji ni tsii lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei ni mli wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekagbee shi.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves into the direct sunlight to produce food energy. Staking the vines ensures the plant can build large, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ aya hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná niyenii hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ afee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking juice from under the leaves. Spraying with neem oil solution or soapy water helps clear them off.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efɔ he.

english: Why do tiny insects destroy my cowpea flowers right as they open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifite mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛfɔ̃ pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers attract pests like thrips because of their sweet nectar. Applying a safe organic or recommended protective spray just before flowering keeps insects away so the pods can form.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ gbalaa kooloi tamɔ thrips yɛ amɛ wuo ni ŋɔɔ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa ni tsiɔ hela naa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ awo mli dani efɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akabote mli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ afee.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their yellow flowers without growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when it gets extremely hot or when wind and insects fail to shake the pollen inside the flower. Keeping the soil evenly moist and allowing airflow helps the fruit set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba amɛnɔ loo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ atswa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he.

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer nutrients, and sunlight directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures all the goodness in the soil goes straight into growing your crops instead.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ koni kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya tɛ̃ɛ kɛya oŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ nɔ moŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees scorching and turning brown during the sunny months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves are tender and burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a canopy that filters the sunlight, keeps the air cool, and retains moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for crops. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant moves whatever nutrients it has left from its bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii Kɛji nitrogen faaa Abɛi tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do older farmers tell me to plant cowpeas or beans in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ midu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans have special bacteria in their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. This naturally enriches the soil with food that neighboring crops like maize can use to grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ niyenii ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why shouldn't I place chemical fertilizer directly touching the stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ tsei ahe tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated salts that draw moisture out of the plant tissue when placed directly on the stem, causing chemical burns. Placing fertilizer a few inches away allows the spreading root system to safely absorb the nutrients without damaging the stem.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ fãji amli kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa tsofai shãa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko lɛ, ehaa shishifã ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ nyɛɔ eŋɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ shweshweeshwe ni efiteee tso lɛ shishifã lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when the rainy season gets heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe, but heavy rains in flat, compact soil cause water logging. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away, keeping the roots safe from rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Shi nugbɔ ni naa wa nɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ lɛ nɔ, ni eha nu lɛ tsĩ shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite

english: Extreme heat and dry winds during periods like the Harmattan stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers to save energy and survive. Providing consistent water and light shade during heatwaves helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi yɛ bei tamɔ Harmattan tomato mli lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ feɔ basaa. Enɛ haa amɛshiɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi. Nu kɛ hulutsoo ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ latsaa be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why are there small caterpillars chewing ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the central funnel (whorl) of the maize plant to feed on tender new leaves. Catching them early and applying safe control measures protects the growing point of the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi (rings) lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛbaakwɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu he ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ lɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or whiteflies sucking the sap from under the leaves and transmitting viruses. Controlling these insect pests prevents leaf distortion and keeps the plant growing healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ ashishi nu lɛ ni amɛhaa hela lɛ baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ tsiɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni ehaa tsei lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to cut tall sticks and stake my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni miduɔ wain tsei ni ŋɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce food for the underground tubers through their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground so leaves receive full sunlight and good airflow, preventing disease and resulting in larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ niyenii amɛhaa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha hulu la ni fa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli, ni ekɛtsiɔ helai anaa ni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why should I cut off the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow around one plantain stool creates competition for soil nutrients, light, and water. Leaving only one main stem and one small successor shoot ensures the main plant produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Ha ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ yɛ ehe. Plantain kome Enɛ haa akaŋshii baa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, la kɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ ajie tso titri kome kɛ tso bibioo kome pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from last year's harvest yield smaller maize than the original seed I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmãa bibii fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds bought from agrodealers are bred for high yield in their first generation. When you save seeds from that harvest to plant again, they lose their hybrid strength, resulting in weaker plants and smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Beni ohereɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ koni oyadu ekoŋŋ lɛ. Nakai dumɔwui lɛ baafite hybrid hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛnáa ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves turn yellow and curl up even when I give them plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu babaoo moŋ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are often caused by insect-borne diseases like the Tomato Leaf Curl Virus or a lack of nutrients in the soil, rather than a lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni kooloi kɛbaa tamɔ Tomato Leaf Curl Virus loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. yɛ nu ni baa shi lɛ najiaŋ

english: Why are my cassava plants producing many flowers and seeds, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa lolo?

english: When cassava plants put too much energy into making flowers and seeds above ground, they have less food left to store in their root tubers below ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsu nii ni amɛkɛwo fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Niyenii fioo pɛ baashwɛ ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Is it true that chemical fertilizers will spoil my soil if I use them every farming season?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaye mishikpɔŋ lɛ awui diɛŋtsɛ kɛ akɛtsu nii daa afi?

english: Chemical fertilizers provide quick nutrients for crops, but if used continuously without organic manure or compost, the soil loses its natural life and ability to retain moisture over time.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii oya. Shi kɛ akɛtsu nii be fɛɛ be ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fataaa he lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ ebɔɔ su kɛ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Can I just leave the weeds to grow around my pepper plants to protect them from the harsh sun?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mashi jwɛi komɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he. Ani pepper tsei baanyɛ abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he?

english: Leaving weeds around crops causes them to compete aggressively for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, which will stunt your pepper plants even if the weeds provide shade.
ga: Kɛji oshi jwɛi yɛ Nibii ni Aduɔ lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, nu kɛ hulu la mli, ni no baaha o-pepper tsei lɛ afee bibioo kɛji jwɛi haa hulutsoo po.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and dry up when I plant them in an open field without shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves burn easily and lose water faster than their roots can absorb it, requiring shade crops like plantains to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya ni amɛfiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Enɛ biɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my stored cowpea seeds get eaten by small insects even when I keep them tied tightly in regular sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ? Kɛji akɛ mikɛ amɛ fĩ kotoku ni afɔɔ feemɔ mli po.

english: Weevils and their eggs often hide inside the seeds before bagging, and regular woven sacks allow air inside for them to multiply, whereas airtight (hermetic) storage starves them of oxygen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ amɛwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli dani akɛwoɔ kotoku mli. Ni kotokui ni akpɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ mli lɛɛɔ. Yɛ be mli ni vacuum (vacuum) ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baaha amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ hɔmɔ.

english: Why is it bad to plant my maize very close together so I can fit more plants into my small plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he koni manyɛ madu tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting too closely forces maize plants to fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin stems that fall over easily and produce small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya. ni enine shɛ dumɔwui bibii loo dumɔwui ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ

english: Should I cut off the lower leaves of my tomato plants, or will that reduce how many tomatoes I harvest?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ? Aloo mikɛ tomato ni mikpaa lɛ ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Pruning lower leaves that touch the ground prevents fungal diseases from jumping from the wet soil onto the plant, allowing the plant to direct more energy into growing healthy fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni taa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa koni ekajɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛba tso lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛwo aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does a mango tree grown directly from a seed take many years to fruit, while a grafted mango tree fruits so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mango ni akɛwo mli lɛ woɔ yibii oya waa lɛ?

english: A seedling starts life from scratch as a juvenile plant, while a grafted plant uses a branch taken from an already mature, fruit-bearing tree, allowing it to start producing fruit in just a few years.
ga: Dumɔwui jeɔ wala shishi kɛjɛɔ shishijee akɛ tsei bibii. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni akɛwo amɛhe lɛ kɛ tsei niji ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni edara ni ewo yibii lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Ha eje shishi ewo yibii yɛ afii fioo komɛi pɛ mli.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the bottom, the plant is starving for nitrogen. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow, and when soil nutrients are low, the plant pulls food out of its older leaves to feed the young leaves growing at the top.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, feemɔ V su ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tsei. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. ni kɛ́ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but give me small, thin tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ekɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or the plants are planted too close together, cassava puts all its energy into growing stems and leaves instead of roots. To get big tubers, the plant needs balanced soil nutrients and enough room so it can send its energy downward to swell the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ eshishifãi lɛ najiaŋ. koni ená yitso agbo Tsei lɛ he miihia niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha hewalɛ aya shi koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plant instead of turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they get stressed by extreme heat, dry Harmattan winds, or uneven watering. High temperatures prevent the pollen inside the flower from working, so the plant sheds the flower because it cannot form a fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji latsaa ni naa wa hao amɛ. harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa pollen ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ tsuuu nii. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into small cups and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle kɔɔpoi bibii ahe lɛ? Ni etamɔ nɔ ni etsake?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, mites, or thrips sucking the juices from under the leaves. As these pests feed, they damage the leaf tissue and spread plant sicknesses, causing the leaves to roll up tightly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, mites, loo thrips ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛji nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ye niyenii Amɛfiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in my farm help my maize grow better in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni mi ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to a plant family called legumes that can trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the cowpea roots rot in the ground after harvest, they release that trapped nitrogen into the soil as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas fata tsei akuu ko ni ale amɛ akɛ legumes lɛ he. Ebaanyɛ emɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛto eshishifãi bibii amli. Kɛji cowpea shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Amɛjieɔ nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ awoɔ sũ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my plantain plants take so long to produce fruit when I leave many small shoots growing around the main mother plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii beni mikɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ lɛ? Amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo bɔle tso wulu lɛ he?

english: All the small shoots—called suckers—compete with the main mother plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Pruning away extra suckers and leaving only one or two allows the mother plant to focus all its energy on growing a big, healthy bunch of plantains quickly.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ akɛ suckers. Ekɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi eko loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso nyɛ lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama plantains akuu agbo ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eeekwɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when I watered the soil in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛtsu nii leebi lɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon, heat causes water to evaporate through the leaves faster than the roots can suck it up from the ground. The leaves wilt temporarily to protect themselves by exposing less surface area to the sun, but they usually recover once the evening cool arrives.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Dɔlɛ lɛ haa nu tsɔɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛtsɔ he ko ni hulu la shɛɛɛ nɔ fioo ni amɛshiɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi bei pii lɛ, amɛhe waaa kɛji fɛ̃i ba.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can capture as much direct sunlight as possible without touching wet soil. The more sunlight the lifted leaves collect, the more food the plant manufactures to swell the heavy yam tuber underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la tɛ̃ɛ bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ ni amɛtaaa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he. Babaoo ni hulu la ni awoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ, babaoo ni hulu la ni ebua naa lɛ buaa naa. Babaoo ni tso lɛ woɔ niyenii lɛ, babaoo ni sweet potato ŋmeii ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baafu.

english: Why do my harvested onions start rotting from the inside when I store them in my shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onions ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ kɛmiijɛ mli beni mikɛtoɔ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Onions rot in storage if they were not properly cured in the sun after harvest until their outer skins turned paper-dry and their necks closed tightly. An unsealed onion neck lets moisture and rot-causing germs get inside the bulb during storage.
ga: Sabala baagbo kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛɛɛ enɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛyashi amɛsɛɛ fã lɛ baatsɔ wolo ni egbi ni ekɛha amɛkuɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Onion tsitsi ni atsĩ naa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni haa mɔ fiteɔ lɛ boteɔ bulb lɛ mli beni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines root into the soil wherever the stems touch the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ shishifãi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekɔɔɔ he eko kɛji tso lɛ shishifã lɛ taa shikpɔŋ loo etaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Sweet potato plants naturally spread by trailing along the soil and putting down new root nodes to search for extra water and anchorage. These additional rooting points can form smaller secondary tubers if the soil beneath them is soft and moist.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛnyiɛɔ kɛ shishifãi heei ni amɛwoɔ shi koni amɛtao nu kroko kɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛma shi lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ shishifãi krokomɛi ni fata he nɛɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmeii bibii ni ji enyɔ lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunshine. Plantains grow very fast with broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and moist soil they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which acts as their main food for growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help them turn green again and produce big ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa amɛdaraa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni eha toi lɛ afee wuji.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater stays in the soil for too long, it drowns the roots and allows rot-causing fungi to attack and destroy the cassava tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛgbeɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa tree leaves drying up and dropping during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During Harmattan, dry winds and hot weather dry out the soil quickly. Cocoa trees shed some of their leaves to save water, protecting the main stem and branches from completely drying out until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ oya. Cocoa tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ekomɛi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Buu tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ kɛ eniji lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi kwraa kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when they suffer from water stress. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, preventing it from fertilizing and forming fruit.
ga: Tomatoi baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu he haomɔ miipiŋ amɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa enyɛɛɛ ekɛ fɔmɔ nii awo ni ewo yibii

english: Why do tiny green caterpillars keep hiding inside the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid on the leaves. They crawl deep into the central leaf funnel to feed safely on tender young leaves where rainwater and sun cannot easily reach them.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli. Amɛshwereɔ kɛboteɔ baai lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nugbɔ kɛ hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he oya lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these insects. Treating the pests early prevents leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kɛ́ atsa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my yam leaves and vines dry up and turn brown late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potatoes lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ blɔfo yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally turn brown and dry up when the plant finishes its growth cycle and sends all its food energy down into the root. This is a natural signal that the yam tuber is fully mature and ready for harvesting.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ tso lɛ gbe edalɛ be lɛ naa ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato tsei lɛ edara ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do my groundnut leaves fold together in the evening and open up in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut baai lɛ shwieɔ shi gbɛkɛ ni amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe leebi lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants naturally fold their leaves at night to save moisture and keep warm during cool nights. They spread their leaves back open when sunlight returns to start making food again.
ga: Peanut tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ gbɛkɛ koni eye ebua ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛha amɛhe adɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ mli. Amɛgbɛɔ baai lɛ amɛshwãa ekoŋŋ kɛji hulu la lɛ ku esɛɛ eba koni amɛje nihoomɔ shishi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea flowers keep falling off before any beans can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani ŋmeii lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers drop when tiny pests like flower thrips feed on the delicate buds. Protecting the crop with proper pest control during the early flowering stage allows the blossoms to stay attached and develop into healthy bean pods.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips lɛ ye ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni sa nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishijee be lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni he wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and dry during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need partial shade from nurse crops like plantains or shade trees to protect their leaves and retain soil moisture while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ nurse tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni abu baai lɛ ahe ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly in cool, wet, and humid conditions. Keeping your farm well-weeded, pruning excess branches to allow air flow, and harvesting ripe pods promptly helps stop the spread.
ga: Fungi hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, kɛ hei ni edɔ. Ehe miihia ni okwɛ ni jwɛi ahi oŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli Ni akpa tsei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do small caterpillars keep eating the leaf centers of my young maize plants before the cobs form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a widespread pest that feeds on the leaf whorls of young maize. Catching them early and applying recommended control measures directly into the leaf centers will protect the plant's growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni egbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baaye abua ni abu he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ he.

english: Why do my maize plants turn pale yellow and stay short even though I clear weeds regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kukuoo eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ amɛ jwɛi daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often indicate that the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help the maize regain its deep green color and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are ready for harvesting since they grow hidden under the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ejaakɛ akɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. Look for lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, along with cracks appearing in the soil around the base of the main stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kwɛmɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni miigbee shi. Kɛfata he lɛ, ŋmeii ni jeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ mli.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and ensuring the plant receives enough light to grow large tubers.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni ekwɛɔ koni tsei lɛ aná la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha bulb agboi ni baa lɛ.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my crop seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the year is often followed by a long dry spell before the main rainy season settles. Planting too early can cause seeds to sprout and then die from heat and lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgboi yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the ground, but legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next main crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers spread dry grass and cocoa husks around the bases of their crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ jwɛi kɛ kookoo ŋmeii amɛshwieɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with organic matter, called mulching, keeps the ground cool, reduces water loss from evaporation, stops weeds from growing, and turns into rich plant food as it breaks down.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli woɔ mli lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi Ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ ni ebafeɔ tsei aniyenii ni jara wa kɛji egbo.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flower blossoms without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa wooo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus in the soil. Consistent watering and keeping the soil cool with mulch helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa ni akɛ mulch haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. When planted with maize, they act like natural fertilizer, helping your maize grow stronger without buying extra chemical inputs.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa Amɛbaatsu nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ehiɛ wa ni okɛ tsofai krokomɛi aheee.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my tomato plants with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plants (mulching) keeps the soil cool under the strong sun, slows down water evaporation so you water less, and stops weeds from growing and stealing nutrients from your tomatoes.
ga: Nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo bɔni afee ni okɛ nu lɛ akawo mli fioo. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need long wooden sticks to climb on instead of growing flat on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni ekwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants make tubers using sunlight captured by their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves into the air and sun, preventing leaf rot from ground dampness and allowing the plant to make bigger, healthier yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hulu la ni amɛbaai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ lɛ feɔ bulbs. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la mli. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa plants turning yellow and scorching during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that cannot handle direct, full sunlight and harsh dry winds. They require temporary shade trees, like plantains, to shield them while their roots establish deep in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa ni mli egbi lɛ nyɛɛɛ abote mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Flowers usually drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Without enough water and food, the plant discards flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo sũ mli niyenii kpakpai haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Kɛji nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants look twisted with yellow patterns on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni efite ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, spread by tiny whiteflies. The virus stops the leaves from making food properly, which leads to smaller cassava roots at harvest time.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Virus lɛ haaa baai lɛ ahoo jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii shishifãi bibii baa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves and dirt inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni mli ewo muji kɛ muji yɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It feeds on the tender leaves inside the whorl, leaving waste behind, which weakens the plant and lowers your grain yield if not managed early.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei ni yeɔ baai bibii yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Shi jwɛi lɛ yɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni ehaa dumɔwui ni baa lɛ baa shi kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ mra.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots spoil and turn black just two days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ fite ni amɛtsɔ ediŋŋ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots do not have a hard protective skin like yams and begin to spoil fast once detached from the ground. Processing them quickly into products like gari or flour preserves them before decay sets in.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni ebɔi fitemɔ oya kɛji akɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afee amɛ oya ni afee nibii tamɔ gari loo ashikishaŋ lɛ, ehaa niyenii nɛɛ hiɔ shi dani amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why should I remove some of the young suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi tsɔne titri lɛ

english: If too many suckers grow around one stem, they all fight for the same soil food and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only two or three, allowing the main stem to produce a much bigger bunch of plantain.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha baai enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi shi. Ehaa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ woɔ dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn into powder with small bugs inside after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ tsɔɔ powda ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Hiɛ mli beni okɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ.

english: Weevils lay eggs inside dry maize grains. If the maize is stored damp or unprotected, the eggs hatch into bugs that eat the grain from the inside out, turning your harvest into worthless dust.
ga: Weevils woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ni egbi mli. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɔ ŋmãa nɔ loo abuuu he lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ kɛfeɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli sũ ni he ehiaaa.

english: Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow strong. When yellowing starts from the lower leaves, it usually means the plant has run out of nitrogen in the soil and needs manure or fertilizer.
ga: Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Beni baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ awo mli.

english: Why is my cowpea crop producing plenty of green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: When cowpeas get too much nitrogen in the soil, they spend all their energy growing leaves and stems instead of producing flowers and beans.
ga: Kɛji tsina ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsina ŋmei yeɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛduɔ baai kɛ tsei ahe. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ngma.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when water collects in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits on the land without draining, the roots choke, drown, and invite rot diseases.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ta shikpɔŋ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛshwieɔ nu mli, ni amɛhaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves to shrink their surface area, which helps them reduce water loss and protect themselves when the afternoon sun gets too hot.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ebuɔ ohe kɛji shwane hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before setting fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme hot dry air, irregular watering, or a lack of essential nutrients in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji amɛyashɛ haomɔ, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni mli egbi lɛ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why are my orange trees dropping their small green fruits onto the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Unripe oranges fall early mainly due to fruit fly attacks, severe water shortages during dry spells, or because the tree has carried more fruit than its roots can nourish.
ga: Akutu ni eshɛko lɛ shwieɔ shi oya, titri lɛ yɛ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni faaa waa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli Aloo akɛni tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe bɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ hewɔ?

english: Why are my cabbage heads remaining soft and loose instead of forming a hard ball?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages form hard heads only when they have enough growing space, steady moisture, and proper nutrients. Overcrowding or dry soil causes them to stay open and leafy.
ga: Kaabage lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa kɛji eyɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ pɛ. Fɛ̃i yɛ jɛmɛ be fɛɛ be. ni eyɛ niyenii ni sa pɛ Shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haa amɛjeɔ kpo ni amɛfeɔ baai.

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. Planting them after heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally feeds and restores your farm soil.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni ooodu yɛ niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ, haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii ni ehaa ehe hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild local plants with very tough root systems that react instantly to rainwater, stealing nutrients and moisture before cultivated crops can settle.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni eshishifãi lɛ wa waa. ni baaha nugbɔ nu lɛ hetoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ Amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ dani tso lɛ baanyɛ ama shi.

english: Why do my plantains turn soft so quickly after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ feɔ blɛoo oya kɛji mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains release a natural gas called ethylene as they ripen, which rapidly converts their firm starches into sugars. In warm Ghanaian weather, this process happens very fast, causing the skin to yellow and the fruit to become soft.
ga: Dares jieɔ adebɔɔ mli la ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa lɛ feɔ sugar oya. yɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Nɛkɛ nifeemɔ nɛɛ baa mli oya waa. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni aduawai lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ.

english: Can I just cut a piece of yam I bought from the market and plant it in my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni ahe yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can cut healthy yams into smaller pieces called seed setts to plant. As long as the cut piece has a viable bud or 'eye' and the cut surface is allowed to dry or treated with ash to prevent rotting, it will grow into a full plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ofolɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli bibii bibii. Atsɛɔ lɛ dumɔwui akuu ni abaanyɛ adu. Shii abɔ ni ŋmei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni baanyɛ ada lɛ. ni oha he ni afo lɛ agbi loo okɛ sũ atsu nii koni ekɛtsi fitemɔ naa. Ebaada ni etsɔ tso ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do some of my seed yams start sprouting almost immediately after planting while others take a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ aaafee beni adu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi heɔ be babaoo lɛ?

english: Yams go through a natural resting period called dormancy after harvest. If you plant a seed yam that has already broken its dormancy, it will sprout very fast, whereas yams still in dormancy must finish their rest period before growing.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu sweet potato dumɔwui ni ehi shi lɛ, Ebaakwɛ̃ oya waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, esa akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ mli lolo lɛ agbe amɛ ŋmɔlɔ be lɛ naa dani amɛdara.

english: What makes local plantain varieties like 'Afebɛtua' different from other plantain types on the market?
ga: Mɛni haa maŋ lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi tamɔ ‘Afebɛtua’ lɛ feɔ srɔto yɛ tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Local plantain varieties differ in their starch content, taste, and how fast they soften. Some varieties are specifically suited for boiling or frying when firm, while soft-ripening varieties like 'Afebɛtua' are often preferred for local dishes like tatale or kakro.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli plantain henɔi lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ amɛ starch ni yɔɔ mli, amɛmli ŋɔɔmɔ kɛ oyaiyeli mli. Ekomɛi hi jogbaŋŋ titri kɛha shãa loo shãa kɛji akɛ amɛwa. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ akɛ srɔtoi ni yɔɔ blɛoo tamɔ ‘Afebɛtua’ tsuɔ nii yɛ maŋ niyenii tamɔ tatale loo kacro mli.

english: How do I know if a seed yam is healthy enough to sprout well in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A good seed yam should feel firm to the touch, be free from soft spots or fungal rots, and show no signs of deep insect damage. Early visible buds near the head of the tuber are a strong sign that it is ready to grow.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ afee nɔ ni wa kɛji mɔ ko ta he. He ni egbɔjɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni efite bɛ jɛmɛ. ni okadi ko bɛ ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii efite nii waa. Hiŋmɛii ni baanyɛ ana nii kɛjɛ shishijee Mli ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmei lɛ yiteŋ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaada.

english: How can I stop my harvested yams from going soft and rotting before I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafee blɛoo ni efite dani madu?

english: Store your yams in a well-ventilated, shaded yam barn raised off the bare ground. Avoid bruising the tubers during harvest, as wounds allow fungal rots and bacteria to enter and spoil the crop quickly.
ga: Kɛ sweet potato ato sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli ni ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ni oootswa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, pilamɔi haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya.

english: Why are the plantains on my farm ripening while the bunch is still small and on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwereɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Premature ripening on the tree usually happens when the plant suffers from environmental stress, such as severe drought, poor soil nutrients, or root damage caused by pests like nematodes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ shweremɔ baa oya kɛ́ shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ hɔmɔ ni naa wa ko miikpe. Niyenii ni ehiii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo shishifãi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes kɛbaa.

english: Is it better for me to plant small whole yams or cut pieces of big yams?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii wuji?

english: Small whole yams (seed yams) are generally better because their unbroken skin naturally protects them from soil rot and pests. However, cut pieces from large yams work well if seed yams are scarce, provided the cut surfaces are dried properly.
ga: small whole sweet potato Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ dumɔwui ewo mli lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ hewolo ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛhe lɛ ahe yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛji akɛ afolɔ mli lɛ, ebaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ obɛ sweet potatoes ni dumɔwui ewo mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛji akɛ ŋwɛi ni afo lɛ mli egbi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do market women prefer buying very soft plantains instead of green firm ones from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayeli yei sumɔɔ ni amɛhe plantains ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ waa moŋ fe plantains ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Market women buy soft plantains because they have a high sugar content, making them ideal for immediate processing into traditional foods like fried plantain cakes (tatale) or roasted plantain snacks, which require sweet, soft fruit.
ga: Yei ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ heɔ plantains ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ sugar ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha nitsumɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni efeɔ blema niyenii tamɔ plantain keeki ni ashã (tatale) loo plantain niyenii ni ashã ni biɔ aduawai ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo.

english: Why is my yam plant growing a lot of green leaves very fast but producing small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ naa baai eŋɔlii babaoo oya shi ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: If soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the yam plant focuses all its energy on growing long vines and leaves above ground rather than storing energy in thick tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe lɛ, Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ wain tsei kɛ baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi yitsei ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why should I plant plantains in the same farm alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ mi-kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the essential shade and moisture young cocoa needs during its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha kookoo bibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ haa.

english: Why is it bad if I scatter my maize seeds very close together instead of leaving clear spacing between them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji migbɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ashwã amɛhe yɛ he ni mikɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow thick stems and large ears.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ toi wuji.

english: Yam plants are natural vines that need to climb upward to catch maximum sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, which prevents fungal diseases and helps the plant produce larger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli wain tsei ni ehe hiaa ni akwɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient needed for leaf growth. Applying manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore the green color and boosts plant health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ akwɛ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha tso lɛ mli awa.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and attracts persistent pests. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ.

english: Why do people spread dry leaves and grass around the base of crop stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi shwieɔ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi amɛshwieɔ tsei ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Spreading dry leaves or grass around crops is called mulching. It traps moisture in the ground so crops do not dry out quickly in the hot sun, and it stops weeds from growing and taking over the farm.
ga: Atsɛɔ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ ji koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi akakwɛ̃ ni eŋɔ ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting beans or cowpeas between rows of crops like cassava or corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds nearby crops and improves overall soil fertility.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my young maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the center shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni akɛtee mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in West Africa. Early detection and applying recommended treatments like biopesticides or clean wood ash inside the central leaf whorls helps stop them from destroying the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ Afrika Anaigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni anaa mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tso sũ ni he tse ni yɔɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baaye abua ni amɛtsi amɛnaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baa ko egbɔ kɛji baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa

english: Why does my harvested maize develop black mold and small beetles inside the storage bags after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ, okɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Mold and weevils occur when maize is bagged before it is completely dry. Drying corn thoroughly in the sun until the grains are rock-hard prevents fungal growth and stops insects from multiplying during storage.
ga: Mold kɛ weevils baa kɛji akɛ awo ŋmãa kotoku mli dani egbi kwraa. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ ni kooloi bibii lɛ akafa babaoo yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I clear all the big trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and need partial shade to survive. Direct, intense sunlight burns their young leaves and dries out the topsoil, while shade trees create a cooler environment and hold soil moisture.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛ he hiaa shade fioo koni amɛhi shi. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni kpɛɔ waa lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves at the bottom of my maize plants turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ abele tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for green leaf growth. The plant starves and moves its remaining nitrogen up to the newer leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai eŋɔli lɛ daa lɛ Tso lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni ebaajie nitrogen fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya baai heei anɔ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting underground before it is even time to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani be po shɛɔ ni abaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water sits in the soil for too long without draining properly. Heavy rain combined with clay soil creates swampy conditions that drown the roots and encourage fungal decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ sũ fataa he lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli ewo muji ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ baa.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the weather becomes too hot or when they do not get steady water. High temperatures stress the plant and dry out the pollen, preventing the flower from forming fruit.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu daa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ mli egbiɔ. Tsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding underneath. They suck the fresh sap out of the leaf tissues, causing new leaves to grow deformed and wrinkled.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛ nuɔ nu hee ni jɛɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa baai heei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What is this purple-flowered weed that attaches to my maize roots and stops my corn from growing?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ jwɛi ni hiɛ fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekpɛtɛ mi-abele shishifãi lɛ ahe ni etsĩɔ abele lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ nɛɛ?

english: That weed is Striga, commonly called witchweed. It is a parasitic plant that attaches its own roots to maize roots, stealing all the water and food before the maize can use it.
ga: Nakai jwɛi lɛ ji striga. Aloo nɔ ni afɔɔ lɛ tsɛmɔ akɛ Witchweed. Eji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpãa ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛtsɔ nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni ejuɔ dani akɛ ŋmãa lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during storms even before the bunch is fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli dani ŋmeii lɛ daraa kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that stay near the surface. When the soil gets soft from rain and the growing fruit bunch becomes heavy, wind easily pulls the shallow roots right out of the mud.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ fee blɛoo kɛjɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli ni aduawai lɛ dara ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni tsii Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooojɛ muji lɛ mli

english: How do I stop my harvested yams from sprouting and shrinking while stored in my barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni egbɔjɔ be mli ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams sprout when exposed to light and heat because they sense it is time to grow again. Keeping them in a cool, shady, well-ventilated barn on raised bamboo racks keeps them dormant longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ la kɛ dɔlɛ wo amɛmli ejaakɛ amɛnuɔ he akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli yɛ ŋmei ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why did my maize seeds fail to germinate when I planted right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain often moistens only the top layer of dry ground. If a long dry spell follows immediately after, the hot dry soil scorches the seeds before they can establish deep roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ gĩɔ ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ baashã dumɔwui dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why did my corn plants burn and dry up after I put fertilizer right next to their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii efata he yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer is made of concentrated salts. Placing it directly against the stem or root base draws water out of the plant tissue, effectively burning and killing the crop.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei ni mli edɔ feɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso lɛ shishi loo shishitoo lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbala nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ fãji lɛ amli. Enɛ kɛ shãa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akpãtãmɔ baa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees require so much constant work and attention throughout the year compared to other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛ akɛto tsei krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees are sensitive plants that continuously react to changes in shade, rain, and weeds. Regular field maintenance like weeding, pruning, and inspecting pods prevents sudden disease outbreaks and keeps the tree producing high yields year after year.
ga: Cocoa tsei ji tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tsuɔ tsakemɔi ni baa daa yɛ hulutsoo, nugbɔ, kɛ jwɛi ahe nii. Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ saamɔ daa, tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akwɛɔ Kɛ ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ baaye abua ni helai akaje shishi trukaa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo daa afi

english: Why does trimming or cutting off healthy-looking branches help my cocoa trees produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afoɔ loo afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-cacao tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes useless foliage that steals food from the tree and opens up the canopy so sunlight and air can flow through. Good airflow reduces dampness that causes diseases, allowing the tree to direct its energy into growing pods instead of unnecessary leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ baai ni he ehiaaa ni juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ, ni egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni kɛ hela baa lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ hewalɛ yaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai ni he ehiaaa baatsu nii.

english: Why do I need to apply chemicals and fertilizers to my cocoa farm to get a good harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsofai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ he koni maná yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Over time, soil loses nutrients that crops need to grow strong. Applied fertilizers replace missing soil food, while protective chemicals stop common pests like capsids and fungal diseases from destroying pods before harvest.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ. Nibii ni akɛtoɔ niyenii ni elaaje yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ tamɔ capsids kɛ fungal helai anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani akpa.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray protective chemicals on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Spraying early in the morning or late in the afternoon works best because the sun is mild, preventing the chemical from drying out too fast or scorching the crop leaves before it has a chance to work.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ leebi loo shwane mli beni hulu la ni tsoɔ fioo lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haaa tsofa lɛ agbi oya loo eshã tso lɛ baai lɛ dani ebɔi nitsumɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees falling off before turning into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ anɔkwa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Dropping flowers is the plant's way of saving energy to survive tough conditions.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa trees turning black and drying up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, damp, and overly wet conditions. It quickly spreads from pod to pod if trees are not pruned or sprayed with recommended fungicides.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine. Ebaagbɛ eshwa oya kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli kɛya ekroko mli kɛji akɛ afolɔɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ loo akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ efɔɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How does too much direct sunlight affect the way my young cocoa trees grow?
ga: Te hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo lɛ saa mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: While cocoa trees need light, young trees in harsh, full sunlight lose water too quickly, get leaf burn, and can dry up and die. Shade crops help shield young cocoa plants until they grow strong enough.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ la he miihia kookoo tsei moŋ, shi tso bibioo ko Mɛi ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ amɛ fɛɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nu baaje amɛmli oya tsɔ, baai lɛ baashã, ni ekolɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi. Tsei ni yɔɔ shade mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my crops slow down their growth and shed leaves during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa oya ni amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry, dusty Harmattan winds remove moisture from the air and soil. Crops intentionally drop leaves to conserve water and protect themselves from drying out until the rains return.
