ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsɔɔ yiŋtoo ko nɔ amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How do weeds growing near my young cocoa plants affect their growth?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ saa amɛdalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds act like competitors; they aggressively steal water, sunlight, and essential soil nutrients from your young cocoa plants, causing the cocoa trees to stay small and weak.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akaŋshilɔi. Amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu ni he hiaa, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ o-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: How can I tell if my farm's soil is suitable and healthy enough for planting cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi ni eyɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ?

english: Healthy cocoa soil is deep, dark, rich in organic material, and drains excess rainwater easily without staying muddy or waterlogged for long periods.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ediŋŋ, ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ mli. Ni ejieɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ oya ni ekɛ muji loo ŋmɔtɔ baaa mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain plants look weak even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Extra shoots or weeds growing close to the main plantain tree steal water and nutrients from the soil, leaving the mother plant without enough nourishment to stay strong.
ga: Tsobii ni fa fe nine loo jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ masɛi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso nyɛ lɛ náaa niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ehewalɛ ahi shi.

english: Is it bad if many small plantain shoots grow right next to my main tree?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji akɛ plantains lɛ ji bibii? Ekwɛ̃ yɛ mitso titri lɛ masɛi.

english: Yes, having too many shoots growing very close to the mother plant puts pressure on it because all the plants end up fighting for the same water and soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ekɛ nɔnyɛɛ baa ejaakɛ esa akɛ tso fɛɛ tso awuu koni ená nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: How do plants growing too close together starve each other of water?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha nu akafee nɔ ko?

english: When extra shoots grow near a main plant, their root bases sit in the same soil area and continuously draw water away, depriving the main plant of the moisture it needs.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ kwɛ̃ ni bɛŋkɛ tso wulu lɛ Amɛshishitoo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛgbalaa nu kɛyaa jɛmɛ be fɛɛ be. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ bɛ nu ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off unwanted suckers from around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni ataooo kɛjɛ mi-plantain he lɛ?

english: Cutting off unwanted suckers stops them from pulling water and strength away from the mother plant, allowing the main tree to nourish itself properly.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni ataooo lɛ amli lɛ, ehaaa amɛná nu kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ haa ehe niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens if I cut a plantain shoot but leave its base lying on the ground?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mifo plantain tsei lɛ shi mishi shishitoo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: If the base of a cut shoot remains on the ground or in the soil, it can continue drawing water from the earth and depriving the main plant of its strength.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tso ni afo lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ tee nɔ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ Ebaanyɛ eya nɔ ejie nu kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tso titri lɛ he waaa

english: Why do extension officers tell us to prune fast-growing side stems near our crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfolɔ tsei niji ni daa oya yɛ sɛɛgbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ wɔŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Fast-growing side stems quickly get close to the main plant and take away the essential food and water it needs to develop properly.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni daa oya lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe oya kɛyaa tso wulu lɛ he ni amɛwoɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛyaa.

english: Why is my plantain tree growing so slowly compared to others on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ akɛto tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Slow growth often happens when extra shoots grow around the main plant and take away the nourishment needed for fast, healthy development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ baa kɛji ŋmeii babaoo ebɔle tso lɛ he. tso titri lɛ ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha shweremɔ oya kɛ hewalɛ

english: Will leaving extra stems around my plantain plant reduce the size of my harvest?
ga: Ani mi plantains lɛ baaha mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: Yes, leaving extra stems causes them to steal nutrients and water, which prevents the main plantain tree from nourishing itself well enough to produce large bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii krokomɛi ni akɛbaashwie shi lɛ baaha amɛju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu. Enɛ haaa dumɔwu titri lɛ aha ehe niyenii jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Why does my plantain crop lose its strength as it grows bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: As nearby suckers grow larger, they pull more water and soil nutrients toward themselves, gradually robbing the main plantain tree of its strength.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ dara lɛ Amɛgbalaa nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛbaa amɛhe ni amɛjuɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ hewalɛ fiofio.

english: How can I make sure my main plantain tree gets all the food I put in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni dumɔwui titrii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You must cut away any extra shoots or volunteer plants growing near the mother plant so they do not absorb the soil nutrients before the main tree can use them.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine loo tsei ni kɛ amɛhe eha ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani tso titri lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when temperatures get too high or when the soil gets too dry. Keeping the soil regularly watered and using mulch around the roots to retain moisture helps the plant hold onto flowers and produce tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ tsu nii koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔmɔ fɔfɔii lɛ ni amɛwo tomato.

english: What causes my pepper plant leaves to curl up and become tiny?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper tsei lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant sap. Spraying the leaves early with neem oil or recommended treatments helps control these pests and restores healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Ni akɛ neem fɔ baashwie baai lɛ anɔ mra Aloo, tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni eha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when left in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to harsh heat and direct sunlight in their first couple of years. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to cocoa seedlings creates shade and keeps the air moist so the seedlings can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni eye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Does it matter which direction I stick my cassava stem into the ground?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni adu ŋmei tsei lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, planting cassava stems upside down prevents roots from developing properly and lowers your harvest. Always ensure the small buds on the stem point upward toward the sky before planting.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmei tsei ni okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ, ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, ni ebaaha onibii ni oooha lɛ aba shi. Kwɛmɔ be fɛɛ be akɛ ŋmeii lɛ afee bibii. Yɛ tso lɛ shishi ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi dani aduɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Yam leaves need to catch direct sunlight to produce food for growing big tubers underground. Staking holds the vines up off the wet ground, giving the leaves maximum sunlight and preventing rot.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs ni miida lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa baa lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ, ni ehaaa egbo.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the small shoots growing around my plantain stem to stay?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi plantain tsei lɛ ji nɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: If too many suckers grow around one main plantain stem, they steal water and nutrients from each other, resulting in small bunches. Removing extra suckers leaves enough food for the main plant to produce large, heavy fruit.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe single main trunk Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso yibii bibii Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei bibii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea around the roots helps the leaves become deep green and improves overall growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni eha amɛdalɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil drains specific nutrients every season and allows pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abele ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi kpo daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Weeds compete directly with young crops for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the available nourishment to grow strong before weeds choke them.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Ebaaha onibii lɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa dani jwɛi lɛ agbe amɛ.

english: Why should I wait until the main rainy season settles before planting my corn seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Planting corn seeds in dry soil during false rains can cause the seeds to rot or fail to sprout. Waiting for consistent, steady rainfall ensures the ground has enough moisture for seeds to germinate and survive.
ga: Abele dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbo loo amɛkakwɛ̃. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa, ni baa shi lɛ mɛmɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and fall off when the weather gets very hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop during hot, dry weather as a natural defense to keep the tree from losing too much water. Planting shade trees like plantains or terminalia alongside young cocoa keeps the farm cooler and protects the leaves from burning.
ga: Cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ, ni egbiɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, tso lɛ akafite nu babaoo. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo terminals ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa baa lɛ shãaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when water supply is irregular. Heat causes severe stress to the plant, so it drops its blossoms to save energy rather than trying to feed developing fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tsei anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ efɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni eeebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves soil soaked for long periods, water fills up all the air spaces, suffocating the roots and allowing fungal rot to attack them. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, sũ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ be kplaŋŋ. Nu lɛ baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ fɛɛ amli. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli.

english: Why are the young leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, mites, or aphids feeding on the sap under young leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Spragging the farm with recommended organic or insecticidal soaps early stops this damage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni yeɔ latex ni yɔɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ shwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ mra lɛ, ehaa nɔ ni fiteɔ nii nɛɛ kpaa.

english: Why do I see small holes in my young maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa mli lɛ nɔ

english: Holes and sawdust-like dirt inside young maize shoots are signs of armyworms or stem borer caterpillars feeding on the plant. Placing a pinch of clean sand mixed with ash or targeted bio-insecticides into the central leaf funnel kills these pests before they destroy the crop.
ga: Buu kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmei bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii loo stem borer ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ yeɔ nii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋã ni he tse ni akɛ sũ efutu mli fioo loo tsofa ko ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli ni akɛ hiɛ fɔ nɔ lɛ fata tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ he lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever a rainstorm hits my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baatswa miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that stay near the top of the soil. As the plant develops a heavy bunch of fruit, its top becomes heavy, making it easy for high winds to pull the roots out. Supporting heavy bunches with strong wooden or bamboo props prevents them from falling.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ wo yibii babaoo lɛ Eyiteŋ baafee tsiimɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa shishifãi lɛ kɛje kpo. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa fiɔ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why does my cowpea crop produce lots of green leaves but almost no flowers or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi eshwɛ fioo ni fɔfɔi loo ŋmeii bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Giving cowpeas too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant focus entirely on growing big leaves instead of flowers. Cowpeas make their own nitrogen naturally, so they need fertilizers higher in phosphorus to encourage abundant flowering and pod formation.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tsina ŋmei mli fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai wuji ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ fɔsfɔs ni fa babaoo awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni eha fɔfɔi babaoo aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii afee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do my yams know when to start sprouting inside the barn even when there is no light?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni mi-sweet potato lɛ leɔ be ni esa akɛ ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji kane bɛ po?

english: Yam tubers have an internal natural clock that wakes them up after a period of dormancy. Changes in air temperature and humidity at the end of the dry season signal to the tuber that the rainy season is near, triggering sprouting regardless of light.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa ko ni teɔ amɛ shi yɛ wɔɔhe be ko sɛɛ. Tsakemɔi ni baa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ naagbee lɛ haa tsei lɛ leɔ akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ebɛŋkɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii baa ni la kɔɔɔ he eko

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in an upside-down 'V' shape from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ‘V’ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛmiijɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the tips of the lower leaves indicates that your maize plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-composted manure near the plant base restores healthy green leaf growth.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai wo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it dangerous to apply dry chemical fertilizer to my crops during dry weather without watering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi ni mikɛ nu wooo mli lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers are salts that require moisture to dissolve so crop roots can drink them up safely. Applying dry fertilizer to dry soil concentrates the salt around the roots, pulling water out of the plant and burning or killing it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni biɔ ni nu atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei abɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Gbalamɔ nu lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli ni oshã loo ogbe.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or when heavy rain drowns the roots. Nitrogen acts like food for green leaves, so feeding the soil with compost or fertilizer helps the leaves stay green and produce big cobs.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi. Nitrogen tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛha baai eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater gathers around them and cannot drain away quickly. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water run off, keeping the soil well-aerated so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa ni enyɛŋ efo oya. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni bulbs lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get dark, rotten patches on the bottom side as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Dark patches on tomato bottoms happen when the plant cannot pull up enough calcium from the soil, usually because watering is uneven. Keeping the soil regularly moist helps the roots continuously feed calcium to the developing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei anɔ ŋmɔtɔ diji baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhaa aduawai ni miida lɛ calcium be fɛɛ be.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the dirt through their roots, naturally fertilizing the maize. Their wide leaves also cover the ground like a carpet, keeping weeds down and preventing the soil from drying out.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa Baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ hu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ kapɛti. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi.

english: Yam is a climbing plant that needs lots of direct sunlight on its leaves to make big tubers underneath the ground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet soil where they could rot and lifts them up into the sun to capture maximum energy.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ aahu akɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. ni baanyɛ afite ni ekɛwo hulu lɛ mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo ato

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when heavy wind and rain hit my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni naa wa ba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and stay close to the top of the dirt, making the heavy stems top-heavy when bearing fruit bunches. Supporting the main stem with a strong wooden prop or bamboo pole holds the plant steady against sudden storms.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni tsii waa lɛ feɔ tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ beni aduawai lɛ feɔ kui lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ ahum ni baa trukaa lɛ he.

english: Why do cocoa flowers fall off my trees without forming cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by hot, dry winds or attacked by tiny sap-sucking insects like mirids. Keeping shade trees in your farm blocks the hot wind and provides the cool, humid climate cocoa flowers need to turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ atatui ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tutua amɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi ni mli ejɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why are small caterpillars chewing holes inside the centers of my young maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miiye bu ni yɔɔ mibii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which love to hide inside the soft central roll of young maize plants where they eat tender leaves. Checking your farm early and putting recommended pest controls directly into the central funnel protects the plant's growing core.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli he ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ yɛ lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛbuɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ŋaa lɛ awo teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni abu tso lɛ mli fã ni miida lɛ he.

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that shields the ground from the hot sun. It traps moisture in the soil so you don't need to water as often, while also blocking weed seeds from getting light to sprout.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu afɔ nɔ shii abɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ la he ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do crops grow better if I plant right after the first major rain rather than waiting a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei daa jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ otsii fioo komɛi

english: The very first rains wake up beneficial soil organisms, causing a sudden natural release of stored plant food in the dirt. Planting right away allows your young crops to eat this rich food supply early and grow deep roots before dry spells return.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ teɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei aniyenii ni abua naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo trukaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amrɔ nɛɛ, dumɔ haa otsei bibii lɛ yeɔ niyenii babaoo mra. ni amɛwo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani hulutsoo be lɛ aku esɛɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because intense direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out their roots. Leaving tall trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains creates a natural shelter that keeps the young cocoa cool and moist until it matures.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli shihilɛhe ko ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients out of the soil. Adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore their deep green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Look for the tiny buds or nodes along the stem and make sure they are pointing upward toward the sky. Planting cassava stems upside down causes the sprouts to waste energy trying to grow toward the light, resulting in very low yields.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni okwɛ akɛ amɛmiitsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Yucca tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara kɛya la lɛ he lɛ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do my vegetable crops dry out so quickly during the Harmattan season even if I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ Harmattan be lɛ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: The dry, dusty Harmattan winds pull moisture rapidly from plant leaves through evaporation. Covering the ground around your crops with dry leaves or straw (mulching) traps moisture in the soil so the plant roots stay hydrated longer.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Mulching around Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) baamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ koni tso shishifãi lɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas in between my main food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas feed the soil by taking nitrogen from the air and trapping it in their roots. They also spread over the ground to suppress weeds and protect the soil from direct heat.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu koni amɛgbe jwɛi ni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the small shoots growing around my main plantain plant stay?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ ji nɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Allowing too many shoots to grow causes them to compete with the parent plant for nutrients, sunlight, and water, leading to smaller plantain bunches. Cutting away extra shoots leaves only one strong suckering successor to produce a large, healthy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ abɔi niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ sɛɛyelɔ kome pɛ ni he wa ni ekɛ ŋmeii agbo ni he wa baa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting when plants experience sudden stress from extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of calcium in the soil. Maintaining consistent moisture and protecting roots keeps the flowers attached.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ trukaa kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni abuɔ lɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ akamɔ shi.

english: Why is it important to make high soil mounds before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ama gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani adu ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose, and well-drained soil to expand freely underground. High mounds give the roots room to stretch deep into the earth while preventing standing water from rotting the young tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Gɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nu ni ekã shi lɛ naa koni ekaha bulb bibii lɛ akafite.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects like aphids or mites are hiding underneath and sucking the juice out of the leaves. Spraying plants with diluted neem oil or soapsuds can clear these small pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo mites, kɛ amɛhe ewo shishi ni amɛmiinu nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni akɛwo mli lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ akashɛ he.

english: Why does black, composted soil produce better vegetables than hard, dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ diŋ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ewo mli lɛ hi kɛha aduawai fe shikpɔŋ ni wa ni egbi lɛ?

english: Dark composted soil is filled with decayed plant matter that acts like a sponge, holding onto water and slowly feeding essential nutrients to plant roots. Hard, dry soil compresses root growth and lets water run off without soaking in.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ eyi kɛ tsei ni fiteɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Too nu ni fiofio Ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei shishifãi Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wa lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ehaa nu hoɔ ni eboteee mli.

english: How can I process my harvested corn so that I do not lose or waste so much of it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsu mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ he nii koni ekafite loo ekafite babaoo?

english: To prevent waste, dry your corn cobs thoroughly on a clean raised platform, shell them carefully to avoid crushing the kernels, and winnow away chaff before storing them in clean, airtight bags.
ga: koni akafee jwɛi Ha ŋmãa lɛ agbi yɛ he ko ni he tse ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ hewolo lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni dumɔwui lɛ akakumɔ. Ni jiemɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani okɛwo vacuum bag ni mli tse mli.

english: Why do so many of my rice grains break during processing, and how can I fix it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice ŋmeii babaoo fite beni atsuɔ he nii lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Rice breaks if it is harvested too late or dried too fast in hot sun. Harvesting when the stalks turn yellow and parboiling the grains before milling hardens them, keeping the grains whole and reducing waste.
ga: Omɔ baagba kɛji akɛ akpa lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ loo egbi oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akpa dumɔwui lɛ beni ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, ni okɛ la awo mli dani okɛ ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa dumɔwui yeɔ emuu ni ehaa fitemɔ baa shi.

english: Why is processing my crops into flour or dried grains better than selling them fresh from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mafee miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ashikishaŋ loo dumɔwui ni egbi fe ni mahɔ̃ɔ amɛ ehee kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Fresh crops spoil quickly, forcing you to sell at low market prices. Processing extends their shelf life, prevents post-harvest rot, and allows you to hold your crop to sell at higher prices later.
ga: Nibii ni adu ehee lɛ fiteɔ oya. ni nyɛɔ onɔ ni ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ Nitsumɔ haa shihilɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. ni ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ toɔ koni okɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ sɛɛ mli.

english: What makes a harvest of rice good quality compared to poor quality rice?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛ akɛto ŋmãa ni baa shi lɛ he?

english: Good quality rice consists of clean, whole grains with no dirt, weed seeds, or discoloration. Proper drying and gentle milling preserve grain appearance and increase its value to buyers.
ga: Omɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji ŋmaa ni he tse ni muji, jwɛi dumɔwui, loo su ni tsakeɔ bɛ mli. Ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ bɔ ni ashwieɔ lɛ blɛoo lɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ sui lɛ hiɔ shi, ni ehaa ejara yaa hiɛ kɛhaa mɔ ni heɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my corn so I do not ruin the crop quality?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Bɔni afee ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Corn is ready to harvest when the husks turn brown and dry, and the kernels are hard when pressed. Harvesting too early causes the corn to mold, while harvesting too late leaves it vulnerable to field pests.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi. ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ kɛji akɛ anyɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ aná ŋmei. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aye nɔ.

english: Can I dry my harvested rice in full midday sun to make it dry faster?
ga: Ani manyɛ magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni egbi oya?

english: Drying rice under direct, intense sun makes the grains crack internally. When milled, these cracked grains shatter easily. It is better to dry rice slowly under partial shade or during cooler morning hours.
ga: Omɔ ni agbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ haa omɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ mli fãa. Kɛ́ atswa lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni egbɛ eshwa nɛɛ fãa oya. Esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa lɛ blɛoo. Yɛ hulutsoo be fioo shishi loo yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli.

english: Which local crops give us the most energy when we make them into food or drinks?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ haa wɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ kɛ́ afee amɛ niyenii loo nii ni anuɔ?

english: Grain crops like maize, rice, millet, and sorghum are rich in carbohydrates that supply high body energy. Processing them into milled porridge or fermented drinks breaks down complex starches, making the energy easily available to your body.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa mli tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ carbohydrates ni haa gbɔmɔtso lɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ashã loo nii ni anuɔ ni edɔ lɛ, efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa lɛ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ ni enáa hewalɛ

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil or go moldy so quickly when I store it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ loo ehiɛɔ oya kɛji mikpa lɛ?

english: Maize spoils when stored with too much moisture or placed directly on damp ground. Sun-drying the corn until the kernels sound hard and metallic when dropped ensures moisture levels are low enough to stop mold growth.
ga: Abɛi baafite kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli loo akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Abɛi ni agbiɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaafee dade kɛji akɛ amɛshwie shi Enɛ baaha hulutsoo be lɛ aya shi bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ akakwɛ̃.

english: What simple steps can I take at home to protect my stored grains from insect damage?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Mɛni abaanyɛ afee yɛ shia koni akɛbu ŋmaa ni ato lɛ he koni kooloi akafite?

english: Clean your storehouse completely, ensure grains are completely dry, and seal them tightly inside hermetic (airtight) bags or drums, which deprives insects of air and stops them from breeding.
ga: Tsumɔ onitoohe lɛ he kwraa. Kwɛmɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ agbi kwraa. ni okɛwo kotoku loo baagi ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni no baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa ni ebaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafɔ.

english: Why do weevils attack my stored maize even when I keep it inside a dry room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ tsu ko ni mli egbi mli moŋ?

english: Weevil eggs often come from the field inside the corn husks before you even bring the crop home. Shelling the corn promptly and storing it in sealed bags stops these eggs from hatching and destroying your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii akui jɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli dani okɛ ŋmãa lɛ po baa shia. Kɛ́ otsi ŋmãa lɛ he tsɔi amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni okɛwo kotoku ko mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmãa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ̃ ni efite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How can I tell if the seed rice I want to plant will produce good yields in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni misumɔɔ ni madu lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Good yield starts with certified seed varieties that are suited to your area's soil and rainfall. Look for sealed, labeled seed packages from accredited dealers, and check that the seeds are uniform, clean, and free from insect damage or disease spots.
ga: Yibiiwoo kpakpa jeɔ shishi kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni awo he odaseyeli ni sa kɛha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ. Taomɔ dumɔwui ni atsĩ naa ni aŋmala nɔ nii kɛjɛ jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ. ni okwɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ebɔle amɛhe, amɛhe tse, ni kooloi loo helai efiteee amɛhe.

english: Why do buyers prefer buying long-grain rice varieties over other types?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmãa ni mli edɔ fe ŋmãa srɔtoi krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Long-grain rice varieties stay separate, light, and fluffy after cooking, which is what many households and commercial food vendors in Ghana look for when making popular dishes like Jollof.
ga: Ajaraa ŋmãa kakadaŋŋ mli, ni eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni ahoo lɛ sɛɛ, ni no ji nɔ ni shia kɛ jarayeli niyenii ni jarayelɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ taoɔ kɛ́ amɛmiifee niyenii ni ehe gbɛi tamɔ Jollof.

english: Why are my rice plants producing many empty or light grains instead of heavy ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tso lɛ woɔ dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛ nɔ ko loo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni tsii najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Empty grains usually happen when the plant lacks water or fertilizer during the flowering stage, or if high temperatures and insect pests damage the flowers before the grains can fill up properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kpata fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ dani dumɔwui lɛ eyi mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: What makes a rice plant produce many stems and grain heads from a single seed?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa tso ko woɔ ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui ayitsei babaoo kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu kome mli lɛ?

english: This process is called tillering. Rice plants produce more stems when seedlings are transplanted at the right young age, given enough spacing, and fed with nitrogen fertilizer early in their growth.
ga: Atsɛɔ gbɛ nɛɛ akɛ tillering. Omɔ tsei lɛ baawo ŋmeii babaoo kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi. Kɛ jɛkɛmɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii kɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dalɛ be lɛ mli

english: Why are the leaves of my young rice crop turning yellow instead of remaining deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are typically a sign that your crop is hungry for nitrogen fertilizer or that the soil is waterlogged with poor drainage, which prevents the roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia onibii loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Why do so many of my rice grains break into small pieces when they are milled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ fãa bibii bibii kɛ́ mikɛmiitsu nii lɛ?

english: Rice grains break easily during milling if the crop was left too long in the sun to dry on the field before harvest, or if the grain was dried too quickly at very high heat after harvesting.
ga: Omɔ ŋmaa lɛ fãa oya yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi tsei yɛ hulutsoo be mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ koni amɛgbi yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani akpa, loo kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩ oya tsɔ kɛ la ni mli wa waa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my rice to get high-quality grains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa koni maná ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Your rice is ready for harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grain heads turn golden-yellow, and the grains at the base of the head feel firm rather than soft or milky.
ga: O-rice lɛ efee klalo akɛ obaakpa beni dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ amli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 batsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ lɛ. Ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee bɔdɔɔ loo amɛfee tamɔ mliki.

english: What causes black spots and discoloration on my rice grains before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii diji kɛ su ni tsakeɔ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii anɔ dani akpaa lɛ baa?

english: Discolored grains are usually caused by fungal diseases or sap-sucking insects like stink bugs that attack the grain heads while they are still young and soft.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii helai loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii ni tutuaa dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ darako ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni etsake amɛhe lɛ baa.

english: How dry does my harvested rice need to be before I package it in bags for sale?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikpamɔ lɛ agbi aha tɛŋŋ dani abaanyɛ akɛwo kotoku mli koni ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Your rice grains should be dried until they reach about 12 to 14 percent moisture content, which feels hard when you bite a grain; if bagged while damp, mold and heat will spoil the whole bag.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ o-rice ŋmeii lɛ agbi kɛyashi amɛbaafee aaafee oha mlijaa 12 kɛyashi 14, ni no baaha onu he waa kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwie ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ awo kotoku lɛ mli be mli ni edɔ lɛ, Mold kɛ dɔlɛ baanyɛ afite kotoku lɛ.

english: How should I store bagged rice in my storehouse so that pests do not destroy it?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ ŋmãa kotokui awo nitoohe lɛ koni ŋmeii akafite lɛ?

english: Stack the bags on raised wooden pallets rather than directly on the bare floor, keep them away from walls to allow air flow, and ensure the room is dry, clean, and sealed against rats and weevils.
ga: Okɛ kotokui awo tsei ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ. Okɛ kotoku lɛ awo he ko ni kɛ gbogboi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli. Ni kwɛmɔ akɛ tsu lɛ mli egbi, ehe tse, ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akabote mli.

english: Can I use the sweet white juice that drips from freshly opened cocoa pods on my farm to help my crops grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu yɛŋ ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni agbele ehee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: The sweet liquid from cocoa pods is rich in sugars and acids. While it contains nutrients, pouring raw, unfermented juice directly onto soil can attract pests like ants and make the soil too acidic, so it is better used for local food or drink processing rather than as direct crop fertilizer.
ga: Nu ni ŋɔɔ ni jɛɔ kookoo ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ sugar kɛ acid. Eyɛ mli akɛ niyenii mli nibii yɛ moŋ Nu ni mli edɔ ni afɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbala kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛtsu nii akɛ maŋ lɛ mli niyenii loo nibii ni anuɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni akɛbaatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Is it possible to cook and eat fresh cocoa beans at home like regular garden vegetables?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ aho ni aye cocoa ŋmeii heei yɛ shia tamɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii krokomɛi fɛɛ?

english: Fresh, raw cocoa beans are extremely bitter and tough because of natural chemicals called tannins. To make cocoa edible or good for cooking, the beans must first undergo fermentation and drying to break down the bitterness and develop a sweet, chocolate flavor.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni afee lɛ ehee lɛ mli edɔ waa ni amɛhe wa ejaakɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni atsɛɔ amɛ tannins lɛ yɛ mli. Kɛji oosumɔ ni cocoa afee nɔ ni ayeɔ loo akɛtsu nii yɛ niyenii homɔ mli. Esa akɛ afee kɔfe yibii klɛŋklɛŋ ni agbi koni ejie ŋmɔlɔ ni ená ŋmɔlɔ, tamɔ tsokolate.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa crop is healthy and producing good pods without cutting every pod open?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii kpakpai ni mifooo ŋmeii fɛɛ ni agbele lɛ?

english: Healthy cocoa trees produce firm, brightly colored pods—changing smoothly from green to yellow, or red to orange—with smooth outer skins free of black patches, insect holes, or soft spots.
ga: Cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse, ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsakeɔ mlɛo kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ mli. loo etsuru kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ Eyɛ kponɔgbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ diji, kooloi bibii, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo bɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of the tiny flowers on my cocoa trunk drop off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands more flowers than they can feed. Only flowers visited by tiny insects called midges get pollinated, and the tree drops extra flowers to save its energy for growing strong pods.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ, ni fa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Fɔfɔi ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ saraa lɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Ni tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii krokomɛi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do small green cocoa pods on my tree turn black and shrivel up before they get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ ji Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This usually happens because of a damp-weather fungal disease called Black Pod, or because the tree naturally sheds extra pods (called cherelle wilt) when it does not have enough water or nutrients to support them all.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pods lɛ hewɔ. aloo akɛni tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ hewɔ Amɛnáa hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherry wilt (ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherry wilt) beni nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua amɛ fɛɛ lɛ bɛ.

english: How do I know if the soil on my land is good enough to plant cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ kookoo tsei anɔ?

english: Cocoa trees need deep, soft forest soil that holds moisture well but lets extra water drain away easily. If water stays pooled on top of your land for days after rain, the cocoa roots will rot and die.
ga: Koo mli shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ shi ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia koo tsei. Kɛji nu hi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛ sɛɛ. Cocoa shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaagboi.

english: What happens if I plant my cocoa young trees too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: When planted too close, cocoa trees fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Their branches also block airflow, creating humid shade where fungal diseases spread quickly and reduce your yield.
ga: Kɛ adu Cocoa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛniji lɛ hu tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. creating moist shade He ni tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni ehaa onibii ni onáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Will cutting off extra branches and leaves help my cocoa tree produce more pods?
ga: Ani niji kɛ baai krokomɛi ni afolɔ lɛ baaye abua cacao tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Yes, gentle pruning lets sunlight reach the main trunk and improves air movement through the tree. This reduces fungal diseases and encourages the tree to produce more flowering spots on the trunk where pods grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni afoɔ blɛoo lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ titri lɛ he, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni efee fɔfɔii babaoo yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do we cover freshly harvested cocoa beans with plantain leaves for a few days before drying them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔkɛ plantain baai haa kookoo yibii ni akpa ehee lɛ anɔ gbii fioo komɛi dani wɔgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering wet beans with leaves traps heat and starts fermentation. This natural process kills the seed inside, removes bitter flavors, and gives the cocoa bean its rich brown chocolate color and sweet smell.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ baai ha ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaamɔ la lɛ mli ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ nɛɛ gbeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ejieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, tamɔ tsokolate ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Does heavy rainfall help my cocoa trees make bigger pods, or can too much rain harm the farm?
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa ŋmeii wuji. Aloo ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aye ŋmɔ lɛ awui?

english: Cocoa trees need good rain to grow big pods, but constant heavy rain and high humidity cause fungal diseases like Black Pod to multiply and destroy the crop before it ripens.
ga: Nugbɔ kpakpa he miihia kookoo tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa ŋmeii helai, tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ feɔ babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii dani amɛdaraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and dry when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are very sensitive to direct sunlight. Without shade trees or quick-growing nurse crops like plantains planted nearby to block the harsh sun, the young leaves burn and the plant struggles to grow.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains bɛ lɛ, dumɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo koni obu ohe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Baai bibii lɛ shãa ni tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda.

english: Yam vines need to climb high off the ground so their leaves can spread out to catch sunlight. If the leaves stay on the shaded ground, the plant cannot produce enough energy to feed and expand the yam tuber under the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ ajie hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃ amɛ sweet potato tubers lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with many leaves, but the tubers under the ground are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa tsɔ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are crowded, the cassava spends all its strength expanding its top stems and green leaves instead of transferring nutrients downward into the root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Kasava lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛha eŋwɛi tso lɛ kɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ akwɛ̃. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ kɛya shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: What causes the lower leaves of my maize crop to turn yellow in a V-shape along the center?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni V su yɔɔ teŋgbɛ?

english: Yellowing along the main stem of older maize leaves is a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food the plant needs to build strong stems and green leaves.
ga: Abɛi baai ni egbɔ lɛ ashishifãi titrii lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help my maize crop grow better afterwards?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts have natural helpers in their roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acting as natural fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ adebɔɔ mli yelikɛbualɔi yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the crop experiences extreme heat or dry soil, or when small insects attack the delicate stem that attaches the flower to the plant.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he loo shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua tsei bibii ni kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he lɛ.

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes happen when the plant cannot pull up enough calcium from the soil, which usually occurs when watering is irregular and the soil dries out too quickly between rains.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ.

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to hide their leaf surface from the sun and stop water from evaporating out of the plant when it gets hot and dry.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛteeɔ baa lɛ hiɛ kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. ni etsĩ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa kɛ́ edɔ ni egbi.

english: Why should I cut away the small suckers growing at the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plantain tree for food and water from the soil. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main stem gets enough strength to produce a heavy bunch.
ga: Tsobii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso ni tsii.

english: Why does my swamp rice turn yellow and stop growing when deep water covers the leaves completely for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekpaa dalɛ beni nu ni mli kwɔ ha baai lɛ ahe kwraa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Even though swamp rice needs wet soil, its green leaves still need sunlight and air to breathe. Being completely underwater for too long suffocates the plant and prevents it from making food.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋshɔ mli ŋmãa biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ moŋ Shi ebaai eŋɔli lɛ he miihia hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lolo koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ tso lɛ hi nu shishi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ehaaa ehoo nii.

english: What is pollination, and why does my crop need it to produce fruits?
ga: Mɛni ji pollination? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa midumɔ nii lɛ koni ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pollination is the transfer of pollen to the sticky female part of a flower called the stigma. It is essential because without pollen reaching the stigma, the flower cannot produce seeds or develop into fruit.
ga: Pollination ji pollen ni akɛyaa fɔfɔi lɛ yoo fã ni wa ni atsɛɔ lɛ stigma lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ejaakɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui loo amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Can I pollinate my flowers by hand if there are no insects on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi nine awo fɔfɔi amli pollination kɛji kooloi bɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can manually touch or transfer pollen directly to the flower's stigma. This hand-pollination helps ensure your crops produce fruit even when natural pollinators like bees are absent.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ onine ata loo okɛ pollen aya fɔfɔi lɛ ahe muji lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Nɛkɛ nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli nɛɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii. Eyɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ moŋ.

english: Which part of the flower do I need to touch if I am helping my plants pollinate?
ga: Mɛɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fãi esa akɛ mata he kɛji miyeɔ mibuaa tso ko ni ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli?

english: You need to touch the stigma, which is the female central part of the flower designed to receive pollen so the plant can start making fruit.
ga: Esa akɛ ota stigma, ni ji fɔfɔi lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni afee koni enine ashɛ pollen nɔ lɛ he, bɔni afee ni tso lɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Why do some of my flowers drop off the plant without ever growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi fɔfɔi lɛ ekomɛi miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers often drop off when pollen fails to land on the stigma. If proper pollination does not occur, the flower cannot complete fertilization and the plant sheds it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ pollen lɛ nyɛɛɛ akpɛtɛ stigma lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔmɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ afee fɔfɔi lɛ kwraa. ni tso lɛ baafite lɛ.

english: Does a flower instantly turn into a fruit right after it gets pollinated?
ga: Ani fɔfɔii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli?

english: No, fruit formation is not instant. After pollen touches the stigma, the plant must first go through fertilization, which takes several days before fruit development begins.
ga: Dabi, yibiiwoo baaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Beni pollen lɛ kɛ muji lɛ ekpe sɛɛ lɛ Esa akɛ awo tso lɛ mli nu klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ heɔ gbii babaoo dani nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: How many days does fertilization take after pollen touches the flower?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ fɔmɔ heɔ beni pollen lɛ eshɛ fɔfɔi lɛ he sɛɛ?

english: After pollination occurs on the stigma, it takes about six to seven days for fertilization to complete inside the flower.
ga: Beni pollination baa yɛ stigma lɛ sɛɛ. Aaafee gbii enumɔ kɛyashi kpawo dani fɔmɔ nii ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ baagbe naa.

english: How long after pollination will I actually see young fruits appearing on my crops?
ga: Be enyiɛ yɛ pollination sɛɛ mana aduawai bibii ni jeɔ kpo yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: It typically takes about 6 weeks after successful pollination for the small, young fruits to physically appear on the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee otsii 6 beni agbe pollination naa lɛ sɛɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, aduawai bibii bibii baaje kpo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my hand pollination attempt worked?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mɔdɛŋ ni mibɔɔ koni mikɛ minine awo mli lɛ miitsu nii?

english: You will know hand pollination was successful when tiny fruits begin to visibly emerge on the stem, which usually happens around 6 weeks after you touch pollen to the stigma.
ga: Obaale akɛ nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ eye omanye kɛ́ aduawai bibii lɛ je kpo. Eje shishi eeje kpo faŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa aaafee otsii 6 sɛɛ beni okɛ pollen ekpe lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How many months does it take for fruits to fully mature after pollination?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ yɛ pollination sɛɛ?

english: Once pollination and fertilization occur, it takes about 3 to 4 months for the fruits to mature completely and become ready for harvest.
ga: Kɛji pollination kɛ fertilization ba Ebaahe aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 dani aduawai lɛ baakwɛ̃ kwraa ni efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: How long is the entire journey from pollination day to the day I can harvest my mature fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ gbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ gbi ni manyɛ makpa aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: The full cycle takes between 3 to 4 months from the day pollination finishes, during which fertilization happens in week one, tiny fruits show at 6 weeks, and full maturity is reached by month four.
ga: Nɔ ni fe fɛɛ lɛ heɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 kɛjɛɔ gbi ni pollination lɛ baa naagbee lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni fɔmɔ baa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsi lɛ mli lɛ, aduawai bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ otsii 6 mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ nyɔŋ ni ji ejwɛ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my farm's soil has enough natural strength to grow healthy cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Strong, fertile soil for cocoa is usually dark in color, rich in decayed plant leaves, holds moisture well without getting waterlogged, and feels soft and crumbly when you scoop it up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii kɛha kookoo lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Eyɛ tsei ahe baai ni fiteɔ babaoo Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli. Ni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔlɔ shwie nɔ.

english: What causes my soil to lose its power after farming it for several years?
ga: Mɛni haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ afii babaoo ni mikɛtsu nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Continuous harvesting takes nutrients out of the earth. Rain can also wash away topsoil, and without adding organic matter like leaves or fertilizer, the soil naturally gets tired and loses strength.
ga: Nikpamɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ baanyɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ hu kɛya. Ni kɛji akɛ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ he feɔ shoo ni ehewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Can I rebuild the strength of my land if it has become weak and tired?
ga: Ani manyɛ matswa mishikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛji egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ?

english: Yes, you can restore soil strength by adding compost or animal manure, keeping shade trees to drop leaves, planting cover crops, and applying the right fertilizers recommended for cocoa.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ oha oshikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Ha tso lɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo mli koni baai lɛ akagbee shi. ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ adumɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa atsu nii taakɛ atsɔɔ akɛ afee kookoo lɛ.

english: If I get a larger piece of land, does that automatically mean I will harvest more cocoa?
ga: Kɛji minine shɛ shikpɔŋ ni da nɔ lɛ Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ makpa kookoo babaoo yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mihe?

english: Not necessarily. A smaller piece of rich, healthy soil that is well cared for can yield far more cocoa pods than a huge plot of weak or poor-quality land.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Shikpɔŋ bibioo ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baa nii. Shikpɔji ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo ŋmeii babaoo aba fe shikpɔji wuji ni shikpɔji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo nɔ ni ehiii yɔɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do crops grow very well on my neighbor's farm, but poorly on my plot right next to it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Shi eefite kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ minɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Soil quality can change even within short distances due to differences in topsoil depth, water drainage, past farming practices, and how much natural organic matter is in the earth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su baanyɛ atsake yɛ gbɛ kukuji po amli. Nɔ ni ha ebalɛ nakai ji bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli kwɔ ha, nu ni hoɔ, kɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni eho lɛ. ni adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ je lɛŋ lɛ ayibɔ hu yɛ srɔto.

english: Why is cocoa grown in Ghana so famous around the world compared to cocoa from other places?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ni aduɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ehe gbɛi waa yɛ je lɛŋ he fɛɛ he kɛ akɛto kookoo ni jɛɔ hei krokomɛi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Ghana has a unique combination of rich forest soils, tropical rainfall, and ideal temperatures that feed cocoa trees the right balance of nutrients, giving the beans high butter content and rich flavor.
ga: Ghana yɛ koo mli shikpɔji ni baa nii ni yɔɔ srɔto kwraa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa, ni yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tso lɛ ni enáa niyenii kpakpai ni sa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bɔta ni fa babaoo, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does cocoa seem to require stronger soil than crops like cassava or maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa he hiaa kookoo fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a long-term tree crop that produces nutrient-rich pods year after year, so its roots need deep, rich soil with a constant supply of minerals to sustain it over many decades.
ga: Cocoa ji tso ko ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni woɔ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii afi fɛɛ afi. No hewɔ lɛ, eshishifãi lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii. kɛ shika tsuru ni akɛbaatsu nii be fɛɛ be koni akɛkwɛ nɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce plenty of flowers but only a few of them turn into big pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi fioo pɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni feɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: If the soil lacks enough nutrients or water, the tree cannot support all the flowers and will drop them to save its energy for the few pods it can nourish.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ. ni ebaashɛrɛ lɛ ashwie koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha pods fioo ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ amɛ lɛ.

english: How do shade trees help keep the soil strong for my cocoa plants?
ga: Te tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ aha mi cacao tsei lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Shade trees block harsh sunlight that dries out the ground, and their falling leaves rot into the soil to create rich humus that feeds the cocoa roots naturally.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa. Ni tso lɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee humus ni fa babaoo ni haa kookoo shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ.

english: How do heavy rains affect the nutrients inside my farm's soil?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa niyenii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away the top layer of rich soil or push nutrients down too deep where young roots cannot reach them, especially on clear-cut fields with no tree cover.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ loo ekɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aya shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ hei ni tsei bɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do people say I should spray my farm early in the morning instead of in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ leebi moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: In the afternoon, the sun's heat causes liquid sprays to evaporate quickly into the air before the plants can absorb them. Spraying very early in the morning when it is cool allows the chemical to stay on the leaves longer and work effectively.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ haa nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai lɛ shwie nɔ leebi be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ, ebaaha tsofai lɛ ahi tsei lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ ni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it safe to spray my crops late in the evening when the sun goes down?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaashwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ gbɛkɛ beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yes, late evening is an excellent time to spray. The air is cool and calm, which prevents the spray from evaporating quickly, and it gives the chemical all night to stick to the plants without intense sunlight breaking it down.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛkɛ ji be kpakpa ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa nɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni eyɛ dioo. Enɛ haaa nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsɔ oya. ni ehaa tsofai lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ efiteee lɛ.

english: How early in the morning should I ideally be on the farm to start spraying?
ga: Te esa akɛ maya ŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi maŋkpa tɛŋŋ koni mabɔi tsofa lɛ shwiemɔ?

english: It is best to start very early around 5:30 AM before the sun rises fully. At this time, the temperatures are low and the air is calm, making it the perfect condition for chemical application.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooje shishi leebi maŋkpa, aaafee 5:30 AM, dani hulu lɛ ateshi kwraa. Amrɔ nɛɛ hulutsoo be lɛ eba shi ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu efee dioo. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baa.

english: What actually happens to my crops if I spray chemicals on them under the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai shwie nɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi?

english: Spraying under hot sun can cause severe heat stress and leaf burn on your crops. Liquid droplets on leaves act like magnifying glasses under strong sunlight, scorching the plant while wasting your chemical through fast evaporation.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi ni oooshwie nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dɔlɛ mli haomɔ ni naa wa kɛ baai ashã yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Nu ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni ashãa yɛ be mli ni afiteɔ tsofai kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya lɛ nɔ

english: Why does wind speed matter when I am spraying my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ oyaiyeli he hiaa beni mikɛ tsofa shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Strong breezes carry the chemical droplets away from your farm onto unintended areas or onto yourself. Spraying early in the morning or late in the evening usually has calm air, ensuring the spray lands directly on your targeted crops.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ kɛ tsofai ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hei ni osusuuu he loo ebaa onɔ. Bei pii lɛ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ mli jɔɔ. Enɛ haa tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baagbee tsei ni okɛmamɔ ohiɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Will the early morning dew on my crop leaves wash away my farm spray?
ga: Ani leebi ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ baatsumɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: A light morning dew actually helps spread liquid spray evenly across leaf surfaces. As long as it is not heavy rain, spraying early allows the plant to absorb the medicine as the dew gradually dries.
ga: Leebi ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ gbɛɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ eshwaa baa lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shii abɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ waa Mra ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aŋɔ tsofa lɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi fiofio lɛ.

english: How does spraying early in the morning help if afternoon rains come?
ga: Te tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ baaye abua aha tɛŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ shwane?

english: Spraying very early gives the plant several hours during the morning to absorb the chemical completely. By the time typical afternoon rain showers arrive, the treatment has already entered the plant and won't be washed away.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aŋɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo leebi ni ekɛ tsofai lɛ atsu nii kwraa. No mli lɛ, nugbɔ nɛ shwane mli tamɔ bɔ ni efeɔ daa lɛ. Tsofa lɛ ebote tso lɛ mli ni anyɛɛɛ afɔ he.

english: Do crop leaves absorb farm sprays better at certain times of the day?
ga: Ani tsei ahe baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔɔ ŋmɔ mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli?

english: Yes, plants have tiny pores on their leaves called stomata that open up in the cool early morning to breathe. Spraying at this time allows the leaves to take in systemic fertilizers and pesticides much faster.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ baai ni atsɛɔ amɛ stomata lɛ nɔ Enɛ gbeleɔ ehe yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛmu. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa baai lɛ naa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi oya yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo naa.

english: Why do I see more destructive pests on my farm in the evening than during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi ni fiteɔ nii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbɛkɛ fe gbi lɛ?

english: Many farm insects hide from the hot daytime heat under soil or thick leaves and come out to feed when temperatures cool down in the evening. Spraying in the evening targets these pests when they are most active.
ga: Okwaafoi amli kooloi babaoo teeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ he yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo yɛ tsei ahe tsei amli. ni amɛje kpo amɛbaye niyenii beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ. Gbi gbɛkɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛtsuɔ nii waa lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves get burnt after I spray them with pesticides?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie amɛnɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf burning usually happens when chemical sprays are applied during peak sunshine hours. Applying chemicals early in the morning or late evening prevents this damage and keeps your crop leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe tsei ashãa kɛ́ akɛ tsofai shwie shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai wo tso lɛ mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa, ni ebaaye ebua ni otso lɛ baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. They require shade trees or fast-growing companion crops like plantains planted beside them to provide shade and trap moisture until the young trees are strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo nanemɛi tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni ekɛ hulutsoo aha ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi tsei bibii lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: When is the right time for me to plant my maize so the rain does not ruin my crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu ŋmãa koni nugbɔ akafite miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: In southern and central Ghana, there are two rainy seasons. The major planting season begins around April after the early rains settle the ground, while the minor season starts around August or September. Planting at the beginning of these rainy windows gives the seeds enough moisture to germinate and grow.
ga: Ghana wuoyigbɛ kɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ bei enyɔ. Be titri ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ April aaafee beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ eha jɛmɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ be mli ni be ni ji enyɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ August loo September aaafee lɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ samflɛ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and skinny even when the leaves on top grow huge?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii lolo ni amɛhe ejɔ eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ dara moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are placed too close together, cassava puts all its energy into growing tall leaves instead of tubers. Proper spacing and balanced soil nutrients encourage the plant to send its food underground to swell the cassava roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kakadaji yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ niyenii majeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni ewo ŋmei shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do I need to clear the ground and stake my yam vines with sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie he ko ni mikɛ tsei adu sweet potato wain tsei lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves up toward the sun to make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, which prevents fungal diseases and allows maximum light exposure, helping the underground yam tuber grow larger.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ko ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ nɔ koni efee niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa ni eha mɔ aná hela babaoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my main crops help my farm grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ ni edaa?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. This enriches the soil with natural fertilizer that surrounding plants like maize can feed on.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmli amɛjieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsei ni ebɔle ehe, tamɔ ŋmãa baanyɛ aye nii.

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana. They hide deep inside the funnel of the plant leaf, so applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem water early in the morning reaches them before they destroy the growing point of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akɛ amɛ ewo tsei ahe baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo neem nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛtsu nii leebi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe dani amɛfiteɔ hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off before any fruits show up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist by mulching and watering regularly prevents the plant from dropping its flowers due to water shock.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ba kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkafo amɛhe yɛ nu afua hewɔ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra small shoots growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ eje kpo.

english: When too many suckers grow around one main plantain stem, they steal nutrients and water from the parent plant. Pruning away weaker shoots leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the main stem to produce a big, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ Amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo ŋmeii bibii lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baashi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha ŋmeii titri lɛ awo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why is it helpful for me to spread dry grass around the roots of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ pepper shishifãi ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass is called mulching. It acts as a blanket that protects the soil from hot sun, keeps moisture in the ground longer during dry spells, and stops weeds from taking over around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni ekaha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Should I put fertilizer on my crops when the ground is dry or after it rains?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?
