english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist after a light rain. If applied on dry, hot soil, chemical fertilizers can burn the plant roots or evaporate, and heavy downpours can wash the fertilizer completely away before plants can absorb it.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni mli edɔ nɔ Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi ashã loo amɛtsɔ la. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii dani tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nutrients, especially nitrogen, or they are getting too much or too little water. When the soil lacks food, the plant pulls nutrients from its lower leaves to feed the growing corn ears, causing those leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. titri lɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo loo fioo ni anáa Beni niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋmãa toi ni miida lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa nakai baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat, lack of consistent watering, or poor pollination. If the plant feels stressed by weather conditions, it drops its flowers to save energy rather than trying to feed a developing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo pollination ni ehiii Kɛji tso lɛ miinu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii

english: Why do my pepper plants stop producing new fruits during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ yibii heei yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants enter a resting phase when water is scarce because forming fruits requires a lot of water. Without enough soil moisture, the plant saves its energy just to stay alive until the rains return or irrigation is provided.
ga: Pepper tsei boteɔ shihilɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ mli beni nu faaa lɛ ejaakɛ aduawai ni anáa lɛ biɔ nu babaoo. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ toɔ hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi kɛkɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ loo abaaha amɛ nu.

english: Why do some crops in my field grow very tall while others right next to them stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ shɔɔŋ nɛkɛ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ darako lolo.

english: Crops grow unevenly when soil nutrients, organic matter, or water are not spread equally across the land. Small crops are usually competing with hidden weeds, standing in harder soil, or lacking the nutrients that the bigger plants managed to reach first.
ga: Tsei lɛ daraaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, loo nu lɛ ejaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bibii kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ ni damɔ shi loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni tsei wuji baanyɛ aná klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ bɛ mli

english: How can I make my cassava plants grow bigger roots instead of just growing lots of leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-cassava tso lɛ aná shishifãi wuji moŋ fe baai babaoo kɛkɛ?

english: Cassava roots grow thick and heavy when the soil is loose, well-drained, and rich in potassium. If the soil has too much nitrogen from animal manure or certain fertilizers, the plant spends all its energy growing tall stems and leafy tops instead of tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse. Etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni potassium eyi mli obɔ Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo ni jɛ kooloi aŋmei loo ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi amli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How does letting weeds grow in my farm reduce the amount of food I get at harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mahã jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm by taking water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your main crops. When crops have to fight weeds for survival, they grow weaker and produce fewer or smaller fruits.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Be ni esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi awuu koni amɛhi shi Amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ loo amɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the exact time my yam tubers are mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Yam tubers are ready for full harvest when the green leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up naturally. This signals that the plant has finished storing all its energy underground in the tuber and has stopped growing.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kwraa kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ beni baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ e-bulbs lɛ amli ni ekpa dalɛ.

english: Why do insects attack and ruin my stored grains so quickly after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa ni amɛfiteɔ miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ oya nɛkɛ beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects thrive in stored grain if the seeds are not fully dried before storage. Moist grain creates a warm, humid environment that attracts pests and helps insect eggs hatch, allowing them to multiply and feed on your crop.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ anɔ kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto. Dumɔwui ni mli efɔ lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ, ni mli efɔ ni gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi awui ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ. Ha amɛfɔ ni amɛye onibii.

english: Why do my harvested plantains turn soft and spoil so fast before I can carry them to sell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya dani manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains release a natural gas called ethylene as they ripen, which speeds up the ripening of all fruits around them. Leaving harvested bunches in hot sunlight or stacked together traps this heat and gas, causing them to spoil rapidly.
ga: Dares jieɔ adebɔɔ mli la ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha aduawai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ akwɛ̃ oya. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo akɛto amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same plot every year make my harvest smaller each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season without giving the land time to rebuild. It also allows specific pests and diseases that love maize to live in the soil permanently and attack new plants.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛma ekoŋŋ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ hu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa ni amɛtutuaa tsei heei.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate tender leaves and short roots that cannot handle strong, direct heat. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees to block harsh sunlight and keep the soil moist while their roots grow deep enough to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Bɔni afee ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize are usually a sign that the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build strong green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore the green color and improves plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni eha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans on my land make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that can take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it inside the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth, acting as natural food for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okpa amɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars chewing holes into the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are known as Fall Armyworms, and they target the soft, growing heart of the corn plant. Catching them early and applying organic treatments like neem leaf extract or safe recommended pesticides directly into the plant funnel stops them from destroying the crop.
ga: Ale nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ Fall Armyworms, ni amɛtutua ŋmeii tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni miida lɛ atsuii lɛ. Ni aaamɔ amɛ mra ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi yɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛya dumɔ gbɛ lɛ nɔ. Ebaatsi amɛnaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward and stop growing leaves properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa baai lɛ adalɛ kpakpa lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that transmit plant viruses. Controlling these insects early using soapy water sprays or wood ash deters them and keeps new foliage growing flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Nu ni akɛ samla loo tso mli sũ tsuɔ nii lɛ baatsi amɛnaa ni eye ebua baai heei ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the ground after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water suffocates them by cutting off air in the soil. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or high ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the roots safe in dry, aerated soil.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi, ni ekɛ mumɔ baa kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajo foi kɛya. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it better to water my vegetable garden early in the morning rather than at noon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooofɔ aduawai abɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu leebi fe shwane mli lɛ?

english: Watering in the afternoon heat causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the plant roots can drink it. Morning watering lets the soil absorb moisture slowly so the crop stays hydrated through the hottest part of the day.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli leebi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu fiofio koni eha tso lɛ aná nu yɛ gbi lɛ mli be fɛɛ ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: When crops are crowded, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited water, soil nutrients, and light. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets its own space to gather light and food, resulting in bigger fruits and stronger stalks.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ la ni faaa He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ tsu fɛɛ tsu mli lɛ buaa kane kɛ niyenii naa. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ feɔ wuji ni amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ahe waa.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in the sunshine to produce energy that builds big tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the vines off the wet ground, exposing leaves to sunlight and preventing ground rots and diseases from spreading.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã hulu la lɛ mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii wuji baa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ aba. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. ha baai lɛ aya hulu la nɔ ni otsi shikpɔŋ ni fiteɔ kɛ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ anaa.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or erratic watering. Keeping the soil consistently damp by covering the root area with dry grass mulch keeps the plant cool and helps flowers stay attached long enough to produce tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni oookɛha shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ koni eha tso lɛ mli ajɔ ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ he be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛwo tomato.

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, it usually means your maize is lacking nitrogen or the soil is waterlogged. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or NPK early helps the leaves stay green and produce bigger corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK wo mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ adara.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains specific soil nutrients and allows maize-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally restores fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi baa shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aku sɛɛ aba ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amli.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable crops in the early morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering in the early morning is best because cooler temperatures let water soak deep into the soil where roots can drink. Watering in the hot afternoon causes water to evaporate quickly before plants can use it.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ yɛ lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya dani tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the trees during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, overly shaded farms. Pruning dense branches and clearing weeds lets sunlight and air flow through to dry the farm and reduce the disease.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Niji ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking leaf sap and spreading plant viruses. Spraying a neem seed extract solution or appropriate insect control protects young leaves from these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ neem dumɔwui amli nu loo tsofa ni sa ni akɛbaagbe kooloi ahe lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe.

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater sits around them for too long in flat, heavy soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu ebɔle amɛhe. Etsɛ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Young cocoa seedlings get burned easily under harsh, direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have broad leaves that act like umbrellas, providing necessary shade and moisture while the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ latsaa be mli ni kookoo daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants get stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping soil consistently moist with mulch and planting in the right season helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli edɔ be fɛɛ be, ni adu yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and yield poorly when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are overcrowded, roots fight each other for soil nutrients and water, while leaves fight for sunlight. Giving seeds proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed and produce full yields.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fa tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi wuɔ yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ he. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ kɛ hulu la miitswa akaŋ Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yam vines need full sunlight to make food that feeds the underground tuber. Staking keeps leaves lifted toward the sun and off the damp soil, reducing leaf diseases and resulting in larger yams.
ga: Hulu ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ afee niyenii. Staking haa anyɛɔ awoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa baa helai shi ni ehaa sweet potatoes ni dara lɛ baa.

english: Why do my harvested maize kernels turn moldy so quickly when I store them in my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize kernels contain high moisture when freshly harvested. If you store them before drying them properly under the sun, the trapped moisture creates a humid environment where mold and fungi thrive, ruining the grain quality.
ga: Abɛi mli ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ ehee. Kɛji okɛto dani ogbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa. he ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become woody and hard to cook when I leave them in the soil for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ tsei ni ewa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers store starch as they grow, but if left in the ground past their peak maturity, the plant uses up its stored starch for energy, leaving behind tough fibers that make the tubers woody and watery.
ga: Kasava shishifã lɛ toɔ starch be mli ni edaa lɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi ebaashɛ dalɛ ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he lɛ, Tsei kɛ ŋmei ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛnáa hewalɛ. ni eshiɔ tsɔji ni wa ni haa ŋmei shishifã lɛ feɔ tso kɛ nu.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start growing shoots even when they are not planted in soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ aduko amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally break their resting period after a few months. When exposed to warmth and air humidity, the tuber uses its internal water and nutrient reserves to sprout new shoots automatically.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baaya hejɔɔmɔ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo kɔɔyɔɔ mli latsaa kɛ latsaa mli lɛ, bulb lɛ kɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ emli lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛ ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why does the skin on my ripe tomatoes crack open right before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ he hewoloi lɛ miigba dani akpa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes crack open when they receive a sudden heavy flow of water after a dry spell. The inside of the fruit expands faster than the skin can stretch, causing the outer skin to burst.
ga: Tomato baatswa kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo nu ni hoɔ oya trukaa lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ mli fãa.

english: Why do my orange trees shed small green fruits before they can grow into big fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni ji eŋɔli lɛ? Dani ebaada ni etsɔ aduawai agbo?

english: Citrus trees drop young fruits when they experience stress from dry weather, poor nutrients, or insect attack. The tree sheds extra fruit to save its energy for survival.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji akɛ amɛkpe shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ahe haomɔ mli. niyenii ni esaaa loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Tsei woɔ yibii krɛdɛɛi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha wala.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep woody roots like traditional trees. Their roots sit close to the soil surface, so when heavy bunches grow at the top, strong winds easily tilt and pull the whole plant out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ tsei krokomɛi. Amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ jwɛi ni mli edɔ ko kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni egbalaa tsei muu fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or by viruses carried by these pests that damage leaf cells and stop normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ baa lɛ nɔ Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli wala yibii lɛ ni ehaa baa lɛ dalɛ ni sa lɛ kpaɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa pods are yellowing because they are ripe or because they are sick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ejaakɛ amɛkwɛ̃ loo hela mɔ amɛ?

english: Ripe cocoa pods turn a smooth bright yellow or orange and remain firm. If a pod turns yellow with brown or black spots and white powder, it is affected by black pod disease, not ripening.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ ni powda yɛŋ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ eji hela ni jɛɔ ŋmeii diji ni eshɛko mli lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and dry up when I put fertilizer right next to their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain concentrated salts. Placing them directly against plant stems sucks water out of the plant roots and burns the stem tissue, which turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaŋɔ nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni eshã tso lɛ shishi fãji lɛ. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are my rice leaves turning yellow even though my field has plenty of standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nu yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo?

english: When water stays stagnant for too long without air movement, or when soil nitrogen washes away, the rice roots drown and cannot breathe. This prevents them from taking up nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Beni nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ tsiii ehe. aloo kɛ́ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ho Omɔ shishifãi lɛ baagbo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Bɔni afee ni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Pawpaw trees can be male, female, or hermaphrodite. Male pawpaw trees only produce flowers to supply pollen and will never bear fruit themselves, while female and hermaphrodite trees are the ones that grow fruit.
ga: Pawpaw tsei baanyɛ afee nuu, yoo, loo nɔ ni kɛ hii feɔ yakayaka nii. Pawpaw tsei ni hii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi kɛha pollen pɛ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwoŋ yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni ji yei kɛ tsei ni kɛ hii feɔ yakayaka nii lɛ baawo yibii.

english: Why does my maize crop have flowers at the very top and silks coming out of the cob lower down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni siliki jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ ŋmei lɛ mli kɛyaa shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Maize plants carry both male and female parts on the same stalk. The top tassel is the male part that drops pollen, and the silk on the cob is the female part that catches the pollen so corn grains can form.
ga: Abele tsei yɛ hii kɛ yei ahe nibii ni yɔɔ tso kome nɔ. Tassels ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ji mɔ ni baajie pollen lɛ ashwie shi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ nɔ. Ni siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ ji yoo lɛ fã ni mɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ koni ŋmei dumɔwui anyɛ afee.

english: Why do my oil palm trees sometimes produce only male flowers for several months without any fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, mu tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii pɛ nyɔji babaoo ni fɔfɔi ko kwraa bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees alternate between male and female flowering cycles depending on water and nutrients. During dry periods or soil stress, the tree produces mostly male flowers to save energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Mu tsei tsakeɔ amɛhe yɛ hii kɛ yei fɔfɔii ahe. Edamɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii anɔ Yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo shikpɔŋ ni haoɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi hii babaoo koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra shoots or suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine loo ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to steal water and nutrients from the main plant. Removing extra suckers leaves just one strong replacement sucker and helps the main tree produce a bigger, heavier bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii kome ni mli wa baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why is it necessary for me to stake my yam vines high off the ground using sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei awo mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch maximum sunlight for food production while keeping the leaves off damp soil, which protects the plant from fungal diseases and helps tubers grow larger underground.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baa lɛ nɔ koni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛha niyenii feemɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akafee nɔ ni sũ ni mli edɔ yɔɔ nɔ. Enɛ buɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ahe helai ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How can I tell if my cassava plants are starting to form tubers underground just by looking at them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tso lɛ miibɔi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii feemɔ kɛtsɔ ekwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: When a cassava plant stops growing straight up and starts branching out naturally into two or three stems, it signals that the plant is shifting its energy toward swelling tubers in the soil.
ga: Beni ŋmei tso lɛ kpa dalɛ ni ebɔi niji enyɔ loo etɛ ŋmɔmɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miitsake hewalɛ kɛmiiya ŋmeii ni efuu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees alongside my newly transplanted young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that create living shade to protect the young cocoa plants until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: What happens to my maize harvest if I plant the seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When maize plants are crowded together, their roots and leaves compete for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks that produce tiny cobs or no grains at all.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii. loo dumɔwui ko kwraa bɛ mli

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant again in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two specific parent lines to yield high crops. Seeds collected from a hybrid harvest lose these high-performing parent traits in the next generation, resulting in uneven growth and lower yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔi akui enyɔ amli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite fɔlɔi asui ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ nɛɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the yellow flowers on my tomato plants falling off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is too hot or water is irregular. High temperatures dry up the pollen, preventing fertilization, which causes the unpollinated flower to fall off instead of forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu lɛ mli ejɔɔɔ. He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa pollen lɛ gĩɔ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni fɔmɔ bɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ yibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Yellow leaves at the base usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for plant growth. When nitrogen is low, the plant steals food from older lower leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tso lɛ dalɛ Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat or dry conditions. High temperatures stress the plant, preventing the flower from getting pollinated and turning into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo shihilɛ ni mli egbi mli. Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Etsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkafee pollination ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when we have heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in the soil without draining away properly, the roots suffocate from lack of oxygen and begin to rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ gbee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieee lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ, ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ.

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly in wet and shady conditions. The fungus attacks the outer skin of the pod, killing it before it can fully mature.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Fuji lɛ tutuaa pod lɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ ni egbeɔ lɛ dani edaa.

english: Why shouldn't I spray chemical pest medicine on my crops during the middle of the hot day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Hot afternoon sunshine causes spray chemicals to evaporate into the air before they can work effectively. The strong heat combined with the chemical can also scorch and burn your leaves.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Dɔlɛ ni akɛ tsofai lɛ fataa he lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni eshã baai lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my okra plants get white powdery spots on them in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi okra tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: That white powder is a fungal disease called powdery mildew. It thrives in warm weather when air humidity is high, especially on plants that are stressed from dry soil conditions.
ga: Pauda yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa yɛ. Titri lɛ yɛ tsei ni shikpɔŋ ni egbi shihilɛ haa amɛhaoɔ lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking plant juices from the leaves, or by a plant virus carried into your field by insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni kooloi kɛyaa oŋmɔji amli lɛ amli

english: Yam plants naturally climb to reach sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the ground with stakes allows them to capture more sunlight, which gives the plant energy to make bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo bulbs wuji.

english: Why does my maize crop fall over easily whenever a small wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over when their roots are shallow or weak. This happens if seeds are planted too close to the surface, if the soil is packed too hard, or if the soil lacks nutrients like potassium.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo amɛhe waaa. Enɛ baa mli kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ niyenii tamɔ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my watermelons crack open on the farm before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miitswa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Watermelons burst open when they take in a large amount of water suddenly after a dry spell. The fruit's inside grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to split.
ga: Watermelon lɛ tswaa kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo nu babaoo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni egbi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ loo lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why is it important for me to plant my crops in straight lines instead of scattering them across the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni magbɛ mashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines gives every plant equal space to grow, ensures sunlight hits all rows evenly, and makes walking through your farm to weed or harvest much easier without damaging your crops.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Enɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ ŋwɛi ŋta fɛɛ ŋta nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni ehaa nyiɛmɔ kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa jwɛi loo kpamɔ lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa ni efiteee oŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: How do I check if my crop rows are straight when marking out my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ akɛ mi tsei lɛ akutsei lɛ ja kɛji mikadi miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: You stretch a long rope between two pegs along your field edge as a baseline guide, then stand at the back end of the line and look straight down it to ensure all inserted pegs align perfectly.
ga: Okɛ kpã kakadaŋŋ ko shwieɔ ŋmeii enyɔ ateŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa koni ekɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔ titri ko aha. No sɛɛ lɛ, damɔ line lɛ sɛɛ ni okwɛ shi tɛ̃ɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fɛɛ ni akɛwo mli lɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers use ropes and pegs to mark out positions before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ kpãai kɛ ŋmeii kadiɔ he ni amɛduɔ nii yɛ lɛ dani amɛduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Ropes and pegs create precise measuring lines across your field so every plant is placed at the exact recommended distance from its neighbor for maximum growth.
ga: Kpãa kɛ ŋtayaai lɛ feɔ susumɔi pɔtɛɛ yɛ oyale lɛ mli fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, akɛ tsei fɛɛ toɔ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛkɛ amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ koni amɛdara babaoo.

english: When crops are crowded together, their roots compete for soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block each other's sunlight, causing weak stems and smaller yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe hulu la lɛ naa Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: How does keeping proper distance between crop rows help plants get enough rainwater?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei akutsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Adequate spacing ensures that rainwater settles evenly in the soil around each plant's root zone rather than being quickly dried out by overcrowded root networks.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso fɛɛ tso shishifã he lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, shishifãi ni mli eyi obɔ fe nine lɛ haa egbiɔ oya.

english: Why do my crops need even sunlight along the entire row to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulu la he hiaa mi tsei lɛ yɛ amɛ line lɛ mli fɛɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Plants use sunlight to make their food through photosynthesis, so straight and properly spaced rows prevent taller leaves from shading out neighboring plants.
ga: Tsei kɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋtayaai ni ja, ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baatsi tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anaa.

english: How does aligning my crop rows properly affect how my farm handles strong winds?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtoɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaná bɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ tsuɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he nii eha lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Straight, well-spaced rows allow air to move through the farm smoothly without trapping strong wind pockets that can snap weak stems or blow down crops.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni ja ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni etsĩii kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni baanyɛ akumɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo eha ŋmɔshi nibii akumɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why is weeding so much easier when I plant my farm in straight rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaaa kwraa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi kɛji midu miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ?

english: Straight rows leave clear pathways between crops so you can move quickly with a cutlass or hoe to cut weeds without accidentally damaging crop stems or roots.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni ja lɛ haa gbɛi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ tsɔne loo tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ aya oya ni okɛ tso lɛ shishifãi loo shishifãi lɛ efiteee yɛ oshara mli.

english: How does planting in straight rows help me spot diseases on my farm early?
ga: Bɔ ni dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni minaa helai mra yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Open and aligned pathways allow clear visibility down every row, making it easy to spot yellowing leaves or pest damage early before problems spread to the rest of the farm.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni agbele ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ haa anaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛkuu fɛɛ sɛɛkuu mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaana baai ni miifee ŋmɔŋ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ mra. dani naagba lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ hei krokomɛi.

english: Will planting my farm in neatly aligned rows actually increase my total harvest?
ga: Ani miŋmɔ lɛ ni mikɛduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ baaha nibii fɛɛ ni mifeɔ lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, because aligned planting prevents crops from choking each other, allowing every single plant to reach its full size and produce more fruit or grain.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ daa lɛ haaa ŋmɔshi nibii akpɛtɛ amɛhe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei fɛɛ ni amɛshɛɔ amɛdalɛ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii loo dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my young corn plants turning yellow at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow strong, so adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the crop recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the corn cobs on my farm not filling completely with kernels to the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Incomplete kernel filling usually happens when the plant lacks enough water or soil nutrients during the flowering stage, or when high heat prevents proper pollination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni eyimɔ eshɛɛɛ he lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. aloo be mli ni la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa.

english: Maize plants fall over when their roots are weak, which can happen if seeds are planted too shallowly, if soil insect pests damage the roots, or if the plants were sown too close together.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aba mli kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Kɛji kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fite shishifãi lɛ Aloo kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ

english: Why are my corn plants producing tassels and flowers while they are still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miiwo ŋmeii kɛ fɔfɔi yɛ be mli ni amɛji kukuji waa lolo lɛ?

english: When young maize suffers severe heat or drought stress, it flowers early as a survival reaction to try to produce seeds before the plant dries out.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ he haomɔ lɛ Ewoɔ fɔfɔi mra akɛ wala yibiiwoo he nifeemɔ koni ekɛka ni ekɛ dumɔwui aba dani tso lɛ agbi.

english: How can I store my harvested corn so that tiny insects do not turn it into powder?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato koni ekatsɔ sũ ni jɛ kooloi bibii amli?

english: To prevent grain insect damage, dry your maize thoroughly until kernels are hard, clean out your storage area, and store the grain in airtight bags or treat it with approved grain protectants.
ga: Bɔni afee ni kooloi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ akafite. Ha ŋmãa lɛ agbi kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsumɔ he ni akɛ dumɔwui lɛ toɔ lɛ he ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo vacuum kotokui amli loo okɛ nɔ ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why does my harvested corn develop dark mold when I keep it inside my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ waa kɛ́ mikɛto nitoohe lɛ?

english: Mold forms when corn is stored before it is completely dry, or when the storage space is damp and lacks good airflow, allowing moisture to get trapped around the grains.
ga: Mold baa kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa to dani egbi kwraa. aloo be mli ni he ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni mli edɔ lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni ebɔleɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know that my corn is dry enough after harvest to safely put into storage bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛwo kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ mli shweshweeshwe?

english: You can test dry corn by pressing a kernel with your thumbnail; if it leaves an imprint, it is still too wet. When properly dry, kernels feel extremely hard and break cleanly when cracked.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ ni okɛ o-thumbnail lɛ baanyɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji eshi okadi lɛ, no lɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ lolo. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbi jogbaŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa waa ni amɛbaakumɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji amɛgbala.

english: Does drying my harvested corn in the open sun reduce the quality of the grain?
ga: Ani mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ ni migbiɔ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ baa shi?

english: Sun drying does not spoil the grain quality; it safely removes excess water, which hardens the seed and prevents fungi from growing, ensuring your crop stays fresh longer.
ga: Hulu ni haa egbiɔ lɛ efiteee dumɔwui lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ. Ejieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shweshweeshwe. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni ehaaa ŋmeii akwɛ̃. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: If my crop gets a strange disease in the field, how should I bring a sample to your office for testing?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ná hela ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ko aba o-ɔfis lɛ koni aka lɛ akwɛ?

english: Cut a fresh sample of the plant showing both affected and healthy parts, wrap it in a clean paper bag or cloth, and bring it immediately before it dries out or rots in plastic.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tso hee ko ni tsɔɔ fãi ni ena hela lɛ kɛ fãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ. Okɛwo wolo kotoku loo mama ni mli tse mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, jiemɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani plastic lɛ agbi loo egbo.

english: How can I tell if my corn crop needs more fertilizer before it starts forming cobs?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo dani amɛje shishi amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your crop grows very slowly, has pale green leaves instead of deep green, and thin stems, it is a sign that the plants lack nutrients and need top-dressing fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa blɛoo waa Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ. ni eyɛ tso bibioo Eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn cobs are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, a key nutrient crops need to stay green and build heavy grain cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni tsei ni haa niyenii mli hewalɛ waa lɛ ahi shi akɛ eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmaa ni tsii.

english: Can I plant cowpea in the same field as my maize without harming the corn?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa ni miyeŋ ŋmãa lɛ awui?

english: Yes, cowpeas and beans are special because they capture natural food from the air and add nitrogen into the soil, which actually helps feed your maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ji nɔ ko krɛdɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛmɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛ nitrogen fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he, ni no yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ ni ehaa ŋmãa niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and scorching in the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside your cocoa provides living shelter, keeping the soil cool and moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa wɔɔhe. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my young maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛtee ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ anɔ

english: This damage is caused by fall armyworms, a very common pest in Ghana. Early detection and applying appropriate control methods—such as ash, neem extract, or recommended insecticides—can protect your maize harvest before the pests multiply.
ga: Cutworms ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana Anaa mra ni akɛ gbɛi ni sa ni akɛyeɔ nɔ tamɔ sũ, neem mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ atsu nii. Ebaanyɛ ebu o-abele ni okpa lɛ he dani tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ afɔ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots go bad and turn dark inside just a few days after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ duŋ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli beni atsa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots start to spoil quickly once harvested because they lose moisture and react with the air. Processing them quickly into gari or flour, or keeping them covered in moist soil, prevents them from spoiling.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa cassava shishifãi lɛ, amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehiɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ekome. Akɛ oyaiyeli tsuɔ he nii ni akɛfeɔ gari loo ashikishaŋ. loo okɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ aha nɔ koni ekafite

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and soft before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently damp helps the plant draw up the right nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛjie niyenii ni sa kɛjɛ mli.

english: Does supporting my yam vines with wood stakes really help me get larger tubers?
ga: Ani mi-sweet potato wein tsei lɛ ni mikɛ tsei tsei fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi diɛŋtsɛ koni makwɛ bulbs wuji?

english: Yes, staking lifts the leaves toward the sun so the vine can absorb maximum light. When leaves get plenty of sunlight, the plant creates more energy and stores it underground, producing bigger yam tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, staking baaha baai lɛ akwɛ hulu lɛ hiɛ bɔni afee ni wain tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ daraa.

english: How can I tell if my soil is missing nutrients before I start planting my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ?

english: If previous crops grew slowly, had pale yellow leaves, or produced small yields, your soil is likely hungry for nutrients. Adding organic manure or compost before planting restores essential food to the soil.
ga: Kɛji tso ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ da blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. loo ewoɔ nibii fioo Oshikpɔŋ lɛ hu fɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he miihia. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli.

english: Is it good to clean off field dirt from my harvested vegetables before taking them to the market?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ majie muji ni yɔɔ mi-aduawai ni mikpa lɛ amli lɛ dani mikɛbaahɔɔ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Yes, gently cleaning field dirt off freshly harvested produce prevents rot, improves hygiene, and makes your crops look much better than imported or poorly handled produce, helping you get a higher market price.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔ mli muji ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ nibii heei amli lɛ baaye abua ni akafite. improve hygiene Ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii feɔ fɛo fe aduawai kɛ aduawai ni akɛbaa maŋsɛɛ loo ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa jara ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience stress from extreme heat or lack of water. Watering regularly during dry spells and applying compost helps the plants hold onto their flowers and set healthy fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli, ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ekɛ yibii kpakpai aba.

english: Too many extra shoots compete with the main plantain stem for water, nutrients, and sunlight. Pruning away weaker shoots leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring your main tree produces a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ, kɛ hulu la. Niji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ebaaha otso titri lɛ awo jwɛi agbo ni tsii.

english: Weeds act as hidden thieves on your farm, aggressively stealing water, fertilizer, and light meant for your crops. Weeding early and regularly ensures your main crop gets all the nutrients it needs to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ni daa lɛ, tsei titrii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to grow tall and green. The plant moves nitrogen from older leaves to feed newer growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni ekɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cowpea and bean leaves fold up or droop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas kɛ pea baai lɛ miifo loo amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans naturally fold their leaves during the hottest hours to reduce the surface area exposed to direct sunlight, helping them trap moisture and protect themselves from drying out.
ga: Beans lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Koni akɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaaa egbi.

english: Why are the tips of my oil palm seedling leaves turning brown and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ ayiteŋ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi lɛ?

english: Brown and dry tips on young oil palms are usually caused by water stress or a shortage of potassium in the soil, which helps the plant regulate water inside its leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu mli haomɔ loo potassium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ mu tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi lɛ baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ eyeɔ nu ni yɔɔ ebaai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and look like they have white dust on them in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ sũ yɛŋ yɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with white dusting are a sign of cassava mealybugs or spider mites. These tiny pests multiply fast in hot, dry weather and suck the sap out of your plants.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ sũ yɛŋ ji ŋmei loo ŋmeii ahe okadi. kooloi bibii Enɛɛmɛi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni okɛ nu ni jɛɔ otsei lɛ amli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their leaves suddenly after a big heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can cause water to build up around the roots, leading to fungal root rot. When roots choke on excess water and rot, the plant drops leaves to try to survive.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha nu abua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ ji be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ nɔ ni amɛgboɔ. Tsei baagbee shi yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbɔɔ koni amɛhi shi lɛ mli.

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting and dying during the day even though the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that blocks the plant's inner tubes so water cannot move up from the roots to the stem, making it wilt despite wet soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ tsei amli tsɔnei lɛ anaa. No hewɔ lɛ, nu nyɛŋ aya ŋwɛi kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛya tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ sũ lɛ mli efɔ nu po.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees shed their flowers before any pods start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛnáa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they feel stressed by harsh sunlight, poor soil nutrients, or insect pests like capsids damaging the delicate flowering buds.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji hulu la ni naa wa lɛ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids ni fiteɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why are my harvested yam tubers split open and small instead of smooth and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ tswaa ni amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams split and stay small when planted in hard, stony soil that prevents smooth expansion, or when a long dry spell is suddenly followed by heavy rain while the tuber is growing.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakumɔ ni efee bibii kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tɛi eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ, ni no haaa egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. aloo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ trukaa be mli ni bulb lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why are my plantain suckers taking over a year to produce fruit while my neighbor's fruit much faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ heɔ nɔ ni fe afi dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ yibii lɛ woɔ oya kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain growth depends heavily on water, shade management, and spacing. Suckers planted too close together or in poor, unmulched soil will grow slowly and delay fruiting.
ga: Plantain dalɛ damɔ nu nɔ. Shade nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ lɛ da waa Tsofai ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio ni ebaaha yibii lɛ akawo.

english: How can I tell if my soil has enough moisture and is ready for me to plant my maize seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: Scoop a handful of soil from a few inches deep and squeeze it into a ball; if it holds shape without leaking water and crumbles easily when pushed, the soil moisture is ideal for planting.
ga: Okɛ sũ ni mli kwɔ ni ji inchi fioo komɛi ajie ni okɛmimɔ mli ni okɛfee bɔɔlu. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni nu hoɔɔɔ ni efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashɛ lɛ, Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ sa kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why do my crop stalks fall over easily when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ?

english: Plants need potassium from the soil or fertilizer to build strong cell walls. Potassium helps the plant's trunk and stem stand firm so it does not bend or snap easily.
ga: Tsei he miihia potassium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛma wala yibii gbogboi ni wa. Potassium yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛkabɔle loo amɛkakumɔ oya.

english: What helps a tree build a strong and sturdy branch structure?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmaa niji ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ?

english: Potassium is an essential nutrient that strengthens the physical structure of plants, giving branches and trunks the firm support they need to stay upright.
ga: Potassium ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ tsei lɛ agbɔmɔtso lɛ. Ehaa tsei niji kɛ tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni enáa hewalɛ bɔni afee ni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ shi jaŋŋ.

english: How does fertilizer keep my crops from breaking under heavy weather?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ atsĩ miŋmɔshinii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa waa amli lɛ?

english: Fertilizers rich in potassium reinforce the plant's internal structure, making the stems tough and firm enough to withstand wind and heavy environmental stress.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa tsei amli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli waa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi wa ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ edamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi ni naa wa lɛ anaa.

english: What can I do to make my cocoa trees produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni cacao tso lɛ awo ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Adding a fertilizer with a high level of potassium to your soil encourages cocoa trees to flower and bear a lot of healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwo cacao tsei babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees growing nice leaves but not bearing many pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei yɛ baai fɛfɛji shi amɛwooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: While leaves need basic nutrients to grow green, trees require extra potassium in the soil specifically to produce and support heavy fruit load like cocoa pods.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛtsɔ eŋɔli moŋ, shi tsei titri he hiaa potassium yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo, tamɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni amɛye amɛbua amɛ.

english: Does adding potassium to my farm boost my overall crop harvest?
ga: Ani potassium ni mikɛfataa miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni miduɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ?

english: Yes, having plenty of potassium in the soil helps crops like cocoa transition successfully from growth to fruit production, leading to a higher yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, potassium babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo ni amɛtsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ dalɛ mli kɛyaa yibiiwoo mli yɛ omanyeyeli mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ babaoo.

english: What main work does potassium do for crops in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ nitsumɔ titri potassium tsuɔ kɛhaa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Potassium mainly does two things: it gives plants the structural strength to stand firm, and it fuels the tree to produce abundant fruit.
ga: Nibii enyɔ titri ni potassium feɔ: Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ ni ewaa ni edamɔɔ shi shiŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo

english: How do I know if my soil is missing potassium?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ potassium bɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: If your crops have weak stems that cannot stand upright or if your cocoa trees are not producing enough pods, your soil may be low in potassium.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ adamɔ shi shiŋŋ loo kɛji akɛ cacao tso lɛ wooo ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ekolɛ potassium hu faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I mix different fertilizer ingredients together before putting them on my soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi afutu? ekome dani akɛwo shikpɔŋ?

english: Yes, combining nutrients like potassium into a single mixture ensures your plants get both the structural support to stay firm and the nutrients to bear fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii mli nibii tamɔ potassium ni akɛaawo mli lɛ haa otsei lɛ náa nɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ, kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why should I put potassium fertilizer around the roots of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ potassium ŋmɔshi nibii afata mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Applying potassium to the soil near the base allows roots to absorb it easily, helping the tree grow strong stems and feed developing cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ potassium fata shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ lɛ mlɛo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishitso lɛ mli wa, ni ehaa niyenii kɛhaa kookoo ŋmɔji ni miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer gives the maize the nutrients it needs to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is making small holes in the middle leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa gbekɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are often caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed inside the plant. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended pest control stops them before they destroy the yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra kɛ ŋaawoo akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii. Abaatsi nakai ŋmɔji lɛ anaa dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops stay thin and produce small harvests when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli tseee ni ewoɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, their roots compete with each other for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Giving each plant proper space allows it to feed well and produce bigger fruits.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni eye nii jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii wuji.

english: Groundnuts and beans are leguminous crops that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that helps neighboring crops like maize grow better.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele, ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil when the rainy season gets heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave water standing in the soil for too long, the roots drown and rot, which is why planting on raised mounds helps water drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear land and put wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛ tsei akwɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward to catch sunlight, which powers the growth of the tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground and improves light exposure.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi koni hulu la aba amɛnɔ. ni tsirɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ adalɛ Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, ni ehaa la ni tsoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the big trees from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very tender and burn under direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains around young cocoa provides cover and moisture until the cocoa plants grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo plantains ni adu yɛ Young cocoa lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ehe awo mli ni eha ŋmɔtɔ aba kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the bottom tips of my green tomatoes turning black and soft before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ naji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by irregular watering and a shortage of calcium in the plant. Watering your crop regularly keeps the soil damp and stops the fruit from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ lɛ daa kɛ calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaaha aduawai lɛ akafite.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crop yields even after I put fertilizer on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔji amli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and will aggressively steal the fertilizer, water, and light meant for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures your crop gets all the nutrients you apply.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tso titri lɛ. ni ebaaju ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ kɛ yiwalɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds right after the very first rain of the season falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often dries up quickly, leaving the ground hot and dry again. Planting immediately can cause seeds to sprout and then die in the dry soil; it is safer to wait until regular rains settle the moisture in the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ gbiɔ oya. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ ni egbi ekoŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller crops if I farm on the same piece of land every single year without letting it rest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii kɛji mitsu shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ nii afi fɛɛ afi ni mihaaa ejɔɔ ehe lɛ?

english: Just like a person gets tired after working continuously without sleep, land loses its essential nutrients when cropped non-stop. Leaving the land to rest for a season allows the soil to rebuild its natural food and organic matter so future crops grow strong and give good yields.
ga: Taakɛ gbɔmɛi nijiaŋ jeɔ wui kɛjɛɔ nitsumɔ ni yaa nɔ ni amɛwɔɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa lɛ laajeɔ kɛji akɛ aduɔ nii be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe be kome lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ saa ebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ada waa ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce very small roots when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi bibii waa lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots fight one another underground for limited water and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to spread its roots and build large, thick tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni fa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa ni efeɔ bulbs agboi ni mli tse.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is its main growing food. It can also happen when too much water gathers around the roots, preventing them from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tsei he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei miida lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu babaoo bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni eha amɛmumɔ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cowpeas grow so well when I plant them in the same farm as my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ beni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-cassava lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are special crops that feed the soil by pulling invisible nutrients from the air and fixing them into the ground. This natural fertilizer nourishes both the cowpeas and the nearby cassava plants.
ga: Cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ niyenii ni anaaa lɛ ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ fɛɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why don't my maize seeds sprout when I bury them deep in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds need air and warmth to wake up, not just water. When buried too deep, the young sprout exhausts all its stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil and dies before reaching the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ dɔlɛ koni amɛte shi. Jeee nu pɛ Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ Tso bibioo lɛ baafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto lɛ ni ekɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli ni egbo dani eshɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look limp during the hot afternoon sun, but stand up straight again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Shi shidaamɔ tɛ̃ɛ ekoŋŋ leebi?

english: Leaf curling during the heat of the day is the pepper plant's natural defense to reduce water loss and protect itself from burning. Once the air cools down at night, the plant absorbs moisture and recovers.
ga: Baai lɛ ni aaakpã mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be lɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ pepper tsei ahe. Koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni obu ohe kɛjɛ shãa he. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiɛ ba ehe nɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant before turning into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat or a sudden lack of water. The plant drops the flowers to conserve its energy so it can stay alive until conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off the small side branches growing near the bottom of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? Jiemɔ fã ni eda yɛ tomato tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Those extra side branches steal food and water away from the main stem. Removing them directs all the plant's energy into producing bigger, healthier fruit instead of useless extra leaves.
ga: Nakai tsei niji krokomɛi lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he. Amɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni eeekɛ baai krokomɛi ni he ehiaaa lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do pest insects attack my cabbage much harder if I plant cabbage on the same plot twice in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa mi-cabbage lɛ waa kɛji midu cabbage yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii enyɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects and diseases that feed on cabbage hide in the soil after harvest. Planting cabbage again immediately gives those pests a ready feast, whereas planting a different crop like corn starves them out.
ga: Kplukai kɛ helai ni yeɔ kaabii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kaabeji ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha nakai kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ afee nɔ ni anyɛɔ ayeɔ oya. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa ni amɛduɔ lɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye amɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers rot quickly when I dig them up while the vine is still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mifo amɛ be mli ni wain tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: A green vine means the yam tuber is still actively growing and its outer skin is thin and soft. Waiting until the vine dies off naturally ensures the yam forms a thick, tough skin that resists rot in storage.
ga: Wein tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miida lolo. Ni esɛɛ hewolo lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ. Mɛɛ ni wain tso lɛ agbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ sweet potato lɛ yɛ hewolo ni mli tse, ni wa ni teɔ shi ewoɔ fitemɔ yɛ nitoohe mli.

english: Why do people call agrochemicals 'crop medicine', and how does it actually help my crops grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi tsɛɔ agrochemicals akɛ ‘tso tsofa’ ni te amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Agrochemicals are called medicine because, just like human medicine treats or prevents illness, crop chemicals protect plants from diseases caused by fungi, kill pests that destroy leaves, or provide concentrated nutrients through fertilizers so crops remain healthy and produce good yields.
ga: Atsɛɔ okwaayeli mli tsofai akɛ tsofai ejaakɛ, tamɔ adesai tsofai lɛ, akɛtsuɔ nii kɛtsaa loo atsĩɔ hela naa. Tsofai ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Egbeɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ baai lɛ. aloo ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni mli wa aha kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: How can I tell if a crop chemical or pesticide I bought from the market is fake or bad quality?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofai loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ji amale loo ehiii?

english: Fake crop chemicals often lack official registration seals from regulatory bodies like the EPA or COCOBOD, have blurry or misspelled labels, are sold in unsealed containers, or do not dissolve evenly in water. Always purchase inputs from certified and licensed agro-dealers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei amli ni amaleɔ lɛ bɛ nɔ ni jɛ nitsumɔhei ni kudɔɔ nibii tamɔ EPA loo COCOBOD lɛ adɛŋ, amɛyɛ woji ni aŋmalaa nɔ ni mli kãaa shi faŋŋ loo aŋmalaaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ tsɛnsii ni atsĩii naa mli. aloo ekɛ ehe wooo nu mli pɛpɛɛpɛ Hemɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni amɛyɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ be fɛɛ be.

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize plants are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency, meaning the crop is hungry for essential plant food found in healthy soil or fertilizers like NPK and Urea. It can also happen when soil becomes waterlogged, preventing the roots from breathing.
