ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei he miihia tsei niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK kɛ urea. Enɛ baanyɛ aba mli hu kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu

english: Why are my pepper plants growing plenty of big leaves but producing very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi ewoɔ pepper fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer relative to phosphorus and potassium, the plant uses all its energy to build leafy green foliage instead of producing flowers and fruits. Balancing your fertilizer mix encourages better fruit production.
ga: Beni akɛ nitrogen babaoo woɔ tsei amli kɛ akɛtoɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium he. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa yibii lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in high humidity and cool shade. Raindrops bounce fungal spores from the damp ground or infected pods onto healthy ones, spreading the rot quickly across the farm.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ loo pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛyaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. ni egbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is typically caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is transmitted by tiny insects called whiteflies or through planting stem cuttings taken from already infected plants. Planting virus-resistant stem varieties prevents this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ kɛ hela lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ momo lɛ amli lɛ Dumɔ Tsei ni ji fɔlɔi ni nyɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers keep falling off without turning into small cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when they are not pollinated by tiny insects like midges, or when the tree is under stress from drought, lack of soil nutrients, or insect pests like mirids (capsids) sucking the sap from young shoots.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ midges lɛ eshɛɛɛ amɛhe, loo kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ shishi. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo kooloi bibii tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries out the pollen inside tomato flowers, making pollination impossible. When the flower cannot be fertilized, the plant drops the bloom to conserve water and energy until weather conditions improve.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Ehaa enyɛŋ ekɛ pollination awo fɔfɔi mli Beni fɔfɔi ko nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ Tsei lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Plantain plants fall over easily because their roots are naturally shallow and can be weakened further by soil pests like nematodes or stem borers. Planting in deep, rich soil and propping up heavy fruiting stalks with wooden poles prevents them from falling.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ babaoo. Kɛ́ adu shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ nɔ, ni akɛ tsei tsu nii koni akɛfi tsei ni woɔ yibii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Weeds are wild plants that have adapted over centuries to survive harsh conditions, allowing them to suck up water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than domestic crops, which require extra care and weeding to establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛheɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe shia tsei, ni biɔ kwɛmɔ babaoo kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛma shi lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight to make food. Staking leaves off the wet ground reduces fungal diseases and helps the plant produce much bigger tubers under the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha nihoomɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai lɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food to grow strong stalks and big cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are small worms eating the inside of my young maize leaves and leaving ragged holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli ni amɛshiɔ bu ni etse ehe lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a pest that attacks the growing tips of maize. Catching them early and applying approved insecticides or neem leaf extracts protects the plant before it gets destroyed.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa ni miida lɛ yitsei lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu tso lɛ he dani efite.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to steal water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops the chance to use those nutrients to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkɛ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ atsu nii ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil or the soil is too full of standing water. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or improving soil drainage restores the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get extremely hot or when the plant doesn't get consistent water. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu daa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehaa la kpɛɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground when heavy rains stay too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in standing water because roots need air to breathe. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps drain excess rainwater away from the root system.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do farmers cover the soil around vegetables with dried grass or palm leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei tsei haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass, called mulching, keeps the soil moist by stopping hot sun from evaporating water. It also keeps the soil cool and stops weeds from popping up.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ni eeetsi naa lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃.

english: Why do some farmers cut up seed tubers before planting instead of planting them whole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ dumɔwui ayitsei dani amɛduɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadu bulb muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cutting planting material like tubers allows you to multiply your planting stock to cover more land, and it helps stimulate faster shoot sprouting, provided each piece has enough stored energy and a healthy eye.
ga: Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ahe nibii, tamɔ bulbs lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ koni ekɛha he ko babaoo. ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii shwereɔ oya. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ hewalɛ ni ato ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hiŋmɛi hewalɛ kpakpa.

english: Does the size of a sliced seed piece affect how strong my crop grows?
ga: Ani bɔ ni dumɔwui ni atswa lɛ da ha lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ he?

english: Yes, larger seed pieces contain more stored food energy, giving the young sprout more strength to emerge through the soil and establish roots before relying entirely on the ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni dara lɛ yɛ niyenii hewalɛ babaoo ni ato. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛdara kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi dani amɛdamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa.

english: How can I keep my cut seed pieces from rotting after I put them in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi midumɔwui ni mifo lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite beni mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Allowing cut pieces to dry in the shade for a day or dusting the cut surface with clean wood ash creates a protective skin that keeps moisture and soil pests from causing rot.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni fã ni afo lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbi kome loo akɛ tso sũ ni he tse shwie nɔ ni afo lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa hewolo ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ sũ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baa.

english: Will plants grown from sliced seed pieces produce smaller yields than whole ones?
ga: Ani tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni agbɛlɛ mli lɛ baawo yibii ni faaa fe dumɔwui muu fɛɛ?

english: No, as long as the cut piece has enough stored food energy to establish healthy roots and leaves, the mature plant will grow just as large and yield as well as one grown from a whole seed.
ga: Dabi, be fɛɛ be ni ŋmei lɛ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi kɛ baai ni wa akwɛ̃ lɛ. Tsei ni edara kwraa lɛ baadara tamɔ bɔ ni amɛbaafee lɛ, ni amɛbaawo yibii babaoo tamɔ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. kɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa lɛ

english: How does a fresh seed piece feed itself before its roots develop in the soil?
ga: Te dumɔwui heei yeɔ nii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ dani shishifãi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Seed pieces carry their own food reserves stored inside their plant tissues, which nourish the growing shoot until it forms leaves to make food from sunlight and roots to absorb water.
ga: Niyenii ni ato yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ yɛ dumɔwui amli fãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ hewalɛ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ baai ni amɛkɛfeɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ hulu la mli, ni shishifãi lɛ hu shwieɔ nu.

english: Why do some of my cut seed pieces fail to sprout after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mifo lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cut pieces fail if they lack a growth point or 'eye', if the piece is too small to provide enough food energy for the shoot, or if moisture causes the cut area to decay before sprouting.
ga: Nɔ ni afo lɛ baafee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji akɛ ebɛ he ko ni edaa yɛ loo ‘bud’ kɛji akɛ nɔ lɛ ji bibioo tsɔ ni ekɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa baaha tso lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha he ni afo lɛ fite dani ekwɛ̃.

english: Do I need to apply fertilizer right away if the seed piece already has food inside it?
ga: Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ niyenii momo lɛ, ani ehe miihia ni mawo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: While the seed's stored food powers initial sprouting, applying organic fertilizer early ensures rich soil nutrients are available as soon as roots form, keeping growth uninterrupted.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwu lɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ mra moŋ, Shi kɛ akɛ tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ tsu nii kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baaha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ je shishi pɛ. ni eha dalɛ akafee nɔ ni sɛɛ efooo

english: How far apart should I space my cut planting materials when setting them in the field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ midumɔ nii ni mifo lɛ mli beni mikɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Proper spacing prevents crop roots from fighting over soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, ensuring every individual plant gets equal opportunity to feed and grow full yield.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsiɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni ehaa tsei fɛɛ náa hegbɛ ni tamɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni amɛwoɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Which way should I position a cut seed piece when placing it into the ground?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ dumɔwui ni afo lɛ awo shikpɔŋ?

english: Place the cut surface facing downward and the growth eye facing upward so the young sprout travels straight toward sunlight while the cut side remains protected from excessive moisture.
ga: Okɛ ŋwɛi ni afo lɛ awo ŋwɛi ni okɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ awo ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni tso bibioo lɛ aya hulu la lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. yɛ be mli ni fã ni afo lɛ kã he abuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ he.

english: How deep should I cover my planting pieces when placing them on mounds or ridges?
ga: Te esa akɛ maha midumɔi lɛ anɔ ashɛ tɛŋŋ beni mikɛwoɔ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Burying pieces about 5 to 10 centimeters deep protects them from direct drying heat while ensuring the sprout does not waste all its stored energy trying to push through heavy soil.
ga: Kɛ́ afu fã lɛ mli shɔŋŋ sɛntimitai 5 kɛyashi 10 lɛ, ebaabu ehe kɛjɛ la ni haa egbiɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekwɛɔ koni tso bibioo lɛ akafite hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto lɛ beni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ lɛ.

english: If I want to try a new fertilizer on my farm for the first time, how do I test it without risking my entire crop?
ga: Kɛji miisumɔ ni maka ŋmɔshi nibii hee ko makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka lɛ makwɛ ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ wooo oshara mli?

english: You can set up a small demonstration plot by applying the fertilizer to just a few crop rows while leaving the rest of your field untreated. This allows you to safely observe if the crops perform better before spending money to use it on your entire farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee nɔkwɛmɔnɔ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo komɛi pɛ ni okɛbaawo mli lɛ nɔ. ni eshiɔ he ni eshwɛ lɛ ni atsuuu he nii. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsu nii jogbaŋŋ loo etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. Dani obaafite shika ni okɛ oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ atsu nii

english: How can I know if a fertilizer recommended to me is actually suitable for my soil and crop type?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ sa kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Different crops require different nutrients, so you should check the package ratio or consult an extension officer to match the fertilizer to your crop's needs. For example, leafy vegetables need nitrogen, while root crops like cassava need phosphorus and potassium.
ga: Tso henɔ fɛɛ tso henɔ biɔ niyenii srɔtoi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ bɔ ni nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa ha loo okɛ o-extension agent lɛ agba sane koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiamɔ nii kpãa gbee. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ biɔ nitrogen. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ he hiaa fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium lɛ.

english: What does fertilizer actually do to my crops to help them yield more food?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ? Koni eye ebua tsei ni amɛná niyenii babaoo

english: Fertilizer provides essential plant food like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium that soil loses over time. These nutrients help the plant build strong roots, lush green leaves, and big fruits just like good food helps a child grow healthy.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasiɔm. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baaje mli yɛ be ni sa mli Niyenii nibii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, kɛ aduawai wuji. Taakɛ niyenii kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa gbekɛbii ni amɛnáa hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer so the heavy rains do not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a mild rain, but not right before a heavy downpour. Burying or covering the fertilizer slightly with soil near the plant base also prevents rainwater from washing it down the slope.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi esaaa akɛ ofeɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko fu loo okɛ sũ ha nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ nu akafɔ lɛ kɛjɛ ŋshɔ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops right after I put fertilizer on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive, widespread roots that absorb nutrients faster than crop plants. You should always clear weeds around your crop stems before applying fertilizer so your crops get to eat the nutrients first.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. tso lɛ shishifãi dani awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii koni tsei lɛ aye niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ klɛŋklɛŋ

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen and is moving nutrients from its old leaves to feed new growth. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the plant stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen ni eejieɔ niyenii kɛmiijɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha tso lɛ dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but produce very few flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer makes them spend all their energy growing stems and leaves instead of fruit. To encourage flowering and fruiting, plants need fertilizers higher in phosphorus and potassium.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo aya hiɛ Tsei biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi waa yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon is a crop's natural survival behavior to reduce moisture loss under hot sun. If the leaves uncurl in the cooler evening or morning, the plant is fine, but if they stay curled, it needs water.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala su ni tsei feɔ koni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ aba shi. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwieee shi gbɛkɛ loo leebi ni mli ejɔ. Tso lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle lɛ, nu he miihia amɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the plant hold onto its blooms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ shwie shi pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small even when the plants grow very tall and bushy above ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ waa ni efeɔ jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight and soil space. This stress forces the crop to spend its energy growing tall to reach light rather than storing food in its underground tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ he ko he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ nyɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni fa babaoo ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ atsu nii koni amɛná la. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow from the tips instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛyitseiaŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to build green leaves. Adding poultry manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea will help your crop grow green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ okɛ kooloi aŋmei loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant groundnuts on the same land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ makwɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil, but groundnuts and beans are special crops that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. Rotating them restores natural nutrients back into your soil for future crops.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Tsɔɔmɔ koni okɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up right on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads easily in cool, damp, shaded environments. Pruning excess canopy branches to let sunshine in and removing infected pods quickly will help stop it from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la abote mli, ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why am I finding small caterpillars eating holes inside the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the fresh inner leaves of maize. Applying recommended control treatments early in the morning or late evening when the worms come out to feed will protect your field.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai heei amli. Kɛ́ okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ eje kpo amɛmiiya niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oyale lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines onto tall wooden sticks instead of letting them spread across the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make the energy required to grow big underground tubers. Staking lifts the foliage into the light and keeps leaves off damp ground, reducing fungal rot.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ aba. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa la lɛ mli ni ehaaa amɛhi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ha fungal rot he okadii lɛ aba shi

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when plants experience high heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulched helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Look for 'sword suckers', which have narrow, blade-like leaves and a broad base. These grow much faster, produce stronger roots, and yield bigger bunches than 'water suckers' that have wide, broad leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘sword shoot’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tseee ni tamɔ ŋmei kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ. Enɛɛmɛi daa oya kwraa. Bɔɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni ehaa nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ji kui ni da fe ‘nu-nuɔ ŋmeii’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ, ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why should I wait for two or three good rains before sowing my maize seeds at the start of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ kpakpa? Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo komɛi awo mli dani odu ŋmãa yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: The very first light rain after a dry period can deceive you, leaving the deeper soil hot and dry. Waiting for steady rains ensures there is enough moisture underground so your seeds germinate without drying up.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ alaka bo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni egbiɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgbiko.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my pepper plants with dry grass or fallen leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbo loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, prevents water from evaporating under the hot sun. It keeps the roots cool, slows down weed growth, and slowly decomposes into rich organic food for your crops.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni egbɛɔ eshwaa fiofio ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots start to spoil and turn dark inside just two days after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ ni amɛfee ediŋŋ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ mli beni mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots deteriorate rapidly once harvested because they lose moisture and react quickly to small cuts made during digging. Processing them into gari, flour, or dried chips within 48 hours prevents post-harvest loss.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa cassava shishifãi lɛ, amɛfiteɔ oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛhe ejɔ amɛ, ni kɛ́ afo amɛ bibii lɛ, amɛtsuɔ he nii oya. ni ba yɛ shika tsuru ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ mli ni afeɔ lɛ gari, ashikiŋsha loo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ nibii ni laajeɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ naa.

english: During the dry harmattan season, hot winds and direct sunlight cause cocoa trees to lose water faster than their roots can absorb it. Planting shade trees like plantains or Gliricidia near cocoa shields them from intense heat and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo gliricidia yɛ kookoo he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo ni naa wa waa baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Is it good for me to plant cassava and maize on the same farm plot at the same time?
ga: Kasava kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi loo ehiii?

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together works well because maize grows quickly and is ready for harvest in three months, while cassava grows slowly at first and takes over the space after the maize is cleared, giving you two crops from one land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni eshɛɔ he ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni eŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa onine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall with bushy green leaves but produce very small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ waa kɛ baai eŋɔlii akui shi ewoɔ yibii bibii waa lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves instead of fruits. Crops need phosphorus and potassium in the soil to form strong flowers and large fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni ji nitrogen lɛ fa babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe aduawai lɛ. Tsei he miihia phosphorus kɛ potassium yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni he wa kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties from an extension officer prevents this disease from destroying your yield.
ga: Cassava baai ni shwieɔ shi ni cassava mosaic hela ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ kɛbaa Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ duɔ lɛ baaye abua ni hela nɛɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does spear grass keep growing back on my field even after I clear it completely with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpɔlɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mishia lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmei tsuɔ he nii moŋ?

english: Spear grass has deep underground root stems that store energy and remain alive even when the leaves above ground are cut. To eliminate it, you must dig out the underground root network or use appropriate weed killers that reach the roots.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni kɛ hewalɛ toɔ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ wala mli beni afo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baai lɛ po sɛɛ. koni ojie kɛjɛ mli Ehe miihia ni otsa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Aloo okɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni baashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my maize plants produce tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni midu dumɔwui babaoo Ha dumɔwui lɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crowded plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing plants properly ensures each maize stalk gets enough nutrients to produce full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black, sunken spots at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni eshishigbɛ shwieɔ shi dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by irregular watering which prevents the plant from taking up calcium from the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering helps the fruit skin form properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni jɛɔ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be mli baa Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ ahewolo lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper and tomato belong to the same plant family and attract the same soil pests and diseases. Planting a legume like cowpea or groundnut instead breaks the disease cycle and adds useful natural nitrogen to enrich the soil for future crops.
ga: Pepper kɛ tomato jɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛgbalaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii moŋ lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ akpa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ afata he koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into powdery dust full of small insects after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ batsɔ ŋmãa ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni ŋmeii bibii eyi mli obɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Grains stored with high moisture attract grain weevils that lay eggs inside the seeds and eat them from the inside out. Thoroughly drying maize in the sun until it is hard before storing it in airtight sacks protects it from insect damage.
ga: Dumɔwui amli nu ni fa babaoo lɛ gbalaa dumɔwui amli ŋmeii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kpo lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa dani akɛwo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akafite lɛ.

english: Why do my seed yams rot inside the soil when heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when water collects around them in the soil, suffocating the plant roots and causing fungal growth. Making high soil mounds or ridges with drainage channels allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the tubers safe.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii daa. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ ni afee lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni oyitso ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Maize leaves turn yellow mainly because the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants need to stay green and grow well. It can also happen if heavy rains wash the nutrients away or if the ground stays flooded with water for too long.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri ejaakɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii kɛha tsei ni he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dalɛ kpakpa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with big leafy branches but give me very small roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai wuji shi shishifãi lɛ daraaa kwraa lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen in the soil, it puts all its energy into growing tall stems and leaves instead of feeding the roots. Planting stems too close together or using stem cuttings that are too weak can also cause this.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai kakadaji amli moŋ fe ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ niyenii. Tsoi ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo niji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ hu baanyɛ ekɛ naagba nɛɛ aba.

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the sap under the leaves, or transmitting a plant sickness. These bugs cause the leaf to fold up, which slows down the growth of the whole plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo egbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot handle intense heat and strong direct sunlight. They need partial shade from food crops like plantains or shade trees to keep the soil cool and retain moisture around their roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot and dry or when the plant does not get enough water consistently. High temperatures prevent the flower from turning into fruit, so the plant drops it to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkatsɔ aduawai. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do the pods on my cocoa trees turn black and dry up during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal sickness known as black pod disease. Rain drops spread the fungal spores from the soil onto the cocoa pods, and the damp air helps the disease rot the pods quickly.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ gbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: Why am I finding small green and brown caterpillars eating the middle leaves of my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yeɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are known as fall armyworms. They lay eggs on young maize leaves and crawl inside the central whorl of the plant to feed, which leaves holes in the leaves and damages the main stem.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni gbeeɔ shi. Amɛ fɔɔ amɛ wuji lɛ yɛ abɛi baai bibii anɔ ni amɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni amɛ tao niyenii. Enɛ baaha bu aba baai lɛ amli ni efite tso titri lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot inside the ground before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam rot underground is caused by water staying too long in the soil, which smothers the roots, or by tiny worms in the soil called nematodes that bite holes into the tuber, allowing water rot to enter.
ga: Nu ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato fitemɔ baa. ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ Aloo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes ni ŋmɔɔ bu yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Ehaa nu ni mli ewo muji boteɔ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when a small wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko pɛ tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants fall over when tiny pests called nematodes or plantain root borers eat away the underground corm and roots. Without strong, healthy roots anchored deep in the ground, heavy stems cannot stay upright.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii bote mli. Ale amɛ akɛ nematodes loo plantain shishifãi, ni amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi ni wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ bɛ. Tso lɛ ni tsii lɛ nyɛŋ adamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my food crops after the first rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are already sleeping in the soil in huge numbers and are native to the area, so they adapt faster to the soil and rain. They jump to feed on sunlight and water immediately, competing with crops for space.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui ekã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo ni amɛji jɛmɛ jɛɛhei. No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nugbɔ mli oya. Amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛtuɔ amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la kɛ nu. kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛyeɔ akaŋ koni ana he ko lɛ nɔ

english: Why should I split my fertilizer into small portions instead of giving it all to my maize at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mijara ŋmɔshi nibii amli miwo fãi bibii amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ awo mli shikome lɛ?

english: Young plants have small roots that can only absorb a little food at a time. Giving all the fertilizer at once wastes expensive inputs through rain runoff and can burn the tender roots.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii. ni baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii fioo pɛ yɛ be kome mli Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni damɔ nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. ni ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: How do I make sure rain does not wash away the expensive fertilizer I apply on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ nugbɔ lɛ shwieŋ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa ni mikɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Burying fertilizer a few centimeters into the soil near the crop or covering it slightly keeps the nutrients locked in the ground so heavy rains cannot sweep them away.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo sũ lɛ mli sɛntimita fioo ko yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛha he fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ahi sũ lɛ mli. Koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafo kɛya

english: Why do my crop seedlings seem to grow so slowly during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛduɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: During the early stage, seedlings spend most of their energy growing roots underground. Once strong roots are established to collect water and plant food, the leaves grow much faster.
ga: Yɛ shishijee mli lɛ, dumɔwui kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji akɛ ama shishifãi ni wa koni akɛto nu kɛ niyenii ni akɛduɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya kwraa.

english: Why is it harmful to dump fertilizer directly touching the stem of my cocoa plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ kookoo tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is concentrated like salt, so direct contact burns the delicate stem tissue. Placing it a few inches away lets the outer feeding roots draw in the nutrients safely.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle ehe tamɔ ŋoo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ eshɛ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛto he ko ni kɛ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi ni yeɔ niyenii yɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ anyɛ agbala niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my crops look weak and hungry even after I put fertilizer in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ yɛ be mli ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ewo mli po lɛ?

english: Crops cannot absorb dry fertilizer. Soil needs moisture to dissolve nutrients into a liquid form that plant roots can drink in.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni ekɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ afee nu ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ anu.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow faster and look stronger than my cassava crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be ni etamɔ nɔ ni ehe wa fe mi-cassava lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that aggressively grab water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early ensures your cassava gets all the soil food.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛmuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Ehe saamɔ mra Enɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How does compost or animal manure help my soil differently from chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer provides fast, immediate food to crops, while manure acts like long-lasting food that builds up the soil structure so it holds water and nutrients longer.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii oya kɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni maa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii anɔ koni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ahi mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Leaves curl and droop to reduce the surface area exposed to sunlight, helping the plant conserve internal water so it does not dry out in the heat.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle ehe ni eha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he yɛ amɛmli ni ehaaa amɛgbi kɛji akɛ amɛbote hulutsoo be mli.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer early in the morning or during the afternoon heat?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli leebi loo shwane?

english: Applying fertilizer early in the morning or late afternoon is best because cooler temperatures allow the soil to retain moisture so roots absorb nutrients easily.
ga: Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli leebi loo shwane mli lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before turning into actual fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔii dani amɛbatsɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: Plants shed flowers when they suffer from sudden heat stress or a lack of water and essential nutrients needed to support fruit formation.
ga: Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be trukaa loo nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii lɛ bɛ amɛdɛŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist, helping the young cocoa plants survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, a vital nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost can help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts together with my maize helps the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil, giving nearby maize plants extra nutrients to grow better.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ naa niyenii krokomɛi koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know which direction to plant cassava stem cuttings in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni esa akɛ madu mi-cuttings lɛ yɛ?

english: Plant cassava stems with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the roots and shoots will struggle to grow, leading to poor tuber yield.
ga: Dumɔ ŋmei tsei ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ baawa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tuber yibiiwoo ni ehiii.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking elevates the leaves off the ground so they catch maximum sunlight and stay away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ ahe

english: What is eating small holes in my corn leaves and leaving powdery dirt inside the central shoots?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli ni mishiɔ muji ni tamɔ powder yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central shoot of the maize plant during the day and feed on leaves, which drastically reduces your harvest if left untreated.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Enɛ baaha onibii ni owoɔ lɛ aba shi waa kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium or uneven watering while the fruit grows. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant absorb calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Fertilizers need soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb them. Applying fertilizer to bone-dry soil can scorch and burn crop roots, damaging or killing the plant.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wu yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ ashã. Ebaanyɛ efite loo efite tsei.

english: Why is it better to water my pepper plants early in the morning instead of late at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi moŋ fe ni oooha amɛ nu gbɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering early gives plants moisture to withstand afternoon heat, and excess leaf water dries quickly in the sun. Evening watering leaves foliage damp overnight, which encourages fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli mra Ehaa tsei lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ shwane mli latsaa lɛ naa. Ni nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baagbi oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i nyɔɔŋ kome, ni no woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ.

english: Hybrid seeds are bred for a single generation of high yield. Planting seeds harvested from hybrid crops results in weaker plants, smaller cobs, and lower yields in the next season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ kome mli. Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ŋmeii bibii kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli baa.

english: Can I grow corn successfully here in Accra, or does it only do well in other regions?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa jogbaŋŋ yɛ Accra biɛ? Aloo ebaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ pɛ?

english: Corn grows very well in Accra and surrounding coastal areas, as long as you plant at the start of the rainy season and use well-draining soil so the roots do not get waterlogged.
ga: Abɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ Accra kɛ ŋshɔnaa hei ni ebɔle he lɛ. Shii abɔ ni obaadu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli ni okɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ. Bɔni afee ni nu akabote shishifãi lɛ amli

english: Why does corn harvested locally in Accra look or feel different from corn brought in from other parts of the country?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akpaa yɛ maŋ lɛ mli yɛ Accra lɛ hiɛ loo enuɔ he akɛ esoro lɛ kwraa yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ hei krokomɛi kɛbaa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Differences in soil nutrients, rainfall levels, and seed varieties across regions change how much starch and water the corn holds, affecting its kernel size, firmness, and taste.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yɔɔ hei srɔtoi lɛ amli. Etsakeɔ ŋmãa kɛ nu ni ŋmãa lɛ toɔ lɛ falɛ. Enɛ saa dumɔwu lɛ dalɛ, shifimɔ, kɛ ŋmãa lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my young corn plants turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn plants are starving for nitrogen in the soil or their roots are sitting in too much stagnant water, preventing them from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo mli. Enɛ haaa anyɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any fruit when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato flower pollen to dry up or become sticky, which prevents pollination from happening; without pollination, the flower dies and falls off.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato pollen lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haaa pollination aba. Kɛ́ pollination bɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ gboiɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why are some of my harvested corn cobs missing many of their kernels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi bɛ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Missing kernels happen when the corn silks do not get enough pollen during flowering, often caused by dry winds or planting corn stalks too far apart from each other.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmãa siliki lɛ enine shɛɛɛ pollen ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi loo ŋmãa tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa.

english: How do I tell if my crop field is getting too much water during heavy rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ miihe nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: When crops get too much water, their leaves wilts even when the ground is wet, turn pale yellow, and the base of the stems may feel soft or start rotting.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ baagbi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. tsake kɛya ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse Ni tso lɛ shishi baanyɛ anu he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ loo ebɔi fitemɔ.

english: Is it good to plant my corn and tomatoes together in the same space at the same time?
ga: Abɛi kɛ tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he kome yɛ be kome mli Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi loo ehiii?

english: It is better to separate them because tall corn plants cast shade that blocks sunlight from tomatoes, and both crops compete aggressively for the same soil nutrients.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooogbala amɛteŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa hulu la ni jɛɔ tomatoi lɛ amli lɛ naa. Ni tsei enyɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kome lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ waa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black, rotten spots on the bottom before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔi diji yɔɔ dani etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ po lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit, which often happens when watering is irregular or soil moisture fluctuates wildly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni calcium ni faaa lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa.

english: Why do I need to register with agricultural programs before I can buy certain seeds and crop supplies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mihe awo Agriculture Program lɛ mli dani manyɛ mahe dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi?

english: Registering ensures you receive genuine, high-yielding seed varieties approved for your specific area, protecting you from buying poor-quality or fake seeds on the open market.
ga: Woloŋmaa haa onine shɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo, ni ji dumɔwui ni he tse ni akpɛlɛ nɔ kɛha he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ pɛ nɔ. Ebuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni ehiii loo amalei ahemɔ he yɛ jara nɔ.

english: How can I prevent my freshly harvested tomatoes from going soft and rotting too quickly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-tomato ni mikpa ehee lɛ akafee blɛoo ni efite oya tsɔ?

english: Harvesting tomatoes during the cool early morning and storing them in open, shaded crates with good airflow slows down their ripening and keeps them firm longer.
ga: Tomato ni ajieɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli leebi maŋkpa ni akɛtoɔ adeka ko ni agbele mli ni hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tomato lɛ akwɛ̃ blɛoo, ni ebaaha ehi shi shiŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Maize leaves turn pale yellow when the plant lacks essential nutrients, especially nitrogen, or when the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe. Adding compost, manure, or the right fertilizer helps the leaves regain their green color and support proper growth.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa. titri lɛ nitrogen Aloo be mli ni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without setting any fruit during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause severe stress to tomato plants, making the pollen dry up so the flowers cannot form fruit. Regular watering at the base of the plant early in the morning helps keep the plant cool and reduces flower drop.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli muji lɛ gbiɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi daa leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ahe naagbai baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and small even though the leafy tops are huge and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ dara ni eyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and branches above ground instead of feeding the roots below. Balanced soil conditions encourage the plant to store food in the underground tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Yucca tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai kɛ niji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii. Shikpɔŋ nɔ shihilɛ ni ja yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ niyenii toɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight and hot winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain beside them provides the damp, shaded environment young cocoa trees need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Enɛ baaha kookoo tso bibioo lɛ aná he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ. Ehe miihia ni ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same bed where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Maize uses up a lot of food from the soil, but leguminous crops like cowpeas and groundnuts actually take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, restoring soil fertility for future crops.
ga: Abele kɛ niyenii babaoo ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsuɔ nii. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why do my maize plants grow weak and tall with small cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛfeɔ shwilafoi bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each seed proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough resources to form thick stalks and big cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves and tiny dark specks inside the central leaf roll?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli ŋmeii ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ? Yɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ

english: Ragged holes with dark specks in young maize leaves are typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm feeding inside the leaves. Checking crops early and applying neem extracts or safe treatments inside the leaf funnel controls these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ niyenii yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji ni ekumɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋ yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli lɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ baaye nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my plantain leaves turning yellow around the edges and collapsing around the trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing and collapsing leaves on plantain trees are usually signs of a fungal disease that blocks water movement inside the stem. Removing infected leaves and planting clean, disease-free suckers prevents the sickness from spreading across the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eboteɔ shi yɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tsiɔ nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa lɛ he okadi. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ni adu tsei ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why does letting wild weeds grow around my pepper plants lower my total yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi pepper tsei lɛ miiha mi yibii fɛɛ ni miwoɔ lɛ miiba shi?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops and can also hide harmful insects and diseases. Keeping the farm free of weeds allows your crops to get all the nourishment they need to produce a full harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ kooloi kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui hu ato. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo amɛŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams begin to sprout and become soft while stored in the yam barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo kɛji akɛ akɛto sweet potatoes ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams naturally start sprouting when stored in warm or bright conditions because they think it is time to grow again, which drains energy from the tuber. Storing yams in a cool, well-shaded barn and carefully snapping off early sprouts keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes baabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulu tsoɔ loo he ko ni hulu tsoɔ waa. Ejaakɛ amɛsusuɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛdara ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baajie hewalɛ kɛjɛ yitso lɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooto atomo yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni shade yɔɔ mli. Ni kɛ́ ogbala ŋmeii lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops turn brown and look burnt after I spray weedkiller on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni eshã beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ efɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop leaves burn when the chemical mixture is too strong, applied during hot afternoon sun, or sprayed directly onto sensitive young plants. Always follow recommended mixing ratios and spray early in the morning when the sun is cool.
ga: Tsei ahe baai baashã kɛji tsofa ni akɛfutu lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛtsu nii yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Aloo okɛshwie tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Nyiɛmɔ bɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii ahaa lɛ sɛɛ be fɛɛ be. Ni okɛshwie nɔ leebi be mli ni hulu la lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray pesticides on my crop field so they do not destroy my plants?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ? Bɔni afee ni mikafite mitsei lɛ

english: The best time to spray is early morning between 6:00 AM and 9:00 AM, or late evening. High noon heat causes chemicals to evaporate too quickly and heat up on the leaves, which causes leaf burning.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse tsofa lɛ ji leebi ŋmɛji 6:00 a.m. kɛ 9:00 a.m. teŋ loo gbɛkɛ. Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ shwane mli lɛ haa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ mli dɔɔ. ni haa baai lɛ shãa

english: Can I mix two different chemicals together in the same sprayer to save time while working on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai enyɔ afutu yɛ tsɔne kome mli koni mikɛ be akafite beni mitsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Mixing unapproved chemicals together can create a strong reaction that damages your crops and destroys chemical effectiveness. Unless the label explicitly says they can be mixed, apply each chemical separately.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni okɛfutuɔ he lɛ baanyɛ aha yiwalɛ nifeemɔ ko aba ni efiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ni efiteɔ bɔ ni tsofai lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ. Ja nɔ ni aŋmala nɔ nii lɛ tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ abaanyɛ akɛfutu amɛ. Gbalamɔ tsofai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli srɔtoi.

english: Why are some of the seeds I bought from the local market failing to germinate in my farm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jara nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Market seeds may fail to sprout if they are old, damaged by insects, or stored in hot, humid conditions. Using certified seeds from registered dealers ensures high germination rates and healthier crop starts.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji amɛgbɔ. ŋmeii efite loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ Dumɔwui ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo mli ni jɛ jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ babaoo ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from last year's harvest produce weaker crops than new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crop harvests lose their vigor and disease resistance over generations. Buying fresh certified seed each season guarantees uniform crop growth and maximum yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ akpamɔ mli lɛ hewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Dumɔwui heei ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ ada daa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Will putting fertilizer directly against my crop stems make them grow faster or kill them?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mitsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛdara oya loo ebaagbe amɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against young crop stems will burn and kill the plant tissue. Fertilizer should be placed in a small ring or side band a few inches away from the stem so the roots absorb it safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ ashã ni amɛgboi. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. Aloo sɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ. koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that your crop lacks nitrogen, a critical nutrient for plant growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps restore green color and leaf health.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ahe su kɛ baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants dry up and wither so quickly when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young crops with shallow roots lose moisture rapidly in direct dry-season sun. Placing dry leaves or straw as mulch around the base of plants holds soil moisture and keeps roots cool.
ga: Tsei bibii ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there is plenty of land space between the rows?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ gbɛ babaoo yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal fertilizers, water, and sunlight away from your crops underneath the soil, leaving your crops weak, stunted, and low-yielding.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their leaves even though I give them plenty of water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ miifite eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa lɛ nu babaoo daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Overwatering drowns plant roots by driving out oxygen in the soil, causing roots to rot and leaves to drop. Water crops only when the top layer of soil feels dry to the touch.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli fe nine lɛ baaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu tsei pɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi kɛji mɔ ko ta he.

english: Can I use any water source near my farm to water my crops, or does dirty water affect how they grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu jɛɛhe ko ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli nu? Aloo ani nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ saa tsei adalɛ he?

english: Crops require clean water to absorb nutrients properly. Water contaminated with mud, galamsey chemicals, or pollutants can block root intake, stunt crop growth, and introduce toxins into the food you harvest.
ga: Nu ni mli tse he miihia tsei koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni mli ewo mud galamsey tsofai Loo nibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ shishifãi ni ayeɔ lɛ naa. etsĩɔ tsei adalɛ naa ni ekɛ tsofai fɔji woɔ niyenii ni okpaa lɛ mli.

english: Why are my crops turning yellow and failing to grow well when I irrigate them with river water near mining sites?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ faa mli nu ni bɛŋkɛ he ni atsaa shika tsuru yɛ lɛ tsu nii kɛwo amɛnɔ nu lɛ?

english: River water near galamsey sites contains harsh chemicals like mercury and heavy metals. These chemicals damage delicate root systems, preventing crops from taking in essential nutrients and causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Tsofai ni mli wa tamɔ mercury kɛ dade ni tsii yɛ nu ni yɔɔ faa ni bɛŋkɛ Galamsey lɛ mli lɛ mli. Tsofai nɛɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ anine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ nɔ. ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Is it safe for me to wash my chemical spray equipment in the stream near my farm after spraying my crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ mi-spray nibii lɛ ahe yɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikɛ tsofa shwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, washing spray equipment in streams dumps leftover poisons directly into the water. This kills fish and other aquatic life and pollutes the water source for downstream farms and communities.
ga: Dabi, nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ yɛ faa mli lɛ baashɛrɛ nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni eshwɛ lɛ ashwie nu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ gbeɔ loo kɛ nu mli nibii krokomɛi ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni efiteɔ nu ni akɛhaa ŋmɔji kɛ akutsei ni yɔɔ faa lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves look burnt after I spray them with insect medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Using too much chemical pesticide or spraying during the hot sun burns crop leaves. Chemicals must be mixed with clean water in the correct proportions and applied during cool morning or evening hours.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi babaoo tsu nii loo akɛshwie nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ baai lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ tsofai afutu nu ni mli tse mli yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ. Ni okɛwo mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: How far away from a river or stream should I be when spraying chemicals on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ faa loo faa bibioo ko ahi shi teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai miifɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: You should leave a buffer zone of at least 10 to 15 meters from any river or stream. This stops wind and rainwater from washing harmful pesticides into the water and destroying aquatic life.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi buffer zone ni kɛ hoo lɛ, ekɛ faa loo faa lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai 10 kɛyashi 15. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ nu akafɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ awo nu lɛ mli ni efite nu mli nibii.

english: What is the best time of day to spray pesticides on my crops so I do not destroy the plants?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ? Bɔni afee ni mikafite tso lɛ?

english: Spray early in the morning or late in the evening when temperatures are cool. Spraying in high heat causes chemicals to evaporate too quickly and scorch leaves, while calm winds prevent the spray from drifting into nearby water bodies.
ga: Okɛshwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ. Tsofai lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ ni amɛshãa baai lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ kpoo lɛ tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekagbee nu gbɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why must I wait several days after spraying chemicals before harvesting my crops for the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ gbii babaoo yɛ tsofai ni mikɛshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani makpã miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Pesticides take time to break down naturally on the crop. Harvesting too early leaves chemical residues on food, which can make consumers sick and pollute the immediate environment when washed off.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ heɔ be dani efiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ haa tsofai ni eshwɛɔ yɛ niyenii lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ aná hela ni efite shihilɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ afɔ amɛhe.

english: What happens to the pesticide I spray on my farm when heavy rain falls right after?
ga: Mɛni baa tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nyiɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes applied pesticides off your crops into nearby soil and streams. This wastes your money by removing the pest protection and poisons nearby water sources where fish live.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha ofite shika kɛtsɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛ tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ nu ni bɛŋkɛ he ni loo yɔɔ lɛ ni ooojie lɛ nɔ.

english: Does spraying strong pest chemicals on my land harm the living organisms in the soil that help my crops?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mli wa ni mikɛshwieɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, heavy chemical spraying kills beneficial insects, earthworms, and soil organisms. These creatures naturally aerate the soil and break down plant matter to feed your crops, so losing them degrades soil quality over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi babaoo lɛ baagbe kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ. Nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbalaa tsei amli sũi ni efite lɛ koni amɛkɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ amɛlaaje lɛ, ebaafite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do crops on the lower end of my farm wilt after rainwater flows down from sprayed fields above?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ shishi lɛ shwieɔ shi beni nugbɔ nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni akɛshwie nɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Rainwater carries leftover herbicides and pesticides from higher ground down to lower fields. This chemical runoff concentrates in low-lying areas and poisons the root systems of crops planted there.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni eshwɛ lɛ yaa hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ kɛyaa hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ. Nɛkɛ tsofai ni hoɔ nɛɛ fa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ni eji awui kɛha tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ashishifãi.

english: Look closely at the small buds or 'eyes' on the stem cutting; they should point upwards toward the sky so the shoot can grow straight up easily without wasting energy.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘hiŋmɛii’ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ adamɔ shi tɛ̃ɛ mlɛo ni mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak with tiny ears when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli tsɔi ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛyɛ toi bibii yɛ be mli ni adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Planting too close forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving each individual plant without enough food to produce full-sized corn.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tsei lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmãa ni fa babaoo.

english: Why should I remove some of the extra suckers growing around my plantain stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain lɛ eje kpo.

english: Allowing too many shoots to grow forces them to steal water and nutrients from the main mother plant, which results in smaller plantain bunches and weaker stems.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaanyɛ amɛnɔ ni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa plantains bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves off the wet ground into direct sunlight, helping the leaves catch light to make food for bigger tubers while keeping leaves dry from soil diseases.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ naa la koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii wuji lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ahaa baa lɛ mli egbiɔ kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my yellow corn turning yellow at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmɔŋ lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves that start from the tip in a V-shape usually mean your crop is running out of nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy green growth.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ V su mli yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ

english: How do crops like cowpeas and groundnuts help fix the soil for my next crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei baanyɛ aye abua ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha mi ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes have small nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth, leaving natural fertilizer behind for the next season's crop.
