ga: Legumes yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ nɔ.

english: What is causing ragged holes inside the young leaves of my maize shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ pores ni yɔɔ mi-corn shoots lɛ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which crawl inside the central funnel of the plant to eat young leaves, which slows plant growth if left untreated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: This issue, called blossom-end rot, occurs when the plant cannot get enough calcium, often triggered by irregular watering patterns or sudden dry soil spells.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ baa kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbiɔ trukaa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer flowers when I clear out all the big forest trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi fioo pɛ beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ koo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need partial shade to stay cool; direct, hot sunlight causes the tree heat stress, making it drop its flowers and produce fewer pods.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i. Hulu la ni mli edɔ, ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop during hot afternoons even when the soil is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense heat, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than roots can drink it up, so they droop temporarily to conserve water until temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he kɛyashi be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a vital nutrient for growth, or the soil is overly waterlogged. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will help the plants regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting groundnuts or beans together with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that take natural plant food (nitrogen) from the air and put it back into the soil. Planting them alongside corn feeds the soil naturally, reduces the need for expensive chemical fertilizers, and gives you two different crops from the same field.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmã yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Tsɔɔmɔ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together so I can fit more crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni manyɛ makwɛ nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and ground moisture, resulting in tall, skinny plants with tiny yields. Proper spacing gives every plant enough light and food to grow strong and produce a bigger overall harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni mli edɔ Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dalɛ ni mli wa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni da.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to manufacture food for the growing tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they can catch more light and airflow, which prevents leaf diseases and helps produce larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo atsɔ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ foliar hela naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: What is making small holes in the central leaves of my young corn plants, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Small ragged holes in young corn leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the central leaf funnel. You can control them early by sprinkling clean dry sand, neem leaf extract, or approved botanical insecticides directly into the center of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baa lɛ teŋgbɛ tsu lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ mra. Kɛtsɔ ŋã ni mli tse ni egbi ni Neem tso lɛ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ tso ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni oookɛshwie tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are naturally adapted to the local soil, so they absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing the water and food your crops need to survive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni wa ni ekɛ ehe ewo maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ooojie mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my tomato plants with dry grass or cocoa husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo he ni ebɔle he lɛ mli lɛ? Tomato tsei ni jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli

english: Covering the ground with dry organic matter (called mulching) acts like an umbrella that keeps the sun from drying out the soil. It traps moisture in the ground during hot spells, stops weed growth, and eventually decays into rich soil food.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Mulching (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ. Ekpaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: When is the best time of day for me to apply chemical fertilizer to my crops during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Apply fertilizer early in the morning when the soil is already moist, but not during heavy downpours. Applying fertilizer right before heavy rain washes the chemicals away into streams before the plant roots have a chance to soak them up.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaaha tsofai lɛ atsɔ faai amli dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ amɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava is fully ripe and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the bottom leaves begin to turn yellow and fall off naturally. You can also dig carefully around one stem to check if the tubers are thick and firm before harvesting the whole field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu nii kɛbɔle he hu. Tso kome ni akɛkwɛɔ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ shiŋŋ dani akpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees keep falling off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree is under stress from drought, poor soil fertility, or attacks by insects like mirids (capsids). Ensuring proper shade, keeping soil moist with mulch, and controlling pests will help the flowers stay on the tree and turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ shishi. Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ. Shade ni sa he miihia. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying when I clear all the shade trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Large shade trees act like natural shields, keeping the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa roots can establish themselves without scorching.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gãimlibii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Enɛ baaha kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ ahi shi ni shãaa amɛ.

english: How does covering the dirt around my vegetable plants with dry grass keep them from dying in the hot sun?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ehà shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves creates a protective layer called mulch. This layer stops the hot sun from evaporating water out of the soil, keeps the roots cool, and slows down weed growth.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekaha nu lɛ akajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ baa shi

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my green maize plants turning yellow and drying up before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and healthy. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen away, requiring soil feeding or crop rotation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɔɔ nitrogen lɛ shwiemɔ. Esa akɛ ekɛ ehe afɔ̃ shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow huge green leaves but only produce tiny tuber roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shishifãi bibii lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi pɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers down below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baatoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to plant cowpea in the same farm where I plant my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ baakɛɛ mi akɛ midu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have the natural ability to pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them with maize acts like a free natural fertilizer that feeds the hungry maize plants.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni ekɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ abɛi duɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni haa abɛi tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce very small bunches when I let all the tiny shoots grow around the main trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ feɔ kui bibii waa beni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii shwereɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: All those extra shoots, called suckers, steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from the main trunk. Cutting off extra suckers leaves all the food for one main plant, resulting in larger plantain bunches.
ga: Nɛkɛ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kpojiemɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tso titri kome niyenii fɛɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, plantains lɛ baaná jwɛi wuji.

english: Why do I need to spend time putting tall sticks for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite be ni mikɛ tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines up on tall sticks allows every leaf to catch sunlight to make food, while keeping the leaves off the damp ground prevents wet leaves from rotting and spreading leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ haa baa fɛɛ baa naa hulu la kɛha nihoomɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai ni mli efɔ lɛ akafite ni amɛkagbɛ baai hela amɛshwã.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop all their flowers before any pods start forming when the harmattan begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ beni harmattan jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers to save water and protect themselves when water becomes scarce during dry spells. Keeping soil moist and maintaining shade prevents the tree from getting stressed enough to drop its flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛji nu faaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ hulutsoo lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekahao waa aahu akɛ ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling up tightly and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper bush lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni eyɛ bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by microscopic insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaf and sucking out the plant sap, which stunts growth and prevents proper flowering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haaa dalɛ aya hiɛ ni ehaaa fɔfɔii ni sa aba.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turning black and soft before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ naagbeei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani amɛfeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po lɛ?

english: This blacking, known as blossom-end rot, happens when tomato fruits do not get enough calcium or when watering is irregular, causing the bottom cells of the fruit to collapse as it grows.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ diŋfeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato yibii lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. aloo kɛ́ nu lɛ bɛ be fɛɛ mli Enɛ haa wala yibii ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ shishi lɛ shwieɔ shi beni edaa lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for green growth, or the roots are sitting in too much water. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ. Aloo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to stick tall wooden poles in the ground for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves up to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground to prevent diseases and helps the plant send more energy down to grow large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni esa akɛ awo ebaa lɛ nɔ koni enine ashɛ hulu la babaoo nɔ bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni helai akabote mli ni eha tso lɛ akudɔ hewalɛ kɛya shi koni ekɛ bulbs agboi akwɛ̃.

english: Why do people tell me to plant plantains right next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with wide leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kookoo bibioo he miihia bɔni afee ni ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Is it better for me to water my tomato garden early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mitato abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the plants can drink before the heat sets in. Watering in the hot afternoon causes water to evaporate too quickly and can scorch warm leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anu nu dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba.Kɛ́ ashɛre nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ ni ebaashã baai ni mli edɔ lɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts on my farmland help make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts pull nitrogen straight from the air and store it in tiny nodules on their roots. When the groundnut plant dies after harvest, that nitrogen stays behind in the soil to feed whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Akpɔlɔi gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ ŋmeii tso lɛ gbo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I cut away extra shoots growing at the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: If too many young shoots grow around the main plantain stem, they compete for water and plant food. Removing extra suckers leaves just one strong replacement shoot, which ensures your main tree produces a large bunch of fruit.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii dara yɛ tso wulu lɛ he tsɔ lɛ Ebaatswa akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baashwɛ. Enɛ baaha otso titri lɛ awo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up tightly and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛtsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread viruses to the plant, or by extreme heat stress. Spraying the leaves with natural neem oil water can help keep whiteflies away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu he kɛjɛ ŋmeii yɛji ahe.

english: Pepper blossoms drop off when the plant is stressed by severe heat or insufficient watering. Giving the plants consistent moisture during flowering helps them hold onto their blossoms so peppers can form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ mli fũu daa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ anyɛ afee.

english: If I leave my cassava tubers buried in the ground after they mature, will they rot?
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmei shishifãi ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛdara sɛɛ lɛ, ani amɛbaagboi?

english: Cassava tubers can safely stay buried in dry soil for several months as natural storage, but if left too long into the rainy season, excessive soil moisture will cause them to become woody or rot.
ga: Abaanyɛ afu cassava shishifãi lɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ nyɔji babaoo koni akɛbu he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi kɛji akɛ ashi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha etsɔ tso loo egbo.

english: Why do small insects bore tiny holes into my dried cowpea beans after I store them in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ bu bibii yɛ mi-cowpeas ni egbi lɛ mli beni mikɛwo kotoku lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Those insects are bean weevils that lay tiny eggs on the pods in the field or in storage. Storing your thoroughly dried beans in airtight containers or mixing them with clean wood ash suffocates the insects so they cannot ruin your crop.
ga: Kplukai lɛ ji ŋmeii ni fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli loo he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ wo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli loo okɛ tso sũ ni he tse futu mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to grow if I plant them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain after a long dry season often moistens only the top layer of soil while the ground underneath remains dry. If dry weather returns for a week, the germinating seeds dry up and die. It is best to wait for two or three steady rains so the soil has enough deep moisture to keep the young root alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba otsi kroko lɛ, Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi ni edɔ waa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce large leaves that act like living umbrellas, giving young cocoa seedlings the shade and soil moisture they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow starting from the tip down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛyashi amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting at the tip and moving down the middle vein mean your soil is low in nitrogen. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK helps the plant green up and produce energy for big corn cobs.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ ni amɛyaa shishi kɛtsɔɔ fã ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo NPK ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni ehaa hewalɛ baa ŋmãa ŋmeii wuji amli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and turn yellow even when I give them enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa eha amɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Curling and yellowing leaves are usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Watering helps the plant stay hydrated, but to stop the curling disease from spreading, you need to control the whiteflies using yellow sticky traps or safe sprays like neem oil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli. Shi bɔni afee ni frizzy hair hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã Esa akɛ okɛ tsɔnei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe loo tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tamɔ neem fɔ akudɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ.

english: Cassava roots remain thin if the soil is too hard and compacted or lacks potassium. Planting in loose, well-tilled soil or raised mounds allows the roots room to expand, and potassium helps the plant transfer energy into fat, starchy roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi baanyɛ ahi shi bibioo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo potassium bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni atsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amli shwereɔ. Ni potassium yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛjieɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ fɔ, ni mli ewo starch lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin without producing much fruit when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. The plants waste all their energy stretching tall to reach the sun instead of using that energy to make thick stems and fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyashɛ hulu lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛdu tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are fully ready for harvesting under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-peanuts lɛ efee klalo kwraa kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: You can tell groundnuts are ready by pulling up one test plant and opening the pods. If the inside of the shell has dark veins and brown spots, and the nuts fit tightly inside the shell, the crop is mature and ready to dig up.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛtsɔ kaa tsei lɛ eko ni ooogbala kɛya ŋwɛi ni ogbele ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋshɔŋlooi diji kɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ni tsuɔ nii ni ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ ekpɛtɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and turn black at the roots after a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits around the roots for too long without draining, fungal diseases develop and cause root rot, making the stem turn black and the plant wilt.
ga: Pepper shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ebɔle shishifãi ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu efooo lɛ Fungal helai baa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni tso lɛ gboɔ.

english: Why are flowers dropping off my cucumber vines without turning into cucumbers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi kukumba wain tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee kukumba lɛ?

english: Cucumbers produce separate male and female flowers, and male flowers naturally drop off after opening. If female flowers are dropping too, it means insects like bees are not visiting your field to carry pollen from the male to the female flowers.
ga: Kukumba woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Ni fɔfɔi hii lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe beni fɔfɔi lɛ egbele sɛɛ. Kɛji fɔfɔi yei lɛ hu gbee shi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii eyaaa ŋmɔji amli koni amɛjie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi hii amli kɛya fɔfɔi yei amli.

english: Why do my harvested yams start growing green shoots in the barn before I take them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani akɛbaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that wake up from their resting period when exposed to warmth and light. Keeping yams in a cool, dark, and well-ventilated yam barn slows down sprouting and helps them stay fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ amɛwɔhe lɛ mli kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo hulutsoo kɛ la mli. Sweet potato ni akɛtoɔ sweet potato shĩa ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha kwɛ̃mɔ aya hiɛ fioo ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to keep shade trees over my young cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni haa mihe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ he hiaa mi yɛ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile like newborn babies and burn easily under strong sunlight. Shade trees protect them from scorching heat and keep moisture in the soil until the cocoa roots grow deep and strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa tamɔ gbekɛbii ni afɔɔ amɛ ehee lɛ, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ shi ni amɛhe wa.

english: How do I know when to remove the plantain trees shading my cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ majie shade dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees grow big enough for their branches to meet and form a full leaf cover, they no longer need shade. Cutting down the plantains at this stage allows full sunlight to reach the mature cocoa so it can produce plenty of pods.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ da bɔ ni sa lɛ, eniji lɛ kpeɔ ni ebaaha amɛhe. Amɛbɛ hulutsoo he miihia amɛ dɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ afo plantain lɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ kookoo ni eda lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ afee pods babaoo.

english: Why should I cut off extra suckers growing around my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ eje kpo.

english: If too many suckers grow around one stem, they fight over the same soil food and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only the main shoot, ensuring you harvest large and heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii titri lɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ. Enɛ baaha onine ashɛ plantains agbo ko ni tsii nɔ.

english: Why do I need to trim the lower leaves of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo mi tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ?

english: Trimming lower branches keeps leaves off the wet soil where fungal diseases live. It also stops the plant from wasting energy on extra leaves so it can put that food into growing bigger fruits.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ hiɔ lɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ hu fiteɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekwɛ niyenii babaoo ni etsɔ aduawai wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I sow delicate seeds directly in the main farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Starting seeds in a nursery protects young plants from heavy rains, harsh sun, and pests while they are small. Once they build strong roots, moving them to the main field gives them a much higher chance of survival.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe be mli ni amɛji bibii lɛ. Kɛ amɛma shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ lɛ, Amɛ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛná hegbɛ ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa akɛ amɛbaahi shi.

english: How do I know my seedlings in the nursery are mature enough to move to the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu awo ŋmɔ mli?

english: Seedlings are ready when they have developed a firm stem and multiple true leaves. This shows the plant is strong enough to survive direct sunlight and variable field conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo kɛji amɛje shishi amɛfee tso ni wa ni amɛyɛ baai diɛŋtsɛ babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni tsakeɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant my maize right before the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba yɛ Harmatton lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind sucks moisture out of the air and soil very quickly. Planting without steady rain starves young seeds of water, causing them to dry up and die before they can establish.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Dumɔwui ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ daa lɛ baaha dumɔwui bibii lɛ amli nu afee shoo. Enɛ haa egbiɔ ni egboɔ dani enyɛɔ efeɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their leaves when the weather gets too hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ baai beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When water is low, pepper plants drop their leaves as a defense mechanism to conserve water. Shedding leaves prevents the plant from losing moisture through evaporation so the stem and roots can stay alive.
ga: Kɛ nu fioo pɛ eshwɛ Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekaje ŋmɔtɔ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. koni tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded together, they block light from one another and compete for the same soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stalks and small corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛbaafee amɛhe shade ni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii baa.

english: Why do weeds prevent my young crops from growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miitsi mi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and quickly steal food, water, and sunlight from the soil. Clearing weeds gives young crops uninhibited access to the nutrients they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara lɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko etsĩii amɛ gbɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and produce wide leaves that shade the young cocoa plants from heat while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground where diseases easily spread and allows the plant to catch enough sunlight.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ yɛ ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize crop turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize plant lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for making leaves green and strong. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help restore their health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts have special root systems that pull natural nitrogen out of the air and put it into the ground. When you harvest them, that extra plant food stays in the soil for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. beni okpaa lɛ Nakai tsei niyenii ni fa fe nine lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a light rain, or early in the day when gentle rain is expected. Never apply it right before a heavy storm, or the floodwater will wash the nutrients out of reach of plant roots.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. loo leebi be mli ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ nugbɔ baanɛ fioo Kaaha okɛtsu nii dani ahum ni naa wa aba. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, nu afua lɛ baajie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the roots fight each other for water, sunshine, and soil food. Giving each seed proper space allows every plant to grow strong and produce big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso fɛɛ tso ni edara waa ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do weeds around my pepper plants stop them from producing good fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ ebɔle No hewɔ lɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miitsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkawo yibii?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal water, light, and nutrients from the soil. Clearing weeds gives your pepper plants full access to the nourishment they need to bear lots of healthy peppers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ, ehaa o-pepper tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná pepper ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he sɛɛ babaoo.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting underground during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because roots need air to stay alive. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi lɛ koni amɛhi shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is extremely hot or when the plant doesn't get enough water while flowering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant hold onto its flowers so tomatoes can grow.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔmɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni tomatoi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell if caterpillars are hiding and eating inside my maize leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele baai lɛ amli ni amɛmiiye nii?

english: Check the central leafy funnel of your maize plant for small ragged holes and fine waste that looks like sawdust. This is a common sign of Fall Armyworm, which needs early treatment with suitable sprays.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ kɛji bu bibioo ko yɛ mli. Ani egbɛ eshwa ni eyɛ fãji bibii ni tamɔ ŋmei? Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm he okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ ni biɔ ni akɛ tsofai ni sa atsa lɛ mra.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth, or that the ground is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before any fruits start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they face extreme heat, too little water, or when there are no beneficial insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. nu fioo tsɔ loo be mli ni kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he Fɔfɔi lɛ baa koni amɛbawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cocoa trees curl up and turn brown at the edges during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa leaf curling and browning at the edges is a defense mechanism against drought and high sunlight, showing that the tree is losing water faster than its roots can draw it from the dry soil.
ga: Kookoo baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni ebɔleɔ ehe ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. Etsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ.

english: Yam vines need tall sticks to lift their leaves up toward the sunlight; when leaves get maximum sun exposure, the plant can make more food and grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe miihia ni amɛná niji ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Beni baai lɛ ná hulu la babaoo lɛ Tsei lɛ baanyɛ afee niyenii babaoo ni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crops very close to each other so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stems and a smaller overall harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: How can I keep the soil around my vegetable crops moist when the dry weather starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be je shishi?

english: Covering the bare ground around your plants with dry grass, straw, or leaves—a practice called mulching—blocks the hot sun from evaporating soil moisture.
ga: Ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, jwɛi loo baai aha hei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What does putting dry cow manure into my farm soil actually do for my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni egbi ni mikɛfataa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with natural nutrients that plants need to grow strong while also improving the soil's ability to hold onto rainwater during dry spells.
ga: Koolooi aŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm, a common pest that feeds on the soft inner shoots of maize plants, which can severely reduce your yield if not treated early.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei amli ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha onibii lɛ aba shi waa kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Cassava is typically ready for harvest when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to swell and crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plants lack nitrogen, which is the primary food crop plants need to build strong stems and green leaves. Heavy rainfall can also wash these nutrients deep into the soil where young roots cannot reach them.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii nɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Is it safe to pour chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my cassava plants?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baawo mi-cassava tsei lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, placing fertilizer directly against the stem causes 'chemical burn' which damages the plant tissues and rots the base. Fertilizer should always be placed in a shallow ring or pocket a few inches away from the stem so the roots can draw it in safely.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha ‘Chemical burns’ ni fiteɔ tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ aba ni ekɛ base rot baa. Aloo be fɛɛ be lɛ, awoɔ kotoku mli ni kɛ tsɔne lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko. Enɛ baaha anyɛ ajie shishifãi lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark powder inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ powda ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, a common pest in Ghana. They hide in the central funnel of the plant during the hot sun and eat the leaf tissues, leaving behind dark droppings that look like wet sawdust.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni amɛyeɔ baai amli fãji Amɛshiɔ ŋmeii diji ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ.

english: What makes my tomato leaves curl up tightly and turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually spread by tiny whitefly insects carrying a plant virus, or caused by extreme heat and dry soil. Keeping the soil covered with straw mulch keeps the moisture steady and protects the plants from heat stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tsei amli loo ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛbaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi daa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily damaged by full sunlight and harsh dry winds. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad living umbrellas that shade the young cocoa and keep the ground cool and humid for its first few years.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa kookoo bibioo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin like sticks even when the upper plant grows leaves very tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ waa eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ kɛlɛ waa moŋ?

english: When cassava plants are buried too close together, they struggle against each other for light and soil food. The plant spends all its energy stretching tall to reach sunlight instead of growing thick, heavy starch tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni waaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛgbalaa ehe koni eshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, duɔ tso nɛ mi wa nɛ e mi mi wa ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why should I cut down the old plantain stem immediately after cutting off the fruit bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo plantain tsei momo lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mifo aduawai akui lɛ?

english: A plantain stem only produces one bunch of fruit in its entire life and will never bear again. Cutting it down stops it from stealing groundwater and food away from the young suckers sprouting around its base.
ga: Plantain tso lɛ baawo yibii kuu kome pɛ yɛ ewala be fɛɛ mli, ni ewoŋ yibii dɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ofo lɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekaju shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ ahe lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to weed around my yam stakes as soon as the vines start climbing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Sweet potato tso lɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni wain tsei lɛ je shishi amɛkwɔ?

english: Yam vines need full sunlight on their leaves to feed the growing tubers underground. Weeds choke the climbing vines, shade the leaves, and suck up the soil nutrients that the yam plant needs to make big tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu ni fa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni eye ebua amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Jwɛi lɛ haa wain tso lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ehaa baai lɛ ahe ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa sweet potato tso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ bulbs wuji lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they get overly stressed by intense heat, long dry spells, or soil that lacks balanced plant food. Ensuring steady moisture and soil cover prevents the flowers from falling.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hao amɛ tsɔ. Be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni nu hɔmɔ yɔɔ mli loo shikpɔŋ ni tsei amli niyenii ni sa bɛ mli lɛ Nɔ ni haa hulutsoo be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ akagbee shi.

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers are fully mature and ready to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is ready for harvest when the bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, the ground around the stem base cracks open from swelling tubers, and the outer skin of a test tuber peels away easily when scraped.
ga: Cassava efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli egbɛ eshwa kɛjɛ tso lɛ ŋmei ni efuu lɛ mli. Ni kaa yitso lɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Why do my cowpea pods burst open and scatter seeds on the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔji lɛ tswaa ni amɛgbɛɔ dumɔwui amɛshwãa shikpɔŋ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This natural process is called pod shattering. When seed pods reach full maturity and dry under hot sun, the pod walls contract quickly and snap open to release seeds. Harvesting early in the morning when air is cool and moist prevents this loss.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ pod mligbalamɔ. Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ dara ni amɛgbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbogboi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe koni amɛjie dumɔwui lɛ. Nikpamɔ leebi be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso ni edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ nɛkɛ laajemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are the husks on my maize ears opening up by themselves on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-abele toi lɛ anɔ lɛ gbeleɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize husks dry out and open up when the cob reaches maturity or suffers from extreme sun exposure. Once opened, the cob is vulnerable to bird damage, rain rot, and insects, so it should be harvested promptly.
ga: Abɛi ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe beni ŋmeii lɛ daraa loo hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ. Kɛji agbele Cobs lɛ, okpoi baanyɛ afite amɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ kooloi bibii baanyɛ afite amɛ no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ akpa amɛ oya.

english: Why are wild animals like grasscutters coming into my farm to attack my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli kooloi tamɔ jwɛi shwielɔi baa miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ koni amɛbatutua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Wild animals enter crop fields when nearby wild bush dries up or natural food sources become scarce. Clearing surrounding bush, maintaining clean borders, and installing simple fences or traps along farm edges helps keep them away.
ga: Koolooi ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ lɛ boteɔ ŋmɔji amli kɛ́ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ egbi loo adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhei lɛ bafee nɔ ni anaaa. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ahe saamɔ Husui lɛ Ahe Hetsemɔ Kɛ gbogboi loo tsɔnei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkabote mli.

english: What causes my growing crop cobs and fruits to split open and rot while still on the stalk?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cob kɛ mi-fruit ni miida lɛ shwereɔ ni egboɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lolo lɛ?

english: Pests like stem borers or caterpillars bore holes into the crop, creating wounds. Moisture and fungal rots enter these wounds, causing internal gases and pressure that force the fruit or cob to burst open.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ stem borers loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. kɛ pilamɔi baa Fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ boteɔ pilamɔi nɛɛ amli. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ mli kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni nyɛɔ aduawai loo ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why does my farmland stop producing good yields after I farm on it for three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai ni mikɛtsu nii afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops continuously pull essential nutrients out of the soil to grow. Without leaving the land to rest (fallowing) or adding fertilizer and compost, the soil becomes exhausted and cannot support healthy crop growth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be koni amɛdara. Kɛji akɛ aŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe (atsu nii) loo awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛɛɛ eye ebua tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why is it important for me to walk through my field regularly instead of leaving the crops to grow on their own?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔji amli daa moŋ fe ni mahã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Regular farm inspections allow you to catch pests, diseases, and weed outbreaks early before they ruin your harvest. Checking your crops weekly helps you treat small issues before they become major disasters.
ga: Okwaafoi akwɛmɔ daa baanyɛ aye abua bo ni omɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, helai kɛ jwɛi mra. Dani ebaafite onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ Kɛ́ okwɛ onibii amli daa otsi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni otsu naagbai bibii ahe nii dani amɛtsɔ osharai wuji.

english: Leaf rolling is a survival reaction to heat stress. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the leaf surface area exposed to sunlight, helping it conserve water during hot, dry spells.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji wala yiwalaheremɔ hetoo kɛha dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Tsei haa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plants without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: High temperatures, lack of water, or poor pollination cause flowers to fall off. When extreme sun heats up the plant, it sheds flowers to save energy for survival rather than fruit production.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo pollination ni ehiii lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ hulu la lɛ mli wa lɛ ehaa tsei lɛ amli dɔɔ. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii

english: Why do some seeds sprout quickly while others planted in the same soil fail to grow at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya shi ekrokomɛi ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ waaa kwraa lɛ?

english: Uneven seed growth happens when seeds are planted too deeply, receive unequal moisture, or are damaged by soil insects. Seeds planted too deep exhaust their stored energy before reaching the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui ni edaaa ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji adu dumɔwui lɛ mli tsɔ. Na ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee loo kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ efite Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni ato dani eshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up rapidly when the dry season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ oya beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves require high moisture. During dry weather, the plant naturally cuts off water supply to older outer leaves to keep the main stem alive, causing those lower leaves to dry out.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ni fa babaoo. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli Tso lɛ baafo nu ni kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni eha tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ ahi shi. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them to protect their delicate leaves from burning and drying out until they are older.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni yɔɔ tsei anɔ lɛ. Enɛ buɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why are there small caterpillars eating holes inside the central leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that attacks young maize plants. Inspecting your field early and spraying recommended neem extract or suitable insecticides into the plant whorls can protect your crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tutuaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Odumɔi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ abu oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my cassava leaves twisting up and getting yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni etsilɛ, ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by your extension officer is the best way to prevent it.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii yɛji lɛ Adumɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ amɛnaa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow in a V-shape while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your soil is lacking nitrogen. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the growing stage helps the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he mra yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients. Keeping soil moist with mulch and watering regularly helps plants hold onto their blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ bɛ daa loo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ muji ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli fũu kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry spell of several days. If seeds germinate and the rains stop, the young sprouts will dry up and die. It is safer to wait until the major rains start consistently.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ gbii babaoo nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni nugbɔ lɛ kpa Tso bibioo lɛ baagbi ni ebaagbo. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ baabɔi nɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu tsina loo ŋmei dani wɔdu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you plant maize afterward, the maize feeds on that nitrogen and grows much stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ ŋmãa lɛ baaye nitrogen lɛ ni ebaada waa.

english: Why are my plantain leaves getting black spots and dying off before the bunch is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani panicles lɛ daa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Sigatoka, a fungal disease common in warm and wet weather. Pruning and destroying infected leaves helps keep the canopy clean and lets the fruit bunch develop properly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Black Sigatoka, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ ni akpãtãa amɛhiɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli tseɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai akui lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small if I do not weed my farm early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii kɛji mikɛ jwɛi lɛ shwieee ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya lɛ?

english: Weeds compete strongly with young yam plants for light, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures all the goodness in the soil goes straight into growing large yam tubers.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ sweet potato tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Ehe hia ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nibii kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are insects eating up my harvested maize while it is stored in my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi yeɔ mi ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize weevils multiply quickly if the grain is stored while still damp or if the storage container is not sealed properly. Drying maize thoroughly in the sun before storage helps prevent weevil damage.
ga: Abɛi mli ŋmeii lɛ faa oya kɛji akɛ ajie dumɔwui lɛ be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo. aloo kɛji akɛ agbeee nɔ ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ Abele ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛtoɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akafite.

english: Why is it important for me to regularly walk through my cocoa farm and inspect the trees instead of just waiting for harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ kookoo ŋmɔ ko mli daa ni makwɛ tsei lɛ amli lɛ? Mohu ɔ, e he hia nɛ waa mlɛ ní kpami be ɔ kɛkɛ.

english: Inspecting your cocoa trees regularly helps you catch diseases like black pod early, spot pest invasions before they spread, and ensure the trees are getting the right balance of shade and moisture to produce a good yield.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ o-cacao tsei lɛ amli daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni oná helai tamɔ black pods mra. Eyɔseɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ dani amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa. Ni kwɛmɔ ni tsei lɛ ana hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa koni amɛkpa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if a young cocoa pod is changing color because it is ripening or because it is getting sick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ miitsake amɛhe su ejaakɛ amɛkwɛ̃ loo ejaakɛ hela miibɔi amɛ?

english: A healthy ripening pod changes evenly from green or red to a bright golden yellow, whereas a diseased pod usually develops dark brown or black spots that spread rapidly across the pod and make it rot.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ baatsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru mli kɛya shika tsuru ni mli tse po, yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli oya ni ehaa egboɔ.

english: Does counting the pods on my cocoa trees before harvest actually help my farm?
ga: Ani cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ŋmeii ni akaneɔ dani akpaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Counting your pods a few months before harvest allows you to estimate your total yield, plan for the workers and supplies you will need, and quickly notice if pods are being lost to pests, disease, or theft.
ga: Kɛ́ okane ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi dani akpa lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ osusuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ he. Too nitsulɔi kɛ nibii ni he baahia bo lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ. ni okwɛ oya kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai, loo juu efite pods lɛ.

english: Why do some of the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: It is normal for a cocoa tree to drop many flowers because it produces more than it can feed, but excessive flower drop usually means the tree is stressed by drought, poor soil nutrients, or insect attack.
ga: Eji nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ akɛ cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ejaakɛ amɛwoɔ babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye. Shi bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ mli kɛjɛ hɔmɔ mli. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni tutuaa mɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for help from the tree showing that it is getting too much harsh sunlight without shade, lacking rainfall, or missing key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yelikɛbuamɔ ni jɛɔ tso ko ŋɔɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ enine shɛɔ hulu la babaoo nɔ ni ebɛ hulutsoo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: During the harmattan, cocoa trees naturally drop some of their leaves to conserve moisture and slow down their growth to protect themselves until the rainy season comes back.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ekomɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛdara blɛoo koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why should I cut off the small water shoots and suckers growing on the trunk of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi.

english: Water shoots (chupons) steal water and nutrients away from the main tree. Removing them ensures the tree directs all its strength into growing leaves, flowers, and big cocoa pods.
ga: Nu mli tsei (chupons) juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai, fɔfɔii, kɛ kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ amli.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are getting too much shade or too much sunlight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ kookoo tso ko miihe hulutsoo babaoo loo hulutsoo be babaoo?

english: If cocoa trees get too much shade, they grow very tall and thin with very few pods; if they get too much sunlight, their leaves burn, turn brown, and the trees become weak.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo tsɔ lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Kɛji hulu la kpɛ lɛ babaoo lɛ, baai lɛ baashã, ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni tso lɛ hu baagbɔjɔ

english: Planting cocoa trees too close together makes them fight for sunlight and water, and creates a dark, damp environment where fungal diseases like black pod thrive and spread easily.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ nu he akaŋ. ni efee shihilɛ ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli. Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods lɛ daa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya.

english: How do my cocoa trees show me that they need fertilizer or nutrient food?
ga: Mi cacao tsei lɛ tsɔɔ mi bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo niyenii mli hewalɛ he hiaa amɛ.

english: Cocoa trees signal a need for fertilizer when their leaves look pale green or yellow instead of deep green, growth becomes very slow, and pod production decreases significantly compared to previous seasons.
ga: Cacao tsei tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ baai lɛ fee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Dalɛ yaa hiɛ waa. Ni pod ni afeɔ lɛ eba shi kwraa kɛ akɛto be ni eho lɛ he.

english: How does strong wind affect my young crops when they are just starting to grow?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ saa mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛdaraa kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Strong winds can dry out young seedlings, snap fragile stems, and strip away vital topsoil moisture, which slows down crop growth or kills tender plants before they get established.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha tsei bibii agbi. Ekumɔ tso ni egbɔjɔ ni ejieɔ nu ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa oya loo egbeɔ tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ dani amɛmaa shi.

english: How can I arrange my farm layout to reduce wind damage to my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato miŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ akafite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shi?

english: You can plant rows of taller trees or sturdy crops along the outer boundary where the wind usually comes from, creating a natural shield that protects the delicate crops growing behind them.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei kakadaji loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa he ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa yɛ lɛ. koni ekɛfee adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ ahe

english: Why do my newly sprouted crops wilt quickly when exposed to open, windy fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni mikwɛ̃ ehee lɛ gboɔ oya kɛ́ amɛyashɛ ŋmɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Direct exposure to fast-moving wind pulls moisture rapidly out of tender leaves and the topsoil, causing young sprouts to lose water faster than their small roots can absorb it.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa oya lɛ ni akɛkpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai bibii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: Why is plantain a good crop to plant alongside my other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains ji tso kpakpa ni esa akɛ akwɛ mi tsei krokomɛi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and feature broad leaves that act as living shields against harsh wind and sun, while providing a valuable food source and harvest for your family.
ga: Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ tsɔne ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eji niyenii kɛ nikpamɔ jɛɛhe ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha oweku lɛ.

english: How does wind cause plantain trees to fall over, and how can I prevent it?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi? Ni te ooofee tɛŋŋ otsĩ naa?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and heavy broad leaves that easily catch the wind like a sail; you can protect them by planting windbreaks or propping up fruiting stems with strong wooden poles.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse ni mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ oya tamɔ ŋshɔ hiɛ lɛlɛ. Obaanyɛ obu amɛhe kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ naa lɛ ni ooodu loo okɛ tsei ni wa ni akɛfiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: What kind of work and care do plantains need to give a good harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ nitsumɔ kɛ kwɛmɔ esa akɛ atsu koni plantains lɛ aná yibii kpakpai?

english: Plantains require regular clearing of weeds, removal of dead leaves, proper spacing, mulching to retain soil moisture, and physical support against strong winds.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ plantains nɔ daa. Jiemɔ baai ni egboi lɛ. Kwɛmɔ he ni sa Mulching koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ yelikɛbuamɔ koni ekɛte shi ewo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa

english: Why is it important to time my planting before the main seasonal winds begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu be dani be mli kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Planting early allows root systems to grow strong and establish deep in the soil so the plants can anchor themselves and absorb water before dry, heavy winds arrive.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ gbekɛbiiashi Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ anyɛ atswa amɛhe shi ni amɛmu nu dani kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni mli egbi lɛ aba.

english: How do tall trees or tall crops help smaller food crops survive harsh weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei kakadaji loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɔlɔ yeɔ ebuaa niyenii bibii ni aduɔ lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa amli?

english: Tall crops break the force of incoming wind and create a mild microclimate beneath them, reducing heat stress and keeping moisture in the air and soil for smaller crops.
ga: Tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ gbáa kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ mli. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko baa shishigbɛ. Ha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi ni okwɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ kɛha tsei bibii.

english: What happens to my family if I do not properly protect my crops from bad weather?
ga: Mɛni baaba miweku lɛ nɔ kɛji mibuuu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɛɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi gbohii ahe?

english: If crops fail due to unmanaged weather damage, your household loses both food supplies and farm income, which leads to hardship and financial struggle for everyone depending on the farm.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii fite yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ lɛ Oshia lɛ baafite niyenii kɛ ŋmɔ mli shika fɛɛ. Enɛ kɛ naagbai kɛ shika he naagbai baa mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is hard labor required on the farm before the crops start fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atsu nii waa yɛ ŋmɔji amli dani ŋmɔshi nibii abɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Early labor—like land clearing, proper crop positioning, weeding, and creating wind shelters—builds a safe environment that allows crops to mature fully and produce a heavy harvest later on.
ga: Nitsumɔ ni afeɔ mra tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa ni ajieɔ jwɛi kɛ he ni atswaa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli Ehaa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛkpaa babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn turning yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of corn plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient corn needs to grow green and strong. The plant starves its lower leaves to send what little nitrogen it has to the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Tso lɛ baaye eshishigbɛ baai lɛ hɔmɔ bɔni afee ni ekɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ amaje baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them with maize acts like a natural fertilizer boost for the soil.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why won't crops grow well on land that was previously dug up for small-scale gold mining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ ajieɔ shika tsuru bibii kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mining destroys the fertile topsoil where crop roots feed and leaves behind hard subsoil or sand. It can also leave behind harmful chemicals like mercury and heavy metals that stop seeds from sprouting and roots from taking up water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atsaa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii ni tsei shishifãi yeɔ niyenii yɛ nɔ lɛ, ni eshiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ŋã. Ebaanyɛ eshi tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mercury kɛ dade ni tsii ni tsiɔ dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni shishifãi lɛ hu akaŋɔ nu.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa plants the shade and cool soil moisture they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout when I plant them very deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: A seed has only a small pack of stored energy to send its first leaf up to the surface. If planted too deep, the young shoot runs out of energy and dies underground before it can reach sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ato ni amɛkɛbaatsu klɛŋklɛŋ baa lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahewalɛ baaho ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer when the soil is completely dry and there is no rain coming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa ni nugbɔ bako lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water for plant roots to drink it in. When put on bone-dry soil under hot weather, the fertilizer can turn into gas and escape into the air, or burn and damage the plant roots.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli koni tso shishifãi lɛ anu nu. Kɛji akɛ oowo shikpɔŋ ni wui egbi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ atsɔ gas ni ejo foi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. aloo ebaanyɛ eshã ni efite tsei shishifãi

english: Why are green caterpillars hiding inside the center funnel of my young corn plants and eating the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii eŋɔlii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, pests that hide deep inside the moist, soft center whorl of the corn plant to protect themselves from heat, rain, and predators while feeding on the tender new leaves.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni teɔ shi yɛ ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni mli efɔ lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ, nugbɔ, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground when we get heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rain stays trapped in wet, poorly drained soil, the roots suffocate and waterlogged conditions allow soil fungi to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ekpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni nu baatsɔ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why does my maize yield get smaller every year if I keep planting it on the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu yɛ he kome pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ?
