english: Maize draws the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. Planting it in the same spot continuously drains those specific nutrients completely and allows maize-loving pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ hoɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back much faster than my planted crops after I clear my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ beni mijie he ni miduɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are tough and can lie asleep in the soil for years. Clearing the land exposes them to fresh sunlight and air, triggering hundreds of weed seeds to germinate immediately before your crops have a chance to grow.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui wa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛjieɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, jwɛi dumɔwui ohai abɔ kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani onibii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa afee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting maize and cassava together lets you harvest maize early while cassava grows slowly underneath. Once the maize is harvested, the cassava takes over the extra space to form strong tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fee ekome lɛ, ehaa okpaa ŋmãa oya. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo yɛ shishi. Kɛji akpa ŋmãa lɛ agbe naa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ kɛ he ni eshwɛ lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my maize plants staying short and turning yellow even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kukuji ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowish and stunted maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen nutrient. Rain helps the plant grow, but without nutrients from compost or fertilizer, the plant cannot build strong green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa. Shi kɛji akɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ bɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do extension officers say planting cowpeas will make my soil better for maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ akɛ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts pull natural nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience high heat stress or dry soil. If the roots don't get enough steady water during flowering, the plant drops flowers to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ daa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning light green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus, or severe stress from hot sunlight and dry soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo haomɔ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli baa.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves in the dry season to protect themselves from losing too much water through their leaves when the air is dry and warm.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite kɛtsɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants wilt and droop in the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves fold or droop during the hottest part of the day to reduce surface area exposed to the hot sun, which keeps the plant from drying out.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Koni akɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbi.

english: Why didn't the maize seeds I bought from the local eating market sprout after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli niyenii jarayelihe lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji adu lɛ?

english: Grains sold in food markets are meant for cooking and may be old, damaged, or heat-treated. Only certified planting seeds are preserved properly to guarantee high sprouting.
ga: Akɛ ŋmaa ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ niyenii ajarayelihei lɛ tsuɔ nii koni akɛhoo nii ni ebaanyɛ efee nɔ ni egbɔ, nɔ ni efite loo nɔ ni akɛ la ewo mli. Dumɔwui ni adu ni awo he odaseyeli pɛ ji nɔ ni akɛtoɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know underground yam tubers are fully mature and ready to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the green vines and leaves above the ground start turning yellow and dry up completely, showing the plant has finished feeding the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ eda beni wain tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kwraa lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe ŋmeii lɛ niyenii egbe naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and scorching during the sunniest months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight and harsh dry winds. They need temporary shade plants like plantains planted beside them to shield their soft leaves and keep moisture in the soil while they grow.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Enɛ ji koni abu baai bibii lɛ ahe ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow from the tips down the middle of the leaf in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiba shi kɛmiiya teŋgbɛ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves that start at the tip and move down the center stem show that the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni eyaa shi yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli ni etsɔ hewalɛ.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when the tomato plant lacks calcium or receives irregular watering, preventing calcium from reaching the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ calcium bɛ tomato tsei amli loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, calcium nyɛɛɛ ashɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards, shrinking, and turning bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso lɛ? Egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ bushy?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the leaf juices, which damages the leaf tissue and can spread plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwa tsei amli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with dense leaves, but give me small, thin tubers when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi kɛ́ mikpa lɛ, ani mihaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excessive manure, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmeii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight so their leaves can make food, while keeping the leaves off damp soil where fungal diseases can easily infect them.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ahoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ he.

english: Leaving too many suckers around one plantain stem creates competition for water and soil nutrients, which leads to smaller plantain bunches on the main tree.
ga: Ni ashiɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni ebɔleɔ Plantain tso kome pɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa plantain niji bibii baa tso wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center whorl of the maize plant during the day and feeds on the tender expanding leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni eyeɔ baai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa blɛoo lɛ

english: Why do my small vegetable seedlings suddenly collapse and rot at the ground level in the nursery bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui bibii lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛmiifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is a fungal disease called 'damping off', which attacks weak stems when the nursery soil is kept too wet and shady with poor air movement.
ga: Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘damping off’ ni tutuaa tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ eyaaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas in my farm before planting my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing and enriching the soil for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Eji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is essential for green growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted manure helps the plant recover its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers instead of turning them into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers mainly due to water stress during dry spells, insect attacks like mirids, or a lack of essential soil nutrients. Proper shade management and timely spraying against pests help flowers stay on the tree to form healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi titri yɛ nu he haomɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli, kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ tamɔ atatui ni shwieɔ shi, loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. He ni akwɛɔ hulutsoo nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni wa.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot underground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpa amɛ po?

english: Rotting cassava roots are usually caused by waterlogged soil, where excess water starves roots of oxygen and encourages fungal diseases. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps drain extra water and protects the roots from rotting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ebaawo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli, ni ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and looking stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is often caused by tiny pests like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the plant and transmitting viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or recommended sprays prevents the foliage from curling and damaging the yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwie nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do I know if my seed yams are ready to be planted in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Seed yams are ready to plant when small green buds or sprouts begin to emerge naturally from the head of the tuber. Planting them at this stage ensures quick establishment in the soil before weeds take over.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu kɛji ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ba. Ejeɔ shishi edaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmei lɛ yitso mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwereɔ oya dani jwɛi lɛ yeɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches when many shoots grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ feɔ kui bibii yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many shoots (suckers) grow around the main plantain stem, they steal nutrients and water from the main plant. Pruning away extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, which results in bigger and heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii (ŋmei) babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ plantain tso wulu lɛ he lɛ Ebaaju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso wulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii ni da ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the flowers set into healthy fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas help make my soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni efee nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules. When the plant roots decompose in the ground, they naturally release nitrogen that feeds the next crop, such as maize.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei shishifãi fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛjieɔ nitrogen akɛ adebɔɔ niyenii kɛha sɛɛ mli tsei, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why does wild grass grow faster than my upland rice when I plant them at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔ mli ŋmãa lɛ kɛ́ mikɛfee ekome kɛdu lɛ?

english: Wild grasses sprout quickly and are aggressive at stealing light, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds within the first 3 to 4 weeks gives your rice the head start it needs to shade out competing grass.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa ni amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli lɛ, ebaasaa o-rice lɛ koni ekɛha jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I remove tree stumps and big rocks before using plowing machines on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei bibii kɛ tɛi wuji dani mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii atsu nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Hidden tree stumps and heavy stones can bend or break the steel blades of plows and tractors. Clearing the field completely protects equipment from damage and ensures uniform soil preparation for planting.
ga: Tsei akutsei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ tɛi ni tsii baanyɛ abɔle loo akumɔ dade ni akɛtsuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ traktɔi ahe nii lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ, ebaabu otsɔnei lɛ ahe kwraa koni amɛkafite. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni akwɛɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ po asaa he kɛha dumɔwui.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural shade, protecting young cocoa seedlings and keeping the soil moist during their early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen in the soil or the roots are sitting in too much water. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee eŋɔli.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, which usually happens between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: Why should I buy improved seeds from the agricultural center instead of saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ okwaayeli he ko moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Improved seeds are specifically bred by researchers to resist common local diseases, withstand dry spells better, and produce higher crop yields compared to seeds saved generation after generation.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi baadu dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi babaoo. ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni ahere yiwala kɛjɛ yinɔi amli lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without developing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko tomatoi lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when water supply is irregular, or when there is excessive nitrogen in the soil causing the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why must I place wooden stakes next to my yam plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ko ama sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yams are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves up to catch maximum sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal rot and helping the underground tubers grow larger.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from under the leaves, which can also spread leaf-curl viruses to the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ko ni haa baai shwieɔ shi lɛ ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why are my cowpea plants producing many flowers but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Insects like pod borers often attack and feed inside the cowpea flowers before pods can form. Managing these pests early during the flowering stage helps the plant produce full pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ pod borers lɛ tutuaa ni amɛyeɔ cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ amli dani pod lɛ feɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔii lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut away some of the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Leaving too many small shoots (suckers) forces them to compete with the main plant for soil nutrients and water, which results in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Enɛ haa plantain lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall wooden stakes to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high up so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. The sunlight helps the leaves make food, which travels down the vine to grow large, heavy underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɛ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Efãa gbɛ kɛtsɔɔ wain tso lɛ mli ni efeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why should I pull out some of the young sprouts when my maize grows too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tso bibioo ko? Ani mi ŋmeii lɛ miida kɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When maize sprouts grow too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Removing the weaker sprouts leaves enough space and food for the remaining plants to grow thick stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa kwɛ̃ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up like tubes on hot sunny afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ jwɛi yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Curling leaves is the maize plant's way of protecting itself from extreme heat. By hiding part of its leaf surface from the hot sun, the plant reduces how much water it loses through evaporation.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni ŋmãa tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛtsɔ baa lɛ nɔ fã ko ni ekɛteeɔ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei haa nu ni laajeɔ kɛyaa lasu mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to save water and energy. The plant goes into a resting state to protect its roots underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Tso lɛ yaa wɔɔhe koni ebu eshishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or very dry soil. Giving the soil steady moisture keeps the flowers healthy so they can form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: If I pick green peppers from my pepper plants early, will the plant stop producing?
ga: Kɛji mijie chili eŋɔli kɛjɛ pepper tso lɛ mli oya Ani tso lɛ baakpa yibiiwoo?

english: No, harvesting mature green peppers actually encourages the plant to produce more flowers and new fruit. Leaving ripe fruit on the plant signals it to stop making new flowers.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii ni egbɔ ni akpaa lɛ woɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai heei babaoo. Kɛ́ ashi aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ ekpa fɔfɔi heei feemɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I dig deep into the ground right next to the stems when weeding my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli shɔŋŋ beni mikɛ jwɛi shwieɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants have shallow roots near the surface. Digging deep close to the stem cuts these roots, which damages the plant and prevents it from taking up nutrients and water.
ga: Pepper tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ atsa shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaafo nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ ni ehaaa ena niyenii kɛ nu.

english: Why is it important to cut off the extra small shoots growing at the bottom of my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ nɔ ni fa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Those small side shoots, called suckers, steal energy and food away from the main stem. Removing them helps the plant direct its energy into producing bigger, healthier fruit.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same soil drains the exact nutrients maize needs and allows specific pests to build up. Rotating with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ baajɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off the trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce many flowers, but if pollen is not transferred from flower to flower by tiny insects or human hands, the unpollinated flowers naturally dry up and drop off without forming pods.
ga: Kookoo tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii Agbɛnɛ hu adesai aniji kɛ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ. Fɔfɔi ni awoko amɛmli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How does doing pollination by hand help my farm yield more pods?
ga: Te nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ ni eha mi pod lɛ aya hiɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Hand pollination ensures that healthy pollen is placed directly on the flower's female parts, fertilizing almost every flower treated so it grows into a full, healthy pod instead of relying on chance with wild insects.
ga: Nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifã lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Eji ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi ni atsuɔ he nii lɛ mli. Koni eha eda ni efee pod ni mli wa ni eye emuu. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooŋɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ahe sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do my crops only produce flowers during certain months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi pɛ amli lɛ?

english: Plants respond to changes in weather, such as the arrival of rains or changes in temperature, which trigger internal signals telling the plant it is the right season to bloom and set seeds.
ga: Tsei hereɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anɔ, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ loo dɔlɛ tsakemɔi. Enɛ haa mligbɛ okadii ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ be ni sa ni esa akɛ ewo fɔfɔi ni ekɛ dumɔwui awo mli lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when left in strong direct sunlight all day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have tender leaves and short root systems, causing strong sunlight to dry out their leaves faster than their roots can take up water from the soil.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbiɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do tiny young fruits fall off my trees before they grow big and mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai bibii shwieɔ mitso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Trees drop young fruits when they lack enough water, soil nutrients, or proper pollination to support all the growing fruits at once, saving energy for only a few to reach maturity.
ga: Tso lɛ baajie yibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛji nu bɛ ehe. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo pollination ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai fɛɛ ni miida lɛ shikome. Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi ejaakɛ tsei fioo komɛi pɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛdara.

english: Why do some of the flowers on my vegetable crops never turn into fruit at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ lɛ tsakeee aduawai kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Some crops produce separate male and female flowers; male flowers only produce pollen to fertilize the female flowers and will naturally dry up and drop off without producing fruit.
ga: Tsei komɛi woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Fɔfɔi hii feɔ pollen pɛ koni amɛkɛ fɔfɔi yei abɔ. ni ebaagbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaagbee shi ni ewooo yibii.

english: Why is my crop growing tall with bushy green leaves but refusing to yield any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ ni amɛmiiya hiɛ kɛ baai eŋɔlii akui shi amɛwooo ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing tall stems and heavy leaves rather than shifting energy into making flowers and fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni tsii ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsi hewalɛ kɛya fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai afeemɔ nɔ lɛ

english: Why does cutting off weak or extra branches make my crop trees produce better fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ haa mitso lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Pruning stops the plant from wasting food and water on useless branches, allowing all nutrients to go straight into healthy branches that form larger, better-quality fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haaa efite niyenii kɛ nu yɛ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yaa tsei niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli, ni no baawo yibii wuji ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does heavy rain spoil the flowers on my farm and stop them from fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ fiteɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaaa amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall can wash pollen away from open flowers or damage delicate flower parts, preventing successful pollination from happening before the flower closes.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi ni agbele mli lɛ ahe muji loo efite fɔfɔi lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Etsiɔ pollination naa koni ekagbe naa dani fɔfɔi lɛ agbe naa.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is short of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that waterlogged soil is preventing the roots from breathing and absorbing plant food.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ miitsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu ni amɛŋɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii.

english: Why are tiny bugs suddenly appearing on my crop leaves and eating them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii baa trukaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai anɔ ni amɛyeɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies multiply rapidly when weather conditions change or when natural predators are absent, feeding on plant sap and weakening the crop.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies Ebaafee babaoo oya kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsake. aloo be mli ni adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ bɛ, ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do some insects only hide on the underside of my crop leaves during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii komɛi kɛ amɛhe woɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashishi pɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects hide under leaves to protect themselves from scorching sunlight, heavy rain, and predatory birds while safely feeding on the softest parts of the plant.
ga: Kplukai kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai ashishi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ okpoi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe, yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: How do tiny insects spread so quickly from my neighbor's field to my farm?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni kooloo bibioo ko gbɛ eshwa oyayaayai kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛba miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Insects travel easily through strong wind currents, infected seeds, shared farming tools, or by hitching a ride on clothing and livestock moving between fields.
ga: Kplukai tsɔɔ nu ni mli wa lɛ mli mlɛo. dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ Okwaayeli nibii ni ajaa loo kɛtsɔ atadei ni akɛtaraa nɔ kɛ kooloi ni nyiɛɔ ŋmɔji ateŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do agriculture officers take samples of my sick crop leaves to a laboratory?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛ mitso ni hela mɔ lɛ baa lɛ eko tee laboratori lɛ?

english: Laboratory testing allows scientists to identify tiny insects, bacteria, or viruses that are impossible to diagnose with the naked eye so they can recommend the exact treatment.
ga: Laboratory kaa yeɔ ebuaa jeŋ nilelɔi ni amɛyɔseɔ kooloi bibii, helatsɛmɛi loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ. ni anyɛɛɛ ana kɛ hiŋmɛi Koni atsɔɔ tsamɔ gbɛ ni ja.

english: What should I do if I find a strange type of insect on my farm that I have never seen before?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ? Yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni anako eko dã mli?

english: You should collect a few insects in a clear bottle or take photos and immediately inform your local agriculture extension officer so they can check if it is a dangerous new threat.
ga: Esa akɛ obua kooloi bibii fioo komɛi anaa yɛ tɔ ni mli tse mli loo ofo amɛ mfoniri ni okɛ okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ale amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ena kɛji amɛji gbeyeishemɔ hee ko ni yɔɔ oshara.

english: How does the Ministry of Agriculture assist small farmers when a major pest outbreak occurs?
ga: Te Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi bibii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji ba?

english: The Ministry supports farmers by providing subsidized spraying chemicals, deploying extension workers for training, and organizing field teams to control pest spread across affected regions.
ga: Nitsumɔhe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi kɛtsɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ni ekɛhaa kɛha tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsu mɛi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ koni amɛyatsɔse. ni amɛtsu ŋmɔ mli kui koni amɛkwɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni egbɛ eshwa kpokpaa lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow and curling up even when I give them enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves often indicate that tiny sap-sucking insects are draining vital nutrients from the plant or spreading a plant virus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ tsɔɔ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu. Ejie niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli loo egbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops more during the dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season, crops are often stressed by heat and water shortages, making their natural defenses weaker and allowing insect populations to grow faster.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ shoo. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɔjɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa koolooi ayibɔ ni yaa hiɛ oya.

english: Should I spray my crops with chemical pesticides as soon as I notice a few bugs?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔse miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mina kooloi bibii pɛ?

english: No, spraying immediately can kill harmless or friendly insects like ladybugs that naturally eat pests; it is best to monitor pest numbers first and consult an officer for guidance.
ga: Dabi, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi ni bɛ awui loo ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo tamɔ ladybugs ni yeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ ŋmeii lɛ ayibɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni obi onukpai lɛ koni amɛwo bo ŋaa.

english: How can rotating my crops help stop insects from overrunning my farm next season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii ni mitsakeɔ lɛ aaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkatutua miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Crop rotation starves insect pests by removing their main food source for a season, breaking their breeding cycle in the soil so they cannot return in large numbers.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛtsɔ amɛ niyenii titri ni amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ be kome mli lɛ nɔ. Gbalamɔ fɔmɔ be ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni amɛkaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba babaoo.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the top ones stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key food crop plants need to stay green and strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer around the roots helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he Shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Groundnuts pull nitrogen directly from the air into the soil through their roots. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds the maize next to it, while also covering the soil to stop weeds.
ga: Peanuts kɛ nitrogen jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii. Agbɛnɛ hu, okɛ muji awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi lɛ akpa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings get burned easily under the hot Ghanaian sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and shade-moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Ewaaa akɛ ashãa cacao tsei bibii yɛ Ghana hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: What is causing the leaves of my cabbage to get full of tiny holes?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-cabbage baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii?

english: Tiny holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by small caterpillars like the diamondback moth larvae. Spraying a natural solution made from crushed neem leaves early in the morning can stop them from eating the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii, tamɔ diamondback moth lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ kaabii baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni akɛ neem baai ni atswa lɛ fee lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsĩ neem baai lɛ ni ayeɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why are the stems of my pepper plants rotting and turning black near the soil line?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: This is often caused by soil fungus that thrives when rain water collects and stays around the stems. Planting your peppers on raised soil ridges helps excess water drain away quickly so roots stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa ni ekpɛtɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Pepper ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without forming fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air becomes too hot, when the plant doesn't get enough water, or when bees aren't visiting to pollinate them. Regular watering during dry spells helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii baaa koni amɛbawo ŋmɔtɔ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai lɛ ahiɔ shi.

english: Why does my cowpea crop produce plenty of leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi ŋmeii lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: When cowpea plants receive too much rich fertilizer or manure, they put all their energy into making leafy stems instead of flowers and pods. Giving them less fertilizer encourages them to produce more pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cowpea tsei lɛ ná ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, no lɛ Cowpeas kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Kɛ́ aha amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest around 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant starts to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Yams need soft, deep soil to grow straight and large. If the soil is packed hard or full of stones, or if you don't stake the vines high enough to catch sunlight, the tubers remain small and bent.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni ekwɛ̃ shi ni efee agbo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ wain tso lɛ emaaa shi bɔ ni sa ni hulu la lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ nɔ lɛ, Yitso lɛ ji bibioo lolo ni ebɔle ehe.

english: Why does the surface of my farm soil turn hard and crusty after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain breaks down bare soil that lacks organic material, causing it to pack tightly when exposed to the sun. Covering the soil with dry grass or maize stalks protects it from hard rain impact and keeps it loose.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛ́ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmãa tsei wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How many years can a cocoa tree produce good pods before it gets too old?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ko woɔ ŋmeii kpakpai dani egbɔ tsɔ?

english: A cocoa tree usually produces well for about 25 years. With very good soil care and maintenance, it might stay productive for a year or two longer, but naturally, its yield will start to drop significantly after that.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei woɔ yibii kpakpai aaafee afii 25 kɛji akɛ akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ waa ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ekolɛ ebaawo yibii ni fe afi loo afii enyɔ. Shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ E-yibiiwoo lɛ baaje shishi eba shi waa yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: If I take extra good care of my cocoa farm, can my trees produce pods forever?
ga: Kɛ mikwɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Ani mitso lɛ baawo ŋmeii kɛya naanɔ?

english: Proper feeding, weeding, and disease control can keep trees healthy longer, but every cocoa tree has a natural biological limit around 25 years after which it naturally loses its power to produce high yields.
ga: niyenii, jwɛi ni ajieɔ Kɛ helai anɔkwɛmɔ ni sa baanyɛ aha tsei ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Shi kookoo tso fɛɛ tso yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe husu ni ji aaafee afii 25, ni no sɛɛ lɛ, hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaawo yibii babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do wild trees in the bush seem to live longer than the cocoa trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ fe kokoo tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In nature, unharvested trees do not spend huge amounts of energy producing maximum pod yields every year. Farmed cocoa trees work much harder to produce harvestable pods, which wears out the tree faster over its 25-year lifespan.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, tsei ni akpaaa amɛ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuuu nii koni amɛkɛwo pod yibii babaoo daa afi. Kakao tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii waa fe tsutsu lɛ koni amɛná ŋmeii ni abaanyɛ akpa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ afii 25 ni ekɛhiɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods as they grow very old?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni edaa lɛ?

english: As a cocoa tree ages past its prime years, its internal systems for moving water and soil nutrients weaken, naturally reducing its capacity to form and sustain healthy pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ fe amɛ afii ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ Gbɛjianɔtoi ni yɔɔ mli ni haa nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛfeɔ pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: At what age should I expect a young cocoa tree to start bearing pods?
ga: Mɛɛ afii esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ baaje shishi amɛwo ŋmeii?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties usually start bearing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, reaching their full production capacity a few years later and continuing steadily until about 25 years of age.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, ni amɛshɛɔ amɛhewalɛ he yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ ni amɛyaa nɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ amɛyeɔ aaafee afii 25.

english: How long will my farm continue producing pods before the yields drop too low to keep harvesting?
ga: Be enyiɛ miŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ awo pods dani yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eya nɔ ekpa?

english: Most cocoa farms give their best harvests between 10 and 20 years of age. By 25 years, harvest quantities usually drop to a level where continuing to harvest becomes less profitable than replanting.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔji babaoo feɔ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ beni amɛye kɛjɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 20 lɛ. Beni mɔ ko yeɔ afii 25 lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ baa shi kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni sɛɛnamɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ he baaa fe nɔ ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do I know when an old cocoa tree needs to be cut down and replaced?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tsei momoi lɛ ni mikɛtsake amɛ?

english: When a tree reaches around 25 years of age and yields very few pods despite good fertilizing and weeding, it has reached the end of its natural productive life and should be replaced.
ga: Beni tso lɛ eye aaafee afii 25 ni ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ, kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ po wo mli lɛ. Tso lɛ baashɛ esɛɛnamɔ shihilɛ naagbee yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni esa akɛ atsake lɛ.

english: Can I prune an old, low-yielding cocoa tree heavily to make it young again instead of cutting it down?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafolɔ kookoo tsei ni egbɔ ni wooo yibii babaoo lɛ waa koni makwɛ tsei bibii ekoŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mafolɔ amɛ?

english: Pruning can refresh a medium-aged tree, but if the tree has reached its natural limit of around 25 years, heavy pruning will not restore its original yield. Cutting it down to plant new seedlings is better.
ga: Tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ni eye afii teŋgbɛ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ. Shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ eshɛ ebɔɔ su ni ji aaafee afii 25 lɛ he lɛ, tso ni afolɔ waa lɛ haŋ eshishijee yibiiwoo lɛ aba ekoŋŋ. Ehi akɛ ooofolɔ mli ni odu ehee.

english: What will happen to my farm if I do not remove old, unproductive cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mijieee kookoo tsei ni egbɔ ni wooo yibii lɛ?

english: Leaving old trees wastes soil nutrients and light while attracting pests and diseases that can spread to younger, healthy trees on your farm.
ga: Tsei momoi ni ashiɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii kɛ la baa shi yɛ be kome too mli. kɛ kooloi bibii ni gbalaa kɛ helai srɔtoi ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it better for me to clear my whole old cocoa farm at once or replace the old trees gradually?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ majie kookoo ŋmɔ momo lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo matsake tsei momo lɛ fiofio?

english: Replacing old trees in phased sections allows you to keep earning an income from parts of the farm while new seedlings grow to replace the 25-year-old trees.
ga: Tsei momoi ni oootsake yɛ be kɛ bei amli Ebaaha oya nɔ oná shika kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fãi komɛi amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui heei baakwɛ̃ ni baaye tsei ni eye afii 25 lɛ anajiaŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the wind blows hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ miitswa waa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that stay near the surface of the soil. When the heavy bunch of plantains grows at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy and needs a wooden prop or bamboo pole to support it.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Beni plantains babaoo yɔɔ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baafee tsiimɔ ni esa akɛ akɛ tsei loo ŋmei tsei afi sɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread viruses, or by severe heat stress when the plant does not get enough water during hot afternoons.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their flowers before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani ewoɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get too hot, when the soil gets too dry, or if you apply too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant produce leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ awo baai yɛ yibii najiaŋ.

english: What causes black spots to appear on my yam leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sweet potato baa nɔ lɛ baa yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Black spots on yam leaves are usually caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose. Moisture from continuous rain helps the fungus spread quickly across the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. Fɛ̃i ni jɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: Why are my young maize plants dying even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miigboi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Young maize plants can die if underground pests like stem borers or cutworms are eating the stems, or if the soil holds too much water and rots the roots.
ga: Abele tsei bibii baanyɛ agboi kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ stem borers loo cutworms ye tsei lɛ. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni eha shishifãi lɛ fite.

english: Why does my soil become hard like concrete after I plant maize on the same land for three years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ kɔnkrit beni midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afii etɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the soil of its nutrients and organic matter. Adding animal manure, compost, or rotating with beans helps keep the soil loose and soft.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei, loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmei tsɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee blɛoo.

english: Weed seeds are very tough and can stay dormant in dry soil for a long time. They absorb water quickly and are adapted to sprout faster than cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛya wɔɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Amɛheɔ nu oya ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, and the ground around the base of the plant will crack as the roots swell underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli baagbala beni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay small and loose instead of forming a hard ball?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ hiɔ shi bibioo ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ bɔɔlu ni wa lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads stay loose if the plants do not get enough nitrogen fertilizer, if they are planted too close together, or if they lack consistent water while forming the center.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Aloo kɛji nu ni yaa nɔ daa bɛ be mli ni afeɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ.

english: This usually happens when the plant lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for leaf growth. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant takes food from its older bottom leaves to feed the younger top leaves and growing corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ kɛ niyenii ni jɛ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛyeɔ ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ kɛ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or beans makes the soil richer for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special crops that work with friendly bacteria in the soil to pull nitrogen from the air and turn it into natural plant food. When you harvest them, that extra plant food stays in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ naanyobɔɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake lɛ amɛfee adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii. beni okpa lɛ Nakai tso niyenii ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the tiny flowers on my cocoa trees dropping off without turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Yɛ mi koko tso lɛ nɔ koni egbee shi ni etsɔko ŋmeii bibii?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by dry weather, attacked by tiny insects, or do not have enough soil nutrients to support the heavy weight of full pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Kplukai bibii tutuaa amɛ loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ.

english: Plantain roots stay very shallow near the top of the soil. As the heavy bunch of plantains grows at the top, the tree becomes heavy on top and needs a sturdy wooden fork or stake to keep it upright.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Beni plantains babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ hu tsii yɛ ŋwɛi ni ebiɔ tso fɔk loo tso ni wa koni ekɛha ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the field for too long without draining, it suffocates the roots and causes them to turn soft and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha amɛfee blɛoo ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing green shoots in the barn even before I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikɛto lɛ bɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ dani midu lɛ po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are alive and resting after harvest. Once warm weather arrives or moisture gets into the storage barn, the yam senses the change in season and uses its stored energy to sprout.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛmiijɔɔ amɛhe yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ba loo ŋmɔtɔ bote ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Sweet potatoes nuɔ be mli tsakemɔi ahe ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: This soft black spot is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, usually because watering is irregular and the soil dries out too much between waterings.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he diŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni egbiɔ fe nine yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ lɛ hewɔ ni enɛ baa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and twisting like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant sap, or by a disease carried by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewoɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ amli

english: Groundnut flowers bloom above ground, but once pollinated, the plant grows a long needle-like stem that pushes into the soil so the peanut shell can form safely underground.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔii fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ akɛ pollin wo mli Tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaŋŋ agboi ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛha ŋmeii ahe ŋmeii lɛ afee shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and yield tiny harvests if I don't clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. When weeds surround young crops, they starve the crop and prevent it from growing strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ jwɛi bɔle ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe lɛ Amɛbaahã hɔmɔ aye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛtsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: This is often caused by a virus, such as the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The virus attacks the leaves, preventing the plant from making food and drastically reducing your root yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, muawai tamɔ Cassava Mosaic Virus, ni koolooi bibii gbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Ale lɛ akɛ whitefly, ni hela nɛɛ tutuaa baai lɛ, ni ehaaa tso lɛ afee niyenii, ni ehaa shishifãi ni baa lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from larger trees to protect their sensitive leaves from harsh sunlight and drying winds until they grow strong enough to endure direct heat.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni eda lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ he kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: This pattern usually means your soil is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient that plants need to grow dark green leaves and develop full ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa ni amɛná ŋmãa toi ni eyi obɔ.

english: How can a plant disease get into my farm if I didn't bring any sick plants onto my land?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai abote miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Ni kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ baaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu?

english: Many crop diseases are caused by viruses or fungi that travel through the air on the wind, in water runoff, or on insects that fly over from neighboring fields.
ga: Tsei helai babaoo jɛɔ muawai loo ŋmeii ni tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli, kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli, yɛ nu ni hoɔ, loo koolooi ni foɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ mli kɛbaa lɛ amli.

english: Why is it good practice for me to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the surrounding maize so both crops grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ afee nɔ ni woɔ yibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa Bɔni afee ni tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ adara jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are there tiny sticky insects under the leaves of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ yɔɔ lɛ? Mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ ashishi?

english: Those insects are aphids, which feed on the plant's sap and weaken it, while also spreading damaging viral diseases from plant to plant as they move.
ga: Kooloi nɛɛ ji aphids, ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛgbɛɔ helai ni fiteɔ mɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ beni amɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why is it better for my soil if I don't burn the weeds and old leaves before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ ashãaa jwɛi kɛ baai momoi dani aduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys organic matter that would otherwise rot into natural manure, leaving the soil exposed, dry, and depleted of useful nutrients for your new crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni kulɛ amɛbaafite ni amɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egbiɔ, ni ehaa niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha onibii heei lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my tomato leaves roll up inward during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the tomato plant's natural way of protecting itself by reducing the surface area exposed to the sun so it loses less water during hot dry spells.
ga: Leaf curling ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tomato tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛtsɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛbaa shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha nu fioo pɛ amɛfite yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do the seeds I save from my hybrid maize harvest produce smaller cobs when I replant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛji midu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for a strong first generation, but seeds saved from that harvest lose their special vigor and produce weaker plants with lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ ni he wa. Shi dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ kroko ni amɛwoɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do weeds choke out my young yam crop so quickly if I don't clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miigba mi sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe oya kɛji mijieee amɛ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and plant food from the soil before your young yam vines have enough roots and leaves to compete.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei amli dani obi lɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ náa shishifãi kɛ baai ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaaye akaŋ.

english: Tomatoes spoil fast when kept in tightly packed, hot baskets or harvested when wet. Storing them in cool, shaded, well-ventilated areas and handling them gently prevents skin bruises where rot-causing fungi and bacteria enter.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ oya kɛ akɛto tsɛnsii ni mli edɔ ni awo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli. loo akpa kɛji edɔ Akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ. Ni kɛ́ akɛtsu nii blɛoo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ hewolo nɔ he ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni kɛ gangrene baa lɛ baanyɛ abote lɛ naa.

english: Why do strong winds keep blowing down my plantain trees, and how can I protect them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ yaa nɔ etswaa mi dumɔwui lɛ kɛyaa shi lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsĩ naa?

english: Plantain trees have broad leaves that catch strong winds like a sail, combined with shallow roots. Supporting heavy fruiting stems with strong wooden or bamboo stakes and planting windbreak trees around your field perimeter keeps them from falling over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tamɔ lɛlɛ ni akɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ fata he lɛ ahe nii. Akɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa fiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ asɛɛ. kɛ tsei ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa Ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why are fall armyworms destroying my maize leaves so fast, and how do I catch them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall flukes lɛ miifite mi-corn baai lɛ oya nɛkɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mamɔ amɛ oya?

english: Fall armyworms multiply rapidly in hot weather and hide deep inside the central funnel of the plant where rains can't wash them out. Checking your young maize leaves weekly for tiny holes allows you to spot and treat them before they destroy the whole stalk.
ga: Autumn cutworms lɛ faa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. ni ekɛ ehe teeɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. ni nugbɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashwie amɛ bu bibioo mli kwɛmɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli daa otsi lɛ baaye abua bo ni ona amɛ ni otsa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmãa ŋmãa muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why does fertilizer disappear from my field without helping my crops grow taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii miiho kɛmiijɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni eyeee ebuaaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Fertilizer left scattered open on top of the ground gets carried away by strong winds, washed away by sudden heavy rain, or evaporated by the hot sun. Covering or burying the fertilizer under a light layer of soil near the roots ensures the plant absorbs all the nutrients.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baaŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɛ eshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛya. nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa loo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa loo afuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko shishi Ebɛŋkɛɔ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do the maize seeds I buy for planting turn bad and full of holes while stored in my shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mihe koni mikɛdu lɛ fite ni bu eyi mli obɔ beni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weevils and damp air ruin stored seeds. Keeping your dried seeds in airtight containers or hermetic storage bags in a cool, dark room off the floor prevents moisture and insects from eating into them before planting season.
ga: Weevils kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ fiteɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ wo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo vacuum storage bag mli yɛ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni mli ewo duŋ mli kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi akaye dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Why do the pods on my cocoa trees turn black and ruin the beans inside during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfiteɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in wet conditions and high shade. Pruning unnecessary branches to let sunlight reach the trunk and removing infected pods immediately stops the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ waa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ koni hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ shishi ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ebaaha hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during long dry spells to conserve water and stay alive while focusing energy on its underground roots. Once the rains return, the plant safely sprouts fresh green leaves.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli yɛ be mli ni ekɛ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ toɔ he kome. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my pepper plants without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni pepper ko kwraa bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Giving plants steady moisture at the base and balanced soil nutrients helps flowers convert into full peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafite amɛ fɔfɔii kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ ni ahaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ ni amɛhaa sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yeɔ egbɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eda kwraa.

english: Why does the good top layer of my farm soil wash or blow away every time I clear my bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ hoɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ be fɛɛ be ni majie jwɛi lɛ?

english: Clearing all bushes and burning vegetation leaves topsoil bare to heavy winds and downpours. Leaving crop residues as mulch or planting cover crops like cowpeas keeps the rich topsoil tied down and protected.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tsei bibii kɛ tsei ni shãa lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee nɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi baatswa. Tsoi ni afolɔ ashwie shi akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ he ni ebuɔ he.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my main crops after I clean my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit dormant in the dirt in huge numbers and are adapted to spring up faster than crop seeds under sunshine and rain. Clearing weeds while they are still tiny before they set new seeds gradually reduces weed pressure on your field.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui babaoo ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni etsake ehe koni ekwɛ̃ oya fe dumɔwui yɛ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ shishi. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo kɛ dani dumɔwui heei aba lɛ, ebaaha nɔnyɛɛ ni yɔɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ oyale mli lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi fiofio.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there is direct heat from the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ wo amɛmli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and shallow root systems that cannot handle heavy, direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them acts as a canopy, protecting the seedlings from scorching until their roots are strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta. Buu dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ shãa he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam vines produce tubers by converting sunlight into energy through their leaves. Lifting the leaves off the ground with stakes allows them to catch more sunlight and keeps them away from damp soil diseases, resulting in larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo, ni ehaa helai baa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ baatsɔ agbo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to stay green and grow leaves. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer to the soil helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I place fertilizer directly touching the stem of my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts that extract moisture quickly. Placing it directly against the stem will burn the plant tissue; it should be applied a few inches away so the roots can draw it in safely through the soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa oya. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛwo he ko ni kɛ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbala lɛ kɛtsɔ sũ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rain creates standing water around the roots, it cuts off their oxygen supply, causing fungi to breed and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ ha nu ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering. When the plant gets stressed by harsh conditions, it drops its blossoms to save its own energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Kɛ shihilɛi ni esaaa miigba tsei anaa lɛ Ebaawo fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips hiding underneath the leaves. As they suck out the plant sap, the leaves distort and stunt plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Beni amɛmuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ, Baai lɛ hu tsɔɔ sɛɛ ni amɛtsiɔ tso lɛ dalɛ naa.

english: Why do I see small holes in my young maize leaves with dark powdery dirt inside the leaf stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii ni yɔɔ muji ni tamɔ powder ni tsuɔ yɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: This damage is caused by caterpillars such as the Fall Armyworm. They crawl into the tight center of the growing maize plant during the day to feed on the tender leaf tissues and leave behind their waste.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm. Amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ amli fãji ni amɛshiɔ nibii ni fiteɔ nii.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller cobs and light yields when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo cob kɛ light yibii babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planted too closely, crops must fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing seeds out properly gives each plant enough space and food to grow strong, healthy yields.
ga: adu ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atswa hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that have adapted over centuries to survive harsh conditions. Their aggressive root systems allow them to grab available moisture and soil food much faster than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I know the correct amount of farm medicine to measure for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa ni sa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛsusu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe?

english: Every farm chemical comes with specific dosage instructions measured for exact amounts of water or seed weight. Using too much can burn your crops, while using too little will fail to stop pests, so measuring precisely according to the package directions is essential.
ga: Tsofa fɛɛ tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi pɔtɛɛ ni kɔɔ bɔ ni esa akɛ atsu he nii aha lɛ he lɛ baa ni susuɔ nu loo dumɔwu lɛ tsiimɔ pɔtɛɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii ashã. Yɛ be mli ni nɔ fioo pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haŋ tsɛŋemɔ helai akpa lɛ, ehe miihia ni asusu he pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ paketi lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Are all crop medicines imported from places like India safe to use on my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni akɛbaajɛ hei tamɔ India lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Imported farm chemicals are safe as long as they are certified and approved by local agricultural authorities like the Environmental Protection Agency or Ghana Cocoa Board. Always look for approved registration labels on the container before buying.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛji akɛ maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli nitsumɔhei tamɔ Shihilɛ He Buu Nitsumɔhe lɛ ekpɛlɛ nɔ. loo Ghana Kookoo He Nitsumɔhe lɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, taomɔ wolo ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ aŋmala nɔ nii lɛ awo nɔ lɛ nɔ dani ohé.

english: Can I use the same pest medicine for my cocoa trees on my cashew trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii yɛ kookoo kɛ cashew tsei anɔ?

english: Not always. Different crops have different sensitivities to chemical ingredients, and pests vary between cocoa and cashew. You should only use a medicine across different crops if the package label specifically approves it for both.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Tsei srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni amɛnuɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe amɛhaa lɛ srɔtoi. Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ kookoo kɛ cashew teŋ. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ atsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi anɔ. Kɛji akɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ

english: Why should I coat my groundnut seeds with medicine before planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa awo mi-peanut dumɔwui lɛ ahe dani madu lɛ?
