english: Coating seeds with protective medicine guards them against soil fungi, ants, and termites before they sprout. This ensures more of your planted seeds actually germinate into healthy plants.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ ha dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ sũ mli ŋmeii, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ahe dani amɛkwɛ̃. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui ni odu lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ tsei ni he wa.

english: How does a seed coating machine help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui amli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: A coating machine tumbles seeds evenly while applying a precise liquid dose of medicine, making sure every single seed gets an equal protective layer without damaging the seed coat.
ga: Mashin ni akɛwoɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni ekɛ nu abɔ pɔtɛɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ woɔ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu náa hebuu nɔ kome ni efiteee dumɔwu lɛ he tsɔne lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and dry up under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and delicate roots that cannot handle intense heat. They need temporary shade plants, like plantains, to shield them from the sun and keep the soil moist while they establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ naa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛduɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why are tiny pods falling off my cocoa trees before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei anɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Early pod loss often happens when the tree experiences stress from dry weather, poor soil nutrition, or insect attack, causing the tree to drop pods it does not have the energy to support.
ga: early loss of pods Bei pii lɛ ebaa kɛji tsei kɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ mli baa. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa lɛ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaaye ebua lɛ.

english: How long after planting will my cashew trees start bearing nuts?
ga: Be enyiɛ mi-cashew tso lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Grafted cashew trees usually start bringing out their first flowers and nuts within two to three years, reaching full production capacity around five to six years after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cashew tsei ni akɛwo amɛmli lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ shishi yɛ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli. ni ebaashɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ he aaafee afii enumɔ kɛyashi enumɔ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my groundnut crop turning yellow early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on groundnut plants usually indicate a lack of key soil nutrients like nitrogen or iron, or a fungal disease damaging the roots so they cannot draw nutrients from the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo iron bɛ sũ lɛ mli. loo ŋmeii helai ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Will heavy rain wash away the medicine I just sprayed on my crop leaves?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho tsofa ni mikɛshwie mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, if it rains shortly after spraying, the water can wash away the medicine before the plant or pest absorbs it. Chemical sprays generally need a few hours of dry weather to dry completely on the leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji nugbɔ nɛ beni afɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ etsɛɛɛ lɛ Nu hu baanyɛ afɔ tsofa lɛ he dani tsei loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aŋɔ. Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ biɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli koni eha baai lɛ agbi kwraa.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops every single month to make them grow faster?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli daa nyɔŋ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya?

english: No, crops do not need fertilizer every month. Plants require specific nutrients at key stages of their growth—such as right after planting, during active leaf growth, or when flowering. Applying fertilizer on a strict monthly schedule can waste money and damage your crops.
ga: Dabi, ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli daa nyɔŋ nɔ. Niyenii he hiaa tsei yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ pɛ, tamɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ daraa lɛ. aloo beni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ nyɔŋ fɛɛ nyɔŋ nɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite shika ni efite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Will applying fertilizer too frequently cause any harm to my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baafite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shii abɔ?

english: Yes, applying fertilizer too often can burn the plant's roots, cause leaf tips to turn yellow or brown, and spoil the soil. Plants can only absorb a specific amount of food at each growth stage, so excess fertilizer stays in the soil and hurts the roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii shii abɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ Tsei nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii fioo ko yɛ amɛdalɛ be fɛɛ be mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Can I use the exact same type of fertilizer throughout my plant's entire life?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛha tso lɛ wala?

english: Different growth stages require different plant food. Young plants need nutrients that help build strong roots and green leaves, while mature plants need different nutrients during flowering and fruiting to produce bigger yields.
ga: Dalɛ mli fãi srɔtoi biɔ tsei niyenii srɔtoi. Niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ he miihia tsei bibii. Beni tso lɛ daa lɛ, niyenii srɔtoi he miihia lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo be mli koni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it important to fertilize seedlings while they are still in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni awo fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ mli be mli ni yɔɔ fɔmɔhe lɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Fertilizing seedlings in the nursery builds strong stems and deep roots before they are moved to the field. This early nourishment gives young plants the strength to survive the shock and stress of being transplanted into the main farm.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui awo ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani akɛ amɛ awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Tsɔsemɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛye amɛhe yɛ shoofeemɔ kɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli ni aduɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do some crops need to start in a nursery instead of planting seeds directly in the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aje tsei komɛi ashishi yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe moŋ fe ni aaajɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: A nursery protects delicate seeds from harsh sun, heavy rain, weeds, and insects while they are small. It lets you care for them closely so that only strong, healthy plants get selected to go to the main field.
ga: Dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, jwɛi kɛ kooloi bibii ahe be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ. Ehaa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni ahalaa koni akɛdu yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops look weak and droopy right after I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbo amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is known as transplant shock. Moving a plant disturbs its young roots, making it hard for the plant to take in water for a few days while it adjusts to the new soil and bright sunshine.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Tso lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baagbala eshishifãi bibii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ewaa aha tsei lɛ akɛ amɛ nu nu gbii fioo komɛi be mli ni amɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ hee lɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: How do I know when my crop is ready for its first fertilizer application in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee klalo kɛha amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Crops show readiness through their growth stage rather than calendar days. Generally, the first application in the field happens once the plant has recovered from transplanting and begins growing new green leaves.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsɔɔ hesaamɔ yɛ dalɛ be mli yɛ kalanda gbii amli. Shishijee nitsumɔi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fɔɔ baa be mli ni tsei lɛ miihe amɛhe kɛjɛ amɛdumɔ mli. Ni baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yɛ.

english: Why do young seedlings require different care compared to older plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui biɔ kwɛmɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto fe tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have small, tender roots and leaves that burn easily, so they need gentle watering and small amounts of food. Older plants have deeper roots and need larger amounts of nutrients to produce flowers and fruit.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ baai ni shãa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ebiɔ ni afɔ lɛ nu blɛoo kɛ niyenii fioo komɛi. Tsei ni edara lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni ehe hiaa niyenii babaoo koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: Does my crop need extra food when it starts to flower and produce fruit?
ga: Ani niyenii kroko he miihia miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji ebɔi fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo?

english: Yes, flowering and fruiting require a massive amount of energy from the plant. Providing nutrients right before or during this stage helps the plant produce full-sized, healthy fruits, pods, or grains.
ga: Hɛɛ, fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo biɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ dɛŋ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni akɛhaa tso lɛ dani loo yɛ nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ aduawai ni fa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ŋmeii, loo ŋmaa.

english: How does the growth stage of a crop affect how much food or water it consumes?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ bɔ ni tso ko daa lɛ saa niyenii loo nu abɔ ni eyeɔ lɛ he?

english: Just as growing children eat more as they grow bigger, plants need more water and nutrients as they build larger leaves and stems. Their demand for food peaks during active growth and fruiting, then drops as the crop matures.
ga: Taakɛ gbekɛbii ni eda lɛ yeɔ nii babaoo beni amɛdaraa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nu kɛ niyenii babaoo hu he miihia tsei beni amɛdaraa baa kɛ amɛshishifãi wuji lɛ. Niyenii ni ataoɔ lɛ fa fe fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni edara kɛ ewoɔ yibii. No sɛɛ lɛ, ebaa shi beni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves from the bottom up usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food plants use to stay green and grow leaves, so adding manure, compost, or a nitrogen fertilizer will help the maize recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛha amɛbaa lɛ aya hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. Maize uses up a lot of soil nutrients, so planting groundnuts afterwards naturally restores the soil fertility for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Abɛi kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni ooodu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under the strong sun. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that provide necessary shade and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa trees get established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: How does covering the soil around my vegetables with dry grass help them grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, acts like a shade blanket. It keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so you water less often, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo ni otsĩ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye nɔ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot in the ground before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifo amɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining, especially during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water run off so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Planting too close actually reduces your yield because the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing allows each plant to grow big, strong, and produce more fruit or grain.
ga: Kɛ́ odu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo tsɔ lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ baa shi ejaakɛ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso feɔ agbo, ewaa ni ewoɔ yibii loo dumɔwui babaoo.

english: How does clearing weeds early help my crops produce more yield?
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing them early ensures your crops get all the available food and space they need to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ he fɛɛ he ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Fertilizer is best applied when crops are actively growing and the soil is moist, usually shortly after weeding. Applying fertilizer during heavy rains washes it away, while applying it in bone-dry soil can burn the plant roots.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli beni ajie jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaafɔ ehe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wu yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã.

english: Why are small caterpillars chewing holes in the leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mibi lɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on corn leaves and the central stem. Catching them early by inspecting your farm and spraying neem extract or appropriate bio-pesticides will protect your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oookwɛ ni okɛ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, obaaye obua ni obu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant suffers from sudden heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and avoiding long dry gaps during the flowering stage helps flowers turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ hulutsoo ni baa trukaa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ hei ni egbi kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the stems of my young cocoa trees swelling and the leaves turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ efuu ni amɛbaai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Swollen stems and yellowing leaves are signs of swollen shoot disease. It is caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called mealybugs, which slowly weakens the cocoa tree and reduces its ability to produce cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni efuu kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji tso lɛ hela ni efuu lɛ he okadii. Virus ko ni koolooi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ haa cacao tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ fiofio. ni ebaa nyɛmɔ ni ayɔɔ ni akɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ shi

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, wet weather. Rain droplets splash the fungal spores onto pods, but pruning dark branches and clearing weeds lets air and sunlight in to keep pods dry.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ shwieɔ fungal spores nɔ yɛ pods lɛ anɔ. Shi niji ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ ni oookpa ni ojie jwɛi lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted directly in open fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that lose water rapidly in direct sunlight. They need temporary shade from crops like plantains or bananas during their first few years until their root systems grow strong enough to handle full heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛbiɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo bananas amli yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli. Kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ ahe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ la ni tsoɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees growing tall and thin like sticks without sprouting wide branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ mlɛo tamɔ tso nine ni egbɛɛɛ niji babaoo eshwaaa lɛ?

english: Trees grow tall and thin when they receive too much shade from big forest trees. They stretch upwards trying to reach sunlight, which leaves them weak; trimming shade canopy trees helps them grow broader and stronger branches.
ga: Tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ́ amɛná hulutsoo babaoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ adɛŋ. Amɛkpã amɛhe kɛtee ŋwɛi ni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. ni haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ Afolɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ koni eha hulutsoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ mli waa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do flowers on my cocoa trunk drop off before turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by prolonged dry weather, lack of soil nutrients, or when tiny pollinating insects like midges are absent. Adequate shade and healthy soil help the tree hold onto its flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii tamɔ midges bɛ lɛ, hulutsoo be ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: What causes tiny white bugs to cover my crop leaves and make them curl up?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ Haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ni ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Those white patches are usually mealybugs or sap-sucking insects. They suck the food juices out of leaves, weakening the plant and spreading diseases between crops unless they are treated early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ nɛɛ ji mealybugs loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu. Amɛmuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli. Ehaa tsei gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɛɔ helai eshwaa tsei ateŋ. ja atsa lɛ mra

english: Why should I cut off healthy-looking water branches growing from the base of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo nu niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Water shoots grow fast and steal water and nutrients that the tree needs to make cocoa pods. Removing them forces the tree to send its energy directly into developing healthy fruit on the main trunk.
ga: Tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛfee kookoo ŋmeii. Kɛ́ ajieɔ amɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ titri lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farm crops are not getting enough food from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When crops lack nutrients, their leaves turn pale green or yellow from the tips inward, growth slows down, and fruits remain small. Applying compost or fertilizer restores missing nutrients to nourish the plant.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛmligbɛ. shweremɔ blɛoo Ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ faaa lolo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aba ekoŋŋ koni ekɛha tso lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava on a plot where cocoa trees were destroyed by disease?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii, tamɔ ŋmei, yɛ shikpɔŋ ni helai efite cacao tsei lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, food crops like cassava or plantain can grow safely on that land because most cocoa-specific viruses do not affect food crops, allowing the soil to rest while still providing food and income.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, helai ni baa kookoo nɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo enaaa niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe yɛ be mli ni eji niyenii kɛ shika jɛɛhe lolo.

english: How does spraying my crops with government-provided fungicides help them recover after sickness?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni nɔyeli lɛ kɛhaa lɛ ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ hela sɛɛ?

english: Fungicide sprays kill the tiny invisible fungi causing spots and rot on your plants. Once the infection is stopped, the tree stops losing resources to disease and can focus on producing fresh leaves and healthy pods.
ga: Spray ni ajieɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gbeɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii. Mɛi ni anaaa ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa otsei lɛ anɔ lɛ. Kɛji hela lɛ kpa Tso lɛ baakpa nibii ni efiteɔ yɛ helai ahe lɛ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama baai heei kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a major food source plants need to stay green and grow tall. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring the green color back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ jɛɛhe titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves roll inward and curl up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli ni amɛshwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl up in heat to trap moisture and slow down water loss. It is the plant's natural shield to survive hot, dry periods without drying out.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛ dɔlɛ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu lɛ aya hiɛ fiofio. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko haa tsei koni amɛhi shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli ni tso lɛ gĩii.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and bent when I plant them in hard soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams are roots that need soft, loose soil to push through as they grow. When soil is hard, the tuber cannot stretch properly, leading to short, twisted, or small yams.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji shishifãi ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛtsɔ mli beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kuku, ni efite, loo bibii baa.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines grow big green leaves everywhere but give me very few tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ he fɛɛ he shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: If soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, sweet potatoes put all their energy into making leafy vines above ground instead of storing energy in the tubers below.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Sweet potato hu kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ wain tsei ni baai yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato yitso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ

english: Pepper flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil dries out completely. Keep the soil evenly moist to help the flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ koni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get black, flat spots at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔi diji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant. It usually happens when watering is uneven, making it hard for roots to draw calcium from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with small cob size when I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and food to form large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmei agbo ni mli wa.

english: Why should I wait until the main rainy season settles before planting my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Maize seeds need steady soil moisture to sprout and grow strong roots. Planting too early in dry soil can scorch the seeds or destroy weak seedlings before rains become regular.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui hia shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã dumɔwui lɛ loo egbe dumɔwui ni egbɔjɔ lɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ aba.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field help my next season's crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil with free fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants lack nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to build strong stems and produce healthy green leaves that catch sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛma amɛshishifãi ni wa ni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni baanyɛ aŋɔ hulu la lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without big trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei wuji komɛi bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like small children—their tender leaves burn easily under the scorching direct sun. Planting shade crops like plantain beside them creates a cool canopy that keeps the soil moist and protects the cocoa while it establishes roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii tamɔ gbekɛbii bibii. Amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo baa ni ebuɔ kookoo lɛ he beni eshishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with big green leaves, but the tubers under the ground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are crowded, the cassava puts all its energy into growing tall leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to swell the roots into large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niyenii kpakpahi kɛ yaa si konɛ e ha nɛ sisifã ɔmɛ nɛ a gblɛɛ nɛ a pee bulb nguahi.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without turning into any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks sufficient water, or when bees and wind fail to shake pollen inside the flowers to turn them into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atswa pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi ko mli lɛ kɛyashi ebaatsɔ aduawai.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to chew holes in the leaves of my green maize overnight?
ga: Mɛni ha ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwie bu yɛ mi ŋmãa baai eŋɔli lɛ amli nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. The adult moths lay eggs on young maize leaves at night, and the hatched caterpillars hide inside the plant's funnel to feed on the tender leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm kɛ enɛ baa. Kplukai ni eda lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baa bibii anɔ gbɛkɛ. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller fruits when I put three or four seeds together into one small planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ to dumɔ bu bibioo kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants with smaller yields compared to plants given enough room to grow.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baa kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara lɛ ahe.

english: Why does rainwater sit on top of my soil for days instead of sinking down into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: This happens when soil is heavy clay or heavily compacted from footsteps and clearing. When soil particles are squeezed tight, water cannot pass through easily, which can drown plant roots by cutting off air.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo ebɔle ehe kɛjɛ najiaŋdamɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii amli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ mli nibii bibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Nu nyɛŋ atsɔ mli mlɛo. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly on my farm even after I clear them completely with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miikwɛ̃ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dade shwie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ moŋ

english: Cutting weeds with a cutlass only removes the top leaves while leaving underground roots and hidden weed seeds intact in the warm, wet soil, allowing them to sprout again almost immediately.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne ŋmɔ jwɛi lɛ, ebaajie baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi kɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ehiɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛshwereɔ ekoŋŋ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my dried corn grains turn into dust and get filled with tiny insects after a few months in the storage room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli sũ kɛ kooloi bibii lɛ? Ani eyi mli obɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛto he nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ?

english: Storage insects like grain weevils burrow inside dried corn kernels to feed and lay eggs. If the grain is not dried properly to low moisture levels or stored in airtight bags, the pests multiply rapidly and destroy the crop.
ga: Kplukai ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe tamɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli koni amɛye niyenii ni amɛwo ŋmeii. Kɛji akɛ agbiko dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi loo akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ faa oya ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Leaf curl is often caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that transmit plant viruses. As the insects suck the sap from tender shoots, the leaves distort and stop growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kooloi bibii nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to spray my farm around March or April?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ March loo April he lɛ?

english: March and April mark the start of the major rainy season in Ghana. The sudden moisture causes dormant insect eggs to hatch all at once, leading to severe pest outbreaks. Spraying at this specific time destroys pests before they can multiply and ruin your young crops.
ga: March kɛ April ji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee yɛ Ghana. Fɛ̃i ni baa trukaa lɛ haa kooloi bibii ni wɔɔ lɛ awɔlɔi feɔ. Amɛ fɛɛ amɛfɔ shikome ni amɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni naa wa baa Nɛkɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli nɛɛ kpataa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahiɛ dani amɛshwereɔ ni amɛfiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ.

english: What is this 'someboa' pest that other farmers talk about during the early rains?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ ‘Soboa’ tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ ni okwaafoi krokomɛi wieɔ he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ mli?

english: Someboa' is a local Twi term used for destructive caterpillars or insect pests (like armyworms). They tend to emerge rapidly right after the early rains in March or April to feed on fresh foliage.
ga: Someboa’ ji maŋ lɛ mli Twi wiemɔ ni tsɔɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei kroko ni fiteɔ nii (tamɔ asraafoi aŋmei). Amɛfɔɔ kpojee oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ March loo April mli lɛ sɛɛ. koni eye baai heei

english: Why do pests seem to attack my crops so suddenly and aggressively after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ trukaa kɛ yiwalɛ nifeemɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: During the dry season, pests remain hidden or in egg form in the soil. When the first rains arrive, the heat and moisture create ideal conditions for thousands of pest eggs to hatch simultaneously, making the attack feel sudden and severe.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai hiɔ shi yɛ teemɔŋ loo amɛfeɔ oval yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ baa lɛ Dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni ŋmeii akpei abɔ afɔ yɛ be kome mli, ni no haa tutuamɔi baa trukaa kɛ yiwalɛ.

english: Why do certain farm pests appear at the exact same time every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ be kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Pests follow natural seasonal cycles tied to rainfall and temperature. In Ghana, months like March and April bring the moisture and young leaf growth that trigger specific pests to break out of their dormant stage each year.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nyiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli be mli nibii ni kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ dɔlɛ yɔɔ tsakpaa lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ Ghana lɛ, nyɔji tamɔ March kɛ April Fɛ̃i kɛ baai bibii ni shwereɔ lɛ haa kooloi pɔtɛɛ komɛi joɔ wɔɔhe daa afi.

english: How do I know the right time to spray chemicals on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: The best time to spray is at the very beginning of the rainy season (March/April) or at the first sign of pest activity. Waiting until pests have fully multiplied makes them harder to control and damages your crops beyond recovery.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse nii ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. (March/April) loo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai eba lɛ mli. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ baafa kwraa lɛ, ebaaha ewa akɛ oookudɔ ni ofite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fe bɔ ni obaanyɛ okɛtsu nii.

english: What happens to my farm if I miss the early spraying window in March or April?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mifo mi-sprayment be lɛ mli mra yɛ March loo April mli?

english: If you miss spraying during early pest emergence, populations of pests like 'someboa' will grow exponentially. They will eat the soft young shoots of your crops, causing heavy yield losses that are difficult and expensive to fix later.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shishijee tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ashishijee be lɛ mli lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ‘Soboa’ lɛ ayibɔ baaya hiɛ waa. Amɛbaaye odumɔ nii lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ fiteɔ babaoo. Enɛ wa ni ejara wa ni esa akɛ asaa sɛɛ mli.

english: Is it better to spray my crops in the afternoon sun or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ tsofa yɛ shwane loo leebi?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon. Spraying during intense midday heat causes the chemical to evaporate too fast and can cause chemical burns on your crop leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ lɛ leebi loo shwane mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha tsofai lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ. Ni ebaanyɛ eha tsofa ashã otso lɛ baai lɛ.

english: Does rainy weather mean pests will automatically increase on my crops?
ga: Ani nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baaya hiɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Yes, high moisture combined with warm weather creates high humidity, which speeds up insect reproduction and fungal growth. Rain also encourages plants to grow fresh leaves, which attract hungry pests.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ fataa he lɛ haa hulutsoo ni fa babaoo baa. ni haa kooloi bibii lɛ fɔɔ oya, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ hu daa lɛ. Nugbɔ hu yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ baai heei, ni gbalaa kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: How can I spot an early pest invasion before my crops get destroyed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana tsɛŋemɔ hela ko mra dani akpata miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahiɛ?

english: Inspect your crops regularly early in the morning. Look under the leaves and inside young shoots for tiny holes, small eggs, or young caterpillars ('someboa'). Finding them early allows you to spray before widespread damage occurs.
ga: Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli daa leebi. Kwɛmɔ baai kɛ tsei bibii ashishi kɛha buji bibii, ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii (‘someboa’). Kɛ́ ona amɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua. Enɛ baaha onyɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ dani nɔ ko ni fiteɔ nii babaoo aba.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to clear land and prepare early before March?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni asaa he dani March aba lɛ?

english: Preparing early allows you to plant with the very first rains and apply protective sprays right as seasonal pests emerge in March or April, giving your crops a strong head start over weeds and pests.
ga: Hesaamɔ mra Ehaa onyɛɔ oduɔ tsei yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Ni okɛ tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ atsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baa yɛ March loo April mli. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee nɔ ni hi fe jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Is there a different way I am supposed to plant 'agric' hybrid seeds compared to the traditional local seeds my family has always used?
ga: Ani gbɛ kroko yɛ ni esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ makwɛ ‘kwaayeli’ mli dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni teɔ shi ewoɔ maŋ lɛ mli kusum dumɔwui ni miweku lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: No, both agric (improved) and local seeds follow the exact same planting methods, growth stages, and field conditions. You plant them in the soil at the same depths and spacings, though agric seeds are bred to give you higher yields under good care.
ga: Dabi, okwaayeli dumɔwui hu jeee nakai. (Afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ) ni akɛ gbɛi tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui. shweremɔ be kɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ hei ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ yɛ lɛ ji ekome pɛpɛɛpɛ Oduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ kome mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ akwɛɔ okwaayeli dumɔwui anɔ koni eha bo yibii babaoo yɛ kwɛmɔ kpakpa shishi moŋ.

english: Do I need to clear and prepare my land differently if I choose to plant improved agric seeds instead of local seeds?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mafo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni masaa he yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ? Kɛji mihala akɛ madu okwaayeli dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Land preparation is the same for both improved agric and local seeds. Both types require well-cleared, loosened soil with proper drainage to sprout and grow strong root systems.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ saamɔ ji nɔ kome kɛha okwaayeli dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui fɛɛ. Henɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni ajie nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ajie lɛ kpo ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛdara.

english: How deep should I put my seeds in the ground so that they sprout properly?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: As a general rule, seeds should be planted at a depth roughly two to three times their thickness. Planting too deep prevents the young shoot from reaching the surface, while planting too shallow can cause the seed to dry out or be eaten by birds.
ga: Taakɛ eji mla lɛ, esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ aaafee amɛhe 2-3 toi. Kɛ́ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi loo okpoi aye amɛ.

english: Do improved agric crop varieties need more rain or water to grow than our local crops?
ga: Ani okwaayeli mli nibii srɔtoi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ biɔ nugbɔ loo nu babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ fe wɔ maŋ tsei lɛ?

english: Both agric and local varieties go through the same growth stages and require water to develop properly. However, many improved agric varieties are bred to tolerate dry spells better while still following the same basic growth process.
ga: Okwaayeli kɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi lɛ fɛɛ tsɔɔ dalɛ mli ni amɛbiɔ nu koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛlɛ, afɔ okwaayeli mli tsei srɔtoi babaoo ni atsake amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi anaa jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shishijee dalɛ gbɛ lɛ kã he eji nakai nɔŋŋ.

english: Do improved agric crops go through different growth stages compared to the local crops I am used to?
ga: Ani okwaayeli mli nibii ni atsake lɛ tsɔɔ dalɛ shihilɛi srɔtoi amli kɛ akɛto maŋbii tsei ni mile amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe?

english: All crops follow the same main growth stages: germination, leafy vegetative growth, flowering, and producing fruit or grain. Improved agric varieties simply complete these stages more uniformly and often faster.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ dalɛ mli nibii titri kome: kwɛ̃mɔ, tsei adalɛ, fɔfɔi, kɛ aduawai loo dumɔwui afeemɔ. Okwaayeli henɔi ni atsake lɛ baagbe gbɛi nɛɛ anaa daa ni bei pii lɛ oya.

english: Do improved agric crops require a different amount of sunlight compared to local crop varieties?
ga: Ani okwaayeli mli nibii ni atsake lɛ biɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛ akɛto maŋ lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi ahe?

english: No, both agric and local varieties of the same crop have the same natural requirement for sunlight to feed themselves and grow strong plants.
ga: Dabi, okwaayeli mli kooloi kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hiamɔ nii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛha hulu la koni amɛkɛkwɛ amɛhe ni amɛdu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: If I put fertilizer on local seeds, will they yield as much food as the improved agric seeds?
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui wo mli lɛ Ani ebaaná niyenii babaoo tamɔ okwaayeli dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ?

english: Local seeds will grow better with fertilizer, but improved agric seeds are specially bred to turn nutrients into food much more efficiently, producing a significantly larger harvest than local varieties under the same conditions.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli. Shi akwɛɔ okwaayeli mli dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni akɛtsake niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ awo niyenii mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi lɛ yɛ shihilɛi komekomei amli.

english: Does planting agric crops mean I have to protect them from pests differently than local crops?
ga: Ani okwaayeli mli nibii ni miduɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ mabu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe maŋbii tsei lɛ?

english: The basic methods for protecting your field from pests are identical for both seed types. In fact, many improved agric varieties are already bred with natural strength to resist common pests and diseases better than local seeds.
ga: Gbɛi titrii ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ ji ekome kɛha dumɔwui henɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ Afɔ okwaayeli mli tsei srɔtoi babaoo ni atsake amɛ koni amɛná adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni amɛkɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Can I plant improved agric seeds in the exact same field alongside my local seed varieties?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu okwaayeli dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ mimaŋ dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, you can plant them in the same field because they require the same soil, planting techniques, and weather conditions. However, keeping them in separate rows makes it easier for you to see the difference in yield at harvest time.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okwɛ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ taakɛ amɛbiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii Shi kɛlɛ, kɛ́ agbala amɛmli lɛ, ebaaha efee mlɛo akɛ aaale srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ yibiiwoo mli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why can't I just save seeds from my harvested agric crop to plant next season like I do with local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ okwaayeli mli nibii amli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli tamɔ bɔ ni manyɛ mafee kɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Local seeds pass their strong traits down every year, but saved seeds from hybrid agric crops lose their high-yielding strength in the second generation. Buying fresh agric seeds each season ensures you keep getting high yields.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ baatsɔɔ amɛsu ni mli wa lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. Shi dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛ okwaayeli tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Okwaayeli dumɔwui heei ni ooohe yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ baaha onine ashɛ sɛɛnamɔi babaoo nɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I clear all the big trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and burn easily under strong heat. Large trees act as natural umbrellas, keeping the ground moist and protecting young cocoa from direct sun until they are mature enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ agbo bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and weak with small harvests when I plant seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛ ŋmaa bibioo pɛ ni miduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight with each other for space, sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition leaves all the plants starved and weak.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ he ko, hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my farm make the soil better for my cassava during the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmeii ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has the natural ability to take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally enriches the land with free food for future crops.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛyɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up into tight tubes during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔji ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a defense mechanism to save water. By rolling up, less leaf surface is exposed to the hot sun, which prevents moisture from evaporating too quickly during dry spells.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛbu nu he. kɛji akɛ abɔle ehe lɛ Ba lɛ hiɛ baafee nɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɛɛ ehe tsɔ. Enɛ haaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ aya oya tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black while they are still growing on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato aduawai lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ yɛ be mli ni edaa lolo yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This issue, called blossom-end rot, usually happens when the plant gets irregular water. When soil dries out completely and then gets soaked, the plant cannot absorb calcium evenly, causing the bottom of the fruit to spoil.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu daa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa ni edɔ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ calcium daa. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ ashishi shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of green leaves but produce very tiny tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ miiya hiɛ waa nɛkɛ? Baai eŋɔlii babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excess fertilizer, the plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves and branches above ground instead of sending energy down to build heavy tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai kɛ tsei niji wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu hewalɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛfee yitso ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to clear small mounds and stake my yam vines high up on sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋtayaa bibioo ko? Ni adu sweet potato wain tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food for the tubers below. Staking also lifts leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and rotting.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei ahe tsei kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants shrinking and twisting up so that no fruits grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashɛ he ko ni yibii ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Twisted pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or mites that suck plant sap and spread viruses. These pests stunt the plant's growth and stop it from flowering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf twist baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ tsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa ni amɛkpaa fɔfɔi.

english: Why shouldn't I put fertilizer on my crops right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer away off the farm or pushes it too deep into the ground before the roots have a chance to soak it up, wasting your money and labor.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔji amli ŋmɔshi nibii loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ dani shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ. Efiteɔ shika kɛ nitsumɔ fɛɛ.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I saved from my previous harvest fail to grow when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can lose their ability to grow if they were stored with too much moisture, damaged by heat, or eaten internally by insects like weevils before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ afite nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Dɔlɛ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni ayeɔ yɛ mli dani aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and sensitive to direct, intense sunlight. Without shade trees or plantain plants to protect them, the strong heat scorches the leaves, causing them to dry up and fall off.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni buɔ he lɛ bɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do people tell me to cover the ground around my crop roots with dry grass or old leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbo loo baai momo awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei shishifãi ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, keeps the dirt cool, traps moisture so you do not have to water as often, and stops weeds from taking over your crop.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli bɔni afee ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu awo mli shii abɔ. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye onibii anɔ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow from the middle of the leaf down to the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ kɛmiiya shishi kɛmiiya shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is a key nutrient they need to stay green and grow strong. Applying the right fertilizer at the right time helps them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge leafy bushes on top, but very small tubers underground when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ jwɛi wuji yɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛji akpa?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen or if plants are placed too close together, the cassava spends all its energy growing leaves instead of storing food in the roots to make big tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo akɛ tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ tsuɔ nii. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests and diseases that attack that specific crop to multiply in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi kɛ helai ni tutuaa nakai tso lɛ koni amɛshwere yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes these little worms to eat holes in the leaves and center of my growing maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei tsei ni miida lɛ ahe lɛ baai kɛ amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by small moths. They hide inside the center leaf fold of the plant and feed on young leaves, which can destroy the crop if not treated early.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli lɛ amli. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii oya.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak even when there is enough rain falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before your crops can reach them, effectively starving your crops.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize crops grow thin and weak when I plant four or five seeds in one single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ mli tsɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ waa beni midu dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds grow in one hole, the roots fight each other for limited water and soil nutrients, leaving every single plant weak and unable to produce big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni fa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry spell before the real rainy season begins. If you plant too early, the seeds will sprout but then dry up and die from the heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi yɛ latsaa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before any small fruits can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani aduawai bibii lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is extremely hot and dry, or when the plant receives uneven water. High heat stresses the flower, causing it to dry up and drop off instead of forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. aloo kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛ nu nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa fɔfɔi lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa amɛgbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: When is the best time of the year for me to plant cassava stem cuttings?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu ŋmei?

english: It is best to plant cassava stem cuttings at the start of the rainy season. This allows the cuttings to absorb plenty of water to establish strong root systems before any dry spell begins.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmei ni afo lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Enɛ haa tsei niji lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu babaoo koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers, but only a few turn into real pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers if they lack enough water or nutrients, or if tiny insects do not pollinate them. Feeding the soil and maintaining shade helps the tree carry more pods to maturity.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulutsoo ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔi babaoo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eshɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and falling off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the cocoa plants are getting too much direct sunlight without shade, or the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen. Shade and proper fertilizer restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ cacao tso lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo be ko bɛ he. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen, hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ekoŋŋ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads during wet and humid weather. Trimming overgrown branches to let air and sunlight in helps prevent the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la aba lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why am I finding small holes all over the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ

english: Small holes in maize leaves are typically caused by fall armyworms or leaf-eating caterpillars. Checking your farm early allows you to use safe pest treatments before the insects damage the growing tips.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbee shi loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. Okwaafoi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe atsu nii ni okɛjie tsɛŋemɔ helai. Dani kooloi bibii baafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ

english: How do I know if my soil lacks the right food for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: When soil lacks nutrients, crop growth slows down, leaves turn yellow or purplish, and plants look thin. Testing the soil or applying well-rotted manure and fertilizer restores soil health.
ga: Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ adalɛ baafee mlɛo. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo purple. ni tsei lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa loo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I clear weeds from around the base of my crops instead of letting them stay?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi moŋ fe ni mahã amɛhi shi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds gives your crops full access to the food in the soil so they can grow bigger and produce higher yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni agbeɔ lɛ haa onibii lɛ naa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it important for me to prune dead or weak branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso niji ni egboi loo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Pruned trees allow sunlight and fresh air to reach inner branches, which reduces pest hiding spots and fungus while directing the tree's strength into producing healthy pods.
ga: Tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa hei ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ baa shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekwɛɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa aba.

english: Cocoa pods are mature and ready when their outer color changes completely from green or dark red to bright yellow or orange. Harvesting at this stage ensures full seed quality.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ eda ni amɛfee klalo kɛji amɛ kponɔgbɛ su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse waa. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young cocoa trees usually mean they are receiving too much direct sunlight or not enough water. Young cocoa trees need shade from plantain trees or shade trees to protect them while their root system establishes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ cacao tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ miiná lɛ babaoo loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ bɛ. Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ dumɔwui loo hulutsoo tsei amli kɛha hebuu yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ.

english: What causes tiny caterpillars to eat the inside leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which burrow inside the growing tip of maize plants. Identifying them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem mixtures saves the crop from damage.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ. Amɛyɔsemɔ mra Ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo neem ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ baahere ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala kɛjɛ fitemɔ mli.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny pests like aphids, thrips, or whiteflies sucking nutrients from the leaves. Managing these insects early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo whiteflies ni nuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: How do I know if my farm soil needs fertilizer before I plant my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu dumɔwui?

english: If previous crops grew slowly, had pale leaves, or produced smaller yields, the soil lacks key nutrients. Adding animal manure, compost, or crop fertilizer restores nutrients for healthy growth.
ga: Kɛji tso ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ da blɛoo, eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo ewoɔ yibii fioo. Niyenii nibii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I stop weeds from taking over my farm without spending a lot of money on weedicides?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi jwɛi ni yeɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa ni mikɛ shika babaoo tsuuu nii yɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ahe?

english: Planting cover crops like cowpeas or velvet beans spreads across the soil, blocking light from weeds while putting valuable nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ cowpeas loo velvet beans ni aduɔ lɛ baaha amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni ekɛ nitrogen ni jara wa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excessive water pools around them in dense soil. Planting cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Yam leaves need sunlight to produce energy for growing tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves high off the ground, maximizing sunlight and reducing fungal soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ ni oha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off the plant without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plant suffers from sudden high heat, dry soil, or uneven watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch prevents blossom drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ mli edɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Extra shoots compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients and water, resulting in smaller fruit. Leaving only two or three healthy shoots ensures high-quality plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji aduawai bibii. Kɛji akɛ ashi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ yɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha plantains ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu tsei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: It is best to wait until the ground gets thoroughly soaked by two or three heavy rains. Planting after only one light rain risks having seeds sprout and die if a dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ aaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo pɛ sɛɛ Oshara yɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are my seeds taking so long to sprout even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Some crop seeds naturally take longer to break dormancy, often needing three to four weeks or more to sprout depending on the soil temperature, seed coat thickness, and moisture levels.
ga: Dumɔwui komɛi heɔ be babaoo fe bɔ ni sa dani amɛfoɔ wɔɔhe mli. Bei pii lɛ, amɛheɔ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ loo nɔ ni fe nakai dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Edamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ dɔlɛ nɔ dumɔwui atade lɛ mlitsilɛ kɛ latsaa lɛ nɔ

english: If I plant 100 seeds at the same time, why do only a few sprout in the first month while others come up later?
ga: Kɛ́ midu dumɔwui 100 shikome lɛ, mɛni hewɔ fioo pɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli shi ekrokomɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds rarely sprout all at once because individual seeds have slight variations in strength, depth in the soil, and seed coat thickness, which leads to staggered germination over several weeks.
ga: Efɔɔɔ kaa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ shikome ejaakɛ esoro dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko hewalɛ fioo, bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ ha, kɛ bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ ahe tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔi lɛ yɔɔ ha. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ otsii babaoo amli.

english: How long should I keep watering a seedbed before assuming the unsprouted seeds have failed?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ maya nɔ mawo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ nu dani mamu sane naa akɛ dumɔwui ni ekwɛko lɛ egbo?

english: You should maintain continuous watering and care for at least 4 to 6 weeks, as many tree and crop species require a full month or more before initial sprouts begin to emerge.
ga: Esa akɛ oya nɔ okɛ nu awo mli ni okwɛ nɔ kɛ hoo lɛ otsii 4 kɛyashi 6, ejaakɛ tsei kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo biɔ nyɔŋ muu fɛɛ loo nɔ ni fe nakai dani amɛjeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Do I need to keep watering my seedbed even if I don't see any green shoots coming out yet?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni maya nɔ mawo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ nu eyɛ mli akɛ minako ŋmeii eŋɔli ko lolo moŋ?

english: Yes, seeds require constant moisture from the very beginning to soften their outer shells and trigger growth, so watering must continue steadily even before any shoots appear above the soil.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, dumɔwui he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be kɛjɛ shishijee koni amɛha kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afee blɛoo ni eha amɛdara. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ aya nɔ afɔ nu lɛ nɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po.

english: How often should I water my newly planted seeds so they do not dry out in the hot sun?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo midumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ nu koni amɛkagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Nursery soil should be kept continuously moist like a wrung-out sponge, which usually means light watering once or twice a day depending on sunshine, so the seeds never dry out before sprouting.
ga: Esa akɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be tamɔ sponji ni mli efɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ afɔ nu fioo shikome loo shii enyɔ daa gbi. Edamɔ hulu la nɔ No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ gĩii dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Can I harvest seeds from a single healthy tree on my farm to raise new seedlings?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa dumɔwui kɛjɛ tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛdu dumɔwui heei?

english: Yes, you can collect seeds or cuttings from a single mother tree, but keep in mind that seedlings from that same tree may still sprout and grow at slightly different rates.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ obua dumɔwui loo ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛjɛ tso ni ji fɔlɔ kome lɛ mli. Shi ha ehi ojwɛŋmɔ mli akɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ tso kome mli lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ lolo ni amɛdara yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto fioo nɔ.

english: Will seeds taken from the exact same parent tree all grow into shoots at the same speed?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nyɛ tso kome mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii yɛ oyaiyeli ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ mli?

english: No, even seeds gathered from the same mother tree carry natural genetic differences and will experience slight variations in sunlight and soil nutrients, causing them to sprout at different speeds.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso kome mli lɛ po yɛ srɔtoi yɛ amɛfɔmɔ su mli. ni ebaakpe hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yɔɔ srɔto fioo Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli.

english: Is it normal for only a small number of seeds to sprout early while the rest take much longer?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni ja akɛ dumɔwui fioo komɛi baakwɛ̃ oya shi nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo?

english: Yes, it is common for a small batch—like 30 out of a larger group—to sprout early in the first four weeks while the rest take additional time to break through the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ tsei akui bibii, tamɔ 30 ni jɛ kuu wulu mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi lɛ baahe be kroko ni amɛkɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Is there anything I can do to help my tree seeds sprout faster without long delays?
ga: Ani nɔ ko yɛ ni manyɛ mafee ni baaye abua mitso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni mikɛ be babaoo ehiɛɛɛ mli?

english: Soaking hard seeds in clean water overnight or gently scratching their outer coat before planting helps moisture enter faster, which reduces germination delays.
ga: Okɛ dumɔwui ni wa lɛ awo nu ni mli tse mli nyɔɔŋ kome loo okɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ abɔ he blɛoo. Dani abaadu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ abote mli oya. Enɛ haa be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Does planting my seeds too deep in the soil delay when the shoots come up?
ga: Ani midumɔwui lɛ ni mikɛbaadu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃mɔ asɛɛ afo?

english: Yes, seeds buried too deep use up extra energy trying to reach the surface, which causes a delay in sprouting or can prevent the shoot from coming up at all.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni afu amɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa kwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii lɛ akakwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Why do some of my harvested coconuts turn soft and mushy inside instead of staying firm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi ni akpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ mligbɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakpɛtɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Coconuts turn soft and mushy inside when they are overripe, damaged during harvest, or infected by fungal rot through cracks. Harvesting at the right stage and avoiding dropping them hard on rocks or bare ground prevents this spoilage.
ga: Kokoo lɛ baafee bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ emli kɛji aho lɛ fe nine. Efite yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ emɔ lɛ Nikpamɔ yɛ be ni sa mli ni ajie kɛjɛ tɛi loo hei ni agbele nɔ babaoo lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my coconut trees drop their young green fruits before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tso lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Young coconuts fall off early mainly due to severe water stress, lack of soil nutrients like potassium, or attacks by sap-sucking insects like the coconut bug. Regular watering during dry spells and applying proper fertilizer help the tree retain its fruit.
ga: Kokooi bibii lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ oya, titri lɛ yɛ nu he haomɔ ni naa wa hewɔ. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium, loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii, tamɔ ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa mɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How can I tell if a coconut on my tree is ready for drinking water versus making oil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ efee klalo kɛha nu ni anuɔ vs.

english: Coconuts for drinking water are harvested while green at around 7 to 8 months when they are full of sweet liquid. Coconuts for oil extraction are left on the tree for 11 to 12 months until the husk turns brown and dry, signaling that the meat inside has hardened and filled with rich oil.
ga: Akpaa ŋmeii ni akɛnuɔ nu lɛ be mli ni amɛji ŋmɔji, yɛ be mli ni amɛye aaafee nyɔji 7 kɛyashi 8 beni ŋmeii lɛ amli eyi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Ashiɔ ŋmeii ni akɛjieɔ fɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 12 kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni egbiɔ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ loo lɛ wa ni fɔ eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my coconut trees turning yellow and all the fruits dropping off suddenly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ akokoso tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ trukaa ni enɔ yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: This is often caused by Cape Saint Paul Wilt Disease, a lethal infection spread by tiny insects that attack coconut palms in Ghana. Planting resistant coconut varieties, such as Sri Lanka Green Dwarf hybrids, is the best long-term defense against this disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Cape Saint Paul Wilt hela, ni ji hela ko ni naa wa ni kooloi bibii ni tutuaa ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Kokoo henɔi ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ nii tamɔ Sri Lanka ŋmɔŋ ni ji dwarf hybrid lɛ ni yaa hiɛ. Enɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela nɛɛ naa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do my stored harvested crops get full of tiny holes and small insects after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii kɛ kooloi bibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weevils and grain beetles lay invisible eggs in harvested crops, which hatch when stored in warm or damp conditions. Drying your harvested crops completely under the sun and storing them in sealed, airtight bags starves these pests of air and prevents damage.
ga: Kplukai kɛ ŋmeii woɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ anɔ. Amɛfɔ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ amɛ tee he ko ni hulutsoo loo hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha okpamɔ nii lɛ agbi yɛ hulu lɛ shishi ni okɛwo kotoku ko ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akagbala bo, ni ebaatsi nɔ ni efite lɛ naa.
