english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to stay dark green and grow fast. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer to the soil restores the green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ni amɛdara oya. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my main crops grow better when I plant groundnuts or beans alongside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots in the soil. When these roots break down, they release natural fertilizer that feeds nearby crops and improves overall soil health.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ gbee shi lɛ Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ he waa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop trees very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tsei lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni ekɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting trees too close together forces them to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and small yields. Giving each tree proper space allows it to spread its leaves, absorb sunlight, and produce larger fruits.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni egbɛ baai lɛ eshwã, eŋɔ hulu la, ni ewo yibii wuji.

english: Why is it important for me to trim off dead leaves and old branches from my crop trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ baai ni egboi kɛ tsei lɛ aniji momoi amli lɛ?

english: Dead leaves and overcrowded branches block air flow and trap moisture, creating a perfect home for fungi and pests. Pruning opens up the tree to sunlight, reduces disease risks, and directs the plant's energy into growing healthy fruit.
ga: Baai ni egboi kɛ niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa ni emɔɔ nu mli. Enɛ haa shia ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baa. Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ gbeleɔ ehe kɛhaa hulu la. Ehaa helai baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ koni amɛwo yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ

english: Why do my harvested fruits spoil and rot quickly if I pick them right after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ oya kɛji mikpa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops harvested right after rain are swollen with excess water and covered in moisture, which speeds up rotting and mold growth. Waiting a day or two for the field and fruit to dry out before picking extends their shelf life significantly.
ga: Tsei ni akpaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baafu kɛ nu ni fa fe nine ni ŋmɔtɔ baaha amɛhe. ni haa fitemɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yaa hiɛ oya. Kɛ́ omɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ ni ŋmɔji lɛ kɛ aduawai lɛ agbi dani okɛto lɛ, ebaaha amɛshihilɛ be aya hiɛ waa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for healthy leaf growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-decomposed manure will help the leaves turn green and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ adara Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni eha amɛdaramɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously in the same soil drains specific plant food and lets pests and diseases build up in the field. Swapping maize with leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas returns nitrogen to the soil and stops pest cycles.
ga: Abele ni yaa nɔ akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. kɛ gbɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai bua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Abele ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmãa lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa.

english: Covering the ground with dry plant material, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, retains rainwater much longer during dry spells, and stops weeds from sprouting and stealing nutrients from your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Ekɛ nugbɔ nu toɔ be babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the necessary shade and moisture cocoa seedlings need during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kɛha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I have to construct large soil mounds before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ama gɔŋ agbo dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Making big mounds loosens the earth so yam tubers can swell and grow deep without fighting hard ground. Mounding also protects yam roots from standing water, which causes the tubers to rot.
ga: Gɔji wuji ni afeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa akpee. Mounding hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ sweet potato shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ he. ni haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ

english: How do I choose the right cassava stems from my harvest to plant for next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni sa kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni madu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Select mature, healthy stems from plants that are 8 to 12 months old and show no signs of disease or pest damage. Cut pieces from the middle part of the stem that have at least 4 to 6 healthy buds.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni edara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ni hela loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe okadi ko bɛ amɛhe lɛ amli. Kpɔ̃ɔ fãi kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni kɛ hoo lɛ, eyɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 4 kɛyashi 6.

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid on corn leaves and feed inside the growing tip of the plant. Applying recommended organic sprays or approved chemical treatments directly into the funnel early in the morning destroys them.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa baa nɔ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni miida lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ wo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaakpata amɛhiɛ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juice from the underside of the leaves, or by a plant virus. Spraying the plants with neem leaf extract or soapy water helps control these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amli Kɛ́ akɛ neem baa mli nu loo nu ni akɛ saamɔ fee lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the stems before setting any small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani tomato bibii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off without setting fruit when the air gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or if there is too much nitrogen fertilizer. Giving the plants consistent water and light shade during hot weeks helps save the blooms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo kɛji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli lɛ Nu ni oooha tso lɛ be fɛɛ be ni okɛ hulutsoo awo mli yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni ekwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are fully ripe and ready to be dug up from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts are ready for harvest when the leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off, and when you check inside a few mature pods and see that the inner shell skin has turned dark brown or black.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmeii fioo komɛi ni eda lɛ amli ni ona akɛ mligbɛ ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight when they are small. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain creates living shade to protect the cocoa trees from scorching sun and soil dryness during their first few years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛkpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be ni buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ he.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to spread its roots and leaves to grow strong.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ eshwã koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, a key food plant leaves need to stay green and healthy. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or animal manure helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni niyenii titri tsei lɛ baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them during dry weather?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ amli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops heat from drying out the earth too quickly. It holds moisture in the ground for the plant roots and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ekpa dɔlɛ ni haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha tsei shishifãi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my farm before planting seeds or after the crops sprout?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu dumɔwui loo beni tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: It is usually best to apply fertilizer after the seeds sprout and form early roots. Applying it too early can waste the fertilizer or burn delicate new seeds before roots are ready to feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni amɛtswa shishifãi kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo mli oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo eshã dumɔwui heei dani shishifãi lɛ afee klalo akɛ amɛbaaye nii.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and leaves rolled up with dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni baa lɛ yɛ muji yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a pest that hides inside the center whorl of young maize plants and feeds on soft leaf tissue.
ga: Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe fãji lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from under the leaves, or by plant viruses spread by those same insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nakai kooloi bibii lɛ nɔŋŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants suffer from heat stress or irregular watering. Severe heat or dry spells stop flowers from setting fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hulutsoo be lɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need support to spread their leaves high into the sunlight, which allows the plant to produce food and grow big tubers underground while preventing ground rot.
ga: Yelikɛbuamɔ he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ niyenii ni amɛkwɛɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, yɛ be mli ni amɛtsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekafite.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will see the lower leaves turning yellow and dropping off, and cracks starting to show in the soil around the base of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi. ni ŋmeii bɔi kpojiemɔ yɛ sũ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: If it only rains once or twice in March, should I start planting my farm right away?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ shii 1-2 pɛ yɛ March mli lɛ, ani esa akɛ mije ŋmɔ lɛ mli dumɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Early rains in March can be unpredictable. If you plant after just one light rain, the topsoil might dry out quickly, causing your seeds to germinate and then wither if follow-up rains do not come soon.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ March shishijee gbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ. Kɛji odu yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baanyɛ agbi oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaagbi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ mra.

english: Why is it important to finish planting within two or three days after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbe dumɔwui lɛ anaa yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli beni nugbɔ enɛ waa lɛ?

english: Rainwater in the topsoil evaporates quickly under the sun. Planting within two or three days ensures the seeds absorb enough moisture to germinate strong before the soil dries out.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu la lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnáa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ dani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ.

english: Can I put my seeds in dry soil before the March rains even begin?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ midumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani March nugbɔ lɛ aba?

english: Planting in dry soil can be risky because insects or birds might eat the seeds while they wait for rain, or a very light rain might spoil the seeds without giving them enough water to grow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni oookwɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee oshara. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kooloi bibii loo okpoi baanyɛ aye dumɔwui lɛ be mli ni amɛmiimɛ nugbɔ. loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo Enɛ baanyɛ afite dumɔwui lɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛhaaa koni amɛdara lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I check if the ground has enough rainwater to plant my crops safely?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ shweshweeshwe?

english: Dig down a few inches and squeeze a handful of dirt; if it forms a soft ball that holds together without water dripping out, the soil has enough moisture for planting.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ shi inchii fioo komɛi ni okɛ muji ko ajie. Kɛji akɛ etamɔ bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni nu shwieee shi. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui.

english: Why do many farmers bring in extra people to help plant the whole field at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo kɛ gbɔmɛi baa koni amɛye amɛbua amɛ ni amɛdu amɛŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: When rain falls briefly, soil moisture only lasts a few days. Getting extra help allows you to plant your entire farm quickly so all your crops can catch the moisture at the same time.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ be kukuoo ko Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ hiɔ shi gbii fioo pɛ. Yelikɛbuamɔ kroko ni ooona lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni oha oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ oya. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ anyɛ ana ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be kome mli.

english: Is it better to plant all my land in a few days or plant it slowly week by week?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu mishikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli loo fiofio? Dumɔ otsi kome yɛ be kome mli?

english: Planting everything quickly after a good rain gives all your plants an equal start, while planting slowly means later crops might suffer if the rains suddenly stop.
ga: Kɛ́ odu nɔ fɛɛ nɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ fɛɛ aje shishi pɛpɛɛpɛ. be mli ni aduɔ nii blɛoo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ ana amanehulu yɛ sɛɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ trukaa.

english: How does joining a group with other community farmers help me with my planting schedule?
ga: Kuu mli ni mikɛ okwaafoi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ aaafata he Te ebaanyɛ eye ebua mi yɛ mi dumɔ be he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Working together in a group allows you to pool labor to clear and plant one person's field completely in a single day, ensuring everyone's crops get planted right when the soil is wet.
ga: Kɛ́ nyɛfee ekome akɛ kuu lɛ, nyɛbaanyɛ nyɛbua nitsulɔi anaa koni amɛjie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii amɛha mɔ kome yɛ gbi kome mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa koni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ.

english: How do I find out how many months my crop will take from planting day until harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nyɔji enyiɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahe kɛjɛ be mli ni adu kɛyashi be mli ni akpaa nii lɛ?

english: Every crop variety has a specific growth cycle listed on the seed packet or shared by extension officers; for example, early-maturing maize takes about three months, while cassava takes longer.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko ni etsɔɔ nɔ edaa taakɛ aŋmala yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe wolo lɛ nɔ loo mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ jaa lɛ. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ŋmãa heɔ aaafee nyɔji 3 dani ekwɛ̃ɔ oya, yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa heɔ be babaoo.

english: What happens to my young plants if the rain stops for a few weeks right after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ kpa nɛmɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: Without continuous water, young seedlings cannot absorb nutrients from the soil, causing their growth to stall or causing them to dry up completely.
ga: Kɛji nu ni yaa nɔ bɛ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa dalɛ sɛɛ foɔ loo egbiɔ kwraa.

english: Why should I pick crop varieties that mature quickly if the rainy season in my area is short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahala tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ faaa yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Quick-maturing crops need fewer months of water, allowing them to produce full yields before the rainy season ends and dry weather sets in.
ga: Tsei ni daa oya lɛ biɔ nu fioo yɛ nyɔji babaoo mli. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ atsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa naagbee ni hulutsoo be lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear and clear all the weeds off my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crop seeds for water, sunlight, and soil food. Clearing them during land preparation gives your young plants a clean environment and the best chance to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ odumɔwui lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaha odumɔwui lɛ aná shihilɛ ni mli tse kɛ hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛkɛbaadara waa.

english: Why do my crops struggle to grow if I plant them straight into hard, unprepared soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji midu amɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni asaaa he lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Hard soil prevents young plant roots from pushing deep into the ground to find water and nutrients. Breaking up and loosening the soil allows roots to spread easily and take in air.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiɔ tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyana nu kɛ niyenii. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mligbalamɔ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo ni amɛheɔ kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: Why do I still need to work so hard on my farm even after my crops have already sprouted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsu nii waa lolo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ moŋ?

english: Planting is only the first step of farming. Growing crops remain vulnerable to weed competition, insects, diseases, and nutrient loss, so they require regular protection and care until harvest.
ga: Okwaayeli ji klɛŋklɛŋ gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ okwaayeli he nii. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kã he eji nɔ ni jwɛi akaŋshii, kooloi, helai, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni laajeɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ abu tsei nɛɛ ahe ni akwɛ amɛ daa kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop leaves start turning yellow and weak as the plants grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbɔjɔ beni tso lɛ miida lɛ?

english: As plants grow, they demand much more food from the earth. Yellow leaves usually mean the soil has run out of essential nutrients like nitrogen, signaling that your crops are starving.
ga: Kɛ tsei dara lɛ Niyenii babaoo he miihia amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye onibii.

english: Why do insects attack my crops more heavily during certain seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ bei komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Pest populations increase when weather conditions like warmth and rain match their breeding cycle, or when your crops produce tender young leaves that insects love to eat.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tamɔ hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ. ni kɛ fɔmɔ be lɛ kpãa gbee Aloo beni otsei lɛ woɔ baai bibii ni kooloi bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛye lɛ.

english: Why do weeds keep coming back on my land even after I spray them with chemical weedkillers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi moŋ.

english: Some weeds have deep root systems or hard seeds buried in the ground that chemical sprays cannot reach, while others regrow if the chemical was mixed incorrectly or applied at the wrong time.
ga: Jwɛi komɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo dumɔwui ni wa ni afu yɛ sũ mli ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he. Yɛ be mli ni jwɛi komɛi baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai ni ejaaa futu mli loo akɛtsu nii yɛ be ni ejaaa mli lɛ.

english: Why did my crop leaves get scorched and burnt after I sprayed them with chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shãa ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofai eshwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Spraying too much chemical, using the wrong dosage, or applying sprays in the hot afternoon sun can burn delicate plant leaves instead of protecting them.
ga: Tsofai babaoo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ Okɛ nɔ ni ejaaa atsu nii Aloo okɛshwie nɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ eshã tso baai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeebu amɛhe lɛ

english: How do I know if my land actually needs chemical fertilizers to grow good crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia mishikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ koni ekɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: If your crops grow slowly, stay pale, or produce very small fruits despite getting enough rain and sunlight, your soil is low on natural nutrients and requires fertilizer support.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ miida blɛoo, etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ewo yibii bibii waa yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aye abua bo.

english: Can using too much chemical spray on my field ruin the quality of my soil over time?
ga: Ani tsofai babaoo ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Yes, overusing harsh chemicals can destroy beneficial organisms like earthworms and good bacteria in the soil that naturally keep your land rich and fertile.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni mli wa babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akpata nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ. Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii aba.

english: Is there any way I can reduce how much chemical spray I buy without losing my crop yield?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ matsi tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni miheɔ lɛ shi ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ akafite?

english: You can reduce chemical reliance by combining spraying with manual weeding, practicing crop rotation, and applying natural compost or animal manure to build healthy, resilient soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha tsofai ni okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ tsofa ni okɛshwieɔ jwɛi ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ he nitsumɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛfee shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi.

english: Why should I place fertilizer a few inches away from my plant's stem instead of dropping it directly at the base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo tso lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛshwie shishigbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ.

english: Placing concentrated fertilizer directly against the main stem can burn the plant's skin and cause stem rot. A plant drinks nutrients through its outer feeding roots, which spread out beneath the leaf canopy, so placing fertilizer a short distance away reaches the roots safely without damaging the main stem.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo ni eha tso lɛ shishi lɛ agbo. Tsei nuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛtsɔ amɛ kponɔgbɛ shishifãi ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ anɔ, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa baai lɛ ashishi. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ Ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe shweshweeshwe ni efiteee tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ.

english: Why do groundnut plants make the soil better for my next season's maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmei dumɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have beneficial bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the groundnut roots break down after harvest, they leave behind this natural fertilizer, which helps the next crop, like maize, grow greener and stronger.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ Amɛbaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ amɛsɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni ekwɛɔ eŋɔli ni ewaa.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my young cassava plants early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Cassava tsei bibii yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Young cassava plants grow slowly during their first few months and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures the cassava roots get all the energy they need to expand into large tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei bibii lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa trees drying up and burning during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct sun and harsh Harmattan winds. Without shade plants like plantains nearby to block the harsh sunlight and keep moisture in the air, the extreme heat dries out the leaves faster than the roots can suck up water.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ ekãa lɛ bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ni baatsi hulu ni naa wa lɛ naa ni amɛmɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha baai lɛ agbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the fruit bunches start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots like big timber trees; their roots stay close to the surface. As the heavy fruit bunch grows at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for wind or heavy rain to pull the root system out of the shallow soil unless you prop it up with a strong wooden stake.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ tsei wuji. Eshishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji aduawai akuu agbo ko dara yɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baaná ŋwɛi shwiili. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baagbala shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Ja okɛ tso ni wa fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: This is caused by a fungal infection commonly called Black Pod disease, which spreads quickly in wet, shaded conditions. Heavy rain splashes tiny fungal spores from the soil onto the cocoa pods, causing them to rot from the outside in.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni afɔɔ lɛ tsɛmɔ akɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii ni ji fungal spores lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, kookoo yibii lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ kponɔgbɛ kɛboteɔ mli.

english: Yellowing starting at the lower leaves usually means the maize plant lacks nitrogen, an essential food for green growth. To keep growing, the plant moves the remaining nitrogen from its older lower leaves up to its new upper leaves, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmei tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ koni eya nɔ eda Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baa heei amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot inside the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rains cause waterlogging and water sits in the soil for too long, the roots drown from a lack of air, allowing rot-causing soil organisms to invade and destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ ehaa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite amɛ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites feeding on the sap under the leaves. As they drink the plant's juice, they spread viruses and cause the leaf cells to deform, leaving the plant stunted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Beni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ Amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwãa ni amɛhaa baa lɛ mli wala yibii lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant experiences severe dry spells. High temperatures prevent the pollen inside the flower from fertilizing, causing the unfertilized flower to drop off instead of forming a fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ ni naa wa. He ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ tsiɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekafee fɔfɔi. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaf buds and shallow roots that burn easily under direct sun. Leaves need partial shade from bigger trees to retain leaf moisture and protect the soil from drying out while the young root system develops.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Baai lɛ he miihia hulutsoo fioo kɛjɛ tsei ni eda lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛha baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi yɛ be mli ni shishifãi bibii lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a inverted V-shape from the leaf tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛmiijɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tips are a clear signal that your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the primary plant nutrient responsible for leaf greenness and tall, healthy stalk growth.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji tso lɛ mli niyenii titri ni haa baai eŋɔli kɛ tsei kakadaji ni wa lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do agricultural workers tell me that planting groundnuts alongside my main crop helps the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli mli nitsulɔi kɛɔ mi akɛ, kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with natural soil microbes to trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When groundnuts grow, they share this free nitrogen fertilizer with neighboring crops.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai bibii tsuɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ŋmeii kwɛ̃ Amɛbaajara nitrogen ŋmeii ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I push my cassava stem cuttings into the soil at an angle instead of pushing them straight down or laying them flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsi lɛ shi tɛ̃ɛ loo okɛma shi shiŋŋ lɛ

english: Planting stems slanted buries several growth nodes under the ground at different depths. This encourages multiple strong tuber roots to grow evenly without getting clogged near the soil surface.
ga: Tsoi ni adu yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ fuɔ shweremɔ hei babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi yɛ hei srɔtoi. Enɛ haa tuber shishifãi babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ daa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛtsiii amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do I end up with small, light ears of corn when I plant my maize seeds very close together in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, individual plants fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil food. This leaves each plant weak and without enough energy to build large corn cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso fɛɛ tso baawuu koni ená hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko bɛ hewalɛ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee abele ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I need to spend time putting long wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafite be babaoo kɛto tsei kakadaji ahe gbɛjianɔ lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need height so their leaves can spread out and catch full sunlight to make food for growing roots. Keeping vines off wet soil also protects leaves from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia ni amɛkwɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛha shishifãi ni miida lɛ niyenii. Wein tso lɛ ni akɛaatsi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Extra sucker shoots drain water, nutrients, and root energy away from the main fruiting stem. Removing extra suckers leaves maximum food for the main stem to produce a big heavy bunch.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi jieɔ nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ, kɛ shishifã hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa niyenii babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni tsii waa.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off during the hot, dry season without making any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛgbiɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause plant flowers to dry up before they can produce fruit. The plant drops its flowers as a defense to save its remaining water and stay alive.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haa tsei fɔfɔi lɛ gbiɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ naa ni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot during the main rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The heavy rain creates constant moisture and high humidity, which helps fungal spores spread rapidly from pod to pod through splashing raindrops and damp air.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa baa be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa fungal spores lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni shwieɔ shi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upward and becoming stiff and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Upward curling leaves are usually caused by microscopic insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking plant juices from under the leaf while spreading leaf-curl viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso mli nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ hu amɛshwaa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to grow green and strong. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will help bring the healthy green color back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so thin and weak even after I put fertilizer on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni mikɛ ŋmɔji lɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii amli po lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm by taking up the water, sunlight, and fertilizer faster than your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early in the growth stage ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛnuɔ oya fe bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ amɛdalɛ mli mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear away all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shã ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves get scorched easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them provides a living umbrella that gives young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa shade kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do I need to place long sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the wet ground, which prevents fungal diseases from destroying the plant.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ niyenii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii helai akafite tso lɛ.

english: What is causing my cassava roots to turn soft and rot inside the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water for too long or when root rot disease attacks them during heavy rains. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges helps excess rain drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ shishifãi ni egbo lɛ tutua yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: What is eating small holes in my maize leaves and leaving dirt inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Spraying your maize early in the morning or late in the evening with recommended organic or chemical treatments will control them before they destroy the growing point of the plant.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ shwie ŋmãa nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaakudɔ ŋmãa lɛ dani efite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips that carry viruses to the plant. Controlling these insects early using neem oil or appropriate sprays prevents the virus from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ hela lɛ yaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Neem fɔ loo spray ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: It is best to sow your seeds after two or three steady rains have thoroughly soaked the soil, rather than after the very first light rain. This ensures the soil stays wet enough for seeds to sprout without drying out and dying.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ sɛɛ. Mohu ɔ, du ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ nɛ nɛ ɔ se konɛ zugba a nɔ nɛ e hyɛ bɔ nɛ sa konɛ dumi ɔmɛ nɛ puɛ nɛ a be gbie nɛ a gbo we.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get extremely hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when the plant lacks calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold its flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ calcium Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same spot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ŋmãa dumɔ he afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot exhausts specific soil nutrients and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the dirt. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baafite. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when the sun gets very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need shade from taller plants like plantains to keep the soil moist and protect them until they grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abu he kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves up toward the sun to produce energy for tuber growth. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet soil, preventing rot and fungal diseases while maximizing sunlight exposure to grow larger yams.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulb lɛ dalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo koni ekwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special root nodules that pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. This provides a natural fertilizer for your maize, improving soil richness without buying extra chemicals.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha o-corn lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ ni eheee tsofai krokomɛi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, a vital nutrient for leaf growth. When the soil lacks nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has to the newest leaves, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Beni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my young vegetables with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? aduawai bibii ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli

english: Covering the soil, called mulching, acts like a blanket that traps moisture so the sun doesn't dry out the earth quickly. It also keeps the soil cool, prevents heavy rains from washing away topsoil, and stops weeds from sprouting.
ga: Mulching, ni atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ mli, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Tsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃

english: Why does my cassava crop manage to stay green and survive even when there is no rain for months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehiɔ shi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ nyɔji babaoo po lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep root systems that search far underground for stored water. It can also drop some of its leaves to conserve moisture during dry spells, allowing it to survive harsh weather that would kill other crops.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni taoɔ nu ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Abaanyɛ ashi baai komɛi hu yɛ sɛɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ akahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa ni kulɛ ebaafite ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ amli.

english: Why is it best for me to plant my maize right after the first heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ madu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting early allows seeds to absorb deep moisture from the ground for fast germination. It gives crops a head start to develop strong root systems before intense mid-season pests arrive.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ gbekɛbiiashi Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Ehaa tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli wa dani be lɛ teŋgbɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without turning into any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely high heat or irregular watering. When it is too hot, pollen cannot fertilize the flower properly, so the plant sheds it to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ, Pollen nyɛŋ aha fɔfɔi lɛ aná fɔmɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Tsei jieɔ lɛ kpo koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars suddenly show up in the middle of my maize leaves during warm weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo trukaa yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ?

english: Warm weather speeds up the life cycle of pests like the fall armyworm, causing eggs laid by moths on the leaves to hatch rapidly. The young caterpillars crawl into the central whorl of the leaf to feed on tender young tissue.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cutworms lɛ wala yaa oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, wuji ni ŋmeii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɛ̃ɔ oya. Kplukai bibii shwieɔ baai lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ amli koni amɛye fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after I clean the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds produce thousands of wild seeds that lie dormant in the soil for years. They are naturally tougher than crop plants and react immediately to sunlight and water, absorbing available nutrients before crops can establish roots.
ga: Jwɛi woɔ koo mli dumɔwui akpei abɔ ni ŋmɛɔ shi. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛhe wa fe tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ, ni kɛ́ hulu la kɛ nu ba amɛnɔ lɛ, amɛfeɔ amɛnii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ dani tsei lɛ shishifãi kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and burning up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under full sun. Planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shade umbrellas that keep the soil moist and shield the young plants from harsh sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: I noticed tiny caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize crop, what is happening to my farm?
ga: Miyɔse ŋmei bibioo ko. Ye mi-baby corn lɛ teŋ baai lɛ. Mɛni ba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest common in maize fields across Ghana. Spraying recommended treatments early in the morning when the worms are active helps protect your corn.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli yɛ Ghana fɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie nɔ leebi be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ miitsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmei lɛ he.

english: Why does my land yield very little cassava now compared to when I first cleared this forest land years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ akɛto be mli ni mifo koo lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Crops remove nutrients from the ground with every harvest. Planting crops continuously without giving the soil a break or adding compost and manure exhausts the land's natural fertility.
ga: Tsei gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni abaakpa amɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ daa ni akumɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready to dig up without spoiling them?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ amɛ ni amɛfiteee amɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the bottom leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil around the base of the plant starts cracking.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: It is safer to wait until the major rains fully settle after two or three steady downpours. Planting after the first light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then dry up if a long heatwave follows.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ wulu lɛ aba shi kwraa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji hulutsoo be ko ba.

english: Will planting groundnuts between my cassava plants hurt the cassava growth?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaná cassava lɛ dalɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii?

english: No, groundnuts and cassava work very well together. Groundnuts cover the soil to prevent weeds and pull nitrogen from the air into the soil, which naturally fertilizes your cassava.
ga: Dabi, ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ waa. Akɛ ŋmeii woɔ ŋmeii amli koni jwɛi akabote mli ni ejie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha o-cassava lɛ afee nɔ ni woɔ yibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my pepper plants producing plenty of flowers but dropping them before peppers form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi egbeeɔ shi dani pepper lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like potassium. Regular watering and adding well-rotted manure helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: This is usually bacterial wilt, a soil-borne disease that attacks plants when water sits around the roots for too long. Raising your plant beds and rotating crops every season stops this disease from building up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji hela ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tutuaa tsei kɛji nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Tsei kɛ tsei ni atsakeɔ amɛ daa be lɛ baaye abua ni hela nɛɛ akaje shishi.

english: What causes my harvested maize to turn into powdery dust with small holes while stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ tsɔɔ sũ ni bu bibii yɔɔ mli? be mli ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ

english: This damage is caused by maize weevils. Drying your maize until the grains are completely hard before storage and keeping them in airtight bags prevents weevils from invading your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei mli ŋmeii. Kɛ́ ogbi o-abele lɛ mli aahu kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa dani okɛto ni okɛwo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii ni baa he ni okpaa nii yɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops right after I clear and plant my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni midu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds naturally lie dormant in the soil and sprout very quickly once clearing exposes them to sun and rain. Covering open soil with organic mulch smothers weeds before they can take over your crop.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya waa kɛji akɛ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ organic mulch wo shikpɔŋ ni agbele nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe jwɛi dani amɛye onibii anɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed to make food and grow green leaves. This often happens in worn-out soil or after heavy rains wash nutrients deep into the ground where short roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛfee niyenii ni akɛkwɛ baai eŋɔlii Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite nɔ loo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi kukuji nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does mixing dried animal dung into my soil help crops grow better than planting in plain dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Animal dung acts as natural plant food rich in nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. It feeds the beneficial living organisms in the soil and improves the ground's ability to hold onto moisture, giving crop roots a steady supply of nutrients.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii ni nitrogen, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasium eyi mli obɔ. Ehaa sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ niyenii, ni ehaa sũ lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ naa niyenii kpakpai daa

english: Why does placing dry grass around the base of my pepper plants keep the ground wet for longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, forms a protective shield against the direct sun. It reduces heat on the root system and prevents water in the soil from evaporating quickly into the air during dry days.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Efeɔ tsɔne ko ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field with full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, sensitive leaves that burn easily under harsh sunlight. They need temporary shade from fast-growing crops like plantains during their early years to stay cool and retain enough water to build strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains amli yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli. Enɛ ji koni eha edɔ ni ehiɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛma shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need plenty of sunlight to manufacture food for their roots. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground, preventing leaf diseases caused by wet soil and allowing every leaf maximum sunlight to grow bigger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha amɛshishifãi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsi foliar helai ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa. Ni ha baai lɛ fɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo koni eha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ adara.

english: Why do my maize ears stay small when I plant seeds too close together in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ feɔ bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crowded plants compete for limited sunlight, root space, soil moisture, and food. Spacing seeds properly ensures every plant gets enough resources to form full, healthy ears.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he akaŋ. kɛ niyenii ni faaa Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha efee toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell under the ground that my cassava roots are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cassava plants signal readiness when their lower leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off naturally, and the soil right around the main stem starts to crack open due to the swelling tubers pushing outward beneath the surface.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso titri lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmei ni efuu lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without forming any fruit when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries out the pollen inside the blossoms, preventing pollination. When the flower fails to get pollinated, the plant sheds the flower to conserve water and survive until conditions improve.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Tsi pollination naa Beni anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollination Tso lɛ gbálaa efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ekɛ nu ato ni ehi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do tiny green insects hide under the leaves of my cabbage instead of staying on top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ kaabe baa shishi moŋ fe nɔ ni amɛaatee nɔ lɛ?

english: Insects like aphids hide under leaves to protect themselves from harsh direct sunlight, heat, and heavy rain while feeding on the soft, juicy undersides where plant sap flows closest to the surface.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ aphids teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai ashishi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa, dɔlɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa he be mli ni amɛtaoɔ niyenii yɛ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ he ni tso mli nu lɛ hoɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and soft before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo dani ebatsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot and is caused by a lack of calcium inside the growing fruit. It usually happens when dry spells and uneven watering make it difficult for roots to draw calcium up from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛ́ hulutsoo be kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni eyaaa nɔ lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaagbala calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open, cleared field without any shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and hot winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains creates a cool canopy that protects the young cocoa leaves from scorching and helps the soil stay moist.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo baa ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow even though it has been raining regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? He ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green growth. Rain provides moisture, but the crop still needs nutrients from organic compost, manure, or fertilizer to stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ Nugbɔ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii hu he miihia niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is burning my bush after clearing bad for my farm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi jwɛi lɛ ni mishãa yɛ be mli ni mijie lɛ sɛɛ lɛ ehiii kɛha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic matter and beneficial soil organisms that naturally feed your crops. Clearing without burning allows dead leaves and roots to rot into the soil, creating a rich top layer that holds moisture better.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashãaa lɛ haa baai kɛ shishifãi ni egboi lɛ fiteɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ fɛo ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: When cassava plants are packed too tightly, their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other and their roots fight for the same nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and space to develop large, healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ bulbs agboi ni mli wa baa.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cut off some branches from our grown cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifo kookoo niji lɛ ekomɛi lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches so sunlight and fresh air can flow through the farm. Good airflow reduces dampness, which helps prevent black pod disease and encourages the tree to produce more flowers.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ black pod hela naa, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi babaoo.

english: Why are tiny holes appearing in my maize leaves and stalks with small caterpillars inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ni ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-abele baai kɛ abele tsei ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is caused by stem borer caterpillars that eat their way inside the plant stalk. Applying recommended control measures early in the season protects the stem before the caterpillars cut off the plant's food supply.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji stem borers ni yeɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe dani ŋmeii lɛ afo tso lɛ niyenii jɛɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in damp and shady conditions. Keeping your farm weeded, pruning excess tree branches, and removing infected pods stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Kpãa niji ni fa fe nine lɛ. ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ Enɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by the cassava mosaic virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies feeding on the leaves. Planting certified disease-resistant stem varieties prevents this virus from taking over your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Flɔfoi yɛŋ bibii ni yeɔ baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwãa. Kɛ́ odu tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I buy fresh improved seeds instead of planting seeds saved from last year's maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe jogbaŋŋ yɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strength in the next generation, producing weaker plants and smaller yields. Fresh improved seeds are bred to resist local pests, tolerate drought, and produce a bigger harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui heei ni akwɛɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ ni ekɛ yibii babaoo baa

english: Why does water collect and stay on top of my farmland for days after heavy rains, causing crop roots to rot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu buaa ehe naa ni ehiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ? haa tso shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ

english: Water stands on farmland when the soil is compacted or heavy with clay, preventing water from draining down. Building raised beds or digging simple drainage channels allows excess water to flow away so roots don't suffocate.
ga: Nu yɛ okwaayeli hei kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ loo eyɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ. Tsi nu ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi lɛ naa Saa ni awo nɔ lɛ feemɔ loo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni atsaa Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight because their tender leaves burn easily and the soil around them dries out too fast. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides living shelter and moisture, keeping the soil cool while the young cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kookoo tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ shãa oya, ni sũ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ hu shãa. Cacao tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha aná wɔɔhe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up, turning yellow, and growing small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miihoso lɛ? tsɔ ŋmɔŋ Ni ani eji bibioo?

english: This leaf damage is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects that feed on the leaf sap. The virus stops the plant from converting sunlight into food, resulting in distorted leaves and very small cassava tubers under the ground.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Agbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Virus tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkatsake hulu la amɛfee niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni efite kɛ ŋmei shishifãi bibii waa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do I see small chewed holes in my young maize leaves with green dust inside the central leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Mikɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ kɛ sũ eŋɔli ni yɔɔ baai lɛ teŋgbɛ cone lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: These holes and powdery waste are signs of Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant's growing point. These pests eat the leaves from the inside out, weakening the plant so it cannot produce healthy, full cobs.
ga: Nɛkɛ bu kɛ powder sũ nɛɛ ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ he ni edaa yɛ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ baai kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni egbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ abɔ kooloo ni yeɔ emuu ni mli wa.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When these plants mature and decay, they release this natural fertilizer into the soil, which helps neighboring maize crops grow stronger and produce better cobs.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei nɛɛ daraa ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ Ebaajie adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants turn brown and die if I put granular fertilizer right against the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egboɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ji granular wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated mineral salts that draw moisture out of tender plant roots when placed directly against them. Touching the stem burns the plant's skin and roots, stopping the pepper plant from absorbing water and causing it to dry up.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ mineral salts ni mli eyi obɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli kɛ akɛwo mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ota tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaashã hewolo lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa pepper tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu ni ehaa egbiɔ.

english: When too many suckers grow around a single plantain trunk, they all compete for the same soil nutrients, water, and light. Removing all but one or two strong shoots ensures the main plant gets enough nutrients to grow a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe Plantain kome Amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ la mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruits during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fertilization from happening. When flowers fail to pollinate, the plant drops them to conserve its water and energy rather than wasting resources on unfertilized blooms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. ni haa fɔmɔ baaa Be mli ni anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii amli fɔfɔi Tsei shiiɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛsɛɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaafite nibii yɛ fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why do I need to cut tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum exposure to sunlight to create food that feeds the growing yam tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, allowing them to catch sunshine while preventing leaves from rotting due to wet soil fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni baaye abua sweet potato ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛná hulu la. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous hybrid maize harvest produce smaller cobs than new store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mitsutsu ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni mikɛkpa nii lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibii fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are created by crossing two carefully selected parent varieties to achieve high yields, but this high performance only lasts for one generation. Saving and replanting seeds from a hybrid harvest results in offspring that lose this vigor, producing weaker plants and smaller cobs.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ feɔ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi enyɔ ni ahala jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛfoɔ mli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ nɔ. Shi nɛkɛ nitsumɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɛɛ baahi shi kɛyashi yinɔ kome pɛ. Dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ amli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ haa seshibii lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ hewalɛ nɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ bibii.

english: Why do weeds cause my maize crop to grow slowly even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing, aggressive root systems that suck up soil nutrients and fertilizer faster than maize roots can reach them. They also shade young maize crops from sunlight, effectively stealing the food and light your crop needs to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa. Enɛ baaŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ feɔ hulu la. Enɛ juɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa tsei lɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Why are agricultural extension officers encouraging us to plant cocoa on our land instead of other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ hewalɛ koni wɔdu kookoo yɛ wɔshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni wɔdu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Cocoa thrives in our rich soil and forest climate, providing a reliable long-term income because there is always a strong, steady market demand for cocoa beans both locally and internationally.
ga: Cocoa shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ wɔ kooi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. ni haa shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ baa Enɛ ji akɛ, jarayeli nibii ni he hiaa waa ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yɛ kɛha kookoo ŋmeii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɛ majimaji ateŋ fɛɛ.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm is good enough for growing crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Good soil is usually dark, crumbles easily in your hand, retains moisture without staying waterlogged, and contains plenty of decayed leaves and organic matter to feed plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa mli tseɔ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Kwɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni nu akahiɛ mli. Ni baai ni fiteɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛyeɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young crops turn yellow and start dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing and falling leaves are a crop's natural response to extreme heat and drought stress; the plant sheds its leaves to conserve water and survive until the rains return.
