ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛto nu ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell us to leave large shade trees on our farms when clearing land for crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔshi tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo yɛ wɔŋmɔji lɛ amli kɛ́ wɔmiijie okwaayeli shikpɔji lɛ?

english: Shade trees protect young crops from harsh sunlight, keep the soil cool and moist, and shed leaves that decompose into natural nutrient-rich manure for your crops.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Ni baai ni ajie lɛ lɛ fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it better to plant my crops in straight rows instead of scattering the seeds across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni aaadu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting in neat rows ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, air, and room to grow while making weeding, fertilizer application, and harvesting much easier for you.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ waaa kwraa kɛhaa bo.

english: Can I grow food crops like plantain or cassava together with cocoa on the same farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains loo cassava kɛfata kookoo he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting food crops alongside young cocoa is beneficial because fast-growing plants like plantains provide shelter and shade for tender cocoa seedlings while giving you food and quick income.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ ejaakɛ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains haa kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ wɔɔhe kɛ hulutsoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha niyenii kɛ shika oya.

english: What makes one farmer get a huge crop harvest while another farmer on the same size of land gets very little?
ga: Mɛni ha okwaafonyo ko nine shɛ yibii babaoo ni tamɔ nɛkɛ nɔ? Yɛ be mli ni okwaafoi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ naa yibii fioo pɛ?

english: Higher yields come from using improved seeds, keeping proper spacing between plants, clearing weeds early, and protecting the crops from pests and diseases with guidance from extension officers.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ jɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahebuu kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahe kɛtsɔ ŋaawoo ni jɛɔ sɛɛkwɛlɔi adɛŋ.

english: How can I tell if a disease is starting to spread among my crops before it destroys my entire harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela ko miije shishi egbɛ eshwa miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani ekpata miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ahiɛ?

english: Check your plants regularly for early warnings like dark spots on leaves or pods, sudden wilting, strange growths, or unusual insect activity, and report them to an extension officer immediately.
ga: Kwɛmɔ otsei lɛ amli daa kɛha kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii mra, tamɔ hei ni tsuɔ yɛ baai loo ŋmeii anɔ. trukaa ni egboɔ dalɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ loo kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ ni okɛ amaniɛbɔɔ aha hiɛyaa nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ

english: When is the right time for me to put fertilizer on my crops so it doesn't go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛkafite?

english: Apply fertilizer at the beginning of the rainy season when the soil is moist; this allows the growing plant roots to easily absorb the nutrients before heavy rains wash them away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi ni miida lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ amɛ.

english: Why should I try the new crop management practices taught by agricultural officers instead of sticking to my old ways?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ he nifeemɔi heei ni okwaayeli nitsulɔi tsɔɔ lɛ makwɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ mihe akpɛtɛ momo nɔ lɛ he?

english: The practices taught by extension officers are tested to help crops resist changing weather, produce bigger harvests, and keep your soil healthy so your farm remains profitable for years.
ga: Aka nifeemɔi ni mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ akwɛ koni eye ebua tsei ni amɛte shi amɛwo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ. Ha yibiiwoo babaoo ni oha oshikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔ lɛ aya nɔ aná sɛɛnamɔ afii babaoo ni baa lɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers usually drop off because they were not pollinated within a day of opening. Natural pollinators like midges are often too few in number, so many flowers remain unfertilized and simply fall off.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni amɛfɔ lɛ, amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ. Bei pii lɛ, adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa ŋmeii, tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ ayi faaa tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi babaoo ehiɛɛɛ fɔmɔ nii ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Hand pollination is a technique where you manually move pollen from one flower to another. Doing this ensures that more flowers get fertilized, which helps your trees produce far more cocoa pods than relying on insects alone.
ga: Hand pollination ji gbɛ ko ni otsɔɔ nɔ okɛ onine shwieɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ aná fɔmɔ nii babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ kookoo ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe baafɔ̃ kooloi bibii pɛ anɔ.

english: Can I use pollen from a single healthy flower to pollinate multiple other flowers on my tree?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ pollen ni jɛ fɔfɔi kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli lɛ atsu nii ni mikɛwo fɔfɔi krokomɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ amli pollen?

english: Yes, a single healthy flower usually contains enough pollen to fertilize several other flowers, allowing you to maximize pod development across your farm efficiently.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli fɔfɔi ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi krokomɛi babaoo afee fɔfɔi, ni enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohaa pod lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if a cocoa flower on my tree has been successfully pollinated?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ eye omanye yɛ ŋmɔlɔ mli?

english: When a flower is successfully pollinated, its stem stays firm and green instead of turning brown and dropping. Within a few days, you will see a small green pod start to swell at the base of the flower.
ga: Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ye omanye yɛ pollination mli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baakã he ahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ. Mohu ɔ, a peeɔ blɔfo nɛ a gboɔ. Yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ obaana ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Ejeɔ shishi efoɔ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shishi.

english: How will attending farmer training sessions on crop management benefit my farm's output?
ga: Te okwaafoi atsɔsemɔ ni kɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ mli ni mikɛ mihe baawo lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Farmer field training teaches practical skills like hand pollination, proper pruning, and soil care. Applying these modern techniques directly increases your pod yield and improves overall farm productivity.
ga: Okwaafoi aŋmɔ mli tsɔsemɔ tsɔɔ ŋaa ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii tamɔ fɔfɔii ni akɛwoɔ fɔmɔ kotoku mli lɛ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai nɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha o-pod yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni ebaaha oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Is hand pollination something I can teach my family or local workers to do on the farm?
ga: Ani nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ko ni manyɛ matsɔɔ miweku lɛ loo maŋ lɛ mli nitsulɔi lɛ ni amɛfee yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, hand pollination is a straightforward skill that can be easily taught to family members or farm workers. It creates meaningful work on the farm and speeds up the pollination process during the flowering season.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nine nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji ŋaa ni yɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni abaanyɛ atsɔɔ weku mli bii loo ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi lɛ mlɛo. Bɔɔ nitsumɔ ni shishinumɔ yɔɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oha pollination nifeemɔ lɛ aya oya yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Does hand pollination require expensive tools, or can I do it with simple equipment?
ga: Ani nine nɔ pollination biɔ nibii ni jara wa loo abaanyɛ akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu he nii?

english: Hand pollination does not require expensive tools; it can be done with simple, low-cost items like small tweezers or fine brushes, making it accessible for any farmer to practice.
ga: Nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ biɔ nibii ni jara wa. Abaanyɛ akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni jara waaa tamɔ tsɔne bibii ni akɛfoɔ nii loo tsɔne bibioo ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ atsu enɛ he nii. Ha okwaafoi fɛɛ anyɛ atsu he nii

english: Will assisting my cocoa trees with pollination actually lead to more harvested beans at the end of the season?
ga: Ani cacao tsei ni aye abua amɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baaha akpa kɔfe babaoo yɛ be lɛ naagbee?

english: Yes, because hand pollination significantly increases the number of flowers that successfully mature into full cocoa pods, resulting in a larger harvest and more beans to sell.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ haa fɔfɔi ni baanyɛ adara ni etsɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, abaanyɛ akpa babaoo ni ahɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: What time of day is best for me to check and pollinate my cocoa flowers?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ makwɛ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni mikɛ amɛ awo mli?

english: Early morning is the best time for pollination because the flowers are newly opened, the pollen is fresh, and the cooler temperature prevents the flower parts from drying out.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha pollination. Akɛni fɔfɔi lɛ ekwɛ̃ pɛŋ hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ amli muji lɛ yɛ ehee, ni hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ lɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ fãi lɛ agbi.

english: Do my cocoa trees need extra water or fertilizer when they start producing more pods through hand pollination?
ga: Ani mi cacao tsei lɛ baabi nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi kɛji amɛbɔi ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo feemɔ kɛjɛ nine mli ŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Yes, when a tree carries more pods due to successful pollination, it works harder. Giving your trees adequate water and proper nutrients helps ensure all the new pods grow large and healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni tso lɛ yɔɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ pollination ni yeɔ omanye lɛ hewɔ. Tso lɛ baatsu nii waa fe tsutsu lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni sa ha tso lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ mli ŋmeii heei lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when there are no shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo be bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive because direct, harsh sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out the soil moisture. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby protects them until they are strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baafee mɛi ni he wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ.

english: This yellowing pattern usually means your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for green leaf growth. Applying compost, manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea helps the plant recover and grow healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when the rainy season gets very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because they cannot breathe in soggy, waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps heavy rainwater drain away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high into the sunlight so the plant can make maximum food to produce large underground tubers, while also preventing the leaves from rotting on damp soil.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni ená hulu la. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aye ehe niyenii kwraa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: How does planting beans together with my maize help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Beans and other legumes take nitrogen gas from the air and release it into the soil through their roots. This natural fertilizer feeds the surrounding maize plants and improves soil fertility.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ niyenii. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ

english: Leaving too many young shoots (suckers) forces them to compete with the main plant for water and soil nutrients, leading to small bunches. Keeping only two or three strong suckers allows the plant to produce large, heavy fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii (tsei) ni amɛyi fa fe nine lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni kɛ tsei bibii baa Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ awo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen in the soil that causes the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ekɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. aloo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ baa yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly and making the plant stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni eha tso lɛ miikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that transmit plant viruses, or by physical stress from heat and dry soil. Removing infected plants and controlling pests early prevents it from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies, ni hiɛ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli baa lɛ mli. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ mra Ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do weeds on my land cause my crops to stay small even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds have strong root systems that aggressively steal water, light, and nutrients away from your crops, effectively starving your plants even if you care for them.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji okwɛɔ amɛ po.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that target maize to build up in the ground, causing yields to drop each year.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni ekɛbaatsu nii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit when the heat gets strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries up pollen before bees or wind can fertilize the blooms. Without successful pollination, the plant drops the flower to save energy rather than growing a fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ afee fɔfɔi. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ yeee omanye lɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small even though the leaves above ground look huge and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing heavy branches and leaves instead of sending sugars down to build thick, healthy tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji kɛ baai ni tsii. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ sugar kɛ yaa si konɛ e pee yihi nɛ a mi wa nɛ a he wa.

english: Why do young cocoa trees wither and die so quickly if they are planted in an open field without tall trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni tsei kakadaŋŋ abɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have thin leaves and weak root systems that burn easily under full sunlight. Shade crops like plantains protect them from harsh light and keep the air around them humid.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny pests like mites or aphids that sit under the leaves and suck the sap out, or by plant viruses transmitted by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii, tamɔ mites loo aphids, ni shwereɔ yɛ baa lɛ shishi ni amɛ nuɔ nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients out of the soil year after year while giving pests and diseases a permanent home to multiply.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Na shia ni baahi shi daa kɛha fɔmɔ

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my main grain crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ mi-cereal ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for surrounding crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ.

english: Why does putting dry grass around the base of my crops help them stay alive during hot spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ ebɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass creates a protective layer called mulch, which blocks direct sunlight from evaporating water from the soil and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Enɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa tɛ̃ɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why are there ragged holes appearing overnight all over the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni mli ewo muji je kpo nyɔɔŋ kome mli yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the warm central funnel of the corn plant during the day and eat through the soft leaves at night.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli, ni amɛtsɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ amɛyeɔ nii gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two unique parent lines. The seeds you harvest from them lose that combined strength, leading to lower yields and uneven plant sizes if replanted.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ fɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui sɔrɔtoi enyɔ komɛi amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni okpa lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ ni akɛfeɔ ekome lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi ni tso lɛ dalɛ baafee ekome kɛji akɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my stored yams start to rot or sprout leaves inside my barn after a short time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ loo ebaa yɛ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be kukuoo ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams are living roots that keep breathing after harvest. If stored in a warm, unventilated place without good airflow, heat builds up, triggering sprouts to grow or fungus to cause rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni muɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu bɛ mli. Dɔlɛ baanyɛ abɔle ehe, ni eha ŋmeii akwɛ̃ loo ŋmeii agbo.

english: Do I need to secure a bank loan before I can start planting basic food crops on my land?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni maná shika kɛjɛ shikatoohe dani mabɔi niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ dumɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, you do not always need a bank loan. For major food crops, support programs offer input credit, which provides you with essential seeds and fertilizers upfront so you can start farming using just your land.
ga: Dabi, jeee be fɛɛ be ehe baahia ni ofã shika kɛjɛ shikatoohe lɛ. kɛha niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titrii Sponsorship gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ baaha botemɔ credits ni baaha bo dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa bo yɛ hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ aje okwaayeli shishi.

english: What does 'input credit' mean for a smallholder farmer like me?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘credit in’ shishi kɛha okwaafonyo bibioo ko tamɔ mi?

english: Input credit means you receive key supplies like seeds, fertilizers, and pesticides at the beginning of the planting season without paying cash immediately, allowing you to pay back after harvesting your crops.
ga: Shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ obaaná nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ shika awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ owoɔ shika lɛ he nyɔmɔ beni akpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ.

english: If I only have land and no money for supplies, can I still successfully grow food crops?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ shikpɔŋ ni mibɛ shika ni mikɛbaahe niyenii Ani manyɛ makwɛ niyenii yɛ omanyeyeli mli lolo?

english: Yes, having accessible land is the primary requirement. Through crop support initiatives, the rest of what you need—such as seeds and crop nutrients—can be provided to you on credit to get your farm running.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni anyɛɔ ashɛɔ he lɛ ji taomɔ nii titri. kɛ nifeemɔi ni akɛyeɔ abuaa ŋmɔshi nibii Nibii ni eshwɛ ni he hiaa bo lɛ ekomɛi ji dumɔwui kɛ tsei amli niyenii. Abaanyɛ aha bo yijiemɔ akɛ okwɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is the difference between growing crops for food versus growing crops for commercial income?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ kɛhaa jarayeli shika lɛ teŋ?

english: Food crops like maize, cassava, and rice are grown primarily to secure family and community food supply with quick seasonal yields, while commercial cash crops are cultivated specifically to produce raw materials for long-term income and trade.
ga: Aduɔ niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa titri koni akɛkwɛ wekui kɛ akutsei ni yɔɔ be mli nibii ni baa oya lɛ anɔ. yɛ be mli ni aduɔ jarayeli shika ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ koni akɛfee nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa shika kɛ jarayeli ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Which basic food crops in Ghana are easiest to start with if I want reliable harvests?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii titri ni aduɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ akɛ maje shishi kɛji miitao nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ?

english: Staple food crops like maize, rice, cassava, sorghum, and cowpeas are ideal because they adapt well to local soils and are heavily supported by farm input programs.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ. ni enine shɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni mli wa nɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli.

english: Why do improved crop seeds behave differently than seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are specifically bred to germinate faster, resist common local pests, and produce larger yields compared to older saved seeds, which lose vigor over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui momo ni ato ni hewalɛ baaje mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ he

english: Why do my food crops turn yellow and stay small even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi niyenii tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Plants turn yellow when the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen. Rain alone isn't enough; crops need adequate fertilizer inputs to grow tall, green, and healthy.
ga: Tsei feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Dumɔwui hia ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara, amɛfee eŋɔli, ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do food crops yield so much more when I use fertilizer along with good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata dumɔwui kpakpai ahe lɛ?

english: Quality seeds are designed to feed efficiently on nutrients. When combined with fertilizer, the seeds absorb the extra food from the soil to grow stronger stems and heavier grains.
ga: Afee dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni wa kɛ dumɔwui ni tsii.

english: How do I pay back the seeds and fertilizer given to me on input credit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛha mi lɛ aku sɛɛ kɛ shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ?

english: After you harvest your farm produce, you pay back the value of the inputs either by selling a portion of your yield or returning an agreed quantity of harvested grain.
ga: Kɛji okpa okwaayeli nibii sɛɛ lɛ Abaabi ni owo nibii ni okɛwo mli lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ kɛtsɔ nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ fã ko ni ooohɔ̃ɔ loo ŋmaa ni okpa lɛ ayibɔ ni okpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni okɛbaaku sɛɛ kɛba lɛ nɔ.

english: How does receiving planting inputs on time affect how my crops grow?
ga: Te nibii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ ni anáa yɛ be naa lɛ saa tsei lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Applying seeds and fertilizers at the exact start of the rainy season allows young plants to establish deep roots quickly, making them stronger against late-season droughts and pests.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛwo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ oya. Afee lɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ hɔmɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ.

english: Why should I heap high mounds of soil for planting my yam instead of putting the seed yams straight into flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabu shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ koni madu sweet potatoes lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ

english: Yam tubers grow long and big underwater, so they need loose, soft soil to expand without hitting hard earth. High mounds also catch rainwater while allowing excess water to drain off so the tubers do not rot in soaked soil.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa kakadaŋŋ ni amɛdaraa yɛ nu shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia amɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛnáaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Gɔŋ ni kɛlɛ lɛ hu mɔɔ nugbɔ nu yɛ be mli ni ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni bulb lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to raise my tomato seeds in a nursery bed first instead of planting them directly in the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikwɛɔ tomato dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato seeds are extremely tiny and fragile. Raising them in a nursery bed protects them from heavy rain, harsh sun, and insects, allowing you to care for them easily until only the strongest seedlings are selected for the main farm.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ atsɔse amɛ yɛ hei ni akwɛɔ kooloi yɛ lɛ, ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulu la ni naa wa, kɛ kooloi bibii ahe, ni no baaha amɛkwɛmɔ afee mlɛo. Kɛyashi be mli ni abaahala dumɔwui ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ kɛha ŋmɔ wulu lɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil, but legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have roots that pull nitrogen directly from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them restores free fertility back into the ground for your next crops.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei nɛɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to build strong green leaves. When there isn't enough in the soil, the plant pulls nitrogen from its old leaves to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni aná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ faaa Tso lɛ baajie nitrogen kɛjɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves look twisted, small, and yellow instead of growing wide and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ? bibioo kɛ ŋmɔŋ Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, baai lɛ mli kwɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Twisted and yellow cassava leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny insects called whiteflies. Affected plants cannot trap sunlight effectively, resulting in very thin tubers.
ga: Kasava baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Tsei ni enaa lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without forming any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme afternoon heat, severe dry spells, or irregular watering. The plant drops its flowers to save water and keep itself alive rather than spending energy growing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi, tamɔ shwane kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛha amɛhi wala mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees scorch and drop off during the sunniest dry months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi fe fɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have thin, delicate leaves that burn easily in full sun. They need shade crops, like plantains, growing beside them to act as natural umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to endure direct heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta Kɛyashi cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ naa.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding deep inside the central funnel of my maize leaves and chewing holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmei baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a serious pest that targets young maize. They hide deep inside the central funnel of the leaves where it is soft and moist to shelter themselves from direct sun and predators while eating the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ ni yeɔ gbekɛbii abele nɔ. Akɛ amɛ ewo baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛmli edɔ bɔni afee ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛyeɔ tsei lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spray pest control chemicals on my crops during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Spraying in the afternoon heat causes liquid chemicals to evaporate into the air before they can work properly. The heat combined with strong chemicals can also scorch and burn your crop leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tsofai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha tsofai ni ji nu lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Dɔlɛ ni akɛ tsofai ni mli wa fataa he lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni ashã tsei ahe baai.

english: Why must I clear all the weeds around the base of my crops before putting fertilizer down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi fɛɛ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and will quickly steal the expensive fertilizer food from the soil if left nearby, leaving your crops hungry despite the fertilizer applied.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebaaju ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ, ni ebaaha hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii po.

english: Tomatoes spoil quickly because heat and trapped moisture create an ideal environment for bacteria and mold to grow. Keeping harvested tomatoes in a cool, shady, well-ventilated area and packing them in shallow crates instead of deep sacks prevents heat buildup and crushing.
ga: Tomatoi fiteɔ oya ejaakɛ la ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ. Kɛ tomato ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ. Ni kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo adekai ni mli ekwɔɔɔ mli moŋ fe kotokui ni mli kwɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulutsoo akafee ekome ni ekɛ amɛhe akabɔ he.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my maize so it does not spoil during storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Enɛ ji koni ŋmãa lɛ akafite yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves turn brown and dry, and the grains are hard enough that your thumbnail cannot easily dent them. Harvesting when the crop is fully dry reduces moisture, which prevents mold and weevil damage during storage.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi. Ni dumɔwui lɛ wa bɔ ni sa akɛ oshishifa lɛ nyɛŋ atswa amɛ mlɛo. Nikpamɔ beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck plant juices and spread viruses. Checking under the leaves and using neem leaf spray or appropriate insecticides helps control these pests before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi ni okɛ neem baa lɛ mli tsofa ni sa loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot underground before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mifo amɛ?

english: Root rot happens when heavy rainfall leaves water standing in the soil for too long, suffocating the roots and attracting soil fungi. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbalaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do the blossoms fall off my tomato plants without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Flower drop occurs when plants experience extreme heat, water stress, or a shortage of plant nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering and supplying balanced fertilizer helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa he. nu mli haomɔ loo tso mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Maize leaves roll inward to shield themselves from strong sunlight and reduce water loss through evaporation. It is a natural sign that the soil is drying out and the plants are feeling heat stress.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ mli koni ebu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ekɛha nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli okadi akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miigbi ni tso lɛ miiye dɔlɛ he haomɔ.

english: How does planting right at the start of the rainy season help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔ ni aduɔ mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Early planting allows seeds to use the 'nitrogen flush'—a sudden release of rich nutrients from warm dry soil after the first rains—giving seedlings a rapid, healthy start before weeds and pests become widespread.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛ ‘nitrogen flush’ tsuɔ nii, ni ji niyenii kpakpai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi mli trukaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi oya, ni amɛhe wa dani jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my garden egg plants stay pale yellow and small even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow, stunted growth usually means the soil is exhausted of nitrogen, which green plants need to grow strong leaves. Mixing compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer into the soil will bring back their dark green color and speed up growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ fioo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei eŋɔli he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ baai ni mli wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaku esɛɛ etsɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or beans on land where I previously grew maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmei tsutsu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans naturally pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants break down, they leave behind enriched soil that feeds the next crop, reducing your need for expensive commercial fertilizers.
ga: Agbɛnɛ hu, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei gbee shi Ebaashi shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ anɔ. Ehaa jarayeli mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa he hiaa lɛ baa shi.

english: What causes my watermelons to split open on the farm before they are ripe?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-watermelon lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani eshɛɔ?

english: Watermelons crack when they get a sudden surge of water after a dry spell, causing the fruit inside to grow faster than the outer skin can stretch. Watering plants evenly and regularly prevents this sudden pressure inside the fruit.
ga: Watermelons baagbala kɛji amɛná nu ni yaa hiɛ trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ akpã mli. Nu ni oooha tsei lɛ daa kɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni nɔnyɛɛ ni baa trukaa yɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize crop turning pale yellow starting from the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient that gives plants their deep green color and strength. When soil lacks nitrogen, the plant moves whatever little food it has to new top leaves, causing the older bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe wa. Beni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baajie niyenii fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why am I finding ragged holes and saw-dust-like dirt inside the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni etse kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central growing point (funnel) of the maize plant to eat soft leaves. Spraying an approved pesticide or organic neem solution directly into the funnel early in the morning kills the pest before it destroys the plant's heart.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ (cone) lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tsofa ni yɔɔ odaseyeli mli lɛ shwie ŋmeii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite tso lɛ tsui lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy, but when heavy rain fills the ground with standing water, the roots drown and rot. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away so the tubers stay dry enough to grow well.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nui ekã shi. Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaagboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to place long wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce tubers underground by using their leaves to catch sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground, preventing disease and giving the vine maximum sunshine to manufacture food that makes the underground tubers grow big and heavy.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni amɛkɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛmɔ hulu la. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Tsi helai anaa ni oha wain tso lɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo koni ekɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa lɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full, hot sunshine. Leaving mature trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains provides living umbrellas that protect young cocoa from direct sun and keep the ground cool until the cocoa stems grow thick and strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni eda lɛ ni ajieɔ loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua. Umbrella ni akɛbuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their young pods before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miishwie amɛbii bibii lɛ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods often dry up and blacken (a condition called cherelle wilt) because the tree is overloaded and doesn't have enough water, soil nutrients, or shade to feed every pod. Pruning weak branches and applying fertilizer helps the tree retain healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ediŋŋ. (Shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherry blossom disease) lɛ baa ejaakɛ tso lɛ fa babaoo ni nu bɛ mli. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ? Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii ni afolɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ etsitsii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant experiences water stress, like sudden switching between dry soil and heavy watering. Watering your tomatoes regularly at the base early in the morning keeps the roots calm and helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ kpe, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ nu ni mli wa trukaa lɛ teŋ tsakemɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato lɛ nɔ daa leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ dioo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants twisting, curling up, and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ebɔle ehe ni efee bibioo lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are a sign that tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips are feeding on the underside of young leaves, causing them to deform. Sprinkling the undersides of the leaves with soapy water or neem oil repels these insects.
ga: Pepper baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips lɛ he okadi. Niyenii ni ayeɔ yɛ baai bibii ashishi ni haa amɛfiteɔ Okɛ nu ni akɛ saamɔ loo neem fɔ afɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni okɛshwie nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with low yields when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops compete aggressively for the same sunlight, soil food, and water. Giving plants proper spacing ensures each stalk has enough space for roots to spread and leaves to gather sunlight for good yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu kome. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã, ni baai lɛ hu abua hulu la naa koni amɛkpa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry granular fertilizer to my farm when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni ji granular lɛ fataaa miŋmɔ lɛ he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve so plant roots can soak them up safely. Applying chemical fertilizer to dry soil leaves concentrated salts on the roots, which will burn and damage the plant instead of feeding it.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná ŋmei babaoo. Enɛ baashã tso lɛ ni ekɛ naagbai aba moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii.

english: Is there any real difference between the white sweet potatoes I usually plant and the orange-fleshed ones?
ga: Ani srɔtofeemɔ ko diɛŋtsɛ yɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni mifɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ahe lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, orange-fleshed sweet potatoes are rich in Vitamin A, which helps protect your family's eyesight and boosts immunity, whereas the white varieties mostly provide energy without that extra nutrition.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ vitamin A. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ weku lɛ hiŋmɛii ahe, ni ehaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli hewalɛ ni tsiɔ helai anaa lɛ mli waa. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi babaoo haa hewalɛ ni niyenii krokomɛi fataaa he lɛ,.

english: Why are agricultural officers encouraging us to plant orange-fleshed sweet potatoes for the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ akwɛmɔ he hewalɛ kɛha jarayeli lɛ?

english: Orange sweet potatoes mature quickly in about three to four months and have high market demand because bakeries, food processors, and health-conscious families actively buy them.
ga: Orange sweet potatoes lɛ shwereɔ oya yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli, ni jara nɔ nibii babaoo taoɔ. Ejaakɛ aboloofeemɔ niyenii afeemɔ tsɔne lɛ Kɛ wekui ni kwɛɔ hewalɛnamɔ nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhe ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How does a sweet potato plant grow underground when I only plant a piece of the leaf vine?
ga: Te sweet potato tsei lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi? Beni miduɔ wain tso kome pɛ ni baa yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Sweet potato vines have small nodes along the stem that naturally form roots when buried in moist soil, and over time, these roots swell up to store food, becoming the sweet potatoes you harvest.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifã lɛ he ni kɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛshishifãi feɔ shishifãi kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Ni beni be hoɔ lɛ Nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ fũuɔ koni amɛkɛ niyenii ato. ni nyɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii ni nyɛkpaa lɛ

english: Why do sweet potato vines spread out and cover the whole farm so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miiha ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ oya lɛ?

english: Sweet potato vines naturally crawl across the ground to capture maximum sunlight, which also helps shade the soil, keep moisture in the ground, and prevent weeds from growing.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ nyiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. ni yeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: My sweet potato plants are flowering on top; does that mean the crop underground is ready to be dug up?
ga: Mi sweet potato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ. Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔshi nibii efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ?

english: Not necessarily; flowering is just a natural sign that the plant is mature, but you should check the soil for cracks or wait until the foliage starts turning yellow to know if the roots are fully grown.
ga: nɔ ni he ehiaaa; Fɔfɔi ji adebɔɔ mli okadi pɛ ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso ko eda. Shi esa akɛ okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji egbɛ eshwa loo omɛ kɛyashi baai lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni ona kɛji shishifãi lɛ edara.

english: How do I know if sweet potatoes are ready for harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can look for cracks forming in the soil mounds where the expanding roots push the earth, or yellowing leaves at the base of the plant, which signal that growth underground has finished.
ga: Obaanyɛ otao ŋmeii ni eba yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli he ni shishifãi ni mli lɛɛɔ lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. loo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dalɛ eba naagbee.

english: Can sweet potatoes survive and yield well in dry or poorer soils where other crops struggle?
ga: Ani ŋmeii baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo ohiafo nɔ fe tsei krokomɛi ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, sweet potatoes are very tough and drought-tolerant because their underground root network allows them to efficiently search for and store moisture deep in the ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, sweet potatoes wa waa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhiɛɔ mli.

english: If I put a lot of fertilizer on my sweet potatoes, will it give me bigger tubers under the ground?
ga: Kɛji akɛ oowo ŋmɔshi nii lɛ, okɛ sweet potato babaoo afata he. Ani ebaada yitso agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer will cause the plant to grow thick, beautiful leaves above ground while leaving you with small, thin roots under the soil, so balanced feeding is needed.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen wo tso lɛ mli fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná baai fɛfɛji ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni aha niyenii ni sa.

english: Is it good to plant sweet potatoes on the same piece of land right after harvesting maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akpa ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, rotating sweet potatoes with cereal crops like maize helps break the life cycle of pests and uses different soil nutrients, keeping your land healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, atomɔ ni akɛ ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ abele tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ wala shihilɛ mli. ni okɛ niyenii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi

english: How can I keep my sweet potato vines fresh during the dry season so I have planting material for the next rain?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli? No hewɔ lɛ, ani dumɔ nibii yɛ kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ ni baa lɛ?

english: You can plant a small nursery bed near a water source or in a shady backyard area to water a few vine stems during the dry season until the main rains return.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ gbekɛbii ashihilɛhe bibioo ko. Yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhe loo yɛ sɛɛgbɛ he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ koni akɛ nu awo wain tsei ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ wulu lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your soil is running low on nitrogen. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the maize the food it needs to stay green and build large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmei loo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ehaa ŋmei lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ ŋmei wuji.

english: Empty groundnut pods happen when the soil lacks calcium while the pods are expanding underground. Applying lime or wood ash to your soil before planting helps the pods fill up with healthy seeds.
ga: Peanut ŋmɔtɔi ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ miigbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ lime loo tso sũ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ayi ŋmeii lɛ amli obɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers instead of growing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from high heat, lack of shade, or dry soil. Maintaining moderate shade trees in your farm helps keep the farm cool and moist so flowers can turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ hulutsoo be ni sa mli yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off before making peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani mifee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop blossoms when the weather gets too hot or when watering is irregular. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruits form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ haaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How can I make my yam plants produce big tubers instead of just growing lots of leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-sweet potato tso lɛ akwɛ bulbs wuji moŋ fe ni ebaakwɛ baai babaoo kɛkɛ?

english: Yam plants put energy into leaves if the soil is too rich in nitrogen or if mounds are too small. Making deep, loose soil mounds and using tall stakes allows the leaves to gather enough sunlight to feed the tuber below.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hewalɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo ŋtayaa lɛ faaa tsɔ. Gɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ ni afeɔ kɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ buaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ naa.

english: Curling tomato leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a virus, or by extreme dry weather. Controlling insects early and keeping the plants watered stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa mli Mra be mli ni akwɛɔ kooloi anɔ Ni nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akabɔle amɛhe.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings suddenly wilt and die at ground level?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seedlings rot at the stem base when the soil is kept too wet and fungal diseases build up. Planting on raised nursery beds with good drainage prevents water from sitting around tender stems.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ̃ yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe ni awó nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi nu naa koni ekabɔle tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ nɔ ni mikpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in heavy clay soils without draining away. Planting your cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to flow away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni etsɔɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when the fruit bunch starts to grow heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ mli tsii lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are close to the surface and can be weakened by poor soil or pests. Supporting the stem with a strong wooden prop or bamboo pole helps bear the heavy weight of the bunch during wind.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Tso loo ŋmei ni wa ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ Ebaaye abua ni efi ŋmei lɛ muji ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why does my rice crop fall flat on the ground just when it is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shi beni amɛshɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Rice stalks fall over when seeds are planted too closely or when too much chemical fertilizer makes the stems tall and weak. Spacing your plants properly and using balanced fertilizer creates strong stems that hold the heavy grain heads up.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ. Aloo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe wa ni hiɛɔ dumɔwui ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plant turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to stay green and grow strong, or that the roots are drowning from excess water in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Aloo shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why is my cassava plant growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but the tubers under the ground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa lolo?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or shade, it puts all its energy into growing leaves on top instead of storing energy underground to make big tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen loo shade babaoo nɔ lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ebaa lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam vines need to climb up to catch direct sunlight with their leaves. Sunlight helps the plant make food, which then flows down into the ground to grow large yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ amli. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Kɛkɛ lɛ, efoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii agboi akwɛ̃.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts together with my maize helps the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ du ŋmei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa mi-ŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are special plants that pull natural nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, which feeds the neighboring maize plant without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛŋmɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my crops yield less harvest if I plant the exact same crop on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil over time and allows specific pests and diseases that love that crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ afite kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Ni ehaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai komɛi ni sumɔɔ tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off the tree without ever turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers if tiny insects like midges do not pollinate them, or if the tree is experiencing stress from hot weather, drought, or too little shade.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ midges lɛ efɔɔɔ amɛhe fɔfɔi. Aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ miina nɔnyɛɛ kɛjɛ latsaa, hɔmɔ, loo hulutsoo fioo tsɔ mli.

english: This black spot is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the tomato plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he diŋ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive heat causes pepper plants to lose water faster than their roots can absorb it, so the plant naturally drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry spell. If you plant right away, the hot dry soil will bake and destroy your delicate young sprouts before the real rains return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ baashã ni egbe odumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ aku esɛɛ aba.

english: How do weeds actually reduce my harvest if there seems to be enough space in the soil for everything?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aha mikpamɔ lɛ aba shi? Be mli ni etamɔ nɔ ni gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and secretly steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your plants, leaving your crops hungry and weak.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha otsei lɛ yɛ teemɔŋ. Shimɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ hɔmɔ kɛ gbɔjɔmɔ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is 'dead' and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ‘egbo’ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: Soil is considered 'dead' or exhausted when crops grow very slowly, leaves turn yellow, and yields drop significantly despite good rainfall. Adding fertilizer and organic manure restores essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus so crops can grow healthy again.
ga: Abuɔ shikpɔŋ akɛ ‘egbo’ loo egbo kɛ́ tsei miida blɛoo waa. baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi waa yɛ nugbɔ kpakpa ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus aku sɛɛ aba. koni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ

english: Can fertilizer really bring old, tired farmland back to life?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni egbɔ ni efite lɛ aba wala mli ekoŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, continuous farming removes natural nutrients from the ground over time. Applying the right fertilizer replenishes these lost nutrients, reviving the soil so it can support healthy new crop growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aba ekoŋŋ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni enyɛ eye ebua tsei heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ adalɛ.

english: What is the best way to prepare my land when starting a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ masaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ mije kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: When starting a cocoa farm, clear weeds and brush without burning the soil, as fire destroys organic matter. Ensure you keep or plant temporary shade plants, like plantains, to shield young cocoa seedlings from harsh sunlight.
ga: Kɛji ooje kookoo ŋmɔ shishi Jiemɔ jwɛi ni okɛshwie jwɛi nɔ ni okɛshãaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ejaakɛ la fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni okɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, ato loo odu koni ebu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings wilting even when there is rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate roots and cannot handle full, direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantain plants to protect them, extreme heat causes their leaves to lose water faster than their young roots can draw it from the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo plantains ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ bɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: With modern hybrid cocoa varieties and good care—such as proper fertilizing and weed control—trees can begin producing pods in about 2 to 3 years, compared to older varieties that took 4 to 5 years.
ga: Kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cocoa hybrid henɔi kɛ kwɛmɔ kpakpa tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Tsei baanyɛ aje ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, ni akɛto afii 4 kɛyashi 5 he kɛha kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ.

english: Is it safe to apply strong chemical fertilizer directly when planting fresh cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baatsu nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ oodu kookoo dumɔwui heei?

english: No, putting strong chemical fertilizer directly into the hole with fresh seedlings can burn their delicate young roots. It is better to let the seedling establish itself for a few weeks or use organic compost first.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ wo bu ni dumɔwui heei yɔɔ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha dumɔwui lɛ ama shi otsii fioo komɛi loo okɛ organic compost atsu nii klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: How soon after applying fertilizer should I expect to see improvements in my crop?
ga: Te esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaya hiɛ oya ha tɛŋŋ?

english: You will usually see plants turn darker green and grow faster within 1 to 2 weeks after fertilizer application, provided there is enough moisture in the soil to dissolve and carry the nutrients to the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ obaana tsei ni miitsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya yɛ otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ mli yɛ be mli ni awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ. Esa akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ mli ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do some farmers in my area get double the cocoa harvest that I get on the same size land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ naa kookoo ni mifeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ toi enyɔ lɛ?

english: Higher yields come from consistent soil feeding with fertilizer, regular pruning to let sunlight reach the tree trunk, controlling pests like capsids, and planting improved seed varieties.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa lɛ daa lɛ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ tso lɛ daa koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ tso lɛ shishi. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ lɛ adumɔ.

english: How can agricultural bank programs like ADB's 'Agric and More' help small cocoa farmers?
ga: Te okwaayeli shikatoohe gbɛjianɔtoi tamɔ ADB ‘Agric and More’ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua kookoo okwaafoi bibii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Programs like these provide farmers with accessible loans, farm supplies, and financial advice so they can afford inputs like fertilizers, seedlings, and tools needed to expand or restore their farms.
ga: Nitsumɔi ni tamɔ nɛkɛ yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛnáa shika. Okwaayeli mli nibii kɛ shika he ŋaawoo Enɛ ji koni amɛná nibii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, dumɔwui kɛ nibii ni he hiaa koni amɛkɛgbala amɛŋmɔji lɛ amli loo amɛha amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: What do bank officers look at before deciding to support a farmer with an agricultural loan?
ga: Mɛni shikatoohe nitsulɔi susuɔ he dani amɛkpɛɔ amɛyiŋ akɛ amɛbaaye amɛbua okwaafoi kɛ okwaayeli he nyɔmɔwoo?

english: Bank officers look at the size and condition of your farmland, your farming experience, the type of crop you grow, and your plan for managing the farm to ensure you can harvest successfully and pay back the loan.
ga: Sikatoohe nitsulɔi lɛ baakwɛ bɔ ni oŋmɔ lɛ da ha kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha. Okwaayeli mli niiashikpamɔ Nibii ni oduɔ kɛ okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔtoo koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ obaanyɛ okpa nii jogbaŋŋ ni owo nyɔmɔ ni okɛwo lɛ.

english: If I plant trees and food crops together on the same land, won't the trees steal all the water and food from my crops?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsei kɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii fee ekome yɛ he kome lɛ Ani tsei lɛ ejuŋ nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Not necessarily. When planned well, tree roots go deeper into the soil than crop roots, pulling up hidden water and nutrients from lower layers. Also, falling tree leaves rot and add natural food back into the topsoil for your crops.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Kɛ ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ Tso shishifãi yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe tsei shishifãi. Enɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ fãi lɛ amli. Kɛfata he lɛ, tsei ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Can I grow food crops like maize or cassava on land where young forest trees have just been planted?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ani abaanyɛ adu tsei bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni adu nɔ etsɛko lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, while the trees are small and young, there is plenty of space and sunlight for food crops like maize or cassava. This allows you to harvest food for a few years before the tree branches grow wide enough to cover the farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ bibioo moŋ. Shi he ko kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ kɛha niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii afii fioo komɛi dani tso lɛ niji lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do tree roots sometimes make it difficult to harvest root crops like yams or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tso shishifãi haa ewaa akɛ abaakpa shishifãi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Tree roots spread out underground and can wrap around or block tuber crops as they expand. This makes the soil hard to dig and can damage both your crops and the tree's root system during harvest.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi ni ebaanyɛ ebɔle loo etsĩ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ naa beni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ abaatsũ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ebaanyɛ efite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsei shishifãi fɛɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: How far apart should I space trees from my crops so both can grow without fighting for space?
ga: Esa akɛ mafo tsei lɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe koni amɛdara ni mikɛ amɛhe akawo he akaŋ.

english: Spacing depends on the tree type, but leaving 5 to 10 meters between major tree lines ensures your food crops get enough sunlight and ground space for their roots to spread freely.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ damɔ tso henɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi shi mitai 5 kɛyashi 10 yɛ tsei akui wuji lɛ ateŋ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ oniyenii tsei lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ he ko ni baaha amɛshishifãi lɛ adara amɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do some of my crops grow weak and tall when they are planted under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛyaa shɔŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Crops need full sunlight to make energy. When shade is too heavy, crops stretch upward rapidly trying to reach the light, making their stems thin and weak instead of producing strong branches and fruit.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia tsei koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baajie amɛhe oya kɛya ŋwɛi yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbɔɔ koni amɛha la. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo niji kɛ aduawai ni mli wa.

english: Which crops grow best when there is shade from nearby trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ewo amɛhe shade?

english: Shade-tolerant crops like young cocoa, plantain, cocoyam, and ginger thrive under trees because they naturally prefer cool, moist environments and lower sunlight intensity.
ga: Tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hulutsoo shi tamɔ kookoo bibii, plantain, kookoo, kɛ ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei ashishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛsumɔɔ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni hulu la fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my food crops produce less yield after tree branches grow large and cover the whole farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ wooo yibii fioo yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ niji lɛ eda ni amɛha ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: As trees mature, their thick leaf canopy blocks the sunlight that crops like maize and vegetables need to produce grains and fruits, causing yields to drop naturally as the shade increases.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ yibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ aduawai he hiaa koni amɛwo ŋmãa kɛ aduawai lɛ naa. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: How do trees on my farm help protect my food crops during very hot and dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔɔ waa ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Trees act as windbreakers and sunshades, lowering the ground temperature around your crops and keeping soil moisture from evaporating quickly during hot spells.
ga: Tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsimɔ kɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa ni bɔleɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ lɛ.

english: How do fallen leaves from trees help my crops grow without using chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: When fallen tree leaves rot on the ground, soil microbes break them down into rich organic matter called compost, which adds natural nutrients directly to the soil for your crops.
ga: Kɛji baai ni egbee shi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, nibii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ gbálaa amɛ mli ni amɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Will planting timber or forest trees harm the quality of my farm soil over time?
ga: Ani tsei loo koo mli tsei ni aduɔ lɛ baaná shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: In general, forest trees improve soil quality. Their deep roots prevent rain from washing away the soil, and their falling leaves continuously rebuild topsoil fertility over the long term.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, Koo mli tsei baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo. Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsiɔ nugbɔ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni amɛbaai ni egbee shi lɛ yaa nɔ etswaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and dying off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps your maize stay green, photosynthesize properly, and produce full, heavy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-ŋmei lɛ ni ehi shi ŋmɔŋ. Fotosintɛsis lɛ sa jogbaŋŋ. ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni tsii ni eye emuu

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my vegetable garden during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ aduawai anɔ nu yɛ ŋmɔ mli abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?
