english: It is best to water early in the morning before the sun gets hot, or late in the afternoon. Morning watering gives plants moisture to survive the afternoon heat, while watering in midday heat wastes water because it evaporates into the air before reaching the roots.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi dani hulu lɛ adɔ loo shwane mli. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi lɛ haa amɛnáa nu ni haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shwane latsaa lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ nɔ yɛ gbi mli lɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ejaakɛ efoɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks water, or when flowers are not pollinated. Keeping your soil evenly moist and encouraging bees into your farm helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ eshɛɛɛ amɛhe Pollen Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ ŋmeii ni awoɔ amɛ hewalɛ kɛbaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ he ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When you harvest them, that trapped food stays in the soil, acting as natural fertilizer for hungry crops like maize or cassava planted next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni okpaa Niyenii ni ekã lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni abaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: How can I tell when my yam tubers are fully mature and ready to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-sweet potato tubers lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Yams tell you they are ready when their green leaves turn yellow and the vines dry out naturally at the end of the rainy season. This signals that the plant has stopped feeding the tuber and all the energy is stored underground.
ga: Sweet potato kɛɔ bo akɛ efee klalo kɛ́ ebaai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni wain tsei lɛ gĩ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii lɛ niyenii ni ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites that suck the juice from leaves and spread viruses. Spraying neem oil solution or insecticidal soap kills these tiny bugs and protects new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi bibii lɛ. Enɛɛmɛi kɛ dalɛ hee naa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool soil moisture it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cabbage plants produce big leafy shoots but fail to form hard heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ ŋmeii agboi ni yɔɔ baai shi enyɛɛɛ efee yitsei ni wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form tight heads if they get too much nitrogen fertilizer or if temperatures get too hot. Balanced feeding and keeping the soil consistently cool and moist encourages the inner leaves to fold tightly into a head.
ga: Kaabaji efeŋ yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛji akɛ enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Niyenii ni ja ni akɛaaha ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ baawo mligbɛ baai lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfolɔ amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ kɛya yitso lɛ he.

english: What causes the bottom of my watermelon fruits to turn black and rot before they mature?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-watermelon lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani edaa?

english: Rot at the bottom of watermelons, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant lacks calcium or receives irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture steady and applying agricultural lime prevents the fruit bottoms from turning black.
ga: Rot ni yɔɔ water shishi lɛ Atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ calcium loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ lime ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haaa aduawai lɛ ashishi afee ediŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings rot in the soil instead of sprouting after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings rot if they are planted upside down, planted in waterlogged soil, or taken from diseased parent stems. Make sure the leaf buds point upwards and plant in well-drained soil using healthy, mature stems.
ga: Kasava tsei ni afo lɛ baafite kɛji akɛ adu amɛyitso. Adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. loo ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli Kwɛmɔ akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ kɛtsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Can I use water from a nearby river affected by galamsey to water my vegetable farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ ni Galamsey ena hewalɛ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛha mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu?

english: Water affected by illegal mining often contains dangerous heavy metals like mercury and thick mud. Using it can poison your soil, destroy plant roots, and make your harvested vegetables unsafe for people to eat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dade ni tsii ni yɔɔ oshara tamɔ mercury kɛ sũ ni mli edɔ yɔɔ nu ni shika tsuru ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ saa he lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofa awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, efite tsei ashishifãi, ni eha aduawai ni akpa lɛ afee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ gbɔmɛi yeɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting even though the soil around them is soaked with river water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho eyɛ mli akɛ faa mli nu eyi shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: If the river water is polluted with chemicals or oil waste, it burns the plant's delicate root system. Damaged roots lose their ability to absorb water properly, causing the plant to wilt even in wet soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsofai loo mu ni fiteɔ nii efite faa lɛ mli nu lɛ Ebaashã tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu jogbaŋŋ dɔŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eha tsei agbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ po nɔ.

english: How does dirty, muddy river water affect seeds that I just planted?
ga: Te faa lɛ mli nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ saa dumɔwui ni midu amrɔ nɛɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Muddy water leaves a heavy layer of silt over the ground as it dries. This creates a hard crust on top of the soil that stops young seeds from sprouting and reaching the sunlight.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ shĩɔ sũ ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni egbiɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmei ni wa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni dumɔwui bibii akakwɛ̃ ni hulu la akashɛ amɛnɔ.

english: Can dirty water from a polluted river harm both my crops and my fish pond at the same time?
ga: Ani nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛ faa ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ miloo ŋshɔ lɛ fɛɛ awui yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, polluted water carries chemicals and dirt that reduce oxygen for fish in your pond while also contaminating the soil and roots of nearby crops, harming both harvests.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai kɛ muji ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala ni haa loo ni yɔɔ o-po lɛ mli lɛ náa lɛ baa shi yɛ nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, efiteɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ashishifãi. ni yeɔ nibii ni anáa lɛ srɔtoi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ awui

english: Is it safe for me to plant cassava on land that was previously used for illegal mining?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ ajieɔ ŋmei yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Mined land often lacks fertile topsoil and contains poisonous chemical residues. Root crops like cassava absorb these toxins directly into the tubers, making them dangerous to consume unless the soil is properly tested and restored.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni atsa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni baa nii, ni tsofai fɔji ni eshwɛ yɛ mli. Tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ nɛkɛ tsofai fɔji nɛɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. ni haa efeɔ oshara kɛha niyeli ja aka shikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ ni aku sɛɛ afee lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are earthworms disappearing from my farm soil near the polluted stream?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii miiho kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni bɛŋkɛ faa ko ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Earthworms are very sensitive to chemical pollution and dirty water. When toxic waste enters the soil, earthworms die or move away, leaving your soil hard, compacted, and less fertile for crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii nuɔ tsofai ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ he waa. Kɛji akɛ muji ni yɔɔ gbeyei bote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ gboiɔ loo amɛyaa he kroko, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa, ni ebɔleɔ ehe, ni ehaaa ŋmɔshi nibii aba.

english: Why are my pepper plants failing to grow even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ada eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: If your soil has been contaminated by chemical pollution or polluted runoff, the natural living organisms in the ground die off. Without healthy soil life, plants cannot break down and absorb the fertilizer you apply.
ga: Kɛji tsofai loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Adebɔɔ mli wala ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baagboi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ kpakpa bɛ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ akumɔ ni amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and brown after dirty river water flooded my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ beni nu muji eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Dirty water carrying mud and chemical runoff blocks air from reaching plant roots. Without air, the roots suffocate and cannot send nutrients up to the leaves, causing them to turn yellow and die.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji ni muji kɛ tsofai ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ tsei shishifãi ahe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aya baa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees look weak and drop leaves when planted near polluted streams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ adu yɛ faa ko ni mli ewo muji lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Polluted streams carry harmful chemical runoff that damages the fine feeder roots of cocoa trees. Without strong feeder roots, the trees cannot take up enough water and food, leading to weak growth and leaf drop.
ga: Faai ni mli ewo muji lɛ hiɛɔ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni hoɔ. ni kɛ fitemɔ baa kookoo shishifãi kpakpai lɛ anɔ Kɛji shishifãi ni wa bɛ Tsei hu nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ baai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: How can I protect my crops if dirty runoff water from polluted land flows onto my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe? Kɛji nu ni mli ewo muji ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ewo muji nɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ

english: You can dig shallow drainage ditches along your farm border or plant crops on raised ridges to divert contaminated water away, keeping dirty runoff from touching your crops' roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nubu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ naa loo dumɔ tsei yɛ ŋshɔkei ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ koni ekɛjie nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ kɛya. Etsiɔ nu ni mli ewo muji naa koni ekashɛ otso lɛ shishifãi ahe.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize turning yellow and drying up from the tip inward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaagbee mli kɛyaa mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the bottom leaves usually means the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. The plant moves nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed new top growth, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: In intense midday heat, leaves release water vapor faster than the roots can suck up fresh water from the soil. The plant droops to shrink its leaf area exposed to the sun to protect itself from drying out, usually recovering by evening as temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Baai jieɔ nu lasu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kpakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ ahe he lɛ afee bibioo yɛ hulu la mli koni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and watery if heavy rains come right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa dani akpa lɛ?

english: When heavy rain hits mature cassava, the plant receives a signal to start growing fresh leaves again. It pulls stored sugars and energy back out of the underground tubers to feed new top growth, leaving the tubers watery and prone to rot.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ŋmei lɛ shwereɔ. Tso lɛ baaná okadi ko ni baaha ebɔi baai heei feemɔ ekoŋŋ. Egbalaa sugar kɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ kɛjɛɔ tuber lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Ashiɔ ŋmeii lɛ akɛ nu ni amɛfɔɔ fitemɔ.

english: If I plant my maize very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close makes crops fight each other for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. When stalks compete intensely, they grow thin and weak, producing tiny or empty cobs, which lowers your total yield compared to properly spaced plants.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu fioo Beni ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ waa lɛ Amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa. ni kɛ cob bibioo loo efolo baa Enɛ baaha onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ aba shi kɛ akɛto tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, act like hungry children competing with the mother plant for nutrients and water. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the mother plant to direct its energy into producing a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Efeɔ enii tamɔ gbekɛ ni hɔmɔ miiye lɛ, ni ekɛ tso nyɛ lɛ miishi akaŋ yɛ niyenii kɛ nu he. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings look weak and stop growing for a few days after I move them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ gbii fioo komɛi beni mikɛ amɛ ewo saatso wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is known as transplant shock. Moving delicate plants breaks tiny feeder roots and exposes them to bright sun and dry wind. Transplanting late in the afternoon and watering right away helps seedlings recover quickly without dying.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Tsei ni waaa ni ajieɔ lɛ baakumɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ ni ebaaha hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ aba amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shwane mli ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhe waaa oya ni amɛgbooo.

english: Why do all the tiny flowers on my cocoa trees drop off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ani mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when stressed by prolonged dry spells, hot winds, or when beneficial insects that pollinate them are absent. Providing moderate shade and keeping ground soil covered helps trees retain moisture so flowers can turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ laaje. Shade ni sa kɛ mulching yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: This condition, called blossom-end rot, is caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, which often happens when soil water levels fluctuate unevenly. Keeping soil moisture steady with mulch and adding organic compost helps plants transport calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akɛ mulch haa be fɛɛ be kɛ organic compost ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium lɛ yaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are small caterpillars destroying the inner leaves inside the whorl of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miifite baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer hiding inside the tight funnel of young corn leaves where it is moist and safe from predators. Inspecting farms early and applying targeted neem leaf extract or approved controls inside the leaf whorl protects the growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa bibii amli lɛ amli he ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe lɛ. Nibii ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli mra Ni akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu ni akwɛɔ nɔ loo nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu he ni ŋmɔ lɛ daa lɛ he.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field with my corn help the corn grow better?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have microscopic organisms in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. As their roots decay, they release natural fertilizer directly into the soil for neighboring crops like corn to feed on.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ shishifãi lɛ miifite lɛ Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkɛye tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my corn keep jamming the machine when I take it to be processed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn lɛ yaa nɔ etswaa kɛji mikɛtsu nii lɛ?

english: Processing machines jam when corn cobs, husk remnants, or field debris are mixed in with the grains, or when the maize is still too wet and sticky to pass smoothly through the machinery.
ga: Tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii, ŋmãa ŋmeii, loo ŋmɔ mli jwɛi kɛ ŋmãa lɛ futu. aloo be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ mli edɔ lolo ni ewa tsɔ ni enyɛŋ etsɔ tsɔne lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my harvested maize is dry enough to shell and take to the mill?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafolɔ ni mikɛya ŋmãa lɛ?

english: When maize is properly dry, the kernels make a sharp clinking sound when shaken together, and you cannot easily dent a kernel with your fingernail.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baafee gbee ni tswaa. Kɛji akɛ akpokpo amɛ ekome Ni onyɛŋ okɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa ko abɔ he mlɛo. kɛ oniji ahe tsɔi

english: Why does my bagged corn get warm and moldy inside before I can take it to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa kotoku lɛ mli edɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Corn stored with high moisture content releases water vapor inside the closed bag, creating trapped heat and humidity that cause fungi and mold to grow quickly.
ga: Abele ni akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ jieɔ nu lasu yɛ kotokui ni aŋã mli. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni amɔmɔɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ yaa hiɛ oya.

english: Why do my corn kernels shatter into small pieces during shelling instead of coming out whole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ miigbɛ bibii bibii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ baafo lɛ,

english: Kernels shatter when they become over-dried in the sun or when too much force is used during shelling, making the grain brittle and easy to break.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baatswa kɛji akɛ hulu la babaoo shɛ amɛnɔ. aloo kɛ́ akɛ hewalɛ ni fe nine tsu nii yɛ be mli ni atswaa lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ oya.

english: Why is it important for me to clean out the cob pieces before taking my grain to the miller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsumɔ ŋmei lɛ mli dani mikɛ ŋmei lɛ aya ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hard cob fragments and tough stalks act as blockages inside milling machines, which can clog the grinders, overheat the engine, or damage the blades.
ga: Cob ni wa kɛ tsei ni wa tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni tsiɔ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ grinder lɛ naa. ni haa tsɔne lɛ mli dɔɔ fe nine loo efiteɔ tsɔne lɛ tsɔne lɛ.

english: Why does my stored maize turn into powder with small holes after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ powda ni eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: Insects called maize weevils burrow into the kernels to lay eggs, eating the grain from the inside out and leaving behind a fine powdery dust.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ corn weevils lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli koni amɛwo amɛwui. Eyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ ni eshiɔ sũ bibii pɛ.

english: How does sorting broken kernels away from good grain help me get a better market price?
ga: Te ŋmãa ni ekumɔ lɛ mligbalamɔ kɛ ŋmãa kpakpa mligbalamɔ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni oná jara kpakpa yɛ jara nɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Sorting removes damaged grains and trash that attract pests and mold, leaving clean, uniform corn that buyers trust and pay more money for.
ga: Nibii ni akɛhalaa lɛ jieɔ ŋmaa ni efite kɛ jwɛi ni gbalaa kooloi kɛ ŋmeii kɛbaa lɛ. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmãa ni he tse ni yaa nɔ daa ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ he nyɔmɔ babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants turn yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, which often happens when nutrients are exhausted or heavy rains wash them away from the roots.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii lɛ eho loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho amɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my corn stalks fall over in the farm before I can harvest the cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miigbee shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani abaanyɛ akpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Stalks fall over when stem borer insects chew through the inside of the stem, or when shallow roots cannot support the heavy cobs during strong winds.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji stem borers lɛ tsɔ tso lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ ŋmei ni tsii nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do some of my corn cobs have large empty spaces where kernels are missing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ ekomɛi yɛ ŋmeii wuji shi ŋmeii lɛ bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Missing kernels happen when dry weather or high heat prevents pollination while the corn silks are forming, leaving empty spots on the cob.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa tsiɔ pollination naa yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa siliki miifee lɛ. Enɛ haa he ko ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ ko baa yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ.

english: Maize leaves roll up during the hottest part of the day to reduce their surface area, which keeps the plant from losing too much water through evaporation during dry spells.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛfite nu babaoo kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruit during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ?

english: When tomato plants do not receive enough water, they become stressed and drop their flowers to save energy and moisture for survival rather than spending it on fruit production.
ga: Kɛji tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Amɛhaoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he koni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaafite shika yɛ aduawai afeemɔ mli lɛ

english: Will giving my crops a small amount of water every day make their roots strong?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ nu fioo ha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa gbi lɛ, ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Shallow daily watering keeps water near the soil surface, causing roots to stay near the top. Deep watering done less often forces roots to grow down deep into the soil to find water, making the plant stronger against dry weather.
ga: Nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ daa gbi lɛ baaha nu lɛ abɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ha shishifãi lɛ abɛŋkɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni mli kwɔ nyɛɔ shishifãi anɔ koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao nu. Ehaa tsei lɛ waa kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the tips of older lower leaves usually means the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is the main plant nutrient responsible for green leaf growth and plant vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishijee ŋmɔŋ ni baa yɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji tso mli niyenii titri ni haa baai eŋɔli daa kɛ tso hewalɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants producing huge bushy green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni ebɔle ehe shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to put all their energy into growing foliage above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekɛ ŋmei ato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa saplings turn brown and die when I clear away all the large trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi koko tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong direct sunlight. Shade trees or plantains act as natural shields, protecting tender cocoa leaves from sun scorch and keeping the surrounding air moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei loo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shade mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu. Buu kookoo baai ni mli tse lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: When pepper plants are spaced too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight and stretch upward instead of branching out, leaving them too weak to support heavy fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe teŋ jɛkɛ tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛfeɔ shɔŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee niji. ni ehaa amɛgbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛtere jatsu lɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to lift my yam vines onto tall stakes instead of letting them creep along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves into the sunlight so they can make food more efficiently, while keeping the leaves off the damp soil prevents fungal diseases from attacking the crop.
ga: Staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli koni amɛhoo nii jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akatutua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a water mold that multiplies quickly in cold, wet conditions. Raindrops bounce off the wet soil and spread the mold onto lower cocoa pods.
ga: Nu mli ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa. Nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amɛshwãa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ashishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Can rice grow on regular dry farm fields, or must it always be submerged in standing water?
ga: Ani omɔ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ omɔ ŋmɔji ni egbi ni yɔɔ daa lɛ amli? Aloo esa akɛ akɛwo nu ni mli ejɔ mli be fɛɛ be?

english: While flooded fields help suppress weeds for lowland rice, upland rice varieties are specifically bred to grow on normal dry farmland using regular rainfall or simple watering.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ jwɛi kɛha ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ moŋ, shi atsɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni akɛdu yɛ okwaayeli hei ni egbi kɛtsɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, it means the crop is starving for nitrogen. The plant actively steals nutrients from its older, lower leaves to send to the upper leaves, showing that your soil needs organic compost or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Tso lɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli koni ekɛya baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Etsɔɔ kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have friendly bacteria living in tiny knots on their roots. These bacteria pull nitrogen out of the air and turn it into plant food that stays in the soil to feed whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ naanyobɔɔ helai ni hiɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii ni eshwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense full sun. Plantains grow quickly and produce massive leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and moisture they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall without bearing good fruit when I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛlɛɛmɔ ni yibii kpakpai jɛɛɛ mli baa lɛ? Beni midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ

english: When crops are crowded, they block sunlight from each other. The plants waste all their energy stretching straight up to reach the sun, leaving no energy to build strong stems or produce large leaves and fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ, ebaatsi hulu lɛ naa kɛjɛ amɛhe Tsei lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni amɛkpãa ŋwɛi tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Eshiii hewalɛ ko ni ekɛma tsei ni wa loo ekɛbaa baai wuji kɛ aduawai.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when temperatures get too high or water is irregular. The heat stresses the plant, causing it to drop its flowers as a defense mechanism to save energy and stay alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ haa tsei haoɔ Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ he koni akɛ hewalɛ ato ni ahi wala mli.

english: Why do my cassava leaves wilt and droop during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense midday heat, leaves lose water into the hot air faster than the roots can suck it up from the ground. The leaves droop on purpose to shrink their surface area exposed to the sun, saving water until the cool evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ yiŋtoo akɛ amɛbaahã ŋwɛi ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ afee bibioo. Koni eye ebua ni akɛ nu ato kɛyashi gbɛkɛ

english: Why does my yam vine need a tall wooden stake to give a good yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni ewo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Yam plants make tubers underground using energy created by their leaves in sunlight. Staking lifts the vines high off the ground where leaves can catch maximum light and stay free from ground diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛbaai lɛ feɔ yɛ hulu la mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ baanyɛ aná la babaoo yɛ lɛ, ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees take so long to produce a bunch when I leave many suckers around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani efeɔ ŋmeii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii komɛi yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: A mother plantain stem shares its soil nutrients and water with every sucker connected to its root. If you leave too many suckers, they steal food from the main tree, delaying fruit growth and making bunches smaller.
ga: Dumɔwu nyɛ lɛ jaa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã fɛɛ ŋmei ni kɛ shishifã lɛ yɔɔ tsakpaa lɛ. Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo Ebaaju niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Ha aduawai lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni oha tso yibii lɛ afee bibioo

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up into little cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi bibii ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the juice from under the young leaves. The damaged leaf tissue shrinks and curls as it tries to heal itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Baa lɛ mli fãji ni efite lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebɔleɔ ehe be mli ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsa ehe lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil when rain falls continuously for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Waterlogged, soaked soil starves the roots of air, causing the root tissues to suffocate and rot away from damp soil fungi.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni edɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen, which is the main nutrient that makes leaves green and healthy. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or leaves the soil waterlogged, making it hard for the roots to breathe and feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo nu. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛna niyenii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant feels stressed, usually from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. When it gets too dry or hot, the plant sheds flowers to save water and energy to stay alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛji edɔ loo edɔ tsɔ lɛ, Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni wala ahi shi.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa trees turning black and rotting before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani akpa kpamɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, damp, and overly shaded farms. Clearing excess foliage to let in sunlight and removing infected pods early stops the disease from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Ajieɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la aba kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: What is eating small holes in the leaves inside the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ baa ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that nest deep inside the growing center of the maize plant. Catching them early with recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts protects the growing point before the whole plant is destroyed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni feɔ amɛ ŋmeii yɛ he ni ŋmei tso lɛ daa lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ atsĩ dalɛ naa dani akpata tso muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: Cassava is typically mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off. You can test maturity by carefully digging up one root stem to check if the tubers are thick and firm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ Obaanyɛ oka dalɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ shishifã tso kome ni ooofo mli jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ kɛji ŋmei lɛ mli edɔ ni ehi shi shiŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if the early rain is enough for me to start sowing seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: Do not plant after the very first rain, as dry weather often follows and dries up seeds. Wait until the soil is thoroughly wet down to the depth of your hand, showing that soil moisture is steady enough to support germination.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ sumɔɔ ni enyiɛ dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ ni egbi. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashɛ onine mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Can I plant pepper on the same land with my cassava plant suckers?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu pepper yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ajieɔ ŋmei yɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, pepper and cassava grow well together in the early months. Cassava grows slowly at first, so pepper plants can share the space and harvest before the cassava canopy grows big enough to shade out the peppers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli. Cassava daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ aja ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ amli awo hei srɔtoi ni akpa amɛ dani ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ adara bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when strong winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots stay close to the surface and can be weakened by soil pests like root-nematodes or subterranean weevils. Earthing up soil around the plant stem and propping tall trees with wooden sticks helps anchor them firmly.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo crypt weevils lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ obɔle tso lɛ shishi ni okɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ fe tsutsu lɛ adu koni eye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do crops grow very tall in one area of my farm but stay short in another area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii miiya hiɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he kome shi ebɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Soil richness varies across a farm due to soil depth, previous land use, or water drainage. Areas with shallower soil, poor organic matter, or washed-away topsoil have fewer nutrients to support crop growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɔmɔ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ hewɔ. shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii tsutsu loo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli Hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. Aloo, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni nu lɛ hoɔ lɛ baaná niyenii fioo ni baaye abua tsei lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up quickly during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be kuku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up when the soil mounds lose moisture under direct sunlight. Covering the top of the yam mounds with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool and retains water for the roots much longer.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛji gɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ fo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulching) ha sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa trees turning black before they are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in high humidity and heavy rain. Keeping the farm well-pruned allows sunlight and air to dry out the trees, which reduces the spread of the fungus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmɔ ko mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when the dry Harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ Harmattan be ni nu egbi lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow root systems that cannot reach deep moisture during dry spells. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them protects them from scorching sunlight and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my rice leaves turn yellow and stop growing after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess standing water without good drainage can choke the roots and stop them from taking in air. Heavy rain can also wash nitrogen out of the soil, which causes leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsi shishifãi lɛ anaa ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ akabote mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do some of my rice plants produce empty grains at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ woɔ dumɔwui ni bɛ nɔ ko yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Empty grains often happen when rice plants suffer from severe heat or drought while flowering, or when insect pests like stink bugs feed on the soft, developing grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji ŋmãa tsei lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. aloo beni kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni miida lɛ.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds inside the whorl of maize. Spotting them early and applying appropriate control measures helps save the growing point of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii. Amɛtaomɔ mra Ni akɛ gbɛi ni sa ni akɛbaakwɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akwɛ he ni tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants curl up and turn yellow in patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems recommended by agricultural officers is the best way to prevent it.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Cassava tsei ni helai ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ he ŋaa lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ helai anaa.

english: How do I know if my farm soil needs fertilizer before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ni awo ŋmɔshi nibii dani adu nii?

english: If your previous crops grew slowly, had thin stems, or produced yellow leaves early in the season, your soil is low in nutrients and needs organic manure or mineral fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji onibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ da blɛoo, eyɛ tsei bibii, loo eyɛ baai ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli.

english: Why do my vegetable roots rot when I water the soil every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ mikɛ nu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa gbi lɛ?

english: Overwatering fills up all the air pockets in the soil, suffocating the roots. Plant roots need a balance of water and air; soggy soil encourages fungal rot.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa he miihia tsei shishifãi. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to compete for sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients, leading to tall, weak plants that produce poor yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo lɛ baa.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my crops while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops are weak and cannot outgrow fast-spreading weeds. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing essential nutrients, water, and sunlight from your crops.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye jwɛi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ anɔ kunim. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant the maize seeds I harvested from my own farm last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikpa kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ mli nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strength in the next generation. Buying fresh certified seeds ensures all your plants grow strong, resist diseases, and yield high amounts of grain like their parent crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ haa otsei lɛ fɛɛ daa waa, helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛnɔ, ni amɛwo dumɔwui babaoo tamɔ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why should I keep track of which specific variety of cassava stick I planted in each part of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ anɔ?

english: Tracking seed and crop varieties helps you know which ones yielded the biggest tubers and survived diseases best, so you can plant only the best-performing variety across your whole farm next season.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ tsei srɔtoi ni oookwɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ole henɔi ni woɔ bulbs wuji fe fɛɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ helai ahe. Enɛ ji koni onyɛ odu tsei srɔtoi ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ pɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow and falling off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen or getting too much water. Nitrogen feeds leaf growth, so applying manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ. Nitrogen haa baa lɛ daa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or attacks by tiny pests. Keeping the soil moist with mulch and protecting the leaves from insects allows flowers to turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atuatsemɔ Kɛ́ akɛ muji ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli edɔ, ni abu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Keeping some large shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides shade and moisture while the cocoa roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ baaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to space out my cassava plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe moŋ fe ni aaadu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are too close, their roots compete underground for food and water. Giving each plant proper space allows the roots to expand fully into large, heavy tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baatswa niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ kwraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell. Seeds planted too early will sprout and then dry up before the main rainy season establishes, causing seed loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaagbi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dumɔwui ni laajeɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to apply fertilizer to my maize plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-abele tsei lɛ amli?

english: Maize needs fertilizer at two main stages: first when planting to help roots establish, and again when the plant reaches knee-height to power fast stem growth and ear formation.
ga: Abɛi he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛi titrii enyɔ nɔ: klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, kɛ́ adu koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛma shi; kɛ agbɛnɛ hu beni tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛnaji ahe koni amɛha amɛshishifã lɛ aya hiɛ oya ni amɛtoi lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Maize removes nitrogen from the soil, but legumes like cowpeas naturally pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, making the soil fertile again for future crops.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my garden egg farm produce fewer fruits after the first few harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi abɔɔ mli ŋmeii ŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii fioo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔi fioo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: As crop plants produce fruits, they drain nutrients from the soil. Adding fresh compost and pruning old branches encourages the plant to grow new stems and start producing flowers again.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii lɛ Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii hee fata he ni afolɔ tsei niji momoi lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni ebɔi fɔfɔi ekoŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves into the light and keeps them off wet soil, preventing rot and helping you get much larger yams.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ aje kpo yɛ la mli ni ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa ŋmɔtɔ ni da babaoo.

english: When a plantain tree grows too many young shoots, they all fight for the same water and soil nutrients. Leaving only one or two strong shoots allows the main plant to produce a much bigger bunch of plantains.
ga: Beni dumɔwu lɛ ná ŋmeii bibii babaoo Amɛbaawuu koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants turn brown and wither when planted in open sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains near young cocoa shields them from direct heat and keeps moisture in the soil until they mature.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa tɛ̃ɛ he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year even when I plant the same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Crops remove nutrients from the ground every time they grow. Planting the same crop repeatedly without adding manure or fertilizer, or without letting the land rest, empties the soil of food for future plants.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaadara. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he loo ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛha tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, the main food green plants need to grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients out of the topsoil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei eŋɔli koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark, rotten spots at the bottom before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit. It usually happens when watering is irregular or during dry spells when roots cannot absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ, ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli loo yɛ hɔmɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on the sap and pass on plant viruses. Controlling these small pests early stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛhaa helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii nɛɛ ahe nitsumɔ mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Cassava needs adequate room underground so its roots can swell into large tubers. Planting them about one meter apart stops neighboring plants from competing for sunlight and soil food.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia cassava koni eshishifãi lɛ atsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ adu amɛ aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaatsi tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋshii.

english: Why should I wait for continuous rains before planting my maize instead of planting right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ aya nɔ anɛ dani madu ŋmãa? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain of the season is often followed by a hot dry spell. If you plant immediately, your seeds may sprout and then dry up in the soil before regular rains begin.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ latsaa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be sɛɛ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Odumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ aba.

english: Why are bees and small insects always flying around my okra flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii krokomɛi shwieɔ mi roselle fɔfɔi lɛ ahe be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Those insects are helping your farm by performing pollination. They move pollen from flower to flower, which is the essential step that allows the plant to stop blooming and start growing the actual okra pods.
ga: Nakai kooloi lɛ miiye amɛmiibua oŋmɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ. Amɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi amli kɛyaa fɔfɔi krokomɛi anɔ, ni eji gbɛ ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekpaa fɔfɔi ni ebɔi anɔkwa okra ŋmɔtɔi lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: How do I know that my okra plant has been successfully pollinated?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi okra tso lɛ eye omanye yɛ pollination mli?

english: After pollination happens, the flower will wither and fall off, and you will see a small, green okra pod starting to appear and grow in its place.
ga: Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ wo pollination sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Ni obaana okra ŋmeii bibii. Mohu ɔ, a jeɔ sisi nɛ a jeɔ kpo nɛ a waa.

english: Can I pollinate my crops by hand if I do not see insects on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi nine awo mitsei lɛ amli kɛji minaaa kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can manually transfer pollen between flowers using a soft brush or your fingers. This helps trigger fruit growth when natural insect pollinators are absent.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ brɔsh ni yɔɔ blɛoo loo oniji atsu nii ni okɛ pollen awo fɔfɔi ateŋ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ daa kɛji akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni haa yibii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii lɛ bɛ.

english: What happens to my young okra pods if insects attack them as soon as they appear?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi okra ŋmɔji bibii lɛ anɔ kɛji kooloi bibii tutua amɛ kɛji amɛje kpo pɛ?

english: Insects can bore into young pods, lay eggs, or feed on them, causing the okra to turn crooked, develop black spots, rot, or drop off before maturing.
ga: Kplukai baanyɛ afo amɛhe awo ŋmeii bibii amli, amɛwo ŋmeii loo amɛye amɛ, ni enɛ baaha okra lɛ abɔle, ená ŋmeii diji, egbo loo egbee shi dani eda.

english: When is the best time to start spraying my farm to protect the growing vegetables?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabɔi miŋmɔ lɛ mli tsofa lɛ shwiemɔ koni mikɛbu aduawai ni miida lɛ ahe?

english: You should begin protecting your crops as soon as the small fruits start to appear, because young fruits are soft, tender, and most attractive to hungry pests.
ga: Esa akɛ oje oŋmɔshi nibii ahe buu shishi kɛji aduawai bibii lɛ je kpo pɛ. jeɔ shishi ejieɔ ehe kpo Enɛ ji akɛ, aduawai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe yɛ mlɛo ni amɛgbalaa kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I keep insects from damaging my vegetables while they are forming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-vegetables lɛ be mli ni amɛfeɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: You can protect tender young vegetables by applying targeted sprays early, keeping the field clear of weeds where insects hide, and checking your farm regularly for early signs of pest activity.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akɛtaoɔ nii amli lɛ ni oookɛshwie nɔ mra lɛ nɔ. Ha jwɛi akafee he ni kooloi baanyɛ ahi amɛhe yɛ lɛ. Ni kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa kɛji ona mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai eba.

english: What is a fungicide and what does it do for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni te amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: A fungicide is a specialized chemical spray used to prevent and cure diseases caused by fungi, such as leaf mildews, blights, and rots, especially during rainy weather.
ga: Fungicides ji tsofai pɔtɛɛ ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ ni akɛtsaa ŋmeii helai tamɔ downy mildew, leaf blight kɛ ŋmeii, titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Will a fungicide kill insects that are eating my crop leaves and pods?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ baagbe ŋmeii ni yeɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: No, a fungicide only treats fungal diseases. If insects are eating your crop, you need to use an insecticide, which is designed specifically to kill pest insects.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ tsaa ŋmeii ahe helai pɛ. Kɛji kooloi yeɔ onibii lɛ Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni afee lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni ekɛgbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii.

english: How do I choose between different sprays for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala spray kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: First inspect your crop carefully: if you see crawling or flying pests eating the plant, buy an insecticide; if you see spots, white powder, or rots on the leaves and stems, buy a fungicide.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, kwɛmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ: kɛji ona kooloi ni shwieɔ shi loo amɛmiifo yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, hemɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi Kɛji ona ŋmeii, powda yɛŋ, loo ŋmeii yɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ Hemɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why is it important to spray my okra pods as soon as they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afɔse okra ŋmeii lɛ ashwie nɔ kɛji amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Spraying early creates a protective shield around the delicate young pods, preventing insect damage before it starts and ensuring your produce grows clean and healthy for harvest.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ mra Ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ bɔleɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibioo lɛ he, ni ehaaa kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ anaa dani ebɔi. ni okɛ nɔmimaa aha akɛ onibii ni obaakpa lɛ he baatse ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kpamɔɔ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a hot dry spell. If you plant too quickly, the seeds will sprout but then dry up and die because there is not enough lasting moisture in the ground.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ latsaa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my crops flowering earlier or later than they used to in past years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi mra loo sɛɛ mli fe bɔ ni amɛwo yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Changes in temperature and unpredictable rainfall affect a crop's internal clock. Extreme heat can make a plant rush to flower early to survive, while a lack of rain can delay flowering altogether.
ga: Tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii amli ŋmɛlɛtswai ahe. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha tsei awo fɔfɔi oya tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhi shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ asɛɛ afo kwraa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without growing any peppers when the weather becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni eduuu pepper ko kwraa be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When the heat is too intense, the plant enters survival mode. It drops its flowers to conserve water and energy rather than trying to feed growing fruits.
ga: Kɛji latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baaya wala shihilɛ mli. Ekɛ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's defense mechanism to save water. By shrinking the leaf area exposed to the sun and wind, the plant prevents moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni atsiɔ lɛ ji tso hebuu gbɛ ni akɛtoɔ nu he. Kɛtsɔ baa lɛ he ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni abaaba shi lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off during extended dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves on purpose to reduce water loss. Dropping leaves helps the stem and underground roots stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Baai ni egbee shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei kɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: How does leaving big trees on my farm help my young cocoa plants survive harsh weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei wuji ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa amli?

english: Shade trees block direct, blazing sunlight and lower the temperature around young cocoa plants. They also slow down soil drying, creating a cooler microclimate that keeps young crops from scorching.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. ni eha hulutsoo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ aba shi Kookoo tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu egbiɔ fioo. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bibioo ni mli ejɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ akashãa.

english: Why does my farm soil dry out much faster now after a short rain than it used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kwraa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ lɛ? Ani fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: Higher temperatures and stronger sunlight bake exposed soil rapidly. Without mulch or ground cover to shade the land, moisture evaporates into the warm air almost as soon as the rain stops.
ga: Hulu ni mli edɔ waa kɛ hulu la ni naa wa baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ kpo lɛ nɔ agbi oya. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa bɛ lɛ, Moisture lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli nɔ ni miihe ashɛ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ pɛ.

english: How does spreading dry weeds or grass around the base of my crops help them stay healthy?
ga: Jwɛi loo jwɛi ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ Te mi tsei lɛ ashishitoo yeɔ ebuaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: This practice, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket over the soil. It shades the ground from direct sun, keeping the soil cool and locking in water so root systems stay hydrated longer.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Efeɔ enii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehiɔ nu mli. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do insect pests seem to attack my vegetable farm much more when there is a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ babaoo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ yɛ lɛ?

english: Drought stress weakens plants, making their natural defenses low. Insects are attracted to these weak plants because they are easier to feed on, and high heat causes insect populations to multiply faster.
ga: Hɔmɔ he haomɔ haa tsei gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa amɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nii lɛ baa shi. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii sumɔɔ tsei ni egbɔjɔ nɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛyeli waaa. Ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa kooloi ayibɔ yaa hiɛ oya.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale green or yellow when the soil stays dry for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need water to swallow nutrients like nitrogen from the dirt. When the soil is completely dry, the roots cannot pick up plant food, causing the leaves to turn pale from hunger.
ga: Tse shishifãi taoɔ nu koni amɛ gbala niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli be mli ni sũ lɛ egbi kwraa. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hɔmɔ hewɔ

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to build strong leaves. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost early in the season will turn the leaves dark green and help the plant produce bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ baa lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Maize takes away nutrients from the soil, but legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground through their roots. Planting them restores the soil naturally so your next crops grow better without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei nɛɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that hide under the leaves and suck the plant's juices, or transmit viruses. Spraying with neem oil or a recommended insecticide kills these insects and protects new leaves.
ga: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects such as aphids or mites that hide on the underside of leaves and suck sap from the plant or spread viruses. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi nɛɛ ni ebaabu baai heei ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers fall off before turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off mainly due to attacks by insects like mirids (capsids), lack of tiny insects that pollinate the flowers, or dry weather stress. Managing shade and controlling pests with insect sprays helps the flowers set into healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ babaoo baa ji kooloi bibii tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ. The lack of small insects pollinating flowers or stress from dry weather Shade management and pest control with insect spray help the flowers set into healthy pods.

english: Why do my tomatoes get dark, soft spots at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, usually because the soil moisture keeps changing between too dry and too wet. Watering your crops regularly and adding agricultural lime or eggshells to the soil prevents this issue.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ nɔ ni edɔ tsɔ teŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo onibii amli daa ni okɛ lime loo ŋshɔŋlooi awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the soil before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe in soggy ground. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over during windstorms when they start carrying fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ ahum be mli beni ejeɔ yibiiwoo shishi kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and tiny worms in the soil called nematodes can damage them, making the tree unstable under the weight of heavy fruits. Propping the trees with sturdy wooden poles and using clean planting suckers keeps them standing.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ akpata amɛhiɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ aduawai ni tsii ni tsii lɛ fiɔ esɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ, ni akɛ tsɔne ni mli tse tsuɔ nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔ shi.

english: Will planting my crops very close together give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani tsei ni mikɛduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo?

english: No, planting too close causes crops to fight over sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin, weak plants with smaller yields. Giving each plant proper space allows it to grow full and produce larger fruits or cobs.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ shi yibiiwoo faaa. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni eda kɛyashɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ, ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do some of my yam setts fail to sprout after I plant them in the mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ gɔŋ ko mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam setts fail to sprout if they are damaged by rot before planting, buried in completely dry soil, or exposed to excessive heat in the mound. Treating setts with wood ash or fungicide before planting and covering mounds with dry grass keeps them cool and healthy.
ga: Sweet potato tsei nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ amɛfite kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni amɛfiteɔ dani aduɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ. Fuu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ. loo dɔlɛ babaoo yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ tso sũ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii tsu he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ he nii dani adu ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How do weeds reduce my crop yield even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Jwɛi baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli po.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early in the crop's life ensures all nutrients go directly to growing your produce.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ tso lɛ wala mli lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and tender roots that easily burn and dry out under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a natural umbrella that shields the cocoa seedlings and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually show that the plant is starving for nutrients, especially nitrogen, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots. Feeding the soil with compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green so the crop can grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens if I plant my cassava stems too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots and leaves compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This stress causes the plants to grow tall and thin while producing very small cassava tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmei shishifãi bibii waa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell before the main rainy season truly begins. If seeds sprout during this dry break, the young seedlings will dry up and die from lack of moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ hulutsoo be ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How does spreading dry leaves and decomposed animal dung help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni mikɛshwãa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Organic matter like dry leaves and manure acts like a sponge in the soil, holding water longer during dry days while gradually releasing nutrients that feed your crops over time.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmeii tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛhiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, fiofio lɛ Ejieɔ niyenii ni haa oŋmɔshi nii lɛ hewalɛ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli.

english: Why do caterpillars eat up the leaves of my vegetable crop so quickly during hot dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yeɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ oya yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Warm weather speeds up the life cycle of insects, causing pest populations to multiply rapidly. Because wild weeds dry up in the heat, pests move onto your green crops to feed on their leaf moisture.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa kooloi ashihilɛ yaa oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ oya. Ejaakɛ koo mli jwɛi lɛ gbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fãa kɛyaa otsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ koni amɛye ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid planting tomatoes in the exact same spot where I harvested pepper last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tomato dumɔ he yɛ he ni mifo ŋmɔtɔ yɛ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Tomatoes and peppers belong to the same plant family and share the same soil diseases and pests. Planting them in the same spot back-to-back allows hidden soil diseases to multiply and attack the new crop.
ga: Tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he kome ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ feɔ babaoo ni amɛtutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii heei.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or poor soil nutrients. The plant drops flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
