ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Too many suckers steal water and nutrients from the main parent plant. Removing extra shoots leaves only the strongest stem, which will produce a much bigger and heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ. Enɛ baaha plantains akuu ko ni da ni tsii kwraa aba.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than the maize crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe ŋmãa ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to steal water and food from the soil under harsh conditions. If you do not clear them early, they will choke your young maize and take away essential nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Kɛji ojieee mli mra lɛ, Amɛbaatsi obi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ naa ni amɛbaajie niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tip downwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ kɛyaa shishi lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tips and moving down the central vein means your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build healthy green leaves and grow tall.
ga: Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naagbee ni eyaa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-abele lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara.

english: Can I plant cowpeas and maize together in the same field?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize helps your soil because cowpeas trap nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil, which helps feed the maize and reduces your need for chemical fertilizers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ejaakɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni aná niyenii aha ŋmãa lɛ, ni ebaaha tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he hiamɔ aba shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my corn roll up tight like tubes during the middle of the hot day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Corn leaves roll up as a defense mechanism to protect themselves from losing water through evaporation when the afternoon heat and sun are at their strongest.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ hewɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without making any fruit when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extremely high temperatures dry out tomato pollen before insects or wind can fertilize the blossoms, causing the plant to shed the unpollinated flowers to save its strength.
ga: He ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ haa tomato mli fɔfɔi lɛ gĩɔ dani kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ afee fɔfɔi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ koni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing pale yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with yellow spots are a main sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadii titri. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ tsɛŋeɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: Plantain trees fall easily when tiny underground worms called nematodes or stem borer insects destroy their roots and corm, leaving the plant without a firm grip in the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe oya. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes loo kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahiɛ lɛ fiteɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun, so fast-growing plantains provide the temporary shade and moisture cocoa seedlings need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ náa be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it better to buy certified seeds instead of keeping seeds from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i ngɔ dumɔwu komɛ kɛ je ye nyagbe ngma kpami ɔ mi.

english: Saved seeds from hybrid maize lose their natural vigor and strength in the second generation, leading to lower yields and weaker defense against local crop diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi, ni jɛmɛ tsei ahe helai ahebuu lɛ baa shi.

english: Yams rot quickly if they get bruised by farm tools during digging or if they are stored in a hot place without proper airflow, which allows rot fungi to enter through skin cuts.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii fite amɛ yɛ be mli ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii tsɔɔ hewolo lɛ mli kɛboteɔ mli.

english: Why do my stored cowpea seeds end up full of small holes after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui stash lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: The small holes are made by seed beetles called weevils, which lay tiny eggs on the pods in the field that later hatch into larvae that eat their way out of the stored seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui amli ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ bu bibii lɛ. ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii Yɛ pod lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Sɛɛ mli lɛ enɛɛmɛi fɔɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ amɛ gbɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa plants are like small children—they easily get scorched and dehydrated under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that create living shade, keeping the young cocoa cool and preserving moisture in the soil until the trees are strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ gbekɛbii. ni hulu lɛ shãa amɛ oya ni nu hu faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Ha kookoo ni mli tse lɛ mli ajɔ. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant usually show that the crop is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil food. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves what little it has to the upper leaves to survive, leaving the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ he miihia tso lɛ. Kɛ nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa amɛbaai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my crops perform poorly when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and gives crop-specific pests and diseases a permanent home. Alternating with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil and starves pests.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi kɛ tsei ahe helai ahi shi daa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii wo mli lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmeii.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and weak with small cobs when I put many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to grow thick stems and full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why didn't my seeds sprout after I buried them deep under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds need warmth, air, and moisture near the soil surface to wake up and grow. If they are planted too deep, the young shoot runs out of energy before it can push through the heavy soil to reach the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ dɔlɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ fɛ̃i ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ koni amɛte shi ni amɛdara. Kɛji akɛ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ ahewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ koni amɛyashɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant is stressed, usually by extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of key plant nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants during peak heat helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tso mli niyenii kpakpai ni bɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni abu tsei ahe yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their green fruits before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho aduawai eŋɔli dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Early fruit drop in peppers is often caused by tiny pests like fruit flies or thrips attacking the fruit, or by irregular watering. Controlling pests early and watering on a regular schedule keeps the fruit attached until harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii loo thrips ni tutuaa aduawai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili ŋmeii ni shishijee lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ Early Pest Control Ni nu ni akɛhaa daa lɛ baaha aduawai lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi kpamɔ be mli.

english: What is making ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dirt inside the stalk?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni eshiɔ muji yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that burrows into the growing center of young maize plants. Detecting them early and applying appropriate control methods saves the plant before the center is destroyed.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmei tsei bibii ni miida lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ ayɔse amɛ mra Ni akɛ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ amɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu tso lɛ he dani akpata eshishigbɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ hiɛ.

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively drink up the water and fertilizer meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow fast and strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛyeɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha otsei lɛ waa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting or getting hard if I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ loo amɛfeɔ ais kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots reach a peak maturity time, after which the plant stops storing food and begins turning its roots woody or waterlogged. Leaving them underground too long also exposes them to rot and soil insects.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji nɔ ni daa be fe fɛɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ kpaɔ niyenii ni ekɛtoɔ lɛ, ni ebɔi shishifãi ni tamɔ tsei loo nu ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsakemɔ. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛgboi ni kooloi bibii aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow and spreading so fast to the rest of my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbɛ amɛshwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves that spread quickly are usually a sign of a fungal disease or insect-borne virus. Removing infected plants early helps stop the disease from traveling to your healthy crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ kooloi amli kɛbaa loo hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ he okadi. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akaya onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Should I cut down a cocoa tree if I notice it is sick, or can I treat it?
ga: Kɛji oyɔse akɛ hela mɔ lɛ Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso lɛ? Aloo abaanyɛ atsa lɛ?

english: If a cocoa tree has a contagious disease like Swollen Shoot Virus, it cannot be cured. Cutting it down and burning it immediately isolates the sickness and stops it from jumping to nearby healthy trees.
ga: Kɛji kookoo tso lɛ yɛ hela ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ, tamɔ bud swollen virus lɛ, anyɛɛɛ atsa lɛ. Kɛ́ ofo lɛ ni oshã amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ ajie ehe kɛjɛ he kroko, ni ebaaha ekajo foi kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: If my neighbor's crop gets a disease, can it easily infect my farm next door?
ga: Kɛji akutsoŋnyo ko tso lɛ ná hela lɛ Ani ebaagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ mli mlɛo?

english: Yes, crop diseases travel easily between neighboring farms through wind, water runoff, shared tools, or insects. Clearing a boundary buffer zone and cleaning your tools helps protect your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai yaa ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ateŋ mlɛo kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nu ni hoɔ, nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo kooloi bibii anɔ. Buffer zones kɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ muji lɛ baaye abua ni abu onibii ahe.

english: Why does heavy rain cause my pepper plants to rot at the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain splashes soil onto leaves, carrying soil-borne fungi directly onto the plant. Waterlogged soil around roots also starves them of air, causing rot to set in fast.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa sũ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ. ni okɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ awo tsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu damɔ ehe lɛ Shishifãi lɛ hu kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa. ha efite oya

english: Why do my crops seem to get sick more often when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hela shii abɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Tight spacing traps air and moisture around plants. This warm, humid environment allows diseases to grow easily and spread rapidly from leaf to leaf.
ga: He ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ he lɛ. Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ haa hela daa oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ baa kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ.

english: Why do weeds in my farm make my crops more likely to catch diseases?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miihe helai babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds act as hideouts and breeding grounds for pests that carry crop diseases. Keeping your field clear removes these pests' shelters so they cannot spread sickness to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɛ tsei ahelai baa lɛ teeɔ amɛhe kɛ amɛfɔɔ yɛ. Kɛ́ oha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaajie nɛkɛ kooloi awuiyelɔi ashihilɛhei nɛɛ kɛya. Enɛ ji koni hela akagbɛ ashwã onibii amli.

english: Can I cut stems from a sick cassava plant to grow new ones for the next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafolɔ ŋmei tso ni hela mɔ lɛ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: No, planting stems or seeds from diseased crops passes the sickness directly to the new generation. Always use clean, disease-free planting materials for a healthy yield.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ashishifãi loo dumɔwui ni miida lɛ baaha hela lɛ aya yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ dumɔ nii ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli lɛ atsu nii be fɛɛ be koni ená yibii kpakpai.

english: How can I tell if my crops are sick from a disease or just need fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela miimɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ loo ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛkɛ?

english: Nutrient shortages usually cause whole fields or older leaves to yellow evenly. Diseases usually start as spots, wilting, or patches on individual plants before moving to others.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ haa ŋmɔji muu fɛɛ loo baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ jeɔ shishi akɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ. yɛ tsei aŋkroaŋkroi anɔ dani egbɛ eshwa tsei krokomɛi anɔ.

english: Why do caterpillars attack my crops more during the dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: In dry weather, pests search aggressively for green crops for moisture. Fewer natural predators exist in the dry heat, allowing pests to multiply and spread sickness quickly.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli lɛ, ŋmeii taoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛna ŋmɔtɔ. Adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ faaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Enɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayiɔ babaoo ni amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa oya.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt in the afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Strong afternoon heat causes leaves to lose water faster than roots can draw it up. If they bounce back by evening, it is heat stress; if they stay wilted, it could be bacterial wilt or root disease.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa baai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. Kɛ́ oku osɛɛ oba gbɛkɛ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ miigba onaa. Kɛji egbo lolo lɛ Ebaanyɛ efee bacteria wilt loo shishifã hela.

english: Why is it important for me to plant my plantains in neat, straight rows instead of scattering them around the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-plantains lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo ni ja lɛ mli? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ

english: Planting in straight, well-spaced rows ensures that each plantain gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with its neighbors. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier for you.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja, ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa plantain fɛɛ plantain naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo.

english: Can plantains yield well in areas like Krachi East, or do they only grow in heavy forest zones?
ga: Ani plantains baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai yɛ hei tamɔ Krachi Bokagbɛ loo amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ kooi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli pɛ?

english: Plantains can grow well in transition areas like Krachi East if the soil is deep and rich. However, because these areas experience dry seasons, you need to use heavy mulch around the stems to trap moisture in the soil.
ga: Plantains baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsakemɔ hei tamɔ Eastern Krabi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi, akɛni hei nɛɛ naa hulutsoo be hewɔ lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ ehe baahia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo atsu nii ni ebɔle he. tso lɛ mli koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Do my plantain plants need full sunlight to grow well, or should I plant them under big trees?
ga: Mi dumɔwui lɛ he miihia hulu ni fa bɔni afee ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Aloo esa akɛ madu yɛ tso agbo ko shishi?

english: Plantains need plenty of direct sunlight to make their food and produce large bunches. Heavy shade from big trees will slow down their growth and cause them to produce very small fruits.
ga: Plantains he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ ehoo ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba. Shade ni mli tse ni jɛɔ tsei wuji amli lɛ haa amɛdaraa oya, ni no haa tsei ni woɔ yibii bibii waa baa.

english: Why do small shoots keep growing around the base of my main plantain stem, and should I cut them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ɔ ebɔleɔ Mi plantain shishitoo titri lɛ he Ni ani esa akɛ mafo lɛ?

english: Those shoots are called suckers. If you leave too many, they will steal food and water from the main plant. You should cut off the weak ones and leave only one or two strong suckers to grow after the main plant is harvested.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ akɛ suckers. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ agbo tsɔ lɛ, amɛbaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni oha tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃ beni akpa tso titri lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does a plantain stem die after I harvest the bunch, and will that same stem ever bear fruit again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ gboiɔ beni mikpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Ni ani nakai tso lɛ nɔŋŋ baawo yibii ekoŋŋ?

english: A plantain stem is designed to produce fruit only once in its lifetime. After harvest, that stem naturally dies, but the root system lives on to feed the sucker growing beside it, which will produce the next bunch.
ga: Afee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. kpamɔ sɛɛ Tso lɛ baagbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi shishifãi lɛ baahi shi koni amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii. ni baaha kuu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches at the top, making them top-heavy. You can prevent them from falling by supporting the stems with bamboo poles or wooden crutches once the bunch starts forming.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ panicle ni mli wa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. make it top heavy Obaanyɛ otsĩ enaa koni ekagbee shi kɛtsɔ ŋmei tsei loo tsei ni akɛfiɔ esɛɛ kɛji ŋmei lɛ bɔi feemɔ pɛ.

english: Why did my plantain plant take so long to produce fruit while my neighbor's flowered very early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ nɔ lɛ fɔɔ oya waa lɛ?

english: How fast a plantain fruits depends on soil richness, regular water supply, and the health of the sucker you planted. Plants in poor soil or dry conditions take much longer to produce flowers.
ga: Bɔ ni plantain lɛ daa oya lɛ damɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni fa babaoo ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ tsei bibii ni oduɔ lɛ ahewalɛ Tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi nɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: How can I tell that my green plantains are ready to be harvested before they start ripening on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantains eŋɔli lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa dani amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Plantains are ready for harvest when the individual fruits become full and round, and the sharp edges on the skin start to smooth out, even while the skin is still completely green.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko eyi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewolo lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji akɛ hewolo lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo po.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain plant turning yellow and drying up before the bunch is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani tso lɛ shishigbɛ tso lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Lower leaves turn yellow naturally as the plant gets older and sends its nutrients to the growing bunch. However, if many leaves turn yellow quickly, it could mean the soil lacks nutrients or the roots are suffering from drought.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni tso lɛ daa ni ekɛ niyenii haa tso kuu ni miida lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai babaoo batsɔ ŋmɔŋ oya lɛ, Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ miipiŋ yɛ hɔmɔ hewɔ.

english: What type of soil is best for my plantains if I want them to give me very big bunches?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mi plantains lɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni amɛfee panicles wuji waa?

english: Plantains thrive best in loose, dark soil rich in decayed plant matter (humus) that drains water easily. They do not do well in rocky ground or heavy clay soils that stay waterlogged.
ga: Plantains kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ, ni tsei ni egbo (humus) ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tɛi loo sũ ni tsii ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland is fertile enough for planting cocoa before I start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu kookoo dani mije shishi?

english: Fertile land usually has dark, soft soil with lots of natural forest or weed growth and stays moist. Checking for lush natural vegetation helps confirm if the soil has enough natural nutrients to support young cocoa trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hei ni baa nii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. Adebɔɔ mli koo loo jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. and remains moisturized Adebɔɔ mli tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ amlipɛimɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni amaa nɔ mi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua cacao tsei bibii lɛ.

english: If my farmland has grown into a thick bush, does that mean the soil is very rich?
ga: Kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ da ni etsɔ jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ, ani no tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii waa?

english: Yes, dense forest or overgrown bush usually means the soil is full of nutrients and decomposed plant material, which makes it very fertile and ideal for growing crops like cocoa.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, bei pii lɛ, koo ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ brɔshi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eyi kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛ tsei ni fiteɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii waa, ni ehi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo dumɔ.

english: Why do some of my young cocoa plants die right after planting while others survive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ekomɛi gboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu amɛ yɛ be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi lɛ hi wala mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants die mainly from severe heat, poor soil moisture, or root damage during transplanting. Seedlings survive best when planted during early rains with adequate shade to protect them from direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii babaoo gboiɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii loo shishifãi ni efite yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ Dumɔwui hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ mli. Kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baabu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: What steps can I take to make sure my newly planted cocoa trees do not die in their first year?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mi-cocoa tso ni midu ehee lɛ akagbo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli?

english: To protect young cocoa trees, plant temporary shade crops like plantains around them, plant early in the rainy season so their roots go deep, and keep weeds cleared so they do not steal water and nutrients.
ga: Bɔni afee ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe Dumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, yɛ he ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ shishijee mli koni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. ni ojie jwɛi lɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: What causes my crop leaves to turn dark green and grow very fast?
ga: Mɛni miiha mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya nɛkɛ?

english: Fast growth and deep green leaves mean your crops are absorbing plenty of nitrogen and water from fertile soil, showing that the plants are healthy and thriving.
ga: Nɔ ni yaa hiɛ oya kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ onibii lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen kɛ nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni eshwereɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow very well on one part of my farm but look weak on another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome shi etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ fã kroko lɛ?

english: Soil quality can change across the same piece of land due to differences in topsoil depth, water drainage, or past farming. Weak areas may need organic manure or fertilizer to catch up.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su baanyɛ afee srɔtoi yɛ he kome lɛ fɛɛ. Nɔ ni ha ebalɛ nakai ji srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, nu ni hoɔ, loo okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni eho lɛ amli. Hei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ baanyɛ abi humus loo humus ni akɛjie ŋmeii.

english: Can I plant cocoa directly on land that was recently cleared from forest?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajie kɛjɛ koo lɛ mli etsɛko lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, newly cleared forest land is rich in topsoil organic matter, which provides cocoa with high natural fertility. However, you must ensure you leave or plant shade trees to protect the young crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooi amli hei ni ajie ehee lɛ amli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo adebɔɔ mli babaoo lɛ yaa hiɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, ehe miihia ni okwɛ jogbaŋŋ ni oshi loo odu tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa koni obu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Will keeping shade trees on my farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Ani tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni madu lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, shade trees protect delicate crops like young cocoa from harsh sunlight, drop leaves that turn into natural compost, and help keep moisture in the soil during dry weather.
ga: Hɛɛ, shade tsei buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni waaa tamɔ kookoo tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. Baai ni egbee shi lɛ bafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: How does early rain help my young seedlings establish themselves safely?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni mi dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe?

english: Early rain provides constant moisture that allows tender seedling roots to spread into the soil and absorb nutrients easily, preventing the plants from drying out and dying.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra be mli lɛ haa fɛ̃i daa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: How do I know if my land needs organic manure to help crops flourish?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛshwere?

english: If your soil is light in color, hard, dries out quickly, or produces slow-growing crops with yellowish leaves, adding animal manure or decomposed plant material will improve fertility.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egbiɔ oya, loo oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa blɛoo ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kooloo ŋmei loo tsei amli nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa fɔmɔ yaa hiɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the leaf tip in a V-shape usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to keep leaves green and help the plant grow strong.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ baa lɛ naa ni feɔ V su lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Amɛji tsei aniyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops every year even though I clear and burn it clean before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ baa daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mifoɔ mli ni mishãa dani miduɔ nii moŋ?

english: Burning destroys the natural layer of dead leaves and organic food in the dirt, along with beneficial soil insects. Over time, burning starves the soil, making it hard and weak unless you add organic manure or compost.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli fã ni ji baai ni egboi kɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ fata he. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Shãa baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Ha efee nɔ ni wa ni egbɔjɔ. Ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he.

english: How do I know if fall armyworms are eating my maize crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ fall armyworms miiye mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: You will notice ragged holes eaten out of the leaves right at the top center (the funnel) of the maize plant, along with dark, sawdust-like droppings left behind inside the leaves.
ga: Obaana bu ko ni etse ni aye kɛjɛ baa lɛ mli yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ ŋwɛi teŋgbɛ (cone) lɛ mli. Kɛfata ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni ashiɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ he.

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Virus, a disease carried from plant to plant by tiny white insects called whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwiemɔ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: This is Black Pod Disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, wet weather and wet shade. Pruning extra tree branches helps sunlight and air dry out the pods so the fungus cannot spread.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́ kɛ hɔɔ ni mli ewo fɔ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji krokomɛi ni oookpa lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi. Fuji lɛ gbɛɛɛ eshwaaa.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when the air gets too hot during the daytime or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly soaked, which stresses the plant.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ trukaa lɛ nɔ. ni kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ lɛ

english: Why do my pepper plants look wilted in the hot afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense heat, pepper leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it up. As long as the soil has moisture, the plants usually recover and stand up straight again by evening.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ he jɔɔ lɛ ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ.

english: What makes my yam tubers grow small and crooked instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Yam tubers grow twisted or stunted when the soil is too hard and compact for the tuber to push through, or when small worms in the soil (nematodes) attack the soft tip of the growing yam.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli (nematodes) lɛ tutua ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground if I leave them in the soil too long during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rain fills the soil with water, air cannot reach the roots. Without oxygen, the cassava roots suffocate and rot in the soggy soil.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu yiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Koni maye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in corn fields. They hide in the center growing tip of the plant and eat the tender leaves; treating them early stops them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ tso lɛ naatsei lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii. Amɛ ni oookwɛ amɛ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: Does it matter if I plant my cassava stems straight up or at a slant?
ga: Ani ekɔɔɔ he eko akɛ madu mi-cassava lɛ shi shiŋŋ loo mikɛ shi shiŋŋ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slant (about 45 degrees) helps the plant grow deeper root systems and produce larger cassava tubers compared to planting them straight up.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ (aaafee digrii 45) lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ daa. ni eha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ afee wuji yɛ dalɛ mli kɛ akɛto amɛhe ni aduɔ shi jaŋŋ lɛ he.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crop seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crop seeds are planted too closely, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants and a smaller harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa bibioo baa.

english: Staking holds yam leaves up high so they catch maximum sunlight and stay off the hot ground. More sunlight helps the vine make more food to grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Okɛ sweet potato baai lɛ awo ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ ohe babaoo ni okɛ ohe akabɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Hulu la babaoo yeɔ ebuaa wain tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii babaoo koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize plants turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tseee lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen nutrients in the soil or is sitting in too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure restores their green color and health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo eyɛ nu babaoo mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ená hewalɛ kpakpa.

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil. Legumes like groundnuts put natural nitrogen back into the dirt, naturally fertilizing the soil for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, stops soil water from evaporating under the hot sun, keeps roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaatsi nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ la yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds right after the very first small rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a heatwave or dry spell. If you plant immediately, seeds will sprout and then dry up and die before the main rainy season fully sets in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, latsaa loo nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat, dry soil, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and allowing insects into the field helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo pollination ni ehiii ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ ni aha kooloi bibii bote ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do I have to uproot my whole cocoa tree if only a few leaves are showing sickness?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ajie cacao tso muu lɛ fɛɛ be mli ni baai fioo pɛ jieɔ hela he okadi kpo lɛ?

english: Certain tree diseases, like Swollen Shoot, spread through the sap and root system long before you see symptoms on the whole tree. Uprooting sick trees completely stops the sickness from traveling underground and killing healthy trees nearby.
ga: Tso helai komɛi, tamɔ akɔɔble ni efuu lɛ, gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ mli nu kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli dani onaa okadii yɛ tso lɛ mli fɛɛ. Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haaa hela lɛ aya shikpɔŋ shishi ni egbe tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ kwraa.

english: If I uproot a diseased crop today, can I plant new seeds in that exact same spot right away?
ga: Kɛji mijie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ŋmɛnɛ Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui heei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, because disease germs and fungi can remain alive in the soil for weeks. You need to let the soil rest under sunlight or treat it so the newly planted crops do not catch the same disease immediately.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ muawai kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ hela baa lɛ baanyɛ ahi sũ lɛ mli otsii babaoo. Esa akɛ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo otsa nɔ koni tsei ni adu ehee lɛ akamɔ hela kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How does removing sick plants from my farm help protect my neighbor's crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mikutsoŋbii lɛ anibii ahe?

english: Crop diseases and pests easily travel from one farm to another through wind, water, or jumping insects. Destroying infected plants early removes the source of the sickness before it can spread across farm boundaries.
ga: Tsei ahe helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fãa gbɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli oya kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nu loo kooloi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ anɔ. Tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ akpãtãmɔ mra Enɛ baajie hela jɛɛhe lɛ kɛya dani egbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ fɛɛ amli.

english: How long do I need to wait after spraying strong farm medicine before it is safe to harvest my food?
ga: Beni mɔ ko kɛ tsofa ni mli wa ewo ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ emɛ dani enyɛ ekpa niyenii shweshweeshwe?

english: Every farm chemical has a required waiting period, usually between 7 to 14 days, which allows the strong medicine to break down naturally so the harvested food is safe for human consumption.
ga: Tsofai fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ be ni ato ni akɛmɛɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ gbii 7 kɛyashi 14, ni no haa tsofa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, niyenii ni akpaa lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha adesa niyenii.

english: Can the strong spray medicine I use on weeds hurt my food crops if the wind blows it onto them?
ga: Ani tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ jwɛi anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye miniyenii tsei lɛ awui kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswa amɛ?

english: Yes, chemical drift from strong weedkillers can land on healthy crop leaves, causing severe chemical burns, stunted growth, or even killing the plant entirely.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni he wa lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ. Ekɛ tsofa shãa ni naa wa baa. shweremɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo egbeɔ tso lɛ kwraa po.

english: If I mix my pest medicine extra strong, will it clear the pests faster without damaging my crop?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ pɔtɛɛ ko futu mli hu? Ani ebaajie tsɛŋemɔ helai oya ni efiteee miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: No, making chemical mixtures too concentrated can scorch plant leaves and damage root systems. Always follow the correct mixing water ratio so you kill pests without harming your crop.
ga: Dabi, tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ baai lɛ ni efite shishifãi lɛ. Nyiɛmɔ nu ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ mlijaa ni ja lɛ sɛɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ ji koni onyɛ ogbe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ni okɛyeee oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: What is the best time of day to apply chemical spray to my crops so the leaves do not burn?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ atsu nii koni baai lɛ akashã?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is best because intense midday sunshine heats up the chemical droplets on wet leaves, which can scorch and damage your crop.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli Enɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa tsofai ni shwieɔ tsei ni efɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shãa ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Will strong chemical sprays stay in the soil forever and ruin my future planting seasons?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya naanɔ ni efite miwɔsɛɛ be ni mikɛbaakwɛ nii lɛ?

english: Most modern farm chemicals break down in the soil after a few weeks or months through sunlight and soil microbes, as long as you do not severely overuse them.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ otsii loo nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ anɔ. Shii abɔ ni okɛtsuuu nii fe nine waa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over and collapse in the farm before they are fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛshɛɔ shweremɔ he lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over when their root systems are weak, shallow, or eaten by underground insects like rootworms and stem borers. Proper planting depth and pest control keep roots anchored.
ga: Abɛi baashwie shi kɛji shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, amɛmli ekɔɔɔ, loo shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi kɛ shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ yeɔ lɛ. Dumɔ mlibotemɔ ni sa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants rotting from the bottom roots upward and dying off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ miifite kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi ni egbo oya lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water or carries fungal pathogens. This root destruction prevents the plant from drinking water and nutrients, causing the top parts to wither and die.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo loo eyɛ ŋmeii ni gbeɔ helai. Nɛkɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ nɛɛ haaa tso lɛ anu nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Ehaa ŋwɛi fã lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow at the bottom while the crop is still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of young maize plants mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow tall. Applying fertilizer or compost supplies this missing food so the leaves turn green again and produce better yields.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha yibii kpakpai aba.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry weather to conserve water inside its stem and roots. By losing its leaves, the plant reduces water loss through evaporation and stays alive underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni egbiɔ koni nu ahi tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Baai ni laajeɔ lɛ haa nu ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ, ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant before turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil lacks steady moisture. Heat stress prevents proper pollination, causing the plant to shed the unpollinated flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ be fɛɛ be. Dɔlɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Ha tsei afɔ fɔfɔi ni pollination bɛ mli koni akɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why does cutting off weak branches from my cocoa trees help them produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ aniji bibii ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Removing excess or dead branches lets sunlight and air reach the center of the tree. It prevents diseases and ensures the tree uses its water and soil nutrients to grow heavy cocoa pods instead of wasteful leaves.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni egboi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ helai anaa ni ekwɛɔ koni tsei lɛ kɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni tsii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ baai ni afite lɛ baatsu nii

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb instead of spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce bigger underground tubers when their leaves are lifted off the ground into sunlight. Staking gets the leaves light to make plant food and keeps them away from damp ground diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji kɛ́ awó amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni hulu la aba amɛnɔ. Staking baaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná la ni ekɛye nii ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small twisted shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe bibii ni etsake lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from under the young leaves. Controlling these insects early protects the leaves so the plant can grow proper fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ anyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Groundnut plants pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the groundnuts are harvested, this natural nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanut tsei gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛye ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my watermelons rot on the bottom side that touches the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miifite yɛ he ni shishi lɛ taa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Watermelons rot when they rest directly on wet soil because damp ground attracts fungi and soil pests. Placing dry straw or wood underneath the fruit keeps it dry and prevents the bottom from rotting.
ga: Watermelon baagbo kɛji akɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ baagbala ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo tsei ni egbi wo aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ agbi ni ebaaha shishi lɛ akafite.

english: Why should I remove extra young shoot suckers from the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi-plantains lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Too many shoot suckers fight with the main plantain tree for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main tree gets full nourishment to produce a large bunch.
ga: Tsobii babaoo tsɔ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ tso lɛ ŋmei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni efee ŋmei agbo.

english: Why can swamp rice grow in standing water while maize plants die if water collects on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔŋ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei gboiɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air tubes in their stems that carry oxygen from the air down to their roots underwater. Maize roots do not have these tubes, so standing water drowns them by cutting off their oxygen.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ nɛkɛ tsɔnei nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: What is an irrigation system, and why shouldn't I just rely on rainfall for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji nu shwiemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo? Ni mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔshiimɔ nɔ kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: An irrigation system is a way of supplying water to your farm using pipes, pumps, or canals instead of waiting for rain. It ensures your crops get a steady supply of water throughout the year, protecting them from drying out during long dry spells.
ga: Nu shwiemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ paipii, pɔmpii loo faai haa oŋmɔ lɛ mli nu, moŋ fe ni ooomɛ nugbɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nu ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkagbi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How do I know if my crops are suffering from lack of water or getting too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu efo miŋmɔshi nibii amli loo nu efo fe nine?

english: When crops do not get enough water, their leaves roll up, turn brown, and wilt. When they get too much water, the soil stays soggy, roots begin to rot, and leaves turn pale yellow.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ naaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe, amɛfeɔ asarasu, ni amɛgbiɔ. Kɛ́ amɛná nu babaoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ, ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do modern watering methods like drip irrigation work better for crops than watering by hand with buckets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nu shwiemɔ gbɛi tamɔ drip irrigation No hewɔ lɛ etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ fe nine ni akɛ baagi shwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ?

english: Drip irrigation delivers small drops of water directly to the plant roots where it is needed most. This prevents water waste, keeps the soil moist for longer, and stops water from washing away good soil nutrients.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa nu bibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Akɛ shishifãi adu yɛ he ni ehe hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ Enɛ baaye abua ni nu akafite. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ nu naa koni ekajie niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why are insects chewing holes in my crop leaves, and how does this affect my yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye bu yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli lɛ? Ni te enɛ saa bɔ ni mitsuɔ nii ehaa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Insects like caterpillars and beetles eat leaves to survive. Since leaves are what crops use to capture sunlight and make food to grow fruit or seeds, leaf damage slows down growth and reduces your harvest.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ baai koni amɛhi shi. Ejaakɛ baai ji nɔ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii ni amɛmɔɔ hulu la ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni amɛkɛduɔ aduawai loo dumɔwui. Baai ni fiteɔ lɛ baaha edalɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha okpamɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do insect pests attack my farm more during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry weather, crops become stressed from heat and lack of water, making them weak. Hungry pests target these weak plants because they are easier to feed on and contain the moisture insects need.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ Hɔmɔ ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ shwieɔ tsei ni egbɔjɔ nɛɛ anɔ ejaakɛ amɛyeli waaa ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kooloi lɛ.

english: How can I protect my young crops from pests before the insects destroy everything?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe dani amɛfite nɔ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: You can protect young crops by checking leaves regularly for eggs or tiny bugs, removing damaged leaves, keeping weeds away, and applying recommended organic or chemical pest controls early.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu tsei bibii ahe kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni oookwɛ daa kɛji ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii yɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ baai ni efite lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ, ni okɛ organic loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ atsu nii mra.

english: Why do black or yellow spots appear on my plant leaves, and what does it mean?
ga: Why are black or yellow spots appearing on my plant's leaves? Ni mɛni etsɔɔ?

english: Spots on leaves are usually signs of fungal or bacterial crop diseases. These micro-organisms attack the leaf tissue, stopping the plant from feeding itself and eventually causing the leaf to rot or drop off.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, muji ni yɔɔ baai anɔ lɛ ji tso hela ni fungi loo muawai kɛbaa lɛ he okadi. Nɛkɛ nibii bibii nɛɛ tutuaa baa lɛ mli fãji. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛna niyenii. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Can a crop disease move from one sick plant to all the healthy plants on my farm?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ ajɛ tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ mli kɛya tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, crop diseases spread easily through wind, splashing rain, contaminated farm tools, or insects moving from plant to plant. Sick plants should be treated or removed quickly to protect the rest of the crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ okwaayeli nibii ni mli ewo muji lɛ anɔ. loo kooloi ni fãa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ Esa akɛ atsa tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ loo ajie amɛ oya koni akɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why is protecting my crops from pests and diseases early so important for a good harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahe mra lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia kɛha kpamɔ kpakpa.

english: Early protection keeps plants healthy from the start so they can grow strong roots and thick stems. Strong plants put all their energy into making large fruits, grains, or tubers instead of struggling to survive.
ga: Hebuu kɛjɛ shishijee Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhe wa kɛjɛɔ shishijee No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akwɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa. Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo aduawai wuji, ŋmaa, loo ŋmeii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ohi shi lɛ

english: How does clearing weeds around my crops help keep pests and diseases away?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ ni mijieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai anaa?

english: Weeds act as homes and hiding places for harmful insects and crop diseases. Clearing weeds deprives pests of shelter and stops them from easily moving onto your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ shia kɛ he ni kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai yɔɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ akafee nɔ ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛya oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ anɔ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping off one by one until the tree dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi komekomei kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ gboɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often mean your tree is suffering from swollen shoot disease or severe nutrient deficiency. When the tree's roots or vascular system get damaged, it cannot draw water and food from the soil, causing it to drop leaves to survive before eventually dying if untreated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ ahewɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa lɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ shishifãi loo lá fãji lɛ fite lɛ Enyɛŋ ejie nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛhi shi dani yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛgboi kɛji atsaaa amɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough light and food to build strong stems and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Tall shade trees act like umbrellas that protect young cocoa from extreme sun heat and help keep moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its strength and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your crops grow slowly, look pale green or yellowish instead of dark green, or yield far less harvest than in previous years despite good rainfall, your soil has run out of nutrients and needs manure or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji onibii lɛ daraa blɛoo Etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. loo ewoɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe afi ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become hard and woody instead of soft when I boil them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfee tamɔ tso moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee blɛoo kɛ́ ahoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become woody if they are left in the ground too long past their maturity time, or if the plant suffers through a long dry season, causing the starch in the roots to turn into tough fiber.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. aloo kɛji tso lɛ na amanehulu yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do small worms appear inside the funnel of my young corn plants right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eje shishi lɛ?

english: These worms are Fall Armyworms. The adult moths lay eggs on new green corn leaves right after the rains start, and the hatched caterpillars hide inside the plant funnel to feed on the tender young leaves.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Asraafoi ŋmeii. Kpɔŋɔi ni eda lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baa heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why are my older cocoa trees producing much fewer pods now than they did ten years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei ni edara lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo kwraa fe afii nyɔŋma ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow older, usually past 20 to 25 years, their root systems slow down and cannot absorb food as efficiently, making them naturally produce fewer pods and become more vulnerable to diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ da Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ eye fe afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ tamɔ bɔ ni amɛfeɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo yɛ amɛfɔmɔ su mli, ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe oya.

english: Why is it bad for my crop yield if I burn all the cleared weeds on my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii kɛji mishã jwɛi ni ajie yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ dani midu lɛ?

english: Burning clears the field quickly, but the intense heat kills beneficial soil organisms and destroys organic matter. Allowing cleared weeds to decay naturally adds rich compost back into the soil to feed your crops.
ga: La ni ashãa lɛ haa jɛmɛ tseɔ oya. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa gbeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, ni efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ oha jwɛi ni he tse lɛ fite yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ koni ekɛha onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my fruit trees when I want more fruit to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi yibii tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ? Be ni miisumɔ ni aduawai babaoo akwɛ̃?

english: Cutting away unnecessary or dead branches prevents the tree from wasting energy on leaves that don't produce fruit. This directs the tree's energy into growing bigger, healthier fruits and lets air and sunlight reach the whole plant.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa loo ni egboi ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ tsei ni wooo yibii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ekwɛ̃ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ he

english: Why do seeds saved from my hybrid maize harvest produce weaker plants than the original seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred in a laboratory to give maximum yield in their first generation. The seeds saved from that harvest lose those special traits, resulting in uneven growth and smaller yields if replanted.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ yɛ laboratori ko mli krɛdɛɛ koni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni fa fe fɛɛ aba yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ yibiiwoo fioo baa kɛji akɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: How often should I spray liquid fertilizer on my maize crops to make them grow bigger?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ afɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ koni efee agbo?

english: Liquid fertilizers give plants a quick nutrient boost, but spraying too often can burn the leaves. Applying it once every two to three weeks during the early growth stage is usually enough for healthy maize.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Shi kɛ́ afɔse tsofa lɛ shii abɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ashã. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛwo mli daa otsii 2-3 yɛ shishijee dalɛ mli lɛ, no fa kɛha ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Will rain wash away the medicine I spray on my crops if it rains right after I apply it?
ga: Ani nugbɔ baaho tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ beni mikɛwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, heavy rain shortly after spraying can wash liquid chemicals off the leaves before the plant absorbs them. It is best to spray on dry leaves when rain is not expected for at least a few hours.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be mli ni ashwie tsofa lɛ nɔ etsɛɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ afɔ tsofai ni ji nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ahe dani tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ baai ni egbi lɛ anɔ beni akpaaa gbɛ akɛ nugbɔ baanɛ kɛ hoo lɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi.

english: Do I need to feed my soil with manure every month, or can I wait longer between applications?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he daa nyɔŋ nɔ? Aloo ani manyɛ mamɛ be babaoo yɛ fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ teŋ?

english: You do not need to apply manure every month because organic manure breaks down slowly over time. Adding well-rotted manure once at planting and again midway through the season provides a steady supply of food for your crops.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he daa nyɔŋ nɔ. Ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baafite fiofio. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he shikome yɛ dumɔ be mli kɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves often turn yellow and drop off during dry periods as a natural way for the plant to save water and stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: What happens to my tomato plants if I plant the seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close forces crops to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and small fruit. It also reduces airflow, which makes it easier for plant diseases to spread.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ aduawai bibii baa. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ hu baa shi. Enɛ haa tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Is it better to water my pepper plants with a lot of water once a week or a little bit every day?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ oookɛ nu babaoo awo ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ nɔ? Shikome yɛ otsi mli loo fioo daa gbi

english: Soaking the soil deeply once or twice a week is better because it encourages the pepper plant to grow long, strong roots that search deep into the soil for moisture.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo mli shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ eyeɔ ebuaa pepper tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ shishifãi kakadaji ni mli wa ni taoɔ nu ni mli kwɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do armyworms keep damaging my maize farm even after I have sprayed the crops with chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miifite mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ moŋ?

english: Armyworms hide inside the tightly rolled central leaves of young maize during the hot sun. Spraying early in the morning or late in the evening helps ensure the spray directly touches the worms when they come out to feed.
ga: Asraafoi akuu mli ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni abɔle amɛhe waa lɛ amli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ehaa tsofa lɛ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ kpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ amɛje kpo amɛmiitao niyenii.

english: Trimming extra branches allows sunlight and air to reach the inner trunk. This prevents humidity from building up, which stops fungal diseases like black pod from growing and helps the tree produce larger cocoa pods.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ mligbɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ akabɔle ehe. Enɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods lɛ aya hiɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How soon after planting my maize should I clear the weeds from my field?
ga: Beni adu ŋmãa sɛɛ Te esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya ha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds should be cleared within the first three to four weeks after planting. Young crop roots need all the soil nutrients and space they can get during this early stage to build a strong base.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ he miihia niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ he ni yɔɔ lɛ shishijee mli koni amɛma shishitoo ni wa.

english: How can I tell when my yam tubers are fully mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Yams indicate maturity when the above-ground vines and leaves turn yellow and dry out, showing that the plant has finished storing energy underground in the tuber.
ga: Atomɔ tsɔɔ akɛ edara kɛji wain tso lɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why is it important for an extension officer to inspect my land before I plant new crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni extension officer lɛ akwɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani edu tsei heei lɛ?

english: Inspecting your land helps identify soil conditions and existing plant health, ensuring you choose crops that will naturally thrive in that specific environment without wasting money on seeds.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ona shikpɔŋ lɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ momo kɛ tsei lɛ ahewalɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohalaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ nakai shihilɛ pɔtɛɛ lɛ mli ni ofiteee shika yɛ dumɔwui ahe.

english: Why should I examine the weeds and old plants growing on my farmland before clearing it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ jwɛi kɛ jwɛi momo ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ midumɔi lɛ amli dani majie mli lɛ?

english: Existing plants act as clues that reveal nutrient levels in the soil, as well as hidden diseases or pests that could attack your new crops if not managed first.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ momo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nibii ni tsɔɔ bɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fa ha. Nakai nɔŋŋ eji yɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo kooloi ni baanyɛ atutua onibii heei lɛ kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ hu he.

english: How can I check if there are harmful pests living in my field before putting seeds in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu dumɔwui?

english: Looking closely at crop leaves, digging up soil samples for worms, and checking old roots helps you spot soil pests early so you can treat the land before planting.
ga: Tso baai lɛ akwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni oootsu koni otao ŋmeii Ni shishifãi momoi amlipɛimɔ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii mra. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ otsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii dani odu nii.

english: How does water standing in pools on my farm after heavy rain affect my crops?
ga: Te nu ni yɔɔ nubu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Water pooling around roots suffocates crops and causes root rot. Observing where water settles helps you plant water-tolerant crops or build drainage channels.
ga: Nu ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ he ni nu lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni odu tsei ni nyɛɔ nu mli loo ofee gbɛi ni nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ.

english: Why do I need to track when the rains start and stop in my community each season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ be ni nugbɔ jeɔ shishi kɛ be ni ekpaa yɛ mi akutso lɛ mli yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting in sync with the arrival of regular rainfall ensures your seeds get enough moisture to build deep, strong roots before dry spells set in.
ga: Dumɔ ni kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ kpãa gbee lɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ naa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Can very intense rain damage my crops even if plants need water to grow?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nu he miihia amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ moŋ?

english: Heavy downpours can erode rich topsoil, wash away fertilizer, and break young shoots, so understanding rain intensity helps you build soil ridges to protect crops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afite shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. ni ebaanyɛ efo ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ onu bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ha lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ofee shikpɔŋ ŋmeii ni baabu onibii ahe.

english: How does intense afternoon sun and hot weather affect the behavior of my crops?
ga: Te shwane hulu ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ajeŋba he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Extreme heat forces plants to lose water quickly, leading to wilting and stunted growth, which tells you when your crops need shade trees or mulching.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Etsɔɔ bo be ni ehe baahia ni otsei lɛ aná hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ.

english: Why does the way rainwater flows across my sloping land matter for my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mi ŋshɔkpɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Fast-flowing water sweeps away topsoil and young seedlings down slopes. Knowing water flow paths helps you plant crops along contours to prevent soil loss.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ tsei bibii kɛyaa ŋshɔ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ole gbɛ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ oduɔ tsei yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ akafite.

english: Why might crops fail on my land even when my neighbor grows them successfully across the road?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii shwereɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ naa moŋ?

english: Small differences in sunlight, wind exposure, soil moisture, and water settling mean two nearby fields can behave differently for the same crop.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔi fioo yɛ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. kɛ nu mli shwiemɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ akutsei enyɔ baanyɛ aná subaŋ srɔtoi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kome.

english: Why should I report new pests or strange crop damage on my farm to an extension officer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔ mi-extension officer lɛ amaniɛ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai heei loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ?

english: Reporting pests allows officers to identify dangerous insects or infections early and give you the right treatment strategy before the problem destroys your entire harvest.
ga: Amaniɛbɔɔ ni kɔɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa onukpai lɛ ni amɛyɔseɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mra. ni eha bo tsamɔ gbɛ ni sa dani naagba lɛ akpata onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing fewer pods now compared to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo fe afii komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce less as they grow old, especially after 20 to 25 years. Over time, the soil also loses its nutrients, and older trees become weaker and more vulnerable to diseases.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ afii 20 kɛyashi 25 sɛɛ, beni be hoɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ laajeɔ. Ni tsei ni edara lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping off before time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your trees are either lacking key nutrients in the soil like nitrogen, or they are stressed by intense sun exposure and a lack of water during dry weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo hulu la ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haaa ená haomɔ.

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, cool, and dark conditions. If your farm has too much shade or uncollected rotting pods, rainwater splashes the fungus onto healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ. Kɛji oŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo be babaoo loo ŋmeii lɛ miifite lɛ, Rainwater shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: What are those tiny bugs leaving dark burnt marks on my tree stems, and why are the branches dying?
ga: What are these tiny insects that cause dark burn marks on tree trunks? Ni mɛni hewɔ nine lɛ gbo lɛ?

english: Those pests are likely mirids (capsids). They suck the juice out of young stems and pods, creating wounds that let in fungal infections, causing the tips of the tree to dry up and die back.
ga: Ekolɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ji mirids (capsids). Amɛmuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii amli. Enɛ haa pilamɔi ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa lɛ baa. Ehaa tso lɛ naagbee lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to prune or cut extra branches from my crop trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛfo loo amɛfo niji krokomɛi ni fata he kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes useless or diseased branches so the plant doesn't waste energy on them. It allows sunlight and air to move freely through the tree, which keeps fungi away and encourages bigger fruits.
