ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajieɔ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ yɛ nakai niji lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ hela baa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ daraa.

english: Does having large shade trees in my farm help or hurt my crop yield?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa loo enaa miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Shade trees protect young crops from harsh heat and keep soil moist. However, too much shade prevents crops from making food from sunlight and creates wet conditions where pod diseases thrive.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, hulutsoo babaoo baanyɛ atsĩ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii kɛjɛ hulu lɛ mli. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ ni pod helai baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my farm has become weak and needs help?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia yelikɛbuamɔ?

english: Weak soil shows when crops grow very slowly, have pale or yellowish leaves, produce small fruits, or easily dry up when rain stops for just a few days. Adding compost or proper fertilizers helps rebuild it.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ tsɔɔ be mli ni tsei daa blɛoo waa. Amɛyɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ, amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii, loo amɛgbiɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi pɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etswa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops produce flowers during rain, but the flowers fall off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Heavy rainfall or sudden high heat can stress the tree and cause flowers to drop prematurely. Strong rains can also wash away pollen or prevent insects from pollinating the flowers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo latsaa ni naa wa trukaa lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ aná haomɔ ni eha efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi oya. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi amli fɔfɔi lɛ ahe loo etsĩ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: How does severe dry weather affect the internal behavior of my crops?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa lɛ saa subaŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When water is scarce, crops slow down their growth and drop young fruits or leaves to preserve moisture in their trunks. Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) helps trap moisture around the roots.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaha edalɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ekɛ aduawai bibii loo baai baashwie shi koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Is it better for my family's income to plant only cocoa, or should I intercrop with cassava and plantain?
ga: Ani ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha miweku lɛ shika ni amɛnáa lɛ akɛ amɛbaadu kookoo kɛkɛ? Aloo esa akɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei?

english: Planting food crops alongside cocoa provides shade for young trees, improves food security, and gives you cash flow throughout the year while you wait for the main cocoa harvest.
ga: Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo. niyenii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ ni eha oná shika afi muu lɛ fɛɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ kookoo kpamɔ titri lɛ.

english: Maize leaves curl up during extreme heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and trap moisture inside, protecting the crop from drying out during intense sunshine.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi la ni shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni emɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Buu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops look droopy and wilted at midday even though I watered them early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During peak afternoon heat, water evaporates from crop leaves faster than their roots can drink from the soil. This causes temporary wilting, but the plants usually bounce back as temperatures cool in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni latsaa lɛ mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa be kukuoo ko mli. Shi tsei lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall with bushy green leaves but produce almost no flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo shi ebɛ fɔfɔi loo aduawai ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes tomato plants to put all their energy into growing tall stems and leafy branches instead of developing flowers and setting fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii ni ewo yibii lɛ

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its lower leaves to save water and food for the top leaves and underground tubers, especially when nitrogen or water in the soil is running low.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishigbɛ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ato ŋwɛi baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ nitrogen loo nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help my maize grow bigger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cowpea ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, providing natural food for the nearby maize.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ naa adebɔɔ mli niyenii.

english: Why do my yam vines constantly seek out and climb up wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ miitao tsei ni akɛfee tsei lɛ ni ekwɔɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb upward to reach full sunlight, which allows their leaves to produce maximum energy needed to grow large tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛná hulutsoo be fɛɛ. Enɛ haa ebaai lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni he hiaa koni akɛwo bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Groundnuts bloom above ground, but after pollination, the plant pushes its stalks into the dark, moist earth so the actual pods can safely grow into nuts underground.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi yɛ pollination sɛɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ eshishifã lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni anɔkwa ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during storms even when the leaves look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top, making them top-heavy and prone to tipping when rain softens the soil and wind blows.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo ni esumɔɔ ni egbee shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ fee blɛoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswa.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look twisted during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by microscopic pests like mites or thrips that suck plant sap during dry spells, or by heat stress as the plant tries to save water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli beni tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the branch before they are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in humid, shady farm conditions with limited airflow between trees.
ga: Fɔ̃ɔ ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni shade yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa. ni kɔɔyɔɔ fioo pɛ hoɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full tropical sun. Fast-growing plantains provide living shade and keep the soil moist, giving the young cocoa trees the right environment to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ naa shihilɛ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil, which leads to weak stalks and small corncobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, a key plant food in the soil that helps crops grow strong green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa baai eŋɔli ni mli wa.

english: Why does my soil give me less maize yield when I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly steals the same specific nutrients from the soil year after year, leaving the land exhausted unless you switch crops or add fertilizer.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ juɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Tsɔɔmɔ he fɛɛ he Ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he.

english: Why do small caterpillars chew inside the centers of my young corn plants and leave powdery holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ŋmɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ powder lɛ?

english: These pests, often Fall Armyworms, hide inside the center whorl of the corn plant because it offers tender young leaves to eat and protects them from heat and rain.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ ni bei pii lɛ amɛgbeeɔ asraafoi akui anɔ lɛ, kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ ejaakɛ amɛyɛ baai bibii ni amɛyeɔ ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the soil before I get the chance to dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifoɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them without draining away properly, suffocating the tubers and causing fungal rot underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. ni enyɛɛɛ ejie nu jogbaŋŋ Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmei shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches and leaves from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji kɛ baai krokomɛi ni jɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree so sunlight and fresh air can pass through, which prevents fungal diseases like black pod and encourages the tree to produce more cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ mli tseɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji anaa, ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and thin if I leave them in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the water, sunlight, and nutrients from the ground that your crops need to mature and produce good fruits.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do seeds I save from last year's maize harvest grow weaker corn than commercial seeds bought from an agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmãa ni bɛ hewalɛ fe jarayeli dumɔwui ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Commercial hybrid seeds are specially bred for strong single-season performance, but seeds collected from their harvest lose those high-yield qualities in the next generation.
ga: Akwɛɔ jarayeli dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛ be kome mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa aba. Shi dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛsui ni haa mɔ yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my crops so it doesn't get wasted?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo midumɔ nii lɛ amli koni nɔ ko nɔ ko akafite?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil during early plant growth, but not right before heavy rainfall, which will wash the nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ shishijee bei amli. Shi esaaa akɛ ofeɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Enɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: This usually means your soil is low in nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to grow heavy cobs, and when it lacks enough in the soil, the plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ ekwɛ ŋmãa ni tsii. ni kɛ́ ebɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and lets soil pests build up. Planting legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas between seasons helps restore nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. and allowing pests in the soil to accumulate Planting legumes such as peanuts or cowpeas between seasons will naturally restore nitrogen to the soil.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer right after a very heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa waa?

english: Excess water from a heavy storm washes fertilizer away into gutters and streams before root systems can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is damp so the nutrients stay near the roots.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ ahum ni naa wa mli lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa nubui kɛ faai amli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ koni niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ abɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in dark, overly wet, and humid conditions. Pruning extra shade branches lets sunlight and fresh air into the farm to keep pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ Fɛ̃i tsɔ ni edɔ waa, ŋmei ni fa babaoo ni akɛfoɔ ŋmei lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Koni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and getting small and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiitsake lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from under the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these insects early keeps the plant healthy enough to bear fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to clear small weeds when my main crop plants are already taller than them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi bibii lɛ? Beni mi tso titri lɛ kɛlɛ fe amɛ momo lɛ?

english: Even small weeds steal fertilizer and soil moisture away from your crop's roots underground. Weeds also provide hiding places for harmful insect pests that attack leaves and fruits.
ga: Jwɛi bibii po Ejuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nu kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ ashishifãi amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Jwɛi hu haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni tutuaa tsei ahe tsei kɛ aduawai lɛ náa he ko ni amɛhiɔ amɛhe.

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen can stress the plant, making it drop its flowers to conserve energy. Keeping soil evenly moist and avoiding over-fertilization helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen babaoo baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees tip over easily when heavy winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa amɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be damaged by underground pests or waterlogged soil. Using sturdy wooden Y-sticks to prop up stems carrying heavy bunches prevents them from uprooting in high winds.
ga: Plantains shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite. Kɛtsɔ tso ni mli wa ni tamɔ Y ni akɛfiɔ tso ni hiɛ fɔfɔii ni tsii lɛ anɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkajie amɛshishifãi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: How do I know if the ground has enough water to plant seeds after the first rain of the year?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ okɛdu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain often only wets the top layer of dirt, which dries out quickly and kills germinating seeds. Dig a small hole with your finger; the soil needs to be moist at least finger-deep before sowing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa egbiɔ oya ni egbeɔ dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Okɛ onine atsu bu bibioo ko. Esa akɛ kɛ hoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ inchi kome dani adu dumɔwui.

english: Why do my cassava stem cuttings dry out and die without sprouting when I plant them in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ ni ekwɛɛɛ kɛji adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings rely on moisture around their buried leaf nodes to trigger root growth. Planting cuttings during dry spells causes them to lose water faster than they can grow roots to absorb it.
ga: Bɔ ni afoɔ ŋmei lɛ damɔ hulutsoo ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ. Afu baa lɛ mli ŋmeii koni eha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ada ni amɛŋɔ nu lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct, harsh sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out soil moisture. Keeping tall shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantain alongside cocoa protects the young seedlings until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ aha tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ aya hiɛ loo adu tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes and sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei kɛ tsei ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread out their leaves to catch maximum sunlight, which helps the plant produce large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot, damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping the plant capture the light it needs.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni edɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa la ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK will give the leaves their deep green color back so the corn can grow big ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei tamɔ NPK fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmãa lɛ aná toi wuji.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and causes soil pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil and keeps it fertile naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni eha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ayi afa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsake ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmeii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What happens if I plant my corn seeds very close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each corn plant gets enough resources to grow thick stalks and produce large, full ears.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmãa ni mli tse ni ekɛ toi wuji ni eyi obɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and stay thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni efee mlɛo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm, stealing the water, fertilizer, and sunlight intended for your crops. Clearing weeds early in the growth cycle allows your main crops to use all available nutrients for fast, healthy growth.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ amɛdalɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara oya, ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are small worms eating holes inside the leaves of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These worms are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that attacks young maize leaves and growing points. Applying recommended organic sprays like neem oil or appropriate pesticides early in the morning destroys the pests before they ruin the entire field.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tutuaa ŋmei baai bibii kɛ hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ wo mli leebi lɛ, ebaakpata kooloi lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling and yellow spots on cassava are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension agents prevents this issue.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ adumɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or lack of water in the soil. Giving the plants consistent water during dry spells and adding compost helps the flowers stay on and turn into full peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpe. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tsei lɛ anɔ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee nɔ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava is fully matured and ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 and 12 months after planting. You can tell it is ready when the bottom leaves dry up and drop, and by carefully digging up one root near the base to check if it has expanded to a good size.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo hiɔ shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ efee klalo kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. kɛtsɔ shishifã kome ni aaafo mli jogbaŋŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ koni ana kɛji egbɛ eshwa kɛyashɛ dalɛ kpakpa nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually show that your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to grow healthy leaves. Adding animal manure, well-made compost, or a nitrogen fertilizer can restore the green color and boost crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni wa lɛ adalɛ. Kooloo ŋmei ni akɛfataa he Kompost ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ Loo nitrogen ŋmei baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers grow very thin and weak when I plant many of them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ amli tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa lɛ, kɛ́ midu tsei babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plantains are planted too close to each other, their leaves block sunlight and their roots fight over the same water and nutrients in the soil. Giving each plant enough space allows sunlight to reach them and ensures their roots get enough food to grow thick trunks and heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ. Ni aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni hulu la abote mli ni eha shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee tsei ni mli tse kɛ jwɛi ni mli tse.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my okra leaves and how can I protect my farm?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ okra baai anɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ lɛ he?

english: Tiny holes in leaves are typically caused by small leaf-eating beetles. You can protect your okra crop by spraying a mixture made from neem tree leaves or using approved botanical sprays early in the morning when the insects are active.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ obu o-okra tsei lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛ neem baai fee lɛ ni oookɛshwie nɔ lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii leebi maŋkpa be mli ni kooloi lɛ miitsu nii lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme stress, especially from high heat, lack of soil moisture, or too much fertilizer at once. Keeping the soil consistently moist with water and organic mulching helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji amɛhao. titri lɛ kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo afata he yɛ be kome mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni akɛ organic mulching wo nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Maize consumes a lot of nutrients from the ground. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next planting season without costly chemicals.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa tsuuu nii.

english: Should I clear away dry grass and dry leaves from around my crops or leave them on the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni egboi kɛ baai ni egboi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli loo mashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Leaving dry organic material around the base of your crops creates a protective blanket called mulch. Mulch keeps the soil cool under the strong sun, prevents water from drying up quickly, stops weeds from growing, and slowly decays into rich organic plant food.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni oooshi yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch. Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekagbi oya Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii ni jara wa, ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under strong, direct sunlight and harsh heat. Shade trees act like living shelters that keep the air cool and moist around young cocoa trees until they grow old and strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ko ni haa he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. light cocoa tree Kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baagbɔ ni ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ.

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water settles around the roots due to poor drainage, or when soil insects and fungal infections enter the tubers. Planting yams on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu babɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. aloo kɛ́ kooloi kɛ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa lɛ bote ŋmeii lɛ amli. Sweet potato ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni eha yitso lɛ mli egbi ni ehiɛ hewalɛ

english: Why are some of my planted maize seeds failing to sprout out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are buried too deep in the soil, if the ground is completely dry, or if soil insects and birds eat the seeds before they sprout. Planting good quality seeds at about a finger's depth in moist soil ensures quick germination.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ okpoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ye dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ ni mli kwɔ aaafee inchi 1 lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Curled and patchy leaves are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. You can prevent this by planting disease-free stem cuttings and immediately pulling out affected plants so the disease does not spread to healthy crops.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ. Obaanyɛ otsi enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni hela bɛ mli lɛ ni ooodu ni ojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: This yellowing is usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to grow healthy green leaves. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizers like Urea or NPK at the right crop stage will help restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele babaoo he miihia koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo NPK ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dumɔ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What is eating holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark droppings inside the central whorl?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common caterpillar pest in Ghana. Inspecting your field early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or approved chemicals directly into the central funnel of the plant stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni odu lɛ amli mra ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ awo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily in direct sun. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside your young cocoa provides living shade and holds moisture in the soil, helping the seedlings survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Kɛ́ odu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ o-cocoa bibioo lɛ masɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the cocoa pods on my trees turning black and rotting from the tips during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod Disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in excessive moisture and shade. Pruning your cocoa trees regularly to allow sunlight and air into the canopy, alongside clearing infected pods, reduces moisture and controls the disease.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo fe nine mli kɛbaa. Esa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ amli daa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. kɛfata he lɛ, ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi ni eyeɔ helai anɔ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves twisting up and getting yellow patches on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny flying insects called whiteflies and infected stem cuttings. You can avoid this by planting certified disease-resistant stem varieties recommended by extension officers.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni foɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly kɛ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Obaanyɛ okpa enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni extension officials lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow out short, twisted, and small instead of long and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ kukuji, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛfeɔ bibii moŋ fe ni amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep, and well-drained soil to push down and swell smoothly. If the soil is hard or compacted, the tubers struggle to grow, so building high mounds or deep ridges gives the tubers space to grow large.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛtsi shi ni efuu jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ Tubers lɛ shweremɔ wa. No hewɔ lɛ, gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ loo ŋshɔ ni mli kwɔ ni afee lɛ baaha bulb lɛ aná he ko ni da ni ekɛda.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When you harvest them and leave the plant residues to decay, they act as a natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji okpa ni oshi tso lɛ mli nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ koni amɛgboi lɛ Amɛbaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and flat before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato aduawai shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, usually due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist rather than letting it dry out completely stops this from happening.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ moŋ fe ni oooha egbi kwraa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni enɛ akafee.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer heat stress, extreme dryness, or if too much nitrogen fertilizer was applied. Water your plants regularly and avoid over-fertilizing with nitrogen during the flowering stage.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. ŋmɔlɔ ni fe nine loo kɛji akɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ nɔ Nu daa ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli fe nine lɛ he yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: How can I keep my garden soil from drying out too fast during the hot season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ akagbi oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli nyɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli?

english: Covering the bare soil around your plants with dried grass, straw, or leaves—a practice called mulching—traps soil moisture, blocks weed growth, and keeps plant roots cool during hot weather.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni ebɔle tsei ahe lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi, jwɛi, loo baai shwieɔ nɔ—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—haa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli

english: Can I use borehole water directly to water my vegetable crops during the dry season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ nubu ko mli lɛ atsu nii ni mikɛwo aduawai amli nu tɛ̃ɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Borehole water is generally safe and very helpful for crops during the dry season. However, water deep from underground can sometimes contain high amounts of minerals or salts, so it is best to test a small patch first or allow the water to settle in a storage tank before application.
ga: Borehole nu lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Shi kɛlɛ, bei komɛi lɛ, nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni mineral loo ŋmeii babaoo yɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooka he bibioo ko okwɛ. klɛŋklɛŋ loo ha nu lɛ ahi nutoohe lɛ mli dani okɛtsu nii

english: Why are rats constantly digging up and destroying my cassava tubers right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yaa nɔ amɛfoɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Rats are attracted to mature root crops like cassava because they provide both food and moisture, especially when dry weather sets in. Clearing weeds around the farm boundary, removing crop debris, and using safe traps helps eliminate their hiding places and protect your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii sumɔɔ shishifãi ni edara, tamɔ ŋmei, ejaakɛ amɛhaa niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi. Ajieɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ, ajieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ. Ni tsɔnei ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ejie hei ni okɛ ohe ewo mli lɛ kɛya ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Can I plant maize on swampy or muddy land where water sits for a long time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize does not grow well in muddy or waterlogged soil because standing water suffocates the plant roots and causes root rot. Muddy or swampy areas are much better suited for water-loving crops like rice unless you construct raised beds and drainage channels.
ga: Abɛi edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ sũ ni mli ewo muji loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ. Hei ni muji yɔɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei ni sumɔɔ nu tamɔ ŋmãa, ja ofee saatsoi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for leaf growth, or that excessive water is preventing roots from breathing. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea restores healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa. Aloo nu babaoo haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei tamɔ urea ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmei lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers but drop them without making fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi eshiɔ ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat, lack consistent water, or lack pollinators like bees. Providing regular morning watering and mulching around the roots helps keep the plants cool enough to set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni faaa daa loo ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ mli, nu ni afɔɔ amɛ daa leebi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ ŋmeii Shishifãi lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ mli ajɔ bɔ ni sa ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants have lush green leaves but refuse to produce any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ shi ekɛ pepper ko baaa lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil encourages pepper plants to grow thick leaves and stems at the expense of fruits. Switching to a fertilizer rich in phosphorus and potassium signals the plant to stop growing leaves and start producing flowers and peppers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ chili tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli wa, ni ekɛ aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ tso lɛ tsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ ekpa baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ ni ebɔi fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii feemɔ.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant plantain trees alongside young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and moisture to protect cocoa seedlings during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni ebu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: What will happen if I plant my crops very close together to save space?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mikɛ he akafite?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak plants that yield very little harvest and makes it easier for plant diseases to spread rapidly from crop to crop.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii mli nibii ahe. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ baa. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ tsei ahe helai baagbɛ ashwã oya kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long heat streak before regular rains start. If you plant too early, the hot sun will dry out the topsoil and scorch the delicate newly germinated seedlings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ dɔlɛ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli gĩɔ ni eshãa dumɔwui heei.

english: How do I stop insects and weevils from destroying my harvested maize stored in the barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ŋmãa ni akpa ni akɛto mi ŋmãa lɛ naa?

english: Insects thrive in grains that still hold moisture. To protect your harvest, sun-dry the maize until the kernels are completely hard, then store them in airtight storage bags or sealed containers stored off the bare floor.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ dumɔwui ni mli edɔ lolo lɛ amli. koni obu onibii ahe Ha ŋmãa lɛ agbi kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo tsɛnsi ko ni atsĩ naa ni akɛto shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do buyers in the market prefer imported rice over the local rice I grow, and how can I change that?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmãa ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ fe maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa ni miduɔ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsake nakai?

english: Imported rice is often popular because the grains are uniform, long, fragrant, and clean. You can achieve this same high quality by planting certified improved local seeds and using tarpaulins during harvest so dirt and stones do not mix with your grains.
ga: Omɔ ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ baa lɛ ehe gbɛi waa yɛ eŋmãa ni yɔɔ ekome, kakadaŋŋ, ni ŋɔɔ ni ehe tse lɛ hewɔ. Obaanyɛ onine ashɛ su kpakpa ni nɔ kwɔ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ kɛtsɔ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ tarpaulin atsu nii yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli Enɛ ji koni muji kɛ tɛi akafutu odumɔwui lɛ.

english: What are improved seed varieties, and how do they actually help my farm compared to saving seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ ni te amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua miŋmɔ lɛ amɛha tɛŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ? Kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni mikɛbaahere kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Improved seeds are special seeds selected by scientists to grow stronger, resist diseases, and yield more crop. Reusing seeds from previous harvests causes crops to slowly lose their strength, resulting in smaller harvests and uneven growth.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi ni jeŋ nilelɔi ehala koni amɛdara waa, amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii ekoŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi fiofio. Enɛ haa kpamɔ bibioo kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa baa.

english: Why do some rice varieties fall over easily when strong winds blow before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa dani akpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Older or traditional rice varieties tend to grow very tall with thin stems, making them top-heavy when grains mature. Newer high-yielding varieties are bred to stay shorter and thicker so they can hold heavy grain heads without falling over.
ga: Kusum mli ŋmãa ni etsɛ loo nɔ ni fe nakai lɛ fɔɔ dalɛ ni ekwɛɔ waa ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ tsiimɔ kɛ́ ahoo dumɔwui lɛ. Amɛmiifɔ ŋmeii heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ koni amɛfee kuku ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ ebaanyɛ ehiɛ dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii ni egbeee shi.

english: Does rice really need to sit in standing water to grow well, or can it grow on dry land like maize?
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmãa ata nu ni mli ejɔ mli koni eda jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ. Aloo abaanyɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛha kooloi aniyenii?

english: It depends on the seed type. Upland rice varieties are designed to grow on dry, rain-fed land just like maize, while lowland rice varieties thrive in flooded areas because water prevents weeds and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Edamɔ dumɔwu henɔ lɛ nɔ Afee ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ nɔ tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ejaakɛ nu yeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi lɛ tsiɔ naa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my rice crop turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-rice tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants use to make food. Applying the right fertilizer at the right growth stage turns the leaves green again so the plant can feed itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ana niyenii.

english: Is it better for me to plant my rice seeds directly in the field or start them in a nursery first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo mabɔi amɛdumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Starting seeds in a nursery lets you protect young seedlings from pests and select only the healthiest ones to transplant, leading to a stronger crop. Direct planting saves labor, but weeds can easily choke young seedlings.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. ni ohala dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ pɛ ni okɛdu. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hewalɛ. Dumɔ tɛ̃ɛ haa nitsumɔ baa shi. Shi jwɛi baanyɛ afite tsei bibii oya.

english: Why do birds and insects seem to attack my rice field much more than my cassava crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi kɛ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ babaoo fe mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Rice produces soft, sweet grains exposed at the top of the plant that are easy for birds and insects to eat. Cassava hides its crop underground and has bitter leaves that naturally scare away many pests.
ga: Omɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni jeɔ kpo yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ ni okpoi kɛ kooloi yeli waaa. Cassava kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii teeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni eyɛ baai ni mli edɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, eshwieɔ kooloi bibii babaoo.

english: Why do my rice grains break into small pieces when they are milled, and how can I keep them whole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli fãa bibii bibii kɛ́ atsɔ mli lɛ, ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mahere ŋmãa lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Rice grains crack inside if they are dried too quickly under hot, direct sunlight. Drying your harvested grains slowly in thin layers under partial shade keeps the grains strong so they stay whole during milling.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii lɛ baagbala yɛ mli kɛji amɛgbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ni agbiɔ fiofio yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ hulutsoo fioo shishi lɛ baaye abua ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehiɛɔ emuuyeli mli yɛ be mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ miitsu nii lɛ.

english: Why do my neighbor's crops produce bigger grain heads even though we farm on the same soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ dumɔwui ayitsei wuji eyɛ mli akɛ wɔmiitsu shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Bigger grain heads usually come from using certified seeds, weeding early before weeds steal food from the crop, and applying fertilizer at key stages like flowering rather than just at planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ayitsei wuji jɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli baa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Dani jwɛi lɛ baaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ bei ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔfɔii amli, shi jeee yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli pɛ.

english: How do agricultural extension officers help me get better results from my land?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni maná yibii kpakpai kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Extension officers bring modern farming knowledge directly to your farm. They teach you proper plant spacing, effective pest control, and post-harvest methods so you get higher yields and better crop prices.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli he nilee baa oŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛtsɔɔ bo bɔ ni esa akɛ ato tsei ahe gbɛjianɔ aha. Gbɛi ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni akɛyeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ koni ona ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara ni hi.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize stalk usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from its older lower leaves to feed new growth, showing that your soil needs nitrogen fertilizer or compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants turn purple or reddish during early growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ purple loo etsuru yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ?

english: Purple leaves in young maize usually mean the plant is struggling to absorb phosphorus from the soil. This often happens when the ground is cold or too wet, which temporarily slows down root development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miitao ni ejie fɔsfɔs kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt in the hot afternoon heat even when the ground is not completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbiko kwraa moŋ?

english: During peak afternoon heat, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can draw water from the soil. This temporary wilting is the plant's way of protecting itself from drying out, and it typically recovers by evening.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa fe fɛɛ mli yɛ shwane mli Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ be kukuoo mli shwiemɔ nɛɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekagbi. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling upward and turning a pale yellow color?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. These insects suck plant sap and spread infections, especially during hot, dry spells.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa. Titri lɛ, yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear away all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need partial shade because direct, intense sunlight dries out their delicate leaves and soil too quickly. Keeping shade trees or planting plantains nearby protects young cocoa plants until their roots are deep enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya tsɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ebaabu cacao tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baakɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my yam vines produce larger tubers when I train them onto wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ naa bulbs wuji beni mitsɔseɔ amɛ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam vines off the ground so their leaves can trap more sunlight to produce food for the growing tuber below. It also improves air flow around the leaves, reducing the risk of fungal diseases.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni ebaa lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hulu la babaoo koni ekɛ niyenii aha bulbs ni miida yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ yaa hiɛ. Ha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep falling off without growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience environmental stress, such as very high temperatures, dry soil, or a lack of plant nutrients like phosphorus.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tso mli niyenii tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ lɛ kpe.

english: Why do my crops grow tall, skinny, and weak when I plant the seeds very close to one another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe kpaakpa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil moisture, and food. This causes them to stretch rapidly upward to reach light, resulting in weak stems and poor fruit yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛyeɔ amɛhe Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛyaa oya kɛyaa la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants leave my farm soil richer for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally work with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen gas from the air. When the cowpea plant foliage decays after harvest, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as natural plant food.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ. Beni tsina tsei ahe baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii.

english: Why do my mature cassava roots start rotting underground if I leave them in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water in waterlogged soil cuts off oxygen to cassava roots and encourages rot-causing fungi to thrive, causing mature tubers to decompose rapidly before they can be harvested.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli. ni ekanyaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ adalɛ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni eda lɛ fiteɔ oya dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ.

english: Leaves turn yellow mainly when the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow green and strong, or when too much water around the roots is suffocating the plant. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back the dark green color.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri lɛ kɛ́ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. aloo beni nu ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishifãi babaoo tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without giving me any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miifɔlɔ ni ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the days get too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients. Keeping the soil constantly moist by placing dry grass around the stems helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni okɛbaabɔle he lɛ nɔ. Tsoi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and get tiny white insects under them in dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ yɔɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ shishi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli?

english: Cassava leaves curl up during dry periods to save water, which attracts tiny sap-sucking pests like whiteflies and mealybugs to hide underneath. Spraying the leaves with clean water mixed with a small amount of liquid soap or neem oil helps wash these pests away.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies kɛ mealybugs koni amɛbahi shi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli tse ni akɛ samla ni ji nu fioo loo neem fɔ efutu mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ atsu nii.

english: What causes my pepper leaves to shrink and gather close together like a bunch?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: This leaf shrinkage is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects like aphids or thrips that suck the plant's juice. Removing and carefully destroying infected plants early stops the sickness from spreading to healthy pepper plants nearby.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ mli shwiemɔ baa. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ kɛ hiɛdɔɔ mra kɛ amɛkpãtãmɔ Enɛ baatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa pepper tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my bean plants make the soil better for my maize when I plant them together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-corn lɛ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ fee ekome lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are special crops that capture natural nitrogen from the air and trap it in their roots. When these roots decay in the soil, they release free fertilizer that feeds nearby crops like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ mli ni amɛŋmɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji shishifãi nɛɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ejieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni ekɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out small and bent even when the soil looks fine on top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, deep soil so the tubers can expand easily downwards. If the soil underneath is hard clay or full of gravel, the tuber cannot push through easily, causing it to stay short, twisted, or small.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo. Kɛji shishigbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ŋmei eyi mli obɔ lɛ Yitso lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli oya, ni no haa efeɔ kuku, egbɛɔ eshwaa, loo efeɔ bibioo.

english: How can I check if my farm soil is healthy without using expensive tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛ nibii ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: Healthy farm soil is dark in color, crumbles easily in your hands, holds water after rain without pooling, and contains visible soil life like earthworms. Hard, pale, or sandy soil that drains instantly needs animal manure or compost added to rebuild its strength.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kpakpa mli lɛ yɛ diŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ekɛ nu toɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli. ni shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni anaa tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli tseee, loo ni ŋã yɔɔ mli ni nu hoɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ biɔ ŋmei loo kooloi amli ŋmei koni ekɛtswa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop many of their leaves when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ shwieɔ baai babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their leaves during dry weather to stop water from evaporating out through the foliage. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or shade trees alongside young cocoa keeps the air cool and protects the soil from drying out.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi koni nu akatsɔ baai lɛ amli kɛho. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi.

english: Why do my plantain suckers stop growing quickly during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekpaa dalɛ oya yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The cool, dry harmattan wind causes plantain plants to slow down their growth to protect themselves from moisture loss. Covering the soil around the base with dry leaves or plant stalks helps retain underground moisture until the warm rains return.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni egbi lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ daraa fioo koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo tsei ahe tsei shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do wild weeds come up so much faster than my planted seeds right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ oya fe dumɔwui ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and can sleep in dry soil for months, ready to jump into growth at the very first drop of rain. Clearing weeds as soon as they sprout gives your young crops sunlight and nutrients before the weeds overpower them.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ nyɔji babaoo. ni efee klalo akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ pɛ Jwɛi ni agbeɔ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ naa hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai dani jwɛi lɛ yeɔ amɛnɔ kunim.

english: How can I get food to eat and sell while waiting for my cocoa trees to grow and bear fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana niyenii ni mahɔ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: You can plant fast-growing crops like plantain, cassava, or maize between your young cocoa trees. These short-term crops give you quick harvests and income within the first year while providing shade to protect the young cocoa.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains, cassava loo ŋmãa yɛ o-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli nɛɛ haa yibiiwoo kɛ shika baa oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and the plants staying very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsei lɛ hu ji bibii waa lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves and stunted growth usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, a key food crops need to grow strong. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea will help the leaves turn green and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni ehe hiaa ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni yɔɔ nitrogen tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni eha amɛdaramɔ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is rich enough to give me a good yield this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai aba yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, feels soft and moist, and contains earthworms or decaying leaves. Hard, pale, or dusty soil lacks nutrients and needs compost or animal manure added before planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ su ni tsuɔ. Enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni edɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo baai ni fiteɔ yɛ jɛmɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ sũ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi ashishifãi afata he dani adu.

english: What is the correct way to plant cassava so that the roots grow large and healthy?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ ŋmei koni shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛhe awa?

english: Cut healthy cassava stems into pieces about 20 to 30 centimeters long and push them into loose, well-drained soil at a slant. Planting in loose soil makes it easier for the roots to expand into large tubers.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmei tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli bibii ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30 ni okɛshwie shikpɔŋ ni nɔ etse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, will I harvest more crops from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting too closely forces crops to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in small and weak yields. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to grow big and produce more harvest.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ faaa ni ebɛ hewalɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni eda ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt quickly during hot days even when it rained a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ moŋ?

english: Vegetable roots are near the surface where the hot sun quickly dries out the dirt. Covering the soil around your plants with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil cool and traps moisture longer.
ga: Aduawai shishifãi bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ, he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa muji lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What is eating small holes in my tomato leaves, and how can I protect them?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi tomato baai lɛ anɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he?

english: Small holes in leaves are typically caused by insects like caterpillars or beetles. Spraying a mixture of water and ground neem tree seeds early in the morning acts as a natural pest control that repels these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ baa. Nu ni akɛ neem dumɔwui ni atswa lɛ efutu mli ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni gbeɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni shwieɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to take up nutrients and water faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds within the first three to four weeks after planting gives your main crops a chance to grow strong without competition.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhe niyenii kɛ nu oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛdara waa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: How can I stop insects from destroying my stored maize after harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmãa ni ato lɛ yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Insects thrive in damp grain. You must dry your maize completely in the sun until the kernels are hard, then store them in sealed, airtight bags like PICS bags to starve pests of oxygen.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ ŋmãa ni mli efɔ mli. Esa akɛ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛwo kotoku ko ni vacuum tsiɔ mli, tamɔ PICS kotoku mli, koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa mli.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with beans, groundnuts, or cowpeas naturally restores soil fertility.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii, ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient in soil. Rain can wash this nutrient away, or the soil may be exhausted, requiring manure or appropriate fertilizer to help the leaves stay green and make food for the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nugbɔ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii nɛɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afite. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa atsu nii koni eye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛha niyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why did my crops wilt and dry up after I applied chemical fertilizer to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ewo mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer acts like salt; if placed directly against the stem or applied when the soil is completely dry, it pulls water out of the plant roots instead of feeding them. Fertilizer should always be applied a few inches away from the stem when the soil is moist.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋoo. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ loo akɛwo nɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ. Ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi inchii fioo komɛi beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that transmit viruses, or by severe heat stress. Protecting plants from heavy insect infestations early on keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli ni abuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui waa lɛ ahe mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep falling off without forming any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or attacks from microscopic insects called thrips. When the plant gets stressed, it drops flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ thrips lɛ tutua amɛ. Kɛ tsei miihao Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛto hewalɛ he kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why is it necessary for me to stake my yam vines with tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ niji ni kɛlɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to build food that travels down to grow big tubers underground. Staking holds leaves up toward the sun and keeps them off damp ground where diseases easily spread.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni nyiɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji. Staking haa baai lɛ kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ he, he ni hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the fruit bunch starts getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that can be weakened by tiny soil worms called nematodes or stem borer pests. Because the heavy bunch changes the plant's balance, supporting the stem with a bamboo fork helps hold it up until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ tso lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni tsii baatsake bɔ ni tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi ehaa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei fɔk tsu nii kɛfi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ tso lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Why do many tiny green pods on my cocoa tree turn shriveled and black before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ babaoo egbo ni amɛtsɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdara lɛ.

english: This is called cherelle wilt, a natural process where the cocoa tree reduces its fruit load because it does not have enough water or nutrients to grow every pod to full size. Proper pruning and soil feeding can reduce this loss.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni cacao tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ehaa jatsu ni kã aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ adara kɛyashɛ amɛhe. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛhaa lɛ baanyɛ aha nɛkɛ nɔ ni laajeɔ nɛɛ aba shi.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are mature and ready for harvesting without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: When cassava is ready for harvest, the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack as the underground tubers swell up.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ baaje shishi egbɛ eshwa be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ mli shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow faster and yield better during the major rainy season than in the minor rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be bibioo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The major rainy season offers longer periods of consistent rain and soil moisture combined with steady sunlight, allowing crops to feed and grow constantly compared to the shorter, less predictable minor season.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa be kakadaŋŋ. kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ daa lɛ fataa he Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii naa niyenii ni amɛdaraa daa. Kɛ akɛto sɛkɛndre be ni yɔɔ kuku ni anyɛɛɛ atsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ he.

english: How do weeds growing close to my crops slow down the growth of my farm plants?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ aha tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ fioo?

english: Weeds act as thieves in your farm; their fast-growing roots steal the water and nutrients from the soil before your crop can reach them, and their leaves block sunlight from reaching your plants.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Eshishifãi ni daa oya lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ otsei lɛ ahe.
