english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, intense sunlight because their roots and leaves dry out quickly. Leaving or planting shade trees keeps the soil moist and protects young cocoa leaves from scorching until the plants mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ oshi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo odu lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebaabu kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on to get a good yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni akwɔ koni ewo ŋmaa kpakpa lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to lift their leaves higher toward the sun. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where diseases live and exposes them to sunlight, allowing the plant to produce food for growing large tubers below ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ he. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ yɔɔ lɛ ni ekɛ amɛ awo hulu la mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize crop lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen away, so applying balanced fertilizer or manure helps restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are spaced too closely together, the cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves instead of root tubers. Proper plant spacing and balanced nutrients encourage the plant to store food in the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ. Yucca kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe shishifãi lɛ. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ niyenii toɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into thin tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Rolling up leaves is the maize plant's natural defense mechanism to preserve water. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, stopping water from evaporating too fast until the weather cools down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni abele tsei yɔɔ koni amɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya tsɔ kɛyashi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why does lowland rice survive in flooded fields while my maize rots and dies in standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels in their stems that transport oxygen from the air down to their underwater roots. Maize roots do not have these channels and drown because they cannot breathe in waterlogged soil.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ŋtayaai krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ nɛkɛ gbɛi nɛɛ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nu mli ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when extreme afternoon heat or sudden changes in soil water stress the plant. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps the plant stay cool enough to turn its flowers into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu tsakemɔi trukaa hao tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni ehaa fɔfɔii feɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruit bunch starts growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ je shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and stay near the surface of the soil, making it hard for the stem to support a heavy bunch of fruit. Using wooden Y-props to support the heavy stem prevents the wind from pushing the plant over before harvest.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tso lɛ tso lɛ akɛ ebaakwɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ Y-shape tsu nii ni akɛfi tso lɛ tso ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekatswa tso lɛ shi dani akpa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the tender young leaves, or by a virus carried by these insects. Spraying appropriate organic or chemical controls early stops the insects from stunting the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ loo helai ni kooloi nɛɛ hiɛɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛkwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra ni sa. Ehaa kooloi bibii shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Continuous rain and high air humidity create ideal conditions for a fungus called Black Pod disease to spread. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight and wind flow through the farm, drying out the pods and stopping the fungus.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ kpaa.

english: Yellowing starting from the bottom leaves upward usually means your maize is lacking nitrogen, a major plant food. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the newer top leaves, causing the older lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii titri ko bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei amli. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Yam tubers need loose, soft, and deep soil to push down smoothly. If the soil is hard, compacted, or stony, the growing tuber gets blocked and is forced to bend or stay short.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ koni amɛtsi amɛhe blɛoo kɛya shi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ tɛi lɛ, abaatsi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anaa ni ebaanyɛ amɛkoto loo amɛfee kuku.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle full, direct sunlight. They need temporary shade from crops like plantains to protect them from burning until their roots are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ tomato ko kwraa wooo lɛ?

english: When the weather gets too hot or the soil dries out completely, tomato plants drop their blossoms to preserve water and energy instead of spending it on growing fruit.
ga: Be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaafite yɛ aduawai ni amɛduɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my leafy green vegetables wilt in the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni mifeee nakai lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose water into the hot air faster than roots can draw it from the soil. Mulching around the plants helps keep the soil moist and cool, reducing this afternoon heat stress.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ haomɔ ni jɛɔ latsaa mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ shi.

english: Curled and wrinkled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites hiding on the undersides of the leaves, or by a plant virus carried by insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ji kooloi ni kɛ helai baa lɛ amli

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in the ground without draining, the roots drown, rot, and become easy targets for soil fungus.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ tsi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛfeɔ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he oya.

english: Why are insects eating my cowpea flowers before the pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi yeɔ cowpea fɔfɔii dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet scents that attract flower thrips and beetles. Protecting the plants with safe treatments just as flowering begins stops these pests from destroying the flowers before pods develop.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni gbalaa fɔfɔi thrips kɛ lady beetles. Kɛ́ abu tsei ahe kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe nɔ kɛ agbɛnɛ hu kɛha fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite fɔfɔi lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ aba.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when carrying heavy bunches of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ mihiɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots near the surface of the soil, making them top-heavy when carrying full fruit bunches. Supporting them with sturdy wooden props helps keep them standing during heavy rain or wind.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa tsɔne lɛ tsiimɔ babaoo baa kɛ́ etere aduawai akuu ko. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdamɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli.

english: Why are the outer branches of my oil palm trees turning brown and hanging down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiifo shi lɛ?

english: As oil palms grow, the lowest fronds naturally age, dry out, and droop so the tree can focus energy on new growth at the center, though widespread yellowing can also mean the soil needs potassium.
ga: Kɛji akɛ mu tso lɛ da lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ daa, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ ama dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ he fɛɛ he lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia potassium moŋ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes start spoiling and softening so quickly after I pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo oya beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continue to breathe and produce natural ripening gases even after harvest. In warm weather, high heat speeds up this respiration process, causing the fruit to lose moisture rapidly and soft rot bacteria to multiply.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ emuɔ ni ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa mɔ shwereɔ lɛ kpo yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ po. yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa mumɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yaa oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya, ni helai ni fiteɔ lɛ faa babaoo.

english: Why does my plantain bunch ripen all at once before I am ready to handle it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ shikome dani mifeɔ klalo akɛ matsu he nii lɛ?

english: Plantains produce a natural ripening gas called ethylene. Once one finger on the bunch releases this gas, it triggers all the neighboring plantains to ripen simultaneously, especially if stored in warm, direct sunlight.
ga: Plantains jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni haa mɔ shwereɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene. Kɛji akɛ nine kome ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ jie kɔɔyɔɔ nɛɛ Ebaawo dumɔwui fɛɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛshwere yɛ be kome mli, titri lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulu la ni mli edɔ, ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers growing much smaller this season even though I used the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ daraaa kwraa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ? akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii

english: Cassava draws heavily on soil nutrients like potassium to grow large roots. Planting on the same land repeatedly depletes these nutrients, causing the plant to produce smaller tubers unless the soil is given rest or enriched.
ga: Cassava gbalaa shikpɔŋ mli niyenii tamɔ potassium waa koni eshishifãi lɛ adara. He kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ baa shi. Ehaa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii. ja shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔ ehe loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers split open underground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ amli gbalaa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers split when there is an uneven water supply—such as sudden heavy rain after a long dry spell. The inside of the tuber expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing it to crack open.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni baa trukaa lɛ bɛ, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ sɛɛ. Yitso lɛ mligbɛ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers as a defense mechanism when stressed by extreme heat, drought, or poor soil nutrients. The plant drops its blossoms to conserve water and energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ akɛ hebuu gbɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up before the crop is fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi dani tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves in maize are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency or excess water choking the roots. When the plant lacks nitrogen, it pulls available nutrients from older lower leaves to feed the younger top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli loo nu babaoo ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ tsei bɛ nitrogen Ejieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni eda ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni ekɛhaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do all my vegetable crops mature at the exact same time, making it hard for me to manage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ fɛɛ miida yɛ be kome mli lɛ? Ehaa ewaa akɛ makwɛ nɔ

english: Crops planted on the same day under identical soil and rain conditions follow the same biological clock. Staggering your planting dates by two-week intervals allows crops to mature in manageable batches.
ga: Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ gbi kome nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ shihilɛ kome shishi lɛ nyiɛɔ wala yibii ahe ŋmɛlɛtswaa kome lɛ nɔŋŋ sɛɛ. Gbi ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ mlijaa yɛ bei amli Otsii enyɔ baaha tsei lɛ adara ni amɛfee kui ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the ends of my maize cobs missing grains when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ naagbee beni mikpaa lɛ lɛ?

english: Incomplete grain filling happens when drought or dry winds hit during the flowering stage, preventing the silks at the tip of the cob from receiving enough pollen to form seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ baa kɛji hɔmɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ba yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ naa lɛ aná pollen ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee dumɔwui.

english: How does heavy rainfall right before harvest affect my groundnuts in the soil?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani akpaa nii lɛ saa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excess water right before harvest forces groundnuts to absorb too much moisture, causing pods to break away from stems, rot in the damp earth, or sprout seeds prematurely inside the soil.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine dani akpa lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fãa kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Rot yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ loo dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya

english: Why do tiny insects burrow inside my bean pods while the plants are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifo mi-bean pods lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Pests like pod borers are attracted to the sweet nectar of young bean flowers. They lay eggs on green pods, and when the larvae hatch, they bore inside to eat the developing beans before you can harvest.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pod borers lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔi bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ. Amɛwoɔ wɔji yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Amɛbaafo mli koni amɛye ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and dry up from the bottom when there is a short dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ be mli ni ŋmãa be kukuoo ko baa lɛ?

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting from the lower leaves, it means the plant is starving for nitrogen because there is not enough moisture in the soil to drink up nutrients. Mulching the base of the plants keeps the soil cool and wet so the plant can keep feeding.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli ejaakɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko ha tsei ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛyeɔ niyenii.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, heavily shaded conditions. When air cannot circulate around the tree, humidity stays high, allowing the fungus to attack the pods and ruin your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ waa. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi. Ha ŋmeii lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ ni efite onibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by cassava mosaic virus, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. When infected, the plant cannot produce enough energy, leading to smaller roots underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Beni hela lɛ emɔ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off to the ground without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when temperature heat spikes or when soil moisture drops too low. The plant gets stressed and sheds its flowers to save water and energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ba shi tsɔ. Tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do some of my plantain trees give very small bunches while others nearby give large ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa tsei niji wuji lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers attached to the main stem steal water and food from the mother plant. If you do not prune away extra suckers and leave only one or two stems, the bunches will remain small and light.
ga: Plantain tsei ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ofolɔɔɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii 1-2 pɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ aniji lɛ baafee bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing taller once they start making small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ beni ebɔi yibii bibii womɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants naturally focus all their nutrients into ripening fruit rather than growing taller. Picking off the very first blossoms allows the bush to grow bigger and stronger before producing a much larger crop.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ fɛɛ maa amɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ yɛ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaatsɔ shɔŋŋ. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi lɛ amli Enɛ baaha jwɛi lɛ adara ni ehe awa dani ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aba.

english: Why are my yam tubers coming out short and crooked instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo kuku ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become bent when the soil underground is too hard or full of rocks, preventing the tuber from pushing straight down. Planting on high, well-mounded loose soil allows the tubers to grow thick and long.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baabɔle kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haaa yitso lɛ ashɛ shi tɛ̃ɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni etse ehe nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize stalks fall down easily when heavy rains and wind blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks fall over, or lodge, when their roots are too shallow or when stem borers weaken the lower stem from the inside. Piling soil tightly around the base of the plant gives roots a firmer grip.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛjeɔ kpo kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ haa shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ shishi shiŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting right at the first rain help my crops yield more than planting weeks later?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔ ni miduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fe nɔ ni miduɔ yɛ otsi kome sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The very first rains trigger a rapid release of accumulated nitrogen in the dry soil, known as a nitrogen flush. Crops planted immediately tap into this free nutrient boost for early growth.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa nitrogen ni ebua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo oya, ni ale lɛ akɛ nitrogen flush. Tsei ni adara lɛ baaná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ he sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛdara mra.

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow plenty of leafy green leaves but yield very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cowpeas to put all their energy into making thick green leaves instead of flowers. Cowpeas need balanced soil and full sunlight to switch energy from leaf growth into bean pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni ja kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia tsina ŋmeii koni ekɛtsake hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ ŋmeii amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build strong stems and green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure to the soil will help them regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ená eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before the small pods start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii bibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ? Ani ebaaje shishi efee?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as lack of water during dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or attack by pests like capsids. Providing moderate shade and maintaining good soil moisture helps the flowers stay on the tree to become pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛkpe haomɔi, tamɔ nu ni bɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids lɛ tutuaa. Shade ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa ni ahiɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the heavy rain season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them without proper drainage, suffocating the roots. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to flow away and keeps the tubers healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu babaoo atsɔ mli ni eye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and become top-heavy as the bunch grows. Tiny soil worms called nematodes or stem borers can also destroy the roots, making the plant unstable. Supporting the trees with wooden poles and using healthy planting suckers prevents them from falling.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ be mli ni kuu lɛ daa lɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela bibioo Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ hu baanyɛ afite shishifãi. ha tsei akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ fi tso lɛ sɛɛ, ni okɛ nu ni mli wa tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbee shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Wilting despite watering is often caused by soil-borne diseases like bacterial wilt or fungal root rot that block water from moving up the stem. Rotating your crops so you don't plant tomatoes in the same spot every season helps clear these diseases from the soil.
ga: withering Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli tamɔ bacteria wilt loo fungal root rot ji nɔ ni kɛ nu baa. Enɛ haaa nu aya ŋwɛi tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ atsake ŋmɔshi nibii koni akadu tomato yɛ he kome daa be lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie helai nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I get smaller yields if I pack my seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibii fioo nɔ kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for water, light, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures every single plant gets enough sunlight and room to feed, leading to bigger stems and larger harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei fɛɛ ahe lɛ haa hulu la kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛyeɔ nii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛkpaa nii babaoo.

english: Why are caterpillars destroying the center whorl leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miifite mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar pest that hides deep inside the growing center of maize plants to eat young leaves. Checking your farm early and using recommended, safe treatments stops them before they ruin the entire crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni eye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu nii lɛ atsu nii. Koni akpa ŋmɔji nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than the food crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe niyenii tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally survive poor soil and harsh weather much better than cultivated crops. They quickly steal drinking water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your crops if you do not weed early in the growing season.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa nɔ jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛjuɔ nu ni anuɔ, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ onibii amli lɛ oya. Kɛji okɛ jwɛi lɛ shwieee shi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ,.

english: You should wait to plant until the rains are steady enough to soak the soil deeply, rather than planting after the very first light shower. Planting into dry or barely moist ground causes seeds to dry up and fail to germinate.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni odu nii kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baanɛ shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ hei ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ fioo lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛkwɛ̃ŋ.

english: Why do experienced farmers say planting cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize makes the soil better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When these roots decay, they release natural food into the ground that helps neighboring crops like maize grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shishifãi nɛɛ fite Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my maize taking so long to sprout after planting it in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ beni adu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize seeds require adequate soil moisture and air to sprout. If the soil is too dry, compacted, or if the seeds were planted too deep, germination slows down significantly or fails completely.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ, ebɔle ehe, loo adu dumɔwui lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ baa shi waa loo ebaafite kwraa.

english: Does planting corn seeds too deep in the soil delay how fast they come up?
ga: Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃mɔ aya hiɛ fioo?

english: Yes, planting seeds deeper than 3 to 5 centimeters forces the seedling to use up all its energy trying to push through heavy soil, which delays sprouting and weakens the plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni mli kwɔ fe sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5 lɛ baaha dumɔwu lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛbaatsu nii waa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: What can I do to ensure my crop seeds germinate quickly right after planting?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni midumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Plant your seeds immediately after a good rain when the soil is moist, plant at the correct shallow depth, and cover the seeds lightly with loose soil so water and air reach them easily.
ga: Dumɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Dumɔ yɛ he ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni sa. ni okɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse aha dumɔwui lɛ ahe fioo koni nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ashɛ he oya.

english: Why do certified seeds from agricultural officers sprout better than seeds I save from my old maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ewo he odase lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa momo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected for high vigor, uniform drying, and treated against pests and diseases, whereas saved seeds often lose strength or carry hidden pest damage from storage.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha hewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ, ni egbi po, kɛ heyeli kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahe waaa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛɔ nitoohe lɛ fiteɔ amɛ.

english: How do I choose crop varieties that sell easily in the local market without buyers complaining?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ mlɛo ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ ewieee huhuuhu?

english: Market buyers prefer crops with appealing physical traits like smooth skins, bright color, and good size. Choosing high-demand, clean-looking varieties allows you to sell quickly at fair prices.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jarayelihe lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ sui ni ŋɔɔ tamɔ hewolo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, sui ni kpɛɔ kɛ dalɛ kpakpa. Kɛ́ ohala tsofai srɔtoi ni mɛi sumɔɔ waa ni amɛhe tse lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ amɛ oya kɛ jara ni sa.

english: Which crops can I plant that yield quickly so I do not have to wait a long time for harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛmɛ be kakadaŋŋ dani amɛkpa?

english: Short-duration crops like fast-maturing maize varieties, cowpeas, okra, and garden eggs yield within 2 to 3 months, providing early food and quick cash flow.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ ŋmãa srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tsina ŋmãa, okra kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, ni ehaa niyenii oya kɛ shika ni baa oya.

english: Are there low-maintenance crops I can plant that do not need heavy daily care to perform well?
ga: Ani tsei komɛi yɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni makwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni manyɛ makwɛ nɔ daa gbi koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Crops like cassava, sweet potatoes, and certain local bean varieties are tough and resilient. Once established, they survive poor weather better and require less frequent attention.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmei komɛi wa ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo. Kɛji ato amɛ shishi lɛ Amɛbaahi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my land is suitable for a specific crop before I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ko dani madu nii?

english: Observe your soil's texture, depth, and how well it holds water after rain. Crops perform best in rich, soft soil that drains excess water while holding enough moisture for root growth.
ga: Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ yɔɔ, bɔ ni emli kwɔ ha, kɛ bɔ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Tso lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ adara lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to clear and break up hard soil before I plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie sũ ni wa lɛ mli ni akumɔ mli dani adu nii lɛ?

english: Loosening hard soil allows rainwater to soak in and soft roots to spread easily, helping young shoots push up to the surface much faster without wasting energy.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu boteɔ mli ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa nu lɛ hiɛ oya kwraa ni amɛfiteee hewalɛ.

english: Why do some crops require much more weeding labor and effort than others before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi biɔ nitsumɔ kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo koni amɛjie jwɛi fe ekrokomɛi dani akpa amɛkpamɔ lɛ?

english: Slow-growing crops leave open soil exposed for longer, allowing weeds to grow aggressively. Fast-growing crops form a wide canopy early, shading out weeds and reducing farm labor.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tseɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ daa waa Tsei ni daa oya lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli kwɔ mra. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ baa shi.

english: What is the difference between new improved seeds like 'Asante Mo' rice and the traditional seeds we have always grown?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ tamɔ ‘Asante Mo’ ŋmãa kɛ blema dumɔwui ni wɔduɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ ateŋ?

english: Improved varieties like 'Asante Mo' are developed by plant breeders to grow faster, yield more grain per acre, and resist local pests better than traditional seeds, which are familiar but usually take longer to mature and yield less.
ga: Mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ fee tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ ‘Asante Mo’ lɛ koni amɛdara oya. Ewoɔ ŋmaa babaoo yɛ acre kome mli. ni eteɔ shi ewoɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe blema dumɔwui. ni ale Shi amɛfɔɔ be babaoo hemɔ dani amɛshwereɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my crops seem to produce smaller yields every time I plant seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Reusing saved seeds over many seasons causes them to lose their genetic vigor and accumulate seed-borne diseases. Buying fresh, certified seeds ensures your crops grow strong and produce high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii ekoŋŋ yɛ bei babaoo mli lɛ haa ehewalɛ ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa lɛ baa shi, ni ebuaa helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa lɛ anaa. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ada waa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know which rice variety is best suited for my specific piece of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmãa ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha he pɔtɛɛ ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Different varieties thrive in different conditions; for instance, some prefer flooded lowlands while others grow well in rain-fed uplands. Checking your soil's drainage and water availability with an extension officer will help you pick the right variety.
ga: Henɔi srɔtoi shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi srɔtoi amli. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, mɛi komɛi sumɔɔ shikpɔji ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ. yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni gɔji yɔɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ o-extension officer lɛ kwɛ bɔ ni nu hoɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ohala tso ni sa.

english: Are newly introduced crop varieties able to survive unexpected dry spells better than old seeds?
ga: Ani tsei srɔtoi heei ni akɛba lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni akpaaa gbɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni etsɛ?

english: Many modern crop varieties are specifically bred to mature early or tolerate drought, allowing them to produce a good harvest even if the rainy season is shorter than usual.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei srɔtoi babaoo pɔtɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya loo amɛnyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmaa kpakpa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ faaa fe bɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ moŋ.

english: Do new, high-yielding seed varieties require different farming practices than our traditional crops?
ga: Ani dumɔwui heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ biɔ okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni yɔɔ srɔto yɛ wɔ blema ŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Yes, high-yielding crops usually need precise plant spacing, timely weeding, and adequate fertilizer application to reach their full harvest potential, unlike traditional crops which may tolerate poorer management but yield much less.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo biɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛ pɔtɛɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be naa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni anyɛ akpa ŋmaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ blema ŋmɔshi nibii ni baanyɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ shi amɛwooo yibii babaoo lɛ.

english: Are new crop varieties better at resisting insect pests and plant diseases?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii heei nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai?

english: Many new varieties are bred with natural resistance to major local pests and diseases, which reduces crop losses and saves you money on chemical sprays.
ga: Afɔ kooloi heei babaoo koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa shika ni akɛshwieɔ tsofai anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are some farmers in my community giving up on farming, and how can I stay profitable?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ miikpa okwaayeli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ mi sɛɛnamɔi lɛ anɔ?

english: Farmers often leave due to rising costs, poor yields from old practices, or changing weather. You can keep your farm profitable by adopting improved seed varieties, managing your soil health, and linking directly with reliable buyers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi kpaɔ nitsumɔ yɛ shika ni yaa hiɛ lɛ hewɔ. Yibiiwoo ni ehiii kɛjɛɔ nifeemɔi momo loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli Obaanyɛ oha oŋmɔ lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake lɛ ni oooŋɔ lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ nɔ ni okɛ jarayelɔi ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ lɛ abɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Is it worth spending extra money to buy certified seeds instead of using free seeds from my neighbor?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ ooofite shika ni fa lɛ ni okɛhe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni okɛ dumɔwui ni aheee nɔ ko kɛjɛɔ okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋɔɔ baatsu nii?

english: Yes, certified seeds undergo quality checks to ensure high germination rates and uniform growth, meaning the extra upfront cost is offset by a significantly bigger and higher-quality harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni amɛhi ha lɛ mli koni ana nɔmimaa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo ni amɛdaraa daa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ŋmaa ni fa babaoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ shika ni fata he ni akɛwoɔ hiɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I find out what crop research experts in Ghana are recommending for my region?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe niiamlitaomɔ he nilelɔi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afee kɛha mikpokpaa lɛ?

english: Agricultural institutes like the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) work with local Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) officers to test crops and provide regional crop recommendations directly to farmers.
ga: Okwaafoi anitsumɔhei tamɔ Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) lɛ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (MoFA) onukpai lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛka ŋmɔshi nibii amɛkwɛ ni amɛkɛ kpokpaa nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ŋaawoi aha okwaafoi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What support is the government of Ghana offering to help small farmers access better crop varieties?
ga: Mɛɛ yelikɛbuamɔ Ghana nɔyeli lɛ kɛhaa koni eye ebua okwaafoi bibii ni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: The Ghanaian government supports farmers through national agricultural programs that provide access to subsidized seeds, fertilizers, and technical training through extension officers.
ga: Ghana Nɔyeli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi kɛtsɔ maŋ lɛ okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni haa amɛnáa dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ ŋaa tsɔsemɔ ni akɛyeɔ abuaa amɛ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ nitsulɔi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: This usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for the leaves to stay green. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps restore their green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni no yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: This is often caused by a soil disease called bacterial wilt, which blocks water from moving up the stem. Rotating your crops with non-vegetable crops and planting disease-resistant seeds helps prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ bacteria wilt lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ haaa nu lɛ aya ŋwɛi tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni jeee ŋmɔshi nibii tsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ni odu dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the sap from young leaves. Spraying the plants with a neem leaf extract or appropriate insecticide clears these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn watery and rot inside the soil before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Excess water trapped in heavy soil suffocates cassava roots and causes rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the roots.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni etsi shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli lɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Should I sow my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady. The first rainfall is often followed by a long dry period that can scorch and kill young sprouting seeds before they settle.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui bibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni egbe amɛ dani amɛgbee shi lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Is it harmful if I apply fertilizer on dry soil around my crops?
ga: Ani oshara yɛ he akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, dry fertilizer stays concentrated and can burn crop roots. Always apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after rain so the plant roots can drink it safely.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ eyi mli obɔ lolo ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers drop off without turning into young pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when trees suffer from extreme dry weather, nutrient lack, or insect attacks like mirids (capsids). Keeping shade trees and spraying at the right time protects the flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo kooloi tamɔ capsids ni tutuaa lɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ wo hulutsoo be mli ni okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: What happens if I plant my crops too close to each other in the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Crowded crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This makes them grow tall, thin, and weak, resulting in smaller harvests than properly spaced plants.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa, amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ, ni no haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ baa shi fe tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow slowly and look hungry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi tsei titrii lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni hɔmɔ miiye amɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the growing season ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do I need to place wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for swelling the underground tubers. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so the leaves catch maximum sunlight without rotting.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he ni efiteee.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which acts as food for the plant. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back the green color and keeps the crop growing strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni haa tso lɛ niyenii lɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba, ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting beans or cowpeas in the same farm make the soil better for my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas belong to a plant family that captures natural nitrogen from the air and traps it in their roots. When they grow, they release this natural fertilizer into the soil, which feeds neighboring crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas fata tsei aweku ko ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ amɛdara lɛ Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young crops need fertilizer when they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Ni eji nɔ bibioo kwraa lolo?

english: Young crops need quick nutrients to build strong root systems and healthy stems early on, giving them the foundation required to produce a bountiful harvest.
ga: Niyenii he miihia tsei bibii oya koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni wa mra. Ehaa tsei lɛ shishitoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmaa babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my crops need fertilizer to grow better?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitsei lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: When crops lack proper nutrition, their leaves often turn pale green or yellow, their stems remain weak, and their overall growth slows down significantly.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lolo. ni dalɛ fɛɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Can putting too much fertilizer on my farm harm my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, applying too much fertilizer can burn the roots of young plants, damage the soil quality, and end up killing the crops instead of helping them grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi. efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii kpakpai Ni ebaagbeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: What is the best way to drive pests and insects away from my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ ajie kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi bibii kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Keeping the farm free of weeds, practicing crop rotation, and applying recommended natural or chemical treatments will deter pests and protect your crops.
ga: Ni oooha jwɛi akafee ŋmɔ lɛ mli Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ Kɛ adebɔɔ mli loo tsofa gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ ni oootsɔ nɔ okɛtsu nii lɛ baatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: How do weeds affect the growth of my small crops?
ga: Te jwɛi lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal essential water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your crops, making the young plants weak and reducing your total harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa onibii fɛɛ ni obaawo lɛ baa shi.

english: What does good farm management actually mean for a smallholder like me?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ kɛha okwaafonyo bibioo ko tamɔ mi?

english: Good farm management involves regular weeding, applying the right plant foods on time, protecting crops from diseases, and maintaining clean field boundaries.
ga: Nɔ ni fata ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ kpakpa he ji jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa. tsofa niyenii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be naa; Nibii ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ helai ahe kɛ ŋmɔ mli husui ni he tse lɛ akwɛmɔ.

english: Why are my crops not yielding a full harvest even though I planted good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kpakpai moŋ lɛ?

english: Good seeds need continuous management, such as timely soil feeding, weed control, and adequate watering, to reach their full potential and produce high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ daa, tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni akɛhaa yɛ be naa. jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Koni anyɛ aná nibii ni afeɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my crops so they do not spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Koni tsei lɛ akafite?

english: Crops show clear physical signs when ready, such as leaves changing color, grains drying naturally, or fruits reaching a specific size and firmness.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baajie gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo kɛji amɛfee klalo, tamɔ baai ni tsakeɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ egbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. aloo aduawai lɛ yɛ dalɛ kɛ shifimɔ ni ataoɔ lɛ

english: Why should I clean up my farm immediately after completing a harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsumɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji akpa ŋmaa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Clearing farm debris after harvest removes hiding places for pests and diseases, ensuring your soil remains healthy and prepared for the next planting season.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ejieɔ hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni esaa ehe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do crops grow so well in Ghana compared to other regions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kɛ akɛto kpokpai krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Ghana has favorable tropical sunshine, warm temperatures, and fertile soils that create ideal natural conditions for many staple crops to thrive when properly cared for.
ga: Ghana yɛ hulutsoo be mli. hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni haa adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii wuji babaoo koni amɛshwere kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are starving for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil, or that waterlogging is preventing the roots from breathing. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-decomposed manure will help turn the leaves green and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha amɛdara.

english: Why should I avoid burning dry bush and grass on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashãa dani madu nii lɛ he?

english: Burning kills essential organisms in the soil and burns away natural organic matter that retains soil moisture. Leaving cut weeds to rot naturally or using them as mulch improves soil fertility and protects crops from heat.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni eshãa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi ni afo lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe loo akɛtsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii babaoo ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in damp, shaded conditions during the rainy season. Pruning extra branches to let air and sunlight through, along with removing infected pods, helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Afolɔ nibii krokomɛi ni fata he koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ hu. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa helai gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from under the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or approved sprays prevents the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ atsĩ curling naa.

english: Yam plants rely on sunlight to make food for growing tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the soil so they can catch maximum sunlight and avoids diseases caused by wet leaves touching the ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ hulu la nɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni baai ni efɔ ni taa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or if there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Regular watering at the root level and mulching help keep the soil cool and preserve the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ejaaa loo kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa yɛ shishifã lɛ he kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔii lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and moisture they need during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce long thick stems but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ tsei kakadaji ni mli tse shi eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei bibii waa lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, causing the plant to put all its energy into leaf and stem growth instead of expanding its roots into tubers.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ baai kɛ tsei ashishifãi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ shishifãi lɛ ashwã ni amɛfee bulbs lɛ

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves start turning yellow and falling off, and the ground around the base of the main stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso wulu lɛ shishi miije shishi egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do tiny insects destroy my harvested maize when I store it in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ kɛ́ mikɛto kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Grain weevils lay eggs inside maize kernels if the grain is not dried completely before storage. Drying maize until it is hard and using clean, airtight bags or storage chemicals keeps insects from destroying your harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ŋmeii baawo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii amli kɛji ŋmeii lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto. Kɛ́ oogbi ŋmãa kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛ vacuum bags loo tsofai ni he tse ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe lɛ atsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow even though I give them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu ha lɛ po lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants lack essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is holding too much water and choking the roots. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer can help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miimɔ nu babaoo mli ni ekɛmiimɔ shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: When is the best time for me to apply NPK fertilizer to my maize crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: The best time to apply the first round of NPK fertilizer is about 10 to 14 days after your maize sprouts, and a second round of nitrogen-rich fertilizer when the plants reach about knee-height.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ baatsu nii ji aaafee gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. kɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli fã ni ji enyɔ lɛ beni tsei lɛ shɛɔ aaafee amɛnaji ahe lɛ.

english: What is eating the middle leaves of my young maize plants and leaving small holes?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni eshiɔ bu bibii?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the growing tip of the plant. Spraying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening when the caterpillars are active helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ ashwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akudɔɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛyibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to grow leaves instead of holding onto its flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ewo baai moŋ fe ni eeehiɛ fɔfɔi.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide temporary shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa seedlings mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũuɔ be mli ni kookoo dumɔwui lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slanting angle of about 45 degrees helps roots form closer to the soil surface, resulting in larger, higher-yielding tubers that are easier to harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ adu cassava niji yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ aaafee digrii 45 lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo, ni amɛkpamɔ hu waaa.

english: Why do I need to make big mounds of soil before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee shikpɔŋ agbo dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose, and deep soil to expand properly. Making large mounds collects rich topsoil in one place, allowing the tubers to grow thick and long without pushing against hard ground.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ koni egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Gɔŋ agbo ko ni afeɔ lɛ buaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa lɛ naa yɛ he kome. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsiii waa.

english: How can I tell if the soil has enough moisture for me to start planting after the dry season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You can plant when the rain has soaked deep enough into the ground—about the depth of your hand—so the soil stays consistently moist for several days to support seed germination.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa—aaafee bɔ ni onine lɛ mli kwɔ ha lɛ—koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii babaoo koni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why is it dangerous to let weeds grow around my crops while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? Ani eyɛ oshara kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, soil nutrients, and water from young crops. Because weeds grow faster, they can easily choke your young plants and significantly reduce your final harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la ni he hiaa waa. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli Enɛ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ odumɔwui lɛ baagbɔjɔ, ni ehaa naagbee ŋmaa lɛ baa shi waa.

english: How can I protect my harvested maize from being destroyed by weevils in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ he koni ŋmeii akafite yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: You should thoroughly dry your maize until the kernels are very hard, then store the grains in airtight containers or specialized hermetic bags (like PICS bags) to suffocate any insect pests.
ga: Esa akɛ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotoku krɛdɛɛ ko ni atsĩ naa (tamɔ PICS kotoku) mli koni okɛmu tsɛŋemɔ helai fɛɛ ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves shrivel and curl up when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpãa amɛhe yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa leaves shrivel because the plant loses water through heat evaporation faster than its roots can pull moisture from dry soil. Curling is the tree's natural response to reduce the surface area exposed to direct sunlight and slow down water loss.
ga: Cocoa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ tso lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Curling ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hetoo ni ekɛbaa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ shi ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ baa shi.

english: Can severe sun and hot weather actually kill my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe mi-kookoo tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, intense sun can permanently damage a cocoa tree's stem and root tissue. When extreme heat dries out the tree completely, it loses its ability to transport water, causing the plant to wither and die.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afite kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kwraa. Kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli wa lɛ, tsei lɛ egbi kwraa. Tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛkɛ nu aya dɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tso lɛ baagbi ni ebaagbo.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are just thirsty or actually about to die from heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kumai miiye mi-cacao tsei lɛ kɛkɛ loo amɛmiigboi diɛŋtsɛ yɛ latsaa lɛ hewɔ?

english: Thirsty trees usually droop during the hot afternoon but recover by early morning. If the leaves become dry, brittle, and brown, and stay shriveled even overnight, the tree is under severe stress and in danger of dying.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli shi amɛhe baajɔ amɛ leebi kɛji amɛbaai lɛ egbi, amɛmli shwieɔ shi, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni ebaagbo nyɔɔŋ kome po Tso lɛ baatsɔ haomɔ ni naa wa shishi ni ebaatsɔ gbele he oshara mli.

english: Why do leaves on young cocoa trees turn brown faster than on older trees during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya fe cacao tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow roots and tender leaves that cannot store much water. Because they are not yet fully established, intense heat burns their leaves much quicker than mature trees with deep root systems.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaa bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu babaoo. Ejaakɛ amako lɛ kwraa lolo. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa baai lɛ shãa oya fe tsei ni eda ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do cocoa trees need shade trees planted around them on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ kookoo shade tsei yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Shade trees act as protective umbrellas that shield sensitive cocoa leaves from harsh sunlight, keep the farm microclimate cool, and prevent the soil from losing moisture too quickly during hot periods.
ga: Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: How does intense sunlight affect the soil around my cocoa crops?
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ saa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he. Ni mi-kookoo tso lɛ hu?

english: Strong sun bakes the topsoil, evaporating ground moisture rapidly. Dry soil hardens, making it difficult for tree roots to absorb water and nutrients, which leaves the plants weak and prone to shriveling.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ baawa. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tso shishifãi akɛ amɛaaŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni esumɔɔ ni egbo.

english: What should I do immediately if I see my cocoa farm starting to dry up under extreme heat?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mina akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ miibɔi gbimɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ shishi?

english: You should act quickly to protect the soil moisture by spreading dry leaves or grass as mulch around the base of the trees, provide temporary shade structures for young plants, and reach out for technical advice.
ga: Esa akɛ ofee oya koni obu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni oooshwie nɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛbaabɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Feemɔ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo gbɛjianɔtoo kɛha tsei bibii. ni obi ŋaawoo ni kɔɔ ŋaa he

english: Why is it important to gather extra workers quickly when a farm is suffering from drought stress?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ aná nitsulɔi krokomɛi oya nɛkɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔji kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ miikpe lɛ?

english: Heat damage spreads fast across a farm. Gathering extra help allows you to rapidly carry out urgent interventions, such as clearing weed competition and applying mulch to cover large areas before the trees burn beyond recovery.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ gbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya. Yelikɛbuamɔ krokomɛi ni ooobua naa lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ oyaiyeli nibii ni asaa lɛ tsuɔ nii oya, tamɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ ajiemɔ. kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛha hei wuji dani ashã tsei tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhi shi ekoŋŋ.

english: How can an agricultural extension officer help me when my crops are struggling in severe heat?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extension officers can assess the health of your trees, identify whether pests are worsening the heat stress, and demonstrate practical emergency techniques like shade management and soil moisture conservation.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ bɔ ni otso lɛ yɔɔ ha. Kwɛmɔ kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ haa dɔlɛ he haomɔ lɛ mli waa. ni etsɔɔ oyaiyeli he ŋaai ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii tamɔ hulutsoo nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni abuɔ he.

english: How can I prepare my farm before the dry season so direct sun does not destroy my cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba koni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akafite mi-kokoo lɛ?

english: You can prepare by maintaining adequate shade cover, keeping a layer of mulch around your plants to trap soil moisture, and regular monitoring so you can intervene before leaves start shriveling severely.
ga: Obaanyɛ osaa ohe kɛtsɔ hulutsoo be ni sa ni oookwɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii abɔle he. Tsei ni akɛbaamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ni okɛ ohe awo mli daa koni onyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli dani baai lɛ aje shishi egbo waa.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow so much faster right after I clear the weeds around them with my cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya waa beni mijie jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ? Kɛ tsɔne kuku?

english: Weeds constantly steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your crops. When you clear the weeds around your plants, you instantly remove that competition, allowing the crop roots to absorb all available nutrients and grow rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi ni bɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ojieɔ nakai akaŋshii lɛ kɛyaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why do weeds come back so quickly on my field even after I have spent days clearing them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiku amɛsɛɛ amɛba miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya nɛkɛ? Beni mikɛ gbii babaoo shwie jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ po.

english: Weed seeds sit hidden in the soil and sprout as soon as rain and sunlight hit the exposed ground. Because weeds are naturally tough and fast-growing, they take advantage of open space before your planted crops can grow big enough to shade the ground.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji nugbɔ kɛ hulu la shɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛdaraa oya. Amɛkɛ hei ni agbele lɛ tsuɔ nii dani tsei lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Will leaving a small amount of weeds near my crop roots really reduce my harvest?
ga: Ani jwɛi fioo ko ni mashi yɛ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baaha mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, even a small circle of weeds around your crop's base actively steals fertilizer and soil moisture. Clearing weeds directly around the plant root area ensures the crop gets maximum nutrition for a bigger harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi bibii po. Otsei lɛ ashishigbɛ hei po baanyɛ aju ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu. Jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ he lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ naa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛha ŋmaa babaoo.

english: How close to my crop's main stem should I clear with my machete without damaging the plant?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ machete abɛŋkɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tso titri lɛ he tɛŋŋ ni mifiteee tso lɛ?

english: You should cut weeds in a clean circle around the base of the crop, but avoid scraping or chopping the crop's main stem or shallow roots, as open wounds make the plant vulnerable to fungal diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ kooyigbɛ ni he tse ni obɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ he, shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ loo shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ he, ejaakɛ pilamɔi ni agbele naa lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ etswaa tsɛŋemɔ hela.

english: How do large farms manage to keep huge hectares of land clean when weeds grow so aggressively?
ga: Te ŋmɔji wuji feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛhaa shikpɔji wuji ahe tseɔ? Beni jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ waa lɛ?

english: Large farms divide their land into smaller manageable zones, employ dedicated labor teams on strict clearing schedules, and often combine manual machete work with cover crops or targeted herbicides to stay ahead of weed growth.
ga: Okwaafoi wuji jaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewoɔ hei bibii. ni abaanyɛ akwɛ nɔ lɛ Ha kuu ko ni ejɔɔ ehe nɔ ni kɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa ni akɛjieɔ nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii. Ni bei pii lɛ, amɛkɛ machete nitsumɔ ni akɛ niji tsuɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛtoɔ hiɛ lɛ feɔ ekome koni amɛhi shi yɛ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ hiɛ.

english: Is clearing my farm manually with a cutlass enough to keep my crops healthy as my land gets bigger?
ga: Ani miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikɛ mi niji tsuɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ be mli ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Manual cutlass clearing works very well for smaller areas, but as your land expands, weeds may grow faster than you can manually cut them. Integrating methods like mulching or mechanical slashers helps keep large fields under control.
ga: Nibii ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa kɛha hei bibii. Shi kɛ́ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli lɛɛ Jwɛi lɛ hu baanyɛ ada oya fe bɔ ni obaanyɛ okɛ onine afo amɛ. Gbɛi ni akɛfee ekome tamɔ mulching loo tsɔne ni akɛtswaa ŋmeii. Ehaa hei wuji hiɔ shi yɛ kudɔmɔ shishi.

english: Why does my land require so much continuous labor for weeding during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ biɔ nitsumɔ babaoo koni ajie jwɛi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Frequent rain combined with warm sunshine creates ideal growing conditions for weeds to multiply at double their normal speed, requiring extra hands and regular field work to prevent weeds from choking your crop.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii abɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ fataa he lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha jwɛi lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ oya fe bɔ ni sa lɛ toi enyɔ. Enɛ biɔ nitsumɔ kroko ni akɛ niji tsuɔ kɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ daa koni jwɛi akagbala onibii amli.

english: Can I leave the weeds I cut down on the soil around my crops, or will they harm my plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi jwɛi ni mifo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ? Aloo amɛbaaye mi tsei lɛ awui?

english: Leaving cut weeds on the ground around your plants creates mulch. This layer of dead leaves blocks sunlight from reaching new weed seeds, traps moisture in the soil, and turns into rich organic matter as it rots.
ga: Ni aaashi jwɛi ni afolɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ baafee ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɛkɛ baai ni egboi nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui heei ahe. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni ehaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ nii babaoo kɛ́ egbo.

english: When is the best time for me to clear weeds so my young crops do not suffer?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafo jwɛi lɛ koni miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ akapiŋ?

english: The best time to weed is when the weeds are still small and before your young crops start flowering. Clearing weeds early prevents them from overshadowing your crop and stops the weeds from setting new seeds in your soil.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ okɛjie jwɛi lɛ ji be mli ni jwɛi lɛ darako lolo kɛ dani otsei bibii lɛ baabɔi fɔmɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ, ni ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekawo dumɔwui heei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Does cutting weeds around my crops help them produce flowers and fruit faster?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni afoɔ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye abua amɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai oya?

english: Yes, clearing away weed competition frees up extra nutrients and water in the soil, which gives the plant the sudden burst of energy it needs to flower and produce healthy fruit earlier.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni he hiaa trukaa koni amɛwo fɔfɔi oya ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your soil is running low on essential food like nitrogen, or the ground is holding too much water around the roots, preventing the plant from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo tsɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ amu
