english: If your crops from the previous season grew slowly, had pale or yellowish leaves, or produced very small yields, your soil is exhausted and needs nutrient replenishment through compost or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛwo mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ miida blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ loo ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my maize crops grow thin and weak even when I add fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your maize, leaving your crop starved despite your hard work.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji otsu nii waa po.

english: What is eating holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni ayeɔ yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli ni ashiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is usually the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a pest that hides inside the main stem funnel of the maize plant to feed on tender new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji Fall Armyworm caterpillar, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ agbɛi titrii amli koni eye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomatoes turning black and soft while still hanging on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo be mli ni amɛkã wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why are my yams soft and rotting inside the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Yam rot in the soil is caused by waterlogging in poorly drained soil or fungal infections entering through tiny wounds made by soil insects or worms.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa ji nu ni ahi shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni boteɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ pilamɔi bibii ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast with large leaves that create shade, keeping the cocoa cool and retaining soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long hot spell. If seeds sprout and the rain stops, the tender seedlings will dry out and die from lack of moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why should I leave measured space between my crops instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato he kroko moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When plants are overcrowded, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in small, weak plants with low harvest yields.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔi tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress or sudden dry weather, saving their energy to survive instead of making fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ kpe. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni akɛhiɔ shi lɛ baa shi moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and burn easily. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that create living umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting the cocoa seedlings until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛshãa oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛnáa hulu la ni fa.

english: Why do my yam vines need long sticks to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tsei kakadaji koni ekɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make the energy required to swell the tuber underground. When vines climb tall on sticks, leaves spread out toward the light instead of clumping on the damp ground where they can rot or get diseased.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ aba. Kɛ́ wain tso lɛ kwɔ nine lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, a buaa a he nya ngɛ he nɛ tsɔ nɛ a ma nyɛ maa puɛ loo a ma nyɛ maa ngɔ hiɔ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my maize seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ehiii lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded, their roots and leaves fight for the same limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. This competition leaves all the plants thin and weak, resulting in small or empty ears of corn.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la ni faaa lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ toi bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually show a lack of nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant starves its older bottom leaves to send the remaining nutrients to the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ shi, baai ni egbɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje baai heei ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and lets soil-borne pests build up. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen naturally and starves maize pests.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eha shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ abua amɛhe naa Abele tsakemɔ ni ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmeii fata he lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmei mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Why does putting dry grass or leaves around my tomato plants help them stay alive in heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni akɛfataa he lɛ ji nɔ ni ebɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-tomato tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Dry leaves act as a blanket over the soil, called mulch. Mulch blocks hot sunlight from evaporating soil moisture and keeps the root area cool, allowing the tomato plant to stay hydrated with less watering.
ga: Baai ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ kuntu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Mulch tsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee sũ mli nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Eyeɔ ebuaa tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli kɛtsɔ nu fioo ni amɛhaa amɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive fertilizer. The plant drops flowers to save water and energy so it can survive harsh conditions.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground during heavy rainfall seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles in the soil without draining away. Waterlogged soil cuts off oxygen to the roots, causing them to drown and allowing decay fungi in the wet soil to attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejeee kpo. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Okɛwo nu mli ni oha ŋmeii ni egboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do armyworms hide deep inside the center whorl of my maize leaves during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ mi-abele baa lɛ teŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms hide inside the rolled center leaves during daylight to stay safe from high sun temperatures and birds. They come out during the cooler nighttime to feed on the tender leaf tissues.
ga: Fall armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ teŋgbɛ baai ni abɔle amɛhe lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa, hulu la kɛ okpoi ahe. Amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be mli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ahe fãji.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my cultivated crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild species adapted over hundreds of years to survive tough weather and thin soils. They absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than domestic crops, allowing them to overpower young crop plants if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli kooloi ni atsake amɛ yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tseee nɔ. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe shia tsei. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ tsei bibii anɔ kunim kɛji ajieee amɛ mra.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and droop when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rain floods the soil, it pushes out all the air pockets, effectively suffocating the roots so they cannot absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ fɛɛ kɛje kpo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why should I wait for the main rain season before planting my maize instead of planting right after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli dani odu ŋmãa moŋ fe ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a dry spell that can scorch new sprouts, whereas waiting for steady, reliable rains gives seeds the constant moisture they need to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baanyɛ aha tsei heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ashã lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ ni abaamɛ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni he hiaa amɛ daa koni amɛdara.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up when I clear away all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves burn easily; shade trees protect them from overheating and help keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo ni fe nine lɛ he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my cocoa trees without turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when small beneficial insects are not around to pollinate them, or when the tree is stressed by hot weather and lacks enough water or plant food to support full pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ bɛ amɛhe koni amɛha amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Aloo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa ni ebɛ nu loo tso niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and rot right while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly during cool, wet weather when damp conditions stay on the pods for too long.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod kɛ enɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ mli. Beni shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ hiɔ pod lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ

english: Why is it important for me to cut off extra branches and chupons from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ niji kɛ jwɛi krokomɛi ni fata mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Trimming unnecessary branches allows sunlight and air to pass through the tree, which keeps leaves dry to stop disease and directs energy into growing pods.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ gĩɔ koni helai akpa ni ekɛ hewalɛ aya ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my maize grow slow and thin when weeds are growing close to it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa blɛoo ni efeɔ mlɛo beni jwɛi bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your maize needs to grow big and produce healthy corn ears.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni he hiaa o-ŋmãa lɛ mli koni etsɔ agbo ni ekɛ ŋmãa toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba lɛ mli.

english: Why do my farm yields get smaller every year if I keep planting the same crop in the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ mli nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii komekomei yɛ hei komekomei pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop every season drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Will planting cassava together with cowpea help my land stay rich?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni akɛ tsina ŋmei baadu lɛ baaye abua ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Yes, cowpeas collect nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which enriches the land for surrounding crops like cassava.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmeii buaa nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa jɛmɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle he lɛ tamɔ ŋmei.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is healthy enough to support a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua nikpamɔ kpakpa?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, feels soft and moist, smells earthy, and contains broken-down leaves or earthworms that show the land is full of natural food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ehaa henumɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni mli edɔ Ehe ŋmɔlɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ. ni baai ni ekumɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ jɛmɛ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli obɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my crops wilting and dying even though the rainy season just started?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigboi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eje shishi pɛŋ lɛ?

english: Unpredictable weather patterns cause dry spells early in the season. Mulching your farm with dry grass helps hold moisture in the soil so young roots do not dry out.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ kɛ hɔmɔ baa yɛ be lɛ mli mra. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ha ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Koni shishifãi bibii akagbi

english: What fast-growing crops can I plant right now to harvest food quickly during this hunger period?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ madu bianɛ koni manyɛ makpa niyenii oya yɛ nɛkɛ hɔmɔ bei nɛɛ amli?

english: Short-duration crops like sweet potatoes, cowpeas, and early-maturing maize varieties yield food within two to three months, giving your family quick relief from food shortages.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ ŋmeii, tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ baawo yibii yɛ nyɔji enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli. Ye obua oweku lɛ ni amɛjie niyenii ni faaa lɛ oya.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce smaller tubers every time I plant on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii be fɛɛ be ni adu lɛ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the soil every season. Repeated farming without resting the land or adding animal manure drains the soil, making plants produce smaller harvests over time.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. okwaayeli ni afɔɔ feemɔ Kɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe loo akɛ kooloi aŋmei afata he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu baatsɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa baadu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture natural food from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the neighboring maize grow stronger without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ daa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa ni jara wa awo mli.

english: What causes small green worms to eat holes in my young maize leaves, and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli lɛ Ni te abaafee tɛŋŋ akpa amɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms that hide in the center of the plant during the day. Spraying natural neem leaf extracts or approved remedies early in the morning reaches and stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ gbi mli. Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaashɛ he ni ekpa dani ekpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects or viruses spread by them. Removing heavily infected plants and spraying soapy water or organic insect sprays helps protect healthy plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni akɛ nu ni akɛ samla loo organic insect spray shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from my last harvest grow into weaker plants with smaller yields than certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ dara ni amɛbatsɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni wooo yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid harvests lose their strength in the next generation. Buying fresh, certified seeds ensures all plants grow uniform, healthy, and yield high amounts of food.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ baaha tso fɛɛ tso adara pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ yibiiwoo babaoo aba.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to survive harsh conditions, so they absorb sunlight and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops unless you clear them early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛmɔɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Ja ojie amɛ oya.

english: Why do my vegetable plants yellow and rot when the rains become too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water drowns plant roots by removing air from the soil. Digging small drainage channels around your bed allows extra rainwater to flow away so roots can breathe.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei shishifãi shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔ gbɛ bibioo ko ni aaafo yɛ saatso lɛ he lɛ, nugbɔ nu baajo foi kɛya koni eha shishifãi lɛ amu.

english: Why does my harvested maize get full of insects and rot while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ ni efiteɔ beni akɛtoɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Storing maize before it is completely dry traps moisture inside, attracting tiny beetles and mold. Drying grains until they crack easily between your teeth keeps them safe in storage.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa to dani egbi kwraa lɛ, ebaamɔ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli. Egbalaa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ ogbala dumɔwui lɛ aahu kɛyashi amɛbaakumɔ oya yɛ onyanyɔji ateŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning light yellow before the corn is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to stay green and grow heavy ears. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps feed the soil so the leaves stay healthy and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eha toi lɛ awa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Baai lɛ ahe wa ni amɛyɛ eŋɔli.

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains the same nutrients from the soil and allows maize-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating your plot with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ni ebaaku tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my young vegetable plants with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the hot sun from evaporating water out of the soil. It traps moisture in the ground, keeps root temperatures cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ akajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ha shishifã lɛ mli latsaa lɛ afee fɛ̃i. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it wrong to plant my maize seeds very close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each seed proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough room and nourishment to produce big, full cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko to dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo dumɔwui wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my yam mounds when the vines are just starting to sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi yɛ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ he be mli ni wain tsei lɛ miije shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Young yam sprouts grow slowly at first and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for food and water. Clearing weeds early ensures the young vine gets all the soil nutrients it needs to climb strongly and form large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ daaa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa wain tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɔ kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfee bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is it unsafe to apply chemical fertilizer onto bone-dry soil during a dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ebɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ ni egbi tamɔ wui lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve into a form that plant roots can drink safely. When placed in bone-dry soil, the concentrated dry chemicals can burn and damage plant roots instead of feeding them.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛtsɔ mli ni amɛfee nɔ ko ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ anu shweshweeshwe. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni fãji yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ Tsofai ni egbi ni eyi obɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei shishifãi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha amɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and rot while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni miyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black, sunken bottoms on tomatoes are caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which usually happens when soil moisture fluctuates too much between dry and wet spells. Keeping the soil evenly damp helps the roots steadily feed calcium to the developing fruit.
ga: Tomato ni shishi lɛ mli edɔ ni ebote mli lɛ jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ mli baa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ tsɔ yɛ be ni hulu enyɔ shi kɛ be ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ teŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛha aduawai ni miida lɛ calcium be fɛɛ be.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and weakening the plant. Spraying neem leaf water or mild soapy water helps clear these insects so new leaves grow flat and full.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛhaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Neem baa nu loo samla ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni ajie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ. Baai heei lɛ yɛ tɔrɔmɔɔ ni amɛyi obɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when heavy rains fall for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays trapped around them without draining away. Planting cassava on raised mounds or sloping ridges allows rainwater to run off, keeping the roots well-aerated so they grow firm and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine ebɔle amɛhe. without draining out Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu lɛ atsɔ mli. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni shishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ ni amɛhe awa

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop their early flowers during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ fɔɔ mra yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers as a defense mechanism to save energy when they experience heat stress or lack water. Providing shade trees like plantains and keeping moisture in the soil helps the cocoa trees retain their flowers so pods can develop.
ga: Cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛji amɛkɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ loo nu ni faaa kpe. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo tamɔ plantains haa, ni anáa ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the ground gets waterlogged, crop roots cannot breathe air and struggle to take up nitrogen from the soil. This starves the plant, causing its green leaves to lose their color and turn yellow.
ga: Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ. ni ekɛ naagbai kpe yɛ nitrogen ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Enɛ haa ebaai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I bury my maize seeds deep in the soil when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifuɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: If seeds are buried too deep, they exhaust all their stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil to reach daylight. Planting them shallowly allows them to sprout quickly and establish strong roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Akɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni atsiɔ waa koni ana la lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants curl their leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to intense sunlight, which helps them conserve water. It is a natural defense mechanism to keep the plant from drying out.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi Eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ tsei ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why will my crop yield reduce if I plant my crops too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are overcrowded, their leaves block sunlight from reaching one another, and their roots fight for the same water and nutrients. This leaves all the plants small, weak, and low-yielding.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ bibioo, egbɔjɔ ni ewooo yibii babaoo.

english: How do weeds slow down the growth of my young cassava plants?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aha mi-cassava tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal moisture, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients from the soil before your cassava can reach them, effectively starving your young crop underground.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔtɔ, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani ŋmei lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts on the field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily and drains nitrogen from the soil. Groundnuts and other legumes trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, restoring natural fertility for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ kooloi babaoo ni ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Peanuts kɛ legumes krokomɛi Mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni akɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I throw chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated salts that burn and destroy the soft stems and fine root systems of plants when touched directly. Fertilizer should be placed in a circle a few inches away from the stem.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni shãa ni efiteɔ tsei bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ. ni ji tsei lɛ ahe kɛji akɛ amɛkpe tɛ̃ɛ Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ kokroo nɔ ni kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi.

english: Why do people cut off some branches from tomato plants while they are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi shwieɔ tomato tsei aniji komɛi anɔ be mli ni amɛmiida lɛ?

english: Trimming excess leaves and side branches directs the plant's energy and nutrients away from growing extra foliage and straight into developing bigger, healthier fruit.
ga: Baai kɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa tso lɛ baa lɛ tsiɔ baa ni fa fe nine lɛ naa. ni ekɛ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops more severely during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry periods, wild green plants dry up, driving hungry insects toward your irrigated farm. Additionally, heat-stressed crops are weaker and less capable of naturally resisting bug attacks.
ga: yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli Tsei eŋɔli ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ miigbi. Tsɔɔmɔ kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ kɛya oŋmɔ ni okɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli. Kɛfata he lɛ, tsei ni hulutsoo haoɔ amɛ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛte shi amɛwo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do seeds saved from my last harvest produce smaller yields than bought certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odase ni mihe lɛ?

english: Harvested seeds from hybrid crop varieties lose their strong traits and disease resistance in the next generation. Store-bought certified seeds are specifically bred to maintain high purity, strength, and high yield potential.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛ helai ahe sui yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛhiɛ hetsemɔ, hewalɛ, kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo mli.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when I cut down all the large trees around my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mifo tsei wuji ni bɔle miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from bigger canopy trees to protect their foliage from intense sun and heat. Without shade, direct sunlight scorches the leaves and causes moisture stress, turning them yellow and brittle.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋwɛitsu agbo ko nɔ koni ebu amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ haomɔ aba. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over so easily when heavy winds blow during the rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that stay near the top of the soil. When the soil becomes soft from rain and the plants carry heavy bunches, strong winds easily pull their shallow roots out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ efee blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ hewɔ ni tsei lɛ ená jwɛi ni mli tse. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant cassava together with maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa baadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows quickly and gets harvested early, while cassava grows slowly underground. Planting them together allows you to get two different food crops from one plot without them competing for space at the same time.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Tsei enyɔ lɛ ni ooofee ekome lɛ haa onáa niyenii tsei srɔtoi enyɔ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛyeee he akaŋ yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why are my cassava plants producing many big leaves above the ground, but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai wuji waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big leafy tops instead of sending nutrients down to expand its root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ lɛ Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni baai yɔɔ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛba shi koni ekɛgbala shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Rolling up leaves is a self-defense reaction. The maize plant reduces its leaf surface exposed to the sun to hold onto water and keep from drying out during the hottest part of the day.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji nɔ ko ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he. Abɛi tsei haa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni nu ahi mli ni eha baa lɛ akagbi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as sudden hot spells, inconsistent watering, or lack of soil nutrients. The plant drops flowers to save energy to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛmiihao, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ trukaa lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops get burned or dry up after I put fertilizer on the field during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa loo amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔji amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve into a form plants can safely drink. Applying dry fertilizer without enough water creates a salty condition in the soil that draws water out of the roots, burning the plant.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ nɔ ko ni tsei baanyɛ anu shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fata he ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni ejie nu kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni eshã tso lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my corn plants turn purple when the weather stays cold and wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ purple kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: Cold, wet soil makes it hard for young roots to absorb phosphorus from the ground. The lack of phosphorus causes a temporary buildup of sugars in the leaves, turning them a reddish-purple color.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni efɔ lɛ haa ewaa ahaa shishifãi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ fɔsfɔs kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Fosfɔs ni faaa lɛ haa sugars lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ baai lɛ amli be kukuoo ko, ni ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and hard while they are still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifee shiŋŋ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, overly shaded farms. Raindrops splash the fungus spores from the wet soil or infected leaves onto healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ loo baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot inside the soil before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when heavy rain leaves standing water in the soil, suffocating the roots, or when soil pests bite small holes into the tubers that allow waterborne rot fungi to enter.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha nu lɛ ŋmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Aloo kɛ́ kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɔ bu bibii. Tuber lɛ mlibotemɔ haa ŋmeii ni egbo ni hoɔ yɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ mli.

english: Why are my young maize plants curling their leaves and turning yellow after just three weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miihoso amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ otsii etɛ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When maize leaves curl and turn yellow early in their growth, it usually means the plant is under heat stress, lacks water, or suffers from a nitrogen shortage in the soil. Adding some nitrogen fertilizer like urea and ensuring proper watering can help them recover.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwie shi ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ latsaa he haomɔ shishi, nu efo emli, loo nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea kɛ nu ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhe awa amɛ.

english: I noticed strange white spots on my cassava leaves that I have never seen before; what is happening to my crop?
ga: Miyɔse ŋmɔtɔ komɛi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ. yɛ mi-cassava baai ni minako dã lɛ nɔ Mɛni ba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: White spots or powder on cassava leaves are typically caused by pests like cassava green mites or fungal diseases. You can control this by using pest-resistant cassava stem cuttings and spraying neem leaf extracts or recommended agricultural soap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmei green mites loo fungal helai ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ loo powda ni yɔɔ ŋmei baa nɔ lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okudɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmei tsei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooofo ni okɛ neem baa mli nu loo okwaayeli he samla ni ajieɔ yi lɛ afɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers instead of forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Flower dropping in tomatoes often happens when temperatures get too high, water supply is irregular, or there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps protect the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi lɛ mli lɛ jeee nɔ ni sa. aloo nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: What critical care do my pepper seedlings need during their first six weeks in the field?
ga: Mɛɛ kwɛmɔ ni he hiaa he baahia mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enumɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: During the first six weeks, young pepper seedlings need light shade from intense sun, regular light watering, prompt removal of competing weeds, and a mild boost of fertilizer around the third week to build strong roots.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enumɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Young pepper dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulu la ni naa wa, nu ni fa bɔ ni sa, kɛ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ ajiemɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo afata he yɛ otsi ni ji etɛ lɛ mli koni shishifãi ni wa aba.

english: My cocoa seedlings seem to be growing very slowly in their first month; is this normal?
ga: Etamɔ nɔ ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ miida blɛoo waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli. Ani enɛ ji nɔ ni ja?

english: Yes, during the first few weeks, young cocoa plants spend most of their energy growing deep underground roots before sending out new leaves. Ensuring they have shade crops like plantains nearby keeps them cool while roots develop.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli. Cacao tsei bibii kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ dani amɛtsuɔ baai heei. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ to he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are my young cowpea seedlings dying suddenly just two weeks after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ gboi trukaa yɛ otsii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Sudden seedling death is usually caused by a soil condition called damping-off, which is a fungal attack promoted by overly wet soil. Planting in well-drained soil and avoiding overwatering protects fragile young stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dampening off, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ fe nine lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ dumɔwui gboiɔ trukaa. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ, ni ajie nu babaoo kɛjɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if my crop problem is caused by insects or by poor soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ji nɔ ni kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe naagbai lɛ baa?

english: Pest damage usually shows up as bite marks, holes in leaves, or visible insects on stems. Soil problems typically affect the whole field evenly, causing widespread leaf yellowing, weak stems, or overall stunted growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ he okadi, bu yɛ baai amli, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni anaa yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ he naagbai saa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ babaoo, amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, loo amɛdaraa kwraa.

english: My maize is growing much slower than my neighbor's farm even though we planted at the same time; what could be wrong?
ga: Mi-abele lɛ daaa blɛoo kwraa fe mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ wɔdu yɛ be kome mli moŋ. Mɛni sane nɛ?

english: Slower growth often comes down to poor soil fertility, low-quality seeds, or late weeding. Using certified seeds, weeding early within the first month, and adding organic manure improves growth speed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo baa. dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ loo jwɛi ni ajieɔ blɛoo Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Jiemɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ shishijee mli. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young plantain suckers turning brown and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: The drying of bottom leaves can be a normal sign of older leaves making way for new growth, but rapid drying may indicate transplant shock or root damage. Ensure suckers are planted deep enough in moist, nutrient-rich soil.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni agbiɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ baai momoi miiha gbɛ kɛha dalɛ hee. Shi baai lɛ ni egbiɔ oya lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ atsake amɛ loo shishifãi lɛ efite. Kwɛmɔ akɛ adu ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: What should I do when my yam vines start turning black and wilting out of nowhere?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ bɔi ediŋŋ trukaa ni egbo?

english: Blackened, wilting yam vines are usually a sign of Yam Anthracnose disease, a fungal attack spread by moisture. Removing infected leaves early and avoiding working in the field while plants are wet stops it from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei ni egbo ni etsɔ ediŋŋ lɛ ji ŋmei anthracnose hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Ajie baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra Ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nitsumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be mli ni tsei lɛ edɔ lolo lɛ he. Ebaaye ebua ni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting the tender leaves until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellowing starting from the tips of lower maize leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure early in the crop's growth helps the leaves stay green and produce big ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tso lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha toii wuji aba.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dirt inside the shoot?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms hiding inside the central shoot of the maize plant. Dropping a small handful of clean dry sand, wood ash, or applying recommended natural treatments like neem oil into the shoot can suppress them early.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋã ni egbi ni he tse, tso mli sũ loo adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni ajieɔ yi tamɔ neem fɔ tsu nii yɛ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa mra.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully grown and ready to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 8 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off. You can carefully dig around one plant to check if the roots are thick enough before harvesting the whole field.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo shɛɔ shweremɔ he yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli. Okɛ hiɛdɔɔ adu tso kome koni ona kɛji shishifãi lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to produce food, which flows down into the ground to build large, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Pepper flowers often drop off when the soil gets too dry, when the weather is extremely hot, or if too much nitrogen fertilizer was used. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛji akɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ mulch woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do elderly farmers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts before planting maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko baakɛɛ mi akɛ midu tsina loo ŋmeii dani midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas out of the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plants die, this nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as free natural fertilizer for the next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my tomato plants with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground during hot days, stops weeds from taking over, and keeps rain from splashing disease-causing soil onto tomato leaves.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nɔ. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekashwie sũ ni kɛ hela baa lɛ nɔ yɛ tomato baai anɔ.

english: This rot is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, damp, and shady environments. Pruning extra shade tree branches to let in sunlight and clearing infected pods quickly stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ hulutsoo kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ hulutsoo be kroko koni hulu la aba ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa oya kɛya ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce very thin roots when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems too close together causes them to compete aggressively for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Giving each plant proper distance ensures the roots have enough space and energy to grow thick and healthy.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko kɛ ehe teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers during dry spells to save water and energy. Without enough soil moisture, the tree prioritizes its own survival over producing cocoa pods.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala nɔ fe ni eeefee kookoo ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cassava plants naturally shed leaves in dry weather to reduce water loss. Once rainfall resumes, the plant uses stored energy in its roots to sprout fresh green leaves.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ.

english: How does heavy rain during flowering affect my maize crop?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ saa ŋmãa he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excessive rain during flowering can wash away pollen from maize tassels before it reaches the silks, resulting in poorly filled corn cobs with missing grains.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ahe dani amɛyashɛ siliki lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ bɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why do leafy green vegetables like kontomire grow so quickly after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ contomire lɛ daa oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The initial rains release trapped nitrogen in warm soil, giving leafy greens an immediate boost of essential nutrients needed for rapid leaf growth.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ jieɔ nitrogen ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ kpo. Amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ehaa aduawai ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni baai lɛ adara oya.

english: Why do yam vines need to climb up tall stakes or trees instead of growing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei akwɔ tsei loo tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam vines climb naturally to expose more leaves to sunlight, which allows the plant to make more food energy and build larger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la babaoo he. Enɛ haa tsei feɔ niyenii hewalɛ babaoo. ni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji

english: Why do my plantain suckers grow slowly right after I cut down the main harvest stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daa blɛoo beni mifo tso lɛ yitso titri ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Before harvest, plantain suckers receive nutrients directly from the main stem. Once it is cut, the sucker must rely entirely on its own roots, causing a brief slowdown in visible growth.
ga: dani abaakpa Dumɔwui lɛ amli nu lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji afo lɛ pɛ Esa akɛ sucker lɛ kɛ ehe afɔ̃ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ kwraa. Enɛ haa dalɛ ni anaa lɛ baa shi fioo.

english: What causes cocoa trees to produce smaller pods in some seasons compared to others?
ga: Mɛni haa cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ bei komɛi amli fe ekrokomɛi?

english: Pod size depends heavily on rainfall during early pod development. Dry weather while young pods are forming restricts nutrient flow, resulting in smaller mature pods.
ga: Pod lɛ dalɛ damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ pod lɛ shishijee bei amli lɛ nɔ waa. Shihilɛi ni mli egbi be mli ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ lɛ tsiɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii momo lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree when there is too much shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive shade creates high humidity and dark conditions that allow the black pod fungus to thrive and spread quickly among cocoa pods during rainy periods.
ga: Shade babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ baa. Enɛ haa black pod fungus lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when soil temperatures are too high or water is scarce. Heat stress causes the plant to shed flowers before they can form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ jɛmɛ. Dɔlɛ haa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How does planting crops on raised earth mounds help them in wet soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Raised mounds lift crop roots above standing water, allowing oxygen to reach the roots so the plants do not suffocate or rot in waterlogged soil.
ga: Gɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ woɔ tsei shishifãi anɔ kɛyaa nu ni yɔɔ dioo lɛ nɔ. koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe Enɛ ji koni tsei akafo loo amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or banana trees planted nearby to protect them from intense heat and keep moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe jɔɔ, tamɔ dumɔwui loo banana tsei, ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi cacao tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow starting from the bottom of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant turn green again and produce good ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmei toi kpakpai.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water suffocates them because they cannot breathe in soggy soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli, ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ejaakɛ enyɛŋ emu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants before any tomatoes start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets too stressed by high heat or a lack of water. Keeping the soil moist by placing dry grass around the roots as mulch helps the plant hold onto its flowers and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao waa kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap from the young leaves. Spraying the plants with neem oil mixed with mild soapy water helps clear these insects.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Akɛ neem fɔ ni akɛ nu ni mli edɔ efutu mli lɛ shwieɔ tsei anɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ajie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛya.

english: Yam plants need their leaves high up in the sunlight to make energy for building big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground where diseases easily spread.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni baa lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Cowpeas and beans pull natural nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the cowpea plants die, that nitrogen stays in the soil as free food for the next crop of maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsina tso lɛ gbo Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches of fruit at the top. Supporting the fruiting trees with bamboo poles or strong wooden forks prevents the wind from pushing them over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo tso ni akɛfee ŋmeii ni wa fi aduawai tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ akatsɔ amɛmli.

english: Why does keeping shallow water in my rice field stop weeds from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ haaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Rice plants can grow with their roots covered in water, but most broadleaf land weeds drown and die under water. Flooding the field naturally smothers weeds so the rice can get all the sunlight and soil food.
ga: Omɔ tsei baanyɛ ada ni nu ehà amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Shi jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ nu shishi ni amɛgboiɔ. Nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa no hewɔ lɛ ŋmãa lɛ nine shɛɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my garden egg plants wilt suddenly during the hot afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is caused by bacterial wilt, a sickness inside the plant's stem that blocks water from traveling up to the leaves. Changing the crop location every season stops this disease from building up in the dirt.
ga: Bacteria ni shwieɔ shi trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ jɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ ji hela ko ni yɔɔ tso shishi ni haa nu nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ otsake he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ daa be lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akabua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my crop fertilizers and farm chemicals becoming so expensive to buy these days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ mli tsofai kɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai lɛ jara wa waa yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli lɛ?

english: Most chemical fertilizers are imported from other countries, making their prices change with fuel and shipping costs. You can reduce how much you spend by mixing chemical fertilizers with animal manure or compost made from dried crop waste.
ga: Akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo jɛɔ maji krokomɛi anɔ. Enɛ haa jara lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ bɔ ni fuɛl kɛ gbɛfaa he nyɔmɔwoo lɛ ji lɛ naa. Obaanyɛ oba shika nɔ kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni okɛfutuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ tsei ni egbi ni egbo lɛ feɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I keep my farm soil fertile without buying expensive bags of fertilizer every season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee fɛo ni miheee ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kotokui daa afi?

english: Planting legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts in rotation with crops like maize naturally puts nitrogen back into the soil. When these plants decay, they feed the soil for your next crop for free.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ tsei nɛɛ fite Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ yaka.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry weather to save water and protect itself from dying. The plant stays alive by resting and will quickly grow fresh leaves once the rainy season begins.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ. Koni okɛ nu aba shi ni obu ohe kɛjɛ gbele he. Tsei hiɔ shi kɛtsɔ hejɔɔmɔ nɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ daa oya beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small ears even after I spend money caring for them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ toi bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ mifite shika kɛkwɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Maize plants need plenty of water and food right when the tassels and silks appear. If the plant lacks water or soil nutrients during this short stage, it cannot grow full, large corn ears.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii babaoo he miihia abɛi tsei kɛji akɛ ŋmeii kɛ siliki lɛ je kpo pɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be kukuoo nɛɛ mli lɛ, enyɛŋ ekwɛ ŋmãa toi wuji lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep, tough root systems designed to survive harsh conditions. They quickly steal water and nutrients from the soil before your cultivated crops get a chance to drink.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni afee koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ naa hegbɛ amɛnuɔ.

english: Is it better for me to grow food crops my family can eat or focus only on cash crops like cocoa?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ niyenii ni miweku lɛ baanyɛ aye loo mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama shika nibii tamɔ kookoo pɛ nɔ?

english: Growing a mix of both is safest. Cash crops provide large lump sums of money during harvest, while food crops give your family daily meals and quick money at the local market to cover immediate expenses.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ ooodu nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni akɛfutu mli. Shika ŋmɔshi nibii haa anáa shika babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ haa oweku lɛ daa gbi niyenii kɛ shika oya yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ koni ekɛwo shika ni he hiaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ he nyɔmɔ.

english: Which short-season crops can I plant to make quick income when farm money is low?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo manyɛ madu koni maná shika oya kɛ́ ŋmɔ mli shika faaa?

english: Vegetables like pepper, okra, and garden eggs take only two to three months to produce food. They allow you to harvest and sell multiple times in a season to recover your investment quickly.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ ŋmeii, okra kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii heɔ nyɔji 2-3 pɛ dani amɛfeɔ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ni ohɔ̃ɔ shii abɔ yɛ be kome mli koni onine ashɛ shika ni okɛwo mli lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Why does food brought from outside our district sell cheaper than the crops I grow on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ahɔ̃ɔ niyenii ni akɛbaa kɛjɛɔ wɔkpokpaa lɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ jara waaa fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Large commercial farms outside often use big machines to grow massive quantities of food at once, which lowers the cost for each crop. Small local farms cost more per plant because work is mostly done by hand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, jarayeli ŋmɔji wuji ni yɔɔ kpo nɔ lɛ kɛ tsɔnei wuji tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ niyenii babaoo yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ haa shika ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Kuu lɛ mli ŋmɔji bibii lɛ aheɔ shika babaoo yɛ tso kome mli ejaakɛ akɛ niji tsuɔ nitsumɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so fast before I can carry them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continue to breathe and soften quickly after being picked, especially under hot sun. Harvesting early in the morning and keeping the fruits in well-ventilated, shaded crates slows down rot.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ emuɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo oya beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ. Titri lɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akpa aduawai lɛ leebi maŋkpa ni akɛto adekai ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efite sɛɛ.

english: Why are insects still destroying my vegetables even after I spray them with chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-vegetables lɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ nɔ moŋ?

english: Insects can build resistance if you use the same chemical spray repeatedly. Switching between different types of pest treatments and spraying early in the morning makes the application much more effective.
ga: Kplukai baanyɛ aná hewalɛ ni tsiɔ hela naa kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii shii abɔ. Ni atsakeɔ tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛtsaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ateŋ Ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ haa akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain stems weaken and fall over at the base even when there is no heavy wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛgbee shi yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko bɛ po lɛ?

english: Plantain stems often fall over because of damaged roots or weak bases, usually caused by pests like banana weevils, root rot from excess water, or carrying a fruit bunch that is too heavy without a support pole.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ efite loo amɛshishi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ banana ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ nu ni fa fe nine mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. aloo ni ehiɛ aduawai akuu ko ni tsii tsɔ ni tso ko bɛ ni fiɔ sɛɛ

english: How can I prevent my fruiting plantain trees from bending and snapping at the bottom?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi midumɔwui ni woɔ yibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakumɔ ni amɛkumɔ yɛ shishigbɛ?

english: You can prop up your plantain trees using strong wooden or bamboo poles placed firmly under the fruit bunch stem to absorb the weight and keep the main stem upright until harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ shishi lɛ aye abua dumɔwui lɛ koni ekɛjie muji lɛ ni eha tso titri lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ kɛyashi kpamɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves at the base of my plantain tree turning dark and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ shishi lɛ mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ?

english: As plantains grow, their lowest leaves naturally turn dark brown and die. However, if many leaves darken prematurely, it could indicate water stress, nutrient deficiency, or leaf spot diseases like Sigatoka.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ Ebaai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgboiɔ. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai babaoo fee duŋ mra lɛ, May tsɔɔ nu he haomɔ. Niyenii ni esaaa loo baa mli hela, tamɔ Sigatoka.

english: Do I need to clear all existing trees and wild plants before planting plantains on a new plot of land?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni majie tsei kɛ koo mli tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ momo lɛ dani madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ?

english: You do not need to remove every large tree, as some shade preserves soil moisture, but clearing dense brush around planting holes prevents weeds from competing with young plantains for light and nutrients.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni ojie tso agbo fɛɛ tso. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulutsoo fã ko yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Shi kɛ́ ajie brɔshi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛbɔle dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye akaŋ kɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ koni amɛná la kɛ niyenii kpakpai.

english: Can I plant plantains on land where other trees like cocoa were already growing before I started?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsei krokomɛi, tamɔ kookoo, kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ dani mabɔi dumɔ?

english: Yes, plantains grow very well alongside cocoa trees because they thrive in similar soil conditions and plantain leaves provide helpful shade for young cocoa plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ cocoa tsei ahe ejaakɛ amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ. Ni plantain baai lɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Why does my plantain farm look green and healthy at first, but growth slows down after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ shishijee mli lɛ? Shi dalɛ lɛ baa shi yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Young plantains initially grow fast using nutrients stored in the planting sucker, but as they grow bigger, they require high levels of nutrients like potassium and nitrogen from the soil to sustain that growth.
ga: Shishijee lɛ, dumɔwui bibii lɛ baatsɔ niyenii ni akɛto tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli lɛ nɔ amɛda oya. Shi kɛ amɛdara lɛ Amɛbiɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa babaoo tamɔ potassium kɛ nitrogen hu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛha nakai dalɛ lɛ aya nɔ.

english: What causes the bottom base of a plantain stem to turn soft and dark black?
ga: Mɛni haa plantain tso shishi feɔ ediŋŋ?

english: A dark, soft stem base is usually a sign of stem rot caused by water standing around the plant roots for too long or fungal infections triggered by poor drainage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ shishi ni yɔɔ ediŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji tso lɛ shishi ni nu ni ebɔle ehe lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he okadi. tso shishifãi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Will planting a lot of plantain suckers very close together give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani plantains babaoo ni madu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: Planting too close forces the plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stems that fall easily and produce much smaller bunches.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tsei lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni gbeeɔ shi oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ baa.

english: How do I select the best plantain sucker from an old farm to start a new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Choose 'sword suckers'—young shoots with narrow, blade-like leaves and a broad stem base—because they form strong root systems much faster than 'water suckers' that have broad leaves.
ga: Halamɔ ‘tsobii bibii’, ni ji tsei bibii ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ ŋmei kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni mli wa oya kwraa fe ‘nu mli ŋmeii’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know when an old plantain stand needs to be cleared and replaced with fresh plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ majie dumɔwui momoi ni mikɛ ehee awo najiaŋ?

english: After a main plantain stem fruits and dies, new shoots grow from the same spot, but over several years the root system becomes weak, produces smaller bunches, and easily topples over, showing it is time to replant.
ga: Beni dumɔwui titrii lɛ wo yibii ni amɛgboi sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii heei baakwɛ̃ kɛjɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Shi beni afii lɛ hoɔ lɛ Shishifã gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Yɛ tsei bibii ni akuɔ ashwieɔ shi oya mli lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I leave them under full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mishi amɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and small roots that cannot handle direct heat. Planting them under nurse crops like plantains provides shade and keeps the moisture in the soil so the young trees can mature safely.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ nurse tsei tamɔ plantains shishi lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ada shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants start curling up and stopping the fruits from forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiikpa aduawai ni baa lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually a reaction to tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites that spread viruses. The plant curls its leaves to protect itself, but this stops proper photosynthesis and fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Shi ekpaa fotosintɛsis kɛ aduawai adalɛ ni sa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize plant turning yellow from the middle outward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ kɛmiiya kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize is a natural warning sign that the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen gives plants their green color, so when it runs low, the plant moves what remains to the newer top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nɔ ko fioo pɛ eshwɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baajie baai ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it better for me to plant groundnuts on the field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nitrogen, leaving the ground weak. Groundnut plants pull nitrogen out of the air and put it back into the earth through their roots, restoring the soil naturally for the next planting season.
ga: Abele haa nitrogen babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ egbɔjɔ. Peanut tsei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: What does adding dried chicken manure do inside the soil to make my crops grow faster?
ga: Mɛni tsina ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ oya?

english: Chicken manure feeds useful microscopic soil life and slowly releases vital nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus while improving the soil's ability to hold onto water.
ga: Kooloi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus fiofio. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Which way am I supposed to insert a cassava stem cutting into the ground when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, te esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei tsei ni afo lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should always be planted with the buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the new sprouts to struggle to find the light, resulting in weak growth and fewer tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu amɛ kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui heei lɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛná la. Enɛ haa edalɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why does leaving weeds around my crops make my harvest so small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ha mikpamɔ lɛ ba shi kwraa.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. When weeds grow close to your crops, they steal food from the soil that your main plants need to form big fruits or tubers.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni otso titri lɛ he hiaa koni ekwɛ aduawai wuji loo bulbs lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plow or clear my land when the ground is soaked right after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ matsuɔ nii loo mafoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ?
