english: Working wet soil damages its structure and causes it to dry into hard clumps. This makes it difficult for seed roots to breathe and spread deep into the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baafite tsɔne lɛ ni ebaaha egbi ni etsɔ ŋmeii ni wa. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛha dumɔwui shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the stems before turning into tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi dani ebafeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat or dry soil. Dropping flowers is the plant's way of conserving energy to survive until conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni ehi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the young shoots growing around my main plantain tree to remain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ ni amɛkafite?

english: If too many plantain suckers grow around one mother plant, they fight with each other for water and plant food. Removing extra suckers leaves enough energy for the main stem to produce a big, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ fɔlɔ kome he lɛ, Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli yɛ amɛteŋ. Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen out of the soil, so adding fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores the nutrients plants need to stay green and produce big ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ toi wuji aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field without plantain trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni dumɔwui ko bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting plantains alongside young cocoa creates living shade umbrellas that protect the seedlings from scorching heat until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ

english: This leaf damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the corn plant during the day and feed on the soft growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do I need to lift yam vines off the ground with wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso awo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers. Staking holds their leaves up high to catch more sunlight, which allows the plant to produce more energy and grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ gɔŋ. Staking haa ebaai lɛ daraa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekwɛ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava roots start turning dark and spoiling just two days after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔi diŋ kɛ fitemɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni akpa lɛ?

english: Once cassava roots are dug out of the soil, they react rapidly with oxygen in the air and break down inside. Leaving them safely in the ground until you are ready to sell or process them prevents early spoilage.
ga: Kɛji ajie ŋmei shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsuɔ nii oya ni efiteɔ yɛ mli. Kɛ́ oshi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaahɔ̃ɔ loo obaatsu he nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkafite oya.

english: Extreme heat or sudden dry spells stress tomato plants, forcing them to drop their flowers to save water. Keeping the soil consistently damp helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ ajie fɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni nu akafite. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I wait until the main rainy season settles before sowing my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Planting after just one early rain trick seeds into germinating, but if a dry period follows, the delicate new roots will dry up and die before the real rains arrive.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome pɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Shi kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Shishifãi heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔ diɛŋtsɛ aba.

english: Why do my vegetables grow better when I mix animal manure into the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Manure feeds beneficial soil organisms and acts like a sponge, helping sandy soil hold onto water and nutrients so crop roots can easily feed during dry weather.
ga: Manure haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ana niyenii yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ yɔɔ lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and wrinkling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites. As they feed on the leaves, they deform them and can spread plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ amɛye baai lɛ Amɛfeɔ shwɛm ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwã tsei amli.

english: How do weeds growing near my crops hurt my harvest yield?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ masɛi lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, root space, sunlight, and soil nutrients. When weeds take these resources, your crops become weak and yield much less food.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, shishifãi, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ jwɛi ye nibii nɛɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaawo yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Yam tubers need deep, soft, and loose soil to stretch down and grow large. Making mounds prevents water from pooling around the roots, which stops the yam from rotting, and makes it easier to harvest later.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛgbala amɛhe ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ ko lɛ, ebaatsi nu ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ naa, ni no baaha sweet potato lɛ akafite. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaakpa sɛɛ mli

english: Why should I cut cassava stems into short pieces instead of planting the whole long stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmei mli kukuji lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu tso muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cutting the cassava stem into short pieces (about 20 to 30 centimeters) forces the plant to concentrate its strength on forming multiple root nodes close together, leading to more and bigger cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ afo ŋmei tso lɛ mli kukuji (aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30) lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi babaoo ni kwɛɔ amɛhe lɛ anɔ, ni no haa ŋmei tso lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why is it important to cut off extra small suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ehe miihia ni ajie mi plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: The extra suckers act like hungry children competing for the mother plant's food, water, and sunlight. Pruning them leaves only one or two strong suckers, ensuring your main plant produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbekɛbii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ otso titri lɛ baawo tso wuji babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why do people advise me to leave some big shade trees on my land when planting new cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mashi tsei wuji yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu kookoo hee lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct hot sun. Leaving big shade trees protects young cocoa from severe heat during the dry Harmattan season and keeps moisture in the soil so the plants stay green.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ tsei ni eda lɛ haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ, ebuɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he yɛ Harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ mli, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: What is causing small holes in my corn leaves and little green worms inside the funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ amli

english: That is caused by Fall Armyworms, a pest that eats young maize leaves and shoots. You can protect your field by applying safe pesticides or putting a small handful of clean dry sand or wood ash in the center of the young plant to choke the worms early.
ga: Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔji lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo ŋã ni egbi loo tso sũ ni mli tse ni okɛbaawo dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛgbe kooloi lɛ mra.

english: Why does covering the ground around my pepper plants with dry grass help them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool and traps moisture during hot days. It also stops weeds from growing and turns into rich organic manure as it breaks down.
ga: Mulching (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Ehaa jwɛi hu shwereɔ, ni kɛ́ efite lɛ, ebafeɔ humus ni jara wa.

english: Yellow leaves mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for leaf growth. It can also happen when too much water drowns the roots, preventing them from feeding properly.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ adara Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo ha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi, ni no haaa amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before any tomatoes start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without making fruit when the weather becomes too hot, when the soil gets too dry, or when tiny pests bite the flower stems. Keeping the soil evenly damp helps the flowers stay attached and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ŋmɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why shouldn't I scatter fertilizer on dry ground just before a heavy rain hits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: A heavy rain will wash away loose fertilizer before your crops can drink it up. This wastes your money and sends the plant food away into streams. It is best to apply fertilizer when the ground is already moist and lightly cover it with soil.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nuɔ lɛ. Nakai feemɔ baaha ofite shika ni okɛ tsei aniyenii baaje kpo kɛya faa lɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo ni okɛ sũ aha nɔ fioo.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year without changing crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ abaadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi ni atsakeee ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the same spot continuously drains the exact same nutrients out of the ground and allows maize-eating pests to multiply in the soil. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts puts natural nitrogen back into the soil and keeps it healthy.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ ayiɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to use pegs and lines to space out my cocoa trees instead of planting them anywhere I like?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ ŋtayaai kɛ ŋtayaai atsu nii ni mikɛgbala mi-cacao tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he ni misumɔɔ?

english: Using pegs ensures each crop gets enough space, sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without fighting its neighbors. Proper spacing also makes it easier to walk through the farm to clean, spray, and harvest.
ga: Pegs ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ awuu. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa hu haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaatsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔ lɛ mli saamɔ, shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant too many seeds close together in one small area?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he bibioo kome?

english: Overcrowding forces plants to fight for the same water and soil food. This makes them grow tall and weak with thin stems, producing fewer fruits or pods because they are starving.
ga: Nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye niyenii, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ kome. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnáa ŋmeii bibii. Enɛ haa aduawai loo ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa yɛ hɔmɔ hewɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn yellow and burn when there are no shade trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa be mli ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have soft, tender leaves that cannot handle direct, hot sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains provides living umbrellas that shield the cocoa leaves from sun damage while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shade ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo baai ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Can I plant cassava in the middle of my young cocoa farm to get quick food, or will it harm the cocoa?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ bibioo ko teŋ. Mihe ni mana niyenii oya? Aloo ebaaye kookoo awui?

english: Cassava grows very fast and drinks a lot of soil water and nutrients. If planted too close to young cocoa, the cassava will choke the young trees and steal the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Cassava daa oya waa ni eŋɔ shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ cocoa bibii lɛ tsɔ lɛ, Cassava lɛ shwieɔ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ ni ejuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tight like tubes during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense trick to trap moisture inside and prevent the burning afternoon sun from drying out the plant completely.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. ni etsi shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha tsei lɛ agbi kwraa

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before growing into full peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani etsɔ pepper kwraa lɛ?

english: Plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme sun heat, lack of water, or too much fertilizer. It is the plant's way of saving energy to stay alive.
ga: Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛnu he akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ fe nine, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Eji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni tsei ahi shi.

english: Why does cassava manage to stay green during long dry seasons while my maize dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mi-ŋmei lɛ gboɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava stores water and food in deep underground tubers, allowing it to survive long dry spells, whereas maize has shallow roots that dry out quickly when rain stops.
ga: Cassava kɛ nu kɛ niyenii toɔ ŋmeii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, abele yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, egbiɔ oya.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year even though I work just as hard on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Ni mitsuɔ nii waa nakai nɔŋŋ?

english: Soil gets exhausted when crops draw out nutrients year after year without rest or manure. Without feeding the soil with compost or resting the land, the crop yield naturally reduces over time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi beni tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii afi fɛɛ afi ni amɛhejɔɔmɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli lɛ. ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ loo akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off the extra shoots and dead branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifo mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ yitsei kɛ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unwanted branches that waste the tree's energy. It lets light and fresh air into the branches, which stops black pod disease and encourages the tree to produce bigger pods.
ga: Kpojiemɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni ataooo ni haa tso lɛ hewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ la boteɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa black pod hela lɛ ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Do high weeds around my crops harm them, or do they protect the soil from sun heat?
ga: Jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔle Miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ ji oshara kɛha amɛ. Aloo amɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu dɔlɛ he?

english: Weeds act like thieves that steal water, fertilizer, and light directly from your crops. Leaving weeds unchecked slows down your crops' growth and invites pests into your farm.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ oshi jwɛi lɛ ni okwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo, ni ebaafɔ̃ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nine kɛba oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and have broad leaves that provide vital shade and hold moisture in the soil, helping the young cocoa survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni haa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to provide long wooden poles for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko lɛ? Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves toward sunlight to produce energy. Lifting the vines off the damp ground prevents leaf rot, exposes more leaves to sunlight, and allows the plant to send more energy down to grow bigger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya hulu la lɛ he koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ owó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite. Ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo. ni ehaa tso lɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow in the middle of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which gives plants their rich green color. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the plant build healthy leaves and form strong corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai ni wa kɛ ŋmãa ni mli wa.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ŋmãa dumɔ he afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop loves and allows pests that feed on it to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ edaa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops at the same time I put the seeds in the dirt?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ be kome too mli ni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Applying strong chemical fertilizer directly against a seed can burn it before it sprouts. It is best to wait until the plant germinates and develops roots, or place the fertilizer a few inches away from the seed hole.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ wo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni eshishifãi ewo. Aloo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo he ko ni kɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi.

english: How do I know if the early rain in April is enough for me to plant my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ April shishijee gbɛ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: A single heavy rain after a dry season can be misleading because the subsoil remains dry. You should check if the soil is moist at least hand-deep; planting too early risks seeds germinating and then drying up if a dry spell follows.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shikome yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ alaka mɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ mli egbi. Esa akɛ okwɛ kɛji kɛ hoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tamɔ nine. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ba.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites sucking sap from under the leaves. Treating the plants early with insecticidal soap or recommended sprays stops the damage before fruit growth halts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Akɛ samla loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ atsu tsei ahe nii mra. Ehaa nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ kpaa dani aduawai lɛ kpaɔ kwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my pepper plants before turning into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiitsɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers often drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil dries out completely, or due to sap-sucking insects. Ensuring consistent watering during hot spells helps flowers set into peppers.
ga: Fɔfɔi fɔɔ shigbeemɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo yɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ahewɔ Nu ni oooha amɛ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do weeds lower my crop yield even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and steal essential soil nutrients, sunlight, and root space. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food and light they need to produce a full harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to cassava roots if I leave them in the soil long after they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmei shishifãi anɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ beni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: While cassava can stay stored underground for a while, keeping it in the soil too long causes the roots to become woody, fibrous, and lose their starch quality, making them difficult to eat or process.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmei ato shikpɔŋ shishi be fioo moŋ, Shi kɛji akɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee tsei, amɛhe afee ŋmeii ni amɛhe ejɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ ayeɔ loo atsuɔ he nii.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa plants turning yellow and drying up in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need shade trees or plantain plants grown nearby to block harsh sunlight and keep the surrounding soil moist until the cocoa roots grow deeper.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ekɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruit when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries out the pollen inside tomato blossoms, which prevents the flowers from fertilizing properly. When fertilization fails, the plant naturally drops the flowers to save its water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ aná fɔmɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji fɔmɔ nii lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot under the ground when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excessive rain water stays stagnant in the soil for too long, it suffocates the roots and encourages fungal diseases that cause rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii helai ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants suddenly covered in ragged holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii ni etse ehe lɛ ehà mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. These pests hide inside the deep funnel of the maize stem during the day and eat the fresh leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei amli ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni oye baai heei lɛ dani amɛje kpo

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the undersides of young leaves, or from a virus transmitted by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ amli

english: Why do my green orange fruits keep falling off the tree before they are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibii ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Citrus trees drop young fruits when they experience water stress during dry spells or when the tree has produced more fruits than its branches and nutrients can support.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛ́ amɛbote nu mli haomɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Aloo beni tso ko woɔ yibii babaoo fe bɔ ni eniji kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the small shoots to keep growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Allowing too many shoot suckers to grow forces them to compete with the mother plant for food and water. Cutting away extra suckers ensures the main plant gets enough nutrients to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tso lɛ yibii babaoo gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ tsei agboi ni tsii.

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to create food for the growing tuber. Staking lifts the vines off the ground, increasing light exposure and preventing leaf diseases caused by contact with damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha bulbs ni miida lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. Ha la ni tsoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni otsi foliar helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni akɛkpeɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ naa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my farm make the soil better for my maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant decomposes, it leaves natural nitrogen fertilizer in the soil for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei fite Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃.

english: Why can rice plants grow in standing water while my corn crops drown and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special hollow tubes inside their stems and roots that channel air down from above the water level, allowing the roots to breathe even when completely submerged.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni kɔɔyɔɔ jɛɔ nu lɛ ŋwɛi kɛbaa shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmuɔ kɛji amɛbote nu lɛ shishi kwraa po.

english: Why should I buy certified crop seeds from registered seller groups instead of just planting seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ? Mohu ɔ, mo du wuhi nɛ a je kpami be nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ pɛ.

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred to resist local pests, tolerate drought, and give higher yields. Seeds saved from past harvests slowly lose these strengths, leading to weaker plants and smaller yields over time.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ naa ni ehaa yibii babaoo Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Hewalɛi nɛɛ baafite Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What will happen to my pepper crops if I plant them too close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When pepper plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition causes tall, thin plants that produce very few peppers and catch fungal diseases easily.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ, ni ŋmeii helai yeɔ amɛ oya.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that create living shade, keeping the young cocoa plants cool and moist during their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo. Ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants curl up tightly into tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during extreme heat to protect themselves from losing too much water. It is the plant's natural way of saving moisture until the air cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Eji tsei adebɔɔ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell before the real rainy season starts. If seeds sprout during that brief wet period, the hot dry days that follow will kill the young seedlings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ baaje shishi Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ, gbii ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ baagbe dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do my yams grow short, twisted, and small when I plant them in hard soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ kuku, etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ bibioo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose earth to push downward and expand smooth tubers. Hard or unplowed soil blocks the root growth, forcing the yam to bend and stop expanding.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni ekɛtsi shi ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ akwɛ̃. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni atsuuu he nii lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛmli shwereɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young corn turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves mean your soil lacks nitrogen fertilizer. The corn plant takes whatever nitrogen it has from its older bottom leaves and sends it to the top to keep growing new leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele tsei lɛ heɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni amɛyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni egbɔ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛya nɔ amɛkwɛ baai heei.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers before growing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ shwie efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi dani midu tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when the weather gets too hot or when they do not get enough water. Heat stress causes the plant to drop flowers to preserve its energy for survival.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo ahaaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans together with my cassava help my soil stay rich?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmei duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii baa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that feed the soil by trapping nitrogen gas from the air and storing it in their roots. This acts as a natural fertilizer for nearby cassava crops.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ nitrogen gas ni amɛmɔɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my stored dry corn grains turn into dust and develop tiny holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ sũ ni eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: This destruction is caused by maize weevils—small insects that lay eggs inside dry corn. When the eggs hatch, the tiny larvae eat the grain from the inside out, turning the core into powder.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei ŋmei. Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi bibii ni woɔ wɔji yɛ ŋmãa ni egbi mli. Kɛji wɔji lɛ fɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. ni otsɔ mli lɛ mli powda

english: How do I know the right distance to leave between my crops when planting them in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni sa ni kã ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ kɛ́ midu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Proper spacing ensures crops do not compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Leaving enough space between plants allows each crop to develop strong stems and produce a bigger harvest.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akaŋ. Kɛ́ ashi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná shishifãi ni wa ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Will planting more crops closely together give me a bigger harvest from my small piece of land?
ga: Nibii babaoo ni madu yɛ he kome lɛ baaha manyɛ makpa nibii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. mi nɔ loo daabi

english: Planting crops too close together actually reduces your overall yield because the plants crowd each other out. Sticking to a set number of plants per meter gives each crop enough room and soil nutrients to reach its full potential.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha yibiiwoo fɛɛ aba shi ejaakɛ tsei lɛ baabɔle amɛhe. Kɛ́ ato tsei ayibɔ pɔtɛɛ ko he gbɛjianɔ yɛ mita kome mli lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni enyɛ etsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I arrange my crop rows neatly in lines instead of scattering the seeds randomly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mato miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo naa moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã trukaa lɛ?

english: Planting in neat rows makes it easy to calculate how many crops fit on your land, gives plants equal access to light, and makes weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much faster.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ooobu ŋmɔshi nibii enyiɛ ni baashɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he akɔntaa. Ehaa tsei náa la hegbɛ ni tamɔ amɛhe. ni ehaa jwɛi shwiemɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ yaa oya.

english: How long does it usually take for crops to grow to full height after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani tso ko daa kɛyashɛɔ eshishijee he beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Most fast-growing crops reach their full height over a period of 18 to 20 weeks, provided they receive steady rainfall, proper sunlight, and adequate soil nutrients.
ga: Tsei ni daa oya lɛ ateŋ babaoo shɛɔ amɛhe yɛ otsii 18 kɛyashi 20 mli, kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ amɛ daa. hulu la ni sa kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why do my crops seem to grow much faster in certain weeks than in others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya kwraa yɛ otsii komɛi amli fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Once a plant's roots are established in the first few weeks, it enters a rapid growth stage where it absorbs maximum water and nutrients to quickly build tall stems and leaves.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ te shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ Ebaabote dalɛ be lɛ mli oya. Ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi koni ekɛfee ŋmeii kɛ baai kakadaji oya.

english: How tall should I expect my crops to grow before they start producing fruit?
ga: Te esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ dani amɛje yibiiwoo shishi amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Depending on the variety, healthy crops will focus energy on gaining height—often several meters tall—before shifting energy into flowering and producing fruit.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa amɛhewalɛ nɔyaa nɔ. ni bei pii lɛ amɛyaa ŋwɛi mitai babaoo dani amɛtsakeɔ hewalɛ amɛfeɔ fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo

english: How do I calculate how many seeds or seedlings I need to buy for my farm size?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu dumɔwui loo dumɔwui enyiɛ ni esa akɛ mahe lɛ he akɔntaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ naa?

english: First measure the total length and width of your land to get the total area, then multiply that area by the standard number of plants recommended per meter for your specific crop.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, susumɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ kɛlɛ kɛ elɛɛmɔ fɛɛ he koni ona shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ tsei ayibɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akwɛ yɛ mita kome mli kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ lɛ abɔ nakai kpokpaa lɛ he.

english: How can I tell if my farm land is big enough to support the number of crops I want to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ayibɔ ni misumɔɔ ni makwɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Calculate the total area of your plot in square meters; if the space is too small for your desired crop count at proper spacing, you will need to reduce plant density to avoid overcrowding.
ga: Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ he akɔntaa yɛ sqɛɛ mitai amli. Kɛji akɛ he ni yɔɔ lɛ faaa tsɔ kɛha tsei ayibɔ ni he hiaa bo yɛ he ko ni kɛ bo teŋ jɛkɛmɔ sa lɛ, Ebaabi ni Oba tsei lɛ ayibɔ shi koni akafee mɛi babaoo.

english: Why are my young crops growing very tall and thin instead of strong and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ miida waa ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Crops stretch quickly and grow tall and skinny when they are struggling to find sunlight. If they are heavily shaded, they waste energy reaching upward rather than growing strong, thick stems.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baakpã oya ni amɛbaafee shwiili kɛ shwiili be mli ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná hulu la lɛ. Kɛji hulutsoo be ni mli wa yɛ lɛ Amɛfiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaama tsei ni wa ni mli tse.

english: How can I tell if my crops are growing at a healthy rate during their first few months?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli?

english: Healthy crops consistently put out fresh green leaves and gain steady height each week, showing thick stems rather than weak, pale, or stunted shoots.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛyaa ŋwɛi daa otsi. Amɛyɛ tsei ni mli tse moŋ fe tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants turn yellow and fall off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during the dry season as a natural survival mechanism to reduce water loss through evaporation, allowing the plant to stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Ha tso lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How does putting dry leaves or straw around the base of my crops help them survive hot weather?
ga: Baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, creates a protective layer that keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly under intense sunlight.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ baa, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stalks and smaller harvest yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when planted in an open field with no trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under direct heat; they need fast-growing shade plants like plantains to shield them from full sunlight during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, koni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do insects quickly destroy my harvested maize when I keep it in my storehouse after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-ŋma ni mikpa lɛ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛto mi-nitoohe lɛ beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects thrive when stored grain contains hidden moisture or is kept in unsealed containers; thoroughly drying your grain to low moisture levels and storing it in airtight bags stops insects from multiplying.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ tee koni nu akabote mli loo akɛto tsɛnsii ni aŋã mli jogbaŋŋ amli. Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi atsu nii ni okɛgbi ŋmaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli koni kooloi bibii akafɔ.

english: Why does my harvested corn develop black mold while stored inside my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ ná ŋmɔtɔ diŋ beni akɛtoɔ mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Mold grows on grain that was stored before being completely dried, or when stored in a room with high humidity and poor ventilation.
ga: Muji kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ dani amɛgbiɔ kwraa lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛ́ akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ waa ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu ehiii mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt in the afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During peak midday heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil; watering early in the morning or late evening helps reduce this heat stress.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni oooha mɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baaye abua ni eha dɔlɛ he haomɔ nɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ ekɛ ehe wo latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the plant, causing it to shed blossoms to save energy and water rather than investing resources into growing new fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii baawo aduawai heei akwɛmɔ mli lɛ

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell; seeds planted too early may sprout but then dry up and die before the main rainy season truly starts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shi no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to turn pale yellow and stop growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and steal essential plant nutrients like nitrogen directly from the soil, leaving your crops hungry and weak.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ tsei lɛ amli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ, ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii ni ogbɔjɔ.

english: Why does my maize crop yield get smaller every year even though I farm on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele yibiiwoo lɛ miiba shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikwɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Crops feed on specific nutrients in the soil to grow. Planting the exact same crop on the same plot season after season drains those specific nutrients faster than the soil can rebuild them, leading to smaller harvests unless you rotate crops or restore soil fertility.
ga: Tsei yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛdara. Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ haa nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ ama amɛ ekoŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afee lɛ fioo. Ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do people say planting legumes like beans together with cassava helps the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛfataa ŋmei he lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas have special roots that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. This nitrogen feeds neighboring crops like cassava, acting like a natural fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmei niyenii, he ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and weak with small cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Instead of making big cobs, they spend all their energy stretching upward to reach the light.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee ŋmeii wuji Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsu nii ni amɛkɛgbala amɛhe kɛtee ŋwɛi koni amɛyashɛ la lɛ he.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need plantain trees planted right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii amli yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn and dry out easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that shield the young cocoa plants from harsh sun and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni shwereɔ oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves droop and curl during the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In extreme heat, tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the ground. They temporarily droop to protect themselves and conserve moisture, usually recovering when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaakoto shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu amɛhe ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni bei pii lɛ, ehaa ehe baa shi kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: How does applying fertilizer right before a heavy rain affect my crops?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: A sudden heavy rainfall washes granular fertilizer off the top of the farm into drains before the crop roots can absorb it. Fertilizer works best when applied into small holes in the soil or right before a gentle rain.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa nu tsɔji amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ akɛwo bu bibii amli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo dani nugbɔ fioo anɛ

english: Curled and yellowing leaves on cassava are usually a sign of mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The disease stops the plant from making food, which prevents the roots from growing large.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔŋ yɛ yucca nɔ lɛ ji mosaic hela he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Hela nɛɛ haaa tsei afee niyenii. ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara

english: Why should I not plant pepper in the exact spot where I just harvested tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he ni ajie tomatoi lɛ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper and tomato belong to the same crop family and share the same diseases and pests. Planting them in the same spot back-to-back lets pests surviving in the soil immediately attack the new crop.
ga: Pepper kɛ tomato yɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛyeɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi ni afɔɔ namɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ haa kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tutuaa nibii heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the young shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: If too many sucker shoots grow around one plantain tree, they steal water and plant food away from the main stem. Removing extra shoots ensures the main tree gets full nourishment to produce a heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo miikwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ, dumɔwu kome Ejuɔ nu ni ekwɛɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo tsei niji ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii miifee ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that drink up soil nutrients much faster than crops can. Even with rain, your crops turn yellow because the weeds are starving them of essential soil food.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni boteɔ mli ni yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ yeɔ amɛ hɔmɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, an essential food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant recover and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil because standing water cuts off air to the roots. This lack of oxygen allows rot fungi to grow quickly and destroy the tubers before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Oxygen ni bɛ lɛ haa rot fungus lɛ daa oya ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani akpaa.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in damp, overly shady conditions. Pruning extra tree branches to let sunlight in and removing sick pods helps keep the rest of the tree healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Tsoi ahe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he koni hulu la abote mli ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when temperatures get too high or water is inconsistent. Extreme heat stresses the plant, forcing it to shed flowers to conserve energy and moisture.
ga: Tomato baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ mli ejɔɔɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei ajie amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ kɛ fɛ̃i he.

english: Why does my plantain bunch take much longer to grow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains require large amounts of water to transport nutrients into the bunch. Without enough water in the dry season, the plant slows down its growth to survive, delaying fruit maturity.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia plantains koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ baaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo koni amɛhi shi. ni ekɛ aduawai lɛ ashweremɔ asɛɛ afo

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding and eating inside the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn lɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, destructive pests that feed on the soft growing tip of young maize. Applying natural remedies like neem leaf extract or recommended treatments directly into the center funnel stops them.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi. Adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsɔnei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa enɛɛmɛi kpaa.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips that feed on plant sap and spread viruses. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat so they can absorb sunlight properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them restores natural nutrients into the ground so your next crop grows better without relying only on chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei nɛɛ adumɔ baaye abua ni adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ ohe akafɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it harmful to burn all the dead weeds and bushes on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashã jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni egboi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani madu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the top layer of organic matter that holds water in the soil. It also kills beneficial insects and natural microbes that break down dead leaves into food for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni hiɛɔ nu yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ŋwɛi fã lɛ. Egbeɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii bibii ni gbálaa baai ni egboi lɛ amli koni ekɛ niyenii aha onibii lɛ hu.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Leaves high on stakes make more food for the plant, resulting in much larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Baai ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa.

english: How long can my cassava roots stay in the soil before they start to spoil?
ga: Be enyiɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛje shishi amɛgboi?

english: Most cassava varieties reach full maturity between 9 to 12 months. If left in the ground beyond 15 to 18 months, the roots become woody, lose starch, and may rot, especially when the rainy season begins.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo shɛɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ. Kɛ́ ashi yɛ sũ lɛ mli fe nyɔji 15 kɛyashi 18 lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ tsei, amɛbaafee ŋmɔtɔ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi.

english: How many years does it take for a newly planted cocoa tree to start bearing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Traditional cocoa trees usually take 4 to 5 years to start producing fruit, but modern hybrid varieties (like Akokoabra) can begin bearing pods in about 2 to 3 years if properly cared for.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema cacao tsei lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cocoa hybrid henɔi (tamɔ Akokoabra) lɛ baabɔi yibiiwoo yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How many years can my oil palm tree produce good yields before I need to cut it down and replant?
ga: Afii enyiɛ dani mi-oil palm tso lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai lɛ, ehe baahia ni afo lɛ ni adu ekoŋŋ?

english: An oil palm tree can produce fruit for over 25 to 30 years. However, after about 20 to 25 years, the tree becomes too tall to harvest easily and yields begin to drop, which is when replanting is recommended.
ga: Mu tsei baanyɛ awo yibii fe afii 25 kɛyashi 30. Shi, yɛ aaafee afii 20 kɛyashi 25 sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ daraa tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ekpa amɛ oya. ni nibii ni anáa lɛ bɔi shibaa ni woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ekoŋŋ

english: How do I know when my plantains are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantains lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Plantains are mature when the fruits become plump and full, the ridges on the outer skin become less sharp and rounded, and the small dried flowers at the tips of the fingers rub off easily.
ga: Plantains lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kwraa kɛ́ aduawai lɛ egbɔjɔ. Gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛji ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. kɛ fɔfɔi bibii ni egbi Ewaaa akɛ aaatsi niji ahe.

english: Why should I buy new hybrid maize seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my old harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mikpamɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved hybrid seeds lose their strength in the second generation, leading to uneven growth, smaller cobs, and lower yields. Buying fresh certified seed each season ensures strong growth and maximum yield.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: When is the right time to cut down my old cocoa trees and replace them with new seedlings?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei momoi ni akɛ dumɔwui heei awo amɛ najiaŋ?

english: You should replace old trees when they show signs of severe decline, low yields, or disease like swollen shoot. It is best to replant at the onset of the major rainy season so the new seedlings get enough water to settle.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsei momoi lɛ atsake kɛji amɛbɔi shigbeemɔ waa, amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo, loo helai tamɔ akɔɔblei ni efuu lɛ ba amɛmli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ekoŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ shishijee mli bɔni afee ni dumɔwui heei lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛma amɛhe shi.

english: How old should my tomato seedlings be before I transplant them from the nursery to my main field?
ga: Esa akɛ mi tomato dumɔwui lɛ aye afii enyiɛ dani majie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Tomato seedlings are ready for transplanting when they are 3 to 4 weeks old and have grown about 3 to 4 true leaves. Transplanting them at this age helps them recover quickly from planting shock.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu amɛ kɛji amɛye otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 ni amɛyɛ baai diɛŋtsɛ 3 kɛyashi 4. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli yɛ afii nɛɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ oya kɛjɛɔ dumɔ he shoofeemɔ mli.

english: Flower drop in pepper plants usually happens due to environmental stress, such as extreme heat, lack of water, or a shortage of nitrogen and phosphorus in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa yɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa, loo nitrogen kɛ phosphorus ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves in a 'V' shape usually means the plant lacks nitrogen. The plant moves available nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed the younger top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni tamɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni ji ‘V’ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛya ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: If I cut my sugarcane, can the old roots grow a new crop or do I have to plant new stems?
ga: Kɛ́ ofo sugar cane lɛ, ani shishifãi momo lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ eheei? Aloo esa akɛ madu tso hee?

english: Sugarcane can regrow from the old roots, a process called 'ratooning.' You can harvest 2 to 3 ratoon crops from the original planting before you need to clear the field and replant fresh stems.
ga: Sugarcane baanyɛ akwɛ shishifãi heei kɛjɛ shishifãi momo amli. Enɛ ji gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ 'tilling'. Obaanyɛ okpa tsei 2 kɛyashi 3 kɛjɛ shishijee dumɔ mli. Dani no aaaba lɛ, ehe baahia ni ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni okɛ tsei heei adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that provide essential shade and cool moisture, protecting the cocoa plants until they grow big enough to survive on their own.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ. Ebuɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to build green leaves. It can also happen when the soil is waterlogged and the roots cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why do my crops yield less food when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naaa niyenii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition leaves all the plants weak, leading to small stalks and lower harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make my soil better for maize next season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop season ends, that natural nitrogen remains in the dirt to feed nitrogen-hungry crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji dumɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Adebɔɔ mli nitrogen hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen he hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot in the soil when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Excessive rain makes the soil stay soaked with water, which starves the roots of air. Without air, the cassava roots die and underground bacteria and fungi easily rot the tubers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Kasava shishifãi lɛ baagboi. Ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why do Fall Armyworms focus on attacking the center funnel of my maize plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ema mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ anɔ tutuamɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: The central funnel of a maize plant holds the softest, newest leaves that are easy for worms to eat. The funnel also shields the pests from direct hot sunlight and rain.
ga: Abɛi tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tsɔne lɛ hiɛɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ehee fe fɛɛ lɛ, ni ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ amɛ oya. Channels lɛ hu buɔ kooloi ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat stress or lack of water. The plant drops the flowers to save its own energy so it can survive until conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do weeds in my field hurt the growth of my vegetables?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miifite mi-aduawai lɛ adalɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most vegetables and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops, which starves your vegetables and reduces your yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe aduawai babaoo ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ o-vegetables lɛ ni ehaa o-vegetables lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to wait until the yam leaves turn yellow before harvesting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi sweet potato baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani akpa sweet potato?

english: Yellow leaves mean the yam plant has finished sending all its energy down into the root tuber. Digging the yam up before this happens means harvesting smaller tubers that spoil quickly.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato tso lɛ etsu ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛtee shishifãi lɛ amli. Ni aaakumɔ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ dani enɛ aba lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ abaakpa ŋmeii bibii ni fiteɔ oya lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl upwards during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl upwards as a protective defense against extreme heat. By curling, the leaves reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the sun, preventing the plant from losing too much water.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ abɔle baai lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Tsi tsei anaa koni amɛkafite nu babaoo tsɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying after it rains heavily and water sits on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When heavy rain creates standing water on your farm, it drowns the crop roots by cutting off oxygen. Without air in the soil, roots cannot absorb nutrients, causing maize leaves to turn yellow, stall in growth, and eventually die.
ga: Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ nu ni ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa. Ehaa tsei shishifãi shwieɔ nu mli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Ehaa ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ ni naagbee lɛ egboɔ

english: How do ridges and mounds help protect my crops during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋshɔkei kɛ gɔji buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Planting on raised mounds or ridges keeps your crops' main roots elevated above standing water. This allows excess water to drain into the channels while keeping the roots in aerated soil so they do not rot.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi titrii lɛ yaa ŋwɛi fe nu ni damɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛboteɔ tsɔne lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ koni amɛkafite.

english: Can I use water from a muddy nearby pond to water my crops during the dry season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ sũ nubu ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Dirty or muddy water can be used if allowed to settle in a container first so heavy dirt sinks to the bottom. However, if the water contains chemical waste or sewage, it can poison your plants and cause root decay.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ nu ni mli ewo muji loo nu ni mli ewo muji atsu nii kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ehi tsɛnsi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Bɔni afee ni muji ni tsii lɛ atsɔ shishi. Shi, kɛji tsofai loo muji yɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ Ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofa awo tso lɛ mli ni eha shishifãi lɛ afite.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable crops heavily once a week or lightly every day?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai amli nu babaoo shikome yɛ otsi mli loo oooha amɛ nu fioo daa gbi?

english: Deep watering once or twice a week is usually better because it encourages plant roots to grow deep into the soil. Deep roots keep crops strong against hot sun, whereas shallow daily watering keeps roots near the top where they easily dry out.
ga: Nu ni mli kwɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ he waa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ daa gbi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ, ni ebaanyɛ egbi oya.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the afternoon sun even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: When soil stays soaked for too long, waterborne fungi can damage the root system. Even if the soil is wet, damaged roots cannot draw water up to the leaves fast enough to withstand the hot afternoon sun, causing the plant to wilt.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Fungi ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite shishifãi lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ Shi shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbala nu kɛya baai lɛ anɔ oya bɔ ni sa koni amɛdamɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Ebaanyɛ eha tsei agbi.

english: Cassava roots rot when planted in soil that traps water without draining. Wet soil encourages harmful bacteria and fungi that attack and decay the tubers underground long before harvest time.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hiɛɔ mli ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni tutuaa ni amɛfiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants remaining small and refusing to flower after sitting in water for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ji bibii lolo ni amɛkpooɔ fɔfɔi beni amɛta nu mli gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil puts tomato plants into survival mode. The lack of root air stops the plant from absorbing growth nutrients, causing it to stall completely and delay flowering until conditions improve.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ haaa tso lɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa edara. Enɛ haa tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shihilɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my seeds if the rain stops completely for two weeks right after I plant?
ga: Mɛni baa midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa kwraa otsii enyɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young seeds need consistent soil moisture to germinate and establish shallow roots. A sudden dry spell causes germinating seeds to dry out and die before they can push up through the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ haa dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why did my seeds fail to sprout after I flooded my planted beds with too much water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛ nu ewo midumɔ saatso lɛ nɔ fe nine lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Pouring too much water on newly planted seeds suffocates them by removing air pockets from the soil, or it causes a hard crust to form on top that young shoots cannot push through.
ga: Nu babaoo ni oooshwie dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ anɔ lɛ baaha amɛgbɔjɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Aloo ha ŋmei ni wa afee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii bibii akabote mli.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away the top layer of dirt on my sloping farm and expose my crop roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ muji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni etse ehe lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ejieɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akpo lɛ?

english: Water running down a slope carries away the fertile topsoil that protects roots and holds nutrients. Planting crops in lines across the slope rather than down it slows the water flow and protects your crops.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ hiɔ shi. Kɛ́ odu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ moŋ fe ni ooodu yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaabu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with small cobs when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni miduɔ amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close to each other, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to stretch upward to reach light instead of building strong stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi koni eha la lɛ abote mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee tso ni mli wa kɛ ŋmei agbo.

english: Why do weeds kill my young crops so much faster than they harm my mature crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi gbeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ oya fe bɔ ni amɛtutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii ni eda lɛ?

english: Young crops have small, shallow root systems and few leaves, making them too weak to fight weeds for sunlight, water, and soil food. Older crops have deep roots and large leaves that block sunlight from weeds underneath them.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai fioo pɛ, ni no haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi jwɛi kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai wuji ni haa hulu lɛ shwieɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellowing of the bottom leaves is usually a sign that the crop is short on nitrogen. The corn plant moves nitrogen from its older, lower leaves up to feed the growing top leaves, causing the bottom leaves to fade and dry out.
