ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and dry out during the hot dry season even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up during hot weather to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and prevent water loss. Extreme curling can also be caused by tiny pests like whiteflies sucking the sap out of the leaves.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu ni elaaje lɛ naa. Nɔ ni baanyɛ aha ŋmeii bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmeii ni naa wa.

english: Why does my cassava crop produce giant bushy leaves above ground but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, cassava puts most of its energy into growing thick stems and leaves instead of storing energy in the roots. Balanced soil nutrients help the plant shift its focus to growing large tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni mli tse. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baato shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛjwɛŋmɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii wuji ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do some of my young cocoa pods turn black and shrivel while still attached to the tree stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ ekomɛi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo lɛ? Ani ekpɛtɛ tso lɛ shishi lolo?

english: Young cocoa pods shrivel either because the tree has produced more pods than it can feed and naturally sheds the extra ones, or because of black pod disease caused by too much moisture and excess shade.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ gboiɔ ejaakɛ tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eye ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. aloo yɛ black pod hela ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ

english: Why do my stored yam setts refuse to sprout immediately after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ ekwɛɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers go into a natural resting state called dormancy after harvest. During this time, the yam will not sprout regardless of watering or sunlight until its natural internal clock signals the start of the new planting cycle.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ boteɔ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ ko ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, Sweet potatoes lɛ kwɛŋ, ekɔɔɔ he eko nu ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli loo hulu la ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ, kɛyashi be mli ni amɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baatsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiiya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans in my field make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans work with beneficial microbes in the soil to pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decompose, this stored nitrogen acts as natural food for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Ekɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei fiteɔ Nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cover the soil around my crop roots with dry grass during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi atsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbɔleɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the soil from direct sunlight. This keeps the soil cool and stops moisture from evaporating quickly into the air, keeping root zones wet longer.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before any peppers start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely hot temperatures, irregular watering, or a lack of essential nutrients needed to support fruit growth.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai lɛ adalɛ ni bɛ

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a main food plants need to stay green. When the plant doesn't get enough from the soil, it steals nitrogen from its old leaves to feed the new ones growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Ejuɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining, which smothers the roots and allows soil fungi to attack them. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why are there small holes in my young maize leaves with tiny dark powders inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni eyɛ powda bibioo ni tsuɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the young leaves and eats them from the inside. Applying the recommended pest control chemical early in the morning or late in the evening helps reach and kill these worms before they ruin your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ baai bibii amli ni ejɛɔ emli eyeɔ nii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni oshɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe ni ogbe amɛ dani amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do the small flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Yɛ mi koko tso lɛ nɔ koni egbee shi ni etsɔko pod?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers if they are stressed by lack of water, attacked by tiny insects like mirids, or lacking nutrients in the soil. Providing shade, protecting the trees from pests, and keeping the soil moist helps the flowers stay on and grow into full pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ hao amɛ, ni kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen tutua amɛ. loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa hulutsoo, ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ahe Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: If I plant cowpeas together with my maize, will the cowpeas steal food from the maize?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmãa du tsina ŋmãa Ani tsina ŋmãa baaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmãa mli?

english: No, cowpeas actually help maize because leguminous plants pull food from the air and store it in the soil, which feeds the maize. As long as you leave enough space between them, both crops will grow well together without competing.
ga: Dabi, cowpea yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa diɛŋtsɛ. Enɛ ji akɛ, ŋmãa gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, he ni ŋmãa yeɔ nii yɛ lɛ. Shii abɔ ni obaashi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ. Tsei enyɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe etswaaa akaŋ.

english: You should wait until the soil is thoroughly wet from two or three heavy rains that soak deep into the dirt. Planting after just one light rain can cause your seeds to sprout and then die if the sun comes back strong.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa ejaakɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Tumɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha odumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba waa.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetables with dry leaves instead of burning them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Aduawai ni baai egbi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ashãa amɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating in the heat. Over time, those dry leaves rot and turn into natural manure that feeds your soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Nakai baai ni egboi lɛ baafite ni amɛbaatsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotten while still hanging on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni amɛkã wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This black rot happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil, usually because watering is uneven—like going from very dry to very wet. Keeping the soil moisture steady helps the plant transport calcium to the fruit properly.
ga: Nɛkɛ black rot hela nɛɛ baa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ hewɔ ni enɛ baa lɛ. Etamɔ nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ nu ni egbi waa mli kɛyaa nu ni mli edɔ waa mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium lɛ yaa aduawai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to spray chemical pest control on my farm when the afternoon sun is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ehiii beni shwane hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Spraying in the hot sun causes the liquid to dry up or evaporate into the air before it can work properly, and the combination of hot sun and chemical can burn your crop leaves. It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu lɛ shwie hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ agbi loo etsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani enyɛ etsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa ni akɛ tsofai fata he lɛ baanyɛ ashã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ lɛ leebi loo shwane mli.

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce the food that builds large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they get full sun and stay safe from soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni feɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛ hulu ni yeɔ emuu aha ni ebu he kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil. Applying a balanced fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the plants turn dark green and grow healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɛ edɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines produce plenty of green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When yam plants get too much nitrogen, they put all their energy into growing vines and leaves instead of tubers. They need more potassium in the soil during tuber development to grow large.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo Amɛbaakɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii yɛ wain tsei kɛ baai ni amɛduɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛbaadu bulbs. Amɛmiitao potassium babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni tuber lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ koni amɛhi shi agbo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand full, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that shields the cocoa trees from excessive heat until they are strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ, yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi tso lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ni buɔ kokoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ehaa ehe waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot or when the soil dries out suddenly. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps the plant retain flowers and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩ trukaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water suffocates them in flat, poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi, ni ehaa amɛmuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that hides inside the central funnel of maize plants. Applying recommended treatments directly into the plant funnel early in the morning or late afternoon helps control them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo shwane mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or mites that suck plant sap and spread viruses. Protecting the plants from these insects keeps new leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni baa heei lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings collapse and rot right at the soil level in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ miifite ni amɛmiifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This issue, known as damping-off, happens when nursery beds are kept too wet or crowded, allowing soil fungi to attack young stems. Spacing seeds well and avoiding overwatering protects seedlings.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ damping lɛ baa kɛ́ gbekɛbii asa lɛ nɔ edɔ loo eyi obɔ kɛ mɛi tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa tsei bibii lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ kpakpa kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu dumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily before the fruit is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani eyibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be damaged by underground pests or wet soil, making heavy fruiting trees top-heavy. Staking the plants with strong poles provides the support needed until harvest.
ga: Plantains shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baafee tsei ni tsii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa wo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná yelikɛbuamɔ ni he hiaa amɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help my other crops grow better afterwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ? Minɔ lɛ da jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules. When the plant roots decay, that nitrogen enriches the soil for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ fite Nakai nitrogen lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain beside them creates a protective canopy that keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Ehaa shade ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why is it helpful to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas fix nitrogen from the air into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that helps neighboring maize plants grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: How does covering my garden bed with dry grass help my vegetables during the hot dry season?
ga: Te jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mibɔɔ mli saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Placing dry grass on the soil (mulching) acts as a shield against the hot sun, preventing soil water from evaporating quickly and keeping root zones cool.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. kɛ shishifã lɛ he ni aaaha afee fɛ̃i

english: Why should I avoid applying dry chemical fertilizer when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve into a form plant roots can absorb. Applying it to bone-dry soil can cause root burn and waste the fertilizer.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ nɔ ko ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings sprout faster when I plant them slanted instead of straight down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ́ adu yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni adu lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Slant-planting buries multiple growth nodes under the soil at favorable depths while exposing the top stem to air, encouraging quicker root formation and foliage growth.
ga: Sloping planting futuɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni miida lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ he ko ni sa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ŋwɛi tsitsi lɛ jeɔ kpo kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ oya kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants produce bigger tubers when I give the vines wooden sticks to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ hiɛ bulbs wuji beni mihaa lɛ tendrils koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam vines off the ground so their leaves catch more sunlight to make food, while preventing leaves from rotting on the damp soil.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni efoji lɛ aná hulu la babaoo kɛha nihoomɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves is typically a sign of nitrogen deficiency; the plant moves nitrogen from older leaves to feed newer top growth to stay alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii koni ehi wala mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat or water stress, or when the soil lacks enough nutrients like phosphorus needed to convert blossoms into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ. aloo be mli ni niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni he hiaa koni fɔfɔii atsɔ aduawai lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do armyworm caterpillars hide deep inside the center leaves of my maize during the daytime?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Armyworms hide inside the leaf whorls during the heat of the day to protect themselves from predators and harsh direct sunlight while feeding on the soft inner growth.
ga: Asraafoi amli ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be lɛ mli. Koni obu ohe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ahe. yɛ be mli ni eyeɔ mligbɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves get white powdery spots during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Continuous rain and high humidity create ideal moist conditions for fungal spores to bloom and spread quickly across wet plant leaves.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa hulutsoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha fungal spores lɛ koni amɛfɔ̃ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya yɛ tsei ahe baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that hides inside the young maize funnel (whorl) to feed on soft leaves. If left untreated, they destroy the plant's growing point, preventing it from producing corn ears.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa bibii (rings) amli koni eye baai bibii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Ebaafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Tsi ŋmãa toi lɛ anaa koni ekafee.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites, or a virus they transmit. The insects suck the juices from young leaves, causing them to deform and reducing the plant's ability to grow healthy fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Kplukai nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli. Efiteɔ tso lɛ ni ehaa nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellowing starting at the tip and moving down the central vein of older leaves is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency. Maize needs nitrogen to build green leaves, so when the soil lacks it, the plant pulls nutrients from older leaves to feed new growth.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ ashishigbɛ ni eyaa shi yɛ amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain next to my new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantain yɛ kookoo tso hee ko masɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under the strong Ghanaian sun. Plantains grow fast and develop broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, shielding young cocoa plants from heat stress while keeping the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ Ghana hulu ni naa wa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛnáa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often a 'false rain' followed by a dry spell. If you plant immediately, seeds will germinate, but the young seedlings will quickly dry up and die if regular rains do not continue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji ‘amale nugbɔ’ ni nugbɔshiimɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃. Shi tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ daa.

english: Why must I build tall soil mounds before planting my yam seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow straight down deep into the earth. Loose, elevated soil mounds make it easy for the tubers to expand without resistance, resulting in larger, well-shaped yams and preventing roots from suffocating in waterlogged soil.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewó nɔ lɛ haa bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii amɛnaa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛo, ni ehaaa amɛshishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the daytime temperature gets too high or when plants experience water stress. High heat damages the pollen, causing the plant to shed the flower because it cannot successfully form a fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ kpeɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nyɛmɔ ni amɛnyɛɛɛ amɛwo yibii yɛ omanyeyeli mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Young crops have small, weak root systems. If weeds grow alongside them, the weeds will steal water, sunlight, and soil food, causing your crops to become stunted and weak.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ. Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ amɛmasɛi Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is ready to harvest since the root is hidden underground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ etee shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the plant reaches 9 to 12 months old, lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack as expanding tubers push upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo beni tso lɛ eye nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 lɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tso lɛ ni eda lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why does my stored dry maize turn into powder and get filled with tiny holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ powda ni eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani eyi obɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: This damage is caused by maize weevils that lay eggs inside dry grains. If maize is not dried thoroughly to low moisture levels or treated properly before storage, the larvae hatch inside and eat the grain from the inside out.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni egbi mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa kɛyashɛɛɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi loo akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛtoɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ yɛ mli ni eyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow so much better when I use proper irrigation instead of just waiting for the rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ mikɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tsu nii moŋ fe ni mamɛ nugbɔ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Irrigation supplies water directly and consistently to crop roots whenever needed, preventing plant stress and allowing continuous growth even during long dry spells.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ kɛ nu baa tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛ nu baa shishifãi ni aduɔ lɛ amli be fɛɛ be ni ehe baahia. Etsiɔ tsei ahe haomɔ naa ni ehaa amɛyaa nɔ amɛdaraa yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli po.

english: Is simply pouring a bucket of water on my farm the same as proper irrigation?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛshwieɔ baagi mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ egbɔ?

english: No, pouring water manually often leads to uneven watering and heavy evaporation; proper irrigation delivers water directly to the root zone where the plant can actually drink it.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi waa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ nu yaa shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ he ni tso lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ lɛ.

english: Watering early in the morning or late in the evening reduces water loss from heat evaporation, allowing the roots maximum time to absorb moisture.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ haa nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ nu babaoo.

english: I want to farm in Northern Ghana where it is dry; why do crops struggle more during the dry season there?
ga: Miisumɔ ni matsu okwaayeli yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ he ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli egbi lɛ. Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Without sufficient moisture in the soil during prolonged dry seasons, plants cannot absorb nutrients, causing leaf wilting, stunted growth, and low yield.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ, Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi. Stifled dalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi

english: Why do some crops survive dry conditions in northern regions while others wither quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yeɔ wala yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ kpokpai anɔ lɛ amli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi gboɔ oya lɛ?

english: Different crops have different root structures; drought-tolerant crops have deep taproots that reach underground water, while shallow-rooted crops depend heavily on frequent surface moisture.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi srɔtoi. Tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ damɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are receiving too much or too little water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni miduɔ lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ?

english: Under-watered crops have crisp, yellowing, or curling leaves, whereas over-watered crops develop soft, pale leaves and damaged, rotting root systems.
ga: Tsei ni nu yɔɔ mli fe nine lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, loo ni ebɔle ehe, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni nu yɔɔ mli fe nine lɛ baa baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ shishifãi ni efite ni miifite.

english: Why do my crops droop in the afternoon heat even when the ground feels slightly damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo po.

english: Hot afternoon weather causes leaves to lose water faster than roots can pull it from the ground, creating temporary wilting until the air cools down.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: How does regular watering throughout the season increase my final harvest yield?
ga: Te nu ni mikɛwoɔ mli daa yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha minaagbee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Consistent water prevents the crop from spending energy battling drought stress, allowing it to put all its energy into producing bigger fruits, grains, or tubers.
ga: Nu ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akatsu nii ni amɛkɛwu amɛshi hɔmɔ he haomɔ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni akɛwoɔ aduawai, ŋmaa, loo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my fertilizer seem to work better when the farm is properly watered?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-fertilizer lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ nu wo ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers cannot feed plants in dry powder form; water is needed to dissolve the nutrients so the roots can drink them up.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aha tsei yɛ powda ni egbi mli. Nu he miihia koni akɛjie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ.

english: At what stage of my crop's life should I put in the most effort with watering and feeding?
ga: Mɛɛ be mli esa akɛ mikɛ mihewalɛ fɛɛ awo nu kɛ niyenii ni mikɛhaa lɛ mli yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashihilɛ mli?

english: Crops require the most water and nutrients during their flowering and fruiting stages, as this is when they build the actual food you will harvest.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii he hiaa tsei fe fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, be nɛɛ mli ji be ni tsei lɛ feɔ niyenii diɛŋtsɛ ni obaakpa lɛ.

english: How long does maize usually take from the day I plant it until it is ready for harvesting?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ ŋmãa heɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eshɛɔ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Most common maize varieties grown in Ghana take between 3 to 4 months (90 to 120 days) to reach full maturity, depending on whether you plant an early-maturing or late-maturing variety.
ga: Abele henɔi ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 (gbii 90 kɛyashi 120) dani eshɛɔ shweremɔ he. Edamɔ ŋmãa henɔi ni shwereɔ mra loo ŋmãa ni shwereɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: How will I know that my cassava crops are fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tsei lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, and the soil around the base of the stem cracking as the tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli gbalaa beni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I clear and prepare my farm plot weeks before I actually sow my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo miŋmɔ mli saatso lɛ nɔ ni masaa he otsii babaoo dani madu dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Preparing land weeks in advance gives cut weeds time to dry out and decay into nutrients, exposes soil pests to the sun, and ensures the soil is soft enough for tender plant roots to spread quickly once planted.
ga: Kɛ́ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ otsii babaoo kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua jwɛi ni afo lɛ ni amɛgbi ni amɛgbala amɛhe ni amɛfee niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Ehaa kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shɛɔ hulu la he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔ ni sa koni tso shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya kɛji adu amɛ pɛ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close to each other, will I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting seeds too close causes the crops to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and small cobs. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to grow big cobs.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmei agbo ko akwɛ̃.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my young crop after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa awo tsei bibii amli beni midu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first application is usually done about 2 weeks after planting when the young roots have formed, followed by a second application around 4 to 6 weeks when the plant enters its fast growth stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afeɔ klɛŋklɛŋ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ aaafee otsii 2 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ, beni shishifãi bibii jeɔ shishi lɛ. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji shi ni ji enyɔ yɛ aaafee otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 mli beni tso lɛ boteɔ dalɛ oyaiyeli be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Is it good for me to plant groundnuts together on the same field as my cassava?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmei?

english: Yes, groundnuts cover the soil to prevent weeds and trap nitrogen from the air to enrich the soil, which helps feed tall crops like cassava without competing for the same canopy space.
ga: Hɛɛ, akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmeii ni akɛtsiɔ jwɛi anaa ni akɛmɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akwɛɔ tsei kakadaji tamɔ ŋmei ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ akaŋ awo ŋwɛi ŋta kome lɛ nɔŋŋ mli.

english: How many times do I need to clear weeds from my crop field during the first two months of growth?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji enyɔ ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: You should weed at least twice in the first two months. Young seedlings grow slowly and can easily be choked by weeds that steal moisture, sunlight, and fertilizer.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii shii enyɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji enyɔ lɛ amli. Tsei bibii lɛ daa blɛoo ni jwɛi ni juɔ ŋmɔtɔ, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aha amɛhe oya.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily in direct sun. They need shade crops like plantains during their first two years to protect them from harsh weather and retain moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ ahe, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants start rolling up after two weeks without rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ otsii enyɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural survival response to drought. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to heat to conserve the water stored in its stem.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji bɔ ni tso lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Tsei haa he ni hulutsoo baa amɛnɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli koni nu ni ato yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ akafite lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are tiny holes appearing on the leaves of my tomato plants a few weeks after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Eje kpo yɛ mi tomato baai lɛ anɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Holes in young leaves are usually caused by feeding insects like beetles or caterpillars. Treating the farm early with recommended organic or chemical sprays prevents insects from ruining the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni kooloi akafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I know which crop is best to plant on my farm land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Different crops require specific types of soil and weather conditions to thrive. Knowing your land's soil type and rainfall patterns helps you choose crops that naturally grow best in your specific region of Ghana.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi biɔ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Shikpɔŋ henɔ kɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ole lɛ baaye abua bo ni ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ okpokpaa ni ji Ghana lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I plant cocoa anywhere in Ghana as long as I clear the land and water it?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo yɛ Ghana he fɛɛ he? Shii abɔ ni majie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ ni mawo nɔ nu jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: No, cocoa requires deep, nutrient-rich soil and heavy rainfall found mostly in the southern forest zones of Ghana. It will not yield well in dry, sandy, or savanna soils.
ga: Dabi, Cocoa biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli, kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, ni anaa yɛ kooi ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ amli babaoo. Ewoŋ yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi, ŋã loo savannah nɔ.

english: Is it possible for my neighbor's farm to be good for maize while my farm next door is better for cassava?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmãa? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ ni bɛŋkɛ minɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmei?

english: Yes, soil depth, water drainage, and soil composition can change even over short distances, making one piece of land suited for shallow-rooted crops like maize and another suited for tuber crops like cassava.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, nu ni hoɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii baanyɛ atsake yɛ gbɛ kuku po mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fã kome feɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni ekroko hu feɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha tuber ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: How can an extension officer tell if my land is good for a specific crop before I start planting?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ ale kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ko dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Officers use soil maps and testing to look at your soil's depth, texture, and ability to hold water, matching those characteristics with the requirements of the crop you want to grow.
ga: Amralofoi kɛ shikpɔŋ he mfonirii kɛ kaai tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛna bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ ha, bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni enyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu. Kɛtsɔ nakai sui lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni otaoɔ odu lɛ ahiamɔ nii ni oookɛto he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow well in one part of my farm but struggle and die in another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ? Shi esa akɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ ni agbo yɛ fã kroko mli?

english: Soil conditions often vary across the same farm field. One area might hold water and plant nutrients well, while another part might have hard, rocky, or dry soil that prevents roots from growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛi srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli. He ko baanyɛ ahiɛ nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii jogbaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni ekolɛ ekrokomɛi hu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa, tɛi, loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni haaa shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why does my cassava have big healthy green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: If the soil is too hard, compact, or waterlogged, the cassava plant puts all its energy into top leaf growth because the tubers cannot easily expand underground.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ, ŋmeii tso lɛ baafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ ebaa lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo.

english: Why does yam yield bigger tubers in loose, sandy-loam soil compared to heavy clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potatoes woɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ ŋã ni mli ejɔ mli kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, well-drained soil so they can easily push downward as they grow. Heavy clay soil is too tight and traps excess water, which stunts tuber expansion.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni anyɛ ashɛre lɛ shi mlɛo beni edaa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ebɔle ehe tsɔ ni ehiɛɔ nu ni fa fe nine. Enɛ baatsi yitso lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and stop growing when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain on poorly draining soil drowns the roots by filling all the air spaces with water, preventing the plant from taking up essential nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu ni ekɛbaawo kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ fɛɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen.

english: Why does maize grow very tall in places like the Bono region but stay short in drier areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shwereɔ waa yɛ hei tamɔ Bono kpokpaa lɛ nɔ shi ebɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Regions with rich soil and steady, adequate rainfall provide the steady moisture and food maize needs to reach its full height and produce large cobs.
ga: Kpokpai ni shikpɔji ni baa nii yɔɔ nɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa, ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ haa ŋmãa ni haa ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ he daa ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ ŋmãa babaoo baa.

english: How does the soil beneath my crops affect how much yield I get at harvest time?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ saa yibiiwoo ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Soil acts as a storage tank for water and plant food. Soil that holds nutrients and moisture balanced for your specific crop ensures the plants remain healthy and produce maximum yield.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni akɛ nu kɛ tsei aniyenii toɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni toɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa kɛha onibii pɔtɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants need to be planted under plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ dumɔwui ashishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily scorched by intense direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow rapidly and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing critical shade and preserving soil moisture during the cocoa's first few years of growth.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the cobs are formed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize typically indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for green leafy growth, so when it is lacking, the plant pulls nutrients from its older, lower leaves to feed the growing upper parts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ elaaje Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai bibii kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛya ŋwɛi fã ni miida lɛ mli.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my maize when the rains begin in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mije ŋmãa dumɔ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: It is best to wait until the soil has received two or three steady, heavy rains so moisture settles deep into the earth. Planting immediately after the very first light rain can cause seeds to germinate and then dry out if a brief dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni yaa nɔ daa. koni ŋmɔtɔ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji ŋmɔtɔ be kuku ko ba.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground if I leave them buried during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water in flooded or poorly drained soil deprives cassava roots of oxygen. This creates ideal conditions for fungal diseases and root-rot organisms to multiply quickly and spoil the tubers before harvest.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo nu shwieee nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ koni amɛshwere oya ni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani akpa.

english: Why are there holes in my young maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This pattern of damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central funnel of the maize plant to feed on fresh leaves. Applying recommended treatments directly into the funnel early in the morning or late evening helps clear them out.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ okadii nɛɛ baaho aya.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stems too close together on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting cassava too close causes the plants to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives leaves room to catch sunlight and allows tubers enough soil space to grow thick and healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha gbɛ aha hulu la. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛnáa shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhe wa.

english: How does growing cowpeas together with my maize help improve my harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cowpea ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mikpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that take nitrogen gas from the air and lock it into the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil with free fertilizer that nearby maize plants can use to grow stronger.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii koni amɛdara waa lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What causes black spots and curling on my tomato leaves during humid weather?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa tomato baa nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Black spots and leaf curling during damp or humid weather are usually caused by fungal leaf blights. High air humidity and rain splashing onto leaves allow fungal spores to travel and grow across tomato foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ni ji fungal leaf blight lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo loo hulutsoo be mli lɛ baa. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii amli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ fãa gbɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ tomato baai lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without turning into pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers often fall off due to stress caused by extreme heat, long periods of dry soil, or a lack of essential mineral nutrients during the flowering stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ haomɔ ni dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ. loo minerals ni he hiaa ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli

english: Why is it necessary to weed around my crops in the very first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young crop sprouts grow slowly at the beginning and cannot outcompete fast-growing weeds. Clearing weeds early ensures that water, sunlight, and soil nutrients go directly into your crop instead of feeding unwanted plants.
ga: Tsei bibii daaa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ anɔ kunim. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha tsei ni he ehiaaa amɛ niyenii lɛ.

english: Why should I start my tomato seeds in a small nursery house before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔi tomato dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli lɛ? dani aya shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ

english: Young seedlings are delicate like newborns and easily killed by heavy rains or severe heat; a protected nursery house shields them until their roots are strong enough to handle outdoor conditions.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa tamɔ abifabii ni afɔɔ amɛ ehee lɛ, ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo latsaa ni naa wa lɛ gbeɔ amɛ oya. Greenhouse ni abuɔ he lɛ baabu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu kponɔgbɛ shihilɛi ahe nii.

english: What is the benefit of growing sensitive vegetables inside a shade house instead of the open field?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli moŋ fe ŋmɔji ni mli tse mli lɛ he?

english: Shade houses control heat, reduce direct exposure to heavy downpours, and block large insects, which keeps crops healthy and productive even during extreme weather.
ga: Greenhouse ni shade kudɔɔ kɛ dɔlɛ kudɔmɔ Ha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baa shi tɛ̃ɛ. ni etsĩɔ kooloi wuji anaa Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa po amli.

english: How does a simple raised storage shed keep my harvested crops from rotting?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsũ bibioo ko ni awó nɔ lɛ aha mikpamɔ lɛ akafite?

english: Keeping harvested crops off the damp ground allows air to flow freely around them, preventing moisture build-up, mold growth, and insect infestation.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛbɔleɔ he jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baaa amɛhe shi. ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa

english: Why is proper plant spacing so important when setting out cassava in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa he hiaa waa beni aduɔ ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaving organized space between plants ensures each crop gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with neighboring roots, resulting in larger yields.
ga: Gbɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni ekɛ shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ akaŋ akaŋ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii babaoo ni afeɔ.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting legumes like cowpeas alongside my maize rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Interplanting creates a natural arrangement where cowpeas cover the soil to block weeds while feeding nitrogen back into the dirt to help the maize grow stronger.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli gbɛjianɔtoo ko baa. Kɛtsɔ tsina ŋmeii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akaje mli lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting crops in straight rows across a sloped land help them grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Row arrangements across slopes trap rainwater and topsoil, preventing heavy rains from washing away nutrients and exposing tender roots.
ga: Kɛ́ ato ŋshɔkei lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ yɛ ŋshɔkei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaamɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Etsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekajie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ejie shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ kpo.

english: If I leave an unused plot of land empty, why do weeds and wild bush take over so quickly?
ga: Kɛji mishi shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ efolo Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kɛ koo mli jwɛi yeɔ nɔ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Empty soil naturally attracts fast-growing wild weeds; keeping land managed or planting cover crops prevents nuisance plants from colonizing and draining soil nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ gbalaa koo mli jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ adumɔ baatsi tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkajie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why must I remove and destroy rotten cocoa pods from under my trees instead of leaving them there?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mijieɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni efite lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni mifiteɔ amɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mashi amɛ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving diseased pods under crops creates a breeding ground for fungal diseases like black pod, which easily spread back to healthy pods during rainy days.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ tsei ashishi lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii helai, tamɔ ŋmeii diji, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ gbii amli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops wilt and stress during dry spells even when I water them every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛhaoɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Without ground coverage, heat causes surface water to evaporate rapidly; adding mulch like dry grass acts as a protective blanket to lock moisture in the root zone.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ ko bɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya. Mulch tamɔ jwɛi baatsu nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather suddenly becomes extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ baai kɛji edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When heat becomes overwhelming, crops shed flowers as a defensive reaction to save water and energy; providing temporary shade trees helps protect them from heat stress.
ga: Beni latsaa lɛ jeɔ shishi eyeɔ nɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ akɛ nɔ ko ni akɛbuɔ he koni akɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa plants originally evolved on forest floors, so direct sunlight dries them out too quickly. Shade trees shield them from heat and keep the soil damp so the young cocoa can grow safely.
ga: Shishijee lɛ, cacao tsei bibii je shishi yɛ koo lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa kookoo tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves during peak heat as a natural protection mechanism to reduce surface area and stop water from evaporating too quickly from the plant.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu ni hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why does planting maize in the exact same field every season reduce my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Maize takes specific nutrients like nitrogen out of the soil every time it grows. If you plant it repeatedly without rotating crops or adding nutrients, the soil becomes depleted and cannot support healthy yields.
ga: Abele jieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ebaakwɛ̃. Kɛji odu shii abɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsakeee loo okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataaa he lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai anɔ.

english: Why is it better to space my maize seeds out instead of putting many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaagbala ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooŋɔ dumɔwui babaoo Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaabua dumɔwui lɛ anaa yɛ bu kome mli.

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves compete with each other for water, sunlight, and food. Proper spacing ensures every single plant gets enough resources to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why does covering the dirt around my crops with dry leaves help them during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ baai ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves, known as mulching, blocks direct sunlight from hitting the soil. This traps moisture in the ground for much longer so your crops can keep drinking during hot days.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi haa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu la lɛ akatswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be babaoo. Koni oha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee nɔ ni anuɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than the food crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe niyenii tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive wild plants that naturally absorb soil nutrients and water much faster than domesticated crops, allowing them to overpower your planted crops if not removed early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shia. Enɛ haa amɛyeɔ tsei ni ama shi lɛ anɔ kunim kɛji ajieee amɛ mra.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up off the wet ground to get plenty of sunlight to feed the tuber below, while keeping the leaves away from soil diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛjɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn tough and hard to cook if I leave them in the ground for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni ehoomɔ wa kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store tender starch when ready for harvest. If left underground too long, the plant converts that starch into hard wood-like fibers to support its ongoing growth, making the root tough.
ga: Cassava shishifãi hiɛɔ starch ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛji amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Tsei tsakeɔ nakai ŋmei lɛ ewoɔ tsei ni tamɔ tsei ni wa mli koni eye ebua amɛdalɛ ni yaa nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shishifãi ni mli wa

english: Why do black spots spread across my cocoa pods during heavy rainy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain creates wet, cool conditions where fungus thrives. Water drops splash fungus spores from the soil onto the pods, causing black pod disease to spread quickly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmeii baanyɛ ada yɛ mli lɛ baa. Nu mli nui ni hoɔ lɛ shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa pods lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do small caterpillars show up inside the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Moths fly in at night and lay eggs directly inside the central funnel of young maize because the hidden tender leaves give the hatching worms shade and easy food.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi lɛ fãa kɛboteɔ mli gbɛkɛ ni amɛwoɔ amɛwui lɛ yɛ ŋmãa abifao lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Baai bibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need temporary shade from fast-growing canopy crops like plantains to shield them from heat stress until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do my yam vines produce smaller tubers if I leave them on the ground instead of staking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ amɛ baawo tso mli lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb tall wooden stakes to spread their leaves and capture maximum sunlight. Full sun exposure allows the leaves to make more food energy, which the plant sends down to grow bigger underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei kakadaji anɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ kwraa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii hewalɛ babaoo. ni akɛ tsei tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that the soil is running out of nitrogen. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa lɛ, Abɛi gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ, ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in the same field as my maize help the soil stay rich?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that work with good bacteria in the soil to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay, that extra nitrogen feeds the soil and surrounding crops.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ bacteria kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei shishifãi fiteɔ lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off before any fruit can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani aduawai baanyɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and erratic watering cause stress to tomato plants, making them drop their blossoms to preserve survival energy. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomatoi shwieɔ shi koni amɛbu amɛhewalɛ he kɛha wala. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the top leaves of my pepper plants curling up and shrinking into tight bundles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the underside of the leaves. As they suck the sap, they weaken the leaf tissue and spread plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. be mli ni amɛnuɔ mliki lɛ Amɛhaa tso lɛ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ tso lɛ mli helai lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: Why do I see ragged holes and dark dirt in the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni etse kɛ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ mi-babi corn baa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The pest crawls into the center funnel of young maize plants during the day to feed on the tender inner leaves, leaving behind dark waste.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye amɛmli baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ su diŋŋ ni ashiɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain saturates poorly drained soil for too long, water blocks air from reaching the roots, causing them to suffocate and decay.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ ewo nu be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Nu tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni efiteɔ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small stems growing around my main plantain shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajie Mi plantain titri lɛ.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow around one plantain stem creates fierce competition for water, sunlight, and soil food. Pruning extra shoots directs all the plant's energy into growing one large, heavy bunch.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he Plantain kome pɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli fe nine lɛ, ebaahe tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ koni etsɔ tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do crops planted right after the very first major rain grow faster than those planted later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ daa oya fe nɔ ni adu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first rain after a dry spell breaks down dry organic matter in the ground, causing a natural release of plant food called a nitrogen flush. Crops planted immediately take full advantage of this quick boost in soil fertility.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso niyenii ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen flush lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Tsei náa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ oya lɛ he sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are my pawpaw trees flowering heavily but never producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Some crops like pawpaw have distinct male and female trees. Male trees only produce pollen-bearing flowers and cannot bear fruit themselves, while female trees need pollen from a nearby male tree to form fruit.
ga: Tsei komɛi, tamɔ pawpaw, yɛ tsei hii kɛ yei srɔtoi. Tsei ni ji hii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni pollen yɔɔ mli pɛ, ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii. Yɛ be mli ni tsei yei ahe hiaa pollen ni jɛ tsei hii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: How can I tell if a seedling is male or female before I plant it in my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwu ko ji nuu loo yoo dani madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: For most crops grown from seeds, you cannot tell the sex just by looking at the young seedling or leaf. You usually have to wait until the plant matures and produces its first flowers, unless you buy grafted plants from known parent stock.
ga: Kɛha tsei babaoo ni jɛ dumɔwui amli akwɛ̃ lɛ Onyɛŋ ole bɔ ni eji nuu loo yoo kɛtsɔ tso bibioo lɛ loo baai lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ esa ni omɛ kɛyashi tso lɛ eda ni ewo eklɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi. Ja oohe tso ni akɛ tso ko ni ale lɛ ebɔ he.

english: Do I need to keep both male and female plants on my farm for crops to bear fruit?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni makwɛ tsei hii kɛ yei fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni tsei lɛ awo yibii?

english: Yes, for crops that have separate sexes, you need mostly female trees for yield, but you must keep a few male trees nearby so bees and wind can transfer pollen to fertilize the female flowers.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛha tsei ni ji dioecious. Ohe miihia tsei yei babaoo koni onyɛ owo ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi ehe miihia ni okɛ tsei hii fioo komɛi ahi he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo bɔni afee ni ŋmeii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ajie pollen kɛya fɔfɔi yei lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it safe to buy crop seedlings from informal traders along the roadside?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooohe dumɔwui kɛjɛ gbɛjegbɛ nɔ jarayelɔi ni bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli lɛ adɛŋ?

english: Buying unverified seedlings carries risks because you cannot guarantee the variety, plant sex, or disease status. It is safer to source from certified nurseries or agricultural officers to ensure high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akwɛɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahemɔ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ onyɛɛɛ oma nɔ mi akɛ amɛji srɔtoi lɛ, bɔ ni tso lɛ ji nuu loo yoo, loo bɔ ni hela lɛ yɔɔ ha. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooona kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli loo okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ koni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aba.

english: Why is it better to grow plants from suckers or grafted cuttings instead of regular seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaakwɛ tsei kɛjɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni afo mli lɛ amli moŋ fe dumɔwui folo lɛ?

english: Growing from seeds can result in unpredictable traits and unknown plant gender. Using suckers or grafted cuttings guarantees that the new plant inherits the exact good qualities and sex of the parent crop.
ga: Dumɔ mli dalɛ baanyɛ aha sui ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ aba ni aleee bɔ ni tso lɛ ji nuu loo yoo. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli loo nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ tso hee lɛ baaná sui kpakpai kɛ bɔ ni tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ ji lɛ gboshinii diɛŋtsɛ.

english: If I buy seedlings from a warm area like Accra and plant them in a different region, will they grow well?
ga: Kɛ mihe dumɔwui kɛjɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ tamɔ Accra ni midu yɛ kpokpaa kroko nɔ lɛ. Ani dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Crops can experience shock when moved to a new region with different rainfall, temperature, or soil types. They may take longer to adapt or require extra watering and care during their initial stages.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ ana shoofeemɔ kɛji ajie amɛ kɛtee kpokpaa hee ko ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ, latsaa loo shikpɔŋ henɔi sɔrɔtoi yɔɔ nɔ. Ekolɛ amɛbaahe be babaoo dani amɛtsake loo amɛbaabi ni aha amɛ nu babaoo ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why do my fruit trees drop all their flowers before any fruit begins to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso ni woɔ yibii lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani aduawai jeɔ shishi ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Flower drop usually happens when plants suffer from water stress, lack of essential soil nutrients, extreme heat, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ naa nu he haomɔ. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ.

english: Why do some of my crops take many years to fruit while my neighbor's same crop fruits very quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋbii lɛ aŋmɔshi nii lɛ nɔŋŋ woɔ yibii oya waa lɛ?

english: Plants grown directly from seeds take much longer to mature and fruit than plants established from grafted seedlings or vegetative shoots, which mature and yield much faster.
ga: Tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fe tsei ni ajɛ dumɔwui ni akɛwo amɛhe loo tsei ahe ŋmeii amli afee lɛ. Amɛbaadara ni amɛwo bii oya kwraa.

english: What will happen if I plant my crop seedlings too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Planting too close forces crops to compete for sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients, causing them to grow tall and thin with very poor fruit yield.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: How do I know if my young crops are starving for food in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Nutrient-starved crops show clear physical signs such as yellowing leaves, stunted height, thin stems, and failure to produce healthy flowers or branches.
ga: Tsei ni akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ baajie gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo, kɛ nyɛmɔ ni amɛnyɛɛɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi loo niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kpo.

english: When is the best time of the year to transplant my young cashew seedlings onto the farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ mi-cashew dumɔwui lɛ awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to plant is right at the start of the main rainy season. This allows the young root system to establish deep into the soil with natural water before the dry harmattan season arrives.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛ adebɔɔ mli nu dani harmatta be ni mli egbi lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why does my land need clearing and preparation weeks before the rainy season actually begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni asaa he otsii komɛi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Preparing early removes weed seeds and pest habitats before planting. It also ensures the soil is loose and ready to absorb the very first rains, giving your seedlings a head start.
ga: Hesaamɔ mra Abaajie jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ ŋmeii ashihilɛhei dani adu. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ klalo akɛ ebaaŋɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ náa sɛɛnamɔ.

english: How many years will it take after planting before my new cashew trees start giving nuts?
ga: Kɛ́ adu lɛ, afii enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi-cashew tso hee lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Grafted cashew seedlings usually start bearing nuts within 2 to 3 years, whereas trees grown directly from untamed local seeds can take 4 to 5 years or longer to fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cashew dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahe afii 4 kɛyashi 5 loo nɔ ni fe nakai dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do I need to cut off the lower branches of my young cashew trees as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli beni edaa lɛ?

english: Pruning lower branches forces the tree to build a strong single trunk, improves airflow, prevents ground pests from climbing up, and directs energy into growing healthy flowering branches on top.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni aaafolɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ afee tso kome ni mli wa. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa tsei niji ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi ni he wa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ

english: Why do the flowers on my crop drop off without turning into fruits when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops do not get enough soil moisture during high heat, they experience heat stress and shed their flowers to save energy and water just to keep the main plant alive.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ Tsei kɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ kpeɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni tso ni amɛyɔɔ mli lɛ ahi shi kɛkɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, or that heavy waterlogging around the roots is preventing the plant from breathing and absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops more heavily during short dry spells in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry spells weaken the crops' natural defenses, and warm dry weather allows many harmful insects to multiply faster and feed on the stressed leaves.
ga: Be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ haa tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni ekɛbuɔ ehe lɛ baa shi. Ni shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa kooloi bibii babaoo ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwereɔ oya ni amɛyeɔ baai ni haoɔ mɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it harmful if I plant my crops too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight over sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow tall and thin with weak stems and produce very low yields.
