ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ Ebaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ mlɛo ni tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi waa lɛ baa.

english: Can I grow cassava or food crops between my young cashew trees while the trees are small?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei loo niyenii krokomɛi yɛ ŋmei tsei ateŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop with food crops during the first 2 to 3 years. It keeps weeds down and gives you food and income while the cashew trees grow, provided you leave enough space around each tree base.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii adu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli. Amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa ni jwɛi akaboteɔ mli ni amɛhaa bo niyenii kɛ shika be mli ni cashew tso lɛ daa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ oshi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ he lɛ. tso fɛɛ tso shishi

english: Why do grafted tree seedlings perform better than trees grown from regular raw nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni akɛ ŋmeii ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Grafted seedlings combine a strong root system with a branch taken from a proven, high-yielding mother tree, guaranteeing fast growth, disease resistance, and reliable fruit quality.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛwo tso mli lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni ajie kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso ko ni ana he odaseyeli ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ekome. Dalɛ oya, helai nyɛɔ eyeɔ kɛ aduawai kpakpai ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to remove the shade cover from my crop nursery?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ majie ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-greenhouse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings need shade to protect them from scorching sun when they are delicate. You should only remove the cover gradually when the plants show strong stems, usually a few weeks before transplanting, so they adapt to full sunlight.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛ́ amɛhe waaa. Esa akɛ ojie nɔ ni akɛhaa lɛ blɛoo pɛ kɛji tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa aaafee otsii 2-3 dani atsakeɔ tso lɛ. Koni tsei lɛ atsake amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt and die if I remove their protection too early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie hebuu lɛ oya tsɔ lɛ?

english: Tender young plants cannot handle direct sunlight and strong winds all at once. Removing their cover too soon dries out their thin leaves faster than their small roots can drink water from the soil.
ga: Tsei bibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa nɔ shikome. Kɛ́ ojie nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ oya tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Egbiɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii. koni enyɛ enu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why is it important for me to leave dry leaves and grass covering the soil around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mashi baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbɔleɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with organic matter acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the ground cool, preserves moisture during dry weather, and prevents harsh weather from damaging the soil surface.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni etsiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ fɔŋ naa koni ekafite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Should I remove mulch from my field when the rainy season ends, or leave it in place?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee loo mashi lɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ?

english: You should leave the mulch in place. It protects the soil from drying out rapidly under the hot sun and keeps the ground moist for your crop roots for a longer time.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What happens if I harvest my crops before the right time?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani be ni sa lɛ shɛ?

english: Harvesting too early means your crop hasn't fully developed its strength or size. The produce will shrink, spoil easily, and won't fetch a good price at the market.
ga: Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ enáko hewalɛ loo elɛɛmɔ kwraa lolo. Nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ baagbɔjɔ, ebaafite oya ni enaŋ jara kpakpa yɛ jara nɔ.

english: How can I tell if bad weather will spoil my crop while it is maturing in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii lɛ baafite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ be mli ni amɛmiikwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat or sudden heavy rains during maturity cause stress to crops. Checking your crops regularly for yellow leaves, drooping stems, or rot helps you take action before the harvest is ruined.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa trukaa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli daa kɛji baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ mli. tso ni egbee shi loo ni egbo lɛ baaha ofee nɔ ko dani akpata ŋmaa lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I dry my harvested crops directly on the bare dirt ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ migbiɔ mikpamɔ nii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Drying directly on bare ground exposes your harvest to dampness, soil pests, and dirt. Using clean mats or raised platforms keeps the crop clean and allows air to dry it evenly.
ga: Kɛ́ ogbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ Kooloi kɛ Muji Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔji ni he tse loo shikpɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe tseɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How do I know when my harvested crops are dry enough to store safely?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mikpamɔ lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto shweshweeshwe?

english: Crops are ready for storage when they feel hard, crisp, and show no moisture when squeezed. Storing crops before they are fully dry causes mold and decay to destroy your harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ efee klalo kɛha nitoo kɛji enu he akɛ eyɛ shiŋŋ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ejieee ŋmɔtɔ kpo kɛji akɛ amɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii to dani amɛgbi kwraa lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What causes the leaves of my crops to change color and drop off on their own?
ga: Mɛni miiha mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsake amɛhe su ni amɛmiigbee shi?

english: Plants shed leaves when they suffer from stress like poor soil nutrients, pest attacks, or lack of water. It is the plant's way of saving energy to keep its main stem alive.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔi, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ. Nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ loo nu ni faaa yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni eha tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ ahi shi.

english: Can I leave my mature root crops in the ground until I am ready to sell them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi shishifãi ni edara lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni mafee klalo akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ amɛ?

english: Many root crops can remain in the soil safely for a short time after maturing, but leaving them too long during heavy rains or heat can cause them to become woody or rot.
ga: Shishifãi babaoo baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe be kukuoo ko. beni edara sɛɛ Shi kɛ́ ashi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo latsaa be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha etsɔ tso loo egbo.

english: Why do extension officers call farm spray 'pesticide' or 'weedicide', but we farmers call it 'medicine'?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi tsɛɔ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ akɛ ‘tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi’ loo ‘tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi’ shi wɔ okwaafoi lɛ wɔtsɛɔ amɛ ‘tsofai’ lɛ?

english: Calling farm chemicals 'medicine' can be dangerous because medicine is meant to cure, but weedkillers and pesticides are designed to kill living things. Using the wrong product or applying too much can destroy your crop instead of helping it.
ga: Kɛ́ atsɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai lɛ akɛ ‘tsofai fɔji’ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efee oshara. Ejaakɛ tsofa yɛ ni akɛbaatsa Shi afee tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ koni amɛgbe nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli. Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni ejaaa tsu nii loo okɛtsu nii fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua lɛ.

english: If I use just a small amount of weedkiller on my farm, can it still damage the food growing under the ground?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofa fioo ko pɛ tsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani ebaanyɛ efite niyenii ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo?

english: Yes, even small amounts of strong weedkillers can seep into the soil and reach the roots. Root crops like cassava absorb these chemicals, which can cause the tubers to stunt, spoil, or rot before harvest.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsofai bibii ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni he wa lɛ po baanyɛ abote sũ lɛ mli ni eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Tuber ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cassava lɛ shwieɔ tsofai nɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha bulb lɛ afee bibii, efite, loo egbo dani akpa.

english: Why do chemical bottles have warning signs, and what do they mean for my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma tsɛnsii lɛ yɛ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii lɛ? Ni mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Warning signs show how dangerous a chemical is to humans, soil, and crops. They indicate if a spray is too strong for certain plants or if it will poison the soil if applied incorrectly.
ga: Kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii tsɔɔ bɔ ni tsofai yeɔ adesai, shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awui amɛhaa. Ekɛɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei komɛi anɔ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ awui kɛji akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: How long must I wait to harvest my cassava after spraying chemicals on my farm?
ga: Kɛ́ wɔkɛ tsofai shwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ wɔmɛ dani wɔkpa ŋmei?

english: Every crop chemical has a required waiting period called a Pre-Harvest Interval. Harvesting too early means active chemicals remain in the soil and roots, which can cause the crop to rot or make it unsafe to eat.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei amli lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be ni akɛmɛɛɔ ni ale lɛ akɛ dani kpamɔ be lɛ. Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ tsɔɔ akɛ tsofai ni tsuɔ nii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii agbo loo eha efee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ.

english: What causes cassava tubers to rot inside the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa?

english: Cassava roots rot mainly from fungal diseases in waterlogged soil or from harsh farm chemicals that sink into the ground and damage the root tissue.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli loo ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni mli wa ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ mli.

english: Is it safe to spray weedkiller directly around the base of my cassava plants?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oookɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ afɔ mitso lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ? Mi-cassava tso lɛ shishi

english: No, spraying near the base allows the stem and shallow roots to absorb the chemical. This weakens the plant, causes leaf drop, and often leads to rotten tubers.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa shwie shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaafite tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eŋɔ tsofai Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni bei pii lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: How can I clear weeds around my cassava without using chemicals that might damage the roots?
ga: Majie jwɛi kɛjɛ he ni ebɔle he lɛ. Te aaafee tɛŋŋ adu ŋmei ni akɛ tsofai ni baanyɛ afite shishifãi lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can clear weeds manually using a cutlass or hoe, or plant low-growing cover crops like egusi melon to block weeds naturally without putting harmful chemicals into the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ cutlass loo hoe ajie jwɛi lɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ. Aloo dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ fioo, tamɔ Egusi melon, koni ekɛtsi jwɛi anaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Can spraying chemical weedkillers spoil my soil for future crops?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ afite mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, heavy or repeated use of strong chemicals can kill beneficial soil organisms like earthworms and good microbes, leaving the land weak and less fertile for future planting.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii waa loo akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii bibii ni hi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ gbɔjɔmɔ ni ehaaa adu nii wɔsɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are dying from a plant disease or from a chemical I sprayed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigboi yɛ tsei ahe helai loo tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ahewɔ?

english: Chemical damage usually appears quickly within days of spraying and affects all sprayed plants equally. Disease damage usually spreads slowly from plant to plant over weeks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baa oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli yɛ be mli ni akɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. ni enaa tsei fɛɛ ni afɔ amɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Bei pii lɛ, helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa fiofio. Kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛtee tso kroko nɔ otsii babaoo.

english: Why do crop leaves sometimes turn yellow or burn right after spraying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛshãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ afɔ amɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves burn when the chemical mixture is too strong, sprayed during the hot midday sun, or when the product is not suited for that specific crop.
ga: Baai lɛ shãa kɛji tsofa ni akɛfutu lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Spray yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni nɔ ni afee lɛ esaaa nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there are no bigger trees or plantains around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji loo plantains bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide shade and shelter, keeping the air cool and moist around young cocoa trees so they do not dry out and die.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo kɛ wɔɔhe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe bɔni afee ni amɛkagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my green maize plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the maize the food it needs to stay green and grow strong ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eha etoi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does mixing dry animal manure into my soil make my crops grow better than planting in normal dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni mikɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Animal manure adds rich plant nutrients, helps soil hold water longer during dry days, and loosens hard ground so roots can easily grow deep to search for food.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã haa tsei aniyenii yaa hiɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ada kɛya shɔŋŋ koni amɛna niyenii oya.

english: How do I know which way to stick my cassava stem cuttings into the dirt?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male bɔ ni akɛ ŋmei niji woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small bud knots on the cassava stem. Make sure those buds point upward toward the sky so the leaves can sprout quickly above ground.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmei bibioo lɛ. Kpɛtɛ ŋmei tso lɛ he Kwɛmɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni baai lɛ adara oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to push wooden poles into the soil for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi tso tso ko awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves high in the air and prevents diseases caused by leaves touching damp ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni ekɛfee hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa helai ni baa lɛ kɛbaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ tsiɔ naa.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my crops with dry grass during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ? Akɛ jwɛi ŋmɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool, stops sunshine from drying up soil moisture, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ. Tsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why are there small holes and dark dirt inside the central leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Kɛ muji ni tsuɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the center leaves to eat the tender green plant material, but spraying approved control solutions early stops them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Shi tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ hela lɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ haa amɛkpaa mra.

english: Why are the bottom tips of my green tomatoes turning soft and black before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi eŋɔli lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This rot happens when plants get irregular amounts of water and cannot absorb calcium properly. Giving tomato plants steady, even watering keeps the fruit bottoms healthy.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ nine shɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Tomato Tsei ni Haa Ehiɔ Shi Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ ashishi hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when the air gets too hot or when the soil gets too dry. Regular watering keeps the plants cool enough to turn flowers into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni ehaa fɔfɔii feɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and short when I put many seeds into one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ kukuji beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots compete for the same food and water in the soil. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed and grow thick stalks.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when I clear all the tall trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei kakadaji fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the topsoil before their roots grow deep enough to gather ground moisture.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ amli aba mli bɔ ni sa ni amɛbua ŋmɔtɔ naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on lower maize stalks usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it relies on to build healthy green leaves and large corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni akɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Does it really make a difference if I do not train my yam vines onto wooden stakes?
ga: Kɛ mitsɔseee sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso nɔ Ani ebaaha srɔtofeemɔ aba diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Staking exposes the yam leaves to direct sunlight, allowing the vine to generate more energy to feed and expand the tubers growing underneath the ground.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa wain tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaatsu nii akɛ niyenii ni ekwɛ̃ɔ bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Which way should I point the stem cuttings when I am planting cassava in my field?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ atsɔ nɔ atsɔɔ ŋmei ni afo lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should be planted with the small bud nodes pointing upwards towards the sky so the shoots grow smoothly into the air while roots develop underground.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can harvest more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stems and smaller harvest yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my land help my next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and beans capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground through their root nodules, naturally enriching the soil for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and preventing the fruits from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi yibii anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that carry plant viruses, which weaken the crop and stop fruits from developing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni hiɛ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ehaaa aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or leaves on top of the soil around my vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ashwã shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material acts as a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool and moist under heat while slowing down weed growth.
ga: Tsoi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ hulutsoo be mli, yɛ be mli ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ daalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops weak even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your plants, leaving them undernourished.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha otsei lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout when heavy rain floods my farm right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa ba miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu lɛ?

english: Buried seeds need oxygen from the soil air gaps to wake up and sprout; standing water fills these gaps and suffocates the seeds, causing them to rot.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afu lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ eyiɔ nɛkɛ hei nɛɛ amli ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What should fresh cocoa leaves look like when the seed first sprouts?
ga: Te esa akɛ kookoo baai heei lɛ afee tɛŋŋ beni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves often start with a reddish, light purple, or pale green color before turning dark green. This soft, colorful stage is completely normal as the young leaf expands before it hardens.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo baai bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi akɛ etsuru, purple ni mli tse, loo eŋɔli ni mli tse dani etsɔɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ sui sɔrɔtoi nɛɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa beni baai bibii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ dani amɛwaa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and falling off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the young plant is getting too much harsh direct sunlight, not enough water, or lacks nutrients in the soil. Providing light shade and steady moisture helps them recover.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso bibioo lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛnáaa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shade ni mli tse kɛ hulutsoo ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhe waa.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa sprout is developing healthy stems and roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ yɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: A healthy sprout has firm, unblemished young leaves and a stem that stands upright. Over time, the soft green stem will naturally thicken and turn woody as the root system expands.
ga: Tsei bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai bibii ni mli wa, ni muji ko bɛ amɛhe kɛ tsei bibii ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ tso be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my cocoa plants when setting up my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ beni mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ toɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa plants are generally spaced about 3 meters by 3 meters apart. Proper spacing gives the roots room to spread, ensures proper air movement, and prevents trees from overcrowding each other as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 x mitai 3. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa shishifã lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni sa. ni etsĩ tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ekome tsɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why is it important to mark out straight lines before I plant my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atɛŋ line dani adu kookoo tso lɛ?

english: Planting in neat, organized rows makes it much easier to move around your farm, manage weeds, apply fertilizer, prune, and harvest without damaging neighboring crops.
ga: Kɛ́ oodu nii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo nɔ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ oootsi oŋmɔ lɛ he, okwɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, oookpa tsei lɛ, ni oookpa. ni efiteee tsei lɛ kɛ naagbai ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ

english: Why does the stem at the base of my young cocoa tree look so thin compared to its leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso bibioo ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ shishi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ mlɛo waa kɛ akɛto ebaai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants focus early energy on growing leaves to collect sunlight. As the tree gets older, the stem base will naturally thicken into a strong trunk to support the upper branches.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ kɛ amɛ mra be mli hewalɛ lɛ maa baai ni miida lɛ anɔ koni amɛbua hulu la naa. Kɛ tso lɛ eda lɛ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni etsɔ tso ni mli wa ni baaye abua niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Can I plant oil palm trees on the same farm with my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu mu tsei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ kookoo tsei?

english: Yes, but you must space them wide apart. Oil palms grow very tall and broad, so planting them too close will block too much sunlight and compete with cocoa roots for soil water.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ nyɛtsi nyɛhe kɛjɛ nyɛhe. Mu tsei lɛ daraa waa ni amɛlɛɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi hulu la babaoo naa ni ekɛ kookoo shishifãi lɛ baabɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Which crop should I put in the ground first when starting a mixed tree farm?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ madu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kɛ́ mije tsei ni akɛfutuɔ nii akwɛmɔ shishi?

english: It is best to plant temporary shade crops like plantains first, then plant your young cocoa seedlings so they are immediately protected from the hot direct sun.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, aduɔ kookoo tsei koni ekɛbu hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How do I prepare the soil properly before putting my young cocoa sprouts into the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani madu kookoo tsei bibii?

english: Clear heavy weeds, dig planting holes, and fill them with rich topsoil or well-rotted manure. Soft, nutrient-rich soil allows young seedling roots to establish quickly.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi ni tsii lɛ, tsumɔ bu ni akɛduɔ nii, ni okɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ awo mli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi oya.

english: How many years will it take after sprouting for my cocoa tree to start bearing pods?
ga: Kɛji mi-cacao tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ ebaahe dani ebɔi ŋmeii feemɔ?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties typically begin flowering and producing pods in 2 to 3 years under proper care, while older varieties usually take 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: Why shouldn't I just dig up plants growing along the roadside to plant on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ he lɛ ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants growing wild or along roadsides often carry hidden pests and diseases. Planting them can spread infection to your whole farm and produce very poor yields compared to certified seeds from approved dealers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kooi amli loo gbɛjegbɛi ahe lɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Amɛ ni ooodu lɛ baanyɛ atswa oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hela ni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi waa aba kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni jɛ mɛi ni jaa ni akpɛlɛ amɛnɔ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Can I save money by planting seeds from crops I bought to eat at the market?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ shika ato kɛtsɔ tsei ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ dumɔwui ni madu lɛ nɔ?

english: Market food crops are often treated or harvested from hybrid plants whose seeds won't grow into healthy or high-yielding crops, leading to wasted time and effort on your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsuɔ niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ he nii loo akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni amɛdumɔwui lɛ nyɛɛɛ ada ni amɛfee tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ loo ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ofiteɔ be kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if a new stem or sucker is healthy enough to plant on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso loo tso yibii hee ko mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Healthy planting material should come from reliable, disease-free sources and show no signs of spots, root rot, or insect damage before you put it in your soil.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔ nii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ajɛ he ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ, ni helai akafee nɔ ko, ni ejieee ŋmɔtɔ, shishifãi ni egbo, loo kooloi ni efite dani odu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is the crop chemical I bought cheaply from an unregistered seller not working on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni mihe yɛ jara ni waaa nɔ kɛjɛ nihɔɔlɔ ko ni aŋmako egbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cheap farm chemicals bought from unapproved vendors are often expired, fake, or diluted, which means they will fail to control pests and can even ruin your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni jara waaa ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni hɔ̃ɔ nibii ni bɛ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ, amɛbe eho, amɛji amalei, loo amɛwo mli nu, ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛye tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can I use any farm medicine I find to spray my crops when they look unhealthy?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni ana yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe bɛ hewalɛ?

english: No, using the wrong chemical can burn your crops or leave the disease untreated. Every crop problem requires a specific, approved chemical applied at the correct dosage.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni ejaaa ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã oŋmɔshi nibii loo ekɛ helai ni atsaaa lɛ aba. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe naagba fɛɛ naagba biɔ ni akɛ tsofa pɔtɛɛ ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii yɛ bɔ ni sa mli.

english: Why do my newly transplanted crop seedlings wilt and struggle to grow in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui heei ni midu lɛ miiho ni amɛmiibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings experience shock when moved to direct sunlight and open fields; they need proper watering and temporary shade until their roots settle in the ground.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ ahe feɔ amɛ yaa kɛji ajie amɛ kɛtee hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse mli. Nu ni sa kɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli he miihia amɛ kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baatswa shi shiŋŋ yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow after applying farm chemical treatment?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai etsu nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves can happen if a chemical is mixed too strong or applied during hot hours, causing root burn and stress to the crop instead of helping it.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aba kɛji akɛ tsofai lɛ futu mli waa tsɔ loo akɛtsu nii yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shãa ni ehaa tso lɛ haoɔ moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua lɛ.

english: Why do crops planted in the same spot keep getting the same disease season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ he kome lɛ náa helai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Disease organisms stay alive in the soil long after crops are harvested. Without rotating your crops or treating the soil, new plants will catch the same sickness.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ atsakeee ŋmɔshi nibii loo akwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, tsei heei hu baaná hela nakai nɔŋŋ.

english: Is it a good idea to dig up a sick plant and replant it in another field to save it?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ aaakumɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ ni adu amɛ yɛ saatso kroko nɔ koni akɛhere amɛyiwala?

english: Moving a diseased plant will only transfer the sickness to healthy soil and surrounding crops, damaging more of your farm instead of saving the plant.
ga: Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛ hela yaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ. Efiteɔ oŋmɔ lɛ babaoo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaabu tso lɛ he lɛ

english: Why am I putting in so much hard physical labor on my farm but still getting very small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mihe woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli babaoo ni mináaa yibii fioo lolo lɛ?

english: Hard work alone isn't enough if you start with poor planting materials or wrong chemical treatments; good yields depend on high-quality seeds, correct timing, and proper crop care.
ga: Nitsumɔ ni wa pɛ faaa kɛji akɛ okɛ dumɔ nibii ni ehiii loo tsofai ni ejaaa tsu nii kɛje shishi. Yibiiwoo kpakpa damɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ. be ni ja kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ

english: You should wait until the soil is thoroughly soaked from two or three good, steady rains rather than planting after the very first light shower, so your seeds do not dry up and die in hot soil.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔ kpakpai enyɔ loo etɛ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mli, moŋ fe ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Afeɔ enɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi ni amɛkagboi yɛ sũ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I clear my farm land without burning the dry weeds and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mikɛshãaa jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter and kills helpful living organisms in the ground. Leaving dry plant material to decay naturally enriches the soil with food and helps retain moisture for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa lɛ ahiɛ, ni egbeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ oshi tsei ahe nibii ni egbi lɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ni eye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or beans helps restore soil nutrients naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele tsakemɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for strong green growth. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha hewalɛ, eŋɔli dalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and moisture it needs during its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo lɛ ni enáa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Does tying my yam vines to wooden stakes really help me get bigger yams?
ga: Ani sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛfiɔ tsei ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi diɛŋtsɛ ni minine shɛɔ sweet potatoi wuji anɔ?

english: Yes, lifting the vines onto stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight, which the plant uses to make food. More sunlight on the leaves directly results in larger and heavier yam tubers under the ground.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, wain tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ haa hulu la babaoo shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ. ni tsei baanyɛ amɛkɛfee niyenii Hulu la babaoo ni tsoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ baa shikpɔŋ shishi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients, water, and light. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food and moisture they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, nu kɛ la mli. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ehaa tsei lɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays around them because the soil does not drain well. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or attacks from tiny pests. Watering regularly during dry spells and protecting plants from insects helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tutua amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa kɛ tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies sucking the plant's juices or spreading viruses. Controlling these insects early stops the leaves from twisting and keeps the plant healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ tomato nu loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baaha baai lɛ akatsɔ ni eye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant plantains on the same land where I am planting my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo tsei bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa shoots burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa trees mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow better when I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the soil before them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on nitrogen in the soil. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and fix it into the ground, acting as a natural fertilizer for the next maize crop.
ga: Abele haa nitrogen babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This causes thin, weak stalks that produce very small cobs instead of healthy ones.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ baa.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to harvest, and what happens if I leave it in the ground too long?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa? Ni mɛni baaba kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, about 9 to 12 months after planting. If left in the ground too long, the cassava roots become hard, woody, and less pleasant to eat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Cassava shishifãi lɛ wa, amɛji tsei ni amɛhiɛ kpaaa nɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves dry up and die during the harmattan season even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ harmatta be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: The harmattan winds are extremely dry and pull moisture directly out of plant leaves faster than roots can draw water from the soil. Placing dry grass or mulch around the base of the plant helps trap water in the ground.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa ni ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli tɛ̃ɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he. Shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves off the ground and spread out in the sunlight. Staking allows the leaves to trap sunlight efficiently, which produces the energy needed to grow large yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã hulu la lɛ mli. Staking haa baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa anáa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit viral diseases, or by heat stress. Catching and controlling these small pests early stops the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni hiɛ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli Mɔmɔ ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How should I put fertilizer on my farm so the heavy rains do not wash it away?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni nugbɔ ni naa wa akanɛ?

english: Avoid spreading fertilizer on top of dry ground before a heavy downpour. Place the fertilizer a few centimeters away from the plant stem, push it into the moist soil, and cover it lightly with earth so the roots can absorb it.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ he. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo sɛntimitai fioo komɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. Tsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ sũ aha nɔ fioo. koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after the first rains drop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally built to survive in local soils with very little water. They react instantly to the first rain, whereas crop seeds take longer to wake up and establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni abɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji ni nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Amɛtsuɔ he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui heɔ be babaoo dani amɛteɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I stored from my last harvest fail to sprout when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Stored seeds fail to sprout if they were put away while still damp or if small insects like weevils damaged the inside of the seed. Seeds must be dried thoroughly and kept in airtight containers to remain alive for planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji ajie amɛ be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo lɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii fite dumɔwu lɛ mli. Esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli koni amɛhi shi kɛha dumɔ.

english: What key features should I look for when choosing land to grow plantains?
ga: Mɛɛ sui ni he hiaa esa akɛ matao beni mihalaa shikpɔŋ ni mikɛbaadu plantains yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains need rich, dark soil that drains water easily and receives plenty of rain. You should avoid swampy land where water sits for days, as waterlogged soil rots the underground roots and kills the plant.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni mli edɔ ni nu hoɔ oya ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo lɛ he miihia plantains. Esa akɛ okpa hei ni nu yɔɔ ni nu baanyɛ ahi shi gbii babaoo lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ agbo ni efite tsei.

english: Why do farmers often plant plantains alongside young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ okwaafoi duɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily under the harsh sun. Plantains grow very fast and have massive leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool soil moisture it needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: How long does a plantain sucker take from planting until I can harvest the fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani akpaa plantain tsei lɛ?

english: With good rain and rich soil, a plantain stalk usually flowers at around 8 to 12 months. The bunch then takes another 3 to 4 months to mature, making the full journey from planting to harvest about 11 to 15 months.
ga: Ejaakɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu baa nii. Bei pii lɛ, plantain tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi beni amɛye aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12, no sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ aheɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 krokomɛi dani amɛdaraa. Enɛ haa gbɛfaa muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui kɛyashiɔ ŋmaakpamɔ mli lɛ feɔ aaafee nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 15.

english: Why are extra little plants growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii babaoo yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Special kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Mi plantain shishitoo titri lɛ he

english: Plantains multiply naturally by sending up shoots called suckers from their underground roots. These are new plants growing, but if you leave too many, they will steal food and water from your main plant.
ga: Plantains fɔɔ bii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ ni amɛtsuɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei heei ni miida. Shi kɛji oha etee shɔŋŋ tsɔ Amɛbaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ otsei titrii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves split into strips when there is strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ fãi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves split naturally along their side veins during windy weather. This is a special survival design that lets wind pass through without pulling the entire tree out of the ground.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ fãji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ amli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Enɛ ji gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ejieee tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my plantain tree turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: It is normal for the oldest bottom leaves to turn yellow and die as the tree puts its energy into growing new green leaves at the top. However, if many leaves turn yellow quickly, your soil may be low on nutrients or water.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi be mli ni tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai heei eŋɔli yɛ nɔ lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai babaoo batsɔ ŋmɔŋ oya lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ niyenii loo nu faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I cut away the small shoots growing at the foot of my main plantain stem?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? Ani eekwɛ̃ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi?

english: Yes, you should prune away most extra shoots, keeping only one or two strong ones. This practice, called desuckering, ensures the main tree gets enough food to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ateŋ babaoo. Akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 1 loo 2 pɛ toɔ. Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ suction jiemɔ. (desuckering) koni tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: What causes my plantain tree to fall over before the fruits are ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Plantains have shallow roots, so a heavy bunch of fruit can pull the whole tree down during strong winds. Underground pests eating the roots can also weaken the tree, so farmers use wooden poles to prop up heavy bunches.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso yibii ni tsii lɛ baanyɛ agbala tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, okwaafoi kɛ tsei tsuɔ nii kɛfiɔ jwɛi ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ.

english: How do I tell if a bunch of plantains is ready for me to cut down?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ plantain falɛ ko efee klalo akɛ mafolɔ?

english: Plantains are ready to harvest when the individual fruits look plump and rounded rather than sharp and square, and the dried flower tips at the ends rub off easily when touched.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ni fɔfɔii ni egbi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ ata he.

english: Will a plantain stem produce fruit again after I cut the main bunch?
ga: Ani banana tso lɛ baawo yibii ekoŋŋ beni mifo tso titri lɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, a single plantain stem flowers and fruits only once in its lifetime. After harvesting the bunch, you cut down the main stem so the underground shoots can grow up and produce the next crop.
ga: Dabi, plantain tso kome pɛ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii yɛ eshihilɛ mli. Beni akpa tso lɛ fã lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Ehe miihia ni ofo tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli koni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛwo tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can I still grow vegetables on my farm during the dry season if I have water on my land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli? Kɛji miyɛ nu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, crops can grow all year if you have a reliable water source. During the dry season, plants actually get plenty of sunlight to make food fast, as long as their roots receive regular water from irrigation or moist soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛji oyɛ nu jɛɛhe ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsei lɛ baaná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛye nii oya. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baaná nu kɛjɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa lɛ.

english: Does watering my crops with ground water from a well work as well as rain water?
ga: Ani nubu nu ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ?

english: Groundwater is great for crops during dry months because it gives them reliable drink. Rainwater contains a bit of natural nitrogen from the air that gives plants an extra quick boost, but ground water will keep your crops healthy and producing when rain fails.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi nu hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli ejaakɛ eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnuɔ nu. Nitrogen fioo ko ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ nugbɔ nu mli, ni no haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ oya. Shi shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ baaye abua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ.

english: Why do some of my crops turn yellow and die when water stays on the land for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like people do. When soil stays flooded or soaked with water for too long, it drowns the roots, preventing them from taking up food and causing the leaves to turn yellow and decay.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ekɛ nu wo mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ehaaa amɛye niyenii ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ.

english: What kinds of crops grow best in low areas of my farm where groundwater comes up naturally?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ yaa ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ?

english: Crops like rice, sugarcane, and taro (cocoyam) love wet soils and can thrive where underground water keeps the soil wet. Most popular vegetables prefer well-drained soil, so they do better on raised beds or higher ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ taro (kookoo) sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ efɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ̃ yɛ hei ni shikpɔŋ shishi nu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɔ̃ɔ lɛ. Aduawai ni ale waa lɛ ateŋ babaoo sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu yɛ saatsoi ni awó nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ.

english: Why do crops grow faster and greener near natural wet spots or streams on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ adebɔɔ mli hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ loo faai ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Plants near continuous water sources have steady access to moisture, allowing their root systems to constantly absorb soil nutrients without suffering from dry spells or heat stress.
ga: Tsei ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhe ni yaa nɔ lɛ naa ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ be fɛɛ be ni hɔmɔ loo dɔlɛ he haomɔ ko enaaa amɛ.

english: Is the water drained from a fish pond good for watering my crops?
ga: Ani nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ loo ŋshɔ mli lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa?

english: Yes, fish pond water is excellent for crops because fish waste adds natural nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus to the water, acting like a gentle liquid fertilizer that helps plants grow greener and stronger.
ga: Hɛɛ, loo ŋshɔ mli nu lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ ji akɛ, loo mli jwɛi kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus fataa nu lɛ he. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nu ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: If I dig a fish pond on my land, can I plant crops along the banks?
ga: Kɛ mifo loo ŋshɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa?

english: Yes, the soil along pond banks stays naturally moist from seepage. Planting crops like bananas, leafy vegetables, or papaya along the edges makes good use of space and keeps the plants hydrated without extra manual watering.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ faa lɛ naa lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ kɛjɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli. Tsei tamɔ banana, aduawai ni yɔɔ baai, loo papaya ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ baaha akɛ he ni yɔɔ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni eye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ niji tsuuu he nii.

english: Why do my crops look wilted during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the soil is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up when the sun is very strong. This wilting is a natural defense mechanism to reduce leaf surface area exposed to heat, and they usually recover by evening.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛji hulu la lɛ mli wa waa. Nɛkɛ shwiemɔ nɛɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he koni akɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulutsoo baa lɛ shi. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ

english: Why do some crops handle dry weather better than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe nii jogbaŋŋ fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Deep-rooted crops like cassava and tree crops can reach far underground to drink hidden groundwater during dry periods, while shallow-rooted crops like lettuce rely strictly on surface water and dry out quickly without frequent watering.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aya shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni amɛyanu shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tamɔ lettuce lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya ni afɔɔɔ amɛ nu.

english: How can I tell if my soil holds enough water for crops during short dry spells?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ ni baa be kukuoo mli lɛ mli?

english: You can test your soil by squeezing a handful from a few inches deep; if it forms a ball that stays together without dripping water, it holds moisture well. Adding organic material like animal manure or compost helps soil hold onto water much longer.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka shikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ fioo ko ni oootsi kɛjɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ eji nɔ ko ni yɔɔ kokroo ni akɛkpɛtɛ he ni nu shwieee shi lɛ, ebaahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he. Ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and die when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct, harsh sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the soil. Planting shade trees or plantains nearby shields the young cocoa from intense sun until its leaves are strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashi baai lɛ baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before they turn into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting when the weather gets extremely hot or when the plant does not get enough water. Heat stress prevents successful pollination, so the plant drops the blossoms to conserve its energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ mli haomɔ tsiɔ pollination ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: How do weeds actually hurt my pepper crop when they are just growing in the same bed?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye mi-pepper tsei lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ saatso kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very quickly and act like thieves in your farm. They steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients directly from the soil that your pepper plants need to grow big and produce good fruit.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa o-pepper tsei lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer gives the maize the food it needs to grow green leaves and healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava roots get soft and rot underground when it rains continuously for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains leave the soil flooded with water for days, the air pockets fill up, causing the cassava roots to drown, decay, and rot underground.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ gbii babaoo lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ amli eyiɔ, ni no haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛshwieɔ shi, ni amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why is it bad if I plant four or five maize seeds close together in the same small hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ midu ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu bibioo kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing stalks fight each other for soil food, water, and sunlight. Because none of them get enough, they all remain thin and weak, producing tiny or empty cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsoi ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli ejaakɛ amɛfaaa. Amɛ fɛɛ amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa. ni kɛ cob bibioo loo efolo baa

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a crop family that can pull nitrogen food out of the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, that natural food remains in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans fata tsei aweku ko ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ he. beni okpa lɛ Nakai adebɔɔ mli niyenii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does placing dry grass around the base of my crops keep them from wilting in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ haaa amɛgboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass creates a protective blanket called mulch. It prevents the hot sun from evaporating water directly out of the dirt, keeping the roots moist and cool for a longer time.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe jɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I place strong chemical fertilizer right against the stem of my plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli lɛ woɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated mineral salts. Placing them directly against the stem can burn the plant's skin and roots, so it is safer to place the fertilizer a short distance away where the roots can safely reach out to absorb it.
ga: Fertilizer lɛ yɛ mineral salts babaoo. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ eshishifãi lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo he ko ni kɛ jɛmɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ fioo. ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he ni amɛŋɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ

english: Why do armyworms hide deep inside the leaves of my maize during the day instead of being outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-corn baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli moŋ fe kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Armyworms hide in the deep folds of maize leaves during the hot day to protect their soft bodies from drying out in the sun and to hide from birds. They come out during the cooler nights to feed on your leaves.
ga: Asraafoi akuu lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛgbɔmɔtsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ ahe koni hulu lɛ akagbi, ni amɛkɛtee amɛhe kɛjɛ okpoi ahe. Amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛbaye obaai lɛ.

english: This usually happens when your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the primary plant food responsible for leaf growth. Applying balanced NPK fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure early in the crop's life keeps the leaves green and helps produce larger corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa. NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni eye ebua ni aná ŋmei toi wuji.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hot afternoon even if it rained two days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii enyɔ ni eho nɛ moŋ?

english: Soil without enough organic matter cannot hold moisture for long, so it dries out quickly under intense tropical sun. Adding compost or dry leaf mulch around your crops helps the soil trap and hold water closer to the roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi awo he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi ni eha nu lɛ abɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small brown droppings inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This is a classic sign of Fall Armyworm attack. The caterpillars hide inside the central leaf whorl during the day and destroy tender growing leaves, which can severely reduce your harvest if not controlled early with approved sprays or neem extracts.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he okadi ni ale waa. Kplukai lɛ baahi amɛhe yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni efiteɔ baai ni miida lɛ blɛoo Enɛ baanyɛ aha okpamɔ lɛ aba shi waa. Kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ mra kɛ neem spray loo nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and showing bright yellow and green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ?

english: Your cassava has Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies or passed through infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties from the agriculture office prevents this virus from destroying your farm.
ga: O ŋmei lɛ yɛ ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ loo kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ Odumɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kɛjɛɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akafite oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting and curling upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips, mites, or aphids feeding on the leaf juices. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat so the plant can make food and flower properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ahoo ni ewo fɔfɔi jogbaŋŋ.

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crops end up fighting each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, tall stems that fall over easily and produce very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Nibii ni adu lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbeeɔ shi oya lɛ baa. ni ekɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko baa

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb high instead of trailing on the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso koni ekwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ moŋ fe ni eeenyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make the food that grows big tubers underground. Lifting the vines on stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight and protects them from soil-borne fungi and damp rot.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ awó wain tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la babaoo naa tsei lɛ ahe, ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting tender cocoa seedlings during their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Tomatoes shed flowers when they experience stress from intense heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping soil moisture steady and avoiding heavy chemical fertilizers during flowering helps the blooms set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli ni tsii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ haa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai shwereɔ.

english: Why are my rice plants turning pale yellow and remaining short in my lowland swamp field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lolo yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pale, stunted rice in lowlands often suffers from nutrient blockage due to water standing still for too long, or iron toxicity in acidic mud. Draining the field periodically allows root air flow and helps the rice absorb nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni mli tse ni egbɔjɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ naa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ ehe naa yɛ nu ni ehiɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. loo dade ni yɔɔ muji ni mli edɔ mli lɛ mli tsofa ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie nu kɛjɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil has too much water drowning the roots. Adding compost or proper fertilizer helps the maize regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-ŋmei lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni etsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before any pods actually form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from excessive sun heat, lack of water, or insect attacks. Keeping enough shade trees around your cocoa field and managing pests helps the flowers stay on to produce pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi bibii tutua amɛ. Tsei akwɛmɔ koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔ ni sa Cocoa ŋmɔji kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi koni amɛwo ŋmɔji.

english: Planting maize on the same spot repeatedly drains the same nutrients from the soil and allows pests to settle in permanent homes. Alternating maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts refills nitrogen in the soil and keeps it healthy.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ feɔ shihilɛhei ni hiɔ shi daa yɛ shĩai amli. Akɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii tsakeɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt in the afternoon sun even when I water them every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa leebi moŋ?

english: Under strong sunshine, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the ground. Covering the soil around your plants with dry grass or leaves keeps the ground cool and retains moisture longer.
ga: yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very bushy with lots of leaves but produce very little fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen makes them focus entirely on growing branches and leaves instead of flowers. Balancing the soil nutrients encourages the tomato plant to stop leafy growth and start putting energy into setting fruit.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ haa amɛsusuɔ tsei niji kɛ baai ni miida lɛ ahe moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ woɔ tomato tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkpa amɛbaai lɛ akwɛmɔ ni amɛbɔi hewalɛ babaoo hamɔ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: What makes my yam tubers grow small and twisted instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Yams need soft, loose, deep soil to expand easily. If the soil is too hard, stony, or compacted, the tuber cannot push through smoothly, resulting in stunted or crooked shapes.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ koni egbɛ eshwa oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ, eyɛ tɛi, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa mɔ he feɔ shoo loo egbɔjɔ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds while my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have weak roots and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures your young crops get all the food they need to establish themselves.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei bibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛto amɛhe shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and growing small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap out of new leaves. Spraying with natural pest solutions like neem leaf extract early on helps stop these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai heei amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi tamɔ neem tso mli nu lɛ shwie nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi kooloi nɛɛ anaa.

english: Does burning the bush on my field before planting help or hurt my crops?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mishãa dani miduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa loo eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Burning clears the land fast, but it destroys beneficial organic matter and kills helpful soil organisms. Clearing without burning leaves organic material behind to rot naturally into valuable food for your crops.
ga: Shãa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse oya. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ otsi ohe ni oshãaa lɛ, eshiɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ sɛɛ koni efite yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni etsɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest produce lower yields than fresh certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mikpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can carry hidden diseases from the previous season and naturally lose vigor over time. Certified seeds are selected and treated to resist common local diseases and produce uniform, high-yielding plants.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ atere helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛfite amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ni atsaa amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. The plant naturally moves its remaining food from older lower leaves to feed new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing very tall with thick green leaves but no flowers or peppers?
