ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni ebaa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔii loo ŋmeii bɛ?

english: Giving your crops too much nitrogen fertilizer causes them to spend all their energy growing stems and foliage instead of developing flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off before any fruit can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the crop experiences sudden heat stress, lack of soil moisture, or extreme humidity, which prevents the flower from successfully setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ trukaa. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fa tsɔ Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable crop leaves curl inward into tight tubes during the sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural shield to protect itself from losing too much water in intense heat, though persistent curling indicates the roots need deeper watering.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu babaoo ni efiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛ́ eyaa nɔ ebɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni awo shishifãi lɛ amli nu ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all big trees and plant them in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji ni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa crops have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. They need partial shade from nurse crops like plantains to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell that my cassava crop is fully ready for harvest under the ground without digging up every plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni okɛ tso fɛɛ tso tsuuu nii?

english: When cassava roots reach full maturity, the lower leaves on the main stem naturally dry up and shed, showing the plant has finished storing starch in its underground tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara kwraa lɛ, ŋmei titri lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa.

english: Why do my yam vines start drying up and turning brown before the rainy season completely ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa naagbee lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally die back when the underground tuber reaches full growth, but early drying can be caused by fungal leaf diseases like anthracnose attacking the plant.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ. Shi tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni ji fungal leaf tamɔ anthracnose ni tutuaa tso lɛ baanyɛ aha egbi oya.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over on their own when the fruit bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbeeɔ shi beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that cannot hold heavy weights easily. As the fruit bunch grows heavier, the plant loses balance unless supported with strong wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ jatsui ni tsii nɔ mlɛo. Kɛji akɛ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsiimɔ ba Ja tsei ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsiimɔ bɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to grow properly if I plant them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain usually only wets the surface soil. If you plant immediately, intense heat returns, drying out the soil and killing the newly germinated seeds before the main rain begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ pɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dɔlɛ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ ni efiteɔ dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ dani nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize get eaten by tiny insects even after drying it well under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-abele ni akpa lɛ yɛ be mli ni egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli po lɛ?

english: Insects like maize weevils often lay microscopic eggs inside the grain while the crop is still standing in the field, which then hatch inside your storage bags later.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmei lɛ woɔ amɛwui bibii lɛ amli yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Enɛ baafo sɛɛ mli yɛ onitoo kotoku lɛ mli.

english: Why do tiny insects like bees visit my crop flowers, and how does that help my farm yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yasaraa mitsei lɛ afɔfɔii lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ enɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii?

english: Insects visit flowers to feed on nectar. As they move from flower to flower, they carry pollen on their bodies, which fertilizes the flowers so they can form healthy, full-sized fruits and seeds.
ga: Kplukai yasaraa fɔfɔi koni amɛye nu ni mli tse. beni amɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ Amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi fɔfɔi yɛ amɛgbɔmɔtsei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛwo yibii kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my watermelon plants produce so many flowers, but only a few of them turn into big fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi watermelon tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai wuji?

english: Watermelon plants have separate male and female flowers. Only the female flowers can form fruits, and they will only grow into big watermelons if insects transfer pollen to them from the male flowers.
ga: Watermelon tsei yɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Fɔfɔi yei pɛ baanyɛ awo yibii. Ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ watermelon agboi pɛ kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ pollen ni jɛ fɔfɔi hii lɛ amli lɛ ba amɛŋɔɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and burn when I clear away all the big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Taller trees provide essential shade and keep the air moist so the young cocoa can survive its early growth years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba, ni amɛbaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni kookoo bibioo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very thin and tall when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛlɛɔ tsɔ beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded crops fight each other for sunlight and stretch upward quickly, resulting in weak, skinny stems that can easily fall over in wind or rain.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ yeɔ akaŋ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo, ni kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, egbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves near the bottom of a crop usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, a key food plant roots absorb to build strong leaves and healthy green foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei shishifãi shwieɔ koni ekɛfee baai ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do cassava plants manage to stay alive during the long dry season when there is no rain?
ga: Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tsei hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli beni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava stores water and energy in its thick underground roots and drops its leaves when moisture is low, allowing it to rest safely underground until rains come back.
ga: Yucca kɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ toɔ eshishifãi ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli, ni ekɛ baai shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ faaa. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ ejɔɔ ehe shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do my cashew trees drop many of their flowers before any nuts start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi babaoo dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Cashew flowers fall off prematurely if they do not get pollinated by insects, or if the tree is attacked by small pests or lacks sufficient water to support the flowers.
ga: Cashew fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi oya kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii shwieee amɛ nɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tutua tso lɛ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ aye abua lɛ bɛ.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids sucking the sap from the leaves, which distorts their growth and weakens the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ dalɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why should I spend energy clearing weeds when they are not touching my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ hewalɛ agbe jwɛi be mli ni mifeee nakai lɛ? Ni etaaa mi tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe?

english: Weed roots spread deep into the soil and drink up the water and fertilizer meant for your crops, starving your plants even if they do not touch above ground.
ga: Jwɛi shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni amɛnuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ kɛji amɛshɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po.

english: Why do people tell me to cut off lower leaves and extra branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ mifo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai kɛ amɛniji ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Trimming away extra lower leaves redirects the plant's food and energy away from unnecessary foliage and sends it directly into making larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ afo shishigbɛ baai lɛ, etsɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ amli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tɛ̃ɛ ni afeɔ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ shi ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower maize leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for growth. The plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the growing upper leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmã baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get flat, black patches on the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ okadii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ji ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or inconsistent watering, which prevents the plant from moving nutrients to the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting and smelling bad in the soil before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite ni amɛhe miiwo sũ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground due to waterlogged soil or fungal infections that thrive in wet conditions, causing the roots to decay before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli lɛ hewɔ. Ha shishifãi lɛ agbo dani akpa.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark black and drying up right on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in humid, damp weather, damaging the pods and destroying the beans inside.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Gbalamɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni ofite ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat stress, lack of water, or poor pollination, causing the plant to shed flowers to save energy.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii lɛ mli baa lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and die down completely near the end of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni hulutsoo be lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ naagbee lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally turn yellow and dry up when the plant finishes its growth cycle, signalling that all energy has been transferred to mature the underground tuber for harvest.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbi kɛji tso lɛ gbe edalɛ be lɛ naa. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ajie hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛtee koni akɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli koni akpa amɛ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally restoring the nutrients that maize plants stripped out during their growth.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ekɛ niyenii ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli beni edaa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it important for me to gather and clear rotten fruits and dead crop leaves from my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mabua aduawai ni egboi kɛ tsei ahe baai ni egboi lɛ anaa ni majie kɛjɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Leaving diseased crop remains on the ground allows pests and fungal spores to hide, survive, and infect the new, healthy crops you plant next.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli, amɛhiɔ shi, ni amɛhaa tsei heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ yeɔ hela.

english: Plantain plants naturally have shallow roots that struggle to hold heavy bunches, especially if tiny soil pests like nematodes have damaged the root system.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛmɔ panicles ni tsii lɛ amli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes fite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt during the hot afternoon even if the soil is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon sun, leaves lose water faster than roots can draw it up, so the plant temporarily wilts to protect itself from losing too much moisture.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomatoes turn soft and rot so quickly after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes spoil fast because they continue to breathe and release heat after being picked, especially in warm weather. Storing them in cool, well-ventilated places away from direct sunlight slows down this process and keeps them firm longer.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ oya ejaakɛ eyaa nɔ emuɔ ni ejieɔ dɔlɛ kɛjɛɔ mli beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, Akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli. Ekɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ Enɛ baaha nifeemɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni eha ehi shi shiŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do tiny black insects appear and chew holes in my dried maize grains after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii diji je kpo ni amɛye bu yɛ mi-abele ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli beni mikɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: These are grain weevils that lay microscopic eggs inside the maize while it is drying in the field. Drying your maize thoroughly until it is bone-dry and storing it in airtight sacks or sealed containers stops the eggs from hatching and starves the pests.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji dumɔwui amli ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ ŋmeii amli be mli ni egbiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Abɛi ni agbiɔ kɛyashiɔ fãji lɛ agbiɔ ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo tsɛnsii ni atsĩ naa mli. Ehaa wɔji lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting shoots even when I store them in a dark barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ewo duŋ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams are living roots that naturally wake up and sprout when their internal clock signals that the planting season has arrived. Carefully breaking off the young sprouts as soon as they appear stops the yam from losing its moisture and food value.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ eba. Gbalamɔ tsei bibii lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ kɛji amɛje kpo pɛ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ naa.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is a main food crops need to stay green. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant stay healthy and produce strong ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ abele ni wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight. Leaving some shade trees or planting temporary crops like plantains nearby gives the young cocoa essential protection from the hot sun and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Enɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by sudden heat, dry soil, or too much water. Watering the soil regularly and placing straw mulch around the base keeps the soil moist and encourages the flowers to turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni baa trukaa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu babaoo hao amɛ. Okɛ nu afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ jwɛi aha nɔ. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ tsei lɛ aniji je shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots close to the surface, making them top-heavy when bearing fruit. Propping up the fruiting stems with strong wooden poles gives them support so wind does not knock them down.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ehaa efeɔ tsii kɛji ewo yibii. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni wa ma tso ni woɔ yibii lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efi tso lɛ sɛɛ, ni ebaatsi enaa koni kɔɔyɔɔ akatswa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains soak the ground and water sits for days, the roots drown and rot. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets extra water drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũuɔ ni nu shwieɔ nɔ gbii babaoo. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why are tiny worms eating the leaves deep inside the central leaf funnel of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ tɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which like to hide inside the wet funnel of the maize plant where it is safe. Checking your farm early and sprinkling wood ash or applying recommended sprays into the funnel stops them before they ruin the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhi amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei ni mli efɔ lɛ amli yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ tso sũ ashwã nɔ loo okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani akpata tsei lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why is a small weed with purple flowers causing my whole maize field to stunt and dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa bibii lɛ? Ani purple miiha mi-ŋmaa ŋmɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ?

english: That weed is called Striga, or witchweed, and its roots attach directly to maize roots to steal water and food. Rotating your field with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps clear the weed seeds from the soil over time.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi nɛɛ akɛ Striga, loo abɛi, ni eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsake saatsoi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie jwɛi dumɔwui kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What does 'plant population' mean, and why is it important for my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘tsei ayibɔ’ tsɔɔ ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Plant population is the total number of healthy crops growing on your land. Having the right plant population ensures you use your land fully without overcrowding your crops, leading to a much higher harvest.
ga: Tsei ayibɔ ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni adu yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ ayibɔ. Kɛ́ oyɛ tsei ayibɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miitsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyimɔ obɔbɔ. Enɛ kɛ kpamɔ ni fa babaoo baa.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, won't I get more harvest from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani mana yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting too closely forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in small, weak crops. Proper spacing gives you the right plant population so your crops grow big and healthy.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni oootsɔ nɔ okɛ ohe awo mli lɛ baaha oná tsei ayibɔ ni sa. Koni onibii lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if I have planted the right amount of crops on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miduɔ nibii ni sa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can tell by checking your field after sprouting; if almost all your planted spots have grown healthily with equal spaces between them, your land has the right plant population.
ga: Obaanyɛ ole kɛtsɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli ni oookwɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ odumɔi lɛ fɛɛ miida waa ni gbɛ ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ lɛ yeɔ egbɔ lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ tsei ayibɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I measure distance between my mounds instead of just planting anywhere I see space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu bɔ ni gɔji lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ he moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he ni manyɛ mana ŋwɛi?

english: Measuring distances prevents messy or random planting. It gives every single plant equal access to soil nutrients and water, allowing almost all of them to grow well and produce good yields.
ga: He ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ susumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ basabasa loo ni aduɔ trukaa lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ tsei fɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do extension officers tell us not to plant our crops haphazardly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkadu ŋmɔshi nibii ni wɔsumɔɔɔ lɛ?

english: Planting without a neat pattern wastes land, makes weeding difficult, and causes some crops to shade or starve others. Structured planting makes farm work easier and increases both the quantity and size of your produce.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ ni afeee nɔ ko jogbaŋŋ lɛ baafite he ko. Ewa akɛ abaajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli ni ehaa tsei komɛi náa hulutsoo loo hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ. Dumɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi feɔ mlɛo. ni oha nibii ni ofeɔ lɛ ayibɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ

english: How does organized planting help my crop yield compared to traditional random planting?
ga: Te gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛduɔ nii lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto blema dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ he?

english: Organized planting maximizes how many seeds successfully turn into strong plants. It ensures no space is wasted and no crops are crowded, resulting in a full farm with bigger produce.
ga: Gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii lɛ baaye omanye ni eha dumɔwui ni baatsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haaa he ko afite, ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ hu bɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, ŋmɔ lɛ mli baayi kɛ nibii babaoo.

english: What causes my yams to grow very small even when the leaves look big and green?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ bibioo waa eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ?

english: Small yams usually happen when mounds are made too close together or too small. Without enough underground space and soil nutrients free from root competition, the yam tubers cannot expand to their full size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii baa kɛji ŋmeii ni ato lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo amɛji bibii tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni shishifãi akaŋshii bɛ mli lɛ, Sweet potato tubers lɛ nyɛŋ adara kɛyashɛ amɛhe.

english: Will spacing my yam mounds properly give me larger yam tubers?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni kã mi-sweet potatoi lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaha sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji?

english: Yes, giving each mound adequate space allows the roots to spread and gather enough nutrients and water, giving the yam tubers room to grow very big.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ aha ŋmeii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛbua niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa naa. Ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa waa.

english: Why do some farmers get plenty of big yams while others get only a few small ones on the same size of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi naa ŋmeii wuji waa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mɛi komɛi naa ŋmeii bibii fioo komɛi pɛ yɛ he ni amɛdalɛ tamɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Farmers who get plenty of big yams usually follow proper spacing and planting measurements. This gives them a higher count of surviving plants that all have the space needed to yield heavy tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi ni nine shɛɔ ŋmeii wuji babaoo anɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ gbɛ ni sa kɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe susumɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ ha amɛná tsei babaoo ni hiɛ ka, ni fɛɛ yɛ he ni he hiaa koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: What can I do during planting to make sure almost all my planted yam seeds germinate successfully?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ dumɔ be mli koni makwɛ akɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ sweet potato dumɔwui ni midu lɛ fɛɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Preparing well-measured mounds with good soil depth and proper spacing keeps the soil moist and soft, helping almost every yam seed sprout beautifully and grow into a strong plant.
ga: Kɛ́ asaa gɔŋ ko ni asusu he jogbaŋŋ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ teŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee blɛoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ sweet potato dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu ni ekwɛ̃ɔ fɛfɛo ni eda ni etsɔɔ tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I saved from last year's harvest fail to grow well when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi edaaa jogbaŋŋ beni midu lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can lose their strength if stored in places where heat, moisture, or insects reach them. Also, many modern high-yielding seeds are bred to give a great harvest for only one season, so planting seeds saved from that harvest usually results in weaker plants and lower yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ afite hewalɛ kɛji akɛ akɛto hei ni dɔlɛ, fɛ̃i, loo kooloi baanyɛ ashɛ he. Kɛfata he lɛ, akwɛɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui babaoo ni woɔ yibii babaoo koni amɛná ŋmaa ni hi kɛha be kome pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ahereɔ kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani minine shɛɛɛ ŋmaa babaoo nɔ kɛjɛŋ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too close makes your crops compete against each other for sunlight, soil water, and plant food. This leaves you with thin, weak plants that produce very small yields instead of strong plants that give big harvests.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abɔi hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ tsei niyenii he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso nɛ ngɛ he wami nɛ woɔ yiblii babauu.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is missing nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves. It can also happen if heavy rains flood the farm and prevent the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha ŋmɔ ko mli eyi ni eha shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and droop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl or droop as a natural defense to save water. In the heat of the afternoon, plants lose moisture through their leaves faster than roots can suck it from the dry soil, so the plant wilts to protect itself until the weather cools down.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle ehe loo efolɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni akɛhere nu. Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei gboɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without turning them into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they face stress from dry weather, bad insect attacks, or poor soil food. When water is scarce or heat is too high, the tree drops its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛkɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni niyenii kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ kpeɔ. Kɛ nu faaa loo latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why does my land yield less maize every year if I plant it on the same farm continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Maize draws the exact same nutrients from the dirt season after season. Growing it in the same spot continuously drains the soil of those nutrients and lets soil pests build up, leading to poorer harvests each year.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ mli woɔ wu daa afi.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have helpful natural bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil as natural fertilizer, which feeds whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Egbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii, ni no sɛɛ lɛ, ekɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger on my farm than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that have adapted over a long time to survive harsh weather and poor soil. They are fast at stealing water, fertilizer, and sunlight before your domestic crops can get to them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsɔ amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la oya dani omaŋ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when the rainy season stays for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in the ground for a long time without draining, it suffocates the roots, allowing water-loving soil bacteria to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ tutuaa amɛ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing huge leafy branches but failing to produce fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai wuji shi enyɛɛɛ ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Giving your tomatoes too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant focus all its energy on growing leaves instead of making flowers and fruits. Extremely hot temperatures can also prevent tomato blossoms from setting fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tomato lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni ebaawo lɛ nɔ moŋ. He ni dɔɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo yibii.

english: Why does my farm produce less maize when I plant it on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season. Over time, the soil becomes exhausted, and pests that feed on maize build up in the soil, leading to smaller yields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ baajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be mli yɛ be ni sa mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafite ni kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ baabua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow faster and stronger than my main crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe mitso titri lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, native plants adapted to survive harsh conditions. Their roots spread quickly to grab available water and nutrients from the soil long before young cultivated crops can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya koni amɛgbala nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei bibii lɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars hiding inside the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which prefer feeding on the tender inner leaves (the funnel) of young maize. They hide inside to protect themselves from sunlight and predators while eating the plant's growing point.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye ŋmãa bibii (cones) ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli lɛ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ hei ni tsei lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is often caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, spread by tiny whiteflies. The virus prevents the leaves from producing food properly, leading to stunted growth and reduced tuber size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Virus lɛ tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa edalɛ baa shi ni eyitso lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and drop off when the sun gets very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have thin, delicate leaves that burn easily under direct heat and intense light. They need shade trees, like plantains, to shield them and trap moisture until their canopy matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ la ni tsoɔ waa shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu amɛhe ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi be mli ni ŋwɛitsu lɛ baadara.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms fall off the stem without producing any fruits when it is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: High temperatures destroy the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fertilization. When a blossom fails to get fertilized, the plant sheds it automatically to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔii lɛ Tsei lɛ baajie amɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch maximum sunlight for leaf food production, keeps leaves away from hot ground heat, and prevents soil-borne fungal diseases from destroying the leaves.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni ená hulu la babaoo kɛha foliar niyenii feemɔ. Ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Ni tsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite baai lɛ.

english: Can I grow cowpeas together with my maize, or will they starve each other?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmãa kome loo hɔmɔ baaye amɛ?

english: Cowpeas and maize work well together. Cowpeas naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, which helps feed the neighboring maize plant and improves overall soil health.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmãa tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why should I cut away the smaller shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: A plantain root system has limited nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest main stem and one small follower stem, allowing the plant to produce a much larger, heavier cluster of fruits.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ bɛ niyenii kɛ nu babaoo. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, tso titri ni wa fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛ tso bibioo kome ni nyiɛɔ esɛɛ lɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ yibii ni dara ni tsii kwraa.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are big enough to harvest if they are hidden underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa kɛji akɛ akɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava shows visible clues above ground when mature: lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, the main stem thickens significantly, and the soil around the base starts to crack as the tubers expand beneath.
ga: Yucca jieɔ okadii ni anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni edara lɛ: baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli edɔ waa. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong sunlight dries out their tender leaves and soil quickly. Planting taller crops like plantains alongside cocoa gives them shade and moisture needed to survive their early years.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa baai lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to put sticks for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ niji akpɛtɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ he koni ekwɔ moŋ fe ni mahã egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need full sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing large tubers under the ground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp soil, improving air circulation and preventing diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu ni fa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni otsi helai anaa.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excessive moisture, cassava plants focus all their energy on growing leaves above ground rather than storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Yucca tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves in maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, a crucial nutrient for leaf growth, or that the soil is waterlogged and preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Fertilizers must dissolve in soil moisture for roots to absorb them. Applying chemical fertilizer to dry soil can burn and destroy the roots rather than feeding the plant.
ga: Esa akɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite shishifãi lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures become too hot, when watering is irregular, or when there are not enough pollinating insects to fertilize the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo be mli ni pollinators ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ

english: Why are caterpillars hiding deep inside the central funnels of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworms hide in the central whorl of young maize plants because the tender inner leaves provide rich food and shelter from sunlight and rain.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii babaoo kɛ wɔɔhe kɛjɛɔ hulu kɛ nugbɔ he.

english: How does planting cowpeas in the same field as my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Te tsina ŋmãa ni mikɛduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for nearby maize while covering the ground to stop weeds.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛkpaa jwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield less food if I plant maize in the exact same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naaa niyenii babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up in the ground over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables spoil so quickly before I can transport them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ fiteɔ oya dani akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Vegetables harvested during the hottest sun retain heat and breathe rapidly, causing fast decay. Harvesting in the cool early morning and keeping produce in well-ventilated baskets delays rotting.
ga: Aduawai ni akpaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ hiɛɔ dɔlɛ mli ni emuɔ oya, ni no haa efiteɔ oya. Nikpamɔ yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli kɛ nibii ni adu lɛ ni akɛtoɔ tsɛnsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains nearby, the intense heat burns their delicate leaves and turns them yellow.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baaha ebaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ashã ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly during heavy rains and humid weather when there is too much shade or poor ventilation on the farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa be mli ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves and dark caterpillars inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai amli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ su diŋŋ yɛ baa lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm. They hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant and eat the tender leaves, which weakens the crop if not treated early.
ga: Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ oya.

english: Why do whiteflies cluster under my cassava leaves, and make the leaves curl up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛji miibua amɛhe naa yɛ mi-cassava baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmiiha baai lɛ miihoso lɛ?

english: Whiteflies suck nutrients from the cassava leaves and spread the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which distorts leaf growth and prevents the plant from producing full tubers.
ga: Fɛ̃i yɛŋ lɛ nuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛjɛɔ ŋmei baai amli ni amɛgbɛɔ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ amɛshwãa. Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni ehaaa tso lɛ afee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with thick green leaves, but the tubers underground remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: Adding too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the cassava plant to spend all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of expanding its root tubers below ground.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baaha ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ shishifãi lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: How do I know if my soil needs fertilizer before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: If your previous crops had pale or yellow leaves, thin stems, or yielded very little harvest, your soil is likely low in nutrients and needs organic manure or chemical fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ, tsei bibii, loo yibiiwoo fioo ko pɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai awo mli.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and allows specific pests and crop diseases to build up in that field.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches. Without wooden stakes to support the main stem, strong winds easily push the heavy trees over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni mli tse. Kɛji tso ko bɛ ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ shwieɔ tsei ni tsii lɛ anɔ oya.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl and droop to conserve moisture when the heat makes water evaporate faster than the roots can take it up from dry soil.
ga: Shi ni ebɔle ehe koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli ejaakɛ la ni tsoɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of the vegetable seeds I bought fail to sprout after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds may fail to sprout if they are old, damaged by insects, planted too deep in dry soil, or if the soil lacks sufficient moisture during planting.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji amɛgbɔ tsɔ. ŋmeii efite Adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ tsɔ. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni aduɔ nii lɛ

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means your soil is running low on nitrogen. The maize plant automatically pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate hot, direct sunlight because their root systems are still small and tender. Leaving large shade trees shields them from harsh heat, preserves soil moisture, and protects their delicate leaves from burning.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifã lɛ ji bibioo lolo ni eyɛ mlɛo. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ la he.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of green leaves, but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or fertilizer, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves and tall stems instead of storing energy in the root tubers underneath the ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji kɛ ŋmeii kakadaji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Why do my maize crops grow thin, weak stems when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This forces them to stretch upward quickly to catch light, resulting in tall, fragile stems that fall over easily.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ ehe bahiaa ni atsake oya koni anyɛ amɔmɔ kane lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause severe stress to tomato plants, making their flowers drop off before pollen can fertilize them. Keeping soil moist and cool helps the plant retain its blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani pollen lɛ nyɛɔ ewoɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why does putting dry grass or cocoa pod husks around my crops help them survive during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmeii ni akɛfataa he lɛ ebɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli.

english: Covering the ground around crops with plant waste—a practice called mulching—blocks direct heat from the sun. This keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly, leaving moisture for the roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle Nibii ni Aduɔ lɛ ahe lɛ ni akɛ tsei ahe jwɛi (nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching) baaha lɛ baaye abua ni abu he kɛjɛ hulutsoo ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Shi ŋmɔtɔ kɛha shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars like armyworms appear on my maize leaves so quickly after the early rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-abele baa lɛ nɔ oya beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Moths lay their eggs on tender green shoots right after the early rains trigger fresh growth. The eggs hatch quickly, and the tiny caterpillars begin eating the soft leaves when nutrient levels are highest.
ga: Kplukai lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ leebi lɛ sɛɛ, ni no haa tsei heei daa. Wɔɔji lɛ baafo oya. kɛ ŋmeii bibii Amɛjeɔ baai bibii lɛ ayeli shishi beni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and twisting like a cup?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or whiteflies hiding under the leaves and sucking out plant sap, or by viruses transmitted by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I wait until the soil is moist before applying fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires water to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Applying chemical fertilizer to dry soil under high heat can burn the plant's roots and waste the fertilizer into the air.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ nu koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster and stronger than my planted crops after clearing the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni midu beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions. Their seeds lie hidden in the soil for years and germinate immediately when exposed to sunlight and rain, outrunning young crops that grow more slowly.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Akɛ edumɔwui lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo ni kɛ́ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ekwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Edaa oya fe tsei bibii ni daaa blɛoo lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running out of nitrogen, which acts as food for the plant to grow green and healthy. As the plant grows, it pulls whatever nitrogen is left to the new leaves at the top, leaving the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara Ebaagbala nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: How often do I need to walk through my farm to check on how my crops are growing?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa amɛhaa?

english: You should walk through your field at least twice a week. Regular visits allow you to spot early signs of pest attacks, diseases, or water stress before they spread and destroy your harvest.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ otsɔ oyale mli shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Saramɔi ni afeɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai, loo nu mli haomɔ miiba mra. dani egbɛ eshwa ni ekpata oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before any fruit grows on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as sudden hot spells, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay on the plant long enough to turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiihao, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ trukaa lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why does my maize fall over easily whenever strong winds blow across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa kɛfo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over when their roots are not deep enough in the soil, often because seeds were planted too shallow or because stem borer pests have eaten away the inside of the lower stalk.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ eshɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ebote tso lɛ mli ni amɛye tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cassava roots growing thin and woody instead of big and fat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee agboi ni amɛwo fɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soft, loose soil to expand easily under the ground. If your soil is packed too hard or lacks nutrients like potassium, the plant cannot swell its roots into large tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi oya. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ potassium bɛ mli lɛ, tsei lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ shishifãi ni amɛfee bulbs agboi.

english: What happens to my yams if I plant the mounds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-sweet potato lɛ nɔ kɛji midu gɔji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When yam mounds are placed too close, the leaves overlap and fight for sunlight, while the underground roots struggle against each other for soil moisture and food, leading to smaller harvested yams.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potatoes ni abua naa lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii he akaŋshii mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by very small insects like aphids or thrips hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices, which distorts how the leaves grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni fiteɔ bɔ ni baai lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods turn black and rot before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii So minɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani edaa lɛ?

english: Black pod rot is caused by a tiny fungus that spreads quickly in damp, dark environments. Pruning excess branches from your cocoa trees lets sunshine and air in to keep the pods dry.
ga: Fungi bibii kɛ pods diji ni egbo baa. No gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni duŋ ewo mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: How can I tell if my crops have enough water during dry periods in northern Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ?

english: Dig a few inches down near your crops and scoop up a handful of dirt. If you squeeze it and it holds together in a soft ball, there is good moisture, but if it crumbles like dry powder, your crops need water.
ga: Tsɔmɔmɔ shikpɔŋ inchii fioo komɛi ni bɛŋkɛ onibii lɛ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ ko awo mli. Kɛ́ okɛmimɔ mli ni efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ, ebaaná ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa. Shi kɛji efo mli ni etsɔ powda ni egbi Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he miihia nu.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing plenty of green leaves but almost no seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi eshwɛ fioo ni ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, cowpeas put all their energy into building lush green leaves instead of producing flowers and bean pods.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ, Cowpeas hu kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii

english: Why does my farm soil get so hard and dry like stone after repeated chemical spraying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli wa ni egbi tamɔ tɛ yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ shii abɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical sprays can kill beneficial soil organisms like earthworms and tiny microbes. These creatures naturally burrow and break down organic matter, creating air pockets that keep soil soft, moist, and loose.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii bibii. Nɛkɛ bɔɔ nii nɛɛ tsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛfiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, edɔɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa.

english: Are the tiny worms and bugs inside my soil good or bad for my crops?
ga: Kplukai bibii kɛ kooloi Ani mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi loo ehiii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Most organisms inside the soil are helpful partners. They eat decaying plant matter, turn it into rich plant food, and create channels that help crop roots breathe and absorb water.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ateŋ babaoo ji nanemɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Amɛyeɔ tsei ni egboi. Tsɔɔmɔ lɛ ni efee tsei aniyenii babaoo. ni amɛfee gbɛi ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛjieɔ nu

english: How can I make my hard farm land soft again so crop roots can grow easily?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee blɛoo ekoŋŋ koni tsei shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ mlɛo?

english: You can soften hard land by adding decomposed animal manure, dead leaves, or compost. Adding this organic matter brings soil life back, restores air space, and prevents the ground from baking hard under the sun.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha hei ni wa lɛ afee blɛoo kɛtsɔ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. baai ni egboi loo ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli nɛɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aba wala mli ekoŋŋ. ha kɔɔyɔɔ mli hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni etsĩ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekafee ais yɛ hulu lɛ shishi.

english: Why does my land dry out and bake so quickly when I leave it completely bare?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa oya kɛji mishi nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ?

english: Bare soil is directly exposed to intense sunlight and rain, which bakes the surface into a hard crust and evaporates moisture. Keeping the soil covered with mulch or cover crops protects it and keeps it cool.
ga: Hulu la kɛ nugbɔ baa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa ŋwɛi lɛ mli waa ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ha shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu he ni eha edɔ.

english: Will using weedicide on my farm harm my main crops in the long run?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ awui yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Frequent use of harsh weedicides can build up in the soil, damage root growth of main crops, and destroy natural soil nutrients, making your land less productive over time.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ lɛ baanyɛ abua naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Efiteɔ tso titri lɛ shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. ni efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Enɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are my crops struggling to grow even though I cleared all weeds with chemical sprays?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitao ni amɛkwɛ̃ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ jieɔ jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ moŋ?

english: While weedicide removes competing weeds, it can also destroy friendly soil bacteria and earthworms. Without these organisms, the soil loses its natural fertility, making it hard for crops to absorb nutrients.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ moŋ, Shi ebaanyɛ efite shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu. Kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ nɛkɛ bɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ebɔɔ su mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Is clearing weeds with a cutlass safer for my soil than spraying chemical weedkillers?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni akɛ dagger tsuɔ he nii lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ fe tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, weeding with a cutlass keeps beneficial soil life alive and leaves weed roots in the ground to rot into organic matter, which keeps the soil fertile and soft compared to chemical sprays.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni akɛ ŋmei shwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ wala ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ hiɔ shi. ni eha jwɛi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbo ni amɛtsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni efeɔ blɛoo kɛ akɛto tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow stronger when I leave dead weeds and dry leaves to rot on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli wa waa kɛ́ mishi jwɛi ni egboi kɛ baai ni egboi lɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rotting plant matter acts as natural food for the soil. As microbes break down the leaves, nutrients are released back into the earth, providing free fertilizer for your growing crops.
ga: Tsei ni fiteɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛji nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ kpata baai lɛ ajieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aha otsei ni miida lɛ ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: What causes land that used to give good yield to suddenly stop producing well?
ga: Mɛni haa shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ ewoɔ yibii lɛ kpaɔ yibii kpakpai trukaa lɛ?

english: Land loses its yield potential when soil life dies off from heavy chemical use, lack of organic matter, or continuous exposure to harsh sun, leaving the soil infertile and compacted.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ekɛ nibii awo nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ gboi yɛ tsofai ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ hewɔ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni bɛ loo hulu la ni naa wa ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What are cover crops, and how do they stop my farm land from spoiling?
ga: Mɛni ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi miŋmɔ lɛ naa koni ekafite?

english: Cover crops, like leguminous beans, are planted to cover and protect bare soil. They block harsh sunlight, prevent rain from washing away soil, and naturally feed nitrogen into the earth.
ga: Cover crops tamɔ legumes Aduɔ koni akɛtee shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni abu he. Amɛtsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Tsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ekɛ nitrogen boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall and thin with very small cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛmli ŋmeii bibii waa yɔɔ mli lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves the plants weak and unable to build big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni wa.

english: Why is it recommended to plant plantains next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ adu plantains yɛ mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that provide natural shade and conserve soil moisture for the young cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛhaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay dark green and make food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli kɛ nihoomɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or water stress. The plant sheds its flowers to save energy so it can survive the harsh weather.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, pull food and water away from the main mother plant. Removing them allows all the nourishment to go into forming a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ agbo ko ni tsii.

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that blocks the narrow water pipes inside the stem, preventing water from reaching the leaves even when the soil has plenty of moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsiɔ nu gbɛi bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa, ni ehaa nu shɛɛɛ baai lɛ ahe kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ jogbaŋŋ po.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from a disease or just lack water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela emɔ miŋmɔshi nibii loo nu efo mli?

english: Plants lacking water will perk up in the cool early morning or late evening. Diseased plants stay wilted, develop yellow spots, or show dark patches on leaves regardless of water or temperature.
ga: Tsei ni bɛ nu lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baagboi. Ayɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Aloo okadii diji yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ekɔɔɔ nu loo hulutsoo he.

english: Why do insects attack my crops more during the dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Hot, dry weather stresses plants and weakens their natural defenses. Insects look for green crops during dry periods to feed on their sap for hydration.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ haa tsei haoɔ ni ehaa amɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu hewalɛ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kplukai kwɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛna niyenii kɛjɛ amɛmli nu lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots remain thin and hard even after growing in the ground for a whole year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe wa lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ amɛ ewo shikpɔŋ mli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Hard, thin cassava roots usually mean the soil is too packed for the roots to expand or lacks potassium, the key nutrient that helps starch build up inside the tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi ni wa ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã loo potassium bɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni yeɔ ebuaa ni afeɔ starch yɛ tuber lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start to rot quickly after I store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya beni mikɛtoɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Small scratches or cuts on the skin during harvest allow unseen bacteria and fungi into the yam. Storing them in warm, poorly ventilated rooms speeds up the decay.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ bibii loo ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ hewolo lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli, ni haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ boteɔ sweet potato lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛfite oya.

english: Young cocoa plants naturally thrive in forest understories. Without shade trees or temporary shade crops like plantains, direct sunlight scorches the delicate leaves and dries out the soil before the roots can establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ koo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains bɛ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why is it necessary to leave big gaps between oil palm trees when planting them in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi ŋmeii wuji yɛ mu tsei ateŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Oil palms grow wide leaf fronds and extensive root systems. Spacing them properly ensures each tree receives enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to produce heavy fruit bunches without shading out neighboring palms.
ga: Mu tsei yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛ shishifãi babaoo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii ni tsii ni etsĩii tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anaa.

english: How long do I have to wait after planting oil palm seedlings before I can start harvesting fruit to sell?
ga: Kɛ́ odu oil palm dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani obɔi aduawai lɛ akpamɔ ni okɛbaahɔɔ lɛ?

english: Improved varieties of oil palm typically take about three to four years after field planting to start producing harvestable fruit bunches, with yield increasing as the trees mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ yɛ be mli ni adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ dani amɛjeɔ aduawai akui ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ shishi. Yibiiwoo lɛ yaa hiɛ kɛ́ tsei lɛ dara.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many tiny flowers without them turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ miijie fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? A babaoo ni etsɔko pod?

english: A cocoa tree produces thousands of flowers, but only a small percentage get pollinated by tiny insects called midges. Unpollinated flowers naturally fall off, and excessive flower drop can also be triggered by dry weather or nutrient stress.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ ji nɔ ni kooloi bibii shwieɔ amɛmli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ pollen lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ni fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ajɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ mli aba.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot whenever the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a water-loving fungal infection. Raindrops splash the fungal spores onto pods, and high humidity in dense, unpruned farms helps the rot spread rapidly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji black pod hela, ni ji ŋmei ni sumɔɔ nu. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores nɔ yɛ pods lɛ anɔ. Ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni afolɔko mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do my cocoa trees look wilted and lose their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi ni amɛbaai fiteɔ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry Harmattan winds strip moisture from leaves faster than roots can draw water from dry soil. Shedding leaves is the tree's natural survival mechanism to reduce water loss and protect itself from drying out completely.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso tsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi. Koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni oha ohe akagbi kwraa.

english: Should I cut off the lower fronds of my oil palm trees, or leave them on the trunk?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ loo mashi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi?

english: Removing dead, diseased, or lower yellowing fronds makes harvesting easier and reduces pests. However, keeping healthy green fronds is essential because they capture sunlight to make food for fruit production.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shishigbɛ baai ni egboi, hela emɔmɔ amɛ, loo ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha kpamɔ lɛ afee mlɛo, ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai aba shi. Shi kɛlɛ, ehe miihia ni aha baai eŋɔli lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛmɔɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii kɛha aduawai afeemɔ.

english: Why does planting cocoa feel like my capital is locked up for years compared to planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔ haa minuɔ he tamɔ nɔ ni mi maŋtiase lɛ efo mli afii babaoo kɛ akɛto ŋmãa dumɔ he lɛ?

english: Maize is a short-term crop that yields cash within four months, whereas cocoa is a long-term tree crop that requires continuous investment in care for three to five years before giving substantial, long-term annual returns.
ga: Abɛi ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo ni ekuɔ esɛɛ ebaa yɛ nyɔji ejwɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni biɔ ni akɛ shika awo mli afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ daa dani ebaaha sɛɛnamɔi babaoo aba daa afi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or vegetables between my young palm trees without hurting them?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo aduawai yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ ni miyeee amɛ awui?

english: Yes, intercropping short-term food crops between young oil palms during the first two to three years helps generate immediate cash flow and suppresses weeds, as long as you keep a clear area around the palm seedlings so they do not compete for nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni akɛyeɔ be kukuoo mli nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei tsei ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shika aba amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa. Shii abɔ ni obaakwɛ he ko ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. palm dumɔwui koni amɛkaye niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ
