english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing far fewer pods now than they did ten years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii babaoo fioo fe afii nyɔŋma ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, they deplete soil nutrients and become more susceptible to pests and diseases. Without regular soil feeding, pruning, and gradual replacement of very old trees, overall yield naturally declines over time.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ eda Kɛji akɛ ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai baanyɛ atswa lɛ oya. tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ tsei momo ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ fiofio lɛ. Nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow before the crop is fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential food for plant growth. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen down into the ground where short roots cannot reach, so applying urea or organic compost early in the season fixes this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni shishifãi kukuji nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsu nii yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the exact same spot where I harvested garden eggs last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ he ni mifolɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Tomatoes and garden eggs belong to the same crop family and share the same soil pests and fungal diseases. Planting them in the same spot back-to-back lets pests survive in the soil and attack your new seeds immediately.
ga: Tomato kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛjaraa shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kome. Kɛ́ odu amɛ yɛ he kome ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutuaa odumɔwui heei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What is this small caterpillar eating inside the growing center of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ ŋmei bibioo nɛɛ ni miiye yɛ mibi lɛ ŋmei baa ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: That pest is the Fall Armyworm, which feeds on young cereal crops across Ghana. Spraying recommended bio-pesticides or a mixture of local neem leaf extract early in the morning when the caterpillar is active will protect the leaf funnel.
ga: Nakai tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmaa nibii ni adu yɛ Ghana fɛɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛfee lɛ loo neem baa ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli nu ni akɛfutu mli lɛ shwie nɔ leebi be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baa lɛ gbɛi lɛ ahe.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, humid conditions. Pruning extra shade trees and clearing infected pods from the trees allows sunlight and fresh air to keep the cocoa farm dry.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ fɛ̃i, fɛ̃i shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo babaoo lɛ ni afoɔ ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aba lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ mli egbiɔ.

english: Why do my cassava stems grow very tall and thin with small tubers when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs direct sunlight to make energy for storing starch in its tubers. When shaded by tall trees, the plant wastes its energy growing upward to reach light instead of swelling its roots underground.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee hewalɛ ni ekɛ starch ato eshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni yɔɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko shishi Tsei lɛ laajeɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛshɛ la he lɛ. Mohu ɔ, e sisi ɔmɛ puɛɔ ngɛ zugba sisi.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers next to my newly planted young cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and moist air to protect the cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ koni ebu kookoo lɛ he kɛyashi ebaada.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up like small cups during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to shrink their surface area and avoid losing water through heat. Watering your farm early in the morning and spreading dry grass around the plant stems helps retain soil moisture.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu ni fiteɔ yɛ dɔlɛ hewɔ lɛ naa. Okɛ nu awo oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwã he. Tsei ashishifãi yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat or lack of water in the soil. Keeping soil cool with mulch and avoiding too much chemical fertilizer will help flowers stick and become peppers.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ muji ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ babaoo he lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How can I tell if the soil is ready after the dry season for planting seed yams?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until two or three heavy rains have soaked the ground wrist-deep. Planting seed yams in dry, hot soil causes them to bake and rot underground before they can send up sprouts.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashɛ oniji ahe. Kɛ́ adu sweet potato dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛshã ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why is it bad to save and replant seeds harvested from store-bought hybrid maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ abaato dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ mli lɛ ni adu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially cross-bred to give high yields for one season only. Replanting seeds saved from that harvest produces weak crops, uneven plant sizes, and much smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ be kome pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ aba. Tsei lɛ adalɛi lɛ jeee ekome. ni ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ bibioo kwraa

english: Why do my cassava stems need to be planted at an angle instead of straight into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni aaadu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a 45-degree angle encourages roots to develop evenly near the soil surface. This gives the tubers plenty of room to swell up thick and makes them much easier to dig up during harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei niji yɛ 45 degree angle mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ náa gbɛ babaoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfutu babaoo ni ehaa amɛfomɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: How come my yam tubers are small and twisted even though the leaves and vines are growing so tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni amɛtsake amɛhe eyɛ mli akɛ baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ daraa babaoo lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep soil to grow long and smooth. If the soil underneath is hard, compact, or full of rocks, the tubers cannot push through easily, resulting in stunted or misshapen yams. Making high, soft mounds helps prevent this.
ga: Sweet potatoes hia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli tse kɛha dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ Anyɛɛɛ atsɔ yitso lɛ mli mlɛo. Enɛ haa sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ bibii loo efiteɔ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni aaafee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Yellowing leaves in young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen or the soil is waterlogged. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost early in the season restores their green color so they can grow strong stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look wrinkled during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism crops use to reduce water loss during intense heat. If the leaves open back up in the cooler evening, the crop is fine, but if they stay curled, the plants need watering or checking for tiny insect pests.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba nu ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ shi. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ gbeleɔ amɛhe yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai eba, shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle lɛ, ehe miihia ni awo tso lɛ nɔ nu loo akwɛ kɛji ŋmeii bibii komɛi yɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their blossoms without producing any tomatoes during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ tomato wooo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High heat and lack of moisture stress tomato plants, causing their pollen to dry out so flowers fall off before fruiting. Regular watering and using grass mulch to keep the soil cool and moist helps the plant keep its flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo ni bɛ lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa pollen ni egbi lɛ baa. No sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: What causes my cocoa saplings to wither and die when there are no shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sunlight. Intercropping them with fast-growing plantains provides living shade and traps moisture, helping young cocoa trees survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni akɛ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ duɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is my cowpea farm covered in healthy green leaves but showing very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyi kɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ? Shi pods fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes cowpeas to put all their energy into producing vines and leaves rather than flowers. Because cowpeas naturally add nitrogen to the soil on their own, they need very little artificial fertilizer to produce pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni haa anáa wain tsei kɛ baai tsuɔ nii yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsina ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛhe ehiaaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee lɛ fioo ko pɛ koni amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my okra plants stop bringing out new flowers after I leave a few big pods on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ kpa fɔfɔi heei feemɔ beni mishi ŋmeii wuji fioo komɛi yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When old okra pods mature and turn hard on the plant, the crop thinks its job is done and focuses on seed production rather than new fruit. Picking young pods every few days signals the plant to keep flowering continuously.
ga: Beni okra ŋmeii lɛ edara kwraa ni efee shiŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baasusu akɛ etsu enitsumɔ lɛ he nii ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ baama dumɔwui afeemɔ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai heei. Gbii fioo komɛi baatsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ ebaaya nɔ ewo fɔfɔi.

english: How do I know that my groundnuts are ready to harvest since the nuts grow under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ejaakɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts show maturity above ground when the main leaves start turning yellow and dropping off. You can pull up one plant to inspect: if the inner shells have dark brown markings and the nuts fill the pod tightly, the crop is ready.
ga: Akɛ ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni baai titrii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ ogbala tso kome kɛya ŋwɛi ni okwɛ: kɛji akɛ emli ŋmei lɛ yɛ okadii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines spread all over the place without growing big tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ miigbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he ni ŋmei agbo ko bɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When sweet potato vines grow too wild, they spend all their nutrients expanding leaves instead of roots. Trimming excess vine tips directs the plant's energy down into expanding the underground tubers.
ga: Kɛji sweet potato wain tsei lɛ dara tsɔ Amɛkɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo baai amli yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Wein tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baaha tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshishifãi lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings need shade cover when they are very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ he hiaa hulu kɛji amɛji bibii waa lɛ?

english: Very young seedlings have delicate leaves and small root systems that dry out quickly under direct, intense sunlight. Providing shade protects them from excessive heat and helps them build strong roots before facing harsh weather.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii waa lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ aha amɛ hulutsoo lɛ, ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛtoɔ shishifãi ni wa dani amɛyajeɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa amli.

english: How do I know when my crops are ready for me to remove the shade cover or nursery lights?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee klalo akɛ majie shade loo ŋmɔ mli kanei lɛ?

english: Seedlings are usually ready when they reach about 8 to 10 weeks of age, have several fully formed leaves, and possess sturdy stems that can withstand open weather conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo beni amɛye aaafee otsii 8 kɛyashi 10, ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ni eyɛ tsei ni wa ni baanyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli tse lɛ anaa.

english: What will happen to my plants if I take off their shade cover all at once without preparing them?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mijie hulutsoo lɛ kwraa ni mikɛhaaa amɛ?

english: If you remove the shade suddenly, the strong direct sunlight can shock the plants, cause leaf burn, or make them wilt rapidly because they need time to adjust to hotter conditions.
ga: Kɛji ojie hulutsoo lɛ trukaa Hulu la ni mli wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ahe afee shoo, eshã amɛbaai lɛ, loo eha amɛgboi oya beni amɛheɔ be dani amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How many weeks should I keep my vegetable seeds in the nursery before moving them to the field?
ga: Otsii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ aduawai adumɔwui awo ŋmɔ mli dani mikɛwo ŋmɔ mli?

english: Most vegetable seedlings need between 4 to 6 weeks in a protected nursery setting to become strong enough to survive transplanting into the main farm.
ga: Aduawai dumɔwui babaoo biɔ otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni abuɔ he mli. Koni ehe awa bɔ ni sa ni efã kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli

english: Why are my young crops growing very tall and thin instead of strong and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ miida ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ waa ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔji najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When crops do not get enough light, they stretch upwards as fast as they can to reach a light source, resulting in weak, thin stems that can easily fall over.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baajie ehe kɛya ŋwɛi oya bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni eshɛ he ni la lɛ jɛɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni baanyɛ agbee shi oya lɛ feɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do the leaves on my shaded plants turn light green or yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mishia tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Plants turn yellow when they lack sunlight because they cannot produce enough chlorophyll, which is the green chemical they use to make food from light.
ga: Tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji hulu la bɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee klorofil ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ ji tsofa ni ji eŋɔli ni amɛkɛfeɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ la mli.

english: Leaf curling is a defense mechanism plants use to shrink the surface area exposed to the sun, helping them save moisture and protect themselves from severe heat.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he.

english: Does giving my crops extra light during the night help them grow bigger faster?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ la mli gbɛkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya?

english: Extra light allows plants to make more energy, but plants also need hours of darkness to rest and carry out natural processes like nutrient distribution within their stems.
ga: La ni yaa hiɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ babaoo. Shi tsei hu he hiaa ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo yɛ duŋ mli koni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsu adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛjaa yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he nii.

english: How long does it usually take for a crop to transition from the nursery stage to full outdoor growth?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kwraa?

english: Most nursery crops take around 6 to 10 weeks to fully mature out of the seedling stage, depending on the crop variety and the care provided.
ga: Tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee otsii 6 kɛyashi 10 dani amɛdaraa kwraa kɛjɛɔ amɛdumɔwui lɛ amli. Edamɔ tso henɔi lɛ kɛ bɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ ahaa lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I protect my farm budget when prices for crop supplies keep changing in the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ mli shika he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ he? Akɛni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ jara nɔ hewɔ lɛ.

english: Planning your purchases early, buying basic supplies like netting or seeds in groups with other farmers, and using local natural alternatives where possible helps manage unpredictable price increases.
ga: Too nibii ni obaahe lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ mra. Nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ ŋshɔŋlooi loo dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛ okwaafoi krokomɛi baahe Kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii krokomɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ he ni ebaahi lɛ baaye abua ni atsu jara ni yaa hiɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ he nii.

english: Why are there small holes in my young maize leaves and tiny caterpillars hiding inside the stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji ŋmeii lɛ? Mi nɔ lɛ yɛ bu bibioo ko. Akɛtee tso lɛ shishi?

english: This is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. The caterpillars hatch from eggs laid on the leaves and eat the young tender leaves and growing points, which can destroy the maize plant if not treated early with appropriate pesticides or organic controls like neem extract.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Kplukai lɛ fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii kɛ hei ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmãa tsei kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ mra. kɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛyeɔ nɔ tamɔ neem mli nu.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning yellow with green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Your cassava likely has Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies or by planting diseased stems. It stops the plant from making food properly, leading to small roots, so it is best to use disease-resistant stem cuttings from the agriculture officer.
ga: Ekolɛ o-kasa lɛ yɛ kasa mosaic hela. Virus ko ni whiteflies bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. loo kɛjɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ ni miida lɛ amli Ebaaha tsei lɛ akafee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. make shishifãi bibii No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni helai ni jɛɔ okwaayeli he onukpai adɛŋ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ baatsu nii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark brown spots and rot when I spray water directly on them during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu shwie nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Watering overhead leaves them wet in warm air, creating the perfect damp warm environment for fungal diseases like late blight to grow. Watering directly at the root level keeps the leaves dry and prevents fungi from attacking the plant.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ amɛyiteŋ lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ late blight lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ shishigbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ agbi ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akatutua tso lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the tip of older leaves is a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to make leaves green and grow strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure will help fix this.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ anaa lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ni he hia kɛha tsei koni amɛ baa lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛ dara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do farmers recommend planting groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food from the soil, but legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees next to my newly transplanted young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn and dry out under strong sunshine. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that shade the young cocoa from direct sun and keep the soil moist during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya ni egbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to heap the soil into big mounds before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabua shikpɔŋ agbo ko naa dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft, and deep soil so the tubers can expand downward and outward easily. Mounds make it easy for the root to grow big while also preventing standing water from rotting the yam tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛya shi kɛ kponɔgbɛ oya. Gɔŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa oya yɛ be mli ni etsĩɔ nu ni ekã shi lɛ hu naa koni ekaha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fite.

english: Why do my maize plants stay weak and produce small cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space ensures every crop gets enough resources to grow thick stalks and full cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli eyi obɔ.

english: Why should I wait for two or three heavy rains before planting my seeds instead of planting after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ dani madu dumɔwui moŋ fe ni madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain after a dry season often only wets the top layer of soil, which quickly dries out under the hot sun. Waiting for consistent rains ensures deep soil moisture so your planted seeds can germinate and survive without drying up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mɛmɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from my farm within the first month after planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli beni adu nii lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and will quickly steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight your seeds need to establish strong roots. Clearing them early gives your main crops a head start to grow big enough to shade out future weeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛbaaju nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa odumɔwui lɛ oya koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha otso titri lɛ ada oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaaha jwɛi ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my millet manage to survive dry spells, but my maize dies when the rains stop for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-millet lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ? Shi mi-abele lɛ gbo beni nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ otsii fioo komɛi lɛ.

english: Millet has deep root systems and narrow leaves that reduce water loss, making it naturally drought-resistant. Maize has broad leaves and shallower roots, so it loses water quickly and needs consistent rainfall to stay healthy.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai bibii, ni no haa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi. ni haa enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa Abɛi yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Nu lɛ fiteɔ oya ni ehe miihia ni nugbɔ anɛ daa koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: The first rain often moistens only the surface of the soil, which tricks seeds into sprouting. If a long dry stretch follows before the real rainy season begins, the hot, dry dirt will burn and kill the tender new roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ pɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ ɔ ma ha nɛ wu ɔmɛ nɛ a puɛ. Kɛji akɛ be kakadaŋŋ ko yɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ, muji ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ baashã ni ekpata shishifãi heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahiɛ.

english: How does growing groundnuts on my farmland make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which means their roots work with friendly soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the dirt. This natural nitrogen feeds the crops you plant next, such as maize.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛshɛrɛ amɛshwie sũ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Can I plant groundnuts and tall maize together in the same field without them fighting for food?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kakadaji yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛkaaa niyenii he akaŋ?

english: Yes, they make good partners. Maize grows tall to feed on high sunlight, while low-growing groundnuts cover the soil to prevent weeds, trap moisture, and feed nitrogen into the dirt for the maize roots to share.
ga: Hɛɛ, amɛji hefatalɔi kpakpai. Abɛi daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni eye hulu la. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ fioo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akabote mli, emɔɔ nu ni mli ewo muji ni ekɛ nitrogen woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ agba he sane.

english: Why do I need to clear the land and make big dirt mounds before I plant my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie he ko ni mafee muji babaoo dani madu sweet potato lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow long and heavy underground. Deep, loose dirt mounds make it easy for the tuber to expand freely without fighting hard, packed soil, resulting in much larger and smoother yams.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, amɛlɛɔ ni amɛtsii. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ bulbs lɛ baagbɛ eshwa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ akpee. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ daraa kwraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do groundnut plants make flowers up in the air, but the actual nuts grow under the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ fɔfɔii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli, shi ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: After the yellow flowers open and get pollinated above ground, the plant grows long pegs that bend downward and push themselves into the dirt. Once hidden under the soil, the tips expand to form the shell and nuts.
ga: Beni fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwoɔ pollination yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Tso lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ ŋmei kakadaŋŋ ko ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ akɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, naagbee lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei.

english: Why do wild shea trees take many years to produce fruits, while crops like maize fruit in just a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli shea tsei lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa heɔ nyɔji fioo pɛ?

english: Shea trees are long-term woody plants that spend their first 15 to 20 years building deep taproots and strong trunks to survive severe droughts before they have enough energy to produce fruit.
ga: Shea tsei ji tsei ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ, ni amɛheɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 15 kɛyashi 20 dani amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni wa koni amɛye amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa mli dani amɛnáa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How can I tell if my maize leaves are rolling up because of afternoon sun heat or because the ground is dry?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abɛi lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ hewɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi?

english: Maize leaves roll up temporarily in the afternoon heat to trap moisture. If the leaves unroll and open up by early morning, the soil has enough water; if they stay tightly rolled in the morning, the crop is suffering from dry soil.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko yɛ shwane mli koni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji baai lɛ gbele ni amɛgbele leebi lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛji amɛfolɔ shi shiŋŋ leebi lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baaná naagbai yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi he.

english: Why do insects destroy my harvested maize in storage so quickly while my millet stays good for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ yɛ be mli ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize kernels hold more moisture and have soft centers that insects can easily chew through. Millet grains are tiny, dry, and covered in a hard shell that bugs cannot easily bite into.
ga: Abɛi mli ŋmeii lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo mli, ni amɛyɛ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni kooloi baanyɛ atsɔ mli oya. Sorghum dumɔwui lɛ daraaa, amɛgbi, ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmei ni wa ni koolooi nyɛŋ akɔmɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why do my stored seed yams start shooting out green sprouts in the barn even without dirt or water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ŋmɔmɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ loo nu bɛ jɛmɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams are living storage organs with an internal clock. Once their natural resting period ends, they use the food and moisture stored inside themselves to push out new shoots in search of light and soil.
ga: Yam ji gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nibii ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ ŋmɛlɛtswaa yɛ emli. Kɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Akɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni ato yɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛtsi ŋmeii heei kɛje kpo koni amɛyatao la kɛ shikpɔŋ.

english: Why do my farm crops need air to blow freely through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ koni etsɔ mli oya lɛ?

english: Good air circulation between crops reduces trapped moisture on leaves and branches, which prevents fungal diseases and allows sunlight to reach the inner parts of the plant so it can grow properly.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa nu ni etsi ehe yɛ baai kɛ tsei aniji anɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ehaa hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops get tangled and stop growing well when they are planted too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are overcrowded, their leaves and branches tangle up, blocking sunlight and airflow. They end up competing for air and soil nutrients, which stunts their growth.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle ehe tsɔ lɛ Baai kɛ tsei niji lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe. Etsiɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa Amɛgbeɔ naa kɛ akaŋshii kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni haa dalɛ kpaa

english: How do I know if the canopy on my crop trees is too thick and needs trimming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni afolɔ mli?

english: If the ground under your crop trees remains constantly dark and damp without any breeze or sunlight passing through the middle branches, the canopy is too thick and needs trimming.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli ewo duŋ ni edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo hulu la ko bɛ ni boteɔ tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli eyi tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni afolɔ mli.

english: What happens if I do not prune or cut back excess branches on my crop trees?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mifolɔɔɔ loo mifolɔɔɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving overgrown branches leads to crowded stems that trap damp air, waste soil nutrients on non-producing shoots, lower your crop yield, and make it easy for pests to hide.
ga: Niji ni eda fe nine ni ashiɔ lɛ feɔ tsei ni mli ewo muji ni mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ. Akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni wooo yibii lɛ anɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ

english: Why is it important to cut away leaves and branches that are blocking air inside my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ baai kɛ tsei niji ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Trimming thick leaf growth lets fresh air pass through the tree, drying up excessive dampness that causes rot and giving main branches space to spread out correctly.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni mli tse lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. ni oha niji titrii lɛ aná he ko ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ.

english: What should I do when my crop branches get stuck together and start entangling neighboring plants?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ tsei niji lɛ kpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛbɔi tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: You should carefully cut through overlapping branches to free up space, let air flow through, and help each plant stand properly without choking its neighbor.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ afo tsei niji ni tsɔɔ amɛhe lɛ amli koni gbɛ babaoo aba. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli. ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso damɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni etsĩii ekutsoŋbii lɛ anaa.

english: Why does removing dead or overgrown branches make my crop trees produce more yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni egboi loo ni eda fe nine lɛ ni mijieɔ lɛ haa mitso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cutting off dead or weak branches directs the tree's energy and soil nutrients straight into producing healthy flowers and fruits instead of wasting energy on useless shoots.
ga: Niji ni egboi loo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ koni ekɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: What causes fruits and pods on my crop trees to rot before they mature?
ga: Mɛni haa yibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛdaraa?

english: Rot is usually caused by excessive moisture trapped around the pods due to poor air circulation and heavy shade. Letting air into the farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni eyaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ hulutsoo ni mli wa hewɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does proper pruning help my farm trees last for many years?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni afolɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Pruning keeps crop trees healthy by removing old or sick branches and admitting fresh air and sunlight, preventing premature aging of the tree and ensuring high yields over many seasons.
ga: Tsei ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ni aduɔ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni egbɔ loo ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ. ni agbeleɔ naa kɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la Etsiɔ tsei ni edaa oya lɛ naa ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo yɛ be babaoo mli fɛɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to follow specific farming guidelines rather than just letting crops grow naturally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni anyiɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi asɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ

english: Following practical farm techniques like proper spacing, seasonal pruning, and opening up air paths keeps the soil and trees productive so your farm stays healthy for decades.
ga: Okwaayeli ŋaai ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii tamɔ gbɛ ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ asɛɛnyiɛmɔ. Be mli nibii ni afoɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi ni agbeleɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii. Koni oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni baa lɛ

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for growing maize before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ dani mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ?

english: Observing your land's soil type and water drainage helps determine suitability. Dark, rich loam soil that retains moisture without staying waterlogged provides the essential nutrients and stability maize roots need to yield heavy cobs.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ henɔ kɛ bɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ baaye abua ni ana kɛji ehi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii, ni eyɛ ediŋŋ, ni mli ewo muji ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni he hiaa koni ekɛ ŋmãa ni tsii aba.

english: Why should I test my soil before deciding which crop to plant on a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka mishikpɔŋ lɛ makwɛ dani makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ nibii ni esa akɛ madu yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli lɛ he?

english: Soil testing reveals the hidden chemical makeup and acidity of your land. Different crops like yam, cassava, or cocoa require specific soil conditions, so analyzing your soil beforehand prevents crop failure and saves you money on unnecessary fertilizers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa jieɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ acidity ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpo. Nibii babaoo ni aduɔ, tamɔ sweet potatoes, cassava loo cocoa, biɔ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwɛmɔ mra lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii akafite, ni ebaaha okɛ shika akafite kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he ehiaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli.

english: Why do my vegetable roots rot when it rains heavily for several days on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: When land has heavy clay or poor drainage, continuous rain fills all the small air pockets in the ground with water. This suffocates the roots because they cannot breathe oxygen, causing them to decay and die.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ ni mli wa loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ bɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii aba. Nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ. ni haa amɛgboiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal that the plant lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or it is experiencing stress from extended dry weather or pests like mealybugs. Adding well-rotted manure or compost helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo amɛmiina haomɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mealybugs lɛ mli lɛ, kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji komɛi bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby creates a gentle umbrella that protects the cocoa leaves from intense heat and keeps the surrounding air moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ baa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the hot afternoon even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During peak heat, tomatoes lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the ground. Covering the soil around the base with dry grass or mulch stops soil moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ, Tomatoi shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ, ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ.

english: Why is my cowpea crop growing plenty of bushy green leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ hiɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cowpea plant focuses all its energy on building green foliage rather than producing flowers and fruit. Balancing soil nutrients encourages the plant to shift its energy into producing pods.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ, Cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛbaafee lɛ he nii moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhewalɛ koni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: What happens to my pepper plants if I sow the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Crowding forces pepper plants to compete for sunlight, ground water, and soil food. Instead of bushy plants with many peppers, you will get tall, weak stems with very small fruits and higher chances of leaf diseases.
ga: Nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ nyɛɔ pepper tsei anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso ko nɛ pepper fuu ngɛ mi. Obaagbe naa kɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni aduawai bibii yɔɔ mli waa kɛ hegbɛ ni fa babaoo akɛ foliar hela baaná bo.

english: Why do my plantain harvests get smaller every year when I keep planting on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ bibioo daa afi beni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains draw huge amounts of specific nutrients, like potassium, out of the soil. Growing them continuously in one spot exhausts those nutrients and allows underground pests like root nematodes to multiply.
ga: Plantains jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo, tamɔ potassium, kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ amɛ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ afite. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ root nematodes lɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my main crop right after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitso titri lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that swallow nutrients quickly before young crop roots can reach them. Clearing all weeds from around your crops before applying fertilizer ensures your plants get full benefit from the nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni yeɔ niyenii mli nibii oya dani tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ onibii amli dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ ana niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ ahe sɛɛ fɛɛ.

english: When maize plants are crowded together, their roots fight for the same water and nutrients in the soil, while their leaves block sunlight from each other. This leaves you with thin, weak stalks and very small or empty cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why do you extension officers always advise us to plant in straight rows instead of scattering seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ dumɔwui ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures that every crop gets its own equal share of space, sunlight, and fertilizer. It also leaves clear walking paths, making it much easier for you to weed, spray, and harvest without stepping on your crops.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ naa he ko, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Eshiɔ gbɛ ni mli ka shi faŋŋ hu. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, okɛ tsofa afɔ, ni okpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni okɛ onaji efɔɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep scorching and dying when I clear all the tall trees from the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under intense direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or tall forest trees overhead to act as natural umbrellas, keeping them cool and protecting the soil moisture while they are young.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo koo mli tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ amɛyiteŋ lɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he be mli ni amɛdarako lɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava and hot pepper together on the same farm plot?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, but you must space them properly. Cassava grows tall with broad leaves; if planted too close to pepper, it will cast too much shade and steal sunlight, preventing the pepper plants from producing plenty of fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ okɛ ohe akabɔ he bɔ ni sa. Cassava lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ pepper tsɔ Ehaa hulutsoo be babaoo baa ni ejuɔ hulu la. Enɛ haaa pɛpɛɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are my plantain suckers growing so slowly and bearing small bunches when planted under my big mango trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛmiifee kui bibii lɛ? Be ni adu mi mango tso agbo lɛ shishi?

english: Plantains need full, direct sunlight to make the food required for fast growth and heavy fruit bunches. Big mango trees block this essential sunlight and steal soil nutrients, starving the plantain.
ga: Plantains he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni eha niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii ni tsii. Mango tsei wuji tsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa waa nɛɛ naa, ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ha hɔmɔ aye plantain lɛ

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow bottom leaves are usually a sign that the plant is short on soil nutrients like nitrogen, getting too much water at the roots, or that the lower leaves are shaded and not receiving enough light and air flow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni shishifãi lɛ miiná nu babaoo. aloo baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli ewo hulutsoo ni amɛnáaa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Pepper leaves curl up in the heat to reduce water loss and protect themselves from drying out. However, if they stay curled even in the cool morning, it usually means sap-sucking insects like thrips or a plant virus are attacking them.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ la mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Shi, kɛji amɛtee nɔ amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli po lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ miitutua amɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my yam setts too deep into the soil mounds?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ?

english: If yam setts are buried too deep, the sprouting shoot wastes all its stored energy trying to reach the soil surface. This leads to slow emerging, weak vines, or even rotting in damp, cold soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu sweet potato lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa wain tso lɛ daa blɛoo ni ebɛ hewalɛ. loo egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ po.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops when they are just growing nearby?
ga: Te jwɛi ji oshara kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eha tɛŋŋ kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi?

english: Weeds are aggressive thieves. Even if they do not touch your crop, their strong roots steal underground water and fertilizer, while their leaves steal sunlight, leaving your crops weak and malnourished.
ga: Jwɛi ji julɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa. Shi kɛlɛ, amɛtaaŋ onibii ahe. Shi amɛshishifãi ni he wa lɛ juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. yɛ be mli ni ebaai lɛ juɔ hulu la lɛ Enɛ haa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnáaa niyenii kpakpa.

english: Why do insect pests attack my farm much more when I grow cassava on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ beni miduɔ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: When you grow the same crop repeatedly on the same land, pests that feed on that crop settle in the soil and multiply season after season. Rotating with a different crop breaks their life cycle and starves the pests away.
ga: Beni okɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ duɔ shii abɔ lɛ. yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛfɔɔ bii yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei krokomɛi tsake amɛhe lɛ, ebaafite amɛshihilɛ gbɛ lɛ, ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ akabote mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees start dying early, while my grandfather's trees stayed productive for over 50 years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miibɔi gboimɔ oya nɛkɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mi-cocoa tsei lɛ etee nɔ ewo yibii nɔ ni fe afii 50 nɛ.

english: Older cocoa varieties grew more slowly and were hardier, while modern high-yielding varieties produce fruit earlier but require more soil nutrients, shade management, and disease control to reach a long life.
ga: Kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ daaa blɛoo ni amɛhe wa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ woɔ yibii mra shi amɛbiɔ niyenii babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Shade nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ helai anɔkwɛmɔ kɛha wala be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do my older cocoa trees produce fewer pods as the years go by?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei ni egbɔ lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, their canopy branches get crowded, preventing light from reaching flower spots. At the same time, the tree exhausts the surrounding soil nutrients needed to make new fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ, eniji lɛ ebɔle ehe. Tsi la ni shɛɔ fɔfɔii lɛ ahe lɛ naa. yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa koni akɛbɔ aduawai heei

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm is failing because the soil is tired or because of a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo hela hewɔ?

english: Tired soil causes slow, general yellowing and weak growth across the whole farm over time, whereas disease usually causes fast, specific signs like swollen stems, black pods, or leaves drying up on tree after tree.
ga: Shikpɔji ni efite lɛ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ bɔjɔmɔ baa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ kɛ okadii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni baa oya tamɔ tsei akutsei ni efuu, tsei ahe tsei ni efee diŋ, loo tsei ahe baai ni egbi yɛ tso sɛɛ tso baa.

english: Can farmland actually run out of food for crops after growing cocoa for many years?
ga: Ani niyenii ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaho yɛ afii babaoo ni akɛdu kookoo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, cocoa trees pull natural nutrients out of the earth every season to make pods. If you do not put nutrients back into the soil through organic mulch or fertilizer, the ground becomes empty of plant food.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cacao tsei lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be mli koni ekɛfee ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛji okɛtsuuu nii lɛ, okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei niyenii.

english: What causes a fully grown cocoa tree to dry up and die all of a sudden?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ gbiɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ?

english: Sudden drying of mature trees is usually caused by severe insect attacks like mirids or underground root diseases that cut off the tree's ability to pull water from the soil, rather than just old age.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ tsei ni eda lɛ agbiɔ trukaa lɛ baa ji kooloi ni naa wa waa, tamɔ myrid loo shikpɔŋ shishi shishifã hela. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jeee onukpayeli kɛkɛ.

english: Why did old cocoa farms planted by our elders yield so much fruit without modern chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji momo Ni wɔ onukpai lɛ du lɛ haa ewoɔ yibii babaoo ni ekɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsofai tsuuu nii lɛ?

english: Old farms were planted on freshly cleared virgin forest land that had rich topsoil accumulated over centuries. Today, that natural soil wealth has been used up, so modern trees need active support to produce well.
ga: Adu ŋmɔji momoi yɛ kooi heei ni mli tse ni sũ ni yɔɔ nɔ ni baa nii babaoo ni abua naa yɛ afii ohai abɔ lɛ amli lɛ amli. Ŋmɛnɛ, akɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ etsu nii. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei he miihia yelikɛbuamɔ ni hiɛdɔɔ yɔɔ mli koni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do cocoa farms often break down and die when left in the hands of hired laborers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ amɛgbee nitsulɔi adɛŋ lɛ?

english: Hired labor without close supervision may skip essential care like regular weeding, removing sick pods, and pruning, which allows pests and fungal diseases to silently spread until the trees are beyond saving.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni akɛ amɛ woɔ nitsumɔ mli ni akwɛɛɛ amɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aku amɛhiɛ amɛshwie nibii ni he hiaa, tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ nɔ. Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni afoɔ Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii helai gbɛɔ eshwaa dioo. Kɛyashi tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni fe yiwalaheremɔ.

english: How does leaving weeds to grow thick under my cocoa trees hurt my crop?
ga: Te jwɛi ni mahã ekwɛ̃ babaoo yɛ mikookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Thick weeds trap humidity around the trunks, creating a wet, dark home where fungal diseases like black pod thrive and bad insects hide before attacking the cocoa.
ga: Jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mɔɔ nu yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe, ni efeɔ shĩa ni mli ewo fɔ, ni ewo duŋ. Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai fɔji lɛ teeɔ amɛhe dani amɛtutuaa kookoo lɛ.

english: What is the best thing to do if a section of my cocoa farm dies completely?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ fã ko gbo kwraa?

english: Instead of just abandoning it, you should clear out and burn the infected dead trees to destroy lingering diseases, let the soil rest or plant food crops, and then replant with fresh, disease-resistant seedlings.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshɛrɛ ashwie lɛ Esa akɛ ojie tsei ni egboi lɛ ni oshã amɛ koni okpata hela fɛɛ hela ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ hiɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe loo niyenii akwɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔ dumɔwui heei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ.

english: Why is trimming old branches necessary for keeping a cocoa tree healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo tsei niji momoi amli koni kookoo tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Trimming removes diseased or dead wood and opens up the tree so sunlight and fresh air can flow through, which dries out dampness that causes diseases and encourages new flowers to grow.
ga: Tso ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ loo ni egboi lɛ. ni ogbele tsei lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ hela baa lɛ mli egbiɔ, ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi heei adalɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why is it that just pouring plenty of water on my young oil palm tree does not automatically make it grow fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ nu wo ŋmei tsei bibii amli fe nine lɛ, ehaaa amɛdara oya lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Young oil palms need time to build strong root systems first. Simply pouring excess water without balanced nutrients, good soil drainage, and proper weed control can drown the roots or wash away topsoil nutrients rather than speeding up growth.
ga: Palm tsei lɛ he miihia be dani amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa. Nu ni fa fe nine ni ashwieɔ shi ni niyenii ni ja bɛ mli lɛ sũ mli nu kpakpa Ni jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi loo amɛfɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha dalɛ aya hiɛ oya

english: How long do I need to keep giving special care and patience to a newly planted oil palm tree before it starts producing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ ehe baahia ni makwɛ mihe krɛdɛɛ kɛ tsuishitoo koni mi-oil palm tso ni midu ehee lɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Oil palms usually take about 3 to 4 years of dedicated care—including regular weeding, pest control, and watering during dry spells—before they establish themselves and bear their first fruit bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei aheɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 dani akwɛɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni fata he ji jwɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ajiemɔ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Dani etswa ehe ema shi ni ewo klɛŋklɛŋ aduawai akuu lɛ.

english: Why do my young seedlings seem to stop growing for a few weeks right after I transplant them into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ kpa dalɛ otsii fioo komɛi beni mijie amɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: This pause in growth is called transplant shock. The plant is shifting its energy underground to rebuild and spread new roots into the field soil. Once the roots are settled, the stem and leaves will start growing again.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ dalɛ ni kpaa shi yɛ be kukuoo mli nɛɛ akɛ transplant shock. Tso lɛ miitsi hewalɛ kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛfee shishifãi heei ni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli wa lɛ, shishifãi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ baabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is the best way to apply water to my young crops during the dry season so I do not damage them?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli? koni akafite tsei lɛ

english: Apply water gently around the base of the plant early in the morning or late in the evening. This allows the soil to absorb moisture deeply without scorching the leaves under full sun or washing away root soil.
ga: Nu awo tso lɛ shishi blɛoo leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni eshãaa baai lɛ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi loo ekɛ shishifã sũ lɛ efɔɔɔ.

english: Can using a strong water hose or pump force too much water onto my young crops and hurt them?
ga: Hose ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛshwieɔ nu nɔ waa Aloo ani pɔmp lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ nu babaoo awo midumɔwui lɛ anɔ ni eye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, high-pressure water can strip away topsoil, expose tender young roots, and break delicate stems. Heavy flooding also compacts the soil, which prevents oxygen from reaching the roots.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni mli wa waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Ejieɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo, ni ji oblahii kɛ oblayei lɛ akpo. ni ebaanyɛ efo tsei ni egbɔjɔ Nu afua ni naa wa hu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves of my young crops turning yellow even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often indicate that the plant lacks important soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is waterlogged. Overwatering without good drainage chokes the roots, preventing them from taking up plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine ni nu kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye tso lɛ niyenii.

english: How can I keep moisture in the soil around my young crops so they do not dry out quickly on hot days?
ga: Makwɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ. Te mi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ? Koni ekagbi oya yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ?

english: You can cover the soil around the plant stem with dry grass, leaves, or crop leaves—a method called mulching. Mulch blocks direct sun from drying out the soil, keeps roots cool, and eventually decomposes into fertilizer.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai ehà tso lɛ shishi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Mulch lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ni ehaaa sũ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni yɛ naagbee lɛ efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Should I apply fertilizer to a crop immediately after transplanting it into the field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛwo he kroko lɛ?

english: It is better to wait a few weeks after transplanting until the seedling recovers from transplant shock and grows new root tips. Applying strong fertilizer too early can burn fragile young roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ otsii fioo komɛi yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ni adu lɛ sɛɛ kɛyashi be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ he baajɔ amɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ ni adu lɛ mli lɛ he gbeyeishemɔ mli ni amɛbaakwɛ shishifãi heei. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds harm my young tree crops so much more than the mature trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ awui babaoo fe tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young tree crops have small, shallow root systems and few leaves, making them weak competitors against aggressive weeds for groundwater, nutrients, and sunlight. Mature trees have deep roots and high leaves that shade out weeds.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai fioo pɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ akaŋshilɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛha jwɛi ni baa shikpɔŋ shishi nu, niyenii kɛ hulu la. Tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛ baai kakadaji ni haa jwɛi lɛ náa hɔnɔ.

english: Do my young seedlings need temporary shade when I plant them out in the open sun?
ga: Ani be kukuoo mli hulutsoo he miihia midumɔwu lɛ kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ?

english: Yes, delicate seedlings like cocoa or young tree crops often need shade from plantains or shade nets. Intense, direct sunlight can burn tender leaves and dry out the upper root zone before the tree gets established.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ kookoo loo tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo kɛjɛ dumɔwui loo hulutsoo ŋshɔŋ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii ni eha shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi dani tso lɛ ama shi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Nurse trees shield young cocoa from harsh heat until the cocoa plants grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Nurse tsei lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and curling up into strange shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The virus stops the leaves from making food properly, causing them to twist, shrink, and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Virus lɛ haaa baai lɛ ahoo jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow even when I give them plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu babaoo moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer gives the plant the food it needs to turn green and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without turning into fruits during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and prevents pollen from fertilizing the flowers. When daytime temperatures get too high, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ nyɛɛɛ ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Planting seeds too close together causes the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leaves you with thin, weak stalks and small maize cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do armyworms destroy my maize leaves mostly at night instead of during the daytime?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ babaoo gbɛkɛ moŋ fe shwane mli lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms avoid the hot sun during the day to keep their bodies from drying out. They hide deep inside the center of the maize plant when it is hot and come out to feed when the air cools down at night.
ga: Fall armyworms tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ he koni amɛkagbi. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ. Ni ebaaje kpo koni eyatao niyenii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my cassava help my farm soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa fataa ŋmãa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground. This naturally enriches the soil, feeding nearby crops like cassava without tiring out the field.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii, tamɔ ŋmei, ni amɛhaaa ŋmɔji lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop producing new peppers during heavy continuous rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ pepper heei feemɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much rain fills all the tiny air spaces in the soil with water, which chokes the pepper plant roots by cutting off oxygen. Under this water stress, the plant stops making flowers and focuses only on surviving.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii baa. Nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ pepper tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. yɛ nu mli haomɔ shishi Tso lɛ baakpa fɔfɔi feemɔ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama wala pɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and misshapen when I plant them in hard ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni efite waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil to push downward and expand as they store food. If the ground is hard or full of rocks, the tuber cannot grow freely, resulting in short, twisted, or stunted yams.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni ekɛtsi shi ni egbɛ eshwa be mli ni ekɛ niyenii toɔ lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ Tubers lɛ hu nyɛŋ ada amɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ kuku, ni efite loo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds harm my young crop seedlings much faster than mature plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi tutuaa mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ oya fe mi tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have very small roots and few leaves, making them too weak to fight for food. Weeds grow much faster, quickly blocking sunlight from reaching the seedlings and stealing water from their shallow roots.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi bibii waa kɛ baai fioo pɛ. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛha niyenii. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa. Amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa oya koni ekashɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ amli.

english: How many fresh fruit bunches do I need to harvest to produce one full drum of palm oil?
ga: Yibii heei akui enyiɛ ehe baahia ni makpa koni manyɛ mafee ŋmei fɔ tsɛnsi kome ni eyi obɔ?

english: A standard mature oil palm fruit bunch yields about 20% oil by weight. To fill a standard 200-liter drum, you typically need to harvest and process around 50 to 70 large, fresh fruit bunches from healthy mature palms.
ga: Mu tso ni eda ni ji ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ lɛ haa mu ni miihe ashɛ 20% yɛ etsitsinɔnii naa. Bɔni afee ni okɛ lita 200 ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ awo mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ ehe baahia ni okpa aduawai agboi heei aaafee 50 kɛyashi 70 kɛjɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda lɛ mli ni otsu he nii.

english: Why are my young oil palm trees producing very small fruits with very little oil in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ fɔ fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Young oil palms in their first year or two of fruiting are still directing most of their energy into growing stems and roots. As the tree matures over 3 to 4 years and gets proper rainfall and fertilizer, the fruit bunches will grow larger and produce more oil.
ga: Mu tsei bibii ni yɔɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi loo afii enyɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ mli lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni miida lɛ ahe nii lolo. Beni tso lɛ daa yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli ni enine shɛɔ nugbɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa nɔ. Yibii akui lɛ baafee wuji ni amɛbaafee fɔ babaoo.

english: Why do I have to train my yam vines onto wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make food that feeds the tuber underground. Lifting the vines off the ground on poles exposes the leaves to sunlight and keeps them away from damp soil diseases, leading to much bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ awó wein tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe, ni ehaaa helai aba shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmɔtɔ ni da kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your crop is running out of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow fast, so applying manure or NPK fertilizer will stop the yellowing from spreading upwards.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋwɛi.

english: Why do my crops grow faster when I clear the weeds even if I don't add any fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya kɛ́ mijie jwɛi lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ko wooo mli moŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Removing weeds removes this competition, allowing your crops to take all the food and water for themselves.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when insects fail to pollinate them. Keeping the soil evenly moist and planting flowering weeds nearby to attract bees will help fruits form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ jwɛi ni woɔ fɔfɔi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Koni agbala ŋmeii lɛ baaye abua ni amɛwo yibii.

english: What is the best time of the day for me to apply fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is best because the soil is cooler. Applying fertilizer in the hot midday sun can cause nitrogen to evaporate into the air before the roots can absorb it, and can burn tender leaves.
ga: Leebi loo shwane ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha nitrogen lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. ni eha baai bibii lɛ ashã.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to be harvested from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Most cassava varieties are ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the main stems turn woody and the bottom leaves begin to yellow and drop off. You can also carefully dig up one stand to check if the roots have expanded into tubers.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, beni tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ feɔ tso ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbeeɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa shidaamɔhe lɛ hu koni okwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ egbɛ eshwa ni etsɔ ŋmeii.

english: If it rains heavily right after I plant my maize seeds, why do some seeds fail to come out of the soil?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa beni midu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Heavy rain can pack the soil tightly into a hard surface layer that soft young shoots cannot push through. It can also flood the seed hole, suffocating the seed by cutting off the air it needs to germinate.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni wa ni ŋmeii bibii nyɛŋ abote mli. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ nu awo dumɔwui akutsei amli hu. Gbalamɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni ooofo mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some extension officers advise us to keep tall trees on our farms until the land looks like a thick forest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi komɛi woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔkɛ tsei kakadaji ahi wɔŋmɔji lɛ amli kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee tamɔ koo ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Tall trees provide natural shade, keep the soil cool and moist during hot weather, and protect delicate crops like young cocoa from harsh sunlight and dry winds.
ga: Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he.

english: Why does my field look bushy like an unmanaged forest when I plant my crops close together, and how does that affect my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni abua naa tamɔ koo ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ? Ni te enɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to catch sunlight and produce a larger harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ená hulu la ni ekɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Is it safe for me to try growing seed varieties brought from other countries on my farmland in Ghana?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ maka dumɔwui ni akɛjɛ maŋ kroko nɔ aba lɛ makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Foreign crop varieties can produce very high yields, but they often require extra care, proper fertilizer, and protection against local pests that they are not naturally resistant to.
ga: Maŋsɛɛ tsei srɔtoi baanyɛ aha yibii babaoo aba. Shi bei pii lɛ, amɛbiɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko. ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni nyɛɛɛ amɛye nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ ahe.
