english: How can I tell if my crops need full open sunshine outdoors or if they prefer growing under shade?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ fɛɛ? Aloo amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shia mli?

english: Crops like maize, cassava, and tomatoes need full outdoor sunlight all day to grow strong, while crops like young cocoa or plantain seedlings grow better under partial shade.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ tomato he miihia hulu la yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo bibii loo plantains kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be fioo ko shishi.

english: What is the benefit of planting specific trees or hedges along the outer edges of my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni aduɔ loo atswaa gbogbo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ he?

english: Planting trees or hedges around the edges of your farm forms a natural windbreak, prevents soil erosion, marks your land boundaries, and stops animals from entering your fields.
ga: Tsei ni ooodu loo gbogbo ni ooobɔle oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko. Tsi shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa Kadimɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ husui. ni nyɛtsi kooloi anaa koni amɛkabote nyɛŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do crops grow so much bigger on freshly cleared forest land compared to land I have farmed for years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii daa babaoo yɛ koo mli shikpɔŋ hee ni ajie lɛ nɔ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto he ni mikɛ afii babaoo etsu nii yɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Forest soil is packed with years of decomposed leaves and organic matter, giving it rich natural nutrients that old, continuously cultivated soil has lost over time.
ga: Koo mli shikpɔŋ lɛ eyi kɛ baai kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbo yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli Shikpɔŋ momo ni atsuɔ he nii be fɛɛ be lɛ elaaje yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli.

english: Why do crops growing under dense tree shade stay green longer into the dry season than crops in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ashishi lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Tree canopies block direct heat from the sun, preventing moisture in the soil from evaporating quickly and keeping the ground damp for longer periods.
ga: Tso lɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ tsiɔ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why are many farmers hesitant to try new agricultural technologies and seed types from abroad?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo sumɔɔɔ ni amɛkaa okwaayeli he ŋaalee kɛ dumɔwui heei amɛkwɛɔ lɛ? kɛjɛ maŋsɛɛ

english: Farmers often hesitate because new methods require upfront money and carry risks if the crop fails. Starting with a small test plot helps farmers learn without risking their entire yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi shashaoɔ shi yɛ gbɛi heei ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahewɔ. Ebiɔ shika kɛtsɔ hiɛ, ni eyɛ oshara kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii. Kɛjɛ kaa shikpɔŋ bibioo nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛkaseɔ nii ni amɛkɛ amɛŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ wooo oshara mli.

english: Can I grow food crops directly beneath tall forest trees, or will the big tree roots take away all the plant food?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii yɛ koo mli tsei kakadaji ashishi tɛ̃ɛ? Aloo ani tsei wuji ashishifãi baaju tsei lɛ aniyenii lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can intercrop beneath tall trees if you pick shade-tolerant food crops and add organic manure, as tree roots usually draw water from deep underground while small crop roots feed near the surface.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei awo tsei kakadaji ashishi kɛji ohala niyenii tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hulutsoo shi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei shishifãi gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ, yɛ be mli ni tsei shishifãi bibii lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ.

english: How do I test a new crop variety or fertilizer to know if it will perform well on my local soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka tso henɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii hee ko makwɛ kɛji ebaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Divide a small portion of your farm to grow the new crop side-by-side with your traditional method. Compare the health, yield, and cost of both before planting the new variety across your entire farm.
ga: Jaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fãi bibii amli koni odu ŋmɔshi nibii heei yɛ he kome yɛ otsutsu gbɛ nɔ. Okɛ amɛyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ hewalɛnamɔ, yibiiwoo, kɛ amɛjara ato he dani odu ŋmeii heei yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which acts as essential food for leaf growth. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green again so the plant can grow strong ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ ŋmãa toi ni mli wa.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomatoes turn black and soft before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering or a lack of calcium in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and adding wood ash or lime helps the fruit develop normally without rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa loo calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛ tso ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfiteee.

english: Why do my vegetable plants droop in the middle of the afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu wo amɛmli leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In intense afternoon sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the soil. Adding a layer of dry grass or leaves (mulch) around the roots keeps the soil cool and retains moisture longer.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (Mulch) wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell which end of a cassava stem cutting should face up when I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tso lɛ naagbee ni esa akɛ ekwɛ ŋwɛi beni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Look closely at the small nodes or 'eyes' where old leaves grew out. Plant the stem so these nodes point upward toward the sky, allowing new shoots to grow easily above ground while roots develop below.
ga: Kwɛmɔ nodes bibii loo ‘buds’ ni baai ni edara lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔ tsei lɛ ni nɛkɛ nodes nɛɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii heei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my young rice crop so early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Mi ŋmãa tsei kɛjɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Young rice seedlings have small root systems that cannot easily compete. Fast-growing weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, choking the young rice plants before they get a chance to grow strong stems.
ga: Omɔ tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe yeee akaŋ mlɛo. Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Etsiɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anaa dani amɛnáa hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why is it important to lift and tie my yam vines onto wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ ni mafi tso ko he lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce the food required to grow big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, catching maximum sunlight while preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛná bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. ni enine ashɛ hulu la babaoo nɔ bɔ ni eeenyɛ yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai hu ahe

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over during strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow close to the soil surface, making heavy fruit-bearing plants top-heavy. Mounding rich soil around the base and supporting the main stem with a sturdy wooden prop stops them from uprooting.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni woɔ yibii ni tsii lɛ tsiimɔ waa. Shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ shishi kɛ tso lɛ shishi. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi enaa koni ekaje shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before they turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when stressed by extreme dry weather, poor soil food, or pest attacks. Providing shade from taller plants, keeping soil moist, and managing pests gives the flowers time to set into healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. niyenii ni ehiii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Ni haa hulutsoo kɛjɛɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ amli Haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ haa fɔfɔi lɛ be ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: Why are tiny insects swarming my cowpea flowers, and will they harm my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiyi mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ amli obɔ lɛ? Ni ani amɛbaaye midumɔ nii lɛ awui?

english: Pests like flower thrips feed on the delicate cowpea blossoms, causing them to fall off before forming seed pods. Spraying organic solutions like neem leaf extract early in the morning protects the flowers so pods can develop.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips lɛ yeɔ cowpea fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ha amɛgbee shi dani amɛfee dumɔwui ŋmeii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem tso mli nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ shwie fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ leebi lɛ, ebaabu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling upward and growing very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper bush lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or aphids that feed on plant juices and spread viruses. Washing the leaves with mild soapy water or neem oil gets rid of the insects and protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ okɛ samla kɛ nu ni mli ejɔ loo neem fɔ afɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi bibii ni ebaatsi baai heei adalɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or waterlogged ground, which prevents the plant roots from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Enɛ haaa tso shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do cowpea crops make the soil richer for the maize I plant after them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina tso lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ fee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ni midu yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea roots work with helpful bacteria in the ground to grab nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, creating natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpea shishifãi kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Bɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or damage from insects like mirids, which prevents successful pollination.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen fite tso lɛ, ni no tsiɔ pollen naa.

english: Why are the blossom ends of my tomato fruits turning black and sunken?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiibote mli lɛ?

english: This is blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the growing fruit, which usually happens when watering is irregular or the soil dries out completely between rains.
ga: Enɛ ji blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ.

english: Twisted and curling leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking on the leaf undersides, or by viruses spread by insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etsɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli

english: Why does my swamp rice crop turn a rusty reddish-brown color after flooding?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-swamp rice ŋmɔji lɛ efee ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nu afua lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This reddish-brown tint is often iron toxicity, which happens in acidic flooded soils when excessive dissolved iron builds up and damages the roots and leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ su ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ ji dade ni yɔɔ gbeyei. Enɛ baa mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ beni dade ni mli ewo muji babaoo lɛ bua ehe naa ni efiteɔ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ.

english: Why do my planted yam setts take so many weeks before sprouting out of the earth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ otsii babaoo dani mi-sweet potatoes ni midu lɛ jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam setts enter a natural dormant resting phase after harvest; if planted during deep dormancy or in dry soil, they delay sprouting until moisture and warm weather wake them up.
ga: Sweet potatoes boteɔ wɔɔhe be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehiɔ shi waa loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, Dalɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ teɔ lɛ shi.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are rotting underground before I harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa?

english: If lower leaves turn yellow and drop off too early while the main stem feels soft or smells foul near the soil level, the cassava tubers below are likely rotting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ loo eŋmɔɔ waa yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ. Kasava shishifã lɛ shishi hu nyɛɔ efiteɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees push over easily when heavy winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over easily if microscopic worms called nematodes have damaged their roots, or if the soil lacks potassium to build strong, stable stems.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ fite amɛshishifãi lɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛma tsei ni wa ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during afternoon heat even when the ground is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can pull it up from the soil, causing temporary wilting to conserve moisture until it cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ tso lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashi ebaajɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out the soil very fast. Keeping big shade trees or planting plantains next to young cocoa protects the crop until it grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya waa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ to loo dumɔwui ni adu yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi ebaada waa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow from the tips instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to grow green and healthy. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help bring back their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts in the same field where I harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpaa ŋmei yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth. Legumes like beans and groundnuts naturally put nitrogen back into the soil through their roots, which refreshes the land for your next crop.
ga: Abele jieɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha jɛmɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha odumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped around them for too long because the roots cannot get air. Planting cassava on raised mounds or soil ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant goes through dry periods without steady water. Watering the base of your plants regularly and covering the soil with dry grass keeps the roots cool.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ tsɔ be ni nu bɛ mli ni nu bɛ mli daa lɛ mli. Okɛ nu awo tso lɛ shishi daa ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo nɔ koni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: When a main plantain tree produces too many small shoots (suckers), they all compete for the same food in the soil. Cutting away extra suckers and leaving only two or three per plant allows the mother plant to grow larger bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwu titri lɛ wo ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ niyenii kome he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Afoɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ. Enɛ baaha tso nyɛ lɛ alɛɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to put long sticks in the ground next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shikpɔŋ yɛ ŋmei tso ko masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need to lift their leaves high to catch sunlight. Staking helps the leaves make food efficiently, which leads to bigger yam tubers growing beneath the ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la. Staking haa baai lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects sucking the sap from under the leaves. Spraying the plants with a mild soapy water mixture or neem oil helps clear the insects so the leaves can expand normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni haa baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ akɛ nu ni mli ejɔ loo neem fɔ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi bibii koni baai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does clearing weeds while my crops are still very small make such a big difference?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ srɔtofeemɔ kpele ni tamɔ nɛkɛ baa jwɛi nɔ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and will quickly steal the sunlight, water, and food meant for your plants. Weeding early prevents young crops from being choked and stressed during their early stage.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii, ni ebaaju hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ otsei lɛ ahe lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi tsei bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe ni amɛkahao yɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Saved seeds will rot or lose their power to sprout if they were stored while still damp or attacked by insects. Sun-drying seeds completely and storing them in sealed, dry containers keeps them healthy for the next planting season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baagboi loo amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ amɛha amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ loo kooloi bibii tutua amɛ. Ha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kwraa ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni egbi ni atsĩ naa mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops dry up during the dry season even if there is a river running right next to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ faa ko hoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ masɛi moŋ?

english: Being close to a river is not enough on its own; if water is not actively drawn and carried to the root zone of the plants, the soil around the crops will still dry out under the hot sun.
ga: Faa ko he ni ooobɛŋkɛ kɛkɛ lɛ faaa. Kɛji akɛ ajieee nu kɛtee tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni egbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Can I plant my vegetables right at the edge of a stream where the ground is always muddy?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai yɛ faa ko ni mli ewo muji be fɛɛ be lɛ naa?

english: Most vegetables will rot if planted in constantly waterlogged mud because roots need air to breathe just as much as they need water. It is better to plant slightly away from the edge and carry water to them.
ga: Aduawai babaoo baagboi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ muji ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Ejaakɛ shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni nu he hiaa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ Esa akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ ŋshɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo ni akɛwo nu mli.

english: How does putting dry leaves around the base of my crops help them hold onto water?
ga: Baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ nu amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil around plants with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that shades the dirt, stopping the hot sun from evaporating the water stored in the ground.
ga: Ale shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni okɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi baaha lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni tsiɔ muji naa. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni ebua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants look wilted in the afternoon even when the soil still has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, pepper leaves lose water faster than the roots can pull it up from the soil. The plant intentionally wilts to reduce its surface area exposed to the sun and save moisture.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Pepper baai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei jwɛŋɔ koni amɛba shikpɔŋ ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop many of their leaves when the Harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai babaoo fiteɔ kɛ́ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ bɔi tswaa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry and windy periods to protect themselves. Fewer leaves mean the tree loses less water through evaporation, helping it survive until the rain returns.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Baai fioo tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ fiteɔ nu fioo yɛ la ni hoɔ lɛ hewɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up tightly during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves roll up when it gets very hot to hide their surface from direct sunlight, which prevents the plant from losing water too quickly.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni naa wa he koni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ akashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ nu lɛ afite oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without making fruit when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Too much rain can wash away pollen from the flowers, and soil that stays too wet stresses the root system, causing the plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ajie pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ lɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ baa shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ afɔ̃ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: How do I know if my cassava plants under the ground are getting too much water?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-cassava tso ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ miiná nu babaoo tsɔ?

english: If cassava gets too much standing water, the leaves above ground will turn yellow and fall off, and the tubers under the ground will smell bad and turn soft instead of growing firm and thick.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ nine shɛ nu ni ekã shi babaoo nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaafee blɛoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee shiŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when rainwater sits in the field for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: When water stands in the field, it pushes out all the air in the soil. Without air, the maize roots stop taking up nutrients like nitrogen, which causes the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Be ni nu lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛya. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Abɛi shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ yeli.

english: Why do crops planted on sloping ground often stay healthier during heavy rains than crops on low, flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji anɔ lɛ fɔɔ hewalɛ kpakpa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli fe tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sloping ground naturally drains away extra rainwater, allowing the soil to stay moist without drowning the roots, whereas low flat land collects water that can cause root rot.
ga: Hei ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ hoɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shishifãi lɛ shwieee nu mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ buaa nu ni baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo lɛ anaa.

english: When maize is planted too close together, the leaves shade each other from sunlight and the roots fight over the same water and soil food. The plants stretch upward to search for light instead of using energy to grow strong stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa ni shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii he akaŋshii mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu kome mli. Tsei baajie amɛhe kpo ni amɛtao la, ni no najiaŋ lɛ, amɛbaafite hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why didn't my maize seeds sprout after I buried them very deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds need a small amount of air, moisture, and warmth near the surface to sprout. If you bury them too deep, the seed runs out of stored energy before the young shoot can push through the heavy soil to reach the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ dɔlɛ fioo ni bɛŋkɛ ŋwɛi koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji ofu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ Hewalɛ ni dumɔwu lɛ eto lɛ baa shi dani tso bibioo lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ kɛyashɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen. The plant is smart and moves whatever nitrogen it has from its older lower leaves to feed the young, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ le nii ni amɛtsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli lɛ koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my cassava produce plenty of big green leaves but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava put all its energy into growing tall stems and thick foliage above ground, leaving little energy to build heavy tubers underground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛ ni akɛbaafee yitso ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my crop yield get smaller every year when I keep planting cassava on the exact same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land year after year pulls the exact same nutrients out of the soil continuously. Without crop rotation or fallowing, the soil becomes exhausted and weak.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Kɛji akɛ sɛɛkuu loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I clear all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak root systems that burn easily under full sunlight. Tall shade trees act as natural umbrellas that cool the air and keep moisture in the soil for the young cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛhaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before they can turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ebatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress or sudden dry conditions. Dropping flowers is the plant's way of saving its remaining water and energy just to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ ahe. Fɔfɔi ni ejieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ toɔ koni ehi wala mli kɛkɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and look limp during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon heat is a protective behavior. The plant rolls its leaves inward to hide them from direct sun rays so it doesn't lose too much water through evaporation.
ga: Abuɔ baai ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ akɛ eji hebuu subaŋ. Tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ amli koni ekɛtee hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, nu babaoo laajeee kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: How do wild weeds hurt my crops if there is enough sunlight for all of us in the field?
ga: Te koo mli jwɛi lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛji hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha wɔ fɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Even if there is enough sun, weeds grow much faster than main crops and aggressively steal the hidden soil water, nitrogen, and root space that your crops depend on to produce fruits.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ moŋ, shi jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ, ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ sũ mli nu, nitrogen, kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ yibii lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees take so long to produce a big bunch when I leave all the young suckers growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: All those extra suckers suck water and food away from the main mother plant. Removing extra suckers leaves only one strong follower, allowing the main stem to fruit quickly and bear larger bunches.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha sɛɛnyiɛlɔ kome pɛ ni he wa ahi shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii oya ni ewoɔ yibii kui wuji.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and delicate roots that dry out easily under direct sunlight. Leaving tall shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides a canopy that keeps the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa bushes grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. releasing tall trees Shade loo dumɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe koni eha hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the leaves regain a healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: If I plant my seeds very close to each other, won't I harvest more crops from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Ani minɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aya hiɛ?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to spread roots and produce bigger fruits or heavier grains, giving you a better harvest overall.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa enáa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa ni ewoɔ yibii wuji loo dumɔwui ni tsii. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmaa fɛɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers cover the ground around plant stems with dry grass during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛtsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It traps moisture in the ground, shields the soil from hot sun, and stops weeds from taking over the field.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Traps ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni amɛtsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are mature enough to dig up without opening every plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafo ni migbeleee tso fɛɛ tso?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves dry up and drop, and the base of the stem becomes thick. You can gently clear soil around one root to check its thickness before harvesting the entire field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Obaanyɛ okɛ blɛoo atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifã kome he lɛ nɔ okwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ha dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller maize harvests when I plant maize on the same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same soil nutrients every season and allows pests to build up in the field. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts recharges the soil with nitrogen and keeps pests away.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aaaya nɔ akwɛ lɛ baaha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ajɛ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ebaakɛ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni ebu he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures become extremely hot or when the plant experiences sudden dry periods without water. Regular watering and avoiding excessive fertilizer during flowering help fruits to set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na be ni nu bɛ mli trukaa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Should I pour chemical fertilizer directly on my seed right when I drop it into the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ awo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛji amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly on seeds can burn and kill the germinating shoot. It is best to wait a few weeks after the seedling emerges and place the fertilizer a short distance away from the stem so the roots can drink it safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashã ni amɛgboi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ otsii 2-3 beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo koni shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I remove extra young shoots growing around the base of my plantain stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain shishitoo lɛ jie

english: Removing extra suckers prevents them from stealing food and water from the main mother plant. Leaving only one or two healthy shoots ensures the main plant grows strong and produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii krokomɛi lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ adara waa ni ewo tso wuji babaoo ni tsii.

english: What causes ragged holes in my young maize leaf whorls and small dark droppings inside the shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni etse ehe yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: Ragged holes and droppings inside maize shoots are caused by caterpillars like the fall armyworm eating the leaves. Early detection and spraying with recommended biological or chemical solutions stop them before they ruin the farm.
ga: Buji ni ekumɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ amli. Anaa mra ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ afɔ nɔ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: I noticed black spots on my cassava leaves and some are falling off, how do I know if my crop is sick?
ga: Miyɔse ŋmeii diji yɛ ŋmei baai lɛ anɔ ni ekomɛi egbee shi. Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela mɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Black spots and falling leaves are clear signs of fungal or bacterial leaf spot disease. When a crop shows unusual spots, wilting, or premature leaf drop, it means the plant is sick and needs damaged leaves removed or suitable treatment applied.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ kɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ ji fungal loo bacteria leaf spot hela he okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ. Beni tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni esaaa, amɛgboiɔ, loo amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ oya. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela mɔ tso lɛ ni ehe miihia ni ajie baai ni efite lɛ loo akɛ tsofa ni sa awo mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and rolling up tightly during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpɛɔ amɛhe waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during hot afternoons to save water when the soil is dry. However, if the leaves turn yellow starting from the tip in a V-shape, it means your crop is suffering from a lack of nitrogen in the soil.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛbu nu he be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaagbɛ yɛ V su mli lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: If I find one cocoa tree on my farm with swollen branches, what action should I take to protect my other trees?
ga: Kɛji mina kookoo tso ko yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli ni eniji efuu Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mabu mitsei krokomɛi lɛ ahe?

english: Swollen branches on cocoa trees indicate Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which spreads easily to neighboring trees through insects. You must cut down and safely dispose of the infected tree immediately to prevent the disease from spreading to healthy trees.
ga: Niji ni efu yɛ kookoo tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ kookoo bud virus ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii anɔ. Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli ni okɛ amɛ ashwie shweshweeshwe amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves have holes in them even though I never see any insects on them during the daytime?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ yɛ bu lɛ? Ni minaaa kooloi bibii komɛi pɛŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli?

english: Pests like caterpillars and armyworms often hide under leaves or in the soil during the hot day to avoid heat and predators. They come out to eat your crops at night or early morning, so inspecting your farm at dawn helps you catch them.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ Bei pii lɛ amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ baai ashishi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni akafee dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ Amɛbaaje kpo koni amɛbaye oŋmɔshi nibii gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my yam vines growing very short and turning yellow long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines turn yellow early when tiny worms called nematodes are attacking the roots underground or when the soil lacks food. Adding well-rotted manure to the soil before planting helps nourish the roots and keeps pests away.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ tutua shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ loo kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo sũ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ebaabu he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants rot near the soil line and die right after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Pepper roots and stems rot when water sits around them for too long because of poor drainage. Building raised soil ridges or raised beds allows excess rainwater to flow away from the stem and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Pepper shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu tsɔ amɛhe. sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ Ŋshɔ loo saatso ni awo nɔ lɛ ni afee lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are my groundnut seeds failing to sprout after I planted them in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnut seeds require moisture to break open and start growing. If you plant them in dry soil during hot weather, the seeds will either dry out completely or get eaten by soil insects before rain comes.
ga: Peanut dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛgbele ni amɛbɔi dalɛ. Kɛji odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ egbi kwraa loo kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ amɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ baa.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the weather is extremely hot or when they do not get water consistently. Watering your plants regularly early in the morning helps cool them down and allows flowers to set fruit.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo ahaaa amɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo otsei lɛ amli daa leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhe jɔɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How do I know if I planted my plantain suckers too close to each other?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ adu plantain tsei lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: If plantain suckers are too close, they will shade each other out and fight for nutrients, causing them to grow thin and take much longer to produce fruit. Proper spacing allows every plant enough sunlight to form strong stems.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛhaa amɛhe shade ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni wa.

english: Why is my papaya tree dropping its young fruits before they can mature and ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi papaya tso lɛ woɔ yibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo dani amɛshwereɔ ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Papaya trees drop young fruits when they experience sudden water stress, like going from dry soil to heavy rain, or when the tree has more fruit than it can feed. Consistent watering helps the tree hold onto its fruits.
ga: Papaya tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji amɛkɛ nu he haomɔ kpe trukaa, tamɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nɔ. Aloo kɛ́ tso lɛ wo yibii babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ yibii.

english: How do I know when my mangoes are ready to be harvested from the trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ ajie mango kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Mangoes are ready to harvest when they change shape from flat to full and round, and the skin near the stem turns slightly yellowish or lighter green. You can also gently press the fruit to feel if it has softened slightly.
ga: Mango lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa kɛji etsake ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni hewolo ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ fioo loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse fioo. Obaanyɛ onyɛ aduawai lɛ hu nɔ blɛoo. Koni onu he tamɔ nɔ ni efee blɛoo fioo?

english: After my fruit trees finish flowering, how long does it usually take before I can harvest the fruits?
ga: Beni mi aduawai tsei lɛ egbe fɔmɔ naa lɛ Be enyiɛ bei pii eheɔ dani anyɛɔ akpaa aduawai?

english: For crops like mangoes, it typically takes between 3 to 5 months after flowering for the fruits to mature fully and become ready for harvest, depending on the weather and variety.
ga: Kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ mango lɛ, bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 5 yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ asɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ ni efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ Edamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why can't I see any small fruits on my crop immediately after the flowers dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mana berry lɛ? yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni fɔfɔi lɛ egbi lɛ.

english: After pollination, the tiny young fruits are hidden beneath dense leaves and take a few weeks to swell up before they become large enough to be clearly visible on the branches.
ga: Yɛ pollination sɛɛ lɛ, akɛ aduawai bibii bibii lɛ teeɔ tsei ni mli tse lɛ ashishi. Ni eheɔ otsii fioo komɛi dani egbɔjɔɔ dani edaa bɔ ni sa ni enaa niji lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my harvested fruits to spoil quickly before I can sell them at the market?
ga: Mɛni haa aduawai ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani anyɛɔ ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Harvesting during the hot heat of the afternoon, rough handling that causes bruises, or storing fruits in closed plastic containers causes heat build-up that speeds up rotting.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ he nitsumɔ ni mli wa ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe Loo aduawai ni akɛtoɔ plastic tsinsii ni agbe naa lɛ mli lɛ baaha latsaa aba ni eha fitemɔ aya oya.

english: How can I estimate the money I will make from my farm harvest before I apply for a loan?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu shika ni maná kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he akɔntaa dani mabi ni aha mi shika?

english: Calculate your estimated yields based on your farm size, subtract expected crop losses from pests or bad weather, and look at average market prices over the past few seasons rather than peak prices.
ga: Buu yibiiwoo ni osusuɔ akɛ obaaná lɛ he akɔntaa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ naa. Jiemɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ ebaafite kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi gbohii amli. Ni kwɛmɔ jara ni jara wa yɛ bei fioo ni eho lɛ amli lɛ mlijaa mlijaa. yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ najiaŋ

english: Is it wise to rely on a single harvest to buy expensive equipment like a tractor or start building a house?
ga: Ani nilee yɛ mli akɛ akɛ he aaafɔ̃ nikpamɔ kome pɛ nɔ koni akɛhe nibii ni jara wa tamɔ traktɔ loo akɛje tsũ maa shishi?

english: It is safer to save profits across multiple harvests before making major purchases, because unpredictable weather, market price drops, or pests can reduce your expected earnings in any single season.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oookɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni jɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi babaoo mli baa lɛ ato. Dani obaahe nɔ ko wulu Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ hewɔ lɛ jarayeli jara ni baa shi Aloo tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aha shika ni okpaa gbɛ akɛ obaaná lɛ aba shi yɛ be kome mli.

english: When is the best time for me to seek a farm loan for tree crops like mangoes?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabi ŋmɔ mli nyɔmɔwoo kɛha tso mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ mango?

english: Request farm loans a few months before the flowering and fruiting season begins so you have funds ready for crop protection, labor, and harvesting materials right when they are needed.
ga: Bi ni aha bo ŋmɔ mli nyɔmɔwoo nyɔji fioo komɛi dani fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo be lɛ aje shishi. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni oná shika ni okɛbaabu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe, nitsumɔ, kɛ nibii ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ehe baahia.

english: Why are my tree crops growing plenty of healthy green leaves but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo shi ewoɔ aduawai fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer encourages leaves to grow instead of fruits. Tree crops need balanced nutrients, especially potassium and phosphorus, to trigger strong flowering and fruit production.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha baai akwɛ̃ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei. titri lɛ potassium kɛ phosphorus Koni ekɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ yibii ni mli wa mli hewalɛ

english: Why are my mango trees taking so long to yield fruit even after I weed and clean the farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli saamɔ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: While weeding removes competition for nutrients, fruit production also depends on tree age, adequate water timing, sunlight, and proper pruning to allow light into the branches.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii ni yaa nɔ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he lɛ moŋ, Shi yibii ni anáa lɛ hu damɔ afii ni tso lɛ eye lɛ nɔ. Be ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la kɛ tsei ni afoɔ jogbaŋŋ koni la abote tsei lɛ aniji amli.

english: How often should I do routine maintenance like pruning and weeding on my fruit farm?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafee nibii ni afeɔ daa tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ mi aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeding should be done every 4 to 6 weeks during the rainy season to prevent weeds from stealing soil food, while pruning is best done once a year right after harvest to clear out dead branches.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ daa otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 yɛ nugbɔ be mli koni jwɛi lɛ akaju niyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaakpa tsei lɛ shikome yɛ afi mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ koni ajie tsei niji ni egboi lɛ.

english: How can I easily spot early signs of crop disease on my farm before it spreads?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hela he okadii mra yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani egbɛ eshwa?

english: Look closely at the leaves for unusual brown or black spots, pale yellowing patterns, white fungal powder underneath, or wilting stems during the cooler parts of the day.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ona ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni yɔɔ srɔto. Eyɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Fungal powder yɛŋ yɛ shishi. Aloo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is waterlogged, which suffocates the roots and stops them from feeding.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛha niyenii.

english: How does adding fertilizer to my soil change the way my crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer acts like food for crops, giving them concentrated minerals that help build strong roots, deep green leaves, and bigger fruits or grains.
ga: Fertilizer acts like food for crops. Ehaa minerals ni mli eyi obɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi ni wa lɛ maa shi. dark green leaves and larger fruits or grains

english: Can applying too much fertilizer harm or destroy my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui loo efite?

english: Yes, using too much fertilizer increases salts in the soil, which pulls water out of the roots, causing the leaves to scorch, burn, and potentially kill the plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa ŋmei ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli Ehaa baai lɛ shãa, amɛshãa, ni amɛgbeɔ tso lɛ po.

english: How do pest control chemicals work to protect my crops from insect damage?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ koni ebu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe?

english: Pest control chemicals either kill insects directly on contact or coat the plant leaves so pests get poisoned when they try to eat the crop.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ loo amɛwo amɛhe bɔni afee ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ aná poison kɛ́ amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: When is the best time of day for me to spray chemicals on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when temperatures are cool and winds are calm, preventing the heat from burning leaves or evaporating the spray.
ga: Okɛshwie nɔ leebi loo shwane mli. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu efee kpoo Koni hulutsoo lɛ akashã baai lɛ loo ekafee ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if heavy rain falls right after I spray them with pest chemicals?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes the chemical off the crop leaves before it can kill the pests, leaving your plants unprotected and wasting the spray.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ tsei ahe baai amli lɛ ahe nii dani amɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ bɛ hebuu ni efiteɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, leaves lose moisture through transpiration faster than roots can draw water up, causing the plant to temporarily droop to conserve water.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli latsaa mli lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ latsaa nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛya ŋwɛi. Gbimɔ tsei yɛ be kukuoo mli koni nu akafite.

english: How do I choose the right crop to plant if the rainy season starts late?
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi sɛɛ mli lɛ, te ooofee tɛŋŋ ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa?

english: Select early-maturing or short-duration crop varieties that can grow, flower, and produce yield quickly before the shortened rainy period ends.
ga: Halamɔ tsei srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra loo ni hiɔ shi be kukuoo ni baanyɛ adara, awo fɔfɔi ni awo yibii oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ aba naagbee.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and thin when planted too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots and leaves compete heavily against each other for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa kɛha hulu la ni faaa, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii.

english: How do I decide whether to grow local seeds or improved seed varieties on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ kɛji makwɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui loo makwɛ dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Local seeds are usually cheap and adapted to your local climate, but improved seeds are bred to mature faster, resist local diseases better, and yield significantly more crop at harvest time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ jara waaa, ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe kɛyaa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe. But improved seeds are bred to ripen faster. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli

english: Why should I plant my crops in neat straight rows instead of scattering the seeds randomly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo, ni ja lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui trukaa lɛ?

english: Planting in rows gives each crop equal access to sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, while making it much easier for you to weed, apply fertilizer, and walk through your farm.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni onyiɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I determine how much of my harvested crop to keep for my family and how much to take to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male mikpamɔ lɛ mli nibii enyiɛ ni mikɛbaato miweku lɛ kɛ nɔ ni mikɛbaaya jara nɔ?

english: First, calculate how many bags of produce your family consumes between harvests and add a small extra reserve; any harvest remaining after securing that family food supply can be safely sold for profit.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, bu nibii ni oweku lɛ kɛbaatsu nii yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ ayibɔ he akɔntaa ni okɛ fioo afata shika ni okɛto lɛ he. Abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ ŋmaa ni eshwɛ yɛ niyenii ni akɛha weku lɛ sɛɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe koni ana sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Why does crop farming require so much more daily effort than people usually expect?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ biɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo daa gbi fe bɔ ni gbɔmɛi kpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: Crops are living things that require precise timing for land preparation, weeding, pest control, and watering; delaying any of these steps creates extra labor later and reduces your final yield.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni ebiɔ be kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ, jwɛi ahe nitsumɔ, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ. kɛ nu ni akɛhaa pɛpɛɛpɛ Gbɛ fɛɛ gbɛ ni oootsi kɛya sɛɛ Nibii nɛɛ ni ooojie lɛ baaha nitsumɔ kroko aba sɛɛ mli ni ebaaha naagbee nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ aba shi.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods to conserve water and protect themselves from heat; once the rains return, the stems will naturally sprout fresh green leaves again.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms before any peppers actually start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from intense heat, drought, or too much strong fertilizer, which causes the plant to save its energy rather than feed growing fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛ latsaa ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ ehe woɔ hewalɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeeye aduawai ni miida lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is tired and needs extra plant food to grow healthy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni akɛ tsei niyenii krokomɛi afata he koni tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Tired soil produces crops with pale yellow leaves, thin stems, and slow growth; applying compost or fertilizer puts essential nutrients back into the dirt so plants can thrive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse lɛ haa tsei lɛ baa ŋmɔŋ, amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo, ni amɛdaraa blɛoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni tsei lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Can I put fresh manure from my goats directly onto my vegetable beds right after sweeping it?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ too ŋmei hee afata mi-vegetables saatso lɛ he kɛji mijie ŋmei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Fresh manure is too strong and releases high heat as it breaks down, which burns sensitive plant roots; you must let it rot and cool down in a heap for a few weeks before applying it to crops.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ejieɔ dɔlɛ babaoo kɛji efite. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Esa akɛ oha egbo ni edɔ yɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: Why are caterpillars eating the fresh leaves right in the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ miiye baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworm target the hidden center funnel of young maize plants because the newly forming leaves are soft, nutritious, and offer shade from the hot sun.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai heei ni abɔ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he hulutsoo

english: Wilting in wet soil is usually caused by invisible bacterial diseases or root rots that block the plant's internal tubes, preventing water from reaching the upper stems regardless of how much you water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni anaaa loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ ni tsiɔ tso lɛ mli paipii lɛ anaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ haaa nu ashɛ ŋwɛi tsei lɛ ahe bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni oooha amɛ nu oha.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge bushes of leaves on top, but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ jwɛi wuji yɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava plants are grown in soil with too much nitrogen or planted too closely together, they spend all their energy growing leaves to catch light instead of storing food in their roots to make big tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ nɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ edalɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni enine ashɛ la nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight because their young leaves burn easily. They need temporary shade from shade trees or companion crops like plantains to keep them cool and moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ hulutsoo tsei loo tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds from around my groundnut plants if weeds also provide shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? mi ŋmei tso lɛ Kɛji jwɛi hu haa hulutsoo

english: Unlike young cocoa, groundnut plants need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food and flower properly. Weeds block this essential sunlight and steal nutrients and water from the groundnut roots.
ga: Peanut tsei, ni tamɔɔɔ cocoa tsei bibii lɛ, ehe miihia ni hulu la ashɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛye niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi. Jwɛi tsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa nɛɛ naa ni ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ ŋmei shishifãi amli.

english: Why do I have to put long wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kakadaji ahe hiaa mi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to lift themselves up to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce big tubers. Lifting the vines off the ground also prevents damp leaves from catching fungal diseases from wet soil.
ga: Esa akɛ awó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la babaoo aba bɔ ni aaanyɛ koni ekɛ bulbs wuji aba. Wein tso lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ shɛɛɛ baai ni mli efɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before any small tomatoes start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani tomato bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as extremely hot weather, irregular watering, or insect damage. Without steady water and warm—not scorching—weather, the plant drops its flowers to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao, tamɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kooloi ni fiteɔ amɛ Kɛ́ nu ni bɛ daa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ bɛ—jeee dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ—tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛhi shi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny, invisible insects like mites or thrips sucking the juice out of the young leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips Nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ.

english: Why do small caterpillars attack the inside funnel of my corn plants during the dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii tutuaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli gbɛjegbɛi lɛ yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars, known as Fall Armyworms, prefer tender young leaves hidden inside the center whorl of the corn plant where it is moist and safe from predators during dry weather.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni ale amɛ akɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ sumɔɔ baai bibii ni akɛtee ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ, ni mli efɔ ni amɛhe bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: The first rain is often followed by several weeks of heat and dry weather. If your seeds sprout after the first rain, the young seedlings will dry up and die before the main rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, otsii babaoo ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔ lɛ anɛ.

english: Why can swamp rice grow directly in standing water, but my garden vegetables drown if water stays on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ? Shi ani mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ baagbo kɛji nu lɛ tee nɔ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Rice plants have special tubes inside their stems that carry oxygen down from the air into underwater roots. Vegetables like tomatoes or peppers do not have these air tubes, so their roots rot when submerged in water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Aduawai tamɔ tomato loo ŋmɔtɔ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛ. The roots therefore rot when soaked in water.

english: When the lower leaves turn yellow starting from the tip and moving down the middle, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Maize is a heavy feeder, and adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or organic manure helps keep the leaves green so the cobs can grow large.
ga: Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaagbee kɛtee teŋgbɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ji niyenii ni tsii. Ni kɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi ŋmɔŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or groundnuts helps make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special bacteria on their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, this natural nitrogen stays behind to nourish the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa amɛ Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ baahi sɛɛ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my plantain plants give small bunches when I plant them close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: Plantain plants need plenty of room, sunlight, and water to produce large fruit. When planted too close together, their roots and large leaves fight each other for soil food and light, causing all of them to produce smaller bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui hia gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la, kɛ nu koni amɛ wo aduawai wuji. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai wuji lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Make them all break up into small bunches.

english: Yam plants store energy in their underground tubers through sunlight captured by their leaves. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground so leaves receive full sunlight and are kept safe from fungal diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ hulu la ni amɛbaai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking woɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ashɛ amɛhe ni eha amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni sũ ni mli edɔ kɛbaa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when heavy rains last for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe and stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the farm without good drainage, water fills all the air spaces, causing anaerobic rot and soil fungi to destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi hia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛmu ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ. Nu lɛ baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ fɛɛ amli. Enɛ haa anaerobic rot kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves look limp and wilted in the hot afternoon even if the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During very hot afternoons, pepper plants lose water from their leaves faster than the roots can drink it from the ground. This is a natural defense to protect the plant, and it will usually recover in the evening as temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ tso lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their young flowers without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii ni amɛwooo ŋmɔtɔ ko lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when stressed by intense heat, drought, or attacks from sap-sucking insects like mirids. Providing shade trees and keeping the farm protected from major pests encourages the flowers to turn into healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ pollen lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ ni abuɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi wuji ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and dry out when the weather turns dry and hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato leaf curling can happen as a reaction to severe heat stress or as a sign of viral infections spread by small insects like whiteflies. Covering the ground around the stems with dry grass keeps the roots cool and reduces leaf curling.
ga: Tomato baa lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa. Aloo eji hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why shouldn't I grow maize on the exact same plot of land three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains the exact same nutrients out of the soil every year and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field. Rotating with crops like beans or cassava keeps the soil balanced and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to apply chemical fertilizer to my crops right before a heavy rain storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baawo mli dani ahum aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away loose granular fertilizer off the soil surface before the plant roots have a chance to drink it in. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is damp but no immediate heavy downpours are expected.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe dani tsei shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛnuɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi akpaaa nugbɔ ni naa wa gbɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them out in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates shade that acts like an umbrella, protecting young seedlings from drying out until they are strong enough.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela baa. Buu dumɔwui bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from under the leaves, or viruses spread by these insects. Sprinkling wood ash or using targeted organic sprays helps protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Tso mli sũ ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build healthy leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their dark green colour.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛma baai ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them after maize restores nutrients back into the soil naturally without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa ni jara wa awo mli.

english: How does my cassava crop survive long dry spells when other crops wither and die?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi-cassava tso lɛ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli beni tsei krokomɛi egboi ni amɛgboi lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its top leaves during dry weather to conserve water, while relying on its deep underground tubers that store moisture and starch until rain comes back.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi koni ekɛbu nu he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba lɛ anɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when the soil lacks steady water and essential minerals like calcium, preventing the flowers from setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Aloo kɛ́ nu kɛ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa, ni no haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii.

english: Making mounds loosens the soil so yam tubers can easily grow big and long underground, while also preventing heavy rain from soaking the seeds and causing root rot.
