ga: Gɔji ni afeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji ni kɛlɛ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha dumɔwui lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ akagbo.

english: Why will I get a smaller harvest if I plant my crops too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots fight each other for water and plant food in the soil, and their leaves shade one another from the sunlight needed for growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋshii mli ni amɛduɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la ni he hiaa koni amɛdara lɛ akashɛ amɛhe.

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell that can dry out newly sprouted seeds. Waiting for consistent, steady rains ensures seeds get continuous moisture to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ agbi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa, ni baa daa lɛ mɛmɔ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to take up nutrients, water, and sunlight much faster than farm crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing vital resources from young crop seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhe niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nibii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛ dumɔwui bibii amli.

english: Why shouldn't I cut down all the large trees when I am clearing my land to plant a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni mijieɔ shikpɔŋ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from larger trees to protect them from direct sun damage, harsh winds, and soil drying out during the dry season. Keeping select shade trees helps the young crop survive and grow strong.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni eda lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ he. Tsei ni akɛ hulutsoo haa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why is it recommended to plant plantains alongside young cocoa trees on a new field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ adu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ shikpɔji heei anɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and moisture retention for young cocoa seedlings during their first few vulnerable years.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Amɛhaa hulutsoo ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ amli yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni amɛgbɔjɔ lɛ amli.

english: Does it matter which direction I face a cassava stem cutting when pushing it into the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ ootsi ŋmei lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ atsɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, you must plant the cassava stem with the small buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting it upside down makes it very difficult for the shoots to emerge, leading to weak plants and poor root yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni odu ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛ́ adu kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu ehiii.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push stems into the soil after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ eshishifã lɛ ewoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts form their pods underground. After the flowers above ground are pollinated, the plant grows special stems called 'pegs' that bend downward and burrow into the dirt so the groundnut pods can safely develop beneath the soil.
ga: Peanuts feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Beni afɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ pollen sɛɛ lɛ, Tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ ni kotoɔ shi ni amɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks next to my yam plants as they begin to sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo sweet potato tso ko masɛi beni ejeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine, so staking provides support for the leaves to spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the plant make food, which results in larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes are a climbing vine. No hewɔ lɛ, staking yeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on young maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or overly waterlogged roots that cannot soak up nutrients. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil drains the specific nutrients maize needs to grow and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating with legumes like beans or groundnuts re-enriches the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abɛi koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ hoɔ. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsu nii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow around one plantain stem creates competition for nutrients and water. Pruning down to one main stem and one or two replacement suckers ensures high quality and larger bunches of fruit.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Tso kome pɛ he lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni ashi tso lɛ yibii titri kome kɛ suckers kome loo enyɔ ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ haa tso yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ agboi baa.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before any fruit develops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ dani aduawai jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering. Under severe stress, the plant conserves energy by shedding blossoms instead of spending resources to form fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. yɛ haomɔ ni naa wa shishi Tsei buɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii koni amɛkɛwo yibii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or by viruses spread by these insects. Controlling the insects protects the leaves from curling and keeps the plant growing healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kooloi ahe nitsumɔ tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the rains start late these days, and how does that affect when I should plant my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ lɛ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ mli nɛɛ? Ni te enáa be ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Shifting weather patterns have altered traditional rainfall seasons across Ghana. Planting maize by traditional calendar dates rather than waiting for sustained rainfall can cause seeds to dry up and die in hot, unwatered soil.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi etsake blema nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yɔɔ Ghana fɛɛ lɛ. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ blema kalanda gbii lɛ anaa Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ mɛmɔ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nu bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does sudden heavy rainfall rot my seeds right after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa trukaa lɛ ha midumɔwui lɛ fite amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Unpredictable changing weather causes intense downpours that flood the soil and wash away nutrients. When seeds sit in waterlogged soil without air, they drown and rot before they can germinate.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ shihilɛi ni tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baa lɛ baa. Beni dumɔwui tara shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ baagbee nu mli ni amɛbaagboi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Rising global temperatures create intense heat stress. Young cocoa trees need shade trees planted around them to block direct afternoon sunlight and keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Jeŋ dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni naa wa miiba. Ehe miihia ni akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ abɔle kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛtsi hulu ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ naa. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without turning into fruit during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, causing the plant to drop its blossoms to save energy rather than producing fruit.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei baa fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why is my cassava crop producing smaller roots now compared to previous years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi bibii fe afi ni eho lɛ?

english: Hotter ground temperatures and longer dry periods force the cassava plant to use its energy just to stay alive, leaving very little energy to store in thick tuber roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ be ni hulutsoo be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ biɔ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ afite hewalɛ babaoo koni amɛhi shi kɛkɛ. Hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ eshwɛ ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi ni mli tse lɛ amli.

english: Why do my bean pods stay small and empty even though the leaves look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea pods lɛ ji bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli moŋ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of water during the pod-filling stage stop the plant from transferring nutrients into the seeds, resulting in empty or stunted pods.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ pod lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni awoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aya dumɔwui lɛ amli. Enɛ haa pods lɛ feɔ efolo loo egbɔjɔ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out and crack so much faster after rain than it used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya kwraa kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Higher sun intensity bakes bare topsoil and causes moisture to evaporate rapidly. Covering the soil with organic mulch or cover crops protects it from the harsh sun and holds water longer.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ jieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni ehaa nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during windstorms before the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Extended hot, dry spells shrink soil moisture and weaken plantain roots. When sudden strong winds blow before the rains start, the shallow, thirsty roots cannot anchor the heavy plant.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, ni egbiɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ baa shi ni ehaa plantain shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswa trukaa dani nugbɔ lɛ nɛ Shallow, shishifãi ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ nyɛŋ amɔ tso ko ni tsii.

english: Why am I seeing more caterpillars and insects on my crops during hot dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Warmer weather speeds up the breeding cycles of many farm insects, causing them to hatch and multiply much faster while heat-stressed crops are too weak to resist them.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ eha kooloi bibii babaoo ni akwɛɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ebɔi gbalashihilɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfɔɔ ni amɛfɔɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni hulutsoo haoɔ amɛ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛte shi amɛwo amɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops catch diseases faster when the heat increases?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ yeɔ hela oya kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ?

english: High heat puts crops under constant stress, weakening their natural defense systems and making it easier for bacteria and viruses to spread through the farm.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ haomɔ shishi be fɛɛ be. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ helatsɛmɛi kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: How does fertilizer actually help my crops produce a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer acts as food for the soil and plants by replacing essential nutrients that crops drain from the ground, allowing plants to develop stronger roots, green leaves, and larger yields.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ kɛtsɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei shwieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ najiaŋdamɔlɔ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji, kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo.

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient plants need to stay green and grow well; applying the right fertilizer early helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii mra Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields every year even though I clear the weeds and plant at the right time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mifoɔ jwɛi ni miduɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli moŋ?

english: Every crop you harvest takes nutrients out of the soil, so without feeding the land with manure or fertilizer, the soil becomes exhausted and cannot nourish new crops properly.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni okpaa lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei jogbaŋŋ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I apply too much fertilizer to them at once?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii yɛ be kome mli?

english: Using too much fertilizer at one time can burn the crop's roots and dry out its leaves, which can stunt the plant's growth or even cause it to die.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni eha baai lɛ agbi. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tso lɛ dalɛ naa loo egbe tso lɛ po.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves in hot, dry weather to reduce water loss and protect themselves from dying, and they naturally grow new leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Ni kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, baai heei baakwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings need plantains planted next to them when they are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu mi-kokoo dumɔwui lɛ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Beni tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct heat, so planting fast-growing plantains provides large leaves that act as natural umbrellas to shade and protect the cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu kookoo dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ, ebaana baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta, ni ehaa kookoo lɛ hulutsoo kɛ hebuu.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and skinny without producing good fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete with each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, spending all their energy stretching upward instead of growing strong stems and yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛtsɔɔ ehe shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ tsei kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa.

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and the plant roots are active, usually a few weeks after sprouting, so the roots can soak up the nutrients efficiently.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooowo ŋmɔshi nii be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miitsu nii. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 2-3 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I apply my fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm comes?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba?

english: No, heavy rainfall will wash the fertilizer away from your farm before the plant roots can absorb it, so it is better to apply it when the soil is moist after moderate rain.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛwo nɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and stunted even when I feed the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ kɛ́ mikɛ niyenii ha shikpɔŋ lɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients meant for your main crops, so leaving weeds in the field starves your crops of the care they need.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii titrii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛná kwɛmɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the new improved seeds I bought grow so differently from the local seeds my family used in the past?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ ni miheɔ lɛ daraa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto kwraa nɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni miweku lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii be ko ni eho lɛ he lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are specially bred by scientists to resist modern pests, tolerate erratic weather, and produce higher yields, though they often require different spacing and care than traditional seeds.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi efɔ tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni bɛ shiŋŋ ni ehaa yibii babaoo Eyɛ mli akɛ bei pii lɛ amɛbiɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto kɛ amɛkwɛmɔ fe blema dumɔwui lɛ moŋ.

english: How can I tell if a new crop variety will mature quickly or take a long time before harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso henɔ hee ko baakwɛ̃ oya loo ebaahe be babaoo dani akpa?

english: Fast-maturing varieties are usually bred with shorter life cycles (often 60 to 90 days) so farmers can harvest before dry spells start, whereas long-duration varieties take more time to build strong root systems for higher total yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ tsei srɔtoi ni daa oya ni amɛwala be kukuoo (bei pii lɛ gbii 60 kɛyashi 90) bɔni afee ni okwaafoi lɛ anyɛ akpa nii dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛtoɔ shishifãi ni mli wa koni amɛná yibii fɛɛ ni fa babaoo.

english: Why does my farmland show dark and light layers of dirt when I dig ridges for my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse beni mifoɔ ŋmeii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ?

english: The dark top layer is soil rich in decayed leaves and nutrients, while the lighter layer underneath is subsoil with fewer nutrients; mounding them properly keeps the fertile dark layer near the crop roots.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ediŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni baai ni fiteɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli. yɛ be mli ni shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ shishi ni niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo, ediŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why does a white crust form on top of my dry soil after I apply fertilizer near my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ baa mishikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A white crust forms when chemical fertilizer stays on top of dry soil instead of dissolving, which can burn plant roots; always cover fertilizer with soil or apply it when the ground is moist.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ yɛŋ baa kɛji tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ta shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefo. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi ashã. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛwo nɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ.

english: What causes white spots and brown edges to appear on my pepper leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii yɛŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ?

english: This is usually caused by fungal or bacterial diseases that thrive when the leaves stay wet for too long or when plants are crowded together without good airflow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal loo bacteria hela ni daa kɛji baai lɛ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. aloo kɛ́ tsei ebɔle amɛhe ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots turn brown and discolored inside if I leave them out for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmli su tsakeɔ kɛji mishi amɛ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots spoil quickly after harvest due to a natural process called post-harvest physiological deterioration, so they must be processed or eaten within two to three days.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ fitemɔ hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ atsu he nii loo aye yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli.

english: Is it better for me to plant my maize seeds close together or leave wide spaces between them?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe loo mashi gbɛ ni da yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ?

english: Planting too close makes crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and small ears; proper spacing gives each plant enough food to produce full grains.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ toi bibii. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Why do some of my tomato plants produce flowers very quickly while others just keep growing taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ekomɛi fɔɔ oya waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi yaa nɔ amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Determinate tomato plants stop growing tall early and produce all their fruit quickly at once, while indeterminate types keep growing taller and produce fruit slowly over a longer season.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni tomato tsei lɛ akpa dalɛ oya ni amɛwo yibii shikome. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tomato ni bɛ shishitoo lɛ daa ni ewoɔ yibii fiofio. Yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli

english: How do I know when my homemade compost pile is fully ready to put on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mishia ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Ready compost looks like a dark brown, crumbly layer of earth, smells like fresh forest soil, and no longer feels hot when you dig into the center of the pile.
ga: Kompost ni asaa he lɛ baafee tamɔ sũ ni mli edɔ, ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehe ŋmɔlɔ tamɔ koo mli shikpɔŋ hee. Ni enuuu he akɛ edɔ dɔŋŋ kɛ́ okɛ ohe wo ŋtayaa lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Why are my crops flowering earlier than usual this season even though the heavy rains have not started?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifɔlɔ mra fe bɔ ni afeɔ daa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ? Ni nugbɔ ejeko shishi enɛ waa lolo?

english: When crops experience unexpected dry spells or heat stress, they often flower early as a survival reaction to produce seeds quickly before the plant dries up.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulutsoo be ni akpaaa gbɛ loo dɔlɛ mli haomɔ kpe Amɛfɔɔ fɔfɔi feemɔ mra akɛ wala yibiiwoo he nifeemɔ koni amɛwo dumɔwui oya dani tso lɛ agbi.

english: Why do weeds keep coming back on my farm even after I clear them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ po lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can lie dormant in the soil for years. When you clear the field, sunlight and rain hit the soil, which triggers those hidden seeds to sprout and grow again.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ awɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo Kɛ́ ojie jɛmɛ Hulu kɛ nugbɔ lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa nakai dumɔwui ni aŋɔtee lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crops are starving for nitrogen, which is a key plant food, or that the ground has become too waterlogged for the roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri Aloo etsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under direct harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain next to them creates living umbrellas that give young cocoa the shade and cool soil it needs to grow.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛhaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ koni amɛná hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops each year if I plant the same crop every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi kɛji akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year. Rotating different crops gives the soil time to rest and rebuild its natural food supply.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛmaa e-adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my seeds very close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants end up fighting each other for light, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and small yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do the stems of my vegetable plants rot during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai tsei ashishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When too much water settles around plant roots without draining away, it suffocates the roots and encourages soil diseases that make the stems soft and rotten.
ga: Kɛ nu babaoo kpɛtɛ tso shishifãi ahe ni efooo Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why are there small holes all over the leaves of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Mi pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Holes in leaves are usually caused by pests like beetles or caterpillars eating the plant. Checking under the leaves regularly helps you spot these pests early before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu baa baa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra. dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of essential nutrients needed to hold the fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛkpa aduawai lɛ ni bɛ

english: Cassava needs loose, well-draining soil so its tubers can expand easily underground. If your land is hard clay that traps water, the roots will struggle to swell and may rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni mli tse he miihia cassava bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni hiɛɔ nu lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baafuu ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi.

english: Why are my garden eggs staying small and refusing to grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji bibii ni amɛkpooɔ ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Stunted growth happens when weeds steal water and nutrients from your plants, or when tiny pests under the soil damage the roots so they cannot feed the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni baa ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ ju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ Shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛha tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do I need to raise my crop seedlings in black plastic bags before moving them to my main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ tsei ahe dumɔwui yɛ plastic kotokui diji amli dani mikɛ amɛ awo miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Raising seedlings in plastic bags protects tender young plants from pests, weeds, and harsh weather. It lets their roots develop strongly in rich soil so they have a much higher chance of surviving when transplanted to your farm.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ plastic kotokui amli lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai, jwɛi kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi gbohii ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛshishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛyɛ hegbɛ babaoo kwraa akɛ amɛbaahi shi kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛtee oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: What is the difference between a single-stage nursery and a two-stage nursery for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kome kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta enyɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: A single-stage nursery grows seeds in one container until they are ready for the field. A two-stage nursery starts seeds in small germination beds or tiny bags first, then moves the best seedlings into larger black tubes for extra growing time before final planting.
ga: Nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ lɛ duɔ dumɔwui yɛ tsɛnsi kome mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha dumɔwui. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui amli ni yɔɔ gbɛi enyɔ nɔ lɛ jeɔ dumɔwui ashishi yɛ dumɔwui bibii loo kotokui amli klɛŋklɛŋ, no sɛɛ lɛ amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ amli amɛwoɔ tsɔnei wuji diji amli koni eha amɛ be babaoo ni amɛdara dani amɛdu naagbee.

english: Why are long, narrow black plastic tubes used for growing tree seedlings instead of short, wide containers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ plastic jwɛi kakadaji, ni mli tse, ni ji ediŋŋ atsu nii kɛdu dumɔwui yɛ tsɛnsii kukuji ni mli kwɔ lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Long, narrow black tubes encourage taproots to grow straight down into the soil. Deep, straight roots help young trees anchor firmly into the ground and reach water deep underground during dry seasons.
ga: Tubu diŋ kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ haa taproot lɛ daa tɛ̃ɛ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso bibioo lɛ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ maa shi shiŋŋ ni eshɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: What kind of soil should I put inside the plastic nursery bags for my young plants?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ esa akɛ mikɛwo plastic ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli kɛha mi dumɔwui lɛ?

english: You should fill nursery bags with dark, fertile topsoil collected from under thick bushes, mixed with well-rotted animal manure or compost. This soil stays moist, drains well, and gives young roots essential food.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni mli edɔ ni abua naa kɛjɛ jwɛi ni mli tse mli lɛ afata he. kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii atoohe lɛ mli Okɛ kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ afutu mli. Shikpɔŋ nɛɛ baakã he afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa shishifãi bibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ

english: Why do my plastic seedling bags need holes punched at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plastic dumɔwui kotokui lɛ amli lɛ, afo bu yɛ amɛshishi lɛ?

english: Holes allow excess water to escape after rain or watering. Without drainage holes, water gets trapped, rotting the seedling's roots and causing the plant to turn yellow and die.
ga: Buu lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ loo nu ni awoɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ nu homɔ bu bɛ lɛ, nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ, ni no haa dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. ni ehaa tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ.

english: Why do my crop seedlings grow much faster in a nursery than when I plant seeds directly in the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ daa oya yɛ ŋmɔ mli fe be mli ni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ jwɛi lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: In a nursery, seedlings receive controlled shade, regular water, rich soil, and protection from weeds and pests. Direct-seeded crops in the field must fight harsh direct sunlight, heavy weeds, and thirsty soil from day one.
ga: yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Dumɔwui lɛ baaná hulutsoo ni akudɔɔ, nu ni yaa nɔ daa, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ. kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe. Esa akɛ tsei ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akpee hulu ni naa wa, jwɛi ni eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ anaa kɛjɛ gbi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I remove the black plastic bag from around the seedling roots when planting in the main farm?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ, ani esa akɛ ajie plastic kotokui diji kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi amli?

english: Yes, you must carefully slice open and remove the plastic bag before planting. If left on, the bag traps the roots inside, preventing them from spreading into the field soil and eventually killing the plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ogbele plastic kotoku lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ojie dani okɛdu. Kɛji oshi lɛ Baagi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ shishifãi lɛ yɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni shishifãi lɛ akagbɛ amɛshwã sũ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni yɛ naagbee lɛ eha tso lɛ agbo.

english: What happens if I leave my crop seedlings in nursery bags for too long before planting them?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi mi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ grow bag lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani midu?

english: If left too long, roots fill the bag and start coiling tightly in circles. These twisted roots will never spread properly in the ground, making the adult plant weak, stunt-grown, and easily blown over by rainstorms.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baayi kotoku lɛ mli ni amɛje shishi amɛbɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee kooyigbɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɛkɛ shishifãi ni etsake nɛɛ gbɛŋ eshwaŋ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, amɛhe waaa, ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt or die if I take them straight from the nursery shade into full sunshine on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie amɛ kɛjɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni hulu lɛ fɛɛ aná amɛ?

english: Seedlings raised under nursery shade develop soft, tender leaves. Moving them suddenly into harsh sunlight causes sun-shock; they need to be gradually exposed to direct sun over a week or two to harden up before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaná baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ trukaa kɛtee hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa. Esa akɛ amɛfee fiofio ni Akɛ amɛ awo hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ otsi kome loo enyɔ koni amɛhe wa dani adu.

english: How can I tell if a crop seedling in a nursery bag is healthy enough to survive in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A healthy seedling has a firm woody stem, vibrant green leaves free of insect damage, and strong white roots holding the soil tightly together without bursting through the bottom of the bag.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ tsei ni mli tse, ni tamɔ tsei. Baai eŋɔli ni mli tse ni kooloi fiteee. Ni shishifãi yɛŋ ni he wa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ sũ lɛ shi shiŋŋ ni etseee kɛjɛɛɛ kotoku lɛ shishi.

english: Why are my green oranges dropping off the tree before they grow big or ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tangerine lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara loo amɛdara lɛ?

english: Fruit drop usually happens when the tree suffers from heat stress, lack of water, or attacks from insect pests. Supplying enough water during dry spells and keeping pests away helps the tree hold onto its fruit until harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso yibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni faaa yɛ emli, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ aduawai amli kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Why does my mango tree bloom with so many flowers but produce very few actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Strong winds, lack of water, or sap-sucking pests can cause flowers to drop before forming fruit. Protecting your farm with tree borders and managing pests during flowering helps turn those flowers into mangoes.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbɔjɔ dani aduawai aba. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ahe ŋmeii bu oŋmɔ lɛ he, ni okwɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nakai fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ mango.

english: How do I know when my plantain bunch is ready to be cut down?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni plantains kuu ko efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Plantain is ready to harvest when the individual fruits look plump and full, and the sharp ridges on their skin become soft and rounded. Cut the bunch while it is still green if you need to transport or sell it before it ripens.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewolo lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kpãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo kɛji oosumɔ ni okɛya loo ohɔ̃ɔ dani ekwɛ̃.

english: Is it safe to collect and sell fruit that has already fallen to the ground by itself?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaabua aduawai ni egbee shikpɔŋ lɛ anaa ni ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Fallen fruit often gets bruised or punctured, which allows insects and rot-causing germs from the soil to get inside quickly. It is better to harvest ripe fruit directly from the tree and sort fallen ones immediately so bad fruit doesn't ruin the rest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atswaa aduawai ni egbee shi lɛ loo atswaa amɛ. Enɛ haa kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni fiteɔ ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ mli oya. Esa akɛ akpa aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni ajie aduawai ni egbee shi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni akaye aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ awui.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava so that I can walk through the farm easily?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ tɛŋŋ koni efee mlɛo akɛ oootsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Plant cassava about 1 meter apart in straight lines. This gives the stems enough space for roots to spread into large tubers while leaving a clear path for you to weed and harvest without damaging the plants.
ga: Dumɔ ŋmei aaafee mita kome yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eshiɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kɛhaa bo ni obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii ni okpa ni ofiteee tsei lɛ.

english: Should I trim the branches of my cocoa trees so they do not grow too tall?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji koni amɛkakwɛ tsɔ?

english: Yes, trimming or pruning cocoa trees keeps them at a manageable height so you can easily reach pods to harvest them and spot pests early. It also allows sunlight and air to move through the farm, reducing diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, cacao tso lɛ ni afoɔ loo afoɔ lɛ baaha cacao tso lɛ aya nɔ ahi he ko ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oya pods lɛ amli kɛha nikpamɔ ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai mra. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hela baa shi

english: Why is it important for me to clear the weeds and fallen leaves beneath my fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie jwɛi kɛ baai ni egbee shi yɛ mi aduawai tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds around the base of your trees stops pests and snakes from hiding near your crops, prevents weeds from stealing fertilizer from the tree roots, and makes it easy to spot and collect your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ni ajieɔ Tsei shishitoo baaha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ onufui akatee amɛhe yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaju ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi amli. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ooona ni okpa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yellow leaves are a common sign that the soil is running low on nutrients, especially nitrogen. Applying animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer gives the maize the food it needs to stay green and form full cobs.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛ akɛ ŋmei, ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni efee ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Pepper leaves curl during intense heat to conserve moisture and protect themselves from burning. If the leaves unroll in the cool evening, the plant is fine; if they stay curled, it means your soil needs watering.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he. Kɛji baai lɛ shwie shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ Tso lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji amɛkoto Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Do my vegetable crops need direct sunlight all day, or do they grow better under shade?
ga: Mi aduawai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli. Aloo ebaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Most vegetables like tomatoes, peppers, and garden eggs need at least 6 hours of full sunlight each day to produce strong stems, healthy flowers, and plenty of fruit.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, ehe miihia ni aduawai babaoo, tamɔ tomato, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ aná hulutsoo ŋmɛlɛtswai 6 daa gbi koni amɛwo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. fɔfɔi ni mli wa kɛ aduawai babaoo

english: Officer, can I buy certified crop seeds in small quantities if I only have a small piece of land?
ga: NITSUMƆ Kɛji miyɛ shikpɔŋ fioo pɛ Ani manyɛ mahe dumɔwui bibii ni awo he odaseyeli?

english: Yes, seed companies and agricultural distributors sell certified seeds in small, affordable sachets meant for smallholder farmers. Buying certified seeds ensures high germination rates and protects your farm against seed-borne diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ahe nitsumɔhei kɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔi hɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ paketii bibii ni jara waaa amli amɛhaa okwaafoi bibii. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ baaha ekwɛ̃ babaoo ni ebaabu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa lɛ ahe.

english: If I save seeds from my harvested crops to plant next season, will they yield as well as fresh seeds from a company?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni mikpaa lɛ to koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, Ani nakai dumɔwui lɛ baawo yibii tamɔ dumɔwui heei ni jɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ?

english: Not always. Many improved crop varieties are hybrids, meaning seeds saved from the harvest will produce weaker plants with lower yields. Purchasing fresh, certified seeds each season guarantees strong plants and better harvests.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Tsei srɔtoi babaoo ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji tsofai ni akɛfee tsofai. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ baawo tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waa ni amɛkpaa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants turn light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-based fertilizer like Urea or adding well-decomposed manure will help the leaves regain their green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ aya hiɛ waa Kɛji akɛ akɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ urea tsu nii loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Flower drop occurs when plants experience environmental stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of essential soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying balanced fertilizer helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ kpe. aloo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do agricultural officers always advise us to leave measured space between crops instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔjie ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ he kroko moŋ fe ni wɔbaadu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing prevents plants from competing with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. It also improves airflow around the foliage, which significantly reduces the spread of fungal diseases.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tsei akaye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ hu yaa hiɛ, ni no haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Can I plant leguminous crops like cowpeas together with my maize on the same field?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, this practice is called intercropping. Legumes capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, which actually helps feed nearby crops like maize while maximizing your land use.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ intercropping. Legumes lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tamɔ ŋmãa niyenii yɛ be mli ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in high humidity and excess shade. Pruning unnecessary branches to let in sunlight and clearing weeds will improve airflow and reduce fungal growth.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ koni hulu la aba mli, ni ojie jwɛi lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aba shi.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops more during dry spells than during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Many pests, like spider mites and aphids, multiply rapidly in warm, dry weather because heat speeds up their life cycle. Additionally, dry conditions weaken crops, making them easier targets for insects.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni jɛmɛ egbi lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ haa amɛshihilɛ yaa oya. Kɛfata he lɛ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kooloi bibii.

english: Why does cassava take up to a year to harvest while vegetables are ready in just two months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei heɔ afi dani akpaa yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ ayeɔ yɛ nyɔji enyɔ pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Vegetables invest energy quickly into fast-growing leaves and fruits, whereas cassava is a root crop that stores energy gradually over many months to build large, starch-rich tubers underground.
ga: Aduawai kɛ hewalɛ woɔ baai kɛ aduawai ni daa oya lɛ amli oya. Yɛ be mli ni cassava ji tso ko ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni fiofio lɛ Ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ nyɔji babaoo koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni starch eyi mli obɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops wilt and dry out fast when I water them in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering under intense sunlight causes water to evaporate before reaching the roots, and hot sun can scorch wet leaves. It is best to water early in the morning or late in the afternoon so the soil retains moisture longer.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha baai ni efɔ lɛ ashã. Esa akɛ afee nu lɛ leebi loo shwane koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers, but most of them just drop off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ pods?

english: Flowers need to be pollinated—meaning pollen from one flower must reach another—to form pods. If there are not enough natural insects like midges around, or if hand pollination isn't done, the unpollinated flowers simply wither and fall off to save the tree's energy.
ga: Ehe miihia ni awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ pollen ni jɛɔ fɔfɔi kome mli lɛ ashɛ ekroko he dani pod lɛ afee. Kɛji akɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi bibii, tamɔ midges lɛ faaa, loo kɛji akɛ akɛ niji shwieee amɛ nɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni no haa tso lɛ hewalɛ hiɔ shi.

english: What is hand pollination, and how does it help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni ji nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Hand pollination is a practice where trained workers manually transfer pollen from male parts of flowers to female parts using small brushes or tweezers. It ensures that a higher percentage of flowers successfully turn into healthy fruits or pods, significantly increasing your total harvest.
ga: Nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ji nifeemɔ ko ni nitsulɔi ni atsɔse amɛ lɛ kɛ amɛdɛŋ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fã ni ji nuu lɛ mli kɛyaa yoo lɛ fã ni ji fɔfɔi lɛ mli kɛtsɔ brɔshi bibioo loo ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛfoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni fa fe oha mlijaa 100 lɛ yeɔ omanye ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ waa.

english: Why do some crops need insects like bees or midges to yield well while crops like maize do not?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ahe hiaa kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa wooo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Crops like cocoa, watermelons, and vegetables have sticky pollen or separate flower parts that rely on insects to move pollen around. Crops like maize have light pollen that the wind easily carries from the tassels at the top down to the silks.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo, watermelon, kɛ aduawai yɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi, loo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fãi ni mli egbala ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kooloi anɔ koni amɛtsi fɔfɔi lɛ kɛya he fɛɛ he. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa ŋmãa lɛ nɔ oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛyaa siliki lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are some trees in my farm yielding heavy fruits while trees right next to them stay bare?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ woɔ yibii lɛ? Ani oyɛ yaka lolo?

english: Trees differ in health, access to sunlight, soil nutrients, and pollination success. A tree might look healthy, but if its flowers were not pollinated or if its roots are struggling with a hidden disease, it will fail to produce fruit.
ga: Esoro tsei yɛ amɛhewalɛ mli. hulu la ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nine shɛɔ nɔ kɛ omanyeyeli yɛ pollination mli Tso lɛ baanyɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ eshishifãi lɛ kɛ hela ko ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ miiwu. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: What causes young cocoa pods to turn shriveled and black before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdaraa?

english: This can happen because of fungal infections like black pod disease, pest damage, or because the tree has more young pods than its water and soil nutrients can support, causing it to naturally discard some.
ga: Enɛ baanyɛ aba yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahewɔ. Aloo akɛni tso lɛ yibii lɛ darako tsɔ hewɔ lɛ, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua amɛ. Enɛ ha tsei komɛi je kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my crops flower heavily after the first rain, but stop flowering when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Shi ekpaa fɔfɔii lɛ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ?

english: Rain signals to the plant that water is available to support new life, triggering flower production. Extreme heat and dry weather cause water stress, making the plant drop flowers to protect itself from drying out.
ga: Nugbɔ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ akɛ nu yɛ ni baaha wala hee ahi shi. stimulate flower production Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa lɛ kɛ nu mli haomɔ baa. Ha fɔfɔi lɛ agbee shi koni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: If a government assistance program like artificial pollination pauses on my farm, will my trees stop bearing fruit entirely?
ga: Kɛji nɔyeli yelikɛbuamɔ nitsumɔi tamɔ fɔfɔii amli ŋmɔtɔ Pause on my farm Ani mi tso lɛ baakpa yibiiwoo kwraa?

english: No, your trees will still bear fruit naturally through wild insects and wind pollination. However, your yield may drop back to normal natural levels compared to the higher output achieved during intensive hand pollination.
ga: Dabi, otsei lɛ baaya nɔ awo yibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ koo mli kooloi bibii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, nɔ ni ofeɔ lɛ baanyɛ aba shi kɛya bɔ ni eji daa lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Akɛ enɛ toɔ yibii ni fa babaoo ni anáa kɛjɛɔ nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli waa lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why do agricultural extension officers sometimes ask farmers to temporarily hold off on certain farm practices?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ biɔ okwaafoi lɛ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔi komɛi ahe yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ?

english: Officers may pause activities to evaluate crop health, update techniques, resolve supply issues, or prevent the spread of diseases across neighboring farms when unexpected weather or plant conditions occur.
ga: Amralofoi baanyɛ akpa nifeemɔi koni amɛkwɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ ha. improve technique Tsu nibii ahe naagbai ahe nii loo tsi hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ naa kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaaa gbɛ ba.

english: How can I tell if my farm has enough natural insects to pollinate my crops on their own?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ mli kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Look at the ratio of flowers to developing fruits. If your trees are full of open blossoms during the season but very few small pods or fruits start setting, your farm likely lacks sufficient natural pollinators.
ga: Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai yaa hiɛ ehaa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ otsei lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ fɔfɔii yɛ be lɛ mli shi amɛmiibɔi ŋmeii bibii loo aduawai kpojiemɔ lɛ, no lɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli adebɔɔ mli fɔfɔii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ.

english: How does clearing weeds around the base of my tree crops affect how they flower and carry fruit?
ga: Te jwɛi ni bɔleɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ saa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, nutrients, and water from the soil that your trees need to form flowers and nourish growing pods. Keeping the base clear ensures all soil nutrients go directly into boosting your crop's yield.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, niyenii, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛha amɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ oha shishitoo lɛ mli tse lɛ, niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayibii yaa hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How often am I supposed to spray medicine on my crops to keep them healthy?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Spraying schedules depend on the specific treatment and crop needs. Some crop medicines need to be applied every week, while others work best when applied every two weeks to effectively protect your farm.
ga: Be ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ damɔ tsofafeemɔ pɔtɛɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hiamɔ nii anɔ. Ehe miihia ni akɛ tsei ahe tsofai komɛi awo mli daa otsi. Yɛ be mli ni ekomɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ akɛtsu nii daa otsii enyɔ koni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do some farm medicines require spraying every week while others say every two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afɔ ŋmɔ mli tsofai komɛi anɔ daa otsi lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mɛi komɛi kɛɔ akɛ daa otsii enyɔ?

english: Different crop medicines have different strengths and protection periods. Following the recommended weekly or two-week interval ensures the medicine remains active enough to prevent pests and support plant growth.
ga: Tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ yɛ hewalɛ kɛ be ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he lɛ srɔtoi. Beni ajie lɛ kpo daa otsi loo enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ Tsofa lɛ baatsu nii lolo bɔ ni sa ni ebaashwie kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni eye ebua tsei lɛ adalɛ.

english: How can I tell if the crop medicine I sprayed on my farm is actually working?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsu nii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You will know the medicine is working when your plant flowers remain healthy without wilting, your young fruits grow larger without dropping, and pests are unable to stay on the crop.
ga: Obaale akɛ tsofa lɛ miitsu nii kɛ́ otso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ tee nɔ ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ni egbooo. Oyibii bibii lɛ daa ni amɛgbeeee shi. Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛŋ ahi ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why do the flowers on my crop wither and dry up before forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers often wilt and dry up due to pest attacks or diseases. Applying the correct crop treatment protects the flowers from damage, allowing them to successfully turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ahewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaabu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ he. ni eha fɔfɔi lɛ afee aduawai yɛ omanyeyeli mli

english: What steps can I take to make my crops produce a very large harvest?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii babaoo?

english: Regularly applying the right crop protection medicine keeps the flowers intact and healthy, which allows the plant to produce and support fruit in high abundance.
ga: Tsofai ni sa ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ayi obɔ kɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei woɔ yibii babaoo ni amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa amɛ.

english: What can I do to ensure my young fruits stay on the plant and grow big?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni miyibii bibii lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdara?

english: Protecting your crops with timely chemical treatments prevents early damage, giving young fruits the strength and protection needed to grow to full size.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ bu onibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite mra. Enɛ haa aduawai bibii lɛ hewalɛ kɛ hebuu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara kɛyashɛ amɛdalɛ he.

english: At what stage of growth are my fruits most vulnerable to pest attacks?
ga: Mɛɛ dalɛ mli mi aduawai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai fe fɛɛ?

english: Fruits are most vulnerable when they are small and newly formed. Pests like stone weevils target these young fruits early in their development.
ga: Yibii lɛ waaa kwraa kɛ́ amɛji bibii ni amɛfee ehee. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ tɛ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ nɛkɛ aduawai bibii nɛɛ anɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli.

english: What damage do stone weevils cause to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ fitemɔ tɛ ŋmei kɛbaa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Stone weevils target and attack fruits when they are still small, which can stunt their growth or cause them to drop if the crop is not protected.
ga: Tɛ ŋmeii lɛ kwɛɔ aduawai anɔ ni amɛtutuaa amɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha amɛdalɛ afee mlɛo loo eha amɛgbee shi kɛji abuuu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: How does spraying crop medicine protect my small fruits from stone weevils?
ga: Tsei ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ aduawai bibii ahe. Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná minɔ lɛ kɛjɛ tɛ ŋmei mli?

english: When you apply the proper treatment, it creates an environment where stone weevils cannot survive or stay on the young fruits, stopping them from destroying your crop.
ga: Kɛ okɛ tsofafeemɔ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ Ehaa shihilɛ ko baa ni tɛ ŋmeii nyɛŋ ahi shi loo amɛhi shi yɛ aduawai bibii anɔ. ni otsĩ amɛnaa koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Should I spray my crops regularly even before I notice heavy pest damage?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ nu daa dani mana akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai efite amɛ waa?

english: Yes, applying crop medicine on a consistent weekly or two-week schedule prevents pests like stone weevils from settling on your farm and stops flower loss before damage occurs.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ tsu nii daa otsi loo otsii enyɔ mli lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ tɛ ŋmei lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ebaaha fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ akpa dani nɔ ko aba.

english: What is a greenhouse, and how can it help my crops grow better than planting directly in the open field?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: A greenhouse is a shelter covered with clear plastic or net that protects crops from harsh heat, heavy rain, and pests, allowing plants to grow faster and yield better produce all year round.
ga: Greenhouse ji he ko ni akɛ plastic loo ŋshɔŋlooi ni mli tse ehà nɔ ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ awui ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why is it better to start seeds in a nursery before moving them to my main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui akwɛmɔ yɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe dani mikɛ amɛ aya miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A nursery gives tender seeds a safe, protected environment to grow strong roots and leaves before facing the harsher weather, pests, and weed competition on the main field.
ga: He ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ lɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ náa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni abuɔ he. Enɛ ji koni akɛwaje shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ dani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ jwɛi akaŋshii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ aba.

english: How do I choose good planting materials so that my crops don't fail after planting?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ahala dumɔ nii kpakpai koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbee shi yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ?

english: Good planting materials—such as seeds or suckers—should be clean, free from holes or spots, bought from reliable sources, and suited to the weather and soil conditions in your area.
ga: Esa akɛ nibii ni hi ni akɛduɔ nii, tamɔ dumɔwui loo ŋmeii lɛ ahe atse ni bu loo ŋmeii akafee nɔ ko. Hemɔ kɛjɛ hei ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young seedlings wither and die when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young plants have shallow roots and delicate leaves that lose water very quickly in full sunlight, so they need temporary shade and moisture until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nu fiteɔ oya kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ be kukuoo ko kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: Can my crops grow well and produce good yield if I stop using chemical fertilizers?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛji mikpa tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ?

english: Yes, using natural compost, animal manure, and decaying plant matter feeds the soil slowly, building long-term fertility and helping your crops grow strong without damaging the land.
ga: Hɛɛ, adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi ashishifãi, kɛ tsei ni fiteɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ fiofio. Bɔɔ nibii babaoo ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni oye obua oŋmɔshi nibii ni okwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni okpataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ.

english: How long does it take for worn-out soil to become fertile again using natural methods?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ atsɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛi anɔ atsu nii ekoŋŋ?

english: Improving soil naturally is a gradual process that usually takes one to two planting seasons of adding compost, planting cover crops, and avoiding land burning.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔyaa ji nɔ ko ni yaa nɔ fiofio. Eheɔ be kome kɛyashi enyɔ dani anyɛɔ akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ adumɔ ni ajie shikpɔŋ ni ashãa lɛ kɛjɛ mli

english: Why do people spread dry grass and leaves around the base of their crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai amɛshwieɔ amɛtsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so you water less, and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Locks in moisture bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it important to leave proper space between my crops instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ ni sa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each crop gets enough sunlight, airflow, soil nutrients, and water without competing with neighboring plants, which leads to bigger and healthier harvests.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. kɔɔyɔɔ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ Enɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ ni da ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant the exact same crop on the same land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests and diseases that attack that specific plant to multiply in the soil over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha niyenii mli nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ajɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi kɛ helai ni tutuaa nakai tso lɛ koni amɛshwere yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Rainy weather encourages soft, fast plant growth, which provides abundant food for insects, while warm and humid air creates ideal conditions for pests to hatch and spread quickly.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛhiɔ shi blɛoo. ni ji niyenii ni fa babaoo kɛha kooloi bibii Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni kooloi bibii lɛ afɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya.

english: Why are small worms eating up my young maize leaves right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mibi lɛ ŋmeii baai beni nugbɔ enɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms that hatch quickly when warm dry spells are followed by rain. They hide inside the central leaves of young maize plants to feed, but checking your field early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract can stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye niyenii. Shi ŋmɔ lɛ mli he ni akwɛɔ mra Ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ ni ajieɔ yi lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ amɛnaa dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong direct sunlight or harsh heat. Leaving taller shade trees or planting temporary crops like plantain creates a cool, moist environment that protects tender cocoa plants until they grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu tsei ni yɔɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaha shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ aba. Enɛ buɔ cacao tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer during the early growing stage helps keep leaves healthy and green so the plant can produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. koni tsei lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmeii wuji

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start rotting quickly when I store them in my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot easily if kept in warm places without air circulation or if bruised during harvest. Storing them off the ground on raised bamboo racks inside a cool, well-ventilated yam barn prevents moisture build-up and decay.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulu tsoɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli loo kɛji akɛ egbo yɛ kpamɔ be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ to shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmeii atoohe ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akabɔle amɛhe ni amɛfite.

english: What causes my cassava leaves to curl up with yellow patches and yield tiny tubers?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhaa yitsei bibii?

english: This is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. Using disease-free, improved cassava cuttings stops the disease and allows tubers to grow large and full.
ga: Kasava mosaic hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ Kɛ ŋmeii shishifãi ni atsake ni hela bɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii Ebaaye ebua ni akpa hela lɛ ni eye ebua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛdara.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my tomato seeds very close together in the bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to fight for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in weak stems and small fruit. Proper spacing allows air to flow through, which prevents damp diseases and improves fruit size.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ awuu kɛha hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ helai ni mli edɔ naa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ daraa.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off during the hot dry season without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ mli ni efeee pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: High heat combined with dry soil stresses pepper plants, causing them to drop flowers to save water and survive. Covering the soil around plants with dry grass (mulching) keeps the roots cool and retains water to help fruit form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi fataa he lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛhere nu ni amɛhi shi. Mulching around Kɛ akɛ jwɛi (mulch) ha tsei ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi koni eye ebua ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly on my farm even after I clear them with my cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miikwɛ̃ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛ mikɛ dade jie lɛ po?

english: Weeds produce underground roots and seeds that sprout as soon as sunlight touches the bare soil. Covering bare ground with dry grass or growing cover crops like cowpeas shades out weed seeds so they cannot sprout.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi kɛ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji hulu la lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ pɛ. Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii aha hei ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ ahe koni jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into food inside the soil. This naturally enriches the soil for surrounding crops like maize while providing you with an extra harvest.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle he lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ be mli ni eyeɔ ebua bo hu ni ohaa onibii babaoo yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do certified seeds from agricultural officers produce more yield than the seeds I save from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni Okwaafoi anitsumɔ he nitsulɔ lɛ wo he odase lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can carry hidden diseases and lose vigor over time. Certified seeds are specially bred to resist local pests, tolerate dry weather, and produce higher, uniform yields under local Ghanaian growing conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni amɛhewalɛ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi ni ehaa yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ shihilɛi amli yɛ Ghana.

english: Why should I learn to save seeds from my best maize plants instead of buying new imported seeds every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makase bɔ ni afeɔ ahereɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ mi-abele tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛjɛ maŋsɛɛ aba daa afi lɛ

english: Saving seeds from your healthiest local plants ensures you remain self-reliant, saving money while growing crops that are already naturally adapted to Ghana's specific soil and weather conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui ni jɛ omaŋ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ ni oookɛto lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni oya nɔ okwɛ ohe. Kɛ shika ato be mli ni oduɔ tsei ni kɛ Ghana shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ kpãa gbee yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow better when I plant cowpeas in between the rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas act like natural fertilizer factories by pulling nitrogen from the air and storing it in the soil, which feeds the cassava and keeps your land fertile without extra cost.
ga: Cowpeas tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔhe kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. ni kwɛɔ ŋmei ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shika kroko fataaa he.

english: Why do insect pests attack my vegetables less when I plant strong-smelling herbs around my farm boundaries?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fioo pɛ tutuaa mi-aduawai lɛ beni miduɔ tsofai ni he yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ waa yɛ amɛhe lɛ? miŋmɔ lɛ naa

english: Strong-smelling plants confuse hungry insects by masking the scent of your main crops, creating a natural protective shield around your farm.
ga: Tsei ni he yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ waa lɛ futuɔ koolooi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ kɛtsɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhaa amɛfeɔ lɛ nɔ. Efeɔ adebɔɔ mli gãimlibii ni bɔleɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants act like delicate babies that burn easily under full sunlight; they require the cool shade of larger trees to protect their leaves and retain soil moisture until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii feɔ amɛnii tamɔ abifabii ni he waaa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni eda lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ ni mli ejɔ he miihia amɛ koni amɛbu amɛbaai lɛ ahe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up into tight tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a plant's natural defense mechanism to protect itself from heat, reducing the amount of water that escapes through its leaves during the hottest hours.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do local Ghanaian yam varieties survive heavy rains better than foreign crop varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Ghana ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ gbɛ jogbaŋŋ fe maŋsɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Local crop varieties have adapted over generations to withstand Ghana's specific climate patterns, making their root systems stronger against sudden flooded soils.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ etsake amɛhe yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu afua ni tswaa lɛ tswaa lɛ he.

english: Why does my land yield fewer plantains if I keep planting them on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dumɔwui fioo pɛ baa kɛji midu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the ground over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my pepper plants with dry bush foliage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi aha he ni agbele ni bɔle mi-pepper tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material acts like a blanket that traps moisture, suppresses weeds, and slowly turns into natural food for your crops as it breaks down.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ tsei ni egbi woɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa ni fiofio lɛ ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii beni amɛfiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants give me very small fruits when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei woɔ yibii bibii waa lɛ? Adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots and leaves compete fiercely with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients, leaving the plant with less energy to produce big fruits.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaawo yibii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground if I leave them in the soil too long after they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once a crop reaches full maturity, its natural defenses drop, making the tubers vulnerable to soil dampness and fungal infections if left unharvested.
