ga: Kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa bulb lɛ woɔ oshara mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni akpaaa amɛ.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for planting coconut trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmei tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: Coconut trees grow best on flat or gently sloping land that receives plenty of direct sunlight and is free from overcrowded tall trees that block light.
ga: Kokoo tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo hei ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ. Ni tsei kakadaji komɛi bɛ jɛmɛ ni amɛtsiɔ la lɛ naa.

english: Does it make a difference if my farm land is flat instead of hilly for growing crops?
ga: Ani ebaaha srɔtofeemɔ aba kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ji ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe gɔŋji ni akɛduɔ nii?

english: Flat land is ideal because it holds rainwater and soil nutrients better, reduces erosion, and makes field work and clearing much easier.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ sũ mli niyenii kpakpai amli jogbaŋŋ, ehaa shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do coconut palms need an open area without large trees surrounding them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei he hiaa hei ni tsei wuji ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Coconut palms require maximum sunlight and wide root space to gather nutrients and energy needed to produce heavy nuts without competing with neighboring trees.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛ shishifãi babaoo he miihia ŋmei tsei koni amɛbua niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛná ŋmei ni tsii ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ akaŋ akaŋ.

english: Why must I clear all the weeds and heavy bush before putting my crops in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Fɛɛ dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Clearing the land removes weeds that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, giving your young crops the best environment to establish strong roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ jwɛi ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ha otsei bibii lɛ shihilɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: How clean or clear should my field be before I start planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ he atse loo ehe atse tɛŋŋ dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: Your field should be cleared of heavy brush, tall grass, and major debris so that sunlight directly hits the soil and you can easily walk around to care for your seedlings.
ga: Esa akɛ tsei bibii, jwɛi kakadaŋŋ agboi, kɛ jwɛi wuji akafee oyale lɛ mli koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. ni obaanyɛ onyiɛ kɛbɔle Koni okwɛ dumɔwui anɔ mlɛo

english: How does thorough land preparation help my crops get enough energy to grow strong?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni misaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara waa?

english: Preparing land properly loosens the soil, allowing crop roots to easily spread out, absorb water, and draw essential nutrients for healthy growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa mlɛo, amɛmɔɔ nu, ni amɛjieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ kpakpa.

english: How can I check the soil on my farm to see if it is healthy for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni mana kɛji ehi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: You can check soil quality by examining its texture, color, and depth, and by testing how well it holds moisture without becoming waterlogged.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ hi ha kɛtsɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ, bɔ ni eyɔɔ su, kɛ bɔ ni emli kwɔ ha lɛ nɔ, kɛ bɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli lɛ kaa nɔ.

english: What type of soil do coconut trees need to produce lots of fruit?
ga: Mɛɛ sũ nɛkɛ ŋmei tso he hiaa koni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Coconut trees thrive best in well-draining, deep sandy or loamy soil that allows their fibrous roots to breathe and absorb moisture easily.
ga: Kokoo tsei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã loo ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ fiber lɛ muɔ ni amɛheɔ ŋmɔtɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do crops grow very well in one section of my farm but look weak in another section?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome shi etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ fã kroko lɛ?

english: Soil depth, moisture retention, and nutrient levels vary across a farm, which directly affects how much food and water crop roots can find in different spots.
ga: shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ Fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ mli Kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. Enɛ saa niyenii kɛ nu mli tsei ashishifãi ni abaanyɛ ana yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ ayibɔ he tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What happens to young crops if I plant them in soil that has too many thick roots and weeds left in it?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ ni jwɛi babaoo eshwɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Old roots and dense weeds choke young plants underground, blocking root expansion and depriving the new crop of critical water and soil nutrients.
ga: Shishifãi momo kɛ jwɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa tsei bibii hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ naa Ni ehaa nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei amli.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over and snap whenever a strong wind blows across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Strong winds push against tall crops with shallow roots, causing them to bend or break. Planting tall tree barriers along your field edges acts as a windbreak, slowing down harsh wind currents and keeping your crops upright.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa tsei kakadaji ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ he eko. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi loo efoɔ. Tsei kakadaji ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baatsu nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii damɔɔ shi jaŋŋ

english: Why do my plantain leaves tear into thin strips during dry and windy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi bibii yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves are large and act like sails in the wind. They split naturally along their veins to let air pass through without snapping the whole plant stem, though protecting them with tree shelterbelts helps them stay whole and produce better fruit.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ dara ni amɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋshɔ hiɛ lɛlɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Amɛjaraa amɛhe yɛ fãji lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni amɛkuuu tso lɛ shishi. Shi kɛ́ okɛ tso he tsɔne ni akɛbuɔ amɛhe lɛ bu amɛhe lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers drop off without making fruit during hot, windy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ?

english: Dry winds pull moisture out of the plant and dry up flower pollen. When a crop is stressed by harsh winds, it sheds its flowers to conserve water and survive rather than spending energy growing peppers.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ mli egbiɔ. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miigba ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why do young crop seedlings die so quickly in open fields compared to mature plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bibii gboiɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔji amli kɛ akɛto tsei ni eda lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have small, shallow roots that cannot pull up water fast enough when hot winds dry out their stems. They need temporary shade or wind barriers to protect them until their root systems grow strong.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni mli ekɔɔɔ. No nyɛŋ agbala nu oya bɔ ni sa beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ lɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko loo kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni baabu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ amli baawa.

english: Why do the edges of my crop leaves dry up and turn brown when I farm close to the sea?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mifee okwaayeli yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ?

english: Breezes coming off the ocean carry invisible sea salt particles that settle on crop leaves and draw out moisture, scorching the edges. Planting salt-tolerant crops or living tree fences near the coast blocks this salty spray.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋshɔ mli ŋmei bibii ni anaaa ni kpɛtɛɔ tsei ahe baai ahe ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. charred edges Tsei ni nyɛɔ ŋmei loo ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ ni aaadu lɛ baatsi ŋmei nu mli ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Will using ground water near the ocean harm my vegetable crops?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ ni mikɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye mi-aduawai lɛ awui?

english: Underground water close to the sea often contains high salt levels. Salty water prevents crop roots from absorbing water properly, making the plants look wilted and weak even when the soil is wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ŋmei fa babaoo. Nu ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ tsei shishifãi anaa koni amɛkaná nu jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo ni egbɔjɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why does the dark topsoil on my newly cleared farm blow away in the wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ miitswa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ hee ni ajie lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Clearing trees and grass leaves the light, fertile topsoil exposed directly to wind currents. Planting cover crops or leaving plant mulch on the ground holds the soil in place so wind cannot sweep away valuable nutrients.
ga: Tsei kɛ jwɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ mlɛo ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ tsɔɔ jɛmɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akajie niyenii ni jara wa lɛ kɛya.

english: How do tiny insect pests travel into my farm so quickly to attack my vegetables?
ga: ŋmeii bibii Te fee tɛŋŋ ni ebote miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya koni ebatutua mi-aduawai lɛ?

english: Many small insects are carried into fields on wind currents or travel along cleared farm footpaths. Planting thick hedges around your farm acts as a physical net that stops pests from blowing directly onto your crops.
ga: Akɛ kooloi bibii babaoo yaa ŋmɔji amli kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ loo amɛfãa gbɛ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ mli naneshi gbɛjegbɛi ni ajie lɛ anɔ. Tsoi bibii ni mli tse ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋshɔŋloo ni akɛbaamɔ kooloi ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow much better when planted near shelter trees rather than out in the open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ adu yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ ahe moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Shelter trees create a calm environment by blocking harsh winds and excessive heat. This protected area keeps moisture in the air and soil, preventing crop stress and allowing plants to focus energy on yields.
ga: Tsei ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ kpoo kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine ni amɛtsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. He ni abuɔ he nɛɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Tsi tsei ahe haomɔ naa ni eye ebua tsei ni amɛkɛ amɛ hewalɛ ama nibii afeemɔ nɔ.

english: How does constant strong wind lower the overall harvest yield of my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni yaa nɔ lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni miduɔ lɛ aba shi?

english: When plants are continuously shaken by wind, they close their leaf pores to save water, which stops them from taking in air to grow. The crop spends its energy defending itself against wind stress instead of growing big fruits.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ miitswa tsei be fɛɛ be lɛ Tsei lɛ ŋaa amɛbaai lɛ amli buji lɛ koni amɛbu nu he. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ nyɛŋ amu kɔɔyɔɔ koni eda. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli haomɔ he moŋ fe ni amɛaadu aduawai wuji.

english: How can I tell if my newly sprouted crop seedlings are healthy or sick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ loo hela mɔ amɛ?

english: Healthy seedlings have firm, upright stems and deep green leaves. If you notice wilting, yellowing leaves, or dark spots soon after sprouting, it usually means the young plant has a fungal infection, pest damage, or poor soil moisture.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ tsei ni ja kɛ baai eŋɔli ni tsuɔ. Kɛji ona akɛ tso lɛ mli egbo, baai lɛ efee ŋmɔŋ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni eje kpo lɛ Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso bibioo lɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Akpãtãa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahiɛ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ jogbaŋŋ

english: How do I know if my pawpaw plants are male or female, and will all of them give me fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi papaya tso lɛ ji nuu loo yoo? Ni ani tso fɛɛ tso baawo yibii eha mi?

english: Male pawpaw plants produce long branches with many small flowers that do not bear fruit, while female plants have larger flowers close to the main trunk that develop into fruits. You need a few male plants nearby so insects can pollinate the female trees.
ga: Pawpaw tsei hii lɛ woɔ niji kakadaji ni fɔfɔi bibii yɔɔ mli. babaoo ni wooo yibii yɛ be mli ni tsei yei yɛ fɔfɔii wuji ni bɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri ni baatsɔ yibii lɛ. Esa akɛ oná tsei hii fioo komɛi ni bɛŋkɛ bo. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni kooloi bibii anyɛ afee tsei yei lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the cocoa pods I harvested this season so small and light in weight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni mikpaa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Light and small pods happen when the cocoa tree does not get enough water during the pod-growing stage, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients. Pests feeding on the stem can also restrict the flow of food to the developing pod.
ga: Pod bibii kɛ bibii baa kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ pod lɛ dalɛ be mli. aloo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ hu baanyɛ atsĩ niyenii ni hoɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why are some of the pods turning black and rotting while still attached to my tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ mitso lɛ he lolo lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy and humid weather. Removing affected pods immediately prevents the disease from spreading to healthy pods on the same tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ oya lɛ, ebaatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tso kome nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: If my main plantain tree is sick, will the young shoots growing around it also get sick?
ga: Kɛji midumɔwu titri lɛ hela mɔ lɛ Tsobii bibii ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani mi hu hela baamɔ mi?

english: Yes, many crop diseases and pests transfer directly from the parent plant to its young shoots through the underground root system. It is best to take shoots only from healthy mother plants for new plantings.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo jɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooŋɔ ŋmeii kɛjɛ nyɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli pɛ kɛha dumɔwui heei.

english: How can I check if the seeds I saved from my last harvest are good for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ hi kɛha dumɔ?

english: Place a sample of your seeds in a bowl of water. Healthy seeds that will sprout usually sink to the bottom, while dead, empty, or insect-damaged seeds will float to the top.
ga: Okɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ awo nu tsɛnsi mli. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛyaa shishi. Dumɔwui ni egboi, ni nɔ ko bɛ mli, loo ni kooloi efite lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: Why does my pepper plant produce many flowers, but most of them drop off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Flowers fall off when plants suffer from water stress, extreme heat, or a lack of insect pollinators. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting flowers nearby to attract pollinators helps fruit formation.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ nu mli haomɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nɔ ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ bɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni odu fɔfɔii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings die shortly after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ ekomɛi gboiɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings can fail if they are taken from an old or diseased parent stem, planted upside down, or buried in soil that is too dry to trigger new leaf and root growth.
ga: Yucca tsei ni afo lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji akɛ ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni egbɔ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli, adu amɛ ŋwɛi, loo afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ ni haaa baai kɛ shishifãi heei akwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I sort my harvested maize to prevent bad grains from ruining the good ones?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majara mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ mli koni ŋmeii gbohii akafite abele kpakpai?

english: Spread the harvested maize on a clean surface, then separate grains showing mold, dark spots, or insect holes from clean grains. Store only completely dry, undamaged grains in sealed sacks to avoid spoilage.
ga: Okɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ashwã he ko ni he tse. No sɛɛ lɛ, gbálamɔ dumɔwui ni mli eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ diji, loo kooloi bibii amli kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni he tse lɛ amli. Kɛ ŋmaa ni egbi kwraa ni efiteee lɛ pɛ ato kotokui ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli koni ekafite.

english: What should I do for my crop trees after harvesting all the fruits so they stay healthy for next year?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee mitsei lɛ beni mikpa aduawai lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: After harvest, prune away dead or broken branches and apply organic manure or compost around the base of the tree. This gives the parent plant the strength to recover and produce strong fruits for the next season.
ga: kpamɔ sɛɛ Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ekumɔ lɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata tso lɛ shishi he. Enɛ haa tso ni nyɛ lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekɛtsaa ehe ni ewoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why are dark green leafy vegetables like kontomire said to be so good for human health?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ kontomire lɛ hi kɛha adesa hewalɛnamɔ lɛ?

english: Kontomire leaves contain powerful natural substances called antioxidants and rich vitamins that help build strong blood and boost the body's immune system to fight off sickness.
ga: Kontomire baai lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ antioxidants kɛ vitamini ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa lá ni yɔɔ hewalɛ feɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nibii ni gbeɔ helai lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during drought as a natural defense behavior to save water and stay alive; once the rains return, it sprouts fresh leaves and continues growing roots.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baa shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛdaraa.

english: People say eating orange-fleshed sweet potatoes helps children stay healthy, but how does the crop do that?
ga: Mɛi komɛi kɛɔ akɛ, kɛ́ aye ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ewo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa gbekɛbii. be healthy Shi te ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ nakai tɛŋŋ?

english: Orange sweet potatoes are naturally loaded with beta-carotene and antioxidants, which the human body converts into vitamin A to protect eyes and strengthen the immune system.
ga: Beta-carotene kɛ nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ji orange mli lɛ mli. Nɔ ni adesa gbɔmɔtso lɛ tsakeɔ efeɔ vitamin A koni ekɛbu hiŋmɛii ahe ni ewaje gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nii ni gbeɔ helai lɛ.

english: Why do some of our traditional local crop varieties suffer less from pests compared to new seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔ kusum mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni wɔkwɛɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ahe lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ amɛhe tsɔ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Traditional crops have built up natural defense chemicals over generations that make their leaves bitter or tough to insects, protecting the plant from pest damage.
ga: Kusum nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ebɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa amɛbaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔ loo amɛhe wa kɛha kooloi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why do my young maize plants bend towards the direction where the sun is brightest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛtee he ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize plants naturally bend toward light because sunlight triggers growth chemicals inside the stem, encouraging the plant to reach for the energy it needs to make food.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa la lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa ejaakɛ hulu la lɛ haa tsofai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ daa. Ekanyaa tsei koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛfee niyenii.

english: Why does mixing well-rotted animal manure into my soil make crop leaves look darker green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo ni mikɛfutuɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Manure feeds the crop essential nutrients like nitrogen, which helps the plant produce chlorophyll—the green material leaves use to absorb sunlight and build plant strength.
ga: Muji haa tsei niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ klorofil. Enɛ ji nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni baa lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛgbala hulu la lɛ ni ewo tso lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into tomatoes when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomatoi kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the plant, causing it to drop flowers as a survival choice to preserve water and energy until weather conditions become cooler.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do green pawpaws turn yellow and taste much sweeter as they mature on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pawpaws eŋɔlii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni amɛdaraa yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: As fruits mature, the tree converts bitter starches into natural sugars and fills the fruit with health-boosting compounds that attract animals to spread the seeds.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ yibii lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ lɛ ewoɔ adebɔɔ mli sugars mli. kɛ aduawai ni akɛfataa nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ahe ni gbalaa kooloi koni amɛgbɛ dumɔwui lɛ amɛshwã.

english: How does spreading wood ash on my pepper farm help the plants fight off fungal sicknesses?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tso sũ ni migbɛɔ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela?

english: Wood ash provides potassium and minerals that harden plant cell walls, making it much harder for disease germs to enter and harm the crops.
ga: Tso mli sũ haa potassium kɛ mineral ni haa tsei amli wala yibii lɛ ahe gbogboi lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Enɛ haa ewaa kwraa kɛhaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akɛ amɛaaye tsei awui.

english: Why do cocoa pod husks turn brown and dry up quickly when the trees do not get enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya kɛ́ tso lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ?

english: When water is scarce, cocoa trees focus their remaining moisture on keeping the main trunk alive, causing them to sacrifice young pods that they cannot afford to nourish.
ga: Beni nu faaa Cacao tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ baama ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛkwɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa cacao tso lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii lɛ shaa afɔle.

english: Why do some of my maize seeds fail to sprout after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need the right mix of moisture, air, and warmth to wake up. If they are buried too deep, planted in hard dry soil, or eaten by insects, the seeds will rot or die before reaching the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui hia ŋmɔtɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ dɔlɛ ni sa koni amɛte shi. Kɛji afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ Adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wa nɔ loo kooloi yeɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baagboi loo amɛbaagboi dani amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it helpful to mix clean sand with topsoil when I am raising seed nursing bags?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ mikɛ ŋã ni he tse baafutu shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni miduɔ dumɔwui kotokui lɛ?

english: Yes, mixing sand into heavy soil creates tiny air spaces that help water drain easily, preventing young seedling roots from suffocating or rotting from standing water.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋã ni akɛfutuɔ sũ ni tsii mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii baa. ni haa nu hoɔ oya Tsi tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafo loo amɛkafite kɛjɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need plantain trees grown right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ aná plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Baby cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that create living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool air it needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during high heat to reduce the amount of surface exposed to the sun, helping the plant conserve internal water until the air cools down.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni hulu la ni shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛbuɔ nu he yɛ amɛmli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: How do I know if my soil has become too tired to support a healthy cassava crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ egbɔjɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ makwɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: If your crops grow slowly, have pale or yellow leaves, and yield smaller roots than previous years, the soil has lost its nutrients and needs organic manure, compost, or a rest period.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo lɛ Na baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ ni oha shishifãi lɛ afee bibii fe afii ni eho lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni ehe baahia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo hejɔɔmɔ be aba.

english: Can I plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize on the same field?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cowpeas loo beans kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, beans and maize work well together because bean plants take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally feeds and strengthens the surrounding maize plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ niyenii ni ewoɔ amɛ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ

english: Seeds need steady, uninterrupted moisture during their first few weeks. Planting during dry spells at the start of the season can cause newly sprouted roots to dry up and die.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ hia ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa, ni nɔ ko nɔ ko kpaaa amɛnaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli. Dumɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi heei agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience severe heat stress, sudden dry soil, or attacks from tiny insects like thrips feeding on the flower stems.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Trukaa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbi. loo tutuamɔi ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni yeɔ fɔfɔii ahe tsei lɛ adɛŋ.

english: When plants are overcrowded, their roots fight over underground water and nutrients, while their leaves block sunshine from each other, leading to tall, weak plants with very small yields.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni amɛhe waaa shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ baa.

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and aggressively steal nutrients and fertilizer directly from the soil, leaving your main crops starving despite receiving enough water.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Hɔmɔ aye otsei titrii lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct hot sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out the soil before their roots can grow deep. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides a cooler environment for the young plants to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani amɛshishifãi lɛ atsɔ shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ baa koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why should I trim off some of the suckers growing at the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Leaving too many suckers allows them to compete with the main plantain tree for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers ensures the main tree receives enough energy to produce a large, healthy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ehaa amɛkɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ plantains babaoo ni mli wa.

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to produce food. This extra energy is sent down to the roots, helping the plant grow bigger underground tubers.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. Akɛ hewalɛ ni fa nɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the essential food maize needs to grow green leaves, or that heavy rain has washed the nutrients too deep for the roots to reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ko ni he hiaa ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli. Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli kɛtee shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my land make the soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni adu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants die, that stored nitrogen remains in the dirt as free food for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I check if the packaged seeds I bought from the store are still alive and good to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji dumɔwui ni awo mli ni mihe yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni esa akɛ adu?

english: You can perform a simple germination test by wrapping ten seeds in a damp cloth for a few days; if at least eight of them sprout roots, the seeds are fresh and good to plant across your whole farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni oookɛwo mama ni mli efɔ mli lɛ nɔ. gbii fioo komɛi Kɛji kɛ hoo lɛ shishifãi kpaanyɔ kwɛ̃ Dumɔwui lɛ baafee ehee ni sa kɛha dumɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What is causing small, ragged holes in the leaves at the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ baa ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center whorl of the maize plant to feed on tender leaves during the early growth stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli koni amɛye baai bibii yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Which part of the cassava stem should I cut to use as planting material for a good yield?
ga: Mɛɛ fã esa akɛ afo ŋmei tso lɛ mli koni akɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔ nii koni aná yibii kpakpai?

english: The middle section of a mature stem is best because it contains strong, healthy buds; the very top section is too young and dries out easily, while the bottom section is often too woody to sprout quickly.
ga: Tso lɛ tso ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ewoɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ tsɔ lolo ni egbiɔ oya. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ fã lɛ ji tsei tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to protect itself rather than set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekwɛ ehe nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do my tomatoes split open at the bottom just as they start turning red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ tswaa yɛ shishigbɛ kɛ́ ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when watering is uneven; if the plant goes through a dry period and then suddenly gets a lot of water, the inside of the fruit grows faster than the skin can stretch.
ga: Tomatoi lɛ fãa kɛji akɛ afɔɔ nu lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛji tsei tsɔ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛná nu babaoo trukaa lɛ Yibii lɛ amli daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect their tender leaves from direct sunlight and heat. Leaving larger trees or planting plantains alongside them provides shade and moisture while the cocoa roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo be koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Enɛ baaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of a maize plant usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow tall and green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps fix this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaatsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating small holes in the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that hides inside the leaves of corn plants. Checking your farm early and applying recommended control measures will protect your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmeii tsei ahe baai amli lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ lɛ ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the heavy rainy season arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water stays around them in soggy soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots remain healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the growing tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines so leaves can catch light and stay safe from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ anyɛ ana la ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the small shoots keep growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii shwereɔ yɛ midumɔwui titrii lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Having too many shoots causes them to fight with the mother plant for water and soil nutrients. Pruning extra shoots down to just one or two leaves enough food for the plant to produce large plantain bunches.
ga: Kpoji ni shwieɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa amɛkɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafo mli kɛyashɛ baa kome loo enyɔ pɛ he lɛ fa bɔ ni sa koni tso lɛ aná plantain tsei wuji.

english: Why does putting animal manure on my farm help my crops grow better than relying only on rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ mli kooloi ashishifãi ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe nugbɔ nu pɛ ni mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rainwater gives plants moisture, but animal manure supplies essential food nutrients that soil loses over time. Manure also improves the soil's ability to hold water during dry days.
ga: Nugbɔ nu haa tsei lɛ fɛ̃i. Shi kooloi ashishifãi haa niyenii ni he hiaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ. Manure hu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu mli yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plants without turning into fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of water cause stress to tomato plants, making them shed flowers to survive. Consistent watering and putting dried grass mulch around the base keeps the soil cool and preserves water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ afɔ fɔfɔi bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi. Nu daa ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo he lɛ. Shishitoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and weak even when there is plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miyɛ nu babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the resources they need to grow thick and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing huge, bushy green leaves, but when I dig them up, the tubers under the ground are very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? Shi kɛ́ atsa Shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the plant spends all its energy growing beautiful leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots. Balancing your soil nutrients helps the plant focus on making big tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo tsei ahe tsei fɛfɛji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa bulb agboi afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why are my maize plants growing very tall and green, but the cobs end up empty with no corn inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi ŋmãa lɛ mli efee efolo ni ŋmãa ko bɛ mli.

english: Too much fertilizer can make maize foliage look lush and healthy, but without enough phosphorus or proper pollination, the plant fails to produce grain inside the cob.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmãa baa lɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa loo pollination ni sa bɛ lɛ, Tsei nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui yɛ cob lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves turn bright yellow before the whole plant suddenly wilts and dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse dani tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Bright yellowing is often a hidden sign of root rot or viral infection. Even though the leaves look colorful, the roots are decaying underground, stopping water and food from reaching the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ egbo loo hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa. Eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ yɛ fɛo moŋ Shi shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii nyɛɛɛ ashɛ tso lɛ he.

english: Why do my healthy-looking cocoa pods turn black and rot right when they are almost ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmeii ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ trukaa ni amɛgboɔ beni eshwɛ fioo ni amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease. The pods look fine while growing, but excessive shade and moisture allow a hidden fungus to attack and ruin the beans just before you pick them.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Pods lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ beni aduɔ lɛ. Shi hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite amɛ dani okpa amɛ.

english: I see a green weed with nice flowers spreading quickly across my farm—is it fine to leave it there to cover the soil?
ga: Minaa jwɛi eŋɔli ni fɔfɔii fɛfɛji yɔɔ mli ni gbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya—ani manyɛ mashi amɛ koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Some attractive, fast-spreading weeds secretly steal water and nutrients from your crops beneath the soil, or attract harmful pests, eventually weakening and killing your crops.
ga: Jwɛi komɛi ni yɔɔ fɛo ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli yɛ teemɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. loo egbalaa kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ kɛbaa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ baa shi ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egboɔ.

english: Why are colorful insects on my vegetable plants dangerous if I do not see them eating the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni hiɛ sui sɔrɔtoi ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ji oshara kɛji minyɛɛɛ mana amɛ ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ?

english: Many attractive insects do not chew leaves directly, but they carry plant diseases in their saliva or lay hidden eggs that hatch into destructive caterpillars later.
ga: Kplukai fɛfɛji babaoo ŋmɔɔ baai tɛ̃ɛ. Shi amɛhiɛɔ tsei ahe helai yɛ amɛmli loo amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni sɛɛ mli lɛ amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii.

english: If fertilizer helps crops grow, why did my vegetables turn brown and die after I gave them a large amount?
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa Mɛni hewɔ mi aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo eha amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Using too much fertilizer causes 'nutrient burn.' It draws water out of the plant roots, causing the crop to dry up and die even if the soil is wet.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ kɛ ‘Nutrient Metabolism’ baa Ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Can watering my crops heavily every single day actually cause them to dry up and die?
ga: Ani nu ni okɛwoɔ otsei lɛ amli babaoo daa gbi lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbi ni amɛgboi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, overwatering fills all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots. Drowned roots rot and can no longer drink water, causing the plant to wilt and die from lack of moisture.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe nine lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ayi obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛnu nu dɔŋŋ. Ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why should I cut off green, healthy-looking branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji eŋɔli ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Having too many leaves blocks sunlight and traps moisture, creating a damp home for diseases. Pruning extra leaves directs energy into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Baai babaoo tsiɔ hulu la naa ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa helai srɔtoi baa jɛɛhe ni mli edɔ. Baai ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baatsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛya tomato agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many beautiful flowers that just dry up and fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi fɛfɛji babaoo ni gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects to pollinate them. If the farm is sprayed with harsh chemicals or lacks proper shade and moisture, the insects disappear and the flowers drop off without forming fruit.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii biɔ kooloi bibii koni amɛfee pollination. Kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai ni mli wa shwie ŋmɔji anɔ loo hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ mli lɛ, kooloi bibii he miihia kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔji lɛ amli. Kplukai laajeɔ ni fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Does it matter which direction I insert cassava stems into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei tso lɛ awo?

english: Yes, always plant cassava stem cuttings with the growth buds pointing upwards towards the sky. If planted upside down, the stems struggle to sprout and tuber yields will be very low.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ adu yucca tsei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii wuji lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu ŋwɛigbɛ Stems lɛ shweremɔ baafee nɔ ni wa ni tuber yibiiwoo lɛ baafee bibioo kwraa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in weak plants and small yields. Proper spacing gives every plant enough space to feed and grow strong.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni eda ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-decomposed animal manure will help the leaves turn green and boost plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to plant groundnuts on my land before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu ŋmei dani wɔdu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting maize after groundnuts allows the maize to feed on that natural fertilizer left behind in the soil.
ga: Agbɛnɛ hu, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ beni akɛ ŋmeii efata he lɛ haa abele lɛ yeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Should I put fertilizer on my field at the exact same time I plant the seeds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kome too mli ni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ aduɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds carry their own built-in food to sprout. It is better to wait until the seeds have sprouted and formed their first leaves and roots before applying fertilizer so the plant can actually absorb it.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ niyenii yɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛjie klɛŋklɛŋ baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is too hot or when the plant gets stressed from irregular watering. Giving the plants consistent moisture early in the morning helps them retain their flowers and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekwɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa tomatoi lɛ feɔ ekome.

english: Yam leaves need to catch direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers under the ground. Staking keeps the vines off the muddy soil and away from shade, leading to larger yam tubers.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha wain tso lɛ akabote muji mli ni ekabote hulutsoo mli. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable bed in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: It is best to water early in the morning. Watering in the hot afternoon causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the plant roots can drink it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap out of young leaves. Spraying with recommended neem water or suitable pesticides will clear the insects and allow healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem nu loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ ni ebaaha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How long does it usually take for my maize to mature and be ready for harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mi-ŋma lɛ daa ni efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Most standard maize varieties grown in Ghana take about 3 to 4 months (90 to 120 days) from planting to reach full maturity and be ready for harvesting.
ga: Abɛi srɔtoi ni aduɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 (gbii 90 kɛyashi 120) dani amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why are some plants in my field growing very big while others in the same row remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daraa waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ sɛɛkuu kome mli lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii lɛ?

english: Crops often grow unevenly because soil nutrients and moisture are not spread equally across your land, or seeds were planted at different depths. Giving extra organic manure to the smaller plants helps them catch up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ejaakɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ejaaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Aloo dumɔ dumɔwui yɛ hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ha tsei bibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛshɛɔ he.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant plantains next to my new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ madu tso bibioo ko yɛ kookoo tso hee ko masɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa seedlings need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Planting seeds too close forces plants to compete for light, water, and soil nutrients. This causes thin stems, yellow leaves, and a lower harvest compared to well-spaced plants.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛbaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni akpaaa nibii babaoo kɛ akɛto tsei ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Is it better for my soil if I burn the weeds on my land before planting?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani madu nii?

english: Burning clears land quickly, but it destroys vital topsoil nutrients and natural organic matter. Leaving cleared weeds to decompose or using them as mulch keeps the soil cooler and retains moisture longer.
ga: Shãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ oya. Shi efiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite loo akɛtsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping to the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves often mean the plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil or is stressed from dry weather. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ miihao lɛ. Kooloo ŋmãa ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmãa ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips living under the leaves. Spraying an organic neem oil solution or soapy water helps clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ aphids loo thrips, ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem oil solution loo nu ni akɛ samla shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when weather gets too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when the soil lacks phosphorus. Regular watering and applying balanced fertilizer keeps flowers attached so tomatoes can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi bɔni afee ni tomatoi lɛ anyɛ afee.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: How can I store my harvested maize so that insects do not destroy the grains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato koni kooloi akafite ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Maize must be thoroughly dried under the sun until the grains are hard before storage. Storing clean grain in sealed hermetic bags or raised, ventilated cribs protects it from insect damage and mold.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani akɛto. Dumɔwui ni he tse ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli loo tsɛnsii ni awó nɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni abu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi kɛ ŋmeii ni baafite amɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees yield so little harvest when I do not spend money on fertilizer or spraying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao ni mikpaa lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ? Be ni mifiteee shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Farming works like a business where your harvest reflects your investment. If you do not invest money in soil nutrients and plant protection, the crops cannot produce maximum pods, resulting in low yield and minimal profit.
ga: Okwaayeli tsuɔ nii tamɔ jarayeli nitsumɔ ko ni okpamɔ lɛ jieɔ shika ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ kpo. Kɛji akɛ okɛ shika wooo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ tsei ahebuu mli lɛ, Ŋmãa lɛ nyɛŋ ajie pod yibii babaoo. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi, ni sɛɛnamɔi ni anáa lɛ hu baa shi.

english: How can treating my farm like a real business help me make more money at the end of the season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ tsu nii tamɔ jarayeli nitsumɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua mi ni maná shika babaoo yɛ be lɛ naagbee?

english: When you treat your farm as a business, you track your expenses on seeds, inputs, and labor against your sales. Investing time and capital intentionally ensures that your farm yields high-quality produce that brings back strong financial returns.
ga: Kɛji okɛ oŋmɔ lɛ ye tamɔ jarayeli Obaakwɛ dumɔwui ahe nyɔmɔwoo. nibii ni kɔɔ nibii afeemɔ kɛ nitsumɔ he kɛ onihɔɔmɔ. Be kɛ shika ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ajɛɔ yiŋtoo mli atsuɔ he nii lɛ haa oŋmɔ lɛ woɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni kɛ shika helɛtemɔ ni mli wa baa.

english: Why do my crops look weak and yellow even though I planted good seeds in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ midu dumɔwui kpakpai yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Good seeds need continuous nourishment to grow strong. If the soil lacks essential nutrients or fertilizer, the crop cannot express its full potential, leading to weak stems and poor leaf growth.
ga: Niyenii he miihia dumɔwui kpakpai be fɛɛ be koni amɛdara ni amɛwa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa lɛ Nibii ni adu lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kpo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni baai lɛ hu edaaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvests get smaller every year if I plant on the same land without adding anything to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛ nɔ ko fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Crops remove food from the soil every season they grow. If you keep taking from the land without putting nutrients back through fertilizer or compost, the exhausted soil stops supporting healthy crop growth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be ni aduɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ oŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ pɛ ni okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataaa he ekoŋŋ kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ kpaɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ adalɛ sɛɛfimɔ.

english: Why is my cocoa tree producing many leaves and green branches but very few cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ baai kɛ niji babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi kookoo ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: When a tree puts all its energy into growing extra unpruned branches, it has little energy left for pods. Trimming unnecessary growth directs the tree's food directly into pod formation and yield.
ga: Kɛ tso ko kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsu niji ni miida ni afolɔko amɛhe krɛdɛɛ lɛ ahe nii lɛ, Hewalɛ fioo pɛ baashwɛ kɛha tso lɛ. Dalɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii lɛ kɛyaa pod feemɔ kɛ efeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa seedlings very close to each other to squeeze more trees onto my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni mikɛmi tsei babaoo awo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops planted too tightly together fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to feed well, grow strong, and produce a larger overall harvest.
ga: Tsei ni adu babaoo tsɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. shwere waa ni ekpa nibii babaoo yɛ fɛɛ mli

english: Why do weeds in my maize farm cause my crops to grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi-abele ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds actively compete with your crops for water, sunlight, and nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures that all the care and fertilizer you give your field goes directly to your maize plants.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa koni kwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni okɛhaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya oŋmei tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my cocoa trees more when the farm is bushy and overgrown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo miitutua mi-kookoo tsei lɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsei babaoo lɛ?

english: Overgrown weeds and dense shade create a damp, dark environment where pests and diseases thrive. Keeping your farm weeded and pruned lets sunlight in, which naturally discourages pests from settling on your pods.
ga: Jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ewoɔ duŋ. Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai yaa hiɛ yɛ. Ha oŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi akafee jwɛi ni ofolɔ mli koni hulu la abote mli.

english: Why do buyers offer me lower prices for my harvested cocoa beans compared to other farmers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ jara ni baa shi haa mi-kokoo yibii ni mikpa lɛ kɛ akɛto okwaafoi krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Buyers pay top money for well-fermented, thoroughly dried, and clean beans. The care and effort you put into properly processing your harvest directly determines the price quality buyers are willing to pay.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ shika babaoo kɛhaa ŋmeii ni edɔ jogbaŋŋ. Akɛni egbi ni ehe tse jogbaŋŋ hewɔ lɛ, bɔ ni okwɛɔ ohe nɔ ohaa kɛ mɔdɛŋ ni obɔɔ koni otsu okpamɔ lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ jara ni mɔ ni heɔ nii lɛ baasumɔ ni ewo lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do young vegetable plants dry up and die quickly during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ hɔmɔ ni baa be kukuoo mli lɛ?

english: Young plants have small, shallow roots that cannot reach deep underground moisture. Supplying adequate water and putting dry grass or leaves around the base keeps the soil moist so the crops survive hot weather.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔ he Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Shishitoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to grow strong. The plant moves nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the young upper leaves, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara waa Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why should I spread dry leaves and grass around the roots of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi mabɔle he lɛ? Tomato tso shishifãi

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, stops moisture from evaporating quickly in the heat, and prevents weeds from taking over your crop.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye onibii anɔ.

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a plant family that extracts nitrogen from the air and traps it in the soil through their roots. When the crop is done, that extra nutrient stays in the ground to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei aweku ko ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ogbe dumɔ naa lɛ Nakai niyenii ni fa lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when I plant them in a clear, open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse, ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong, direct heat from the sun. They need shade trees or plantain plants nearby to shield them from burning heat and retain moisture in the air while they grow their roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava cuttings in the farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu ŋmei niji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Cassava cuttings should usually be planted about one meter apart from each other. Giving them enough space prevents roots from competing underground for water and nutrients, allowing the tubers to grow big.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome. Kɛ́ aha he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yitso lɛ daa.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to spread their leaves out in the sunlight to produce energy. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, helping the plant catch full sunlight while protecting it from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tso ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ekɛ ebaai lɛ awo hulu mli bɔni afee ni ená hewalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hulu la ni fa babaoo, ni etsiɔ helai hu anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: If too many young shoots grow around one plantain stem, they steal food and water from the main mother plant. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant grows big bunches of fruit.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ ni miida yɛ plantain kome he lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ mli tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo yibii babaoo.

english: What is the best time of the day for me to water my vegetable farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mafɔ miŋmɔ mli aduawai lɛ anɔ nu?

english: The best time to water vegetables is early in the morning before the sun gets hot. This allows the roots to soak up the water before it evaporates in the heat, giving the plants energy for the day.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ aduawai anɔ nu ji leebi, dani hulu lɛ adɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ nu dani etsɔɔ la yɛ latsaa mli. Ehaa tsei hewalɛ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli

english: What causes tiny ragged holes in my young maize leaves and powdery dust inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ baai kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the center of the maize plant during the day and eats the leaves. Catching them early with proper spraying or natural controls protects your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ yɛ gbi mli ni eyeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo adebɔɔ mli nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ, abaabu onibii ahe.

english: Why does my harvested maize get destroyed by small black insects after storing it in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii diji fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ beni akɛwo kotokui amli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Those insects are weevils, which lay eggs inside grains when the maize is not completely dried before storage. Thoroughly drying your maize in the sun until it is hard prevents weevils from multiplying in your storage bags.
ga: Kplukai lɛ ji ŋmeii, ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli beni ŋmaa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛtoɔ. Kɛ́ ogbala o-corn lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii ni baa yɛ onitoo kotokui lɛ amli lɛ anaa.

english: Yam leaves act like solar panels that capture sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking raises the leaves off the damp ground so they get maximum sunlight and don't rot, which helps the plant direct energy underground to produce bigger, heavier tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulu la, emɔɔ hulu la koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Staking haa ajieɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛkafite. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛfee bulbs wuji ni tsii.

english: Why should I leave specific space between my maize seeds instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, their roots fight each other for limited soil nutrients and moisture, and their leaves shade each other from the sun. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room, light, and food to grow strong and produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛtsi niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa. ni baai lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ, la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land make the soil better for my maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that have special bacteria on their roots. These bacteria pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil. When the crop is harvested, that natural fertilizer remains in the ground to feed the next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Muawai nɛɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow in a V-shape from the tips while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ kã he efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen. Because nitrogen moves inside the plant, the maize steals nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves so it can keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nitrogen lɛ nyiɛɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmãa juɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli lɛ koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and droop during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In the hot sun, plants lose water through tiny openings in their leaves. Curling and drooping is the plant's natural defense to reduce the leaf surface area exposed to heat, helping it conserve internal moisture until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ anɔ. Curling kɛ drooping ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ tsei ahe koni ekɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulutsoo baa lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ mli kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ mli fɛ̃i baa.

english: Why does swamp rice grow well in flooded water while my maize plants die if water stays on the field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔŋ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu afua mli lɛ? Taakɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ gboiɔ kɛji nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Rice plants have hollow air channels inside their stems and roots that act like snorkels, sending oxygen from the air down to the underwater roots. Maize roots lack these air channels, so standing water smothers them and causes them to drown.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsuji ni mli ewo muji yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ paipii ni akɛmuɔ nii. Kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ha enɔ ni eha lɛ nu.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme stress, such as very hot temperatures, irregular watering, or a lack of insects to pollinate them. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa, tamɔ hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ be ni sa mli loo kooloi ni baafee pollination bɛ Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with plenty of dark green leaves, but the tubers underground remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or gets too much rain early on, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food below ground to swell the root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo nugbɔ enɛ babaoo mra. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ tsei ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ, moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi koni shishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains or shade trees next to my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui loo mawo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that create living umbrellas, providing the damp shade young cocoa needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa kɛfeɔ ambrella. Ehaa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I see small holes in my young maize leaves with light brown powder inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni mli tse yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli.

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm attack. The adult moth lays eggs on the plant, and when the tiny caterpillars hatch, they crawl into the leaf funnel to feed on the soft growing center, leaving behind chewed leaves and saw-dust like waste.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he okadi. Kplukai ni eda lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ tsei anɔ. Ni beni ŋmei bibioo lɛ fɔ lɛ Amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ baai amli koni amɛyaye hei bibii ni miida lɛ. Amɛshiɔ baai ni ashɛre kɛ ŋmeii ni atswa yɛ amɛsɛɛ tamɔ jwɛi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for healthy leaf growth. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or NPK early in the season helps the leaves turn green and produce a strong yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ ni hi Kɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking sap from the leaves, or by a virus carried by those insects. Controlling these pests early stops the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kudɔɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Ekpaa ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the soil without proper drainage, water fills the air spaces, causing the tubers to drown and rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ.

english: What causes my small green cocoa pods to turn black and dry up on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ? Minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy and humid weather when there is too much shade and moisture around the trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ fɛ̃i be mli beni hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i babaoo ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when the soil lacks moisture, or when there isn't enough phosphorus in the soil to help fruit set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni sũ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo be mli ni sũ lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ ni amɛwo lɛ.

english: Why do my orange trees drop their small green fruits before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Dani ebaafee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Citrus trees drop young fruit if they suffer from water stress during hot periods or if insect pests, such as fruit flies, attack the fruit early in its development.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ baashwie aduawai bibii kɛji amɛna nu he haomɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii tutua aduawai lɛ yɛ shishijee mli.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving less energy for the plant to grow thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo pɛ eha tso lɛ koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal the fertilizer and soil moisture faster than your crops can take them in, effectively starving your crop plants.
