ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field this season make my maize grow better next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baaha mi-ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, leaving rich nutrients behind that nourish the next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛshiɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I stop my harvested yams from sprouting roots and shoots while in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii be mli ni miyɔɔ he ko ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Yams sprout when exposed to light and heat because they sense it is time to grow. Storing them in a cool, dry, and well-shaded barn keeps them dormant for much longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ la kɛ dɔlɛ wo amɛmli ejaakɛ amɛnuɔ he akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni egbi, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛwɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to leave a specific distance between cassava sticks when planting them in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi ŋmei tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ mli beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving enough space between cassava plants gives the roots room to expand into large tubers under the soil. If planted too close, the crops compete with each other for water and soil nutrients, resulting in small, thin roots.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ amli gbɛ lɛ aya hiɛ ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Kɛji adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni jɛɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe tseee.

english: Why is planting my maize in straight lines better than scattering the seeds across the field by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni akɛ niji duɔ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines ensures every plant gets equal access to sunlight and air. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier compared to seeds scattered randomly.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ehaa jwɛi shwiemɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ trukaa.

english: What will happen to my plantain trees if I plant them too close to one another?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi plantains lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When plantains are planted too close together, their broad leaves block sunlight from each other, leading to tall, weak stems and very small fruit bunches because they are fighting for nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ he tsɔi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛfeɔ aduawai bibii waa ejaakɛ amɛwuɔ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do older farmers advise me to plant plantains on the same land with my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa dumɔwui bibii lɛ duɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot withstand harsh direct sun. Fast-growing plantain leaves act like shade umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa seedlings from drying out during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Plantain baai ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa feɔ ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas naturally trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow strong, while the tall maize stalks provide light shade and support for the farm.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to sow my maize seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the land receives two or three heavy, steady rains so the ground is thoroughly soaked. Sowing after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then die if the sun comes back strong.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni naa wa nɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ kɛtsara nɔ bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afɔ jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Be kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba waa.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and stop growing during hot dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛkpaa dalɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in dry weather is often a defense reaction to extreme heat and pests like mites that attack stressed plants. Giving them water and shade helps the leaves open up and return to healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii ni tutuaa tsei ni haoɔ lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ aha amɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe ni amɛdaraa ekoŋŋ kɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do tomato seeds need to be nursed in a small bed first before planting them out in the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu tomato dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ? dani abaanyɛ adu yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Tomato seeds are tiny and delicate. Nursery beds protect them from heavy rain and pests while they are weak, allowing you to select only the strongest seedlings to move to the main field.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. Nursery saatsoi lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe, yɛ be mli ni ehaa amɛfeɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohalaa dumɔwui ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ni okɛbaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: How deep should I bury yam seed tubers inside the mounds when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ midu?

english: Yam seeds should be planted about wrist-deep into the top of the mound with the head pointing up. This keeps the seed moist enough to sprout while protecting it from scorching ground heat.
ga: Esa akɛ adu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ aaafee nine mli shɔŋŋ kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya shikpɔŋ gɔŋ lɛ mli ni bulb lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃, yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do crops grow tall very quickly on land where bush was recently burned, but the soil becomes weak after two years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ashã jwɛi etsɛko lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ bagbɔjɔ yɛ afii enyɔ sɛɛ?

english: Ash from burned bush provides a quick burst of food for plants, making them grow fast at first. However, burning destroys the living natural matter in the soil, causing it to lose fertility quickly over time.
ga: Sũ ni jɛɔ jwɛi ni ashã lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ yeɔ nii oya. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daa oya yɛ shishijee mli. Shi kɛlɛ, shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli wala ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa fɔmɔ he nyɛmɔ lɛ baa shi oya yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my crops grow bigger and produce more harvest when I feed the soil with fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ́ mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Crops need food from the soil just like humans need food to grow strong. Fertilizer supplies essential plant foods like nitrogen and phosphorus that might be missing in your soil, helping the crops grow bigger, greener, and produce a much higher yield.
ga: Niyenii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii. Taakɛ niyenii he hiaa adesai koni amɛná hewalɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ anáa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus ni ekolɛ ebɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa Ekɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kpãaa gbee jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo

english: Why does my farmland produce less maize now than it did five years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ miiwo ŋmãa fioo fe afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Every time you harvest crops, they take nutrients out of the ground. If you keep planting on the same piece of land without giving nutrients back through fertilizer, animal manure, or compost, the soil becomes weak and exhausted.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuuu sɛɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaagbɔjɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my corn plants turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants are hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main plant nutrient responsible for keeping leaves deep green and helping the crop process sunlight into food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nitrogen ji tso mli niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa hulu la yɛ eniyenii mli.

english: Why do my crops look so much greener after a heavy rainstorm compared to when I water them myself?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto be mli ni mikɛ nu haa mihe lɛ he?

english: Rainwater picks up small amounts of natural nitrogen from the air during storms. When this rain hits the ground, it delivers a natural food boost directly to the roots, making plants look instantly brighter and greener.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ jieɔ nitrogen fioo ko kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ ahum be mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii haa shishifãi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa otsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛkpɛɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Is it safe for me to use the exact same type of fertilizer on all the different crops on my farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ kome pɛpɛɛpɛ baatsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: Different crops have different food requirements. Leafy crops like maize need high nitrogen to grow tall, while fruiting plants like tomatoes or cocoa need more potassium and phosphorus. Using the wrong fertilizer type can waste money or lower your harvest.
ga: Niyenii srɔtoi yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he hiamɔ nii srɔtoi. Tsei ni yɔɔ baai, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, he miihia nitrogen babaoo koni amɛdara. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni woɔ yibii tamɔ tomato loo kookoo He miihia potassium kɛ phosphorus babaoo Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ofite shika loo eha onibii ni onáa lɛ aba shi.

english: When is the best time to put fertilizer on my farm so the rain doesn't carry it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the crop is actively growing and the soil is slightly moist. Avoid putting down fertilizer right before a heavy downpour, as strong rain will wash the plant food into gutters before the roots can swallow it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni tsei lɛ miida ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa tsei aniyenii hoɔ kɛboteɔ nubui lɛ amli dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmiɔ.

english: Can putting too much fertilizer on my crops make them wither and die?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, ebaaha amɛgboi ni amɛgboi?

english: Yes, putting too much fertilizer is like putting too much salt in food. It creates high heat in the soil, burns the delicate roots of the crop, and sucks water out of the plant, causing the leaves to dry up.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tamɔ ŋmei babaoo ni akɛwoɔ niyenii mli. Ehaa hulutsoo ni naa wa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eshãa tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. ni ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli, ni no haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ

english: Is chemical fertilizer better for my crops than using dried animal dung?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi?

english: Chemical fertilizer works faster because it gives plants an instant meal, but animal dung improves the soil structure so it holds water longer. Using both together gives you fast plant growth while keeping your land fertile for many years.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ tsuɔ nii oya ejaakɛ amɛhaa tsei lɛ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shi kooloi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo, no hewɔ lɛ, ehaa nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni odara oya, yɛ be mli ni ohaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii afii babaoo ni baa lɛ.

english: How do farmers in other towns manage to get abundant harvests even when rain is small?
ga: Te okwaafoi ni yɔɔ maji krokomɛi anɔ lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛnáa ŋmaa babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ?

english: Farmers with heavy yields often combine fertilizer with soil practices like mulching—covering the ground with dry grass or leaves—which traps moisture in the dirt and prevents the fertilizer from drying out under the hot sun.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ mulching, kɛtsɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni amɛkɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ mli tseɔ ni ehaaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: What helps young crops develop deep and strong roots under the ground after planting?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni wa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni amɛdu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young crops need a specific soil nutrient called phosphorus to build long, tough roots. Applying a starter fertilizer rich in phosphorus early in the plant's life helps it dig deep for underground water and anchor firmly against strong winds.
ga: Tsei bibii hia shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni atsɛɔ lɛ phosphorus koni amɛfee shishifãi kakadaji ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo tso lɛ shihilɛ mli mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni ehiɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees shed leaves during hot, dry weather to protect themselves from losing water. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them keeps the soil moist and cools down the cocoa seedlings.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ amli jɔɔ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the young shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi tsɔne titri lɛ

english: Leaving too many shoots around the main plantain tree makes them compete for soil nutrients and water. Keeping only two or three strong shoots allows the main plant to produce bigger and heavier plantain bunches.
ga: releasing surrounding shoots Dumɔwui titrii babaoo tsɔ baaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei fioo komɛi pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which the crop needs to grow healthy green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores dark green leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ baai ni wa, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsuɔ waa lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when excess rainwater stays pooled around them for a long time. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily, protecting the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Ye obua ni abu yitso lɛ he

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines off the ground using tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji ajie mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce energy to grow large tubers below the ground. Lifting the vines on stakes also keeps the leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tso lɛ nɔ ni awoɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ koni ekabote shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: Why do caterpillars attack the central leaf funnels of my maize plants before I even see them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ dani minaa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Moths like the Fall Armyworm lay their eggs inside the tight central leaves of young maize because it provides protection and soft food. Inspecting the center funnel early helps you spot pests before major crop damage occurs.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ejaakɛ ehaa hebuu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ebaaye ebua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai dani amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ waa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience extreme midday heat or inconsistent watering. Providing light shade and keeping the soil evenly moist prevents flower stress so fruits can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa yɛ shwane mli loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse ha ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akaha fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ haomɔ aba koni aduawai aba.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites that spread plant viruses. Spraying neem oil early controls these insects and keeps new leaves growing straight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Eyeɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ ni ehaa baai heei kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Growing maize repeatedly on the same plot drains specific plant nutrients and lets maize pests multiply in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores soil nitrogen and reduces pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, tsei amli niyenii pɔtɛɛi baa shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi.

english: How does spreading dry grass on top of the soil around my crops help them grow?
ga: Akɛ jwɛi fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering topsoil with cut grass acts like a protective blanket that traps soil moisture and stops weeds from taking root. As the grass decomposes, it also adds rich natural plant food back into the earth.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni afolɔ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ fite Ekɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii babaoo baafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sun exposure. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a natural umbrella, protecting the young trees from heat stress and keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni ekwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning brown and falling off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan, dry winds and low moisture cause trees to lose water faster than their roots can pull from the ground. Cocoa trees drop their leaves naturally to conserve water and survive until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulutsoo be ni baa shi lɛ haa tsei amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛto nu ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crops turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential soil nutrient needed for leaves to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Eji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hia koni baa lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do farmers say planting groundnuts or beans on my land will make the soil richer for my next crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny bacterial pods on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the plants die, that stored nitrogen fertilizes the soil naturally for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ bacteria pods bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nitrogen ni ato lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce thin, watery roots instead of big, healthy tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ woɔ shishifãi bibii ni nu yɔɔ mli yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots fail to expand if the soil is too hard and compacted, or if plants are sown too close together. Loosening the soil into mounds or ridges and giving each plant proper space allows the roots room to swell and store food.
ga: Kasava shishifãi nyɛŋ alɛɛ mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni ajieɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛfeɔ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni ahaa tso fɛɛ tso he gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛfu ni amɛkɛ niyenii ato.

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water pools around the roots without draining away properly. Building raised mounds and avoiding waterlogged land helps excess water flow away from the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni enyɛɛɛ eho jogbaŋŋ. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni afeɔ kɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ edɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my maize plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ye mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, which hide inside the tight funnel of the maize stem during the hot day to avoid sunlight and come out to feed on tender young leaves when it cools down.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji cutworms ni kɛ amɛhe ewo gbɛjegbɛi bibii amli. ni ji ŋmãa tsei yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli Koni hulu la akashɛ nɔ ni eje kpo ebaye baai bibii lɛ kɛji edɔ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and soft before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering and a lack of calcium in the soil while the fruit is forming. Keeping the soil consistently moist prevents the fruit bottoms from drying out and blackening.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni aduawai lɛ miikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaatsi aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ naa koni ekagbi ni efee ediŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I just take seeds from last year's harvested maize crop to plant in the new season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋɔɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni jɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛduɔ yɛ be hee lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from harvest lose their vigor and disease resistance over generations, leading to smaller yields. Fresh, certified seeds are bred to produce uniform, strong plants with higher resistance to local pests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ mli lɛ hewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo. Akwɛ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ koni amɛwo tsei ni wa, ni yaa nɔ daa ni nyɛɔ amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Why do weeds on my farm grow so much faster than the food crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from crowding out your crop plants while they are young.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Okɛ ohe awo mli mra Enɛ baatsi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni ekafee mɛi babaoo yɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. This happens when the soil lacks nutrients or when heavy rains wash the fertilizer away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ mli loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii jeɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why does my corn harvest get smaller every year when I keep planting on the exact same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ bibioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Corn takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil every season. Planting it in the same place year after year starves the land unless you rotate with other crops or add compost and fertilizer to restore soil strength.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ odu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tsake loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my corn grow tall and strong in some parts of my small field, but stays short and weak in other parts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ fãi komɛi amli, shi eyɛ kuku ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Soil quality is rarely the same across a whole field. Short crops usually point to spots where water collects, where the earth is packed too hard for roots to spread, or where organic food in the soil is low.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su lɛ efeee ekome yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kukuji tsɔɔ hei ni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ, he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã, loo he ni niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa yɛ.

english: If I plant my corn seeds very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ he bibioo ko. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: Planting seeds too close creates crowding. The plants will fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin stalks and very small or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha mɛi ayi obɔ fe nine. Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Is it good to plant beans together in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ wɔɔfee ekome kɛdu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, planting beans or cowpeas alongside maize is very beneficial. Legumes take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which helps feed the maize while giving you two different crops from the same field.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Legumes lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ haa kooloi lɛ yeɔ nii, ni ehaa ŋmãa sɔrɔtoi enyɔ hu jɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why do my corn leaves roll up tight like tubes during the middle of hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's way of sweating less and saving water during intense sunshine. It reduces the surface area exposed to heat until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛshwieɔ latsaa fioo ni amɛbuɔ nu he yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa he ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ baa shi kɛyashiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: What causes small green or brown worms to show up and eat the heart of my young corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo ni amɛyeɔ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ atsui?

english: These are usually Fall Armyworms. Moths lay eggs on the leaves, and when the caterpillars hatch, they head straight for the soft, juicy growing center of the young corn plant to feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai anɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ Amɛyaa ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ lɛ aŋɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛyaye nii.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my crops right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants built to survive harsh conditions, so their seeds germinate extremely fast when rain falls. They aggressively consume water and fertilizer before crop roots have time to settle.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni abɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛdumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya waa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ. Amɛkɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli kɛ hiɛdɔɔ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛbaa shi.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my maize crop so that I get big cobs?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo ŋmãa mli koni ená ŋmãa wuji?

english: Maize needs fertilizer at two main stages: first when planting or shortly after to build strong roots, and second when it reaches knee-high height to help it form full, heavy cobs.
ga: Abɛi he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛi titrii enyɔ nɔ: klɛŋklɛŋ beni aduɔ loo no sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ koni etswa shishifãi ni wa. kɛ gbɛ ni ji enyɔ lɛ beni eshɛɔ enaji ahe lɛ koni eye ebua lɛ ni ehiɛ eyi obɔ ni etsii.

english: Why do seeds bought from the extension officer grow bigger cobs than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihe kɛjɛ extension agent lɛ dɛŋ lɛ dara fe dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought seeds are often specially bred hybrid varieties engineered for high yields and strong disease resistance. Saved seeds lose those powerful traits over generations, producing weaker crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aheɔ yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ ji dumɔwui ni afee amɛ srɔtoi ni afee amɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi.

english: How does planting Elephant grass on my land help me produce good quality food for my pen-fed cattle and goats?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shwuɔ jwɛi ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi koni maná niyenii kpakpa aha tsinai kɛ tooi ni mikwɛɔ amɛ yɛ ŋtayaai amli lɛ?

english: Elephant grass is a fast-growing pasture crop that regrows quickly after being cut, providing a continuous supply of green feed for farm animals even when natural grazing fields dry up.
ga: Shɔ jwɛi ji jwɛi tso ko ni daa oya ni kɛ́ afo lɛ, ekwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ oya. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ náa niyenii ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi alɛɛhe shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi moŋ

english: Why do extension officers advise planting legumes like cowpea or Stylo alongside regular grass for crop feed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmãa tamɔ cowpea loo stylo yɛ jwɛi ni afɔɔ namɔ ahe kɛha niyenii lɛ?

english: Legume crops capture nitrogen from the air to enrich the soil and contain high levels of protein, which helps livestock build muscle and grow faster when mixed into their feed.
ga: Legumes lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ, ni protein babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kooloi lɛ ni amɛnáa gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa oya kɛ akɛfata niyenii he.

english: What kind of feed trees can I plant along my farm boundaries to keep my animals fed during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii tsei manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ he koni mikɛha mikooloi lɛ niyenii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Fodder trees like Gliricidia and Leucaena have deep roots that keep their leaves green during dry spells, providing rich protein feed when ground grasses turn brown.
ga: Niyenii tsei tamɔ Gliricidia kɛ Leucaena yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛbaai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ehaa niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ protein kɛ́ jwɛi ni atsɔ mli lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How should I handle fresh cassava peels from my harvest before giving them to my farm animals?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mafee ŋmei heei ni akpa lɛ dani mikɛha miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ?

english: Fresh cassava peels contain natural bitter chemicals that can make animals sick, so they must be sun-dried or fermented to make them safe and healthy for feed.
ga: Tsofai ni mli wa ni baanyɛ aha kooloi hela amɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ cassava ŋmɔji heei amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ agbi cassava hewolo lɛ yɛ hulu mli loo afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni efee shweshweeshwe ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha niyenii.

english: When is the best time for me to harvest my pasture grass so that my animals gain the most weight?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ makpa ŋmɔ mli jwɛi koni maha mikooloi lɛ agbɔjɔ fe fɛɛ?

english: Pasture grass has the highest amount of protein and water just before it flowers; if you wait until it produces seeds, the leaves become hard, woody, and less nutritious.
ga: Jwɛi ji nɔ ni protein kɛ nu babaoo yɔɔ mli dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi. Kɛ́ omɛ ni amɛwo dumɔwui lɛ, baai lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, tsei, ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa.

english: How often can I cut grass crops like Brachiaria for feed without destroying the plants?
ga: Shii enyiɛ manyɛ mafo jwɛi tsei tamɔ Brachiaria kɛha niyenii ni mifiteee tso lɛ?

english: Brachiaria grass stores food in its roots, allowing it to sprout new leaves every 4 to 6 weeks after cutting, provided you leave a few inches of stems above the soil.
ga: Brachiaria jwɛi lɛ toɔ niyenii yɛ eshishifãi amli. Koni enyɛ ekwɛ baai heei daa otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 yɛ be mli ni afo lɛ sɛɛ. Esa akɛ ashi tso lɛ shishi aaafee 2-3 inch yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my pasture crop grow poorly after I harvest it several times from the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi kooloi alɛɛhe lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ beni mikpa ŋmɔ kome mli shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Fodder crops draw large amounts of nutrients out of the earth as they grow, so without returning plant compost or animal manure to the soil, the land becomes weak and crop growth slows down.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ jieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ akuuu sɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi ashishifãi lɛ ewooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Can I feed my farm livestock with the leaves and stems left over after harvesting my maize crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii kɛ baai kɛ tsei ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, leftover maize stalks make good energy feed, but because they get dry and tough quickly, chopping them up and mixing them with moist green leaves makes them easier for animals to eat.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni eshwɛ lɛ haa hewalɛ kpakpa. Shi akɛni ŋmãa tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛhe wa oya hewɔ lɛ, Kɛ́ afolɔ mli ni akɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli efɔ futu mli lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kooloi akɛ amɛyeɔ.

english: How does packing chopped green corn stalks into sealed containers keep them fresh for feeding livestock months later?
ga: Te ŋmãa ni afo lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi ko ni atsĩ mli lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi ehee kɛha kooloi yɛ nyɔji komɛi asɛɛ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Sealing fresh green crops tightly removes oxygen, causing good bacteria to ferment and preserve the plants as silage without rotting, saving feed for the dry season.
ga: Tsei heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni oootsi naa jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni ejie kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ. Enɛ haa helai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛbuɔ tsei lɛ ahe akɛ silage ni amɛfiteee. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni akɛ niyenii toɔ kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ.

english: Can I grow fast-growing feed grass on the same land where I am planting cassava without ruining my cassava crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu forage jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ ni miyeŋ ŋmei tsei lɛ awui?

english: Yes, but you must space them properly so the tall feed grass does not block sunlight from reaching the cassava leaves or compete heavily with its roots for water.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi ehe miihia ni okɛ amɛ abɔ he bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni jwɛi kakadaji akatsi hulu la naa koni ekashɛ ŋmei lɛ baai lɛ ahe loo ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ akatswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu.

english: How many bags of maize should I expect to harvest from one acre of land?
ga: Esa akɛ makpa ŋmãa kotokui enyiɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome nɔ?

english: On one acre of land, using improved seed varieties and correct fertilizer application can yield between 10 to 15 bags (50kg each). Without proper inputs and soil management, yields often drop to only 3 to 5 bags.
ga: Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome nɔ lɛ, kɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha baagi 10 kɛyashi 15 (kg 50 eko fɛɛ eko) aba kɛji akɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa bɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ajieɔ yibiiwoo lɛ shi kɛyaa kotokui 3 kɛyashi 5 pɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better for me to clear a larger farm or focus on making a small piece of land produce more?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafo ŋmɔ agbo ko mli loo makɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama shikpɔŋ bibioo ko ni mafee nɔ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ nɔ?

english: Focusing on a smaller piece of land with good seeds, timely fertilizer, and proper care usually produces more food and profit than spreading your labor and money thin over a large, poorly managed farm.
ga: Shikpɔji bibii ni dumɔwui kpakpai yɔɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ ni akɛjwɛŋmɔ maa Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa Bei pii lɛ, ehaa niyenii kɛ sɛɛnamɔi babaoo baa fe nitsumɔ kɛ shika ni akɛhaa ŋmɔji wuji ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do I weed my farm three times in a season but still end up with very small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli shii etɛ yɛ be kome mli shi mináaa yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeding removes competition for light and space, but crops also need nutrients to produce good yields. If your soil is exhausted or lacks organic matter and fertilizer, weeding alone will not make the crops yield well.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii ni kɔɔ la kɛ he ko he lɛ kɛyaa. Shi tsofai hu he miihia tsei koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai. Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. Jwɛi ni aaajie kɛjɛ jɛmɛ kɛkɛ lɛ haŋ yibii kpakpai aba.

english: Does plowing and disturbing the soil multiple times before planting help my crops grow better?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii ni mifiteɔ lɛ shii abɔ dani miduɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Over-working the soil can actually damage its structure, wash away topsoil, and dry out moisture. Plowing once and harrowing is usually enough to prepare a good bed for crops without exhausting the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ atsu nii babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite sũ lɛ mli nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. ni eha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔ kome ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛsaa he ko ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteee.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or the ground is waterlogged. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea shortly after germination helps turn them green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe awa.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my maize so I don't waste my money?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo ŋmãa mli ŋmãa? No hewɔ lɛ, ofiteee shika?

english: Apply NPK fertilizer about 10 to 14 days after planting when the seeds have sprouted, and top-dress with Urea about 4 to 6 weeks after planting when the stalks are growing rapidly.
ga: Okɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli aaafee gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 yɛ dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Ni okɛ urea afɔ nɔ aaafee otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ beni ŋmeii lɛ miida oya lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with big leaves but have small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava puts all its energy into leaf growth when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or when planted in heavy shade. Tubers also need 10 to 12 months of growth to fully expand and store starch.
ga: Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai lɛ adalɛ mli kɛ́ nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ eda yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nyɔji 10 kɛyashi 12 hu he miihia ni ŋmeii lɛ adara koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kwraa ni amɛhiɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: How do I ensure that the cassava I harvest yields a lot of gari when processed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mi-cassava ni mikpaa lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai kɛji akɛ atsu he nii?

english: High gari yield comes from harvesting high-starch cassava varieties at full maturity (around 12 months) and processing the tubers within 24 to 48 hours of harvest before they lose water weight.
ga: Gari yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo jɛɔ ŋmei srɔtoi ni starch babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akpaa yɛ be mli ni edara (aaafee nyɔji 12) kɛ ŋmei lɛ ni atsuɔ he nii yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 mli yɛ ŋmei ni akpaa lɛ sɛɛ dani nu lɛ mli tsiimɔ baa shi lɛ mli.

english: Why does the gari I process from my cassava sometimes turn out heavy and sour instead of dry and crispy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, gari ni mikɛ ŋmei tsuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ kpo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Gari becomes heavy and sour if the grated cassava is left to ferment for too many days before pressing, or if the water is not completely squeezed out before roasting.
ga: Gari baafee nɔ ni tsii ni ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmei ni atswa lɛ gbii babaoo dani atswa. Aloo kɛji akɛ ashɛko nu lɛ mli kwraa dani ashã.

english: How can I plan when to plant my crops when the rains no longer come at the usual time each year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato be ni esa akɛ madu nii yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ be ni afɔɔ enɛ daa afi lɛ mli lɛ he gbɛjianɔ?

english: Rather than planting on fixed traditional dates, wait until the soil receives consecutive heavy rains that soak deep into the ground, or choose early-maturing seed varieties that require less rainfall over the season.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu yɛ gbi ni ato lɛ nɔ taakɛ kusum tsɔɔ lɛ. Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa ni yaa nɔ lɛ baashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Aloo halamɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra ni biɔ nugbɔ fioo yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up when the Harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ bɔi tswaa lɛ?

english: During the dry Harmattan season, hot dry winds cause plants to lose water faster than their roots can absorb it. Young cocoa trees shed leaves to protect themselves from losing too much moisture and drying out completely.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni amɛshwieɔ shi kwraa lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii, ni ehaa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing down the center of maize leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the plant food responsible for keeping leaves dark green and healthy so the corn can grow big ears.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa teŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. koni ŋmãa lɛ anyɛ aná toi wuji

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts before corn makes the soil better for the corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei dani awo ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the groundnuts are harvested, that natural fertilizer stays in the dirt and helps the next crop of corn grow bigger.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why is it dangerous for me to plant my maize immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛha mi akɛ madu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rainfall is often a 'false rain' followed by many hot dry days. If you plant too early, the seeds will sprout but then die from heat and lack of water before the main rainy season truly starts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ ji ‘amale nugbɔ’, ni gbii babaoo ni mli edɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ shi amɛgboiɔ yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni bɛ hewɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground if heavy rain falls right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: When soil gets soaked with too much rain water, air cannot reach the roots. The cassava roots get trapped in water, suffocating them and causing rotting fungi to spoil the tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ kɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kasava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ mli, ni ehaa amɛmuɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on to produce big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he hiaa ni akɛ tsei kakadaji akwɔ koni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Staking gets yam leaves up off the ground so they catch maximum sunlight. The leaves use sunlight to manufacture food, which is then sent down into the ground to build large, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Staking baawó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ nɔ. Baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛ feɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, atsuɔ amɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant juices, which damages leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ mites loo thrips, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ

english: Tomato blossoms drop off without fruiting when daytime temperatures get too hot, when the soil dries out suddenly, or when there are no bees around to move pollen inside the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi trukaa loo be mli ni ŋmeii komɛi bɛ ni miimɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Planting plantains too close forces them to fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. This competition results in thin plants with small, light bunches that can easily fall over in wind.
ga: Plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, kɛ nu he. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ jwɛi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni baanyɛ agbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do some of my cocoa flowers drop off the tree without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need to be pollinated by tiny insects like midges or by hand. If a flower is not pollinated within a day or two of opening, it naturally dies and falls off the tree.
ga: Esa akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo nine afee cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ pollen. Kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen yɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ mli beni amɛfɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baagboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaagbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: What is hand pollination, and why are other cocoa farmers doing it on their farms?
ga: Mɛni ji nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi krokomɛi No hewɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ enɛ yɛ amɛŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Hand pollination is a practice where a farmer manually transfers pollen from one cocoa flower to another using small tools like tweezers. Farmers do this to ensure more flowers turn into pods, which significantly increases their harvest compared to relying only on insects.
ga: Nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ji nifeemɔ ko ni okwaafoi kɛ amɛdɛŋ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ nibii bibii tamɔ tweezers nɔ. Okwaafoi feɔ enɛ koni fɔfɔi babaoo afee ŋmeii. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ waa kɛ akɛto kooloi bibii pɛ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ he.

english: What is the best time of day for cocoa flowers to get pollinated?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afee kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers usually open early in the morning, making the morning hours the best time for pollination because the pollen is fresh and the flower is most ready to receive it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ fɔmɔ leebi. Enɛ haa leebi feɔ be ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha pollination. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, pollen lɛ ji ehee ni fɔfɔi lɛ efee klalo fe fɛɛ akɛ amɛbaaŋɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce flowers directly on the main trunk instead of just on the small branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe niji bibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce flowers on their main trunk and thick branches—a feature called cauliflory. This allows the tree to support heavy cocoa pods easily as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ nɔ kɛ tsei niji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ. ni atsɛɔ lɛ cauliflower Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekwɛɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ anɔ mlɛo beni edaa lɛ.

english: Are all tiny insects on my cocoa farm bad for my crop?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii?

english: No, not all insects are harmful. Tiny insects like midges are beneficial because they carry pollen between cocoa flowers so pods can grow. Only specific pests like capsids cause damage.
ga: Dabi, jeee kooloi bibii fɛɛ yɛ oshara. Kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ ejaakɛ amɛwoɔ pollen yɛ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ ada. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui komɛi pɛ, tamɔ capsids lɛ, fiteɔ nii.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow when there is too much direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees thrive best under filtered light. Too much intense, direct sun scorches the leaves and breaks down their green pigment, which makes them turn yellow and stunts the tree's growth.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ kane ni mli tse lɛ shishi. Hulu la ni naa wa tsɔ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaakumɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa tso lɛ dalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop a lot of their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ baai babaoo yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a survival mechanism. By shedding leaves during dry weather, the cocoa tree conserves water and prevents itself from drying out completely until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala. Kɛtsɔ baai ni eshwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ nɔ. Kakao tsei lɛ hiɛɔ nu mli ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe gbɛ koni amɛkagbi kwraa kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do some small green cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Koni amɛtsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbi be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: This can be caused by fungal diseases like black pod disease, or by natural cherelle wilt, where the tree sheds extra pods it cannot support due to a lack of water or soil nutrients.
ga: Enɛ baanyɛ ajɛ ŋmei hela ko, tamɔ black pod hela, loo cherel tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni baa lɛ mli aba. He ni tsei yɔɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ yɛ nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees flower heavily during certain months but end up with very few pods later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli shi amɛhe tsɔi fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy flowering often follows the first rains, but if there are not enough pollinating insects or if heavy rains wash the pollen away, those flowers will fail to set pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni tsii baa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ faaa lɛ faaa Aloo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ Nakai fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmeii.

english: Does pruning my cocoa trees help them produce more flowers and pods?
ga: Ani cacao tsei ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Yes, pruning removes dead or weak branches, allowing more sunlight and air to circulate around the main trunk. This creates better conditions for flower production and pod growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɔleɔ he fɛɛ he. more main trunk Enɛ haa shihilɛ kpakpa baa kɛha fɔfɔii afeemɔ kɛ pod lɛ dalɛ.

english: Why do many cocoa farmers in Ghana plant plantains on the same farm with their young cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ duɔ kookoo tsei yɛ ŋmɔji ni amɛduɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide essential shade to protect young cocoa seedlings from harsh sunlight, while also providing food and early income for the farmer before the cocoa starts producing.
ga: Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni abu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ahaa okwaafoi lɛ niyenii kɛ shishijee shika dani ajeɔ kookoo feemɔ shishi.

english: How does heavy sunlight affect my young cocoa seedlings during the dry season?
ga: Te hulu la ni naa wa lɛ saa mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Excessive sunlight without proper shade scorches tender cocoa leaves, causes soil moisture to dry up fast, and can stunt or kill young trees before their roots are fully established.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo ni hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ mli lɛ baashã kookoo baai ni mli tse lɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsei ni egbɔjɔ dani shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ kwraa.

english: How do I make sure my soil stays fertile after harvesting cocoa from my land for many years?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii yɛ be mli ni mikɛ afii babaoo kpa kookoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Harvesting crops continuously removes nutrients from the soil. You can restore fertility by applying organic manure or recommended fertilizers, and leaving fallen leaves on the farm floor to rot into natural nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Obaanyɛ okɛ fɔmɔ hegbɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba kɛtsɔ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. kɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni efite ni etsɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Is it a good idea to plant food crops like cassava alongside mature cocoa trees, or will it damage my farm?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei yɛ kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ ahe? Aloo ebaafite miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Food crops are helpful when cocoa trees are young, but planting heavy feeders like cassava close to mature cocoa can strip the soil of water and nutrients, reducing cocoa yields.
ga: Niyenii tsei ahe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ́ kookoo tsei lɛ darako. Shi niyenii tsei ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmei, ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo ni eda lɛ baanyɛ aha nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni faaa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, kookoo ni afeɔ lɛ ba shi.

english: What is the best way to store harvested cocoa beans so they do not spoil before sale?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ toɔ koni ekafite dani ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: After fermenting the cocoa beans properly for six days, dry them evenly under direct sunlight on raised wooden platforms and keep them in clean jute bags in a well-ventilated area off the bare ground.
ga: Beni afee kookoo ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ gbii enumɔ sɛɛ. Egbi pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tso ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ. ni okɛto jute kotoku ni mli tse mli yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How can I get my plantain plants to produce bigger and heavier bunches?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-plantain lɛ awo jwɛi wuji ni tsii?

english: To get larger plantain bunches, remove excess suckers so only two or three grow per plant stand, clear surrounding weeds, and apply compost or poultry manure around the plant base.
ga: Kɛji ootao ni oná plantains kuu ni da lɛ Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni anyɛ adu 2-3 pɛ yɛ tso kome mli. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii abɔle tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa tree turning yellow and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often indicate a lack of key soil nutrients like nitrogen, insufficient water during dry spells, or early signs of pest attacks and cocoa diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni nu hu faaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. loo mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai eba.

english: Why is it important for me to prune extra branches off my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata cacao tso ni eda lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to let in air and sunlight, which reduces damp conditions that cause black pod disease and encourages the tree to direct energy into pod formation.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi. ni ekanya tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ amaje koni ekɛfee pods

english: What should I do if insects start eating my young cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji kooloi bɔi mi-kookoo bibii lɛ yeli?

english: Inspect your farm regularly to catch pests like capsids early, remove infested pods, keep weeds low, and consult an extension officer for approved spraying schedules.
ga: Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa koni omɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids mra. Jiemɔ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ jwɛi lɛ shi kɛyashɛ he ko ni baa shi. ni okɛ extension nitsulɔi lɛ agba sane koni amɛna be ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ.

english: What key habits make a farmer successful enough to win best-farmer awards in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni ji sui titrii ni haa okwaafonyo yeɔ omanye bɔ ​​ni sa ni enáa Okwaafonyo ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ he jweremɔ nii lɛ?

english: Successful farmers practice timely weed control, prune trees regularly, maintain shade balance, apply correct soil nutrients, and manage pests before they destroy crop yields.
ga: Okwaafoi ni yeɔ omanye lɛ tsuɔ jwɛi akudɔmɔ he nii yɛ be naa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei daa. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ Okɛ niyenii ni sa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii. ni akwɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting them under shade trees like plantains protects them from extreme heat, traps moisture, and helps them build strong roots before facing direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo shishi tamɔ plantains lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa edɔ fe nine, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shishifãi lɛ dani hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why does my yam crop produce bigger tubers when I give the vines wooden tall sticks to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ naa bulbs wuji beni mikɛ ivy niji kakadaji ha amɛ koni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to make food in their leaves. When you stake them, their leaves spread out to catch more sun, sending extra energy down underground to swell the tubers.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii yɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ Amɛbaai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Etsuɔ hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ ko kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni eha tsɔne lɛ mli alɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow fast. Heavy rain can also wash this nutrient out of the topsoil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nɛkɛ niyenii kpakpa nɛɛ he kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow much better when I plant cowpeas in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ fɛo waa kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are natural soil restorers. Their roots take nitrogen out of the air and put it into the soil, feeding nearby maize while their broad leaves cover the soil to keep it cool and wet.
ga: Cowpea ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛhaa lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha edɔ ni edɔ.

english: Cassava roots need soil with good air space to survive. When water collects around the roots and stays for a long time, the roots choke, rot, and get infected by soil fungi.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baatsi, amɛbaagboi ni amɛkɛ ŋmeii baawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by sudden dry spells or extreme heat. To save water and energy, the plant sheds its flowers instead of spending energy to produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ kɛji trukaa hulutsoo be loo latsaa ni naa wa ko ha fɔfɔi lɛ miihao. Bɔni afee ni akɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ akafite Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo yibii.

english: Why do caterpillars attack the hidden inner leaves of my maize leaves instead of the outer ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa ŋmãa baa mli moŋ fe ŋmãa baa kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: The inner leaves of the maize stem are tender, sweet, and hold moisture. Pests like armyworms hide deep inside to stay protected from hot sunlight, dry air, and birds while feeding on soft plant tissue.
ga: Abele tsei amli baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe ŋɔɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni mli edɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi kɛ okpoi ahe be mli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up into small tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often a plant's defense response to tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips, or viruses carried by them. The leaves twist and curl because the insects damage the veins as they suck out nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji bɔ ni tso lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa yɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips lɛ ahe. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni kɛ amɛ baa lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛhe ejaakɛ kooloi bibii fiteɔ fãji lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛmuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back so much faster than my crops even during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, yɛ hɔmɔ be mli po lɛ?

english: Wild weeds have deep, tough root systems designed by nature to search for small amounts of hidden water deep underground. Farm crops have weaker roots that depend heavily on surface soil moisture.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni adebɔɔ fee koni ena nu bibii ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Okwaafoi adumɔi yɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ waa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily once the fruit bunch gets large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep, woody taproots like oak or mango trees. Their roots spread shallowly near the topsoil, so a heavy fruit bunch makes them top-heavy and easy for wind to tip over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ oak loo mango tsei. Amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, aduawai akutsei ni tsii lɛ baaha amɛfee tsiimɔ ni ebaafee mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatswa amɛ shi.

english: How long does a new coconut tree take before it starts bearing fruit that I can harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso hee woɔ yibii kɛyashiɔ be mli ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: Dwarf coconut varieties usually start producing fruit in 3 to 4 years, while traditional tall varieties take about 6 to 7 years to yield fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni ji dwarf lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ blema lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What type of coconuts should I harvest if I want to make oil from them?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei esa akɛ makpa kɛji miitao mafee fɔ?

english: Fully mature, brown coconuts yield the most oil because the meat inside is thick and dry, whereas young green coconuts contain mostly water and thin meat.
ga: Kokooi ni eda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni haa fɔ feɔ babaoo ejaakɛ loo lɛ mli edɔ ni egbi. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ babaoo yɛ nu kɛ loo ni mli tseee.

english: Is it better to extract coconut oil by hand or use a simple machine?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ niji baajie ŋmei fɔ loo akɛ tsɔne ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii?

english: Manual boiling works for small batches, but using a simple manual or motorized oil press extracts more oil from the meat and saves a lot of time.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ niji afee wain ni akɛfeɔ wain bibii. Shi kɛ okɛ tsɔne ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii loo tsɔne ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ mu lɛ tsu nii lɛ Enɛ baaye abua ni ojie mu babaoo kɛjɛ loo lɛ mli ni ebaaha okɛ be babaoo akafite.

english: Why do my mango trees drop so many flowers before they can turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo dani etsɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Mango trees drop flowers naturally to reduce load, but excessive dropping is usually caused by dry soil during flowering or insect pests like thrips and fungal infections like anthracnose.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni ekɛba jatsu lɛ shi. Shi bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ thrips kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ anthracnose ji nɔ ni kɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ shi fe nine.

english: Should I prune my mango trees, and how does it help the fruit growth?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ mi mango tso lɛ mli? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ebaanyɛ eye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Yes, pruning dead or overcrowded branches allows sunlight and air to reach the inner canopy, which reduces fungal diseases and encourages larger, healthier fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei niji ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baatsi hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso yibii lɛ daraa ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell when my mangoes are mature enough to harvest for selling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-mango lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa koni ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Mangoes are ready to harvest when the skin color turns light green or yellowish near the stem base, the shoulders of the fruit become broad, and the flesh turns yellow inside.
ga: Mango lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji ehewolo su lɛ batsɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Yibii lɛ atsitsii lɛ mli kwɔ fe no. ni loo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Can I plant cassava or vegetables between my young coconut trees while I wait for them to mature?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei loo aduawai yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Yes, intercropping short-season crops like legumes, maize, or cassava between young trees gives you food and income while suppressing weeds until the trees grow large enough to shade the ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaha oná niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be mli ni ojieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How many laborers do I need to clear and maintain a one-acre tree farm?
ga: Nitsulɔi enyiɛ ehe baahia ni mafolɔ tso ŋmɔ ni dalɛ ji acre 1 lɛ mli ni makwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: For a one-acre farm, one or two dedicated farm workers can handle regular weeding and maintenance, though extra daily labor is usually helpful during initial land clearing and harvest periods.
ga: Kɛha ŋmɔ ni dalɛ ji acre 1 lɛ, ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔ kome loo enyɔ ni ejɔɔ amɛhe nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsu jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ daa ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe nii. Eyɛ mli akɛ bei pii lɛ, sɛɛnamɔ baa daa gbi nitsumɔ kroko nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kpamɔ bei amli mra moŋ, shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young coconut trees turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ashishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves often mean the plant is lacking key nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, or that the soil is getting waterlogged during heavy rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium bɛ tso lɛ mli. Aloo nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: How do I prevent my harvested mangoes from rotting before I can process or sell them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mango ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite dani matsu he nii loo mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Harvest mangoes with a small piece of stem attached to prevent sap leaking, store them in cool shade, and pack them flat in ventilated plastic crates instead of heavy bags.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ mango kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni okɛbaakpɛtɛ he lɛ nɔ. Eji koni akɛtsi mliki ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Okɛto he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. ni akɛwoɔ plastic adekai ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli yɛ kotokui ni tsii amli.

english: What should I check on a piece of land near a river before I agree to farm on it?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ makwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ faa ko nɔ dani makpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ mafee ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: You should check how high the river rises during the heavy rains to avoid flooding, and make sure the soil drains water well so your crop roots do not drown and rot.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ bɔ ni faa lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ ehaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli koni nu afua akaho. Ni kwɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ akabote nu mli ni amɛkafite.

english: Why do my crops dry up and die so quickly during the dry season if I do not water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kɛji mifɔɔɔ amɛ nu lɛ?

english: Crops need water to carry nutrients from the soil up into their stems and leaves. In the dry season, the hot sun pulls moisture out of the leaves faster than the roots can find it in dry ground, causing the plant to wilt.
ga: Tsei hia nu koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya amɛshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ana yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. haa tsei gboiɔ

english: If I pull water from a nearby river to water my farm, will my crops grow better than depending on rainfall alone?
ga: Kɛji mijie nu kɛjɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli koni mikɛha ŋmɔ lɛ Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe nɔ ni mikɛ mihe aaafɔ̃ nugbɔshiimɔ pɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, because drawing water from a river allows you to give your crops steady moisture whenever they need it, allowing them to grow year-round even when the rains stop.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ nu ni ooojɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ haa onibii lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be ni ehe baahia amɛ. Ehaa tsei kwɛ̃ɔ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa po.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting too much water from my irrigation system?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu babaoo kɛmiijɛ mi-irrigation system lɛ mli?

english: When crops get too much water, their leaves usually turn pale yellow, look weak or limp, and the stems near the ground may become soft and rotten due to lack of air in the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ loo enyiɛɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ Ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee blɛoo ni amɛgboi kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Is river water safe to put directly onto my young crop seedlings?
ga: Ani faa mli nu lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛbaawo mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: River water is generally safe and contains helpful natural nutrients, but if the water is very muddy after heavy rains, the thick silt can coat tender leaves and block them from receiving sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, faa mli nu lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe, ni adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ mli. Shi kɛji nu lɛ mli ewo muji waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ, sũ ni mli edɔ baanyɛ aha baai bibii ahe ni etsĩ amɛnaa koni amɛkashɛ hulu la he.

english: What happens to crop roots when the soil around them stays soaked in water for many days?
ga: Mɛni baa shishifãi ni adu lɛ anɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Ani awo lɛ nu mli gbii babaoo?

english: Roots need oxygen from air pockets in the soil to breathe. When soil stays soaked for too long, air is pushed out, causing the roots to drown, turn black, and lose the ability to feed the plant.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli koni amɛmu. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Abaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛje kpo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛfeɔ duŋ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛha tso lɛ niyenii dɔŋŋ.

english: Can I grow vegetables during the hot dry season if I have a company help me set up water pumps?
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ani manyɛ madu aduawai kɛji miyɛ nitsumɔhe ko ni eye ebua mi ni mato nu pɔmp?

english: Yes, dry season farming with irrigation is often very successful because crops get strong, full sunlight all day without high risk of fungal diseases that usually spread during heavy rainy seasons.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be mli okwaayeli ni akɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ omanye waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ naa hulu la ni fa yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli. Oshara ko bɛ ni ji fungal helai ni bei pii lɛ egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why are my crops growing tall and thin with few fruits under the big trees near the riverbank?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ kuku ni aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ faa lɛ naa lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make their own food. Under heavy tree shade, plants stretch upward searching for light instead of putting energy into growing strong stems and heavy fruits.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee amɛ niyenii. Yɛ tsei ni mli tse lɛ ashishi Tso lɛ shwieɔ shi koni eyatao la lɛ. Mohu ɔ, e kɛ he wami tsuɔ ní kɛ haa tsohi nɛ a he wa kɛ yiblii nɛ tsii wawɛɛɔ.

english: Is it better to pour water directly around the base of the crop or spray it over the leaves?
ga: Ani ebafeŋ nɔ ni hi akɛ ooofɔse nu kɛbɔle he? kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ Aloo okɛshwie baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Pouring water around the base is better because roots absorb the water directly, and keeping the leaves dry helps prevent leaf diseases and fungal spots from forming.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Ni kɛ́ aha baai lɛ agbi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa.

english: If I expand my farm to cover more land, will each crop need the same amount of water as before?
ga: Kɛji migbala miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eshɛ he babaoo Ani tso henɔ fɛɛ henɔ baabi nu abɔ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ?

english: Each individual plant needs the same amount of water, but a larger field will require a much larger water supply and better equipment to ensure water reaches every row evenly without starving any plants.
ga: Nu ni he hiaa tso fɛɛ tso lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Shi hei ni dara lɛ baabi nu jɛɛhe ni da kwraa kɛ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni nu lɛ ayashɛ ŋwɛi ŋta fɛɛ ŋta nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ekomefeemɔ ni hɔmɔ yeee tsei lɛ
