english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen. When the soil runs out of nutrients, the plant pulls food from its older leaves at the bottom to feed the growing new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye nitrogen. Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli koni ekɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants fall off when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry weather to save water and protect itself from harsh heat. The plant is resting its top half while keeping the roots underground safe until the rains return.
ga: Yucca shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. Tso lɛ jɔɔ ehe yɛ eshishigbɛ fã lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do I need to make raised soil mounds before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose, and warm soil so the tubers can expand easily without rotting. Mounds keep excess rainwater away from the tubers and collect the rich topsoil together for better growth.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli edɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni amɛfiteee. Gɔŋ lɛ baaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ akashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa lɛ mli awa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings wilting and dying under the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane hulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft roots and cannot survive full sunlight. They need fast-growing shade crops like plantains planted nearby to shield them from burning sun until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi yɛ blɛoo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ gbɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are there big holes in my pepper leaves when I cannot see any bugs on the plant during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ yɛ buji wuji lɛ? Beni minaaa kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli?

english: Certain pests, like cutworms and armyworms, hide under the dirt during the hot daylight hours and come out to eat leaf foliage at night when it is cool.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui komɛi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ lɛ amli Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye baai gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when the soil stays too dry or when daytime temperatures get too hot. The plant sacrifices the flowers to conserve energy and keep the main stem alive.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lolo loo be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔɔ tsɔ. Tsei kɛ fɔfɔi shaa afɔle koni amɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛha tso lɛ yitso lɛ ahi wala mli.

english: Why do weeds make my maize grow tall and thin with weak stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-abele lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa eshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal light, water, and soil nutrients from your crops. When weeds surround your maize, the maize stretches too fast to reach sunlight above the weeds, making the stem weak.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ la, nu, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni jwɛi ebɔle o-ŋma lɛ he lɛ Ŋmã lɛ baakpã mli oya tsɔ ni ekɛ hulu lɛ baashɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: Why does rain water stay sitting on top of my farmland for days after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Water stays on top when the soil is packed too tightly or contains heavy clay that blocks drainage. This drowns the crop roots because roots need air spaces in the soil to breathe.
ga: Nu hiɔ shi yɛ nɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo eyɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same soil every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and attracts pests that like maize. Rotating with beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmãa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I avoid spraying liquid fertilizer or chemicals on my crops during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ he?

english: In the hot sun, liquid sprays dry up too quickly before the leaf can soak them in, and the hot sun on wet leaves can burn and damage the plant surface.
ga: hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ dani baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tso lɛ hiɛ.

english: Yellow, curled leaves on cassava are usually a sign of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties helps keep your farm healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle yucca he lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: White powdery spots are caused by fungal diseases that thrive in damp, humid weather. Spacing your plants further apart allows air to flow through and reduces the humidity around the leaves.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni edɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ powder spots yɛŋ baa. Kɛ́ ajie tsei lɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know if my maize is yellowing because of poor soil or too much rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ efee ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ hewɔ?

english: If yellowing starts at the tips of older leaves and moves down the center in a V-shape, the soil lacks nitrogen. If the whole field turns pale uniformly during heavy rains, the soil is waterlogged and roots cannot breathe.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ anaagbɛ ni amɛyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ yɛ V su mli lɛ, no lɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ bafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaho ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu.

english: Why should I place fertilizer close to the roots instead of scattering it everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛshwã he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer near the base of the crop ensures the roots absorb the nutrients directly before heavy rains wash them away or surrounding weeds consume them.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ, ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ amɛ loo jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together on the same land with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ wɔɔfee ekome kɛdu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally feeds the maize crop and improves overall soil fertility.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees have large leaves that act as living shade umbrellas to protect the cocoa seedlings during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up into a tube during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling in the afternoon heat is the plant's natural way of reducing water loss. If the leaves unroll by evening, the plant is fine, but if they stay rolled up, your crop needs watering.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa nu ni efiteɔ lɛ baa shi. Kɛji baai lɛ shwie shi gbɛkɛ Tso lɛ hi. Shi kɛji eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo Oŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia nu.

english: Why do farmers spread dry grass on top of the soil around young garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi shwieɔ jwɛi amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛbɔleɔ ŋmeii ahe yɛ amɛbɔɔi amli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, retains soil moisture during dry spells, and stops weeds from sprouting.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃

english: Pruning removes unnecessary foliage so sunlight and air can penetrate the canopy, which prevents black pod disease and encourages the tree to produce more cocoa pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ atsɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ black pod hela lɛ naa, ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo kookoo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do my harvested yams start to rot quickly after I store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya beni mikɛtoɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised during harvest or kept in hot, poorly ventilated spaces. Storing them on raised racks in a shaded, well-ventilated barn prevents fungal decay.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo akɛto hei ni edɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛto shwɛmɔhei ni awó nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akafee nɔ ko.

english: Young cocoa leaves turn yellow and fall off mainly due to excessive direct sunlight, lack of soil moisture during dry spells, or a shortage of nutrients like nitrogen. Providing shade trees or plantains shields young cocoa plants and preserves soil moisture.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa titri. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli loo niyenii mli nibii tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ, ni haa ŋmɔtɔ loo dumɔwui yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I harvest more corn from my farm?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmãa babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting maize too closely causes the plants to compete for sunlight, water, and nutrients, resulting in thin stems and small or missing ears. Proper spacing yields larger, healthier cobs and a higher total harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no baaha eshishifãi lɛ afee bibii kɛ toi bibii loo elaaje. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha cob lɛ agbo aba. Na hewalɛ kpakpa ni okpa nii babaoo

english: Why should I make large soil mounds for my yams instead of planting them on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ agbo kɛha mi-sweet potatoes lɛ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mounding loosens the soil, making it easy for yam tubers to expand freely into large shapes. Loose soil mounds also promote good drainage, preventing the tubers from sitting in pooled water and rotting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaawo lɛ haa sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji. Gɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Tsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote nu jɛɛhei amli ni amɛkafite.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before setting any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when stress occurs from high afternoon temperatures, prolonged dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Maintaining steady watering and providing light shade helps flowers stay on the vine to form fruit.
ga: Tomato baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ hao lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ. loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ hulutsoo fioo yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do ragged holes appear in my young maize leaves early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the central leaf funnel. Checking the plants early and applying control measures directly into the leaf whorl protects the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa ŋmeii bibii amli. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ tsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the afternoon heat even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Hot afternoon air causes water to evaporate from pepper leaves faster than the roots can drink it up, leading to temporary wilting. Adding grass mulch around the plant base keeps the soil cool and moist longer.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ baai amli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Mulching ni ooobɔle otsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and look twisted during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl to reduce their surface area and conserve water during heat. However, curling can also be caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like whiteflies that multiply quickly in hot, dry conditions.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi ni amɛhiɛ nu mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Shi kɛlɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies, ni feɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha curling lɛ aba.

english: Is it good to plant cassava on the same plot where I just harvested maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akpa ŋmãa yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nutrients from the soil, especially nitrogen. While cassava can grow in poorer soils, adding poultry manure or compost before planting cassava will restore the soil and lead to bigger tubers.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ moŋ, Shi kɛ akɛ kooloi ashishi loo ŋmei fata he dani adu ŋmei lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmei lɛ afee wuji.

english: Why does my maize grow tall and leafy green but fail to produce big cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ shi enyɛɛɛ ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer encourages lush stem and leaf growth at the expense of grain development. Balanced fertilization with phosphorus and potassium is needed for strong cob formation.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli fe nine lɛ haa amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ. Fosfɔs kɛ potassium ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni ja lɛ he miihia koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Can I save seeds from the high-yielding hybrid maize I harvested this year to plant next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni mikpa afi nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their special strength in the next generation, leading to uneven growth and lower yields. Buying fresh certified hybrid seeds each planting season guarantees high productivity.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ kroko yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi. Dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ baaha yibiiwoo babaoo aba.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun and cannot regulate heat well. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a protective canopy that keeps the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi, ni amɛhe esako yɛ dɔlɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ masɛi lɛ ni aduɔ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo bibioo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Can I plant maize and cowpeas together on the same field at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cowpeas is very beneficial. Cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which naturally feeds the maize and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛfutu mli lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Cowpeas mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the center out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a primary sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize requires heavy nitrogen to grow strong leaves; adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores healthy green growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi titri ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ni tsii he miihia ŋmãa koni ebaa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cowpea farm grow plenty of green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cowpeas to put all their energy into growing foliage instead of flowers. Limiting rich fertilizers encourages the plant to switch its energy to pod production.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni yɔɔ lɛ amli ni atsiɔ naa lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛtsake hewalɛ amɛwo pod feemɔ mli.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, or a virus spread by them. Sprinkling neem oil extract or using recommended pest controls stops the insects and saves new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Neem mu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ helai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsuɔ he nii lɛ tsuɔ nii. Ehaa kooloi bibii lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe ni ehaa baai heei ni daraa lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and rot before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition, called blossom-end rot, happens when tomato plants cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering. Consistent watering keeps nutrient flow steady so the fruits develop properly.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ baa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be koni eha tso yibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai bibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of insect pollinators can cause tomato flowers to drop off. Mulching the base to retain soil moisture and allowing good airflow helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii baa lɛ ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato fɔfɔi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava roots get watery and soft if left in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Mature cassava roots absorb excess water from waterlogged soil, which breaks down their stored starch. Harvesting promptly when roots mature prevents them from becoming watery and losing market value.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. ni baafite ŋmei ni ato lɛ Nikpamɔ kɛji shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa pɛ kɛkɛ ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee nɔ ni nu bɛ mli ni amɛkafee nɔ ni jara wa.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers develop soft rot soon after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ fiteɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akpa lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if harvested with cuts or stored while wet. Curing tubers in a dry, shaded area for a few days before storage thickens their skin and heals minor cuts, keeping out decay fungi.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmeii amli loo akɛto ni efɔ. Kɛ́ atsa ŋmeii lɛ yɛ he ko ni egbi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli gbii fioo komɛi dani akɛto lɛ, ebaaha hewolo lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaatsa pilamɔi bibii koni ŋmeii akafite.

english: Why does my harvested produce spoil quickly when packed tightly in bags right after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛwo kotokui amli shiŋŋ beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly picked crops generate natural heat and moisture. Stacking them tightly without airflow creates a hot, damp environment that speeds up spoilage and molds; proper ventilation keeps crops fresh longer.
ga: Nibii ni adu ehee Ekɛ adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo baa. Nibii ni akɛtoɔ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ baaha fitemɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aya hiɛ oya. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my rice crops need so much water on the field compared to my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ he hiaa nu babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛ akɛto mi ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally thrive in waterlogged conditions because water prevents weed growth, keeps the roots cool, and makes it easier for the plant to absorb essential minerals from the soil compared to dryland crops.
ga: Omɔ tsei daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ejaakɛ nu tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛbaajie minerals ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my green crops starting to turn pale yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal that the crop is starving for nitrogen—a key plant nutrient needed for green leaves—or that heavy water accumulation in the soil is suffocating the plant's roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli Aloo muji ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: What happens to my harvested rice if I store it without drying it under the sun properly?
ga: Mɛni baaba mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛto ni hulu lɛ shɛɛɛ mihe jogbaŋŋ?

english: Wet rice grains trap moisture inside, creating an ideal environment for mold and fungi to grow, which quickly rots the harvested grains and makes them smell bad and unfit for sale or eating.
ga: Omɔ ŋmaa ni efɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ agbo oya. Ni enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ ŋmɔɔ ni esaaa akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ loo ayeɔ.

english: How does spreading cow or poultry manure on my farmland make my crops give a better harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo kooloi ashishifã ni mikɛfataa miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛnáa ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: Animal manure feeds tiny beneficial organisms in the dirt and slowly releases rich nutrients into the soil, helping crop roots grow deeper and hold water much better during dry weather.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã lɛ yeɔ nibii fioo komɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni ejieɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli fiofio. Ehaa tsei ashishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds make my main crops grow thin and produce smaller fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ miiha mitso titri lɛ miifee bibioo ni ewo yibii bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds act as aggressive thieves on your farm; they rapidly drink up the soil water, block sunlight, and steal fertilizer away from your crops, leaving your plants with too few resources to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛnuɔ sũ mli nu oya, amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa, ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, otsei lɛ baaná nibii fioo ko pɛ ni baaha amɛdara waa.

english: Why should I space out my seeds properly instead of planting many of them closely together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala midumɔwui lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu babaoo Ha dumɔwui lɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for light and underground nutrients, resulting in weak, crowded stalks that yield small or empty heads.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ baawuu kɛha niyenii ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe wa ni haa yitsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my young crop leaves droop and wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense heat, leaves lose moisture into the air faster than the roots can pull water out of the ground; the plant wilts on purpose to fold its surface away from the hot sun and conserve water.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Baai lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei gboiɔ kɛ yiŋtoo akɛ amɛbaafolɔ amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni amɛbu nu he.

english: Why do worms and insects prefer eating the newest tender leaves of my crops first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Fresh, young leaves are soft and packed with water and natural sugars, making them much easier for insects to digest and feed on compared to old, tough leaf tissues.
ga: Baai bibii ni afee ehee lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni adebɔɔ mli nu kɛ sugar eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa kooloi akɛ amɛaaye nii ni amɛye. Kɛ akɛto baa fãji ni egbɔ ni wa lɛ ahe

english: Why is it beneficial for my soil if I plant groundnuts or beans after harvesting cereal crops like rice or maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei loo ŋmei beni mikpa ŋmãa nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa sɛɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans pull natural nitrogen gas from the air and store it back into the earth, which recharges the soil's fertility for the next season's crop without requiring extra fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii gbalaa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fata he he ehiaaa.

english: How does using a processing machine or mill on harvested rice help increase the money I get at the market?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsɔne ni akɛkpaa ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛkpaa ŋmãa ni mikɛtsu nii lɛ aha shika ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ jara nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Milling machines remove the hard outer hulls and clean off the chaff cleanly without breaking the grain, producing high-grade, attractive white rice that buyers in markets pay top money for.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshãa ŋmei lɛ jieɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa lɛ, ni etsuuɔ ŋmei lɛ he jogbaŋŋ ni ekuuu ŋmei lɛ. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmãa yɛŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mɛi ni heɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ woɔ shika babaoo kɛhaa.

english: As tree crops age, their vascular systems become less efficient at pulling up water and soil nutrients, causing their yield to naturally decline over time.
ga: Beni tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ daraa lɛ Amɛ lá fãji lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ.

english: If I remove an old crop and plant a new seedling in the same spot, why does the new seedling struggle to grow?
ga: Kɛji mijie tso momo lɛ ni midu dumɔwu hee yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui heei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Old crops drain specific nutrients from that spot and can leave behind pests in the soil, so new seedlings need soil enrichment or temporary shade to establish well.
ga: Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ nakai he lɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ sũ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui heei biɔ shikpɔŋ tsakemɔ loo be kukuoo mli shade koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crop is just stressed from dry weather or if it is too old and needs to be replaced?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miihao kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli? Aloo etsɛ tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni atsake?

english: Stressed plants usually recover their leaves after rain, whereas aging plants show permanent leaf loss, dead branches, and consistently low yields even when water is plentiful.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni haoɔ lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni edara lɛ jieɔ baai ni fiteɔ daa, niji ni egboi, kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi be fɛɛ be kɛ nu babaoo po yɔɔ mli lɛ kpo.

english: Why do some of my harvested maize grains turn dark or moldy while others stay clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi miitsɔ ediŋŋ loo amɛmiifee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu ahe tse lolo lɛ?

english: High moisture levels during harvest or improper drying allow fungi to grow on the grains, which causes dark spots, mold, and a lower quality grade when selling.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo egbimɔ ni esaaa lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni baa shi baa kɛji akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do crops harvested from the same field end up with different sizes and weights?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ naagbee lɛ amɛdalɛ kɛ amɛtsiimɔ yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Differences in soil nutrients across the field, uneven water supply, and shade from nearby trees cause individual plants to grow at different rates.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii mli nibii amli yɛ ŋmɔji amli Nu babaoo kɛ hulutsoo ni jɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee Enɛ haa tsei srɔtoi daa yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli.

english: How does harvesting my cassava early affect its quality when it gets measured for sale?
ga: Kasava ni akpaa mra Te ebaaná bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ asusu he koni ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Crops harvested before full maturity have not built up maximum starch, making the roots lighter in weight, watery, and inferior in quality grade.
ga: Tsei ni akpaa dani amɛdara lɛ ebuaaa ŋmeii babaoo naa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, nu bɛ mli, ni amɛhe ehiaaa tsɔ.

english: Why do my crops look very healthy and green with big leaves but fail to produce large fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ baai wuji shi enyɛɛɛ ewo yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil encourages plants to grow green leaves instead of flowers and fruits, which require balanced phosphorus and potassium to grow well.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai najiaŋ. ni biɔ ni fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium ahi shi jogbaŋŋ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my freshly harvested cassava roots start going bad just a few days after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni akpa ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli beni atsa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Unlike yams, cassava roots lack a thick protective skin, causing rapid internal deterioration and spoilage within two to three days after harvest unless processed.
ga: Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ sweet potato lɛ, cassava shishifãi bɛ hewolo ni mli wa ni buɔ mɔ he. Enɛ haa emli fiteɔ oya ni efiteɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. ja etsɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli

english: Why do my vegetables wilt so quickly if I pick them during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ ajie aduawai yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ, amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Crops rapidly lose water through leaf pores in hot sunlight, so harvesting during high heat causes sudden wilting; harvesting in the cool morning keeps water inside the crop.
ga: Tsei laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli ŋmeii amli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akpa amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, ebaaha amɛgbi trukaa. Nikpamɔ yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why do buyers pay me less for my produce when everyone in my district harvests at the exact same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ mi nyɔmɔ fioo yɛ nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe lɛ? Akɛni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ kpaa nii yɛ be kome mli hewɔ lɛ

english: When a large amount of crop enters the market at once, supply exceeds local demand, which naturally drives buying prices down until produce becomes scarce again.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo bote jara nɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ, Nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ baaho nɔ ni maŋ lɛ mli taoɔ lɛ he. Enɛ baaha nɔ ni aheɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛyashi nibii ni afee lɛ baafee nɔ ni faaa ekoŋŋ.

english: How does a little bit of rain right after planting help my young seedlings?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ fioo ni nɛɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Early light rain settles the soil around the roots and gives young seedlings the immediate moisture they need to build strong roots and start growing healthy leaves.
ga: Nugbɔ fioo ni nɛɔ leebi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha dumɔwui bibii lɛ aná nu ni he hiaa amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa. ni amɛjeɔ baai ni mli wa lɛ shishi

english: If I plant my seedlings in March but the heavy rains do not start until May, will my crops die?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu dumɔwui yɛ March mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ waa kɛyashi May hu? Ani midumɔ nii lɛ baagboi?

english: A delay in rainfall can severely stress young plants, causing slow growth or wilting. However, if they get occasional light showers, they may survive until the main rains begin in May.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei bibii lɛ aná haomɔ ni naa wa. Enɛ haa edaa fiofio loo egbɔjɔɔ. Shi, kɛji nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ, Amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ titri lɛ baaje shishi yɛ May mli.

english: Should I plant my crop seeds before the rains start or wait until after the first heavy rainfall?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui dani nugbɔ lɛ aje shishi loo mamɛ kɛyashi klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is usually safest to wait until the first good rain has thoroughly soaked the soil, ensuring seeds have enough moisture to germinate without drying out in the hot earth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ kpakpa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: What happens to my freshly planted crops if no rain falls at all during the first few months?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii ni midu ehee lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli?

english: Without any rain or hand-watering, young seedlings cannot absorb nutrients and will dry up and die, which means you will have to replant the field when rains return.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ loo akɛ niji shwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. ni ebaagbi ni egbo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe baahia ni odu ekoŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: If the rains arrive late in May instead of March, can my crops still produce a good harvest?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ba yɛ May naagbee gbɛ yɛ March najiaŋ lɛ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai lolo?

english: Yes, crops can still produce a good harvest if the rains remain steady once they start, though late rains may reduce the overall yield compared to a full rainy season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai lolo kɛji nugbɔ lɛ tee nɔ ehi shi yɛ shishijee mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aba shi kɛ akɛto nugbɔshiimɔ be muu lɛ fɛɛ he moŋ.

english: Is light rainfall during a hot dry spell enough to keep my young crops alive?
ga: Ani nugbɔ fioo ni nɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahi shi?

english: Light rainfall is often enough to keep seedlings alive and prevent them from completely dying, but they will need deeper rains soon after to grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ fioo ni nɛɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi ni etsĩ amɛnaa koni amɛkagboi kwraa. Shi nugbɔ ni naa wa babaoo he baahia amɛ yɛ no sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will a long dry period early in the season affect how much food my crops produce later?
ga: Ani hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni baaba yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baaná niyenii ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo lɛ nɔ hewalɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, early drought usually reduces crop yields because young plants waste energy trying to survive the heat instead of building strong stems and roots for high production.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni baa mra lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bibii fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tso ɔmɛ nɛ a he wa konɛ a ná yiblii babauu.

english: How can I tell if my young crop seedlings are suffering from a lack of rainfall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ midumɔwui bibii lɛ miina nugbɔ?

english: Young plants lacking water will show drooping or curling leaves, yellowing stems, slow growth, and the dry soil around them may begin to crack.
ga: Dumɔwui ni nu efo mli lɛ baatsɔɔ baai ni egbee shi loo ebɔle amɛhe, tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛdaraa blɛoo, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. baanyɛ aje shishi egbɛ eshwa

english: What can I do to protect my newly planted seedlings while waiting for the rainy season to fully begin?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mabu midumɔwui heei ni midu lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ?

english: You can protect young plants by covering the soil around them with dry grass or palm leaves (mulching) to trap soil moisture and shade them from direct sunlight.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu tsei bibii ahe kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni oookɛwo mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo tso baai (mulch) aha nɔ koni emɔmɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni etsĩ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: If my seedlings dry up because the rains were delayed, how do I know if I need to replant my farm?
ga: Kɛji mi dumɔwui lɛ gĩ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ hewɔ Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ehe miihia ni adu ekoŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If more than half of your seedlings have turned brown, dried out completely, and show no green leaves after a light rain, it is time to clear them and replant fresh seeds.
ga: Kɛji akɛ odumɔwui lɛ ateŋ nɔ ni fe fã batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, amɛgbi kwraa, ni amɛbɛ baai eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ. Be eshɛɛ ni abaajie ni adu dumɔwui heei.

english: How much oil can I expect to get from processing one ton of my fresh oil palm fruit bunches?
ga: Mu enyiɛ manyɛ maná kɛjɛ mu tsei heei ni afee lɛ tɔn kome ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli?

english: On average, one ton of good quality fresh oil palm fruit bunches yields roughly 180 to 200 kilograms of palm oil, which fills about one standard drum depending on how well the fruits are processed.
ga: Kɛ aja mli lɛ, tsofa-kɛ-ŋma hee ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ tɔn kome baaha tsofa-kɛ-ŋma he aaafee kilogram 180 kɛyashi 200, ni ji aaafee tsɔne kome ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Edamɔ bɔ ni atsuɔ aduawai lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ ahaa lɛ nɔ.

english: How many drums of oil can I get if my farm produces over one ton of oil palm fruits?
ga: Mu barrel enyiɛ maná kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ wo mu tso ni fe tɔn kome?

english: For every 1.1 to 1.2 tons of fresh fruit bunches you harvest and process, you can generally expect to fill 1 full standard drum of oil.
ga: Kɛha aduawai heei ni okpaa ni otsuɔ he nii lɛ tɔn fɛɛ tɔn 1.1 kɛyashi 1.2 Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ gas tanki 1 awo mli.

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce large fruit bunches, but I get very little oil after milling them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ? Shi beni ashɛre tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, fɔ fioo ko pɛ anáa.

english: Low oil recovery despite big fruit bunches usually happens if the fruits are harvested before they fully ripen or if the trees suffered from poor nutrition and drought while the oil was forming inside the fruit flesh.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔ ni anáa kɛjɛɔ aduawai akui wuji amli po lɛ baa kɛji akɛ akpa aduawai lɛ dani ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Aloo kɛji niyenii ni esaaa kɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ tso lɛ he amanehulu yɛ be mli ni fɔ bua ehe naa yɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How do I know when my oil palm fruits are ripe enough to produce the maximum amount of oil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-oil palm yibii lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ ajie fɔ babaoo?

english: Oil palm fruit bunches are ready when their color turns bright orange-red and a few loose fruits start to fall to the ground naturally. Harvesting at this stage ensures the oil content is at its peak.
ga: Oil palm aduawai akui lɛ efee klalo kɛji amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ-tsuru ni mli tse. Ni aduawai ni egbee shi lɛ ekomɛi bɔi shikpɔŋ shwiemɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa mu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do my palm trees drop their young fruit bunches during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees drop their young fruit bunches during dry periods to save water and protect themselves from drought stress, which reduces the final harvest yield.
ga: Mu tsei shwieɔ amɛyibii bibii lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ he. Enɛ baaha naagbee nibii ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: What can I do on my farm to help my fruit bunches build up more oil content?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eye ebua mi aduawai akui lɛ ni amɛbua mu babaoo naa?

english: Applying fertilizers rich in potassium, keeping the base of the trees free of weeds, and ensuring proper tree pruning helps the fruits build thicker, oil-rich flesh.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Ha jwɛi akafee tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ afolɔ aduawai lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni fɔ babaoo aba mli.

english: Why does my neighbor get more drums of oil from their harvest than I do from the same acreage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ naa tsɛnsii babaoo kɛjɛɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli fe mi ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Higher oil yields often depend on planting improved high-yielding varieties like Tenera, good soil fertility, proper spacing, and processing the fruits quickly after harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔ ni anáa babaoo lɛ damɔ tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni atsake amɛ, tamɔ Tenera, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ. sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ aduawai lɛ ahe nitsumɔ oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ.

english: Does waiting several days after harvesting before pressing my palm fruits affect how much oil I get?
ga: Ani gbii babaoo ni mimɛɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani mimimɔ ŋmei yibii lɛ nɔ lɛ baaná fɔ ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Waiting too long after harvesting causes the fruit quality to spoil and reduces usable oil quality; processing within 48 hours of harvest yields the best quality and quantity of oil.
ga: Kɛ́ mɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ, efiteɔ aduawai lɛ ahe ni ehaa mu ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he tseee. Kɛ́ atsu he nii yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa mu ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ bɔ ni fa babaoo baa.

english: How many years after planting will my new oil palm trees start producing fruit bunches?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ ni mi-oil palm tso hee lɛ baabɔi yibiiwoo?

english: Improved varieties of oil palm usually start producing their first harvestable fruit bunches about 3 to 4 years after being planted in the field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ shishi aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ beni adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How do extension officers calculate how much processed oil a farmer should get from their crop harvest?
ga: Te mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ buɔ mu ni atsuɔ he nii lɛ shika ni esa akɛ okwaafoi lɛ aná kɛjɛ amɛŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he akɔntaa amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Officers use standard extraction ratios based on weight, calculating that good quality fresh fruit bunches will yield around 15% to 20% of their total weight in pure liquid oil.
ga: Amralofoi kɛ tsɔne ni akɛjieɔ nii kɛjɛɔ mli ni damɔ tsiimɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Akɛ akɔntaabuu ha akɛ, aduawai heei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha aaafee 15% kɛyashi 20% yɛ mu ni mli tse ni mli tse lɛ mli tsiimɔ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why is it recommended that I pick planting seeds from a coconut tree that is around 20 years old?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akwɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmeii ni eye aaafee afii 20 lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Trees that have survived and produced well for 20 years have proven they are resistant to local pests, diseases, and harsh weather. Using seeds from these mature mother trees gives your new farm the best chance of growing strong, high-yielding palms.
ga: Tsei ni hiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ afii 20 lɛ ejie ehe kpo akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛshi tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai kɛ jɛmɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ fɔlɔi tsei ni eda nɛɛ amli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔ hee lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How do I choose the best mature coconut from a tree to use as a seed for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmeii ni edara ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli koni mikɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Select fully ripe, dry brown coconuts from a high-yielding, healthy mother tree. When you shake the nut, you should hear water sloshing clearly inside, which shows the seed embryo is alive and well-developed.
ga: Halamɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni egbɔ kwraa kɛjɛ nyɛ tso lɛ mli koni ená yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ hewalɛnamɔ. Kɛ́ otsi ŋmeii lɛ Obaanyɛ onu nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ gbɛɛmɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛmiiya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How long can I keep a harvested seed coconut before I have to plant it in the soil?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ makɛ mi-ŋmei dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ahi shi dani ehe baahia ni madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: You can store mature seed coconuts in a cool, shaded, well-ventilated spot for a few weeks before planting. However, planting them sooner prevents the water inside from drying out, ensuring faster and healthier germination.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei dumɔwui ni eda lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ jogbaŋŋ otsii fioo komɛi dani odu. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛ́ odu mra lɛ, ebaatsi nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Enɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How long do I have to wait after planting a coconut seedling before it starts producing fruit?
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmei tso lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani ebɔi yibiiwoo?

english: It depends on the variety you plant. Fast-growing dwarf coconut varieties start fruiting in about 3 to 4 years, while traditional tall varieties take between 5 to 7 years to bear their first harvest.
ga: Edamɔ tso srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ. Dwarf ŋmeii srɔtoi ni daa oya lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema ŋmeii srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ afii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛshɛɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ he.

english: What is the difference between the short dwarf coconut trees and the tall ones?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso kuku ni ji dwarf kɛ ŋmei tso kakadaŋŋ teŋ?

english: Dwarf coconut trees produce fruit much earlier (in 3 to 4 years) and are easy to harvest because of their low height. Tall coconut trees take longer to fruit (5 to 7 years), but they usually live longer and survive drought conditions better.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ woɔ yibii oya waa (yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli) ni akpamɔ waaa yɛ bɔ ni amɛkwɔ ha lɛ hewɔ. Kokoo tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii (afii 5 kɛyashi 7) shi amɛfɔɔ shihilɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some coconut trees on the same farm take longer to fruit than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Variations in soil nutrients, access to water, sunlight exposure, or weak seed stock can slow down a tree's growth. Healthy seedlings from strong mother trees planted in good soil will always mature much faster.
ga: Tsakemɔi ni baa shikpɔŋ mli niyenii mli nibii amli Nu, hulu la, loo dumɔwui ni faaa lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni jɛ nyɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya kwraa be fɛɛ be.

english: How can I tell if a coconut on my tree is ready for drinking water versus ready for seed planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ efee klalo akɛ anuɔ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui?

english: For fresh drinking water, harvest the nut when it is green and about 7 to 8 months old. For planting seed, leave the coconut on the tree until it turns fully brown and dry, which takes about 12 months.
ga: kɛha nu kpakpa ni anuɔ Kpaa ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛye aaafee nyɔji 7 kɛyashi 8 kɛha dumɔwui adumɔ. Shi ŋmei lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi kwraa. ni heɔ aaafee nyɔji 12 lɛ

english: Can I plant crops like cassava or vegetables between my young coconut trees while waiting for them to yield?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei tamɔ ŋmei loo aduawai yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛwo yibii?

english: Yes, intercropping short-term crops like cassava, maize, or legumes between young coconut trees during their first 2 to 3 years is a good practice. It provides food and income while the trees grow and helps keep weeds away.
ga: Hɛɛ, be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ŋmãa dumɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsei bibii ateŋ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Ehaa niyenii kɛ shika be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young coconut seedlings turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the tree lacks key soil nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, or that water is sitting around the roots. Adding well-rotted animal manure and ensuring good soil drainage will bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. aloo nu yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he ni akwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How do I care for my young coconut trees during the dry season in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ Ghana?

english: Young coconut trees need extra water 2 to 3 times a week during dry months. You should also place dry leaves, grass, or coconut husks around the base of the stem (mulching) to trap soil moisture and shield roots from heat.
ga: Nu kroko he hiaa ŋmei tsei bibii shii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ otsi mli yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. Esa akɛ okɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi loo ŋmei ŋmɔji hu abɔle tso lɛ shishi (mulch) koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebu shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he.

english: Why are some of my maize plants growing much taller than others even though I planted them all on the exact same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ekomɛi daraa kwraa fe ekrokomɛi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Just like children in the same family grow at different speeds, plants compete for underground nutrients, water, and sunlight. Small differences in soil richness across your field, weed competition, or natural seed strength cause some maize plants to grow faster than their neighbors.
ga: Taakɛ gbekɛbii ni yɔɔ weku kome mli lɛ daraa yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tsei hu kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he akaŋshii mli. Srɔtofeemɔi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oyale mli lɛ mli Jwɛi akaŋshii loo adebɔɔ mli dumɔwui ahewalɛ Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei komɛi daa oya fe amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ.

english: Why are the cassava tubers I dug up from the same mound not all the same size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni mifo kɛjɛ gɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ fɛɛ dalɛ jeee ekome lɛ?

english: Cassava roots grow based on how much food energy the leaves send down and how much loose space the soil provides. Roots that find softer soil and get more sun energy grow larger, while roots blocked by hard soil or shaded leaves stay small.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ daa yɛ hewalɛ ni baai lɛ tsuɔ kɛbaa shi kɛ he ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi ni naa shikpɔŋ ni mli jɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ daa. yɛ be mli ni shishifãi ni sũ ni wa loo shade baai tsiɔ amɛnaa lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibii.

english: Why are some tomatoes on the very same branch large while others stay tiny and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato komɛi ni yɔɔ tso nine kome nɔ lɛ dara yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ji bibii ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: The tomato plant sends food and water to the first flowers that open. Those early fruits get a head start and pull in most of the nutrients, leaving the fruits that bloomed later with less energy to grow large.
ga: Tomato tsei kɛ niyenii kɛ nu majeɔ klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi ni gbeleɔ lɛ. Yibii ni baa mra fe fɛɛ Enɛɛmɛi naa amɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai ni fɔɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara.

english: Why do the leaves on some of my pepper plants turn yellow while the plants right next to them stay dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ani eji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ lolo?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean a plant is struggling to absorb nutrients like nitrogen, often due to localized soil dampness or weak root systems, while neighboring plants with stronger roots can still feed properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miitao ni eŋɔ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen, bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ he kome loo shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ hewɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa lɛ baanyɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ lolo.

english: Why are the cabbage heads growing at the edge of my garden bed so much bigger than the ones in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kaabe yitsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mibɔɔ saatso lɛ naa lɛ dara kwraa fe nɔ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbages on the outer edges have no competitors on one side, giving them extra sunlight, air, and room for their roots to spread. Plants in the middle must share nutrients and space tightly with neighbors on all sides.
ga: Kaabaji ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ bɛ akaŋshilɔi yɛ he kome. Enɛ haa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ gbɛ kɛha shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Esa akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ kɛ akutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ afãi fɛɛ lɛ aja niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I plant small maize seeds, will the corn cobs I harvest also turn out small?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmã dumɔwu bibioo ko Ani ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ hu baafee bibioo?

english: Not at all. Seed size does not limit harvest size. As long as the seed is healthy and receives good water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, it carries the full strength to grow into a tall plant with large, full cobs.
ga: Jee nakai kraa. Dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ haaa kpamɔ lɛ dalɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Shii abɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛnáa nu kpakpa, hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ náa hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛdaraa ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees drop their flowers before pods can form while other trees keep theirs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao fɔfɔi lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu hiɔ shi lɛ?

english: Dropping flowers is a cocoa tree's natural way of managing its energy. If the tree feels stressed by heat, dry weather, or lack of shade, it sheds extra flowers so it can focus on feeding only the pods it can afford to mature.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ cacao tso lɛ hewalɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ miinu he akɛ hulutsoo, kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi, loo hulutsoo ni bɛ lɛ miihao lɛ, Tso lɛ hu baafite fɔfɔi krokomɛi koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmeii ni baanyɛ adara lɛ pɛ niyenii nɔ.

english: Why do my okra plants droop and look tired during the hot afternoon sun even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tsei lɛ miiho ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni etɔ amɛ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Under intense heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it up from the soil. Drooping is the plant's temporary defense strategy to curl away from direct heat until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Drooping ji tso ko gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he yɛ be kukuoo mli, ni ji ni ekɛ ehe abɔ ehe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edɔɔ lɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why did some of my cassava stem cuttings sprout in one week while others planted next to them take a month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ otsi kome mli lɛ? be mli ni tsei komɛi ni adu yɛ Take nyɔŋ kome?

english: Cuttings taken from the mature middle section of a mother plant have more stored energy and wake up quickly. Cuttings taken from softer, younger top stems or drier bottom stems take much longer to form roots and sprout leaves.
ga: Niji ni afo kɛjɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ ni eda lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ato ni amɛtsuɔ nii oya. Nibii ni afolɔ kɛjɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi loo shishigbɛ tsei ni egbi lɛ amli lɛ baahe be babaoo dani efee shishifãi ni amɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: Why are the top plantains on a bunch much longer and thicker than the ones at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ babaoo fe plantain ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ?

english: The top group of plantains forms first and receives the strongest flow of sap directly from the stem. The fingers at the bottom develop later when the plant's nutrient flow is spread thinner across the whole bunch.
ga: Plantain kuu ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni enine shɛɔ nu ni mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daa sɛɛ mli beni tso lɛ mli niyenii lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ mlijaa bibioo yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my plantain trees turning yellow and drooping?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves usually turn yellow due to a lack of water, insufficient nitrogen in the soil, or root damage caused by pests like nematodes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nu ni bɛ hewɔ. Nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo shishifãi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes kɛbaa lɛ.

english: How long does it take for a plantain sucker to produce fruit after I plant it?
ga: Beni adu sɛɛ Be enyiɛ plantain suckers lɛ baawo yibii?

english: Plantains usually take about 9 to 12 months to flower after planting, and another 3 to 4 months for the fruit bunch to fully mature for harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ, kɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 krokomɛi dani aduawai akui lɛ shwereɔ kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why should I remove the small shoots growing around the main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: These extra shoots, called suckers, steal nutrients and water from the main plant. Removing most of them leaves more energy for the main stem to produce a larger fruit bunch.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers nɛɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛfeɔ aduawai akuu agbo.

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches. Adding extra soil around the base and supporting the stems with wooden props helps keep them upright during windstorms.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ewoɔ aduawai babaoo. Shikpɔŋ kroko ni akɛfataa shishigbɛ lɛ he kɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ mli.

english: Yes, you can intercrop cassava and plantain, but you must space them properly so the bushy cassava leaves do not block sunlight from the young plantain shoots.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei. Shi obaasumɔ ni okɛ gbɛ abɔ he jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmei baai lɛ akatsi hulu la ni jɛɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why do farmers plant plantains next to young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as living umbrellas, supplying shade and keeping the soil moist for the young cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛha kookoo tsei bibii.

english: Why does my maize grow very tall but fail to produce big cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ miida shi ewooo ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: This usually happens when maize plants are sown too close together or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like phosphorus and nitrogen during the flowering stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ nitrogen yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before fruits can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer causes heat stress, which makes pepper plants drop their flowers before fruiting.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Enɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What causes black spots to appear on my crop leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji baa tsei ahe baai anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: High rainfall and humidity create an ideal environment for fungal and bacterial diseases to spread on leaves. Proper crop spacing helps air flow and reduces leaf moisture.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa baa lɛ mli nu lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil needs compost or manure before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii dani adu?

english: If previous crops grew poorly, showed pale yellow leaves, or if the soil feels very hard and sandy, adding compost or well-rotted manure will improve soil fertility and water retention.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni wa ni eyɛ ŋã Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni ahiɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like pencils during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ pensil yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during the hottest part of the day to reduce the leaf area exposed to the sun. This natural defense helps the crop trap moisture inside and prevent water loss when soil water is low.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ naa kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt in the afternoon heat but stand upright again by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Shi shidaamɔ tɛ̃ɛ ekoŋŋ leebi?

english: Afternoon heat causes crops to lose water through their leaves faster than roots can draw it from the soil. At night, when temperatures drop, the roots catch up and refill the plant with water, restoring its upright strength.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbi gbɛkɛ, kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ baafo kɛya ŋwɛi ni amɛkɛ nu baafata tso lɛ he. Koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni efee jalɛ nii.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without producing any peppers during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pepper baaa yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ?

english: When pepper plants suffer from water stress during dry weather, they drop their flowers to save energy and protect themselves. The plant will not produce fruit until it receives enough reliable moisture.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ na nu he haomɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Amɛbaashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe. Tso lɛ wooo yibii kɛyashi ebaaná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my garden egg fruits turn small and bitter during hot, dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Heat and water shortages cause garden egg plants to produce natural defensive chemicals that give the fruit a bitter taste, while the lack of water prevents the fruit from expanding to its normal size.
ga: Dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ haa eggplant ni yɔɔ abɔɔi amli lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he. ni haa aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni bɛ lɛ baatsi aduawai lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa kɛyashɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Is it harmful to my crops if I pump too much water onto my field every day?
ga: Ani ebaaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui kɛji mikɛ nu babaoo wo miŋmɔji amli daa gbi?

english: Yes, overwatering fills all the small spaces in the soil with water and pushes out air. Without oxygen, crop roots cannot breathe and begin to rot, causing leaves to turn yellow and plants to stop growing.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni ashwieɔ nɔ fe nine lɛ baaha he bibioo ko afite. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyi kɛ nu ni etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa. Kɛji oxygen bɛ Tso shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu ni amɛbaabɔi fitemɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ wuɔfɔ ni tso lɛ kpaa dalɛ.

english: How does using a water pump to irrigate my field change the way crop roots grow in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu pɔmp ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni tsei shishifãi lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: If you water lightly on the surface every day, roots stay shallow where water is easy to reach. Giving deeper, thorough soakings encourages roots to grow deep into the ground, making the crop stronger against heat.
ga: Kɛji okɛ nu shwie nɔ fioo daa gbi lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baafee mlɛo yɛ hei ni nu baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe oya lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu lɛ wo mli jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaawo shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdara kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ yɛ dɔlɛ he

english: Why do leaf edges burn when I pump water onto my crops under full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ shãa kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ?

english: Water droplets left on leaves act like small magnifying glasses under intense heat, scorching the leaf tissue. Additionally, rapid evaporation leaves mineral salts on the leaves that cause the edges to dry up and burn.
ga: Nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase bibioo ko ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo yɛ la ni naa wa shishi. scorch leaf tissue Kɛfata he lɛ, la ni hoɔ oya lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa.

english: Why are my cassava stem cuttings taking so long to sprout after planting in dry ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca ni mifo lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ beni adu yɛ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings require soil moisture to signal their dormant buds to wake up and start growing roots. In dry ground, the stem stays inactive to prevent itself from drying out entirely and dying.
ga: Kasava tsei ni afoɔ lɛ biɔ ni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni etsɔɔ ŋmeii ni ehiɛ edɔ lɛ akɛ amɛte shi ni amɛje shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ shishi. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ tsuuu nii koni amɛkagbi kwraa ni amɛgboi.

english: Can bright lights from nearby power lines or streetlights affect how my maize crop grows at night?
ga: Ani kane ni jɛɔ tsɔnei ni bɛŋkɛ loo gbɛjegbɛ kanei amli lɛ baanyɛ aná mi-abele lɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbɛkɛ?

english: Yes, continuous bright light at night can confuse light-sensitive crops like maize or rice. It disrupts their natural dark resting period, which can confuse their internal biological clock and delay flowering or grain filling.
ga: Hɛɛ, la ni tsoɔ be fɛɛ be gbɛkɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ni nuɔ la he tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ afee shoo. Egbalaa ebɔɔ su mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ afite amɛmli wala yibii ahe ŋmɛlɛtswaa lɛ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ fɔfɔi loo dumɔwui ni eyi lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings wither so quickly if they do not get steady water during their first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛnáaa nu daa yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow root systems and delicate leaves that lose water rapidly. Without steady water during their first year, they cannot take up nutrients from the soil, causing them to dry up and die.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaai lɛ hu yɛ mlɛo ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Kɛji nu ni yaa nɔ daa bɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni haa amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong, green leaves. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-based fertilizer will restore their green color and help them grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara oya.

english: Beans and cowpeas pull natural nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When those roots decay, they feed the soil, providing free nutrients for your maize crop and reducing the need for chemical fertilizers.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ nakai shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa o-mai lɛ. ni eha tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ aba shi

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are mature enough to dig up and harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafo ni makpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: What is making ragged holes in my young corn leaves and leaving sawdust-like dirt inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni amɛshiɔ muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, a common pest in Ghana that hides inside the whorl of the maize plant. Catching them early and applying organic neem extract or recommended insecticides can save your farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei amli lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ organic neem extract loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to place tall wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Lifting the leaves off the damp soil with stakes gives them maximum sunlight and prevents wet leaves from catching rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo, ni ebaatsi baa ni efɔ lɛ naa koni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why do so many blossoms drop off my cocoa trees without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce far more flowers than they can support. Many flowers drop because of dry weather, lack of soil nutrients, or a lack of tiny insects like midges that are needed to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Fɔfɔi babaoo egbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ hewɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni he hiaa kɛha fɔfɔii amli ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Why do older farmers cover the bare soil around pepper plants with dry grass and palm leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni edara lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ lɛ? Pepper tso ni jwɛi ni egbi kɛ ŋmei baai yɔɔ mli?

english: This practice is called mulching. Covering the ground protects the soil from the harsh sun, traps soil moisture during dry spells, and keeps the ground cool so plant roots don't overheat.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi akadɔ fe nine.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and stopping the fruits from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi yibii anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Curling leaves in tomatoes are usually caused by a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects, or by extreme heat and uneven watering. Keeping whiteflies away with insecticidal soaps helps protect the plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu ŋmeii yɛji ahe nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from my farm when my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo?

english: Young crop plants have short roots and small leaves. If weeds grow next to them, the weeds steal all the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before the crop plants can get strong.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji kɛ baai bibii. Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ emasɛi Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ dani tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the soil if I plant them too deep or right before a heavy rain storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ loo adu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani ahum ba?

english: Seeds need air as well as water to wake up and grow. Planting seeds too deep or in flooded, waterlogged soil suffocates them, causing them to drown and rot before they can push through the surface.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu he miihia dumɔwui koni amɛte shi ni amɛdara. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni amɛgboi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. Without enough nitrogen, the crop cannot produce chlorophyll, which gives leaves their green color and helps the plant create energy to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ afee klorofil. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa hewalɛ kɛha dalɛ.

english: Pepper plants often shed their flowers when they suffer from high heat or drought stress. The plant sheds its blossoms to conserve energy and water so it can survive the dry period instead of spending energy on growing peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ he haomɔ hewɔ. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu ŋmɔtɔ

english: This is typically caused by bacterial wilt, a disease where microscopic bacteria enter the plant's roots and block the internal tubes that transport water, causing the plant to dry up from the inside out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni helai bibii ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ boteɔ tsei ashishifãi amli ni amɛtsiɔ paipii ni yɔɔ mli ni kɛ nu yaa lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛmli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines grow lots of big leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?
