english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer encourages the yam plant to spend all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground rather than storing energy in the tuber below ground.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baawo sweet potato tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli lɛ

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, shady conditions. The fungus attacks the pod tissues, turning them dark and soft before the seeds inside can mature.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Fung lɛ tutuaa pod fãji lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo dani dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my cassava leaves are curling because of disease or because of tiny insects?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ hela loo kooloi bibii ahewɔ ni ŋmei baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Insects like whiteflies spread viruses that cause leaves to turn pale yellow and curl tightly into hard shapes, whereas water stress or drought causes leaves to droop softly without changing color or texture.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ helai ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu he haomɔ loo hɔmɔ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi blɛoo ni amɛtsakeee amɛhe su loo amɛhefɛo.

english: Why do insects come back to attack my cabbage crop even after I spray them with crop medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiku amɛsɛɛ amɛbatutua mi-cabbage tsei lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa shwie tsei lɛ anɔ moŋ.

english: Insects may return if heavy rains wash the medicine off the leaves, if the spray was diluted too much, or if the pests in your area have built up resistance to that specific type of crop medicine.
ga: Kplukai lɛ baanyɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie tsofa lɛ kɛjɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli ewo nu tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ebɔi nakai tso tsofa pɔtɛɛ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: How does crop medicine sprayed on leaves actually work to protect the whole plant?
ga: Te tso tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni ebu tso muu lɛ fɛɛ he lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Systemic crop medicines get absorbed into the plant's internal sap system. When pests bite into any part of the leaf or stem, they ingest the medicine inside the plant tissue and stop feeding.
ga: Akɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli. Kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai ŋmɔ baai loo tsei lɛ fã ko Amɛwoɔ tsofa lɛ amɛwoɔ tso lɛ fãji amli ni amɛkpaa niyenii yeli.

english: How long should I wait after spraying crop medicine on my vegetables before it is safe to harvest and sell them?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ beni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ewo aduawai amli sɛɛ dani abaanyɛ akpa ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: Every crop medicine has a required waiting period specified on its bottle label, allowing the crop time to break down the active chemicals naturally so the harvested food is safe for human consumption.
ga: Tsofai fɛɛ ni akɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma fee lɛ yɛ be ni akɛmɛɛɔ taakɛ aŋma yɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma lɛ nɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfiteɔ tsofai ni tsuɔ nii. No hewɔ lɛ, niyenii ni akpaa lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha adesa niyenii.

english: How can I tell if a crop medicine I buy at an agrochemical store is genuine and safe for my plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miheɔ yɛ agrochemical shwapo mli lɛ ji anɔkwale ni ehi kɛha mi tsei lɛ?

english: Genuine crop medicines have clear manufacturer labels, official seal stamps, batch numbers, and distinctive company branding stamped directly on the bottle packaging to protect against fake products.
ga: Tsofai ni jɛ tsei amli diɛŋtsɛ lɛ yɛ mɔ ni fee lɛ wolo nɔ. Akɛ naatsii, nɔmba ni ji nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ kɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ kadimɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ woɔ tɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ amale nibii ahe.

english: Why are my maize leaves still turning yellow even after I applied fertilizer to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it, and yellow leaves often mean the plants are either lacking nitrogen or cannot take up nutrients because the soil is too dry or too packed.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Ni bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen loo enyɛɛɛ eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ.

english: Why does rainwater just sit on top of my land instead of sinking into the ground to feed my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii lɛ?

english: When soil gets dry and compacted from continuous farming without organic material, it hardens like concrete, preventing water from reaching deep crop roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi ni egbɔjɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuuu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baawa tamɔ kɔnkrit. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekashɛ tso shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do these new hybrid crop varieties wilt so easily compared to my old traditional crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ tsei heei ni akɛfee ekome nɛɛ gboɔ oya kɛ akɛto mishishijee tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: High-yielding improved varieties focus their energy on producing fruits fast, so they are delicate like pampered seeds and need regular water and proper care compared to hardy native varieties.
ga: Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni atsake amɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai ni baa oya lɛ nɔ, no hewɔ lɛ amɛhe waaa tamɔ dumɔwui ni amɛtsuɔ he nii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni ebiɔ nu ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni wa lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my corn stalks growing very tall and thin instead of thick and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daa ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants stretch upward to compete with each other for sunlight, resulting in weak stalks that fall over easily.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baagbala amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya.

english: How come weeds keep growing faster and stronger than the tomato crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tomato ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to poor conditions, so they aggressively steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight from your farm crops before your crops get a chance to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii amli dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up and droop in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl during peak afternoon heat as a natural defence mechanism to hide from direct sunlight and stop water from evaporating out of the plant.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni etsĩ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa

english: Why are the roots of my cassava plants showing above the dirt instead of staying buried?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni abaafu lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers expand as they grow, and if the topsoil is washed away by heavy rain or was planted too shallow, the growing roots push up through the surface.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Ni kɛji akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ loo adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Shishifãi ni miida lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: Why are my pepper flowers dropping off the stems before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani ebatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience heat stress, inconsistent watering, or a shortage of essential plant foods like calcium in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa loo tsei niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ, tamɔ calcium ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees have a white sticky powder on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ powda yɛŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: White powdery coatings are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects or fungi that feast on leaf juices and leave behind sugary waste that attracts mold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu loo ŋmeii bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ powder yɛŋ lɛ baa. No yeɔ baa mli nu ni eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni gbalaa ŋmeii.

english: Why do my harvested yams spoil and rot quickly in my barn while my neighbor's yams stay fresh for months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miifite ni miifite oya yɛ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ hiɔ shi nyɔji babaoo.

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised during harvesting or stored in hot, dark rooms without good air circulation, which creates damp conditions for rot to spread.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni mli ewo duŋ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. ni haa ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani abele lɛ afee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize feeds on heavily, or the plants are getting too much water around their roots. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves stay green so the plant can make big corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa yeɔ kooloi babaoo loo tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmãa agboi.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny dark droppings inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the center shoot of the young plant during the day and chews through tender leaves as they open up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei bibii ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii beni amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly during wet, humid weather when there is too much shade or thick bush around the cocoa trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Beni hulutsoo be babaoo loo jwɛi ni ebɔle kookoo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil becomes too dry, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil, which forces the plant to grow leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛwo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, shields the ground from the hot sun so water does not dry out quickly, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. koni nu lɛ akagbi oya Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃.

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem, which typically happens between 8 to 12 months after planting depending on the variety.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. Bare trunk left Enɛ fɔɔ baa yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to place tall sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei kakadaji awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce enough energy to grow large underground tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where they could easily rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi oya.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer to my crops before it rains or after it rains?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli dani nugbɔ anɛ loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer right after a light rain while the soil is moist. Dry soil cannot feed nutrients to the roots, but heavy rain immediately after applying fertilizer will wash the nutrients away.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ enɛ fioo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi nyɛŋ aha shishifãi lɛ niyenii. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ afite.

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally adapted to survive harsh conditions, allowing them to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why are field mice and rats eating my planted maize seeds before they can sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Field mice are attracted to the high energy in buried seeds, especially when food in the surrounding bush is scarce. Clearing nearby weeds and treating seeds before planting removes hiding spots and protects your crops.
ga: Hewalɛ ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni afu lɛ amli lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii faaa yɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ amli lɛ, jwɛi ni oookpa yɛ hei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni oootsu he nii dani odu lɛ baaye abua ni ejie hei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: What can I plant around my field boundary to stop roaming farm animals from destroying my cassava?
ga: Mɛni madu kɛbɔle ehe? Gbɛjegbɛ lɛ naa koni akɛtsi ŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ agbɛfaa lɛ naa koni amɛkafite mi-cassava lɛ.

english: Planting hedge crops like vetiver grass, thorny shrubs, or cassava varieties with bitter leaves around your field creates a natural barrier that deters animals from wandering onto your farm.
ga: Hedge tsei tamɔ vetiver, thornbush loo bitter cassava ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ kooloi anaa koni amɛkabɔle oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do pests attack my vegetable crops much more heavily during the dry season than the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa mi aduawai lɛ waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season, green wild plants die off, making your irrigated crop field the primary source of moisture and nutrients for insects and small animals in the area.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baagboi. Ha odumɔ nii ni okɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ lɛ afee nɔ titri ni haa kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai.

english: Does planting strong-smelling crops like onions next to my main crops help keep farm pests away?
ga: Ani tsei ni shãa mɔ waa, tamɔ sabolai, ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ titri lɛ masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, intercropping strong-smelling plants like onions, garlic, or marigolds helps confuse and repel destructive insects by masking the natural scent of your main crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa tamɔ sabolai, galiki loo marigolds ni akɛwoɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa mɔ yiŋ feɔ lɛ kɔshikɔshi ni eshwieɔ kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ onibii titri lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛhaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my young yam tubers showing deep chew marks when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ amli ŋmɔlɔ he okadii ni mli kwɔ kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Underground pests like mole rats, cane rats, and beetle larvae feed on tubers beneath the soil because root crops store high amounts of water and carbohydrates.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ toɔ nu kɛ carbohydrates babaoo.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up and turn yellow when tiny insects touch them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji kooloi bibii ta amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling and yellowing are stress reactions caused by sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or aphids, which drain the plant's nutrients and can pass along viral plant diseases.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔŋ ji nɔnyɛɛ ni kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids kɛbaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tso helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ aba.

english: Why do the stalks of my maize plants break and fall over before the ears are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ fãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani toi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Stem borers chew inside maize stalks to feed on the tender core, weakening the plant structurally until wind or the cob's weight causes it to snap.
ga: Stem borers lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmãa ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ aahu akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo ŋmei lɛ tsiimɔ haa efoɔ.

english: Why do my plantain roots push up above the topsoil instead of growing deep down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain shishifãi lɛ miitsi amɛhe kɛmiiya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaya shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems by nature; if heavy rains wash topsoil away or if soil is heavily compacted, exposed roots fail to gather necessary water and nutrients.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ebɔle Shishifãi ni jeɔ kpo lɛ nyɛŋ abua nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ naa.

english: Early pod loss usually happens when sap-sucking bugs like capsids damage the pod surface or when fungal diseases like black pod attack during humid weather, causing the tree to discard the damaged pod.
ga: mra be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji kooloi ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ capsids lɛ fite ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ tutua mɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli tseɔ lɛ. Ha tso lɛ ashɛrɛ ŋmeii ni efite lɛ ashwie.

english: Why do my harvested grains attract so many small insects and mice shortly after I store them at home?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii babaoo kɛbaa mihe beni mikɛto shia sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Stored grains give off warmth and moisture, which attracts pests. Properly drying grains until they are hard and storing them in sealed, airtight bags prevents pests from entering and multiplying.
ga: Ŋmãa ni ato lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i baa, ni no gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi amɛhe wa ni akɛto kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote mli ni amɛshwere.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees lose water quickly through their leaves during hot, dry weather. If they do not have enough shade trees or soil moisture, the tree drops its leaves to conserve water and protect itself from drying out completely.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ hulutsoo loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛtsi amɛhe gbɛ koni amɛkagbi kwraa.

english: Why are my maize plants staying short and turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ hiɔ shi be kukuoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves and short stems usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to grow strong. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant grow taller and green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmeii kukuji tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni enyɛ eda waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava is mature and ready to harvest since the crop grows underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava shows it is mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem with leaves mostly at the top. You can also dig carefully around one stem to check if the roots have swollen into thick tubers.
ga: Yucca jieɔ dalɛ kpo kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni baai lɛ fa yɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu nii kɛbɔle he hu. Tso kome koni ana kɛji shishifãi lɛ efuu ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛfeee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Pepper blossoms drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil becomes too dry or overly wet, or when insects damage the stem joints. Keeping the soil evenly damp and protected helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ tso lɛ shishi fãi lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ehi shi be fɛɛ be ni abuɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: The extra shoots, called suckers, steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from the main stem. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the mother plant to grow thick and produce large, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ adara ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make the food that grows big tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil, exposing them to full sunlight while protecting them from leaf diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ hulu la ni eŋmɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe helai hu ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it risky to plant my crop seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry break before the main rains settle in. If seeds sprout after just one rain, the heat and dry soil in the days that follow will scorch and kill the young seedlings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ baa. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Dɔlɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi yɛ gbii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli Yaa shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baashã tso bibioo lɛ ni egbe lɛ.

english: Is it good for my soil if I plant groundnuts together in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei du yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, groundnuts belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen gas from the air and puts it back into the soil naturally. Planting them with maize feeds the soil and gives you two different crops from the same plot.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii weku lɛ mli, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ jɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This sudden wilting is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a germ living in the soil that blocks the narrow tubes inside the stem so water cannot travel up to the leaves. Rotating crops helps stop this sickness from building up in your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsiɔ tsɔnei bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa koni nu akayashɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hela nɛɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I leave dry grass and leaves covering the soil around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi jwɛi kɛ baai akɛ mulch yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry plant material, called mulching, acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the dirt so it stays cool, prevents weeds from sprouting, and stops the hot sun from drying out the roots.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ koni eha edɔ. Ehaa jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: Why do I need to dilute some crop sprays with a lot of water while other sprays only need a little?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ nu babaoo awo mi-crop spray lɛ mli lɛ? be mli ni sprays krokomɛi lɛ he miihia fioo pɛ?

english: Different sprays have different strengths or concentrations. A stronger spray needs more water to weaken it so it effectively protects your crops without burning their leaves, whereas a weaker spray needs less water to do the same job.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni spray henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yɔɔ hewalɛ loo bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha. Spray ni mli wa lɛ biɔ nu babaoo koni egbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ebuɔ onibii ahe jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ baai shãaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ biɔ nu fioo ko pɛ koni enyɛ etsu nakai nitsumɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: If I switch from chemical fertilizer to chicken manure, how do I know how much to use to get the same crop yield?
ga: Kɛji otsake kɛjɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli kɛtee tsina ŋmɔ mli lɛ, te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole bɔ ni esa akɛ okɛtsu nii koni onine ashɛ yibiiwoo ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Chicken manure is generally milder and releases nutrients more slowly than concentrated chemical fertilizer. Because its strength is lower, you need to apply a larger quantity of manure to give your crops the same amount of feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsina ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ blɛoo fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli lɛ. Ejaakɛ ehewalɛ lɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ ehe baahia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo afata he koni eha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni fa tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ.

english: Why does putting too much strong fertilizer on my pepper plants cause them to wither instead of growing bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa babaoo wo mi-pepper tso lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa egboɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ agbo lɛ?

english: Strong fertilizers are highly concentrated plant foods. If you apply too much at once, the high strength draws water out of the plant's roots instead of feeding them, causing the leaves to dry up and burn.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji tso niyenii ni mli edɔ waa. Kɛ okɛ babaoo tsu nii shikome lɛ Hewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso shishifãi amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa.

english: How do I make sure two different brands of liquid crop booster give my vegetables the exact same growth result?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ niyenii mli lɛ henɔi srɔtoi enyɔ haa mi-aduawai lɛ daa tamɔ nɔ kome pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: You must check the recommended strength on the label for each brand. Since one brand might be twice as strong as another, adjusting the amount you mix into your knapsack sprayer ensures your crops get the exact same level of nutrients.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni okwɛ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ yi yɛ nibii ni afee lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji akɛ, ekolɛ tsofa kome mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fa fe nɔ kroko lɛ shii enyɔ. Kɛ́ otsake bɔ ni okɛfutuɔ o-backpack sprayer lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How can two different cocoa tree varieties produce beans that give the exact same rich chocolate smell?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni cacao tsei srɔtoi enyɔ afee kɔfe ŋmeii ni tsokolate ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa tamɔ nɔ kome pɛpɛɛpɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Even though cocoa varieties can differ in leaf size or pod color, their underlying chemical compounds responsible for aroma can be identical. Proper fermenting and drying methods help bring out that same standard chocolate scent regardless of the tree type.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ekolɛ kookoo henɔi lɛ baa lɛ dalɛ loo pod lɛ sui yɛ srɔtoi moŋ, shi tsofai ni haa ŋmɔlɔ baa lɛ baanyɛ afee ekome. Gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ afeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbiɔ lɛ haa tsokolate lɛ he muji ni sa lɛ jeɔ kpo ekɔɔɔ he eko tso lɛ henɔ.

english: Why do two different cassava varieties yield the same quality starch even though one needs much more fertilizer than the other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei henɔi enyɔ haa ŋmei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei henɔ kome biɔ ŋmei babaoo fe ekroko lɛ moŋ?

english: Some cassava varieties are efficient at drawing nutrients from poor soil (strong feeders), while weaker varieties need extra help from added fertilizer to produce the same quality root and starch output.
ga: Kasava henɔi komɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ mli lɛ jiemɔ mli. (niyenii ni wa) yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ he miihia yelikɛbuamɔ kroko kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do some pepper varieties taste extremely spicy while others are mild, even when I plant them in the exact same soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper henɔi komɛi yɛ ŋmɔlɔ waa ni ekrokomɛi hu ŋmɔlɔ fioo lɛ? Kɛji akɛ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ po.

english: Spiciness comes from natural chemicals inside the pepper plant called capsaicin. The variety's genetics decide how strong or weak this chemical is produced, regardless of the soil condition.
ga: Nɔ ni jɛɔ tsofa ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ capsaicin lɛ mli baa. Genetics ni yɔɔ srɔtoi Etsɔɔ bɔ ni tsofa nɛɛ he wa loo egbɔjɔ ha. Ekɔɔɔ he eko bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha

english: Why do I need to apply dark composted manure in smaller quantities than fresh green leaves to get the same soil strength?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ fioo pɛ afata he fe baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ lɛ koni anyɛ ana shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Well-aged compost is densely packed with concentrated, ready-to-use nutrients, making it strong. Fresh green leaves contain mostly water and light nutrients, so you need a much larger pile of leaves to match the strength of compost.
ga: Akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni mli wa ni yɔɔ klalo akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ eyi ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli, ni no haa ewaa. Nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔlii heei amli babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni oná baai ni da kwraa fe tsutsu lɛ koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewalɛ lɛ akpã gbee.

english: If my soil is already very fertile, why can adding extra strong crop food make my tomatoes taste watery?
ga: Kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo ŋmɔshi nii waa momo lɛ Mɛni hewɔ tso niyenii ni wa babaoo ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa mi-tomato lɛ feɔ nu lɛ?

english: When crops receive excessive nutrients beyond what they need, they absorb extra water to balance the high strength in their roots. This dilutes the natural sugars in the fruit, resulting in a weaker flavor.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo fe bɔ ni he hiaa lɛ Tso lɛ baaŋɔ nu kroko ni fata he koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ afee ekome. Enɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli sugars ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ afee mlɛo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔlɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: Why does my young maize turn yellow if I apply a strong weedkiller nearby, but my neighbor's older maize stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã bibioo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji mikɛ tsofa ko ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni he wa tsu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi, shi mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa ni eda lɛ hiɔ shi ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Young plants are delicate and easily damaged by high chemical concentrations. Older, established crops are stronger and can tolerate mild exposure to the same spray without showing signs of stress.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni tsofai babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Tsei ni edara ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ wa waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ fioo ni amɛjieee haomɔ he okadii akpo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field with no large trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade because direct sunlight scorches their young leaves and dries up the soil quickly. Planting shade crops like plantain alongside them protects the tender seedlings until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings fail to sprout after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings often fail if they are planted upside down or if the stems are too old or dry. Planting healthy cuttings right-side up with the eye buds pointing skyward ensures proper root development and shoot growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca tsei ni afo lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ ŋwɛi loo kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ egbɔ tsɔ loo amɛgbi. Nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni aduɔ hiɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu ada.

english: Why should I wait for the major rainy season to fully start before planting my crops instead of planting right after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ aje shishi kwraa dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a short dry spell that can dry out newly planted seeds before they germinate. Waiting for steady rains ensures the soil stays moist enough for seeds to sprout and establish strong roots.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ. No baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ agbi dani amɛkwɛ̃. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and drying up before the cobs are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth. Applying balanced fertilizer or organic compost gives the plant the food it needs to stay green and produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I pour raw fertilizer directly against the stem of my growing crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against a plant stem can cause chemical burns that damage or kill the crop. Fertilizer should be applied a few inches away from the stem in moist soil so the roots can safely absorb the nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofai ashã ni efite loo efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi inchii fioo komɛi. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do weeds in my field cause my crops to grow thin and give a poor harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ miifee miŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni ekɛ yibiiwoo baaa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early gives your main crops full access to the resources they need to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa otsei titrii lɛ naa nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is a sudden lack of water. Keeping the soil moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers and turn them into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu faaa trukaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that targets the growing center of maize leaves. Catching them early and applying proper control methods prevents them from destroying the main growing point of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmei baai lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra Ni akɛ gbɛi kpakpai ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ amɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite hei titri ni tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant pepper on the exact same piece of land where I just harvested tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa tomato nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Peppers and tomatoes belong to the same plant family and attract the same soil diseases and pests. Planting them continuously in the same spot allows diseases to build up in the soil; rotating with crops like maize or beans breaks this cycle.
ga: Pepper kɛ tomato ji tsei akuu kome mli ni amɛgbalaa helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Efoɔ nɛkɛ sɛɛkuu nɛɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground into the air, preventing leaf diseases and encouraging larger tuber growth.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni ehaa tsei wuji lɛ daraa.

english: This usually means your soil is low in nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to grow, so when food in the soil runs low, the plant steals nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the young, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛye baai bibii ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with tiny organisms in the soil to trap nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into natural plant food. When the cowpea roots rot after harvest, that trapped food stays in the soil for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni emɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii. Beni tsina shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Niyenii ni ekã shi lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry weather to save water. The plant is not dying; it is protecting itself by going quiet above ground while keeping the tubers alive beneath the soil.
ga: Yucca shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni egbiɔ koni ekɛbu nu he. Tso lɛ gbooo. Ebuɔ ehe he kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni efeɔ dioo lɛ nɔ, yɛ be mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ hu hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt and go limp in the hot afternoon sun but wake up by evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ? Limping yɛ shwane hulu lɛ Shi teɔ shi gbɛkɛ?

english: During peak afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the soil. Wilting helps the leaf expose less surface to the sun. Once the air cools down, the plant recovers its strength.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Wilting haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hulu la lɛ he babaoo. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli bawo wu lɛ Tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without making any fruits when the heat gets strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers so they cannot form fruits. When the plant senses too much heat stress, it sheds the flowers to conserve its energy for survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ, ni ehaaa amɛwo yibii. Kɛ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni fe nine lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha wala.

english: Why should I cut away extra suckers from my plantain stool instead of leaving them all to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ plantain ŋmeii lɛ amli moŋ fe ni mahã amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ he fɛɛ he?

english: If too many suckers grow around the main plantain tree, they all fight for the same soil nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, which results in larger and heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shwɛɔ, ni no haa ŋmeii ni da ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ baa.

english: Why do my yam vines keep climbing aggressively up any tall stick or tree near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ kwɔɔ tso nine kakadaŋŋ loo tso ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ nɔ kɛ yiwalɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb so their leaves can reach maximum sunlight. The leaves use sunlight to make food, which travels down the stem to feed and expand the big yam tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he babaoo. Baai kɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi koni eyatao niyenii ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yam tsei wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why does standing water in my lowland rice field help the crop grow instead of rotting its roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni ekã shi yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa moŋ fe ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ agbo lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels in their stems that carry oxygen down to roots underwater. The flooded water blocks weeds from growing while letting the rice thrive.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ŋtayaai krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Nu afua lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ehaa ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves, or by viral sicknesses spread by those insects. As the leaves lose sap, they grow out twisted and wrinkled.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kɛ́ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ fite Ebaafee nɔ ni efite ni ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are tiny, young cocoa pods on my tree turning black and shriveling up before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, yɛ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo dani etsɔ agbo.

english: This is often a natural condition called 'cherelle wilt,' where the tree sheds excess pods it cannot feed due to limited nutrients or water. However, if it spreads to big pods, it could be black pod disease caused by excess moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ ‘cherelle wilt’, he ni tsei shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aha niyenii yɛ niyenii loo nu ni faaa lɛ hewɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ egbɛ eshwa ŋmeii wuji amli lɛ, ekolɛ eji ŋmeii diji hela ni ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛbaa.

english: How do I measure my farm size without expensive equipment so I don't buy too much seed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikɛ nibii ni jara wa tsuuu nii koni ehe ehiaaa ni mahe dumɔwui babaoo?

english: You can measure your farm easily using standard rope lengths or by counting equal strides across the field boundaries. Knowing your land size helps you buy the exact amount of seed and fertilizer you need, saving you money.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kpãa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ asusu oŋmɔ lɛ he yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ loo kɛtsɔ gbɛ ni tamɔ amɛhe ni oookane kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ole bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ da ha lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ohé dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa lɛ. ni haa shika baa shi

english: Does it really matter how far apart I plant my cassava sticks, or can I just plant them anywhere?
ga: Ani bɔ ni mikɛ mi-cassava lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ ha lɛ he hiaa mi? Aloo abaanyɛ adu yɛ he fɛɛ he?

english: Proper spacing is essential because roots need enough room to spread underground and leaves need room to catch sunlight. Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for nutrients, resulting in smaller tubers.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ he miihia ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ he miihia he ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Ni esa akɛ baai lɛ aná he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso bibioo.

english: Why do crops grow better when I dig and loosen hard soil before planting instead of just poking small holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mifo shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mifo mli dani midu yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mafo bu bibii lɛ?

english: Loosening the soil creates small air spaces and allows young roots to push deep into the earth easily. Deep roots help the plant collect water from deep underground during dry weeks.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii baa. ni ehaa shishifãi bibii lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ oya Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ebua nu naa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: If I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year without resting it, what will happen in the future?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ, Mɛni baaba wɔsɛɛ?

english: Continuous planting on the same soil without resting or adding organic manure drains the soil's natural food. Over time, your crops will turn yellow, grow weak, and produce far smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni ajɔɔɔɔ he loo awooo mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ajie. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Is it better to burn all the bush when clearing my land or leave the cleared grass to decay on the ground?
ga: Shãa jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ beni ojieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Aloo ehi akɛ aaashi jwɛi lɛ ni egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Burning clears land quickly, but leaving the vegetation to decay on the surface creates natural mulch. Mulch keeps the soil moist under hot sun and slowly breaks down into free nutrients for your crops.
ga: Shãa lɛ jieɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ oya. Shi tsei lɛ ni ashiɔ amɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa. Mulch haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi, ni fiofio lɛ, egbɛɔ eshwaa ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni haa onibii ni okwɛɔ lɛ ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil as natural food for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I plant long-term tree crops like cocoa if they take years to produce fruit while maize yields in months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tamɔ kookoo yɛ be mli ni eheɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: While maize provides quick food and income in a few months, cocoa trees act as long-term investments that keep producing crops for decades, securing food and income for your family as you get older.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa ji niyenii kɛ shika jɛɛhe oya yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli moŋ, shi abuɔ Cacao tsei akɛ eji shika ni akɛwoɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Eji niyenii kɛ shika jɛɛhe kɛha oweku lɛ beni odara lɛ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wither and die when I clear away all the big shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full midday sun. Leaving a few shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains creates a cooler environment that protects seedlings while their roots grow strong.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ ashi tsei fioo komɛi ni haa hulutsoo loo adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow so much faster than my planted crops after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to suck up water and soil nutrients instantly. Because they feed faster than domestic crops, clearing them early stops them from stealing food away from your growing plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ amɛyeɔ nii oya fe shia tsei. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ehaa amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei ni oduɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my tree crops if the branches look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ amli kɛji akɛ niji lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa?

english: Pruning removes crowded inner branches so sunlight and air can reach all parts of the plant. This prevents diseases and forces the tree to send its energy into producing large fruits rather than extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ mli lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ tsiɔ helai anaa ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ lɛ nɔ koni ewo yibii wuji yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do some crop varieties on my farm get sick easily while others nearby stay completely healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hela mɔ amɛ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu? Ani mɔ ko yɛ akutso lɛ mli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yeɔ emuu lolo?

english: Crops have different natural defenses. Crops that get sick easily are considered susceptible, while resistant varieties have built-in defenses that prevent specific plant diseases from attacking them in the first place.
ga: Tsei yɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu srɔtoi. Abuɔ tsei ni hela mɔɔ amɛ oya lɛ akɛ amɛhe nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ hela. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ hela lɛ yɛ nibii ni tsiɔ tso helai komɛi anaa koni amɛkatutua tso lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Is it possible to find crop seeds in Ghana that never catch disease at all?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ana tsei ahe dumɔwui ni hela bɛ mli kwraa yɛ Ghana?

english: Yes, certain improved crop varieties are fully immune or highly resistant to specific common local diseases, meaning those particular sicknesses cannot infect the plant regardless of weather or field conditions.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei komɛi ni akwɛɔ amɛ lɛ nyɛŋ amɛye amɛhe kwraa loo amɛnyɛŋ amɛye helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ helai komɛi nyɛŋ atswa tsei ekɔɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo ŋmɔ mli shihilɛ he.

english: What does it actually mean when people say a crop variety is 'susceptible' to sickness?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ́ gbɔmɛi kɛɛ tsei srɔtoi ‘nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ’ helai?

english: When a crop is susceptible, it means the plant lacks natural defenses against a specific sickness, making it very easy for disease to attack and destroy the plant if conditions are right.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ hewalɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni tsiɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ helai komɛi ahe. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo waa akɛ helai baatutua tsei ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ kɛji shihilɛi lɛ ja.

english: Why do some high-yielding crop seeds require so much chemical spraying compared to local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ biɔ ni akɛ tsofai babaoo afɔ nɔ kɛ akɛto maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Some seeds bred purely for high yield are more susceptible to local diseases, meaning they need extra chemical protection, whereas traditional varieties often have natural strength to withstand local crop sicknesses.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui komɛi koni amɛwo yibii babaoo pɛ. amɛhe yɔɔ oya kɛha helai ni jɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni akɛ tsofai krokomɛi abu amɛhe. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, kusum mli tsei srɔtoi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni amɛkɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe helai.

english: If my crops catch a disease, does it mean I will lose my whole harvest?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ná hela lɛ Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ baafite?

english: Not always. Some crop varieties are tolerant, meaning even if disease enters the plant, the crop is strong enough to withstand the sickness and still produce a good harvest for you.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ekomɛi nyɛɛɛ helai amɔ amɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kɛji hela lɛ bote tso lɛ mli po lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ hela naa ni eha bo ŋmaa kpakpa lolo.

english: Why do some of my cassava plants have yellow spotted leaves from disease but still yield big tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni jɛ hela mli shi amɛyɛ ŋmeii wuji lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: That cassava variety is tolerant to the virus. Although the disease shows on the leaves, the plant is strong enough to withstand the sickness and continue feeding the tubers under the soil.
ga: Cassava henɔi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛji hela lɛ jie ehe kpo yɛ baai lɛ anɔ po Shi tsei lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ helai anaa ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii.

english: Can a crop plant recover and give good produce on its own after pest attacks without me spraying heavy chemicals?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko etutua amɛ lɛ sɛɛ ni mikɛ tsofai ni tsii shwieee amɛnɔ?

english: Yes, tolerant crop varieties have the physical strength to withstand damage from pests or diseases and naturally rebuild themselves to produce yields without heavy chemical intervention.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni wa lɛ yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ nibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai baafite amɛ lɛ. ni ekɛ ehe woɔ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛ yibiiwoo aba ni tsofai ni tsii kɛ ehe wooo mli.

english: Why is my neighbor’s farm surviving the dry spell better than my crops when we planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ́ wɔdu yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties behave differently under stress. Your neighbor likely planted a drought-tolerant variety that can withstand heat and dry weather, while weaker varieties wilt quickly.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ nɔnyɛɛ shishi. Ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ miidu tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa ni baanyɛ adamɔ hulutsoo kɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi anaa. yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ baagboi oya.

english: Why should I care about asking for specific seed varieties if all seeds look the same in the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ koni mabi dumɔwui srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ ko? Kɛji dumɔwui fɛɛ tamɔ nɔ kome yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Even if seeds look identical, their behavior in the soil is very different. Asking about the variety helps you choose seeds that withstand local diseases, match your soil, and secure your harvest.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ kome moŋ Shi amɛjeŋba yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ srɔto kwraa. Kɛ́ obi tsei srɔtoi lɛ ahe saji lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ohala dumɔwui ni helai ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ, ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kpãa gbee, ni ehaa nɔmimaa baakpa.

english: How can I know which crop variety is best to plant on my farm before buying the seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mahe dumɔwui?

english: You can ask your local agriculture extension officer about the variety's characteristics—specifically whether it cannot get sick easily (resistant) or can withstand sickness and dry weather (tolerant) in your area.
ga: Obaanyɛ obi okpokpaa lɛ nɔ okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ lɛ sui ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ he, titri lɛ kɛji enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai (ehiɔ shi) loo enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi (ehiɔ shi) yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves to conserve water during dry periods or Harmattan, but excessive leaf loss usually means they lack sufficient shade trees or soil moisture to shield them from high heat.
ga: Cocoa tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛto nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo yɛ harmattan mli. Shi bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ baai babaoo fite lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ cacao tso lɛ bɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baabu cacao tso lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he.

english: Why is my maize growing tall but the leaves look pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ kɛlɛ shi baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize relies on heavily during its early vegetative stage to build strong leaves and stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ waa yɛ shishijee dalɛ mli koni ekɛfee baai kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, inconsistent watering, or a lack of balanced nutrients, saving their energy to survive rather than produce fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni ja ni bɛ Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ wala mli lɛ baa shi moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves into the sunlight where they can make food efficiently, which keeps the foliage off the damp ground to prevent disease and encourages larger tuber growth.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia shishitoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la mli he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛho nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni helai akabote mli ni eha bulbs wuji lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Leaving too many suckers around the main plantain stem causes them to compete for water and nutrients, resulting in smaller bunches and weaker stems.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii lɛ abɔle ŋmeii lɛ ahe Too main stem babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ aniji lɛ feɔ bibii ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight, leading to thin stalks and smaller, underdeveloped cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do weeds always seem to sprout and grow faster than my main crop after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe mitso titri lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants naturally adapted to germinate rapidly and absorb available surface moisture and soil nutrients before cultivated crops can establish deep roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii lɛ dani tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes curling up and showing sticky white spots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and sticky spots are typically caused by sap-sucking insects like whiteflies, which transmit viral diseases such as cassava mosaic disease between plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies, ni gbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli kɛbaa tamɔ cassava mosaic lɛ kɛbaa tsei ateŋ.

english: Why does my land become hard and dry like brick after farming it for a few consecutive years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbi tamɔ brikii beni mikɛ afii babaoo etsu nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ?

english: Continuous farming without adding organic material like manure or plant mulch breaks down the soil structure, stripping away its natural ability to hold water and nutrients.
ga: Okwaayeli ni aya nɔ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ afite. Enɛ haa amɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛhiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do experienced farmers say planting cowpeas or groundnuts makes the soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ, kɛ́ adu tsina loo ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas work with beneficial soil bacteria to take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Is it good to clear all the big forest trees before I plant my food crops, or should I leave some?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ aaajie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ dani adu niyenii? Aloo obaashi ekomɛi yɛ sɛɛ?

english: It depends on the crop you are planting. While sun-loving crops like maize need complete clearing, crops like young cocoa or yams thrive better when some tall forest trees are left to shield them from excessive sun and harsh winds.
ga: Edamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa ni ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni sumɔɔ hulu tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ kwraa lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo bibii loo ŋmãa Ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ashi tsei ni kɛlɛ yɛ koo lɛ mli koni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why does my farmland in the bush lose its power to produce good yields after a few seasons of farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ okwaayeli bei fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Every crop you harvest draws vitamins and nutrients out of the earth. Without returning goodness to the soil through compost, manure, or letting the land rest, the soil becomes exhausted and can no longer feed new crops well.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni okpaa lɛ jieɔ vitamini kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ohaaa sũ lɛ jɔɔ ehe lɛ kuuu sɛɛ kɛbaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ tsei heei anɔ jogbaŋŋ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops struggle to grow well when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other underground for soil water and nutrients, and above ground for sunlight. Giving each plant proper space ensures it gets enough food and light to grow strong.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛwuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii. kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ena hulu la Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaha ená niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my crops bending and stretching toward one direction instead of growing straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛhe yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ?

english: Plants naturally reach toward direct sunlight. If tall trees or bushes block light on one side of your farm, the crops will bend and lean in search of the sun.
ga: Tsei baaná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji tsei kakadaji loo jwɛi shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome nɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛtao hulu la.

english: What happens if I leave my crop bushes to grow wild without trimming the extra branches?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi jwɛi lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni mifolɔɔɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: When a plant grows wild with too many extra branches and leaves, it wastes its food energy maintaining foliage instead of developing large, healthy fruits or tubers.
ga: Beni tsei daraa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛ niji kɛ baai babaoo tsɔ. Efiteɔ niyenii hewalɛ koni ekɛkwɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ yiblii nguahi nɛ a he wa loo bulbs.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster and stronger than the food crops I carefully plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe niyenii tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally tough survivalists adapted to thrive in harsh bush conditions without care. Domesticated food crops are softer and require human protection and weeding to compete successfully.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi ji kooloi ni hiɛ wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛshwere yɛ koo mli shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shia niyenii tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni ehe miihia ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ adesai ahe ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli koni amɛye omanye yɛ akaŋshii mli.

english: Can I pick wild crop seedlings straight from the forest and replant them on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafo koo mli tsei ahe dumɔwui kɛjɛ koo lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Wild varieties often yield smaller or bitter fruits because they haven't been bred for farming. It is better to use improved nursery seeds that are designed to produce high yields and resist local diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koo mli tsei srɔtoi lɛ woɔ yibii bibii loo ni ŋɔɔ waa ejaakɛ afɔɔɔ amɛ koni akɛtsu nii. Esa akɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni akwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni ekɛ yibiiwoo babaoo aba ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ maŋ lɛ mli helai lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do some climbing crops spread across the ground and choke my other food plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni kwɔɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ ni amɛhaa mi niyenii tsei krokomɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Certain creeping or vine crops naturally expand aggressively to capture space and sunlight. If left unmanaged, they cover neighboring plants and starve them of light.
ga: Tsei loo wain tsei komɛi ni shwereɔ lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã oya koni amɛmɔ ŋwɛi kɛ hulu la. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Ebaaha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ ni ebaaha amɛná la.

english: Why do my cassava plants fall over or come out of the soil so easily during strong rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shwieɔ shi loo ejɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops with shallow root systems or those planted in hard, unplowed soil cannot anchor deep enough. Without deep roots, heavy wind and rain easily overturn the plants.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo nɔ ni akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuko nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atswa shi kɛya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa. Kɛji shishifãi ni mli kwɔ bɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei agbo oya.

english: Why do wild animals in the surrounding bush target my yams and cassava more than wild forest plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli kooloi ni yɔɔ koo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ kwɛɔ mi sweet potato kɛ yucca lɛ nɔ fe koo mli tsei lɛ?

english: Cultivated tubers are softer, sweeter, and packed with more water and nutrients than wild bush roots, making your farm an easy and delicious target for forest animals.
ga: Bulbs ni eda lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe ŋɔɔ, ni nu kɛ niyenii babaoo eyi mli obɔ fe koo mli tsei ashishifãi. Ni oooha oŋmɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋɔɔ kɛha koo mli kooloi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers if they are not pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or if the tree experiences stress from extreme heat and drought. Keeping shade trees helps protect the insects and keeps the cocoa trees cool.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafee fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. aloo kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ahe, ni ehaa kookoo tso lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Heavy rain fills all the air spaces in soil with water, suffocating the roots and allowing rot-causing fungi to spread.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli obɔ kɛ nu. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up to reduce water loss when the weather is very hot, but if they turn yellow and brittle, it could mean whiteflies have passed a leaf curl virus to your plants.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Shi kɛji akɛ amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ hu? Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ miigbɛ leaf curl virus lɛ amɛshwã otsei lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops grow bigger when I plant cowpeas in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli yaa hiɛ kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans absorb nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the field, they naturally fertilize the soil for other crops growing around them.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Amɛkɛ tsei krokomɛi baafɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the young plants end up fighting each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin stems and small yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei bibii lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Yam leaves need as much sunlight as possible to make energy that feeds the tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves high and exposed to the sun instead of shaded on the ground.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛfee hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsi amɛ gbɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do small caterpillars hide inside the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This is usually the Fall Armyworm, a pest that prefers feeding on the tender, growing leaves tucked inside the center whorl of young maize.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni sumɔɔ ni eye baai bibii ni miida ni akɛwo ŋmãa bibii ateŋ lɛ.

english: Why does fertilizer burn my crops if I put it right next to the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii shãa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikɛwo tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated minerals that act like salt. Placing them directly against a tender stem pulls water out of the plant tissue, causing it to dry up and burn.
ga: Minerals ni mli wa ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋoo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛ́ okɛwo tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbala nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ fãji lɛ amli. ni haa egbiɔ ni eshãa

english: Why do seeds I save from my previous harvest yield less than new seed packets from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni jɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds from agro-dealers are often specially bred hybrids designed for high performance in their first year. Saving seeds from that harvest causes the crop to lose its uniform strength and yield potential in the next generation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni jɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ ji dumɔwui ni afee amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe waaa be fɛɛ be ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Officer, why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Officer Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellow and curling leaves usually mean pests like fall armyworms are attacking your maize or the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen. Applying the right crop protection medicine or fertilizer early helps save your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi tamɔ fall armyworm miitutua o-corn lɛ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, kɛ tsofai ni sa ni buɔ tsei ahe loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ atsu nii mra Ebaaye ebua ni okwɛ nibii ni owoɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I plant plantains on the same land with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Is it necessary for me to apply fertilizer if my farm soil already looks dark?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ?

english: Even dark soil loses its nutrients over time as crops feed on it. Adding fertilizer provides the right balance of food that crops need to yield heavy, high-quality produce.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ po laajeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei yeɔ amɛ lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni fa babaoo lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava plants give me small tubers when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close, their roots compete for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food to grow large, thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, nu lɛ mli, kɛ hulu la mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ bulbs agboi ni mli tse baa.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow slowly and produce poorly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛmiiwo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Weeds grow aggressively and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds regularly ensures your crops receive all the nourishment they need.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the sunshine becomes too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil put stress on pepper plants, forcing them to drop flowers to preserve water. Watering regularly and placing dry grass around the plant base keeps the soil cool.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ ashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ashwie koni nu akafite. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Will removing extra leaves and side branches from my tomato plants help them fruiting better?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mijie baai kɛ esɛɛ niji kɛjɛ mi-tomato tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: Yes, trimming unnecessary side branches prevents the plant from wasting energy on foliage. This redirects the plant's food straight into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes.
