ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛ niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii lɛ yaa tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred for high performance in their first planting. Seeds saved from that harvest lose their strength, resulting in weaker plants and lower yield in the next season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwu lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Planting groundnuts or cowpeas afterwards naturally restores nitrogen back into the dirt, keeping the land fertile for future crops.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting quickly when stored in a enclosed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛ́ akɛto tsu ko ni aŋã mli lɛ?

english: Harvested yams are living tubers that breathe and release heat; storing them in hot, enclosed spaces encourages rot and mold. Storing them in a well-ventilated, shaded yam barn keeps them fresh much longer.
ga: Akpaa sweet potatoes akɛ ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni muɔ ni amɛjieɔ dɔlɛ kpo. Kɛ́ oha edɔ ni okɛ nɔ ko awo mli lɛ, ebaawo ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he hewalɛ. Okɛ amɛ ato sweet potato ŋmɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli ni hulutsoo hu yɔɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out soil moisture. Planting plantains or shade trees nearby protects them until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni ooodu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure around the roots early in the growth stage helps the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛfataa Mra be mli shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: What causes small green worms to eat holes in the middle leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These green worms are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that destroys crop leaves. Catching them early by checking the leaves and applying the recommended spray inside the leaves helps save your harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii eŋɔli nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni fɔɔ baa ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe tsei. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same field drains specific nutrients from the ground and lets crop pests multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients to the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai fɔɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water builds up around them for too long. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ebua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do extension officers advise me to put wooden stakes next to my growing yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ mikɛ tso ko ama sweet potato wain tsei ni miduɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can reach sunlight and stay off the damp ground. Staking protects the vines from leaf diseases and gives the plant the energy needed to form big tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛbaji lɛ ashɛ hulu la he ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ahe. Staking buɔ wain tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe helai ahe, ni ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfee bulbs agboi.

english: Is it helpful to plant beans and maize together in the same field?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very beneficial. Beans absorb nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, which naturally feeds the maize plants and improves your harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa okpamɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Healthy soil is typically dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds water well after rain, and contains earthworms or soft organic matter that feeds plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ji niyenii kɛha tsei yɛ

english: Why does leaving weeds in my farm cause my crops to produce smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds act as thieves in your farm by stealing light, water, and food from the soil that your crops need. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients to produce big yields.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa onibii lɛ ni amɛjuɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa otsei lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkpa nii babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or dry soil conditions. Mulching the soil around the plant to keep it cool and moist helps the flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi shihilɛ. Mulching around Plant lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ koni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How do I know if my maize crops are suffering from a lack of water during a dry spell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni miiye lɛ miiho yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: When maize lacks sufficient water, its leaves roll inward like narrow tubes during the hottest hours of the day to save moisture. If the dry spell continues, the lower leaves will turn yellow and dry up, leading to small or empty maize cobs.
ga: Beni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmãa lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli tamɔ tsɔne bibioo ko yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Kɛji hɔmɔ lɛ tee nɔ lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Can I plant my vegetable crops directly in a swampy area so they always have water?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni maná nu be fɛɛ be?

english: While vegetables need water, roots sitting in waterlogged soil cannot breathe and will rot. It is better to build raised soil beds near the water source so the excess water drains away while keeping the root zone moist.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni nu he hiaa aduawai lɛ Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nyɛŋ amu ni amɛbaagboi. Esa akɛ ama shikpɔŋ nɔ tsũi ni awó nɔ yɛ nu jɛɛhei lɛ ahe koni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli, ni koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land has good soil for farming before I start clearing it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni abaanyɛ atsu nii yɛ nɔ dani mabɔi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ?

english: You can judge soil quality by looking at the natural plants already growing there. Dark green, thick vegetation and trees usually indicate rich, healthy soil, whereas areas dominated by sparse grass or stunted bushes often mean the soil is poor.
ga: Obaanyɛ okojo bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hi ha lɛ kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ momo lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hei ni jwɛi egbɛ eshwã loo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ fɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii.

english: Why do my crops grow much better when I plant cowpeas before planting maize on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmei dani midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground through their roots. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth to act as free, natural fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa amɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat, which dry out their leaves faster than their young roots can drink water. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects them until they grow strong roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ anu nu lɛ. Be kukuoo mli tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baaje shishi.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing tall with plenty of green leaves but no flowers or peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miida ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo lɛ? Shi fɔfɔii loo ŋmeii bɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich manure without balanced sunlight and phosphorus, they spend all their energy growing tall stems and leafy foliage instead of producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aha tsei nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni hulu la kɛ fɔsfɔs ni sa bɛ mli lɛ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai kakadaji. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up and turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies feeding on the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Removing infected leaves early and keeping insects away helps keep the rest of the crop healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ kɛ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli. Baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Ni ajieɔ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants shed all their leaves during the dry season, and will the crop die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani ŋmɔshi nii lɛ baagbo?

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during long dry spells to reduce water loss and survive the heat. The plant is not dead; its root tubers remain healthy underground, and fresh leaves will sprout as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni nu ni elaaje lɛ aba shi ni ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Eshishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: What will happen if I plant my seeds too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Placing seeds too close together forces the growing plants to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition results in thin, weak stalks and small, low-quality yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibii ni ehiii baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when strong winds and rain come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that do not reach deep into the soil. When a plantain tree develops a heavy bunch of fruit, its top becomes heavy and wind can easily push the roots out of the ground unless you support the stem with wooden stakes.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni dumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ Amɛyitsei lɛ tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo. Ja okɛ tsei ni akɛfee tso lɛ fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and burn easily under harsh sunlight. They need temporary shade from crops like plantain trees to shield them and keep them cool while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ dumɔwui, koni ebu amɛhe ni eha amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Can harsh weather like strong sunshine really damage my cocoa trees like a disease would?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii tamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ agbe mi-kookoo tsei lɛ tamɔ hela ko?

english: Yes, direct sun scorch damages the leaves and weakens the tree's internal system just like a sickness, which stops the tree from growing strong and producing pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ mligbɛ gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ tamɔ hela. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ adara waa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are getting too much sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tsɔ?

english: If the leaves start turning pale, yellow, or scorched and crisp at the edges, your tree is getting too much direct sunlight and needs more shade cover.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eshã ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ miiná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni ená ŋmɔlɔ kroko.

english: How can strong wind affect my cocoa trees after I plant them?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baaná mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Strong winds can bend or snap the delicate stems of young trees, tear off leaves, and shake off flowers before they can turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ abɔle loo akumɔ tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ, agbá baai ni ekpokpo fɔfɔi dani amɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: What can I do on my farm to protect my cocoa trees from being damaged by strong winds?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mabu mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akafite amɛ?

english: You can plant tall shade trees around the borders of your farm to act as a windbreak, which reduces the strength of heavy winds before they hit your cocoa.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei kakadaji. Ha hulutsoo abɔle oŋmɔ lɛ he koni okɛtsu nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he tsɔne Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ hewalɛ baa shi dani etswaa kookoo lɛ.

english: What harm does it cause if bushes and weeds grow around my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ awui baaba kɛji jwɛi kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ he fɛɛ he? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Overgrown weeds steal water, sunshine, and soil nutrients from your cocoa. They can also choke young seedlings and shelter pests that attack your farm.
ga: Jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ baaju nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ okokoo lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfo dumɔwui bibii kɛ kooloi ni tutuaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hu.

english: How far should I clear the bush around my cocoa seedlings to keep them safe?
ga: Esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ. Te kookoo yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ha tɛŋŋ?

english: You should clear the weeds in a wide circle around the base of each cocoa tree so the seedling doesn't have to compete for soil nutrients or get covered by wild vegetation.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ jwɛi awo kooyigbɛ ni mli kwɔ ni obɔle he lɛ mli. Kookoo tso fɛɛ tso shishitoo Enɛ ji koni ehe akahia ni dumɔwui lɛ atswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo koo mli tsei aha amɛhe.

english: Is planting my cocoa seedlings well all I need to do to get a good harvest later?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ koni sɛɛ mli lɛ maná yibii kpakpai kɛkɛ?

english: No, planting is only the first step. You must regularly protect the young trees from hot sun, wind, and weeds so they survive and produce a full harvest.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ji klɛŋklɛŋ gbɛ pɛ. Esa akɛ obu odumɔwui lɛ ahe daa kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ jwɛi ahe. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ ahi shi ni ewo eyibii babaoo.

english: Why am I getting very few cocoa pods even though I planted many cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi fioo ko pɛ nɔ nɛkɛ? He ni aduɔ kookoo tsei babaoo yɛ lɛ?

english: Low pod production often happens when young cocoa trees were neglected or damaged early on by wind, sun scorch, or weeds, which prevents them from building the strength to bear many pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi lɛ baa kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ, hulutsoo, loo jwɛi kuɔ hiɛ ashwieɔ cacao tsei bibii anɔ loo efiteɔ amɛ mra, ni no haaa tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: What regular checks should I perform on my cocoa farm to make sure my trees stay healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ kwɛmɔi esa akɛ mafee daa yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana nɔmimaa akɛ mitsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ?

english: You should regularly inspect your farm for tall weeds choking seedlings, leaves showing signs of sun scorch, stems bent by wind, and any early pests hiding on the plants.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa kɛji jwɛi kakadaŋŋ atsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa. Baai ni tsɔɔ hulutsoo he okadii, tsei akutsei ni ebɔle kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli, kɛ mra be mli kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ amli ni amɛtee amɛhe amɛwo tsei lɛ amli.

english: This usually happens when your soil is low on nitrogen, a key nutrient maize needs to stay green. The plant automatically moves its remaining nitrogen from older bottom leaves to nourish the new top leaves, causing the lower ones to yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Akɛni ŋmãa ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ehi shi eŋɔli. Tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jieɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my crops give smaller harvests when I plant many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe be mli ni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same limited water, sunlight, and food in the soil. This leaves all the plants weak and undersized instead of letting a few grow strong and productive.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu fioo, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni efeɔ bibioo. Mohu ɔ, a ngmɛɔ tso komɛ blɔ nɛ a wa nɛ a woɔ yiblii.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny root nodules that capture natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the legumes are harvested, that leftover nitrogen feeds the next crop you plant, like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi bibii. No lɛ, ejɛɔ adebɔɔ mli emɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa Nakai nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛhaa ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight. Keeping taller shade trees or planting temporary crops like plantains provides cool shade and preserves soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ.

english: Why do I need to train and tie my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔseɔ ni mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to create food that feeds the growing tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground away from weeds, helping them catch light and preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni fiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ asɛɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ni ajie kɛjɛ jwɛi lɛ ahe. Ehaa baa lɛ naa la ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do some shoot suckers on my plantain tree produce small bunches while others yield big ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ tsei bibii yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi woɔ yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Shoots with narrow, spear-like leaves (sword suckers) have strong root systems connected to the main tree and yield large bunches. Shoots with wide, broad leaves early on (water suckers) have weak root bases and produce poor harvests.
ga: Tsei bibii ni baai bibii tamɔ akpɔlɔi (klante ŋmeii) lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni kɛ tso titri lɛ kpãa gbee ni amɛwoɔ aduawai akui wuji. Tsei bibii ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ, ni mli kwɔ (ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu) lɛ bɛ shishitoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Tomato flowers drop when heat is too intense, when water is inconsistent, or when there is insufficient wind or insect activity to shake pollen inside the blossom to form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji la lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ mli ejɔɔɔ loo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ akpokpo kɛyashi ebaawo yibii.

english: Why does my maize plant produce tassels at the top and sticky silks lower down before forming corn ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛ siliki ni ŋmɔɔ yɛ shishigbɛ dani abele toi lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: The tassel at the top sheds pollen into the air, which must fall onto the sticky silks below. Each silk connects to a single grain on the cob; without successful pollination on the silk, the ear will be empty.
ga: Tassels ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ shwieɔ pollen kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. ni esa akɛ egbee siliki ni shwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ Akɛ siliki tsɔi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko kpãa ŋmei kome ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ pollination ni yɔɔ siliki nɔ lɛ yeee omanye lɛ Toi lɛ baafee efolo.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites hiding on the underside of leaves to suck out the sap, or by plant viruses transmitted by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛmu nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain saturates the farm without proper drainage, the standing water suffocates the roots and allows fungal rot to develop.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyiɔ ŋmɔji amli ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɛ mli lɛ. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or planting beans in the soil helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo adu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for me to apply fertilizer on dry soil right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli dani ahum baa lɛ ehiii kɛhaaa mi lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes away fertilizer from dry topsoil before plant roots can absorb it. Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil so it dissolves slowly where the roots can reach it.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaho fiofio. yɛ hei ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ayashɛ he lɛ

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rain floods the ground for too long, water fills all the air spaces, causing the roots to drown and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Nu lɛ baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ fɛɛ amli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting inside my barn even when I want to store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji miisumɔ ni mahi shi po?

english: Yams are living roots that naturally wake up and sprout when they sense warm, humid air. Storing them in a cool, well-ventilated barn delays sprouting and keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ amɛbote kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛkwɛ̃mɔ asɛɛ afo, ni ebaaha amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Cocoa flowers fall off if the tree gets stressed by dry winds, lack of water, or insect pests like mirids. Ensuring good shade and protecting trees from pests helps flowers develop into healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, nu ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pollen tswa tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kpakpa ha tso lɛ ni abu he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that do not go deep into the soil. Supporting them with strong wooden stakes or planting them in groups helps protect them from blowing over in storm winds.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni wa fi amɛsɛɛ loo okɛ amɛ wo kui amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe koni ahum akatswa amɛ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, often when watering is irregular. Consistent watering helps the plant absorb calcium evenly to form healthy fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ kɛbaa. ni bei pii lɛ, awoɔ lɛ nu be fɛɛ be Nu ni awoɔ lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium lɛ tsuɔ nii pɛpɛɛpɛ koni ená hewalɛ kpakpa.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce fewer peppers when I plant them directly under dense tree shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ pepper fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need full sunlight to make energy for flowering and fruiting. Under heavy shade, the plant grows tall and leafy searching for light, but lacks the energy to produce peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaafɔlɔ ni amɛwo yibii. yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ebaa lɛ he baahia la. Shi hewalɛ ko bɛ ni akɛbaafee chili ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do small caterpillars destroy my cowpea flowers before the pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii fiteɔ tsina fɔfɔi lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Insects like pod borers lay eggs in cowpea buds, and the hatching caterpillars eat the flowers. Spraying safe neem extract or approved treatments at the start of flowering protects the blossoms.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ pod borer lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ tsina ŋmeii amli. ni ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ lɛ yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem mli nu ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my groundnut plants suddenly dry up and die while the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa ni egboɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is often caused by soil diseases that attack the roots and block water from reaching the rest of the plant. Rotating groundnuts with maize or cassava helps prevent these diseases from building up in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni etsĩɔ nu gbɛ koni ekashɛ tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai nɛɛ akabua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better for me to plant my crops early or late in the season?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii mra loo yɛ be ni shɛɔ naagbee lɛ mli?

english: The best planting time depends on rainfall patterns. Planting too early can expose young seeds to sudden heat dry spells, while planting too late leaves tender crops vulnerable to heavy end-of-season rains that can flood and destroy them.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ damɔ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui bibii lɛ agbi trukaa kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni darako tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ ni baanyɛ aha nu afua aba ni efite amɛ lɛ.

english: What should I do on my farm if the rains arrive much earlier than expected?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ oya fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ?

english: When rains arrive early, prepare your land quickly but avoid planting all your seeds at once. Early rains can sometimes be false starts, so staggered planting protects you from losing your entire crop if the dry weather returns.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ba mra lɛ Saamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ oya. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ ni ooodu shikome lɛ he. Bei komɛi lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra be mli lɛ baanyɛ afee amale shishijee. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔ ni ooodu yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɔ lɛ buɔ ohe koni onibii fɛɛ akafite kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: What risks do I face if I plant my seeds very early in the season?
ga: Mɛɛ osharai mikɛkpeɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui yɛ be lɛ mli mra kwraa?

english: Early planting carries the risk of unpredictable weather. If the rains start and then suddenly stop, the scorching sun can burn young seedlings or prevent seeds from germinating properly.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Oshara yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni bɛ shiŋŋ he. Kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ni ekpa trukaa Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii loo etsĩ dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops rot and die when there is heavy rainfall on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills air pockets in the soil, suffocating plant roots so they cannot breathe. Too much water also promotes root rot diseases and washes essential plant nutrients deep into the ground out of reach of the roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ obɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hu haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni efɔseɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How can I prevent heavy water from destroying crops that I planted late?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mihe ni miitsii lɛ naa koni ekafite miŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: You can construct raised soil beds or mounds and dig simple drainage channels around your fields. This allows excess rainwater to flow off safely without standing around the base of your crops.
ga: You can create raised beds or mounds. ni otsa nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ he gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo Ehaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe ni edamɔɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away crops on my farm while my neighbor's farm remains fine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli hi lɛ?

english: Farms differ in soil drainage, land slope, and preparation methods. Land that is flat without drainage ditches or soil with heavy clay will hold too much water, whereas sloped or well-drained land allows excess water to escape.
ga: Esoro ŋmɔji yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli. slope of the soil and how to prepare Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli loo shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ ni sũ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baaha nu babaoo ahi shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hei ni shwieɔ shi loo hei ni nu hoɔ yɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my crops are dying from a plant disease or from a lack of water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela loo nu ni faaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ miigboi?

english: Water shortage usually causes crops across the entire field to wilt uniformly during the heat of the day. Crop diseases typically appear as spots, yellowing, mold, or rotting on specific plants before spreading to others.
ga: Nu ni faaa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai jeɔ kpo tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei komɛi anɔ dani egbɛɔ eshwaa tsei krokomɛi anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops withering even though there has been plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ? He ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ lɛ?

english: Withering during rainy periods often indicates fungal or bacterial disease fostered by high moisture, or damaged root systems caused by waterlogged soil preventing nutrient uptake.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo mli baa lɛ ji fungal loo bacteria hela. loo shishifãi ni efite ni shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ kɛbaa ni haa enyɛɛɛ eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: How can I figure out what specifically went wrong if my harvest is poor this year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nɔ pɔtɛɛ ni ejaaa kɛji akɛ mikpamɔ afi nɛɛ ehiii?

english: Inspect your farm carefully by checking for signs of pest damage, withered leaves, waterlogged patches, or diseased plants. Comparing these signs against weather patterns during the season helps identify the exact problem.
ga: Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni otao okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai efite, baai ni egbo, kɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ he hei. loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ Kɛ́ akɛ okadii nɛɛ to be mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ana naagbai lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How do I know if my low crop yield was caused by my farming methods or bad weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi lɛ jɛ gbɛi ni mitsɔɔ nɔ mitsuɔ okwaayeli he nii loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ?

english: Compare your yield with nearby farms that planted at different times or used different land preparation techniques. If everyone experienced low yields, bad weather is likely responsible; if only your farm suffered, your planting timing or soil management might need adjustment.
ga: Okɛ onibii ni onáa lɛ ato ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ bo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli lɛ ahe. loo okɛ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ gbɛ̀i srɔtoi atsu nii Kɛji mɔ fɛɛ mɔ naa nibii ni baa shi lɛ Ekolɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛji oŋmɔ lɛ kɛ naagbai miikpe lɛ Ekolɛ ehe baahia ni atsake Dumɔ bei loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense direct sunlight and burn easily. Fast-growing plantains provide big, broad leaves that create necessary shade and keep the soil moist during the cocoa tree's early stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa, ni amɛshãa oya. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa baa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ cacao shishijee bei amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the leaves on top look big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: When cassava receives too much water or nitrogen, it directs its growth energy into producing tall stems and broad leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to develop big tubers below ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nu loo nitrogen babaoo nɔ lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ ni haa eda lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛba shi koni ekɛ bulbs agboi aba shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves in young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, or the ground is so waterlogged that the plant's roots cannot take up oxygen and nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aahu akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat, lack of regular water, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on leaves rather than setting fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama ebaai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe eyibii lɛ.

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival response. By shedding leaves during dry periods, the tree prevents water loss through transpiration and conserves its internal moisture until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hetoo kɛha wala. Kɛtsɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli lɛ nɔ. Tsei baatsi nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. ni okwɛ koni fɛ̃i ahi mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why does my cowpea crop produce plenty of leaves but very few seed pods when it rains too much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are adapted to drier conditions. Excessive rainfall signals the crop to keep growing vegetarian shoots and vines instead of triggering the stress response needed to flower and produce seeds.
ga: Akɛ cowpeas lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aya nɔ adu aduawai tsei kɛ wain tsei. Mohu ɔ, e haa nɛ haomi nɛ he hia kɛ ha fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi a fɔmi ɔ jeɔ kpo.

english: Why do armyworms attack my maize plants so aggressively while ignoring my nearby cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ waa ni amɛkuɔ amɛhiɛ amɛshwieɔ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms prefer grass-family plants like maize, sorghum, and sugarcane because the leaves are tender and easy to digest compared to the tougher, chemically defended leaves of cassava.
ga: Fall armyworms sumɔɔ jwɛi tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ejaakɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ oya kɛ akɛto ŋmãa baa ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni tsofai buɔ he lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upward and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Curled, small leaf growth in tomatoes is typically caused by the tomato yellow leaf curl virus, which is spread between plants by tiny insects called whiteflies during warm weather.
ga: baai bibii adalɛ Yɛ tomato mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tomato yellow leaf curl virus lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. ni ŋmeii bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ateŋ lɛ Atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Yam tubers rot underground when soil drainage is poor and rainwater sits for too long, allowing waterborne fungi and nematodes to enter and destroy the soft tuber tissue.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni hiɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my okra plants grow tall and thick like trees without giving me many pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ daa ni ekwɛɔ tamɔ tso shi ewooo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Okra plants grow tall and woody without fruiting if they are planted too close together—causing them to compete for sunlight—or if seed pods are left unpicked for too long, signaling the plant to stop fruiting.
ga: Rosella tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji hulu la ni ajuɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ ashi dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ ni ajieee amɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Etsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ ekpa yibiiwoo.

english: This usually happens because the plant lacks nitrogen. Maize moves nitrogen from its older, lower leaves up to the younger leaves at the top to keep growing, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Abɛi tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni eda ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni baai lɛ aya nɔ ada. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Pepper plants often drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli baa lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane latsaa mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In extreme afternoon heat, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to conserve moisture and will usually recover in the evening when it cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ beni edɔ lɛ.

english: How come my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich manure, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing heavy leaves above ground instead of sending food down to expand the tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baatsu nii koni ekɛwo bulb lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do fall armyworms attack the middle funnel of my young maize plants instead of the outer leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ tutuaa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋgbɛ faa lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: The central funnel or whorl of a young maize plant contains tender, juicy leaves that are easy for young armyworms to chew and hide in, protecting them from sunlight and natural predators.
ga: Abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ funnel, loo whorl lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni ewaaa akɛ aaaye ni akɛ asraafoi amli ŋmeii teeɔ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu kɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why do fungal diseases spread so fast on my vegetable farm during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fungi thrive in warm, damp air. Rain splashes fungal spores from the soil onto plant leaves, and constant wetness allows the fungi to quickly enter and infect the crop.
ga: Mold yeɔ omanye yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Nugbɔ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli lɛ shwieɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa ŋmeii boteɔ tsei amli ni amɛyeɔ hela oya.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to grow or rot in the soil when I bury them deep?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ loo amɛgbooo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni mifuɔ amɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds need oxygen and warmth near the soil surface to sprout. If buried too deeply, the seedling runs out of stored energy before reaching sunlight and dies underground.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ dɔlɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli tsɔ Hewalɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ ato lɛ baaho dani hulu la lɛ abashɛ amɛnɔ ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does animal manure take longer to show results on my crops compared to chemical bag fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani kooloi ashishifãi jieɔ yibiiwoo kpo yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ akɛto tsofai ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer releases nutrients immediately into soil water, whereas manure must first be broken down by soil organisms over several weeks before the plant roots can feed on it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ agbala ŋmɔshi nibii amli klɛŋklɛŋ otsii babaoo dani tsei shishifãi lɛ aye.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers rot faster when kept in a warm, closed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harvested yams are still alive and breathing. Heat makes them breathe faster and sweat out water, creating a warm, damp environment where bacteria and mold grow quickly.
ga: Atomɔ nii ni akpaa lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛmiimu. Dɔlɛ lɛ haa amɛmuɔ oya ni ehaa amɛwoɔ latsaa. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. he ni bacteria kɛ fungi daa oya yɛ lɛ

english: Why do tomatoes brought from dry regions like Burkina Faso last longer in the market than my locally grown tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni akɛbaa kɛjɛɔ hei ni nu bɛ tamɔ Burkina Faso lɛ hiɔ jara nɔ be kakadaŋŋ fe tomato ni miduɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes grown in drier climates or bred as specific firm varieties naturally have thicker skins and lower moisture content, which helps them resist soft rots and bruising during storage and transport.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli egbi loo ni akwɛɔ lɛ pɔtɛɛ aha henɔi ni wa lɛ baaná hewolo ni mli tse ni ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hu baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomato ni eshiɔ fitemɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni efiteɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ kɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves burn and turn brown when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out the soil. Leaving shade trees or planting temporary cover like plantains protects young plants until they are strong enough to handle more sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni ashiɔ loo aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa he be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo.

english: If I plant my cassava sticks very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from the land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he waa Ani maná yibii babaoo?

english: Planting cassava too close causes the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak plants with very small roots. Giving them proper space yields larger, heavier tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shishifãi bibii waa baa. Kɛ́ okɛ he ko ni sa ha lɛ, ebaaha yitso lɛ afee agbo ni etsii.

english: Why does my old plantain tree stop giving me big bunches when many small shoots grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu momo lɛ kpa ŋmeii wuji feemɔ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani oooda yɛ tso lɛ he?

english: The small shoots (suckers) take food and water away from the main mother plant. Cutting away extra suckers and leaving only one or two healthy ones ensures the main tree has enough energy to produce a large bunch.
ga: Tso bibii lɛ (tso lɛ) kɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni jɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young growing top leaves, showing it needs fertilizer or compost.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia bo.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans makes the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni adu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots rot in the ground after harvest, that natural fertilizer stays in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tso shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã sũ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do small insects suddenly swarm my pepper plants right after a short rain when the hot sun comes back?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ trukaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ lɛ? Beni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa?

english: Warm and humid conditions after rain cause pest populations to explode quickly. Insects like aphids thrive in heat and feed on the soft, fresh shoots that grow fast after receiving rainwater.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ oya. Kplukai tamɔ aphids lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii heei ni daa oya kɛji amɛná nugbɔ nu lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks water, or if bees are not visiting to pollinate them. Without pollination or under heat stress, the plant sheds the flower to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be ni tso lɛ bɛ nu Aloo kɛji ŋmeii baaa koni amɛbafee pollination. Kɛji akɛ pollination bɛ loo yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ shishi. Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch maximum sunlight for building underground tubers. Staking also keeps the foliage off the wet ground, preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ eshwɛɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni akafoliar helai anaa.

english: Why do my vegetable seeds rot in the soil instead of sprouting during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil gets soaked with too much water, it loses oxygen, causing seeds to drown and rot. Excess moisture also encourages fungi in the soil to attack the seeds before they can sprout.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lɛ ebaafite kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ hu woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua dumɔwui dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Should I put fertilizer on my crop right before a heavy downpour comes?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba?

english: It is best not to fertilize right before heavy rain because torrential water washes the nutrients away before plant roots can soak them up. Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not during heavy storms.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akawo mli dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa aba ejaakɛ nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ baajie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi jeee yɛ ahum ni naa wa be mli.

english: How do I know when my cocoa pods are completely ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cocoa pods change color when fully ripe, usually turning from green to bright yellow, or from red/purple to orange. Harvesting them at this stage ensures the beans inside are mature and ready for proper fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. aloo kɛjɛ red/purple kɛyashi orange Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it recommended to crack cocoa pods open with a wooden club instead of a sharp knife?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tso agbele kookoo ŋmɔ mli moŋ fe ni akɛ tsɔne ni mli wa baatsu nii lɛ?

english: Using a sharp metal knife can slice into the beans inside the pod. Damaged beans rot quickly, ferment unevenly, and reduce the quality grade of your harvest, whereas a blunt wooden club opens the pod safely.
ga: Dade ŋmei ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ Baanyɛ afo kɔfe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ pod lɛ mli lɛ. Beans ni efite lɛ baafite oya. Fermentation ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee ni ebaa okpamɔ lɛ nɔ. Akɛni tso lɛ mli ejɔ hewɔ lɛ, ebaafee shweshweeshwe akɛ aaagbele tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I dry my harvested cocoa beans directly on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ migbiɔ mi-kokoo yibii ni mikpa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Drying beans directly on the ground exposes them to dirt, dust, livestock, and moisture from the soil, which causes mold to grow. Drying them on raised wooden mats or clean plastic sheets keeps the beans clean and high quality.
ga: Beans ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa muji, sũ, kooloi, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa amɛ. ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa Kɛ́ agbi yɛ tsei ni awo nɔ loo plastic ni he tse nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔfi ŋmɔji lɛ ahe tseɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the correct way to ferment my fresh cocoa beans after taking them out of the pods?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ afeɔ kookoo ŋmeii heei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ mli beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Ferment fresh beans by piling them on fresh plantain or banana leaves, covering them tightly, and leaving them for about six days while turning the heap every two days. This process turns the beans brown and creates the chocolate flavor buyers look for.
ga: Okɛ ŋmeii heei afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛtsɔ amɛ ni oookɛto plantains loo banana baai heei anɔ lɛ nɔ, ni okɛha nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni oshi amɛ aaafee gbii enumɔ, ni otsake ŋmei lɛ daa gbii enyɔ. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni ehaa tsokolate ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, cool, and overly shaded conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let in sunlight and removing infected pods quickly helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni jɛmɛ ejɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli fe nine. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni hulu la aba mli, ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry weather or the Harmattan season, cocoa trees drop their leaves to conserve water and protect themselves from heat stress. Planting shade trees and placing mulch around the trunk helps hold moisture in the soil.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi loo harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ amɛtsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are some of my cassava roots rotting underground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water collects around them in poorly drained soil. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why do my young maize leaves start turning yellow at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which crops need to build healthy green leaves. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help your crop recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii awo baai ni wa, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do shade trees help my mature cocoa farm in the long run?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Shade trees protect crops from severe sunlight, keep the soil cool during dry seasons, and drop leaves that decay into free natural fertilizer for your soil.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni ehaa baai ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: How often should I clear weeds around my young crops?
ga: Esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Shii enyiɛ tsei bibii kwɛ̃ɔ?

english: You should clear weeds whenever they begin growing close to your crops, typically every 4 to 6 weeks. Removing weeds early stops them from stealing light, water, and plant nutrients from your main crop.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe, bei pii lɛ daa otsii 4 kɛyashi 6. Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju la, nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii kɛjɛ otsei titrii lɛ amli.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my crops when the weather keeps changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu nii yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Crops need steady soil moisture to germinate. Planting too early during a brief 'false rain' causes seeds to dry up and die before the true rainy season establishes.
ga: Tsei he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ yɛ "nugbɔshiimɔ amale" be kuku lɛ mli lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ aba.

english: Can mobile phone weather forecasts really tell me what will happen on my specific farm in the village?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he adafitswaa ni yɔɔ mi-mobile phone lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ mi nɔ ni baaba miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ akrowa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Phone forecasts provide general weather patterns for a broad area, but local features in your village can cause rain to fall in one place while completely missing a farm just a short distance away.
ga: Tɛlifon kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he gbalɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ henɔi kɛha he ko ni da. Shi akutso lɛ mli sui ni yɔɔ nyɛ akrowa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha nugbɔ anɛ yɛ he kome. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔji komɛi bɛ ni kɛ jɛmɛ jɛkɛɛɛ.

english: What can I do to protect my young crops from dying if the rains stop for two weeks right after planting?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mabu mitsei bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi kɛji nugbɔ kpa nɛmɔ otsii enyɔ yɛ be mli ni midu lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil around plant stems with dry grass or leaves (mulching) acts as a protective blanket, trapping moisture in the ground and keeping soil cool during dry spells.
ga: Mulching around Ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha tso lɛ shishifãi ahe (mulching) tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli

english: If I spend money to hire a tractor to clear my land, will I lose my investment if the rain fails?
ga: Kɛji okɛ shika lɛ ha trakta ni okɛjie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, ani nɔ ko baafite?

english: Yes, heavy machines help prepare land quickly, but without sufficient rain or irrigation, seeds will not grow, and the money spent hiring the machine cannot be recovered from harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni tsii yeɔ ebuaa ni asaa shikpɔŋ oya. Shi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Dumɔwu lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ. Ni anyɛɛɛ ana shika ni akɛhaa tsɔnei ni akɛhaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli.

english: Does using heavy machinery on my farm harm the soil for my crops?
ga: Ani tsɔnei ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ nii lɛ awui?

english: Heavy machines can pack topsoil down tightly, making it hard for crop roots to spread and for rainwater to soak into the ground unless the soil is properly managed.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛha tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ni nugbɔ nu baanyɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ja akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do insects and pests always seem to attack my crops at a specific time during the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi kɛ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ bei komɛi amli yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests follow seasonal life cycles triggered by warmth and humidity, hatching in large numbers precisely when young, soft crop shoots appear for easy feeding.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nyiɛɔ be mli wala shihilɛi ni dɔlɛ kɛ latsaa kɛbaa lɛ sɛɛ. Amɛfɔɔ babaoo kɛji ŋmeii bibii je kpo koni amɛye niyenii mlɛo.

english: How can I tell if pests are starting to attack my farm before they destroy all my plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ miibɔi miŋmɔ lɛ tutuamɔ dani amɛfite mitsei lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Walking through your field early in the morning to inspect the undersides of leaves and crop stems helps you spot tiny eggs or early damage before an outbreak spreads.
ga: Kɛ́ onyiɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi ni okwɛ tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona ŋmeii bibii lɛ. loo nɔ ni fiteɔ mra dani hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa

english: Why do crops grow very tall on one section of my farm but stay short and weak on another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome shi amɛhe waaa yɛ fã kroko lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil depth, nutrient levels, and water holding capacity vary across short distances on land, causing plants in richer soil spots to grow faster than those in poor spots.
ga: shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ Nutrient level Ni nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu lɛ srɔtoi yɛ gbɛ kukuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli, ni no haa tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ shika babaoo lɛ daraa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni ehiii lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a survival mechanism where the plant shrinks its leaf surface exposed to the sun to reduce water loss through evaporation during intense heat.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala. Tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ ebaa lɛ nɔ kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. Koni ajie nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I combine my elders' traditional knowledge of our land with modern farming advice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ wɔ onukpai lɛ akusum nilee ni kɔɔ wɔshikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ afata ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli he ŋaawoi ahe lɛ?

english: Local knowledge tells you the history of pests and soil behavior on your specific land, while modern advice helps you protect against unpredictable weather changes and plan modern farm investments safely.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli nilee baatsɔɔ bo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe yinɔsane kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ subaŋ yɛ oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaawoi yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ ahe. ni ato shika ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmɔji amli lɛ he gbɛjianɔ shweshweeshwe

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong, direct sunlight because their root systems and leaves are delicate. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and preserves soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crop turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the soil is waterlogged. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea after clearing weeds helps the leaves turn green and promotes growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa amɛdaraa.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my pepper plants drop off when the ground gets dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their lower leaves during dry periods as a self-defense reaction to save water. Mulching the soil with dry grass helps keep moisture in the ground during hot spells.
ga: Pepper tsei shiɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ ni amɛhiɛɛɛ nɔ ko nɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ amɛhe nɔ koni nu akafite. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spray strong insect chemical medicine on my cocoa farm when the trees are covered in flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni he wa lɛ shwieɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? He ni fɔfɔii ehà tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Spraying chemicals during flowering kills tiny beneficial insects called midges that carry pollen between cocoa flowers. Without these midges, cocoa flowers cannot turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ baagbe kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Kɛ gbɔmɛi nɛɛ bɛ lɛ, Cocoa fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee cocoa ŋmeii.

english: Why do weeds make my maize grow thin and short even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni efeɔ kuku kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight from the maize roots underground. Clearing weeds during the first month allows the maize to get all the nutrients it needs to grow thick stalks.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ abele shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni enáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmãa ni mli tse.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers drop off the branches without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress from heat, prolonged dry weather, insect attacks, or nutrient shortages. Proper shade management and timely fertilization help retain flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ba amɛnɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, kooloi ni tutuaa mɔ, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa He ni akwɛɔ hulutsoo nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi.

english: Why is it necessary for me to stake my yam vines with wood sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso tswaa sweet potato wain tso lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the damp ground so they can catch direct sunlight for growth while preventing soil-borne fungal diseases from destroying the leaves.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potatoes kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛdara yɛ be mli ni etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hu naa koni amɛkafite baai lɛ.

english: How do I know if my cassava tubers are mature enough for harvesting under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the bottom leaves dry up and drop off, and cracks begin to appear in the soil around the base of the stem due to expanding roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Ni ŋmeii bɔi baa yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli yɛ shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ hewɔ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra suckers growing at the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight with the main plant for food and water, resulting in small bunches. Pruning extra shoots ensures the main stem yields a heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ afee ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Black rotted bottoms on tomatoes, known as blossom-end rot, happen when plants cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, often due to inconsistent watering.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni fiteɔ yɛ tomato nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ blossom end fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do so many flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers but drop most of them when the tree lacks enough water, shade, or soil nutrients to feed full pods.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu, hulutsoo loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in damp, heavily shaded conditions. Pruning excess branches and weeding allows sunlight and air to keep the pods dry.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ egbiɔ.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees giving me fewer pods now than five years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo fe afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 years, their root systems weaken and the surrounding soil gets drained of nutrients, meaning old trees need soil fertilization, pruning, or gradual replanting.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tsei ye fe afii 20 lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ, ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni awo tsei momo lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii, afolɔ amɛ loo adu amɛ ekoŋŋ fiofio.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the essential nutrient plants need to stay green and build strong grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava plant have big tall leaves but small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai kakadaji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much leaf-building nutrient (nitrogen) but not enough tuber-building nutrient (potassium), cassava puts all its energy into growing tall branches instead of expanding roots.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni haa baai lɛ maa (nitrogen) babaoo tsɔ shi ebɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmeii (potassium) lɛ fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha eshishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my young corn plants turn a purplish color?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ purple lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young corn usually indicate phosphorus deficiency, showing that the plant roots cannot get the energy nutrients they need to grow strong early on.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ mra.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up tightly when the afternoon sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce the leaf area exposed to direct sun, preventing internal water from evaporating too fast during heat.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi. Enɛ ji koni nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni edɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my farm soil dry out and harden so quickly after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ewaa oya kɛji nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil without leaf cover loses water rapidly to heat. Adding organic materials like dead leaves or mulch acts like a sponge to trap rainwater in the soil longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni baa bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛyaa dɔlɛ mli. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ hu tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni ekɛmɔɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit dormant buried in the soil. Clearing land exposes them to sunlight, allowing them to sprout rapidly and consume available nutrients faster than newly planted seed crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ewɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ. Enɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe dumɔwui tsei ni adu ehee lɛ.

english: Why are the outer leaves on my plantain trees turning yellow and snapping at the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifo yɛ eshishifã lɛ he lɛ?

english: This typically occurs when root parasites or stem fungi block water channels inside the plant, causing the heavy lower leaves to dry out and snap under their own weight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shishifãi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai loo fɔlɔi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai tsi nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ baai ni tsii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfoɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsiimɔ shishi.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting and becoming soft while I am waiting in the village for buyers to come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi shweremɔ ni efee blɛoo beni mimɛɔ mɔ ko ni baahe yɛ akrowa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harvested yams are still living tubers. When kept in warm, dark storage, they naturally use up their stored nutrients and water to sprout new shoots, which shrinks the tuber and makes it soft over time.
ga: Yams ni akpa lɛ ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka lolo. Kɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ kɛ duŋ Amɛbaafite niyenii kɛ nu ni ato lɛ ni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii heei. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What happens to my plantains if I leave them on the tree too long while waiting for market prices to go up?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi plantains lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni mimɛɔ ni jara nɔ jara aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving plantains on the stalk past maturity causes them to ripen and soften rapidly. Once soft, they bruise easily during transport and spoil quickly, making market buyers reject them or offer lower prices.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi plantains lɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ ni efee blɛoo oya. Kɛji eyɛ bɔdɔɔ lɛ Efoɔ oya yɛ gbɛfaa mli ni efiteɔ oya. Enɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ kpooɔ loo amɛkɛ jara ni baa shi haa.

english: Why do my stored cocoa beans develop black mold while sitting in my house waiting for a buyer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni ato lɛ feɔ ŋmeii diji beni amɛtara shia ni amɛmiimɛ mɔ ko ni baahe lɛ?

english: If cocoa beans are not dried completely before storage, residual moisture trapped inside combined with warm room air encourages fungal spores to grow, leading to mold that ruins the bean quality.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛtoɔ lɛ Fɛ̃i ni eshwɛ yɛ mli lɛ kɛ tsu mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe hewalɛ koni amɛdara. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ni fiteɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa.

english: Why do my harvested fresh peppers shrivel up and lose weight after sitting for just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper ni mikpa ehee lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔɔ beni mita shi gbii fioo komɛi pɛ lɛ?

english: Once peppers are picked, they are cut off from the plant's water supply. They continuously lose water through their skin into the air, causing the cells to collapse and the fruit to wrinkle and lose weight.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmeii lɛ anaa lɛ, ajieɔ Chili ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛɔ nitsumɔhe lɛ nu jɛɛhe lɛ mli. Amɛjieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛhewolo nɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli be fɛɛ be. ehaa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni aduawai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe waaa

english: Why do my stored cowpeas turn into powder with tiny holes after keeping them for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni ato lɛ tsɔɔ powda ni amɛyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Beni akɛto otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Weevils often lay microscopic eggs on the pods in the field. After harvest, these eggs hatch inside storage, and the grubs eat the inside of the seeds before chewing their way out, leaving hollow shells.
