ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ. beni akpa kpamɔ sɛɛ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baafɔ yɛ he ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ mli. Ni ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli dani amɛyeɔ amɛ. ni eshiɔ ŋmei ni mli ewo muji

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are fully mature and ready to harvest before they spoil in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa dani amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves yellow and drop off. Leaving roots in the ground too long past maturity causes them to become woody, fibrous, and lose their starch content.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shɛɔ dalɛ he beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛfeɔ tsei, amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers without producing fruits during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato pollen to dry out and become sterile. When flowers are not successfully pollinated, the plant naturally drops the blossoms to save energy instead of forming fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato mli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Kɛ fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination lɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔii yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves curl up and droop in the afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: On hot days, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can absorb it from the soil. Curling and drooping is a natural defense mechanism to reduce leaf surface area exposed to the hot sun.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Curling kɛ falling off ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛi ni akɛbaa baa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ shi.

english: Why do my maize grains crack and break easily when I dry them directly on the bare ground under intense sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ fãa ni amɛkuɔ oya kɛ́ migbi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Drying maize directly on hot ground under harsh sun causes the outer part of the grain to dry much faster than the inner core. This uneven drying creates stress inside the grain, leading to internal cracking.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ he ko ni mli edɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe emligbɛ fã lɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ejaaa nɛɛ kɛ haomɔ baa ŋmaa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji mligbɛ fãmɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods during certain months of the year even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi amli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees follow natural reproductive cycles dictated by seasonal temperature changes and daylight hours. The trees temporarily pause flowering to conserve energy for leaf growth and survival.
ga: Cacao tsei nyiɛɔ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni be mli latsaa kɛ hulutsoo be mli la tsakemɔi tsɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Tsei kpa fɔfɔi fɔmɔ be kuku koni amɛbu hewalɛ kɛha baai adalɛ kɛ wala.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when there is no shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be ko bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are very tender and cannot handle direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains to shield them, the intense heat burns the leaves and dries up the soil moisture, causing the seedlings to die.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni baaha nɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji dumɔwui lɛ agbele.

english: Does it matter which way I point the cassava stem when planting it in the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ otsɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cassava stems upside down causes the roots and shoots to grow backwards, which reduces tuber yield or kills the plant. Always make sure the buds or nodes are pointing upwards toward the sky.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ adu ŋmei tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaha tuber yibii lɛ aba shi loo ebaaha tso lɛ agbo. Kwɛmɔ be fɛɛ be akɛ hiŋmɛi loo node lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: Planting too closely makes crops compete heavily with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin plants and smaller harvests compared to crops given enough room to grow.
ga: Tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋshii mli waa. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ baa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto tsei ni aha amɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ ahe.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to produce green leaves and grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does adding decomposed plant leaves and animal manure help my crops grow better than soil alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ kooloi ashishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ni mikɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ pɛ lɛ?

english: Organic matter like manure and decomposed leaves improves the soil's ability to hold water during dry spells and slowly releases essential nutrients that feed plant roots over time.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ kpo fiofio.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my field after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them after heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally restores fertility back into your land.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni ooodu yɛ kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ, baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aba ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What is eating ragged holes into the center of my young maize leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni ye bu ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is usually caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm. They hide deep inside the central whorl of the plant during the day and feed on the leaf tissues at night.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛ teɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ teŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi mli ni amɛ yeɔ baa fãji gbɛkɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these insects. Controlling the insects early helps prevent leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Mra Be mli Kooloi Ahe Nitsumɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ baai lɛ ahe fitemɔ naa.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomatoes turn black and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium to the developing fruit, usually caused by irregular watering or dry soil conditions.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ baa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha yibii ni miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi shihilɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do market buyers pay higher prices for specific cassava varieties over others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ jara nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi krokomɛi ahe nyɔmɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Buyers prefer specific cassava varieties based on how they process the crop; high-starch varieties are best for making gari or industrial starch, while softer varieties are preferred for making fufu.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmãa henɔi pɔtɛɛ ni damɔ bɔ ni atsuɔ ŋmãa lɛ he nii ahaa lɛ nɔ. Srɔtoi ni starch babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kari loo nitsumɔhei starch feemɔ. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ akɛ henɔi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ feɔ fufu.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a living umbrella that protects the cocoa from heat and preserves soil moisture until the trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ he kroko. Ehaa hulutsoo baa koni ebu kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ahi shi kɛyashi tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off instead of producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. The plant sheds flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he haomɔ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the primary food plants use to build green leaves, so when it runs low, the plant draws remaining nutrients from older lower leaves, turning them yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nɔ ko fioo pɛ eshwɛ Tso lɛ baajie niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli ni ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are my sweet potato roots thin and small even though the leaves on top are bushy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ ji ŋmɔji ni eyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant focuses all its energy on growing long vines and leaves above the ground instead of storing food in the roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ wain tsei kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ toɔ sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ sisi ɔ a mi.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and die when water sits around their roots after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu shwie shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper roots need oxygen from spaces in the soil to breathe. When water sits for too long without draining, it smothers the roots, causing root rot which prevents the plant from taking up water and nutrients.
ga: Pepper shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hei lɛ amli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ aŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Spreading dry grass, known as mulching, acts as a blanket over the dirt. It blocks sunlight from drying out the soil, keeps root temperatures cool, and prevents unwanted weeds from growing.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ hulu la naa ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni otsi jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny insects called whiteflies as they feed on the sap of the leaves.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ beni amɛyeɔ baai amli nu lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cowpea plants curl inward during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea leaves fold or turn away from direct sunlight during peak midday heat to reduce leaf surface area exposed to the sun, which stops moisture from escaping and protects the plant from drying out.
ga: Akɛ cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni akɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ haa nu ni hoɔ lɛ kpaa, ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he koni ekagbi.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes turn soft and rot so quickly before I can sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continue to ripen and generate heat after being picked. If they are harvested when overly soft, bruised in transport, or packed tightly in deep unventilated wooden boxes, rot fungi spread rapidly.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ baa beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ akpa loo lɛ blɛoo tsɔ Atswa lɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko loo akɛwo tso adekai ni mli kwɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ amli Fungal rot gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when heavy bunches of fruit start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai babaoo bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that stay near the surface. As the heavy fruit bunch develops at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy and can easily pull out of soft soil during high winds unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli shwereɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni tsii ni abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ nɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. ja akɛ tso nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsu nii

english: How do I know if my cassava leaves have pests on them before I decide to spray?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava baa lɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai dani makpɛ miyiŋ akɛ mafɔ amɛ nɔ?

english: You should walk through your farm and look closely at the undersides of the leaves and stems. Look for small insects, tiny holes, curled leaves, or unusual sticky spots, which mean pests are actively feeding on your plant.
ga: Esa akɛ otsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okwɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ jogbaŋŋ. Taomɔ kooloi bibii, buji bibii, baai ni ebɔle amɛhe, loo hei ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni shwieɔ shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ otsei lɛ miiye.

english: Why should I inspect my crop for insects instead of just spraying medicine on a set calendar schedule?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni mana kɛji ŋmeii yɛ mli? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ tsofa afɔ shi yɛ kalanda he gbɛjianɔtoo ko nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ.

english: Spraying on a strict schedule without checking wastes expensive chemicals if there are no insects present. Checking first ensures you only spray when pests are actually damaging the crop, saving you money and protecting your plants.
ga: Akɛ tsofa shwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa naa ni akwɛɛɛ kɛji jwɛi yɛ mli. tsofai ni jara wa Kɛji kooloi bɛ jɛmɛ Kwɛmɔ klɛŋklɛŋ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ baashwie nɔ pɛ be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ onibii lɛ miifite diɛŋtsɛ lɛ haa okɛ shika baa shi ni ebuɔ otsei lɛ ahe.

english: What signs on my cassava plant show that insects are troubling it?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii yɔɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ anɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ji naagba?

english: When insects attack cassava, you will usually see yellowing leaves, twisted or stunted shoots, holes eaten through the foliage, or leaves falling off early. Inspecting under the leaf usually reveals the tiny bugs responsible.
ga: Beni kooloi bibii tutua ŋmei Bei pii lɛ onaa kaadii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Tsoi ni etse loo egbɔjɔ, bu ni yeɔ baai lɛ, loo baai ni shwieɔ shi oya. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akwɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ, anaa ŋmeii bibii. no ji nɔ ni kɛbaa

english: Why do insects usually target the leaves of my cassava plant first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii lɛ tswaa mi-cassava baai lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Leaves are soft and filled with sap and nutrients that insects need for food. Since leaves act as the plant's food factory, heavy pest attacks on foliage directly reduce the plant's ability to grow big tubers underground.
ga: Baai lɛ ji bibii ni amɛyi obɔ kɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kooloi kɛha niyenii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii nitsumɔhei kɛhaa tsei. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni naa wa ni baa tso lɛ baai anɔ lɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛ bulbs wuji baa shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baa shi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Does cassava produce flowers, and what does it mean when I see them on my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmei haa fɔfɔi? Ni mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ mina lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: Yes, cassava plants can produce flowers as they mature. Flowering is a natural sign that the plant is moving into a new growth stage, but it also means the plant needs to be healthy and free of pests so it can focus energy on building tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei tsei baanyɛ akwɛ kɛji amɛdara kwraa. Fɔfɔii ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso ko miibote dalɛ be hee mli. Shi etsɔɔ hu akɛ ehe miihia ni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafee nɔ ko. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekɛ hewalɛ ama yitso lɛ maa nɔ.

english: What happens if I ignore pests on my young cassava plants and leave them untreated?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji miku mihiɛ mishwie tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ yucca tsei bibii anɔ lɛ anɔ ni mishi amɛ ni mikɛtsaaa amɛ?

english: If you leave pests untreated early on, their population will explode. They will destroy the leaves, stunt the plant's growth, and leave you with tiny or empty tubers at harvest time.
ga: Kɛji oshi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mra lɛ, Amɛyibɔ ​​baatswa. Amɛbaafite baai lɛ. ŋmɛɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ shi ni eshiɔ bo kɛ yitso bibioo loo yitsei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli

english: Why is it important to deal with pests early before my crops reach the flowering stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atsa tsɛŋemɔ helai mra lɛ? Dani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ fɔfɔii ahe?

english: Early protection keeps the leaves green and strong so the plant can make plenty of food. If pests weaken the plant before or during flowering, it won't have enough strength to develop thick, healthy tubers.
ga: Hebuu kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe awa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii babaoo. Kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ha tso lɛ gbɔjɔ dani ewo fɔfɔi loo yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Ebɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee yitso ni mli tse ni mli wa.

english: When is the right time to give my crops the first chemical spray?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa?

english: The first application should happen as soon as you spot living pests or early signs of damage during your farm checks, rather than waiting until the insects have multiplied and spread across the whole farm.
ga: Esa akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nitsumɔ lɛ aba mli pɛ kɛji ona kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli loo mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ nɔ ko efite yɛ be mli ni okwɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ kɛyashi kooloi bibii lɛ baafa babaoo ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ,.

english: Will spraying chemical medicine on my cassava harm the crop if there are no insects on it?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mi-cassava lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui kɛji kooloi bɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Yes, applying chemicals when there are no pests puts unnecessary stress on the plant leaves and burns your money. Chemical medicine should only be used as a targeted treatment when pests are present.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni he ehiaaa baa tsei ahe baai anɔ ni eshãa oshika. Esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ atsu nii akɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii pɛ kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: How many times am I supposed to spray my cassava field during the season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: There is no set number of times. You should only spray when regular farm checks show that pests have returned and are causing damage that requires treatment.
ga: Bei ayibɔ ko bɛ ni ato. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ pɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛmɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ eku esɛɛ eba ni eefite nii ni biɔ ni atsa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the nutrient plants need to make green leaves and food. Adding organic compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the maize grow green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli kɛ niyenii Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava grow giant leaves above ground but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big leaves instead of developing tubers. Balancing the soil with potassium-rich nutrients encourages the plant to store food in the roots instead.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmeii. Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ potassium lɛ to he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ niyenii toɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli moŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark black and rot right on the tree during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, damp conditions. Pruning heavy branches to let air and sunlight through, along with removing infected pods, helps stop the rot from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela, ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli ejɔ kɛbaa. niji ni tsii ni afoɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ hu. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in my young maize leaves, and how can I protect them?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he?

english: These holes are usually caused by Fall Armyworms feeding on tender foliage. Checking your farm early in the morning and applying approved neem extracts or targeted pesticides direct into the plant whorl can kill the worms before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ni yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi ni okɛ neem mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why should I plant plantains next to my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe?

english: Young cocoa seedlings get scorched easily under direct Ghanaian sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce large, broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, shielding the young cocoa trees from the heat until they are strong enough.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui shãa oya kɛji akɛ amɛ shɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ Ghana. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Can I grow cowpeas together with my maize in the same field without harming the maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cowpeas kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miyeŋ ŋmãa lɛ awui?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is beneficial because cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and enrich the soil, acting as a natural food source for the maize while covering the ground to prevent weeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ tsina ŋmãa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa lɛ yɛ be mli ni ekɛ ŋmãa shwieɔ nɔ koni jwɛi akabote mli.

english: How do I know if the first rainfall after the dry season is enough for me to start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: You should wait until two or three heavy rains have deeply soaked the soil rather than planting after the very first shower. Planting too early in dry soil causes seeds to dry out and die before they sprout properly.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efɔ. Mohu ɔ, mo du lɛ ngɛ kekleekle nu ɔ se. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll inward and look wrinkled during the hot dry afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl inward during high heat to trap moisture and prevent water from evaporating from the leaf surface. Covering the soil around the roots with dry grass (mulching) keeps the roots cool and reduces leaf curling.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle ehe kɛya mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni emɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛtsi nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and turn brown on their stakes when the tubers are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ beni bulb lɛ efee klalo lɛ?

english: When yams reach full maturity, the plant naturally stops growing leaves and transfers all remaining energy into the underground tuber. The drying of the vine is nature's signal that the yam is ready for harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ haa baai lɛ adalɛ kpaa ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ yaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Wein tsei lɛ ni agbiɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potatoes eshɛ he kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ.

english: Why do my tomatoes develop soft black patches on the bottom end of the fruit while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni mli tse lɛ? Yɛ aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ naagbee be mli ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom end rot and happens when tomato plants cannot get enough calcium due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture steady during fruiting stops the rot from developing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa beni tomato tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ yibiiwoo be mli lɛ baaye abua ni akafite.

english: How should I properly prepare my land before I plant oil palm seedlings?
ga: Te esa akɛ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ dani adu mu tso dumɔwui?

english: Proper land preparation involves clearing weeds, removing big stumps, and plowing or digging proper planting holes. Clearing well gives young oil palm seedlings space, prevents weeds from stealing nutrients, and allows their roots to spread easily into the soil.
ga: Nɔ ni fata shikpɔŋ he saamɔ kpakpa he ji jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. tso shishifãi wuji ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni aduɔ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mu tso dumɔwui bibii lɛ aná hegbɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why do extension officers say I must leave a wide space between oil palm trees when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ ashi he ko ni da yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ adu lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees grow very large fronds (leaves) and broad roots as they mature. Giving them wide spacing—usually about 9 meters apart—ensures each tree gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to produce heavy fruit bunches without crowding each other out.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii (baai) wuji waa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛji amɛdara kwraa. Too gbɛ ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ. Bei pii lɛ, amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 9, ni no haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ewo yibii ni tsii ni ekɛ amɛhe ebɔko amɛhe.

english: How can I tell if an oil palm seedling is healthy enough to plant on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mu tsei ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: A healthy oil palm seedling has dark green leaves, a thick and sturdy stem base, and a strong root system contained in its polybag without signs of disease, yellowing, or stunted fronds.
ga: Oil palm dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyɛ shishitoo ni mli tse ni mli wa. kɛ shishifã ni mli wa ni yɔɔ poly kotoku mli ni hela he okadi ko bɛ he, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni egbɔjɔ.

english: If I plant oil palm today, how many years will it take before I can start harvesting the fruits?
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei ŋmɛnɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ ebaahe dani aje yibii akpamɔ shishi?

english: Improved oil palm varieties usually begin producing their first small fruit bunches about 3 to 4 years after being planted in the main field, provided they receive good care, weed control, and fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ yibii bibii. Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ ji aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ beni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: How many years can an oil palm tree keep producing fruits once it starts bearing?
ga: Afii enyiɛ mu tso ko baanyɛ awo yibii kɛji ebɔi yibiiwoo pɛ?

english: An oil palm tree is a long-term investment that can continuously produce harvestable fruit bunches for 25 to 30 years or more before the tree grows too tall to harvest easily.
ga: Mu tsei ji shika ni akɛwoɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ aha aduawai akui ni abaanyɛ akpa be fɛɛ be afii 25 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai aba. Dani tsei lɛ baadara tsɔ ni abaanyɛ akpa amɛ mlɛo

english: Why do the lower leaves of my young oil palm trees turn yellow and droop during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry spells, oil palms conserve water by slowing down growth. Lower fronds turn yellow or brown and hang down because the tree is sending its limited water and nutrients to the newest leaves at the top to stay alive.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Oil palm yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi kɛtsɔ edalɛ ni ehaa ebaa shi lɛ nɔ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ejaakɛ tso lɛ kɛ nu kɛ niyenii fioo ko pɛ majeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ koni ehi shi.

english: Does oil palm need full sunlight to grow well, or can it grow under big shade trees?
ga: Ani hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia oil palm lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ loo abaanyɛ akwɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi?

english: Oil palm requires full sunlight throughout the day to grow strong and produce heavy fruit bunches. Planting them under deep shade will make the trees grow tall and thin with few or no fruits.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ he miihia hulu ni yeɔ emuu yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ afee kakadaŋŋ ni efee mlɛo ni ewooo yibii fioo loo ewooo yibii ko kwraa.

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava or maize between my oil palm trees while they are still small?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mu tsei ateŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop food crops like maize or vegetables between young oil palm trees during their first 2 to 3 years. However, avoid planting tall or spreading crops like cassava too close to the young palms, as they can compete with the palms for sunlight and food.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ yɛ mu tsei bibii ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli. Shi kɛlɛ, tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ loo ni gbɛɔ eshwaa, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ ni ooodu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei bibii tsɔ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ ŋmei tsei ashi akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know if the soil in my area is suitable for growing oil palm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ hi kɛha mu tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: Oil palms thrive best in deep, fertile, well-drained soils in areas that receive good rain throughout the year. If water sits on the land and forms a swamp for long periods, oil palm roots can rot and fail to perform well.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni baa nii, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ Kɛji nu damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eji ŋshɔkpɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Mu tso lɛ shishifãi baanyɛ agbo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it risky to plant long-term tree crops like oil palm on land where the ownership is not clear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tamɔ mu tso yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aleee mɔ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Because oil palm trees take 3 to 4 years to bear fruit and live for over 25 years, planting them on disputed or unverified land creates a risk of losing your investment if the land ownership changes or is challenged by local authorities or landowners.
ga: Akɛni mu tsei heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 dani amɛwoɔ yibii ni amɛhiɔ shi fe afii 25 hewɔ lɛ, mu tsei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni awieɔ he loo shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ oshara ni ji nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baafite kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔyeli lɛ tsake loo maŋ onukpai loo shikpɔŋtsɛmɛi lɛ te shi amɛwo lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees dry up and turn brown when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle intense direct sunlight because their tender leaves dry out faster than the roots can take up water. Planting shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a canopy, protecting the young cocoa plants from heat burn until they are fully established.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, cacao tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baafee tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛshwereɔ kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to build strong, green leaves. Adding well-composted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the crop regain its green color and grow healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before any fruits can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is inconsistent watering. Heat stress prevents successful pollination, so the plant drops the unpollinated blossoms to save energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ haaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Dɔlɛ mli haomɔ tsiɔ pollination ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shiiɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and light when I plant the stem cuttings too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni adu ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava cuttings are planted too close together, their underground roots compete fiercely for soil nutrients, space, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant has enough underground room to expand and build thick, starch-filled tubers.
ga: Kɛ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ŋwɛi, kɛ nu lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni egbɛ eshwa ni efee ŋmeii ni mli tse ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ starch.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward and stopping the plant from growing taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are a natural sign that tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or aphids are feeding under the leaves. Their feeding weakens the leaf tissue and often spreads plant viruses that cause growth stunting.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids miiye baai lɛ ashishi. Amɛ niyenii lɛ haa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni bei pii lɛ, egbɛɔ tsei amli helai ni haaa amɛdara lɛ eshwa.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can soften and lose their grip in waterlogged soil. Creating proper drainage channels allows excess rain to flow away, preventing the soil around the roots from turning into weak mud.
ga: Plantain lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni baanyɛ agbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ ekɛ ehe awo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu homɔ gbɛi kpakpai ni afee lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ muji ni yɔɔ blɛoo.

english: Why do my seed yams stay underground for weeks without sprouting when planted in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ taraa shikpɔŋ shishi otsii babaoo ni amɛkwɛɛɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam seed tubers enter a natural resting phase called dormancy and require consistent moisture and heat signals to break out of it. Dry soil keeps the yam seed asleep until the rains come to trigger root and shoot growth.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ boteɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ko mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy. ni ebiɔ ni afee hulutsoo kɛ dɔlɛ he okadii ni yaa nɔ daa koni ekɛgbala kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haa sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ wɔɔ kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ ni shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why does my watermelon field have many open flowers but very few watermelons growing on the vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon ŋmɔji lɛ amli fɔfɔii babaoo ni agbele naa lɛ? Shi watermelon fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Watermelon plants produce separate male and female flowers on the same vine. Fruit only forms when bees carry pollen from the male flowers to the female flowers, so low fruit count often means there are not enough pollinators around.
ga: Watermelon tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi yɛ wain tso kome nɔ. Afeɔ aduawai kɛ́ wuobii woɔ fɔfɔi ni ji hii fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyaa fɔfɔi yei amli. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, aduawai ayibɔ ni faaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts are fully mature and ready to harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnut maturity is shown above ground when the leaves turn yellowish and start to drop. Checking a few pods underground will confirm maturity if the inside of the pod shell turns dark and the seeds fill out the casing tightly.
ga: Ajieɔ ŋmei shweremɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ akwɛ ŋmeii fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ebaama nɔ mi akɛ ekwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli etsɔ duŋ ni akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ewo ŋmeii lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting quickly when I stack them in a heap in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpaa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight cooks the harvested yams and causes them to sweat, creating a warm, damp environment that rots the skin. Storing yams off the ground in a well-ventilated, shaded yam barn keeps them dry and extends their shelf life.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ashwere ni eha amɛhe afee latsaa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔɔ kɛ fɛ̃i baa ni haa hewolo lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ ŋmeii atsu ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do crops seem to grow faster inside a greenhouse compared to my open farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛ akɛto miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ he lɛ?

english: A greenhouse traps warmth and keeps moisture trapped inside, making the air several degrees warmer than the outside air. This warm, protected climate helps young plants absorb nutrients and grow without being stressed by harsh winds or direct burning sun.
ga: Greenhouses mɔɔ dɔlɛ ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ mli. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ digrii babaoo fe kponɔgbɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ. Nɛkɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔɔ, ni abuɔ he nɛɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhaooo amɛhe yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he.

english: Can a greenhouse get too hot for my crops if I keep it completely closed?
ga: Ani greenhouse lɛ baanyɛ adɔ tsɔ aha miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji mikɛwo mli kwraa?

english: Yes, because greenhouses trap heat, the temperature inside can easily rise 5 to 10 degrees higher than the temperature outside. If it gets too hot, crops will wilt and get heat stress, so greenhouses need netted vents to let hot air escape.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ tsũi ni mli edɔ lɛ hiɛɔ dɔlɛ mli. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ hulutsoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ fe hulutsoo ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ digrii 5 kɛyashi 10. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ hulutsoo he haomɔ, no hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni greenhouses lɛ afee mesh vents koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ajɛ mli.

english: Why do my outdoor crops dry up and wilt so quickly when the afternoon sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi kpo nɔ tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hot afternoon air causes water to evaporate quickly from both the soil and the plant's leaves. When the air temperature is much hotter than the plant prefers, it loses water faster than its roots can drink it from the ground.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ahe baai fɛɛ amli. Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa fe bɔ ni tso lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ Efiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I protect my outdoor vegetables from strong heat without building an expensive greenhouse?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabu mi kponɔgbɛ aduawai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni mimaaa ŋmɔ ni jara wa?

english: Yes, you can build simple shade structures using palm fronds, tall grass roofs, or shade netting over your beds. This lowers the temperature around your crops by a few degrees and keeps the hot sun from burning delicate leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmei tsei afee hulutsoo he gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Jwɛi ŋwɛitsu ni kɛlɛ Aloo okɛ shade ŋshɔŋloo awo osɛɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo ni ebɔle he lɛ aba shi. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi 2-3 degrees ni otsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without making fruits when the weather becomes extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When outdoor temperatures rise too high, the heat damages the pollen inside the blossoms, preventing them from forming fruit. Keeping the plants cool with shade or soil cover helps reduce heat stress during flowering.
ga: Kɛji kponɔgbɛ latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ lɛ latsaa lɛ kpataa pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ hiɛ. ni etsĩ enaa koni ekatsu nii jogbaŋŋ Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo loo ŋmɔtɔ ha tso lɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Is it true that watering my crops in the middle of a hot afternoon can hurt them?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ nu ni ashwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye amɛ awui?

english: Yes, watering when the ground is extremely hot causes rapid evaporation and can warm up the root zone. It is best to water early in the morning or late in the evening when temperatures are cooler so the roots can drink efficiently.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni edɔ waa lɛ haa hulutsoo baa oya ni ehaa shishifã lɛ mli dɔɔ. Esa akɛ awo nu lɛ mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: What can I put on my outdoor farm soil so it does not get as hot as the sun outside?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ yɛ mi kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni edɔɔɔ tamɔ hulu ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Covering the bare soil around your crops with dry grass, straw, or leaves—a practice called mulching—acts like a blanket. It blocks direct sunlight, keeping the soil temperature lower and locking in moisture.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni okɛbaabɔle ohe lɛ Okɛ jwɛi, jwɛi, loo baai aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ mli. Etsĩɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do older farmers leave big shade trees in the middle of their open farm fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni edara lɛ shiɔ tsei wuji yɛ amɛŋmɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Shade trees act as natural temperature regulators for the field. Their canopy blocks harsh direct light, lowering the air temperature beneath them by several degrees and protecting lower crops from heat stress.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ shia lɛ mli. Kpoji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli dɔlɛ baa shi digrii babaoo ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Why do young crop seedlings die so easily when transplanted straight into open sunny fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bibii gboiɔ oya kɛ́ adu amɛ awo ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulu la kpɛɔ yɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have fragile roots that cannot collect water fast enough to survive high outdoor heat. Providing temporary shade for a few days gives their roots time to establish before facing full outdoor temperatures.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni waaa ni nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa koni amɛdamɔ kponɔgbɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ naa. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ha shishifãi lɛ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛma shi dani amɛshɛɔ kponɔgbɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ he.

english: What can I add to my open field soil to help crops handle hot dry weather better?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛfata shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ he koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni enyɛ ekpee shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Adding organic compost or well-rotted animal manure improves your soil so it holds water like a sponge. Soil with plenty of organic matter stays cooler and retains moisture much longer during hot spells.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu tamɔ sponji. Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees on the same farm with my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very tender and burn easily under direct sun. Planting plantains creates quick shade that acts like an umbrella to protect the young cocoa while also giving you food and income while you wait for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa oya ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need plenty of direct sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers underground. Lifting the vines up on stakes helps all the leaves catch sun easily and prevents diseases caused by leaves touching damp ground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛná hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ shɛɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ oya, ni ehaa helai ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni baa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually show that the plant has run out of nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves the remaining nitrogen to its upper leaves to survive, which signals that you need to apply fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ebaai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ fɔ awo mli.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that put nitrogen back into the soil, restoring its strength naturally for the next crop.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava and maize plants grow weak and thin when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava kɛ ŋmãa lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Proper spacing gives every plant enough space to feed and grow strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni eda ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rain collects in the soil without draining, the roots drown and soil fungi attack them, causing rot. Planting on raised mounds helps extra water drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baatutua amɛ. kɛ fitemɔ baa Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛjeɔ kpo.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cover the soil around my crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi abɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool under hot sun, stops water from drying out quickly, and prevents weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaa jwɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I wait for the first heavy rain before planting my seeds instead of planting early in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ dani madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Seeds need steady moisture to sprout and build strong roots. Planting in dry soil makes seeds vulnerable to ants, rotting, or dying from sudden heat right after sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii baanyɛ aye amɛ, amɛgboi, loo amɛgboi yɛ latsaa ni baa trukaa lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat stress, dry soil, or excessive fertilizer. Keeping the soil moist and cool helps the plant retain its flowers so they can form peppers.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pepper fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa ji haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ fɔfɔi ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ amli koni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What causes my tomato leaves to curl up tightly and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl when tiny insects like whiteflies transmit a plant virus, or when the plant suffers from sudden dry heat. Managing tiny pests early and maintaining regular watering protects the leaves.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛ tso mli helai. aloo beni tso lɛ naa hulutsoo ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ. Nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops dry up so fast when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ gbiɔ oya kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Scorching sun and high heat cause water to evaporate quickly from both the soil and the plant leaves, making crops lose moisture faster than they can absorb it.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ahe baai fɛɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ.

english: Why do my crops look wilted during the afternoon even if it rained a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Intense afternoon heat pulls moisture out of crop leaves rapidly, causing plants to temporarily drop or wilt when soil water gets low.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya. Ehaa tsei shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa.

english: What happens to my crops when there is a long drought without rain?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ ba ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: During a drought, crops suffer severe water stress, stop growing properly, produce smaller yields, and can wither completely if they do not receive extra water.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ ni naa wa kpeɔ. ekpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ewoɔ yibii fioo ni ebaanyɛ egbo kɛji akɛ ahaaa lɛ nu kroko

english: Do my crops still need water during the dry season, or can they survive on their own?
ga: Ani nu he miihia miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ lolo yɛ hɔmɔ be mli loo amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi?

english: Crops need water in every season to survive and grow well; leaving them without water during dry periods will lead to crop failure.
ga: Nu he miihia tsei yɛ be fɛɛ mli koni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ oshi lɛ ni nu bɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How does hot weather change the amount of water my crops need?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ tsakeɔ nu ni he hiaa mi tsei lɛ?

english: When the weather is scorching, crops consume and lose water much faster, meaning they require more frequent watering than during cooler days.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ nii ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kwraa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni afɔ amɛ nu shii abɔ yɛ gbii ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I collect and save water when it rains so I can use it later for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabua nu naa ni mikɛto kɛji nugbɔ nɛ koni mikɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ mli?

english: You can harvest rainwater by directing rain flowing off building roofs into storage tanks, drums, or covered containers to save for dry days.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa nugbɔ nu kɛtsɔ nugbɔ ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsu ko yiteŋ lɛ ni oootsɔ nɔ okɛwo nutoohe, baagi, loo nɔ ko ni akɛ nɔ ko eha nɔ koni akɛtsu nii yɛ gbii ni nugbɔ bɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I use rainwater collected from the roof of my farm structure to water my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nugbɔ nu ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ atsu nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, water collected from farm roofs or buildings is clean and safe to store and apply to your crops when dry weather sets in.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsũi ayiteŋ loo ŋmɔ mli tsũi amli lɛ he tse ni ehi akɛ oookɛto ni okɛtsu nii yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ miibɛŋkɛ.

english: What kind of containers can I use on my farm to store water for my plants?
ga: Mɛɛ tsɛnsii manyɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛto nu kɛha mitsei lɛ?

english: You can use large plastic drums, water tanks, metal barrels, or built storage basins placed near your farm buildings to hold rainwater.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ plastic tsɛnsii wuji, nu tsɛnsii, dade tsɛnsii, loo nutoohei ni ama yɛ oŋmɔ mli tsũi lɛ ahe lɛ atsu nii ni okɛ nugbɔ nu ato.

english: Why should I store rainwater during the rainy season when there is already plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔbua nugbɔ nu naa yɛ nugbɔ be mli be mli ni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ babaoo momo lɛ?

english: Rainfall can stop unexpectedly, so saving rainwater while it is falling ensures you have a backup supply ready whenever a sudden dry spell hits.
ga: Nugbɔ baanyɛ akpa trukaa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ to be mli ni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ, ebaaha oná he ko ni okɛto be fɛɛ be ni hɔmɔ baaba trukaa.

english: Is there a simple way to keep my crops alive if the rains stop early this year?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni matsɔ nɔ maha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahi shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa yɛ afi nɛɛ shishijee mli?

english: Storing rainwater in containers during periods of rain provides a reserve supply that allows you to manually water and protect your crops if the rains stop early.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni okɛtoɔ tsɛnsi mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa onáa sɛɛfimɔ ni haa onyɛɔ okɛ nu haa ohe, ni ebuɔ onibii ahe kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra.

english: Why do my crops rot in the farm before I even get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ po nɔ ni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Crops usually rot on the farm due to excess water in the soil, fungal diseases, or poor soil drainage that starves plant roots of oxygen and allows rot-causing organisms to thrive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ nu babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tsɛŋemɔ helai, loo sũ lɛ mli nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ náaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. ni ehaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ daa.

english: Why do my harvested fruits spoil and rot so quickly after I pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ oya beni mikpa amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvested produce keeps living and breathing after picking; exposure to high heat, direct sunlight, and physical bruising speeds up decay, so keeping them in cool, shaded, and well-ventilated places extends their life.
ga: Nibii ni akpa lɛ yɛ wala mli ni amɛmuɔ beni akpa amɛ sɛɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ fãji ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baaha efite oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu boteɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛwala sɛɛ atsɛ.

english: How can I dry my crop harvest properly so it does not mold and go to waste?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkashwie jwɛi?

english: Drying crops on raised mesh racks in well-ventilated, shaded areas allows moisture to escape evenly, preventing the damp conditions that cause mold and rotting.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋtayaai ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ ni agbiɔ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo pɛpɛɛpɛ. Etsiɔ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ naa.

english: How can I turn my fresh fruit harvest into juice or drinks so it does not rot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔ aduawai ni akpa ehee lɛ mafee nu loo nibii ni anuɔ koni amɛkafite?

english: Fruits can be processed by crushing to extract the juice, heating it briefly to kill spoilage bacteria (pasteurization), and sealing it tightly in clean bottles to preserve it for months.
ga: Abaanyɛ atsu aduawai ahe nii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛjieɔ nu lɛ mli. Heat kɛha be kukuoo ko. Koni egbe helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ. (ni akɛ pasteurized ewo mli) ni akɛwo tɔ ni mli tse mli jogbaŋŋ koni akɛto nyɔji babaoo.

english: What basic setup do I need on my farm to start processing my crops into drink flavors?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee gbɛjianɔtoo esa akɛ maná yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ koni afee nibii ni anuɔ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli?

english: Basic processing requires a clean water source, hygienic strainers or presses to extract juice and oils, heat sources for pasteurization, and airtight bottling containers.
ga: Nitsumɔ shishijee lɛ biɔ nu ni mli tse jɛɛhe. Hetsemɔ tsɔne loo tsɔne ni akɛjieɔ nu kɛ fɔ Dɔlɛ jɛɛhe kɛha pasteurization kɛ tɔi ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli

english: How do companies extract strong flavors from crops like ginger or hibiscus to make bottled beverages?
ga: Te nitsumɔhei feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛjieɔ tsofai ni mli wa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo hibiscus mli koni amɛkɛfee dãa ni akɛwoɔ tɔ mli?

english: Companies crush or steep dried aromatic crops in clean water or alcohol solutions to draw out natural flavor oils, which are then concentrated and blended into drinks.
ga: Nitsumɔhei lɛ shwieɔ tsei ni egbi ni ŋɔɔ lɛ anɔ loo amɛkɛwoɔ nu ni mli tse loo dãa mli koni amɛjie amɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔ ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛwoɔ mli ni afutuɔ nii ni anuɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my crops if I want to sell them for flavor extraction?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Kɛji miisumɔ ni mahɔ̃ɔ koni majie flavor

english: Flavoring crops should be harvested at peak maturity when their natural color and aroma are strongest, but before they become overripe or soft.
ga: Esa akɛ akpa tsei ni akɛ tsofa ewo mli lɛ yɛ amɛhewalɛ mli beni amɛ adebɔɔ mli su kɛ amɛhenumɔ lɛ mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ. Shi dani ebaakwɛ tsɔ loo ebaafee blɛoo tsɔ.

english: Why do my harvested crops lose their strong smell and taste after a few weeks in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni akɛtoɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The essential oils responsible for flavor evaporate when exposed to open air, direct light, and heat, so crops must be stored in cool, dark, and airtight containers.
ga: Mu ni he hiaa ni haa ŋmɔlɔ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ akɛwo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli tse, la kɛ dɔlɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ, no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo tsɛnsi ko ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli.

english: How can I prevent insects and pests from destroying my stored crop harvest while I search for buyers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nibii ni mikɛto lɛ ahiɛ yɛ be mli ni mitaoɔ mɛi ni baahe lɛ?

english: Storing thoroughly dried produce in airtight bags or sealed drums starves pests of oxygen, stopping insects from breeding and destroying the crop.
ga: Nibii ni egbi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto vacuum kotokui loo tsɛnsii ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ. Enɛ haaa kooloi kɛ amɛhe akabɔ, ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do some crop varieties rot faster than other varieties of the same plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi komɛi fiteɔ oya fe tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties have different skin thicknesses, water contents, and natural resistance to fungi, making certain varieties store longer than others.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ amɛhewolo nɔ ŋmɔlɔ, nu ni yɔɔ mli, kɛ bɔ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii. Enɛ haa henɔi komɛi hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ fe ekrokomɛi.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand strong direct sunlight because their roots are shallow and their leaves are soft. They require plantain trees or shade trees planted nearby to filter the sunlight and retain moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ amɛbaai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ ahewɔ. Amɛ hia dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛ tsi hulu la lɛ naa ni ehiɛ sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i mli.

english: I see small caterpillars hiding in the funnels of my young maize plants eating the leaves. What is happening to my crop?
ga: Mina ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ agbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ni amɛmiiye baai lɛ. Mɛni ba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on the soft inner leaves where the stem grows. If left unchecked, they destroy the central shoot and stop the maize from producing ears.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ baa bibii ni yɔɔ mligbɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Ebaakpata ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ hiɛ ni ekpa ŋmãa lɛ toi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Does it matter if I plant my cassava stem cuttings slanting or standing straight in the dirt?
ga: Ani ekɔɔɔ he eko kɛji mikɛ mi-cassava niji lɛ shwie shi loo tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava stem cuttings at a slant helps the plant develop roots deeper in one direction, making the cassava tubers grow bigger and making them much easier to pull out of the ground at harvest time.
ga: Kasava ŋmɔji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daraa waa, ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ abaajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Why are my tomato fruits cracking and splitting open just as they start to turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ miigba ni amɛmiijara beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they receive a sudden, large amount of water after a dry spell. The inside of the fruit grows faster than the skin can stretch, causing the outer skin to burst open.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛ́ amɛná nu babaoo trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ mli fãa.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants look pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient plants use to build green leaves and make energy from sunlight. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps them regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I have to cut long wooden sticks to support my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo tsei kakadaji lɛ? Koni akɛfi sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the ground prevents diseases caused by damp soil and helps the plant put more energy into growing large underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ helai ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛbaa lɛ anaa. ni ehaa tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Will planting cowpeas on my farm help the soil for next season's maize?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmãa ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmãa ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, cowpeas and other legumes have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer for future grain crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small cups and stopping new growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ hee lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or by viruses transmitted by these pests. Managing insects early prevents the leaf curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Mra be mli ni akwɛɔ kooloi anɔ Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant my maize seeds after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is risky because the first rain is often a 'false start' followed by weeks of hot, dry weather. If seeds germinate in dry soil, the tiny seedlings will die; it is safer to wait until the rains are regular and the soil stays damp.
ga: Oshara yɛ ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji ‘Apasa shishijee’ ni otsii babaoo ni mli edɔ, ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui bibii lɛ baagboi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baaku esɛɛ eba ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo.

english: Why are weeds growing so much faster than my cassava after I put fertilizer on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-cassava lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that steal fertilizer nutrients faster than young cassava plants can absorb them. Clearing weeds before applying fertilizer ensures your crop gets the benefits instead of the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni ŋmei tsei bibii baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ooojie dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, onibii lɛ baaná he sɛɛ yɛ jwɛi lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot handle harsh sun. They need shade crops like plantains to protect them from intense heat and conserve soil moisture until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do small green cocoa pods on my tree dry up and turn black before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Ani mitsei lɛ egbi ni amɛji ediŋŋ dani amɛdaraa?

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease or natural cherelle wilt. Excess humidity, shade, or fungal attack can destroy young pods, so keeping the farm weeded and pruned helps air flow freely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji black pod hela loo adebɔɔ mli wilt hela. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine, hulutsoo, loo ŋmeii ni baanyɛ afite ŋmeii bibii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni akpɛɔ tsei lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if I do not trim the extra branches regularly?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ kɛji mifolɔɔɔ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ daa?

english: Untrimmed cocoa trees waste energy growing unnecessary leaves instead of pods. Pruning lets sunlight reach the main stems, reduces disease risks, and encourages the tree to produce more pods.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni afolɔko amɛhe lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ baai ni he ehiaaa yɛ ŋmeii lɛ najiaŋ. Nibii ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ tso lɛ shishi. Ha helai ni baanyɛ aba lɛ aba shi ni oha tsei lɛ afee ŋmeii babaoo

english: Can I plant cassava in the middle of my mature cocoa farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ ni eda lɛ teŋ?

english: Mature cocoa trees have extensive root systems and thick canopies that need full space. Planting food crops like cassava among older cocoa trees creates competition for nutrients and water, reducing cocoa yields.
ga: Kokoo tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi babaoo kɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni biɔ he ko ni fa babaoo. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ ateŋ Enɛ haa akaŋshii baa kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, kookoo ni afeɔ lɛ ba shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry spells, cocoa trees shed flowers to save water and survive drought stress. Keeping shade trees on the farm and spreading dry leaves around the base helps retain soil moisture during dry months.
ga: yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛye amɛhe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa amɛhe lɛ Shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are the stems of my young cocoa trees swelling up and leaf colors changing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ efuu ni amɛbaai lɛ ahe su tsakeɔ lɛ?

english: Swelling on stems and discolored leaves are key signs of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease. It is spread by tiny mealybug insects, and affected trees must be removed so the virus does not spread across the farm.
ga: Fuumɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai ni etsake lɛ ji okadii ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ cocoa bud virus hela lɛ eba. Mealybugs bibii ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. Ni esa akɛ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do I tell if my soil is missing nutrients just by looking at my cocoa leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ kookoo baai ni makwɛ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: If leaves turn pale yellow while the veins stay dark green, or if the leaf edges look scorched, the plant is starving for nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, signaling that fertilizer or compost is needed.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ yɛ be mli ni fãji lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia.

english: Why is my old cocoa farm giving me fewer pods each year even when rains are good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 30 years, their production naturally slows down and they become weaker against pests. Replacing very old trees with fresh, improved seedlings restores farm productivity.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tsei ye fe afii 20 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛfeemɔ baa shi, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aye amɛ oya. Tsei momo ni atsakeɔ Kɛ dumɔwui heei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa trees flower heavily right after the first major rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rainfall after a dry period signals to the tree that water is now available. This moisture triggers an immediate biological reaction in the cocoa tree to produce new buds and blossoms.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ lɛ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ agbɛnɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ nɔ ko amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ cacao tso lɛ mli koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ fɔfɔii heei aba.

english: Why do weeds grow faster under my cocoa trees after I prune the upper branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi beni mifo tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy, allowing sun rays to hit the farm floor. Weeds react quickly to sunlight and soil moisture, so clearing them right after pruning prevents them from stealing nutrients from your cocoa trees.
ga: Tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tsei lɛ ashishi koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi lɛ tsuɔ hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he nii oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ofo tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ o-cacao tsei lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why is it important to plant my crops in neat lines rather than scattering them across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo naa moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines gives every crop its own space to get enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. It also makes it much easier for you to walk through the farm to remove weeds, apply fertilizer, and harvest without damaging the plants.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ hegbɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Agbɛnɛ hu, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ ooonyiɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okpa ni ofiteee tsei lɛ.

english: When plants are crowded together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves them weak, thin, and prone to diseases, which results in a much smaller yield at harvest time.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛhe waaa, amɛhe ejɔ amɛ, ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi kwraa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why do farmers prefer to plant seeds or young suckers early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi sumɔɔ ni amɛdu dumɔwui loo ŋmeii bibii leebi lɛ?

english: The soil is cool and moist in the early morning, and the heat of the sun is not yet strong. Planting at this time gives the young roots a gentle start so they do not dry out or suffer heat stress.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ leebi. ni hulu lɛ mli dɔlɛ lɛ waaa lolo Dumɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi bibii jeɔ shishi blɛoo. Enɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi loo amɛkaná dɔlɛ he haomɔ.

english: What is a plantain sucker and how do I plant it on my land?
ga: Mɛni ji plantain sucker kɛ bɔ ni aaafee adu yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ?

english: A plantain sucker is a small shoots growing out from the root base of an older plantain tree. You carefully separate it from the main plant and dig it into fresh soil where it grows into a new plantain tree.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ji tsei bibii. ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni edara lɛ ashishi Okɛ hiɛdɔɔ gbalaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ he. ni okɛwo shikpɔŋ hee mli he ni ebaakwɛ̃ ni etsɔ dumɔwu hee.

english: How can I tell if a plantain sucker is healthy enough to give me a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji sucker dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?
