english: A healthy plantain sucker has a firm, strong base, fresh green growth, and no visible dark rot, holes, or pests around the bulb at the bottom.
ga: Plantain suckers ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ shishitoo ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ, ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Nɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yaa hiɛ yɛ jɛmɛ. Ni ŋmɔtɔ ni mli ewo duŋ, bu, loo kooloi krokomɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ. yitso yɛ shishigbɛ

english: Does the way my land lies or slopes affect how my crops will grow?
ga: Ani he ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ loo bɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ he?

english: Yes, the slope of your land controls how water moves. Flat land retains moisture longer, while sloped land drains quickly and can lose fertile topsoil during heavy rain, so choosing the right crop for the terrain is important.
ga: Hɛɛ, bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ehaa lɛ kudɔɔ bɔ ni nu lɛ yaa nɔ ehaa lɛ. He ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ nu hoɔ oya, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite amɛshikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe hia ni ahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Can I plant plantains together on the same land with young tree crops like rubber?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ plantains yɛ he kome kɛ tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ rɔbɔt tsei?

english: Yes, planting plantains alongside young tree crops is very useful. The large plantain leaves provide shade and weed protection while the tree crops grow, and the plantains yield food and income long before the tree crops mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ tsei bibii ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Plantain baai agboi lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ jwɛi ahe be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ. Ni plantains haa niyenii kɛ shika baa be saŋŋ dani tsei kɛ tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I prepare my land and get workers ready before planting day arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nitsulɔi hu afee klalo dani dumɔ gbi lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Having your land cleared and workers ready in advance means you can plant quickly while the soil is moist and the seedlings or suckers are still fresh, preventing roots from drying out before getting into the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie he ni atsuɔ nii yɛ lɛ ni nitsulɔi lɛ efee klalo kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ obaanyɛ odu oya yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo ni dumɔwui loo ŋmeii lɛ hu ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lolo lɛ. Enɛ ji koni shishifãi lɛ akagbi dani adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ.

english: Why do some farmers invest in long-term tree crops like rubber alongside food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ amɛshika woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ rɔba mli kɛfataa niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ?

english: Rubber trees take several years to grow, but once mature, they can produce sap continuously for decades, giving the farm a steady, long-term source of steady income.
ga: Rɔba tsei heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛdaraa. Shi kɛ́ amɛdara kwraa lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee rɔba be fɛɛ be afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ náa shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How do I grow crops that are good enough to sell to buyers sending produce abroad?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ maha mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni amɛkɛmajeɔ maŋsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Foreign markets look for high quality, uniform size, and undamaged produce. Following proper spacing, protecting crops from pests, and harvesting at the correct stage helps ensure your yield meets export standards.
ga: Majimaji ateŋ jarayeli hei taoɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni dalɛi tsakeee kɛ nibii ni efiteee. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa lɛ he nitsumɔ Nibii ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ haa onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ yeɔ shishitoo mlai ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it good for me to plant oil palm directly in a swampy area during the rainy season?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu mu tso yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: No, planting directly in a swampy area is risky. Excess standing water deprives roots of oxygen and causes root rot, so you should dig drains to let the excess water flow off before planting.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yɛ oshara. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ebaaha amɛgboi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ otsa paipi ni nu tsɔɔ mli koni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli dani odu.

english: Why do I need to dig trenches on my farmland before putting my young oil palm seedlings in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo bu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ mu tso dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Trenches create channels for trapped rainwater to drain away. Digging them before planting ensures the soil isn't waterlogged, giving your young seedlings a dry, healthy environment to establish strong roots.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ feɔ gbɛi ni nugbɔ nu ni emɔ lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ehoɔ kɛyaa. Kɛ́ akumɔ shikpɔŋ dani adu lɛ, ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekahiɛ nu. Ehaa tsei bibii lɛ naa shihilɛ ni mli egbi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: How do I know if my land has too much standing water for oil palm trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo kɛha mu tsei?

english: If rainwater settles on your land and remains there for weeks or months without soaking into the ground or flowing away, the soil is waterlogged and requires proper drainage channels before planting.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehi jɛmɛ otsii loo nyɔji babaoo ni ekɛ ehe wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ejooo foi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni esa akɛ gbɛ ni sa ahi nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli dani adu.

english: Should I construct water drains on my farm before planting, or can I wait until after the oil palms start growing?
ga: Ani esa akɛ matswa paipii ni haa nu hoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu nii? Aloo esa akɛ wɔmɛ kɛyashi be mli ni oil palm lɛ baabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ?

english: You should construct drains before planting. If young oil palms are planted in flooded ground, they can rot or die within weeks, so the water must be cleared first.
ga: Esa akɛ ofee nu homɔ paipii dani odu. Kɛji akɛ adu mu tso yɛ he ko ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baanyɛ afite loo egbo yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ nu afɔ he klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my oil palm trees turning yellow when water sits on my farm for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When water covers the ground for months, it smothers the roots and cuts off their air supply. Without healthy roots, the tree cannot absorb soil nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow and growth to stall.
ga: beni nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo Nu baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu ni ebaafo kɔɔyɔɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa bɛ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: What happens to the roots of my oil palm trees if rainwater stays on my land for several months?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu hi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo?

english: Prolonged standing water suffocates the root system, causing the roots to rot. Damaged roots cannot support the tree or absorb essential fertilizers, leading to weak plants or plant loss.
ga: Nu ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ tso lɛ nɔ loo amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo tsei lɛ laajeɔ.

english: Will my oil palm trees produce fewer fruit bunches if rainwater collects around their bases every year?
ga: Ani mi-oil palm tso lɛ baawo aduawai fioo kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ eshishigbɛ he daa afi?

english: Yes, waterlogged soil weakens root systems and prevents trees from absorbing the nutrients needed to develop heavy fruit bunches, resulting in smaller yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ehaaa tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ewo yibii ni tsii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: Can I still successfully farm oil palm on a piece of low-lying land that gets flooded easily?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ mu tsei lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu shwieɔ nɔ oya lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, but only if you manage the water first. By digging deep outlet ditches across the land, you can direct floodwaters away from the trees so the soil remains moist without drowning the crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi kɛji akɛ okwɛ nu lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ pɛ. Kɛtsɔ bu ni mli kwɔ ni oootsi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ Obaanyɛ ojie nu afua lɛ mli nu lɛ kɛjɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akabote nu mli.

english: Why does rainwater stay on some parts of my farmland for up to three months after heavy rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔji lɛ ekomɛi anɔ kɛyashiɔ nyɔji etɛ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ekpa lɛ?

english: Flat, low-lying areas or soils high in clay trap water because there is no natural incline for it to escape. Without dug channels to guide the water off the field, it sits trapped in place.
ga: Hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo shikpɔji ni nu babaoo yɔɔ nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ. ejaakɛ adebɔɔ mli suɔmɔ ko bɛ ni haa mɔ joɔ foi. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa nubu ko ni akɛ nu baajɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nu lɛ baahi he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: How do water drainage trenches help protect my crops during long periods of heavy rainfall?
ga: Te nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Drainage trenches act like gutters for your farm. They collect overflowing surface water and guide it away from the roots of your crops, preventing root damage while keeping the soil properly balanced.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nu ŋshɔ kɛha oŋmɔ lɛ. Amɛbuaa nu ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa ni amɛtsɔɔ lɛ gbɛ kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Etsiɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ naa yɛ be mli ni ekwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the tall shade trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ? Mashi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and delicate roots that dry out easily under direct sunlight. Tall shade trees act like natural umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting young seedlings from excessive heat until they are strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize plants turning pale yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food crop leaves need to stay green and healthy, so adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves regain their green color and support proper grain growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei ahe koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su eŋɔli ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together in the same field without them damaging each other's growth?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mifiteee amɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ dalɛ?

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together works well because they grow at different speeds. Maize grows fast and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slowly underground over a full year, meaning they do not fight for sunlight or soil nutrients at the same time.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛdaraa oyaiyeli srɔtoi. Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Beni ŋmei lɛ daa blɛoo lɛ Shikpɔŋ shishi afi muu lɛ fɛɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyeee akaŋ yɛ hulu la loo niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he yɛ be kome mli.

english: What causes tiny caterpillars to eat holes through the center leaves of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ko kɛtsɔɔ mi-ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli?

english: These caterpillars are known as Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by moths on crop leaves. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended neem extracts or safe insecticides directly into the plant funnel stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni ale amɛ akɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii kɛwoɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ lɛ amli. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra Ni okɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ akɛ awo mli lɛ awo tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do farming experts advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my plot before planting my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nilelɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu mi ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which naturally captures nitrogen gas from the air and stores it in the soil through small root nodules. When you harvest them, the enriched soil provides free food for the next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli. Ejɛɔ ebɔɔ su mli emɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi amli lɛ anɔ. Beni obaakpa Shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ baafee niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the stems and lower leaves of my tomato plants turn black and rot during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishi baai lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess water pooling around plant roots creates damp conditions that encourage soil fungi to spread and rot the leaves and stems. Planting tomatoes on raised earth mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni buaa ehe naa yɛ Tse lɛ shishifãi ahe lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa, ni no woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni ehaa baai kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start turning dark and spoiling just two days after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifee diŋ ni amɛmiifite gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni akpa lɛ?

english: Once cassava roots are dug up and cut from the plant, their tissue reacts rapidly with oxygen in the air, causing fast internal decay. Processing harvested cassava into gari or flour immediately, or storing unwashed roots in moist sawdust, keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Beni ajieɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ni afoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Efãji lɛ tsuɔ nii oya kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ. ni kɛ mligbɛ fitemɔ baa oya Akɛ ŋmei ni akpa lɛ tsuɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni efeɔ gari loo ashikishaŋ. aloo shishifãi ni ahooo lɛ ni akɛtoɔ ŋmei ni mli efɔ mli. Ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after the first rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that adapt aggressively to local soil, allowing them to absorb available rainwater and nutrients much faster than cultivated seeds. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing food and choking your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ jɛmɛ shikpɔji lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii ni amɛkatsi oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anaa.

english: Will cutting away unwanted branches from my cocoa tree hurt it or help it produce more pods?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni ataooo lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baafite tso lɛ loo ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo?

english: Pruning unnecessary inner branches helps cocoa trees produce more pods because it allows fresh air and sunlight to circulate through the tree. Good air flow keeps fungal diseases like black pod away and helps the plant direct energy into growing bigger pods.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ mli ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo ejaakɛ ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pod blackening naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa pods wuji amli.

english: Why do I need to place tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb tall stakes so their leaves can spread out widely and catch full sunlight without touching damp soil. Better exposure to sunlight allows the leaves to make more food, which results in much larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛtaaa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ he. Hulu la ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ feɔ wuji babaoo.

english: Why are my crops struggling to grow on ground that feels very hard and packed tight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitao ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ mlɛo waa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Hard, packed soil makes it difficult for delicate young crop roots to push deep into the earth to find water and nutrients. Breaking up and plowing hard ground creates loose soil, allowing roots to spread easily and feed the crop properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ashishifãi akɛ amɛaabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛhaa tso lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I still grow good crops if my farmland has a lot of small stones in the ground?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lolo kɛji akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛi bibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, crops can grow very well in stony land as long as the ground is properly worked. Mechanized plowing breaks open hard soil around stones and loosens the earth so crop roots can reach deep into the nutrient-rich soil beneath.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ, kɛji akɛ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Tsɔne ni akɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni bɔle tɛi lɛ ahe lɛ mli, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tsei ashishifãi lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii kpakpai eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Will using a tractor to plow my field help my crops grow better than clearing by hand?
ga: Ani trakta ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe ni mikɛ nine baatsu he nii?

english: Yes, a tractor can break open heavy, hard, or stubborn soil much deeper than hand tools can. Deeply tilled soil holds rainwater better and gives crop roots the soft space they need to expand quickly.
ga: Hɛɛ, traktɔi baanyɛ agbele shikpɔŋ ni tsii, ni wa, loo ni mli wa lɛ mli kɛya shɔŋŋ kwraa fe nibii ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni atsu he nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ náa he ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout evenly on land that hasn't been plowed before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni atsuko nɔ dani adu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Unplowed soil forms a hard surface crust that makes it difficult for seeds to get sufficient air, moisture, and soft space to push through. Plowing creates a soft seedbed where young sprouts can easily emerge.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atsuuu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa yɛ nɔ ni haa ewaa ahaa dumɔwui lɛ akɛ amɛaana kɔɔyɔɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ he ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛbote mli. Gbɛjianɔtoo haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni tsei bibii baanyɛ ajɛ mli aba lɛ baa.

english: Is it possible to turn tough, unused land into a productive farm for maize?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ atsake shikpɔŋ ni ehao ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ afee ŋmɔ ni woɔ yibii kɛha ŋmãa?

english: Yes, virtually any land can support good crops like maize once it is properly cleared and tilled. Even difficult or abandoned land becomes fertile planting ground when heavy equipment softens the soil structure.
ga: Hɛɛ, nɔ ni miihe ashɛ shikpɔŋ srɔtoi fɛɛ baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai, tamɔ ŋmãa, kɛji ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni atsu he nii. Shikpɔji ni wa loo ni ashi amɛ po bafeɔ okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni baa nii beni tsɔnei ni tsii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ.

english: How does breaking up hard soil help my crops survive when rain stops falling?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni shwieɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa?

english: Loosening hard soil allows rainwater to soak deep into the earth instead of running off the surface. Crop roots can then grow deeper to reach that underground water supply during dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni eeejo foi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei shishifãi baanyɛ adara kɛya shikpɔŋ shishi nu jɛɛhei amli shɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why do my crop roots stay short and shallow instead of growing deep into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni amɛmli ekɔɔɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Roots stay shallow when they hit a hard layer of compacted soil or rocks beneath the surface. Deep plowing removes these physical barriers, encouraging roots to grow downward and hold the plant firm.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nitsumɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ jieɔ nɛkɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii nɛɛ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shi ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Should I loosen the hard soil surface around my young crops after heavy rains?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni bɔle mitsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, heavy rain can bake the topsoil into a hard crust that chokes the soil of air. Gently loosening the surface soil helps air and water reach the root system, keeping the crop healthy.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ afee sũ ni mli wa ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ blɛoo lɛ Haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ha tsei lɛ awa

english: Can hard ground be turned into a good farm for growing delicate vegetables?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ atsake shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee ŋmɔ kpakpa kɛha aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo?

english: No soil is unusable for vegetables if properly prepared. Even very hard or stony ground can be softened using tractors and tillage tools to create the light, airy soil condition that delicate vegetable roots require.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ ko afee aduawai kɛji akɛ asaa he jogbaŋŋ. Abaanyɛ akɛ traktai kɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa waa loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ po afee mlɛo koni akɛfee shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli ni aduawai shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ biɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my crops growing tall in some parts of my field but staying very small in other parts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi shi amɛfeɔ bibioo kwraa yɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Soil hardness often varies across a single field, causing roots in soft areas to thrive while roots in hard spots stay stunted. Evenly plowing the entire field ensures all your crops get uniform soil conditions to grow equally well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ha lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he fɛɛ he. Ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ daa. yɛ be mli ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ hei ni wa lɛ yaa nɔ egbɔjɔ. Amɛfeɔ ekome kɛkwɛɔ koni onibii fɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ aná shikpɔŋ shihilɛ po kɛha dalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why are small worms eating holes right through the center of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. They hide inside the central leaves of maize plants and feed on them. Clearing weeds around your field early and applying recommended biological or chemical controls can protect your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni ooojie mra Ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ abu onibii ahe.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies that feed on the sap and spread viruses. Keeping the farm free of weeds and using insecticidal soap or recommended sprays helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okɛ samla loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and moist climate they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil for too long, suffocating the roots and allowing harmful fungi to grow. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer around the base of the plant will restore its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii tso titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ Shishitoo lɛ baaha tso lɛ aku sɛɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does my farmland become hard like stone during the dry season, making it difficult to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ wa tamɔ tɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli, ni no haa ewaa akɛ aduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it loses its organic matter and moisture. Covering your soil with dry grass or leaves (mulching) and adding compost helps the ground retain water, stay cool, and remain soft for planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ elaaje. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ nu mli, ehi shi fɛ̃i, ni ehi shi blɛoo kɛha dumɔwui.

english: Why do my bean plants produce plenty of leafy greenery but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ miiwo baai eŋɔli babaoo shi bean pods fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil encourages plants to build stems and leaves instead of flowers and pods. Using balanced fertilizers with more phosphorus helps bean plants switch their energy into making flowers and pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii kɛ baai yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii tsei lɛ ni amɛjieɔ hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a shortage of plant food. Watering your tomatoes regularly at the base and applying mulch keeps the roots cool so the plant can hold onto its flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tso niyenii ni bɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tomato nɔ daa yɛ shishigbɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ fɔfɔii lɛ.

english: Why are my yam vines drying up and dying early before the yam tubers get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya dani sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Early drying of yam vines can be caused by yam leaf spot disease, dry spells, or beetles attacking the root zone. Ensuring good crop rotation and planting healthy seed yams prevents early dieback so tubers can mature fully.
ga: Nɔ ni baanyɛ aha sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbi oya ji sweet potato baa lɛ he hela, hulutsoo be, loo ŋmeii ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Ni aaakwɛ koni ŋmɔshi nibii atsake jogbaŋŋ ni adu sweet potatoes ni dumɔwui ni hi yɔɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni akafite mra bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ adara.

english: Why do my cabbage plants stay open with loose leaves instead of forming hard round heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ashiɔ mi-cabbage tso lɛ ni egbele kɛ baai ni etse ehe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee yitsei ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head properly when temperatures get too high, water supply is irregular, or plants are crowded together. Giving each cabbage enough space and maintaining steady soil moisture helps leaves wrap tightly into solid heads.
ga: Kaabaji nyɛŋ atsɔ yitso nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ daa. loo tsei ni ebua amɛhe naa babaoo Kɛ́ aha kaabii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ babaoo ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ abɔle amɛhe jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee yitso ni wa.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains next to my young cocoa trees on new land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ he ko hee lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when water sits on my farm for too long after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater stays on the land without draining, it suffocates the roots and allows soil fungi and bacteria to attack and rot them.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni eha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ni amɛgboi.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans before my maize help the soil grow better crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei dani adu ŋmei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. When you plant maize after them, the maize uses that natural nitrogen to grow strong leaves without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa kɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni tsofa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from under the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Treating the farm early for pests stops the spread and allows normal fruit development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Okwaafoi lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Bɔni afee ni ana tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ, ebaakpa egbɛfaŋnɔ ni eye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still hanging on the trees during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, humid weather and heavy shade. Pruning farm trees to let in sun and removing infected pods regularly helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ afo ŋmɔ mli tsei lɛ amli daa koni hulu la babaoo aba mli, ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ akpa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips on maize mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is essential for green leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea when the soil is damp will help them recover.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔlii lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without growing any tomatoes when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛduuu tomato ko kwraa kɛji edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries up pollen, preventing flowers from producing seeds and fruit. Giving the plants sufficient water and light shade lowers their stress so fruits can form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Etsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo dumɔwui kɛ aduawai. Nu kɛ hulutsoo ni sa ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ haa nɔnyɛɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni aduawai aba.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out small and twisted even when the green vines on top look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni efite eyɛ mli akɛ wain tso ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow downwards underground and need soft, loose soil to expand smoothly. Hard soil, rocks, or shallow planting prevent the tuber from swelling properly, resulting in small or misshapen yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa, tɛi, loo dumɔwui ni mli ekwɔɔɔ Enɛ baatsi yitso lɛ naa koni ekafu jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: Why do my maize stalks break and fall over easily when strong winds blow through the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa kɛbote ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize stalks become weak if plants are sown too close together—making them tall and thin—or if the soil lacks potassium. Proper planting distance and balanced nutrients make stems thick enough to stand up to wind.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Ha ekwɛ tsɔ ni efee mlɛo Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium He ni sa ni akɛduɔ nii kɛ niyenii ni ja haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds while my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have small roots and easily lose the fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients against fast-growing weeds. Weeding early ensures your young crops get all the resources they need to establish strong roots.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei bibii lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛma shishitoo ni wa.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. The plant moves nitrogen from its older, bottom leaves to feed the younger leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-ŋmã lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out the plant juices, or passing along a virus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo egbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ eshwaa

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when the soil around them is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tso lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This sudden wilting in wet soil is often caused by bacterial wilt, a disease in the ground that blocks the water pipes inside the plant stem so water cannot travel up to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, bacteria wilt ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ anaa. Ehaa nu nyɛɛɛ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my plantain tree give me small, light bunches if I leave all the young shoots growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain lɛ haa mi niji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji mishi ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ?

english: Young plantain shoots, called suckers, drink water and food from the mother plant's roots. Leaving too many suckers starves the main stem, resulting in smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Atsɛɔ plantains tsei bibii lɛ akɛ tsei bibii. Nuu nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ nyɛ tso lɛ shishifãi amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei bibii babaoo shwie shi lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye tso titri lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do many tiny cocoa pods turn dark and shrivel up on the tree trunk while they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo feɔ duŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lolo lɛ?

english: This is known as cherelle wilt. It is mostly a natural process where the cocoa tree sheds extra young pods it cannot feed properly, though severe dry spells or pests can cause even more to wilt.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherel ni shwieɔ shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni cacao tso lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii bibii krokomɛi ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ babaoo. Eyɛ mli akɛ hulutsoo be loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ fe tsutsu lɛ po moŋ.

english: Why does my lettuce start producing flowers and seeds so quickly instead of growing big leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-lettuce lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui ashishi oya yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ baai wuji lɛ?

english: When leafy vegetables experience hot weather or drought, they get stressed and think they are about to die. They quickly produce seeds to survive and leave offspring before the weather gets worse.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo hulutsoo be kpe lɛ Aduawai lɛ haoɔ ni amɛsusuɔ akɛ amɛbaagboi. Amɛwoɔ dumɔwui oya koni amɛhi shi ni amɛshiɔ seshi dani kɔɔyɔŋ lɛlɛ lɛ mli woɔ wu.

english: Why do my cassava tubers soften and rot underground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When soil stays flooded for too long, the roots drown and fungi in the water attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ baatutua amɛ ni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ agboi.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts on my plot will help my maize crop grow better next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to a family of crops that take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil, naturally enriching the land for heavy feeders like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji tsei aweku ko ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Taakɛ eji lɛ, enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii kɛha niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do I need to erect tall wooden stakes for my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsei kakadaji toɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahã amɛfo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines up on stakes helps the leaves capture more sunlight to make food for big tubers and keeps the foliage off the damp soil where diseases easily spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnáa hulu la babaoo koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii wuji lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ he ni hela baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do cocoa trees shed many of their flowers without setting pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can ever support as pods. Insects must pollinate the flowers, and the tree naturally drops any flowers that are unpollinated or too numerous to carry.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe ŋmeii. Esa akɛ kooloi bibii awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen. Ni tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ loo fɔfɔi babaoo tsɔ yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I plant them in a field with no big trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong direct sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides necessary shade, keeps the soil cool, and protects the young plants until they grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the maize plants to compete for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly allows each plant to grow strong stems, deep roots, and produce bigger, healthier cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná shishifãi ni mli wa, shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to grow a good maize crop this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmãa kpakpa yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Healthy soil usually looks dark, feels loose and crumbly, holds moisture well without becoming waterlogged, and has earthworms present. If your soil is pale, hard, or sandy, adding compost, animal manure, or proper fertilizer will restore its nutrients before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ feɔ duŋ. Enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaaa nu lɛ ahi shi. Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ. Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli tse, ewa, loo ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba dani odu.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same land wears out specific soil nutrients and allows maize pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ he kome lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi aba shi. ni ehaa ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Leaf yellowing and curling in cassava is often caused by sap-sucking pests like whiteflies or viral diseases like Cassava Mosaic Disease. Removing affected plants early and using clean, disease-free stem cuttings for planting prevents the problem from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli tamɔ ŋmeii mosaic lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Ni niji ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii beni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni naagba lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hot afternoon even when it rained earlier in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, intense sunlight causes water to evaporate rapidly from crop leaves faster than their roots can draw water from the soil. Providing shade, mulching the soil with dry grass, or watering early in the morning or evening helps plants retain moisture.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ haa nu shwieɔ tsei lɛ ahe oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shade: Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛ́ afɔ tsei lɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do experienced farmers spread dry grass around the roots of their pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi amɛshwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass around crops is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation during hot weather, prevents weed growth, and turns into rich organic matter as it decomposes.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ehaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ eyi mli obɔ be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with very strong, aggressive roots that adapt quickly to rainfall and steal nutrients from the soil. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks of planting prevents them from choking your crops and taking away vital water and plant food.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni wa, ni yɔɔ basabasa. Amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ nugbɔ lɛ mli oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkatsi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa, ni amɛbaaŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛ tsei lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Is it good for me to cut off some of the lower leaves on my tomato plants as they grow?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yes, removing the lower or yellowing leaves off tomato plants improves airflow around the stem, prevents soil-borne fungal diseases from splashing onto leaves, and directs the plant's energy toward producing bigger, healthier fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ajie baai ni yɔɔ shishi loo ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ kɛjɛ tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akashwie baai lɛ anɔ. ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my harvested grains like maize and beans rot or get eaten by insects in my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmaa ni akpa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa miifite loo kooloi ni yɔɔ mi nitoohe lɛ miiye lɛ?

english: Grains rot or attract insects like weevils if they are stored while still wet or in damp rooms. Thoroughly drying your grains in the sun until they are hard and storing them in airtight bags or clean, dry containers protects them from pests and mold.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa fiteɔ loo egbalaa kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛji akɛ akɛto be mli ni edɔ loo yɛ tsu ko ni mli efɔ mli. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo nɔ ko ni mli tse ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaabu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii ahe.

english: Why do I need to dig such a deep hole when planting cocoa or palm trees instead of just setting them on top of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atsa bu ni mli kwɔ tamɔ nɛkɛ beni aduɔ kookoo loo ŋmei tsei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaafu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Digging a deep hole breaks up hard soil so that young roots can easily grow downwards, reach underground water, and anchor the growing tree firmly against heavy winds.
ga: Bu ni mli kwɔ ni atsa lɛ gbalaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii anyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shishi mlɛo. nine shɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu nɔ ni eha tsei ni miida lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he

english: What will happen to my fruit tree saplings if I plant them in a shallow hole instead of a deep one?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi tso yibii dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo bu ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ mli moŋ fe bu ko ni mli kwɔ mli?

english: If the hole is too shallow, the roots cannot spread deeply enough, causing the young tree to dry out quickly in the sun or fall over when it gets bigger.
ga: Kɛji bu lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he ni sa. Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ loo amɛgbee shi beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: How deep should I dig the soil when I am getting ready to plant young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Kɛ́ oosaa ohe koni odu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ, te esa akɛ otsa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ oha tɛŋŋ?

english: A good planting hole for cocoa should be about 30 to 40 centimeters deep and wide, giving the soft taproot enough room to stretch straight down without bending.
ga: Esa akɛ bu ni hi ni akɛduɔ kookoo lɛ mli lɛ mli kwɔ aaafee sɛntimita 30 kɛyashi 40 ni elɛɛmɔ bɔni afee ni taproot ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ehe ashɛ shi tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛ ehe akabɔ.

english: Why is it important to loosen the hard soil at the bottom of the hole before placing my seedling inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie sũ ni wa ni yɔɔ bu lɛ shishi lɛ dani akɛ dumɔwu lɛ awo mli lɛ?

english: Loosening the bottom soil makes it easy for tender new roots to push deep into the earth without spending too much energy struggling against hard dirt.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ babaoo awuu amɛshi shikpɔŋ ni wa.

english: Why do living crops like trees need deep soil holes to stand up, while objects like farm chairs can just stay on top of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni hiɛ ka tamɔ tsei he hiaa bu ni mli kwɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdamɔ shi lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nibii tamɔ ŋmɔ mli sɛii baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ.

english: Unlike non-living objects, living crops grow heavy and continuously draw food and water from deep underground, so they need deep roots to hold them up and feed them.
ga: Esoro tsei ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ yɛ nibii ni wala bɛ mli lɛ ahe yɛ gbɛ ni ji akɛ, amɛdaraa waa ni amɛjieɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baaye abua amɛ ni amɛha amɛ niyenii.

english: Why do tree crops like oil palm take so much soil preparation compared to fast crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni ji jwɛi tamɔ oil palm lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ babaoo fe tso ni daa oya tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Tree crops stay in the soil for many years, so they need deep, well-prepared soil from the beginning to build a permanent foundation for years of harvests.
ga: Tsoi ni yɔɔ jwɛi mli lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ he miihia amɛ kɛjɛ shishijee koni amɛfee shishitoo ni hiɔ shi daa kɛha afii babaoo ni akɛkpaa nii.

english: Can I just scatter fruit seeds directly on top of my farmland and cover them lightly with dirt?
ga: Ani manyɛ magbɛ aduawai dumɔwui ashwã he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni mikɛ sũ aha nɔ fioo?

english: Most seeds need to be buried at the proper depth in loose soil so the emerging roots stay moist and protected from birds, heat, and heavy rain.
ga: Ehe miihia ni afu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ. Enɛ ji koni shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ okpoi, dɔlɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my oil palm seedlings dry out and die faster if I plant them too close to the surface during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soil near the surface dries out very fast under the hot sun, but deeper soil holds onto moisture longer to keep the roots hydrated.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya waa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shi shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Is it better for me to plant fruit trees using young saplings from a nursery or by planting fresh seeds directly in the field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikɛ tsei bibii ni jɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai tsei loo mikɛ dumɔwui heei baadu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Nursery saplings have already developed early roots, giving them a head start to establish quickly in deep planting holes compared to seeds planted straight in the field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ gbekɛbii askul lɛ shishifãi mra. Ha amɛje shishi oya yɛ dumɔ bui ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli. kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he

english: Why are deep roots so important for permanent crops on my farm as they grow older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baahi shi daa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni midaa lɛ?

english: Deep roots act as an anchor to support heavy branches loaded with crop yield, while reaching deep underground water reserves during long dry spells.
ga: Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni fiɔ tsei niji ni tsii ni eyi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ asɛɛ. yɛ be mli ni enine shɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu jɛɛhei ni mli kwɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How many years does it take for a newly planted cocoa tree to start bearing fruit?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ yibii?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties usually start producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years. Good farm management, proper shading, and weeding help them bear fruit earlier.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5. Okwaafoi akwɛmɔ kpakpa shading ni sa Kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot handle direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or temporary shade trees planted alongside them to protect their leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ ji koni baai lɛ akashã, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: It is not recommended because cassava grows fast, feeds heavily on soil nutrients, and blocks sunlight. Instead, plantains or cocoyams are better temporary shade crops for young cocoa because they do not aggressively compete with the cocoa trees.
ga: Akɛɛɛ akɛ afee nakai ejaakɛ ŋmei daa oya. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ waa ni etsiɔ hulu la naa lɛ, plantain loo kookoo ji tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni haa be kukuoo mli hulutsoo baa kɛha kookoo bibii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ kookoo tsei ashi akaŋ waa.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection common in high humidity and rainy seasons. Pruning extra branches to let in air and sunlight, removing infected pods, and using approved fungicides help control it.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni bei pii lɛ anaa yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Afolɔ nibii krokomɛi ni fata he koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Jiemɔ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ni tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ tsei niji lɛ.

english: Cocoa grows best in deep, fertile loamy soil that drains water easily without becoming waterlogged. Land that has rich topsoil from previous forest cover or fallow vegetation is usually ideal for cocoa.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ sũ ni baanyɛ atsɔ mli oya ni nu bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔji ni nɔ sũ babaoo yɔɔ nɔ ni jɛ kooi amli loo tsutsu ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How far apart should I space my cocoa trees during planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mafee mi-cocoa tsei lɛ ateŋ be mli ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Standard spacing for cocoa trees is 3 meters by 3 meters (about 10 feet by 10 feet). Proper spacing gives each tree enough room to spread its leaves, absorb nutrients, and receive sunlight without competing with neighboring trees.
ga: He ni esa akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai 3 x mitai 3 (aaafee ninetalɔi 10 x ninetalɔi 10). Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaai lɛ agbɛɔ eshwaa. ŋmɛɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni enine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ

english: Pruning removes dead, diseased, or unnecessary branches so the tree can focus its energy on growing healthy pods. It also allows air and light into the tree canopy, which reduces fungal diseases like Black Pod.
ga: Niji ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ jieɔ tsei lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la hu boteɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my young crops turn light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are often a sign that the plant lacks nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that the soil is holding too much water around the roots. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo tsɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests when I plant the same crop on it every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year. Rotating crops or leaving the land to rest allows the soil to rebuild its natural fertility and stops soil diseases from multiplying.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa ebɔɔ su ni eyɔɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ helai shwereɔ.

english: How many pods can I expect to harvest from one healthy cocoa tree in a year?
ga: Pods enyiɛ manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ cacao tso kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli yɛ afi kome mli?

english: A healthy, well-maintained mature hybrid cocoa tree can yield between 20 to 50 pods per year, depending on soil fertility, weather conditions, rainfall, and proper pest control.
ga: Cacao tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmeii 20 kɛyashi 50 daa afi, ni enɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ bɔ ni akwɛɔ ŋmeii anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it good to plant plantains on the same land where I want to grow young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo tsei bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Plantain leaves grow quickly and wide, acting like natural umbrellas that protect young cocoa seedlings from burning under the hot sun while keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ daa oya ni amɛshwereɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkashã yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Should I plant my plantains before I bring my cocoa seedlings to the farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu plantains dani mikɛ kookoo dumɔwui aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, planting plantains first allows them to grow large leaves ahead of time so shade is ready to protect the sensitive young cocoa as soon as it is planted.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ baai wuji dani be shɛɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, hulutsoo yɛ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛji adu amɛ pɛ.

english: If young cocoa trees get too much sun, their leaves will turn yellow, get brown dry spots, or burn, showing that they need more shade cover from plants like plantain.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ná hulu la babaoo lɛ, Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. He ni egbi, ni tsuɔ, loo ni eshã lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia ni aha lɛ hulutsoo kroko.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to draw straight lines and use pegs when planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mafolɔ linei ni ja ni mikɛ pins atsu nii kɛ́ midu tsei lɛ?

english: Planting along straight lines ensures every crop gets equal space, air, and sunlight, while making it much easier for you to weed, apply fertilizer, and move through the farm.
ga: Nibii ni yaa hiɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa he ko, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okɛ ohe awo oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Do I need to leave my land empty for a long time after clearing it before I can plant plantain?
ga: Kɛ́ mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii lɛ, ani esa akɛ mashi nɔ ko nɔ ko be kakadaŋŋ dani manyɛ madu plantains?

english: No, once the land is cleared and marked with pegs, you can plant plantain right away as long as the rains have started and the ground has good moisture.
ga: Dabi, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse ni akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ema shi pɛ. Obaanyɛ odu plantains amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my cocoa plants if rainwater sits on the farm floor without draining away?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu lɛ ta ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efooo?

english: Too much standing water can drown the roots of young cocoa trees, preventing them from breathing and causing root rot, which slows down plant growth or kills the tree.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli. Ehaaa amɛmu ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo loo ebaaha tso lɛ agbo.

english: Why does the soil stay wetter under plantain trees than on open farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ yɛ dumɔwui ashishi fe ŋmɔji ni agbele naa lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: The big leaves of plantain trees block the hot sun from directly touching the soil, which stops water from evaporating quickly into the air.
ga: Plantain baai agboi lɛ tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why should I cut off some of the old leaves from my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai momoi lɛ ekomɛi kɛjɛ mi-plantain lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Removing dead or lower plantain leaves lets in just enough light for the cocoa underneath to grow properly and prevents pests and diseases from living in the dry leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie plantain tso lɛ baai ni egboi loo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ, ebaaha la ni fa bɔ ni sa aha kookoo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahi baai ni egbi lɛ amli.

english: How can I make sure all my cocoa seedlings grow evenly at the same speed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni kookoo dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ ada bɔ ni sa kɛ oyaiyeli kome?

english: To get even growth, ensure all seedlings get equal shade, keep weeds away from their base, and plant them at the exact same time during the rainy season.
ga: koni ekwɛ akɛ edara daa Kwɛmɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ aná hulutsoo ni tamɔ amɛhe. Ha jwɛi lɛ akashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni aduɔ yɛ be kome mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: Why does establishing a new cocoa farm require so much hard labor during the first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔ hee ni ato lɛ heɔ nitsumɔ babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate like infants and need constant weeding, shade regulation, and water management until their roots become deep enough to survive on their own.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa tamɔ abifabii. ni ehe miihia ni ajie jwɛi be fɛɛ be Shade nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ nu nɔkwɛmɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act like living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Is it good for my soil if I plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei wo mli?

english: Yes, planting beans or groundnuts with maize is very good. Beans naturally trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which acts like free fertilizer for your maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa. Beans lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni damɔ shi ekome kɛhaa o-corn lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or adding well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant gets too hot or doesn't get enough water. Watering regularly at the base and covering the soil with dry grass helps keep the moisture in and saves the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo enáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daa kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Which part of the cassava stem is best to cut and plant in the soil?
ga: Kasava tso lɛ fã ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaafo ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Use the middle part of a healthy, mature stem about the thickness of a thumb. Avoid the soft green top and the very hard bottom, because the middle section sprouts roots the fastest.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ teŋ fã ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni edara ni miihe ashɛ tsitsi wulu lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ shishi ni wa waa lɛ he. Ejaakɛ fã ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ baakwɛ shishifãi oya fe fɛɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb up so their leaves can catch direct sunlight. When the leaves get plenty of sun, they make more energy to feed and grow bigger yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaaha hewalɛ babaoo aba ni ekɛtao niyenii ni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting after the dry season ends?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu nii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because the ground underneath is still hot and dry. Wait until you get two or three heavy rains so the soil holds enough water to sprout your seeds safely.
ga: Kaadu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli edɔ lolo ni edɔ. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa shii enyɔ loo etɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I tell if my farmland has good soil or if it needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa loo ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If crops grow thick stems and dark green leaves naturally, the soil is rich. If plants stay short, thin, and turn pale green quickly, the soil lacks food and needs compost or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli tse kɛ baai ni ji eŋɔli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii Kɛji tso lɛ yɛ kuku, eyɛ mlɛo ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ oya Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ mli ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for food, water, and sunlight in the soil. Clearing weeds early leaves all the moisture and nutrients for your crops to grow big.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaashi ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni baaha onibii lɛ adara.

english: What makes the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tightly and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from under the leaves. Spraying the leaves with light soapy water or neem oil helps clear these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ samla ni mli ejɔ loo neem fɔ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ajie amɛhe.

english: I farm in the Afram Plains area; which crops grow best in this kind of land?
ga: Mitsuɔ okwaa yɛ Afram shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ; Mɛɛ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɛkɛ he nɛɛ?

english: The Afram Plains has fertile, low-lying land that holds moisture well, making it ideal for fast-growing grains like maize and rice, as well as root crops like yam and cassava. Choosing drought-tolerant seed varieties helps your crops withstand hot dry spells in this region.
ga: Afram Gbɛjegbɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni baa nii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ehi kɛha ŋmaa ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa, kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ŋmãa ni shwereɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa. Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ ni ooohala lɛ yeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛdamɔɔ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ hɔmɔ ni yɔɔ kpokpaa nɛɛ nɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do stray pigs destroy my cassava farm so much faster than cattle do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsinai ni elaaje lɛ miifite mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ oya fe tsinai lɛ?

english: Pigs move very quickly and naturally use their strong snouts to dig underground for tubers. While cattle mostly eat leaves above the ground, pigs uproot the entire plant within minutes to get to the sweet cassava roots underneath.
ga: Kplootoi nyiɛɔ oya waa. Ekɛ etsitsi ni mli wa lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni ena adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Yɛ be mli ni tsinayei babaoo yeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ baai lɛ, Kplotooi baajie tsei muu fɛɛ yɛ minitii fioo komɛi amli koni amɛyashɛ shishifãi ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahe.

english: How can I stop wandering farm animals from trampling my young maize field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni nyiɛɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ ni amɛkanyiɛ mi-bibii ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ?

english: Planting a dense boundary layer of prickly crops like jatropha or thick elephant grass around your field creates a natural wall. These living fences deter fast-moving animals while also acting as windbreaks to protect your soil.
ga: Aduɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmeii babaoo, tamɔ jatropha loo shwuɔ jwɛi ni mli tse. Abaama adebɔɔ mli gbogbo abɔle ŋmɔji lɛ ahe. Nɛkɛ gbogboi ni hiɛ ka nɛɛ tsiɔ kooloi ni yaa oya lɛ anaa, yɛ be mli ni amɛtsuɔ nii hu akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni buɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up when the sun gets very hot in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense to save water. When sunlight is intense, the plant closes tiny openings on its leaves to keep moisture inside, making the leaves look wilted until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛ hulu la lɛ mli wa lɛ Tso lɛ baaŋmɛ gbɛ bibioo lɛ. yɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: If animals chew off the top leaves of my growing crops, will the plants grow back?
ga: Kɛji kooloi ye mi tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ baai lɛ Ani tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ?

english: If the main growing tip on the central stem is still undamaged, the crop will usually sprout new leaves, though harvest will be delayed. If the main stem is bitten down to the root, the plant will likely die and should be replanted.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta titri ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ efiteee lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, Nibii ni Aduɔ lɛ jieɔ baai heei. Kɛji akɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ po Kɛji akɛ atswa tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛyashi shishifã lɛ Tso lɛ hu baanyɛ agbo ni esa akɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow and spread much faster than my crop seedlings after the early rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe mitso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that have adapted over years to survive with minimal nutrients and water. They germinate instantly to seize sunlight, whereas cultivated crop seedlings grow more deliberately and need extra care and weeding to compete.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi kɛ niyenii kɛ nu fioo ko pɛ. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu lɛ daa waa ni ebiɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli koni amɛye akaŋ.

english: Why do my yam mounds collapse so easily when farm animals walk through the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋtayaa lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmɔ mli kooloi nyiɛ he lɛ?

english: Yam mounds are built with loose, raised topsoil so that tubers can expand easily underground. Because the soil is kept soft for root growth, heavy hooves crush the mounds, exposing growing yams to sunlight and damaging heat.
ga: Akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nɔ kwɔ feɔ sweet potato piles koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, afeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ blɛoo koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Naji ni tsii shwie gɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato nɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ fiteɔ.

english: What fast-growing plant can I grow around my farm borders to keep livestock out?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ makwɛ yɛ mihe? Okwaafoi husu koni kooloi akabote mli

english: Planting pigeon peas or fast-growing thorn bushes around your farm edges creates an effective live fence. Pigeon peas grow rapidly to block animals, improve your soil's nitrogen levels, and yield extra food for your family.
ga: Pigeon peas loo ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he. Okwaafoi akutsei lɛ feɔ wala gbogbo ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Pigeon peas lɛ daa oya koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe. Ha nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ni eha niyenii kroko aba oweku lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my cassava yield thick tubers in some spots of my farm but very thin roots in others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa yɛ hei komɛi?

english: Cassava roots need loose, soft soil to expand properly. In areas where the soil is hard or heavily packed down, the roots struggle to swell, resulting in thin cassava tubers compared to softer areas of the field.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa lɛ, ewa akɛ shishifãi lɛ baafu, ni no haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ akɛto hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Is the manure left behind by cattle passing through my farm good for my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsinai shwieɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ehiii kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Yes, animal manure adds vital nutrients like nitrogen to the soil. However, fresh, hot manure can burn crop roots if placed directly against tender seedlings, so it is best left to dry or mixed thoroughly into the soil before planting.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen fataa sũ lɛ he. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi kɛji akɛ akɛwo dumɔwui ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ aŋmɛ amɛ gbɛ ni amɛgbi loo akɛ amɛ afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani adu.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your crop is running out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay green and grow tall. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer around the stems will restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛsu eŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛdara. Kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛbaabɔle tso lɛ he lɛ baaha tso lɛ aku sɛɛ afee eŋɔli.

english: Why do groundnuts and cowpeas make the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground. When these crops die or drop leaves, they leave free plant food behind in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ helai bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji tsei nɛɛ gboi loo amɛbaai lɛ fite lɛ Amɛshiɔ tsei niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do earthworms in my farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?
