english: Earthworms swallow dirt and dead leaves, turning them into rich manure that feeds your crops. As they burrow through the earth, they also make small tunnels that help rain water and plant roots move easily through the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii miɔ muji kɛ baai ni egboi. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa ni akɛyeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii. Beni amɛfoɔ lɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii hu. No yeɔ ebuaa nugbɔ nu kɛ tsei shishifãi ni amɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Young cocoa trees are soft and sensitive to full heat from the sun. Leaving shade trees like plantain or forest trees above them keeps the air cool and protects their tender leaves until they grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ darako ni amɛnuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui loo koo mli tsei, yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha edɔ ni ebu ebaai bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi ebaada ni enyɛ edamɔ hulutsoo tɛ̃ɛ naa.

english: Why do plant leaves bend and lean toward open spaces where the sun shines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa hei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ lɛ?

english: Plants use light from the sun to cook food inside their leaves. They naturally stretch their stem and bend their leaves toward direct sunlight so they can trap maximum energy to grow healthy roots and fruits.
ga: Tsei kɛ hulu la hoɔ niyenii yɛ amɛ baai lɛ amli. Amɛhaa amɛshishifãi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni amɛfoɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛto hewalɛ babaoo koni amɛkɛwo shishifãi kɛ aduawai ni mli wa.

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When heavy rain sits in waterlogged soil without draining, the roots drown, stop working, and rot. Planting cassava on high mounds or ridges lets excess water flow away.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛkpaa nitsumɔ ni amɛgboiɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Why do farmers cover the ground around their crops with dry grass and maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi kɛ ŋmãa tsei haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry leaves or grass—called mulching—acts like a blanket. It prevents the hot afternoon sun from baking the ground and keeps water in the soil longer so plant roots do not dry out.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi, ni ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Tse shishifãi lɛ gĩii.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get stressed from extreme sun heat, dry soil, or a lack of small insects like bees to carry pollen from flower to flower. Watering regularly and keeping the soil moist helps flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulu ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni hiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi kome kɛyaa ekroko mli lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: This black spot is caused by a shortage of calcium inside the developing fruit, which happens when watering is uneven. Keeping the soil consistently moist allows the plant's roots to continuously suck up calcium from the ground.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do small caterpillars chew the center leaves of my maize only during the night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ gbɛkɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: These pests, known as Fall Armyworms, hide inside the plant stalk during the hot daytime to avoid drying out, then come out at night to feast on fresh leaves. Checking the plant funnels early and applying neem oil or appropriate treatments keeps them away.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ, kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ashishifãi amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli koni amɛkagbi. Kɛkɛ lɛ, amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye baai heei gbɛkɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni neem fɔ loo tsofafeemɔ ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni akafee nakai.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn brown and drop off when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need protection from direct sunlight because high heat dries out their foliage quickly. Without shade plants like plantains nearby, heat stress causes the leaves to burn, dry out, and fall off.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ejaakɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi oya. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Heat stress haa baai lɛ shãa, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow before the corn is ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that your corn lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for plant growth. The plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves and cobs at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha baai bibii kɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaa lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites, or a virus spread by whiteflies. They feed on the tender young leaves, damaging them as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo mites, loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni kɛ fitemɔ baa beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain saturates the soil without draining away, oxygen is cut off, allowing fungi and rot-causing organisms to attack the roots.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɔ̃ɔ ni nu hoɔɔɔ. Afoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why should I not plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously in the same spot exhausts specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply in the ground over time.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer so the rain does not waste it?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ lɛ akafite?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a light rain, but avoid doing it right before a heavy downpour. Heavy rain sweeps fertilizer away off the top of the soil before the plant roots can absorb it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi kaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dirt inside the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli ni mishi muji yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide deep inside the center whorl of young maize plants and chew on the growing tissue before the cobs form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ fãji ni miida lɛ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow smaller and give me a low yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like aggressive neighbors that steal soil food, water, and sunlight away from your crops, leaving your main plants hungry and unable to produce big yields.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii titri lɛ ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ nibii babaoo aba.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when stressed by extreme heat or dry soil. If conditions are too hot or dry during flowering, pollination fails and the plant sheds the blossom instead of growing fruit.
ga: Tomato baagbee shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi hao lɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii ni tso lɛ fɔfɔii yɛ aduawai ni ebaawo lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How do I know if my harvested maize or cocoa is dry enough to store without molding?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa loo mi-kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto ni mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko?

english: Grains and beans must be properly sun-dried until hard. Maize kernels should not dent when pressed with a fingernail, and dried cocoa beans should crackle softly when squeezed in your palm.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbi ŋmaa kɛ ŋmeii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Esaaa akɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ akɛ nineshi ŋmei miimɔ nɔ. Ni esa akɛ agbele kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli blɛoo. Beni ashɛreɔ yɛ nine lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees from my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the soil. Keeping large trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides a canopy that protects young seedlings from heat until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei wuji loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ akwɛmɔ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does my yam plant need long wooden poles to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ tsei kakadaji ni amɛkɛkwɔɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs to spread its leaves out to catch sunlight, which feeds the growth of the tubers underground. Staking the vines off the ground allows maximum sunlight exposure and prevents fungal diseases from forming on leaves touching damp soil.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. ni ji niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ Wein tso lɛ ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa enáa hulu la babaoo ni ehaa ŋmeii helai baa baa ni taa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the essential nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow tall. Applying animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans help make my soil better for maize in the next season?
ga: Te ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehi aha ŋmãa ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which has special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays behind as natural fertilizer for future crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nitrogen ni amɔ lɛ lɛ baakã he ahi shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the soil when heavy rains stay on the field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rainwater sits on flat farmland without draining away, it chokes the roots and creates damp conditions where rot fungi thrive. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets extra water drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ta okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha shihilɛ ko ni mli edɔ aba ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: It is best to water early in the morning because cool morning temperatures allow water to soak deep into the soil for roots to drink. Watering in the hot afternoon causes water to evaporate rapidly before plants can absorb it and can burn wet leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ leebi hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ lɛ baaha nu lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ anu nu. Nu ni akɛhaa yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya dani tso lɛ nyɛɔ eŋɔɔ ni eshãa baai ni efɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I allow many small plantain shoots to grow around one main mother stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa plantain tsei bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? Mɛi babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe. Tso titri kome pɛ shishi

english: When too many shoots grow from the same base, they fight with each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Pruning away excess shoots leaves only one strong sucker, which concentrates the plant's energy into producing bigger plantain bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shishitoo kome nɔ. Amɛbaawuu koni amɛná nu. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baashi. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ hewalɛ lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama panicles wuji afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do farmers tie tomato plants to wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi fĩɔ tomato tsei ahe yɛ tsei amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tying tomato plants upward keeps leaves and fruits off wet soil, preventing rot and soil-borne diseases. It also improves airflow through the plant, which keeps the foliage dry and healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tomato tsei lɛ fĩ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaa kɛ aduawai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ hu yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off before producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani pepper yibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or attacks from tiny insects like thrips. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting plants from pests helps the flowers develop into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa amɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tsei ahebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do insect pests keep attacking my vegetables if I plant the exact same crop on the same land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa mi aduawai lɛ be fɛɛ be kɛji midu tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop over and over provides pests with a continuous food source, causing their population to build up in the soil. Rotating your farm with different crop families starves pests and breaks their life cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai náa niyenii ni amɛyeɔ daa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛyibɔ ​​buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Oŋmɔ lɛ ni okɛ tsei akui srɔtoi baatsake Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmeii lɛ ni ebaafite amɛshihilɛ gbɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen nutrients or their roots are logged with too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or clearing water channels will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen niyenii. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu wo mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up under strong midday heat. They naturally rest and recover by evening, but placing grass mulch around the base helps keep the root soil cool.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ shishi. Amɛjɔɔ amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛhe wa amɛ gbɛkɛ. Shi sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress from prolonged dry weather, lack of soil nutrients, or attacks from tiny insects like capsids. Proper shade management and watering during dry spells help flowers mature into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ mli haomɔ mli. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids ni tutuaa amɛ. Kɛ́ akwɛ hulutsoo be lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ nu ni awoɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Leaf curling on cassava is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-free stem cuttings for planting stops the disease from spreading in your farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ woɔ amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei niji ni hela bɛ mli lɛ tsu nii yɛ dumɔwui amli lɛ, ehaaa helai agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: This black rotting is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant during fruit development, often made worse by irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and adding lime helps correct this issue.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end ŋmɔtɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ. Ni bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ haa enɛ feɔ nɔ ni ehiii kwraa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ lime fata he lɛ, ebaatsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why are green caterpillars eating large holes through my cabbage leaves so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye buji wuji kɛmiitsɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli oya nɛkɛ?

english: Moths lay eggs on the tender cabbage leaves, and once they hatch into hungry caterpillars, they feed constantly to grow. Checking under leaves early and picking them off or using safe bio-pesticides will protect the head of the cabbage.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ kaabe baai bibii anɔ. Ni kɛ́ amɛfɔ lɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ. Amɛbaaye niyenii be fɛɛ be koni amɛdara. Nibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ amɛ akaje kpo loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu kaabe yitsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why does fertilizer work better when I apply it right after it rains instead of when the soil is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ fe be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: Plants cannot absorb dry fertilizer granules directly. Rainwater dissolves the fertilizer into liquid form so the roots can drink up the nutrients easily without getting burned by direct contact with dry chemicals.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ efeɔ nu bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãaa kɛtsɔ tsofai ni egbi lɛ ni amɛkɛbaabɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it helpful to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas out of the air and deposit it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil, making it richer for heavy-feeding crops like corn.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa efeɔ fɛo waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with tall sticks instead of leaving them on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji adu mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ moŋ fe ni mashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to capture direct sunlight, which gives the plant energy to build large tubers underground while keeping the leaves off damp soil where diseases spread.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akafee shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ yɛ he ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why did the leaves of my crops burn after I sprayed weed medicine on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ shãa beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ eshwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop leaves burn if chemical weedicides touch them directly or if the spray mixture is made too strong. Reading chemical bottle directions carefully and using a spray shield prevents medicine from damaging your main crops.
ga: Tso lɛ baai baashã kɛji tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ bashɛ he tɛ̃ɛ loo kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ jwɛi lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ́ okane tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tɔ mli lɛ he gbɛtsɔɔmɔi lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ shield spray tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsofa lɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is essential food for growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-decomposed compost early in the season helps keep the leaves green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ebaaha yibii kpakpai aba.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under intense heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them creates a shield against direct sunlight until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains yɛ ehe lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ akafee nɔ ko kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Cassava roots rot when sitting in waterlogged soil for too long because water blocks air from reaching the roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to create food for the roots beneath. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp ground into the sun while protecting leaves from soil-borne fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la mli yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ hu ahe.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when plants experience heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the base helps the flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ekɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha ebɔle Shishi lɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during strong winds when they start carrying bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli kɛji amɛbɔi ŋmɔshi nibii feemɔ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, making the plant top-heavy once heavy bunches grow. Supporting the main stalk with sturdy wooden or bamboo forks helps keep the tree upright until harvest.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni no haa tso lɛ feɔ nɔ ni tsii kɛ́ fɔfɔi lɛ amli tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso loo ŋmei ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why are small holes appearing in my maize leaves with tiny caterpillars hiding in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmãa baa ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ? Akɛtee teŋgbɛ?

english: These holes are caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on young plant tissues. Inspecting fields early and spraying recommended neem extract or bio-pesticides controls the infestation.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei bibii amli fãji lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra Ni neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why are my maturing cocoa pods turning black and hard while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni ewaa be mli ni mikɛkpeɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads quickly in damp, shaded environments. Pruning excess farm branches allows sunlight and airflow to dry out moisture on the cocoa pods.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni eha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ agbi.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up tightly and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛkpa shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies sucking plant sap and transmitting viral diseases. Spraying plants early with neem oil or soapy water keeps these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla shwieɔ tsei anɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why does my harvest drop every year when I plant maize on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously exhausts specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Alternating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns vital nutrients to the ground naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my plantain and cassava plants fail to grow well on certain parts of my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains kɛ mi-cassava lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ midumɔ he lɛ fãi komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Different crops require different soil and moisture conditions. Cassava and plantains prefer well-drained soil, so if your land holds too much water, their roots will struggle and rot, while water-loving crops like sugarcane will thrive there.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi biɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shihilɛi srɔtoi. Cassava kɛ plantains sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ to nu babaoo tsɔ. Eshishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛgboi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni sumɔɔ nu tamɔ ŋmei baakwɛ̃ yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: If my food crops like cassava keep failing on a piece of wet land, can I switch to growing sugarcane instead?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ miniyenii tsei, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ hu? Ani manyɛ matsake kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ nɔ moŋ?

english: Yes, switching to sugarcane is a great strategy if your land is naturally low-lying or marshy, as sugarcane loves wet conditions where cassava and plantains usually fail.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei tsakemɔ kɛmiiya ŋmei nɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kpakpa kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ ji ŋmei loo ŋmei kɛjɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei sumɔɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni bei pii lɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei shwieɔ shi yɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my land is better suited for sugarcane than for other regular crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmei fe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni afɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your land stays damp for long periods, receives plenty of sunlight, and causes underground tuber crops like cassava to rot, it is far better suited for sugarcane.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ Na hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni oha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmei lɛ agbo. Ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shɛ̃.

english: Why do cassava tubers rot in the ground when the land gets too wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When soil stays soaked in water, air is blocked, causing the tubers to suffocate and decay before you can harvest them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ lolo yɛ nu mli lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatsi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Will growing sugarcane on my land over time drain all the nutrients and ruin the soil?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baajie niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Sugarcane uses up a lot of soil nutrients as it grows. If you do not replenish the soil with manure or fertilizer, the soil will eventually lose its strength and produce smaller harvests.
ga: Sugarcane kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii beni edaa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, yɛ naagbee lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni ebaawo yibii babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its nutrients and can no longer support healthy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ efo mli ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ dɔŋŋ?

english: Signs of exhausted soil include plants with yellowish leaves, slow or stunted growth, thin stalks, very small harvest yields, and crops that get sick easily.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite lɛ he ji tsei ni baai yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo loo egbɔjɔ, tsei bibii, kpamɔ fioo ko pɛ. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela mɔɔ amɛ oya

english: What can I do to restore my land after crops have exhausted the nutrients in the soil?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mikɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba beni ŋmɔshi nibii efite niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You can restore your soil by applying animal manure or compost, using suitable fertilizers, planting leguminous crops like beans to feed the soil, or leaving the land to rest for a period.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha oshikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa atsu nii Dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. loo oshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe be fioo

english: How many years can a single sugarcane plant stay in the ground and keep producing harvests?
ga: Afii enyiɛ ŋmei kome baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Sugarcane is typically productive for about two to three years. After harvesting the first crop, new shoots grow back from the old roots for one or two more seasons before production drops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ aaafee afii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Beni akpa klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii heei baaya nɔ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shishifãi momo lɛ amli kɛyashi be kroko loo enyɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: What does it mean when someone says a crop like sugarcane has a duration of two to three years?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛɛ akɛ tso ko tamɔ sugar cane hiɔ shi afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: It means the plant will produce good yields from the same original planting for two to three years, after which the parent plants grow weak and you need to clear and replant fresh stems.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai kɛjɛ shishijee dumɔ mli afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Ni esa akɛ ofɔ tsei ahe ni odu tsei heei.

english: Can my family keep harvesting from the same sugarcane patch for many years without ever replanting?
ga: Ani miweku lɛ baanyɛ akpa sugar cane kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii babaoo ni amɛduuu ekoŋŋ?

english: No, you cannot harvest indefinitely from the same plants. After two to three years of harvests, the roots become old, yields drop significantly, and the stems become too thin, so fresh planting is required.
ga: Dabi, onyɛŋ okpa nii kɛjɛ tso kome mli kɛya naanɔ. Yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ sɛɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ daa, yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa. ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ egbɔjɔ tsɔ No hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow slower when I plant them on a steep hill compared to flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ daa blɛoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ kɛ akɛto hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away the fertile topsoil and fertilizers down the hill before crop roots can absorb them, leaving plants on slopes with fewer nutrients and less water.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ ahe lɛ kɛyaa dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ naaa niyenii kpakpai babaoo, ni nu hu faaa.

english: Why is it more expensive for me to clear and prepare hilly land before I can start planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejara wa waa akɛ abaajie gɔŋ ko he ko ni asaa he dani aje dumɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Hilly land requires extra labor or machinery to level the ground, remove large rocks, and build soil barriers to keep water from washing your seedbeds away.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni gɔji yɔɔ nɔ lɛ biɔ nitsumɔ krɛdɛɛ loo tsɔnei koni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Jiemɔ tɛi wuji lɛ kɛjɛ ohe. ni ofee shikpɔŋ nɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni baaha nu akafɔ odumɔwui ashishi.

english: What happens to my crops if I dig flat steps into my hillside land before planting?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mifo ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtee gɔŋ lɛ shishi dani midu?

english: Creating flat steps, known as terracing, traps rainwater, keeps fertilizers around the plant roots, and prevents your crops from being washed away during heavy storms.
ga: Atsɛ̃rɛ̃ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni afee Ale lɛ hu akɛ atsɛ̃rɛ̃. Ebaaye ebua ni akɛ nugbɔ nu ato. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii abɔle tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe ni otsi ŋmɔshinii lɛ anaa koni nu akaho yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli.

english: Which types of crops grow better on sloped land if I cannot afford to level the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ kɛji minyɛɛɛ mafee shikpɔŋ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Deep-rooted tree crops like cocoa, cashew, or oil palm do better on slopes because their strong roots anchor into the ground and help hold the soil together.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ tamɔ kookoo kɛ cashew loo mu tsei lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi ni wa lɛ fiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ he.

english: How does heavy rain affect my vegetables if my farm is located on a slope?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaná mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ?

english: Fast-moving rainwater flows down slopes quickly, which can strip away topsoil, expose young roots, and push tiny seedlings out of the ground.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ hoɔ oya kɛyaa gɔji lɛ anɔ. ni baanyɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ Ejieɔ shishifãi bibii akpo ni etsiɔ dumɔwui bibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does the soil at the top of my hill dry out faster than the soil at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sũ ni yɔɔ gɔji anɔ lɛ gbiɔ oya fe sũ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Gravity pulls water downward through the soil, causing moisture to drain quickly from the hilltop and gather at the valley floor, keeping lower land wet for longer.
ga: Nibii ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛbaa shi. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ ni ebua ehe naa yɛ jɔɔ lɛ shishi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it difficult to water my vegetable crops evenly when my farmland is on an incline?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ mawo mi tsei lɛ nu pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ etse lɛ?

english: Water naturally runs off toward the lowest point, meaning crops at the bottom will get flooded while crops at the top remain dry unless water flow is controlled.
ga: Nu baatsɔ adebɔɔ naa kɛya he ni eyɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu baaho ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kã he amɛgbi. ja akudɔ bɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ ehaa lɛ

english: Is it true that I cannot build a greenhouse on sloped land to grow my tomatoes?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ minyɛŋ mama ŋmɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ koni mikɛdu tomato?

english: Greenhouses require flat land so that irrigation water distributes evenly to every plant and the structure stays stable against heavy winds and storms.
ga: Greenhouses biɔ he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ aja mli pɛpɛɛpɛ aha tsei fɛɛ. Ni tsɔne lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ ahum ni tswaa lɛ mli.

english: Why do strong winds damage my crops more easily when they are planted on elevated land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ oya kɛ́ adu yɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ?

english: High and sloped ground is exposed to open air currents without natural windbreaks, making it easy for winds to snap plant stems, blow off leaves, or knock down tall crops.
ga: He ni nɔ kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ ji he ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli tse ni adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ hebuu ko bɛ he lɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baakumɔ tsei aniji, ebaatswa baai, loo eha tsei kakadaji lɛ agbee shi.

english: Does the direction my hillside faces affect how much crop yield I get?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni migɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, crops planted on the side of a hill that gets direct sunlight throughout the day will produce food faster than crops planted on the shaded side.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni adu yɛ gɔji anɔ ni hulu la kpɛɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ baawo niyenii oya fe tsei ni adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ.

english: Yellow lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant moves the limited nitrogen it has from older bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ko kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ dara shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baatoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when exposed to extreme heat or lack of water. The plant sacrifices its flowers to conserve water and energy so the main plant can survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ mli lɛ he. Tsei kɛ fɔfɔii shaa afɔle koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he bɔni afee ni tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop tiny, shriveled young pods before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ feɔ ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is often 'cherelle wilt,' a natural process where the cocoa tree sheds excess pods it cannot support with its available water and nutrients, though fungal diseases can also cause it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji ‘cherel wilt’, ni ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni haa kookoo tso lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwui ni fa fe nine ni nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai hu baanyɛ aha amɛba moŋ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce empty shells without any nuts inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni ŋmeii bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods, known as 'pops,' happen when the soil lacks calcium during pod development or when there is severe drought while the nuts are forming.
ga: Peanut pods ni bɛ nɔ ko, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ ‘pops’ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium yɛ pod lɛ shweremɔ be mli loo kɛji hɔmɔ ni naa wa ba be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miifee.

english: Why do cowpeas and beans grow well without adding nitrogen fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to pull nitrogen directly from the air, feeding themselves without needing added chemical nitrogen.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofa ni ji nitrogen afata he.

english: Why do the leaves and vines of my yam plants turn yellow and dry up after several months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ nyɔji komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally yellow and dry up when the plant finishes its life cycle. This signals that all energy has moved into the underground tuber and it is mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji tso lɛ gbe ewala shihilɛ naa. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ efã kɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi. ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ

english: During strong afternoon heat, tomato leaves lose water into the hot air faster than the roots can pull it up from the soil, causing temporary wilting to protect the plant from drying out.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni tso lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops even if my crops are taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɔ fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that steal water and fertilizers from the soil underneath, starving your crops of essential nutrients even if they look taller.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ oya ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa niyenii ni he hiaa ni oduɔ lɛ aná kɛji akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ babaoo po.

english: Why does a plantain sucker take over a year before it flowers and yields a bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afi dani plantain tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Plantain plants need 12 to 15 months to build a strong underground root network and grow enough big leaves to generate the energy required to support a heavy fruit bunch.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ he miihia nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 dani amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli wa. ni amɛkwɛ̃ baai ni dara bɔ ni sa ni baaha hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear away all the big shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. Keeping shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains creates a cool canopy that shields young cocoa from intense sun heat and keeps moisture in the air and soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be ni naa wa lɛ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: Yam plants use their leaves to catch sunlight and convert it into food stored in the underground tuber. When vines climb stakes, their leaves catch maximum sunlight and stay off the wet soil, preventing diseases and helping produce much larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛheɔ hulu la ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ wain tso lɛ kwɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ baaná hulu la fe fɛɛ ni amɛbaatsi amɛhe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ he. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii ni dara babaoo baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow in the shape of a 'V' and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ‘V’ su mli ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green and strong. The plant steals nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Tso lɛ juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do farmers say planting groundnuts or cowpeas together with my maize makes the soil better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which can pull nitrogen gas out of the air and store it in their roots. When these roots decompose in the soil, they release natural fertilizer that feeds nearby crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji shishifãi nɛɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my pepper crops with dry grass and dead leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egboi kɛ baai aha he ni mi-pepper tsei lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It stops the sun from drying out the soil, keeps the roots cool during hot afternoons, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot or when they lack water. High heat destroys the pollen inside the flower, so the plant sheds the flower to conserve energy until conditions improve.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu faaa yɛ amɛmli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ kpataa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and twisting like small baskets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe tamɔ tsɛnsii bibii lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves. As they suck the plant's juices, they inject saliva that makes the leaves grow deformed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. beni amɛmuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei amli lɛ Amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa baai lɛ fiteɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn watery and rot if heavy rains stay on the field too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When rain continuously floods the soil, water replaces all the air pockets, suffocating the roots and allowing rot-causing organisms to multiply rapidly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ tee nɔ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ Nu yeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ najiaŋ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ shwereɔ oya.

english: If you leave too many suckers growing around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same soil food and water. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong suckers, ensuring the main tree produces a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ, Plantain kome Amɛbaatswa niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ afee ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Why is it risky for me to sow my seeds right after the very first rainfall of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by several dry, hot weeks. If you plant immediately, the seeds might germinate, but the young roots will dry up and die in the hot soil before the main rainy season fully establishes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ otsii babaoo ni mli egbi ni edɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃. Shi shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ shi kwraa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps fix this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which naturally takes nitrogen from the air and puts it back into the soil, refreshing the land for future crops without needing as much commercial fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ehaa jɛmɛ feɔ fɛo kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo he ehiaaa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning yellow and green in patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems from the agricultural extension office stops the disease from taking over your field.
ga: Enɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi, ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ oodu ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akaye he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if fall armyworms are eating my young maize crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ fall armyworms miiye mibi lɛ ŋmãa?

english: Fall armyworms leave ragged, chewed holes in the maize leaves and leave powdery, sawdust-like droppings inside the central funnel of the plant. Checking early in the morning helps you catch them early.
ga: Fall armyworms lɛ shĩɔ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ ni amɛyeɔ yɛ ŋmãa baai amli ni amɛshiɔ ŋmãa ni tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ mli mra.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, dry spells, or attack by tiny pests like mirids. Keeping shade trees in your farm helps preserve soil moisture and protects the flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ba amɛnɔ. shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo tutuamɔi ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu fɔfɔi ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop producing fruits during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat forces pepper plants to drop their flowers to save water and protect themselves. Providing light shade and watering the soil regularly helps them keep their blossoms and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ nyɛɔ pepper tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe. Kɛ́ aha amɛ hulutsoo ni mli tse kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs water before the sun gets hot, allowing plants to drink without losing moisture to heat evaporation.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ dani hulu lɛ haa edɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nuɔ nu ni hulutsoo ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ sɛɛ efooo.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida yɛ kui bibii amli lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When plantain suckers are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows it to grow large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni etsɔ kuu agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds grow back so fast right after I clear my farm land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni mijie he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit dormant in the topsoil for a long time and quickly sprout as soon as clearing exposes them to rain and direct sunlight. Covering bare soil with organic mulch stops weed seeds from receiving light.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ehi shi. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ba enɔ pɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ organic mulch ha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ akaje kpo.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start rotting shortly after I store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised or cut during harvest or if they are stored in a hot, damp space. Handling them carefully and storing them in a dry, shady, and well-ventilated yam barn helps them last longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ loo afo amɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni okɛto he ko ni egbi, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce smaller ears when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ toi bibii yɔɔ mli beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded together, their leaves fight for sunlight and their roots fight for water and soil nutrients. Because the energy is shared among too many plants, each plant ends up producing smaller, weaker ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji abua ŋmãa tsei anaa yɛ kui amli lɛ Baai lɛ baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la. Shishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ajaa hewalɛ yɛ tsei babaoo ateŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tso fɛɛ tso woɔ ŋmãa toi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Is it better to give my cassava plants more space in the field or plant as many as possible?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ maha mi-cassava tso lɛ gbɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tso lɛ mli bɔ ni manyɛ?

english: Giving cassava plants proper space allows their roots room to expand fully underground. Overcrowding makes the plants compete for food, resulting in long, thin tubers instead of large, heavy roots.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli tsũi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kakadaji ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ shishifãi wuji ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Yam vines naturally search for height to catch direct sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch more light to make food, which leads to bigger yam tubers growing beneath the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei taoɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná la babaoo ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow long, thin stems but very few pods when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ shishifãi kakadaji ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ? Shi pods fioo pɛ yɔɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ tsei wuji ashishi.

english: Cowpeas need direct sunlight to bloom and form pods. In deep shade, the plant wastes its energy stretching upward to search for light instead of using that energy to grow flowers and beans.
ga: Cowpeas he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekwɛ fɔfɔi ni efee pods. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, tsei fiteɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni amɛkpãa kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛtao la lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, moo ngɔ jamɛ a he wami ɔ kɛ du fɔfɔi kɛ ngma.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they suffer from high heat or a lack of water. The plant sheds the flowers to conserve its moisture and energy until growing conditions get better.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ hewɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my plantain tree give me small bunches when I let all the shoot suckers grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni mihaa ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ he lɛ?

english: The extra suckers act like extra mouths to feed, stealing water and food from the main mother plant. Removing excess suckers leaves more energy for the main plant to build a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tsoi krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ krokomɛi ni akɛhaa niyenii. Kɛtsɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni ejuɔ kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my garden egg plants get dense leaves and rot quickly during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baai lɛ mli edɔ ni egboɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When garden egg plants grow too thick and close together, air cannot flow between the branches. Moisture stays trapped on the leaves and stems, which allows fungal diseases to grow and rot the fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ eggplants ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ dara tsɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ateŋ. Fɛ̃i kpɛtɛɔ baai kɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ daa ni egboɔ.

english: Why do my okra plants stop forming new pods after a short time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-okra lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔtɔ heei feemɔ yɛ be kukuoo ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If older okra pods are left to ripen and turn hard on the plant, the plant thinks its life cycle is complete. Harvesting pods regularly while they are still young encourages the plant to keep producing new flowers and fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi okra ŋmeii momoi lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ susuɔ akɛ eshihilɛ be lɛ egbe naa. Kɛ́ okpa tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ daa be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni eya nɔ ewo fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai heei.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants turn yellow after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away important soil nutrients like nitrogen, or waterlog the soil so roots cannot breathe. When the roots cannot absorb food, the lower leaves lose their green color and turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hia yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu baanyɛ afɔ sũ lɛ mli ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ hu baafite amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my young cocoa seedlings grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight before your young cocoa seedlings can reach them, keeping the cocoa weak and starved.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la dani kookoo tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshɛɔ he. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, Cocoa bɛ hewalɛ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away nitrogen—the essential nutrient that keeps leaves green and healthy—deeper into the soil where roots cannot reach it. Excess water also fills up air spaces in the soil, preventing roots from breathing.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa. Nɔ ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe wa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hu eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu

english: Is it safe for me to use water directly from the local river to water my vegetables during the dry season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli faa lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii tɛ̃ɛ koni mikɛwo aduawai anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Natural river water is usually great for crops because it naturally contains tiny aquatic organisms like algae and organic nutrients that help plants grow, as long as the water is clean and free from chemical pollution.
ga: Nu ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli faai amli lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ejaakɛ nu mli nibii bibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ yɛ mli. Shii abɔ ni nu lɛ mli tse ni tsofai fɔji bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass, or mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It blocks direct sunlight from drying out the earth, keeps the soil cool, and helps hold moisture longer so your plants do not wilt quickly.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi loo mulch tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ No hewɔ lɛ otsei lɛ akagbo oya tamɔ bɔ ni eji lɛ.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when they experience stress, usually caused by extremely hot temperatures or inconsistent watering, which causes the plant to protect itself rather than expend energy making fruit.
ga: Tomato baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ ekɛ haomɔ kpe. Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni eyaaa nɔ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during strong winds before the fruit matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani eyibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches at the top. Because they are top-heavy, supporting them with strong wooden props or stakes helps keep them upright until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwu lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋwɛi. Ejaakɛ eyɛ muji babaoo Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli loo tsei ni wa fi esɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi shiŋŋ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my crops as soon as they appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji amɛje kpo pɛ?

english: Weeds act like competitors on your farm. They steal the soil nutrients, sunlight, and ground moisture that your main crops need to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akaŋshilɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nu ni he hiaa otsei titrii lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why should I avoid planting cassava on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ he?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating crops gives the soil time to recover and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe ni efoɔ helai ni baa lɛ amli.

english: What is causing the leaves on my cassava plants to curl up and develop yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Curled and yellowing leaves on cassava are typically caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a viral infection carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny insects called whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca mosaic hela lɛ kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ tso mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wither and die quickly when water accumulates around their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ oya kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Standing water around roots suffocates them and creates ideal conditions for fungal diseases that cause root rot, preventing the plant from taking up food and water.
ga: nu ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaye niyenii kɛ nu.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that cannot handle full, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates living umbrellas that shelter young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle sunlight.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa kookoo bibioo lɛ he feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ enáa hulu la.

english: What is eating holes in the leaves of my young maize crop and hiding inside the stalk?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni ayeɔ yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni akɛteɔ shi awoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves (the whorl) during the day to feed on soft growth, requiring early farm checking and targeted spraying before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli (whorls) yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye gbekɛbii bibii ni daraa lɛ. Esa akɛ akwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ awo mli dani ofite tip ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and stopping the plant from bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekawo yibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips that suck the sap and spread a virus. Controlling these tiny insects early with neem oil or appropriate insecticide stops the curl from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni yɔɔ pepper tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ŋmeii bibii ahe nitsumɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Kɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii. Enɛ baatsi tsitsii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn dark and rot before they get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani edara lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering and a lack of calcium in the growing fruit. When soil water goes up and down, the plant cannot move calcium from the soil into the fruit effectively.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni bɛ tso yibii ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsake lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛya aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with many leaves but gives me very thin tubers when I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ, shi kɛ́ atsa lɛ, eyɛ ŋmei ni mli tse waa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava put all its growth energy into stems and green leaves instead of root storage. Avoiding nitrogen-heavy fertilizers late in the season encourages the plant to direct food down into the tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni haa edara lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛ́ otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ niyenii amaje ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight without protection. Keeping tall trees or planting plantains nearby provides light shade and keeps moisture in the soil so the tender leaves do not burn.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ kɛji abuuu amɛhe. Tsei kakadaji ni aduɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Enɛ baaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha sũ lɛ mli ahi shi koni baai bibii lɛ akashã.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with tall wooden poles after they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji afi sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ beni edara sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high into the sunlight so their leaves can make food. Catching maximum light gives the plant the energy it needs to grow large, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Hulu la ni akɛwoɔ mli koni ebaai lɛ afee niyenii. La ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily whenever a strong rainfall comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots stay close to the top of the soil. If planted too shallowly or in overcrowded conditions, their shallow roots cannot anchor the heavy tree against strong wind and soaked ground.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo yɛ hei ni mɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ Shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ nyɛŋ amɔ tso ni tsii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow weak even though I put fertilizer on the farm during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water for plant roots to drink it. Applying dry fertilizer on dry soil means the crop cannot absorb the nutrients, and concentrated dry fertilizer can actually burn the plant roots.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli koni tso shishifãi lɛ anu nu. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm make the soil better for maize next season?
ga: Te ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth. When the plants die, that stored nitrogen acts as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ tsinabii yɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nitrogen ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my lowland rice turn yellow and stop growing when the mud in the field dries out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa shweremɔ kɛ́ muji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: Lowland rice requires standing water or very moist mud to freely drink key nutrients like nitrogen and iron. When the soil hardens and dries out, the roots lose access to those nutrients and the leaves lose their green color.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi loo sũ ni mli edɔ babaoo he miihia ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ koni enyɛ enu niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ iron lɛ ehe. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbi lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛná nakai niyenii lɛ. ni baai lɛ baafite amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in a clear, open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse, ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and intense heat. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides shade and preserves soil moisture, protecting the young seedlings until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Nurse tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko. Buu dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara waa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen feeds green leaf growth; when it runs out, the plant moves nutrients from older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa baai eŋɔli lɛ daalɛ niyenii. Kɛji akɛ efo mli lɛ, tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have roots that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the farm for leafy crops like maize that will be planted next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni abaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Should I apply my fertilizer on top of dry soil, or is it better to wait after rain has fallen?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is always best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a rain. Dry soil cannot break down the fertilizer for roots to absorb, and concentrated chemical fertilizer on dry roots can burn and damage the plant.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nyɛŋ agbala ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ. Ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi ni egbi lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei.

english: How do I know which way to stick my cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole bɔ ni aduɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Check the growth nodes (the small bumps where leaves used to grow) along the stem cutting; they should point upward toward the sky. Planting stems upside down forces the plant to waste energy growing stems downward first, leading to weak tubers.
ga: Kwɛmɔ dalɛ hei (ŋmeii bibii ni baa lɛ da yɛ be ko ni eho lɛ) yɛ tso lɛ shishifomɔ gbɛ lɛ he. Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Tso lɛ shishifã lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ ni ekwɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: Why do I need to clear the ground and put tall stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie he ko ni mikɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to manufacture food that goes down into building large tubers. Staking lifts leaves off the ground where they can catch sunlight better and avoids soil-borne fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bulbs wuji lɛ. Ajieɔ staking elevator lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni baanyɛ aná hulu la jogbaŋŋ ni ekwa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds closer together, won't I get a larger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too closely causes plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This competition leaves you with thin, weak stalks and tiny corn cobs, while proper spacing allows each plant to yield large cobs.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso akwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I prune or cut away extra shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo loo majie tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main plant. Pruning away unwanted suckers ensures the parent plant concentrates all its energy into producing one heavy, large bunch of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni ataooo lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei wuji ni tsii.
