english: Tomato flowers drop when the crop is stressed by extreme heat or inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the flowers stay attached long enough to form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking leaf juices, or by viral diseases spread by these pests. Controlling insect populations early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kooloi ayibɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I bought fail to sprout after I plant them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui komɛi ni miheɔ lɛ kwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds are living things that need proper moisture and warmth to wake up. If seeds are old, damaged by heat, or stored improperly before planting, they lose their life strength and will not germinate even when you water them.
ga: Dumɔwui ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni ehe hiaa hulutsoo kɛ dɔlɛ ni sa koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji latsaa fite dumɔwui momoi, loo akɛto he jogbaŋŋ dani adu lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ baaje mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ŋ kɛji okɛ nu wo amɛnɔ po.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my crops when the rains keep changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Planting in dry soil burns seeds, while planting in flooded soil suffocates them. The best time to plant is right after the soil gets its first deep soak of rain that keeps the ground moist for at least three consecutive days.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ ashã. yɛ be mli ni dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha mɔ agbɔjɔ. Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu nii ji beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ hoo lɛ, enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i gbii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can I save seeds from my current harvest to plant next season, or will the crop grow differently?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ bianɛ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli? Aloo ŋmɔshi nibii baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ?

english: Many modern high-yielding seeds are bred to give a great harvest only once. If you save and replant those seeds, the second generation often produces weaker plants, smaller fruits, and succumbs to diseases much faster.
ga: Atsɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui babaoo ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpa kome pɛ. Kɛji obua nakai dumɔwui lɛ anaa ni odu lɛ Bei pii lɛ, yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ woɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ. aduawai bibii ni hela mɔɔ amɛ oya kwraa

english: Crops compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. When planted too close, they stretch upward to fight for sunlight instead of spending energy to build strong stems and large, full cobs.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ebaakpã ehe koni ekɛ hulu la lɛ akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, e kɛ he wami tsuɔ ní kɛ peeɔ tso nɛ mi wa kɛ tso nguahi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a cry for help indicating the plant is hungry for nitrogen or its roots are drowning in waterlogged soil. Without air and food in the soil, the plant cannot produce the green color needed to make its energy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji haomɔ he okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen loo akɛ eshishifãi lɛ efo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee su ni ji eŋɔli ni he hiaa koni akɛfee hewalɛ.

english: If I apply extra fertilizer to my crops, will it make them grow twice as fast?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Ani ebaaha tsei lɛ adara oya fe shii enyɔ?

english: Too much fertilizer acts like salt on plant roots, burning them and preventing the crop from taking up water. Excessive fertilizer can stunt your crops, cause leaves to burn brown, or kill the plant entirely.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso mli babaoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋoo yɛ tsei shishifãi anɔ. Eshãa tsei ashishifãi ni ehaaa tsei lɛ aŋɔ nu. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee shoo. Ehaa baai lɛ shãa ŋmɔtɔ. loo eha tso lɛ agbo kwraa.

english: Tomatoes continue to breathe and age after being picked. High temperatures during transport and rough handling create tiny bruised spots where bacteria and fungi enter, causing the fruit to soften and rot rapidly.
ga: Tomato yaa nɔ emuɔ ni egbɔɔ beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ. Dɔlɛ ni mli wa yɛ gbɛfaa mli kɛ nitsumɔ ni mli wa Ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe bibioo. ni bacteria kɛ fungi boteɔ mli Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: Why do my crops look very healthy on the farm, but go soft and lose quality a day after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Shi efeɔ blɛoo ni ehiɛ kpaa nɔ gbi kome yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If crops absorb too much water right before harvest or lack essential minerals like calcium, their cell walls remain weak. Once picked, exposure to sun and hot air causes them to collapse and lose firmness fast.
ga: Kɛji tso ko shwie nu babaoo dani akpa loo ebɛ minerals ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium lɛ, tso lɛ mli wala yibii lɛ baafee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛto he ko, ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha efo ni ehiɛ aka shi oya.

english: Why do tiny insects destroy my stored dry maize inside the room even when the door is closed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ ŋmãa ni egbi ni ato yɛ mitsu lɛ mli lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ agbe shinaa lɛ naa moŋ?

english: Insects like weevils often lay tiny, invisible eggs inside the grain while it is still growing in the field. When you bring the grain indoors, the warm room causes those eggs to hatch into bugs that eat the grain from the inside out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ wɔji bibii. Anaaa yɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mli beni eyaa nɔ edaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ okɛ dumɔwui ba shĩa lɛ mli Tsu ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha nakai ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to turn hard and woody if I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Cassava roots reach a point of maturity where they stop storing good starch and begin turning that energy into tough, woody fibers. Leaving them past their maturity time in wet ground also attracts soil fungi that rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ lɛ, he ni amɛkpaa ŋmei kpakpa ni amɛhiɛɔ lɛ. ni ebɔi nakai hewalɛ lɛ tsakemɔ ewo tso mli tsɔi ni wa mli Kɛ́ ashi amɛ koni amɛdara yɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni egbalaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains rot so quickly when I store them after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛto beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvested maize rots quickly if it is not dried completely before storage. Trapped moisture allows mold and bacteria to grow rapidly, which spoils the grain and makes it unsafe to eat or sell.
ga: Abele ni akpa lɛ baafite oya kɛji akɛ agbiko lɛ kwraa dani akɛto. Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ daa oya. Enɛ baafite ŋmãa lɛ ni ebaaha efee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ loo ahɔ̃ɔɔ.

english: What will happen if my crop seeds get wet before I plant them in the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ dani midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If seeds get wet before planting, they absorb the water and can either spoil, grow mold, or start germinating too early in storage, which ruins their ability to grow into healthy plants later.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ mli edɔ dani adu lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baaŋɔ nu ni ebaanyɛ egbo. kwɛ̃ɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmei loo ebɔi shweremɔ oya tsɔ yɛ nitoohe Enɛ baafite amɛnyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛbaatsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does cocoa bean quality drop if rain falls on them while they are drying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miigbi lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ baa shi lɛ?

english: Rainwater adds moisture back into drying cocoa beans, which causes mold to grow inside the beans. This ruins the chocolate flavor and reduces the price buyers will pay for them.
ga: Nugbɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa ekoŋŋ kɛyaa bɔ ni agbiɔ kookoo lɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Enɛ fiteɔ tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ ni ehaa jara ni esa akɛ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ awo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my stored groundnuts attract insects and go bad so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Insects thrive in warm, damp conditions. If groundnuts are stored with moisture inside the bag, pests will multiply rapidly and eat the nuts. Drying them thoroughly before bagging keeps pests away.
ga: Koolooi yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i mli. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ to kotoku lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baafa oya ni amɛye ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbi amɛ dani okɛwo kotoku mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akabote mli.

english: Why do I need to mix liquid fertilizer into water before applying it to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii futuɔ nu mli dani mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Mixing liquid fertilizer with water dilutes the strong nutrients so the crop's roots and leaves can absorb them safely without getting burned or damaged by concentrated chemicals.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni akɛfutu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afee mlɛo. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli shweshweeshwe ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ akashã amɛ loo amɛkafite amɛ.

english: Why is it important to use the exact amount of water recommended when mixing pest medicine for my vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ atsu nii kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai miifutu mi-aduawai lɛ?

english: Using too little water makes the medicine too strong and damages your crop, while using too much water dilutes it so much that it fails to kill the pests harming your plants.
ga: Nu fioo pɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaha tsofa lɛ mli awa tsɔ ni ebaafite oŋmɔshi nibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ nu babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsofa lɛ mli agbɔjɔ waa bɔ ni egbeee tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa otsei lɛ.

english: Can my crops absorb plant food if I spray it directly on their leaves with water?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ tsei amli niyenii? Ni kɛji akɛ mikɛ nu shwie baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ hu?

english: Yes, plants have tiny pores on their leaves that can quickly absorb liquid nutrients mixed with water, giving the crop a fast boost if the soil is weak.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei yɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni ji nu ni akɛ nu efutu mli lɛ oya. Enɛ haa tsei kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waaa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and wilt when water sits on my farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Too much standing water suffocates the plant roots, preventing them from taking up air and nutrients from the soil, which makes the leaves turn yellow from lack of proper feeding.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Etsiɔ enaa koni ekaná kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii kpakpa ni ahaaa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings collapse and die after I give them too much water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ nu babaoo ha amɛ lɛ?

english: Overwatering creates a damp environment near the stem base where microscopic soil fungi grow and attack the young plant stem, causing it to rot and fall over.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa ni bɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Biɛ ji he ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ daa ni amɛtutuaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. ni haa egboɔ ni egbeeɔ shi

english: How can I tell if the dry fertilizer I bought from the market has spoiled before I use it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ efite dani mikɛtsu nii?

english: If dry fertilizer gets wet or exposed to moisture in the store, it forms hard lumps or turns soggy, which means its nutrients have degraded and it will not dissolve or spread evenly on your farm.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ kpe lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee ŋmɔtɔ ni wa loo ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli nibii lɛ baafite ni amɛshwieŋ loo amɛjaŋ amɛhe pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops need added fertilizer when there is already natural soil in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔji lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ momo lɛ?

english: Just like people need balanced food to grow strong, soil loses its natural nutrients over time as crops grow and absorb them. Fertilizer supplies essential plant food like nitrogen and phosphorus that soil alone can no longer provide in high enough amounts.
ga: Taakɛ niyenii ni ja he hiaa gbɔmɛi koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛheɔ amɛ lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. ni shikpɔŋ pɛ nyɛŋ aha yɛ falɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa mli dɔŋŋ lɛ

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your crop is running out of nitrogen. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant starves its older bottom leaves to send remaining nutrients to keep the young top leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ koni ekɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ aha koni eha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ aya nɔ ada.

english: Can using animal manure feed my cocoa plants the same way factory-made fertilizer does?
ga: Ani kooloi ashishifã baanyɛ aha mi cacao tsei lɛ niyenii yɛ gbɛ ni tamɔ nɔ ni akɛhaa nitsumɔhei ashishifãi lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, animal manure feeds plants by releasing nutrients slowly over time while also improving the soil's ability to hold water, whereas factory-made fertilizer releases nutrients quickly directly to the plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii haa tsei niyenii kɛtsɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ejieɔ lɛ fiofio lɛ nɔ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni afeɔ yɛ nitsumɔhei lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii oya kɛyaa tsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to sprout even after I plant them in wet soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Seeds need energy stored inside them as well as air and water to wake up. If a seed is old, damaged by insects, or planted too deep, it runs out of stored energy before it can push through the soil surface.
ga: Hewalɛ ni ato yɛ amɛmli lɛ he miihia dumɔwui. Nakai eji yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɛlɛtswaa mli lɛ hu he. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ ni kooloi bibii efite amɛ loo adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ Hewalɛ ni ato lɛ baaho dani abaanyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or a sudden lack of water. Under stress, the plant drops its flowers to save water and energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ trukaa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. yɛ haomɔ shishi Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do my cowpea plants look sick and stop growing after rain floods the field for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When floodwater fills all the small spaces in the soil, the roots drown and cannot absorb the nutrients needed to keep the plant growing.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu afua lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ bibioo ko mli obɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii ni he hiaa koni tsei lɛ ada lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall and skinny with tiny roots when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa, eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight and soil food. The plants stretch up tall to fight for light instead of using their energy to grow big tuberous roots.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛkɛ la akaŋ moŋ fe ni amɛaafite hewalɛ ni amɛkɛda shishifãi wuji.

english: How do weeds hurt my pepper crop even if I water the field regularly?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ?

english: Weeds act like unwanted guests that steal nutrients, water, and sunlight directly from your pepper plants, leaving less food available for your crop to produce fruits.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbɔi ni ataooo amɛ, ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ o-pepper tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ faaa koni ewo yibii.

english: Why should I cut away extra shoots from my plantain tree instead of leaving them all to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ dumɔwu ko mli ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ moŋ fe ni maŋmɛ gbɛ ni eda kwraa?

english: Leaving too many shoots forces the mother plantain tree to share its nutrients with all its young suckers. Removing extra suckers directs all the food energy to one main stem, giving you a much larger bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwu nyɛ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ agba niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Nibii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ kudɔɔ niyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tso titri kome nɔ. Ehaa onine shɛɔ plantains babaoo nɔ.

english: Maize consumes the same specific nutrients from the soil every season. Planting maize repeatedly drains those exact nutrients and allows soil pests to multiply, whereas changing to crops like groundnuts restores soil fertility.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii daa be. Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ nakai niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei tsakemɔ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is needed for healthy green leaves, so when it is missing, the plant takes whatever nitrogen is left from older bottom leaves and sends it to new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ elaaje Tso lɛ baajie nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli ni ekɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know which direction to plant cassava cuttings into the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole gbɛ ni esa akɛ odu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Look closely at the small leaf nodes or 'eyes' along the stick. These small buds should always point upwards toward the sky so the plant grows strong roots down and leafy shoots up.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ loo ‘ŋmɔji’ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be koni eha tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get enough water during flowering. Poor pollination by insects or wind can also cause unpollinated flowers to drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ shwieee fɔfɔi lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha fɔfɔi ni shwieee fɔfɔi lɛ agbee shi.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer right before a heavy rain storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ ashwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani ahum baatswa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall will wash away the fertilizer before your crops can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a mild rain so the roots can soak up the nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the ground where they can catch maximum sunlight and stay safe from rot and pests.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ lɛ, ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe.

english: How does spraying water boiled with neem leaves protect my vegetables?
ga: Te neem tso mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu mi-aduawai lɛ ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Neem leaves contain natural bitter compounds that insects hate. When sprayed on crops, it stops insects from eating the leaves and disrupts their breeding without using expensive chemical pesticides.
ga: Nɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni kooloi nyɛɔ lɛ yɛ neem baai lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashwie tsei anɔ lɛ Enɛ baatsi kooloi bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ni ebaatsi amɛnaa ni amɛkabote gbalashihilɛ mli ni tsofai ni jara wa ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why is it bad to grow maize on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing maize on the same spot every season drains the same nutrients from the soil over and over. It also allows pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply in the dirt.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ hu feɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does rice grow so well in flooded water while other crops rot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu afua mli shi ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fiteɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air tubes in their stems that bring oxygen down to their roots underwater. Flooding also suffocates weeds while keeping the rice continuously hydrated.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi lɛ. Nu afua hu haa jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding underneath, sucking the sap out of young leaves. It can also be a virus spread by tiny whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛtsɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ni enuɔ lɛ nɔ Ebaanyɛ efee hela ko hu ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why is it important for me to clear all the weeds from under my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie jwɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your cocoa trees. Clearing them down to the ground ensures that your cocoa roots get all the food they need to grow strong and produce healthy pods.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hia, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei amli. Kɛ́ ojie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa o-cocoa shishifãi lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Is it safe for my soil and crops if I weed my cocoa farm while it is raining?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha mishikpɔŋ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji mijie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni nugbɔ miinɛ?

english: Clearing weeds in light rain is fine, but completely clearing ground down to the bare soil during heavy downpours can cause rainwater to wash away fertile topsoil. It is best to leave a light cover or mulch to protect the soil from heavy raindrops.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Shi shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha nugbɔ nu lɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Should I carry cut weeds off the farm or leave them on the ground under the cocoa trees?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo jwɛi ni afo lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo mashi amɛ yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi?

english: Leaving the cleared weeds on the ground acts as mulch. As the weeds rot, they return rich nutrients back to the soil and help keep the cocoa roots cool and moist during dry periods.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ fite lɛ Amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa niyenii ni jara wa lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: How many farm hands do I usually need to clear one acre of cocoa farm efficiently?
ga: Okwaafoi aniji enyiɛ he miihia mi koni manyɛ mafo ŋmɔ ni dalɛ ji acre kome mli lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ?

english: For a standard one-acre cocoa farm, a group of about 5 to 10 workers can clear and weed the land effectively in a single day without overworking the soil or leaving the task unfinished.
ga: Kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ ko ni dalɛ ji acre 1 ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ, nitsulɔi akuu ko ni feɔ mɛi aaafee 5 kɛyashi 10 baanyɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛjie jwɛi yɛ gbi kome mli ni amɛtsuuu nii fe nine loo amɛshiŋ nitsumɔ lɛ ni amɛgbeee naa.

english: Can women perform the same cocoa farming tasks as men, or are some tasks strictly for men?
ga: Ani yei baanyɛ atsu nii yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli tamɔ bɔ ni hii tsuɔ nii yɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ? Aloo ani nitsumɔi komɛi yɛ ni ato aha hii pɔtɛɛ?

english: Women can perform almost all cocoa farming activities effectively. While heavy forest clearing is often done by men, women excel in critical tasks like planting, weeding, harvesting, and pod breaking, which require careful handling.
ga: Yei baanyɛ atsu nɔ ni miihe ashɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ hii shwieɔ koo lɛ mli waa moŋ Shi yei hu he esa yɛ nitsumɔi ni he hiaa tamɔ dumɔwui, jwɛi shwiemɔ, ŋmaakpamɔ, kɛ ŋmeii ni akumɔ, ni biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli.

english: Will using sharp cutlasses near the base of my cocoa trees harm them?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ akɛ kakla ni naa wa baatsu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo tso shishi?

english: Yes, if a cutlass accidentally wounds the trunk of a cocoa tree, it leaves an open cut where pests and fungal diseases can enter. You must weed very carefully around the stem base to avoid scraping the bark.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ tsɔne lɛ pila kookoo tso lɛ shishi yɛ oshara mli. Ebaashi he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ abote mli. Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Okɛ hiɛdɔɔ afɔ tso lɛ shishi koni akafolɔ tso lɛ yibii lɛ.

english: Why do most farmers go to work on the cocoa farm early in the morning around seven o'clock?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo yaa nitsumɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji amli leebi maŋkpa, aaafee leebi ŋmɛji kpawo lɛ?

english: Starting early allows you to complete heavy field labor before the heat of the afternoon sun sets in. It also lets you inspect wet leaves under morning dew, making it easier to spot early signs of pests and diseases.
ga: Kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ haa ogbeɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ ni wa naa dani shwane hulu lɛ tswaa. Ehaa okwɛɔ baai ni efɔ yɛ leebi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shishi lɛ hu. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaana tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahe okadii mra.

english: While cocoa needs good rainfall to grow, excessive heavy rain during the flowering stage can knock delicate flowers off the branches or encourage fungal diseases like black pod, preventing the flowers from turning into pods.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ kpakpa he miihia cocoa koni ekwɛ̃ moŋ, Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa fe nine yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbo kɛjɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ loo ewo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji, ni tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe hewalɛ.

english: How long after planting my young cocoa seedlings should I expect them to start bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ baabɔi yibiiwoo yɛ adumɔ sɛɛ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start flowering and producing pods within 2 to 3 years, whereas older traditional varieties can take 4 to 5 years under good weeding and shade management.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfee tsofai lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5 yɛ jwɛi kɛ hulutsoo nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees seem to suffer when there are no bigger shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa from sun damage and keeps the soil humid for proper growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa seedlings need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do experienced farmers cover the soil around their crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, called mulching, keeps the ground cool, retains soil moisture during dry spells, stops weeds from growing, and adds nutrients to the soil as the grass rotted over time.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he be mli ni jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni ehoɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do I have to tie my yam vines to tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce large tubers. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so the leaves get full sunlight while keeping them off damp soil where they might rot or catch diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo bulbs wuji. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ fɛɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ wain tso lɛ naa koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ yɛ he ni ebaanyɛ egbo loo hela aba enɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves in young maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or waterlogged roots. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How can I tell when my cassava is ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready for harvest when the bottom leaves yellow and drop off, and the soil at the base of the stem begins to crack due to the swelling tubers beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ ashishi feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ yɛ ŋmei ni efuu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ hewɔ.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in the shoots of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni miiye buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ yiteŋ lɛ?

english: Small holes in maize leaves and shoots are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the central leaf funnel. Applying recommended insecticides or neem water early in the morning can control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ baa lɛ teŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ baai kɛ yiteŋ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye nɔ.

english: Tomato leaf curling is commonly caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies, or by extreme heat and lack of regular water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high, when water is inconsistent, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer promoting leaf growth over fruit growth.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa Aloo be mli ni nitrogen ni yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ fa babaoo.

english: Cutting extra shoots leaves only 2 or 3 strong stems per plantain stand, preventing them from competing for soil nutrients and water so the main tree produces larger bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, eshiɔ tsei 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ dumɔwu kome mli. Etsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ he akaŋshii. No hewɔ lɛ, tso titri lɛ feɔ kuu ko ni da fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry hot spell that can dry out the soil and kill freshly germinated seeds. It is safer to wait until the major rains become steady before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be ni baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ aba shi dani odu.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing lots of green leaves but the roots inside the soil are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava plants build leaves first to capture sunlight before putting energy into swelling their roots. If the soil has too much nitrogen or if you harvest too early, the plant keeps making leaves instead of tubers, so it needs time and balanced soil nutrients to direct energy underground.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ feɔ baai klɛŋklɛŋ koni ekɛmɔ hulu la dani ekɛ hewalɛ lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo eshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ eshɛ mra tsɔ Tso lɛ baaya nɔ ewo baai yɛ bulbs najiaŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, eheɔ be kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja dani anyɛ atsu shikpɔŋ shishi hewalɛ he nii.

english: Why do my maize crops turn yellow and grow thin when I plant seeds close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Giving each seed proper space allows every plant to get enough nutrients to grow thick stalks and produce full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni ewo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: How can I tell if my pepper plants are dying from too much rain or from not getting enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ miigbo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ hewɔ?

english: Plants lacking water will look dry, limp, and crispy, usually during the dry heat of the day. Plants getting too much water will turn yellow and droop even when the soil is wet, because drowned roots rot and cannot breathe.
ga: Tsei ni nu efo mli lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni egbi, egbɔjɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, bei pii lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ. Tsei ni nu babaoo baa amɛnɔ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbee shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaagbɔjɔ.

english: Why do caterpillars destroy my crop leaves much faster right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai mra yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The rain causes crops to sprout soft, fresh young leaves, which attract insects to lay eggs. Checking leaves early and picking caterpillars off bit by bit prevents them from multiplying and eating the farm down.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii kwɛ̃ɔ. ni gbalaa kooloi kɛbaa koni amɛwo amɛ ŋmeii lɛ Akwɛ baai lɛ amli mra Ni abua ŋmeii lɛ anaa fiofio lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafee babaoo ni amɛye nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my land yield less food each year even though I work hard and plant the same way every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ lɛ faaa daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nii waa ni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi moŋ?

english: Crops pull food out of the soil every time they grow. If you harvest continuously without adding plant food back through manure, compost, or fertilizer, the soil becomes tired and empty over time.
ga: Tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni adu amɛ. Kɛji okpaa nii be fɛɛ be ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii wooo tsei aniyenii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ni ebaafee shwɛm yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my young cocoa trees dry up and fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by too much harsh sunlight, lack of shade, or dry weather. As the tree grows stronger roots and gets proper shade from companion plants like plantains, it will keep its flowers and turn them into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulu la babaoo, hulutsoo bɛ, loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi. Kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli wa ni enine shɛɔ hulutsoo ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni fata ehe, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ lɛ, ebaahiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni efee ŋmeii.

english: Should I leave weeds around my crops to keep the soil shaded, or will they hurt the plants?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi jwɛi komɛi yɛ jɛmɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ koni akɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo akɛfeee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ani ebaaye tsei lɛ awui?

english: Even though weeds cover the ground, they steal essential water, fertilizer, and light directly from your crops. Clearing weeds regularly around the base of your plants lets your crops get all the food they need to grow well.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ jwɛi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ, shi amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ Tsoi akutsei ni atswaa daa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young vegetable seeds sprout nicely at first but then suddenly fall over and die after a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ daa yɛ shishijee mli, shi trukaa lɛ amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: This usually happens because of a dampness disease called 'damping-off', caused by keeping the nursery soil too wet and shaded. Giving young sprouts good air circulation and light watering prevents their tiny stems from rotting at the ground level.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ dampness hela lɛ hewɔ ni enɛ baa lɛ. ‘Damping’, ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ hulutsoo lɛ mli baa Kɛji akɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ nu fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Kaaha egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my tomato plants if I want to harvest more tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-tomato tso lɛ he lɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni makpa tomato babaoo?

english: Tomato plants spend a lot of energy feeding green leafy side branches that don't produce good fruit. Pruning off these extra shoots forces the plant to send all its energy into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛhaa tsei niji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli, ni enɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my yams so they don't spoil under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii? Koni ekafite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yams tell you they are ready when the above-ground leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up. This shows that the plant has finished storing all its food down in the underground tuber and is ready to be dug out.
ga: Sweet potato kɛɛ bo akɛ efee klalo beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe eniyenii fɛɛ ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa, ni efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ lɛ.

english: What is the difference between hybrid seeds and the local seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome kɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred by combining two strong plant varieties to produce bigger yields and resist diseases better than traditional seeds, though you need to buy fresh hybrid seeds each planting season for best results.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ kɛtsɔ tsei enyɔ ni wa ni akɛaafee ekome lɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ehe baahia ni ohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ koni onine ashɛ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ nɔ moŋ.

english: Do hybrid crops require more water to survive than local crop varieties?
ga: Ani tsei ni akɛfee tsofa kroko lɛ he miihia nu babaoo koni amɛhi shi fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Because hybrid crops grow much faster and produce larger leaves and bigger fruits, they require reliable moisture, especially during their early growth stage, to reach their full harvest potential.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai kɛ aduawai wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, hulutsoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ he miihia amɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ shishijee fãi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli bɔni afee ni anyɛ ashɛ nibii ni afeɔ lɛ fɛɛ he

english: Why is it important for me to wait until the rains are well established before planting my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Seeds need steady moisture to sprout and grow strong roots; planting too early during unreliable light rains can cause seeds to dry out and die in the hot soil before fully germinating.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni yɔɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli Dumɔwui ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: What will happen to my crops if I miss the main rainy season and plant late in the year?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mifo nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli ni midu yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ?

english: Late-planted crops may run out of water while trying to form grains or fruit when the dry season arrives early, leading to stunted growth and poor yields.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ nu baanyɛ afite yɛ be mli ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛfee dumɔwui loo aduawai beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shɛɔ mra lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: How does knowing the exact measurements of my farm land help me plant better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ dalɛ pɔtɛɛ ni mile lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi koni mida jogbaŋŋ?

english: Knowing the size of your land helps you buy the exact amount of seeds, fertilizer, and spray you need, preventing you from wasting money or under-feeding your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ ole bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ da ha lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ohé dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ abɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Etsiɔ bo gbɛ koni okafite shika loo okaha oŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together to fit more crops onto my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and small yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: How can I keep water in the soil for my crops when the sun is hot and rains stop for a few days?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso ni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around your crop bases with dry grass or leaves shields the ground from direct sunlight, stopping soil moisture from evaporating quickly.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie otsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ oya.

english: Why do some seeds fail to grow up out of the soil even after heavy rain has fallen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds may fail to sprout if they were planted too deep in the soil, if the soil becomes too waterlogged and lacks air, or if underground insects damage the seed.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli loo kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How do I know if my growing crops are hungry for nutrients in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mi tsei ni miida lɛ yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Crops usually show lack of food through their leaves, which turn yellowish instead of deep green, and by growing very slowly compared to healthy crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ amɛmli lɛ kpo kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. ni edaa blɛoo waa kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe.

english: Why is it good for me to start preparing my land long before the rainy season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔi shikpɔŋ lɛ saamɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba?

english: Preparing land early clears away weeds and loosens the soil so that as soon as the first proper rains fall, your seeds can be planted immediately without losing precious growing days.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. koni kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ ni sa pɛ lɛ, abaanyɛ adu Odumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni afiteee dumɔ be ni jara wa.

english: Is it safe for me to mix two different chemical powders together in the same tank before spraying my tomato crop?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai powda enyɔ baafutu yɛ tanki kome mli dani mikɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashwie nɔ?

english: Not always. Combining different chemicals without guidance can cause a reaction that ruins their effectiveness, clogs your sprayer, or burns your tomato leaves. You should only mix powders if the manufacturer's label specifically says they are compatible.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ. kɛji akɛ akɛfee ekome ni gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ko bɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ nɔ ko aba ni fiteɔ bɔ ni tsofa lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ. Ehaa tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ loo ehaa tomato baai lɛ shãa. Esa akɛ okɛ powda afutu pɛ kɛji akɛ mɔ ni fee lɛ wolo lɛ kɛɛ akɛ amɛkɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee.

english: Will mixing two different weed control powders together make them kill weeds faster on my field?
ga: Ani kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ahe powda enyɔ futu mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛgbe jwɛi oya yɛ mishia lɛ mli?

english: Not necessarily. Mixing two weed killers without understanding how they interact can cause them to cancel each other out or become too strong, which can damage your main crop's roots and waste your money.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai enyɔ ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ futu ni onuuu bɔ ni amɛtsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛfo amɛhe loo amɛhe awa tsɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ashishifãi ni efite oshika.

english: Why does the fertilizer powder I spread on my vegetable beds leave a white layer on top of the soil after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ powda fee ni mikɛshwieɔ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛŋ ko shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A white residue usually means the fertilizer was applied too heavily or the soil was too dry to absorb it properly. Fertilizer needs sufficient soil moisture to dissolve completely so that plant roots can draw in the nutrients safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni eshwɛ ni ji white lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ewo mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eŋɔ nu lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni etsɔ mli kwraa bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I cover fertilizer powder with soil instead of leaving it on top of the bed around my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mashi yɛ saatso ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Leaving powder exposed on top of the bed lets the hot sun evaporate the nutrients and heavy rain wash them away. Covering the fertilizer traps the nutrients in the soil where the plant roots can easily reach them.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi powda lɛ yɛ saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii lɛ kɛyaa. Mulching lɛ mɔ̃ɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ he oya lɛ.

english: If I treat my nursery bed with pest powder to kill soil insects, how long must I wait before planting my seeds?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi powda tsu nii yɛ mi-nursery lɛ mli koni mikɛgbe kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu dumɔwui?

english: You usually need to wait between 7 to 14 days after treating a seedbed. Strong chemical powders leave residues in the soil that need time to break down so they do not stunt or burn young tender sprouts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehe baahia ni omɛ gbii 7 kɛyashi 14 beni otsa gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe lɛ sɛɛ. Tsofa powda ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shĩɔ nɔ ko yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni heɔ be dani efiteɔ. Enɛ baatsi tsei bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee blɛoo loo amɛkashã.

english: How can I tell if the insect control powder I bought from the agro-dealer has gone bad before I put it on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji powda ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ ni mihe kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nihɔɔlɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ efite dani mikɛwo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: If the powder has formed hard lumps, changed color, or has a strong unusual odor, it has likely absorbed moisture or expired. Good chemical powder should be dry, uniform, and dissolve easily in water.
ga: Kɛji akɛ powda lɛ bafee nɔ ni wa, etsakeɔ ehiɛ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa waa. Ekolɛ eŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo egbo. Esa akɛ tsofa powda kpakpa lɛ afee nɔ ni egbi, ni efee ekome, ni ehiɛ nu mli oya.

english: Can the chemical powder I spray on my vegetables leave something behind that makes the food unsafe for my family to eat?
ga: Ani tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ aduawai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashi nɔ ko ni baaha niyenii lɛ afee nɔ ni bɛ shweshweeshwe aha miweku lɛ?

english: Yes, chemical powders leave residues on and inside the plant. Every chemical has a required waiting period, usually 7 to 21 days after spraying, before the crop is safe to harvest and consume.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ shĩɔ nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ mli kɛ kponɔgbɛ fɛɛ. Tsofai fɛɛ biɔ ni amɛmɛ, bei pii lɛ gbii 7 kɛyashi 21 yɛ be mli ni akɛwo mli lɛ sɛɛ. Dani abaanyɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii shweshweeshwe ni aye

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants turn yellow after I spray them with pest control powder?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ powda ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ efɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves after spraying can happen if the powder mixture was mixed too strong, sprayed during the hottest part of the day, or applied when the plants were already struggling from lack of water.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ashwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ baanyɛ aba kɛji akɛ akɛ powda ni akɛfutu lɛ futu mli waa tsɔ. Okɛshwie nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Aloo okɛtsu nii kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why is it better for my maize crop if I use both animal manure and chemical fertilizer powder together instead of just using one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mi ŋmãa lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ fɛɛ fee ekome moŋ fe ekome loo ekroko lɛ?

english: Using both works best because organic manure improves the soil structure so it holds water better, while chemical fertilizer provides a quick supply of essential nutrients that feed the growing maize plants.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsu nii lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo koni nu lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa ni akɛhaa ŋmɔ mli tsei ni miida lɛ oya.

english: Why are my cocoa pods still turning black even after I sprayed them with black pod powder medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ shwie nɔ moŋ?

english: Fungicide powder works by protecting healthy cocoa pods from catching the disease, but it cannot heal pods that were already infected before spraying. You must remove and destroy infected pods by hand so the disease does not spread.
ga: Fungicide powder tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ helai ahe lɛ nɔ. Shi anyɛɛɛ atsa ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ momo lɛ dani afɔ amɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ okɛ onine ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly like tubes when the afternoon sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from losing moisture. By rolling up, less of the leaf surface is exposed to the heat and drying wind, which helps the crop save water until the temperature cools down.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ he. kɛtsɔ shwiemɔ nɔ Ba lɛ hiɛ lɛ, hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shɛɛɛ he tsɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is dying because of a long dry spell or because of a disease in the roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ miigbo kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ loo shishifã hela hewɔ?

english: During a dry spell, the cassava plant will lose its leaves slowly from the bottom up to save water, but the stem remains alive and will sprout leaves again when rains return. If it is a root disease, the plant will wilt suddenly, leaves will rot or dry up quickly, and the stem or tubers will smell foul or soft underground.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Cassava tsei lɛ baa lɛ fiteɔ fiofio. Kɛjɛ shishi kɛtee ŋwɛi koni akɛhere nu Shi tso lɛ yitso lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni ebaakwɛ baai ekoŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ. Kɛji shishifã hela ji lɛ Tso lɛ baagbo trukaa. Baai lɛ baagboi loo amɛbaagbi oya. ni tso lɛ shishi loo tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaná ŋmɔlɔ loo egbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How can too much heavy rain hurt my crops when plants need water to grow?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ be mli ni nu he miihia amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: When soil receives too much water, the space between soil particles gets completely flooded, driving out air. Crop roots need air to breathe, and without it, they begin to rot and cannot absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Gbɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli eyiɔ nu kwraa. shwiemɔ kɔɔyɔɔ Tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Ni kɛji akɛ ebɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔi fitemɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants are hungry for nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that the soil is overly waterlogged and preventing the roots from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha niyenii tamɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant feels stressed, especially from sudden high temperatures, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. The plant drops its flowers to save energy to stay alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Titri lɛ kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa trukaa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli. Tsei baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha wala.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop their leaves during the long dry season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ gbee shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during prolonged dry weather as a self-defense mechanism. Dropping leaves reduces the amount of water the plant loses into the air, allowing the roots to stay alive in the soil until the rain returns.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ehe. Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ haa nu ni tsei lɛ laajeɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I plant them in a clear open field with no shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate stems and roots that burn easily under full sunlight. Planting companion shade crops like plantains or leaving shade trees provides living umbrellas that shield the young cocoa and keep the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei tamɔ dumɔwui loo shade tsei ni ashiɔ lɛ baaha shade ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with small cobs when I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops compete for the same sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. The plants stretch tall to fight for light rather than building thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu lɛ nɔŋŋ mli Tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛye la he akaŋ, ni no najiaŋ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei akutsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: All shoots attached to the main plantain tree feed on the same soil nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, which ensures the plant has enough strength to bear a large bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii fɛɛ ni kpɛtɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ yeɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ aba ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ mli awa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ plantain babaoo nɔ.

english: Why do my seeds sometimes rot in the ground when I plant immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry period. If seeds germinate after the first rain and the soil dries out completely right after, the fragile sprouts die in the hot, dry soil and rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ kwraa yɛ no sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ baagboi yɛ sũ ni mli edɔ, ni egbi mli ni amɛbaagboi.

english: Why is it important to plow my land before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii dani adu nii lɛ?

english: Plowing loosens hard soil so your crop's roots can spread easily to find water and food. It also buries weeds and brings rich nutrients from deeper underground up to where young roots can reach them.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii. Efuɔ jwɛi hu ni ewoɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ kɛyaa he ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: What will happen to my crop if I miss the main rain and plant late in the season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mifo nugbɔ titri lɛ mli ni midu yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ?

english: If you plant too late, your crops won't get enough rainwater during their critical growth period. This leads to stunted growth, poor flowering, and a very small harvest because the rains end before the crops fully mature.
ga: Kɛji odu nii sɛɛ tsɔ Onibii lɛ naaa nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa mɔ dalɛ sɛɛ foɔ. fɔfɔi ni ehiii kɛ ŋmaa bibioo ko kwraa ejaakɛ nugbɔ lɛ naagbee dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will heavy tractors press my soil down too hard and hurt my crops?
ga: Ani trakta agbo ko baami mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa tsɔ ni ebaaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Heavy machinery can compact the soil if used when the ground is too wet. This makes it difficult for roots to breathe and spread, so it is best to plow when the soil is moist but not muddy.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ akɛtsu nii be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ atsu he nii yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi jeee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my seeds fail to come up if I plant them too deep in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds carry just enough stored energy to sprout and reach the surface. If buried too deep, the young shoot runs out of energy before seeing sunlight and dies under the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni ato ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, oblahii kɛ oblayei lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi dani amɛnaa hulu la ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are packed tightly together, they fight like crowded children for the same light, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and produce small, weak fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ abɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Amɛbaawuu tamɔ gbekɛbii. Hei ni gbɔmɛi eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ tsɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: How does using a planting machine help my crops grow better than planting by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe ni mikɛ niji duɔ lɛ?

english: A planter drops seeds at the exact same depth and distance apart across the whole field. This gives every crop equal space, air, and sunlight to grow strong and mature at the same time.
ga: Okwaafoi duɔ dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ naa he ko, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛha dalɛ ni mli wa kɛ dalɛ ni akɛfee ekome

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up into tight tubes during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling up leaves is a crop's natural survival trick to shade itself and stop water from escaping through its leaves when the sun is too hot.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi koni ekɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛtsi nu naa koni ekatsɔ baai lɛ amli kɛji hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant the exact same crop on the same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: The same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and attracts specific pests that build up over time, which weakens future harvests.
ga: Tsei nɛɛ nɔŋŋ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa wɔsɛɛ ŋmaakpamɔi lɛ baa shi.

english: What happens if I leave my ripe crops on the field for too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani mikpa?

english: Leaving mature crops in the sun too long makes them dry out and break, or rot if it rains. It also gives birds, insects, and molds more time to ruin your farm's output.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ hulu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha amɛgbi ni amɛkumɔ loo amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. Ehaa okpoi, kooloi bibii, kɛ ŋmeii hu be babaoo ni amɛkɛfiteɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii.

english: Why is it risky to harvest a very large farm slowly by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔji wuji waa ni akɛ niji kpaɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani oshara ko yɛ he?

english: Manual harvesting on a large field takes many days, meaning crops on one end of the field may dry out, spoil, or get destroyed by weather and pests before you can reach them.
ga: Nine ni akɛkpaa nii yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli lɛ heɔ gbii babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ naagbee lɛ eko baanyɛ agbi, egbo loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baafite amɛ dani obaanyɛ oyashɛ amɛhe.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa lɛ Abɛi tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes the soil richer for my next farm season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mikwɛ̃mɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the roots and leaves decay, they leave nitrogen behind, which nourishes the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ fite Amɛshiɔ nitrogen yɛ amɛsɛɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the rainy season becomes too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess water sits in the soil without proper drainage, it drowns the roots and creates room for rot-causing fungi to attack the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni eha gbɛ aha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ koni amɛtutua ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my watermelons split open in the field right before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Watermelons burst open when they receive a sudden surge of water or heavy rainfall after a long dry period. The inside of the fruit absorbs water quickly and expands faster than the outer skin can stretch.
ga: Watermelon lɛ tswaa kɛji nu ni fa trukaa loo nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling tightly and causing the fruits to stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ehaa aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus, or by severe heat stress. The virus prevents the plant from moving nutrients properly, stopping fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Virus lɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkajie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa aduawai lɛ daalɛ kpaa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during high winds even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be weakened by tiny soil pests called nematodes or by root rot. When the root anchor is damaged, the heavy weight of the stem and fruit bunch makes the tree easy to push over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Atsɛɔ nakai feemɔ akɛ nematodes loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ. Kɛji shishifã lɛ mli ŋtayaa lɛ fite Tso lɛ shishi kɛ aduawai lɛ aniji lɛ tsii, ni no haa tso lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many tiny flowers, but very few of them grow into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo, shi fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ fioo ko pɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ cocoa ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers rely on tiny beneficial insects called midges for pollination. If there are few insects, or if the tree lacks water and nutrients, the tree naturally sheds unpollinated flowers to save energy.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ damɔɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ anɔ. Atsɛɔ nakai midge kɛha ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji kooloi bibii fioo pɛ yɔɔ loo nu kɛ niyenii bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni bɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the blossoms and small fruits dropping off my pepper plants before they can mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai lɛ daraaa nakai lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, egbee mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani eda kwraa?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers and young fruits when exposed to extreme heat, irregular watering, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai anɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do my yam plants grow very leafy vines, but the yams underground remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ yɛ wain tsei ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi yam lɛ ji bibioo lolo?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes yam plants to put all their food energy into leaf and stem growth above ground instead of sending energy down to build large tubers underground.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai kɛ tsei ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ he wami tsuɔ ní kɛ peeɔ zugba agbo ko nɛ ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why do my vegetables grow thin and weak when I sow many seeds close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the young plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow thick and strong.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe baatswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ wa.

english: How do I know if the soil on my new land is good enough for growing maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ?

english: Healthy soil for maize is usually dark in color, holds water well without becoming swampy, crumbles easily in your hands, and has plenty of decomposed plant material mixed in.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ni nubu bɛ mli. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli ni tsei ahe nibii ni fiteɔ babaoo efutu mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big roots sometimes, but only small woody roots other times?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi wuji lɛ? Shi bei komɛi lɛ, shishifãi bibii pɛ yɔɔ?

english: Cassava needs loose, well-drained soil to expand its tubers. If the ground is too hard or packed down, the roots cannot swell properly, resulting in thin, woody cassava.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ he miihia cassava koni ekɛdu ŋmeii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɔjɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ mli tseee ni eyɛ tso.

english: Why do some of my crops grow very tall and thin without producing much fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When plants do not receive enough direct sunlight, they stretch upward searching for light. This uses up all their energy for growing stems instead of producing flowers and fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ ehe shi koni etao la. Gbɛ nɛɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant my seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting seeds too close causes the crops to fight each other for water, light, and soil nutrients, leaving all the plants weak, small, and low-yielding.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ, efeɔ bibioo ni ewoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants turn yellow and curl up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl and yellow when plants are stressed by extreme heat and lack of water, or when tiny pests like whiteflies suck their sap and spread plant viruses during hot weather.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ mli. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ nuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: My parents taught me to burn the bush before planting, but why do my crops still turn pale green after a few seasons?
ga: Mifɔlɔi tsɔɔ mi bɔ ni ashãa jwɛi dani aduɔ amɛ. Shi mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo yɛ bei fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Burning cleared bush creates temporary ash nutrients, but over time it destroys organic matter and drives away nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay dark green and leafy.
ga: Brɔshi ni ajie lɛ ni ashãa lɛ haa ashwishwɛ niyenii ni he hiaa be kukuoo ko baa. Shi beni be hoɔ lɛ Efoɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli ni ejieɔ nitrogen lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow faster and stronger than the crops I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that adapt quickly to local conditions and absorb water and fertilizer faster than domesticated crops, allowing them to overcrowd your crops if not weeded early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni tsakeɔ amɛhe oya kɛyaa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shihilɛi amli. ni ekɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi oya fe shia tsei Enɛ baanyɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayi obɔ kɛji ajieee jwɛi lɛ oya.

english: Why does my piece of land produce fewer crops every year even though I plant the exact same crop every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi moŋ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests and diseases that feed on that specific crop to build up in the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaya nɔ ajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are dying because of insects or because of a disease in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigboi yɛ kooloi loo helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahewɔ?

english: Insects usually leave physical marks like chewed leaves, holes, or webs, whereas soil diseases usually cause the root to rot or the entire plant to wilt and collapse suddenly without visible bites.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii shĩɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii, tamɔ baai ni atsɔ mli, bu loo ŋmeii, yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ loo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni efoɔ ni anaaa okadii ni akɛyeɔ ŋmeii.

english: How do I know when my yams under the ground are mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?
