english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines above ground naturally turn yellow and dry up, showing that the plant has stopped growing and stored all its energy in the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ miito bulb lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their foliage is soft and delicate. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects young cocoa trees from heat and retains soil moisture until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he lɛ baa. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes next to my yam plants as soon as they shoot up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko ama ŋmɔshi tso lɛ masɛi kɛji ŋmɔshi tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach sunlight. Guiding the vines up stakes exposes more leaves to direct light, which helps the plant manufacture food efficiently and send energy down into the root to grow larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ ba tso ko nɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ jeɔ kpo tɛ̃ɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni ekwɛ̃ bulbs wuji.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and hiding inside the plant stems?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛ ehe teeɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, a common pest in Ghana. Inspecting your maize early and applying target treatments directly into the central plant whorl helps destroy them before they destroy the crop harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Abɛi mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni efiteɔ abɛi dani enyɛɔ efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting and dying suddenly even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil-borne disease that blocks water transport inside the plant stem. Rotating your field with crops like maize or cassava helps clear the bacteria from the soil over time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ nu gbɛfaa naa yɛ tsei ashishifãi amli. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ejie helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why is my crop growing very slowly and looking pale green despite receiving good rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛ po lɛ?

english: Pale leaves and slow growth usually mean the soil is deficient in nitrogen. Adding organic compost, well-rotted manure, or nitrogen fertilizer gives plants the necessary nutrients to form healthy green leaves and grow rapidly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ organic compost ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii Loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo baai ni wa, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara oya.

english: Will planting groundnuts together with my maize damage or steal food from my maize crop?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ lɛ fiteɔ loo ejuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ mi ŋmei lɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts actually help maize grow better. As a leguminous crop, groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil, naturally fertilizing the neighboring maize.
ga: Peanuts yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni edaa jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ. Taakɛ eji ŋmei lɛ, Peanuts mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ

english: How far apart should I plant cassava stems to get large cassava tubers?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu amɛ kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni anyɛ ana ŋmei shishifãi wuji?

english: Cassava stems should be planted about one meter apart. Planting them too close causes the roots to fight for underground space, nutrients, and water, resulting in thin, small tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cassava tsei lɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe aaafee mita kome. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi he ko, niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa.

english: Should I cut away the small side shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ani ajie plantain tsei titrii lɛ?

english: Yes, you should trim away excess shoots, leaving only one or two strong suckers. Leaving too many shoots causes them to steal nutrients from the main stem, leading to smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ni oshi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Wait until the ground receives two or three heavy rains and stays consistently damp. Planting after only a single light shower can cause the seeds to sprout and then die if dry weather returns immediately.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni ohi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba trukaa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by intense heat dry spells or over-application of fertilizer. Regular watering during hot periods helps stabilize the plant so the flowers can set into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ afɔlɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How do I know that my corn is completely ready to be harvested from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When corn is fully mature, the plant leaves turn brown and dry, the outer husk turns pale, and a tiny black spot forms at the base of each grain kernel, showing it has finished growing.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ Tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ. Kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaa yɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbe shweremɔ naa.

english: Why do my corn grains keep falling off the cob onto the ground when I touch them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ kɛ́ mita he lɛ?

english: If corn stays on the plant too long after maturing, the dry cob shrinks and the attachment holding the grain breaks easily, causing the seeds to shatter and fall loose at the slightest shake.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa hi tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ŋmãa ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baakumɔ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ akpokpo fioo lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ gbáa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why do my maize plants fall flat on the ground just when the cobs get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over—a condition called lodging—when heavy winds or rain hit top-heavy plants with shallow roots, or when pests like stem borers weaken the base of the stalk.
ga: Abele tsei ni shwieɔ shi Enɛ ji shihilɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ shĩa. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ miinɛ tsei ni amɛyitsei tsii ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ. aloo be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ stem borers lɛ haa tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do corn cobs naturally bend and point downwards towards the soil as they dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: The cob stalk naturally weakens and bends down so rainwater runs off the outer leaves instead of seeping inside, protecting the grains from rotting while they dry on the stem.
ga: Cob tso lɛ baafee blɛoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekoto shi. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ asɛɛ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ mli. Enɛ haaa ŋmaa lɛ afite beni egbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do new corn plants start growing by themselves on my farm after the main harvest is over?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei heei jeɔ shishi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ eba naagbee lɛ?

english: Grains that fall to the soil during harvest get covered by dirt and watered by later rain, causing them to sprout on their own as spontaneous growth.
ga: Akɛ sũ haa omɔ ŋmaa ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ nɔ, ni sɛɛ mli lɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ naa.

english: Why does my corn turn moldy and black inside the husk if rain falls near harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efeɔ ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Rainwater trapped inside the tight, warm husk creates a wet home for fungi, which quickly multiplies and turns the grain moldy before harvest.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni emɔ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ ni mli wa lɛ mli lɛ feɔ shĩa ni mli ewo fɔ kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛyibɔ ​​yaa hiɛ ni ehaa ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii oya dani akpaa.

english: Why do birds and insects suddenly start attacking my corn field only when the cobs turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi kɛ kooloi bibii bɔi mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ tutuamɔ trukaa shi ŋmãa lɛ pɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: As corn turns yellow, the grains fill with sugars and release a strong scent that signals to birds and insects that the crop is soft, sweet, and ready to eat.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, sugar eyi ŋmãa lɛ mli ni ejieɔ ŋmãa ni naa wa ni haa okpoi kɛ kooloi bibii leɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ, ni esa akɛ aye.

english: Why do some of my corn cobs have empty patches with missing grains on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn cobs lɛ ekomɛi yɛ diski ni nɔ ko bɛ mli kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty spaces happen when dry heat or lack of rain damages the silk strands at the top of the cob before wind can carry pollen to them, stopping grains from forming.
ga: He ni etse lɛ baa kɛji latsaa ni mli egbi loo nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ lɛ fite siliki kpãai ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. Dani kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ pollen baa ni etsiɔ ŋmaa naa koni ekafee

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow and dying while the cobs are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: When the soil lacks nitrogen, the maize plant takes stored food from its lower leaves and sends it up to feed the growing cobs, causing the bottom leaves to wither.
ga: Kɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Abɛi gbalaa niyenii ni ato kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni etsuɔ ​​kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eyaha ŋmei ni miida lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my corn grains shrink and become hard a few days after I pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewaa yɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni ajie lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fresh corn holds a lot of water inside its grains; as exposed air and heat dry the harvested corn, the water evaporates, leaving behind tightly packed, hard starch.
ga: Abele hee toɔ nu babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ latsaa ha ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ gĩ lɛ, Nu lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ashiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa ni akɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop is hungry for nitrogen. When the soil lacks nutrients or when heavy rains wash them away, the plant cannot make green food for itself, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps it regain its color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ. Tsei nyɛŋ afee niyenii eŋɔli amɛha amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Which direction should I push my cassava stick into the ground when planting?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ ashɛre ŋmei tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Always plant the cassava stem with the small buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant it upside down, the stems have to bend around to grow up, which weakens the plant and reduces the size and number of tubers you harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu lɛ kɛtee shishi Esa akɛ tso lɛ tso lɛ abɔle ehe kɛyaa kɛbaa koni eda. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni okɛ ŋmeii ni okpaa lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛyibɔ ​​aba shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need plantain trees growing right beside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ aná dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily under the hot, direct sun. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the gentle shade and humidity cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How does spreading dry grass around my crop stems help them grow during the dry season?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves acts like a blanket over the soil. It blocks the harsh sun from drying out the earth, keeps water in the root zone longer, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shishifã lɛ he be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes in the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are typically fall armyworms that hatch from eggs laid by flying moths. They hide inside the soft central leaves of the maize to feed, so identifying them early allows you to use appropriate measures before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji asraafoi akuu mli ŋmeii ni fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ amli. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa teŋ lɛ amli koni amɛye niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kadimɔ amɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua bo ni ofee nɔ ni sa dani amɛfite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously steals the same specific nutrients from the soil until the land becomes completely exhausted. Rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts gives the soil a break and puts valuable plant food back into the earth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaju niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be kɛyashi sũ lɛ mli baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ tsei aniyenii ni jara wa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens if I plant my seeds very close together so I can fit more into my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni enyɛ ebote ŋmɔ lɛ mli babaoo?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants end up fighting each other for light, soil food, and water. Giving each crop enough space ensures every plant gets what it needs to produce large, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Kɛji amɛto amɛhe shi pɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa tso fɛɛ tso lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop when the plant gets stressed by intense heat or unpredictable watering. When the plant feels it does not have enough steady water or strength, it drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ nu loo hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Ebaajie fɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if I leave them growing together on the farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji miha amɛfee ekome kɛkwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds act like silent thieves that steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. They also hide insect pests and diseases that can jump onto your healthy crops and ruin your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni efee dioo, ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Amɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baanyɛ atswa onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ ni amɛfite onibii lɛ hu teeɔ.

english: Why do the stems of my pepper plants turn soft and die when water sits on the farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air in the soil to breathe just like humans do. When standing water covers the roots for days, they drown and begin to rot, which allows harmful fungi in the wet soil to kill the whole plant.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha shishifãi lɛ anɔ gbii babaoo Amɛbaagbee shi ni amɛbɔi fitemɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ tsei muu fɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants turn yellow and stop growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the roots are waterlogged from heavy rains, which stops the plant from taking up essential plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ ni shishifãi lɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye tsei niyenii ni he hiaa waa.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to sprout after I plant them on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need constant soil moisture and clean roots to start growing; if planted during dry weather or with old, damaged root corms attached, sprouting will be very slow.
ga: Plantain suckers biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ shishifãi ni he tse koni amɛje dalɛ shishi. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi loo kɛji akɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi momo lɛ efite lɛ, ekwɛ̃ɔ oya waa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high and water is low, tomato plants get stressed and drop their flowers to save energy and water rather than spending it on growing fruit.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni nu lɛ hu faaa lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite shika yɛ aduawai akwɛmɔ mli lɛ

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa trees turning black and rotting while still hanging on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite lɛ? Ani ekã tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly during the heavy rainy season when the farm has too much shade and damp air.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli ewoɔ hulutsoo ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli tsɔ.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up into tiny cups and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the sap and transmitting leaf curl virus to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ baai lɛ ahe hela lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛtee baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: That is damage from the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the young leaves inside the plant's funnel before the maize can form ears.
ga: No ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ fiteɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa toi amli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thin stems but yield very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii shi ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together or have too much nitrogen, they fight for sunlight and put all their energy into growing tall leaves instead of storing food in the roots.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ mli lɛ Ebaatswa hulu la he akaŋ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai kakadaji moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: If I plant cowpea between my rows of maize, will it spoil my maize crop?
ga: Kɛ midu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ Ani ebaakpãtã mi ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ?

english: No, cowpea actually helps maize because legumes pull nitrogen from the air into the soil, providing free food that helps your maize grow stronger.
ga: Dabi, cowpea yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa diɛŋtsɛ. Ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa o-corn lɛ ni edara waa ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers under the ground are fully mature for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the leaves and vines on top of the ground naturally turn yellow, dry out, and die down completely.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛdalɛ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their leaves right when the dry harmattan wind starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ahe baai babaoo fiteɔ kɛji harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ je shishi pɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves naturally during dry winds to prevent water from evaporating out of the tree, allowing the trunk and roots to survive until the next rains.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ koni nu akajɛ tso lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting from the tip down the center, the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green growth. Adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛtee teŋgbɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tsei he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into little cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi bibii ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips, or by extreme heat. Inspecting under the leaves helps identify if insects are draining food from the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mites loo thrips lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ona kɛji kooloi bibii miinu niyenii kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: Cassava puts its energy into leaves when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or too much shade. Reducing nitrogen and giving plants enough sunlight encourages the crop to store food in the roots instead.
ga: Yucca kɛ hewalɛ woɔ ebaai lɛ amli kɛ́ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo hulutsoo be babaoo. Nitrogen ni abaaba shi ni aha tsei lɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ baaha amɛto niyenii yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli moŋ.

english: How can I tell if my land is fertile enough for a new crop before planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei bɔ ni sa kɛha tsei heei dani madu nii?

english: Fertile soil is usually dark, crumbly, retains moisture well, and supports healthy wild vegetation. Testing soil texture and observing natural weed growth gives good clues about its richness.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ koo mli tsei Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ akaa ni akwɛɔ bɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daraa yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ haa anáa jwɛi lɛ ahewalɛ he susumɔ kpakpa.

english: Extreme midday heat or sudden dry spells cause tomato plants to drop their flowers to conserve water. Providing shade or consistent watering during dry periods keeps the flowers intact.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo loo nu ha amɛ daa yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce plenty of leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas often produce excess leaves instead of pods if planted during very heavy rainfall or in soil with too much nitrogen, which tricks the plant into growing stems instead of flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsina ŋmeii woɔ baai ni fa fe nine yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ kɛji akɛ akwɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa waa mli loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwereɔ yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my maize so it does not rot in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Koni ŋmãa lɛ akafite yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer cob husks turn papery and dry, and a tiny black layer appears at the bottom of the individual grains, showing the plant has stopped feeding the seed.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ bafee wolo ni egbi lɛ. Ni ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko yɛ jɛmɛ. lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa edumɔwui lɛ niyenii hamɔ.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables spoil and soften so quickly before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo oya dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Vegetables continue to breathe and lose water after harvest. Picking them during the cool early morning and keeping them covered away from direct sunlight slows down spoilage.
ga: Aduawai yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛnuɔ nu yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ shwie shi yɛ leebi maŋkpa ni hulu lɛ shɛɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛfite fioo.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt in the hot afternoon even when the soil was moist in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense sun, leaves lose water to the air faster than roots can drink from the ground. Plants temporarily drop their leaves to reduce water loss, usually recovering when the afternoon cools down.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baashwie baai lɛ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni nu ni elaaje lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa shi beni shwane lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops after the first rains of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally adapted to local soils and weather, allowing their seeds to sprout and soak up water much faster than cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛdumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛmɔɔ nu oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: Why are small worms eating the centers of my young maize plants, and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: Those are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds inside the young leaves (the whorl). You can manage them by checking your farm early, applying recommended control sprays during the early morning or evening when worms are active, or using neem-based organic sprays.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ baai bibii (rings) lɛ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ amɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oookwɛ mra lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ emɔ bo lɛ. Aloo okɛ neem spray ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii yɛ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when I plant them in an open field without any trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or leguminous trees around them for the first two to three years to shelter them until their leaves form a full canopy.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo bean tsei, ni ebɔle amɛhe. Klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ haa nɔ ko nɔ ko nɔ ko nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni baai lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ nɔ ko ni eyi obɔ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning excess branches to let in air and sunlight, removing infected pods immediately, and applying recommended fungicides during the wet season will keep the pods healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ he. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ni kɛ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Your cassava likely has Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies or spread through infected stems. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by local extension officers is the best way to prevent this problem.
ga: Ekolɛ o-kasa lɛ yɛ kasa mosaic hela. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ loo amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛtsɔɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni maŋ lɛ mli nitsumɔhe nine lɛ mli onukpai lɛ kɛhaa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off mostly due to high heat, irregular watering, or a lack of key soil nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and using balanced fertilizers helps the plant turn flowers into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa fe fɛɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etsɔ fɔfɔi ni etsɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the roots of my pepper plants rot when I water them heavily every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ daa gbi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need well-drained soil because standing water suffocates their roots and encourages fungal diseases. It is better to water deeply only when the top layer of soil starts to feel dry rather than keeping the ground constantly soaked.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu babaoo pɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ je shishi enu he akɛ egbi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize turn yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize requires plenty of nitrogen to stay green and grow strong, which you can fix by applying fertilizers like NPK or Urea at the right growth stages.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛbaafata he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields when I plant maize on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows crop pests to build up in the field. Rotating your maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen back to the soil naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ aba shi be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsakeɔ Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ kɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni efo ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and put wooden stakes next to my growing yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? ni ekɛ tso tso ko ma emasɛi Sweet potato wain tsei ni aduɔ

english: Yam is a climbing plant that needs sunlight on its leaves to produce big underground tubers. Staking lifts the vines off the ground where they can get maximum sunlight and stay safe from damp leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ ni hulu la ashɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ, ni amɛyɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ baai ni mli efɔ lɛ ahe helai ahe.

english: Why are my heavy plantain trees falling over during strong winds before the fruit is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani yibii lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees easily fall when pests like banana weevils or microscopic worms (nematodes) damage their root structure under the ground. Planting clean, treated suckers and piling soil firmly around the base of the plant gives them strong root support.
ga: Ewaaa akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ banana ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. (Nematodes) lɛ fiteɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni he tse ni atsa amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ni akɛ sũ ni ato shishi lɛ he shi shiŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field without plantains nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni plantains ko bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and hot winds. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside them creates temporary shade and holds moisture in the air, protecting the delicate seedlings until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko baa ni emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ. Koni abu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers under the ground. Staking also lifts the leaves off the wet soil, preventing fungal diseases and rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulbs wuji ni baa shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetables with dry grass or cocoa pod husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil, which is called mulching, keeps the hot sun from drying out the ground too quickly, stops weeds from taking over, and slowly breaks down into food for your soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa, ni atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ haa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaye nɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio akɛ niyenii kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for crop growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth. Planting them improves the soil naturally so your next maize crop grows better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist, usually right after a good rain, so the plant roots can soak it up. Applying it on dry soil can burn the crop, and applying right before a heavy downpour can wash it away.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ pɛ kɛkɛ. koni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii ashã. Ni okɛwo nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ashwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will know it is ready when the bottom leaves dry up and drop off, and the ground around the base of the plant starts cracking as the roots swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I wait for the main rains to establish before sowing my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani madu ŋmãa?

english: Maize seeds require steady moisture in the soil for several days to germinate and push roots deep. Planting after just one early light rain can cause the seeds to dry out and die under the hot sun.
ga: Abele dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be gbii babaoo bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛtsi amɛshishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why should I prune off extra or dead branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ niji ni fa fe nine loo ni egboi lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the cocoa tree canopy to allow sunlight and fresh air to flow through. This prevents black pod disease caused by trapped dampness and encourages the tree to put its energy into making healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. Bɔni afee ni atsĩ black pod hela ni ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa. ni ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ afee kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is making ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaves look like they were chewed overnight?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ nɔ ni aye amɛ nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This is usually caused by pests such as the Fall Armyworm caterpillar that hide inside the central leaves of young maize. Checking your field early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or treatments keeps them from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni akɛtee ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow green and strong. Adding compost or the right fertilizer restores nutrients to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba tso lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do farmers say planting beans or cowpeas helps make the soil richer for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant leaves and roots decay in the soil, they leave behind free fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso lɛ baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Amɛbaashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the tall trees from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains or leaving some taller forest trees shields the young cocoa from burning.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ loo koo mli tsei kakadaji ni ashiɔ Enɛɛmɛi ekomɛi yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã.

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground on stakes allows the leaves to spread out and catch full sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture energy to grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni enáa hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and covered in a white sticky substance?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi yucca tso lɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni nɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by small insects called mealybugs that suck nutrients out of the plant leaves. Planting healthy, clean cassava stems from safe sources prevents this pest from taking over.
ga: Kooloi bibii kɛ enɛ baa. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ mealybugs ni shwieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli lɛ. Cassava tsei ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akwɛɔ kɛjɛɔ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ naa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, usually from extreme sun heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, preventing the flower from forming fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna haomɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ jɛɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Enɛ ɔ haa nɛ fɔfɔi ɔmɛ nyɛ we nɛ a wo yiblii.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black, sunken patches at the bottom before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni eboteɔ shishi dani etsɔɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: This black patch is called blossom end rot. It happens when the soil moisture changes drastically from wet to dry, preventing the plant from taking up enough calcium to build strong fruit walls.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he ni yɔɔ duŋ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ waa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛma aduawai gbogboi ni wa.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting seeds after the dry harmattan season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje dumɔwui ashishi beni harmatta be ni egbi lɛ eho lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the early rains become regular and wet the soil deeply—usually after two or three heavy rains—so seeds don't sprout and then dry up during a dry gap.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afɔ—bei pii lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ—koni dumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni amɛkagbi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up permanently in the ground.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa.

english: Why do weeds in my field lower the total crop harvest I get at the end of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni miwoɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil food directly from your crops. When weeds grow close to crops, your main plants become weak and yield smaller produce.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe Otsei titrii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when there is too much direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots. Heavy sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out the surrounding soil before the roots can establish deeply, which is why shade plants are needed to protect them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ amli aba. No hewɔ ni tsei taoɔ hulutsoo koni ebu amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when they start carrying heavy fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ebɔi aduawai babaoo womɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that do not go deep into the earth. When heavy fruit bunches form, the top becomes too heavy for the shallow roots to hold, especially during strong winds, requiring wooden props for support.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ aduawai lɛ je kpo yɛ tso ni mli edɔ mli lɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baafee tsiimɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ amɔmɔ. Titri lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni biɔ ni akɛ tso atsu nii lɛ mli

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the key nutrient needed to build green leaves and produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli ni afee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it bad for my farm if I plant maize on the exact same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover, while also allowing pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up in the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does chemical fertilizer burn my crop roots if I apply it when the ground is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shãa mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛji akɛ mikɛwo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain salts that need water to dissolve safely into the soil. In dry ground, the concentrated fertilizer pulls water directly out of the roots, causing them to scorch and wither.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli ŋmeii ni he hiaa nu koni etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil. When water collects and cannot drain away, it starves the roots of air and creates wet conditions where root-rot fungi multiply rapidly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu buaa ehe naa ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛya. Nu baaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ amli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ baa Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baagbɛ eshwa oya.

english: Extreme daytime heat or irregular watering stresses the tomato plant, causing it to drop its blossoms to conserve energy and water rather than producing fruit.
ga: Gbi mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and growing out twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the underside of leaves, or by diseases spread by insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce much smaller harvests even when I put fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa midumɔ nii lɛ awo yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal sunlight, soil moisture, and fertilizer away from your main crops before the crops can use them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ Ni ŋmɔshi nibii yaa kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts together with my maize make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen from the air and fixes it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer for neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to strong sunlight. They need shade from taller crops like plantains to cover them and protect them from burning until their roots mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ekɛha amɛhe ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen food in the soil, or the ground is flooded with too much water, preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. loo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off before growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani miduɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as very high heat or lack of regular water, saving their energy to stay alive instead of growing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛna haomɔ tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ baaha hewalɛ akafite yɛ shihilɛ mli yɛ aduawai ni aduɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Can I plant groundnuts on the same land with my corn, or will they steal food from each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ? Aloo amɛbaaju niyenii kɛjɛ amɛhe?

english: Groundnuts and corn work very well together. Groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which actually feeds and enriches the soil for your corn.
ga: Peanuts kɛ ŋmãa tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa niyenii diɛŋtsɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa o-corn lɛ.

english: If I put fertilizer directly against the stem of my young plant, will it grow faster?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso bibioo ko shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, Ani ebaada oya?

english: Putting fertilizer directly against the plant stem can burn and kill the tender stem and roots. Fertilizer should always be placed a short distance away in the soil so the roots can stretch out safely to feed.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni egbe amɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo be fɛɛ be. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ amɛhe ni amɛye niyenii shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my maize grow thin and weak when I put many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ mli tsɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ waa beni mikɛ ŋmãa babaoo ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for water, light, and soil nutrients, leaving all of them weak and undernourished.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnáaa niyenii kpakpa.

english: How do I know it is safe to start planting my maize seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔwui adumɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: You should wait until the rains become consistent with two or three deep soakings of the soil so the ground stays moist enough for the seeds to germinate without drying out.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ anɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha eshɛ shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to turn soft and rot under the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil and cannot drain away. Standing water suffocates the roots and encourages fungi that cause root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ejɛ mli. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni kɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: What is making small holes in the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ

english: Holes in the center leaves of young corn are usually caused by armyworm caterpillars, which crawl inside the growing leaves to feed on tender parts of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii baa, ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli koni amɛye tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ.

english: Yam plants grow as long vines. Giving them sticks to climb spreads their leaves out into the sunlight, allowing the leaves to generate energy to feed the yam tubers growing underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daa tamɔ wain tsei kakadaji. Kɛ́ oha amɛ tsei niji ni amɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ ashwã koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ ji koni baai lɛ afee hewalɛ ni amɛkɛha sweet potato ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do I need to build a shade structure over my vegetable nursery bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa shade structure yɛ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young sprouts are very fragile and sensitive to extreme weather. Providing shade shields them from excessive sun and drying winds, keeping them at a stable temperature so they do not dry out and die before they are strong.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa waa lɛ ahe waa. Kɛ́ aha amɛ hulutsoo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa amɛgbiɔ lɛ he. Ha amɛhi he ko ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa nɔ daa koni amɛkagbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛhe awa.

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt and die when strong winds blow through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy air currents pull moisture out of young plants faster than their small roots can drink it from the soil, causing them to get cold, dry out, and collapse.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli oya fe shishifãi bibii. ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli ni baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: How do windbreak trees along my farm borders help protect my young crops?
ga: Te tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ buɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting trees or taller grasses around your farm slows down strong, cold wind drafts so they do not directly hit and stress your young, vulnerable crops.
ga: Tsei loo jwɛi kakadaŋŋ adumɔ yɛ Oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni fɛ̃i be mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ aba shi. Bɔni afee ni ekaná oŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔjɔ kɛ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is it important to put well-rotted manure directly into the hole when I am planting my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ awo bu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Just like early nourishment gives a healthy start to life, placing rich manure right at the root zone gives the young plant immediate, concentrated food as soon as its roots sprout.
ga: Nakai nɔŋŋ eji yɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa mra lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni ojeɔ oshihilɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa tso bibioo lɛ naa niyenii ni mli wa kɛji shishifãi lɛ shwere pɛ.

english: What is starter fertilizer, and why shouldn't I wait until the plant is big before applying it?
ga: Mɛni ji shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ omɛɔ ni tso lɛ da dani okɛfataa he?

english: Starter fertilizer provides quick-release nutrients to tiny roots right after germination, giving the plant the strong early energy boost it needs to establish itself before regular growth begins.
ga: Shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii haa shishifãi bibii lɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ oya. Beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ Ehaa tsei lɛ shishijee hewalɛ ni mli wa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛto amɛhe shi dani amɛdalɛ ni sa lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa nursery seedlings need organic compost early on before they can handle inorganic fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo dumɔwui lɛ he hiaa organic compost mra lɛ? Dani obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ wala mli lɛ atsu nii

english: Organic compost acts like mild, rich early food that young root systems can easily absorb without burning, whereas chemical fertilizers can be too harsh for very fresh roots.
ga: Organic ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni mli jɔ. ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ oya ni amɛshãaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni mli wa tsɔ kɛha shishifãi ni yɔɔ ehee waa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to split my fertilizer application into two stages instead of giving it all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mijaraa mi-fertilizing lɛ mli enyɔ moŋ fe fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Crops need a gentle, rich feed when they are young, and then additional heavier feeding later as they grow bigger and prepare to bear fruit.
ga: Niyenii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni fa babaoo he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi tɔ̃ɔ. Ni ehe miihia ni aha amɛ niyenii ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli beni amɛdaraa ni amɛsaa amɛhe koni amɛwo yibii lɛ.

english: What is 'hardening off', and why should I slowly expose my nursery seedlings to full sun before transplanting them?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘erection’ ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ lɛ blɛoo? Okɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ awo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli dani okɛwo he kroko.

english: Hardening off gradually gets seedlings used to the harsher outdoor conditions, transitioning them safely from a sheltered environment to the rough weather of the open field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni mli wa lɛ baaba fiofio. Ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ ebɔi nitsumɔ kɛ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ hei ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛyaa shihilɛi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need shade from plantain plants for their first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni ená hulutsoo kɛjɛ dumɔwu lɛ mli yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily and struggle in direct heat and strong winds. Plantain leaves act as a shield to keep them shaded and humid until they grow mature enough to tolerate open sunlight.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya, ni hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantain baai tsuɔ nii akɛ tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he, ni ehaa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ kpo nɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my tiny tomato plants turn yellow when I water them with very cold water early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ? Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ mikɛ nu ni mli ejɔ tamɔ ais shwie amɛnɔ leebi lɛ?

english: Water or air that is too cold shocks the delicate root system of young plants, preventing them from taking up nutrients properly and causing their leaves to lose color.
ga: Nu loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ tsɔ lɛ baaná tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ hewalɛ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni sa. ni ehaa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: What do those letters N, P, and K on fertilizer bags actually mean for my crops?
ga: Mɛni niŋmaa okadii N, P kɛ K ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kotoku nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: N stands for Nitrogen (which makes leaves green and bushy), P is Phosphorus (which builds strong roots and flowers), and K is Potassium (which helps plants fight off diseases and grow heavy fruits).
ga: N damɔ shi kɛha nitrogen. P ji fɔsfɔs (ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji), P ji fɔsfɔs (ni haa shishifãi kɛ fɔfɔi ni wa baa), ni K ji potassium (ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji). (ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ helai ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni tsii)

english: Can I use the exact same fertilizer for my maize as I do for my pepper plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ amli lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛha mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Different crops have different appetites. Maize needs a lot of Nitrogen to grow tall and leafy, while pepper plants need different amounts of Potassium and Phosphorus to produce plenty of good fruits.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yɛ niyenii he akɔnɔi srɔtoi. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ ni ehiɛ baai. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ tsei biɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus babaoo koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai babaoo.

english: How does potassium help my crops, and why is it important?
ga: Te potassium yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa lɛ?

english: Potassium works like food that gives plants strong immunity. It thickens plant stems so they don't fall over in high winds and helps fruits grow large, juicy, and healthy.
ga: Potassium tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nii ni gbeɔ helai lɛ amli hewalɛ. Ehaa tsei ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni amɛkagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ koni amɛdara, amɛmli nu, ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Why are extension officers advising me to test my farm soil before buying fertilizer this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ maka mishikpɔŋ lɛ makwɛ dani mahe ŋmɔshi nibii afi nɛɛ?

english: Testing your soil shows you exactly which food is missing and which is already present, so you only buy the specific nutrients your land needs instead of wasting money on the wrong fertilizer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa baatsɔɔ bo niyenii mli nibii ni elaaje kɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ momo lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ pɛ oheɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa lɛ he lɛ.

english: I have always used NPK 15-15-15 for all my crops, so why is that no longer recommended for every field?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mikɛ NPK 15-15-15 tsuɔ nii kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ ajieee lɛ yi dɔŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔji fɛɛ lɛ?

english: NPK 15-15-15 gives an equal amount of three nutrients everywhere, but your soil might already have enough of one nutrient while starving for another. A fixed blend can waste money or fail to feed your crop properly.
ga: NPK 15-15-15 lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ etɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he fɛɛ he. Shi ekolɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome yɛ be mli ni hɔmɔ yeɔ ekroko. Nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha ofite shika loo enyɛŋ eha oŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer yields every year even though I apply standard fertilizer every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yibii lɛ baa shi daa afi lɛ? Ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ woɔ mli daa afi?

english: Standard fertilizers only replace major nutrients like Nitrogen, but over time, farming removes other essential micro-nutrients from the soil that basic fertilizers do not replenish.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ niyenii mli nibii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen pɛ najiaŋ. Shi yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, Okwaayeli jieɔ niyenii bibii krokomɛi ni he hiaa waa lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli. kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛŋ awo mli ekoŋŋ lɛ mli

english: How do I know the correct amount of fertilizer to put on my farm so I do not burn my plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Bɔni afee ni mikashã tso lɛ?

english: The right amount depends on what your soil already contains and what crop you are planting. Testing your soil gives you an exact recipe so you feed the plant without burning its roots.
ga: Nɔ ni sa lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ momo lɛ kɛ tsei srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ anɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa baaha bo fɔmula pɔtɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oha tsei lɛ niyenii ni oshãaa amɛshishifãi lɛ.

english: Are there other hidden plant foods my crops need besides the main NPK fertilizer?
ga: Ani tsei niyenii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni he hiaa mi tsei lɛ yɛ shishijee NPK ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, plants also need secondary elements and micro-nutrients like calcium and magnesium, which they require in smaller amounts to grow strong stems and green leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei hu he miihia nibii ni ji enyɔ kɛ niyenii bibii tamɔ calcium kɛ magnesium. Ehe miihia ni amɛná fioo fioo koni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛbaai lɛ afee eŋɔli.

english: Why are the leaves on my plants turning yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves are often a sign of nutrient hunger—usually a shortage of Nitrogen or Magnesium—which prevents the leaf from making its natural green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji niyenii mli hewalɛ hɔmɔ he okadi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji nitrogen loo magnesium ni faaa. Enɛ haaa baai lɛ atsake amɛ adebɔɔ mli su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ.

english: Why are my tomatoes rotting at the bottom before they even get a chance to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miifite yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ shishi dani eshɛ po lɛ?

english: Bottom rot in vegetables like tomatoes is usually caused by a lack of calcium in the soil, which is an essential micro-nutrient needed to build tough, healthy fruit skins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shishigbɛ sũ ni fiteɔ yɛ aduawai tamɔ tomato nɔ lɛ baa. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii bibii ni he hiaa koni akɛfee aduawai ahe tsɔi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather. Pruning extra tree branches to let sunlight and air flow through your cocoa farm helps dry out the pods and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji krokomɛi ahe koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ o-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and transfer plant viruses. Spraying neem oil solution or insecticidal soap helps clear these pests and protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ ni ebaatsi baai heei ni baa lɛ anaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes drastically from very dry to very wet. Giving plants consistent water at the roots and shade during extreme hot afternoons helps fruits set properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ ama shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tips in a V-pattern indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Applying well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-based fertilizer around the base of the crop helps restore leaf color and improves grain yields.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi yɛ V su mli, ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ ahe su aku sɛɛ aba ni eha dumɔwui lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it good practice to plant groundnuts or beans on my field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen from the air and store it naturally in their roots. When harvested, the roots decay and leave nitrogen in the soil, which acts as free natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Be ni esa akɛ akpa Shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛshiɔ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to be trained up wooden stakes instead of spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atsɔse mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso nɔ moŋ fe ni aaagbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants need sunlight on as many leaves as possible to make food and grow large underground tubers. Staking keeps leaves lifted toward the sun and prevents fungal diseases that happen when leaves rest on damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking haa baai lɛ tsɔɔ hulu lɛ he ni etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa kɛji baai lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during strong wind and rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily because their root systems are shallow, and subterranean pests like stem borers or nematodes may be damaging them. Supporting heavy fruiting trees with strong wooden Y-fork props prevents them from tipping over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ stem borers loo nematodes. Ebaanyɛ efite plantain tsei. Fi aduawai tsei ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ kɛ Y-shaped fork props ni akɛ tso ni wa fee lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei akagbee shi.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my cassava stems regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ amli daa lɛ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from cassava. Keeping the base of the plant weed-free ensures all available nutrients go directly into swelling the root tubers underground.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ waa. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Is it better for my soil to cut down clearing vegetation to rot or to burn it off before planting?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaafo mishikpɔŋ lɛ loo ashã dani adu nii?

english: Cutting vegetation and leaving it as organic mulch protects topsoil from drying out and feeds beneficial soil organisms. Burning kills good microbes and destroys organic matter that keeps the soil fertile over time.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tsei amli ni ashi amɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebuɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi, ni ehaa sũ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ niyenii. Shãa gbeɔ nibii bibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni efiteɔ nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell under the soil that my cassava roots are ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava roots are typically mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a mostly bare stem, or when the soil begins to crack open around the base of the stalk from expanding roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cassava shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Trunk lɛ mli babaoo bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko. Aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa ehe lɛ. Stem shishitoo kɛjɛ shishifãi ni mli lɛɛɔ

english: Why do I have to re-spray my crops with pesticide if it rains right after I finish spraying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ ekoŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rain washes the chemical off the leaves before the plant or insects can absorb it. Without enough contact time, the pesticide loses its power, forcing you to repeat the work.
ga: Nugbɔ shwieɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ ahe dani tsei loo kooloi bibii baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛji be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni akɛbaatswa Pesticides lɛ hu fiteɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ehe bahiaa ni otsu nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away the fertilizer I put around my maize crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Fertilizers dissolve easily in water. When heavy rain floods the topsoil, it carries the nutrients away into drainage streams before the maize roots can soak them up.
ga: Nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi oya. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ hoɔ nu. Shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa faai ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ amli dani ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my young tomato leaves turn brown after rain splashes mud onto them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛ muji eshwie amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Soil contains hidden fungal spores. When rain drops hit bare dirt, the splashing mud transfers these fungi directly onto the crop leaves, causing spots and blights.
ga: Fungal spores ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Muji ni shwieɔ shi lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yaa tsei ahe baai amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ baai shãa baa.

english: Why do I sometimes have to replant my farm seeds after a heavy rain storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ ehe bahiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy downpours can wash light seeds completely out of the soil or pack the dirt so hard over them that tiny shoots cannot break through to the surface.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo ŋmaa bibii kɛya. Eje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa. aloo sũ lɛ mli awa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛyashi ŋmeii bibii ni nyɛŋ abote sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings rot in the soil when the rainy season gets too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water fills all the air spaces in the soil, effectively drowning the stem cuttings. Without oxygen, bacteria and fungi quickly cause the wood to decay.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ baaha tsei niji lɛ abote nu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ Bacteria kɛ fungi haa tso lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves turn yellow when rain water stands on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Standing water starves plant roots of air. When roots cannot breathe, they stop taking up food from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow from lack of nutrients.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu lɛ, amɛkpaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii yeli. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my crop flowers drop off the plants during continuous heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much rainwater creates stress in the plant, and heavy drops physically break fragile flower stems. Without flowers, the plant cannot produce fruits.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Ni nu ni shwieɔ shi ni tsii lɛ baanyɛ akumɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe tsei ni waaa lɛ. Kɛji fɔfɔi bɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: Why do black spots spread so fast on my cocoa pods during the wet rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: The fungus that causes Black Pod disease thrives in cool, dirty, wet conditions. Raindrops and high humidity help the fungal spores jump easily from pod to pod.
