ga: Fung ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, muji, kɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔi kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa ŋmeii amli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli oya.

english: Why does driving heavy machinery on wet farm land spoil my crop roots later in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɔnei ni tsii ni akudɔɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi yɛ be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy machines crush wet soil particles close together, creating a hard layer beneath the surface that crop roots cannot easily grow through.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi fã ko ni wa baa shi yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ adara oya lɛ.

english: Why does weed control cost me so much more money during the main rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa mifiteɔ shika babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rain gives weeds optimal growing conditions, causing them to bounce back quickly after clearing and forcing you to repeatedly spend money on clearing or chemicals.
ga: Nugbɔ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha jwɛi lɛ adalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ, amɛhe baa oya. ni enyɛɔ onɔ ni ofiteɔ shika shii abɔ kɛ clearing loo tsofai

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Fast-growing plantain plants produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa.

english: Yellow, curled leaves are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Removing and destroying infected plants early stops the disease from spreading across your entire farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra kɛ amɛhiɛkpatamɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni hela akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I burn the brush on my field when preparing the soil for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa tsei bibii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni misaa shikpɔŋ kɛha dumɔ nii lɛ?

english: Burning kills beneficial insects and destroys topsoil organic matter. Clearing without burning allows the plant waste to decay naturally into organic manure, keeping the soil fertile for longer.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ, ni efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ lɛ. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashãaa lɛ haa tsei amli jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting my maize seeds too close together result in smaller cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛfeɔ bibii lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded, they compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough resources to produce large, healthy ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do my pepper leaves wilt and drop off during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind pulls moisture out of plant leaves much faster than roots can drink from dry soil. Plants shed leaves naturally to conserve water and protect themselves from completely drying out.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛtsi amɛhe koni amɛkagbi kwraa.

english: Why is it a mistake to spread fertilizer on my crops right before a big rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji tɔmɔ akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli ŋmɔshi nii dani nugbɔ wulu ko aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash fertilizer away from the crop roots into nearby paths and gutters. This wastes your money and deprives the crops of the food they need.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli kɛyaa gbɛjegbɛi kɛ nu ŋshɔi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha ofite shika ni ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa bo lɛ akaje onibii amli.

english: Why should I trim off the small extra stems growing on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Jiemɔ shweremɔ ni fa fe nine yɛ tomato tso lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Removing extra side branches (suckers) forces the plant to send its energy and water into producing bigger, healthier fruits rather than unnecessary foliage.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ (tso lɛ tsei) ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu woɔ yibii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts on my plot after I harvest my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nitrogen food out of the soil. Groundnuts and beans put natural nitrogen back into the dirt, restoring fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanuts kɛ beans haa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Koni ekɛ babaoo aba ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli ekoŋŋ

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from hybrid maize to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid corn mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce a high yield only for their first planting. Seeds saved from that harvest lose their strength, resulting in weak plants and a low yield.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo pɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why is weeding my farm during the first four weeks after planting so important?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa waa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ ni mikɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are small and easily choked by fast-growing weeds. Clearing weeds early ensures the young crop gets all available sunlight and soil food to build strong roots.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ ji bibii ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ shwieɔ amɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa.

english: How far in advance should I start clearing my land before planting my crops?
ga: Te esa akɛ mabɔi he lɛ mli shwiemɔ dani madu nii kɛtsɔ hiɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Starting land clearing about three months before planting gives you enough time to clear heavy bush, plant shade trees, and allow cut plant material to break down naturally into useful soil nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ obɔi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ aaafee nyɔji etɛ dani odu nii lɛ, ebaaha oná be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛjie jwɛi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni eyi obɔ lɛ. Dumɔ tsei koni eha hulutsoo. ni eha tso lɛ mli nibii ni afo lɛ afite yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni etsɔ niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What is the best timeline to follow when converting bushland into a healthy farm field?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaatsake koo shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Begin by clearing the bush and planting shade or permanent trees about three months early, allowing the cleared plant debris to decompose before sowing your main crops.
ga: Je shishi kɛtsɔ tsei bibii ni oootsi kɛ hulutsoo loo tsei ni baahi shi daa lɛ adumɔ nɔ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mra. Enɛ ji koni eha tso lɛ mli jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ afite dani odu onibii titri lɛ.

english: Why should I plant trees on my farm months before I plant my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔji babaoo dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ?

english: Planting trees early allows them time to establish roots and grow big enough to provide vital shade, wind protection, and moisture retention for your main crops when they are introduced later.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ mra Enɛ haa tsei lɛ be ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛhaa hulutsoo, kɔɔyɔɔ hebuu, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtoɔ onibii titrii lɛ ahe kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kpo yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do farmers plant shade trees before introducing main crops like cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ dani amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo ba lɛ?

english: Young crops can easily burn under direct sunlight; establishing shade trees early creates a protective canopy cover that shields delicate young plants during their critical early growth.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Afee tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ mra Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ.

english: Is it okay to plant young tree seedlings while the land still has cleared bush lying around?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu tsei bibii yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ jwɛi ni agbele naa lolo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Yes, young trees can be planted right after clearing because the vegetation left on the ground acts as natural mulch, keeping the soil cool and moist around the saplings.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu tsei bibii. Beni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: What should I do with the branches and bush I cut down while clearing my forest land?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee tsei niji kɛ tsei bibii ni mifo beni mijieɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: You can leave cut vegetation on the land; over a few months, it dries out and naturally decomposes into organic matter that enriches the soil without harming your future crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ oshi tsei ni afolɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ. yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli lɛ Egbiɔ ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ shweremɔ ni eyeee onibii ni obaakwɛ wɔsɛɛ lɛ awui.

english: Will leaving dead weeds and cleared plant materials on my farm field hurt my soil before planting?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni egboi kɛ tsei ahe nibii ni ajie yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafite mishikpɔŋ lɛ dani midu?

english: No, left-over vegetation rots naturally into compost, adding organic nutrients back into the soil and protecting it from sun drying and erosion.
ga: Dabi, aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ baagboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔshi nibii. Okɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni egbiɔ kɛ shwiemɔ he.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds immediately on the same day I finish clearing the forest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ gbi nɔŋŋ ni ajieɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Freshly cleared land needs time for cut plant material to settle and decay into natural nutrients, creating a safer and richer soil environment for your seeds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ ehee lɛ he miihia be dani tsei ahe nibii ni afo lɛ ahi shi ni amɛgbala amɛhe amɛwo adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli nibii amli. Bɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni yɔɔ nii babaoo kɛha odumɔwui lɛ.

english: Does clearing my farm months early affect how well my crops will grow later?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni ajieɔ nyɔji babaoo kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ baaná ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Clearing months ahead gives plant debris time to decay into mulch and allows the soil environment to stabilize, making it much easier for your crops to establish.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie nyɔji babaoo kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, ehaa tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ naa be ni amɛgbalaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishitoo feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: If I cut down the bush on my farm plot, how long does the land need before it is ready for crops?
ga: Kɛji mifo jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Giving the cleared land around three months allows cut vegetation to break down and gives tree saplings time to settle before you introduce seasonal crops.
ga: Kɛ́ oha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli aaafee nyɔji etɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efo aduawai ni afo lɛ amli, ni eha dumɔwui lɛ aná be ni amɛhi shi dani okɛ be mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ awo mli.

english: Why do my lettuce plants spoil so quickly if I leave them in the field for a few days after they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-lettuce tsei lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli gbii fioo komɛi beni amɛdara sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Lettuce is a very delicate, tender leafy vegetable. Once it reaches full maturity, it rapidly spoils or turns bitter in the heat, so it must be harvested immediately to avoid crop loss.
ga: Lettuce ji tsofa ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. Kɛ́ eda kwraa lɛ, efiteɔ oya loo efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ ashã la. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ŋmɔshi nibii akafite.

english: Can I leave my mature cabbage in the farm for a while if I do not have farm hands ready to harvest immediately?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi kaaba ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be fioo? Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ mli niji bɛ ni efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, cabbage is much hardier than tender leafy greens. Even if you cannot find workers right away, cabbage can safely wait in the field for about two weeks after reaching maturity before you harvest it.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kaabaji wa kwraa fe ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Kɛji akɛ onyɛɛɛ ona nitsulɔi amrɔ nɔŋŋ po. Shi kaabe baanyɛ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli shweshweeshwe aaafee otsii enyɔ beni edara sɛɛ dani akpa.

english: If I am growing both lettuce and cabbage on my farm, which one should I prioritize harvesting first?
ga: Kɛji midu lettuce kɛ cabbage fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli. Mɛɛ kpamɔ nɔ̃ esa akɛ mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: You should always harvest lettuce first because it is urgent and spoils quickly once ready. Cabbage is less urgent and can safely wait in the soil for about two extra weeks while you manage your time and labor.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa lettuce klɛŋklɛŋ be fɛɛ be ejaakɛ ehe miihia oya ni efiteɔ oya kɛji afee klalo. Kaabaji he ehiaaa oya ni ebaanyɛ emɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe otsii enyɔ kroko loo nɔ ni fe nakai be mli ni okwɛɔ be kɛ nitsumɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why can cabbage stay longer in the ground after maturity compared to lettuce?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni cabbage baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ, kɛ akɛto lettuce he lɛ?

english: Cabbage forms a tight, firm head that protects its inner layers from quick decay, whereas lettuce has open, fragile leaves that expose it to fast spoilage once it completes its growth stage.
ga: Cabbage yɛ yitso ni mli wa ni buɔ emli fã lɛ he kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ oya he. Lettuce, yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, eyɛ baai ni waaa, ni agbele ni haa kaabeji lɛ fiteɔ oya be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: What happens if I delay harvesting my vegetable crops past their normal maturity time?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ aduawai akpamɔ be sɛɛ fe be ni ato lɛ?

english: The impact depends on the crop type. Delicate vegetables like lettuce will spoil and rot quickly in the field, while resilient crops like cabbage can delay harvest for up to two weeks without losing quality.
ga: Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ lettuce fiteɔ ni egboɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi tamɔ kaaba lɛ, abaanyɛ atsake ŋmaa lɛ kɛyashi otsii enyɔ ni nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ efooo.

english: How many extra days can cabbage remain safely in the farm after it is ready for harvest?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ krokomɛi baanyɛ ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe beni efee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cabbage can generally remain safely unharvested in the field for about two weeks after reaching maturity before it begins to spoil or crack.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, kaabe baanyɛ ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe ni akpaaa lɛ aaafee otsii enyɔ yɛ be mli ni edara sɛɛ dani ebɔi fitemɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Which vegetable crops require urgent harvesting as soon as they mature?
ga: Mɛɛ aduawai ehe hiaa ni akpa oya kɛji amɛshɛ shweremɔ he pɛ?

english: Tender leafy vegetables like lettuce require immediate harvesting upon reaching maturity because any delay leads to rapid spoilage and financial loss.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akpa aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ lettuce lɛ kɛji amɛdara jogbaŋŋ pɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, yɛ sɛɛkuu fɛɛ sɛɛkuu hewɔ lɛ, ebaaha efite oya ni shika hu afite.

english: Can I sell my cabbage or lettuce crops to buyers while they are still growing in the field?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ cabbage loo lettuce tsei maha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ be mli ni amɛmiikwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, you can negotiate and sell your standing crop to traders before harvesting begins. This secures your buyer early so you can harvest at the exact right time.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli ni ohɔ̃ɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ oha jarayelɔi dani ŋmaakpamɔ aje shishi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ ahiɔ shi shweshweeshwe mra. Bɔni afee ni nyɛkpa nii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Can I hold off on harvesting my vegetables to wait for market prices to go up?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafo aduawai akpamɔ mli koni mamɛ ni jara nɔ jara aya hiɛ?

english: You can only do this with certain crops like cabbage, which allows you to delay harvest by about two weeks. Delicate crops like lettuce cannot wait for better prices and must be harvested immediately to prevent spoilage.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei komɛi pɛ afee enɛ, tamɔ kaabe, ni baaha okɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo aaafee otsii enyɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ lettuce nyɛŋ amɛmɛ jara kpakpa. ni esa akɛ akpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni akafite

english: How early should I start finding buyers for delicate crops like lettuce?
ga: Te esa akɛ mabɔi mɛi ni baahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ lettuce lɛ taomɔ oya tɛŋŋ?

english: You should find buyers well before the lettuce matures because once lettuce is ready, it reaches a point where it must be harvested immediately or it will spoil.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooona mɔ ko ni baahe dani ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwere pɛ lɛ, esa akɛ akpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, lettuce lɛ baafite.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build healthy green leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer, or planting beans in that spot beforehand, feeds the soil so the maize can grow strong and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ hi. loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ nakai he lɛ kɛtsɔ hiɛ Ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii koni ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of leaves but produce very thin tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are planted too close together, cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves on top instead of roots below. Giving plants enough space and avoiding excess nitrogen helps the crop direct its food into swelling the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ oha tso lɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eŋɔ niyenii ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani aduawai baa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of insects like bees to move pollen around can cause tomato flowers to drop off unused. Keeping the soil moist around the roots and allowing natural flowering weeds nearby to attract bees helps turn those flowers into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ajie pollen kɛya he fɛɛ he lɛ ni bɛ. Ebaanyɛ eha tomato fɔfɔi lɛ agbo kɛji akɛ akɛtsuuu nii. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Root he lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oha jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii koni eye ebua ni etsɔ nakai fɔfɔi lɛ etsɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden sticks next to my yam plants as they grow vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso masɛi kɛ́ midu wain tsei lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb toward sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking holds the leaves up off the ground so they get maximum sunshine, which helps the plant create and store energy to produce much larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ená hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei feɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ koni amɛkɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting groundnuts or cowpeas before planting maize on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei dani adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are special crops that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the crop is harvested, these roots decompose and leave natural fertilizer behind in the soil for the next crop, like maize, to feed on.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ fiteɔ ni amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛye sɛɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my newly planted plantain suckers take a very long time to produce leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani mi-banana tsei ni midu ehee lɛ woɔ baai lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers must grow an entire network of new roots before they can push out new leaves. If they are planted too shallow, cut improperly, or planted in dry soil, root growth pauses until sufficient moisture and soil depth allow the roots to anchor and drink water.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwu lɛ akwɛ shishifãi heei fɛɛ dani abaanyɛ ajie baai heei kɛjɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, afolɔ ni esaaa loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, aŋmɛɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ emlibotemɔ haa shishifãi lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi ni amɛnuɔ nu.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up like little cups during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ebɔle ehe tamɔ kɔɔpoo bibioo ko lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Leaf curling in high afternoon heat is a plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to strong sunlight and prevent losing water too fast. If the leaves unfold again in the cooler evening, the plant is simply protecting itself from drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛbuɔ ehe koni ekɛba shikpɔŋ ni hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ nɔ lɛ shi, ni ekɛtsiɔ nu ni elaajeɔ oya lɛ naa. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ Tso lɛ miibu ehe kɛkɛ koni ekagbi.

english: Young cocoa plants have thin leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight and need cool, humid air to survive. Shade trees block the harsh sun, lower the surrounding air temperature, and keep the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow old and tough enough to handle direct sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ he miihia amɛ koni amɛhi shi. Tsei haa hɔɔŋ kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ mli. Tsɔɔmɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ nɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baagbɔ ni ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni hulu la lɛ baashɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts that draw water out of living plant tissue, which causes severe chemical burns to stems and main roots. Placing the fertilizer in a ring a short distance away allows the fine feeding roots to safely absorb the nutrients dissolved in the soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmei ni mli eyi obɔ ni jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ amli lɛ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa tsofa shãa tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi titrii lɛ waa. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ fioo lɛ haa shishifãi ni yeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni mli ewo muji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes in the soft leaf funnels of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars, often Fall Armyworm, target the tender young leaves inside the central funnel of the maize plant because it is soft and nutritious. Applying recommended natural treatments like neem extract or recommended powders directly into the funnel early stops them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ gbeeɔ shi akɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ejaakɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni eyɛ hewalɛ waa Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni ajieɔ yi tamɔ neem mli nu loo powda wo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akpa amɛ dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: How soon after my seeds sprout should I transplant them to the main field?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ majie dumɔwui lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ?

english: Most vegetable seedlings need to be moved within three to four days after sprouting or once they develop their first set of true leaves. Moving them at this stage prevents root crowding and helps them adapt quickly to the main field.
ga: Ehe miihia ni adu aduawai amli dumɔwui babaoo yɛ gbii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ loo beni dumɔwui lɛ ná amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ baai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli oya.

english: What is the best time of day for me to move my young sprouts out to the farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu dumɔwui kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to move seedlings early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the sun is mild. Hot midday sun will shock and dry out fragile young roots, causing the plants to die.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui lɛ leebi loo shwane mli. ni ji be ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaha shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji tso lɛ gbele.

english: What happens if I leave my sprouted crops in the nursery bed for too long before moving them?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi tsei ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani mikɛ amɛ tee he kroko?

english: If seedlings stay in the nursery too long, their roots get tangled and choked, making the plant weak. When you finally move them, they struggle to grow well and will yield less crop.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ehi ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ Kɛ́ otsi amɛ yɛ naagbee lɛ Ebaafee nɔ ni wa akɛ amɛakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo.

english: Why do my seeds take longer than three days to break through the soil after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be fe gbii etɛ dani amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seed germination speed depends on soil moisture, depth, and temperature. Planting seeds too deep or in dry soil slows down sprouting, while proper watering helps seeds break through in just a few days.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃mɔ oyaiyeli damɔ sũ mli fɛ̃i, emlibotemɔ kɛ dɔlɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃mɔ aya hiɛ fioo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni sa ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli.

english: Why are my young crop seedlings turning yellow and looking weak just days after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow and sickly seedlings are usually caused by overwatering, poor drainage, or a lack of light. Too much water suffocates the young roots, preventing them from feeding the seedling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni awoɔ amɛ fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ baa. nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo la ni bɛ Nu babaoo baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ agbɔjɔ. Tsi dumɔwui lɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ naa.

english: What causes my seeds to sprout but then suddenly collapse and die within three to four days?
ga: Mɛni ha midumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ trukaa lɛ? Ani efoɔ ni egboɔ yɛ gbii etɛ loo ejwɛ mli?

english: This is often caused by a fungal infection called 'damping-off,' which thrives in overly wet nursery soil. Keeping soil damp but not soaked and ensuring good airflow stops this disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ necrotizing fasciitis lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ‘Damping’, ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ fe nine nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni eha efee ŋmɔlɔ shi ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ akafee Ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni tsɔɔ mli lɛ baaha hela nɛɛ akpa.

english: How can I tell if a young seedling is healthy enough to survive being planted on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ahe wa lolo bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A strong seedling has bright green leaves, a firm stem, and healthy white root tips. Avoid planting seedlings that look stunted, pale, or burnt at the stem base.
ga: Tsei bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baaná baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ shishifãi yɛŋ ni mli wa Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eshã yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ dumɔ he.

english: Why do my sprouted seedlings look tall and thin instead of growing strong and thick stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Seedlings stretch and become thin when they don't get enough sunlight. They stretch searching for light, making them flimsy. Giving them controlled sunlight strengthens their stems.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbala ni amɛbaafee bibioo kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Amɛkpãa amɛhe, ni amɛtaoɔ la. make it fragile Hulu la ni akudɔɔ ni akɛhaa lɛ baaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Why do some of my young crops fail to take root firmly in the soil after being planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ ekomɛi nyɛɛɛ ashishifãi awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crops fail to root if the soil is packed too hard or too dry. Loosening the topsoil and adding organic compost gives fragile new roots a soft, moist environment to grow deep.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ bibii nyɛŋ atswa shishifãi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo egbi tsɔ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi heei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ aná he ko ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How much water do my young crop sprouts need right after they emerge from the ground?
ga: Nu enyiɛ he hiaa mi dumɔwu lɛ beni eje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young sprouts need light, frequent watering every morning or evening. You should keep the top layer of soil moist like a wrung-out sponge, but never leave standing water around the stems.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni afɔ amɛ nu fioo ni afɔ amɛ shii abɔ daa leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Esa akɛ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ sponji ni ajie lɛ kpo. Shi kaahã nu tara tso lɛ he.

english: Why should I plant improved laboratory seeds instead of saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ laboratori ni atsake lɛ mli lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ je ngma kpami nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ kɛ to.

english: Improved seeds are carefully bred to survive local Ghanaian weather, resist common pests, and yield far more food than seeds saved from previous harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ Ghana maŋ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ, ni ewoɔ niyenii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do some crops need to start in a protected nursery before I move them to my main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ aje ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ashishi yɛ ŋmɔ ni abuɔ he lɛ mli dani ajie kɛya miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The nursery stage creates a safe foundation for young crops, protecting delicate seedlings from harsh sun and heavy rain until they build strong roots to survive in the main field.
ga: Nursery stage lɛ feɔ shishitoo ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha tsei bibii. Buu dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. kɛyashi amɛbaatswa shishifãi ni wa koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli

english: Why do my crops grow bigger and yield more food when I plant them in straight lines with proper spacing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Proper line spacing ensures each plant gets its fair share of sunlight, air, and soil nutrients without competing against neighboring crops.
ga: Line ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa nɔ ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: How can I produce enough crops to feed my household and still have extra left to take to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mahã mishiabii lɛ niyenii, ni maná eko ni eshwɛ lolo ni mikɛya jara nɔ?

english: By adopting structured farming systems—such as planting high-yielding crop varieties and applying nutrients properly—your land's output will increase, giving you enough to eat and sell.
ga: Kɛtsɔ okwaayeli gbɛjianɔtoo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Yibiiwoo ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaya hiɛ. Ehaa onáa nii ni oyeɔ ni ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why is the early growth stage of my crops so critical for my final harvest size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ he hiaa yɛ mi naagbee ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ?

english: The initial growth stage lays the foundation for the plant's health; if a young plant is stressed or neglected early on, it will remain weak and produce very low yields.
ga: Shishijee dalɛ fã lɛ ji shishitoo nɔ kɛha tsei ahewalɛ. Kɛji akɛ anyɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ loo aku hiɛ ashwie nɔ mra lɛ, Tsei bibii lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni amɛbaafee nɔ ni baa shi kwraa.

english: Why are my cassava plants rotting while my neighbor's crop is growing healthy in the same soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ miifite yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Your neighbor is likely using improved, disease-resistant plant varieties that have been developed to fight off common soil diseases and viruses.
ga: Ekolɛ okutsoŋbii lɛ kɛ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni afee koni akɛwu ashi helai kɛ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ miitsu nii.

english: What is the benefit of changing from my traditional farming habits to a modern step-by-step crop management system?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ mi blema okwaayeli nifeemɔi lɛ amli tsakemɔ kɛmiiya ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ni tsɔɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ mli lɛ he?

english: Following a modern system guides you through the right steps at every growth stage, reducing waste and increasing your harvest so you move from basic survival to profitable farming.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni ooonyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baakudɔ bo yɛ gbɛi ni ja nɔ yɛ dalɛ fã fɛɛ fã mli. Tsɔɔmɔ nibii ni ofiteɔ lɛ shi ni oha nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Koni eha oya kɛjɛ shishijee shihilɛ mli kɛya okwaayeli ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if my growing crops are getting enough food from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsei ni miduɔ lɛ miiná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy crops display vibrant green leaves and sturdy stems; pale or yellowish leaves mean the soil lacks key nutrients, which can be fixed with manure or fertilizer.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ kɛ tsei ni wa. Baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii asaa enɛ.

english: Why do new crop varieties stay green during short dry spells while my traditional crops dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei hiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mishishijee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho lɛ

english: New crop varieties are often bred to grow deeper roots, allowing them to draw moisture from deep underground when surface water disappears during dry periods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ tsei srɔtoi heei koni amɛshishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ajieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ laaje yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: How does caring for my harvested crops properly help me get better prices at the market?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mikpamɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni minine shɛɔ jara kpakpa nɔ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Proper drying and storage protect harvested produce from insects and mold, maintaining quality so you can sell your surplus when market demand and prices are highest.
ga: Kɛ́ ogbi ni okɛto jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ okpamɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi kɛ ŋmeii ahe. Ehaa nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni onyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ be mli ni jarayeli nibii kɛ jara lɛ yaa hiɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow root systems that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Planting taller, fast-growing crops like plantain or banana alongside young cocoa creates living shade that cools the plant and preserves soil moisture until the cocoa is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni daa oya ni amɛkwɔ, tamɔ plantain loo banana lɛ adumɔ. Enɛ, kɛ kookoo bibioo lɛ, haa hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ mli waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves with tiny dark droppings inside the plant center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar pest that feeds on the young, soft leaves inside the heart of the maize plant. Catching the infestation early and applying recommended organic or chemical treatments directly into the funnel of the plant protects the growing tip from being destroyed.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Ni aaamɔ helai ni baa mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baatsu nii lɛ baabu ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe kɛjɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why does my farmland yield much smaller harvests now compared to when I first started farming it five years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe beni mibɔi okwaayeli afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Crops remove nutrients from the soil every time they grow and are harvested. Without replacing those nutrients using animal manure, compost, or crop fertilizers, or giving the field a break to rest, the soil becomes tired and depleted, resulting in lower crop yields.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni akpaa amɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ kooloi aŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsakeee nakai niyenii lɛ, loo ahaaa hegbɛ ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaagbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the ground when I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season often heats up the dry soil without penetrating deep enough, creating a hot, wet environment that promotes fungus and rots seeds before they can sprout. It is safer to wait until the rains become steady and the soil stays moist and cool.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni efooo mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni fiteɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ anɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ lolo.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves off the ground to catch sunlight to make food for their underground tubers. Staking also keeps the leaves off wet soil, preventing fungal diseases and allowing the tubers to grow larger.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛkɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ agbo

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and fall off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plants experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of specific soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping the moisture in the soil consistent with regular watering and protecting plants from extreme drying winds helps the flowers form healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ calcium ni bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ daa kɛ tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready to harvest since they grow under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ejaakɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready for harvest when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil base around the stem begins to crack as the tubers swell beneath. Digging up one plant to check tuber size after 9 to 12 months helps confirm readiness.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni sũ ni yɔɔ shishi ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shishi lɛ. Tso kome ni aaakumɔ koni akwɛ bulb lɛ dalɛ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ama hesaamɔ nɔ mi.

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight one another for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each seed proper spacing ensures every plant receives enough food and light to produce full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko to dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass or palm leaves around my crops help them grow better during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei tsei ashwã he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, keeps the sun from evaporating water from the soil and blocks sunlight from weed seeds so they cannot sprout, keeping moisture around your crop roots longer.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni otsi hulu lɛ naa kɛjɛ jwɛi dumɔwui ahe koni amɛkakwɛ̃. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ otsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do my dried maize grains get eaten by tiny beetles and turn to dust while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-abele dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ ni amɛmiitsɔ sũ be mli ni akɛtoɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grain weevils attack stored maize if the grains are not dried completely before storage or if the storage space allows air and moisture in. Sun-drying the maize until it is hard and storing it in clean, sealed bags or airtight containers prevents weevils from surviving and multiplying.
ga: Dumɔwui amli ŋmeii baatutua ŋmãa ni ato lɛ kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto. Aloo kɛji akɛ he ni akɛ nibii lɛ toɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ boteɔ mli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa kɛyashi ewa ni akɛto kotoku ko ni mli tse ni atsĩ naa loo nɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkahi shi ni amɛshwere.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow after continuous heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes essential nutrients like nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach them. Excessive water also suffocates plant roots, preventing maize from making the green chlorophyll needed for healthy growth.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Nu babaoo hu haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Etsiɔ ŋmãa naa koni ekafee klorofil eŋɔli ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans on the land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ mli beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Legumes like cowpeas and beans capture nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil through their roots, naturally restoring fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ baa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off in the dry season without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when afternoon temperatures get too high or water is scarce. Heat stresses the plant and damages pollen, preventing flowers from turning into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. Dɔlɛ haa tsei haoɔ ni efiteɔ pollen. Tsi fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkatsɔ tomato.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl upward during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense mechanism. The plant closes its pores and rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, preventing excess moisture from evaporating into the hot air.
ga: Baai lɛ ni abɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he. Tsei lɛ ŋaa amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfoɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ amɛhiɛ lɛ akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop producing fruits when the soil gets too dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ yibii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lɛ?

english: Water acts as a bus transporting nutrients from soil to fruit. Without steady moisture, pepper plants drop their flowers and stop fruiting to conserve energy and stay alive.
ga: Nu tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be bɛ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during windy storms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that stay near the surface. When heavy rains soften the soil and fruit bunches grow heavy, strong winds easily tip the plant over because its roots cannot anchor deeply.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Ni aduawai akui lɛ tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa haa tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛma shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do yam tubers grow deep downwards while cassava tubers spread out sideways?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni cassava ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa afãi lɛ?

english: Yams naturally grow downwards into deep, soft soil searching for moisture and food, while cassava forms modified storage roots that spread outward in the upper, air-rich layer of soil.
ga: Sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni mli tse mli shɔŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni eyatao ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii. Beni ŋmei woɔ shishifãi ni atsake ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kponɔgbɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why does cassava rot in the ground if I leave it unharvested for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛji akɛ ashi be kakadaŋŋ ni akpaaa ŋmei lɛ, ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Over-mature cassava tubers lose their resistance to soil organisms. When left in damp soil past maturity, fungi and bacteria invade the starch-rich roots, causing them to break down and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛshi shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛyashi ebaada jogbaŋŋ. Fungi kɛ bacteria boteɔ shishifãi ni starch eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and dry up during the wet rainy months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nu hoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, humid conditions. Splash from raindrops spreads microscopic fungal spores from the soil onto the pods, causing them to turn black.
ga: Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni mli edɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Nugbɔshiimɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ gbɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni anaa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ amli. Ha etsɔ ediŋŋ

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and stronger than the vegetable seeds I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe aduawai dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants fully adapted to local soil conditions and aggressively fight for light, water, and nutrients, whereas cultivated crops rely on human care to grow.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni wa ni ekɛ ehe kpãa gbee kwraa kɛha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. ni amɛwuɔ amɛhaa la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, yɛ be mli ni tsei damɔɔ adesa kwɛmɔ nɔ koni amɛdara.

english: Can I plant corn and plantains together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting corn alongside plantains works well because corn grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, giving you quick food and income while the slower-growing plantains take time to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ plantains masɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Na niyenii kɛ shika oya. Yɛ be mli ni plantains lɛ daa blɛoo lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná be dani amɛdara.

english: What happens if I plant my plantain suckers too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: If plantains are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin stalks and much smaller bunches of fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛfeɔ ekãa ni amɛkɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ aduawai bibii waa baa.

english: Plantain plants produce small side-shoots called suckers at their base. When you cut down the main stem after harvest, one strong sucker takes over to grow into the next bearing plant.
ga: Plantains woɔ ŋmeii bibii. Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ akɛ shoo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ. Kɛji ofo tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ yibii ni mli wa baaba ni baatsɔ tso ni woɔ yibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my plantains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa plantain lɛ?

english: Plantains are ready to harvest when the individual fruits become plump and lose their sharp green corners, but before the skin turns yellow on the plant.
ga: Plantains efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shwieɔ shi ni eshishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ. Shi dani hewolo lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ

english: How can I make sure I am planting a good plantain variety that yields big fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ miidu dumɔwui kpakpai ni woɔ yibii wuji?

english: You can get high-yielding varieties by obtaining healthy suckers from a trusted local farmer's successful farm or from an agricultural extension nursery that provides certified disease-free suckers.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona ŋmeii srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ooona kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ lɛ aŋmɔji ni yeɔ omanye lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli tsei akwɛmɔhei ni kɛ tsei ni helai bɛ mli ni awo he odase akɛ amɛhaa lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young corn plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young corn usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen fertilizer or the plants are getting waterlogged. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi tso lɛ mli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my corn stalks fall over when strong winds and rain come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli lɛ?

english: Corn falls over when its roots are too shallow or weak. Heap soil higher around the base of the stalks (earthing up) during weeding to anchor the plants firmly against wind.
ga: Abele baagbee shi kɛji eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo ebɛ hewalɛ. Okɛ sũ lɛ ato shishitoo lɛ he (okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ) yɛ jwɛi shwiemɔ be mli koni tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ he.

english: What is the best way to prevent my harvested plantains from going to waste before I sell them?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ matsi mi-plantain ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Harvest plantains while they are firm and green, keep them out of direct sunlight in a cool shaded shelter, and handle the bunches carefully to prevent bruising that causes rapid decay.
ga: Kpaa plantains lɛ be mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔji lolo lɛ. Kɛto he ko ni hulu la shɛɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Ni okɛ ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ koni akafee ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa oya lɛ.

english: What type of soil manure helps plantains produce heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa plantains lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔji ni mli tse?

english: Plantains grow best in rich soil fed with decomposed animal manure, compost, or decayed crop waste, which holds moisture and provides continuous nutrients to the roots.
ga: Plantains kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni akɛ kooloi ashishifãi ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egboi ewo mli lɛ nɔ. Amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛhaa shishifãi lɛ niyenii ni yaa nɔ.

english: Why do some farmers get high prices like 100 cedis for a single plantain bunch while others get far less?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi naa jara ni nɔ kwɔ tamɔ cedis 100 kɛha plantains ŋmɔ kome lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni okwaafoi krokomɛi naa jara ni baa shi kwraa lɛ?

english: Buyers pay premium prices for large, well-nourished bunches of popular local varieties that are harvested at the right maturity stage without bruises or pest damage.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ waa kɛha maŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii srɔtoi babaoo ni ehe gbɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Akpaa amɛ yɛ be ni sa ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efiteee amɛ.

english: Can I take parts of the crop I just harvested and plant them directly back into my farm for the next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ maŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa amrɔ nɛɛ ekomɛi ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Yes, many traditional crops like cassava, yams, and sweet potatoes can be replanted using stems, vines, or tubers saved from your harvest, which saves you money on buying fresh seeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ adu blema nibii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ ŋmei kɛtsɔ ŋmeii, wain tsei, loo ŋmeii ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaha okɛ shika akafite yɛ dumɔwui heei ahemɔ mli.

english: How do I choose the best plants from my harvest to save as planting material for next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛto akɛ dumɔ nibii kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Always select planting material from your strongest, healthiest plants that showed no signs of disease or pest damage, as healthy parent plants yield stronger stems and seeds.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, halamɔ nibii ni akɛduɔ nii kɛjɛɔ tsei ni wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ he okadi ko bɛ mli lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ ji akɛ, tso nyɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baawo shishifãi kɛ dumɔwui ni mli wa.

english: Why do some crops grow and mature better during the dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛshwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Certain crops thrive in high sunlight and warm temperatures with lower humidity because heavy rainfall can cause root rot or fungal diseases, provided they receive enough ground moisture early on.
ga: Tsei komɛi yeɔ omanye yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be faaa lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo loo tsɛŋemɔ hela aba. Kɛji onine shɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mra.

english: How do I know when my dry season crops are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi tsei ni miduɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Crops usually show clear physical signs when mature, such as leaves turning yellow or drying up, stems becoming firm, or tubers reaching their full size underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ baai ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛgbiɔ. Tso lɛ jeɔ shishi ewaa. loo shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni dalɛ yeɔ emuu

english: Why do my plants dry up and die before producing yields when the heat gets too intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ?

english: When soil moisture drops and heat is high, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the ground, causing them to wilt and stop developing yield.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ba shi ni la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gboɔ ni ehaaa ewo yibii.

english: What practical steps can I take on my farm to get a bigger harvest yield from my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: To maximize yield, ensure proper plant spacing, clear weeds early so they do not steal plant nutrients, and apply organic manure or fertilizer at the right growth stages.
ga: Bɔni afee ni nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ Kwɛmɔ ni gbɛ ni sa ahi tsei lɛ ateŋ. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. koni akaju tsei amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ atsu nii yɛ dalɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my harvest yields decrease when I keep planting the same crop on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly exhausts specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to build up; rotating different crops helps rest the soil and restores its fertility naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ anɔ lɛ shwereɔ amɛhe Nibii srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni ehaa ebɔɔ su mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How does sunlight affect the speed at which my crops grow and yield fruit?
ga: Te hulu la lɛ saa bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Sunlight provides the energy crops need to make food and fill out fruits or tubers, so healthy exposure to sun helps crops mature faster and produce heavier yields.
ga: Hulu la haa tsei hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛwo amɛyibii loo amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, hulu la ni sa lɛ baaye abua tsei ni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: What is the best time of day for me to harvest my crops during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to harvest early in the morning when temperatures are cool, as harvesting in intense midday heat causes crops to lose moisture quickly and spoil faster.
ga: Esa akɛ akpa lɛ leebi maŋkpa be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ akpa tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya, ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: How can I store my harvested stems or seeds safely so they do not rot before I plant them again?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ tsei loo dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ato shweshweeshwe? Koni ekafite dani adu ekoŋŋ

english: Store your planting materials in a well-ventilated, cool, and dry shaded area elevated off the bare ground to protect them from heat damage, excess humidity, and pests.
ga: Okɛ tso lɛ he nibii lɛ ato he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni awo nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni abu nibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni efiteɔ lɛ he Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow before the corn is even mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ po shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means your soil is running low on nitrogen. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and make food, so applying urea fertilizer or well-composted manure early in the season helps keep the plants healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhaa niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ urea loo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ tsu nii yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize help make my soil richer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means their roots pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the cowpea roots break down, that extra nitrogen feeds the soil and helps your maize grow stronger.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji cowpea shishifãi lɛ fã Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni eye ebua o-corn lɛ ni ewa.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping most of their flowers without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they lack nutrients or are attacked by pests like mirids (akate). Spraying approved insecticides at the right time and providing proper shade and fertilizer helps the tree turn those flowers into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ amɛmli loo kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids lɛ tutua amɛ. Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ kɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ nakai fɔfɔi lɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and turning pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling the whiteflies early using neem oil or recommended sprays helps prevent the virus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Mra be mli whitefly nɔkwɛmɔ Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Is it better to plant my cassava stem cuttings upright or slant them in the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei niji ni ja loo aaatsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slanting angle helps the plant grow deeper roots and produce more tubers, especially in loose, well-drained soil.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo. Titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ etse ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: When planting plantains, should I choose suckers with broad leaves or narrow leaves?
ga: Kɛ́ ookwɛ plantains lɛ, ani esa akɛ ohala tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ loo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo?

english: You should plant suckers with narrow, sword-like leaves because they have stronger food reserves in their base, helping them grow into healthier, higher-yielding plants than broad-leaf suckers.
ga: Esa akɛ odu tsei ni baai bibii ni tamɔ klante yɔɔ mli ejaakɛ amɛyɛ niyenii ni mli wa ni ato yɛ amɛshishi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend staking my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo tso nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaaha amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up into the sunlight so they can make more energy. Direct sunlight on the leaves allows the underground yam tubers to grow much bigger.
ga: Staking baawó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la mli koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, causing them to shed blossoms to protect themselves from losing water. Covering the soil around the plant base with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa chili tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does swamp rice need standing water in the field to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmãa mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Standing water suffocates weeds that compete with the rice for food, while keeping the soil moist so the rice roots can easily absorb nutrients needed to produce full grains.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa jwɛi ni kɛ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ niyenii he akaŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa koni ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ aba lɛ oya.

english: How can I tell if my groundnuts are ready for harvest without digging up my entire field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ kɛha kpamɔ ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can dig up two or three sample plants across the field. If the inside of the pods has dark brown or black markings and the main leaves begin to turn yellow, your groundnuts are ready for harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii enyɔ loo etɛ atsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli yɛ okadii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni baai titrii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-peanuts lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and easily get burned by direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that create living shade, protecting the young cocoa plants from heat and keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni hulu lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tips on lower leaves is a sign of nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow, so when the soil lacks it, the plant steals nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed new upper leaves.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it good for my land to plant groundnuts or beans on a field where I just harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmãa mli kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the ground. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the dirt, which naturally restores nutrients to the soil for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to tie my yam vines to tall bamboo stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ ŋmei tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Lifting yam leaves into the air on stakes helps them catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for big tuber growth. It also keeps leaves off the damp ground, preventing diseases and fungal infections.
ga: Kɛ́ awo sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛtee kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii wuji lɛ adalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaatsiɔ baai anaa koni ekahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: Why do my tomato plants keep dropping their flowers without growing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo yibii ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers usually fall off without producing fruit when temperatures get too hot, when the plant receives irregular watering, or when insects like bees are not visiting the farm to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni afɔɔ tsei anɔ nu be fɛɛ be Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii eyaaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛyawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites hiding under the leaves. As they suck the plant juice, they transmit tiny plant viruses that cause leaves to twist and stunt growth.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. be mli ni amɛmuɔ tso mli nu lɛ Amɛtsɔɔ tso mli helai bibii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni ehaaa amɛdara.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Mikɛ jwɛi baaha miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket that blocks the sun from drying out the earth. It keeps moisture in the soil longer and prevents weeds from taking over your crop beds.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ kuntu ni tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ, ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I place chemical fertilizer directly in the hole with my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts that can chemically burn delicate seeds and young roots. It is best to place fertilizer a short distance away from the seed so roots can reach for it safely as they grow.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsofa ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui kɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ yɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo he ko ni kɛ dumɔwui lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready to harvest without digging up the whole root?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifã lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni okɛ shishifã lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and naturally fall off, leaving a bare stem with leaves only at the top. You will also often see small cracks appearing in the soil right around the base of the stem as tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yitso ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ ni baai yɔɔ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, obaana ŋmeii bibii. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce small yields even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa midumɔ nii lɛ awo yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal applied fertilizers, space, and sunlight away from your main crops. Even with enough water, your crops will stay small and weak because weeds are eating up the plant food.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋwɛi, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otsei titrii lɛ ahe. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo ni amɛhe waaa yɛ jwɛi ni yeɔ jwɛi lɛ ahewɔ.

english: Why does my land stop producing good harvest if I plant maize on it every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛji midu ŋmãa daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land year after year continuously drains the same nutrients without giving the soil time to rebuild. Over time, the land becomes tired and lacks the food your maize needs to grow big ears.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛma ekoŋŋ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baagbɔjɔ ni niyenii ni he hiaa o-ŋmã lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ toi wuji lɛ bɛ.

english: How can I make my soil rich again if I do not have money to buy chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛji mibɛ shika ni mikɛbaahe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: You can enrich your land naturally by adding animal dung, farm compost, or by planting leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts, which naturally feed nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha oshikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Kompost ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli loo kɛtsɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ. ni kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ

english: How can I tell if my farmland has run out of nutrients and needs to be fed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehe miihia ni aha lɛ niyenii?

english: Common signs include crop leaves turning yellow instead of deep green, smaller yields at harvest time, crops taking longer to mature, and the soil becoming hard and easily dried out.
ga: Okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ ji tso baai ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Yibiiwoo ni faaa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni egbiɔ oya

english: Does leaving farm waste like corn stalks on the land help improve the soil?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli jwɛi tamɔ ŋmãa ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo?

english: Yes, leaving crop residues on the field to rot acts as a natural mulch. As they decay, they break down into organic matter that feeds the soil and retains moisture.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni egbo lɛ tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ efite lɛ, egbɛɔ eshwaa ni etsɔɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do people say I should let my land rest when I need to harvest crops every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛɔ akɛ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe lɛ? Be ni esa akɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii daa afi?

english: Resting land allows grass and natural bush to grow and decay, which naturally restores nutrients and rebuilds topsoil structure so the land stays fertile for future generations.
ga: Hejɔɔmɔhei lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛfiteɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ feɔ ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha yinɔi ni baaba lɛ.

english: What crop should I plant after harvesting corn to help the land recover?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ madu yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ koni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: It is best to plant legumes like cowpeas or beans after corn. Legumes fix natural nitrogen into the ground, replenishing the exact food that corn takes away.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Legumes lɛ saa nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. koni akɛto niyenii ni ŋmãa lɛ jieɔ lɛ najiaŋ

english: Will rotating my crops prevent the soil from getting weak?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsakeɔ lɛ baatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbɔjɔ?

english: Yes, different crops feed on different soil nutrients at different depths. Switching crops prevents any single nutrient from being completely exhausted from the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yeɔ niyenii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii komekomei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Does leaving cassava in the ground for a long time ruin the soil for other crops?
ga: Ani kɛ́ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaafite shikpɔŋ ni akɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava is a heavy feeder that draws large amounts of nutrients—especially potassium—out of the soil over a long period. Leaving it in the ground too long leaves the soil dry of nutrients for whatever you plant next.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ji niyenii ni tsii ni gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo. titri lɛ potassium ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Kɛ́ oshi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ agbi.

english: How many years can I keep harvesting plantains from the same suckers on my farm?
ga: Afii enyiɛ manyɛ maya nɔ makpa plantains kɛjɛ ŋmeii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?
