english: Plantains usually produce good fruit for two to three years. After that period, the mother plants weaken, pests build up, and soil nutrients drop, making it necessary to replant with fresh suckers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains woɔ yibii kpakpai afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ. Yɛ nakai be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Pests baafee. ni niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmeii heei atsu nii kɛdu.

english: Why are my young plantain trees growing poorly when planted right next to old cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava dumɔwui bibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ cassava momo masɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots spread wide and feed aggressively. If planted too close together, the cassava steals water and soil nutrients away from the young plantain, slowing down its growth.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ dara ni etsuɔ ​​nii waa. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ lɛ, Cassava juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛjɛɔ plantains bibii amli. Enɛ baaha dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Young cocoa plants have thin leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly in harsh sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain beside them provides the shade and cool soil moisture they need to survive until they are fully grown.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli, tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi amɛbaashɛ amɛdalɛ he.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines high up off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves to catch as much sunlight as possible to grow big tubers. Staking also keeps the foliage off the damp soil, preventing leaves from rotting and spreading fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa baai lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing lots of tall stems and leaves, but producing very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai kakadaji babaoo lɛ? Shi ani eyɛ yitso bibioo waa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, cassava uses all its energy to build leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the underground roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei kɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ tsei ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape and drying out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency. The plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce better yields after I plant pigeon peas on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai beni midu okpo ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pigeon peas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. Their deep roots also break up hard ground, leaving the soil loose and rich in nutrients for the next crop.
ga: Pigeon peas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ hu gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight with the mother plant for nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoot, resulting in bigger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ awuu koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, plantain jwɛi lɛ bafee agbo.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer right before a heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy downpours wash away fertilizer from the topsoil into streams or carry it too deep past the roots before the crops can absorb it, wasting your money.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛyaa faai amli loo emɔɔ mli tsɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ. Shika ni afiteɔ

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from stress caused by extreme heat, dry soil, or sudden changes in water supply. The plant drops flowers to save its own life.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu jɛɛhe tsakemɔ trukaa lɛ mli baa lɛ hewɔ. Tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why do my tomatoes crack open on the sides right before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ afãi dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Tomato fruits split when the plant absorbs a sudden large amount of water after a dry period. The inside of the tomato grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing it to burst.
ga: Tomato yibii lɛ tswaa kɛji tso lɛ shwie nu babaoo trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Tomato lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ be mli ni miyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black pods are caused by a water-loving fungus (Black Pod disease) that thrives in cold, overly damp, and shaded conditions. Clearing excess shade and removing infected pods helps keep the tree dry and healthy.
ga: Hydrophilic fungus (black pod hela) ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ, kɛ he ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Kɛ́ ajieɔ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ, ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is cocoa hand pollination, and how does it help my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nine ni akɛwoɔ kookoo mli lɛ? ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Hand pollination is manually transferring pollen from one flower to another using small tweezers. Naturally, insects only pollinate a small fraction of cocoa flowers, so doing it by hand ensures many more flowers develop into healthy cocoa pods, greatly boosting your yield.
ga: Nɔ ni fata nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ he ji ni akɛ niji ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli kɛtsɔ tsɔne bibii ni akɛfoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, kooloi shwieɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ fã bibioo ko pɛ, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ onine fee enɛ lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo aya hiɛ ni amɛtsɔ kookoo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ waa.

english: How many bags of cocoa can I expect to harvest from one acre of farmland?
ga: Cocoa kotokui enyiɛ manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni ji acre kome nɔ?

english: On average, a traditional farm yields about 3 to 5 bags per acre. However, with improved crop management, proper pruning, hand pollination, and fertilizer, farmers can harvest 15 to 25 bags or more from that same acre.
ga: Kɛ aja mli lɛ, Kusum ŋmɔji woɔ yibii aaafee kotokui 3 kɛyashi 5 yɛ acre kome mli. Shi, kɛji akɛ akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ, akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ Kɛtsɔ nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, okwaafoi baanyɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii 15 kɛyashi 25 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kɛjɛ acre kome mli.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can feed, so the tree drops extra flowers to conserve energy. Excessive flower drop can also be caused by lack of insect pollination, extreme heat, drought, or pest damage.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi krokomɛi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he. Nɔ ni baanyɛ aha fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ aba ji kooloi ni shwieɔ shi fe nine, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii.

english: Why do small green cocoa pods sometimes dry up and turn black before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ No hewɔ lɛ bei komɛi lɛ egbiɔ ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ dani edaa?

english: This is known as cherelle wilt. It happens naturally when the tree has more pods than it can support with water and nutrients, but it can also be worsened by severe dry spells or insect attacks.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherel ni shwieɔ shi. Ebaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ tso ko yɛ ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ ehiɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Shi ebaanyɛ eha ehiɛ afee shoo fe tsutsu lɛ kɛtsɔ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo kooloi ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my cocoa tree if it looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji komɛi kɛji amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead wood, weak branches, and unwanted shoots called chupons. This allows sunlight and air to reach all parts of the tree, reduces fungal diseases like black pod, and directs the tree’s food into producing pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Tso ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei ni egboi, tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ, kɛ tsei ni ataooo ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ hei fɛɛ, ehaa ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji baa shi, ni ehaa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Do mature cocoa trees prefer full sunshine or shade from larger trees?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ sumɔɔ hulu la loo hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni eda lɛ adɛŋ?

english: Mature cocoa trees need a balance of about 30 to 50 percent shade. Too much shade encourages fungal diseases and low fruit production, while full open sun without shade stresses the tree and shortens its lifespan.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ biɔ hulutsoo oha mlijaa 30 kɛyashi 50. Shade babaoo kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ aduawai ni ehiii baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulu la ni naa wa ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ ni eha ewala be lɛ afee kuku.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist at the start of the major rainy season around April or May, and again during the minor rains around August or September so the tree can easily absorb the nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ shishijee mli yɛ April loo May he. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ August loo September aaafee lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mlɛo.

english: How does dry weather affect cocoa pods while they are developing on the tree?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ saa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: During dry weather, cocoa trees lack the water needed to fill out the seeds inside the pods, leading to small pods and flat beans. Applying organic mulch around the tree bases keeps soil cool and retains moisture.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni he hiaa koni amɛkɛ dumɔwui awo amɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ awo ehe. Tsei ashishi yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: A cocoa pod is ready to harvest when its color changes completely from green or red to a bright yellow or orange. Harvesting pods while they are still green produces flat, poor-quality beans.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛhe su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse waa. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ be mli ni amɛji eŋɔli lolo lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiii kwraa aba.

english: Why must I ferment my cocoa beans after harvesting instead of drying them right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli beni akpa amɛ lɛ, moŋ fe ni mahã amɛgbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fermentation removes the sugary pulp around the seeds and triggers the internal chemical changes that create the true chocolate flavor and brown color. Drying without fermenting leaves the beans bitter and unusable for chocolate.
ga: Fermentation jieɔ sugar pulp ni ebɔle dumɔwu lɛ he lɛ ni ehaa tsofai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsakeɔ. Enɛ haa tsokolate kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diɛŋtsɛ baa. Kɛ́ agbi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsokolate lɛ nyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-koko tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves burn easily and lose water quickly. Keeping taller shade trees or planting plantains nearby creates a cool canopy that protects the young cocoa until it is mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya, ni nu lɛ hu sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Enɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ amɛdaraa.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that produce food through their leaves using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil toward the light, preventing leaves from rotting and helping the plant produce larger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛfeɔ niyenii. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa la lɛ he. Ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Yellowing starting at leaf tips usually means the soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the key nutrient corn needs to grow strong and stay green. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni enyɛ eda waa ni ehi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special root nodules that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When the crop is harvested and leaves decay, that free nitrogen remains in the ground to nourish the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni baai lɛ egbo Nakai nitrogen ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eya nɔ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the young shoots growing around my main plantain stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain titri lɛ.

english: When too many shoots grow around a single plantain tree, they steal water and nutrients from each other. Pruning extra suckers and keeping only one or two strong shoots focuses the plant's energy into producing bigger fruit bunches.
ga: Be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli ni ahiɛ tso lɛ mli tsei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ hewalɛ ahi aduawai akui wuji ni eeefee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling up into tight balls and stopping growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like whiteflies or thrips that suck sap from the leaves and spread viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaf damage that stops the plant from bearing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ baai ni fiteɔ ni haaa tso lɛ awo yibii lɛ naa.

english: Why can my cassava survive long dry spells while my corn wilts and dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ be mli ni mi-ŋmei lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep roots that reach water far under the soil surface and can drop its leaves during dry spells to conserve water. Corn has shallow roots and loses moisture quickly, so it requires regular rainfall to survive.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ nu he kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwie shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Abɛi shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ amɛkɛ amɛhe afɔ̃ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ nɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does swamp rice grow well in flooded fields while my maize rots in waterlogged soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli lɛ? Be mli ni mi-ŋma lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have natural air channels inside their stems and roots that pass air down from above the water so the roots can breathe. Maize roots lack these air channels and drown when buried in standing water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni tsuɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ nu lɛ yiteŋ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like phosphorus. High temperatures cause the pollen to dry out, so the flower drops off unpollinated.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni pollination bɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop yields get smaller when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibiiwoo lɛ faaa kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same soil nutrients every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes or root crops lets the soil recover.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aaaya nɔ akwɛ lɛ baaha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ajɛ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ehe feɔ fɛo.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and drying up before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: This is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow leaves, so when there is not enough, the plant moves what little it has to the upper new leaves, causing the older leaves at the bottom to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛbaai lɛ daa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, tso lɛ baajie nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Empty groundnut shells, often called 'pops', happen when the soil lacks calcium during the pod development stage. Groundnut plants absorb calcium directly through their underground pods, not just the roots, so adding lime or gypsum to the soil gives the pods the calcium they need to fill up with seeds.
ga: Peanut ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘nut shells’ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium yɛ be mli ni pod lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Peanut tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ, shi jeee amɛshishifãi lɛ pɛ, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ lime loo gypsum fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ aná calcium ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛwo dumɔwui lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and turning pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is typically caused by a plant virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. When whiteflies feed on the sap of young tomato leaves, they inject the virus, which stunts the plant's growth and makes the leaves twist and turn yellow.
ga: Tso mli hela ko ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Kɛji ŋmeii yɛŋ nu nu ni jɛɔ tomato baai bibii amli lɛ Amɛbaawo hela lɛ mli. ni haa tsei nyɛɛɛ adara ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily at the stem base when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛyaa tso lɛ shishi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain stems often weaken and fall over because microscopic worms called nematodes or banana stem weevils are eating away at the roots and base inside the soil, leaving the heavy tree without a strong anchor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛgbee shi ejaakɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes, loo banana tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miiye shishifãi kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ tsiimɔ ni ŋwɛi ŋta ni ma shi shiŋŋ bɛ he

english: Why do the leaves of my cowpea plants get full of tiny holes right after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Beni eje kpo lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ

english: Flea beetles and aphids love to attack young cowpea leaves because they are tender and sweet. Feeding on the young leaves early on weakens the seedling, so applying early organic or targeted pest control helps protect the leaves so the crop can grow strong.
ga: Flea beetles kɛ aphids sumɔɔ ni amɛtutua cowpea baai bibii ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ blɛoo ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Baai bibii ni ayeɔ niyenii mra Ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any peppers can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ ada lɛ?

english: Pepper plants get stressed when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. To protect itself from losing water, the plant drops its flowers, which prevents peppers from forming until temperatures or watering become steady.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he lɛ Akɛ tsei shwieɔ shi koni akafee ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashi be mli ni hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why are my watermelons splitting open on the vine right before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ dani ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Watermelons crack open when they receive a sudden surge of water after a dry spell. The inside of the fruit absorbs water faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the fruit skin to burst open under pressure.
ga: Watermelons tswaa kɛji amɛná nu ni yaa hiɛ trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛre. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ ahe fãi lɛ fãa yɛ nɔnyɛɛ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil when the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains cause waterlogging in flat or clay soil, the roots get waterlogged, drown, and rot due to fungal infection.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu shwie shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛshwieɔ nu mli, ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ hewɔ.

english: Cocoa trees require beneficial insects like midges to cross-pollinate their tiny flowers. If these midges are missing due to excessive chemical spraying or dry weather, the flowers remain unpollinated and drop off the tree naturally.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ midges, koni amɛwo amɛfɔfɔi bibii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ midges nɛɛ laaje yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi fe nine loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi hewɔ lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ ni amɛbaagbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting shoots in storage even when I haven't planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ nitoohe lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miduko amɛ moŋ?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural resting period called dormancy after harvest. Once temperatures and humidity rise in storage, the yam detects that conditions are right for growth, breaking its natural sleep and sending out new shoots.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ mli lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ, Sweet potatoes lɛ baayɔse akɛ shihilɛi ni sa kɛha dalɛ. efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔ ni ŋmeii heei jeɔ kpo

english: How do I know when my palm fruits are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-palm yibii lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Oil palm fruits are ready for harvest when their color turns bright reddish-orange and a few loose fruits begin falling naturally from the bunch to the ground.
ga: Mu tso yibii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ-tsuru ni mli tse. Ni mu tso yibii komɛi baaje shishi amɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛba shikpɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: What happens to my palm fruit bunches if I leave them on the farm for several days after cutting them?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-palm aduawai lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo beni mifo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If harvested palm bunches are left on the farm too long, the fruits start to ferment and break down, which lowers the quality of the palm oil and reduces its market value.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi tsei ni akpa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Yibii lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbaafite. Enɛ baaha tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni ebaaha jara ni eyɔɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ hu aba shi.

english: How many years does a newly planted oil palm tree take before it starts giving me fruit?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani mu tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Most improved oil palm varieties start bearing fruit bunches about 3 to 4 years after being transplanted into your field, provided they receive proper care.
ga: Mu tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ateŋ babaoo baaje yibiiwoo shishi aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ beni adu amɛ awo oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why is it bad if I plant my oil palm seedlings too close to one another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji mikɛ mi-palm dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When palm trees are planted too close together, their leaves block each other's sunlight and their roots compete for soil water, leading to tall, weak trees with low yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe hulu la lɛ naa. ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛlɛɔ, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young palm trees turning yellow and brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm tso bibioo lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young palms usually show that the plant is short of key soil nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, or it is suffering from a lack of water during dry periods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. loo nu ni bɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or maize between my young oil palm trees?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ani abaanyɛ afee yɛ mu tsei bibii ateŋ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop food crops between young palms during their first 2 to 3 years; this helps maximize your farm space and provides income while the palm trees mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔ lɛ mli he lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo ni ebaaha oná shika be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do some crops grow better when we plant them together in the same field instead of alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi daraa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ wɔdu amɛ kutuu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli moŋ fe ni wɔkome too wɔdu lɛ?

english: Mixing crops helps cover the soil, which retains moisture, keeps the ground cool, suppresses weed growth, and protects weak seedlings from harsh sunlight.
ga: Nibii ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii, ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi lɛ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops whenever the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to take immediate advantage of rainwater and sunlight, allowing them to sprout quickly and steal nutrients away from your cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛná nugbɔ nu kɛ hulu la he sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ mli.

english: How can I protect my crop roots from drying out during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli?

english: Placing dry leaves or grass around the base of your plants—a practice called mulching—keeps the soil shaded, traps moisture, and keeps the roots cool during hot periods.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi wo tso lɛ shishi (ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching) lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: How can I keep my farm soil fertile for many years without spending a lot of money on chemical fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ afii babaoo ni mikɛ shika babaoo tsuuu nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe?

english: You can build soil fertility by leaving crop leaves to decay back into the ground, adding decomposed animal manure, and regularly planting nitrogen-fixing crops like beans or cowpeas.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo kɛtsɔ tsei ahe baai ni oooha amɛgboi kɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Okɛ kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo afata he. ni amɛdu nibii ni haa nitrogen lɛ yaa hiɛ tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii daa.

english: Why do my mangoes look healthy on the outside, but when I open them, I find small worms inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ shi kɛ́ agbele lɛ, ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Tiny insects called fruit flies pierce the skin of young fruits and lay invisible eggs inside. These eggs hatch into worms that feed on the flesh inside while the fruit is growing on the tree.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ fruit flies lɛ tsɔɔ aduawai bibii lɛ ahewolo mli ni amɛwoɔ wɔji ni anaaa amɛ yɛ mli. Nɛkɛ wɔɔji nɛɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ loo yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: When is the right time for me to spray my fruit trees so insects don't destroy my harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ anɔ koni kooloi akafite miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: You must spray early when the tree is flowering and the fruit is just beginning to form. Spraying early stops insects from getting the chance to lay eggs inside the small fruit.
ga: Ehe miihia ni okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ mra be mli ni tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ni aduawai miije shishi kɛkɛ. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ mra Enɛ baatsi kooloi bibii anaa hegbɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ aduawai bibii lɛ amli.

english: If I notice worms in my fruits after picking them, can I spray medicine on them to save them?
ga: Kɛji mina ŋmeii yɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ Ani manyɛ maná tsofa ni mikɛtsa amɛ?

english: No, spraying after the insects have already laid eggs inside will not work because the spray cannot penetrate inside the fruit. Pest control must be done early as a shield before the attack happens.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ beni kooloi lɛ ewo amɛwui lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, etsuuu nii ejaakɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ abote aduawai lɛ amli. Esa akɛ atsu tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nii mra. Koni etsu nii akɛ gãimlibi dani tutuamɔ ko aba.

english: Why isn't spraying my farm just once enough to keep pests away for the whole season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ nu afɔɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ shikome pɛ, ni fa bɔ ni sa ni egbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ be muu fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rain washes the protective medicine off the plants over time, and new fruits grow that were never sprayed. You need to spray at critical growth stages so new fruit stays protected.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ he lɛ he yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. kɛ aduawai heei Ekwɛ̃ ni afɔɔɔ nɔ nu kɔkɔɔkɔ. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa afɔ nɔ yɛ dalɛ mli hei titrii lɛ koni ebu aduawai heei ahe.

english: How can I check if an insect has already attacked my young fruit before it gets ruined?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji kooloi bibii miitutua mi aduawai bibii lɛ dani efite?

english: Check young fruits closely for tiny dark spots, small puncture holes, or clear sticky sap leaking from the skin. These are signs that an insect has pierced the fruit to lay eggs inside.
ga: Kwɛmɔ aduawai bibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii diji, ŋmeii bibii ni efo, loo ŋmeii ni mli tse ni shwieɔ shi ni ejɛ amɛhewolo lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ebote aduawai lɛ amli koni amɛwo amɛwui yɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my young fruits fall off the tree before they are big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibii bibii lɛ ekomɛi miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Young fruits often drop early when insects lay eggs inside them, damaging the fruit's core, or when the tree lacks enough water and nutrients to support all the growing fruit.
ga: Yibii ni edako lɛ fɔɔ gbee oya kɛji kooloi wo amɛwui yɛ mli. ni fiteɔ aduawai lɛ amli fã lɛ loo beni tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aduawai ni miida lɛ fɛɛ aye abua lɛ.

english: Is it harmful to leave rotten mangoes lying on the ground under my trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ aaashi mango ni egbo yɛ tso lɛ shishi?

english: Yes, leaving fallen fruit on the ground attracts pests and allows insect eggs inside them to hatch into adults, creating a huge army of insects that will attack your next harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi aduawai ni egbee shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaagbala kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ, ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ atsɔ onukpai. Enɛ haa ŋmeii babaoo ni baatutua oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa.

english: How do tiny insects know when my trees are bearing fruit so they can attack them?
ga: Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii leɔ akɛ mitso lɛ miiwo yibii? Koni enyɛ etutua amɛ?

english: Pests like fruit flies have an extremely strong sense of smell and can detect the sweet scent released by young flowers and growing fruits from miles away.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa waa. ni ebaanyɛ ena tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ni fɔfɔii bibii kɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ jieɔ kɛjɛɔ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ kilomitai babaoo lɛ.

english: Can mango trees grow well and produce good yields in areas like Sunyani?
ga: Ani mango tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ he ko tamɔ Sunyani?

english: Yes, Sunyani has good soil and rainfall for growing mangoes, but because the climate can be humid, farmers must manage fruit flies and fungal pests carefully to get a healthy yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, Sunyani yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni akɛduɔ mango. Shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ okwaafoi lɛ akwɛ aduawai amli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do insect pests seem to multiply so much faster during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects love warm, moist conditions because it speeds up their breeding cycle, allowing them to lay hundreds of eggs in a short time compared to dry periods.
ga: Koolooi sumɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. ejaakɛ ehaa amɛfɔmɔ be lɛ yaa oya Enɛ haa amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛ akɛto be ni nu hɔmɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ he.

english: What is this strange plant growing directly on the branches of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni ji tso ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mikoo tso lɛ niji anɔ tɛ̃ɛ nɛɛ?

english: That plant is likely a parasitic growth called mistletoe (known locally as nkranpan). It attaches itself to your cocoa tree branches and steals the food and water your tree needs to grow healthy pods.
ga: Etamɔ nɔ ni tso lɛ ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ mistletoe. Ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ kookoo niji ahe ni ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ kookoo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do I safely get rid of parasitic plants growing on my cocoa branches?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kokoo niji lɛ anɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: You should completely cut them down from the tree branches so they stop draining nutrients from your cocoa tree.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ amɛ kɛjɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ kwraa koni amɛkpa niyenii ni haa cacao tso lɛ mli lɛ numɔ.

english: Will removing unwanted growths like nkranpan from my cocoa tree hurt my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni ataooo tamɔ ostrich ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei amli lɛ baaná miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo?

english: No, removing them will actually help your cocoa farm flourish because the soil nutrients will go directly to your cocoa tree instead of feeding unwanted parasites.
ga: Dabi, amɛ ni ooojie lɛ baaye abua o-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ. Ejaakɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa kokoo tso lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha parasaiti ni ataooo lɛ niyenii

english: Is it okay to leave a little bit of the parasitic plant on the cocoa tree after cutting it?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ashi parasait tsei fioo komɛi yɛ cacao tso lɛ nɔ beni afo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to cut all of it off so that not too much remains on the tree to grow back and continue stealing food from your cocoa.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofo fɛɛ mli koni nɔ ko akashwɛ tsɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni ebaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni eya nɔ eju niyenii kɛjɛ okoo lɛ mli.

english: Why is my cocoa tree struggling even though the soil in my farm is good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ miitswa lɛ? Ani shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi lolo?

english: Parasitic plants like nkranpan living on your tree branches can suck up all the nutrients coming from the soil before the tree can use them to produce cocoa pods.
ga: Tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ tamɔ crane ni hiɔ otso lɛ niji anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani tso lɛ kɛtsu nii ni ekɛfee kookoo ŋmeii.

english: How do weeds and parasitic plants affect the food in my farm's soil?
ga: Te jwɛi kɛ tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ náa sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: They consume all the vital nutrients in the soil and tree, leaving very little food behind for your cocoa plants to survive and produce good yields.
ga: Amɛyeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ tsei amli lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ haa niyenii fioo ko pɛ eshwɛɔ koni eha o-cacao tsei lɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: What happens to my cocoa pods if I allow parasitic plants to grow on my tree?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ kɛji miŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ shwere yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ?

english: The parasitic plants will consume the tree's nutrients, causing your tree to produce fewer, smaller, or weaker cocoa pods.
ga: Tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii. Ehaa tso lɛ woɔ kookoo ŋmeii fioo, bibii, loo amɛhe waaa.

english: What can I do with the parasitic branches after I cut them off my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni mifeɔ parasait niji lɛ beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You can gather all the cut parasitic branches and take them home to the kitchen to use as firewood for cooking.
ga: Obaanyɛ obua parasaiti niji ni afolɔ lɛ anaa ni okɛya shia kɛya ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ koni okɛtsu nii akɛ tso ni akɛhooɔ nii.

english: Is it safe to use cut farm parasitic plants as kitchen firewood?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ tsei ni afolɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baatsu nii akɛ tso yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Yes, once you cut down parasitic growths like nkranpan, taking them to the kitchen for firewood is a great way to clean your farm and make good use of the waste.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji okɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ ayibɔ ba shi pɛ lɛ, Amɛ ni okɛbaaya ŋmɔ mli koni oyatao tso lɛ ji gbɛ kpakpa ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ otsumɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okɛ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I leave the cut nkranpan branches on the farm floor after clearing them?
ga: Kɛ́ ojie tsei lɛ aniji lɛ, ani oshiɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is better to clear them completely and bring them home for household use like cooking fuel so your farm stays clean and free of unwanted plant material.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie mli kwraa ni akɛya shia koni akɛtsu nii yɛ shia, tamɔ tsofa ni akɛhooɔ nii. Koni oŋmɔ lɛ mli atse ni tsei ni ataooo akafee nɔ ko.

english: Can I really use pulled weeds as fertilizer for my crops, or will they just grow back and destroy my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ jwɛi jwɛi lɛ atsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ? Aloo amɛbaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni amɛfite miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: When weeds are uprooted and allowed to dry out fully in the sun, they die and stop growing. As they decompose on the ground, they break down into organic matter that returns valuable nutrients back into the soil to feed your crops.
ga: Beni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ ni egbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ. Weeds will die and stop growing. Beni amɛfiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛfiteɔ amɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni kɛ niyenii ni jara wa kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: How do crop roots actually eat the dead leaves and rotten weeds I put on the soil?
ga: Te tsei shishifãi yeɔ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi ni egboi ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Crops do not eat plant waste directly. Rainwater dissolves the tiny nutrients hidden inside the rotting weeds and carries them down into the dirt, allowing the roots to drink them up like soup.
ga: Crops do not directly eat plant waste. Rainwater dissolves small nutrients. Ekɛtee jwɛi ni miifite lɛ amli ni ewo amɛ shi kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Let the roots drink like soup.

english: Why do my crops turn pale yellow and stay small even when rain is falling regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiifee bibii eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Rain provides water, but crops also need food from the soil to stay healthy. Yellow leaves mean the soil has run out of plant food, so adding compost, manure, or decayed weeds will give them the nutrients needed to turn deep green and grow tall.
ga: Nugbɔ haa nu, shi ŋmɔshi nibii hu he hiaa niyenii kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei ahe niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo jwɛi ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ni amɛdara.

english: How do I measure the right amount of organic manure to give my plants using simple farm tools like baskets?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni mikɛbaahã mi tsei lɛ kɛtsɔ okwaayeli dɛŋdade ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tsɛnsi nɔ?

english: You can use a standard container like a small headpan or basket to ensure every crop gets the same amount. Counting out fixed basketfuls across your rows ensures each plant gets enough food without wasting your inputs.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nɔ ko ni akɛwoɔ mli daa, tamɔ yitso ni akɛfoɔ yitsɔi loo tsɛnsi bibioo ko atsu nii. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ náa yibɔ kome. Kɛ́ okane tsɛnsii ni eyi obɔ yɛ ogbɛjianɔtoi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni efiteee nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: Where exactly around the stem should I place compost or plant waste when feeding my crops?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ abɔle tso lɛ he kɛji mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiha?

english: Avoid piling inputs directly against the plant stem, as this can attract pests or rot the stalk. Instead, spread the material in a circle around the drip-line of the leaves where the young feeder roots are actively searching for food.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaanyɛ egbala kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo tso lɛ yibii ni fiteɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai najiaŋ lɛ Gbalamɔ saji lɛ amli yɛ kooyigbɛ kɛbɔle he. Drip lines lɛ ji he ni gbekɛbii ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ taoɔ niyenii yɛ.

english: What happens to my farm if I give a lot of fertilizer to some crops and give very little to others?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei komɛi amli shi mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ wo ekrokomɛi amli?

english: Uneven application causes crops to grow at different speeds, leading to an uneven harvest where strong plants block sunlight from weaker ones. Giving equal amounts to every plant ensures your entire field matures at the same time.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ haa tsei daa oya yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Ekɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni ejaaa baa He ni tsei ni he wa lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso fɛɛ tso ha lɛ falɛ kome lɛ, ehaa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why does spreading dry weeds over the dirt keep my crops fresh during hot, sunny days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni aduɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ehee yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry plant matter creates a protective blanket over the soil. This blanket blocks direct sunlight from drying out the ground, keeping moisture in the soil longer for crop roots to drink.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he. Nɛkɛ atade nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ni ehaaa sũ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu nu be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How long does it take for dry weeds spread on the ground to turn into useful food for my crops?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani jwɛi ni egbi ni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: In warm, damp conditions, small insects and soil organisms break down dry weeds within a few weeks. The nutrients start feeding your crops shortly after the material begins to rot into the dirt.
ga: Yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ baafite jwɛi ni egbi lɛ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli. Niyenii nibii baaje shishi amɛha onibii lɛ niyenii beni nibii lɛ je shishi amɛfite kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ.

english: Are all types of weeds safe to clear and spread back onto my crop rows as food?
ga: Ani jwɛi srɔtoi fɛɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni abaajie ni agbɛ ashwã mi ŋmɔshi nibii amli ekoŋŋ kɛha niyenii?

english: Soft, green weeds make excellent plant food when allowed to dry out completely. However, weeds that have already formed mature seeds or have tough underground tubers should be removed from the farm so they do not sprout again.
ga: Jwɛi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ji tsei niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ amɛ gbɛ ni amɛgbi. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni eda loo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni wa lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. koni ekakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ

english: Why does organic manure made from decayed plants keep my crops green longer than quick chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ tsei ni egboi fee lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji be kakadaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers give crops a fast boost that washes away quickly with heavy rains. Organic plant material breaks down slowly over months, steadily feeding the roots over a long period while improving the soil's ability to hold water.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya. ni kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ shwieɔ lɛ oya. Tso mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ fiofio. nyɔji babaoo Ha shishifãi lɛ niyenii daa be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why did the pest spray I bought fail to kill the caterpillars on my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni miheɔ lɛ egbeee kooloi ni yɔɔ mi-abele lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Chemical sprays can fail if they are mixed with too much water, sprayed at the wrong time of day when heat weakens the chemical, or if the insects have built resistance to that specific medicine.
ga: Tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji akɛ akɛ nu babaoo futu mli. Okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ yɛ be ni esaaa mli beni latsaa lɛ haa tsofa lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii lɛ ná nakai tsofa pɔtɛɛ lɛ he hewalɛ

english: How soon should I re-spray my crops if rain falls right after I apply chemical medicine?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ ewo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ, te esa akɛ mafo miŋmɔji lɛ amli ekoŋŋ oya tɛŋŋ?

english: If heavy rain falls within two hours of spraying, it washes the medicine off the leaves before the plant or pests absorb it, so you will usually need to reapply once the leaves dry.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai enyɔ mli yɛ tsofa lɛ ni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ Tsofa lɛ baaho baai lɛ ahe dani tso lɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ aŋɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ehe baahia ni okɛwo mli ekoŋŋ kɛ́ baai lɛ egbi.

english: Why do insects move from my neighbor's field onto my crops after he sprays his land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fã kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛba miŋmɔshi nibii amli beni ekɛ tsofa efɔ eshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Insects naturally flee chemical sprays by flying or crawling away to neighboring untreated farms in search of food and safe places to live.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, kooloi bibii lɛ joɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ naa foi kɛtsɔ foidamɔ loo amɛfomɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ ni atsako amɛhe lɛ anɔ. koni amɛtao niyenii kɛ wɔɔhe ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe

english: Why do pests keep multiplying on my farm even after I clean the weeds around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ jwɛi shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds removes adult hiding spots, but if pest eggs were already laid under crop leaves or in the soil, those eggs will still hatch into new pests.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ejie hei ni onukpai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ awo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe fɔmɔ kotokui yɛ tsei ahe baai ashishi loo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Nakai fɔmɔ kotokui lɛ baaya nɔ atsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai heei.

english: Why do insect eggs hatch faster on my farm when the weather becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii afɔ̃ɔ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Warm temperatures speed up the life cycle of pests, causing eggs laid on crop leaves or soil to develop and hatch much faster than in cool weather.
ga: He ni mli edɔ lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ yaa oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ tsei ahe baai loo shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ daa ni amɛfɔɔ oya fe shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ mli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and dry out when the sun gets very intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Hot afternoon sun causes plants to lose water rapidly through their leaves, making the leaves curl inward to reduce water loss and protect themselves from scorching.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ baai lɛ amli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ni baa shi ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he.

english: Why do my tomato seeds fail to sprout when I plant them directly under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Direct hot sun bakes the top layer of soil and dries out delicate seeds before they can absorb enough water to germinate properly.
ga: Hulu la ni mli edɔ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni eha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my bean plants drop their flowers without producing pods during dry, hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ shwie fɔfɔi ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ otsi ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High heat stresses the plant, forcing it to sacrifice its flowers to conserve energy and water so the main plant can survive.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei kɛ fɔfɔi ashã afɔle koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni tso titri lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and burn after I apply fertilizer under bright sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Applying chemical fertilizer on dry soil under intense sun draws moisture away from the roots, which burns the root tips and damages the leaves above.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaagbala ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ baashã shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni efite baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Where do pests hide their eggs in the soil during the dry season before crops are planted?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛwui lɛ teeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani aduɔ tsei?

english: Pests bury their eggs inside dry plant stems, crop residue, or deep cracks in the soil, where they wait safely until the rainy season begins.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fuɔ amɛwui lɛ yɛ tsei ni egbi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli. Amɛbaamɛ shweshweeshwe kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaje shishi.

english: Why do some local medicinal herbs taste stronger or work better when grown in specific soils?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai komɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ŋɔɔ waa loo amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔji pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ lɛ?

english: Plants absorb minerals and organic matter from the soil to produce their natural chemical compounds. Rich, healthy soil helps medicinal plants develop higher concentrations of the nutrients and potent qualities that make them effective.
ga: Tsei gbalaa sũ mli nibii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛfee adebɔɔ mli tsofai. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsofafeemɔ tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛ nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni haa tsei woɔ yibii.

english: How can I make sure my crops stay fresh and strong enough to be sold in distant markets or exported abroad?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ehee lolo ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ loo makɛya maŋsɛɛ?

english: Crops retain their strength and freshness longer when harvested at full maturity, handled gently to avoid bruising, and stored in cool, ventilated conditions to slow down spoiling after harvest.
ga: Tsei lɛ baahiɛ amɛhewalɛ kɛ ehee lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ kɛ́ akpa amɛ be mli ni amɛdara. Afee lɛ blɛoo koni akatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ koni ekɛha nɔ ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when there is too much heavy rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess rain washes away mobile soil nutrients like nitrogen and fills soil air spaces with water. Without air, root systems cannot absorb food properly, which causes plant leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ sũ mli nibii ni tsiɔ ehe, tamɔ nitrogen, ni ekɛ nu fataa sũ mli kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ he. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop in the middle of the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ leebi po.

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. Drooping is a temporary defense mechanism to reduce leaf area exposed to the sun and save water.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Defoliation ji be kukuoo mli hebuu gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ baa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni akɛbuɔ nu he.

english: Why is it important to plant plantains or cassava near my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains loo cassava yɛ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing companion crops like plantain or cassava provides essential shade and keeps the surrounding air moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Hefatalɔi tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ Ebaaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba ni eye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Is it better to use animal manure or chemical fertilizer to feed my crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ kooloi ashishifãi loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Chemical fertilizers give crops a quick boost of nutrients, while animal manure improves long-term soil health, helps soil hold water longer, and keeps the soil fertile across multiple farming seasons.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kooloi aŋmei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ okwaayeli bei srɔtoi lɛ amli fɛɛ

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster on my land than the main crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe ŋmɔshi nibii titrii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally adapted to survive harsh local conditions and quickly absorb water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before cultivated crops can establish their root systems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛheɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Dani tso ko baanyɛ afee shishifã

english: Why do insects attack my food crops more heavily during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miniyenii tsei lɛ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season, wild vegetation dries up, forcing insects to move onto farm crops for food and water. Plants under heat stress are also less able to defend themselves against pests.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ baagbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ kooloi bibii aya okwaayeli ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛyatao niyenii kɛ nu. Tsei ni yɔɔ latsaa shishi lɛ hu nyɛɛɛ abu amɛhe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why should I trim off extra branches from my pepper plants while they are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ mli beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Trimming unnecessary branches prevents the plant from wasting energy on foliage, allowing it to direct more nutrients into growing larger, healthier pepper fruits.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni efeɔ pepper aduawai ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it better to buy certified planting seeds instead of using seeds from the grain I bought at the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mahe tsei ahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mɛi ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ baatsu nii lɛ?

english: Market grain is usually meant for food and may come from hybrid plants that do not produce strong offspring. Certified seeds are specially selected to grow uniformly, resist local diseases, and produce higher yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ji niyenii. ni ebaanyɛ ejɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni nyɛɛɛ afɔ bii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdara daa. helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛshishi kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting at the tip and moving along the middle vein usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK around the roots helps the plants regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni nyiɛɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo NPK wo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛdalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: What makes the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips that spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early using neem oil spray or recommended insecticides helps protect the new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai heei lɛ ahe.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, cold, and dark shade. Pruning heavy branches to let sunlight in and spraying approved fungicides will protect your cocoa pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni mli ejɔ, kɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ. Niji ni afolɔ waa Ha hulu lɛ akpɛ ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ nɔ koni eye ebua ni ebu o-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the soil becomes too dry or when daytime temperatures get extremely hot. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the flowers stay on and produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food and grow large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the dark ground into the light and prevents them from rotting in wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ baai anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ kɛyaa la mli ni ehaa baa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ.

english: Why should I mound soil around my groundnut plants when they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabua shikpɔŋ mabɔle mi-peanut tsei lɛ ahe beni amɛbɔi fɔmɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnut flowers produce long pegs after pollination that must grow downward into the soil to form the actual nuts. Mounding loose soil around the base makes it easy for these pegs to enter the ground and mature.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ tamɔ ŋmeii kakadaji yɛ be mli ni amɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ. Esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ. Pile loose soil around Shishitoo lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches at the top, making them unstable. Supporting fruiting plantain trees with bamboo poles or strong wooden props keeps strong winds from pulling them out of the ground.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni ebɔle amɛhe yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ, ni no haaa amɛhi shi shiŋŋ. Fiɔ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ kɛ ŋmei tsei loo tsei ni wa. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akagbala lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are insect pests attacking my bean plants as soon as they start to flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa mi-pea tsei lɛ kɛji amɛje fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi pɛ?

english: Bean flowers produce sweet nectar and bright petals that attract pests like thrips and pod borers. Spraying safe bio-pesticides or neem extract right when flower buds appear prevents pests from damaging your yield.
ga: Pea fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ nu kɛ fɔfɔi ni kpɛɔ ni gbalaa kooloi tamɔ thrips kɛ pod borers. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem mli nu lɛ shwie nɔ kɛji ŋmeii je kpo pɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell they are ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, or when you carefully dig around the base and find firm, full-sized tubers.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo hiɔ shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ amɛfee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. Aloo beni otsaa he fɛɛ he Okɛ shishifãi shwie shi jogbaŋŋ ni ona yitso ni mli wa, ni eyi obɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my rice field need to hold standing water while the plants are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ ahi nu mli be mli ni tsei lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Shallow standing water stops weeds from growing and competing with your rice for nutrients, while also keeping the soil moist. However, you should drain the water a few weeks before harvest so the rice grains dry and ripen evenly.
ga: Nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni damɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmãa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ hu baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ okɛ nu lɛ afɔ shi otsii fioo komɛi dani okpa. Enɛ ji koni ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhoo pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantain next to young cocoa creates a canopy that protects the seedlings from heat and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: The main plantain stalk needs full energy from the soil to produce a heavy bunch. Leaving too many shoots (suckers) creates competition for food and water, which results in smaller, thinner plantain bunches.
ga: Plantain tso titri lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni tsii, ni ŋmeii babaoo (ŋmei) ni ajieɔ lɛ haa akaŋshii baa kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ haa plantains lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe feɔ mlɛo.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the rest of the farm is still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai krokomɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ani ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔji lolo?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Maize consumes nutrients quickly, so applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure early helps the leaves stay green and produce healthy corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Abele yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo afata he mra. Ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmãa toi ni mli wa.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts or beans on my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize drains a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which naturally capture nitrogen from the air and return it to the ground, restoring soil fertility for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is my cowpea crop growing lots of thick green leaves but very few flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo shi fɔfɔi fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas make their own soil nutrients. Adding extra nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves instead of producing flowers and pods.
ga: Cowpea lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo baai lɛ atsu nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii

english: Why does my cassava shed almost all its leaves during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ harmatha be lɛ mli kɛji egbi pɛ?

english: Dropping leaves during the dry season is cassava's natural defense mechanism to conserve water. The plant is not dead; it goes dormant to protect its underground roots and will sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ŋmei he koni ekɛbu nu he. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Eyaa wɔɔ koni ebu eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe. ni ebaakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into small fruits during hot spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai bibii lɛ? Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Extreme heat and dry air can kill tomato pollen before pollination occurs. Supplying water directly at the roots and providing light shade during very hot periods helps the flowers produce fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi baanyɛ agbe tomato mli ŋmɔtɔ dani enyɛ ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to stick long wooden stakes into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee tsei kakadaji lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing tubers underground. Lifting the vines off the muddy ground ensures maximum leaf exposure to sunlight and protects the leaves from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo, ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and turning hard like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee shiŋŋ tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Upward curling in pepper leaves is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites hiding under the leaves. Controlling these pests prevents them from stunting the plant and reducing fruit production.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ anɔyeli yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ anaa, ni ehaa aduawai ni amɛwoɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing wide open leaves instead of folding into tight, hard balls in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaabɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni wa yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbage requires cool root conditions and steady water to roll its leaves into a tight head. Irregular watering or extreme heat causes the plant to stay open instead of forming a solid cabbage head.
ga: Kaabaji biɔ shishifãi ni mli ejɔ kɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa koni ekɛ baai lɛ abɔle yitsei ni mli wa he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baaha tso lɛ ahi shi ni egbele shi moŋ ni eeetsɔ kaabe yitso ni wa.

english: Why do I need to build high mounds of soil before planting my seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams require loose, soft, and well-drained soil to grow long and thick roots. Creating high earthen mounds gives the tuber plenty of soft room to expand easily underground without hitting hard soil, while also preventing water from rotting the seed.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni shishifãi kakadaŋŋ agboi akwɛ̃. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa bulb lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo ni enaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekafite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why should I leave measured spaces between my maize seeds instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving maize proper space ensures every single stalk gets enough food and light to produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Abele ni akɛto he jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha abele toi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark sawdust-like dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmei yɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana. It crawls into the center of the young maize plant, eats the leaves as they unfurl, and leaves behind moist, dark waste.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe shwie ŋmãa tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ. Ye baai lɛ beni amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo lɛ. ni oshi jwɛi ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli efɔ yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites, or a virus spread by whiteflies. As these insects feed on the sap of young leaves, the leaves wrinkle, distort, and roll up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips, aphids loo mites, loo helai ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my plantain trees turning yellow and snapping off near the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: This yellowing and snapping is often caused by leaf spot diseases like Black Sigatoka or root damage from soil fungi. The disease attacks the leaf tissue, weakening the base of the leaf stem until it collapses under its own weight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ jɛɔ baa mli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ helai tamɔ Black Sigatoka loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ amli. Hela nɛɛ tutuaa baa lɛ mli fãji. Enɛ haa baa lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni efoɔ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɔjɔmɔ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge leafy stems but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium and phosphorus. Nitrogen encourages lush green leaf and stem growth, causing the cassava plant to spend all its energy above ground instead of storing food in its root tubers.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ fa fe potassium kɛ phosphorus. Nitrogen haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daraa. Enɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil is low on nutrients and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Signs of poor soil include slow crop growth, pale yellow or light green leaves instead of deep green, and weak stems. If crops produced good yields in previous years but are now producing smaller harvests under the same weather, the soil nutrients are likely depleted.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii lɛ he ji tsei ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo. Baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ loo eŋɔli ni mli tse yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. kɛ tso ni bɛ hewalɛ Kɛji tsei lɛ wo yibii kpakpai yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli Shi amrɔ nɛɛ ewoɔ yibii fioo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni tamɔ nɛkɛ shishi. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ sɛɛ fomɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale yellow when my farmland stays flooded after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ nu eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil is flooded for days, water replaces air pockets in the ground, starving the plant roots of oxygen. Without oxygen, roots cannot breathe or absorb nitrogen and other nutrients from the soil, causing leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo Nu yeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu loo amɛŋɔ nitrogen kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without ever growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomato kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, dry spells, or poor pollination. High air temperatures disrupt the flower's fertilization process, causing the plant to shed the unpollinated blossoms to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo pollination ni ehiii Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ afɔmɔ gbɛ lɛ naa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and lose leaves during the hot dry season?
