ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle full, direct sunlight and dry winds. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh heat and trap moisture, the sun scorches the leaves, causing the young tree to dry out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi nyɛɛɛ abote mli. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo lɛ bɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Koni atsĩ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ naa ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Hulu lɛ miishã baai lɛ. gĩ dumɔwui lɛ

english: Why are some of my palm trees producing flowers but never growing any palm fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm tsei lɛ ekomɛi yɛ fɔfɔi shi amɛkwɛɛɛ ŋmeii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Palm trees produce separate male and female flowers. Male flowers only produce pollen to fertilize other flowers, so a tree producing only male flowers at that time will not bear any fruit clusters itself.
ga: Palm tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Fɔfɔi hii woɔ pollen pɛ ni amɛkɛ fɔfɔi krokomɛi feɔ ekome. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi hii pɛ yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ wooo aduawai akui komɛi.

english: How can I tell the difference between a male flower and a female flower on my oil palm trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei ni yɔɔ mu tso nɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Female flowers are thicker, rounded, and stand upright like a clump of fingers ready to catch pollen, while male flowers look like long, thin, finger-like spikes covered in a yellowish powder called pollen.
ga: Fɔfɔi yei tsii, kokroo, amɛdamɔ shi tamɔ nineshi tsɔi, amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaamɔ fɔfɔi fɔfɔi. yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi hii lɛ tamɔ ŋmeii kakadaji ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Akɛ powda ni ji ŋmɔtɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ pollen lɛ ehà nɔ.

english: Do palm trees have male and female genders like animals do?
ga: Ani ŋmei tsei yɛ hii kɛ yei tamɔ kooloi?

english: Yes, many plants like palms have distinct male and female reproductive structures. While some trees stay mostly male or female, oil palms usually produce male and female flower bunches on the same tree at different times of the year.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei babaoo, tamɔ ŋmei tsei, yɛ nuu kɛ yoo fɔmɔ gbɛjianɔtoi srɔtoi. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei komɛi ji hii loo yei babaoo moŋ, shi bei pii lɛ, mu tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei yɛ tso kome nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli bei srɔtoi amli.

english: What actually happens to the female palm flower to make it turn into palm nuts?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmei fɔfɔi yei lɛ anɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii?

english: For a female flower to produce fruit, pollen from a male flower must land on it—usually carried by small insects or wind. Once pollinated, the female flower swells up over several months into a heavy cluster of palm nuts.
ga: koni fɔfɔi yei lɛ awo yibii Esa akɛ Pollen ni jɛ fɔfɔi nuu lɛ mli lɛ abagbee fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ woɔ amɛ kɛyaa. Kɛji akɛ ashɛre pollination Fɔfɔi yei lɛ shwereɔ yɛ kui ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nyɔji babaoo.

english: How do I know when a female palm flower is ready to receive pollen?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei fɔfɔi yei efee klalo akɛ amɛbaaŋɔ pollen?

english: When a female flower opens up and is ready for pollen, it turns a light cream color and gives off a fresh, sweet smell that attracts pollinating insects to help it form fruits.
ga: Kɛji fɔfɔi yei lɛ gbele amɛhe ni amɛfee klalo kɛha pollen lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baatsake ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ji krim su. And it smells fresh and sweet. Attract pollinators to help produce fruit.

english: Why is it important to check my crops early in the morning to see if they are blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli mra koni mana kɛji amɛmiikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Early morning is when flowers naturally open and release scent or pollen, and when pollinating insects are most active. Checking early helps you know if your crops are successfully blooming and pollinating.
ga: Leebi ji be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛjieɔ amɛhenumɔ loo pollen lɛ kpo. kɛ be ni pollinators lɛ tsuɔ nii waa lɛ Kwɛmɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaaye ebua bo ni ole kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eye omanye ni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo pollination.

english: If a palm tree on my farm only makes male flowers for a long time, should I cut it down?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii pɛ be kakadaŋŋ Ani Esa akɛ Mafolɔ?

english: No, do not cut it down. Palm trees go through natural cycles based on water and nutrients, and a tree that makes only male flowers now can start producing heavy female fruit bunches once conditions improve.
ga: Dabi, kaaŋmala nɔ. Palm tsei tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛi ni damɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ. Ni tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi hii pɛ lɛ baanyɛ aje fɔfɔi yei babaoo shishi kɛji shihilɛi lɛ tee hiɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers put colored markers or tags on specific trees in a field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai kɛ okadii loo okadii woɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tags are placed on specific trees to track their growth stage, such as when they start flowering or how much fruit they produce. This helps farmers keep accurate records of which trees perform best.
ga: Akɛ kadimɔi woɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ koni akɛkwɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa, tamɔ be mli ni amɛjeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi loo bɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo amɛhaa. Enɛ haa okwaafoi nyɛɔ amɛŋmalaa tsei ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe saji amɛshwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my palm trees seem to produce more male flowers during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-palm tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Developing female flowers into heavy fruit clusters requires a lot of water and energy. During dry weather, the tree protects itself from stress by producing male flowers, which require much less water.
ga: Ni aaaha fɔfɔi yei afee kui ni tsii lɛ biɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ babaoo. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli Tso lɛ buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ haomɔ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi hii ni biɔ nu fioo kwraa lɛ ni ewoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do agricultural researchers plant fields containing only male trees or only female trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi duɔ tsei ni hii loo yei pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Researchers isolate male and female trees so they can collect pure pollen from strong male trees and manually apply it to selected female trees, producing high-quality hybrid seeds for farmers.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi gbala tsei hii kɛ yei amli koni amɛbua pollen krɔŋŋ kɛjɛ tsei hii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛwo tsei yei ni akɛ niji halaa lɛ anɔ. Koni afee hybrid dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ aha okwaafoi.

english: Why are my crops flowering at the wrong time of the year nowadays?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miikwɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni ejaaa mli ŋmɛnɛ lɛ?

english: Shifts in local weather patterns and erratic rainfalls confuse the crop's natural growth cycle, causing plants to produce flowers earlier or later than normal due to temperature shifts and water stress.
ga: Tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ejaaa lɛ kɛ basabasafeemɔ baa ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi mra loo sɛɛ mli fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ. yɛ hulutsoo tsakemɔi kɛ nu mli haomɔ hewɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo amɛmli moŋ?

english: When soil is heavily damaged or washed away by erosion and heavy land clearing, it loses its ability to hold nutrients. This prevents plants from absorbing the fertilizer properly through their roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ efite waa loo nu hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ babaoo lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ atsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves dry up and drop off so quickly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Without forest cover to block harsh sun rays, rising temperatures force crops to lose moisture faster than their roots can pull water from the dry ground, leading to severe leaf wilting.
ga: Kɛji koo ko bɛ ni baatsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ, hulutsoo be ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over so easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Cutting down surrounding trees removes natural windbreaks that shield crops. Without these tree barriers, strong winds hit crops directly and push them over.
ga: Tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni afoɔ Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ. Kɛji gbɛtsii nii ko bɛ tsei nɛɛ ateŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛ amɛ shwieɔ nɔ.

english: Why does my land produce much less food now than it did ten years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ lɛ faaa kwraa fe afii nyɔŋma ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous removal of trees and topsoil strips the land of its natural organic richness. Over time, exhausted soil produces smaller harvests unless it is given time to recover and replenished with organic matter.
ga: Tsei kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni ajieɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ baawo yibii fioo. ja aha lɛ be ni ekɛwo hewalɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he.

english: Why am I seeing strange new insects on my farm that were never here before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi heei ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni minako dã yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Warmer weather and changes in rainfall patterns allow pests from other regions to move in, survive, and multiply in areas that used to be too cool or wet for them.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ mli lɛ eha kooloi ni jɛ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ eba, amɛhi shi, ni amɛfɔ bii yɛ hei ni be ko ni eho lɛ, fɛ̃i loo hulutsoo tsɔ kɛha amɛ lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to use muddy water from nearby mining streams to water my vegetables?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛɔ shika tsuru jɛɛhe ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii kɛwo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu?

english: No, water polluted by heavy digging or chemicals carries dangerous toxins and heavy metals that get absorbed into your crops, stunting their growth and making the food unsafe for humans to eat.
ga: Dabi, nu ni shika tsuru ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo loo tsofai efite lɛ yɛ tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ dade ni tsii ni shwieɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli. Enɛ haaa dalɛ aya hiɛ ni ehaa niyenii efeee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha adesai ayemɔ.

english: How does keeping large trees on my farm help my crops survive long dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni eda ni mikɛtoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli?

english: Large shade trees shield smaller crops from extreme heat, keep the surrounding soil cool, and help ground soil retain moisture for a much longer time during dry periods.
ga: Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo ni amɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cassava tubers growing much smaller and harder than usual?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraa kwraa ni amɛhe wa fe bɔ ni amɛfeɔ daa lɛ?

english: Hard, damaged, or dry soil restricts the roots from expanding easily. When soil loses its natural softness and moisture retention, root crops cannot swell into full, healthy tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni efite, loo ni egbi lɛ haa ewaa akɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ bɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ afu ni amɛfee tso ni mli wa ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables rot much faster after picking than they used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni mikpaa lɛ miifite oya fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: Crops grown under severe heat stress or in nutrient-poor soil develop weaker cell walls, making the harvested produce lose moisture quickly and rot faster after harvest.
ga: Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ faaa nɔ lɛ eha wala yibii lɛ ahe gbogboi lɛ egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni akpa lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya, ni efiteɔ oya yɛ nibii ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my soybean leaves turn yellow and drop off when harvest time is near?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ soybean baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi beni kpamɔ be lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is normal crop behavior. As soybeans mature and complete their life cycle, they direct all their energy into filling the seed pods, causing the leaves to naturally turn yellow, dry up, and drop off before harvesting.
ga: This is normal cropping behavior. Kɛji soybean lɛ dara ni egbe eshihilɛ be lɛ naa lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo dumɔwui lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani akpaa.

english: How do soybean crops help make my soil better for the next season?
ga: Te soybean tso baafee tɛŋŋ eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Soybeans are legumes that work with helpful bacteria in the soil to trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food, leaving natural fertilizer in the soil for future crops like maize.
ga: Soy ji ŋmãa ko ni kɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni emɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsɔ tsei aniyenii. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛhaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my soybean plants grow very tall with many leaves but produce very few full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or experience severe heat stress during flowering, they spend all their energy growing leaves instead of forming healthy, seed-filled pods.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo amɛna dɔlɛ ni naa wa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, Nibii ni Aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ podhi nɛ duwuhi nɛ a ngɛ he wami e hyi mɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry up fast during a short drought while my neighbor's farm stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ be kukuoo mli hɔmɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tseɔ lɛ?

english: Crops wither faster in soils low in organic matter. Adding compost or manure acts like a sponge, helping the soil hold onto rainwater longer so plants survive dry spells better.
ga: Tsei gboiɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kompost loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell that my soybeans are fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-soybeans lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Soybeans are ready when most leaves have fallen, the pods turn a light tan or brown color, and you can hear the seeds rattling inside the pods when you shake the plant.
ga: Soybean lɛ efee klalo beni baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo egbee shi lɛ. Pods lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ. Ni obaanyɛ onu dumɔwui lɛ ni miitswa yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ he kɛ́ okpokpo tso lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil and get insects so quickly when stored in my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ ni ŋmeii shwieɔ nɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grains spoil in storage if they are harvested with too much moisture. Drying the harvested grains thoroughly in the sun until they are hard prevents mold and makes it harder for insects to breed.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baafite yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ akpa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmeii anaa, ni ehaa ewaa kɛhaa kooloi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaafɔ bii.

english: What happens to the value of my soybeans if I process them instead of selling raw beans?
ga: Mɛni baaba sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ mi-soybeans lɛ he? Kɛji akɛ mitsu nii moŋ fe ni mahɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni ahoko

english: Raw soybeans spoil or lose market interest quickly if buyers are scarce, but processing them into items like flour, oil, or animal feed extends their shelf life and allows you to charge higher prices.
ga: Soybean ni ahoko lɛ baafite oya loo ebaafite jara lɛ he miishɛɛ kɛji akɛ mɛi ni baahe lɛ faaa. Shi nitsumɔ ni akɛfeɔ nibii srɔtoi tamɔ ashikishaŋ, fɔ loo kooloi aniyenii Enɛ baaha shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ni eha onyɛ okɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ awo mli.

english: What simple foods can my community turn raw soybeans into to increase our earnings?
ga: Mɛni ji niyenii komɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni mi akutso lɛ baanyɛ akɛto soybeans ni ahoko lɛ najiaŋ koni wɔshika aya hiɛ?

english: Raw soybeans can easily be ground or boiled locally to make soy milk, soy flour, soy kebabs, or livestock feed, all of which sell for much higher profits than raw grains.
ga: Abaanyɛ atsɔ soybeans ni ahoko lɛ nɔ loo ahoo yɛ maŋ lɛ mli oya koni aná soy mliki. soybean ashikiŋsha soy kebab loo kooloi aniyenii Ni fɛɛ ahɔ̃ɔ kɛ sɛɛnamɔ ni fa babaoo fe dumɔwui ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why do travelling buyers pay us very low prices for our crops right after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ gbɛfaa nɔ lɛ woɔ wɔ jara ni baa shi nɛkɛ yɛ wɔŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: During harvest, almost every farmer is selling the same crop at the same time, creating an oversupply that lowers prices. Buyers take advantage of this abundance to pay low rates at the farm gate.
ga: yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli Nɔ ni miihe ashɛ okwaafoi fɛɛ hɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ haa nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ fa fe nine yɛ jara lɛ nɔ, ni no haa nibii ajara baa shi. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ nibii babaoo nɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo nyɔmɔ ni baa shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shinaa lɛ naa.

english: Is it better for me to sell my harvested crops immediately at the farm gate or hold onto them?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ minibii ni mikpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shinaa lɛ naa loo mikɛto?

english: Selling immediately gives quick cash but at the lowest market rate; properly drying and storing your crops for a few months allows you to sell when supply is low and prices go up.
ga: Nihɔɔmɔ haa shika amrɔ nɔŋŋ shi yɛ jara ni baa shi fe fɛɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ogbi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ be mli ni nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ faaa ni amɛjara hu yaa hiɛ.

english: Why should I plant shade trees alongside my regular crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ daa lɛ ahe yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Shade trees protect sensitive crops like cocoa and coffee from harsh, direct sunlight, keep the soil cool and moist, and shed leaves that decay into natural fertilizer for your soil.
ga: Shade tsei buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo kɛ kɔfe he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Ni baai ni fiteɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my young crops burn and dry up so quickly during the hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Without shade trees to block direct sunlight, extreme heat bakes the topsoil, evaporates moisture quickly, and scorches delicate young crop leaves, causing them to dry up.
ga: Kɛji tsei komɛi bɛ ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Fɛ̃i lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. ni eshãa baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: How do shade trees help my crops survive during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Te tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ harmattan be ni mli egbi lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Trees act as windbreaks against harsh dry winds, reduce water loss from the soil, and create a cooler climate around your crops so they survive dry spells better.
ga: Tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ gãimlibii ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa lɛ he. Tsɔɔmɔ nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shi ni ofee kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I make sure forestry officers know that I am the one who planted the trees on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ koo mli onukpai lɛ le akɛ midu tsei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can register your planted trees with the local Forestry Commission office, which provides official documentation proving you planted and own those trees.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei ni oduɔ lɛ awo maŋ lɛ mli Kooi Ahe Nitsumɔhe lɛ. Enɛ baaha amralo lɛ woji ni tsɔɔ akɛ bo ji mɔ ni du nakai tsei lɛ ni bo ji onɔ̃.

english: Do I need legal permission before I start planting timber trees on my farm?
ga: Ani mla naa hegbɛ he miihia mi dani mabɔi tsei dumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You do not need permission to plant trees on your farm, but registering them with local forestry authorities after planting protects your rights to harvest or keep them later.
ga: Hegbɛ he ehiaaa bo ni okɛdu tsei yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Shi kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ wo maŋ lɛ mli kooi ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ wolo nɔ beni odu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebuɔ hegbɛ ni oyɔɔ akɛ obaakpa loo okɛto sɛɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Will planting too many trees on my farm prevent my crops from growing well?
ga: Ani tsei babaoo ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, if trees are planted too closely together, they block necessary sunlight and compete with your crops for soil nutrients and water, reducing crop growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei tsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa lɛ naa ni amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Which specific types of trees are best to add to my farm for providing crop shade?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mikɛbaafata miŋmɔ lɛ he koni ekɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Fast-growing indigenous trees like Terminalia (Ofram or Emire) or leguminous trees are ideal because they provide broad shade and enrich the soil with nitrogen.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ Terminalia (Ofram loo Emire) loo ŋmeii lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be babaoo ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: Can I grow food crops together with big timber trees without damaging my crop yields?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii yɛ tsei wuji ahe ni mifiteee miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Yes, as long as you space the timber trees wide apart and prune their lower branches so enough sunlight reaches your food crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, be fɛɛ be ni okɛ tsei lɛ baatse amɛhe ni ofolɔ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ koni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ ashɛ oniyenii tsei lɛ ahe.

english: What should I do if many of the tree seedlings I planted die after planting?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji dumɔwui babaoo ni adu lɛ gboi beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should carry out replanting (also called supplying) early in the next rainy season to fill in missing spots and maintain an even shade cover.
ga: Esa akɛ oya nɔ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ. (ni ale lɛ hu akɛ recruitment) yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ shishijee mli koni akɛwo hei ni elaaje lɛ amli ni eha hulutsoo ahi shi daa.

english: Where can I get expert advice on which trees will grow best with my crops?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana ŋaawoo ni he esa yɛ tsei ni baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe?

english: You can talk to your local Agricultural Extension Officer or visit the nearest Forestry Commission district office for free guidance tailored to your region.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ agba sane. Aloo yaa Forestry Commission nitsumɔhe ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ nɔ koni ona ŋaawoo ni aheee nɔ ko ni sa okpokpaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I get my seedlings from a nursery instead of planting seeds directly from my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui yɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu dumɔwui tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ

english: Nursery-raised seedlings come from carefully selected, high-quality parent plants that resist diseases and produce high yields. Seeds taken directly from your harvest often lose those good qualities, resulting in weaker plants and lower yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ jɛɔ nyɛ tsei ni ahala jogbaŋŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli. Enyɛɔ helai anaa ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ nikpamɔ be lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui kpakpai lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same field with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu banana yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn under harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa plants are strong enough for full sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi cacao tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up tightly into tubes when the sun is strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔnei beni hulu lɛ mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism maize uses to save water during dry spells. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot air, preventing water from escaping into the atmosphere.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baa lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekajo foi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings droop and look lifeless right after I move them from the seedbed to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni wala bɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This behavior is called transplant shock. The fine root hairs get temporarily disturbed during moving, making it hard for the plant to drink water immediately. Watering them well in the evening helps them root firmly and bounce back within a few days.
ga: Atsɛɔ subaŋ nɛɛ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Afutuɔ shishifãi ahe yitsɔi bibii lɛ be kukuoo ko yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaanu nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ afɔ amɛ nu jogbaŋŋ gbɛkɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off instead of growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, dry soil, or damage from tiny insects like thrips. Ensuring consistent watering and protecting the plants from sap-sucking pests helps flowers turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni fiteɔ lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni aha amɛ nu daa, ni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni etsɔɔ tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing leafy and tall above ground, but the tubers underneath remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ yɛ baai ni eyɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ? Shi yitso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji bibioo lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing leaves and stems instead of roots. Adding potassium to the soil encourages the plant to store energy underground, giving you larger tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai kɛ shishifãi yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ potassium wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi. Ehaa onáa yitso ni da fe tsutsu lɛ

english: Why do my maize crops grow thin, weak, and produce small ears when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli tseee, ebɛ hewalɛ, ni ewoɔ toi bibii kɛji akɛ adu yɛ tsei babaoo amli lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: Crops planted too close together compete intensely for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Because no individual plant receives enough food, they all grow tall and slender trying to reach the sun, leading to weak stalks and poor yields.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli ejaakɛ tsei lɛ eko kwraa enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Beni tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eshɛ hulu la lɛ he lɛ, edaa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni efeɔ mlɛo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I trim off some of the leaves and side branches from my growing plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mitsei ni miida lɛ ahe baai kɛ esɛɛ niji lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Cutting off unnecessary branches lets sunlight and air circulate freely through the crop canopy, which prevents fungal diseases. It also forces the plant to send its food energy directly into developing large, healthy fruits rather than extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ. ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa Enyɛɔ tsei hu anɔ koni amɛtsɔ niyenii hewalɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ woji krokomɛi amaje lɛ

english: Why do my crops yield less food each year when I continue to plant on the same farm plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ faaa daa afi beni miyaa nɔ miduɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Crops pull specific nutrients out of the earth as they grow. When you harvest every season without replenishing the soil using manure, compost, fertilizer, or crop rotation, the soil becomes exhausted and can no longer nourish new crops effectively.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Beni okpaa nii daa afi ni okɛ shikpɔŋ fataaa he kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei jogbaŋŋ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops whenever the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Because they grow so aggressively, you must clear weeds early so they do not choke your crops or steal their food.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraa oya. Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha amɛkafo oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli loo amɛkaju amɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it important to leave specific space between my trees when planting them on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ yɛ mitsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Giving your trees enough space ensures that their roots do not fight for nutrients and water in the soil, and their leaves get enough sunlight to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Kɛ́ oha otso lɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni eshishifãi lɛ ewuuuu kɛha niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ni tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ náa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: How does planting my crops in straight rows help my farm perform better than planting them randomly?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ fe ni aduɔ amɛ trukaa lɛ?

english: Planting in neat rows makes it easier to walk through your farm to weed, apply fertilizer evenly, and ensures every plant gets equal light and air.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaatsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ajie jwɛi lɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli daa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni enáa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: What should I do if some of the young tree seedlings I planted die off after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ dumɔwui bibii ni midu lɛ ekomɛi gboi yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: You should replace the dead seedlings as soon as possible with fresh, healthy ones—a practice called supplying—so that your land is fully used without empty gaps.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ato dumɔwui ni egboi lɛ najiaŋ oya bɔ ni ooonyɛ—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ sourcing—koni akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmeii akafee nɔ ko.

english: Is it good to cut down old trees completely before planting new ones, or can I just plant new seedlings right next to the old trees?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ ooofolɔ tsei momoi lɛ fɛɛ dani odu ehee? Aloo obaanyɛ odu tso hee yɛ tso momo lɛ masɛi.

english: It is best to clear out old, non-producing trees first. Old trees block needed sunlight and their massive roots steal nutrients and water from the young seedlings.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaajie tsei ni egbɔ ni wooo yibii lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni amɛshishifãi wuji lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli.

english: Why do I need to uproot some plants if I accidentally planted them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei komɛi kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ oshara mli lɛ?

english: Removing extra plants, known as thinning, stops crops from crowding each other. When overcrowded, plants grow thin and weak trying to reach light and produce very little harvest.
ga: Tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ajiemɔ Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ thinning. Ehaa tsei shwieɔ amɛhe shi. Beni gbɔmɛi babaoo yɔɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná la ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: How deep should I dig the hole when transplanting a new tree seedling to my field?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo bu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ tso dumɔwui heei miiwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Dig the hole wide and deep enough so the roots can spread straight without bending upward. Bending the roots in a shallow hole starves the plant of water and stunts its growth.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ bu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ebote mli bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni amɛkuuu amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ okɛ shishifãi lɛ shwie bu ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli lɛ, nu baaha tso lɛ mli ajɔ ni ebaaha edalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: When is the best time of the year for me to plant new tree seedlings on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu tso dumɔwui heei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time is right at the start of the major rainy season. This helps the young roots establish deep in moist soil so the tree can survive the upcoming dry season.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Can I plant heavy-feeding crops like cassava right next to my young tree seedlings?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmei, yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe?

english: Cassava spreads aggressively and takes up a lot of nutrients and moisture from the topsoil, which can choke and weaken young tree seedlings planted right next to it.
ga: Yucca gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni eŋɔɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha adu dumɔwui bibii yɛ amɛmasɛi. cassava and can weaken it

english: Why should I clear the weeds away from the base of my young trees instead of leaving them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ tsei bibii lɛ ashishi moŋ fe ni mashi amɛ?

english: Weeds growing close to the stem act like thieves, stealing the fertilizer, water, and sunshine that your young tree needs to grow fast and strong.
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi, ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei bibii lɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛhe awa.

english: Can I plant other crops inside my maize field, or will they steal food from each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli? Aloo amɛbaaju niyenii kɛjɛ amɛhe?

english: You can plant crops like beans or cowpeas alongside maize. This practice is called intercropping. Legumes like cowpeas actually put nitrogen back into the soil, which helps feed the maize rather than stealing its nutrients.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmãa adu nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa. Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas ji diɛŋtsɛ No sɛɛ lɛ, abaaku sɛɛ akɛ nitrogen lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ haa kooloi niyenii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Will tall maize plants block the sun and ruin smaller crops planted underneath them?
ga: Ani ŋmãa tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ baatsi hulu lɛ naa ni amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni adu yɛ amɛshishi lɛ?

english: Tall crops like maize do cast shade, but you can prevent problems by leaving wider spaces between your maize rows or choosing smaller plants like groundnuts that tolerate partial shade.
ga: Tsei ni kwɔlɔ tamɔ ŋmãa baaha hulutsoo be aba. Shi obaanyɛ otsi naagba nɛɛ naa kɛtsɔ gbɛ babaoo ni oooshi yɛ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ ateŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo halamɔ tsei bibii, tamɔ ŋmei, ni baanyɛ aŋmɛ hulutsoo be fioo ko gbɛ.

english: Is it safe to plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, cassava and maize grow well together because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, leaving the cassava with plenty of room and sunlight to expand later in the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he kome ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ naa he ko babaoo kɛ hulu la ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshwa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some crops grow much better when planted next to legumes like groundnuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ahe lɛ?

english: Legumes have special roots that take natural nitrogen from the air and fix it into the dirt. This acts like a free fertilizer for nearby plants.
ga: Legumes yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: How can I get the most food and money out of my plot of land in one season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná niyenii kɛ shika babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: You can maximize your land by growing fast-maturing vegetables in the open spaces between your main crops, allowing you to harvest multiple types of food from a single plot.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni ooodu yɛ hei ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni yɔɔ onibii titrii lɛ ateŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii srɔtoi babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Which quick-growing crops can I plant to get cash while waiting for main crops to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ makwɛ koni maná shika yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ tso titri lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Vegetables like leafy greens, okra, and peppers grow rapidly and can be harvested in just a few months, giving you quick income while long-term crops are still growing.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai, okra kɛ ŋmeii daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli. Enɛ haa onáa shika oya yɛ be mli ni onibii ni okɛwoɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ yaa nɔ edaa lɛ.

english: Does filling empty spaces with different crops help stop weeds from growing?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ haaa jwɛi akwɛ̃?

english: Yes, planting extra crops covers the bare ground and shades the soil. Without direct sunlight reaching the earth, weed seeds struggle to sprout and grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha hei ni agbele naa lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji hulu la ni shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ewa akɛ jwɛi dumɔwui baakwɛ̃ ni amɛdara.

english: Do all crops take the exact same nutrients out of the soil?
ga: Ani tsei fɛɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: No, different crops feed on different soil nutrients. For example, leafy grain crops use lots of nitrogen, while root crops pull more potassium, so mixing them balances nutrient use.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yeɔ niyenii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ŋmaa ni yɔɔ baai lɛ kɛ nitrogen babaoo tsuɔ nii. yɛ be mli ni shishifãi ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie potassium babaoo kɛjɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei nɛɛ ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ feɔ ekome.

english: What happens to my land if I plant only maize on the same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?

english: Planting the exact same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field season after season.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: As a new farmer, how do I decide which crops will perform well on a new piece of land?
ga: Ákɛ okwaafonyo hee lɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ tsei ni baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Observe what successfully grows on nearby farms, check if your soil drains water well, and start with sturdy crops like maize or cassava that handle variable weather well.
ga: Kwɛmɔ nɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli lɛ. Kwɛmɔ kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ni oje shishi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni tsuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually means the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or is sitting in too much water. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-decomposed manure will help the plant regain its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmei tso lɛ mli loo eyɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when daytime temperatures get too hot, when watering is irregular, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa Aloo be mli ni nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids spreading viruses, or by severe heat stress and lack of soil moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my bean plants grow lots of green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil encourages beans to produce heavy foliage instead of flowers. Beans need balanced soil with enough phosphorus to encourage blooming and healthy pod development.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii hewalɛ koni amɛwo baai ni tsii yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Beans he miihia shikpɔŋ ni ja ni phosphorus fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli kɛha fɔfɔii kɛ pod ni mli wa lɛ shweremɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that create a living umbrella, offering temporary shade and keeping the soil moist during the cocoa plant's first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa. Ha hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni kookoo tso lɛ yeɔ lɛ mli.

english: Is it better for me to plant cassava on raised mounds rather than on flat ground?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava on mounds or ridges loosens the soil so roots can expand into large tubers easily, while also preventing heavy rains from pooling around the roots and causing rot.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ bulbs agboi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eha amɛgboi.

english: What causes my yam tubers to grow deformed and covered in small bumps?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efite ni ŋmeii bibii ehà nɔ?

english: Deformed or bumpy yams usually happen when the roots hit hard or stony soil during growth, or when tiny microscopic soil pests called nematodes attack the tubers underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes ni efite loo eyɛ bu lɛ baa kɛji shishifãi lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi yɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ tutuaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up and droop in the afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Plants curl their leaves during hot afternoons to protect themselves from losing too much water to the intense sun and wind. Once the sun sets and temperatures cool down, the leaves usually recover.
ga: Tsei baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ he. Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why must I wait for the major rains to settle fully before planting my main maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba naagbee dani madu kooloi aniyenii titri, ni ji ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to germinate and then wither away if an unexpected dry spell follows, resulting in wasted seeds, money, and labor.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji hɔmɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ ba. Enɛ haa dumɔwui, shika kɛ nitsumɔ ni afiteɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cabbages stay loose and leafy instead of forming hard, round heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ baai yɛ yitsei ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cabbages require consistent soil moisture and balanced nutrients like phosphorus to form firm heads. Dry spells or hot, nutrient-poor soil keep the leaves open instead of wrapping tightly.
ga: Kaabaji he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ niyenii ni sa, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, koni enyɛ efee yitsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbele moŋ fe ni amɛaabua amɛhe naa shiŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and scorching in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hulu lɛ shãa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or temporary shade trees planted nearby to act as umbrellas, protecting the tender leaves from sun heat and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo. Buu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do cocoa trees grow and yield so well in the Ashanti Region compared to drier areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ashanti kpokpaa lɛ nɔ kɛ akɛto hei ni nu bɛ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need high humidity, rich forest soils, and consistent rainfall to thrive. The Ashanti Region naturally has these ideal weather and soil conditions, whereas drier areas lack the moisture needed for cocoa pods to develop.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ hia hulutsoo ni fa babaoo. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ baa nii. ni eyɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa koni ehiɛ aya hiɛ. Ashanti kpokpaa lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hei ni egbi lɛ bɛ nu ni he hiaa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shweremɔ.

english: What causes the dark spots on my cocoa pods that make the whole pod rot and turn black?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni haa ŋmeii muu lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ lɛ baa?

english: This is Black Pod Disease, which is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during wet and humid seasons. You can manage it by clearing weeds, pruning thick branches to let air flow, and removing infected pods quickly.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela, ni ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ooojie kɛjɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Pruning ni mli tse koni ekɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya.

english: How can I tell if my soil is running out of food for my crops before they die?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa miduɔ nii lɛ bɛ niyenii mli dani amɛgboi?

english: When soil loses nutrients, the older leaves at the bottom of the crop usually turn pale yellow or brown first, growth slows down, and stems become thin. Adding compost or manure helps restore soil richness.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ. Dalɛ baafee mlɛo. ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ baafee bibioo Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches and unwanted shoots from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmeii ni ataooo kɛjɛ mi-koko tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cutting unwanted shoots directs the tree's food and energy into making pods instead of useless leaves, while also opening up the canopy to let sunlight and fresh air reduce disease risks.
ga: Kpojiemɔ ni ataooo lɛ heɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, agbeleɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote mli, ni no haa helai baa shi.

english: Is it safe for me to plant cassava right next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ ŋmei yɛ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ masɛi?

english: Cassava roots drink a lot of water and feed heavily on soil nutrients, which can starve young cocoa seedlings. It is better to plant plantains or gentle crops that share soil resources better.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nuɔ nu babaoo ni amɛyeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha hɔmɔ aye kookoo tsei bibii. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu plantains loo tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii kome lɛ yeɔ egbɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like tubes during the middle of hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ paipii yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a plant's way of protecting itself from drying out. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun to hold onto its moisture until the air cools down.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Tsei haa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly watered and adding organic fertilizer encourages flowers to turn into fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo sũ mli niyenii kpakpai haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do new cocoa seedlings struggle to grow when planted on an old cleared cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji momoi ni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Old farmlands often have exhausted soil nutrients and leftover pests or diseases in the ground. Restoring the soil with manure, organic cover crops, or fallowing helps new seedlings take root successfully.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔji ni etsɛ lɛ amli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai eshwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ Organic tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui heei ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some cocoa seeds fail to sprout when I take them out of the pod and plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii komɛi kwɛɛɛ kɛji mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa seeds lose their ability to grow very quickly once removed from the fresh pod if they dry out in the heat. They must be planted fresh in moist, shaded nursery beds right away.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ adara oya kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii heei lɛ amli kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbi yɛ la mli. Esa akɛ adu amɛ ehee yɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How can I prepare my land for farming without burning the cleared bush?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ kɛha dumɔwui ni shãaa jwɛi ni ajie lɛ?

english: Instead of burning, you can use the slash-and-mulch method by cutting down weeds and spreading them over the soil. This keeps the soil moist, protects useful soil insects, and adds natural nutrients back to your land as the leaves decay.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshã lɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ slashing kɛ mulching atsu nii kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ooofo ni okɛgbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahe ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ be mli ni baai lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: What is the best way to handle cleared weeds so they do not block my crop planting?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ jwɛi ni ajie lɛ ahe nii? Bɔni afee ni ekatsĩ midumɔ naa?

english: You can gather the cleared weeds into neat rows across your field, called windrows. This leaves clear spaces for planting your crops while allowing the piled weeds to slowly rot and enrich the soil between rows.
ga: Obaanyɛ obua jwɛi ni ajie lɛ anaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ windrows. Enɛ haa hegbɛ ni okɛduɔ onibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni jwɛi ni abua naa lɛ fiteɔ fiofio. ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ aya hiɛ

english: How do I stop bushfires from entering and destroying my farm during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi koo mli la ni baa ni efite miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ naa?

english: You can create a firebreak by clearing a strip of land about 3 to 5 meters wide around the boundary of your farm, removing all dry grass and leaves. If a fire starts nearby, it stops at the cleared strip because it runs out of fuel to burn.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee la ni shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ he ko ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee mitai 3 kɛyashi 5 ni ooojie yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi fɛɛ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji la ko bɛŋkɛ La lɛ baakpa yɛ he ni ajieɔ la lɛ yɛ lɛ ejaakɛ fuɛl lɛ baaho.

english: Why do my crops dry up and die after a fire passes near my farm, even if the flames didn't touch them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩ ni amɛgboi yɛ la ni tso yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Kɛji la ni tsoɔ lɛ etswaaa amɛ po?

english: Extreme heat from a nearby fire bakes the soil and damages plant stems and roots. This prevents the plant from absorbing water and nutrients properly, causing it to wither days after the fire.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ la ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ baashã shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekpata tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahiɛ. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ gboɔ gbii babaoo yɛ la lɛ sɛɛ.

english: If I must use fire to clear my land, what is the safest time of day to burn?
ga: Kɛ ehe bahia ni mikɛ la atsu nii kɛjie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Mɛɛ be ji be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mashã?

english: It is safest to burn early in the morning or late in the evening when the wind is calm, temperatures are cooler, and air moisture is higher. Strong afternoon winds can easily carry fire into neighbouring farms.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ oooshã leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ efee dioo. He lɛ mli dɔlɛ baafee mlɛo. ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli fɛ̃i lɛ baaya ŋwɛi. Gbi gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ashɛre la kɛya ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli oya.

english: What practical steps can I take to secure my farm plantation against theft and destruction?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii manyɛ mafee koni mabu ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he kɛjɛ juu kɛ nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Setting up regular patrol routines around your farm borders, planting living fences of thorny bushes, and organizing joint monitoring watch groups with neighboring farmers are effective ways to protect your farm from intruders.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛkwɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ he lɛ ni ooofee Okɛ ŋmeii tsei awo gbogbo mli Ni ooofee kuu ni kwɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni baabote mli lɛ ahe.

english: How do I protect young tree crops from being eaten or trampled by roaming animals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe koni kooloi ni nyiɛɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ akaye amɛ loo amɛkanyiɛ amɛnɔ?

english: You can place individual protective guards made of woven bamboo, palm fronds, or wire mesh around each young tree until they grow tall and strong enough to withstand stray animals.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ ohe bulɔi ni akɛ ŋmeii ni akpɛ́, ŋmei baai, loo waya ni akɛfee lɛ ebɔle tso bibioo fɛɛ tso bibioo he kɛyashi tsei lɛ baafee shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo kooloi ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ.

english: Why does the soil become hard and dry after I completely clear all the bush from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbi beni mijie tsei bibii fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Removing all plant cover exposes bare soil directly to the hot sun and wind, which quickly evaporates moisture and bakes the ground. Keeping a layer of mulch or cover crops helps the soil stay soft and damp.
ga: Tsei lɛ fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ shɛɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ atsɔ oya ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ashã. Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What can I plant to protect my cleared farm field from weeds before planting my main crop?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ madu koni mikɛbu miŋmɔ ni ajie lɛ he kɛjɛ jwɛi ahe dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ?

english: You can plant cover crops like Mucuna or Cowpea. They grow quickly to cover the bare ground, shade out weeds, and trap nitrogen in the soil to feed your main crop later.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa nɔ ko tamɔ Mucuna loo Cowpea. Amɛdaraa oya koni amɛha hei ni agbele naa lɛ anɔ, amɛha jwɛi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛmɔmɔɔ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛha onibii titrii lɛ niyenii yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: How does burning cleared bush harm the food crops I plan to grow later?
ga: Te brɔshi ni ajie lɛ ni ashãa lɛ saa niyenii tsei ni mito gbɛjianɔ akɛ madu sɛɛ mli lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Burning destroys the organic layer of topsoil, kills helpful earthworms, and burns away essential nutrients like nitrogen. Without these, your soil loses fertility and your crops will produce lower yields.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Gbemɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni oshã niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛji enɛɛmɛi bɛ Oshikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni baa shi ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo yibii babaoo.

english: If I buy crop seeds brought from abroad, will they grow well on my land in Ghana?
ga: Kɛ mihe dumɔwui ni akɛba kɛjɛ maŋsɛɛ Ani dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ nɔ?

english: Imported seeds might be bred for cooler climates or different soils, so they can fail or yield poorly in Ghana unless they are hybrid varieties certified and tested for tropical Ghanaian weather and local pests.
ga: Ekolɛ adu dumɔwui ni akɛba maŋsɛɛ lɛ kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli ejɔ loo shikpɔji srɔtoi, no hewɔ lɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛfeee nɔ ko loo amɛwooo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana. Ja eji tsofa ni akɛfee tsofa ni awo he odaseyeli ni aka lɛ akwɛ kɛha Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ jɛmɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui.

english: How many weeks should my tomato seedlings stay in the nursery bed before I move them to the field?
ga: Otsii enyiɛ esa akɛ mi tomato dumɔwui lɛ ahi ŋmɔ mli dani ajie amɛ kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Tomato seedlings typically need 3 to 4 weeks in the nursery until they develop 4 to 5 strong true leaves and a sturdy stem, which helps them withstand the shock of being transplanted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato dumɔwui biɔ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baaná anɔkwa baai 4 kɛyashi 5 ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ tso ni mli wa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ shoofeemɔ ni jɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ mli baa lɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Plantains grow fast and develop large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa trees need during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛnáa baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo tsei yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or that excessive rainfall has flooded the roots, preventing the plant from taking up essential plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ eha shishifãi lɛ eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aye tsei niyenii ni he hiaa waa.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete fiercely for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight, leading to thin stems, weak plants, and very low harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni hulu lɛ mli wa waa Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei bibii, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa ni akpaa lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Pepper flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when the plant experiences extreme dry spells, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to produce extra leaves instead of holding onto its fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ naa hɔmɔ ni naa wa Aloo be mli ni nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo lɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava plants are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready after 9 to 12 months when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the main stem starts to crack as the underground tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛshwieɔ shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do older farmers cover the ground around yam mounds with dried leaves during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni edara lɛ kɛ baai ni egboi haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dried leaves acts as mulch, keeping the soil cool, reducing water loss through evaporation, and protecting the fragile seed yam from drying out under heat.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ baai ni egbi tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehaa nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi ni ebuɔ sweet potatoes ni waaa lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do weeds make my young crops stop growing even when it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi dumɔwui lɛ miikpa kwɛ̃mɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and steal nutrients and light directly from the soil, essentially starving your crop even if there is plenty of water.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. ni ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ moŋ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot exhausts the specific nutrients maize relies on and allows specialized pests and soil diseases to build up in the ground, lowering your yields year after year.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abɛi lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni damɔ enɔ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Young cocoa plants need shelter from harsh sunlight and heat. Without shade trees or plantain plants to shelter them, the sun dries out the soil quickly and scorches the young leaves before the cocoa plant can establish deep roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia he ko ni hulu kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa baajɛ mli aba. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni baaha hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu la lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya ni eshãa baai bibii lɛ dani cacao tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on growing maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an important plant food. When the soil lacks nitrogen, the plant cannot make green leaves to feed itself properly, so applying nitrogen fertilizer or manure helps restore its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa Beni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee baai eŋɔli ni baaha amɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ, no hewɔ lɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds very close to each other on the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. This competition leaves you with tall, weak stalks that produce very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ tsei bibii loo ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do ragged holes suddenly appear in my maize leaves overnight during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli buji ni etse trukaa lɛ? Ani ebaaje kpo nyɔɔŋ kome yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Ragged holes are often caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. These caterpillars hide deep inside the plant leaves during the day to avoid heat and come out at night to eat the young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ahe baai amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be lɛ he. ni amɛje kpo amɛbaye baai bibii gbɛkɛ

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn to white powder and dust after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ batsɔ powda yɛŋ kɛ sũ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects called weevils feed inside the dry grains and multiply. If the grain is not dried properly before storage or kept in airtight bags, the weevils eat out the inside of the grain until only powder remains.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui ni egbi ni amɛshwereɔ. Kɛji akɛ agbiko dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛto loo akɛwo vacuum bag mli. Kplukai lɛ yeɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni powda pɛ eshwɛɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Extreme heat or lack of steady water stresses the plant, forcing it to drop flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ daa lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ ashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ashwie koni akɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why does covering the soil with dry grass help my vegetables grow better during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching yeɔ ebuaa mi-vegetables lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool and prevents water from drying up quickly under the sun, keeping moisture near the roots longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa nu lɛ agbi oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I know that my cassava roots are mature and ready to harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and the soil near the base of the plant begins to crack open due to expanding tubers underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi, ni amɛshiɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ amli shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow curved and small instead of straight and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii moŋ fe ni amɛaafee tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛfee kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become misshapen when the soil beneath the mound is hard, stony, or heavy clay. The tuber cannot push straight down easily through hard soil, so it bends or stops growing long.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ mli wa, tɛi yɔɔ mli, loo shikpɔŋ sũ eyi mli obɔ. Anyɛɛɛ ashɛ yitso lɛ shi tɛ̃ɛ. Etsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ oya No hewɔ lɛ efoɔ loo ekpaa dalɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Plantain trees do not have deep taproots like large forest trees. As the heavy bunch grows at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy, and strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground unless supported with strong wooden poles.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ koo mli tsei wuji. Kɛji kuu lɛ da yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooojɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ja tsei ni wa fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential food for plant growth. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves stay green and support big, healthy corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eye ebua ŋmãa ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests that target that crop to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or beans restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ koni amɛto amɛhe shi. Okɛ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning excess cocoa branches lets sunlight and air into the farm, drying out the leaves and preventing the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kookoo niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli Enɛ haa baai lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: What is causing large holes in my cassava leaves, and will it affect the roots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmei baa mli lɛ baa? Ni ani ebaana shishifãi lɛ anɔ hewalɛ loo ebaana nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Holes in leaves are caused by chewing insects like caterpillars or grasshoppers. Leaves act as solar panels that feed the plant; when insects destroy them, the plant cannot produce enough energy to grow large cassava tubers underground.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulu hewalɛ ni haa tso lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ kooloi bibii lɛ kpata tso lɛ hiɛ lɛ, enyɛŋ ejie hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato plants fall over and rot when the fruits start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ beni aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants have weak stems that cannot support heavy fruit, especially in wet soil. Staking—tying the stems upright to sturdy wooden sticks—keeps the foliage and fruit dry and off the ground, preventing rotting and disease.
ga: Tomato tsei yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ yibii ni tsii nɔ. Titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ Staking—ni ji tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni akɛfiɔ tso ni wa he lɛ—haa baai kɛ aduawai lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛjeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ kɛ helai anaa

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii bibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When planted too close, plantain suckers compete against each other for underground root space, water, and sunlight. Giving them proper distance ensures each tree receives enough resources to grow large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi, nu, kɛ hulu la he akaŋshii mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry spell before the main rainy season truly begins. If seeds germinate after one rain, the hot, dry ground that follows will dry out and kill the young seedlings before the next rain falls.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ kome sɛɛ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baagbi ni ekpata dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop during the hot afternoon even if I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: Hot afternoon sun causes water to evaporate through leaf pores faster than roots can drink it up. Placing dry grass or mulch around the base of the plant keeps the root zone cool and slows down water evaporation from the soil.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ tsɔɔ baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo otso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ fioo.

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops produce unpredictable, weaker plants with much lower yields than the original crop. Buying fresh certified seeds each season guarantees uniform growth and high harvest yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ woɔ tsei babaoo ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba ni amɛhe waaa ni yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa fe shishijee tsei lɛ. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa amɛdaraa daa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my yam mounds if the yam vines are already tall and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi yɛ sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛji akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ekwɛ ni amɛhe wa momo lɛ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal water and soil nutrients away from your crop, regardless of vine size. Clearing weeds ensures all available nutrients in the soil go straight into swelling the yam tubers underground.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ kɛ ekãa juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Ekɔɔɔ he eko bɔ ni wain tso lɛ da ha. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa sweet potato ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my rice crop require standing water in the field while my maize will rot in it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ he hiaa ŋmãa tsei yɛ amɛŋmɔji amli shi ŋmãa fiteɔ yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels in their stems and roots that allow them to breathe underwater, whereas maize roots suffocate and rot when trapped in flooded soil without air.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he ko krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni haa amɛmuɔ yɛ nu shishi. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu ebɔko he lɛ nɔ.

english: How do improved seed varieties manage to produce so many more bags of grain than my traditional seeds?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ afee dumɔwui kotokui babaoo fe mishishijee dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are specifically bred to direct more energy into growing heavy grain heads rather than tall stems, and they are stronger at absorbing nutrients from the soil efficiently.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛha hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii moŋ fe ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ. Ni amɛmɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young rice plants turning light yellow instead of remaining deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants use to make green leaves; without enough nitrogen, the plant slows down its growth and loses color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji nitrogen he bolɔmɔ. which is the main food plant that plants use to make their green leaves If there is not enough nitrogen The plant will slow its growth and lose color.

english: If I plant my crops closer together, won't I get a much bigger harvest from my small plot of land?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ manyɛ maná ŋmaa babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Ani minɔ ni?

english: Planting too close makes crops compete like overcrowded crowd members for limited sunlight, water, and soil food, leaving you with weak stems and small, empty grain heads.
