ga: Tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli tamɔ asafo babaoo ni ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ. koni onine ashɛ hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa onáa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui ayitsei bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why do my tall rice plants fall over flat in the mud right when the grain heads get full?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ lɛ? Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ gbee muji lɛ mli beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ pɛ?

english: Rice plants fall over when their stems are too thin to support heavy grains, which often happens if they received too much early fertilizer or if water level was managed poorly during stem growth.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ bafee mlɛo tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfi ŋmaa ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛji akɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii oya tsɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nu lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why does applying chemical fertilizer during a heavy downpour waste my money?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ heɔ shika lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer off the topsoil before the plant's roots have time to drink it in, carrying your expensive plant food straight into nearby streams.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ. and take your expensive plant food straight to a nearby stream.

english: Why do weeds always grow faster than my main crop during the early weeks of planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitso titri lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsi ni mikɛduɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to steal water and food from the soil faster than cultivated crops, which need extra care and weed-free space when they are young.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛbiɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni jwɛi ko bɛ mli kɛ́ amɛji gbekɛbii.

english: Why do birds start invading my rice field only when the crop turns from green to light brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi jeɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli tutuamɔ shishi pɛ kɛkɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ etsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli mli kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ?

english: As rice matures and changes color, the developing grains fill with sweet, soft liquid starch that birds love to eat before the grains harden into final harvest seeds.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ eda ni etsake ehiɛ lɛ, ŋmãa ni miiya hiɛ lɛ eyi ŋmãa ni mli ŋɔɔ ni ji ŋmãa ni okpoi sumɔɔ ni amɛye lɛ mli dani ewa ni etsɔ naagbee ŋmãa ni akpa.

english: Why does my harvest yield drop every year if I plant rice on the same piece of land without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Planting the exact same crop every year drains the specific nutrients that crop loves and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ be fɛɛ be Afi lɛ hoɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do government subsidies under programs like Planting for Food and Jobs focus so much on providing certified seeds rather than just land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli yelikɛbuamɔ ni yɔɔ gbɛjianɔtoi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ kɛha niyenii kɛ nitsumɔi ashishi lɛ kɔɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ni akɛhaa lɛ he moŋ fe shikpɔŋ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Good land alone cannot guarantee a high yield; certified seeds guarantee high germination rates and disease protection, giving every farmer a high baseline harvest regardless of land size.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa pɛ nyɛŋ aha sɛɛnamɔi babaoo aba. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi fɛɛ ni amɛnáa shishijee yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ kɔɔɔ he eko.

english: Can I use the same fertilizer I use for my maize on my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa ŋmãa lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii yɛ cacao tsei anɔ?

english: No, cocoa trees and maize have different nutrient requirements. Cocoa needs higher amounts of potassium and phosphorus to produce strong pods over many years, while maize requires more nitrogen for fast leaf and stalk growth.
ga: Dabi, cacao kɛ ŋmãa yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he hiamɔ nii srɔtoi. Cocoa biɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus babaoo koni ekɛfee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa yɛ afii babaoo mli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa he miihia nitrogen babaoo koni baa kɛ ŋmãa lɛ adara oya.

english: Why does every crop seem to require a different kind of fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Different crops feed on nutrients in different ways. For instance, leaf crops need nitrogen to stay green, while flowering and fruiting crops need potassium and phosphorus, so fertilizers are blended specifically to match what each crop needs.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ gbɛ̀i srɔtoi anɔ. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ he miihia nitrogen koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yibii lɛ he hiaa potassium kɛ phosphorus lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futuɔ mli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛtsu tso henɔ fɛɛ tso hiamɔ nii ahe nii.

english: Fertilizer acts like food for plants by supplying essential minerals like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium that may be missing from the soil. These minerals help plants build strong roots, healthy leaves, and large fruits.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛha tsei kɛtsɔ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium ni ekolɛ ebaafee nɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ekɛhaa lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ tɛ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛ naa shishifãi ni wa, baai ni wa, kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: What will happen to my crops if I apply too much fertilizer at once?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii yɛ be kome mli?

english: Applying too much fertilizer can burn plant roots and leaves, stunt their growth, or even kill the crop because excess fertilizer creates salt levels in the soil that prevent plants from drawing water.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ashã. etsĩɔ ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ naa loo efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii po Enɛ ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmei baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaaa tsei lɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Should I apply fertilizer right when I put seeds in the soil or wait until they sprout?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ loo mamɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Most crops benefit from fertilizer applied shortly after sprouting. Placing high-strength fertilizer directly on young seeds can burn them, so it is usually applied near the roots once the plant starts growing.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo náa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ he sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni mli wa waa wo dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛshã. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ he ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ́ tso lɛ bɔi dalɛ.

english: How do I know if my farmland's soil actually needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: If your crops grow slowly, have yellowish leaves, or produce smaller harvests than in previous years, these are clear signs that the soil has lost its nutrients and requires fertilizer to rebuild its strength.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo, amɛyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo amɛwoɔ yibii fioo fe afii ni eho lɛ. Enɛɛmɛi ji okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ miiho lɛ miifite, ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛtswa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are often a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil, not a lack of water. Water helps the plant drink, but without enough nitrogen in the soil, the leaves cannot stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jeee nu ni faaa yɛ mɔ mli. Nu yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnuɔ nu. Shi kɛji akɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Baai lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Do I still need to fertilize my land if I let it rest and fallow for two years?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mawo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lolo kɛji miha ejɔɔ ehe ni ehi shi afii enyɔ?

english: Fallowing restores some natural organic matter, but high-yielding modern crops extract nutrients quickly. Adding fertilizer helps ensure your land has enough nutrients to support a full, heavy crop after resting.
ga: Fallow tsei lɛ adumɔ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ekomɛi aba ekoŋŋ. Shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oshikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hejɔɔmɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do cocoa trees need different care compared to food crops like cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a permanent tree crop that lives for decades and continually produces pods, so it needs long-term soil nourishment and shade, while cassava grows quickly, consumes nutrients fast, and is harvested within a year.
ga: Cocoa ji tso ko ni hiɔ shi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yaa nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aha lɛ niyenii kɛ hulutsoo ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. be mli ni ŋmei daa oya Ye niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya ni akpa yɛ afi kome mli

english: How does the quality of my soil affect the final yield of my harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ bɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ saa naagbee yibiiwoo ni mikpaa lɛ he?

english: Healthy, nutrient-rich soil allows crops to grow deeper roots, resist diseases better, and produce larger, heavier fruits or tubers, whereas poor soil starves the plant even if weather conditions are good.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi, ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Helai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ hela ni ewoɔ yibii loo yitsei ni da ni tsii yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ baaha tsei aye hɔmɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ hi po.

english: Why should I measure and plant my crops in straight lines instead of scattering them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe ni madu yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛshwã?

english: Planting in straight lines gives every crop equal space, sunlight, and nutrients. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier compared to scattering seeds randomly.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko, hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa fe dumɔwui ni agbɛɔ ashwãa trukaa lɛ.

english: How deep should I cover my seeds with soil when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ sũ aha midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛyashɛ he ni eshɛɔ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: A good general rule is to cover seeds with soil about two to three times their size. Planting too deep starves the shoot of energy before it reaches sunlight, while planting too shallow leaves seeds exposed to birds and hot sun.
ga: Mla kpakpa ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ ji ni akɛ sũ ni feɔ dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ aaafee toi 2-3 aha dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ adu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ afite dani eshɛ hulu la lɛ he. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha okpoi kɛ hulu lɛ aná dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why are my seeds taking so long to sprout after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need the right balance of soil moisture, warmth, and depth to sprout. If the soil is too dry, too hard, or the seed was buried too deep, germination will be delayed or fail completely.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ, dɔlɛ kɛ mlibotemɔ teŋ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ, ewa tsɔ, loo afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ, Ekwɛ̃mɔ baahe sɛɛ loo ebaafite kwraa.

english: Is it safe for me to dig up buried seeds to check if they are growing underground?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafo dumɔwui ni afu lɛ koni mana kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Digging up seeds can break the delicate young roots and shoots that are just starting to form, or expose them to insects. It is best to keep the soil damp and give them time to break through naturally.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsa lɛ baanyɛ akumɔ shishifãi bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ kɛkɛ lɛ. aloo ha emɔ kooloi bibii Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oha lɛ be ni ebote mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my neighbor's crops sprout faster than mine even when we plant on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe mi nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔdu amɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Differences in seed quality, how deep the seeds were planted, soil moisture levels, or seed treatments cause crops on nearby farms to sprout at different speeds.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔi yɛ dumɔwui ahe nibii amli Dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ mlibotemɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo dumɔwui lɛ ahe nitsumɔ Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oyaiyeli srɔtoi.

english: How can I check if the seeds I saved from my last harvest are still good to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ sa lolo akɛ adu?

english: You can test them by placing ten seeds in a wet cloth in a warm place for a few days. If seven or eight of them sprout, your seed batch is healthy and ready for the field.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ mli yɛ he ko ni mli edɔ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui kpawo loo kpaanyɔ kwɛ̃ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ odumɔwui akuu lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ adu.

english: What is the advantage of using modern recommended farming practices instead of my traditional local methods?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mimaŋ kusum gbɛi lɛ najiaŋ lɛ he?

english: Modern recommended practices use tested plant spacing, healthy seed varieties, and proper timing for nutrients, which helps you produce much higher crop yields on the same size of land.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nifeemɔ ni ajieɔ yi lɛ kɛ gbɛ ni kã tsei ateŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni akɛka amɛ akwɛ. Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ be ni sa kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ Enɛ baaye abua bo ni oná ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo yɛ he ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young plants turning yellow shortly after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to make leaves green and strong, or that the ground is holding too much water around the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei yɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa amɛbaai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo tsɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and soil food away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the resources they need to grow fast and strong.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do some crop seeds need to grow in a nursery first before I move them to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu dumɔwui komɛi yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani ajie kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tiny, delicate seeds need extra shade, soft soil, and constant care when they are small. A nursery protects them until they are strong enough to survive the harsh sun and rain in the main field.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ he miihia hulutsoo. shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni yaa nɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ darako lolo lɛ Dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ baabu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ hulu ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to grow my tomato seeds in a small seedbed first before moving them to my main farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tomato dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli lɛ? Dani mifã kɛtee miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli

english: When tomato plants are very young, they are fragile and easily killed by harsh sun, heavy rain, or bugs. Raising them in a small nursery lets you care for them easily until they grow strong enough to survive transplanting into the main field.
ga: Beni tomato tsei lɛ darako kwraa lɛ Amɛhe waaa ni hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, loo kooloi bibii gbeɔ amɛ oya. Kɛ́ otsɔse amɛ yɛ shĩa bibioo ko mli lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ amɛ mlɛo kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ okɛwo saatso wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and die if I clear away all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong, direct sunlight. Larger trees act as a natural shelter, keeping the air cool and protecting the baby cocoa leaves from scorching until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli abobaahe. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã kɛyashi tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ enáa hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: If multiple maize seeds sprout right next to each other in one hole, why should I pull out the smaller ones?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie dumɔwui bibii lɛ?

english: When crops grow too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Removing the weaker sprouts gives the remaining stem full access to food, allowing it to grow tall and produce large, full ears of maize.
ga: Kɛ tsei dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekwɛɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmãa toi agboi ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants yield very thin tubers when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse waa kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need room under the ground to swell into fat tubers. Planting them too close restricts underground space and starves the roots of soil food, causing the plant to make thin, woody roots instead of big food tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔni afee ni amɛfu ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haaa he ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ afee bibioo ni ehaa niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ. Ehaa tsei feɔ shishifãi bibii. Yɛ niyenii yitso agbo najiaŋ

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, drink water and steal plant food directly from the main mother plantain tree. Removing most of them focuses all the plant's energy into producing one heavy, healthy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi bibii krokomɛi loo tsei bibii nuɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ tso niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Efã ni fa fe fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa plantains kuu kome ni tsii ni he wa lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize has run out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. The plant starves its oldest leaves to send the last remaining food up to the new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Tso lɛ baaye ebaa ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ hɔmɔ koni ekɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje shweremɔ hee.

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests that feed on that specific plant to multiply in the ground. Rotating different crops gives the soil time to rebuild its strength.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ nakai tso lɛ koni amɛshwere yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛtswaa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any peppers appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani pepper lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience sudden stress, such as severe heat or dry soil. Dropping flowers is the plant's way of saving water and energy to stay alive until conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔii kɛji akɛ amɛ kpe trukaa nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even when my soil is rich and wet?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo fɔ ni edɔ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than domestic crops and steal water, light, and fertilizer out of the soil before your crops can reach them, essentially starving your crops even in good soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe maŋ tsei lɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu, kane kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa po nɔ.

english: Why do I need to tie my tomato plants to wooden sticks off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fĩɔ tsei ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Lifting tomato branches off the soil keeps the leaves away from damp ground where fungi live, preventing rot and leaf diseases while keeping the growing fruits clean and dry.
ga: Kɛ́ owó tomato niji anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ akaje hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi lɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ baa helai anaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha aduawai ni aduɔ lɛ ahe atse ni amɛgbi.

english: How many helpers or laborers do I need to hire to help me plant an acre of plantain?
ga: Yelikɛbualɔi loo nitsulɔi enyiɛ ehe baahia ni maŋɔ koni amɛye amɛbua mi ni madu plantain acre kome?

english: The number of helpers you need depends on how quickly you want to finish and the condition of the land. Typically, hiring 3 to 5 laborers is enough to clear, dig holes, and plant one acre of plantains within a couple of days.
ga: Yelikɛbualɔi ayibɔ ni he baahia bo lɛ damɔ bɔ ni osumɔɔ ni ogbe naa oya kɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nitsulɔi 3 kɛyashi 5 ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛbaajie, atsa bu, ni adu tsei bibii ni dalɛ ji acre 1 yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: How does sharing land with farm helpers or partners work when planting plantains in Ghana?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ ni akɛ ŋmɔ mli yelikɛbualɔ loo hefatalɔ ko jaa lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ oodu plantain yɛ Ghana?

english: In Ghanaian farming communities, agreements like land-sharing or labor-sharing (such as 'nnoboa') allow you to plant on someone else's land or hire helpers who contribute land in exchange for a agreed portion of the crop produce or profits after harvest.
ga: Yɛ Ghana okwaayeli akutsei amli lɛ, kpaŋmɔi tamɔ shikpɔŋ mlijaa loo nitsumɔ mlijaa (tamɔ ‘noboa’) haa onyɛɔ oduɔ nii yɛ mɔ kroko shikpɔŋ nɔ. Aloo ŋɔɔ yelikɛbualɔ ko ni kɛ shikpɔŋ haa koni ekɛtsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ mlijaa oha mlijaa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo sɛɛnamɔi ni anáa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What kind of land preparation do I need to do before my helpers start planting plantain suckers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani yelikɛbualɔ lɛ aje dumɔwui adumɔ shishi?

english: You need to clear the bush, remove heavy stumps, and dig wide holes about 30cm deep. Filling the holes with rich topsoil or well-rotted manure gives the plantain roots a soft, nutrient-rich start.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ. Jiemɔ tsei akutsei ni tsii lɛ ni otsa bu ni mli kwɔ aaafee 30 cm. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋwɛi sũ ni mli eyi obɔ loo sũ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata bu lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha plantain shishifãi lɛ aná shishijee ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: How far apart should I plant my plantain trees on the farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Plantain suckers should be spaced about 3 meters (10 feet) apart from each other. Proper spacing ensures that the large leaves don't block sunlight from neighboring plants and that roots don't fight for soil nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ plantain tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ afee mitai 3 (naji 10). Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa koni baai wuji lɛ akatsĩii hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ naa. ni shishifãi lɛ ewuuuu koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ

english: How long does a plantain plant take from the day I plant it until the crop is ready for harvest?
ga: Kɛjɛ gbi ni midu mi-plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ, be enyiɛ ebaahe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baafee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: Most plantain varieties in Ghana take between 12 to 15 months to produce a ripe harvestable bunch, provided they receive good rainfall and care during their early growth stage.
ga: Plantain henɔi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 dani amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni abaanyɛ akpa. Kɛji akɛ onine shɛ nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ kwɛmɔ kpakpa nɔ yɛ shweremɔ shishijee fãi lɛ amli.

english: What is the best time of the year in Ghana to plant plantains on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana ni mikɛbaadu plantains yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to plant is at the beginning of the major rainy season, usually around April or May. This gives the young suckers enough water to build strong roots before any dry spell begins.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee April loo May. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa dani hulutsoo be lɛ aje shishi.

english: Plantains have broad leaves that lose water rapidly in dry, hot weather. Yellowing or drooping leaves are the plant's natural reaction to heat stress, which can be managed by leaving cut grass around the base as mulch to trap soil moisture.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji bɔ ni tso lɛ feɔ enii ehaa kɛji edɔ waa. Abaanyɛ atsu enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni afolɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ nɔ. Shishitoo lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: I notice many small shoots growing around my plantain tree; should I cut them off or leave them?
ga: Miyɔse tso bibioo ko. Mɛi babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe. mi plantain Ani esa akɛ mafo mli loo mashi?

english: You should trim away excess shoots and keep only 2 or 3 suckers per stand (one main bearing plant, one medium follower, and one small shoot). Keeping too many shoots steals nutrients from the main crop, leading to small plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni okɛ ŋmeii 2 loo 3 pɛ ahi shi yɛ shidaamɔhe kome nɔ (tso titri ni woɔ yibii 1, tso ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ 1, kɛ tso bibioo ni woɔ yibii 1). Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ejuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. ni kɛ plantain tsei bibii baa

english: Why do plantain trees easily fall over when the bunch gets big, and how can I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ da lɛ? Ni te ooofee tɛŋŋ otsĩ naa?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy weight at the top. When the bunch grows large, strong winds can push the tree down; you can prevent this by propping up the stem with a notched wooden pole or strong bamboo stick.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛhe wa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ashɛ tso lɛ shi. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tso ni yɔɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmei tso ni wa ni okɛbaafi sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I plant plantains on the same piece of land alongside other crops like cocoa or cassava?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ tsei krokomɛi, tamɔ kookoo loo ŋmei?

english: Yes, plantains are great companion crops. Their broad leaves provide helpful shade to young cocoa trees during their early years, while leaving enough space in between rows for temporary food crops like cassava or cocoyam.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains ji nanemɛi tsei wuji. Baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛhaa kookoo tsei bibii yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ koni akɛdu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Why are my bean leaves turning yellow after I sprayed medicine on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves usually turn yellow after spraying if the chemical was mixed too strong, applied during the hot midday sun, or if the wrong type of herbicide or pesticide was used for that specific crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛfutu lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛtsu nii yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ejaaa lɛ tsu nii yɛ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: When is the best time of day for me to spray chemical medicine on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is best because cool temperatures prevent the chemical from evaporating too quickly or burning the crop leaves in intense sunshine.
ga: Leebi loo shwane mli ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ hulutsoo be lɛ haaa tsofai lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ. aloo ni ehaa tsei ahe baai lɛ shãa kɛji hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛhe

english: If I spray weedkiller on my plot, how long should I wait before planting my crops?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: You should generally wait at least 2 to 3 weeks after applying weedkiller so the chemical can break down in the soil, preventing it from harming your new seeds as they sprout.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ omɛ kɛ hoo lɛ otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ beni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ etsu nii sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsofai lɛ anyɛ afite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni akafite dumɔwui heei lɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my bean plants drop their flowers before producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Bean plants often drop their flowers when they experience heat stress, lack of water, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo, nu ni bɛ, loo kɛ́ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ ha tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural defense mechanism to reduce its surface area exposed to the sun, helping the plant conserve moisture and prevent drying out during hot weather.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa hulu la ni shɛɔ enɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni ehaaa amɛgbi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why are my crops growing very tall with plenty of leaves but giving me very little yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer and not enough phosphorus or potassium, encouraging leaf growth instead of flower and fruit development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni ji nitrogen lɛ fa babaoo ni phosphorus loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: How can I tell if insects are damaging my crops or if it is a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii miifite miŋmɔshi nibii loo hela miipiŋ amɛ?

english: Insect damage usually leaves visible holes, chewed edges, or clear bite marks on leaves and stems, whereas diseases often show up as spots, colored patches, wilting, or rotting without any chewing marks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ kɛ bu ni anaa, ŋmeii ni atsɔ mli, loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ srɔtoi yɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Yɛ be mli ni hela lɛ fɔɔ baa akɛ ŋmɔtɔ Ayɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Egbo loo egbo ni ŋmɔlɔ he okadi bɛ he

english: Why do my bean pods look twisted and small instead of full and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea pods lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee bibioo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eyi obɔ kɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Deformed or twisted pods are typically caused by sap-sucking insects, such as pod-bugs or thrips, feeding on the flowers and young pods early in their development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni efite loo efite lɛ baa. ni yeɔ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛjɛɔ shishijee fã ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli

english: How close together should I plant my bean seeds so they grow well?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-beans lɛ he ni mabɛŋkɛ he fɛɛ he tɛŋŋ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Beans need about 15 to 20 centimeters between plants so they do not compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and air circulation, which prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Peas he miihia aaafee sɛntimita 15 kɛyashi 20 yɛ tsei ateŋ bɔni afee ni amɛkaye hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: How do I know if my farmland soil lacks nutrients and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Signs of weak soil include slow crop growth, pale yellow leaves, thin stems, and low yields even when there is enough rain and no insect attack.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lɛ he ji tsei ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, tsei bibii, kɛ yibiiwoo fioo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ koolooi ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their leaves and stop flowering during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai ni amɛkpaa fɔfɔi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the dry harmattan season, trees lose water rapidly through their leaves. To protect themselves from drying out and dying, cocoa trees drop leaves and delay flowering to conserve water until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛhaa amɛfɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ koni amɛbu nu he kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba. Koni okɛbu ohe he koni okagbi ni ogbo.

english: Why does cocoa in Ghana produce pods in two separate seasons instead of continuously all year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ bei enyɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ

english: Cocoa tree flowering and pod development are closely tied to rainfall cycles. The long rainy season triggers the main harvest crop, while the shorter rainy period triggers a smaller mid-crop harvest.
ga: Cacao tso lɛ fɔfɔii kɛ eshishifãi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ yɔɔ tsakpaa waa. Nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ akpamɔ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuji haa ŋmaakpamɔ ni baa yɛ be teŋgbɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I don't leave bigger shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ? Akɛni mishiii tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa mihe hewɔ lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective canopy umbrellas, keeping the temperature cool and preventing tender leaves from burning while retaining moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa baai bibii lɛ shãaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn dark black and rot while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ fĩ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Black pods are caused by fungal infections that spread easily in damp, overcast weather. Excess shade and standing moisture allow the fungus to thrive, which rots the pods before they can mature.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ atatu mli lɛ kɛ pods diji baa. Shade ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ daa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: Why should I cut off the straight shoots that sprout at the bottom of my cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers or chupons, steal water and nutrients away from the main trunk. Removing them allows the tree to direct its energy into developing healthy branches and producing more pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots loo chupons lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji ni mli wa ni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo baa.

english: Why do many small cocoa flowers fall off the tree without growing into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi bibii lɛ ji Fɔfɔi babaoo gbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ shi amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: A tree naturally produces more flowers than it can feed. If the tree experiences stress from heat, dry soil, or low nutrients, it drops extra flowers to save its strength for survival.
ga: Tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua. Kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa lɛ, Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi krokomɛi koni amɛhiɛ amɛhewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees yield fewer pods when I plant them very close to one another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close together, their branches block sunlight from reaching inner leaves, and their roots fight for the same limited water and food in the soil.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso niji tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ amli. Ni tsei shishifãi baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning light green or yellow even when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often indicate that the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen. Heavy rain can also wash away vital nutrients from the topsoil, leaving the plant undernourished.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ náaa niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Why do my cocoa trees look weak and stunted when heavy rainwater sits around their roots for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ebɔle amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water covers the roots for too long, it suffocates them, preventing the tree from taking up nutrients and causing root decay.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ha shishifãi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ebaaha okɛ ohe awo mli Etsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekaná niyenii ni haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do weeds cause my young crops to grow so slowly even during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi dumɔwui lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ be mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crop plants and aggressively drink up water, absorb fertilizer, and block sunlight, effectively starving your crop of what it needs to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tso lɛ ni ekɛ ekãa nuɔ nu, ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii, ni etsĩɔ hulu la naa, ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii ni shwereɔ waa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees drying up and dying during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate root systems and leaves that lose water very quickly in harsh dry winds like the harmattan. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby shelters them from direct sun and drying winds until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni haa nu fiteɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni mli egbi tamɔ harmattan mli. Shade tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ baaha abu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ he kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants curling up tightly like pipes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves as a defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, preventing water loss. While it protects the crop temporarily, it is a sign that the soil needs more moisture.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛba he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Tsi nu ni fiteɔ lɛ naa Kɛji ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ be kukuoo mli po Shi eji okadi hu ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ babaoo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many tiny flowers, but almost none of them grow into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo, shi eshwɛ fioo ni fɔfɔi lɛ eko kwraa baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers rely on tiny beneficial insects called midges to pollinate them. If the soil is too dry or harsh chemicals are used, these insects disappear, causing unpollinated flowers to drop off without producing pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ damɔɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ anɔ. Atsɛɔ nakai midge kɛha ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo akɛ tsofai ni mli wa tsu nii lɛ Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ baaje mli. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni bɛ pollen lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear the heavy bush around my cocoa farm before the major rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie brɔshi ni mli wa lɛ? Yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he dani nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ aba?

english: Clearing bush and excess shade allows fresh air and sunlight to reach the stems, which prevents damp conditions where black pod disease thrives once heavy rains arrive.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei bibii ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa yɛ he ni black pod hela baanyɛ ada yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become soft and rot inside when I harvest them in waterlogged soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ akpa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot breathe when trapped in flooded soil for long periods, which causes soil bacteria to break them down and rot them. Planting on raised soil mounds allows excess water to drain away from the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu kɛji akɛ amɛwo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why do my seed yams rot underground instead of sprouting after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam seed setts rot if planted in overly wet soil or if the cut surfaces of the seeds were not allowed to dry and heal before planting, allowing soil fungi to infect the exposed fleshy part.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ baafite kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ nɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ aŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni dumɔwu lɛ hiɛ ni afo lɛ agbi ni etsa dani adu. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atswa hei ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow at the bottom of the plant while the top is still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni ŋwɛigbɛi lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the lower leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for green growth. The plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ, ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ Tsei lɛ yeɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛha ŋmɔji heei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over after heavy rain and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and do not grip deep into the soil. As heavy bunches grow, the plant becomes top-heavy, so propping the stems with sturdy wooden poles prevents them from uprooting.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛshɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji kuu lɛ da lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tso ni mli wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekaje shishi.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout when I push them deep into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds carry limited energy inside them to push their first shoot upward. If planted too deep, the shoot exhausts its energy before reaching sunlight and dies underground.
ga: Dumɔwu lɛ bɛ hewalɛ fioo yɛ emli ni ekɛtsiɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmei lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu mli tsɔ lɛ Hewalɛ baaho yɛ Tsoi lɛ amli dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my pepper plants remain small and stunted when weeds grow around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo ni egbɔjɔ be mli ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ebɔleɔ he lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal essential water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your pepper plants. Removing weeds early allows the crop to get full nourishment to grow tall.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa o-pepper tsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni yeɔ emuu koni amɛdara.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot hours to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the sun. This is the plant's natural mechanism to conserve water and prevent moisture loss during dry weather.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni hulu la ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli lɛ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and turn brown when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sun. They need shade crops like plantains planted beside them to block direct sunlight and keep the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni ebu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow and curling up into strange twisted shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow, twisted cassava leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The disease prevents the plant from producing food, leading to small cassava roots.
ga: Kasava baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etsɔ mli lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Hela nɛɛ haaa tsei afee niyenii. Efeɔ cassava shishifãi bibii

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when water is inconsistent, or when pollination fails. High heat stops the pollen inside the flower from fertilizing the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ nu lɛ ejaaa loo kɛ́ pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee nɔ ko lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haaa pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ akawo tsei lɛ amli.

english: Yams become crooked when the soil is too hard and compact for the tubers to expand easily, or when microscopic worms called nematodes attack the roots in the soil.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni ebɔle ehe tsɔ ni eha ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. aloo kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ tutua shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow from the tips inward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛmligbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tip and moves down the middle stripe is a sign of nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen is essential for leafy green growth and stalk strength.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni eyaa shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen he hia kɛha baa eŋɔli dalɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishi hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when wind blows, even before the fruits mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ? Dani aduawai lɛ po baakwɛ̃?

english: Plantain trees collapse easily when underground pests like banana weevils or nematodes damage their root system, weakening the plant's hold on the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ banana ŋmeii loo nematodes fite shishifãi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ ni baa shi.

english: Why are my green oranges dropping to the ground long before they are ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tangerines lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Fruit drop in citrus is often caused by fruit flies laying eggs inside the fruit, or by sudden shifts between dry soil conditions and heavy rainfall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ citrus aduawai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ baa ji aduawai amli ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ aduawai lɛ amli. aloo kɛjɛ tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ teŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of thick leaves but produce very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai lɛ mli tse waa shi eshishifãi lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ?

english: When leguminous crops like cowpeas receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing stems and leaves instead of forming flowers and seed pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii, tamɔ tsina ŋmeii, nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ŋmɔji

english: Why do seeds I saved from last year's maize harvest grow weaker plants than the packaged seeds I buy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɔjɔ fe dumɔwui ni mihe yɛ paketii amli lɛ?

english: Commercial hybrid seeds are specially bred to yield heavily in their first generation. If you save and replant those seeds, the new plants lose their vigor, uniformity, and disease resistance.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee jarayeli nibii krokomɛi lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ to ni odu lɛ Tsei heei lɛ ahewalɛ, ekomefeemɔ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ.

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and light to grow strong and produce bigger yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to make green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes the nutrients deep into the ground where roots cannot reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava plant grow very tall with plenty of leaves, but produces tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo, shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium, the plant spends all its strength growing tall branches and leaves above ground instead of sending food down to grow big tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo tsei niji kɛ baai ni kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaatsu niyenii kɛya shi koni amɛwo bulbs wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my newly planted plantain suckers drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain tsei ni midu ehee lɛ anɔ lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: Young plantain suckers lose water quickly through their large leaves before their new roots settle in the dirt. Cutting off top leaves when planting helps the sucker hold onto moisture until new roots grow.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ baai wuji anɔ dani shishifãi heei baagbee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli beni aduɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ nu mli nu lɛ kɛyashiɔ shishifãi heei baakwɛ̃ɔ.

english: What is causing small holes in the leaves of my young maize crops?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Small holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by caterpillars like Fall Armyworms that crawl into the central leaves of the plant to feed before the leaf fully unfolds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworms, ni shwieɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye niyenii dani baai lɛ agbeleɔ kwraa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa.

english: Plantains do not have deep wooden roots like trees; their roots are shallow and spread out near the topsoil. When a bunch becomes heavy, the high center of gravity easily pulls the plant down during strong winds unless supported with wooden poles.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ tsei. Eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ kuu lɛ bɔi tsiimɔ Hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ baagbala tso lɛ shi mlɛo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. ja tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off without turning into fruit during the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When heat is too intense and dry winds blow, the flower drops off naturally to save energy because the plant cannot support forming fruits without enough moisture.
ga: Kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi miitswa lɛ Fɔfɔi baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nyɛŋ aye abua ni amɛwo yibii kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli.

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and keeps weeds from stealing nutrients.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya, ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ aju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so crop roots can drink it in. Placing fertilizer on dry soil can burn the roots and damage the crop instead of helping it grow.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ ni efite tso lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua lɛ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow healthy leaves. It can happen when heavy rains wash nutrients away or when the soil is worn out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni baai ni wa akwɛ̃. Ebaanyɛ eba beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, leaving free plant food behind for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in clay or poorly drained soil for too long, the roots drown and soil fungi attack them, causing them to rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baatutua amɛ. ha egbo

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer when the soil is completely dry during a hot dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fataaa he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so roots can safely drink it. If applied to dry soil, the concentrated salts draw water out of the plant roots and burn them.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, Nu ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli ni eshãa.

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when heat is extreme or when water supply drops suddenly. The heat prevents the flowers from pollinating properly, so the plant sheds them to save energy.
ga: Tomatoi fɔ̃ɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ba shi trukaa. Dɔlɛ lɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ akafite hewalɛ lɛ, amɛshwieɔ nu.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and stopping new leaves from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi baai heei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves, or a virus spread by whiteflies that distorts plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mites loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni ŋmeii yɛŋ ni fiteɔ tsei adalɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant four or five maize seeds together in one hole to get more food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ yɛ bu kome mli koni maná niyenii babaoo?

english: When seeds are crowded in one hole, the seedlings fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food, resulting in thin stems and tiny or empty cobs instead of strong stalks with big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ atswa dumɔwui lɛ awo bu kome mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. loo efolo Yɛ tso ni mli wa ni ŋmei agbo yɔɔ mli lɛ najiaŋ

english: Yam leaves are like small solar panels that make food for the tuber underground. Staking holds the leaves high up in the sunlight and air, keeping them dry and preventing disease.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ tamɔ hulutsoo be mli tsɔnei bibii ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi yɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Keeps leaves dry and prevents disease.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetables with dry grass or cocoa husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmeii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil acts like a blanket that keeps the sun from drying out the ground too fast, reduces weed growth, and keeps the soil cool for root development.
ga: Mulching tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu lɛ akagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ oya tsɔ. Ha jwɛi lɛ adalɛ aba shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the soil of the specific nutrients maize relies on and allows soil-borne pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi damɔ nɔ lɛ ni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain tree, they fight each other for water and soil nutrients, resulting in small fruit bunches. Leaving only the main plant and one or two strong suckers ensures large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ, dumɔwu kome Amɛbaawuu amɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa anáa aduawai bibii. Tso titri lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ eshwɛ koni plantains lɛ adara ni etsii.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready to harvest under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the main stem near the soil level becomes thick and woody.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni tso lɛ tso titri ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ tsei.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy that feeds the tubers growing underground. Lifting the vines on stakes helps them catch sunlight and prevents leaves from rotting on wet soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni akɛhaa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Kɛ́ awó wein tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la, ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies spreading viral diseases, or by physical stress from extreme heat and irregular watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ tomato mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa mli baa lɛ mli.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any peppers form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience heat stress, lack of water, or when given too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo haomɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo kɛji akɛ amɛná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: The season's first rain is often followed by a dry spell that can dry out the soil and kill young germinating seeds. It is safer to wait until the rainy pattern becomes regular and reliable.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui bibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and thin even when rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa beni nugbɔ enɛɔ po lɛ?

english: Weeds act like aggressive neighbors that steal water, fertilizer, and light away from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the resources they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants need plantain trees planted right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni adu plantain yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct hot sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the gentle shade and humidity cocoa seedlings need to survive their early stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli jɔ koni amɛhi shi mra.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key plant food. The maize plant naturally pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the growing top leaves and young corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri. Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa ni miida lɛ kɛ abɛi toi bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato flowers drop off without setting fruit when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture swings quickly from dry to wet. Extremely hot air stresses the plant, causing it to shed its blossoms to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni ekɛ yibii baaa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my farmland make the ground better for corn in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha efee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmeii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest the groundnuts, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth, acting as natural fertilizer for the next crop like maize.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okpa ŋmei Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot in the ground when heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the farm and water sits in the soil without draining, the roots get suffocated from lack of oxygen and fungi quickly cause them to soften and rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ ni nu lɛ tsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni nu bɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ haa amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: Why can rice survive in flooded swamp water while my maize plants rot in the same water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmãa ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Be mli ni mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miifite yɛ nu kome mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels inside their stems and roots that pump air down from above the water into their roots. Maize plants do not have these internal air pipes, so their roots drown when submerged in water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsui krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ nu lɛ yiteŋ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Abɛi tsei lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔnei ni yɔɔ amɛmli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ eshishifãi lɛ wo nu mli lɛ, eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the afternoon heat even when the soil still feels moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, pepper leaves lose water into the hot air faster than their roots can pull it up from the ground. The plant temporarily droops to protect itself, but usually recovers in the cooler evening once water uptake catches up.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baashwie baai lɛ shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ehe he. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɛɔ shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli beni nu eŋɔ lɛ lɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes inside the stems and leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei kɛ baai lɛ egbɛ eshwa lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by caterpillars like the fall armyworm. These insects hide in the tight central leaves of the plant during the day and eat the soft young leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ fall armyworm lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baa bibii amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo.

english: Why do I need to place long wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kakadaji ahe hiaa mi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants produce vines that need to lift their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves dry and exposed to light, which helps the plant manufacture energy to grow large tubers underground while reducing leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei woɔ wain tsei ni ehe hiaa ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa la shɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ehaa folier helai baa shi.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables spoil quickly on the way to the market while other crops last longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Vegetables harvested during the hot afternoon heat retain high temperatures and lose water quickly, speeding up spoilage. Harvesting early in the morning when crops are cool keeps them crisp and helps them stay fresh longer during transport.
ga: Aduawai ni akpaa yɛ shwane mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ ni nu lɛ hu sɛɛ foɔ oya. accelerates spoilage Nikpamɔ leebi beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehiɔ shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɔ shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I spend money to buy new crop varieties when I can just keep using my old seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafite shika yɛ tsei srɔtoi heei ahe lɛ? Mɛɛ be manyɛ maya nɔ mikɛ dumɔwui momo lɛ atsu nii?

english: New crop varieties are specially bred to give much higher yields and better survival rates, which can lead to significantly larger profits at harvest compared to older traditional seeds.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha sɛɛnamɔi babaoo aba yɛ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ni etsɛ fe tsutsu lɛ ahe.

english: How can changing the type of variety I plant help increase the amount of money I make at harvest?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tso srɔtoi ni miduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ baanyɛ aha shika ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties produce more fruit or grain per plant and are better at surviving, meaning more of what you plant reaches the market, giving you a bigger harvest to sell for profit.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii loo dumɔwui babaoo yɛ tso kome mli ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nɔ ni oduɔ lɛ babaoo baaha aya jara nɔ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nibii babaoo ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ koni oná sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Is it risky to switch to a new crop variety if my old one has always worked okay for me?
ga: Ani oshara ko yɛ tso henɔ hee ni mikɛbaatsake lɛ he kɛji akɛ mitso momo lɛ etsu nii jogbaŋŋ eha mi be fɛɛ be?

english: While old varieties are familiar, they often reach a limit on how much they produce. New varieties carry high potential for much larger yields and higher income, making them a worthwhile upgrade when managed properly.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ale srɔtoi momo lɛ moŋ, Shi bei pii lɛ, husu yɛ nibii ni afeɔ lɛ he. Hei srɔtoi lɛ yɛ nyɛmɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni baaha yibii babaoo aba ni amɛná shika babaoo. Enɛ haa efeɔ srɔtoi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does it matter where I buy my seedlings, or are all seedlings sold by local farmers the same?
ga: Ekɔɔɔ he eko he ni miheɔ dumɔwui yɛ. Aloo ani dumɔwui ni maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi hɔ̃ɔ lɛ fɛɛ ji ekome?

english: Where you buy seedlings matters a lot because farmers who do not know proper cultivation methods may sell weak or unhealthy plants that will fail to grow well in your field.
ga: He ni oheɔ dumɔwui yɛ lɛ he hiaa waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, okwaafoi ni leee gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni baakwɛ̃ŋ jogbaŋŋ yɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if the crop seedlings I am buying will actually grow well on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Good seedlings come from trained growers who know proper nursery techniques. Healthy seedlings have strong stems, good roots, and are grown under proper conditions so a high number survive after planting.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai jɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsɔse amɛ ni le gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ adɛŋ. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni wa, shishifãi kpakpai ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛ ni sa mli. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui babaoo yɛ ni hiɔ shi kɛ́ adu amɛ.

english: Why do some seedlings die shortly after I plant them on my land while others survive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi gboiɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ, yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hiɔ shi lɛ?

english: Seedlings often die if they were poorly cultivated in the nursery before you bought them, or if they lack the strength to handle transplanting into the field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui gboiɔ kɛji akɛ aduuu amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ dani ohé amɛ. aloo kɛji amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaafã kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Out of 100 seedlings that I plant, how many should I expect to successfully sprout and grow?
ga: Kɛjɛ dumɔwui 100 ni midu lɛ mli Tsei enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛdara yɛ omanyeyeli mli?

english: If you are using high-quality seeds or seedlings cultivated properly, a significant majority—often 80 to 90 out of 100—should successfully sprout and grow into healthy plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ loo dumɔwui ni adu jogbaŋŋ tsu nii. Esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ babaoo—bei pii lɛ 80 kɛyashi 90 yɛ 100 mli—aye omanye yɛ kwɛ̃mɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ mli ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes a batch of seeds or seedlings to have a low sprouting rate after planting?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui akuu loo dumɔwu ko kwɛ̃ɔ fioo yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Low sprouting rates usually happen due to poor quality parent plants, incorrect nursery care, poor seed handling, or buying planting materials from inexperienced growers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kwɛ̃mɔ ni baa shi lɛ baa yɛ fɔlɔ tsei ni ehiii lɛ ahewɔ. Dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe ni ejaaa, dumɔwui akwɛmɔ ni ejaaa loo dumɔ nibii ahemɔ kɛjɛ dumɔlɔi ni bɛ niiashikpamɔ adɛŋ

english: Why do some of my neighbors harvest so much more produce than I do from the same size plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋbii lɛ ekomɛi kpaɔ nii babaoo fe mi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Farmers with higher harvests often use improved, high-yielding crop varieties and source healthy seedlings from skilled growers who prepare the plants correctly for high field survival.
ga: Okwaafoi ni kpaɔ nii babaoo lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ atsu nii. ni amɛná dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛlɔi ni he esa ni saa tsei jogbaŋŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ amli lɛ adɛŋ.

english: What is the most important thing I should focus on if I want to get a very large yield from my crop field this season?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama nɔ kɛji miisumɔ ni maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Focus on selecting high-yield improved crop varieties and obtaining healthy, well-cultivated seedlings so that nearly every plant you put in the ground survives and produces heavily.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛjwɛŋmɔ maa nɔ ji tsei srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ahalamɔ. ni oná dumɔwui ni mli wa ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni nɔ ni miihe ashɛ tso fɛɛ tso ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anyɛ ahi shi ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa trees are tender and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that provide essential shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ ŋmɛɔ ehe shi lɛ.

english: Yam vines need support to spread their leaves toward sunlight. Exposure to sunlight helps the leaves make food, which travels down to make the underground tubers grow bigger.
