ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia yelikɛbuamɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ mli. Hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni eha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii akwɛ̃

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests after planting maize on the same plot for three years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo beni midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afii etɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the ground. Planting it on the same spot repeatedly drains the soil without giving it time to recover, leading to lower yields.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ nu ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: If I plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize, will it help my crops?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmãa du tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Ani ebaaye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, beans and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps your maize grow better.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is causing the leaves of my cassava plants to curl up and turn yellowish-white?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ-yɛŋ?

english: This is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness spread by tiny whiteflies that suck juices from the leaves and weaken the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. No shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do tiny bugs destroy my maize grains after I put them in storage sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii Koni amɛfite mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ beni mikɛwo kotoku lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Weevils attack stored grain if the maize was not dried completely before bagging, or if the storage area is not properly sealed against pests.
ga: Weevils baatutua ŋmaa ni ato lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmaa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛwo kotoku mli. aloo kɛji akɛ atsĩko he ni akɛ nibii lɛ toɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɛɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why should I clear the weeds around my pepper plants regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? daa pepper tso

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight directly from your pepper plants, which slows down their growth and reduces the amount of pepper you harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ pepper tsei amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ fioo, ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni okpaa lɛ aba shi.

english: Will cutting off extra branches from my cocoa tree hurt the plant?
ga: Ani niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso mli lɛ baaye tso lɛ awui?

english: No, pruning dead or overcrowded branches lets air and sunlight flow through the tree, which prevents diseases like black pod and encourages the tree to produce more pods.
ga: Dabi, niji ni egboi loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji anaa ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without forming fruit when the weather becomes too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the tomato plant, causing it to drop its blossoms to save energy and water rather than feeding new fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha yibii heei aba lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and have wide leaves that provide necessary shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa plants are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa lolo lɛ.

english: Why do farmers plant cassava and maize together on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi feɔ ekome kɛduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Maize grows tall and matures quickly in a few months, while cassava grows slowly underground. Planting them together lets you harvest maize early while leaving space for the cassava to mature later without wasting land.
ga: Abɛi daa ni ekwɛɔ oya yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, nanemɛi adumɔ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmei lɛ mra ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ daa sɛɛ mli ni efiteee he ko.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the maize green up again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge green leaves but very tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen or water, it puts all its energy into growing tall leaves on top instead of storing food in the roots below ground.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo nɔ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kakadaji yɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas can make their own plant food from the air. If you add extra nitrogen fertilizer to the soil, the plant gets lazy and grows only leaves instead of flowers and pods.
ga: Cowpeas baanyɛ afee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ tso niyenii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ Tso lɛ bafeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baai pɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants keep falling off without forming peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho ni amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or when there are no bees around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kɛ́ ŋmeii komɛi bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often caused by irregular watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my yam vines curling up and changing color?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsake amɛsu lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in yam plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or by fungal diseases that spread during hot, damp weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo fungal helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ sweet potato tsei anɔ lɛ baa.

english: Plantain roots are close to the surface and can be weakened underground by tiny worms called nematodes or root borers, leaving the tree unsupported.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ, ni ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso lɛ fioo pɛ fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to sow my seeds after the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adũ dumɔwui yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ?

english: Do not plant after the very first rain because the deep soil is still dry. Wait until you get two or three steady rains so the seeds have enough moisture to germinate and stay alive.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli egbi lolo. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni eha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft stems and shallow roots that cannot tolerate extreme heat and dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shade and traps soil moisture to protect them until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ naa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts in the same farm where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they naturally feed nitrogen into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the maize.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛhaa nitrogen woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa.

english: Why should I heap soil into mounds or ridges before planting cassava and yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ato shikpɔŋ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei amli dani adu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei?

english: Root crops need loose, soft soil to expand underground. Making mounds or ridges gives the tubers space to grow big while also preventing heavy rains from washing away topsoil or flooding the roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni afee lɛ haa tuber lɛ náa he ko ni da. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ loo ekɛ nu akawo shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow even when I plant right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ moŋ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long hot dry spell before the actual rainy season begins. If seeds germinate after the first rain but do not get follow-up moisture, the tender roots quickly dry up and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ shi amɛnáaa ŋmɔtɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ. Shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow from the center outward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower leaves is a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and grow leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore healthy green foliage.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni esa akɛ tsei ahi eŋɔli ni eye ebua amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛdara. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Yam leaves produce food for the plant using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get maximum sunlight and airflow, which helps direct more energy down into growing large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo atsɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo yaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is fully ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 and 12 months after planting. You can tell it is ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and cracks appear in the soil around the base of the plant stem.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo hiɔ shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni ŋmeii je kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why is it better to leave cut weeds on top of the soil instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaashi jwɛi ni afo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ moŋ fe ni aaashã lɛ?

english: Leaving clearings on top of the soil creates a protective blanket called mulch. Mulch keeps the soil cool under direct sun, slows down water evaporation, and gradually breaks down into rich plant food.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hei ni agbele lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch baa. Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi fiofio ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the center stem?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is caused by pests like the fall armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of young maize plants to eat the fresh green leaves before the plant produces corn ears.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ dani tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmãa toi.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark spots and rot when there is continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: High moisture and humidity encourage fungal growth on tomato leaves. When water sits on the leaves without drying off, fungal spores multiply quickly, causing spots, leaf rot, and damaged fruits.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii daa yɛ tomato baai anɔ. Kɛ nu kpɛtɛ baai lɛ ahe ni egbiko lɛ Fungal spores lɛ faa oya, ni ekɛ ŋmeii, baai lɛ fitemɔ kɛ aduawai lɛ fitemɔ baa.

english: What should I do to protect my vegetable crops if my farm water supply runs out during a hot week?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mabu mi-aduawai lɛ ahe kɛji nu fite yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ otsi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: You can use mulching, which means covering the dry soil around your plants with dry leaves, grass, or straw. Mulching traps moisture in the soil for much longer and prevents the sun from drying out the plant roots quickly.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ mulching atsu nii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Mulching baaha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be babaoo, ni ebaatsi hulu la naa koni ekaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbi oya tamɔ bɔ ni eji lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to water my crops directly on the leaves or right at the base near the roots?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu yɛ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: You should always water directly at the base of the plant near the roots. Plant leaves cannot drink water to feed the crop, and wet leaves attract fungal diseases like blight, especially in humid weather.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ nu awo tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ be fɛɛ be. Tso baai nyɛŋ anu nu ni amɛkɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii. Ni baai ni efɔ lɛ gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ baa tsɛŋemɔ, titri lɛ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why does my skin itch or burn whenever I break cassava stems or cut certain farm plants during harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mihewolo lɛ shãa loo shãa be fɛɛ be ni mafo ŋmei tso loo mafo ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Some crop varieties release milky sap or natural defensive liquids when cut, which contain substances that irritate human skin. Washing your skin with clean water immediately after contact and wearing long sleeves prevents this irritation.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ekomɛi jieɔ nu loo nu ni buɔ mɔ he kɛji afo amɛ. ni nibii ni haa adesa hewolo nɔ mli fuɔ lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli tse tsu hewolo lɛ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mɔ ko kɛ ehe wo mli, ni owo atadei ni hiɛ nine kakadaŋŋ agbo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafee nɛkɛ mlifu nɛɛ.

english: If liquid farm chemicals or liquid fertilizer accidentally splash onto my skin, what is the first thing I should do?
ga: Kɛji tsofai ni ji nu ni jɛ ŋmɔ mli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwie mihewolo nɔ yɛ oshara mli Mɛni esa akɛ mafee klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: You should immediately rinse the exposed skin with plenty of clean running water and soap to flush away the chemicals, and change into clean clothing to stop your skin from getting chemical burns.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ nu ni mli tse kɛ samla babaoo afɔ ohewolo ni eje kpo lɛ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni okɛjie tsofai lɛ. Ni otsake atadei ni he tse koni tsofa akashã bo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when I plant them in a clear, open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse, ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to strong direct sunlight and can easily get heat-stressed. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a living shelter that protects the young cocoa until its roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he tɛ̃ɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná dɔlɛ he haomɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa anáa he ko ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli waɔ.

english: Maize leaves roll inward during hot afternoons as a natural defense mechanism to reduce their surface area exposed to the sun, which helps the plant conserve internal water and prevent drying out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha he ni hulu lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu toɔ emli ni ehaaa egbi.

english: How can I tell if my pepper plants are hungry for nutrients or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mi-pepper tso lɛ kɛha niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: When crops lack nutrients, their leaves often change color from deep green to light green or yellow, their stem growth slows down, and they fail to produce enough flowers or healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛyaa eŋɔli ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ mli. Tso lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ fioo. ni enyɛŋ ewo fɔfɔi loo aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa

english: Should I pour chemical fertilizer directly against the main stem of my plant?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafɔse tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo mitso lɛ shishigbɛ titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, placing fertilizer right against the stem can burn and damage the plant tissue. You should apply it in a ring or line a few inches away from the stem so the roots can reach out and absorb it safely.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ ashã ni efite. Esa akɛ okɛwo ring loo line mli ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi 2-3 koni shishifãi lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo ni amɛŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: If I notice one cassava plant on my farm with twisted, yellow leaves, why should I pull it out immediately?
ga: Kɛji miyɔse ŋmei tso ko yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsɔ mli lɛ Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Twisted, yellow leaves are usually a sign of a viral disease like Cassava Mosaic, which spreads quickly to healthy crops through tiny sap-sucking insects. Removing and destroying the infected plant early stops the disease from spreading across your entire farm.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni etsake lɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa, tamɔ cassava mosaic he okadi. Egbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli oya kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ anɔ. Gbalamɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ahiɛ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables rot so quickly if I pack them into sacks while they are still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikɛwo kotokui amli be mli ni amɛhe ejɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Trapping moisture inside closed sacks creates high heat and humidity, which provides the perfect environment for rot-causing bacteria and fungi to grow rapidly on your harvested produce.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni akɛwoɔ kotoku ni aŋã mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i babaoo baa. Enɛ ji he ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha helai ni haa mɔ fiteɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baa lɛ oya yɛ okpamɔ lɛ mli.

english: What is urea fertilizer, and how does it help my crops grow?
ga: Mɛni ji urea? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Urea is a nitrogen-rich fertilizer that gives crops the energy they need to grow strong green leaves and stems. When crops look pale or grow slowly, applying urea helps them bounce back quickly.
ga: Urea ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Beni ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛdaraa blɛoo lɛ Urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: What is the difference between urea and ammonia fertilizers for my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ urea kɛ ammonia ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Both supply nitrogen to feed your crops, but urea comes in dry granules that are easy to spread by hand, while ammonia is often a liquid or gas that requires special equipment and careful handling so it does not evaporate into the air.
ga: Enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛ nitrogen haa koni akɛha onibii lɛ niyenii. Shi urea lɛ baa yɛ ŋmeii ni egbi ni ewaaa akɛ akɛ nine baagbɛ ashwã mli. Yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ ammonia ji nu loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni biɔ nibii krɛdɛɛi kɛ nitsumɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ ehe wooo kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops turn pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make their food. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or ammonia helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji tsei ni he hiaa koni akɛfee niyenii Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ammonia ni akɛbaafata he Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni efee hewalɛ.

english: How does feeding my crops nitrogen fertilizer help them give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo?

english: Nitrogen acts like food for plant growth; it helps crops grow bigger leaves to catch more sunlight, which allows the plant to produce more grains, fruits, or tubers at harvest time.
ga: Nitrogen tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛha tsei adalɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ naa baai wuji koni enine ashɛ hulu la babaoo nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ dumɔwui, aduawai loo ŋmeii babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: How can I accurately measure fertilizer so I do not destroy my crops by giving them too much?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayibɔ he pɛpɛɛpɛ? Bɔni afee ni mikafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ nɔ.

english: You can use clean, small containers like empty milk tins or specific measuring cups to give each plant a controlled dose. Giving too much fertilizer at once can burn plant roots and ruin your crop.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsɛnsi bibioo ko ni he tse tamɔ mliki tsinsii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli loo kɔɔpoo krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe lɛ atsu nii ni okɛkwɛ bɔ ni tso fɛɛ tso yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni efite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to put fertilizer on my fields?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔji lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the sun is not too hot. High heat can cause fertilizers like urea to evaporate into the air before the plant roots can drink them up.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni hulu lɛ edɔɔɔ tsɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ.

english: Why do some agricultural stores sell 25-kilogram bags of fertilizer instead of the large 50-kilogram bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli shwapoi komɛi hɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsiimɔ ji kilogram 25 yɛ kotokui wuji ni tsiimɔ ji kilogram 50 lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Smaller 25-kilogram bags are easier to carry across rough farm paths and allow smallholder farmers to buy just the right amount of fertilizer they can afford without straining their backs or budgets.
ga: Ewaaa akɛ akɛ kotokui ni tsiimɔ shɛɛɛ kilogram 25 baatsɔ ŋmɔ mli gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ anɔ. ni eha okwaafoi bibii lɛ anyɛ ahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe ni amɛkuuu shikatoohe loo shika he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli.

english: What do people mean when they refer to 'Obroni' or commercial fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni gbɔmɛi tsɔɔ kɛ amɛmiiwie ‘Obroni’ loo jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Obroni' or commercial fertilizer refers to factory-made, store-bought chemical fertilizers that contain concentrated nutrients, as opposed to natural manures or compost made on the farm.
ga: Obroni’ loo jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii tsɔɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni afeɔ yɛ nitsumɔhei, ni aheɔ yɛ shwapoi amli ni niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni afeɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ he.

english: Is it safe for me to store my harvested grains in an empty fertilizer bag?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ baawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ amli?

english: You should only use an empty fertilizer sack for harvested food if it has been thoroughly washed and cleared of all chemical residues. Leftover fertilizer dust can poison your food crops.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ kotokui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛha niyenii ni akpa lɛ pɛ kɛji afɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ ni ajie tsofai ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mli. Fertilizer sũ ni eshwɛ lɛ baanyɛ afite oniyenii tsei lɛ.

english: Why does fertilizer seem to disappear from my soil after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Nitrogen fertilizers dissolve very quickly in water. Heavy rains can wash the nutrients deep into the soil past the roots where the plant cannot reach them, or wash them away off the surface of your farm.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ nu mli oya waa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛtsɔ shishifãi ni tsei nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ anɔ. loo ofɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe

english: Why are my young cocoa trees not producing any pods after one year of planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ ewooo ŋmɔtɔ yɛ afi kome ni mikɛdu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need time to build strong root systems and mature before flowering. Most hybrid cocoa varieties in Ghana take about two to three years to start bearing fruit, so early patience, watering, and care are required before you see a harvest.
ga: Cacao tsei he miihia be koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa ni eda dani amɛwo fɔfɔi. Cocoa tsei ni akɛfee tsofai ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi, no hewɔ lɛ tsuishitoo, nu kɛ mra be mli kwɛmɔ he miihia. Dani obaana nibii ni akɛfee lɛ

english: Why should I spend money on fertilizer when my crops are still very small and not fruiting yet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo ni amɛwooo yibii lolo lɛ?

english: Applying fertilizer early provides young plants with essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus. This helps them develop thick stems and deep roots, ensuring much higher crop yields and profits once they start producing.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa tsei ni mli tse kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Enɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni anáa lɛ baafee babaoo kɛji akɛ aje nitsumɔ shishi pɛ.

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and easily damaged by intense direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby acts like a natural canopy, protecting the seedlings from heat while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he yɛ be mli ni ekwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i nɔ.

english: How does clearing weeds regularly help my crops produce more harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛná ŋmaa babaoo?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Regular weeding ensures that all the nutrients and fertilizer go straight into your crops, leading to faster growth and bigger harvests.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ekɛ dalɛ ni yaa oya kɛ ŋmaa babaoo baa.

english: Will cutting off extra branches from my crop plants hurt them or reduce my yield?
ga: Ani niji ni fa fe nine ni miduɔ lɛ mli ni mifoɔ lɛ baaye amɛ awui loo ebaaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi?

english: No, pruning removes unproductive or diseased branches, allowing the plant to direct its energy toward growing healthy fruits. It also lets sunlight and air pass through, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Dabi, niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛduɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ mli. Tsi fungal helai anaa

english: Why does my land yield fewer crops now compared to when I first cleared the forest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe be mli ni mijie nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Every harvest removes nutrients from the soil. Over time, continuous farming drains the natural richness of the land, requiring you to restore fertility using compost, animal manure, or chemical fertilizers.
ga: Nikpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ biɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli lɛ aku sɛɛ aha fɔmɔ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava alongside my cocoa trees, or will they spoil the cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei yɛ kookoo tsei ahe? Aloo kookoo lɛ baafite?

english: You can plant temporary crops like plantain or cocoyam with cocoa because they provide initial shade and food. However, deep-rooted crops like cassava should be kept at a safe distance so they do not fight with cocoa roots for soil nutrients.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ be kukuoo mli tsei tamɔ plantains loo cocoa adu kɛ cocoa ejaakɛ amɛhaa hulutsoo kɛ shishijee niyenii. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ akɛ tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ ŋmei lɛ ato he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. Bɔni afee ni kookoo shishifãi akatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, overly shaded conditions. You can manage it by clearing weeds, pruning excess branches to improve airflow, and applying recommended fungicides.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli. Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ooojie kɛjɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my crops dry out so quickly during the dry Harmattan season even after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ po lɛ?

english: Dry Harmattan winds and hot sun cause soil moisture to evaporate rapidly. Covering the soil around your crop roots with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool and traps water longer.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: If my cocoa farm looks weak in the first two years, should I abandon it and try another crop?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ amli Ani Esa akɛ mashɛ mafɔ shi ni madu ehee?

english: No, tree crops like cocoa often look slow and struggling in their early stages while establishing roots. With consistent weeding, pest control, and proper shade management, weak young farms often turn into high-yielding, profitable farms by year three or four.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ, etamɔ nɔ ni tsei tamɔ kookoo lɛ yaa hiɛ blɛoo ni ewaa yɛ shishijee mli yɛ be mli ni amɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ. Kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli daa kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa nɔ Obalaŋtai, bei pii lɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛ hewalɛ bafeɔ ŋmɔji ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he yɛ afi ni ji etɛ loo ejwɛ lɛ mli.

english: If I clear a large piece of fresh land that has never been farmed before, can I plant my crop seeds right away?
ga: Kɛji mijie sũ agbo ko ni atsuko he nii dã lɛ Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Newly cleared soil often has undisturbed weed seeds, hidden pests, and uneven nutrients. It is best to clear, plow, and let the soil rest for a few weeks so beneficial air and moisture can mix in before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, jwɛi dumɔwui ni nɔ ko nɔ ko gbaaa amɛnaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajie ehee lɛ nɔ. tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ niyenii ni ejaaa Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni ajie, atsu nii, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe otsii fioo komɛi. Bɔni afee ni anyɛ akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ afutu mli dani adu.

english: Is it bad for my crop's health if I burn the bush on a newly acquired field before planting?
ga: Ani ebaaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewalɛ nɔ awui kɛji mishã jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ hee ni mihe lɛ mli lɛ dani midu?

english: While burning clears land quickly and creates ash for short-term fertility, it kills beneficial soil organisms, destroys organic matter, and leaves crops vulnerable to soil drying out rapidly in the sun.
ga: yɛ be mli ni la ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ oya ni ehaa sũ baa koni ekɛ be kukuoo mli fɔmɔ aba. Ebaagbe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ.

english: What happens to crop roots when I plant them in hard soil that was cleared using heavy machinery?
ga: Mɛni baa shishifãi ni aduɔ lɛ anɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni akɛ tsɔnei ni tsii etsu nii kɛjie lɛ nɔ?

english: Heavy machines compact the soil, pressing the earth tightly together. This makes it difficult for delicate crop roots to push deep for water and nutrients, which can stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akɛ amɛaatsi nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛya shɔŋŋ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei adalɛ naa.

english: Why do crops grow very tall and leafy on newly cleared bushland, but sometimes fail to produce good fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛfeɔ baai yɛ koo shikpɔŋ hee ni ajie lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi bei komɛi lɛ, enyɛŋ ewo yibii kpakpai.

english: Freshly cleared soil is often high in nitrogen, which makes plants focus all their energy on growing stem and leaves instead of flowering and setting fruit.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ kpo ehee lɛ fɔɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii lɛ

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my main crop whenever I open up a new field for farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ be fɛɛ be ni magbele ŋmɔ hee kɛha dumɔ nii lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can sleep in the ground for years. When you open up new land to sunlight and rain, those wild seeds wake up instantly and grow faster than cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ aka shikpɔŋ afii babaoo. Beni ogbeleɔ he hee ko koni hulu kɛ nugbɔ anɛ. Nakai koo mli dumɔwui lɛ baate shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ oya fe dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: If I clear all the big trees off a new piece of land, will my young crops grow better in full sunlight?
ga: Kɛ mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ hee ko nɔ lɛ, ani miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Some young crops like cocoa need partial shade when they are young to protect their soft leaves from harsh sunlight and conserve soil moisture. Removing all trees can scorch young seedlings.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii komɛi, tamɔ kookoo lɛ, he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo beni amɛji bibii lɛ koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tso muu lɛ fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui bibii.

english: Why do some crops like oil palm take years to harvest while maize takes only a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi, tamɔ oil palm lɛ, heɔ afii babaoo dani akpaa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa hiɔ shi nyɔji fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Maize is an annual crop that lives for one season, focusing energy on fast seeds. Oil palm is a perennial crop that spends its early years building a strong trunk and deep root system before producing fruit for many years.
ga: Abɛi ji tso ko ni yeɔ daa afi ni ehiɔ shi be kome. Hewalɛ ni jɛɔ oya dumɔwui amli lɛ nɔ jwɛŋmɔ. Oil palm ji tso ko ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni ekɛ eshishijee afii lɛ yeɔ daa. koni ekɛfee tsei ahe tsei ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani ewo yibii afii babaoo

english: If I have a huge piece of land, why can't I plant my seeds very close together to get more yield?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ shikpɔŋ agbo Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibiiwoo babaoo?

english: Crops planted too close together compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and underground root space, resulting in weak plants and smaller harvests overall.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: If I plant the exact same crop on my farm every single year, why does my harvest get smaller over time?
ga: Kɛji akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ, mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: The same crop continuously sucks out the exact same soil nutrients every year and attracts specific pests that build up in the soil, weakening future harvests unless crops are rotated.
ga: Tsei nɛɛ nɔŋŋ yeɔ sũ mli niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be afi fɛɛ afi. ni egbalaa kooloi bibii pɔtɛɛ ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmaakpamɔi lɛ baafee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ. ja atsake tsei lɛ

english: How do tree crops stay alive and green during the long dry season in Ghana without dying?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei hiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ Ghana ni amɛgbooo?

english: Established tree crops develop deep taproots that reach underground water tables far beneath the dry topsoil, allowing them to drink even when it does not rain.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ woɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu jɛɛhei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛnuɔ nu be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: Why do my crops still get sick even after I spray chemical medicine on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hela lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai wo amɛmli moŋ?

english: Chemical sprays work best when applied at the right dosage and proper time. If you mix the wrong amount, use an incorrect chemical, or spray right before heavy rain, the medicine washes away and pests or diseases will continue to harm your crops.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo mli bɔ ni sa kɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛji okɛ tsofai ni ejaaa futu mli Okɛ tsofai ni ejaaa tsu nii Loo okɛshwie nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛ waa. Tsofa lɛ baaho ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai fɛɛ ni baa lɛ baaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui lolo.

english: How do I know if my soil needs fertilizer before I start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: Taking soil samples from your field for testing reveals which specific nutrients are missing. This allows you to apply the exact fertilizer your land needs instead of wasting money on chemicals that will not help your crops grow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ko ni oooŋɔ kɛjɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ koni aka lɛ okwɛ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ ni bɛ mli lɛ kpo. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii koni ekɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiamɔ nii akpã gbee. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite shika yɛ tsofai ni yeɔ ebuaaa onibii ni okwɛ̃ lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Why do my young seedlings wither when I move them from the nursery into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings causes transplant shock because their delicate roots get disturbed and exposed to harsh sunlight. Watering them properly and transplanting during cooler late afternoons helps them settle into the new field safely.
ga: Dumɔwui ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ haa amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ haoɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Nu ni sa kɛ ŋmɔji ni aduɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ He ni hulutsoo be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ ŋmɔji heei amli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is it dangerous to guess the amount of crop medicine I mix into my knapsack sprayer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ masusu tsofa ni mikɛfutuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛfutuɔ misɛɛ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Guessing dosages can either make the mixture too weak to kill pests or too strong, which burns crop leaves and leaves harmful chemical residues in the harvest. Proper measurement ensures effective pest control without damaging the plants.
ga: Kɛ́ osusu bɔ ni tsofa lɛ fa ha lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ akɛ tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ egbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo ehe wa tsɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛshiɔ tsofai ni eshwɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ lɛ mli. Susumɔ ni sa haa anyɛɔ akuɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee tso lɛ.

english: What happens to my maize if I put too much fertilizer around the roots?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo shishifãi lɛ ahe?

english: Excessive fertilizer pulls moisture away from plant roots, causing root burn and turning leaves yellow or brown. It is better to apply smaller, measured amounts so the plant can absorb the nutrients safely.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ baajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi amli. Eshãa shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Esa akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ bibioo nɔ, ni asusu he bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker when I plant maize on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: How does chemical weedicide know how to kill weeds without killing my food crops?
ga: Te tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ leɔ bɔ ni amɛgbeɔ jwɛi ni amɛyeee mi niyenii tsei lɛ awui amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Selective weedicides are designed to target specific types of plants, such as broad-leaved weeds, while leaving grass-type crops like maize unharmed. Non-selective weedicides kill all green plants and must be applied carefully away from your crops.
ga: Afee tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ahalaa lɛ koni akɛtutua tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ. yɛ be mli ni eshiɔ jwɛi tsei tamɔ ŋmãa ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efeee amɛ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaaa lɛ baagbe tsei eŋɔli fɛɛ. Ni esa akɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ, ni okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akabɔ he.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and dropping is a natural defense mechanism crops use to survive drought. By dropping leaves, the cassava plant reduces water loss and conserves energy in its underground roots until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Kɛ́ afo baai lɛ, ehaa nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi, ni amɛbuɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Why do certified seeds from the agriculture office yield better than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni Bureau of Agriculture lɛ eŋmɛ gbɛ lɛ woɔ yibii ni hi fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are bred in controlled settings for high yields, disease resistance, and uniform growth. Saved seeds lose these strong genetic traits over generations, resulting in smaller yields and uneven plant growth.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ anɔ yɛ he ko ni akudɔ koni amɛná yibii babaoo, helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe kɛ amɛdalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ fɔmɔ nii ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu daaa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: Flower drop occurs when cocoa trees face environmental stress, such as extreme heat, prolonged drought, or lack of soil nutrients. Providing shade and keeping the soil moist helps trees retain flowers and grow healthy pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji akɛ cacao tsei lɛ kɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kpe. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shade ni akɛhaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow even though I am giving them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmã tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is lacking key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or the roots are diseased and cannot absorb food properly. Water alone isn't enough if the soil lacks essential nutrients.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo hela emɔ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnyɛɛɛ amɛhe niyenii kpakpai. Nu pɛ faaa kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: If one of my cassava plants gets sick with spots on the leaves, can the sickness spread to the healthy plants next to it?
ga: Kɛji mi-cassava tsei lɛ eko hela mɔ lɛ ni ŋmeii yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ Hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Ani manyɛ maná mra?

english: Yes, plant diseases caused by fungi, bacteria, or viruses can easily spread through wind, rain splashes, shared farm tools, or insects moving from the sick plant to healthy ones.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahelai ni ŋmeii, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛbaa lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ. loo kooloi bibii ni fãa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Flower dropping often happens when the crop is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or attacks from tiny pests like thrips that damage the blossom stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo tutuamɔi ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips ni fiteɔ fɔfɔii ahe tsei lɛ adɛŋ.

english: How long do I need to wait after spraying chemical medicine on my crops before it is safe for my family to eat them?
ga: Beni mikɛ tsofai eshwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani amɛfee shweshweeshwe koni miweku lɛ aye?

english: Every crop chemical has a required waiting period, called the Pre-Harvest Interval, printed on the label. Eating the crop before this period ends can cause chemical poisoning because the medicine has not fully broken down yet.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei amli lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be ni akɛmɛɛɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ be ni akɛkpaa nii dani akpaa lɛ ni akala awo nɔ. Kɛ́ aye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani be nɛɛ ho lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ aba ejaakɛ tsofa lɛ efiteee kwraa lolo.

english: If I spray pesticide to kill bugs on my crop, can it cause any bad side effects to the growth of the plant itself?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ Ani ekɛ naagbai gbohii baaba tsei lɛ adalɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, if chemicals are mixed too strong or sprayed during the high heat of the day, they can scorch the leaves, slow down growth, or damage young shoots—a condition known as chemical burn.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ tsofai lɛ futu mli waa tsɔ loo ashwie nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli. Nakai tsofai lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã. ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa fioo loo efiteɔ ŋmeii bibii Enɛ ji shihilɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ tsofa ni shãa.

english: Does mixing more pesticide than the bottle recommends help my sick crops recover faster from pests?
ga: Ani tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ babaoo ni akɛfutuɔ fe bɔ ni awo he ŋaa yɛ tɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ oya kɛjɛ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ amli?

english: No, using too much chemical does not heal the plant faster. It can burn the plant leaves, waste your money, build chemical resistance in the pests, and leave dangerous poison levels in your harvested food.
ga: Dabi, tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ eyeee ebuaaa tso lɛ ni etsa oya. Ebaanyɛ eshã tsei ahe baai, efite shika, etswa tsofai ni teɔ shi ewoɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. ni eshiɔ tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ oshara yɛ niyenii ni okpa lɛ mli.

english: What happens to the medicine on my crop leaves if a heavy rain falls right after I finish spraying?
ga: Mɛni baaba tsofa ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa beni ashwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away the spray before the plant absorbs it or before it can kill the pests. You usually need a few rain-free hours after spraying for the chemical to work effectively.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ aŋɔ loo dani egbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ehe bahiaa ni okɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi atsu nii ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ tsofai lɛ ni okɛshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni tsofai lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plant leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense mechanism plants use to reduce water loss through their leaves when heat is intense. Providing shade trees helps young cocoa plants stay cool and retain moisture.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba nu ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa. Shade ni akɛhaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i mli ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Will putting too much fertilizer on my crop burn the plants instead of helping them grow?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baashã amɛ moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Yes, excess fertilizer increases salt levels in the soil, which pulls water away from the plant roots and causes leaf tips to turn brown and look burnt.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmei ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. ni baajie nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi amli ni eha baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni ashã.

english: Can planting pepper very close to my cassava crops cause any negative effects on how the cassava roots expand?
ga: Ani pepper ni aduɔ yɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aná cassava shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots compete for the same nutrients, space, and water in the soil, which can cause tubers like cassava to remain small and poorly developed.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛha niyenii, he ko kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni baanyɛ aha ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii afee bibii ni amɛdarako jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers talk about 'Season 1' and 'Season 2' when advising us on planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ tsĩɔ ‘Season 1’ kɛ ‘Season 2’ tã kɛ́ amɛkɛ wɔ miisusu dumɔwui ahe lɛ?

english: Most regions in Ghana experience two distinct rainfall cycles each year: the major rainy season (Season 1) and the minor rainy season (Season 2). Matching your planting schedule to these specific seasons ensures your crops receive the right amount of water at crucial growth stages.
ga: Ghana kpokpai babaoo naa nugbɔshiimɔi srɔtoi enyɔ daa afi: nugbɔshiimɔ be klɛŋklɛŋ (Be 1) kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji enyɔ (Be 2). Kɛ́ okɛ odumɔ be lɛ to be pɔtɛɛ nɛɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aná nu ni sa yɛ amɛdalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli.

english: How do I know the best time of the year to start planting rice on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: The best planting time depends on whether you rely on natural rains or an irrigation scheme. Generally, planting rice at the start of Season 1 (the main rainy season) ensures seeds get maximum soil moisture for strong early growth.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ damɔ kɛji akɛ okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ mra yɛ be 1 (nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ) mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo koni amɛdara mra jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow slower during the second rainy season compared to the first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa fioo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: The second rainy season is usually shorter and brings lighter, less consistent rains. Lower soil moisture and cooler or cloudier weather mean crops take longer to mature than in the main season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ feɔ kuku, ni nugbɔshiimɔ ni baa shi lɛ faaa kwraa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi kɛ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ loo atatu yɔɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ fe be titri lɛ mli.

english: Is it better to apply water from above using sprinklers or flood my rice field directly?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ baashwie nu nɔ kɛjɛ ŋwɛi loo akɛ nu ashwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Overhead watering works well for young seedlings or dryland rice varieties, but shallow flooding is best for lowland rice because standing water prevents weeds from growing and keeps root temperatures stable.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ yiteŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa tsei bibii loo ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ. Shi nu afua lɛ hi fe fɛɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmãa. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli hulutsoo be fɛɛ be.

english: Why is the irrigation water supply for my farm often low during certain parts of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa yɛ afi lɛ fãi komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Water supply drops during dry periods or outside the peak rainy months because river levels fall and local water schemes must ration supply so that every farm gets a basic amount.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ baa shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ asɛɛ. yɛ nu lɛ mli ni baa shi lɛ hewɔ Ni esa akɛ maŋ lɛ mli nu he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ aha nu koni ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ aná shishijee shika.

english: Why does my soil dry out so fast even after I apply water from above?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ nu shwie nɔ kɛjɛ ŋwɛi po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Strong sunshine and high heat quickly evaporate water resting on top of the soil. Adding plant waste or compost to your soil helps it hold onto moisture much longer.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni afolɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does my rice crop require so much more water compared to my corn or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ he hiaa nu babaoo fe mi ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally adapted to flooded river valleys. They rely on heavy moisture to absorb nutrients efficiently from the soil and to suppress competing weeds.
ga: Omɔ tsei tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛyaa faa jɔɔi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo nɔ koni amɛjie niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni amɛtsi jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ anaa.

english: What happens to my rice if the water supply drops before the plants are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji nu lɛ ba shi dani tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If water runs low while rice grains are forming, the plants become stressed, resulting in lightweight, empty grain heads and a poor overall harvest.
ga: Kɛji nu lɛ hoɔ fioo yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ miifee lɛ Tso lɛ baaná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ waaa. dumɔwui ayitso ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni kpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ ehiii kwraa.

english: How can I tell when my rice field is ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ eshɛ ni abaakpa?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when the main leaves start drying out, field water levels drop, and about 80 percent of the grain heads turn a bright golden yellow.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai titrii lɛ bɔi gbimɔ. Nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ ba shi. ni dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ aaafee oha mlijaa 80 feɔ shika tsuru ni mli tse.

english: Why should I follow an agricultural officer's planting calendar instead of just planting whenever rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni anyiɛ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ adumɔ kalanda lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu kɛkɛ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Planting calendars are based on long-term weather patterns. Following them helps you avoid sudden dry spells midway through crop growth, keeping your farm investment safe.
ga: Kalandai ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ damɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yaa nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ anɔ. Enɛɛmɛi asɛɛnyiɛmɔ baaye abua bo ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni baa trukaa yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida lɛ he. Ha oŋmɔ mli shika ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ afee shweshweeshwe

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow even though I applied fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ewo mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean heavy rains washed the nutrients deep into the soil beyond the roots' reach, or the soil has too much water logging, which suffocates the roots and stops them from feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛye nii.

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves when water is scarce to protect itself and save moisture for the tubers underground. It is not dying and will grow new leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baabu ehe ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ato kɛha ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ bɛ. Egbooo ni ebaaná baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden poles to climb, while cassava grows straight without support?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei baakwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ ni yelikɛbuamɔ ko bɛ he lɛ?

english: Yam vines are soft climbing plants that need stakes to lift their leaves up to catch sunlight for underground tuber growth, whereas cassava has a thick, woody stem that supports its own leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni shwereɔ ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmei yɛ tso ni mli tse ni tamɔ tso ni fiɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ebaai lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Why does plantain produce huge bunches down near the stream but give small yields on my hillside plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ faai ahe shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ gɔŋ lɛ shikpɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and require constant soil moisture and thick leaf mold found near water streams, while hillside soil loses water quickly and leaves the plant thirsty.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be, ni baa ŋmei ko ni mli edɔ yɛ ni anaa yɛ nu faai ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔji anɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya, ni ehaa kumai yeɔ tsei.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster in my field right after I clear them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Clearing the top surface exposes buried weed seeds to direct sunlight and air, triggering them to sprout quickly unless the soil is covered with mulch or planted immediately.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, jwɛi dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Ja atswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo adu amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are crops on my newly cleared forest farm growing differently than what older farmers told me to expect?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mi koo mli ŋmɔ hee ni ajie lɛ mli lɛ miida yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe bɔ ni okwaafoi ni edara lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ makpa gbɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing forest trees changes how sunlight and rain hit the soil, which can alter soil fertility and moisture faster than traditional wisdom accounts for.
ga: Tsei ni afoɔ yɛ koo mli lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsake shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ oya fe bɔ ni nilee ni afɔɔ namɔ susuɔ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when daytime heat becomes too intense or when the plant experiences extreme dry spells, preventing the flowers from setting fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ naa hɔmɔ ni naa wa. Enɛ ɔ haa nɛ fɔfɔi ɔmɛ nyɛ we nɛ a wo yiblii.

english: Why are worms attacking my young maize plants so early this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miitutua mi-baby corn tsei lɛ yɛ be nɛɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Pests like fall armyworms lay eggs rapidly when early rains are irregular and temperatures are warm, allowing young worms to feed on soft new shoots right after germination.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ woɔ amɛwui oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛɔ mra ni hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ shiŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii heei beni amɛje kpo amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees yield smaller pods when I plant them close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii beni mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting cocoa too close forces the trees to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leaving less energy for individual trees to build big pods.
ga: Kɛ́ adu kookoo yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's harvested maize produce smaller cobs when I replant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibii kɛji midu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Many commercial seeds are hybrid varieties designed for a strong single harvest; saving and planting their seeds causes the crop to lose its original vigor, resulting in uneven growth and smaller cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni akɛkpaa nii shikome ni mli wa. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ ahewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ tsutsu lɛ afite. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why should I cover my seed nursery bed with grass or cloth after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo mama aha mi dumɔwui ashishi lɛ nɔ beni midu lɛ?

english: Covering your nursery bed keeps the soil moist by protecting it from direct sun and prevents heavy rain from washing away tiny seeds before they sprout.
ga: Nibii ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni baa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni ebuɔ he lɛ nɔ. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ. dani ekwɛ̃

english: If I cannot afford plastic sheets to cover my seedbed, what local materials can I use instead?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ minyɛɛɛ mahe plastic ni mikɛha gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe lɛ hu? Mɛɛ maŋ lɛ mli nibii manyɛ mikɛtsu nii moŋ?

english: You can use old jute sacks, palm fronds, banana leaves, or light cloth to shade and cover your seedbed, as long as they block harsh sun while letting air flow.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jute kotokui, ŋmei baai, banana baai loo mama bibioo ko afee hulutsoo ni okɛha dumɔwui lɛ ashishi. Shii abɔ ni etsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: How can I protect my tender seedlings from being broken by heavy rainfall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu dumɔwui bibii ahe koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafite amɛ?

english: You can build a simple low shelter over the nursery bed using wooden sticks covered with cloth or palm leaves to break the force of heavy falling raindrops.
ga: Obaanyɛ oma shĩa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ tso ni akɛ mama loo ŋmei tsei ehà nɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛfo nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa lɛ ahewalɛ lɛ nɔ oya ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Is it better to water my young crops using a hose or a watering can?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikɛ hose loo nu ni akɛwoɔ midumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: A watering can or fine spray hose is better for young crops because strong water pressure from a regular hose can wash away soil around delicate roots and break soft stems.
ga: Nu tsɛnsi loo hose kpakpa hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni naa wa ni jɛɔ hose ni yɔɔ daa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afɔ sũ ni bɔle shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe lɛ, ni eha tsei bibii lɛ akumɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crops need water without using any expensive tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu he miihia miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛ nibii ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: Push your finger two inches into the soil near the plant; if it feels dry and dusty at your fingertip, your crops need water, but if soil sticks to your finger, it has enough moisture.
ga: Tsɔ oniji enyɔ awo shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ he lɛ mli. Kɛji oniji ahe nuɔ he akɛ egbi ni eyɛ sũ Etsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia onibii. Shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ kpɛtɛ onine he lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my crops on the farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo miŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nu?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is best because the sun is cooler, allowing the roots to absorb the water before the hot sun evaporates it.
ga: Leebi loo shwane mli ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ hulu lɛ mli jɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ.

english: How does spreading dry leaves around the base of my plants help them stay healthy?
ga: Baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ Te mi tso lɛ shishi yeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Dry leaves act like a blanket over the soil, holding in water so the soil stays moist longer and preventing weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Baai ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛhiɛɔ nu mli bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Seeds usually delay sprouting if the topsoil has dried out and hardened into a crust, or if the seeds were planted too deep for the shoot to push through.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui haaa amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ gĩ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop in the afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Plants lose water faster through their leaves than their roots can drink during peak heat, so leaves temporarily droop to protect themselves from drying out.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Can giving my crops too much water actually cause them to turn yellow and die?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, overwatering drowns the roots by filling all the air spaces in the soil, which causes the roots to rot and turns the leaves yellow.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ewoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees burning and turning brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct sunshine and heat. Without shade trees like plantains or Gliricidia to protect them, the intense heat burns their leaves and dries out the soil moisture they need to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo loo gliricidia ni buɔ amɛhe lɛ bɛ mli Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ shãa amɛbaai lɛ ni ehaa sũ mli nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my plantain bunches stay very small even when the mother tree looks tall and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ekɛlɛ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: If a plantain stem has too many suckers growing around its base, those young shoots steal water and plant food from the main trunk. Removing extra suckers directs all the plant's energy into growing a bigger, heavier fruit bunch.
ga: Kɛji akɛ plantain tso lɛ shishifãi babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, nakai tsei lɛ baaju nu ni amɛdu niyenii kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ daa ni etsɔɔ aduawai akui wuji ni tsii.

english: When weather gets extremely hot or when watering is irregular, tomato plants experience heat stress and drop their blossoms to preserve water and energy rather than setting fruit.
ga: Be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa loo be mli ni nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Tomato tsei lɛ naa dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling up into tight little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi chili tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves. As they suck the plant's juices, they transmit viruses that cause the leaves to wrinkle and distort.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. be mli ni amɛmuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei amli lɛ Amɛhaa helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ lɛ yaa.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay soft and loose instead of forming hard, tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lolo ni eyɛ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ko ni wa ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads remain loose if they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer late in their growth cycle or if they do not get steady water, which causes the leaves to grow too quickly instead of packing tightly.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ baakã he ahi shi mlɛo kɛji akɛ amɛná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. aloo kɛji onine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa Enɛ haa baai lɛ daa oya tsɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground if I leave them in the soil after heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil. Excess water sitting around the tubers starves them of oxygen, creating ideal conditions for soil fungi to attack and rot the roots before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle Yitso lɛ he lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ faaa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atutua ni amɛfite shishifãi lɛ dani akpa.

english: Why do I need to spend time guiding my yam vines up tall wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe bahia ni maŋɔ be kɛkudɔ sweet potato wain tso ko kɛya tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha efo kɛho shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tuber growing beneath the soil. Staking keeps the leaves high in the sun and off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases caused by wet leaves.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni ejɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Koni akɛtsi fungal helai ni baai ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Why are my maize plants producing small cob ears with many missing grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ toi bibii kɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni elaaje lɛ?

english: Missing grains mean the flowers on the corn silk were not properly pollinated. This happens when dry winds dry out the silk or when maize plants are planted too far apart for pollen to drift from plant to plant.
ga: Dumɔwui ni bɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmãa siliki lɛ nɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ ha siliki lɛ mli egbi. Aloo kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmãa lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ tso kome nɔ kɛya tso kroko nɔ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same plot where I just harvested my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmãa amrɔ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nitrogen out of the soil to grow. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth, naturally refreshing the soil for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi kɛ nitrogen babaoo ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛkwɛ̃. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha odumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my corn stalks growing very tall and thin with pale yellow leaves even after applying fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛ amɛ wo mli po lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves often mean the plant cannot absorb nitrogen properly, usually because the fertilizer was washed away by heavy rain or applied when the soil was too dry for roots to take it up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nitrogen lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo akɛwoɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni shishifãi nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to survive because direct hot sunlight burns their fragile leaves and dries out the soil. Keeping shade trees or planting temporary crops like plantains alongside them protects the young cocoa until it develops a full leaf canopy.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni waaa lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo be kukuoo mli tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ eyi.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants curling up tightly during the hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl inward during hot periods as a natural defense to reduce surface area exposed to the sun, which slows down water loss. While it helps the plant survive brief dry spells, prolonged leaf rolling indicates severe water stress that can reduce cob size.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaha nu ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Eyɛ mli akɛ eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli moŋ. Shi baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ nu he haomɔ ni naa wa, ni baanyɛ aha cob lɛ dalɛ aba shi.

english: Does it matter which direction I point a cassava stem cutting when I plant it in the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ ofo ŋmei niji lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the buds or eye nodes pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the new shoots to curve back up toward light, which wastes the plant's stored energy and results in weak growth and smaller roots.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii loo nodes lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛi ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei abɔle amɛhe kɛba la lɛ he. Enɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni tso lɛ eto lɛ. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ shishifãi bibii.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop without setting fruit due to heat stress, extreme drying of the soil, or lack of pollination. When temperatures get too high or soil moisture changes drastically, the plant sheds blossoms to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why does my land produce better maize crops after I have grown groundnuts or cowpeas on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ beni midu ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ?
