english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful bacteria in the soil to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on this natural nitrogen booster to grow taller leaves and larger cobs.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Eyeɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli nɛɛ koni ekwɛ baai ni kɛlɛ kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam vines need tall stakes to spread their leaves high off the ground where they can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlit leaves produce food for the plant, which is then transported down into the soil to build large, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni amɛkɛbaagbɛ amɛbaa lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ lɛ. Baai ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, akɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni efee sweet potato ŋmeii agboi ni tsii.

english: Why should I remove the extra small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, compete directly with the main plantain stem for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Pruning away weaker suckers allows the parent plant to concentrate all its energy into growing a thick stem and producing large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ plantain tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ afo tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa tso nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛwo tsei ni mli tse ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii baa.

english: Why are white, dry patches appearing on the sunny side of my pepper fruits while they are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbi be mli ni amɛdaraa lolo lɛ?

english: This damage is known as sunscald, which happens when intense, direct sunlight bakes and kills the outer skin tissues of exposed peppers. Maintaining healthy leaf growth helps provide natural shade that protects ripening peppers from sun damage.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɔ ni efite nɛɛ akɛ shãa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shã ni efite ŋmeii ni hulu lɛ eshɛ amɛnɔ lɛ ahewolo nɔ fãji lɛ. Baai lɛ adalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cabbage seedlings collapse and rot right at the soil level in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage dumɔwui bibii lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This condition, known as damping-off, is caused by soil fungi that thrive when nursery beds are overwatered or planted too closely together. Excess moisture softens the delicate seedling stems near the damp soil, allowing fungal disease to destroy them.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ damping off lɛ, jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ awo ŋmeii akwɛmɔhei lɛ amli nu fe nine loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ akpata amɛhiɛ.

english: Why should I wait until a few weeks after my crops sprout before applying fertilizer instead of putting it all in the ground at planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ koni mawo ŋmɔshi nii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ baawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Sprouting seeds rely on stored energy within the seed to shoot up and do not have developed root systems right away. Applying strong fertilizer too early can burn the delicate new roots, whereas waiting allows established roots to absorb and use the nutrients efficiently.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ damɔɔ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛnáaa shishifãi amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni mɛɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi ni wa lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops bend over and snap at the stem when heavy winds blow through the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa kɛfo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is known as lodging. It happens when stalks are too weak or roots are shallow, often caused by planting seeds too close together, lack of potassium in the soil, or damage from pests like stem borers.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ wɔɔhe. Ebaa kɛji tso lɛ shishifã lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ loo shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Bei pii lɛ nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ stem borers lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my plants grow tall and thin and then collapse on top of each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa akɛ amɛgbeeɔ amɛhe nɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, crops compete for sunlight and stretch upward quickly. This makes their stems thin and weak, causing them to fall over against each other when they get heavy.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya. Ehaa tsitsi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ ni ehaa amɛgbeeɔ amɛhe nɔ kɛji amɛhe wa.

english: How can I support my crops so they do not fall over when they start producing heavy fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ koni amɛkagbee shi beni amɛbɔi yibii ni tsii womɔ lɛ?

english: Piling up extra soil around the base of the stem (called earthing up or ridging) gives roots stronger anchor support. For taller crops, tying them to strong wooden stakes keeps them upright.
ga: Shikpɔŋ krokomɛi ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ grounding loo demolition) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. Kɛha tsei ni kɛlɛ Kɛ́ akɛfi tso ni wa he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my plant is falling over because it is ripe or because it is diseased?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ miigbee shi ejaakɛ ekwɛ̃ loo hela emɔ lɛ?

english: When crops mature naturally, the whole plant slowly dries out uniformly across the field. If a plant tilts or collapses while its leaves are still green or rotting at the base, it is usually damaged by disease or pests.
ga: Kɛ tsei dara yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ Tso muu lɛ fɛɛ baagbi fiofio yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ shwie shi loo egbee shi be mli ni baai lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo loo kɛji eegbo yɛ shishigbɛ Bei pii lɛ helai loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops wither and die near the water channel on the side of my field after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ faa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ masɛi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess standing water near trenches or low spots chokes the plant roots by cutting off air. Without oxygen, roots rot and cannot send nutrients to the rest of the plant, causing it to wither.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi fe nine ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmeii loo hei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli, ni no haa amɛgboiɔ.

english: How does rainwater washing through my farm cause my plants to lean and break?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛtsɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ?

english: Fast-moving rainwater washes away the topsoil that holds the crop roots firm. As soil erodes around the base, the plants lose support and tilt over.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ oya lɛ hoɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni ŋmɛɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwie shi yɛ shishitoo lɛ he lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni sɛɛ efooo ni ebaatsi ehe kɛjɛ he.

english: How do I protect my crops from water damage if my farm sits next to a ditch?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni nu akafite amɛ? Kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ bɛŋkɛ nubu ko

english: You can dig small drainage channels to redirect heavy rainwater away from root zones and plant grass along ditch edges to stop water from washing away soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu gbɛ bibioo ko. Koni ajie nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ kɛjɛ shishifã lɛ he. Ni odu jwɛi yɛ nubu lɛ naa koni nu akashwie sũ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crop is getting sick before it actually falls over or dies?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela mɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani egbo loo egbo diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Look out for early warning signs like leaf discoloration, dark spots on the stem, unusual wilting during cooler parts of the day, or soft spots near the base of the plant.
ga: Taomɔ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii mra, tamɔ baai ni etsake su kɛ hei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Wilting ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ be mli. loo hei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ

english: Why do some of my plants stay bright green while neighboring plants turn weak and fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ekomɛi yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Differences in green color often point to nutrient gaps like nitrogen, or localized root damage from soil pests that prevent specific plants from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ tsɔɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni miitsi tsei komɛi anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: What causes a green and healthy-looking plant stem to suddenly break inside?
ga: Mɛni haa tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fãa trukaa kɛyaa mli?

english: Insects like stem borers burrow inside crop stalks, eating them from the inside out while leaving the outside looking green until the weak stem suddenly snaps.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ stem borers lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli. Ye amɛ kɛjɛ mli kɛya kponɔgbɛ, ni oha kponɔgbɛ lɛ afee eŋɔli kɛyashi ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ baafo trukaa.

english: Why are my crops giving me small harvests even though I plant them at the right time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ midu yɛ be ni sa mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops need continuous nutrients to produce big harvests. If the soil lacks organic nutrients, plants remain weak and yield poorly until you enrich the land with compost or manure.
ga: Niyenii he miihia tsei be fɛɛ be koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ baakã he agbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii baawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my land produce less harvest every new farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ okwaayeli be hee fɛɛ be hee mli lɛ?

english: Every time crops grow, they pull nutrients out of the soil. Without putting rich organic matter like compost back into the ground, the soil becomes tired, causing your yields to drop.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni tso ko baakwɛ̃ Ebaajie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my crops are actually flourishing and getting enough food from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ ni minine shɛɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Flourishing crops have strong stems, rich green leaves, and grow rapidly, whereas nutrient-poor crops look stunted, thin, and yield very little fruit.
ga: Tsei ni shwereɔ lɛ yɛ tsei ni wa. baai lɛ eŋɔli kwraa ni amɛdaraa oya Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ amɛmli lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛhe baajɔ ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why are my neighbor's crops green and flourishing while mine on the same soil look weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo tso lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni eshwereɔ yɛ be mli ni mitso ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Crops flourish when the soil is properly enriched with organic matter. Your neighbor is likely adding compost into their soil to feed the crops effectively.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli eyi mli obɔ bɔ ni sa. Ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii miifata shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: What can I do with the dry leaves and crop waste left on my farm after harvest?
ga: Mɛni mifeɔ kɛ baai ni egboi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: You can gather farm waste into a pile in one spot and leave it to decompose naturally into compost, which becomes rich food for your crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ obua ŋmɔ mli jwɛi anaa yɛ ŋtayaa mli yɛ he kome ni oha egbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni etsɔ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi. Enɛ baafee niyenii babaoo kɛha onibii.

english: Why can't I just put fresh farm waste directly around my young crops right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi heei shwieee shi kɛkɛ? Mi tsei bibii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Fresh waste needs to sit somewhere and decompose into compost first. Fresh plant waste can generate heat and pull away nutrients as it breaks down, which can harm crop roots.
ga: Esa akɛ jwɛi heei lɛ ata he ko ni egbo ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii klɛŋklɛŋ. Tsei amli jwɛi heei baanyɛ afee dɔlɛ ni ejie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛ mli beni efiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aye tsei shishifãi awui.

english: Can rotting waste materials really make my crop yield bigger?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, when plant materials fully compost, they turn into nutrient-dense fertilizer. Adding this to poor soil turns weak plants into a flourishing, high-yielding crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni tso lɛ mli nibii lɛ efite kwraa lɛ. Atsakeɔ nakai nibii lɛ afeeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ enɛ fata shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha tso ni bɛ hewalɛ afee tso ni shwereɔ ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Should I just drop my compost on top of the farm land or do I need to dig it in?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ loo esa akɛ mafo mli?

english: Compost works best when you mix it directly into the soil. If left on the surface, sun and rain can wash away nutrients before the plant roots can reach them.
ga: Kompost tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ okɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Hulu la kɛ nugbɔ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why is my harvest still small even after I scattered manure on top of my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Scattering manure on top of the ground is not enough because roots feed beneath the surface. You must mix the compost into the soil so the roots can absorb the food and flourish.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ faaa ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Is it better to mix compost into the soil before planting or after the crops start growing?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani adu loo yɛ no sɛɛ?

english: Mixing compost into the soil before or during planting ensures that young crop roots find nutrients immediately, helping them grow strong and flourish right from the beginning.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani adu loo yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ náa niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛshwereɔ kɛjɛɔ shishijee.

english: How does the shape and appearance of my harvested vegetables affect the price buyers will pay for them?
ga: Te bɔ ni mikpamɔ lɛ yɔɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ saa jara ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baawo lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Buyers and market women prefer uniform, well-shaped produce because consumers buy with their eyes and oddly shaped crops are harder to pack and transport. Damaged or deformed crops are usually sold at a discount or rejected entirely.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii kɛ jarayeli yei sumɔɔ nibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛo. Ejaakɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ amɛhiŋmɛii pɛ heɔ nii. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ wa akɛ abaawo tsɔne mli ni akɛya. Bei pii lɛ, ahɔ̃ɔ tsei ni efite loo efite lɛ yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ loo akpooɔ amɛ kwraa.

english: Why do my garden eggs turn soft and bad very quickly after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛfiteɔ oya beni mikpa amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Garden eggs spoil fast if harvested when overripe or stored in hot, unventilated spaces. Harvesting them while they are still firm and keeping them in a cool, shaded area prolongs their freshness and market shelf life.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ be mli ni amɛshwere tsɔ loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akpa nikpamɔ be mli ni eyɛ hewalɛ lolo ni akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed away the nutrients. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-decomposed manure helps the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are my tomato fruits splitting open on the vine before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ dani ekwɛ̃ po lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when heavy watering or a sudden rain follows a long dry period. The plant takes up too much water quickly, causing the inside of the fruit to expand faster than the outer skin can stretch.
ga: Tomato baatswa yɛ nu ni mli wa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Tsei shwieɔ nu babaoo oya. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, poor soil nutrients, or uneven watering. Giving the soil sufficient water and shade during peak sun helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be Nu ni fa kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet and dark conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let sunlight and air circulate through the farm reduces humidity and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ duŋ mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are tiny worms eating big holes in my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii Koni amɛye bu agbo ko yɛ mi kaabeji baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid on the leaves by moths. Checking under the leaves regularly and spraying recommended biopesticides like neem oil extract keeps them from destroying the leaves.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii kɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli. Akwɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi daa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi tamɔ neem fɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ afɔ nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ akafite.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long in heavy, clay soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots can breathe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. Etsɛ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ sũ mli ni etsii. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce lots of leaves but very few peanuts underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants need loose, soft soil so the flowering stems can easily push down into the earth to form nuts. Hard or compacted soil prevents the pegs from entering the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia ŋmei tsei lɛ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya koni amɛfee ŋmei. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baatsi pin lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ tsɔne mli kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and snap easily during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛkuɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry harmattan weather, plantains lose water rapidly through their large leaves. Mulching the base of the tree with dry grass keeps the soil moist and cools the root system.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, harmattan Plantains lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai wuji lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ.

english: Why should I buy new improved seeds every season instead of just planting the seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ daa be lɛ? Mohu ɔ, du wuhi nɛ a he yi kɛ je ngmɔ kpami nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ pɛ.

english: Improved seeds, like hybrid varieties, are specially bred to give high yields and fight off diseases in their first generation. When you save and replant those seeds, they lose these strong traits, resulting in weaker plants, uneven growth, and lower harvest.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ, yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛkɛ helai awuu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛto ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ Nakai dumɔwui lɛ baafite sui ni mli wa nɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni egbɔjɔ. shweremɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni ŋmaa lɛ ba shi

english: Why do some maize varieties stay green during a dry spell while my local variety wilts and dies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi hiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ? Beni mimaŋ ŋmãa henɔ lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Some seeds are bred specifically to be drought-resilient. They develop deeper root systems to reach deep underground moisture and have leaf features that prevent water loss during hot dry spells.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui komɛi pɔtɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi anaa. Amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ, ni amɛyɛ baai ni tsiɔ nu ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why do some new crop varieties produce cobs much faster than the traditional seeds my parents used?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei No hewɔ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi komɛi woɔ cob oya kwraa fe dumɔwui ni mifɔlɔi kɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ.

english: Crop breeders create early-maturing seed varieties that complete their growth cycle in a shorter time. This helps farmers get a successful harvest even when the rainy season is short or unpredictable.
ga: Mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra ni gbeɔ dalɛ be lɛ naa yɛ be kukuoo mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛkpaa ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ faaa loo anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ po.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing in cassava is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stems prevents this virus from damaging your crop.
ga: Kasava lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela kɛbaa. ni ji kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ ni hiɛɔ Cassava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What causes tiny worms to eat holes in the centers of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ni oooye bu ni yɔɔ mi-babi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Those worms are Fall Armyworms, pests that attack the growing center of maize plants. Inspecting fields early, planting with the first rains, and applying recommended controls early helps protect your maize.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni tutuaa ŋmãa tsei ni daraa lɛ ateŋ. He lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli kɛ mra be mli nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu o-corn lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn brown and drop off when there are no large shade trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo be bɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally thrive in partial shade and humid air. Without shade trees or temporary nurse crops like plantains, direct sunlight scorches the cocoa leaves and dries out the soil moisture they need to survive.
ga: Cocoa tsei daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ. Kɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ plantains bɛ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã kookoo baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni he hiaa koni amɛhi shi lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my crops look weak and yellowish even when it rains regularly on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowish leaves often mean the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen. Continuous farming on the same plot without adding compost, manure, or fertilizer drains the soil's natural food supply.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Will planting my maize seeds very close together give me a bigger harvest from my small farm?
ga: Kɛ́ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli. mi nɔ loo daabi

english: Planting seeds too close together makes the plants compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. This produces tall, thin plants with tiny cobs, leading to a smaller overall harvest than properly spaced crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ nɛɛ haa tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baafee bibioo fe be mli ni akɛ tsei lɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my field before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil with nutrients that the maize crop can use in the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwereɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ niyenii ni ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ ekɛtsu nii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do many of the seeds I stored in my room fail to sprout when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui babaoo ni mikɛtoɔ mitsu lɛ mli lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji adu lɛ?

english: Seeds are living things that spoil if exposed to heat, air, or moisture during storage. Keeping dried seeds in clean, airtight containers in a cool place preserves their energy so they germinate well when planted.
ga: Dumɔwui ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni fiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛ wo dɔlɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ, loo fɛ̃i be mli ni akɛtoɔ. Dumɔwui ni egbi ni akɛtoɔ tsinsii ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ lɛ baaye abua ni amɛhewalɛ akafite. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from taller trees or plantains because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil before their roots are strong enough to absorb enough water.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji loo plantains amli ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to spread their leaves toward the sunlight, which allows the plant to produce enough food to grow big, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei kakadaji anɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient the crop needs to build strong, green, food-producing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛfee baai ni wa, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji, ni eji niyenii jɛɛhe.

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally add nitrogen back into the soil, helping to restore the nutrients that the previous maize crop took away.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni ŋmãa jieɔ tsutsu lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, which results in weak plants and a smaller overall harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli, ni no haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi.

english: The first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell, which can dry out the topsoil and kill young germinating seeds before the steady rains truly start.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ aya nɔ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the dirt before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ nɔ ni mikpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when planted in soil that traps too much water, suffocating the roots and creating a wet environment where rot diseases spread quickly.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu babaoo hiɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ewo fɔ baa ni ŋmeii baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant without forming any actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering, as the plant sacrifices its flowers to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo la ni mli edɔ waa mli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei ashã fɔfɔi koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster and stronger on my field than the crop seeds I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to thrive in harsh conditions, allowing them to suck up soil moisture and fertilizer much faster than domestic crop plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛshwere yɛ shihilɛi ni ehiii amli. Enɛ haa amɛheɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe shia ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding inside the center leaf fold of my corn plants and eating holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ bu yɛ amɛmli lɛ?

english: These pests are Fall Armyworms, which crawl into the tender, growing middle part of the corn plant where they can safely feed while hidden from sunlight and predators.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli. he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye nii yɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ be mli ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Is it okay if I uproot a young crop that didn't grow well and replace it with another seedling from my farm?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba mli kɛji mijie tso bibioo ko ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛ tso kroko ni jɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo najiaŋ?

english: Replacing dead or weak plants in your field is good practice, but simply uprooting a healthy growing crop causes root shock that can stunt its growth. It is better to use nursery seedlings or fresh seeds specifically raised for replacing missing spots.
ga: Tsei ni egboi loo ni egbɔjɔ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni oootsake lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Shi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni no baanyɛ aha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli loo dumɔwui heei ni akwɛɔ amɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ lɛ ato hei ni elaaje lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do some of my young crops die immediately after I dig them up and move them to a new spot on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ ekomɛi gboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mifo amɛ ni mikɛ amɛ tee he hee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When you dig up a growing plant, its tiny root hairs break and can no longer absorb water, causing 'transplant shock.' To help them survive, move them with the soil around their roots, plant them late in the afternoon, and water them immediately.
ga: Kɛ́ otsa tsei ni miida lɛ, amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ fãa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ nu dɔŋŋ, ni no haa ‘graft shock’ baa koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi. Okɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ atsu nii ni okɛdu amɛ, ni odu amɛ yɛ shwane mli. ni awo mli nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ

english: Can I just save part of the maize I harvested for food and plant it as seed for the next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ eko ato kɛha niyenii ni madu akɛ dumɔwui kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Grain meant for eating may not grow well or yield much as seed because it hasn't been selected or treated for planting. Certified seed is specially bred, inspected, and treated to ensure high germination rates, disease resistance, and strong harvests.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui ni ayeɔ lɛ edaŋ jogbaŋŋ loo amɛwooo yibii babaoo tamɔ dumɔwui lɛ ejaakɛ ahalaaa amɛ loo atsuuu he nii koni akɛdu. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ, akwɛɔ mli ni atsuɔ he nii koni amɛkwɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ babaoo, helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛhe ni amɛkpa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I inspect my saved seeds before planting to know if they will actually grow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ mli dani madu koni male kɛji amɛbaakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Good planting seeds should be firm, clean, dry, and free of insect holes or mold. You can test them by placing a few in a bowl of water; healthy seeds sink to the bottom, while weak or damaged seeds float.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni wa, ehe atse, egbi, ni bu loo ŋmeii ni jɛɔ kooloi amli lɛ akafee nɔ ko. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni okɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui kpakpai baagbee shi kɛya shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ loo efite lɛ baaho.

english: Why do certified seeds from the agricultural store give a better harvest than the ones I collect from my own field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni jɛ okwaayeli shwapoi amli lɛ haa ŋmaa kpakpa fe nɔ ni mibua naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds go through strict field checks and lab tests by agricultural officers to ensure purity and strength, whereas seeds saved from your farm lose their vitality over generations and carry diseases from previous crops.
ga: Esa akɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ aka dumɔwui ni awo amɛ hegbɛ lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔ mli kaa ni mli wa kɛ laboratori mli kaa mli koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛhe tse ni amɛhe wa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli ni amɛhiɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How do I know if there is enough time left in the season to plant my maize crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miyɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be lɛ mli ni mikɛbaadu ŋmãa?

english: Every crop needs a specific number of weeks with reliable rainfall to grow and mature. If you plant too late in the rainy season, the rain may stop before the crops finish developing seeds, leaving you with small kernels or total crop failure.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ otsii babaoo ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛshwere. Kɛji odu nii sɛɛ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ Nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adumɔwui lɛ aba shi kwraa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ kwraa.

english: What happens if I plant my crops too early before the rainy season fully starts?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu mitsei lɛ mra tsɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi?

english: Planting too early during unpredictable rains can cause seeds to dry up and rot in the hot soil before they sprout, forcing you to spend extra money buying seeds to replant the entire field.
ga: Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Enɛ haa ehe bahiaa ni ofite shika babaoo kɛhe dumɔwui ni okɛdu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How long does a crop meant for seed production need to stay in the field compared to regular food crops?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛduɔ dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛ akɛto niyenii ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ he?

english: Crops grown for seed usually need extra time in the field to reach full physiological maturity, allowing the seeds to dry naturally on the plant so they store enough energy to sprout vigorously next season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ kɛhaa dumɔwui lɛ biɔ be kroko yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani amɛshɛ shweremɔ he. Kɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni oooha amɛgbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Koni akɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ato kɛha kwɛ̃mɔ ni mli wa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do government officers from the Plant Protection and Regulatory Services (PPRS) come to inspect farm crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli mli onukpai ni jɛ Nitsumɔhe ni Kwɛɔ Tsei Anɔ lɛ baa koni amɛbakwɛ okwaayeli mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: PPRS officers visit fields to monitor for dangerous pests, crop diseases, and invasive weeds. Their job is to help catch outbreaks early so diseases do not spread to neighboring farms and ruin the community's harvest.
ga: PPRS nitsulɔi lɛ yaa jɛmɛ koni amɛkwɛ kɛji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ oshara, ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai kɛ jwɛi ni baa jɛmɛ lɛ yɛ. Amɛnitsumɔ ji ni amɛye amɛbua ni amɔmɔ helai ni baa lɛ mra. Enɛ ji koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli ni efite akutso lɛ mli nibii ni amɛduɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it important for an agricultural officer to inspect my field while my crops are still growing instead of waiting until harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ akwɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida lolo lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaamɛ kɛyashi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbe naa lɛ?

english: Inspecting growing crops helps spot early signs of nutrient hunger, pest attacks, or poor root growth while there is still time to fix them; waiting until harvest is too late to save damaged crops.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni akwɛɛɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni anaa okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye niyenii mli hewalɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo shishifãi ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ mra. Be mli ni be yɛ lolo ni akɛsaa lɛ. Mɛɛ ni kpamɔ lɛ aba sɛɛ tsɔ koni onyɛ ohere ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite lɛ ayiwala.

english: Why do extension officers always advise me to spray my crops early in the morning instead of during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ leebi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshwie nɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: In the cool early morning, plant leaves open their small pores to breathe, allowing liquid treatments and nutrients to be absorbed effectively before the intense sun can evaporate them.
ga: Yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, Baai lɛ gbeleɔ ŋmeii bibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛmu, ni no haa nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ dani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up into tight tubes during the middle of the day, but open back up by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ gbi lɛ mli shi amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe leebi lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl during high afternoon temperatures to protect themselves from losing too much water. Overnight and early in the morning, the plant recovers moisture from the cool air and soil.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Gbi gbɛkɛ kɛ leebi maŋkpa Tso lɛ naa ŋmɔtɔ ekoŋŋ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because it prepares the plants for the daytime heat. Evening watering leaves moisture on the leaves overnight, which encourages fungal diseases and root rot.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ esaa tso lɛ kɛha gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ. Nu ni oooha amɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee fɛ̃i nyɔɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my main crops if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitsei titrii lɛ kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, aggressive plants that quickly consume the soil nutrients, water, and sunlight intended for your crops. Clearing them early ensures your crops do not get starved of vital resources.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli oya kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafee nɔ ni he hiaa.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, sensitive leaves that get burnt under direct sunlight. They require temporary shade trees to block harsh sun and maintain atmospheric moisture while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kukuoo ko koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ mli fɛ̃i ahi shi yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava sheds its leaves during dry spells as a natural survival mechanism to reduce water loss. Once the rainy season starts, the plant uses stored energy from its roots to sprout fresh new leaves.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi. Kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi lɛ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai heei.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my crops when they are still small rather than waiting until they are full-grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli beni amɛji bibii lɛ moŋ fe ni mamɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crops need the most nutrients early in their life cycle when they are building strong roots, stems, and foliage. Feeding them early establishes the foundation needed to produce a heavy harvest later.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ he miihia tsei fe fɛɛ yɛ amɛwala shishijee mli beni amɛfeɔ shishifãi, amɛshishifãi, kɛ baai ni mli wa lɛ. Niyenii ni akɛhaa amɛ mra Eji shishitoo ni he hiaa koni akɛkpa ŋmaa babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why is it important for me to walk through my farm early in the morning to check for insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi koni makwɛ kɛji ŋmeii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many farm pests are most active during the cool morning hours before hiding from the midday sun. Inspecting early allows you to spot infestations before severe damage occurs.
ga: Okwaafoi amli kooloi babaoo tsuɔ nii waa yɛ leebi ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ lɛ amli dani amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ hulutsoo be mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Kwɛmɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Eyeɔ ebua bo ni onaa helai ni baa dani amɛfiteɔ nii waa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms without forming peppers when the afternoon weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pepper baaa beni shwane mli kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, causing them to drop flowers to conserve energy and water. Keeping the soil cool with mulch or providing partial shade helps the plant retain its blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite. Kɛ́ akɛ muji loo hulutsoo fã ko ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce small yields when I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and resources to grow thick stems and large fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct heat and sunlight. They require partial shade—often provided by plantain or leguminous trees—during their first few years to conserve leaf moisture and prevent heat stress.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be fioo. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui loo ŋmeii amli. Koni baa lɛ mli ahi shi ni ebu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Yam plants food and grow heavy tubers by catching sunlight through their leaves. Lifting the vines on stakes spreads the leaves out to receive maximum sunlight while keeping them away from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potatoes kwɛɔ niyenii ni amɛkwɛɔ bulbs ni tsii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛnaa kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ owó wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why should I cut away extra shoots growing around my main plantain crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, fight with the mother plant for water and soil nutrients. Trimming them down to one or two strong stems ensures the main plant gets enough food to produce large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ kɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji amli kɛtee tso kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo plantains agboi ni tsii.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when they lack sufficient water. The plant sheds flowers as a defense mechanism to save energy and water when stressed.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ amɛhe. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛji amɛmiihao.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main nutrient that gives leaves their dark green color and fuels rapid crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ daa oya.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts in my field help my next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When harvested, they leave this natural fertilizer behind, enriched soil for the next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Be ni esa akɛ akpa Amɛbaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yɛ amɛsɛɛ. Enɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni baa nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and short even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ kuku kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong root systems that steal fertilizers and natural soil nutrients faster than your crops can. Even with water, crops starve if weeds eat up all the food in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ nu po yɛ lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji jwɛi ye shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, mites, or whiteflies. As they feed on the leaves, they introduce viruses that cause the foliage to deform and curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites, loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. be mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ Amɛjieɔ helai ni haa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kpo.

english: Why do my crops stop growing and drop some leaves during a short dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli lɛ?

english: When water becomes scarce, plants intentionally drop some of their outer leaves to slow down water loss through evaporation. This behavior allows the plant to survive on limited underground moisture until rains return.
ga: Beni nu faaa lɛ Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshiɔ amɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ ekomɛi koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ subaŋ nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ hiɔ shi kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu fioo ko pɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start turning soft or rotting if left in the ground for too long after maturity?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ loo amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stop growing once mature. If left in wet soil past their harvest window, excess water and soil fungi begin breaking down the starch in the tubers, causing root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ kɛji amɛshɛ shweremɔ he. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ kɛteke kpamɔ be lɛ Nu kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baabɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ mligbalamɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are my older cassava plants growing so big while the small ones planted near them stay tiny and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava momo lɛ da waa nɛkɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Older plants have deeper root systems and bigger leaves, which allows them to take most of the soil nutrients, water, and sunlight for themselves. To prevent this, plant crops of the same age together or leave enough space between young and old plants so the bigger ones do not starve the smaller ones.
ga: Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai wuji. Enɛ haa amɛnáa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Bɔni afee ni atsĩ nɛkɛ Tso nɛɛ naa lɛ, tso ni eye afii kome lɛ afee ekome loo shi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei bibii kɛ tsei onukpai ateŋ. Enɛ ji koni tso agbo lɛ akaye tso bibioo lɛ hɔmɔ.

english: Is it helpful to pull out some seedlings if they are growing too close together in my farm?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ majie dumɔwui lɛ kɛji amɛdara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, this practice is called thinning. When seedlings grow too close together, they fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants. Removing a few gives the remaining crops enough space to grow strong stems and produce bigger yields.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ thinning. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ dara kɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ Ekomɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni he wa, ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do crops planted directly under big shade trees grow tall and thin instead of healthy and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ tsei wuji ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo moŋ fe ni amɛaafee hewalɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to produce food. When blocked by large trees, they stretch upward to reach the light, making them grow tall, thin, and weak instead of developing thick stems and heavy fruit.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛna niyenii. Kɛ tso agbo ko tsi enaa Ebaakpã kɛyashɛ la lɛ he, ni eha efee kakadaŋŋ, egbɔjɔ, ni egbɔjɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeehiɛ tso ni mli tse kɛ yibii ni tsii.

english: What is eating holes in my cassava leaves and stem cut-offs on the farm?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmei baa mli bu ni ayeɔ kɛ ŋmei tsei ni afoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Chewed leaves and stems are usually caused by farm pests such as grasshoppers, caterpillars, or rodents like grasscutters. You can manage this by clearing nearby bush where pests hide, applying organic neem sprays, or erecting simple fences.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii tamɔ jwɛifolɔi ji nɔ ni kɛ baai kɛ tsei ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ otsu enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ ehiɛ amɛhe lɛ ni ooojie lɛ nɔ. Kɛ neem spray ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ atsu nii. loo oma gbogbo ni yɔɔ daa

english: How can I protect my young cassava crop from farm animals and wild rodents that keep destroying them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ amɛ lɛ ahe?

english: Young crops can be protected by constructing simple fencing out of bamboo, mesh wire, or palm fronds around the nursery or plot. Clearing the weeds and brush around the edge of your farm also stops rodents from nesting near your crops.
ga: Abaanyɛ abu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛtsɔ gbogbo ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛ ŋmeii, waya loo ŋmei tsei ahe tsei ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Nursery loo plot Jwɛi kɛ brɔshi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ jiemɔ Okwaafoi lɛ ashishi hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii akafee amɛ ŋmeii yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do cassava stems on my farm fall over even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ waaa moŋ?

english: Stems fall over when underground pests like termites chew through the root system or when root-rot diseases weaken the base of the plant. Inspecting the roots early and keeping the soil properly drained helps prevent this damage.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ ŋmeii, shwie shishifãi lɛ anɔ. aloo be mli ni shishifãi ni egbo lɛ haa tso lɛ shishigbɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ shishifãi lɛ amli mra Ni okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Crops show signs of nutrient hunger through yellowing leaves, slow or stunted growth, and thin stems. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or the right fertilizer replaces missing soil food so the plants can grow vigorously.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hɔmɔ he okadii kɛtsɔɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo loo ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmei, loo ŋmei ni sa ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni akɛ niyenii ni elaaje yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ato najiaŋ koni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my cassava plant producing a lot of heavy green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium. High nitrogen encourages the plant to put all its energy into growing leaves on top rather than expanding the tubers under the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ama baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, ngmlɛfia ɔmɛ yaa zugba a sisi.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots spoil and turn dark so fast after sitting in the house for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ duŋ oya kɛji mita shĩa mli gbii fioo komɛi?

english: Cassava roots start to spoil quickly within two to three days after harvest because they lose moisture and react with oxygen in the air. To preserve them longer, process them quickly into gari or flour, or keep fresh roots buried in moist sand.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ feɔ ekome. Kɛji oosumɔ ni okɛto he be kakadaŋŋ. Oya ni okɛfee gari loo ashikishaŋ. Aloo bua shishifãi heei ni afu yɛ ŋã ni mli edɔ mli lɛ anaa.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to harsh soil conditions, so they absorb water and nutrients much faster than domestic crops. Regular weeding early in the season stops them from overtaking and smothering your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe shia tsei. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ daa yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkaho onibii ahe ni amɛkafite.

english: If animals eat the leaves off my young maize plants, will the maize grow back or is the whole crop destroyed?
ga: Kɛji kooloi ye mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ Ani ŋmãa lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ loo ŋmãa lɛ fɛɛ baafite?

english: If the main growing point deep inside the stem is not eaten, young maize can re-grow fresh leaves. However, it will take longer to mature and might yield smaller cobs because the plant used extra energy to rebuild its leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ he titri ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ, Abele bibii baanyɛ akwɛ baai heei, shi kɛlɛ, eheɔ be babaoo dani edaa ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmeii bibii aba. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei kɛ hewalɛ kroko tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai heei.

english: Why do my tomato plants snap and die so easily when animals walk through my farm compared to other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ fãa ni amɛgboiɔ oya kɛ́ kooloi nyiɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto tsei krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Tomatoes have soft, hollow-like stems and shallow roots, making them physically weak. Unlike woody crops, any heavy pressure easily breaks the stems and disrupts the flow of water and nutrients, killing the plant.
ga: Tomato yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, tamɔ bu kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Ehaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Nɔnyɛɛ ni tsii baaha tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ akumɔ oya. ni etsĩɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Esoro lɛ yɛ tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ ahe Nɔ ni jɛɔ tso lɛ gbele mli baa.

english: Why does my corn fall over so easily when animals push against it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kooloi ba ni amɛbamɔ lɛ?

english: Maize has shallow roots near the surface called prop roots rather than a deep taproot. This makes the tall, top-heavy plant easily untethered from the soil when pushed or disturbed.
ga: Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋwɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ buttress shishifãi yɛ taproots ni mli kwɔ lɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei kakadaji ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya kɛji akɛ atsi amɛ loo agbala amɛnaa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants drop off without forming fruits after my farm is disturbed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni tsɛŋemɔ helai ebote miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when they suffer physical shock or stress. The plant senses it is under threat and conserves water and nutrients for survival rather than putting energy into growing new fruit.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ shoofeemɔ loo haomɔ mli. Tsei nuɔ he akɛ awo amɛhe gbeyei ni amɛbuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ahe gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛdu aduawai heei

english: Why do my tomatoes start rotting so quickly on the vine once their skin gets scratched or damaged?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛ́ ehewolo lɛ shwie shi loo efite lɛ?

english: A tomato's outer skin acts like a protective shield. Once it is scratched or open, bacteria and fungi in the air quickly enter the wound, causing rapid rot and attracting pests.
ga: Tomato lɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he. Kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ loo agbele lɛ, helai ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛ ŋmeii boteɔ pilamɔ lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haa fitemɔ baa oya ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and wilt after livestock step around the base of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi yɛ be mli ni kooloi enyiɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Stepping on the base damages the water-conducting tubes inside the stem and crushes the roots underground. Without water and nutrients reaching the leaves, they lose their green color and begin to die.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ohe wo shishitoo lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaafite nu paipi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. ni efoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Kɛji nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ ni shɛɔ baai lɛ ahe lɛ Baai lɛ hu baafite amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ ni amɛbaabɔi gboimɔ.

english: What kind of fast-growing plants can I plant around my boundary to stop roaming animals from entering my crop field?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ makwɛ yɛ mihe? Mihusui lɛ ji koni matsi kooloi ni nyiɛɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote miŋmɔji lɛ amli.

english: You can plant dense, thorny plants like Jatropha, acacia, or cassava hedges along your farm edges. These form a thick living barrier that animals naturally avoid walking through.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmeii babaoo tamɔ jatropha, acacia loo cassava tsei yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa. Nibii nɛɛ kɛ gbɛtsii nii ni tsii baa kooloi srɔtoi ashihilɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛhoɔ lɛ he.

english: Can planting tall corn around my small tomato patch help shield the tomatoes from stray animals?
ga: Abele kakadaŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ tomato bibii ahe Ani minɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tomato he kɛjɛ kooloi ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, tall maize acts as a visual and physical barrier. Animals are less likely to see or reach lower, softer crops like tomatoes when they are hidden behind a dense border of tall maize.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmãa ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni anaa kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ. Koolooi nyɛɛɛ ana loo amɛshɛɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo tamɔ tomato he kɛji akɛ amɛtee amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmãa ni kɛlɛ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do crops grow so poorly in areas of my field where animals walk frequently?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli hei ni kooloi fɔɔ jɛmɛ yaa lɛ?

english: Heavy animal hoofs compact the soil, pressing out air pockets. Hardened soil makes it difficult for crop roots to spread, breathe, or absorb water, resulting in stunted growth.
ga: Akpɔlɔi ni tsii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui kɛjɛɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni edɔ lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã, amɛmu loo amɛŋɔ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ

english: If an animal bites off part of my tomato plant, should I trim off the damaged branch or leave it?
ga: Kɛji kooloo ko ŋmɔ mi tomato tso lɛ Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni efite lɛ loo mashi amɛ ni amɛfee nɔ ko?

english: It is best to cleanly cut off ragged, damaged branches. Damaged stems attract diseases and pests, while a clean cut helps the plant heal faster and direct energy to fresh, healthy growth.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofolɔ tsei niji ni egboi ni efite lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Tsoi ni efite lɛ gbalaa helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni afolɔ ni he tse lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ shi oya ni ehaa hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend keeping clear distance intervals between my crops instead of planting them closely together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ esa akɛ ahi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni mli ka shi faŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ

english: Giving plants proper space ensures their roots do not fight each other for soil nutrients and water. Good spacing also allows air and sunlight to reach all parts of the plant, preventing diseases and helping them produce larger yields.
ga: Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ he ko ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkaye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni jɛkɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hu haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Tsi helai anaa ni oye obua ni nibii ni afee lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive under direct, harsh sunlight. They need quick-growing shade crops like plantain or taller forest trees to protect their leaves from sunburn and keep moisture in the soil until they grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei kakadaji. Koni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ aaawa.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize turn yellow and roll up tightly during a short dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpãa shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be kuku mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves to stop water from evaporating quickly when the weather is hot and dry. Yellowing leaves mean the plant is stressed and lacks nitrogen, which it can only take up from the soil when there is sufficient water.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu akatsɔ oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao ni nitrogen bɛ ehe. ni tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛ kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ jɛmɛ

english: Why does my cassava produce plenty of long leafy stems but very small tubers underneath the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji babaoo shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of roots below. Balanced soil with phosphorus and potassium is needed for the plant to direct its energy into expanding tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo lɛ, Yucca tsei lɛ kudɔɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni phosphorus kɛ potassium yɔɔ mli ni sa lɛ he miihia waa koni tsei kɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo bulbs.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat, erratic watering, or a lack of nutrients like calcium. Keeping soil moisture steady and avoiding extreme field dryness helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa kpe amɛ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni naa wa ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ amɔmɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Can I plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize crop, and will it help my land?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa? Ni ani ebaaye ebua mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like beans pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them with maize improves soil fertility naturally and provides two different harvests from the same piece of land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni amɛfee nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why is burning the cleared weeds on my plot bad for the crops I am about to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajie yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ashãa lɛ ehiii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter and kills beneficial earthworms and microorganisms that keep soil alive. Leaving cleared bush to decompose creates natural compost that feeds your crops and retains soil moisture.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei bibii lɛ fite lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi lɛ baa.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars keep hiding inside the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These pests are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer to feed on the tender, developing center leaves of young maize. Identifying them early and applying recommended control measures prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye ŋmãa bibii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ahe baai. Kɛ́ ayɔse amɛ mra Ni akɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ amɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Why should I wait until steady rains begin before planting my yam seeds instead of planting right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: The very first rain of the season is often followed by hot dry days that heat up the ground. If yam setts are planted too early in hot, dry soil, they can easily rot or bake before steady rains allow roots to develop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbii ni mli edɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu sweet potatoes mra tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, Ebaanyɛ egbo loo eshã oya dani nugbɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ aha shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why does my harvested cassava start turning dark and spoiling within just two days of digging it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ bɔi duŋ ni efite yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni atsa lɛ?

english: Once cassava tubers are harvested, they react quickly with air and undergo rapid internal breakdown. Because they do not store well fresh, cassava must be processed, sold, or eaten within forty-eight hours of harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ Ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsuɔ nii oya ni etsɔɔ mligbɛ fitemɔ oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ ehiɛɛɛ ehe jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ atsu ŋmãa he nii, ahɔ̃ɔ, loo aye yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai nyɔŋmai ejwɛ kɛ kpaanyɔ mli yɛ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and falling off in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their tender leaves burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them creates a protective canopy that keeps the soil moist and shields the young trees from sun damage.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ emasɛi lɛ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas alongside my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull natural nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds your maize, making the soil richer without needing as much expensive artificial fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛhaa ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa atsu nii.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like straws during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing water through evaporation in extreme heat. It is a natural survival trick the plant uses to conserve moisture until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite yɛ la ni shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ hewɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli wala yibiiwoo he ŋaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi gbɛkɛ mli fɛ̃i baa.

english: How will putting animal manure on my vegetable farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni mikɛwoɔ mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure feeds the tiny beneficial organisms living in the soil and adds essential plant nutrients. It improves the soil's structure so it can hold water longer during hot dry spells, leading to healthier crop growth.
ga: Koolooi ashwiei haa nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ yeɔ niyenii. Nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni he hiaa fataa tsei ahe. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei adalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my cassava leaves to curl up, shrink, and show yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛshwieɔ shi, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: This symptom is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by small whiteflies. The disease stops the plant from making food properly through its leaves, resulting in very small cassava roots at harvest time.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ okadi nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Hela nɛɛ haaa tso lɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my maize seeds very close together to get more plants on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition results in thin, weak stalks and small corn cobs, yielding less grain overall than properly spaced plants.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ akaŋshii nɛɛ mli baa ji ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii. Enɛ haa dumɔwui fioo pɛ baa fe tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why is my yam farm growing very bushy leaves above ground but producing very tiny yams under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ baai akui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or fresh manure, the yam plant puts all its energy into growing green vines and leaves instead of storing energy underground to build large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii heei babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Atomɔ tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ wain tsei kɛ baai eŋɔli. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ he wami toɔ zugba sisi konɛ a kɛ pee tuber agbohi.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my pepper plants with dry grass and dry leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai ni egboi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry foliage, called mulching, acts as a blanket that protects the soil from direct sun. It keeps moisture in the ground for a long time, suppresses weed growth, and prevents soil erosion.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Tsi jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ naa

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and drop dead within days even when there is enough water in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ? Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa po.

english: This sudden dropping is caused by bacterial wilt, a disease living in the soil that enters the plant's roots and blocks the internal tubes that pump water to the leaves, causing the plant to dry up from the inside.
ga: Bacteria wilt ji nɔ ni kɛ tsei lɛ ahe shwiemɔ trukaa nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni eboteɔ tsei ashishifãi amli ni etsĩɔ paipii ni yɔɔ mli ni kɛ nu yaa tsei lɛ amli lɛ anaa. Gbimɔ tso lɛ kɛjɛ emli.

english: Why do my stored dried maize grains turn into powder after keeping them in the barn for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ batsɔ powda beni akɛto ŋmɔ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Small insects called grain weevils bore inside dry maize seeds to feed and lay eggs. As they hatch and eat their way out, they turn the solid starch of your stored grain into useless dust.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed weevils lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli koni amɛtao niyenii ni amɛwo amɛwui. Beni amɛfɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ amɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛjeɔ kpo lɛ. Amɛtsakeɔ ŋmãa ni okɛto lɛ mli ŋmãa ni wa lɛ amɛfeɔ sũ ni he ehiaaa.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a major food source plants need to stay green. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the plants the nutrients they need to grow healthy green leaves.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ jɛɛhe titri koni amɛhiɛ amɛŋmɔji lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the afternoon sun even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: During the hottest part of the day, tomato leaves lose water faster through the heat than the roots can pull up from the ground. If the plant recovers by evening, it is just temporary heat stress, but mulching around the roots helps keep the soil cool.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Tomato baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni latsaa lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbala lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ he wa lɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Eji be kukuoo mli dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛkɛ. Shi kɛ́ okɛ sũ wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a viral infection spread by insects. Spraying with neem oil or appropriate insect control helps protect the foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni kooloi gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo kooloi ahe nibii ni sa shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe.
