english: Why do my young cocoa trees burn and die when I clear all the big trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need protection from harsh, direct sun because their young leaves dry out easily. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and preserves soil moisture so the cocoa can establish.
ga: Esa akɛ abu kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaa bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi bɔni afee ni kookoo lɛ anyɛ ama shi.

english: Cocoa flowers drop if the tree lacks water, lacks nutrients, or if there are not enough tiny insects called midges to pollinate them. Keeping organic matter around the tree base helps retain moisture and supports pollination.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu, niyenii loo kooloi bibii. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa yɛ pollination mli.

english: What causes my plantain trees to fall over when they carry heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni haa mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii wuji wo mli?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that can be weakened by soil pests like nematodes or soft, wet ground during heavy rains. Supporting the stem with a strong wooden prop prevents the weight of the bunch from pulling the tree down.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni sũ mli kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo hei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Tso ni mli wa ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ mli tsiimɔ naa koni ekagbala tso lɛ kɛba shi.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack from the expanding tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ bulb ni miigbɛ eshwa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot inside the soil before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛnáa hegbɛ ni amɛkpaa nii lɛ?

english: Yam rot is caused by fungi or bacteria entering the tuber through waterlogged soil or infected planting material. Ensuring your farm has good drainage and using clean seed yams reduces the chance of rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ baa ji ŋmei loo helatsɛ ko ni boteɔ tuber lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo dumɔ nii ni hela emɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni oŋmɔ lɛ mli aná nu kpakpa ni okɛ sweet potatoes ni he tse tsu nii lɛ baaha hegbɛ ni yɔɔ akɛ ebaafite lɛ aba shi.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil through their roots. When the plant leaves and roots break down, they leave natural fertilizer behind for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ fite Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to remove weeds while my crops are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have small roots and leaves, making them weak competitors against fast-growing weeds. Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, so clearing them early ensures your crop gets all the resources it needs to grow strong.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai bibii. Enɛ haa efeɔ akaŋshilɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛha jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ. Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and get easily damaged under strong direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that shade the young cocoa plants while also giving you food while waiting for cocoa to yield.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ oya. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa bo niyenii be mli ni amɛmɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ afɔ̃ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant stay green and form full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa babaoo taoɔ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo nitrogen ŋmãa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛyi obɔ kɛ ŋmãa.

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell they are ready when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, or by carefully digging up one root to inspect its size.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo hiɔ shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ amɛfee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. aloo kɛtsɔ shishifã kome ni oootsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ bɔ ni elɛɛmɔ ji lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it necessary to build wood stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ma tso tso ko kɛha mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni makwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce food for growing heavy tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where they can rot, allowing them to catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni tsii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akatara hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ. Enɛ haa enine shɛɔ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce flowers, but the flowers drop off without growing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni miduuu tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants suffer from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees. Consistent watering during hot periods and avoiding heavy chemical sprays during flowering will help fruit to form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na amanehulu yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nibii ni haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nu daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he. Yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, ehaa aduawai feɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes thin stems and small cobs, while correct spacing ensures every plant gets enough resources to thrive.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: How can I keep my garden soil from drying out so quickly during the hot dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ akagbi oya yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dry grass, leaves, or crop residue—a practice called mulching—traps moisture in the soil, lowers ground temperature, and reduces how often you need to water.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ—ni ji nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ aba shi ni oha shii abɔ ni esa akɛ okɛ nu awo mli lɛ aba shi.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with powdery waste inside the leaf whorls?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai amli ni starch bibii yɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed inside the center of young maize plants. Catching them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract can stop them from destroying the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ amɛnaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔji.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm plot before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmei yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. Planting maize on that same spot later allows the maize to feed on that leftover natural fertility.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ aye adebɔɔ mli nibii babaoo ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and looking twisted and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite ni eyɛ bibioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies that carry plant viruses. Controlling these pests with mild soapy water sprays or neem oil helps keep leaves healthy and flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni hiɛ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ shwieɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ haa baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my cocoa trees without turning into young pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from prolonged dry spells, a lack of natural insect pollinators like midges, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients during the flowering stage.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna amanehulu yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli. Adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa tamɔ midges ni bɛ, loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily once they start carrying heavy bunches of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ebɔi aduawai babaoo womɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that are easily weakened by pests like nematodes and stem borers, making the heavy plant collapse under strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes kɛ stem borers lɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ oya. Enɛ haa tsei ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa shishi.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the tip downward when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or when heavy rainfall washes fertilizers away beyond the roots.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa shishi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ho shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my maize crops grow stronger when I plant cowpeas or beans in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa waa kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a natural food supply that helps neighboring maize grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot underground before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛnáa hegbɛ ni amɛkpaa amɛ?

english: Cassava root rot is usually caused by waterlogged soil during heavy rainy seasons or fungal infections carried in diseased stem cuttings used during planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. aloo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko yɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start sprouting shoots in the barn before I am ready to plant or sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mifee klalo akɛ madu loo mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break their dormancy state and sprout when exposed to high humidity, warmth, or light, as these conditions signal to the tuber that it is time to grow.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafite amɛ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe kɛ budding shihilɛ lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ ŋmɔtɔ, hulutsoo loo la ni naa wa he, ejaakɛ shihilɛi nɛɛ tsɔɔ bulb lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ eda.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and looking stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by viruses spread by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies, or as a self-defense reaction to extreme heat and lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, loo nɔ ni jɛɔ he ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ mli baa.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings wither and die shortly after I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper seedlings suffer from transplant shock when moved into hot, open sunlight without a hardening-off period, or when their delicate roots get damaged during moving.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ naa amanehulu kɛjɛ transplant shock mli kɛji ajie amɛ kɛtee hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ ni be ko bɛ ni haa ewaa. aloo kɛ́ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ fite yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it better to construct farm ridges across a sloped land instead of up and down the hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaama ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni aaakwɔ kɛba shi yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Building ridges across a slope acts as a barrier that slows down rainwater, preventing soil erosion and keeping fertilizers from washing off your farm.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ ko ni afeɔ yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni haa nugbɔ nu lɛ baa shi. Tsi shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni otsi ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why does clearing weeds early in the first few weeks give me a much better crop yield than weeding late?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fe jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crops suffer the most when competing with fast-growing weeds for soil food, water, and sunlight; clearing weeds early lets your crop establish strong roots without stress.
ga: Naa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ kɛ́ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ehaa onibii lɛ shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Why are so many farmers across Ghana choosing to venture into tomato farming instead of sticking only to traditional crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana fɛɛ lɛ miihala akɛ amɛkɛ amɛhe baawo tomato dumɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ohe akpɛtɛ blema nibii tamɔ ŋmãa pɛ he lɛ.

english: Tomatoes have a short growing cycle of about 3 to 4 months and high year-round market demand across Ghana. This allows farmers to harvest quickly and earn income multiple times a year compared to single-season staple crops.
ga: Tomato yɛ be kukuoo mli ni edaa aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 ni eyɛ jara ni ataoɔ waa afi muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ Ghana fɛɛ. Enɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ kpaɔ nii oya ni amɛnáa shika shii abɔ yɛ afi mli kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni amɛkpaa yɛ be kome mli lɛ he.

english: Why is the Akomadan area in Ashanti region so famous and successful for growing tomatoes compared to other towns?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Akomadan kpokpaa ni yɔɔ Ashanti kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ehe gbɛi waa ni eyeɔ omanye yɛ tomato ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ akɛto maji krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Akomadan has a unique combination of well-drained, fertile soil and favorable micro-climate conditions that allow tomatoes to thrive, along with an established community of experienced tomato farmers and buyers.
ga: Akomadan yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni baa nii kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfee ekome ni yɔɔ srɔto kwraa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomatoi lɛ ni amɛdaraa. yɛ akutso ko ni ato ama shi ni ji tomato okwaafoi kɛ jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ masɛi.

english: When temperatures get too high, heat stress damages tomato pollen, preventing pollination. The plant automatically sheds its unpollinated flowers to conserve energy and survive the hot weather.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Heat stress fiteɔ tomato pollen. ni etsi pollination naa Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni pollin bɛ mli lɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn dark brown or black before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ dani ekwɛ̃ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium, usually caused by irregular watering or long dry spells that prevent nutrients from reaching the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ amli be fɛɛ be loo be kakadaŋŋ ni hulu enyɔ shi ni haaaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ayashɛ aduawai lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant my tomato seedlings very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu tomato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crowding tomato plants traps moisture and blocks sunlight between leaves. This creates a warm, humid environment where fungal diseases spread fast, and causes plants to fight each other for nutrients.
ga: Tomato tsei ni mli wa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni ehaa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he lɛ

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl upward during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. The tomato plant rolls its leaves inward to reduce the surface area exposed to direct sunlight, helping it conserve water during the hottest parts of the day.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ toɔ he yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: What happens to my tomato plants if I give them too much nitrogen fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha amɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen forces the plant to spend all its energy growing huge, dark green leaves and stems while delaying or completely stopping flower and fruit production.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa kɛ ŋmeii agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai afeemɔ baa shi loo ekpaa kwraa.

english: Why do my young tomato seedlings grow tall, thin, and weak in the nursery bed instead of short and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato dumɔwui bibii lɛ miida, amɛmiigbɔjɔ, ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ kuku nɛ e ngɛ bush.

english: Seedlings become tall and weak (leggy) when they are shaded and do not get enough direct sunlight. They stretch upward as fast as possible trying to search for light.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa (naji) kɛji amɛyɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛkpã amɛhe oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ, ni amɛmiitao la lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil and rot so quickly during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rainy weather causes tomatoes to absorb excess water, making their skin tender and prone to cracking. High humidity also accelerates mold growth on harvested fruit if kept in sealed or unventilated boxes.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ. Ehaa hewolo lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa egbɛɔ eshwaa. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ hu haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ aduawai ni akpa lɛ anɔ lɛ daa oya. Kɛji akɛ akɛto adeka ko ni atsĩ naa mli loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli

english: Why do insects like whiteflies swarm my tomato farm more during the dry season than in the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ eyi mitato ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Dry and warm conditions allow whiteflies and other small sap-sucking insects to reproduce much faster, while heavy rains naturally wash them off leaves and destroy their breeding ground.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa whiteflies kɛ kooloi bibii krokomɛi ni nuɔ nu lɛ. Amɛfɔɔ bii oya kwraa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ahe ni efiteɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli he ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested grains rot when I try to store them in my house to sell later for better prices?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ beni mibɔɔ mɔdɛŋ akɛ mikɛto mishia koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ sɛɛ mli yɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Grains rot during storage because they still hold hidden moisture inside them when harvested. If you do not dry them completely in the sun before storing, mold and tiny insects grow rapidly inside the bags and destroy the harvest.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ ejaakɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli lolo ni akɛteeɔ mli kɛ́ akpa. Kɛji okɛgbiko yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani okɛto. Fungi kɛ kooloi bibii Ekwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ kotoku lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How can I keep my yams from spoiling while waiting for market prices to go up?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ aha sweet potatoes akafite yɛ be mli ni mɛɔ ni jara nɔ jara lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Yams spoil quickly if left in hot, closed rooms or directly on the damp ground. Building a simple raised barn with bamboo shelves in a shaded, well-ventilated area keeps the tubers cool and dry, stopping them from rotting or sprouting too early.
ga: Atomo fiteɔ oya kɛji ashi yɛ tsu ko ni mli edɔ, ni aŋã mli loo akɛma he ko ni efɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ama shikpɔŋ nɔ tsũ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛ ŋmei fee yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ mli jɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ. Tsi bulb lɛ naa koni ekafite loo ekwɛ̃ oya tsɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Too much rain fills up all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots. When roots cannot breathe, they stop absorbing essential food from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow from lack of nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ gbo lɛ, amɛkpaa niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɔmɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops right before heavy rain starts?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: No, because heavy rain will wash away the fertilizer before your crops get a chance to drink it in. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after rain, but not when heavy downpours are expected immediately.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hegbɛ amɛnuɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Shi jeee be mli ni akpaa nugbɔ ni naa wa gbɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my main crops during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are naturally stronger and react much faster to water than domesticated crops. They quickly drink up the rainwater and steal soil nutrients unless you clear them early.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni wa waa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛtsuɔ nu he nii oya fe shia tsei. Amɛnuɔ nugbɔ nu oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ja otsi mli klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants during heavy rains instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai?

english: Heavy raindrops can physically knock flowers off the plant, and cold rainy weather stops bees and insects from flying around to pollinate the blossoms. Without pollination, the flowers simply drop off.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ atswa fɔfɔii kɛjɛ tsei anɔ. Ni fɛ̃i ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafo kɛbɔle amɛhe koni amɛyawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii. Kɛji akɛ pollination bɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when water stands on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni nu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil to breathe and grow. When water collects and stands on the land for days, it cuts off oxygen to the soil, causing the tubers to decay underground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa ni edamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo. Ebaafo kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Does heavy rainfall wash away the good soil nutrients that my crops need to grow?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni he hiaa mi tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ kɛya?

english: Yes, heavy rain sweeps away the fertile top layer of soil and washes deep nutrients below the reach of crop roots. Building small soil ridges or planting across slopes helps trap water and keep nutrients in place.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. ni efoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ ashishi shɔŋŋ lɛ Ŋshɔkpɔi bibii ni afee loo dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehaa niyenii mli nibii hiɔ shi yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and spoil when it rains continuously for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous rain creates a damp environment where a fungal disease called Black Pod thrives. The fungus spreads through water droplets splashing from infected soil or pods onto healthy ones.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pods baa. Fuji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nu mli nu ni shwieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔ mli lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rain softens the soil around the roots, making it loose, while the heavy weight of water on the broad leaves and fruit bunches makes the plant top-heavy. Strong rain winds can then easily pull the shallow roots out of the soft ground.
ga: Nugbɔ haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ blɛoo, ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, yɛ be mli ni nu ni tsii ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛ aduawai akui lɛ anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I clear all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Be ni majie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect them from direct, harsh sunlight and hot winds. Leaving some shade trees or planting plantains alongside your cocoa creates a cool environment that keeps the young cocoa alive until it matures.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hɔnɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ ashi tsei yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ baa ni ehaa kookoo bibii lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together causes the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and small cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to produce large, full cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa nitsumɔhe fɛɛ nitsumɔhe náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen or the soil is too waterlogged. Applying the right fertilizer when the soil is moist will help the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even after I add fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food you put into the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot mostly when planted in low land that holds too much water during heavy rains. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ babaoo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu babaoo yɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects sucking the sap or spreading leaf diseases. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat, healthy, and able to produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ loo hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛhe awa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers fall off without making tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee amɛ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or if there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Consistent watering during hot spells helps fruits form properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ baaye abua ni tso yibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so leaves catch maximum sunlight and stay safe from soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulu la babaoo, ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from a dealer instead of saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ jarayelɔ dɛŋ? Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ je ngma kpami nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ kɛ to.

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to fight off local diseases, resist dry weather, and give high yields. Seeds saved from past harvests lose these strong traits over time, leading to smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni akɛwu ashi maŋ lɛ mli helai. Te shi owo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni okɛ yibiiwoo babaoo aba Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baafite sui nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my crops right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛha mi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry spell that bakes the soil. Waiting until the rains become regular ensures the soil stays wet enough for seeds to sprout and survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. Feeding the crop with the right fertilizer early in its growth helps it stay green, strong, and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baaha ŋmɔshi nibii mra Ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji, amɛhe wa ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves and husks turn dry and brown, and a small black spot forms at the base of each grain kernel.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaa yɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi.

english: Does my rice crop always need to stand in deep water to grow properly?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ adamɔ nu ni mli kwɔ mli be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Not all rice needs standing water. Lowland rice benefits from flooded fields because it stops weeds, but upland rice can grow on dry land as long as it gets regular rainfall.
ga: Omɔ henɔi komɛi biɔ nu ni damɔ shi. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa náa nu afua lɛ he sɛɛ ejaakɛ efoɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa. Shi ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ, kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ daa.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my young rice crop after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi dumɔwui lɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that aggressively steal water and soil nutrients faster than young rice. Removing them early gives your rice crop room to feed and grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmãa bibii. Ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha he ni oduɔ ŋmãa yɛ lɛ aná niyenii ni ebaanyɛ eda.

english: Why are the tiny flowers and small pods dropping off my cocoa trees before maturing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ cacao tsei anɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop pods when they suffer from water stress, pest attacks, or lack of soil nutrients during key growth stages.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu he haomɔ, kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ miipiŋ amɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ.

english: Improved cocoa varieties usually start bearing pods within 2 to 3 years if planted properly and given good care, while older varieties can take up to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 5.

english: Why should I plant my crops in neat rows instead of scattering seeds all over the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo nɔ moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ mashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in rows gives each plant enough room to receive sunlight and nutrients while making it much easier for you to weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest.
ga: Tso ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ ená hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okpa ŋmɔshi nii.

english: How often should I return to my field to check on my crops after planting?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ maku misɛɛ kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni miyakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni midu nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should visit your farm at least once or twice a week so you can catch early signs of pests, diseases, or weed growth before they harm your yield.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ oya oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Koni akwɛ mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai loo jwɛi miida. Dani ebaaye oŋmɔshinii lɛ awui

english: Why am I getting smaller harvests every year even though I plant on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ nibii babaoo nɔ daa afi lɛ? Akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Growing crops continuously on the same plot wears out soil nutrients over time. Soil needs nutrient replenishment through fertilizers, organic manure, or resting periods.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ afite yɛ be ni sa mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, humus, loo hejɔɔmɔ be awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: What is the best stage of plant growth to apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni tsei lɛ baakwɛ koni amɛkɛwo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied in stages: once early after germination to build strong roots and leaves, and again just before flowering to support grain or fruit development.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛwo mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli: klɛŋklɛŋ beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ koni etswa shishifãi kɛ baai ni wa. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi koni eye ebua dumɔwui loo aduawai lɛ shweremɔ.

english: I noticed new shoots growing at the bottom trunk of my cocoa tree. Should I cut them off or leave them to grow?
ga: Miyɔse ŋmeii heei ni miikwɛ̃ yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi. Ani esa akɛ mafo mli loo mahã eda?

english: Those bottom shoots are called chupons or watersprouts. You should cut them off early because they steal food and water from the main tree, which reduces your cocoa pod harvest.
ga: Atsɛɔ shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ akɛ chupons loo nu ŋmeii. Esa akɛ ofo amɛ mra. Ejaakɛ ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha o-cocoa pod ni okpaa lɛ aba shi.

english: Will trimming some of the upper leaves and branches help my cocoa tree produce more pods?
ga: Ani ŋwɛi baai kɛ eniji lɛ ekomɛi ni afolɔ lɛ baaye abua cacao tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Yes, pruning overhead leaves lets sunlight and fresh air reach the inner branches. This keeps fungal diseases like black pod away and encourages the tree to produce more flowers and pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tsei lɛ aniji amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji anaa ni ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are getting enough food from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miiná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy leaves are dark green and full of life. If the leaves look pale, yellow, or dry at the edges, your crop is starving for nutrients and needs organic manure or fertilizer.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ eŋɔli ni eyi obɔ kɛ wala. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔŋ, loo egbi lɛ, no lɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ onibii amli ni ehe miihia humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young crops turning yellow with dark spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ diji lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves with spots usually mean your crop is affected by a plant disease or insect attack. Clearing affected leaves and applying the right control measures will protect the rest of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso hela loo kooloi bibii etutua onibii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ, ni atsu gbɛjianɔi ni sa ni akɛbaakwɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves dry up and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves in dry weather to save water and protect themselves from heat. Planting shade trees and placing dry grass around the tree base helps retain moisture so the leaves stay green longer.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa ni aduɔ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to leave tall shade trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mashi tsei kakadaji yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Shade trees act as natural umbrellas that protect delicate cocoa leaves from harsh sunlight, keep the soil cool, and drop falling leaves that decompose into rich natural fertilizer.
ga: Shade tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade ni buɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ehaa baai ni egbee shi ni fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees suddenly grow a lot of fresh green leaves all at once after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ ná baai babaoo ni tsuɔ nii shikome trukaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When rain falls after a dry period, the roots quickly drink up water and trigger a burst of leaf growth called flushing, which prepares the tree to build up energy for flowering.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ Shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu lɛ oya ni ehaa baa lɛ daa ni atsɛɔ lɛ leaching. Enɛ saa tso lɛ he koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha fɔfɔi.

english: Why must I clear weeds away from the base of my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ashishi daa lɛ?

english: Weeds surrounding the base of your crop eat the food and drink the water meant for your cocoa roots, making your trees weak and slow to produce pods.
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle Otso lɛ shishi lɛ haa niyenii kɛ nu kɛhaa o-cocoa shishifãi lɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa oya.

english: What makes a young cocoa tree strong enough to yield pods for many years?
ga: Mɛni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii afii babaoo?

english: A strong tree develops when it gets good shade during its early years, rich soil nutrients, protection from sap-sucking pests, and regular clearing around its base.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ daa kɛji amɛná hulutsoo kpakpa yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli. Niyenii nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eyi obɔ. Hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ nu lɛ ahe ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi daa

english: If I have a very strong cocoa tree on my farm, can I use its branches to grow new healthy trees?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ani manyɛ mikɛ eniji lɛ atsu nii ni mikɛdu tsei heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, through techniques like budding or grafting, you can take a branch from your strongest tree and join it to a seedling so the new tree inherits the same strength and high pod yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ ŋaa gbɛ̀i tamɔ budding loo grafting nɔ. Obaanyɛ oŋɔ nine kɛjɛ otso ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli ni okɛwo dumɔwu lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni tsei heei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ kɛ pod yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are my cocoa trees flowering but not producing many pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛfɔfɔi babaoo bɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need proper pollination by tiny insects like midges, as well as adequate soil nutrients. If the farm canopy is too dense or lacks nutrients, many flowers will drop off before forming pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ biɔ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ afee amɛ pollination ni sa, kɛ agbɛnɛ hu niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli eyi tsɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ Fɔfɔi babaoo baagbee shi dani ŋmeii lɛ afee.

english: What basic steps can I take to make my cocoa trees yield more pods every season?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii manyɛ mafee koni mi-cacao tso lɛ awo ŋmeii babaoo daa afi?

english: To increase pod production, prune branches regularly to allow sunlight, control weeds, apply recommended fertilizers, and protect flower cushions from pests and fungal diseases.
ga: koni eha pod lɛ aya hiɛ Kpãa tsei aniji anɔ daa koni hulu la aba, akudɔ jwɛi lɛ, ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ awo mli. ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi akutsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: What causes small green cocoa pods to turn black and dry up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ? Ani ebaatsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi dani eda?

english: This is often caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads in humid, shady conditions, or Cherelle Wilt, where the tree naturally sheds extra pods it cannot nourish due to stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. loo cherry wilt Tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aye nɔ yɛ haomɔ hewɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I tell if the methods I am currently using on my cocoa farm are actually working?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ gbɛi ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsu nii?

english: You can evaluate your farm by tracking your seasonal harvest yield, checking tree health against high-performing farms in nearby villages, and reviewing your farm maintenance habits with an extension officer.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ be mli nibii ni anáa lɛ asɛɛnyiɛmɔ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ tsei ahewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ akrowai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ. Ni okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ saamɔ he subaŋ lɛ kɛ sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ nitsulɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it helpful for me to visit other cocoa farms that produce very high yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ayasara kookoo ŋmɔji krokomɛi? Eyɛ yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ waa no hewɔ lɛ ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha mi.

english: Visiting successful farms allows you to see effective techniques in practice—such as proper shade management and pruning—so you can adapt those proven methods to improve your own farm.
ga: Kɛ́ oyasara ŋmɔ ko ni yeɔ omanye lɛ, ebaaha ona ŋaai ni mɔɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii, tamɔ bɔ ni akwɛɔ hulutsoo nɔ ahaa kɛ bɔ ni akwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ otsake nakai gbɛi ni ana he odaseyeli lɛ koni okɛha bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does cutting off branches help my cocoa tree produce more fruit instead of harming it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cacao tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo moŋ fe ni eeeye lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unproductive, overcrowded, or diseased branches. This lets sunlight and air reach the trunk, reduces fungal diseases, and directs energy into forming healthy flowers and pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii, ni eyi obɔ kɛ helai, loo ni helai emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe, ehaa ŋmeii helai baa shi, ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii ni he wa.

english: Where on the cocoa tree do the pods actually develop, and how do I protect those areas?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni kookoo tso lɛ nɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ diɛŋtsɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu nakai hei lɛ ahe?

english: Pods grow on the main trunk and large branches from spots called flower cushions. You can protect them by carefully harvesting without damaging the bark and keeping the trunk clear of parasitic plants.
ga: Pods kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ kɛ niji wuji anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni atsɛɔ amɛ floral cushions lɛ. Obaanyɛ obu amɛhe kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oookpa jogbaŋŋ ni ofiteee amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe, ni oooha tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ akabote amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: How does clearing weeds regularly help my cocoa trees grow better cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ kookoo tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal water and plant food from the cocoa tree's roots and trap extra moisture that causes diseases. Keeping the farm clean helps trees stay strong and bear more fruit.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ shishifãi amli ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni kɛ hela baa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How do I choose the best cocoa seedlings to plant so my farm yields well in the future?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala kookoo dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ ni madu koni miŋmɔ lɛ aná yibii kpakpai wɔsɛɛ?

english: Get certified hybrid cocoa seedlings from approved nurseries. These improved varieties grow faster, bear fruit earlier, produce higher pod yields, and resist diseases better than older trees.
ga: Na kookoo dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofa ewo mli ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ tsoi srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ nɛɛ daa oya, amɛwoɔ yibii oya, ni amɛwoɔ pod yibii babaoo. ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe fe tsei ni edara lɛ

english: Is it better to care for and restore my old cocoa trees or abandon the farm completely?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaakwɛ cacao tsei momo lɛ anɔ ni aku sɛɛ afee amɛ ekoŋŋ loo abaashi ŋmɔ lɛ kwraa?

english: Restoring old trees through proper pruning, soil fertility care, and disease management is often valuable because established roots can return to high pod production faster than waiting for new plantings to mature.
ga: Tsei momoi aku sɛɛ aba kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ Kɛ helai ahe nitsumɔ he hiaa bei pii ejaakɛ shishifãi ni wa lɛ baanyɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛba ŋmɔshi nibii amli oya fe ni amɛaamɛ ni tsei heei adara.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily in direct sunlight. Leaving selected shade trees or planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa from harsh sun and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa bushes grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni ahala ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or the ground is overly waterlogged. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or organic manure, along with proper field drainage, helps the leaves return to a healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli tsɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛ su ni yeɔ emuu lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally feeding the soil. Planting them with maize improves soil fertility, lowers fertilizer costs, and gives you an extra harvest from the same piece of land.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Abele ni akɛ abele duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo aba shi ni ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: If I save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant next season, why is my yield much lower?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ to koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ minitsumɔ lɛ baa shi kwraa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for one high-yielding generation. When you save seeds from that harvest to plant again, the second generation loses those strong yields and grows unevenly, so buying fresh certified seeds each season is necessary for maximum yield.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ kɛha henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Beni ohereɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ koni oyadu ekoŋŋ lɛ. Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ baafite nakai yibiiwoo ni mli wa lɛ ni ebaada yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ he miihia waa koni anyɛ ana yibiiwoo babaoo.

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become regular. The first rain is often followed by a heatwave or dry spell that can scorch germinating seeds in the soil before the main rainy season truly starts.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi diɛŋtsɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up wooden stakes to grow good tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for root development. Staking keeps the leaves lifted off the wet ground where they can catch sunlight better and stay safe from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛna hewalɛ kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ. Staking haa anyɛɔ ajieɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe

english: What is causing tiny caterpillars to eat holes inside the fresh center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ye bu ni yɔɔ baa hee ni yɔɔ mi-babi ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, an invasive pest that lays eggs on maize. They feed inside the central whorl of the plant, requiring early scouting and targeted treatment before they destroy the main growing tip.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni baa mɔ nɔ ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ. Amɛyeɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli. Enɛ biɔ ni akwɛ mra. ni amɛná tsamɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani amɛfite fã titri ni miida lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are mature enough to harvest without pulling up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni mijieee tso muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 8 and 12 months depending on the variety. You can spot maturity when the lower leaves yellow and drop off, or by carefully digging around one side of the plant to check if the tubers are thick and firm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ ayeɔ yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 teŋ, ni enɛ damɔ ŋmei lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ ona shweremɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. aloo kɛtsɔ tso lɛ fã kome ni oootsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ shiŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce many flowers but the flowers drop off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi efoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat, insufficient water, or lack of pollination. Regular watering during dry periods and planting during cooler windows helps flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo pollination ni bɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ dumɔ yɛ samflɛ ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How does covering the soil around my vegetable plants with dry grass help them grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or straw—called mulching—keeps the soil cool, prevents sunlight from evaporating soil water, and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi loo jwɛi - ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching - yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i. Tsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and drying up in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight when they are small. They need temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava planted next to them to shield them from heat stress until their roots grow deep and strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ ji koni akɛtsi dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo mli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are the central leaves of my young maize plants filled with holes and small droppings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are a clear sign of Fall Armyworm damage. The caterpillars hide inside the center of the plant (the whorl) to feed, so spraying early in the morning or late evening directly into the center helps get rid of them.
ga: Bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm efite. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ (ring) koni amɛye nii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie tso lɛ teŋgbɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: Yellowing starting from the bottom leaves indicates that your soil lacks nitrogen. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-composted manure early in the plant's life restores the green color and supports healthy growth.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛjɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ atsu nii. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha edalɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curled leaves with yellow patterns are caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies. The best way to prevent it is by planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties recommended by agricultural officers.
ga: Baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ he mfoniri. Nɔ ni kɛ cassava mosaic hela ni ji whiteflies bibii lɛ baa Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ enɛ naa ji ni adu cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ taakɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ wo ŋaa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall and thin without giving me many fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When tomato plants are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight and air, growing tall and weak instead of spreading out to produce flowers and fruit. Proper spacing gives each plant enough light and room to bear heavily.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tomatoi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tomatoi kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he akaŋ. Edaa ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa ni ewo fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa la kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ etsitsinɔnii lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the soil is too dry or the heat is too intense. Mulching the base of the plant with dry grass and watering regularly keeps the soil cool and moist, helping the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo tso lɛ shishi ni okɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe.

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need sun exposure to make food for the plant. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground away from heat and rot, allowing the plant to capture light and build bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tso ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la koni ekɛfee niyenii aha tso lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajie kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ fitemɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ la ni ekwɛɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Black pods are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and shady conditions. Pruning extra shade branches and harvesting ripe pods quickly reduces moisture and stops the spread of the disease.
ga: Black pods hela ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo mli lɛ amli ni akpa tsei ni egbɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi oya, ni ebaaha hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ aba shi.

english: Why do my stored onions soft-rot and smell bad just a few weeks after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onions ni mikɛto lɛ miifite ni miifite yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni akpa lɛ?

english: Onions rot in storage if they are harvested before their leaves dry completely, or if they are stored in damp, unventilated places. Curing them in a dry, shady spot before storage keeps them firm and fresh for longer.
ga: Sabala fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ akpa dani baai lɛ agbi kwraa. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛto he ko ni mli egbi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli dani akɛto lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni loo lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni ehi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: This is normal groundnut behavior. After the flower is pollinated above ground, the plant naturally grows pegs that push into the soil, where the actual groundnut pods form and mature hidden under the earth.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei subaŋ ni afɔɔ feemɔ. Beni afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ. Bean ŋmɔtɔi lɛ jeɔ kpo ni amɛdaraa, ni amɛhiɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight and heat. Planting shade trees or plantains around them creates a canopy that protects the young cocoa from burning, retains soil moisture, and allows the seedlings to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ la he lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oye obua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight to produce energy for the plant. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get full sunlight, which encourages the plant to grow larger tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ amɛha tso lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is an essential food for maize plants that keeps their leaves green and helps them produce strong, healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmãa tsei ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ebaai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa toi ni wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei afee ekome kɛdu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil and helps nearby maize grow better without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli babaoo tamɔ nɛkɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees give me small bunches when I leave all the small shoots growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni mishiɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Nakai tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main mother plant. Removing all but one or two strong suckers leaves enough food for the main plant to grow large, healthy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni etsɔ plantain tso agbo ni mli wa.

english: How does spreading dry grass or leaves around the roots of my crop help during the dry season?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te ŋmɔshi nibii ashishifãi yeɔ ebuaa tɛŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Spreading dry grass around crops is called mulching. It acts like a blanket over the dirt, trapping water in the soil, keeping the roots cool, and stopping weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Efeɔ enii tamɔ kuntu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ aŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are there tiny caterpillars eating holes in the inner leaves of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ mli baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. They hide in the leaves and feed on the growing point of the plant, which can destroy the crop if not treated early with proper sprays or neem solutions.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ hei ni edaa lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra. Kɛ spray loo neem tsofa ni sa.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off before producing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as intense heat, lack of water in the soil, or damage from microscopic insects like thrips.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. loo nɔ ni kooloi bibii waa tamɔ thrips fiteɔ.

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the tomato plant doesn't get a steady supply of water or calcium while the fruit is growing rapidly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu loo calcium nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida oya lɛ.

english: Why should I plant cassava stem cuttings slantwise into the soil instead of laying them flat on top of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-cassava niji lɛ ni mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni makɛ amɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting stem cuttings at an angle firmly into moist soil allows roots to grow deep underground for tuber formation, while the buds above ground can quickly push out healthy branches and leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ bulbs. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashɛre niji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ oya.

english: Can I spray chemical pesticides on my vegetables right before I harvest them to keep insects away?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ dani akpa koni mikɛshwie kooloi lɛ?

english: No, spraying chemicals right before harvest is dangerous because toxic residues stay on the crops, making them unsafe for consumers to eat. You should stop spraying synthetic chemicals weeks before harvesting.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani akpaa lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara yɛ tsofai fɔji ni eshwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haaa efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha nihɔɔlɔi akɛ amɛaaye niyenii. Esa akɛ okpa tsofai ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ otsii komɛi dani akpamɔ.

english: How many days am I supposed to wait after spraying my crop before I can safely pick and sell it?
ga: Beni mikɛ tsofa eshwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ Gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani manyɛ mahala ni mahɔ̃ɔ shweshweeshwe?

english: This waiting time is called the Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI). Depending on the chemical, you must wait anywhere from 3 to 21 days after spraying so the poison breaks down naturally before harvest.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ mɛmɔ be nɛɛ akɛ be ni tsɔ ŋmaakpamɔ hiɛ (PHI). Esa akɛ omɛ gbii 3 kɛyashi 21 yɛ tsofa ni okɛshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ damɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Enɛ ji koni aha tsofa fɔŋ lɛ afite yɛ ehe dani akpa.

english: What will happen to people if I sell crops that were sprayed with chemical pesticides just a day before harvest?
ga: Mɛni baaba gbɔmɛi anɔ kɛji mihɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ gbi ni tsɔ ŋmaa lɛ hiɛ lɛ?

english: Eating crops sprayed right before harvest causes food poisoning, stomach problems, and long-term health issues because the dangerous chemical residue has not had enough time to wash away or disappear.
ga: Tsei ni akɛ tsofa shwie nɔ dani akpa lɛ ni ayeɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii ni mli ewo muji baa. musu mli naagbai kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ mli naagbai ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ ji akɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara ni eshwɛ lɛ bɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii loo amɛbaafite.

english: What does it mean when my crop enters the fruit setting stage?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bote yibiiwoo be lɛ mli?

english: Fruit setting is the critical moment right after flowering when the blossoms fall off and tiny young fruits, pods, or grains start forming on your plants.
ga: Yibiiwoo ji be ko ni he hiaa waa yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ asɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Beni fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ, pods loo dumɔwui jeɔ shishi efeɔ yɛ otso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops become so sensitive and weak when they start setting fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ waaa ni amɛhe waaa beni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: During fruit setting, the plant directs almost all of its water and nutrients into growing the young fruits, leaving the plant with less energy to defend itself against pests, diseases, and harsh weather.
ga: Yɛ yibiiwoo be mli lɛ Tsei kudɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni aduawai bibii akwɛ lɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛkɛbaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, helai kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do insects and pests suddenly flock to my farm when my fruits are almost ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ miiho kɛmiiba miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni eshwɛ fioo ni miyibii lɛ baakpa lɛ?

english: Pests love mature crops because ripening fruits and pods are rich in natural sugars, water, and nutrients, making the harvesting stage the most appealing time for pests to feed.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ sumɔɔ tsei ni eda ejaakɛ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli eyi obɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli sugars, nu kɛ niyenii, ni no haa ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ be lɛ feɔ be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aye nii.

english: What are biosolutions, and how are they different from the usual agrochemicals I buy?
ga: Mɛni ji wala yibii ahe tsabaa? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro lɛ yɛ okwaayeli tsofai ni miheɔ daa lɛ ahe?

english: Biosolutions are eco-friendly crop treatments made from natural ingredients like plants, neem extracts, or beneficial microbes. Unlike harsh synthetic chemicals, they protect your plants without leaving poisonous residues on your food.
ga: Biological solutions ji nibii ni akɛtsaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ tso, neem mli nu lɛ feɔ. loo nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ Etamɔɔɔ tsofai ni akɛfee nibii ni mli wa Amɛbuɔ otsei lɛ ahe ni amɛshiii tsofai fɔji ni eshwɛ yɛ oniyenii lɛ nɔ.

english: If pests attack my crops right at the harvest stage, are biological sprays effective enough to stop them?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutua miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli hu? Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkpa?

english: Yes, biological sprays effectively repel or kill pests at harvest time while keeping the produce completely safe for human consumption immediately or shortly after application.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ loo egbeɔ kooloi bibii yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni adesai aye amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo beni akɛtsu nii sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ.

english: How can I protect my ripe crops from insects when it is too late to use chemical sprays?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe? Mɛɛ be eshɛɔ sɛɛ tsɔ akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ baatsu nii?

english: When crops are ripe, you should switch to natural plant extracts or bio-insecticides, or practice selective early harvesting of ready fruits to protect them from pest damage without chemical risks.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ, esa akɛ otsake kɛya tsofai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ anɔ. Aloo kase bɔ ni ooohala aduawai ni esa akɛ aye lɛ mra. Koni abu aduawai ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe ni tsofai ahe oshara bɛ mli.

english: If my crop gets a fungal disease right before harvest, what is the safest way to control it without contaminating the crop?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ná tsɛŋemɔ hela dani akpa lɛ Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ akudɔ lɛ ni akafite tso lɛ?

english: You can use organic bio-fungicides or copper-based natural sprays that suppress the disease quickly without leaving long-lasting toxins on the food you are about to pick.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛ akɔɔble fee lɛ atsu nii ni okɛtsi hela lɛ naa oya ni oshiŋ tsofai fɔji ni eshwɛ yɛ niyenii ni obaaŋɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How many bags of maize can I reasonably expect to harvest from my land?
ga: Abele kotokui enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ makpa kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yield depends heavily on your seed variety, soil fertility, rain, and farming practices. With improved hybrid seeds and good fertilizer application, a well-managed acre in Ghana can yield anywhere from 15 to 25 bags, while larger commercial fields with high efficiency can reach close to 100 bags total depending on field size and farm management.
ga: Nibii ni anáa lɛ damɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ anɔ. Oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nugbɔshiimɔ, kɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi. Kɛ hybrid dumɔwui ni atsake kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Gbɛjegbɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii kɛjɛ kotokui 15 kɛyashi 25, yɛ be mli ni jarayeli ŋmɔji wuji ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii ni miihe ashɛ kotokui 100 kɛ abu fɛɛ naa, ni enɛ damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ kɛ bɔ ni akwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ahaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better for me to harvest my maize using a machine harvester or hire laborers to do it by hand?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛkpaa ŋmãa lɛ baakpa ŋmãa loo maŋɔ nitsulɔi ni amɛkɛ amɛdɛŋ atsu he nii?

english: A machine harvester saves a lot of time and reduces labor costs on large fields, but its performance depends on the operator's skill—an inefficient driver can waste or crush a lot of grain. Hand harvesting takes more time and manpower, but allows you to inspect and handle each cob carefully, which works well for smaller farms.
ga: Harvester lɛ haa be babaoo baa shi ni ehaa nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo baa shi yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli. Shi bɔ ni tsɔne lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ damɔ ŋaa ni mɔ ni tsuɔ he nii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsɔne kudɔlɔ ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ afite loo efolɔ ŋmaa babaoo mli. Nine ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ heɔ be kɛ gbɔmɛi ahewalɛ babaoo. Shi ehaa okwɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli jogbaŋŋ ni okɛtsuɔ nii. Enɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa ŋmɔji bibii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen feeds leaf growth, so when the plant runs out of it, it draws nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni haa baa lɛ daa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ tso lɛ baai lɛ eho Ebaagbala nitrogen kɛjɛ baai ni edara kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do some of my maize cobs have missing grains and empty spaces on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ ekomɛi amli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Missing grains mean the plant had poor pollination during flowering. If the weather is extremely hot and dry when the silk comes out, the pollen dies before fertilizing the grain spots on the cob.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ehiɛɛɛ pollen jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni egbi beni siliki lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ Pollen lɛ gboɔ dani eshɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: What causes my maize plants to fall over easily whenever a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa tsei shwieɔ shi mlɛo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa?

english: Plants fall over (lodging) when their roots are too shallow or their stems are too weak. Planting seeds too close together, planting too shallowly, or having stem borer pests in the stalk makes the plants fragile against wind.
ga: Tsei gbeeɔ shi (lodging) kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tsɔ loo kooloi bibii kɛ stem borers yɛ tso lɛ mli Ebaaha tsei lɛ afee mlɛo kɛha kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the ground without sprouting after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds rot when the soil is overly soaked with water and lacks air, or if planted too deep. High moisture suffocates the germinating seed, allowing soil fungi to attack and rot it before it emerges.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. aloo kɛji akɛ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, hulutsoo ni fa babaoo baaha dumɔwui ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ agbɔjɔ. Ha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ni amɛfite dani amɛkwɛ̃.
