english: Why are my maize plants thin and weak even though I applied fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer alone cannot make crops strong if the seeds were planted too close together. Overcrowded crops shade each other out and compete intensely for sunlight, air, and water, leading to tall, weak stems and small cobs.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ nu. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni kɛlɛ, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why does my crop wither quickly during short dry spells while my neighbor's crop stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔji lolo lɛ?

english: Your neighbor's soil likely has higher organic matter (from manure or compost), which holds moisture like a sponge. Deep-plowed soil also allows crop roots to grow deeper where water stays hidden during hot weather.
ga: Ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo. (kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli) ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hu haa tsei shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ. Nu lɛ baate shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa?

english: Maize is fully mature when the leaves turn dry and yellow-brown, and a tiny black spot forms at the base of each grain where it meets the cob. This 'black layer' shows the plant has stopped feeding the grain.
ga: Abele lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kwraa kɛ́ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi yɛ ŋmei lɛ shishi. Nɛkɛ ‘ŋmei diŋ’ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa edumɔwui lɛ niyenii.

english: What happens to my maize if I harvest it while the cobs are still wet?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji mikpa be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ mli edɔ lolo?

english: Harvesting wet maize leads to quick spoilage because damp grains attract fungi, mold, and insects. Wet storage can produce dangerous toxins (aflatoxins) that make the maize unsafe to eat or sell.
ga: Abɛi ni efɔ lɛ ni akpaa lɛ haa efiteɔ oya ejaakɛ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi bibii. Nibii ni akɛtoɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui. (Aflatoxin) ni haa ŋmãa feɔ nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ loo ahɔ̃ɔɔ.

english: Does rice need to grow in flooded swamp water, or can I plant it on regular dry land?
ga: Ani esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ anɔ loo abaanyɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni daa lɛ nɔ egbi nɔ?

english: There are two main types of rice: upland rice, which grows on well-drained dry land like maize, and lowland rice, which requires flooded or swampy fields. You must choose the right seed variety that matches the moisture level of your land.
ga: Omɔ henɔi titrii enyɔ yɔɔ: ŋmɔ mli omɔ, ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ ŋmãa, kɛ omɔ folo, ni biɔ hei ni nu hoɔ yɛ loo ŋshɔŋ. Esa akɛ ohala dumɔwui srɔtoi ni sa ni kɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kpãa gbee.

english: Why did my rice crop produce empty heads with no grains inside at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ woɔ yitsei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni dumɔwui bɛ mli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Empty rice heads, often called chaffiness, usually happen when the crop suffers from severe dry spells during flowering, lacks essential soil nutrients like potassium, or gets attacked by insect pests like stem borers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ ŋmãa lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na hɔmɔ ni naa wa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ stem borers ni tutuaa lɛ.

english: How do I protect my young rice fields from birds eating all the grains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔji lɛ ahe kɛjɛ okpoi ni yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ lɛ ahe?

english: Birds attack rice when the grains are soft and milky. You can protect your farm by installing bird netting, using scarecrows, making noise during early mornings and late afternoons, or planting at the same time as neighboring farmers so the bird pressure is shared across many fields.
ga: Okpoi tutuaa ŋmãa kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ mliki. Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ okpoi ahe ŋshɔŋlooi ni okɛbaatsu nii, kɛ gbee ni wa ni ooofee leebi maŋkpa kɛ shwane mli lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ adu tsei bɔni afee ni okpoi anɔnyɛɛ agbɛ ashwã hei babaoo.

english: Why can't I just clear bush land and sow my crop seeds immediately without plowing the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mafo ŋmɔji lɛ amli kɛkɛ ni madu dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuuu nii lɛ?

english: Unprepared bush soil is packed tight and full of wild weed seeds. Wild weeds grow faster than crops and will steal sunlight, water, and nutrients, which often leads to complete crop failure.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ji jwɛi ni asaaa nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni koo mli jwɛi dumɔwui eyiɔ mli obɔ. Jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Ni ejuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii, ni bei pii lɛ ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akpãtãa kwraa.

english: Why is it important to make my field flat and level before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee miŋmɔji lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Uneven land causes rainwater to collect in low spots and run off high spots. Leveling your field ensures that water and fertilizer distribute evenly to every plant so none of them drown or dry out.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni etseee lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ni ejɛɔ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ afee he lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ehaa nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jaa tsei lɛ fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ eko kwraa akagbo loo amɛkagbi.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for limited sunlight, air, and root space. Proper spacing gives each crop enough room to grow strong stems and produce a heavy harvest.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawu koni amɛná hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ shishifãi ahe he ko ni faaa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ shi ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young crops turning yellow instead of staying bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is starving for nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is too waterlogged and drowning the roots, preventing them from absorbing food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ miiho. Ehaa enyɛɛɛ eŋɔ niyenii

english: Why should I buy certified seeds from a dealer instead of planting leftover seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ jarayelɔ dɛŋ? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ piɛ ngɛ ye nyagbe ngmami ɔ mi ɔ.

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred to resist diseases, mature uniformly, and yield more food. Saved seeds lose their vigor over time, producing weaker plants and much lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai. shweremɔ ni yaa nɔ daa ni ewoɔ babaoo Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ sɛɛ foɔ hewalɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: How long does it usually take to see a successful harvest after I start planting a new field?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mináa ŋmaa ni yeɔ omanye beni mibɔi dumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Most grain crops like rice and maize take between 3 to 4 months (90 to 120 days) to mature. Following proper weeding, fertilizing, and water management schedules throughout this period ensures a full harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa mli babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa, heɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 (gbii 90 kɛyashi 120) dani ekwɛ̃ɔ. Kɛji akɛ akwɛ jwɛi, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu he gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa nɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aná ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii.

english: How can working with an agricultural extension officer help me avoid total crop failure on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nitsumɔ ni mikɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baatsu lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi koni ŋmɔshi nibii akafite yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Extension officers provide direct guidance on proper land preparation, correct seed selection, precise fertilizer application, and pest control, helping you avoid costly mistakes and maximize your farm's productivity.
ga: Mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋaawoo tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kpakpa he. Dumɔwui ni ja lɛ halamɔ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ Eyeɔ ebua bo ni otsiɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ tɔmɔi ni jara wa he ni ohaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii babaoo baa.

english: Why should I use black plastic drip hoses to water my crops instead of carrying buckets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ plastic ni ji drip hose diŋ lɛ atsu nii kɛwo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli nu moŋ fe ni mikɛ baagi baawo mli?

english: Drip irrigation hoses deliver water directly to the plant roots in steady, controlled amounts. This saves you heavy manual labor, prevents water loss from evaporation, and keeps plant leaves dry to avoid diseases.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ paipii amli lɛ kɛ nu yaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ bɔ ni sa, ni akudɔɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa onáa nitsumɔ ni he hiaa waa. Etsiɔ nu ni laajeɔ lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei ahe baai lɛ agbiɔ koni helai srɔtoi akamɔ amɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to water my vegetable crops every single day?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mahã mi-aduawai lɛ nu daa gbi?

english: Watering daily depends on your soil type and weather. While young vegetable plants need consistent moisture, overwatering every day can drown the roots and cause them to rot; the goal is to keep the soil moist, not soaked.
ga: Nu ni oooha daa gbi lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ nɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be moŋ. Shi kɛ́ afɔ nu fe nine daa gbi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Otii ni ma ehiɛ ji ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, shi jeee ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does using a water pump for irrigation help my farm during the dry season?
ga: Te nu pɔmp ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: A water pump allows you to move water from a river, borehole, or pond directly to your field. This ensures your crops get water year-round, allowing you to farm and sell crops even when there is no rain.
ga: Nu pɔmpii haa onyɛɔ okɛ nu jɛɔ faa, nu bu, loo nu bu mli kɛyaa oŋmɔji amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa nu yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Ehaa onyɛɔ otsuɔ okwaa ni ohɔ̃ɔ onibii yɛ gbii ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ po nɔ.

english: What are the main steps I need to follow to start growing pepper on my land?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛi titrii ni esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ mabɔi ŋmɔtɔ dumɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: To start growing pepper, you first nurse the seeds in a bed, prepare well-drained soil mixed with manure, transplant the seedlings after a few weeks, and ensure daily moisture and pest protection.
ga: Kɛji ootao oje ŋmɔtɔ shishi Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Saamɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii efutu mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo he kroko yɛ otsii enyɔ komɛi asɛɛ. ni akwɛ koni daa gbi hulutsoo kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe abu.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛtsɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when under stress, which is usually caused by excessive heat, dry soil from irregular watering, or a lack of proper plant nutrients in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛyɛ haomɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni fe nine kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kɛjɛ nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ hewɔ. aloo tsei amli niyenii ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: How can I tell if my pepper plants are receiving too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiná nu babaoo tsɔ?

english: If pepper plants receive too much water, their lower leaves will turn pale yellow, feel soft, and drop off, and the root system will struggle to grow due to lack of air in the wet soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tso lɛ nine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Eshishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo ni egbeeɔ shi, ni shishifãi lɛ naa naagba akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: What main practices do I need to follow to get a high yield from my tomato crop?
ga: Mɛɛ nifeemɔi esa akɛ mafee koni maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ tomato ni miduɔ lɛ mli?

english: High tomato yields require using quality seeds, staking the plants to lift them off the ground, applying balanced fertilizers at the right times, and maintaining consistent watering.
ga: Tomato ni baa babaoo lɛ biɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Staking ni akɛwoɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsuɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli ni akwɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ daa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black rotten spots at the bottom as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔi diji yɔɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Black rotten spots on tomato bottoms are known as blossom-end rot. This happens when the plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ hei diji ni fiteɔ yɛ tomato nɔ lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow plenty of big green leaves but produce very few tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji waa shi ewoɔ tomato fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: When tomato plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing tall stems and thick green leaves rather than producing flowers and fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: Why should I support my tomato plants with wooden stakes as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei akwɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Staking holds the plant upright, keeping the tomatoes off the damp soil where insects and rot can ruin them, while also allowing air and sunlight to reach all parts of the plant.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tomato tsei lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ. Kɛtsɔ tomatoi lɛ ni oooha amɛhi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. he ni kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni fiteɔ nii baanyɛ akpata amɛhiɛ yɛ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe.

english: How do I know when my cashew nuts are fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cashews lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cashew nuts are ready when the cashew apple above the nut turns bright red or yellow and the fruit naturally falls to the ground. Harvesting nuts directly from the ground ensures the nut inside is fully formed and high quality.
ga: Cashew ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ ayeɔ kɛ́ cashew ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ batsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni aduawai lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa Nibii ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my freshly picked cashew nuts feel heavy and wet inside when I cut them open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cashew nuts ni ajie ehee Mine lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ tsii ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ emli kɛ́ mifo mli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested raw cashew nuts contain natural moisture and liquid within the shell. They need to be sun-dried for three to four days until the nuts rattle inside the shell, which prevents rot and prepares them for processing.
ga: Cashew ŋmeii ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nu kɛ nu yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Esa akɛ amɛwo hulu lɛ mli gbii etɛ loo ejwɛ kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ baakpokpo yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni akafite ni asaa he kɛha nitsumɔ.

english: What happens to my harvested nuts if I store them while they still have water or moisture in them?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-beans ni mikpa lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛto be mli ni nu loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Storing wet or damp raw nuts causes mold to grow rapidly, turning the kernel inside black and bitter. Excessive moisture also attracts insects, destroying the economic value of your yield before you can sell it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni ahoo lɛ to he ko ni efɔ loo edɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ adara oya. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ hu gbalaa kooloi. Enɛ fiteɔ shika gbɛfaŋ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ he dani obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: How can I tell if my harvested crops are dried enough to sell or store safely?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mikpamɔ lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ loo makɛto shweshweeshwe?

english: You can test dry cashew nuts by taking a handful and shaking them near your ear. If you hear a clear metallic rattling sound, the kernel inside has shrunk away from the hard shell, meaning moisture levels are low enough for safe storage.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka cashew ni egbi lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni oooŋɔ ni okɛwo otoi he lɛ nɔ. Kɛ onu dade ni miihoso lɛ gbɛɛmɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ efo kɛjɛ ŋmei ni wa lɛ he. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: What steps do I need to follow if I want to process raw cashew nuts myself at home?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛi esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ kɛji miisumɔ ni matsu cashew ŋmeii ni ahoo lɛ ahe nii yɛ shia?

english: Basic processing involves drying the raw nuts in the sun, steaming or roasting them briefly to break down the toxic shell liquid, carefully cracking the outer shell with a tool, and then drying the edible kernel to peel off its thin skin.
ga: Gbɛ titri ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii ji ni akɛ hulu la atsu nii ni akɛgbi ŋmeii ni ahoo lɛ. Steam loo shãa be kukuoo ko. Koni ekɛgbala nu ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni yɔɔ ŋshɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ dɛŋdade ko atsu nii ni okɛfo kponɔgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, agbiɔ dumɔwui ni ayeɔ lɛ koni ajie amɛhewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Can I make use of the juicy cashew fruit attached to the nut, or should I throw it away?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ cashews ni mli ewo muji ni akɛkpɛtɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ atsu nii loo esa akɛ mashɛ mafɔ?

english: The juicy cashew fruit (apple) is full of water and sweet juice that can be processed into fresh juice, jam, or alcohol. While it spoils quickly after falling, processing it immediately creates an extra source of income beyond just the nut.
ga: Cashew nuts (apples) ji nu ni mli ewo muji ni ŋɔɔ ni abaanyɛ atsɔ mli afee nu hee, jam loo dãa. Eyɛ mli akɛ efiteɔ oya kɛji egbee shi moŋ. Shi nitsumɔ ni afeɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ kɛ shika kroko baa kɛfata ŋmeii ahe.

english: How many years will I have to wait after planting cashew seedlings before I can harvest my first crop?
ga: Kɛ́ odu cashew dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani onyɛ okpa oklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Grafted cashew seedlings usually start bearing fruits in 2 to 3 years, while plants grown directly from seeds take about 3 to 5 years to produce their first harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cashew dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni akwɛɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ baa.

english: How far apart should I space my cashew seedlings when planting on a new farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo cashew dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli?

english: Cashew trees grow wide canopies that need plenty of sunlight. Spacing them 10 meters by 10 meters apart prevents branches from overlapping, ensuring each tree gets full sun to produce maximum flowers and fruits.
ga: Cashew tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛitsu ni da ni biɔ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ mli. Mitai 10 x mitai 10 ni jɛkɛmɔ baatsi tsei niji anaa koni amɛkatsɔ amɛhe nɔ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la ni fa nɔ koni ewo fɔfɔi kɛ yibii babaoo.

english: What causes the flowers on my cashew trees to dry up and turn black before setting fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cashew tso nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ dani ewoɔ yibii?

english: Blackened cashew flowers are usually caused by tea mosquito bugs or fungal blossom blight. Spraying approved organic or chemical treatments just before flowering helps protect the blossoms so they can form nuts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Aedes aegypti ŋmei loo fungal baai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cashew fɔfɔi ni feɔ ediŋŋ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ dani ewo fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaabu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe bɔni afee ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why is sticky fluid leaking out from the bark and fruits of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni mli tse miiho kɛmiijɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewolo kɛ amɛyibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Sticky fluid or gum leaking from trees is often a reaction to insect borers damaging the bark or a fungal infection. Clearing weeds around the base and sealing trunk wounds prevents pests from stressing the plant.
ga: sticky liquid Loo bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ tso lɛ yibii loo ŋmeii ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ ahewɔ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ ni ajieɔ Base kɛ tso lɛ shishi pilamɔi lɛ ni aaatsi naa lɛ baatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkahao tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crop turning yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your maize plants are waterlogged, which prevents roots from taking up nitrogen from the soil. Maize plants need nitrogen to stay green and build food for growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi o-corn tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ agbala nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛfee niyenii kɛha amɛdalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and turning dry at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbi yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually a plant's response to extreme heat, drought, or a viral infection spread by tiny insects like whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ ji nɔ ni haa dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ loo helai ni baa mɔ mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ haa.

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from water stress, nutrient shortages in the soil, or when tiny pollinating insects like midges are absent from the farm.
ga: Cocoa tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji nu he haomɔ miipiŋ amɛ. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii bibii tamɔ midges lɛ laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce many flowers but very few fruits grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop blossoms without fruiting if temperatures are too high or if the soil lacks key nutrients like phosphorus during the flowering stage.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii titrii tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper fruits develop black, sunken spots at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi diji ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shishigbɛ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the plant, usually triggered by uneven watering or dry spells while fruits are forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo hulutsoo be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the stem base begins to swell and crack open from expanding roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni egbɛ eshwa kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get eaten into dust after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ tsɔɔ sũ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Storage pests called grain weevils bore into dry corn to lay eggs and feed. If the grain isn't properly dried or treated before storage, these insects multiply and destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ko ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe ni atsɛɔ lɛ seed moth lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ni egbi mli koni ekɛwo ŋmãa ni eye niyenii. Kɛji akɛ agbiko dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ loo atsuuu he nii dani akɛtoɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ baafa babaoo ni amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my plantain suckers dry out and die shortly after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers have weak root systems when transplanted and need shade and plentiful soil moisture to establish. Direct hot sun bakes the young shoots before roots can draw water.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ. ni ebiɔ hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛfee Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ shãa ŋmeii bibii lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and twisted inside the mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ bibii ni egbɛ eshwa yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become small or misshapen if the soil in the mound is too hard and stony, or if weeds compete aggressively for soil nutrients and light during the main growing period.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baafee bibii loo amɛbaafee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni tɛi babaoo yɛ mli. aloo kɛji jwɛi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa shi waa koni amɛná shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ la yɛ be titri ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cabbage plants fail to form tight heads and instead remain loose leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage tso lɛ efeee yitsei ni mli ewo wu ni ehiɛɔ baai ni etse ehe lɛ moŋ?

english: Cabbages fail to head properly if the weather is too hot, if watering is irregular, or if they receive too much nitrogen late in their growth cycle.
ga: Kaabaji nyɛŋ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa loo kɛji akɛ nitrogen babaoo nine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ dalɛ be lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning brown and drying up during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Harsh sun and intense heat cause cocoa trees to lose water faster than their roots can absorb it. Without enough shade or soil moisture, the leaves scorch and dry out as the tree attempts to conserve water.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa cacao tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, Baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ nu ato he lɛ.

english: Does strong sunshine help my cocoa pods grow faster or does it harm them?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya loo eyeɔ amɛ awui?

english: While cocoa trees need sunlight to produce food, intense direct sun can burn young pods and dry out the soil. Cocoa grows best with balanced shade from larger shade trees.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ hulu la he miihia cacao tsei koni amɛná niyenii moŋ, shi hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ŋmeii bibii lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Cocoa daa jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni ja jɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ amli.

english: Why are my cocoa flowers falling off the trees before they turn into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry conditions cause stress to the cocoa tree. To protect itself from dying, the tree sheds flowers so it can save energy and moisture until weather conditions improve.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa ni egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa kookoo tsei anɔ. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe kɛjɛ gbele he Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I continue harvesting my cocoa pods during very hot and dry weather?
ga: Ani manyɛ maya nɔ makpãtã kookoo ŋmeii lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yes, you can harvest ripe pods, but you must be gentle. Damaging the branches during dry weather puts extra stress on the tree when it is already struggling with heat.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃. Shi esa akɛ ofee blɛoo. Tsei niji ni fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛ haomɔ babaoo baa tsei ni kɛ hulutsoo lɛ miiwu omo lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it good to trim and cut branches off my cocoa trees during the sunny months?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaafolɔ kookoo tsei yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli?

english: Heavy pruning during very hot, sunny months exposes the main trunk and soil to direct sun. Light trimming is better so the tree canopy keeps shading the farm and holding moisture.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi waa yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ haa tso lɛ tso titri lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shɛɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofo kane lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ aye abua ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo aba ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why is my farm producing fewer cocoa pods this season compared to last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ miiwo kookoo ŋmeii fioo yɛ afi nɛɛ mli kɛ akɛto afi ni eho lɛ he lɛ?

english: Changes in rainfall patterns and long sunny spells reduce the tree's energy reserves. Proper shade management, soil care, and pruning help keep yield steady across changing seasons.
ga: Tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ haa tsei ahewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ baa shi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be ni sa, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa yibiiwoo lɛ yaa nɔ yɛ bei ni tsakeɔ lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: How can I keep my soil wet for my cocoa trees when the sun is very strong and there is no rain?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ aha kookoo tsei? Beni hulu lɛ naa wa waa ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground around your trees with dry leaves, weeds, or straw (mulching) blocks direct sun from hitting the soil, keeping it cool and trapping moisture near the roots.
ga: Okɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo jwɛi (mulch) aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ koni hulu la akatswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni emɔɔ nu ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Is it safe to put fertilizer on my crops when the ground is dry and the sun is hot?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: No, applying fertilizer on dry soil under intense sunshine can burn crop roots. Fertilizer needs moisture in the soil to dissolve properly and be absorbed safely by the roots.
ga: Dabi, shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi. Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I see more insect pests on my cocoa trees during dry, hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Hot weather weakens the crop's natural defenses, making it easier for pests like capsids to attack stems and pods that are already stressed by heat.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids lɛ akɛ amɛbaatutua tsei kɛ tsei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ.

english: Which food crops can I plant on my farm to shield young cocoa trees from intense sunlight?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛbu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he?

english: Planting plantains or cassava alongside young cocoa trees creates quick shade. Their broad leaves act like sunshades, protecting young cocoa plants from scorching while keeping the air humid.
ga: Kɛ́ adu plantains loo cassava yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba oya. Ebaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo be. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to protect their tender leaves from harsh sunlight and to keep the soil moist. Without shade trees or plantains nearby, the intense heat dries out the soil and burns the young crops before they can establish strong roots.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni eshãa tsei bibii dani amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow from the bottom up when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen if the roots are sitting in waterlogged soil for too long and cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shishifãi tara shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant is stressed, which usually happens during very hot dry spells or when the plant gets too much or too little water. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant retain its flowers and turn them into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ hɔmɔ kɛ latsaa ni naa wa be mli. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ náa nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides inside the central funnel of young corn plants where it is soft and moist. Catching them early and applying recommended natural or chemical controls protects the plant's growing point from total destruction.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu he ni tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ he kɛjɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɔ kwraa.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when heavy rain leaves excess water standing in the soil, causing waterlogging that suffocates the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows water to drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa, ni no haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nu shwieɔ shi, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛyaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce smaller yields when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other underground for water and plant food, while their leaves fight for sunlight. Giving each crop proper spacing gives it enough resources to grow big and fruit well.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna nu ni amɛdu niyenii. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha ená nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛkwɛ ni ewo yibii.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch plenty of sunlight, which the leaves use to make energy that feeds the growing yam tuber underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off damp ground, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Akɛ baai lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni akɛhaa sweet potato ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: Why does covering the dry soil around my plants with dry leaves help them survive the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle mi tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni akɛ baai ni egboi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that shields the ground from the hot sun. It traps moisture in the soil longer so your plants do not dry out quickly.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ gĩii oya.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ekomɛi? Ajie mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ

english: A main plantain tree can only support a few strong suckers at a time. If too many shoots grow at the base, they steal water and nutrients from the main stem, leading to smaller bunches of plantain.
ga: Dumɔwu titri lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ŋmeii fioo komɛi pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ be kome mli. Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa plantains bibii shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does clearing wild grass and weeds around my crops make them grow much faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie koo mli jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya kwraa.

english: Weeds act like thief plants that quickly steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds gives your crops sole access to the soil's resources, allowing them to grow much faster.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ nii, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ooojie lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ pɛ náa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya kwraa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential food it needs to grow strong, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha gbɔmɔtso lɛ dalɛ kpakpa Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do people say planting beans or cowpeas makes the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni adu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil, acting like natural fertilizer for the crops you plant afterwards.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni eshiɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I place solid fertilizer right against the stem of my pepper plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa woɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is very strong and concentrated; placing it directly against the stem can burn the plant's delicate outer bark and roots, causing it to dry up and die.
ga: Fertilizer lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ waa. Kɛ́ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa egbiɔ ni egboɔ.

english: Why are holes suddenly appearing in the middle whorl leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu ko eba trukaa yɛ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in the center leaves of young corn are usually caused by the fall armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip to feed on fresh leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ cutworm lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. ni kɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli koni eye baai heei lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots soft-rot under the ground when the heavy rainy season comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because the excess water suffocates the roots and encourages soil fungal diseases to grow.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct heat and sunshine; removing all forest shade exposes them to harsh rays that burn their leaves and dry them out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Koo lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa amɛnaa la ni naa wa ni shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when the weather becomes too hot or when the plant experiences water stress, causing the plant to shed its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ kpeɔ. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak if I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ebɛ hewalɛ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, they compete with one another for light, ground moisture, and soil nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough food to grow thick and healthy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ la lɛ he. shikpɔŋ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haaa tso ko aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha eda babaoo ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight, which helps the leaves manufacture food to build large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii ni amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I cut off extra small shoot suckers growing around my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra suckers act like hungry children stealing water and food from the main mother plant, which results in smaller plantain bunches if you leave too many attached.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbekɛbii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ dɛŋ. Enɛ haa plantains bibii baa kɛji oshi amɛ ni amɛdara tsɔ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow at the bottom when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to stay green and grow well. Adding compost, poultry manure, or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color and strength.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi ashishifãi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha efee ŋmɔŋ ni efee hewalɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas before maize help my soil grow better crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ dani aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and legumes have tiny nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the cowpea plants die and decay, that trapped nitrogen acts as free natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ legumes yɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni tsina tsei lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi lɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before any fruit appears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani yibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat or a lack of water. When stressed by severe weather, the plant drops its flowers to conserve energy and water just to stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛ haomɔ ba kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi gbohii amli lɛ Tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛhi wala mli kɛkɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when the rainy season is heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits around the roots without draining away, it smothers them and creates damp conditions that cause fungal rots to destroy the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kpɛtɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ejeee kpo lɛ Ekɛ fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin with small cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving crops proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food to build thick stalks and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kã ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my young crops grow so slowly when weeds are left around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo nɛkɛ be mli ni jwɛi eshwɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before crop roots can reach them. Clearing weeds early leaves all the plant food in the soil for your main crop to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi shɛɔ amɛhe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaashi tso niyenii fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha otso titri lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to lift them off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso koni ekɛwo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make the energy required to expand tubers underground. Lifting vines on stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight while keeping them away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ baai lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akaba shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Black pod is a disease caused by a fungus that spreads fast in damp and heavily shaded farms. Trimming extra tree branches lets in sunlight and air, which dries out the farm and stops the fungus.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba Enɛ baaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up into tight shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl when tiny insects like whiteflies suck sap from the leaves or pass a virus to the plant. Extreme heat and erratic watering can also cause leaves to curl up to save water.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ nu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ loo amɛgbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwã tso lɛ mli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ abɔle amɛhe koni nu akafite.

english: Why are there small holes chewed into all my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are caused by hungry insects like caterpillars and beetles eating the plant. As pests feed on the foliage, they prevent the plant from making food to form a solid cabbage head.
ga: Kplukai ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kooloi yeɔ baai lɛ. Amɛbaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekahoo kɛyashi ebaatsɔ kaabe yitso ni wa.

english: Why is it important for me to leave a measured distance between my crop rows instead of planting seeds randomly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ ni asusu he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui trukaa?

english: Proper row spacing ensures that each plant receives enough sunlight, air, and soil nutrients without competing with neighboring plants, leading to healthier growth and better harvest yields.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ Enɛ haa amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkpaa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I create clear paths through my field when setting up my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kɛtsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni misaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Clear paths prevent you from stepping on young plants or compacting soil near root zones during weeding, spraying, and harvesting, while also improving airflow across the farm.
ga: Gbɛ ni mli tse tsiɔ bo gbɛ koni okanyiɛ tsei bibii loo shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishifã lɛ he lɛ nɔ yɛ jwɛi shwiemɔ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and weak when I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they stretch unnaturally toward the sun to get light, making their stems thin and fragile instead of growing strong enough to support heavy crop yields.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ shwereɔ yɛ gbɛ ni jeee adebɔɔ nɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he koni amɛmɔ la lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl up during the hottest hours of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural survival trick where the plant reduces its exposed surface area to conserve water and protect itself from severe heat and drying winds.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa. Tsei baa amɛhe shi koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he.

english: How do I know if water is staying in my soil for too long after heavy rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: If water collects on the soil surface for days and crop leaves start turning yellow or wilting, the roots are suffocating from a lack of air in overly wet soil.
ga: Kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo ni tso lɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ loo amɛgboi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ tsɔ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small even when the green leafy top looks very large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much leafy growth fertilizer like nitrogen, the crop puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground rather than storing energy in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni baaha baai lɛ akwɛ̃, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ he wami ɔ ngɛ tso sisi nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do my young seedlings need temporary shade when I first put them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ he hiaa ni maná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko beni midu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Young plant roots are small and cannot absorb water fast enough to survive direct midday sun, so shade trees reduce heat stress until the crops grow strong root systems.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmɔmɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be mli haomɔ baa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow so much faster than my planted crops after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are adapted to instantly grab water and nutrients from the topsoil much faster than cultivated crop seeds can.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli oya fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: When a plant lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, it moves the few remaining nutrients from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the newer top leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ tso ko bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ ekomɛi kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my crops in straight lines instead of scattering the seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines makes it much easier to walk through the farm, clear weeds quickly, apply fertilizer accurately, and estimate how many crops your land can support.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyiɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ oya Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli pɛpɛɛpɛ ni osusu ŋmɔshi nibii ni abaanyɛ aye abua lɛ ayibɔ he akɔntaa

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct heat and harmattan winds because their roots are not deep enough yet. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides canopy shelter and keeps the soil moist while the young cocoa trees mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ adamɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants and leaving dark droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu bibioo ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ ni eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the growing tip of the maize plant. Inspecting your farm early and spraying targeted biological treatments or recommended insecticides into the funnel of the plant can stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni akɛkwɛɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛwoɔ tsei akutsei amli lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes twisting, shrinking, and showing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egbɔjɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Your cassava has Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies and by using infected stem cuttings. You can prevent this by planting improved, disease-resistant cassava varieties and using only healthy stems for planting.
ga: O ŋmei lɛ yɛ ŋmei mosaic hela. Virus ko ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Ni okɛ tsei ni wa pɛ atsu nii kɛdu nii.

english: How can I tell if my farmland has lost its nutrients and needs fertilizer before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ efo mli ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli dani madu nii?

english: If your crops grow slowly, have pale or yellowish leaves instead of deep green, or yield smaller fruits than before, your soil is nutrient-depleted. Adding organic compost or the right fertilizer restores essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus to the soil.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa blɛoo Ha baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ loo okɛ yibii bibii aba fe tsutsu lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I space my maize seeds apart instead of putting three or four seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala ŋmãa lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mikɛ ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ baawo bu kome mli?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole causes the plants to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each stalk enough room to grow strong and produce large, full ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmãa toi wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: The very first rainfall often only wets the surface and is followed by dry, hot days that bake the ground. It is best to wait until the rains become steady so the soil stays consistently moist enough for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ pɛ. Nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ ji gbii babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shãa lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ anɛ daa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do people recommend planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my field before planting maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu ŋmãa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil. When you plant maize on that same land next season, the maize uses that natural nitrogen to grow faster and healthier.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni eshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa kɛ nitrogen tsuɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni eda oya ni ená hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer feeds every plant in the soil, and weeds often have stronger roots that absorb nutrients faster than crop seedlings. Clearing all weeds before applying fertilizer ensures your crops get the food instead of the weeds.
ga: Fertilizer haa tsei srɔtoi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii. Ni jwɛi lɛ fɔɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni ŋɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei amli dumɔwui. Kɛtsɔ jwɛi fɛɛ ni ooojie dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaaha onibii lɛ niyenii yɛ jwɛi najiaŋ.

english: Why does my harvested maize develop mold and spoil when I store it inside bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni egboɔ kɛ́ mikɛto kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Maize spoils in storage if it is bagged while still containing internal moisture. Drying the cobs thoroughly in the sun until the grains are hard and crack when bitten prevents mold growth and insect infestation during storage.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lolo. Agbiɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee shiŋŋ ni amɛkuɔ kɛji akɛ amɛye. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii akadara yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant suffers from sudden heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulching around the roots helps the plants retain their flowers and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ trukaa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni okɛ shishifãi lɛ wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient crops need to grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps the leaves turn healthy green again and produce larger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛdara waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔji wuji.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the plants grow very tall leaves above the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ yɛ baai ni nɔ kwɔ waa fe shikpɔŋ lɛ moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or lacks potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of expanding its underground roots. Adding potassium-rich plant food or wood ash helps the plant direct energy into growing bigger tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi. Tso niyenii ni potassium eyi mli obɔ loo tso sũ ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛ bulbs wuji baa.

english: How do I know when it is safe to start sowing my seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground stays moist several inches deep after two or three steady rains, rather than planting after the very first light rain. Planting too early can cause seeds to dry out and die if the rains stop for a few weeks.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baawo inchii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, kɛ́ odu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without producing any tomatoes during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air stress tomato plants, causing them to drop their blossoms to save water and energy. Keeping the soil constantly moist with mulch and providing light shade during peak heat helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking sap from the undersides of leaves, or by heat stress. Spraying leaves with mild soapy water or neem extract helps control these pests so new leaves can grow flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli Kɛ akɛ nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛ saamɔ fee loo neem mli nu lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha baai heei lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in wet, dark, and crowded conditions. Pruning extra shade tree branches and farm leaves allows sunlight and air to dry the pods, which prevents the fungus from destroying your yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, duŋ, ni gbɔmɛi eyi obɔ lɛ. Niji kɛ baai ni afoɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli koni aná hulutsoo babaoo lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akafite nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the soil when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need oxygen to stay healthy, and standing water starves the roots, allowing rot fungi to attack. Building high mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away from the tuber so it stays healthy in wet weather.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Ni nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ amli nu afee shoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, rot fungus baanyɛ atutua. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tuber lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do plantain trees take much longer to produce fruit when weeds grow around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii beni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from young plantain roots. Clearing a wide ring of weeds around the base of each plantain tree allows its roots to get full feeding so it can grow fast and fruit sooner.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ plantain shishifãi bibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ he ko ni da ni bɔle jɛmɛ lɛ. Plantain fɛɛ plantain shishi haa shishifãi lɛ naa niyenii ni fa babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ ebaanyɛ eda oya ni ewo yibii oya.

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, they grow long stalks called pegs that push down into the earth to form the nuts underground. Soft, heaped soil makes it easy for these pegs to enter the ground and grow large pods.
ga: Beni afee ŋmei fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔi. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ haa ewaa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baadu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does planting cowpeas together with my maize help my farm grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ ni edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally feeds nearby maize plants. Intercropping also covers the bare soil to hold moisture and lowers the risk of losing your entire farm income if one crop fails.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Intercropping lɛ hu haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli ni ebaa oshara ni ji akɛ obaafite oŋmɔ mli shika fɛɛ kɛji ŋmãa kome fite lɛ shi.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil moisture quickly. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains provides shelter and maintains soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa mɔ náa he ko ni ehiɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ edamɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow from the tips down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tips is a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient maize needs to stay dark green and grow properly. Applying compost, manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores healthy green growth.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ mli lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures are extremely high or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Maintaining consistent watering and keeping soil cool with mulch helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to spend time putting wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be ni mikɛ tsei awo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to make food for the plant. Vines that climb properly produce much larger and healthier tubers under the soil than those left spreading on the ground.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛfee niyenii aha tso lɛ. Wein tsei ni akwɔɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba shikpɔŋ shishi fe nɔ ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and showing patches of yellow and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects and infected planting cuttings. Using disease-free planting materials and resistant cassava varieties stops this disease from destroying your yield.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ Kɛ okɛ nibii ni aduɔ ni hela bɛ mli kɛ ŋmei henɔi ni hela nyɛɔ eyeɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen gas from the air and traps it in the soil. This enriches the soil naturally, feeding the neighboring maize crop without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I get more crop yield from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: Planting seeds too close forces the crops to fight each other for limited water, soil nutrients, and sunlight, leading to weak plants and small harvests. Correct spacing gives each plant enough space and food to produce maximum yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi nu he tawuu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni faaa Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it harmful to plant maize on the exact same patch of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the earth. Rotating with legumes or root crops breaks pest cycles and restores soil health.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl inward during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling in the afternoon heat is the plant's defense mechanism to reduce water loss from its leaves. If the leaves uncurl in the evening when temperatures cool down, the plant is managing heat stress, but providing steady moisture helps reduce this shock.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni ekɛba nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ shi. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ kɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ miikpe. Shi hulutsoo be fɛɛ be ni akɛaaha lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ shoofeemɔ nɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow weak even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than domesticated crops and aggressively steal the nutrients, space, and sunlight intended for your plants. Clearing weeds during the early weeks of crop growth ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to mature strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe shia tsei. ni ekɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, he ko, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ otsei lɛ ahe lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need maximum sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet soil, catching more sun while preventing fungal diseases from spreading on damp leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa baai ni mli efɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting shoots in the barn before I even plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu amɛ po lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally wake up from their resting phase when temperature and air humidity change. Sprouting is the yam's way of using its stored energy to prepare for the next rainy season, so keeping the barn cool and airy helps delay this process.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ amɛwɔhe lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli latsaa kɛ latsaa tsake. Gbɛ kome ni ŋmeii ni shwereɔ lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛsaa amɛhe kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ nifeemɔ nɛɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: How do I know if my yam tubers are swelling underground when I cannot see them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efuu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi? Ni minyɛɛɛ mana?

english: You can judge tuber growth by watching the leafy vine above ground. When the vine leaves turn deep green and bushy, it means the plant is healthy and actively sending energy downward to grow and swell the tubers beneath the mound.
ga: Obaanyɛ okojo bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa amɛhaa lɛ kɛtsɔ wain tsei ni baai yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji wain tso lɛ baai lɛ batsɔ eŋɔli ni efee ŋmɔji lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni etsuɔ ​​hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekwɛ̃ ni egbɛ bulbs ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to let cut seed yams dry in the shade before putting them in the soil mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aha ŋmeii ni afo lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cutting a yam creates an open wound that rots easily in warm, moist soil. Letting the cut piece rest in a dry, shady place allows it to heal and form a protective skin that keeps out rot and soil pests.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni afoɔ lɛ haa pilamɔi ni mli tse ni fiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ koni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe yɛ he ko ni egbi ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛtsaa ni amɛfeɔ hewolo ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dry before the corn ears are fully formed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani abele toi lɛ eda kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants use for green growth. The maize plant naturally pulls nitrogen from its old bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves and developing corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa amɛ eŋɔli dalɛ. Abɛi yeɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ koni ekɛha baa bibii lɛ niyenii ni ekɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii aba.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or beans in the same field where I grow main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas have beneficial bacteria in their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil food. When you harvest them, that extra plant food stays in the soil to feed your next main crop.
ga: Muawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni okpaa lɛ Nakai tsei niyenii ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha onibii titri ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: How can my cassava plants stay green and alive during the long dry season without rain?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava survives dry spells by dropping its outer leaves to cut down water loss while storing thick starch reserves in its underground roots. When the rains come back, it quickly uses that root food to grow new leaves.
