ga: Cassava baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli kɛtsɔ esɛɛ baai ni eshwieɔ koni ekɛba nu ni efiteɔ lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ toɔ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba Ekɛ niyenii ni jɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii oya ni ekɛbaa baai heei.

english: Why does my plantain tree produce only one bunch of fruit and then start dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ yibii kome pɛ ni no sɛɛ lɛ ebɔi gbele lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is designed by nature to flower and bear fruit just once in its lifetime. Once harvested, that main stem naturally dries up so that young shoots growing from the base can get sunlight and take over to produce the next harvest.
ga: Adebɔɔ ji nɔ ni fee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. Kɛji akpa lɛ Akɛ tso titri lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ aná hulu la ni akɛtsu nii yɛ kpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Cocoa trees naturally bloom with hundreds more flowers than they can actually feed. The tree intentionally sheds unpollinated or weak flowers to save its strength and water for developing the healthiest pods into full size.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi ohai abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua diɛŋtsɛ. Tso lɛ jwɛŋɔ ni eshiɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe loo ni bɛ hewalɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni ekɛwo fɔfɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli kɛyashɛ he ni eshɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my food crops immediately after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miniyenii ni miduɔ lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, native plants perfectly adapted to the local climate, so their seeds wake up instantly after the rain. They quickly spread aggressive roots to grab water and plant food before young crops have time to establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni etsake amɛhe ewo maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛdumɔwui lɛ teɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ. Amɛgbɛɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ basabasa lɛ amɛshwãa oya koni amɛhe nu ni amɛdu niyenii dani tsei bibii lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛma shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure helps restore their rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni aná ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba emuuyeli mli.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my dry fertilizer right before a very heavy rain begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy downpours wash away dry fertilizer from the soil surface before the plant roots can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the ground is already moist or after light rains so it stays near the roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ koni ebɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm help make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas straight out of the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, they leave behind natural plant food that feeds your next maize crop without buying extra fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni okpaa Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ sɛɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii akɛ niyenii kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why do I see small caterpillars hiding inside the leaves of my maize and eating holes through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa baai amli ni amɛyeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which love to hide in the soft center of young maize plants. Spraying approved organic treatments or recommended insecticides early in the morning destroys them before they ruin your harvest.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ shwie amɛnɔ leebi lɛ, ebaakpata amɛhiɛ dani amɛbaafite onibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tight bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the plant's sap. Spraying your pepper plants early with soapy water or neem oil stops these pests and keeps leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni akɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ baashwie pepper tsei anɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni akpa nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ. ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting plantains next to my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu kookoo tsei yɛ emasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa trees the shade and cool moisture they need during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Does my yam crop really need tall wooden stakes to climb, or can I let the vines creep on the ground?
ga: Mi sweet potato dumɔ lɛ biɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni manyɛ makwɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Aloo manyɛ mashi wain tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛkɛ?

english: Yam vines need tall stakes so their leaves can catch full sunlight to make food for growing big tubers. Letting vines creep on bare ground exposes them to soil heat and diseases, resulting in small yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛha niyenii aha bulb agboi ni miida lɛ. Wein tsei ni ashiɔ amɛ ni amɛhoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa dɔlɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ helai. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot under the soil when heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays trapped around them without draining away. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows water to run off safely, protecting the tubers from waterlogging.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine ebɔle amɛhe. without draining out Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ yitso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce yellow flowers that drop off without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shwieɔ shi ni edaaa ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too hot or when the plant experiences drought stress. Giving your tomatoes steady water at the roots and placing dry grass mulch around the base keeps the soil cool so flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji tsei lɛ na hɔmɔ he haomɔ. Okɛ nu awo tomatoi lɛ amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi aha amɛhe. Shishitoo nɔ ni akɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why should I cut off the extra small shoots growing at the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and soil nutrients away from the main plantain stem. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the main plant to produce a much larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ plantain tso titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when there are no bigger trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle full, direct sunlight because their tender leaves burn easily and lose moisture too fast. Taller trees like plantains or forest trees provide shade and keep the soil damp, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ. Akɛni cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ shãa oya ni amɛmli shwieɔ oya tsɔ hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ hulutsoo. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape while the top remains green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves is a clear sign that your soil is low in nitrogen, which gives plants their green color. The maize plant is taking whatever nitrogen it has left from its old lower leaves and sending it up to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli Abɛi tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛhaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have tiny bumps on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth and acts as natural food for your next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ Beni okpaa amɛ Nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebaafee adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to apply my chemical fertilizer right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away off the surface of the soil or pushes it too deep into the ground where the plant's roots cannot reach it. This wastes your money and leaves your crops without the nutrients they need.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Enɛ baaha ofite shika ni ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa bo lɛ akaje onibii amli.

english: Upward curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. These insects feed on the leaf sap, which prevents the leaf from opening properly and stops the plant from growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ baa mli nu. Enɛ haaa baai lɛ agbele jogbaŋŋ ni ehaaa tso lɛ ada.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and stunted even when I give the farm enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ? Kɛji akɛ miha ŋmɔ lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po.

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal fertilizer, soil nutrients, and sunlight away from your main crop. Even with enough water, your crops are effectively being starved by the surrounding weeds.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ hulu la ni kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ po Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ po yeɔ hɔmɔ kɛjɛɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam vines produce smaller tubers when I let them spread on the ground instead of staking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii beni mihaa amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ amɛ baawo ŋmeii amli lɛ?

english: Staking holds the yam leaves up off the ground so every leaf can catch sunlight to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Leaves lying flat on the ground get shaded by each other and are more likely to rot or catch diseases from damp soil.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ fɛɛ anyɛ ana hulu la koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Baai ni ekã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi loo helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without forming any fruits when the heat gets very high?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, the pollen inside tomato flowers gets damaged and dries up, preventing the flower from being fertilized. When fertilization fails, the plant drops the flower to save its energy.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ baafite ni ebaagbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, anyɛɛɛ aŋɔ fɔfɔi lɛ awo fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ mli. Kɛji fɔmɔ nii lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots become woody and watery if I leave them in the ground for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ tsei kɛ nu kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots reach their best starch level at full maturity. If you leave them in the ground past their prime, the plant starts using up its stored starch for energy, leaving behind hard fibers and water.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yɛ starch ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛji amɛdara kwraa. Kɛji oshi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛteke he ni amɛyɔɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ baaje shishi ekɛ ŋmei ni ato lɛ atsu nii kɛha hewalɛ kɛyashi ebaashwɛ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ nu.

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically created by crossing two distinct parent plants to produce a high yield in the first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special qualities, resulting in uneven growth, smaller cobs, and much lower yields.
ga: Abɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni akɛfoɔ mli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains or shade trees next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Staking lifts the vine leaves toward the sunlight, allowing the plant to produce more food for growing large tubers while keeping the leaves off damp soil where diseases spread.
ga: Staking baaha wain tso lɛ baai lɛ akwɛ hulu la lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akafee shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ yɛ he ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which maize needs to grow green and healthy. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps correct this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ ni eyɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ he.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a virus carried by these insects. Controlling pests early stops the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Early Pest Control Ekpaa ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinators like bees to fertilize the flowers.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa loo pollinators tamɔ ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ ni bɛ

english: Tubers rot when water sits in the soil for too long during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess water to drain away safely.
ga: Tubers lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy rains and wind come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches. Supporting them with wooden props and controlling root-damaging worms in the soil keeps them standing upright.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ewoɔ aduawai babaoo. Tso ni akɛfiɔ amɛsɛɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni akudɔɔ lɛ haa amɛdamɔ shi jaŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and lets crop-specific pests and diseases multiply in the soil year after year.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni eha tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why shouldn't I spray my crops with pest chemicals during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane mli?

english: Hot afternoon sunshine causes chemicals to evaporate too fast or scorch the plant leaves. Spraying early in the morning or late evening protects the crop and works better.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ loo amɛshãa tsei ahe baai. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaabu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ni ebaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I wait until my seeds germinate before applying fertilizer near the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mitsei lɛ ahe?

english: Young seeds use their own stored energy to sprout. Applying strong fertilizer too early can burn the delicate new roots before the plant is ready to absorb nutrients.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii kɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani tso lɛ afee klalo akɛ ebaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why is my maize crop failing to grow when the rains stop coming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ?

english: Maize needs a steady supply of water to develop leaves and cobs. Without adequate rain or watering, the plant cannot absorb nutrients from the soil, causing leaf drying and failed grain production.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmãa be fɛɛ be koni ebaa kɛ ŋmãa. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ egbiɔ ni dumɔwui ni nyɛɛɛ akwɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stop growing during a dry stretch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plants take up soil nutrients like nitrogen through water. When the soil dries out, the roots cannot suck up nitrogen, which causes the green leaves to turn yellow and stunts growth.
ga: Tsei gbalaa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛtsɔɔ nu nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, shishifãi nyɛŋ aŋɔ nitrogen. Enɛ haa baai eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa amɛdaraaa.

english: What crops can I plant on my farm if the rainy season keeps becoming shorter?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ tee nɔ efee kuku?

english: Crops like cassava, millet, sorghum, and cowpeas have deep root systems or low water needs, allowing them to survive drought conditions much better than water-heavy crops like maize.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo nu ni he ehiaaa tsɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ nu babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Are there special seeds I can buy that grow food fast before the rains run out?
ga: Ani dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ mahe koni mikɛdu niyenii oya dani nugbɔ lɛ aba naagbee?

english: Yes, there are early-maturing or 'short-duration' seed varieties available through agricultural offices that complete their life cycle in 60 to 90 days, helping you harvest food before dry spells begin.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui komɛi yɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya? ‘Be kuku’ ni yɔɔ okwaayeli nitsumɔhei lɛ. Ewala be lɛ gbeɔ naa yɛ gbii 60 kɛyashi 90 mli, ni no haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii dani hɔmɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: How can I keep my soil wet for longer after a dry spell begins?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ beni mije hulutsoo be shishi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Mulching—covering the soil around your crops with dried grass, leaves, or crop leftover straw—acts as a blanket that blocks the sun and keeps soil moisture from evaporating quickly.
ga: Mulching—Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli. Okɛ jwɛi, baai, loo jwɛi ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ atsu nii—ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni ehaa sũ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: Why does my soil dry out so quickly after rain, causing my crops to wither?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ lɛ? Mahã midumɔ nii lɛ agbi?

english: Soil low in organic matter cannot hold onto water. Adding compost or animal manure mixes into the soil and acts like a sponge, helping retain rainwater for your crops' roots to drink over time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli faaa yɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ ahiɛ nu. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii futuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi koni otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What simple methods can I use to harvest rainwater for my crops during dry weeks?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akpaa nugbɔ nu kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ otsii ni nugbɔ bɛ lɛ amli?

english: You can dig simple farm ponds lined with tarps or collect rainwater from farm roofs into drums, using this stored water to hand-water crops during short dry spells.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nubu ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni akɛ tarpaulin ehà nɔ. Aloo bua nugbɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmɔji ayiteŋ lɛ naa kɛwo baagi mli. Akɛ nu ni ato nɛɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my seeds when rain patterns keep changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Instead of planting on fixed calendar dates, wait until the soil is thoroughly wet to a depth of about 10 to 15 centimeters after two or three strong rains to ensure seeds germinate safely.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ gbi pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ lɛ, Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ kwraa kɛyashɛ aaafee sɛntimita 10 kɛyashi 15 yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can planting two different crops together in the same field help my farm survive bad rainfall?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ ni mikɛaadu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ ni ehi shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, intercropping maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts shades the soil to reduce water loss, and gives you a backup harvest if the main crop fails due to low rainfall.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ni baa shi. Ni ehaa bo sɛɛfimɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ fite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ hewɔ.

english: How do I get official support or extension help for my farm when my crops fail due to poor rainfall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná maŋ yelikɛbuamɔ loo yelikɛbuamɔ kroko kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ? Beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ hewɔ lɛ

english: You can connect with local District Agricultural Extension Officers who register farmers to receive subsidized seeds, fertilizer assistance, irrigation advice, and weather-alert updates.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ okpokpaa nɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ni ŋmaa okwaafoi agbɛi awoɔ wolo nɔ koni amɛná dumɔwui ni akɛyeɔ abuaa amɛ lɛ abɔ. Nuŋtsɔ yelikɛbuamɔ Nu shwiemɔ he ŋaawoo kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he kɔkɔbɔɔ tsakemɔi

english: Why do some farmers plant their seeds in small plastic bags instead of directly in the main farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi miidu dumɔwui yɛ plastic kotokui bibii amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadu yɛ okwaayeli hei titrii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in small bags allows you to use clean sand or soil, which prevents young crops from catching harmful soil-borne diseases that might be present in the main land.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ kotokui bibii amli Ehaa okɛ ŋã loo shikpɔŋ ni he tse tsuɔ nii. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ akamɔ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do my young crops keep getting sick even when my farmland looks clean and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ yaa nɔ hela mɔɔ amɛ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ

english: Farmland often harbors hidden soil-borne diseases underground that infect plant roots, which is why starting crops in separate bags filled with disease-free sand helps keep them safe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaayeli hei lɛ hiɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa tsei shishifãi amli lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni tsei ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ kotokui sɔrɔtoi ni ŋã ni helai bɛ mli eyi mli obɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: How can I protect my new seedlings from diseases that are already living inside my farm's dirt?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu dumɔwui heei ahe kɛjɛ helai ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe?

english: You can isolate your plants by putting clean planting sand into small bags and growing your crops inside them, keeping the roots away from infected ground soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ ogbala tsei lɛ amli kɛtsɔ ŋã ni he tse ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ ni oookɛwo kotoku bibioo mli lɛ nɔ. ni adu tsei yɛ mli Enɛ ji koni shishifãi lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Can crop diseases stay alive in the soil even after I clear all the weeds from my land?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mijie jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po?

english: Yes, many soil-borne diseases live permanently underground in the dirt, which is why planting in bags with fresh sand is used to avoid exposing crops to infected land.
ga: Hɛɛ, helai babaoo ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ sũ lɛ mli daa. Enɛ hewɔ ni akɛ dumɔwui woɔ kotokui ni ŋã hee eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akashɛ hei ni hela lɛ yɔɔ lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: What is the benefit of putting sand into small bags for planting my crops?
ga: Ŋã ni akɛwoɔ kotokui bibii amli Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ tsei ni aduɔ lɛ he?

english: Using sand inside small planting bags provides a controlled, disease-free medium for crops to grow without being bothered by sicknesses present in the surrounding soil.
ga: Ŋã ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli lɛ ji gbɛ ni akudɔ, ni hela bɛ mli ni haa tsei lɛ daraa ni helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ he haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Why do my crop roots decay shortly after I sow seeds directly into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Root decay is often caused by soil-borne diseases in the land, which can be prevented by planting seeds in small bags filled with clean sand instead.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shishifãi fiteɔ. Abaanyɛ atsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ kotokui bibii amli lɛ nɔ. ni akɛ ŋã ni he tse eyi mli obɔ moŋ

english: Is it helpful to grow my crops in bags if I know my land has a history of crop sickness?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔi komɛi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ kotokui amli lɛ he? Kɛji mile akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai ahe yinɔsane

english: Yes, planting in bags with clean sand allows you to bypass diseased land entirely so your crops can grow healthily without soil-borne infections.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ odu nii yɛ kotoku ni ŋã ni mli tse eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa otsiɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ hei ni helai yɔɔ lɛ ahe kwraa. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni hela akabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: What does soil pH mean when agricultural officers talk about it, and why should I care?
ga: Mɛni shikpɔŋ pH tsɔɔ kɛji okwaayeli he onukpai wie he? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu he?

english: Soil pH is a scientific measure of how acidic or alkaline your planting soil is, which determines how easily your crops can take up nutrients to grow properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ pH ji jeŋ nilee mli susumɔ ni tsɔɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni okɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ ji acidic loo alkaline. Enɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ atsu nii mlɛo koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it easier for an extension officer to test my soil when I plant in small bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaaa kɛhaa extension nitsulɔi lɛ akɛ amɛaaka shikpɔŋ lɛ amɛkwɛ kɛ́ amɛmiidu nii yɛ kotokui bibii amli lɛ?

english: Planting in small bags keeps the sand contained in a manageable amount, making it simple for officers to accurately measure scientific factors like soil pH.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ kotokui bibii amli Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋã lɛ ahi shi bɔ ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii. Enɛ haa onukpai lɛ susuɔ jeŋ nilee mli nibii tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ pH lɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How does using bagged sand help me monitor the scientific conditions of my crop's root environment?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋã ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni mikɛ jeŋ nilee taoɔ bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ mli?

english: Because the sand is isolated inside a bag, officers can easily measure key parameters like pH without interference from the surrounding field soil.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋã lɛ mli egbala kɛjɛ kotoku lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, mɔ ni tsuɔ he nii lɛ baanyɛ asusu nibii titrii tamɔ pH lɛ he mlɛo. ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ mli lɛ tsiŋ enaa

english: Can I grow rice during the dry season if I have access to water from a dam?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ nu kɛjɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ, ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ be mli ni nu bɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, rice can be grown during the dry season if you have a dam or water source, as long as you use irrigation channels to supply continuous moisture to the crop's roots when there is no rain.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli kɛji oyɛ faa loo nu jɛɛhe. Shii abɔ ni okɛ nu shwieɔ shi lɛ baatsu nii koni ekɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ aya nɔ okɛdu shishifãi be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ,

english: Why does water sit on top of the soil in my rice field instead of soaking in quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ oya lɛ?

english: Rice fields often have heavy clay soil that holds water on the surface, which is actually good for rice because flooded water prevents weeds and keeps the plant roots continuously moist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eji nɔ ni hi diɛŋtsɛ kɛha ŋmãa lɛ ejaakɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi anaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do some parts of my field dry out faster than others after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fãi komɛi gbɛ́ɔ oya fe ekrokomɛi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?
